# VibeSpace — engineering log

This file is the engineers' record of every release: the lanes, the verification rounds and what they found, the gate reds and their causes, measurements, the choices made and why. Below its own `# Changelog` title it holds the changelog as it stood before 2026-09-29, verbatim (2.369.198 and older).

`CHANGELOG.md` (with `CHANGELOG.zh.md` and `CHANGELOG.ja.md`) is the user's: what changed for the person using VibeSpace, one plain line per change, in the interface's language — the rules are in docs/changelog-style.md. From 2.369.199 on, every release also writes its section here, under the same `## <version> — <date>` heading as its user entry and in the same commit, newest first above the verbatim record.

## 2.369.422 — 2026-11-27

### 2.369.422: the hotfix of 2.369.421

#### What it is
- After 2.369.421 an account row in Manage Agents could turn «unknown».
- The cause is a premise nobody measured: the belief that the event stream states a reset to its own second, so an equal instant could only be a copied window.
- The miss is the coordinator's: a premise about the shape of a vendor's data was taken without a measurement. The rule since: such a premise is measured on real data before a unit is taken.

#### The cure
- THE LAW: no row is held, no reading is set aside and no member is kept out of a pool because two accounts' weekly resets coincide. What proves a foreign window is identity, never a clock.
- A release whose write is refused is said in the journal and made at the row's next reading.
- Not in the hotfix: the door (a row's own read at a person's press); its widening on the one notion of a row's own account rides the train. The window guard's own re-file of a moving row's first readings of a new week is the train's as well.
- The device: src/reading-lag.js is an input of the device agent's bundle, so a newly signed agent rides this release.

#### Its proofs
- THE PICK: ONE product commit on the release 2.369.421 (1a4abf716), no merge: 2649d67de (lane login-request-card), its unit's record below. Picked clean, no meeting; its tree (f54a49b2b) is the commit's own; ten files (the three CHANGELOGs, docs/changelog-engineering.md, docs/kb-file-structure.md, scripts/test-account-reset-door.mjs, scripts/test-reading-truth.mjs, src/reading-lag.js, src/reading-repair.js, src/server/usage-pool-engine.js), none of the four spend files. Then the bump 2.369.421 → 2.369.422 (package.json, its lock's two own lines, src/agentd/version.js) and this notes commit.
- THE AMEND: 2649d67de is the words-only amend of 45528d45e, the tip the round and the rows read (the round's one must was in the words). Under src/ every changed line is a comment, and the three product files with their comment lines taken out hash equal at both tips (the coordinator's read).
- THE DEVICE BUNDLE, built and stripped as section 107 builds it: at 2649d67de 5329341 bytes, sha256 3650c55426d14840aa97ede5f3fc569a8dd7a3a2fce784cfacb495847641dd69 (kit run 02b647f8f-20261127171718-box), byte for byte 45528d45e's (kit run 484cb600a-20261127165649-box); unstripped 6734195 bytes; 677 inputs, one of them changed: src/reading-lag.js. ### login-request-card — the hotfix's unit: no row is held because two accounts' weekly resets coincide (主开发 r5407 / r5410 / r5442, the owner's hub)
- WHAT THE OWNER SAW: the hub took 2.369.421 (it ran 2.369.418 before) and at its first start one account row turned «unknown — the same as (another row)'s to the second, press refresh». The coordinator measured on a real hub (counts and shapes only, never committed): every weekly reset instant the event stream stated there was on a whole hour, and a panel's statement on a whole minute. The vendor puts weekly resets on the hour, so honest accounts share one.
- THE FAULT, three clock holds of row B-6a92, each resting on «a window that agrees with another account's is that account's»:
  · (a) THE STANDING CHECK (2.369.419; reading-lag sameInstantHolds through the engine's holdSameInstants, at the start, hourly and at every anchor write) held a row whose unproven anchor shared another account's instant to the second;
  · (b) the REPAIR's «others on this instant» skips (2.369.419) left such a row un-seeded, un-restamped, un-confirmed;
  · (c) the RING's HOLD AT A MOVE (2.369.418: 6d6e4d3e7, r541 / r560) held a row whose run of readings MOVED its phase onto a window another known account holds (within the reading-match tolerance). With resets on the whole hour that is a clock's coincidence, about one in 168 for each other account at every move, and at a vendor-wide reset every row but the first to move.
  A held row's readings on that instant were archived (guardReadingTarget); the pool never placed a conversation on it and moved a start off it (heldForPool, reason held-same-instant). A whole paid account dropped out of the pool's placement until a person's press.
- THE CURE, PURE REMOVAL on the release 1a4abf716 (ruled r5410, made again on the true premise r5442): (a) and (b) are gone, as at 2.369.418 — the standing check and its instant rule (sameInstant, SAME_INSTANT_SEC, sameInstantHolds, eventPreciseStamp, provenOwnStamp), and the repair seeds, restamps and confirms as at 2.369.418; (c) is gone BY THE INCIDENT LAW, not as an undo: the ring writes no hold and carries none, so a move re-anchors as before 6d6e4d3e7 (through 2.369.417); the guard archives no reading for a same-instant hold. The hotfix therefore goes BEYOND 2.369.418 for a move.
- WHAT THAT LEAVES OPEN: a row whose sign-in folder holds another known account's login re-anchors onto that account's window after K readings, and that login's readings are then filed under the row, as through 2.369.417; identity closes it with the train's unit, never a clock.
- A HOLD ON DISK (either kind, written by 2.369.418 to 2.369.421) IS RELEASED at the start's warm (usage-pool-engine releaseClockHold, the identity repair's boot run and again hourly): the row shows its window again and the pool may place on it at once, no press; one journal line a row. In the seconds before the first warm a panel read or a press still meets a hold on disk as in the release, and the warm ends it.
- LEFT AS IT IS, said: the door (liftHeldWindow) returns at «no hold» — no scene at this tip exercises its code (the train's widening brings its legs back); the pool's held-same-instant reason and notice words, heldForPool, the windowUnknown words of the holds and their dictionary rows read a hold nothing writes any more (the build's key check does not ask; the train removes them). The window guard's own re-file (decideReadingTarget) is unchanged here: the train's row.
- LEGS (test-reading-truth, each with its red: the release's rule planted back in a copy of this tree's engine): the MEASURED scene (two honest rows, anchors and event-precise witnesses on one whole hour, Vela's unproven, Orin's proven: after the start neither held, nothing unknown, each files its reading, the pool places on both); A PHASE MOVE ONTO ONE NEW HOUR (both rings move there: neither held, both re-anchored, Vela's next reading filed); A START WITH EACH HOLD KIND ON DISK (both free at once, the start says it once a row). The B-6a92 section's legs that encoded the premise are restated as no-hold legs or gone (named in the line); test-account-reset-door: the repair's read count 14 → 13.

## 2.369.421 — 2026-11-26

### 2.369.421: the hotfix of 2.369.420

#### What it is
FIVE commits on the release 2.369.420 (0eed6b0f5), no merge: ONE product commit and four tests-only commits.
1. aac185e41 (lane paced-wake-retry; data/bin/chat-wrapper.js, 22 lines, with its leg): THE STOP REACHES THE CLI FIRST. 2.369.420 SHIPPED A REGRESSION: on a person's Stop the conversation wrapper first dropped the held messages, and that drop's record went through the handed records' write, which this train (2.369.420, the wrappers' unit B) had made a SYNCED replace: the interrupt was forwarded to the CLI only after that sync. On a slow or network data folder the Stop landed late by the sync's length, and a tool that ended inside the wait handed the model the held message: a request after the Stop. THE CURE: on a Stop's road the handed records' write is OWED until the interrupt is forwarded (inside a batch: until the batch's end, before any line of it is said); what makes «nothing held runs after the Stop» stays in memory and in front of the forward. THE LAW, from this release on: NOTHING BETWEEN A PERSON's STOP AND ITS INTERRUPT WAITS ON A DISK.
2. 62102d289 (lane bl-chat-a, tests only): test-chat-first-hold's two legs take their starting point as PAINTED; the rows of «one reader» by identity; a row not there is a named skip.
3. 247b03b51 (lane bl-tests-chrome, tests only): test-design-window's PDF step on Chrome 158.
4. 79a892472 and db32c48b4 (lane bl-tests-chrome, tests only): the exit family's stand-in pages on Chrome 158 (they answer the unload permission for themselves, so the browser keeps them out of its back and forward cache as the suite's premise asks); a leg skips only on positive evidence that the page was loaded again, else it is judged.

#### PLACED, before it was called anything (the correction of the release word of 2.369.420)
The mirror of 2.369.420 read test-claude-steer-chrome section A leg 3 (the stop law) red on both tries in its first attempt and green in the re-run on the same runner image. THE RELEASE WORD OF 2.369.420 CALLED IT «the one hosted flake»: THAT WAS WRONG, and it was the coordinator's sentence. Lane paced-wake-retry placed it at will after the push, three tries of three (the probe 915d221fa, never lined; the kit run 915d221fa-20261126160506-box): with the handed records' sync HELD 1.5 s the Stop reached the CLI 1.5 s late and the tool's result carried the held frame to the model; with the sync free the Stop reached it in 2 ms. A hosted red in a path the train changed is the train's until it is placed otherwise: «flake» is written only on a placement.
WHO MET IT: a person on 2.369.420 only (pushed 15:20Z 2026-11-26), and in proportion to the data folder's sync: milliseconds on a local disk, seconds on a network folder.

## 2.369.420 — 2026-11-26

### lg-recovery — the synced stores' flush off the hub's loop (the coordinator's r3321; B-0248's first row, lane bl-loop-b's page)
- THE HARM (measured by lane bl-loop-b, run 0bb87c578-20261123145953-box): src/sync-store.js rewrote the whole file through a rename ON THE MAIN THREAD 2 s after each burst of typing — 502 ms a flush with 500 ms placed on each rename, about 300 flushes in ten minutes of typing; every client's echo waited behind it.
- THE CURE (one commit on the store-read unit): every change hands the file to the store writer under its row `sync-store.write` (src/timed-sync.js) — bytes made at the write, on the writer's thread; `rank: 0` (a person's typing, written in the stop's first pass); due within `saveDelay` of the first unsaved change; a failed write said (the writer's line, and the store's once a failing run); `flush()` writes nothing on the loop; held, nothing is asked and the bytes refuse by name (EHELD).
- THE LEGS: test-sync-store-hold ⑯ — the loop's longest turn with 300 ms placed in each main-thread rename / fsync under half the release's write at the call (its red, a copy); typing in the stop's first pass (red: a copy without rank 0); a failed write said once (red: a copy without onWritten); a held store asks nothing and the lift asks once.
- CENSUSES: test-store-write-census: the row of src/sync-store.js 4 → 2 (the boot's ensureDir stays), DEBT_MAX 803 → 801; test-temp-rename-census: the flush's unsynced rename row dropped, OWED_MAX 141 → 140; test-sync-fs-census: the row 5 → 3; test-architecture §72: the row `sync-store.write`; scripts/ci.mjs: test-sync-store-hold restated 0.98 → 1.9 s (alone 1918 / 1915 ms on the test machine, both zones, run 524d0e33a-20261125035654-both, ALL PASS 88, on line 750's fourth cure), FAST_SUM_CAP_MS 2471 → 2472 s by arithmetic on the train's second pick a570e01a8 (the stated sum 2471.081 s over 899 rows), test-ci-gate's pin with it. The two suites that read drafts.json right after the door (test-queue-putback, test-doc-comments-sync) hand the store scratch.mjs `landingWriter()` (r3428 law 2).

### lg-recovery — the synced stores' one read under the store-read law (the coordinator's r3262 / r3271, its cure round r3654; the store census's item 2)
- THE HARM: src/sync-store.js read a failed or torn drafts.json / stage-sync.json / uploads-sync.json / settings-sync.json as «nothing at version 0»; every stop, crash and 2 s save wrote it over the file, and every page took the empty answer as the truth (a fresh page loaded it; a reconnecting page's rollback branch re-pushed its whole copy; an idle composer was cleared; Stage closed side windows; the Doc strip deleted its local copy). LEG RED AT THE RELEASE 0a031b541: run 424f6e95a-20261123135941-box, 16 ✗.
- THE CURE (for 2.369.419; moved from the hotfix trial tip 83d286175 onto 2.369.417 because its pick met src/ui-needs.js, then onto 2.369.418's release 51400954d and onto the 2.369.419 train's first pass 725162b8a (r3874), because its pick met the held-word tables, the held-list names and the dictionaries — appends at their ends, both sides kept): the one read through src/store-read-hold.js (held: nothing written over; read again off the loop; torn bytes kept aside once); both doors answer HELD (503 by name, `state-held`).
- THE CURE ROUND (r3654, the first round's six musts all in what a person typed while held): the hub's overlay, the lift's merge and the named-version rule LEFT. WHILE HELD THE HUB TAKES NOTHING: a page's set or delete is answered `state-held` with its key and reaches no other page; the lift loads the file and sends ONE snapshot. THE PAGE OWNS WHAT IT HOLDS UNSENT (StateSync): nothing sent while unread; text stays in the page's map and is sent once at the store's first snapshot — a true edit from a page that held the data, a JOIN (the saved text, then what was typed, landed as a prefix) from a page that never saw it, whose deletions are nothing. A page unread says so at its reconnect and gets the full snapshot (the restart road). Structured changes (Stage, an upload row) act for that page only and are said not kept; Clear History refused. Stop's put-back while held is owed and joined in front at the lift, said by count. The Doc strip's add refusal and Stage's recent-use guard left (their reason is gone).
- THE SECOND ROUND (r3890, two musts with one root: the owed put-back): Stop's put-back while held now goes to every OPEN page at once (`state-held-putback`), which keeps the words as typed text, so a page's own edit at the lift sends them and a hub restart loses nothing a page holds; only with no page open is it owed (at most 20, said «in memory only»), handed to the first page that connects while held, else laid on the ordinary road AFTER the lift's snapshot with the door's belt noted at its version. «Had seen the data» means «had seen this version»: a page whose last version is older than the first snapshot joins its text and its deletion is nothing. Smalls: a held answer arriving after a snapshot is dropped; the hub's held words said by store (Stage and uploads keep nothing); the census comment and the put-back's journal line say what is true.
- THE THIRD ROUND (r3972): the rollback re-push stands for a page that had seen the data, held or not — at a torn lift (version 1) its drafts of before the hold are pushed again, at a lift below its version its newer draft stands; a unit typed or cleared while held is rule (C)'s alone, never pushed twice. A fresh lift (torn bytes set aside, or no file) says `fresh`, in its snapshot and in an unread page's resync, so a page's version equal to the new counter by chance is no true edit and no skip. A held reply read after the lift's snapshot still lands the put-back words it handed (owed words leave the hub only to a page that has them).
- THE FOURTH ROUND (r4040), LAW (E): a restore never beats a write, and the hub decides. The page's rollback re-push goes as a restore (`restore: true`); the hub applies it only to a key nothing has written or cleared in this life (since its start or its lift), an applied restore being a write; a page never restores absence; a refused restore is answered `state-restore-refused` and the page takes the hub's value. A page that wakes late after a torn lift no longer writes its old copy over another page's work, and at the lift an idle page's old copy never beats a page's held-time text.
- THE REQUIRED FOLLOW (r4106): an owed put-back laid at a torn lift no longer takes the key before the page's earlier draft comes back — the hub joins the two (the words in front), whichever arrives second, and answers the page with the joined value. The waking page's box shows the hub's value while a restore is decided (no flash of the old text); a person typing meanwhile keeps their text; a restore no longer stamps the conversation as mid-draft. The kb says law (E)'s known costs plainly (an earlier life's writes, a crash-lost clear, a restore meeting a new hold, a short draft inside the queued words, a keystroke inside a joined restore's round trip). Its cure (r4180): a restore unanswered at a socket drop goes back into the page's own copy (the box told); a lift at a lower version joins the put-back's words and the page's newer draft once (the hub keeps what stood under the words). test-sync-store-hold's row stays 1.9 s (alone 1914 / 1893 ms with r4180's cure, run 8836347f0-20261125081425-both, ALL PASS 111); the fast cap holds at 2472 s (the stated sum 2471.081 s over 899 rows).

### lg-rewind B-437e files tier — what must hold before U1 turns the tier on (主开发 r2372, round wh0ju65os's five + its smalls)
- (1) THE RECORD FOLLOWS THE CONVERSATION: the kept copies and their lines are keyed by the harness's own conversation id (src/server/rewind-kept-door.js convKeyOf → data/rewind-kept/<backend>-<id>/), so a resume or an exit — a new session id — keeps every line and its door; told frames name the page's session (`sid`). **B. NEW WITH THIS TRAIN**

- **N1 (a new known fault of the release, found by the build machine's row 1026: NOT CURED HERE).** In a person's words: **a kept browser that nobody else holds can end at once when the person's own browsing ends, where it was to stay one more idle period.** The cause, in src/server/browser-keeper.js: when a person's browsing ends, the keeper removes the person's holder row first, then waits for the tabs' read and the CLI's closes, and only after that stamps the idle clock. A keeper tick whose idle check falls in that window finds no holder and the old drop time, and stops the browser one idle period early. ### cli-update-needs-nothing B-9584 — THE PLACE'S ROAD (B), the owner's choice (主开发 r1791 / r1898): a place is given only to the sites the person lists
- THE LIST (src/browser-environment.js, PURE): a place's `sites` — each an EXACT origin (scheme, host, port; no wildcard, no suffix match), default none, at most 20, judged at the door and again at use (a list that fails gives no site the place); beside «blocked» refused; the log carries their count, never an origin. Only the dialog (the next unit) writes it; no agent verb does.
- THE HOLD IS THE ONLY GIVER (src/server/browser-geo-hold.js): on its own socket, once every open tab holds the place, an every-origin «denied» and then a «granted» per listed site — nothing written into the profile, so a dead hold, a stopped hub, a crash leave every site «denied» (measured). A new context is granted after its first tab's place, before its release; a re-arm grants again only after its places, and an arm or a re-arm releases its paused tabs only once those grants are set (a tab a dead socket left paused read «denied» on its listed site when released at its place, measured). No browser prompt: every other site is denied in silence.
- THE FOLLOW'S ROUND'S FOUR LAWS (主开发 r2172), before a place is reachable: (a) an ephemeral profile or a paired machine's asking a place or «blocked» is REFUSED BY NAME at its start (browser_place_unsupported) — it has no hold and no stored denial, never started «not applied»; (b) OURS KEPT APART: the denial stamps every row it writes, and the give-back restores a row only while it still carries that stamp — a person's later «block» is never given back as «allow»; the default only while it still reads our «block»; (c) the record's «confirmed» falls when the hold is lost, down or refused at a restart, and comes back when it holds; (d) a give-back that half ran never runs again over what the person changed since (the same stamp rule).
- With sites on the list, a tab the hold could not place is CLOSED; the person is told once a run, and the agent whose tab it was hears why by name at its next command (the rebound note's «place»).
- OPEN, the owner's to choose (主开发 r1907): an «Allow» the person gives in the browser's own bar on a held profile is stored by the browser and outlives the hold — the measure (e)/(f) of test-browser-geo-hold-measure reads both ways first. Until then the hold's every-origin denial covers it while the hold lives.
- ROUND w3ajkyup0 (主开发 r2311), four musts: (1) LAW (b) OVER TWO HELD LAUNCHES — a row the person changed since our last denial (a stamp none of ours) is the person's in the kept values, so a block set while held gives back a block (the kept file carries the stamp before, for a crash between the two writes); (2) a context holding a tab the hold could neither place nor close gets no grant — none under an empty name for the default context, and one already granted has its listed origins set back to «denied» at once; (3)(4) an agent's set or clear of a tab's position and the LOCATION permission are refused by name (`place_held`, src/browser-mediation.js placeVerdict) on a profile with a place or «blocked». ### login-request-card — B-9dd0: every suite Chrome resolves no name but the loopback's and the suite's own (主开发 r3727)
- **Why (the harm measure, the probe 55394096f, never lined; run 55394096f-20261124170543-box):** 164 rows were sampled, 159 of them census rows. The hub, the CLIs and every child that is not Chrome reached NOTHING past the loopback, and no model vendor's address appeared in any row. But all 14 rows with a Chrome child reached Google's background services (component downloads on :80, 443 over TCP and QUIC, the push channel on :5228) in spite of CHROME_QUIET's switches.
- **What (tests and harness only):** scripts/scratch.mjs gains `chromeNames({ map, own })`, THE ONE names rule. Every name is mapped to «^NOTFOUND» except the loopback's (127.0.0.1, [::1], localhost) and the suite's own (`map`: a name to an address, ahead of the rest; `own`: EXCLUDEd, resolved as usual). CHROME_QUIET carries it, so every suite Chrome gets it, and chromeBelt takes its rule from the same builder.
- **The vendor's source** (chromium.googlesource.com, tag 157.0.8103.78):
  - services/network/public/cpp/network_switches.cc: `kHostResolverRules[] = "host-resolver-rules"`, «These mappings only apply to the host resolver»;
  - net/base/host_mapping_rules.cc: the list splits at «,» and a rule at « »; the FIRST matching MAP wins, and a matching EXCLUDE stops the search;
  - net/dns/mapped_host_resolver.cc: a name mapped to «^NOTFOUND» fails with ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED, and «any invalid mapping» is treated as if it were «^NOTFOUND».
  The belt wrote «~NOTFOUND», which the source does not name: it failed only as an invalid mapping. The builder writes the vendor's literal.
- **The launches that wrote the switch themselves now take it from the builder:**
  - test-artifacts-intent-chrome and test-phone-titlebar-ui keep their own dead proxy and take the rule from CHROME_QUIET (chromeBelt would bring r1521's probe-the-belt law with it);
  - test-chat-mermaid-chrome → chromeNames();
  - test-integrations-ui, test-voice-chrome, test-voice-teach-chrome and test-tailnet-reach-chrome's RULES → chromeNames({ map }).
  test-integrations-ui's rule had only its two MAPs, so every other name resolved; now none does.
- **The belt's CONTROL** (chromeReach, a Chrome with no belt): CHROME_QUIET's rule refuses the box's own name too, so the control gets that one name through the rule's allow list (`own: [the box's name]`), the switch's last copy. Without it the control SKIPs: «with no belt this box did not reach its own name», found by the unit's own heavy read of test-https-hub-chrome.
- **The lasting guard is a census, not a reader** (test-architecture §47d over scripts/chrome-store-census.mjs):
  - a launch that does not spread CHROME_QUIET brings no rule, and is red;
  - a launch whose own list names the switch is red by name;
  - so is any file of the scope whose text names it, unless a NAMES row says why. The rows: scratch.mjs; the agent browser's own config in two suites' scratch HOME; the tailnet suite's driver line; the census's own controls.
  - RED controls: a literal-only quiet launch, a launch naming the switch, a planted file holding it in a const, and a stale row.
- **Named remainders, out of this unit:**
  - the agent browser's own Chrome in the real-driver rows (test-browser-live reached Google's :5228 and :443). The product already has a seam for a suite's row: the scratch HOME's ~/.agent-browser/config.json `args`, which test-browser-propose-chrome and test-vault-login-chrome already use;
  - test-window-target's Chromes, launched by the product's desktop-app road with the suite's catalog `args` (its NET list).
- **THE ROUND wefb09ae6 (主开发 r3968, the tests round; NOT TAKEN, one must):** the catch-all takes an address written as numbers too. The vendor's net/base/host_mapping_rules.cc RewriteHost matches `base::MatchPattern(host_port->host(), map_rule.hostname_pattern)` with no branch for an address, and base/strings/pattern.h says «* matches 0 or more characters» (tag 157.0.8103.78). So a page at the box's own LAN address failed.
  - Cured: test-desktop-v2-latency-chrome, test-mac-ard-signin-chrome and test-browser-live-input give their LAN address through the builder's `own`. scripts/xpra-window-boot.mjs gives the box's own name (its seven xpra suites' plain-http pages); the sweep found it.
  - The builder now REFUSES a name that would split the rule (a space, a comma) or open it (a star in `own`, an empty name).
  - test-architecture §47d runs the builder from its own text: the order (a suite's map ahead of the catch-all) and the refusals, each with a red copy.
  - The belt's comment is reworded: the names rule alone now refuses all three probes, and the control tells belt from no belt. The control's `args` (after its rule) are handed by no caller.
- **Line 889's follow (主开发 r4009, taken with no must; four smalls):**
  - CASE: the vendor lowers every pattern (net/base/host_mapping_rules.cc AddRuleFromString: `rule.hostname_pattern = base::ToLowerASCII(parts[1]);`, for MAP and EXCLUDE), and a page's host is canonical lower case. So a machine name with a capital letter needs nothing.
  - The builder refuses a question mark in `own` beside the star (pattern.h's two wildcards), and the empty name's refusal says it would OPEN the rule.
  - Two pure legs in §47d: a machine with only the loopback never throws at a launch (the four guarded forms read from their text, and the belt handed nothing builds its rule); and, by text, the value each of the four hands the builder is the value its page is opened at. The xpra boot's HOSTNAME is opened by test-desktop-xpra-window-open and -seamless, the two of its seven suites that open a page at the name. Each leg has its red.

### bl-browser-a — rows B-98f5 / B-bcf8: the idle-paint thaw's flip tab is born where no browser driver looks (主开发 r3944 / r3960)
- THE CAUSE (placed on the box by probes 6 to 10, rows 721-725; the driver's published source at v0.38.2 read by three readers): the thaw's blank (about:blank, alive 20-43 ms) is a page tab a driver on the raw road takes. Its drain (every 100 ms, and at every command's start and end, under ONE lock) attaches and prepares it; a tab closed mid-prepare holds that lock 30 s, since nothing fails a CDP call whose target went away. Unpinned (a conversation's own browser), the registered blank also becomes the session's active tab, and its close leaves the session on its LAST tab, with no notice.
- THE CURE (src/browser-idle.js FLIP_TAB_URL, PURE; src/server/browser-dialogs.js showFront): the flip tab is born at chrome://version/ (Chromium's kChromeUIVersionURL at 154.0.8037.57), which the driver's should_track_target never takes (chrome://, chrome-extension://, devtools://), on the event road and the connect road alike. THE GUARD ON THE FACT: while a flip runs the watch keeps each tab's birth address (Target.getTargetInfo when the event is late). A browser whose flip tab is born where a driver would take it is never frozen again, said once in the journal (idle_paint_flip_tab_taken). It is checked once before its first freeze, in a window of its own, unfocused, and at every flip. The census row thaw-blank (src/browser-windows.js) names both create sites.
- MEASURED (probe 10, row 725, Chrome 154.0.8037.57 + agent-browser 0.38.2):
  - the flip at that address held 0 times in 180 (no command in flight; commands ending inside its life; asked inside its life, where neither a pinned nor an unpinned session listed it), and every birth address was chrome://version/;
  - the about:blank flip held 2 times in 100, and moved the unpinned session to another tab in 35 of 100;
  - the paint: hidden to visible, 30 frames in 500 ms, the same as the blank;
  - nothing stays: 0 tabs back at a restore, 0 History rows.
- LEGS:
  - fast test-browser-tabs (the stand-in now sends each tab's birth): every thaw create carries the address, and the one check runs in its own unfocused window; RED control: the release's about:blank flip. The guard: a birth reported at about:blank, or empty, means the browser is never frozen, said once; a thaw flip born elsewhere after a passing check means it is not frozen again.
  - heavy test-browser-hidden-paint g: 30 product flips. An unpinned session with a second tab after A's reads its own page every time, no command runs over 2 s, every birth is chrome://version/, and neither session's own tab counter moves.
  - A DRIVER UPDATE THAT CHANGES ITS FILTER turns these red (the note at src/browser-verbs.js AGENT_BROWSER_CLI).
- NOT IN IT: row B-bcf8 (the relaunch's 15-30 s first command, with Chrome's own restore) is not placed (0 of 15 relaunches) and stays open.
- ROW B-346d, test-browser-resume-ui ⑩ (3) (主开发 r4191; placed by lane card-door-in-chat's deciding read, page-r4169-deciding.md): its one red try was the LEG's race — a push of the browsers' digest from the hub itself (the keeper's 5 s tick) fell between the leg's plant and its read at 390. ### bl-loop-b — the machine login's kept read keyed on what two contents cannot share (主开发 r2551 / r2575, for 2.369.417)
- WHY: src/usage-routes.js kept its read of ~/.claude/.credentials.json keyed on the file's TIME alone. The time ticks in 1 ms on a local disk (measured: a write, a stat and a write got the same time in 1808 of 2000 tries, run a84994d06-20261122212331-box), so two writes by the vendor's CLI inside one tick, with the hub's read between, kept the first token. Once it expired, the poll kept the last-known usage until the CLI's next write.
- THE CURE: the key is the time, size AND inode (a refresh by rename has a new inode). A kept sign-in past its own life is READ AGAIN FROM THE FILE whatever its key says — a file read and nothing else (no request, no child, no timer: the hub never refreshes this sign-in), once at the expiry and then at the poll's own pace (5 min). That closes the residual (an in-place same-size rewrite inside one tick). ALSO CURED: a sign-out in the file, or the file gone, drops the kept sign-in (the previous token was still used); an unchanged signed-out file is not read again; the past-life pass never asks the macOS Keychain (no child). The kept read lives at module scope now (it read nothing of setupUsage's).
- Legs: scripts/test-cli-usage-parse.mjs «the machine login's kept read» — two writes inside one frozen tick by rename and in place, the bound (50 asks: one read; at the pace one more), the sign-out, zero requests and children counted; the size, a read that throws past the life, macOS's Keychain, a gone file; reds: the time alone, the inode cut, the size cut, the read again past its life cut, the pace cut, the stamp cut, the Keychain guard cut, the sign-out's and the gone file's drop cut, a request on the past-life pass. The module exports getOAuthToken (its legs).

### lg-store-writes — the writer unit: two lanes, the fence a file, a whole write by reference in pieces (the coordinator's r1323 / r1328; row B-360d's unit 2 with lane bl-mail)
- LAW 1, NO WHOLE WRITE HOLDS A TURN: a store may hand a whole write as `byRef(list)` (one turn's Buffers, never written into after the hand-over, with that turn's seq); the writer copies it in pieces of 4 MB, one piece a turn, to the whole-write thread (pieceJob: the last piece synced, closed, renamed). Measure 6 on the test machine (186 MB, 200 000 rows): today's join 127–265 ms a turn, a list posted whole 134 ms, 4 MB pieces 3.8–5.2 ms.
- LAW 2, A SMALL APPEND NEVER WAITS BEHIND ANOTHER FILE'S WHOLE WRITE: a second writer thread for appends; the bytes pick the lane; the FENCE IS A FILE (one job of a file across both lanes). Each lane restarts and falls back to the main thread on its own, said by its name; an append lost with its thread fails (ETHREAD) and is written again. A synchronous flush or the exit mid-pieces sends the rest in its call. «Beside» weighed: asynchronous calls in one thread would use the process-wide libuv pool, the outage class the writer was built to avoid.
- LEGS: scripts/test-store-writer-lanes.mjs (a)–(n), split out of test-store-writer-r4 for its fast seconds, each with its RED where one exists (one lane; no fence; a plain list; the sync removed; the settle without its check; the exit's parked loop without its list).

The census's smalls (r1365) and its «mv» gap (r1366 (4)) ride along: an mv at a template piece's end, «mv» as a program name — each with a planted control; a bare call is excused by its SCOPE, never a whole file. ### bl-loop-b — the sign-in guards compare the content (主开发 r2697, for 2.369.417)
- WHY: src/account-material.js guards a member's .credentials.json before the long-lived-token sync writes over it, sets it aside or removes it, by its inode + time + size as read. A refresh by the vendor's program of the SAME SIZE written IN PLACE inside one tick of the file's time (1 ms on a local disk, run a84994d06-20261122212331-box) keeps all three equal. The guard then passed, and a FRESH sign-in could be replaced by an older one or set aside.
- THE CURE: the guard compares the BYTES. The sha256 of the bytes read is kept in memory only, in a WeakMap beside the read's stat: never written, logged, answered, broadcast or put in an error text. It is compared on the moved file itself, right after the atomic rename, in the move aside and the archive's post-check, and on the remover's re-read. A change means ours is not written and the fresher file stands; accounts.js says it once an episode by the member's name. No vendor call, no refresh, no timer.
- THE WINDOW: the compare reads the inode the rename moved, which is out of the name. A writer that opens the file by name after the rename lands at the name: link(2) of ours refuses EEXIST, or its own rename replaces ours. What is left is a writer that opened the OLD inode before the rename and writes through that open file after the compare: its bytes go into the aside, which the act then unlinks. That window runs from the compare's read to the aside's unlink (one read of a few KB and one link); nothing on our side closes it short of a lock the vendor's program would honour (not verified that it writes so).
- THE SAME UNIT, its fresh read's finds: (1) the read's stat is taken AFTER its bytes, so a write between them pairs a newer time with the bytes read (a refusal, never a pass). (2) An expect that carries no sum (a copied stat) is a change, never a silent fall back to the stat alone. (3) A filesystem WITHOUT hard links (link EPERM / ENOTSUP / EXDEV…): the put-back after a refusal (the move aside's and the archive's) copied nothing back, so the fresher sign-in rested at a .dead name with its own name EMPTY and the next tick wrote ours; now it goes back by an EXCLUSIVE copy (COPYFILE_EXCL: never a replace; a third write there leaves it archived), 0600 and synced before its source is removed. Ours into the empty name takes the same exclusive copy instead of the check-then-rename, which could replace a sign-in that landed between them. The journal words are neutral: «its credential file changed or went since it was read — ours is not written; what is there stands».
- Legs: scripts/test-oat-materialize.mjs §8 «r2697 the content guard» — a same-size refresh in place inside one frozen tick at the move aside of a re-mint, a clear and a strip; by rename; at the archive's rename of a dead login; before the remover's own read again; two refused acts back to back (said once); with no hard links (the put-back of both roads, and ours into an empty name that a sign-in took); an expect with no sum (the swap and the remover); no content sum, nor its first 16 characters, on any console door, in the reply, the facts or accounts.json. Each with its red: the content compare cut in all three acts, the inode and content cut, the archive's compare cut, the remover's compare cut, the once clause cut, the journal line cut, a sum prefix planted in a warning, the copy back cut, the check-then-rename fallback, a missing sum read as the same (swap, remover). Censuses: scripts/mount-reader-census.mjs account-material 13 → 15 (the compare's read; the copy's sync); test-oat-mint ② and ⑦ name copyInto (the third content writer: an exclusive copy into an empty name, secret-box's key-mint fallback shape) and drop the archive's own link / unlink and linkInto's rename; test-key-file-law's RULE 5′ classifies account-material (its sha256 is of the bytes read, memory only, never written); test-temp-rename-census drops linkInto from account-material's «move» row (its check-then-rename is gone; a named family, so OWED_MAX stays). The HEAVY scripts/test-oat-materialize-sweep.mjs: its r1 control's sync stand-in for account-material's fs.promises gains readFile and copyFile (every member the module now calls; its 200 dead logins take the archive road, whose compare reads the moved file). src/account-material.js is a DEVICE BUNDLE input (src/agentd/agentd.js requires it for repointPoolSymlink).

### bl-browser-a — B-3dbd (主开发 r3305; found by bl-tests-a): a late measure judges a put-back by its own fact, never by a clock
- THE FAULT (bl-tests-a's page, work/b3dbd/engine-distribution-finding.md): test-engine-distribution's round-3 leg lost on loaded machines (6 of 287 runs, machine 2). The PRODUCT lost, not the leg. An ask whose ONE bound was spent only LOOKED at its put-back, `within(p, 50)`: 50 ms of wall clock raced the put-back's real file reads (its stats of the copy beside the place and of the place). On a busy machine the reads outlasted it, and the forced measure was refused «being put back» while nothing was aside and a kernel stood in its place — the refusal the round-three law says never happens there. A person met a false refusal; a second try could pass.

### lg-vault-file — the run door's store HELD on a failed read (主开发 r2920: a find of the store-read law's independent verification, lane lg-store-writes VR1; for the hotfix after 2.369.416)
- THE FIND: the owner turned two entries OFF for runs; at the door's next life ONE read of data/vault-run.json failed (a network data folder's error or timeout). The door failed closed for that life (right), but `load()` took the failed read for an EMPTY state, so the owner's next switch saved that fresh state plus the one change over the healthy file: the OFF switches were gone, and with them the ON list, the «always» records, the policies with their approvals and hours and the press-opened marks. An OFF suspends every use of its entry, so a use the owner had suspended that way opened again. The release wrote over the same way.
- THE LAW, for this store: a read that FAILED is no state. The store is HELD: the door stays closed for runs; every owner write (switch, policy, «always») answers `store_held` BY NAME (503; the Vault window words it with what to do, zh / ja); nothing is written over the file; it is read again OFF THE LOOP until it answers, and the next load reads it as at a start — no restart, every switch stands. «missing» right after «unreadable» is read once more before it counts as a new store. Bytes read whole that do not parse are kept aside ONCE, named by their digest; the door fails closed as before. While that copy is in flight every owner write answers `store_held`; a copy that FAILED holds the store (the file is their only copy: never written over, src/store-read.js afterSetAside's law) until the read again keeps them.
- ONE law (`lawOf`) judges every read: the load's and the read again's. A data answer resets the «missing» count; only the load's own data read ends the hold's memory, so a flaky «missing» right after a lift is read once more too.
- NOT CHANGED: the sealed run's exec, the scrub. NAMED, its own small: src/server/vault-use-grants.js loadGen has the same shape over data/vault-use-marks.json.
- THE CURE ROUND (主开发 r3040, round wokvqzw2b's must and smalls): A PERSON'S PRESS WHILE HELD IS ATTENDED — «Always», «Allow for 1 hour» and a standing request's Allow share standOpen, which now asks the hold FIRST and answers `store_held` by name; the three callers (and the legacy «always» save) do not settle on it, so the card or request stays open to press again after the lift (it was «could not be put back» over nothing written, and settled «denied»). THE HOLD IS ASKED FIRST at every owner door (a switch OFF no longer takes back grants before its refusal; a Revoke never answers «done, 0»; a resume; an owner's Save in «Who may use it…» while held). THE TORN COPY, THE FAMILY'S WAY (src/store-read-hold.js keep): dated names, a byte compare with the newest 20 copies, written whole under a `.part-` name, synced, and put in place only when whole, a partial removed — no digest of the store's bytes in a name. A HOLD THAT CANNOT MEND BY ITSELF (a link, past the bound, not a regular file) says its cause and what to do (`cause`, worded in the window, zh / ja). The read again reads the file WHOLE (a short read reads on).
- LEGS of the cure (⑥c 7–9, each with its red): a short file from before is never taken for the copy and a copy that fails part-way leaves nothing behind (red: a keep that trusts «exists»); a standing request's Allow while held is refused by name, stays open and lands after the lift (red: a press road with no hold check); a Revoke, a policy and a resume while held are refused, and a store that is a link names its cause (red: a Revoke with no hold check). Censuses: scripts/mount-reader-census.mjs (the door's reader sites 31 → 36: the copy's listing, compares and own open), test-temp-rename-census (the copy's rename: synced, family self-synced), test-task-injection (the copy's dated name: a file name, never shown as a time).
- THE SECOND CURE ROUND (主开发 r3147, round wahuu2ayn — the first round's harm by another order: after a lift the PRESS's own load met the torn bytes again, so a hold asked before it missed it): THE ONE DOOR `ownerLoad()` (loaded, THEN the hold asked) for every owner door and press road; `heldIn()` the callers' one helper (the hold by code OR cause: nothing settled, no «failed restore»); standOpen answers the hold with nothing written before any restore; the For-you card handlers and the route word a held press (zh / ja); the copy's promise has a rejection road; the keep reaps `.part-` files a day old. LEGS ⑥c 10–12: the one door read in the source (red: a planted door that asks the hold itself); the round's torn press across a lift (red: today's order — asked, then loaded); a day-old `.part-` reaped, a fresh one kept. Legs 2, 8, 9 re-pointed at the one door (their reds name each guard they take away).
- LEGS (test-vault-run ⑥c; every failed read PLACED — an fs open that fails as the leg says — never a real mount), each with its red control: the verifier's scene (red: the release load); a switch refused while held, ON and OFF, worded in the window (red: the save with no hold check); the lift without a restart (red: a read again that never lifts); «missing» after «unreadable», at the read again and at the load after the lift (red: a «missing» taken at once); torn bytes kept aside once; torn bytes whose copy failed are never written over (red: a failed copy not held).
- USAGE-RESET-CLAIMS.JSON UNDER THE STORE-READ LAW (主开发 r3003 (b)): a failed read or torn bytes were read as empty with the rewrite mark set, and the save ran AT THE START with no act — the person's «I reset it» claims, their outcomes and the said-once reset memory gone. Now held on the helper (bba938858): nothing written over it, a claim and a dismissal refused by name (`reset_claims_unread`, 503), nothing a reading would note is noted while unknown (never a reset said again); lifted as at a start; torn bytes kept aside once, then the empty shape saved once. ### B-e31b part 1 — test-helm-render's API law is the helm version's own (lane chrome-157; 主开发 r896, 2026-11-21)
- **Why.** The hosted runner's image moved to Ubuntu 26.04 with Helm 4.3.1 on 2026-11-07, and the workflow has been pinned to ubuntu-24.04 since 2.369.386 as a seam. Section N's last leg read «the fake API saw discovery GETs only — nothing was written» as `asked.length > 0 && every request a discovery GET`. Helm 3's `install --dry-run=client` reads the cluster's discovery first; Helm 4's contacts no API at all, so the empty list was red every time (int361's .386 mirrors: Helm 3.22.1 green on 24.04, Helm 4.3.1 red ×2 on 26.04).
- **The law, by the helm that ran.**
  - Nothing is written: every request the fake API saw is a discovery read, over ZERO requests too.
  - «It saw discovery reads» is Helm 3's premise alone. A Helm 3 that asked nothing never reached this fake API, so its law would be vacuous, and that is red by name.
  - The major is read from `helm version --short`, and the leg prints every request it judged.
- **Helm 4's behaviour without a Helm 4.** No helm binary is fetched, here or on a test machine. A stand-in for helm (a small module the suite writes into its scratch folder) is spawned as the suite spawns helm, with the same install argv, KUBECONFIG and driver env. By its mode it asks what Helm 3 asks (the four discovery GETs) or nothing (Helm 4), and, the planted write, one POST after either.
  - Each plant is proved to have taken first.
  - The law is green on both behaviours.
  - It is red with the write planted, under either major, and the write is named.
  - Helm 4's empty list judged by Helm 3's premise is red by name: the 26.04 red this replaces.
- **Not in this part.** Running the whole heavy tier once on the newer image, and the unpin, are a hosted run through the coordinator and lane bl-ci, after 2.369.414 is pushed.

### gmail-connect-wall — B-1425: the hub's root facts are read off its loop (one read in flight, ever; a caller that can wait, waits)
- **The fault:** src/server/agent-tool-generators.js read the checkout's .git, its gitdir under <common>/worktrees/ and its commondir with synchronous calls ON THE HUB'S LOOP. It happened once a minute at most, and at every call while the last read erred; the temp roots' and home's realpaths ran at every call. The callers included every remote conversation start. On production the checkout sits on a network mount, so a stat that did not answer held every conversation.
- **The cure:** the reader is async, and only ONE read is ever in flight: the next starts only after the last came back. Its 2 s deadline only decides what a waiting caller is told. The roads that can wait await the facts (boot, the switch, the probe, the routes, both remote starts, the tools install, the watch's re-judge). The rest read the cache, and a stale cache refreshes off the loop. A read that never answered is a NAMED fact, never a hold.
- **Gates:** test-server-root ⑧ (fast) and the new heavy test-root-facts-loop-hold. The placed hold is a FIFO .git and the judge is the 3-number one; the RED CONTROL is the release's synchronous road.
- **The full round's cure (r827):**
  - the person's CLI index waits for the facts at listen, so «not judged yet» never makes a hub a throwaway;
  - a machine's agent-tools status and uninstall await them, and an unknown root's uninstall is refused by name;
  - the journal's refusal line is never spent on «not judged yet»;
  - the async routes answer a throw with a 500;
  - the heavy suite's hold has a second, independent releaser.
- **The narrow round's cure (r872):** the cure's first note was a `//` comment in the MIDDLE of the listen step's last line, so the calls after it (the three boot timers, bootRestored, the first sessions sweep, bootPhase.arm) never ran, while every text pin stayed green. The note now ends the line, and test-server-root ⑧ reads the PARSED tree: the last turn must CALL each of them as code. Its red control (the note put back) loses them by name.
- **The follow (主开发 r953): the law runs where helm is absent.** The pure verdict and the four stand-in legs need only node and a fake API, so they are now N0, BEFORE the «no helm» skip, and every machine judges them (a suite that skips whole where a program is absent hides the legs that never needed it). The skip now names what it leaves blind: sections A–M (`helm template`) and N's real install. Section N keeps the real install, judged by N0's verdict through the same fake-API helper. The box's first run (int361, helm v3.21.3): ALL PASS (127).

### lg-recovery — B-46fc part 2: a page that leaves with its socket not open hands its layout save to the hub by a second road
- THE ROW'S REMAINDER (part 1 shipped in 2.369.412 by bl-windows: the leave's flush): a page reloaded while its socket to the hub was NOT open lost the last layout change — the leave's flush queued the save in the closed socket (ws.js `pending`) and the page took the queue away. Said in layout.js since part 1; not solved there.
- THE PAGE (src/lib/layout.js `_handOffQueued`, after the leave's flush at pagehide / hidden — its own listeners, registered after the flush's): the layout-sync frames the closed socket queued are taken OUT of the queue (a page back from the back-forward cache never sends them twice), the newest per desktop, and handed to POST /api/layout-sync by fetch keepalive (a request that outlives the page; same-origin with the owner's cookie — auth.middleware's gate and same-origin rule stand before it as before every route), within 60 KB in all (a larger frame stays queued, said). src/lib/ws.js stamps every layout-sync frame with this page load's `writer` token.
- THE HUB — ONE «apply a layout save»: the body of ws-handler's `layout-sync` case is `applyLayoutSync(ws, data)` (moved byte for byte, its `break`s now `return`s); the socket's case calls it with its socket, the route through src/server/layout-sync-door.js with a stand-in client whose answers come back in the HTTP reply (`{ok, answers}`). No line in server.js (the door is a module both sides require). The route is bounded (256 KB, 413 by name) and guarded like every desktops door (a held store answers by name).
- THE ORDER against the socket's saves: the frame carries its page's `base`, so the staleness gate (§6b guard 11) refuses a save written from an older base than the record another writer stored since — a late save from a page that left never overwrites a newer layout another device saved meanwhile. THE WRITER TOKEN: the route's save naming its page's token is judged as that page's own socket's writer, so the page's own earlier write (its ack unread when the socket closed) is not «another writer's» — without the token it would be refused stale and lost.
- LEGS: test-layout-sync-route (new, fast, in-process over the REAL ws handler): the same frame by the socket and by the route writes the same record and answers the same ack; a late save from an older base after another writer's newer record is refused stale (the record kept, nothing written or broadcast); the writer token's own-write judgement with its control (no token ⇒ refused); the bounds (no door 503, not a frame 400, past 256 KB by name); the wiring. test-phone-resume-keeps-layout-ui ⑥ (HEAVY, the row's own gate): a real page opens a files window with its socket CLOSED in place (its reconnect stopped), reloads ⇒ the window is on show and in the hub's record; RED CONTROL first, the hand-off cut ⇒ gone after the reload.
- ITS ROUND (wgk4tnn0w — NOT TAKEN, ONE MUST): A HAND-OFF THAT FAILED, OR THAT THE HUB REFUSED, LOST THE SAVE IN SILENCE ON A PAGE THAT LIVES ON — the frames left the queue before the request had an outcome, a rejection was swallowed (the try saw only synchronous throws), and the route's answers were never read; a phone that only goes HIDDEN offline (the commonest case) then reconnected with an EMPTY queue, where the release's socket carried the frame. THE LAW NOW: a frame leaves the queue FOR GOOD only when the hub took it — src/lib/layout-handoff.js (CJS, PURE plan + the driver; layout.js `_handOffQueued` calls it): a failed request (no answer, a 4xx / 5xx) puts the frame back at the queue's head unless a newer frame of its desktop is already there, or onto the socket if it opened meanwhile, said; the hub's answers (the ack, a refusal, the held store) are HEARD through the socket's own handlers (ws.js `heard`, the socket's dispatch moved into it); ONE in-flight set across calls (pagehide and hidden both fire: a frame goes once); the 60 KB budget counts the bytes still in flight. A page that really unloads loses nothing more than at the release.
- THE SMALLS, in the same cure: the 256 KB bound holds BEFORE the body is parsed (the route reads its own body: its express.json layer named in `ownsBody`, so server.js's 50 MB parser skips it; past it 413 by name); a desktop change queued AHEAD of a desktop's layout frame holds that frame back (it would land before its desktop exists — it waits for the socket, in order); the staleness leg's RED (the gate off ⇒ the late save lands); heavy ⑥ waits on the suite's measured settle, not two bare sleeps; a DRIVEN fast leg of the hand-off (a stand-in queue and post: newest per desktop, others kept, the desktop change ahead, once across two calls, the budget with what is in flight, the failure road three ways, the answers heard; RED the first cut's swallow); heavy ⑦: a HIDDEN page offline whose hand-off fails, shown and reconnected ⇒ the hub holds the window (RED the swallow).
- SAID, NOT SOLVED (the round's other lines): a socket frame still in flight after the page saw its socket CLOSING can land after a newer handed-off frame with the same writer token (the older state then wins — rare: bytes in flight past the close); two hand-offs of one desktop from two hidden episodes can arrive out of order (the same rule); after a hub RESTART the writer map is empty, so the page's own unacked write counts as another writer's (refused stale once, then the page adopts and re-sends); a frame over the budget waits for the socket with a console line only; the fetch path is absolute (/api/layout-sync), as the page's /api/layouts read.
- ITS NEXT PART (r908's first items, the narrow round wifz5c3m7): the answer goes by DISCOVERY_ANSWER_MS (10 s, under the hub's 12 s / 15 s waits) while a slow child walks on to its 30 s bound and its landing is kept for the next ask (slow is not hung); ONE walk child at a time — asks that meet a walk JOIN it, one past DISCOVERY_STUCK_MS (60 s) is let go and said once; a child ended for too much output is said as that; the hub's unreachable fallback keeps a row's own age, the row carries why it is old (`staleWhy`) and the page's chip says «could not be read in time» for a machine that answered (zh / ja); the kb says the kept snapshot's size and its loss at the agent's restart. LEGS ④ — the real pair of bounds read from the code; CONTROLS: the deadline cut, the join cut.
- FIND 2: the pool's report (pool-orders-log.ndjson) parsed every line in ONE try, so one torn line answered no event: the hub acked nothing and the line stayed, hiding every report for good. sealed-orders.js reportOf (PURE) reads it line by line, the torn line counted and said once. ⑤ — the release's parse (a copy) ⇒ 0 events; the tree's ⇒ the whole lines.
- ITS CURE (r951, the narrow round wl11e5xw6), THE LAW of item 4: A MACHINE THAT REPLIED IS NEVER CALLED UNREACHABLE anywhere its list is drawn. The walk: a fixed-string search for «unreachable» in src/lib (the three word tables among it), each place that draws a machine's list judged; the zone's own row, its head chip, the search's two rows and the chip's tip now draw through ONE door, src/lib/stale-words.js (PURE): by the rows' `staleWhy` / the hub's error `code` — «could not be read in time» (discovery-slow / -timeout), «could not be read» (too much output, a child that failed or did not start), «is being read again» (the hub's own kept list served after its restart), «unreachable» only when the machine did not answer (zh / ja). THE HUB's FALLBACK remembers the device's own reply through its rungs (src/hosts.js `deviceWhy`, `lastKnownRows`): a device that replied «still walking» while its ssh twin is down keeps that reason on the rows, or — no list kept — the hub answers its words by code; the client keeps a discovery code (client.js replyError), the sessions route and the dirty push pass it, the page keeps it. ALSO CURED (found on the walk): the dirty push sent `d.sessions` of the ROWS array the hub answers (2.310.0) — every push emptied the machine's list until ⟳; server.js: two lines changed, none added. SMALLS: the agent answers by 8 s, not 10 (the hub's 12 s covers the connect, the send and the transfer too); each walk has its own number, so an older landing never replaces a newer list (a guard of its own); a walk let go is ENDED by its held child handle (SIGKILL); the pool append starts on a new line after a torn last one (a last byte it could not read is said, never a close under an empty catch); ④'s children are real ones the leg holds and releases — every order placed, its wall-clock bound gone (test-ci-gate's ratchet), the suite ~10 s → its row; the walk child's kill is declared (test-exit-forensics-pins §6c). LEGS ⑥ — every reason's words; RED: today's row (a copy) and the release's fallback (a copy), driven on a HostManager with the device and ssh stood in; the push's expression over a real answer (RED: the release's ⇒ 0 rows); the older landing and the kill (two controls in copies); the agent's own append statement run on a temp file (RED: the release's line loses the record).

### gmail-connect-wall — B-5b32: a remembered page of an account's own search answers an ask only inside its life (10 min from the account's answer)
- **The fault (report fb-460926fdbc):** since 2.369.233 the vendor-search memo had no life, while the agent CLI's note still said .230's «remembered for 10 min». An agent's `--full` was answered from a page 45 hours old. The age itself was true.
- **The cure:** `SR.SEARCH_MEMO_LIFE_MS`.
  - An ask (a press, a scroll, an agent's `--full`) is answered from memory only inside the life, counted from the account's answer. Past it, the caller's own ask reaches the account again under today's table. Nothing is asked by a timer.
  - The dialog's look still shows an older page, with its age.
  - The agent's answer carries `lifeSec`, and the note states the true age and life from it.
- **Gates:** test-channel-search (PURE, plus §L over the stand-in vendor with a placed clock; RED controls: the release's road and the life counted from the press), test-channels-agent-cli ㉒ (the CLI's note, then the ask 11 minutes later) and test-peer-text-census (the `lifeSec` row).
- ITS THIRD PART (r1044's next items): (a) NO SECOND WALK — a device that said its walk is still running, ran out of its bound, or answered more than its bound (discovery-slow / -timeout / -too-large) is not asked again: its snapshot ask would join the same walk and the ssh rung would walk the same slow home a second time; the hub serves its last list with the device's reason at once (src/hosts.js NO_SECOND_WALK; a wait of about 8 s, it was up to about 36 s). A child that failed or could not start still tries the other roads. (b) THE AGENT's PARSE OF A BIG REPLY ON ITS LOOP is bounded by bounding the reply where its rows are made (discovery-facts: at most 1000 live locks of at most 64 KiB each, the newest — `pickLockFiles`, read through a bounded read; at most 1000 open codex rollouts; the child's answer at 16 MiB, was 64; each kind left out said once by the hub). Measured on the test machine at load 44 (probe e02fea655-20261121054147-box): 4 MiB = parse 15 ms, reply 41 ms, claims 93 ms; 60 MiB = 192 / 612 / 936 ms; a fixture of 2000 conversations answered 68 KB. LEGS ⑧ (RED: the release's rungs) and ⑨ — the agent's REAL child on 1003 fixture locks (RED: the release's loop reads every one whole).
- ITS THIRD PART's FOLLOW (r1082, the round wiaqn5yya's must): ONE LOCK FILE THAT CANNOT BE READ NEVER COSTS ANOTHER LOCK ITS READ. The bounded read of a picked lock stood outside the per-file catch, so a lock that vanished between the pick and the read (an agent that exits during the walk — the very change that starts it) or a folder with a lock's name ended the loop: every running conversation after it listed as stopped, nothing said. Every per-file step (the stat, the identity check, the open, the read, the parse) fails for that file only; a lock gone since the pick is not counted; an entry that is not a file is no lock. The same loop form searched in the unit's other picks: none (the conversation files, the codex walk's stat and each rollout's head read already fail per file; codexOpen is a slice of one list). SHOULDS taken: with no last list, «still walking» joins the same walk once more (no second walk) and a timed-out or too-large walk keeps the ssh road (a home never listed has no other); the kb's 64 MiB → 16 MiB; the cap is the child's (the rows' worst sum passes it); past 1000 live locks the oldest go; the bounds are the device's only. LEGS ⑨ — the agent's real child, a lock removed between the pick and the read (placed by one seam in a copy) and a folder with a lock's name (RED: the tip's loop); ⑧ — no last list, and a device that does not reply. r1096's small find, into it: the zone's head chip printed its age in capitals («26M», read as months) — the chip keeps its own case wherever it sits (public/style.css); ⑥ a leg on its drawn text.

- THE MUST — A REFUSAL NAMES ITS DOOR (src/server/browser-engines.js statesEnvironment, src/server/browser-keeper.js launchEngineOf): the stated-word check had moved before the engine's own verdict, so a profile with an environment on a plugin that was switched off, no longer trusted or not installed was told «update the browser plugin» — the release's refusal (browser_engine_missing, its door, its For-you line, its mark) was never reached. statesEnvironment now answers three ways: `true` (listed valid, enabled, trusted, and states the word), `false` (listed so, does not state it: refused «update the browser plugin» at the early place, before the place hold and any download), `null` (not listed so: falls through to the verdict that names that door). An engine still unstated past the verdict (a built-in one) is refused there, never asked to launch.
- THE PERSON'S WORDS: the relayed 400 carries no `failed` block any more (the kernel's code rides `refusedCode` and the text), so the page reaches the environment's own sentence and its way out; a mismatched echo names WHICH settings differ on the page too — the route forwards `settings` (the three words only) and the sentence names them («another time zone and language … set the time zone and language to «This machine's»», en / zh / ja).

- U2b, THE ZONE ON A LATER CALL: on the driver road TZ rode only the launch's extra env; it now rides the record's launch view too (`rec.launchEnv`), so every later call of that browser — the `get cdp-url` a heal relaunches through, the stop's close — names the profile's zone, and a Chrome its daemon starts again keeps it.
- U2b, RESOLVED ONCE A START: the stock environment is resolved before the road is chosen and handed to the attach road (a display that does not come up falls back to the driver road with the same answer); the store's mark is set by the launch that tells a language, right before that road's own synchronous landing — a start refused before its launch marks nothing.

- NAMED, NOT BUILT (each refused by name or listed as not followed by U3's dialog at the latest): a profile on a paired machine with a language or a zone starts with neither and nothing says so; a vendor or cloud provider row's record says «confirmed» though the local switches may not reach the vendor's browser; a set location on the stock road is recorded as «machine» until U2c.

- THE LAW (r1068): THE SCAN'S WORK A TURN IS BOUNDED BY CONSTRUCTION, WHATEVER THE INPUT. Every turn of the run masker — a push, or the end — counts its steps through one `spend` (a character a read reads: the plain read, each view's, the regex's once; a regex call; the arrival order's characters; a group or a range the cuts visit; the masks; the cut's prefix search). A turn stopped part-way keeps none of its half-counted hits. A turn's 2^25 steps read up to 1.1 s on the test machine at 4–33 ns a step, the run's 2^29 up to 18 s (this entry said 0.7 s and 12 s: the arithmetic restated, and the figures set by a measured rule, in the follow below).

Two roads still said «not watching» (or «cannot watch») of a running browser: (1) while the re-arms were COMING — `down()` deletes the watch, so between a failed socket and its next re-arm (2 s, doubling to 32 s) the view's fact was `not-watched`; the bridge re-reads it 2.5 s after a down, just past the FIRST re-arm, so a first re-arm that also failed showed the line for the rest of the backoff; (2) a re-arm whose ENDPOINT was refused (a daemon between runs answering no CDP url yet) ENDED the tries: the view then said «cannot watch» until the next command.

A refused re-arm keeps the backoff while the keeper's record says the browser runs (`browserRuns`); a browser that does not run keeps its refusal said. After REARM_TRIES the given-up line stands (its Retry door).
- LEGS (test-browser-passkey, fast): a socket closed under an open view whose first re-arms fail — every read of the view's fact in that window says nothing, then watched again (CONTROL: the release's fact says not-watched — RED); a refused endpoint under a running browser — the tries go on, the view silent, watched when it answers (CONTROL: the release's re-arm ends at one ask and says «cannot watch» — RED); the accepted rule: a browser that does not run keeps its refusal. kb-file-structure «B-346d law 1, the watch»; en/zh/ja Fixed line.

### bl-vault — B-f212's remainder: the use row's STAMP judged at its one whole-row write (主开发 r1163 / r1177)
- THE LAW: a «Who may use it» row a client saves over a version it never saw is REFUSED BY NAME — `row_changed` 409, nothing written, the row that holds answered with its stamp — and the dialog shows that row with the person's own edit kept (never a silent overwrite, never a lost edit). Before: POST /api/vault/use-grants judged no stamp, the last writer won; «shown as saved» was the page's promise, not the hub's.
- THE STAMP is the row's own GENERATION the one writer already kept (src/server/vault-use-grants.js `genByRes`, the vault-marked sidecar data/vault-use-marks.json — every write of the one writer moves it: setRow, addMember, revoke, revokeWindow, pruneWindows, drop, restoreRow, the carries; the boot migration that reshapes rows in place, src/server/migrations.js, writes beneath it before any page); no new store. `publicFor` gives it as `rev` (the sidecar read once in the hub's life, then memory — every write of this one writer keeps it true; a row with no members, a hub after a restart, never hand a page a stamp the judgment would not match; a contents list reads no file per row) (every contents row's `use`, every Save's `use` answer); `setRow` judges it FIRST (after the id and the lock), nothing awaited from there to the write. The route and the door's `saveRow` hand it through; a stamp is an integer (a string or a null is refused the same); a body with no `rev` (a page from before this release) is written as before for this one release.
- THE DIALOG (src/lib/vault-use-row.js) keeps the stamp of the row it last knew (the open, every landing, another client's row read on `vault-contents`) and sends it; on `row_changed` it lands the held row by the landing law over `clean` (src/lib/landing-merge.js: the person's changes since are kept over it and stay unsaved), says one line (en / zh / ja), stays open; Save again sends the new stamp; a press kept while the refused Save was out is NOT posted (the person sees the row that holds first). A refusal with no readable row to land (unknown, unverified) says the existing «This grant changed while the dialog was open» words; an entry the dialog read as removed stays said.
- A write of ONE member (a run card's «Always» = addMember, a ✕, its window, the hour's prune, the entry's deletion) is NOT a whole-row write and is never judged — it moves the stamp, so the next whole-row Save over the old one is refused with that member in the row it answers (leg ⑯b; ㉘ through the dialog).

### bl-browser-b — B-21cc: a vault fill by a snapshot ref takes the same refs as a plain fill (the agent feedback fb-2450b6f77a)
- THE FAULT: the CLI hands the hub the refs of each `snapshot` (src/browser-verbs.js parseSnapshotRefs), and the vault fill resolves `@eN` only from them. The line scan read a ref only from a bracket that is exactly «[ref=eN]». agent-browser 0.38.2 prints a field's attributes and its ref in ONE bracket («[required, ref=e3]», «[level=1, ref=e18]» on the box's own listing), so every attributed field — a sign-in page's required boxes — was left out, and `fill @e3 --vault` answered target_not_found right after the snapshot showed ref=e3. A plain fill passes the ref to the driver, which knows it.
- THE CURE: the ref (and an nth) is read from the brackets right after the role and the quoted name, whatever attributes stand beside it (their commas split outside double quotes); only when those hold no ref, the bracket that ends the line, read from the last «[» (linear). A «[ref=…]» inside the quoted name is never a ref, nor one in a value after brackets that hold a ref (today's scan took the first one anywhere on the line); a line whose brackets after the name hold no ref still reads a value ending in «[ref=…]», as the release did. ### lg-vault-stages U1 — vault-job-approval (B-a08e L1b part 1: the approval card and its answer; design-vault-service-secret D1 / D2 / D9)

- **The card.** A Background job whose `--vault` value needs the owner (a free entry, a value the hub minted) WAITS for `approval` — and now the door FILES the card: `src/server/vault-job-door.js` `ask(job, v)` (asked by `src/jobs.js` `_vaultGate` at every spawn that waits for approval) files ONE For-you item per job × entry — action `vault-job-ask` `{askId vj-<16 hex>, jobId, entry, ref, name, conv}`, origin vault, under `claude:<owner conversation>`, NO expiry (a job is asynchronous — D1). Its words and facts are PURE `src/vault-job.js` `askCardOf`: who asks, the job and what its kind means (a service restarts by itself and after a VibeSpace restart once unlocked; a schedule's every run; a task once), the entry's Vault name and reference, the fd its program reads (`$NAME_FD`), the program's real path and — a plain fact, never an alarm — whether an agent can change it (ownership, the run door's rule: root owns every component of the real path, none group/other-writable), the script an interpreter / shell runs, the folder, the command, the destination unknown, what a lock does. Every string through the ONE hidden-character door (`HC.revealHidden` — ⟦U+XXXX⟧), control characters to spaces, cut at 400 with its mark. Names, paths and references only — never a value. A scheduled run's card is its cron's (the approval names the cron — D4).
- **One card, never two.** `index()` re-reads the open cards from the For-you store (the item IS the ask — a card filed before a restart is answered after it); every re-judge of a waiting job (an unlock, a row change, a start, the boot) finds it open and files nothing.
- **The answer** — `POST /api/vault/job/asks/:askId` (src/routes/vault.js, `person()`: any bearer ⇒ human_only): 允许 needs THIS page's 验证是你 window (`reauthed`, the run card's «always» rule — a program will hold the value for as long as it runs) else `reveal_needs_password`, nothing written; it adds the job to the owner conversation's member of the entry's `vault-job` row through the grants store's ONE writer (`VJ.memberWith`: every other member and exception kept; ≤ 64 jobs per member — `too_many_jobs`); the row's change starts the job (L1a's onChange). 拒绝 is a click: the card closes `denied`, the engine refuses the job by name (`vaultRefused` → `vault_denied`, its cron too), and the same conversation × entry is quiet 10 minutes (`ask_quiet` — the next job is refused, no card). The belt: still open, still this card's (`ask_settled`); the job still there (`ask_over`).
- **Bounds, said.** 4 JOBS waiting on cards per conversation (`too_many_asks` — counted by job: a job with five entries holds five cards and still counts once), 64 on the hub (`too_many_asks_hub`), a tray that refuses the item or an entry id past the store's 200-character field (`ask_unfiled`), a job with no owner conversation (`no_owner_conversation`): each a refusal by name — the job is not started and says why, never a silent wait. A job's cards close `ask-over` when it leaves its wait without the card (`_vaultAskOver` in `rm` / `stop` / a refusal / `_refuseRun` / `_settleWait`) and when it STARTS by any road (the gate's go — never the card being answered: `answering`); its next start asks again. A door wired without a For-you store (a scripted engine in a suite) files nothing and the job waits, said in the journal.

### lg-vault-stages follow 2 — B-a08e after the narrow round whmslzr9y (主开发 r1042: two takes, no must; taken as the next block's line 58)

- **ONE read on the pool at a time (item 1, asked as a must):** the door's card facts hold AT MOST ONE thread of the hub's shared file pool from their first read on — a read waits for the door's one slot until its card's deadline, and the slot is freed only when the read RETURNS (a read past its deadline keeps it). A card that cannot have the slot in time reads nothing: its facts «could not be read in time», still filed and decidable. Chosen over the SafeFs worker road: the facts are four small stat / realpath calls once per card, a single slot needs no worker of its own, and a hung mount then holds one pool thread — said. Leg ⑫c: a second card filed while a read is held reads nothing; CONTROL the slot guard cut (the second card reads).
- **The wrappers' own words (item 2, asked as a must):** `WRAP_GRAMMAR` — each wrapper's options that take a value (`timeout -s/-k`, `env -u/-C`, `stdbuf -i/-o/-e`, `ionice -c/-n`, `time -o/-f`, `nice -n`), its flags, its positional words (timeout's duration, taskset's mask, chrt's priority). The card names the program a wrapper runs ONLY when every word before it was understood; a word the table does not know (`timeout --weird`, `env -S`, `taskset -p`) names the outermost wrapper itself, the whole command as typed. Legs for every form the round named; CONTROL: an option's value planted as the program («Program: KILL»).
- **A held read, said (item 3):** while an earlier read holds the slot past its deadline, a card says «A file read for an earlier card did not reply; until it does or the hub restarts, every card says its file facts could not be read.» (en / zh / ja, its own line), and the journal says it once per such read (`[vault-job] a file read … did not reply within 2000 ms (in <folder>)`); once the read replies the next card reads again (leg ⑫c).
- **The chrome suite (item 4):** «on screen» is now the topmost element at the button's centre too (Allow at 1280 and 390, the chip's ✕, the job card's ✕); the scratch second password rides the seed child's env, never its argv.

### lg-vault-stages follow 3 — B-a08e after the round wtjb84nh2 (主开发 r1091: take; follow 2 taken for the next block)

- **env's words that change where the program is found (主开发's law, asked):** `env -C`, `PATH=…`, `-u PATH` / `--unset=PATH`, `-i` / `-` (an empty environment) and `-S` are NOT understood — the card names env itself (what is literally run), the whole command as typed; any other word with «=» before the program is an assignment (GNU env's own reading).
