### bl-jobs — B-323e, the job-log part: the hourly job-log clean-up starts no program from the hub's process (主开发 r1162, r1174 — under the next number's heading; the integrator sets the block's number at the pick)
- THE HARM: src/job-logs-sweep.js createRemover FORKED its remover from the hub's main process — a fork of the whole hub with an IPC channel, its main thread waiting until the child execs; one child kept warm 1 s between batches, another forked after a kill.
- THE CURE: ONE child a batch, started by THE STARTER (src/server/child-starter.js — called, not one line of it changed): `<worker> <logsDir> <hubPid> --once <op> …`, the hub's pid handed (round 3 §4: born of the hub or of a child of the hub, else refused), its env PATH alone (a whole env: spawn-env WHOLE_ROWS `handOver`), its answer one JSON line on stdout. No warm child. Wedged / HELD from the starter's timedOut and onLateExit; a run the starter cannot answer waits WEDGED_MS, then goes on.
- BOUND (1): the arguments carry job folder NAMES only, each judged, at most 32 KiB (ARGV_MAX); every other batch (a sweep's keep set, a path, a note's words) and a whole batch over it rides the remover's own request file in the logs folder — temp + rename through fs.promises (the main side's one fs call), read with 16 MiB and removed by the child that reads it; one never read goes with the next sweep's walk.
- BOUND (2): a sweep's COUNT FILE, rewritten by temp + rename after every removal and never removed by its child, read with a 4 KB bound once a cut child has ended — missing, cut while written, over the bound, not a count or not a file (a FIFO never waited on) answer «not known», never «nothing removed». COUNTED ONCE: its name goes into the record's orphansCounted in the same save as its count, and the next pass's child forgets it once that record is on disk; a file the record does not name (the batch in flight at a stop, a hub killed) is counted by the next engine, once.
- THE MEASURE (scripts/test-job-logs-remover-start §5, the test machine, alone): the loop's hold across ONE start, the test machine, 7 starts each — at the suite's size (79 MB RSS) a fork from the process 1.856 ms median (max 2.322), through the starter 0.114 ms (max 0.156); with 512 MB touched (590 MB RSS, a throwaway probe run 7d0008e03-20261121114351-box, never lined) the fork 31.6 ms (max 38.1), the starter 0.121 ms (max 0.218) — the fork's hold grows with the process's size (about 6 ms per 100 MB here; a 5 GB hub's is not measured), the starter's does not
- ALSO CURED (the unit's fresh read, seven finds, each with its leg and RED in §8 of the new suite or the heavy suite): an end heard with its timeout in one read of the starter's pipe left the remover HELD for good (now kept on the batch); a starter that failed while a killed child was awaited left it HELD for the hub's life (now judged at the next ask by the pid + start read at the timeout); a machine with no /proc refused every batch (the parent check falls back to `ps -o ppid=` — read, not driven); a sweep child that ended with no answer said «nothing removed» (its count is read at once); a forget was handed when durable() answered false (now only on disk); a request file write that never returns could park one pool thread per batch (one at a time); a pass said at once could be said twice across a kill (said after its record is on disk, the done line too); the heavy suite's exit leg now proves the starter ended the blocked child.
- An in-process engine stop no longer ends the batch in flight (it finishes, ≤ 500 removals; its count is in its file); the hub's exit ends it through the starter.
- CENSUSES: spawn-env WHOLE_ROWS +1; exit-forensics' job-logs-sweep.js row gone (the file signals nothing); sync-fs 26 → 29; store-write 10 → 17; mount-reader 15 (±0); loop-child words. The heavy suite's 11 transport legs rewritten BY READING (a stand-in for the starter's run where a fake fork stood; pid files for the hub-gone legs; record + count file for the stop's count): its hosted proof is owed before a take.
- THE FOLLOW (主开发 r1283, round wh2k8sbvj — taken as the next block's line 140): no /proc is no evidence (a wedged child stays HELD there); a count file's name rides the same save as its count, the catch-up's opening one too; the count file is written at the child's start (a cut that removed nothing says zero) and marked `done` at its end; the parent check's refusal names its door; the sweep removes only its own remover's request files or old ones; the next start's words for each kind of count file left; legs + REDs for a request over its bound, a FIFO in its place, a name that does not match and a cut-short keep set (new fast suite test-job-logs-remover-bounds); the heavy exit leg waits for the child's own mark at the FIFO; the idle tautology gone; the kb names the one threadpool write and the two-engines under-count.

### bl-browser-b — B-e799: the manager's stop of a browser on a PAIRED MACHINE (browsers.stop's remote half; on piece 6)
- THE ROAD: the keeper's stop asks the machine's browser-serve `stop` op. It read only its words (`left`), and the manager's stop read «freed» from the record's error text — so a browser of another holder in the profile's folder there (or nothing running) read as freed. The verb refused every paired machine's browser by name (`other_machine`) until the answer is structured.
- THE OP: the same `stop` (an old agent knows it — no new op can hang), asked with `facts: true`, answers its OUTCOME in fields beside its words: `outcome` stopped | survived | not_running | not_ours | failed, `daemon`, `survivors` [{pid, starttime}] (a pid alive after the grace — reported, never signalled), `holder` (not_ours: a holder the tree's profileLockVerdict calls foreign; `user: true` only for a browser with no launch mark of ours). PURE `stopFactsOf` over the lock facts, read AFTER the grace on every branch (round wvdrkjdvx): our own orphan — the keeper's mark or the CLI's --remote-debugging-port=0 on a minted folder — is «survived», a recycled or stale pid «not_running» (the real driver scrubs AGENT_BROWSER_* from its Chrome: the environment is no witness). The fields come only when asked (a person's own stop keeps its road); an idle daemon that ended is `daemonEnded`; a machine that could not be answered says «whether it stopped there is not known».
- THE GATE: capability `browser-stop-facts`, announced by the agent. The hub's client refuses a stop with facts to an agent that does not announce it BY NAME, before any request (`stop_facts_unsupported`), in words true to how an agent is updated: the hub pushes its signed agent at the machine's next connection — ask again after it; never update it yourself (a stuck update is said in Machines and For you). A person's own stop keeps its road (no facts asked).
- THE KEEPER: the manager's stop of a paired machine's browser asks with facts and is FREED only on «stopped»; survived / not_ours / failed / not_running are each their own why; a machine that cannot be asked (unreachable, an old agent) refuses by name and NOTHING moves (the record, the forward, the lease). An ok:false answer (a failed close) is read as the «failed» outcome, never as «could not be asked».
- THE VERB: a paired machine's browser is a NAMED PROFILE on its machine (own and helper browsers run only here: every ephemeral record is made with no host) — stopRows' row is kind «profile» + `machine`; the blanket `other_machine` refusal is gone; its tabs close as a named profile's here (tabs_lost unless --close-tabs); the answer and the list say «on <machine>».
- A DEVICE INPUT IN BEHAVIOUR: src/browser-serve.js and src/agentd/agentd.js are in the device bundle (its stop gains its fields, its capability list one): a signed device update.
- LEGS: test-remote-profile-start ②b (the gate: an old agent never asked; the five outcomes over a stand-in machine) and ④ (the real keeper + access layer + op: old agent refused with nothing moved; stopped ⇒ freed; survived and not_ours ⇒ not freed, named; RED: a keeper copy reading the op's words calls not_ours FREED); test-browser-stop-verb ① ⑤ ⑧ (judged as a named profile here; a machine that cannot be asked refused host_unavailable by name, the record live; RED: the handler's names cut).

- THE TOOL (scripts/guard-inline-helpers.mjs, tests and tools only): it acts on each inline helper the census judges and finds unguarded, IN CODE, and only where its body asks its condition true or false.

### lg-store-writes — B-9275 unit 1: a store's whole-file write syncs its temp before the rename (the coordinator's r1153)
- THE LAW: A STORE'S NEW BYTES ARE ON DISK BEFORE ITS NAME POINTS AT THEM. src/store-writer-worker.js writeJob's whole write is now temp, every byte, FSYNC, close, rename (the append road already synced). Before it, a power loss or a machine's crash after the rename could leave the store's name on an empty or half file, its previous whole version gone. writeJob is the ONE road of every store write: the writer's thread, the exit's flush (it waits for the thread) and the main-only fallback (a thread that died past RESTARTS_MAX an hour) all run it, so one line covers them.
- A SYNC THAT FAILS IS A FAILED WRITE, as a short write or a close's error is: nothing renamed, the temp removed, the store keeps its previous whole version, its waiter hears «not landed», the change stays owed and the writer's own retry writes it again (said once: «not written (EIO; attempt 1) — kept in memory, retrying in 1 s»).
- LEGS (test-store-writer-r4 ⑪): the order by a recording stand-in file system (writeJob, the exit's road, the main-only road) and its RED (today's writeJob, the sync removed by anchored()); a failed sync; the sync off the hub's loop (the thread's sync waits on a file only a main-loop turn writes; its control, the same gate on the main-only road, is never released). test-store-write-census: the worker's row 14 → 15 (the sync). src/secret-file.js is another lane's hotfix and is not touched.

### bl-scratch — B-ddf3 unit 1: a person's mail copy and a rescued transcript are on disk before their names point at them (the coordinator's r1337 / r1347)
- THE LAW (B-9275): a file's new bytes are on disk before its name points at them; a failed sync is a failed write, said to the person. These are two sites of the «person» family (12 sites), the first two by the coordinator's order.
- THE GMAIL MESSAGE COPY (src/gmail-sync.js `_writeMessage`, FIRST by r1347): the folder's file NAMES are the seen index, so a torn copy after a power loss would never be fetched again. Today it was `writeFileSync` on the hub's loop and a rename with no sync. Now it is written, synced ONCE at its end, and renamed on the thread pool (`fs.promises`). A failed write or sync throws by name (`gmail: message <id> could not be put on disk (<code>) — not saved, fetched again on the next pass`): nothing is renamed, the temp is removed, and the message is not marked seen.
- THE RESCUED TRANSCRIPT (src/transcript-service.js `rescue`, hub-only, a person's act): the backup and the rewritten transcript are both synced before the swap, on the thread pool (the rest of the rescue is as before: its copy and its swap stay synchronous). A failed sync is a failed rescue, said by name: nothing is swapped, the temp is removed, the backup is kept. The module is a DEVICE BUNDLE INPUT (esbuild's own input list, test-architecture §107's build): the bundle grows by 620 bytes (6 453 158 → 6 453 778, +0.010 %); `rescue` is hub-only, so a device runs the same code it ran (it rides the next signed bundle). src/gmail-sync.js is not an input.
- WHAT A SYNC COSTS (measured on the test machine, on its /var/tmp disk: a file written whole, then ONE fsync, three times each): 4 KB 0.3 ms · 1 MB 1.2 ms · 8 MB 11.9 ms · 64 MB 74.8 ms — about 1.2 to 1.5 ms a megabyte, on the thread pool, once at the end of each copy. On the owner's network share the close already writes the bytes back (nfs(5), the census's header), so the sync takes that write-back ahead of the close.
- A CLI'S OWN SETTINGS FILE (src/harness-config.js) is NOT in this unit: its writer runs on the hub's loop (applyConfigPlan at boot and at a setting's change, the hook registration at boot), and a sync there would raise the store-write census's debt (fsyncSync on the main thread). Unit 2 asks how it moves off the loop.

### bl-tests-chrome — B-6cf9: a press on a taskbar tile survives a title change (the coordinator's r1479)
- THE FAULT (row B-6cf9, placed by its R1 fact run: test-desktop-small-chrome alone at 37cbfad62 on test machine 1): src/lib/taskbar.js updateTaskbar keyed the whole strip on ONE string holding every window's id AND title AND star (and a group's tab titles), so ANY title change emptied #taskbar-items and built every tile again. A press whose down and up straddled that rebuild had its up on a new element; the browser fired no click and the tile's click listener never ran. The planted press (the title changed in its own mousedown) did not take in both tries; the control took; try 1's one real red had the same shape with nothing planted (press 1's up after 3 rebuilds, no click). A person's press on a tile did nothing while an agent's status moved in a title.
- THE CURE: the strip has TWO names (PURE src/lib/taskbar-fit.js `stripKeys`, JSON): STRUCTURE (the ids in order, a group's tab ids and its active tab) rebuilds the tiles; TEXT (a title, a star, a group's tab titles) is painted IN PLACE by ONE painter `paintTaskbarText`, which both builders call too: a tile's title line, second line, tooltip (single) or accessible name (group), its icon only when ITS key changed (the warmth ring painted again then), and an open group chooser's row titles. textContent and attributes only (a title is a peer's text). A structure change still rebuilds.
- THE READERS that keep a strip element across a title change (law i): the tile's context menu and move mode go by window id (showWindowContextMenu, startMoveMode); the ⧉ window list hangs on the count chip; a drag's source tile now stays (its dragend reaches desktopManager.dragDone; a rebuild used to drop it); the group chooser keeps its anchor (its re-anchor still serves a structure rebuild); fitTaskbarStrip, the warmth tick, the flash and the browser window's names query the strip fresh.
- LEFT (law iii, kb-features «Taskbar»): a press whose down and up straddle a real STRUCTURE change (a window opened, closed, moved to another desktop; a tab added or made active) may still be lost — the person sees the press do nothing and presses again.
- LEGS: test-desktop-small (fast) §3b — the two names on a table (a title / a star / a tab's title ⇒ text only; open, close, reorder, a tab added, the active tab ⇒ structure) with the base's one-key MUTANT red by name; the heavy check (the B-6cf9 FACT turned into a check: the planted press TAKES, 0 rebuilds) rides its own follow line on the fact unit.

### bl-proposals B-b14a — the instance's memory budget for running jobs
- THE FAULT (the row): the per-job cap of jobs-memory-bound r3 caps EACH job at the instance's limit less the hub's share, and nothing summed them — three jobs at a 9 GB cap on a 12 GB pod could all start, and the third took the pod, the hub with it.
- THE RULING (the coordinator's r777, over the lane's shape that counted BOUNDS): the budget is judged against what the running jobs USE, never their bounds (counting bounds refused the third idle job of a pod, and would park a boot replay of thirty small services). A start is refused by name only when the MEASURED memory of the jobs running now plus THIS job's bound would pass the budget (the limit less the hub's share); a missing or stale measure ⇒ no budget enforced, said; a guard at the START, not a ceiling; no limit ⇒ nothing changes.
- THE CODE: PURE src/job-model.js `budgetVerdict` (no-limit · unmeasured · ok · refused, holders by measure, roomMb) + `budgetRefusalWords` (the agent's: own conversation's holders by name, others counted) + a For-you copy `parked-budget`; src/jobs.js: the limit reader moved OFF the loop after its first read (`_refreshLimit`, fs.promises, bounded 1 s), `_sampleUse` (every 5 s, only where a limit exists; each running job's own processes' RssAnon via `_treeAnonMb`, or the deps seam `measureJobUse`), the verdict at the ONE start choke point `_spawn` (and before a create's record exists), `_budgetRefusal` (event line, the code + facts), `_budgetLadder` (a service's refused restart = a failed start on its ladder ⇒ park), a cron fire skipped (its schedule kept), the snapshot's `memoryBudget` (numbers only, memo 1 s); routes hand `code` + `budget`; the panel and the CLI word them (src/lib/jobs-layout.js `budgetWords` / `budgetRefusalPersonWords`, data/bin/vibespace-job `budgetLine`).
- ALSO CURED: a service start DEFERRED behind its last run's reap (`_startAfter`'s promise) swallowed any refusal into a log line — a budget refusal there now counts on the ladder like the start that went at once; the restart policy's timer swallowed throws the same way (now handed to the ladder).
- ROUND wh9e7xe8i (three readers; NOT TAKEN, two musts — cured in one commit): (1) PRIVACY — a holder was marked «own» against the JOB's owner, so a groupmate starting the owner's job by the group's control grant read the owner's session-only jobs by name, and every subscriber read them on the job's event line. Now `_budgetVerdict(job, askedMb, caller)` names a holder only when the CALLER may view it (M.canView), the routes hand their caller (`start/restart(job, {caller})`), and every line many readers read (the event line, the park, the skipped fire) is worded `named: false` — the count and the sum. (2) A REFUSED PRESS WAS NOT UNDONE — start() wrote wanted-up and a fresh supervision before the budget refused, so the next boot's replay (nothing measured) started the very service the person was told was not started. Now the refusal undoes them; a press deferred behind a reap and refused later is undone and told in the For-you tray (a new copy `refused-budget`). Smalls into the same commit: the landing retry ladders a budget refusal; the measure reads pid.json off the loop (and the census row says so); a job whose walk still runs is not walked again; `_budgetLadder` never throws; ONE alarm a stretch of skipped fires (a one-time schedule says it does not come back); no `memoryBudget` field without a limit; holder names bounded at 40 in the person's words too; the kb says what makes the budget generous or silently off (other threads' children, re-parented processes, no children file, cgroup v1, a limit on an invisible parent) and that a deferred boot start can be judged. New legs on the REAL engine, each with its RED copy: a groupmate's start (named against the job's owner ⇒ red), the event line (worded with names ⇒ red), a refused press then a NEW engine over the same data folder (the writes kept ⇒ the boot replay starts it), the real measure over a stand-in tree holding 48 MB (a walk that never descends ⇒ 0), judged on bounds (the idle leg goes red), a guessed limit on a machine with none (the no-limit leg goes red).
- ROUND ws5hby7wv (r1033: one MUST, cured in one commit on 75f566aad): THE PRESS RECORD OUTLIVED A PRESS THAT NEVER BECAME A PENDING START — start() made or joined `job._press` BEFORE its three early returns («already running», the service vet's refusal, «stop it first»); a later automatic start's refusal then undid the STALE record (the ladder's count put back) and woke its presser with «not started after all» for a press told «already running». ### lg-vault-env — B-0248 step 3 (c): the Activity log's archive append through the store writer (r1443)
- **THE HOLD**: every note of a group at its 500 live entries (this group: every lane's note) appended its oldest entry to `task-groups-archive/<id>/<YYYY-MM>.ndjson` on the main thread — an mkdir, an open, a write and a close on the data folder's share at every note.
- **NOW**: the overflow is owed by its ids per month file (`_archQ`) and handed to the store writer as an append job (`'task-groups-archive.write'`, a new timed-sync row; makeDir; the writer's thread opens, appends and fsyncs). The bytes are made AT the write from the live entries; the overflow STAYS LIVE (memory and task-groups.json) until its append landed, then `_archiveLanded` trims it in one more save. A failed append keeps it live, said once until one lands; the writer retries (the release's law). A crash between the append and the trim leaves the entry twice — every reader dedups by id, as before.
- **THE MEETINGS**: a clear of an entry still owed reaches the file cleared (the clear's one-month rewrite settles what is owed to that month first, and the bytes are made from the live entry); an entry cleared while its append flew is cleared in the file once it landed; a month file a clear or an import rewrites is settled first (`_archiveSettle`, a named wait: store-write WAITS task-groups.js 3 → 4); a group's removal drops what it owes and lets an append on its way land before the folder goes (`_archiveDrop`: nothing outlives the group).
- **Censuses**: store-write «*» task-groups.js 11 → 9 (DEBT_MAX 835 → 833); sync-fs «*» 14 → 12; deferred-save: the trim's save (`_archiveLanded`) is «none» (lost = kept twice, read once).
- **Legs (test-progress-archive)**: the legs land the process writer before they read (`land()`); a note at the bound opens nothing on the main thread and stays live until its append landed (RED: the release's synchronous append, a copy); a failed append keeps it live and its retry lands it (RED: a copy that trims at the hand-off loses it); a queued entry cleared reaches the file cleared (RED: both belts removed); a flying one cleared is cleared once it landed (RED: no late clear); a group removed while an append flies leaves no folder (a holding stand-in writer; RED: no settle); the crash duplicate now planted straight into its month file.

### bl-vault — B-a14b's remainder: an approval still live at a RESTART ends, and the agent is told (主开发 r1482)
- Before: grants are memory and the vault locks at each start, so a restart ended every live approval; the start marked the request's For-you record «restart», but wrote NO end for its conversation × entry — `uses` listed nothing and the agent's next run was refused entry_not_runnable («not switched on»), never «your approval ended at the restart — ask again». Every update met it.
- Now: the request's settle fact keeps WHOSE approval of WHICH entry it is (`conv`, `entry`, `at`, `purpose` — the request's own belted words, never a value); the start's sweep that ends live records «restart» also writes the end into the ends store (`restart` joins ENDS_SAID; VR.endedWhy: «the hub restarted at … (the vault locks at each start, which ends every approval)»; the CLI's `uses` words). A record from before (no `conv`/`entry`) is ended on its record only. The run card's 8-hour «Always» is a grant of a command shape, not of a conversation × entry — its end was never in the ends store (noteEnded needs a conversation): named, not this unit; a PASTED grant (grantPasted: 8 hours, no For-you record) has no record to end, so a restart still ends it unsaid — named. ### lg-recovery — B-1217's test-restore-liveness member (the folded B-380f): both runner reds placed by reading; one was the product's (the coordinator's r1401 / r1419)
- LEG «reattachLocalPty RESENDS the input the never-spoke bridge was holding», the PRODUCT's. setupSessionPty stamped the last byte from ANY pty it ever wired, and dated a new bridge's birth at `now`. So a byte of the old attach in the stand-in's birth millisecond (ptyQuietSince's tie reads it «spoke») left writeSessionInput holding nothing, and the heal had nothing to resend. WIDER, IN PRODUCTION: a killed dtach attach client's goodbye (`[detached]`) lands AFTER the new bridge's birth, so after every heal the new attach read «it spoke». B-c20d's hold, the never-spoke detector and the dead-bridge watch then stood down for exactly the bridge they guard.
- THE LAW: A BRIDGE'S LIFE SIGNS ARE ITS OWN. In setupSessionPty, two lines: the stamp only while `session.pty === ptyProcess`, and the birth `max(now, lastByte + 1)`.
- THE OTHER READERS, ATTACKED: the one stamp keeps serving both the bridge's liveness (the hold, the detector, the attach probe, the dead-bridge watch) and the SESSION's last output (conversation-deliver's terminal busy read, the pool's request-time fallback). It is never reset at a birth, and a dying client's goodbye is no output of the program, so no split is needed. Terminal idle and bell are the client's (the output frames). A bridge replaced twice in one millisecond and a paired machine's daemonPtyShim are both driven.
- LEG «§7 RED CONTROL: a feedStdin that does not listen DIES of the first stdin road», the TEST's race. Node destroys a child's stdin when the child exits, and a plain destroy emits no 'error'. The fake ssh closed its stdin and exited at once, so the pre-fix hub died only when the kernel's EPIPE was handled before the exit. CURE (tests only): the fake ssh lingers 3 s after closing stdin (its stderr line first). RED CONTROL, the stall placed: the pre-fix write held until the child's exit LIVES on the release's fake ssh; held 300 ms on the lingering one, it DIES.
- THE ROUND's MUST (wsw3m5yk7, r1632), cured as a third commit, tests only: the §7 race helper wrote its «held until the child's exit» form with an unclosed call, so that copy of src/hosts.js did not parse, its hub never booted, and the check beside it was false by construction. Now each form is written whole and its text asserted. Both copies must COMPILE (vm.Script) before a hub boots on them, and the old form is the compile check's own control. It was lined without a run of the heavy suite; its box run is asked by name.
- SHOULDS, said: (1) the bridge's two stamps are wall-clock. A step back of D inside a heal's window dates a new bridge's birth up to D ahead, so its real bytes read «never spoke» for up to D, and a heal there could replay lines the bridge already forwarded. A per-bridge floor (a current bridge's byte stamped `max(now, birth)`) would close it; it is not built here (a product change, offered as its own follow). (2) The stalled heal runs with Date.now held, so a deadline computed inside the heal is dated slightly in the past once the clock is restored. The leg reads only the replay, so this is harmless today.
- LEGS: test-pty-duck §5 (fast; the stand-in pair through the real setupSessionPty / writeSessionInput / reattachLocalPty: the goodbye, a bridge replaced twice in one held millisecond, a paired machine's shim pair, the session's last output kept; each RED on an anchored copy of the release's two lines); test-bridge-liveness's pin of the two lines; heavy test-restore-liveness (the heal with the clock held at the old attach's last byte: replays on the cure, RED on the release copy; §7's linger and its placed race).

### bl-mail B-360d unit 1 — every change to the channels index rides its journal; index.json is written whole only at the bound (主开发's ruling wi1q6956v)
- THE CURE: every update rides the EXISTING journal channels/index-acts.ndjson (one log, one seq — no new file, no migration; the release's own loader replays it, so a rollback finds everything). index.json is owed only by the journal's 8 MB bound, a whole-map change, a burst (one update past 8 MB of changed rows or 4 096 touched rows — the end compares each touched row in its own turn: 89–149 ms at 4 096 on the test machine, 317 ms at 16 384 — one whole write, nothing appended) or a stop. QUIET IS FREE against the PERSISTED bytes (a per-row fingerprint from the layout warmed at open and from each journaled line — a row changed before its touch is still journaled). `durable()` resolves on the journal's line; `fold()` asks the whole write; a purge waits for the journal's compaction (`journalDurable()`) before the removal says done; owed lines in memory are counted and said, and no journal job carries more than the bound.
- ONE READER of the family (`readIndexFamily`, `replayIndexJournal`): the load, src/server/migrations.js (×2) and grants-migration.js (its named refusal kept). The agent's store rule and manual name every index* file.
- THE INTERIM (r1322): until the writer's unit 2 lands (lane lg-store-writes), a durable act that meets a whole write of index.json in flight waits for it — at most once a bound (about every 2.7 h of steady mail, more under a burst), where the release made every durable act a whole write.
- THE HOLD (moved onto the train, 主开发 r1542 — with B-f276 1b's store hold): while the index is held nothing of its family is read or written. (1) The journal's lines: none made — `actOf` answers 'whole', the change owed to the index's own whole write, which the hold refuses by name (an update is refused at its door; one in flight when the index appeared is refused at its exclusive write). (2) The fold: `fold()` refused by name; `askFold` asks nothing (the index's produce refuses, said). (3) The compaction: `produceActs` refuses (said), `askActs` asks nothing, `journalDurable()` refused by name. (4) The one reader: the load reads the journal only when the index itself was read; the damaged door sets the journal aside with the index (COMPANIONS); `readIndexFamily` runs only where no store holds the family (the two migrations with no engine; grants-unify waits while the engine is paused). (5) The open's warm-up: not run. `durable()` takes the train's road (a whole write its produce refuses). Leg ⑫ + its red control.
- THE MEETING WITH B-526c (moved onto 90d4735d4, 主开发 r1765): A ROW HAS LANDED EXACTLY WHEN ITS OWN CHANGE IS ON DISK BY THE ROAD THAT CARRIES IT — a born row rides its journal line (`bornSeq` = the first line that carried its birth): landed when an append or a compaction holding that line lands, or a whole write that carried it lands; never at its making, never after a failed append; a row born again inside the pace waits for its NEW line; while the family is HELD `landed()` says no. The set's reason (rows the boot's completion cannot find) is met by the replay: what the boot finds on disk now includes the journal's lines, which the load replays. Leg ⑮ + four red controls.
- COST: the top-level tables are compared only when an update reached one (its view, `table()`) or for a durable act (a 214 KB table on the test machine: 1.47 ms a compare, 0.05 ms without).
- LEGS: scripts/test-index-journal.mjs (new, fast, 6.5 s): laws 1+2, 3 (with the before-touch road), 4, 5 (a kill while each step is written and after it), 6 (the writer laws' failed-append scenes with a PACED line; an open tail at load), 7 (the RELEASE'S OWN replay frozen as scripts/fixtures/release-index-replay.cjs, at ten kill points), 8 (no product read of channels/index* outside the store), 11 (also over a journal left holding folded lines); the sliced warm-up at open; a real engine (the fake vendor) under the mail driver and a true refusal storm — no update scope reached the whole map (the store's `onWholeTouch` tap names one), no whole write. Red controls on 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 11 (twice) and the census. test-sliced-walk restated 7.5 → 11.0 s alone (the per-update compare and the open's sliced warm-up), its over: debt on B-fbd6; the fast cap 1600 → 1610 by arithmetic. Legs that asked `durable()` for a WHOLE write now ask `fold()` (test-sliced-walk b1/b2/b4, test-channel-store-writer-laws k1).

### lg-rewind B-437e files tier — the kept copy's FOLLOW (its round wqdnv452s: NOT TAKEN, one MUST by two readers; 主开发 r1505)
- THE MUST: a listed file that is a LINK was «kept» as its link only. A plain write to a link's path lands in its target (the CLI's rewind is read the same way; its binary was not read), so the target's bytes would be overwritten while the kept copy held none of them. A link is now «cannot keep a copy: a link» by name: this hub by its own lstat; a paired machine by its agent's stat answer `link` (an lstat beside the stat — the ONE device-side change, src/agentd/agentd.js: an agent that does not say it is «cannot keep a copy: upgrade the agent»), and the paired read-back proves neither the copy nor the original is a link. - THE HOLD (the test machine, both roads mounted in ONE run by a scratch probe, never lined): GET /api/workflow of a RUNNING workflow (no snapshot yet; its card and its window poll it every 2.5 s) did two things on the hub's loop at each poll. ### lg-vault-file — the scan off the loop (主开发 r1505: «the scan runs on the hub's main loop … up to 0.9 s of every window held»; r1573: the shape stands, four laws)
- THE SHAPE: ONE WORKER A RUN. src/server/vault-run-door.js `startScrub()` starts src/server/vault-run-scrub-worker.js in run(), BEFORE the caller, the caps and the once-grant are asked (so no await sits between the last cap check and runs.add, and a refusal after it spends no grant); its starts are counted with the runs against the caps. spawnRun hands it the run's values once (one message) right before the child spawns; the worker builds the forms (the 135–249 ms compile at 256 values leaves the loop too) and its one createRunMasker. Each pipe read is decoded on the loop as before and posted {seq, stream, text}; the worker answers {out, err, counts} in order — each reply's seq checked against the next owed (out of order ⇒ lost) — and the loop only appends (`onOut`). The end posts {end, cut}; the door's finish waits for its answer, then writes the line and resolves; a lock, a timeout and a gone caller take the same road. The run's own exec is unchanged.
- THE FOUR LAWS (r1573): (a) THE BOUND IS ON SILENCE: armed while a reply is owed, reset by each reply, 10 s (SCRUB_SILENCE_MS), its firing judged one turn later (a reply sent while the main loop itself stalled is read first); a lawful run's work is bounded by the figures only. (b) What is posted and not answered is bounded by the run's output cap: take() posts nothing past VR.OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES. (c) BYTE FOR BYTE: the worker hands on what the masker on the loop hands on — the output and every count, at the end, at a cut and past the figure. (d) NO WORKER OUTLIVES ITS RUN: ended at the end, on a refusal after the start (a lock or a gone caller while it started, a run folder or file that failed), at closeAll (the hub's exit), and at a loss.
- A LOST WORKER (dead, an error, silent past the bound, a reply out of order, an end answered before every piece was — its held text could be half a value — or a build of its masker that threw) WITHHOLDS: everything it had not answered and everything after is under the cut's placeholder with «[vault: this stretch of the output is withheld — its scrubber stopped (scrub_worker_gone)]», and the record says `withheld: 'scrub_worker_gone'` (the CLI too); never raw, never a fallback to the loop. A worker that cannot start (it refuses at its start, no file, no ready within the bound) refuses the run by name — spawn_failed «the scrubber could not start» — before the child spawns. The wait for its start is a window in which the vault may lock or the caller go: both are asked again after it.
- LEGS (test-vault-run): the loop not held (the main thread builds no masker during a costly run; the loop's longest gap read against the scan on the loop — red control «the scan on the loop»); byte for byte against the masker on the loop (9 runs: ending, cut, past a planted figure); a lost worker withholds by name (dies at its third piece; silent past a 300 ms bound from its third piece, its end answered early; its masker's build throws — red controls «a lost worker answered as an empty end», «an end taken before every piece was answered»); the bound on silence, not work (a worker answering every 150 ms, 600 ms in all, under 300 ms — red control «the bound armed once, never reset»); a worker that cannot start (it refuses at its start, no file); the posted bound (a 3 MiB flood); no worker outlives its run (twelve runs, a lock mid-run with its line's record fields, closeAll mid-run, every door of the block). The «two scrubbers, one per pipe» and the «work bound not on the record» controls moved onto the worker's and the door's seams (`scrubWorkerFile`, `scrubSteps`, `scrubSilenceMs`).

### lg-remote-hardening — B-7f0b's engineering remainder, unit 1 (the coordinator's r1220 (1) + r1317): a push mount's reverse tunnel ends at a door of its own; a path with a dot segment is never a door
- A push mount puts a folder of this hub on a paired machine; the device listens on 127.0.0.1:<port> there and carries every connection back. Its hub end was the hub's WHOLE web port (src/machine-mounts.js `_davBase` → `localPort()`): anyone on that machine who could reach its loopback (another account on a shared machine, a container sharing its network, a page opened there) reached the sign-in page and every route that needs no sign-in. Now each push mount's tunnel ends at ITS OWN door (src/server/push-mount-door.js — not src/mount-door.js, B-afc4's blocked-path door; the pattern of the dial-back's agent door since 2.369.413): one 127.0.0.1 listener per mount that hands /dav ONLY to the hub's own app (the one express app; the hub registers it with the door in the wiring module), and only for that mount's own pass (its reverse-mount token): any other path 404 (`not_on_the_mount_door`), no pass or another mount's pass 401 with the WebDAV challenge; every request judged, a kept connection's too. The mount, the boot re-own and the health re-own all end there (two re-owns at once share one door: the pending open is kept); an existing mount moves off the hub's port at its next re-attach. An unmount closes the door and its open connections (it never waits on a request in flight). A record with no pass id is said once in the journal; no hub app registered is refused by its code (`mount_door_unavailable`, zh / ja). The pass reader is one function (webdav.js `bearerOf`). Hub only: the device bundle does not move (computed).
- A PATH WITH A DOT SEGMENT IS NEVER A DOOR (r1317; src/path-dot-segment.js, PURE): the auth layer let a door's prefix (/dav/, /api/agent/, /svc/, /p/, /hook/, …) past the sign-in gate and the public files' handler, mounted after it, resolved the dot segment away — on the release, a signed-out GET /dav/../index.html (or %2e%2e, or ..%2f) was served the app's own page files (nothing of a person's). Now src/auth.js refuses such a path by name before its door list (400 `path_dot_segment`), the push mount's door refuses it before its app, and the agent door's own test is the same verdict (its legs unchanged).
- LEGS: scripts/test-push-mount-door.mjs (new, fast) — the PURE verdicts; a real door bound to one pass (the sign-in page not there; another mount's pass refused, Bearer and Basic; a kept connection's every request judged; an Upgrade a plain request; a dot segment refused at the door; close() ends a request in flight, RED: one that only stops listening waits); the wiring driven (RED: the release's tunnel end serves the sign-in page; two re-owns share one door, RED: the open awaited first opens two); the dot-segment law on the hub's port signed out, 8 door prefixes × 5 spellings (RED: the release's auth layer serves the app's page).

- THE LAW (r1823): an approval the hub's restart ended is told to the agent as that, whatever road gave it — the same words, through the one writer of use ends where it has a conversation and an entry.

- (2) The run card's 8-hour «Always», BY READING: on the hub's one wiring (the use-grants store, src/server/mounts-plugins-wiring.js) it is a STANDING member — the conversation × the card's hosts × until — kept by the grants store; a restart does not end it (locked: unverified, runs refused vault_locked; unlocked: it admits until its until). What was false was the owner's card: the start's sweep stamped it «ended · restart». r1834 — the card says what is true BY THE STORE's OWN ROW, never a second copy: the «Always» record names its member (principal + entries, as the 1-hour window's record) and keeps the row's own until (one value, never a second now()); the record also keeps the card's OWN scopes (`scopeHosts`, or `scopeCmd` for «Always (this command)»); `rowSays` judges the card by EVERY scope its press wrote (each entry × each host, or its command; the entries from the press's own write) on the store's row — 'held' (all listed with the card's own end), 'replaced' (all listed, some end moved), 'gone' (any missing: taken back in part or whole), 'memory' (no store); publicFor lists members while locked too («unverified»); an unreadable row, or a card pressed before this, is no news. The start, at For you's read, stamps «restart» only where the grant was memory (the 8-hour one) and CATCHES UP what the row says of every live store-road «Always» card («replaced» / «revoked» — a change made while For you was held unread, when its road could tell no card). EVERY road that changes the row tells the cards it touches (`alwaysTakenBack`): the ✕ («revoked», that principal's cards only), the Save («revoked» / «replaced»), a second press and a standing Allow («replaced» where they moved its end), a delete («deleted» — the 1-hour window cards too); each tell wrapped and last (a tell never fails a landed write). Today a ✕ or a Save left the card «always allowed». On the road without the store (shortAlways — memory, wired nowhere in production) the restart did end it: «restart», its command draws its card again. NAMED: the card cannot say «unverified while the vault is locked» — the For-you rows hold no vault state (the Vault window's row and the «vault is locked» item say it); a card pressed before this names no member (it is not stamped either).

### lg-group-parents — B-360d part 3 U3: the usage-cache folder's one reader off the loop (主开发 r1444 / r1459)
- THE NUMBER FIRST (a probe in a never-pushed worktree on the test machine's LOCAL disk, the tip before this unit; about thirty readings files and their sidecars, every record invented): each road read the WHOLE folder on the loop at every pass — the identity groups 1 list + 29 reads (4–7 ms), the 30-s ingestion 1 list + 30 reads (about 4 ms), each GET /api/usage 1–2 lists + 30 reads (4–9 ms), a sweep's groups the same; at sixty files about twice that. On the data share each of those calls is a round trip.
- THE CURE: src/usage-cache-folder.js — ONE reader per folder (`forDir`, made by the pool engine): its first fill is the boot's one synchronous pass (the boot read the folder so before); then fs.promises, at most one read in flight, and its reply KEPT. ONE CLOCK: the ingestion runs at each reply (`onReply`); the 30-s pass is usage-routes' own — after the sign-in facts' confirmation (the accounts-list cure, line 228) it asks the reader's `tick()`; GET /api/usage and the anchor sweep ask `fresh()` (a reply from a refresh started after the ask, bounded at 2 s), so a reading another process wrote reaches them no later than before; every other reader (the groups' `via`, the host files' boot read, the codex seed) reads the kept reply, at most one refresh older. The hub's own writes replace their entry at once (usage-cache-write.js atomicWrite → noteWritten; reading-repair's fallback write too), also during a read in flight. A refresh that fails or does not reply keeps the last reply and SAYS its age: `state()` {asOf, ageMs, held, since, error} rides the /api/usage answer (`usageFolder`), the log says it once an episode, the usage popup draws «⚠ The usage folder is not answering: the readings shown are as of …» (en/zh/ja). A folder that does not exist yet reads as no readings, never as held.
- LEGS (scripts/test-usage-folder-reader.mjs, NEW, fast — the REAL pool engine and the REAL setupUsage): ① the groups, a sweep, a refresh's ingestion and a request list nothing and read no reading file on the loop (the boot's fill the one pass); ② a reading another process wrote reaches the request's answer at that request, and a refresh's reply runs the ingestion; ③ the hub's write is in the reply at once, and stands over a read in flight that took the old bytes; ④ a failed read and a read that never replies keep the last reply, held, with its age; a missing folder is no readings. RED CONTROLS: the release's groups, the release's routes, the request without its refresh, the routes without the reply's ingestion, the write path without its notice, the reply without the writes made during its read, a reader that empties its reply.
- SUITES MOVED WITH IT: test-codex-pool's three request helpers await the route (it awaits its refresh now); test-quota-model's ㉑2f pin reads the reply's ingestion instead of the 30-s timer.
- THE ROUND's FOLLOW (wrigll4wp, 主开发 r1976 — one commit on the stack's tip): (a) GET /api/usage answers an error by name after its await (a throw there was an unhandled rejection, the request unanswered); (b) one unreadable file is skipped, only the listing's failure holds the folder; (c) while held, the 30-s pass ingests over the kept reply (the choice: its memory-only work goes on, not a kb limit); (d) the anchors' prime leaves the store not ready on a listing error other than a missing folder; (e) both repairs say their rewrite in a finally; (f) a hung read answers later askers the kept reply at once; (g) the hub's write during a read keeps the later reading. ### bl-browser-a — r3054: the kept browsers' SECOND door, the bindings file — UNKNOWN IS NOT EMPTY (for 2.369.416)
- THE FAULT (bl-machines-b's census; checked by the coordinator at f67463581, the same in the release): `browser-bindings.js readAll` answered an EMPTY list to ANY failed read or bytes that do not parse (a bare catch), and `keys()` never threw. The kept store's sweep — at a start, EVERY HOUR, and from the panel — asked those keys, so its guard «the bindings could not be read: nothing ends this pass» never fired. With an empty list every kept browser that no live conversation carries, stopped past the grace, got «its conversation can never come back», and its profile folder (its sign-ins) was removed. One failed read at any hourly pass was enough. And `record` read all and wrote all, so after a failed read the next record left only the new binding.
- THE CUT:
  - `readState` tells ok / absent (a fresh instance: truly empty) / UNKNOWN (a failed read, torn bytes).
  - `boundKeys` throws on unknown, and the kept sweep asks it: its existing guard ends nothing that pass.
  - `record` writes nothing over an unread file: said once per kind with the base name only, and offered again at the next record.
  - The one-shot grants-unify step waits while the file is unknown.
  - The readers that only SHOW, or resolve a resume, keep `readAll` and `keys()` (unknown ⇒ no rows).
- THE READERS, each with its verdict:
  - the kept sweep: fixed, ends nothing;
  - the fresh-key rule (browser-env keyNamed): mints only, never removes; the env-dir, scratch, meta and kept-store rungs still name every key with a browser on disk;
  - the resume's rung 1 (priorKeyFor): unknown ⇒ rung 2 (the session meta) or a fresh key for that run, never ending or moving the kept browser;
  - the late key's log line, the trace's and the kept panel's names, the proposals' key: shown only;
  - the grants-unify migration: moved a grant to a bare key ⇒ now waits;
  - the env's own sweep: does not read the bindings.
- LEG: test-browser-kept-sweep ④ (fast, in-process, stand-in folders, the refusal PLACED on the very read). A refused read and torn bytes at the REAL kept sweep over the REAL bindings, an hour past the grace: zero ended, zero folders removed, and a record then leaves the file byte for byte. RED: the release's bare catch — both ended, both folders removed, the file written over.

## 2.369.415 — 2026-11-21

### lg-text-legs-3 — B-82c2: a mention in a Lark proposal is a real mention, or it is said
- **The owner's finding** (an agent's proposal on Lark, edited and approved, whose @names notified nobody): neither the proposal nor the edit lost anything — Lark declared no prepare step, so no name was ever decided, the text went out as typed, and the card drew no notify row. Slack's road is the model; Lark is built into that contract.
- **src/channels/lark/mentions.js (new, pure)**: the decision (the longest name beginning the text after an @: one person a mention, two refused by name, nobody plain words; a CJK name may abut its sentence; everyone its own case; a typed `<at>` tag decided like a name) and the wire in Lark's form, quoted from its page (Message content: text): «<at user_id="ou_xxx">user name(optional)</at>», «developers should enter open_id, union_id or user_id in user_id field», «When @mentioning all users, @mention all function must be enabled for the group». The send answer's `data.mentions` (id_type «目前仅支持 open_id») is the receipt's count.
- **Lark** declares `prepareSend` + `mentionId`; its prepare step reads the conversation's own people first (the engine's `known`: the records' authors and mentioned members) and, only for a name not found there, ONE fresh read of the chat's member list (a refused read: plain words, `plainWhy`); its send writes the wire in Lark's form, with and without files, and returns `mentionsTaken`.
- **The registry's id bound** was Slack's for every adapter (it would have dropped every Lark open_id): each adapter now states its own `caps.mentionId` (anchored, checked at registration; none stated = no mention passes); Slack states the old shape.
- **The outbox**: `knownPeopleOf` handed to the prepare step at the proposal and at every edit; `everyone` / `plainWhy` stored and carried; the receipt's `notified` {decided, taken} said (fewer named); the drafter's view says per name notified or plain words and why, the names through the belt (test-peer-text-census's door `agentPrepared`). The card: «Notifies everyone», «Not looked up» (why a name goes as words), the sent footer's count. The manual: the one way to write a mention, for every channel whose row has them.
- **Round wwb543hm7 (the coordinator's full round, three musts)**: the WHOLE name — a known name the text could continue is decided only over the member list read for it (only 王伟 known never notifies 王伟 for 王伟强; Ann never for Ann Lee); the lost send's reconcile carries the decision (its re-issue in Lark's form, its scan comparing one canonical form so a landed message with a mention reads landed); notify names one to one with mentions (an edit from everyone + two names down to the two named them right). Also: a transport failure of the member read said as «no answer»; the read's one-minute copy and the held back-off; everyone's strict boundary.
- **Round wn462wr7s (the coordinator's second round on one law, r845) — the shape changes by taking mechanisms OUT**: ONE decision for every road (`decideMentions({text, known, members})`, fed the text, the known people and the member list with the READ's own «whole or not»); the shared `prepareEdit` keeps nothing (the earlier mentions join the known people as pairs; the keep loop that notified Ann for «Ann Lee» while the read could not run is gone); the caller's `complete` flag is gone (a read cut at ten pages with a page mark left is not whole — a chat over 1000 members no longer hands a shorter known name the win); the open word is its own list to the card («Not looked up» with the read's reason); a read that fails never refuses a proposal (a rate refusal, a dead sign-in: the words stay open, said). Smalls: the registry filters a mention and its notify name as a pair; the scan reads at most 150 at-signs; a typed everyone placeholder is not everyone in the landed compare. Legs: a GENERATED oracle (seeded, the seeds printed) over the one call and the edit road through the engine, REDs the keep loop put back and whole taken from the caller; scene one and scene two each with its RED.
- **Round wfgpbe038 (r960, the third round on one law: a mention is a real mention for the right member, or the card says BEFORE the send that it is not) — four rules that hold by construction**: A, ENDERS NOT CONTINUERS (without a whole member list a known name is decided only before a closed list of enders; a joiner, a space, any unlisted character leaves it open: @Jean-Pierre never notifies Jean, @all-hands is never everyone); B, THE MEMBERS DECIDE WHENEVER THEY CAN BE READ (any at-word reads the members once a proposal, kept for its edits; two members bearing a name are said even when the records know one; the records alone only when the list cannot be read whole, each such name said on the card); C, THE PRESS SENDS ONLY WHAT THE CARD SHOWED (an edit, or a proposal stored before the update, whose decision changed is stored with it and not sent: `mentions-changed`, the card redrawn and armed again, the next press sends; the decision is in the `shown` digest); D, THE WIRE TAGS THE DECISION'S PLACES (offsets stored with the text). Smalls: code spans and fenced blocks hold no at-words; the shared-name refusal names a way out; the at-words past the bounds are counted and said. Legs: the three scenes with REDs (the continuers rule, the records-only shortcut, the one-press send), one read for a proposal and two edits (RED: the kept read cut), the oracle of A written from its sentences over followers from every character class (REDs: continuers, whole from the caller), the wire's places (RED: names matched again), the edit road through the engine.

### lg-vault-file — the run scrubber's three faults (主开发 r858: ahead of the file kind, on the release)
- THE FAULTS (src/vault-run.js, every text value a run injects — an agent's own secret, a login, any entry by --env / --stdin; found by the file kind's cure reads 4–7 and this commit's own five reads; present since round 21's «never drop a byte»):
  (1) at a CUT (src/server/vault-run-door.js `scrub.end(cut)`: the 2 MiB bound, a stop — a timeout, a lock, the caller gone — or a grandchild holding the pipes) createRunMasker's endStep rebuilt the held text STREAM BY STREAM, so a value the program wrote half to stdout and half to stderr was never found and went out whole — and a value whose head went to one pipe and only its middle to the other was a half value on neither pipe alone;
  (2) the cut's uncertain tail could start INSIDE a value printed just before it (its last characters read as a half value's start, or a colour code inside it as an unfinished token), and the certain prefix flushed the value's head in the clear; the same when the cut landed inside an UNFINISHED token right after a value's head (a colour code, a soft break's `=`, a `\x` cut short) or inside a value's CHARACTER (the bound counts bytes: the decoder ends it as U+FFFD) — the text before was never read;
  (3) every loop that matches a VALUE (scan's `look`, and the browser dialog scrubber's three passes in compileTextScrubber; the view-token loops are not value matches) took the leftmost match and jumped past it, so a value that starts inside another value's match — or after a value overlapping itself — kept its tail in the clear.
- THE CURE: endStep decides each stream's tail against the complete finds of its own text AND of the arrival order (`arrivalOf`, now shared with `step`), and the arrival order has its own uncertain tail; a find that reaches into a tail pulls the tail of every stream it covers back to its start there, to a fixpoint; the certain prefixes keep the arrival order. A tail moves only BACK: to a complete find that reaches into it, to an unfinished token, to a broken character, or to the arrival order's own tail. cutTailStart reads the text before a trailing unfinished token and before a trailing run of U+FFFD (that run is only an END, and a run of only U+FFFD is no value's head — a non-ASCII value's UTF-16 form, read as UTF-8, may begin with one: as the tail, every binary output cut at the bound counted a scrubbed hit where no value was; the fourth read found the third's cure of it a no-op — prefixStart answers the end itself when it finds no head, so an end now moves the tail only to a head found before it; and before a broken character only a head whose NEXT character is not ASCII counts, for the character the cut broke was the value's own — the fifth read: a one-character head, NUL or `%` or a hex digit, before a binary tail's U+FFFD counted a hit), raw and through each view (each view read once over the whole text, each end mapped into its decode). The cut reads the WHOLE held text again (a window sized in raw characters missed a value a view spreads without bound — colour codes, soft breaks, line ends between its characters): measured below. Each value loop asks again inside a match for another value; a match of the SAME value inside its own last find is no new find — keyed by the value (each table entry carries its value's index `v`: a web login's passwords share one placeholder), so a value overlapping itself (`0000…`) tiles as the release did, one placeholder and one hit a tile. In the run's scan, while text is held back (never in a final read, which holds nothing — the fifth read: out of the pair's phase a final read's break left a value's tail in the clear), a GROUP of overlapping finds past 2 × (W + 1) characters (only values that tile a repeating text make one: two values that tile it, B = A rotated, would chain their finds over the whole output, and the release's model keeps a straddling chain back — the third read) BREAKS at the first find past each multiple of 4 × (W + 1) of the find's PLACE, its index in its stream's held text — the same in the plain read, every view and the arrival order. That find is taken and jumped past, as the release jumped past every match, so the reads past 2 × (W + 1) that see that occurrence break at it, and the groups `step` joins across them stop there too (the fourth read: a cap at each read's own length was bridged by another read's finds after a line end or a stderr line, and a cap that skipped its find left that find's tail in the clear at the text's end). Where the regex's longest spelling at a position is the same value's, another value starting at that very position is not seen (no more leaks than the release). The dialog scrubber's three passes do the same, so it gives maskText's text on a value overlapping itself (on two values that tile one text it gives one placeholder where the run's scan gives one a group; both mask it whole). The door's exec is not touched; nothing of the file kind is in this commit.
- SAID, NOT CURED: (a) a split value is found in the order the hub READS the pipes — a program that buffers stdout and not stderr can deliver its tail first, and that is not caught, cut or not; (b) the release's arrival order has no seams (the file kind's round 6 brings them): a cut may mask more than a value, a few clean characters of the other pipe among them; (c) pre-existing and unchanged: a value overlapping itself, printed with line ends inside its runs (`xxd -p` after a short header), tiles differently in the raw read and through the line-joining view, and the two tilings chain — the release's model keeps it back as before; and, new with the re-ask, two values that tile one repeating text printed in lines shorter than 2 × (W + 1) (the fifth read: the plain read never breaks there and sees no occurrence across a line end, so its finds bridge the view's breaks) — the output is held to its end, rescanned at every push, and each late push's fixpoint walks the chain back a find a pass (≈ 10⁹ checks a push near the 2 MiB bound: the hub's loop held; the release held about 4 800 characters on that pair). It needs two stored values that are rotations of one another, which no accident makes. The file kind's round 4 carries finds instead, which ends the class; a break on the union of all reads' finds in `step` would end the pair's half here; (d) pre-existing and unchanged: a value overlapping itself with a long period, printed as its head and then itself, leaves its last characters; a view that reads nothing (soft breaks, colour codes) keeps the whole output back and rescans it at every push (the file kind's round 4 caps it); (e) while text is held, in a group past 2 × (W + 1), a value that starts inside the find a break takes and ends past it is not seen by that read (the release's reading at every match); a final read never breaks.
- LEGS (test-vault-run-model ⑦g): the three scenes, each through the RELEASE's function (rebuilt in the suite from this file by putting its lines back, each failing BY NAME — scratch.mjs `anchored`, or the copy's own named throw — and the release's own cutTailStart text kept in the suite) and this one, characters of the value in the clear counted, never a value: scene 2 with values echoed, three unfinished tokens and a CJK value cut inside a character; scene 1 with the rest, the rest then « ok», and the middle only; scene 3 on four roads plus a value after another's self-overlap and two values under one label; a chain of three overlapping values cut inside the last (only the fixpoint's later passes mask it; the release leaks it); a head coloured in pieces cut inside the next colour code (only a view's decode read to that code holds it); two values that tile one repeating text on one pipe, across a line end and across a stderr line (the most characters not yet handed on after a push, against 10 × (W + 1)) and through maskText where such a group ends (A × 13, A × 38, a third value after A × 12, A × 15 out of the grid's phase: none in the clear), and wrapped in lines of 239 (said: printed, never asserted); 50 binary tails cut inside a character, a space or a form's one-character head before the broken character, with an ASCII and a CJK value stored (no hit); a value of one repeated character as a 4 KiB run (the release's output and placeholders, byte for byte); the dialog scrubber's parity with maskText; a run with NO cut — 300 generated runs (seed printed; values with characters every encoding spells its own way, every tenth a self-overlapping value as a run): output, hits, bytes and forms byte for byte the release's; the cost cut at its end (characters scanned, regex exec calls) on a 2 MiB log, 2 MiB of the value back to back, and 256 KiB of soft breaks held whole, one pipe and two. Red controls in ⑧, one per cure line (twenty-three). A new `scanned` count on the masker (characters every scan read) serves the cost leg.

### artifacts-by-intent — B-dc3f (HIGH): a sign-in file that exists and cannot be read or parsed holds the instance closed (the hotfix after 2.369.414)
- **The fault:** src/auth.js `_load()` took such a file as «no sign-in», so the instance ran open to its network until its next start, and a later save wrote an empty table over the real file.
- **The cure:** `auth.held`, set at load and read by every road from src/auth.js:
  - the gate's FIRST line refuses every page, API and door 503 by name with the way out (en / zh / ja);
  - sign-in reads «on», and no login is valid (checkToken, requestAuthed);
  - nothing is written over the file;
  - the journal says it once.
  A truly missing file stays a new instance; a link to nothing is held.
- **Its round (主开发 r1148), four musts:**
  - the hold closes only what the file guards: with single sign-on on, SSO still signs people in (logins in memory only) and the password road is refused;
  - the sign-in page answers 200 with the held words while shut, because the chart's start, ready and alive probes ask it;
  - every upgrade is shut, a public /svc socket included, except a paired machine's dial-in (its own dial token);
  - src/secret-file.js syncs the temp file BEFORE its rename (its other users get it too: frp, host-tokens, sealed-json).
  Also: the way out leads with «restart first», six more shapes are held, and the late-mount road is named as open.
- **Gates:** scripts/test-signin-held.mjs (twelve shapes on a scratch root, the SSO stand-in, server.js's own upgrade dispatcher, the writer's recorded order; a RED for each).

### bl-keys-misc B-5a4d — what changes a conversation is in the claude wrapper's file before it is said
- THE FAULT (K47 of 2.369.412; placed by probe on the real wrapper over the stand-in, no hub): the wrapper wrote its history file on a 2 s timer, a held copy never rides stdout, and a restarting hub reads that file ONCE (boot-restore). The file held neither the copy nor its queue record when the hold was said nor at +100 ms, both at +2.5 s — so a hub restarting within ~2 s of a hold drew no bubble and no strip row, and after its turn no bubble at all (the .413 proof run's ⑧ red-then-green, a NAMED FLAKE until this). A turn's result was likewise not in the file when said: a hub restarting then drew a turn with no end (the page «still working»).
- THE LAW (the coordinator's, 2026-11-20): a record that changes what a conversation is is in the wrapper's file BEFORE it is said upward; the lines that only fill a turn keep the timer. Written through: the queue's records (queue_changed, queued_input, queue_op_result, queue_dropped, input_handover, queue_settle), a rewind (rewind_out), an answered permission (control_response), a turn's start (init, a state word) and end (result, compact_boundary). A turn's START does not heal by the stream: a text-only turn sends nothing that says it runs until its end, so a lost start drew a running turn as idle.
- ONE WRITE PER INPUT (its readers): a chunk of the CLI's stdout or of stdin is handled whole — every interrupt it owes the CLI goes out inside it — then the file is written once and only then are its lines said, in order: never N full rewrites before a Stop reaches the CLI, nor one between an interrupted result and the follow-up's same-tick interrupt (an 800 KB flush is up to ~200 ms on the FUSE workspace). The file is written tmp + rename: a reader caught a truncate-then-write mid-write (§6b's edit witness).
- LEGS: test-queue-putback §6b (fast) — the file at the moment each record is said; a MADE RESTART at +50 ms rebuilds the Queued bubble + strip row; edit / removal / hand-over first in the file; a turn's init / running / result in the file when said; MUTANTS (the base whole) red. test-claude-steer-chrome §B ⑧c / ⑧d / ⑧e (heavy): restarts MADE 50 ms after a hold / a turn's end / a turn's start, each reading the wrapper's file at that instant, then the page. test-queue-putback's row restated 0.2 → 3.5 s (measured 3.4 s), the fast cap 1519 → 1523 s.
- FOUND, NOT MINE: the hub trims its own in-memory buffer to 500 KB past 750 KB with no pin on held copies (src/server/stdout/claude-stream-json.js:523) — a held copy can go before the first page attach; records said in the few ms between a hub's boot read and its dtach attach are lost (dtach replays nothing); pipe sessions (off by default) draw no held copy after a restart.

- THE GAP (found by the read of the .413 pins cure, ruled 主开发 2026-11-20 06:16Z / 07:52Z): a Windows machine WITH a POSIX shell (Git Bash) passes the hub's door and starts its conversations under `sh -lc` (src/spawn/dial.js), yet `loginConfigDir` (src/machine-probes.js) returned '' on win32: a CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set by that login shell was never read there, and a key helper named in that folder could outrank the pick (B-77ed's harm on that road).

None handed (the hub's own process) or no `sh` ⇒ '' (today).
- THE HOW, right by construction: there the value is read by a NATIVE child of that same login shell, the agent's own node handed as `$0` (forward slashes: a word the shell runs as a path) and its program as `$1` (`WIN_CCD_READ` = `"$0" -e "$1"`: nothing of ours quoted in the command text), printing the one value between today's markers and nothing else of that environment. The CLI is such a child, so no table of ours about how that shell spells a drive, a home or a mount. Machines that are not win32 keep the printf read unchanged; the same 60 s memory, 3 s bound and one ask in flight.
- NOT MEASURED: no Windows machine runs in our gates, so what that shell hands a native child is read by construction, not seen; nor whether 3 s holds a Git Bash login plus a node start, nor how the MSYS / Cygwin runtime splits the Windows command line it is started with (it honours single quotes), nor whether the door's `sh` and this read's `sh` are one file (row B-3d06) — each failure reads «cannot be read», billing wins. The first person who pairs such a machine is the measurement, and the start already says when a config folder cannot be read (the kb says so too).
- LEGS: test-billing-pick (2b), here with process.platform as win32 and the native-child read run for real — the last hello said sh ⇒ asked once, named (RED CONTROL: the old «win32 never asks»); bash only / nothing handed ⇒ no login shell started, today's answer (RED CONTROL: asked whatever the hello said); WHICH READ answered: a profile variable set but not exported reads none through the native child (RED CONTROL: win32 given the printf read reads it) and named through today's POSIX printf; a machine that is not win32 keeps today's read whatever list is handed; THE AGENT SIDE text-pinned (the hello-ack keeps the list it says, the agent hands it to the probe; RED CONTROLS for each, and the call has no `?.`). test-windows-device-fs-pins: the machine-probes row is now `win32`, its guard the shell test (pinned by the guard form).

- THE FAULT (found while curing B-77ed's remainder, confirmed by round wdg6h2r4m): src/agentd/agentd.js spawnEnv split PATH on a colon and joined it with one, with no win32 branch, and read `merged.PATH` while a Windows env carries `Path`. - LEGS (test-agentd-hidden-start, pure, Windows-shaped values, the release's own rule as the reference): win32 the person's PATH first and whole + the agent's folders after + `Path` (RED CONTROL: the release's rule run as on Windows — node dir, local bin and Git's usr\bin glued into one entry, two keys); two keys by case ⇒ one; an agent folder already there in another case ⇒ not again, the person's order untouched; no PATH ⇒ the fallback first; a POSIX machine byte for byte over five shapes; the wiring.

### bl-tests-a — r107: test-channels-accounts MAKES its windows and waits for what happened (tests only)
- WHAT HAPPENED (the cut tree's hosted run 44719731500, heavy 4 of 7; the coordinator's placement place-16): red on BOTH tries, a different leg each — green four runs before on the same files, ALL PASS alone at the release. (1) «CONTROL: without the compare-and-swap the late persist REVERTS the re-authorize»: its window was two timers racing (a release + 10 ms against a 150 ms timeout in the adapter's copy, land's fixed 80 ms) — on a loaded shard the re-authorize landed before the re-read or after the late persist, the mutant could not revert. (2) «each account discovered ITS mailbox's thread»: read once after land's fixed 80 ms while the discovery pass is started and not awaited.
- THE CURE: `until(pred, ms, what)` — a wait for what happened, with its own bound, that SAYS what never came. The done hook is seen on the loopback each ENGINE ITSELF HOLDS, wrapped IN PLACE after create (every engine module's `create` hooked once) — which loopback an engine owns never changes (its box pre-run, r135: an injected one is its caller's, so `stop()` no longer closed it and (l2) read the flow still listening): `land()` / the Lark `landL()` wait for the flow's DONE HOOK to end (the loopback answers the browser BEFORE its exchange, so the GET returning proves nothing), and — given the engine (`consent()` does) — for the pass that landing kicked to END (its account's lastPass moved). Block (i)'s window is MADE: the gmail copy waits at a gap after the refresh's re-read, opened only once the re-authorize's write was SEEN; the order (re-read → consent write → late persist) is asserted before the real leg and the no-CAS control judge. The discovery leg polls both threads with a bound and names the missing. The boot stamps (g, h) are waited for, not 30 ms; (l3)'s mid-exchange deadline is waited for by the flow's own word (cancelled 'timeout'), the after-the-write leg by the deadline's instant.
- THE CONTROLS, red by name: the no-CAS mutant must REVERT inside the made window (and the window must be made, its order printed); the discovery law's control is MADE too — a mailbox's thread list HELD at the vendor: a read at the done hook alone misses the thread, the read after the pass ended has it.
- LEFT, named: four `await landing; await sleep(N)` waits in the r8 block (a held exchange released: lines near 999, 1108, 1138, 1177) — the same family, outside the named class; each judges «no pass» or a pass after its landing, so each needs the hook AND (where it judges one) the pass.

### bl-machines-a B-02f6 — a write under a HELD outer pull folder is refused with the hold (it landed in the bare folder, unsaid)
- THE FAULT (left by B-844b + B-6c4f, block line 244 of 2.369.412): two pull records nested, the INNER one holding the place (live inside it), the OUTER one HELD (never mounted). src/machine-mounts.js shadowedBy skipped every pair-held record, so a writer under the outer folder but outside the inner mount point (the files route, WebDAV PUT / MKCOL / COPY-MOVE's destination, the TASK.md writer) met the bare local folder and wrote there: on this hub's disk, never the machine's, and nothing said so.
- THE CURE: a pair-held record answers a WRITER under its folder (and at it) with its HOLD — `pullShadowBody` → 503 `machine_folder_held` {machine, mountpoint (the row's folder as written), heldCode, heldParams}: the English «“{machine}”’s folder {mountpoint} is not mounted — <the held row's words>», the page words it with the row's own code (src/lib/file-explorer-ops.js → mountWords). A READER still lists the bare folder; under the holder's live mount point the machine answers; on ONE folder the holder's own state wins over the held record's.
- ITS READS (fresh agents, told to refute). ### bl-msg B-6edc — an edit never loses a detail by accident (agent feedback fb-f5f3c65a9d)
- THE HARM: `vibespace-task backlog-edit <id> --detail "…"` REPLACED a row's whole detail and said nothing; thirteen rows lost their detail in two days (the coordinator twice, a lane's closing script eleven times), restored only from a day-old board snapshot.
- THE DOOR: data/bin/vibespace-task (`backlog-edit`) → `POST /api/agent/task-backlog` `{edit, detail}` (src/agent-routes.js taskBacklogRoute). The CLI is its only caller in the tree; the agents' manual (docs/agent/task-manual.md) showed the plain form only.
- THE LAW (主开发's): the plain `--detail` ADDS — the old text kept, the new paragraph below it. Replacing or clearing the whole detail is asked for by name (`--replace-detail`, the route's `replaceDetail: true`). A plain `--detail ""` is refused by name (`detail-clear-by-name`); an add past the 6000-character cap is refused (`detail-too-long`, the sizes and the replace recipe). Both are judged before anything of the request is applied. The answer carries `detailEdit {mode: added|set|replaced|cleared, was, now}` in characters, and the CLI says it («14 characters added below the old 23 (now 37)», «detail REPLACED: 37 characters replaced by 20»). An older CLI's plain form gets the safe add. A new CLI against an older server says the server REPLACED.
- …AND NEVER DOUBLES IT (主开发 r246): a plain detail that already holds the whole old detail at its start (after the same trim — the habit of the replace era: read the row, send old + new) takes its place: nothing lost, nothing doubled, and near the cap not refused. The answer's mode is `contained`; the CLI says «the old text was already in it: N characters added».
- The help, the missing-ref hint, the manual's new «Editing an item» section and kb-api say both forms; test-backlog-priority's usage pin follows the line; test-peer-text-census classifies the two counts printed.
- PINS: test-backlog-no-truncation §3b — the real route (add, set, replace by name, plain clear refused, clear by name, the cap refusal that changes nothing) + a RED copy (the old replace in a copy of the route wipes the detail), and §5 — the real CLI (the body it sends, `--replace-detail` alone refused before sending, the answer's words, an older server said, the help and the manual).

### lg-text-legs-3 — B-1ca5: two chains across one ladder await can no longer each start a billed turn for the same delivery
- **The race** (B-43bc's «race left», ruled a row by 主开发 r199): a scope digest flushes under its scope chain alone yet reads the pending rows of every conversation it carries; a conversation wake holds that conversation's chain alone. The same message waiting for the same agent on both — the account digest's row and a Task Group's row whose round-robin picks that agent — could be started twice when the digest's window ended while the group's wake sat in its ladder await (both read the hand-over mark empty).
- **The law and the cure** (src/server/channels-engine.js): one delivery starts at most one billed turn. A billed site TAKES the mark of what it is about to start, under the watcher's and the receiver's names, in the same synchronous step as its read and before its first await; a start that took writes the mark over its takes; any other end gives them back by name in a `finally`. A second chain that meets a take waits for that start (bounded, `heldBound.takeWaitMs`), then reads again — handed: nothing; given back: it may start; past the bound: left out, its row kept. The spend guard is untouched.
