### login-request-card B-03af — the adoption proof in ONE clock (the wrapper's own birth; an older sidecar paired in one instant)
- THE FAULT (placed 2026-11-20 from a one-zone red of test-conversation-facts on the test machine; red at 073cc4a1e too): the adoption proof (src/conversation-facts.js adoptionProof) put a process's start on the wall clock as the hub's `performance.timeOrigin` plus the difference of kernel start ticks — an anchor stamped at another moment than the ticks it was paired with. A hub whose runtime stamped its time origin more than about 2 s after its fork (a restart on a loaded machine), or a wall clock stepped forward by more than about 2 s in a wrapper's life, refused a LIVE wrapper with a false reason («its pid now names a process that started after the file was written»): its background and timers read «unknown» and a key's end of it was refused. A backward step loosened the check.
- THE LAW: the proof compares in ONE clock. data/bin/chat-wrapper.js records its OWN birth beside its pid at its start (`pidStart` in src/proc-identity.js startToken's form + `pidBoot`, the boot id) — the record its child already carried (B-5ee1), through the wrapper's one eager require of proc-identity. The hub judges it with tokenVerdict (the pid's start ticks now against the recorded ones, under the same boot): no wall clock is read.
- AN OLDER SIDECAR (pid + startedAt, a wrapper started before this build): src/proc-identity.js wallStartOf puts the pid's ticks on the wall clock with the boot's uptime and the wall clock read in ONE instant, against startedAt + ADOPT_PAIR_MS (2 s, named: the two clocks' rounding with room, never a recycled pid's minutes). Later than that reads «its start could not be proven» (a younger process and a stepped clock read the same) — never «started after». No process file system and no birth: said.
- THE ONE READ: proc-identity birthReading(pid, {start, boot}) → {proc, state, verdict, startMs} is the boot's only call (src/server/boot-restore.js); no /proc is named at the site; the proof stays PURE. It checks for a process file system FIRST (round w57qbqw4n): without one nothing is read and no program is started — the boot's restore is one synchronous pass, and the token's no-procfs rung is a `ps` — so a macOS hub says «could not be proven» for every conversation (truer than the release's «gone»), and its wrapper takes no birth of its own (no `ps` at its start). The birth road reads no uptime.
- WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: the older road is no stronger against a recycled pid than the release — the same 2 s, no lower bound — and a backward wall-clock step loosens it as the release's bridge did. In a container whose uptime file is virtual (lxcfs) while the start ticks are the host's, every conversation started before the update reads «could not be proven» until it ends (its facts unknown: a key's end refused, a person's end works). On kernels before 5.5 a stat start may not count suspend while uptime does: after a suspend the older road places a start earlier (looser, facts only). The zombie a no-procfs hub would have adopted on the birth road (tokenVerdict's zombie look reads the procfs) is gone with the procfs-first cure.
- A SECOND READER GETS STRICTER: src/left-behind.js already reads a wrapper record's `pidStart` (RECORD_KEYS): the wrapper's own birth now tightens its own-chain proof — a pid whose birth differs no longer proves the chain.
- WHO READS THE FACTS (nothing does more than refuse or hold on «unknown»): conversations.list (the agent reads «unknown» with its reason), conversations.end's end gate (refused; force only for the key's own), and the end proposal (a person's press). The proof gates the facts only: the session is restored and its socket reattached either way.
- LEGS (test-conversation-facts §E, fast): the birth road (same / another process / gone / dead / unreachable; an hour's wall step changes nothing), the older road (adopted within the tolerance, «could not be proven» 60 s after, no procfs said), wallStartOf exact to the tick over a planted machine, and the FAIR SCENE on real processes — the file's birth placed after the child shows in the process table, its ticks, own ticks, time origin and wall time printed. REDs: the anchor taken at another moment (the old bridge, a hub whose time origin came 3 s after its fork) refuses a live wrapper and the one-instant pairing adopts it; without the birth road a 5 s forward step refuses and the ticks adopt; the state look and the start look each removed. test-conversation-facts-wrapper (heavy): the real wrapper's sidecar carries its own birth, judged «same».
- CENSUS: the uptime read counted twice — mount-reader-census (src/proc-identity.js 16 → 17) and test-sync-fs-census («*» 9 → 10); test-loop-child-census's startToken row restated (its `ps` is never reached from the boot's restore). THE DEVICE BUNDLE: src/proc-identity.js is a device bundle input (the agent requires it): this unit changes the SIGNED agent bundle; the two new functions are not called on the device, so its behaviour does not change.

### bl-browser-a B-737b — a suite that ran no leg vouches for nothing: a zero-passed closing is a whole-suite skip in any wording
- THE FAULT (found reading B-737b's row, 主开发 r201): the heavy gate read a green suite as «skipped itself» (B-479e) only when its last line began «SKIP» or read «ALL PASS (0)». A suite that skipped every leg and closed «ALL PASS (0, 1 skipped)» was counted as RUN, so the mirror green put it in `selected` and the release counted it as proven on the hosted runner. At checkpoint 61 of 2.369.412 (run 44601878866, all seven shards read) seven heavy suites ran no leg there yet vouched: test-app-install (no node:22-bookworm-slim image) and test-browser-daemon, -dialog-chrome, -human-ui, -live-fit, -resources, -share (no real agent-browser). test-browser-live-fit had done so since at least 2.369.344. Since B-4829 (ca3d5c414) the skip was NAMED with its reason, but still counted as one skipped leg, never as a suite that ran nothing.
- THE LAW (the coordinator's): a closing with zero legs passed is a whole-suite skip, whatever its wording. It leaves the green marker's proven set and is listed among the suites skipped on that runner, by name with its reason. A suite with one passed leg or more stays a run suite, its skipped legs said as before.
- THE CURE (scripts/ci.mjs): PURE `passedCountOf(line)` reads the passed count the closing states («ALL PASS (N…», «N passed»; never from a ✓/✗ leg line), and `wholeSkipOf(stdout)` = «SKIP…» first, or a stated count of ZERO. The heavy row's `selfSkip` is that.
- THE CLASS, and why there is no third form:
  - the closing lines of every heavy suite of checkpoint 61's hosted run were surveyed (about forty forms);
  - every suite that skipped there closes in a counted form or «SKIP…», except test-frp-plugin («… test passed (① only)») and test-jobs-memory-scopes (a ✓ leg line), and both ran legs;
  - every uncounted-closing suite of the tree skips whole through its own «SKIP: …» exit (read);
  - a census in test-ci-heavy-verdict now holds that no statement printer of scripts/test-*.mjs says its own «nothing ran» words without SKIP or a zero count (none at f550f07e1; a planted one is found by name).
- THE LEGS (fast test-ci-heavy-verdict §5, nine fake suites through the real runSuiteAsync, every fact printed): three zero-passed endings, «SKIP: …» and «ALL PASS (0)» are whole-suite skips; «ALL PASS (1, 1 skipped)», «21 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped», an uncounted closing and a ✓ line quoting «0 passed» are run suites. The pure count table is taken from the hosted run's own endings. CONTROL (anchored()): the release's reader counts the three zero-passed endings as RUN, RED for the law.
- THE CONSEQUENCE (accepted, r201): those seven leave the hosted proof. Their proof is a box row before each cut, in the integrator's proof table. test-app-install stays a named skip wherever no image is present.

### gmail-connect-wall — test-consent-road ⑭: the law's seed 380113 placed (the oracle: a port number is not a sign-in)
- **The find (主开发 r318):** the law found «a listener runs with no sign-in shown» once in 80 runs (seed 380113, the listed-preset world). Replayed alone it held; at rest nothing ran and every sign-in's own record said no listener. A probe that put another listener of the same process on the world's fixed port made the exact red, and removing it made the green.
- **The cause, in the suite:** the law counted any listening socket of the process on a seen sign-in's PORT NUMBER, and a world picked its fixed callback port by binding port 0 and closing it, so a later bind to port 0 in the process could be handed the same number.
- **The cure (tests only, r356):** a listener counts only when it was BORN DURING the seed (its socket is absent from a snapshot taken when the seed begins). A world's fixed port is taken outside the kernel's bind(0) range (read from /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range; a port in use is retried by name, within a bound).
- **The fixed scene, at every gate:** seed 380113 with another listener of the process on the fixed port holds; its red control, a listener born during the seed on that port, is red by the same why.

### cli-update-needs-nothing B-f212 — «Who may use it…»: a landing never takes a person's unsaved pick
- THE FAULTS (left in the row by bl-vault's shoulds2-411, should 3; both still true at ef9323828): (a) a landed row reset the picker (landedRow's setSelected) and took hosts / an end typed during the post into the guard's start; (b) a whole landing called close() over an edit made during the post, no ask. Nor did an open dialog hear another client's save: its next Save compared against, and posted over, the stale row.
- THE LAW (主开发 r281), PURE in src/lib/landing-merge.js `landingOf({ base, now, landed, clean })`: a set = what landed less what the person took out since the base plus what they put in; a value = the person's own if it changed since the base, else what landed; the guard's compare becomes what landed, so the person's change stays unsaved.
- THE DIALOG (src/lib/vault-use-row.js): its own Save's base is the press (the fields as POSTED); members and 除了 land from the hub's answer, the hosts box and words only where the dialog's own do not already describe the row; the policy lands when its post does (the next Save compares against that, not the open's words). A whole landing closes a CLEAN dialog only; with an unsaved edit it asks (the shell's dismiss: Save / Discard / Keep editing), and the ask's own Save hears «what you changed while it was saving». A Save that posts no row lands the fields as pressed.

### bl-mail B-dfa4 cut 3 — a big store's first builds walk in slices
- THE ROW'S HOLDS, MEASURED (the tree's own loop-hold reader at beat 50 / book 200 ms, Node 24, a stand-in store of 96 500 rows written to disk and booted by a SECOND engine as a hub boots; the release 073cc4a1e and this tip, the same script, the test machine): the index's first write after a boot laid out the whole file in one turn (1.5–1.6 s); an account's due index was built in one turn and its due turn deep-copied every overdue row (1.3 s); start() walked every row in its own turn for its censuses (224 ms, the reader booking 0.4 s). After (this commit's code, run c13f41e6f-20261120202948-box against the release's c6dbaabc8-20261120173851-box, the same script): start()'s own turn 124 ms, the reader booking no hold for it; the layout's longest slice 50 ms (30–35 ms in two earlier runs of the cut), the due build's 25 ms (its sort 18 ms), the sweep's 25 ms; the index written once in the 9 s, as on the release. The holds left in the boot's passes are 0.2–0.3 s each and are no first build: a complete discovery's unlist firing every touched row's hooks (163 ms in one update on the stand-in, whose fake vendor lists none of its 89 000 rows) and a pass's per-row copy of its poll instant (lastPollOf ← peek); the first full digest (0.36 s) is cut 4's.
- THE ONE BUDGETED WALK, src/channel-store.js `walkSliced`: a walk over at most WALK_SYNC_ROWS (4000) rows stays in its caller's turn, as before; a bigger one walks a STATED SNAPSHOT in slices of WALK_SLICE_MS (25 ms by its own clock), the first one a turn after the call, a macrotask between two. Each caller says what lands and what a reader gets meanwhile:
- (1) THE INDEX LAYOUT (warmLayout): the keys at its start; a row written since is re-serialized by the write that follows, a row born since joins the last chunk, a whole-map touch STARTS IT AGAIN — what is written equals the whole-file serialization of its instant. Until it lands the store answers the writer LATER — a new answer of src/store-writer.js: nothing written, nothing settled, the file stays OWED (an exit's flush writes it; stats say it) but is not due until its store asks again, every durable() waiter WAITS (a null there would have said «equal to the disk» and resolved a durable act, or a listing's cursor, before its rows were on disk), and a write answered LATER while a waiter waited stays urgent. A synchronous flush (close, the exit, a suite) asks produce({sync: true}) and lays out in its own turn, as before. THE BOUND: three sliced builds without a landed write (a whole touch restarting the layout, rows touched faster than their chunks are re-made) and the next write is made in one turn, said — never a durable() waiting out its 60 s.
- (2) A MASS OF TOUCHED ROWS on an index over 4000 rows (their CHUNKS — ~4 ms each — more than six: a boot's passes, a complete discovery): those chunks re-made in slices (warmApply), the rest kept; a chunk whose bytes changed owes them AT ONCE, so a synchronous flush taking the job over (its rows back in the touched set) still writes them; the drift sweep waits while a sliced build holds the touched rows. (Re-laying out the whole index there kept it from landing while the boot's passes kept touching rows: 0 writes in 9 s on the stand-in.)
- (3) THE PER-ACCOUNT KEYS (keysOf's kept sets): built in slices from the load; a key touched meanwhile is placed at the landing (a birth at its account's end — the map's order kept); a whole touch voids it; an ASYNC reader waits for it (keysReady), a synchronous keysOf() before the landing FINISHES it in its own turn (never a partial set; the release's cost at worst, only in the first instants after the load).
- (4) AN ACCOUNT'S DUE INDEX (dueWarm): the account's keys at its start, read-only (rows(): live() inside an async update in flight would be a whole touch); a row touched meanwhile is re-keyed at the first read after the landing; a whole touch restarts it. Until it lands dueList says NOT READY by name (`notReady`): the tick skips that account unless something else is due (the release's order: the due list asked last), the pass awaits the build before its due turn, a stop ends that wait; a build that THREW is made in one turn next (its error reaches the pass, as before — never a loop of builds). The due TURN (the tick's look, the pass's turn) takes the 2000 most overdue rows (DUE_TURN_MAX) — the release deep-copied every overdue row of an 89 000-row mailbox each turn after a long stop; the rest are counted on the card as waiting (the index's count of keys due by their lower bound). dueListOf (a census; suites only) reads every due row, built in its own turn.
- (5) THE BOOT'S SWEEP (bootSweep): the three censuses (receiptWake rows, notification rows without access, cap-0 digests) and the selfAt heal's plan are ONE walk reading each row once by the one reader (the same rules, shared: orphansAt, capZeroRow, receiptWakeRow, selfAtPlanned), from the turn after start(); a row touched meanwhile is read again at the landing; a grants change (CG.generation) or a whole touch STARTS IT AGAIN (after three, one turn: it always lands). Its only readers are the three log lines and the heal, at the landing; each census still says its own failure. The two walks whose readers act at once stay in start()'s turn, each a cheap read of a row's own field: the stale reservations' release (a wake's cap must never count a dead boot's slot) and the boot deliveries' scan (parkedKeys, the boot timers).

- (L1) THE WALK's RUN BOUND: src/usage-walker.js takes the shipped scanner's own B-6ded law (`maxOutBytes` / `maxMs`, opt-in): a walk that has read something stops after a WHOLE line once its output or its time is spent — the file it stopped in keeps that line's cursor (a compressed rollout read part-way: `zpart`), the files after it keep theirs — and says `more`. The agent's walk child takes `--max-out` / `--max-ms` (the push: 24 MiB / 60 s, inside the child's 64 MiB / 120 s; the hub's usage-scan: its harvest's bound; none named: the scanner's 32 MiB / 60 s) and its manifest says `__more__`. THE PUSH walks the rest after THAT batch's ack, never before (answer-caps.js usagePushWaitMs / usagePushAcked's onMore; a kick meanwhile waits at most 60 s — the hub's deliberately unacked batch walks again, as before). A whole-history walk (a first walk from an empty push cursor, ~250k transcript files ever walked) used to pass the child's buffer or deadline and fail every time.
- (L2) THE CURSOR MAP = THE FILES ON DISK — the device walk child's map (opt-in `prune`; the hub's own in-process walk keeps its cursor writer's hourly L0 sweep), by the hub's own proof (usage-history.js L0): an entry is dropped only when its own folder was listed this walk, no longer holds its file, and still holds a live entry (a gone transcript, agent or rollout beside a live one); an emptied folder (an unmounted mount point answers just that), a gone project folder, an unreadable, blocked or unlisted one keeps every entry — a live cursor dropped re-walks its transcript and appends every request again. The hub hands its kept cursor down WITHOUT each claude entry's `sid` (the walker sets it from the path — the oldest agent that says `usage-scan-hub-cursor`, 18e7d9436, too, run by the suite). The map used to hold every file ever walked; at ~210k it passed the control line and the harvest fell back to the script ship for good.
- (L3) ONE EVENT's STRINGS: an id (rid / mid) over 256 bytes is DROPPED AND COUNTED, never cut (a cut id could collide in the dedup); a model / tier / effort over 128 bytes or a path over 4096 reads as unknown — in the walker and the shipped scanner alike (the scanner's count is its own last line, `{"__oversize__":N}`, which an older hub's ingest skips). An id that is no string is dropped and counted too, and a cursor keeps no unbounded id (a dropped one's first 257 characters). The count reaches the hub on every road (the walk's manifest, the scanner's line, the push's last chunk, the hub's own in-process walk) and is said once in its journal: a dropped usage event is money not counted. An event-less walk (stopped on its bound with none, or every record dropped) still hands its cursors to the hub's copy.

### login-request-card — the left-behind cut and a clock set during the turn (主开发 r274 / r541; B-03af's sibling)
- THE FAULT: src/left-behind.js cuts «started after THIS turn began» with the kernel's btime, which the kernel derives from the wall clock at each read, and the turn's age the door hands it is a wall-clock difference (src/server/left-behind-door.js: now − the turn's start stamp). A step BEFORE the turn moved nothing; a step DURING the stopped turn moved the cut by the step: forward, a process an earlier stopped turn of the same conversation left was listed as this turn's (its own mark — never another conversation's); backward, a process this turn left could go unlisted. Nothing was ever ended on it: only a person's press ends, and it reads each pid again.

A turn with no sample (an older record) is aged as before. On a paired machine the age travels as a duration, so the same correction holds there.
- LEGS (test-left-behind ③, fast): a +3 s and a −2 s step during a 5 s turn (2 s / 7 s), no step, no sample; RED: the age read off the wall clock alone. The kb's door line says it.

A helper of 8 to 34 MB is read WHOLE now (the release kept its newest 8 MB: a write in the first MB of a 9 MB helper is a row now; the control copy loses it). Over 34 MB: its first 2 MB and its last 32 MB (a write between them is not a row — pinned at 34.5 MB).
- THE «tail-only display» LINE (a chat window's word) cannot appear for a helper's file: the door takes the pager's head+tail road (`tailOnly: false`), and readJsonlBounded prints that line on its tailOnly road only — pinned on a 34.5 MB helper, with the same file read on the tailOnly road as the control (the leg hears the worker's line there).
- NO POOL OR A FAILED READ: nothing is read on the main thread — that helper's rows are not derived, and the log says why ONCE a process («[artifacts] a helper's rows were not derived …»); pinned through the history worker's own heap bound (a real refusal road).
- THE CURED PROBE (run 26c7ea52e-20261120212122-box, the same fixtures; never lined): the end record's `observe` returns in 1.0 ms (N = 10) / 1.4 ms (N = 30); the helpers fold off the loop and the longest loop gap meanwhile is 73 ms (N = 10) / 87 ms (N = 30); a workflow of 30 helpers of 2 MB with a write every 200th record: folded in 277 ms, longest gap 10 ms; its rebuild 281 ms (longest gap 16 ms), and 9 ms with the ops kept. The first cured run (039d591f2-20261120210818-box) sliced by COUNT (500 ops a turn) and held 0.7 s a turn on the dense fixture — hence the time budget.
- FOUND, NOT MINE (measured by the same probe; the release had it too, beside its reads): past a conversation's 500-row cap (src/artifacts.js MAX_ROWS) every new row costs ~1 ms of the main thread in the reducer — `apply` copies the whole row set per op and `evictOver` lists and sorts it per birth. The live door now spreads that over loop turns (above); a REBUILD folds one end record's helper ops in one go: 30 helpers × ~100 writes (3 000 rows' worth) = one hold of 2.5–2.8 s («held 2.5–2.8 s — JavaScript»), the same with nothing re-read; 46 770 writes = 53 s. - SUITES: test-artifacts-handover ⑤ (the legs above; ① now waits for the fold — `helperSettled`; the «by» strip control anchors on `helperTagged`), test-agy-store ⑪ (the turn end's main-thread reads under the store: NONE — it named the artifact door's read as the remainder), test-antigravity-session (heavy: the sub's row is awaited — the fold lands after the card). ### bl-keys-misc B-37bc — a window's age is its own stamp, on both sides (the coordinator's r424 / r461)
- **Step 1, measured (no build).** Probes ran the real engine's markLimitBanner, readings seeded through the real write road, the real shipped statusline and the page's age rule (usage-meter: max of the window's instant and when the write path last stated it; staleLaneAge). On typed files a 5h, Fable or weekly banner left every untouched lane its «14h». The row's premise, the banner's fetchedAt, dates no lane. THE HARM: the statusline's 5h-only render drops the plan limit and spreads the week forward with no stamp. The next write (the banner, or a plain rate_limit_event) lifted the stored file with every bucket at its clock, so a week read 14 h ago drew as just read. A restarted hub drew it with no age at all (the stated instants are in memory only). A real week reading measured before the render reached the hub lost the merge to the stale week (mergeWindow: the newer instant wins).
- **The law.** (a) The write road projects each window's `measuredAt` into its legacy bucket of a claude file (`toLegacyView(set, {stamps: true})`). (b) THE ONE ORDER, `quotaModel.bucketInstant`: the bucket's own stamp (`measuredAt`, else a render's `asOf`), else a cap's scoped instant, else the file's clock. The read side (`lanesOfReading`) and the lift of a STORED object (`fromLegacy(…, {stored: true})`) both date through it. A producer's object keeps every window at its write's instant; what it only carried is the stored window again. A re-stated bucket carries no earlier stamp: the capture's `restated` copies the stored bucket whole, and now drops the projected `measuredAt` and a render's `asOf`. The banner's lane is refused, so it takes the write's instant. A producer's own older stamp (a late record, test-account-reset-door lane-f) stays its own. ALSO CURED: before this, the render's `asOf` dated the event's stated lane at the old render.
- **Who decides on an age.** The pool's pick, the wall verdict, a reset claim's view and the idle read (the file's fetchedAt) read no window instant. The merge does, and that is the money line.
- **The round's cure (the coordinator's round wcslt7dwl, no must).** (1) The projection carries a window's `refusedAt` / `statedAt` with its instant. A bucket that carries an instant has a word of its own, so without its marks a refused week spread forward by a 5h-only render read as a MEASURED 100 %: the held fall counted it, the next write's carryStamps made it a stated reading, and a lower reading was a vendor reset. The capture's `restated` drops those marks too. (2) A status-only event (the same status and reset, no number) re-states nothing: the carry keeps the week's instant (a leg, with the carry rule out as its control). (3) The legs that rely on the statusline's render assert it exited 0. (4) «Claude files only» by behaviour: a codex file through the road is byte for byte the base projection's. (5) A stamp from a machine whose clock is ahead wins every merge until the hub's clock passes it. That is older than this unit, and the projection now also keeps it in the stored bucket. It is said here, not cured: a clamp at the write door moves every fixture that writes a future instant, so the coordinator files it. (6) After a downgrade, an older hub's `restated` keeps the projected `measuredAt`, so its first rate_limit_event dates that write's stated lane at the projected stamp (one write's age mark and claim settle). Said, not cured: its first write rebuilds the buckets without stamps.
- **Gates.** New fast test-window-own-stamp: the one order over a table on both sides with its census; the stamp on the file; G and H (the real engine's banner); the reverse harm; files in the field; the merge; a second engine in a fresh process. Its red controls are four anchored mutants of a copy of the write road's module closure. test-quota-model's three `restated` mutant anchors moved to the new line. The row states 1.6 s; the cap is the integrator's (1546.237 + 1.6 = 1547.837 s over the base's 1547: test-ci-gate's cap leg is red by that sum).

### card-door-in-chat — the device suites bundle at a stamp without writing the checkout (B-ba47's class, 主开发 r543)
- THE FLAKE: on the hosted runner test-agentd went red then green — its daemon reported the release's version, not the suite's stamp. Nineteen heavy device suites stamped the checkout's OWN src/agentd/version.js, bundled from it (`npx esbuild src/agentd/agentd.js … --outfile=<scratch>` from the checkout), and eleven wrote it back at their end with a `node -e` run in the checkout. Two suites in one shard's lanes met in that file: a restore landed between another suite's stamp and its bundle.
- THE LAW: no suite writes under src/ of the tree it runs in. ONE helper, scripts/agentd-bundle.mjs: `agentdBundle({ version, outfile, entry })`. THE BUNDLE A SUITE TESTS IS THE BUNDLE THAT SHIPS but for the stamp (主开发 r561): the entry's esbuild step is READ from package.json's build:agentd (buildPlan, each flag mapped to esbuild's JS API, a flag with no mapping throws by name), then comes the build's own strip step when the build strips that entry. One plugin (stampPlugin) answers src/agentd/version.js with the stamp IN THE BUILD. The suites pass no flags of their own: the daemon is now bundled with --external:xlsx and --preserve-symlinks and stripped, as it ships. Nothing is written under src/ and nothing is restored. For the daemon's entry the stamp must be in the bundle, and a moved stamp module throws by name. The hub reads a bundle's version from the bundle's own text (client.js _expectedVersion), so the bundle carrying the stamp is all a suite needs. test-sealed-orders' mutant bundle takes the same plugin.
- THE NINETEEN: test-agentd (its two test stamps 9.9.1 / 9.9.2), -adopt, -bigread, -devicemount, -dial, -m3m4, -reexec-argv, -remote, -robustness, -session, -socks, -tunnel, -wired (+ attach-cli's bundle), test-device-agent-setup, -install-check, -mount-rclone, -secret-quota, test-sealed-orders, test-usage-events-push. Their eleven restore lines are gone.
- THE CENSUS: test-architecture §51 («no suite writes a patched copy into the tree») no longer declares src/agentd/version.js an exception, and it learns the `node -e` writer run with cwd = the checkout. AND THE PIN (r561): the plan re-spells every flag of build:agentd's esbuild steps exactly — the daemon's with its strip, attach-cli's without. CONTROLS: a flag drifted into the build (--minify) is red by name, an entry the build does not bundle is refused, and an external dropped from the build drops from the plan (read, never retyped). Plants: the stamp written into the checkout, and a node -e restore there, are red; the same into a scratch copy, and the helper's build, are not. src/lib/build-version.js's stand-in stays declared: every writer of it writes its own worktree.
- THE FOLLOW (主开发 r641, its round wrpdo2eev's shoulds; no must):
  - A REAL WRITER THE LAW MISSED: test-host-mounts-tunnel (MANUAL) ran `npm run build:agentd` in the checkout, which rewrote src/agentd/version.js and data/bin. It now bundles through the helper into its run's scratch, and keeps its host tokens there too. Its HostManager still reads the checkout's data/ for the real host record it exists to drive.

Each has its plant, red by name; a build in a scratch copy, `npm test` and a harmless `-e` stay green.

### lg-recovery — B-299b A6 follow-up (主开发 r604, its round w7awns90r): the helper reads' own page slot, no fold for a killed conversation, the rebuild's prefetch bounded
- ① THE HELPER READS NO LONGER CUT A PERSON'S PAGED HISTORY READ: the history worker kept ONE page snapshot and every new page 0 replaced it, so a workflow's end (or a rebuild's prefetch) between a person's pages answered that read `gone`, its retry could be cut again and then fall to the one-shot read (one structured clone of every record on the main loop — ~100 ms by the pager's own measure). src/transcript-worker.js now keeps one snapshot per SLOT (`_pageSnaps`: '' the history reads, exactly as before; 'helper' the artifact door's) and the pager passes `slot` (additive, default ''); the registry reads helpers ONE at a time across every conversation (`oneHelperRead`), so the helper slot is never fought over either. Leg: a person's 300-page read beside a helper's read keeps every page (0 gone, 0 one-shot); CONTROL a helper read in the history slot cuts it.
- ② A LATE FOLD NOTES NOTHING FOR A CONVERSATION THAT NO LONGER STANDS (`stands`: a registry with a session store, a session with a socket name, no longer among the live sessions) — before each read and each chunk of rows; its delayed save would have brought back a meta file holding only the rows, for as long as the reads took. Leg: killed while its read is in flight ⇒ no row, no save due; CONTROL the standing one.
- ③ THE REBUILD'S FIRST OPEN NO LONGER WAITS FOR EVERY HELPER: the prefetch waits HELPER_PREFETCH_MS (2 s) at most; the history opens, what it left is said («the history opened before N of M helper transcripts were read»), the reads go on and are kept for the next open (the rows the conversation kept stand meanwhile — a rebuild merges them). MEASURED (probe, never lined): MEASURED (probe run 195caa8ec-20261120221810-box, never lined): one conversation with 100 Task ends, one 2 MB helper each (a write every 200th record) — the first open after a restart 1 067 ms (all 100 reads inside the 2 s bound, nothing left), the next open 122 ms (every read kept), the files touched and the bound lifted 768 ms; the longest loop gap 55 ms in each (the 500-row cap's reducer included); the release's reader over the same 100 files: 273 ms of the main thread.
- ④ The user changelog's bullet says the 500-file cap can push the oldest files out.
- ALSO CURED (the round's smalls): a read that failed is read again at the next rebuild (a leg — a null is never kept as «nothing found»); test-agy-store ⑪ awaits the registry's fold INSIDE its zero-read window; the kb line said «500 a turn» (the first cut's count) — it is paced by time.
- LEFT, said: the live card lands at the chat's tail when its read has (a rebuild places it at its end record); a live fold landing after a rebuild's merge can re-apply a helper's first op (a count only); the hook's sync folder reads per end record (the release's); the rows reducer past its cap — the row's next member.

### bl-msg B-64c1 — the attended tally has a reader (主开发 r590 / r599)

### bl-vault — B-3fb5 (主开发 r542): a value an agent mints again under a deleted entry's name starts its use counts at 0
- THE FAULT (left by bl-vault's shoulds line of 11-18): the Vault window's «used N× by M conversations» is VU.countsOf over the audit tail, keyed by the entry's REFERENCE — an agent's entry's reference is its whole name (`vault://agent:<scope>/<name>`), so a value minted again under a name the person deleted showed the old value's uses (a person read uses that never happened for this value). THE CURE: the person's delete (src/server/vault-paste-door.js dropAgentEntry) names the entry's reference on its `vault-agent-secret-deleted` line (`ref`, built by src/vault-run.js refFor — never a value), and src/vault-use.js countsOf ENDS that reference's count at the line (the tail is the file's order: the uses before it were the old value's); a use of the new value counts. The row's older half (the person's delete of an agent's entry) stays as its detail says. Only a line whose EVENT is the delete resets — a use line merely HOLDING those words (an agent's own purpose) still counts (the read's must). LEGS: test-vault-paste (the agent-delete block) — two uses of the old value by another conversation, the delete, the re-mint: 0 uses; one new use, its purpose worded as the delete's event: 1 use, 1 conversation; the delete line names the reference; REDs (anchored copies of src/vault-use.js): the counts that read through a delete line — 3 for 1; a reset that skips every line holding the words — the real use never counted. LEFT (named): a run that started on the old value and ends after the delete writes its use line after the delete line, so it counts for the new value (forgetEntry stops no run in flight); a forgotten app login or a storage mount made again under the same id shows the old value's counts (the same law would need their delete lines to name their references — rows of their own if wanted). FOUND, NOT MINE: a background job's uses are recorded under the entry's NAME (src/server/vault-job-door.js) while the window reads counts by REFERENCE, so a job's uses never show in «used N×».

### bl-keys-misc B-37bc's follow — a reading's stamp never moves backwards (the coordinator's r639)
- **The defect (the lane's scene I).** rate-limit-capture writes a late event (measured before what the file already states) with `fetchedAt = now` — the event's own instant — so the file's clock moved BACKWARDS, and the file's producer was relabelled although the event lost the merge. The window merge already kept the newer window, but `markRefused` / `markStated` stamped the write's instant on whatever window they found: a late refusal marked a NEWER 40 % reading as a wall, which the held fall, the reset-seen rule and a claim's settle then read.
- **The law, one function.** `quotaModel.laterInstant(held, said)`: the later of what a record holds and what a write says (a missing instant is older; a tie goes to what is said). `mergeWindow` asks it (the same outcomes). `markRefused` / `markStated` stamp no window measured after the statement and never move a held mark back. `writeCacheObject` keeps the stored `fetchedAt` (with the `source` it names) and `scopedFetchedAt` when the producer's are older. That is never on a replace, and never when the producer states no `fetchedAt`. A late event may still fill a window the file does not hold, at its own instant. No read of any vendor is added: passive capture only.
- **A stamp from a clock AHEAD (said, not built).** A paired machine's event stamped in the future wins every merge of its window until this machine's clock passes it, so a true later reading loses. With this follow, the file's clock keeps such a stamp too (it never moves back): the idle read is not due, and the identity pick prefers that file until then. The page draws that lane as just read and marks every lane older than the future stamp by more than 30 min (its words are its true age). A clamp to this machine's now would be one line in `laterInstant`, but it makes the pure rule read a clock and moves every fixture that writes a future instant: the coordinator files it.
- **Gates.** test-window-own-stamp ⑪ late-event, through the real capture and the real door. The week read 10 min ago is not moved by an event measured 30 min ago (numbers, stamp, the file's clock and producer, no reset said). A late refusal marks nothing. A late 5h event fills the missing 5h at its own instant. An older whole panel read moves neither file clock. Its red controls restore the release's behaviour one rule at a time (clock-steps-back, marks-step-back).

### bl-mail B-dfa4 cut 3c — under ordinary row touches a big account's due index never falls back to a whole build in one turn (主开发 r644)
- THE FACT (cut 3b, round wed0m8jzl): a sliced due build that landed with more rows touched meanwhile than the rebuild line counted as a restart, and after three in a row the next build ran in ONE turn — about 1.2 s on an 89 000-row mailbox; on an account an authoritative feed carries the line is about 256 touched rows, so ordinary traffic (a long discovery) reached it.
- THE CURE, THE MERGE: a big account's mass of touched rows (past the line) is no longer rebuilt — the touched rows (a stated snapshot) are keyed again in slices, then the sorted list without them is merged with their fresh keys in slices over a COPY of the list (O(rows) cheap steps; the live list keeps its re-keys meanwhile, each noted and re-placed after the landing). THE INDEX IS SERVED MEANWHILE: the due list judges the touched rows as POSSIBLY DUE by dueRow (the one rule) — the rows touched since the merge began first, then the pending rows by their fresh key once known (before that a cursor that moves each turn), at most turnMax a turn with `more` past it; the tick's re-ask waits for the merge's landing (never a macrotask spin). Nothing is polled late, nothing is polled that is not due.
- THE ONE-TURN FALLBACK stays only for a whole-map write during three sliced builds in a row; its journal line now names that cause. A census build in one turn resets the count; a merge that throws marks the account (the next build in one turn, its error to the pass, as for a throwing build); the due index's per-account maps (restarts, failed, merging, the indexes, the census) are pruned when an account is removed. The due list reads its candidates from the live rows (read-only), never a deep copy each.
- LEG test-sliced-walk (c5): 500 rows touched (past the line) during each of four merges in a row — merged ≥ 4× in slices, never a build in one turn; DURING each merge the served due list answers a whole build's of that instant, after them too. RED CONTROLS: cut 3b's road (the fourth build in one turn); a merge whose touched rows are not judged meanwhile (a served list that is not the whole build's). (c4)'s journal words follow the new line. MEASURED on the full stand-in (scratch scripts/measure-dfa4-3c.mjs, the tree's loop-hold reader: 12 000 of the mailbox's rows touched during each of four due walks in a row) — the numbers are in the line.

### bl-chat-a — B-f3a1: the folder field's «create» tick belongs to the path it was given for
- THE FAULT (in the release since 2.369.411): src/lib/path-field.js kept `st.tick` across the text: only a NEW text found to EXIST reset it (onInput); a set from outside, typing to another MISSING path, a refresh after a Task Group change and a chip that is not «new» left it set — «create» could apply to a folder the person did not tick (the tick is drawn, so what is made was on the person's screen; still not their consent).
- THE LAW AND ITS SHAPE: PURE `tickKey(text, machine, bases)` + `tickHolds({on, key}, cur)` (src/path-field-model.js) — a tick holds only while the PATH's key is the key it was given for: the text on its machine, its bases only when the text is relative (an absolute or «~» text names the same folder under any Task Group — the first cut keyed every text with its bases, and New Session's J5 caught it: a «new» name chip ticked, then a group picked, made nothing). The page gives it with `giveTick(on, text)` (the checkbox, a «new» chip and a «new» row — the consent made at use, given FOR the path it picks) and reads it through `tickNow()` (the model's env, the checkbox), which drops it for good once the key is another: back to the same text later, the person is asked again.
- THE TWO SMALLS: «a relative text after a Task Group change asks again on refresh» was MET by the tree — the model rebases a bases-only key move and arms the ask (src/path-field-model.js, the rebase at the top of step() and the 'refresh' case); pinned now (test-path-field-model ④). «A cap on asks in flight when a page builds many folder fields at once» GREW: one field asks one text per machine today; a page-wide cap needs a priority rule (the person's own ask before the set-from-outside asks queued at a build) and a drawn leg counting asks across fields — said in the line, not built.
- LEGS: test-path-field-model ④ (fast): every road (typing, a set from outside, a refresh after a Task Group change under a relative text, another machine, a non-«new» chip) with its RED CONTROL (the key check taken out: the tick carries); an absolute text keeps its tick across a Task Group change with ITS control (the bases in every key: J5's drop); the consent at use holds, the page's wiring census (no bare `st.tick =`; the env and the checkbox read tickNow; the picks give FOR their path), the refresh's ask; heavy test-path-field-chrome ⑧c (the roads drawn: unchecked after each, a commit takes nothing, back to the same text still unchecked, an absolute path's tick stays across a group pick, a plain chip commits with no create).

### bl-release B-9407 — an agent's job create writes only what its later verbs could (+ the class; ALSO CURED: who asks)
- THE FAULT (found by this lane's adversarial read of B-b461, 2026-11-18): POST /api/agent/jobs copied `access: b.access` whole into the spec and src/jobs.js create stored it as given. Only the later access verb refused an agent's edit of a job `lockedBy: 'user'` and kept view / control within session|group|all — so an agent could create a job already «pinned by the user» (its own later verb then refused as if the person had locked it) or with a scope that is no scope (stored, shown as `view=everyone`, read as owner-only). `--view everyone` from the CLI was such a store.
- THE CURE: PURE `agentJobAccessVerdict` (src/agent-routes.js, module scope, exported): absent ⇒ the engine's default; else ONLY the view / control words given, each one of the three (a word not given stays missing — never widened to «group»); refused by name, nothing created: a lock 403 `lock_person_only`, a word that is no scope 400 `bad-scope`, another key 400 `unknown_field`, another shape 400 `bad-access`. Judged after the field census (its words first for a body of another shape). The person's create (src/server/jobs-wiring.js) does not pass here.
- THE CLASS (every other create field a later verb refuses an agent): notify — at the top the engine stores only on/off (src/jobs.js create), met; inside a run's task NOT met (below); memoryMb — `memoryValueVerdict({ byUser: !!caller.isUser })` at create and for a run's task, met; the wake grant — refused at the top (403) and stripped from a task (storedAction), met; the schedule — `validateSchedule({ agentCreated })`, met; owner / subscribers / interaction at the top — the unknown-field census, met. NOT met: a scheduled run is BUILT from its task (`{ ...a.task }` in _fireCron), so a field no task create takes rode every run — `subscribers` naming another conversation (the subscribe verb adds only its caller) addressed it with a job it never subscribed to; `interaction` (the ask verb's judged panel), `clearedAt` (the person's Clear content); a run's own `notify` (raw, and _notifyOverrideOf puts a run's on/off AHEAD of its schedule's: `notify: 'on'` beat the owner's later `notify <cron> off` and the person's); a run's own `context` (the 8 KB cap reads the schedule's only); a task inside the task (a nested grant past storedAction's one level). Cure: PURE `agentJobTaskVerdict` — the task takes the RUN fields of the create's copy (its keys minus RUN_FROM_SCHEDULE: owner, name, schedule, catchUp, action, access, notify, context, mayRead — B-3992's grant, met on the move: the engine hands the schedule's to the run at every fire, a task's own sat unjudged in the stored task; + notifyOk); a wake grant there 403 as at the top (the base stripped it silently: a control shows it); any other field 400 `unknown_field` by name. A falsy `access` still reads as absent.
- ALSO CURED: the ask verb had no owner gate — any conversation that could VIEW a job (its Task Group's default) could put a question to the person under that job's name, against the design's «mutation (… panel …) = owner or user only». Now 403 `not-the-owner` for a conversation that is not the job's owner (the withdraw gate's shape, B-8bd5). One asker changes: a lineage-less job's creator in a LATER session, bound to the job only by its subscription (ownerLineage), could ask before and is refused now — as withdraw refuses it (the manual's stated limit).
- LEGS: test-jobs-addressed §0b over the REAL routes + the real CLI: the plant (view all · control all kept exactly), a missing word stays missing, twelve refusals each PRINTED with its code and words (lock, no scope, another shape, another key, string access, a run with B as subscriber, a run with a panel and a clear, a run with the wake grant, a run's own notify / context / nested task / access), a task create's own fields still made, the CLI's `--view everyone` refused; B's ask refused, A's asks. RED CONTROLS (ONE copy of the routes with the three cuts, each anchor asserted once; each control drives its own road): the base's whole copy ⇒ a job «pinned by the user» whose owner's access verb is then refused, and a stored «everyone»; no run-field refusal ⇒ the run carries B and M.addressedTo says «subscriber»; no ask gate ⇒ B's question is posted.
- ADVERSARIAL READ r1 (no MUST): the run-field set was every create key — notify / context / access / action rode a run (cured above, legs added: a view-only asker, a session-owned job's owner asks, the REAL CLI's scheduled run with every task flag, the wake grant's control); kb-api gained the refusals; the design's tombstone sentence corrected.
- FOUND, NOT MINE: (1) the lock's rm+recreate tombstone (design §7) was never built — an agent holding control can `rm` a locked job (src/agent-routes.js, `rm` needs control only) and create the same name unlocked and wider; the design now says so. (2) A scheduled run's record gets `access: job.access` (src/jobs.js _fireCron) — one object until a restart, two copies after: a lock or a narrowing of the schedule after a restart does not reach its existing run (by reading; not run). (3) The person's create and access routes (src/server/jobs-wiring.js POST /api/jobs, /api/jobs/:id/access) take the general cookie verdict, not the strict person verdict the wake-grant route beside them uses (`personHere`) — on an instance with no sign-in a local non-browser client passes (by reading).
- NOT TOUCHED: jobs already stored with a lock or a non-scope by an agent (no reader can tell an agent's lock from the person's); the access verb still ignores a word that is no scope silently (it answers the access it kept).

### bl-keys-misc B-360d — the jobs' collection pass asks its files off the loop (the coordinator's r706 / r707)
- **The measure (the owner's hub, read by the coordinator).** On 2.369.413, with 878 jobs (2.2 MB) and the data folder on a network mount, the journal named two loop holds in two and a half hours, 1.2 and 1.4 s, at the jobs' stamp read. That is the hourly collection pass (\`_gc\`): a synchronous open of each job's pid.json, blocked on the mount. The nine-day-old profile's ranks 12c (the discovery sweep: cured since by B-891e, 6ae22965e + c6bcbd45b, the sweep in its own worker) and 9 (the window-open fan-out) were read first; the hub ranks this one first.
- **The law.** No synchronous file call of that pass on the hub's loop. Every ask (the spill folder's listing, stats and removals, and each stamp) goes through \`_gcAsk\`: off the loop (fs.promises), ONE at a time — a read that has not come back is never started again beside itself, in this pass or the next. The whole pass is bounded by GC_FILES_MS (10 s). An ask that does not answer is UNKNOWN, and the pass collects nothing on an unknown (said once). The stamp decides only for a record the pass would collect, so only those stamps are read: on the owner's hub that is a few files an hour instead of 878.
- **Siblings in src/jobs.js, by a search for the synchronous file calls (named, not cured here).** The archive sweep's stamp read (boot and every 5 min) reads only records the clock released, and its sweep stays synchronous by design (one archive write, no interleaving). The sweep tick reads live jobs' stamps every 5 s. The rest are the store's and its sidecars' reads at the load, the lock file, the log tails asked by a person's press, the wrapper's spec file at a start, and the cgroup reads (/proc and /sys, not the data folder).
- **Gate.** The new fast test-jobs-gc-off-loop. A FIFO with no writer as a candidate's stamp: the loop keeps turning, the pass ends at its budget, that record and the one after it are unknown and kept, the one before is collected, and it is said once. A non-candidate's FIFO is never asked. While that read is out a pass asks nothing; once it answers, the next pass collects. The release's read, in a copy (scripts/mutant-copy.mjs), holds the loop while a writer answers the FIFO after 400 ms: RED. A census finds no synchronous file call in the pass's body.

### bl-mail B-dfa4 cut 4 — the first digest after a boot is warmed in slices, never built whole in the reader's turn
- THE FACT (measured on the 96 500-row stand-in, the tree's loop-hold reader): the first full digest after a boot built its three kept indexes whole in its own turn — the row facts' sums (rowKept), the first read's kept facts and heads (firstKept), each account's census index (censusIx) — 0.5–0.6 s, the moment the panel opened after a restart.
- THE CURE: on an index of more than WALK.syncRows rows the three are built in slices from the turn after start() (`digestWarmStart`, walkSliced) over a stated snapshot of the rows and one clock instant; a row touched meanwhile — by the index's touch OR by a due signal that touches no row (a quiet poll's stamp, a watch start: the warm-up taps `markDue`) — is re-read by each index's own road at its first read after the landing; a whole-map touch starts it again (three times — then said once, and the first read builds whole). ITS READERS WAIT: GET /api/channels awaits `digestReady()` (bounded, 5 s — past it the digest builds whole, the release's road); a broadcast asked meanwhile is made ONCE at the landing (the changed keys merged; an ask that left the whole-or-partial choice to notify's own rule keeps it); a synchronous digest() before the landing builds whole (never a partial answer).
- AND THE ROADS AFTER IT: many rows moved at once in the kept heads (`headMoveMany`) and re-judged at once in a census index (`censusRejudgeMany`, and the clock's crossed heads) — each array filtered once and merged with the moved rows' entries (`mergeSorted`), never a splice of a 89 000-entry array per row; the census reads the live rows (read-only), never a deep copy per row.
- The landing turn's own cost is printed (`digestWarmStats().landMs`, its sorts; `notifyMs`, the deferred broadcast); a warm-up that throws is said in the journal (never an unhandled rejection) and the first read builds whole.
- ALSO (主开发 r764, the round wtwe8gyss on cut 3d, into this cut):
  - (1) The due turn says `beyond` (the due rows it did not take) beside `lateTotal` (every row due as the index knows it); the pass's timer turn and the discovery's read it. Before, they read `lateTotal − DUE_TURN_MAX`, which holds only when the overdue heads alone fill one budget: with thousands of pending rows due and few heads during a merge, the card's waiting number came out low.
  - (2) During a merge, the rows touched since it began are read from a cursor that moves each turn, never always from the start of the set (a row touched after 2000 stamps no longer waits for the landing).
  - (3) The unused `extra` set is gone.
  - (4) `dueStats.listRebuilds` / `listRebuildRows`: the whole-list rebuilds the one-merge road makes (its fixed cost on a big account).
  - LEG (c7): with no overdue head (every row polled, then 500 due again), its waiting numbers are the whole build's own turn's.
- LEGS test-sliced-walk (h1)–(h7): parity with a whole build byte for byte, the first digest READING the landed indexes (no rebuild of either); a change between two slices; nobody reads half (digestReady unresolved meanwhile; a broadcast waits, one at the landing); a synchronous digest during it builds whole; the bound (three whole touches, said once); (h6) 300 rows touched after the warm-up — one merge each, no build, the digest a whole build's, the kept first read the walk's; then the clock 30 h on — hundreds of census judgements crossed at once, placed back by one merge; (h7) a stamp (no index touch) during the census walk on a row it had visited — heard, the digest a whole build's. RED CONTROLS: a landing that forgets the rows touched meanwhile → (h2) red; a merge that keeps the moved rows' old entries → (h6) red; the warm-up deaf to markDue → (h7) red.

## 2.369.413 — 2026-11-20

### bl-loop-b — the watch door's block follow (its readers' S1 / S3 / S4 + N4 / N8 / N9 / N10, after the hotfix 2.369.411's push)
- S1: a watch-limit item still open after a restart is ADOPTED (the store's openItems() by its key): the limit taken as met from then, its filing time the item's own createdAt, the probe armed, the item lifted by the same rule — never a second item beside it, never one left open for good. At configure() when the store answers, else at the next turns (tries 0 / 1 / 6 / 36 s after it, unref'd): its fresh reader found the hub's boot configures the door (memory-pressure-watch) BEFORE the store exists — its getter throws until then — so the first form adopted nothing in production.
- N4: the poll's cadence is capped at CADENCE_MAX_MS 5 s, so the notice's «every few seconds at most» holds however many poll. N9: a filing that keeps failing is said ONCE a limit. N10: a reset's generation keeps an older tick from taking or giving a slot of the new one (a turn it held at the reset was the old state's — handing it to the new one over-released: the running-bound leg read 34 of 32 on its gate) and from counting its pollers. N8: the workflow tailer closes a door poll that stands in (its own poll carries the folder).
- LEGS (test-watch-door §1b): the adoption + a control with it cut; the store that arrives after configure (its getter throws first) + a control adopting at configure only; an adopted item lifted by the probe alone + a control with the adoption's probe cut; S3 — the probe lifting the limit with nothing else armed + a refusing-probe control; the arms counted IN A ROW + a control with the reset cut; the 32-running bound counted by the stand-in + a lifted-bound control; N10 — two ticks holding their turns at a reset, then the bound + a control handing the stale turn to the new state; N4 / N9 legs; N8 / N10 source pins. The code controls are mutant-copies through scratch.mjs anchored() (§1's fixed-command control moved there too); the probe's and the bound's are the stand-in's own. S4: §3 waits for the poll's ready, bounded.
### bl-loop-b — the watch door's pool law and three smalls (主开发 2026-11-19 09:53Z), with test-watch-door's tier row restated (7.5 s)
- THE LAW: the door never holds more than HALF the runtime's thread pool — LIMITS.inflight 4 → 2 (the default pool is 4; half of a smaller pool set in the environment; the hub raises its own to 32 in server.js's first lines). The limits are declared ONCE (DEFAULT_LIMITS) and resetForTest() copies them, so the suite reads the shipped values (its fresh reader's must: a second copy in the reset let a declared 4 ship under a green suite). A stat on a wedged mount never returns; at 4 the door could hold every thread of a default pool, and then every async file call of the process waits — the hub-freeze class. The cap of 4 came with the hotfix 2.369.411. The trade, said: two wedged targets hold both slots, and every door poll waits behind them.
- The last adoption try's failure is said ONCE in the journal (LIMITS.adoptRetryMs holds the gaps; the suite moves them). Above 320 pollers the cadence grows again (TICKS_PER_S_MAX 64: n / cadence ≤ 64 a second in a steady state; at 320 both rules give 5 s, below it the step rule is larger or equal) — the notice's «every few seconds at most» then stops being exact; its words KEPT by the coordinator's ruling (19:22Z: 320 refused watches at once is far past anything met). The tailer's no-second-poll now has a behaviour leg.
- THE ROW AND THE CAP: test-watch-door's tier row restated 3.5 → 7.5 s (the median of four readings at bd32d1f0d: 7724 / 7595 ms in its list gate, 7459 / 7474 alone); the fast cap moved by ARITHMETIC in the same commit — on the 2.369.413 base ac70cf7ee: 1448 → 1452 s (the stated truth 1451.248 s over 728 fast rows; FAST_SUM_CAP_MS, its pin in test-ci-gate, the sum in the comment; on its first base it was 1443 → 1447).
- LEGS: the pool — a child with UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=4 polls six refused watches through a stand-in whose stat opens a FIFO nobody writes (a real pool thread held): two stuck and the child's own stat answers, the child reading the DECLARED limits (no reset); CONTROL the cap at 4: four stuck and its own stat waits; the FIFOs opened O_RDWR at the end and held to the exit (never ENXIO), a killed child red, a failed mkfifo red. The last try's line + a control with it cut (mutant-copy + anchored()). N4 re-stated for the floor. The tailer by behaviour + a control with its close cut.

### bl-machines-b — B-0194's next line (主开发 08:03Z, after B-2fa8 and B-0194 TAKEN at block lines 226 and 227)
- (1) A PAIRING MADE AGAIN keeps the device id and so its hello folds: the new pairing's first identical refusal was counted, not said. `agentdMintDialPair` now drops the device's folds (what they owed is said first), so the new pairing starts fresh.
- (2) An owner's reply that lands after unpair made a new store for the gone device — and nothing stops the cached client at an unpair. Each key has a GENERATION (`HELLO_GEN`): `dropHelloFolds` bumps it first, and a hello reads or makes its key's store only at the generation it BEGAN in — `_askUpgrade` stamps it when the ask starts, so the owner's answer to an ask begun before the drop is said and folds nothing; a hello begun after the drop folds as any, on a client kept across it too (a pairing made again in place keeps its link; a graduation rolled back keeps its client). A client stopped by a RE-DIAL (the same generation) still folds into the device's store, so a re-dial that joins the same ask says it once. `_helloFoldEnd` and the «waits» check read without making a store. Accepted: a pairing made again while the owner's card is open — the old ask's answer and the new pairing's first refusal are two lines (two pairings).
- (3) TWO NAME SPACES: a device id folds as `dev:<deviceId>`, an ssh host with none as `host:<hostId>` (they never share a name); a graduation drops the ssh name's store (its count said), its undoing the device name's, a host's removal both.

### bl-accounts B-23c3 — a first start is told apart from a spend ledger that went
- **The harm:** spend-guard read ENOENT as «nothing spent yet», so a first boot, an rm, a cleanup script and a restore without the file looked the same — the count of turns nobody typed went back to zero in silence (bl-accounts batch 1's verdict, 主开发 2026-11-18 00:49Z).
- **The law:** a MARKER beside the ledger (data/spend-budget.born.json: born, seq, resets, lastReset) is written with every ledger write, after it (a crash between leaves the ledger AHEAD, never behind); the ledger carries the same seq. Ledger gone + marker = REMOVED; a ledger's seq below the marker's = AN OLDER COPY put back. The reset stays possible — removing the file is the stated door for an unreadable ledger (B-3b0f) — but it is SAID (the journal and ONE For-you item, `spend-ledger-reset`, urgent, retried until the store answers) and COUNTED (the marker's resets, the snapshot's ledgerResets / ledgerLastReset), and the record is written at once so the next boot reads it whole (said once, never at every boot). Neither file = a first start, silent as before. B-3b0f's road goes through the same judge both ways (the reader's must): the marker is read even while the ledger cannot be (its history outlives the refusal), an unreadable ledger the owner removed is a counted reset, and one REPAIRED from an older copy is said too. A ledger with NO write number under a numbered marker (a VibeSpace before the marker wrote it, or a copy from before it) is said in its own words. An unreadable marker is HELD (the store-read law): never set aside, never read as empty and written over — read again at each write, and once it reads its history is adopted. A notice the store cannot take at boot (it is built later) is owed in the marker and filed at the next boot, or on a minute's timer, or at the next authorize. **The limit, said:** the marker lives in data/ beside the ledger, so restoring the WHOLE data folder from a backup, or removing both files, still resets in silence — the marker tells a lost ledger from a first start, not a lost data folder.
- **Pinned:** test-spend-paths §3g — a first start silent and its first write at seq 1 with the marker; a removed ledger said, counted, written at once and the next start silent; an older copy said and counted (reset #2); a RED copy whose load never reads the marker resets in silence; B-3b0f's door said and counted.

### bl-machines-b — B-4d71: a dial-only unpair leaves no start behind — the device retires its own (the dial's «retired» answer, with a proof)
- THE GAP: a dial-only device has no ssh for the hub to clean it with. An unpair removed the pairing on the hub and left the device's start behind (the systemd user unit, the launchd item, the container boot-hook block of B-8475, the Windows logon task): its agent dialed a refusing hub for ever, every 30 s.
- ONE ROAD — THE DIAL'S ANSWER: `unpairDialDevice` keeps the unpaired token's TOMBSTONE first (`hosts.noteRetiredDial`: its hash, at most 512, 180 days, in hosts.json). The device's next dial with that EXACT token (at once for a device dialed in now — its link ends at the unpair; an offline one whenever it comes back) is answered 401 `retired` with `X-VibeSpace-Retire-Proof` = HMAC-SHA256(key = the hash of the device's HOST token — vsht_, which the hub sends only inside a live link's hello, never on a dial, read before the unpair drops it; the device's own per-dial nonce `x-vibespace-dial-nonce`): whoever merely receives a dial (a lapsed name, a leased address, a relay) cannot make it, and a replay fits no other dial; an empty token never proves. Anyone else (another token for the name) hears the one answer every stranger hears (token-mismatch): no word that the name was ever paired. A tombstone per TOKEN (several a name: an unpair, a re-pair, an unpair again); a new pairing drops none (its fresh token never matches one). A vault locked at the unpair leaves no proof key: that device is told «retired» without a proof and keeps its start. No new op on the live link (it would pass the hub's act gate and its asks); the dial answer serves the online and the offline device alike.
- THE AGENT (src/agentd/self-retire.js, DEVICE): on `refused-retired` whose proof holds for its own HOST token (state/token) and this dial's nonce (`PT.retireProofMatches`), and only while its state/dial.json still holds the dial token just proven (a pairing made again into the root since then is never erased), it runs the installer's own retire: the dial config and the token FIRST (a restart can no longer dial); the boot-hook block (only a whole begin…end pair, through the hook's real file, its mode and link kept, never another user's file — install.sh drop_hook_block's rule); the launchd plist / the systemd unit (disabled, its file gone, reloaded) / the Windows logon task; the supervisor's own stop LAST (launchctl bootout / systemctl --user stop — it ends the unit's processes, what the agent runs with it, as the installer's own retire does; the unpair dialog says so) — its result logged; then it ends. On Windows a logon task registered with the highest run level may refuse a delete from an agent that is not elevated: that step is LEFT, said in the agent's log. The KEY is the installer's: GNU tr counts bytes (Linux), macOS tr characters. A «retired» without a valid proof, or a dial with no nonce (an older agent), changes nothing: it keeps its start, as before. Not removed: the root's own files (the agent's bundle); a person removes the folder.
- WORDS: DIAL_REFUSAL_CODES + `retired` (its sentence), DIAL_FAIL_CODES + `refused-retired` (the dial check says it as a refusal, exit 14); the gate's line goes through the refusal LOG budget.
- LEGS: test-dial-link-kept (the REAL gate, a real HostManager): «retired» + the proof the agent checks, a replay to another nonce / token refused, the tombstone outlives a restart, any other token hears token-mismatch, no nonce ⇒ no proof, the name paired again ⇒ no tombstone; RED CONTROL the gate without the tombstone (token-mismatch for ever). NEW fast suite test-device-self-retire: the proof (PURE); the words; the KEY against the installer's line in a real bash; the hook block against the installer's drop_hook_block in a real bash case by case (a person's lines, a prefix key, no block, a begin with no end) + its link, mode and owner; the steps per platform as the installer names them; the steps over a scratch root with stub supervisors (each done or LEFT with its why, the stop the caller's last); the agent's wiring. RED CONTROLS: the key over characters on Linux, the drop without its open guard, the rewrite at the umask's mode.
- ITS READ (one fresh agent): M1 two fast suites red at the first commit (the closed code set; an injected runner named `exec` read as a child site — now `supervisor`); M2 the proof keyed by the DIAL token's hash, which rides every dial — keyed by the HOST token's now; S1 one tombstone a name, dropped at any mint — one a token, never dropped; S3 the stop ends the agent's processes — said in the unpair dialog (zh, ja); N2 the last step's result logged; N3 the dial config re-read before anything goes; N4 the words (the constants named, the refusal sentence, the changelog lines, the zh line). LEFT: S2 a real-agent leg (a live link unpaired, the re-dial told «retired»: test-agentd-dial's kind, a heavy suite); N1 an elevated Windows task (said in the log); tombstones are not in exportBundle (a moved hub forgets them).
- ITS ROUND (主开发 wz421di05: three lenses take; ONE MUST before it ships — a proof's format is fixed at its first release): THE PROOF NAMES ITS PURPOSE. The HMAC (keyed by the host token's hash) is over `vibespace-retire-v1` \0 <the device's id> \0 <the hash of the dial token that matched the tombstone> \0 <the nonce> (pairing-token `RETIRE_PURPOSE` / `retireMessage`; a part holding \0, or an empty part, makes no proof); the device checks the same message from its id (its dial URL's `device`), its dial token and its host token. THE WORDS MADE TRUE: the host token never rides a dial, but it rides the live link's hello AND the install command the hub minted for the device — so a proof can be made by the hub (its tombstone) and by whoever holds that install command (who can already speak the hub's hello to the device), never by whoever merely receives a dial. The tombstone's proof key (the host token's HASH) sits in the clear in hosts.json: what it can do is make the retire proof for a device that is already unpaired — nothing more (kb). A vault locked at the unpair is never asked for the host token (`hostTokenLocked`, server.js's wiring line changed in place) — no «waiting on the vault» note for a machine just removed; that device keeps its start. A supervisor stop that fails is said with what follows (a restart-always unit or a KeepAlive item brings the agent back idle until it is removed by hand). No supervisor step runs where its unit file / plist is not there (`onlyIf`, read once before the steps: `presentOf`).

- THE EPISODE ON THE ITEM (debt 1): the blocked-pool For-you item's episode lived in the engine's memory alone — a restart re-filed an item the owner had dismissed (the pool still blocked) and never closed an item an earlier run left open once the pool recovered. src/server/usage-pool-engine.js `poolBlockedEpisode` (new) reads the pool's newest filing (by createdAt) back from the For-you store ONCE a run — a live episode is an OPEN item or one a PERSON closed (resolvedBy user / reply / hidden — an allow-list) in an episode no recovery ended; an item its expiry closed (a hub down past the item's expiry, 1 to 2 h ahead: the store's boot sweep closes it before the first tick) or the agent closed is none, so the block files again as the parent did (the parent's fallback read open items only); `poolBlockedTodo` keeps one item an episode across a restart (a dismissed one stays dismissed); `poolBlockedTodoEnd` closes an earlier run's open item at this run's first evaluation that finds the pool serving (the boot's tick) and writes the episode's end ON the item (resolvedFact endedAt / endedBy 'pool-serves' / endedFor = the filing it ended), so a block after the recovery and a restart is a new episode. ### bl-jobs B-2c5c — a job's stop never ends a hub started by hand inside it
- THE HARM: a hub started by hand from INSIDE a Background Work job (a restart run in its shell) lives in that job's scope, its process group and with its mark (VIBESPACE_JOB_ID in its environment). The job's stop then reached it by every whole door: the wrapper's forced end (`systemctl --user kill --signal=KILL` of the scope, then its cgroup.kill), the manager's scope signal when the scope's list could not be read, the rows it signalled one by one (the scope's, the group's, the marked escapees'), the engine's group signal and its own cgroup.kill (the stop ladder's kill step, the reap of an ended run), the clear of kept processes and the stop of a doubted run (every process carrying the job's mark) — B-c134's hub exclusion covered only the tree walk.
- THE CURE: ONE test by the PARENT CHAIN — `keptByChain(pid, keep)` (src/proc-identity.js, a shipped twin in data/bin/job-wrapper.js): the hub (the wrapper: <data>/server.pid and what the engine's intent keeps out; the engine: its own pid) and everything under it are never a stop's. A scope that holds the hub is never killed WHOLE (neither the manager's kill nor cgroup.kill): the job's own processes by force, one by one (identity re-read), the hub's left alone, said ONCE in the job's log; the engine knows the hub is inside from its OWN cgroup (/proc/self/cgroup, read once a life) and answers `'hub'` (the reap and the stop ladder take it as done, said); a job whose process group holds the hub is stopped process by process (its wrapper alone hears the signal; a SIGKILL ends its whole tree by identity, the hub's pruned). Legs: test-stop-tree §10 (the chain over a fake /proc; the wrapper's forced end, its scope signal, the engine's group signal — compiled from their own source; the real chain of a child), test-jobs-memory ⑳ (the engine's scope kill over the fake cgroup tree) — each with its control.

### bl-accounts B-ef83 — one hub process keeps the spend ledger; a reset notice only for a real loss
- **The harm (B-ef83, account hardening):** two hub processes on one data folder (a restart whose old process is still ending, a second server started by hand) each kept their own count of turns nobody typed from the same file — each allowed the caps in full, each wrote its count over the other's.
- **The lock:** data/spend-budget.lock ({pid, host, ns: the pid space, token: the guard's own, ident: src/proc-identity.js identityOf, at}), created WHOLE (a temp file linked into place; created exclusively where the folder makes no hard link), mode 0644. A LIVE holder makes this process refuse every unattended turn by name (`ledger-held-elsewhere`: the authorizer's words, the door, the hand-over line, zh / ja), never write the ledger or its marker, never re-read it (recheck), never warn from its count, and judge no waiting frame (the keeper counted them — none pulled); it counts only what it notes MEANWHILE, asks again every LOCK_RETRY_MS and, at the takeover, reads the record the other kept + that delta (never the file twice), judges it against its marker and writes it. Live = in THIS pid space on THIS host, proc-identity proves the very process the lock recorded; anywhere else (another machine, another pid space — two containers with one hostname), or unprovable, or a lock that cannot be read: live while its heartbeat (the lock's mtime, LOCK_BEAT_MS) CHANGES on this process's clock within LOCK_STALE_MS. A gone holder is set aside under this guard's name, read back (a fresh lock made meanwhile is put back) and taken over, said. The keeper's heartbeat compares the TOKEN: a lock naming another stops it at once; a lock removed by hand is made again (its record never re-read). Removed at exit when it still holds the token.
- **主开发's law (2026-11-19 19:20Z): A RESET NOTICE ONLY FOR A REAL LOSS.** The marker records what each write COUNTS (`counted` {newestAt, until}: spend-authorizer countedOf); a ledger met at load is a loss only when it lacks a turn that still counts (countLost) — whatever the write numbers say. So a crash between the boot's two writes says nothing (order A: the reset's marker counts nothing) or says the hidden loss once (order B); a downgrade and back (no number, every counted turn in it) and a marker repaired by hand (no count) are said in the journal only. A notice has an END: `until`, the instant the last lost turn stops counting — owed past it, it is not filed.
- **Pinned:** test-spend-paths §3h — a live holder refused by name, never written, no waiting frame judged, asked again; the takeover counts the keeper's last record + the delta exactly (3, never the file twice); a recycled pid and a dead holder taken over at once; another machine held while its mtime changes on this clock, taken once silent; the heartbeat that finds another's lock; a lock that cannot be read held; a lock removed by hand made again with the count unchanged; a real process's exit releases it; RED: a copy that sees no live holder allows the turn and writes over the keeper's record; the three false cases silent (each with the release's rule as a RED copy filing the false notice) and order B said once; the notice's end, and a notice owed past it not filed. §3g (7) restated: an unnumbered ledger is a loss only when it lacks a counted turn.
- **Waits (主开发):** the ledger's save onto the queued store writer, after lg-store-writes' census cure is taken and its class hunt is clean. The censuses: store-write 4 → 11 (the lock's sites, durable: authority), sync-fs 3 → 12, mount readers 3 → 9; test-setting-links lists the held door by design.

### conversation-facts — majordomo piece 2: the facts, THE end verdict, `conversations.list` (`src/conversation-facts.js`, `src/server/conversation-facts.js`, `data/bin/chat-wrapper.js`)
- **Measured first (the brief's order):** a scratch hub (the worktree's own data/, the real chat-wrapper under dtach over a stand-in CLI), 12 idle chat fixtures in four shapes, the hub SIGKILLed and booted again with no page: **0 of 12** read known for background tasks, timers and idle age. The boot builds an EMPTY normaliser (boot-restore «populated on first attach»); the ring it holds has no dated record; `_lastPtyDataAt` / `_ptyOpenedAt` are stamped at the reconnect. One page attaching each made 6 of 12 known — only the CLIs that had published a set: the level signal is «emitted whenever membership changes», so under «null = never published» every plain conversation read unknown and therefore busy, for ever.
- **The ruling (road A): the facts are kept where they are born.** The chat wrapper reads every record from its CLI's first line and outlives every hub restart, so it keeps the last background set (or the empty set from the start, once the init names CLI 2.1.274 or later), the one-way CLI-timer mark (a fired wakeup's `wakeup_source` / `scheduled_for`, a `ScheduleWakeup` call — the only tool name the tree states) and the last record's time. One PURE step (`factsStep`) runs in the wrapper AND in the hub's claude-stream-json consumer. In the wrapper it is memory only per record: a change of the set or the mark rides `scheduleMeta`, the time rides the next existing write, or ONE write when nothing wrote for a minute. A failed write never stops the wrapper. `caps.facts` advertises the shape; a sidecar without it is an older wrapper: «unknown (its wrapper is older than this record; it learns at its next start)». Re-measured on the same rig: **12 of 12** known after the restart.
- **The contract per harness:** `sidecarFacts` {background, timers, lastRecordAt} on every backend-caps row (claude all three; codex / opencode / antigravity / shell none — their wrappers' sidecar writes are not driven by records, so a stamp beside them would not be the last record's time); the list reads the row, never a harness id. Where no wrapper kept a time, the idle age is the output file's own time, read in the builder's bounded pass.
- **THE verdict:** `endVerdict(row)` — the ten reasons in the design's order, each its own code; UNKNOWN IS BUSY (`<reason>_unknown` with the fact's sentence); the job reason — the owner's rule of 2026-11-17: refused while the conversation owns a job or schedule WITHOUT the person's grant «may wake its conversation» (piece 7's field; until it is read every grant is unknown, and unknown refuses); when every one carries the grant the reason does not hold — the row lists each with its grant; its input is `VERDICT_FIELDS` only (no idle, no memory — asserted). `refusalOf` is the sentence piece 3's end will answer with.
- **The list:** `conversations.list` (a READ, not billed) — the builder reads in-memory facts per session and runs ONE bounded pass (memory per process tree, the output file's age): one at a time, ended at its time-out, rows it did not finish say «the facts pass ran out of time — ask again» (never last time's values); single-flight.
