### the manager design, piece 7 — deliveries resume their addressee (主开发 2026-11-17 04:00Z; narrowed 04:56Z / 05:02Z / 05:13Z; design int359/majordomo)

A peer's one-addressee `--wake` resumes only a restart-ended conversation; fan-outs, subscribers' copies, channel messages and anything archived only wait, said.
- **The rung.** conversation-deliver's retry park gains `held.why: 'ended'` (`parkEndedWake`, one per conversation, `producers` / `metas` merged); its attempt hands it to the hub's ONE line (piece 4) through `registerEndedWake`; any answer ends it and is said to the producers (`wake`). The jobs engine owes it for a result / missed one-time / an interrupted task (new: a restart-interrupted task now tells its owner) / a reminder; the groups engine for a wake naming one stopped member (a bare hand-over: the report rides the turn's prompt hook).
- **The start** (src/server/delivery-wake.js): verdict → how it ended (each job's grant read at the line) → who pays (the kept record's account, the guard's identity road) → the limit (`quotaVerdictFor`, until when) → the spend guard as a PROBE (`hold: false`, judged in test-spend-paths §5e) → claim → reopen by `system:deliveries` → ONE hand-over under the producer's reason (stash-handover's prepare / finish split keeps each literal on its call line). Delivered ⇒ `resumedBy` on the session (the window's line; piece 5's row).

An agent token's write is refused by name (`wake_grant_person_only`, naming propose-wake). The Terminate confirm lists the conversation's live jobs and schedules with their ticks (src/lib/wake-grant-rows.js; `showConfirmDialog` takes the caller's node as `extra`); Background Work's job row has the checkbox.

### bl-jobs B-2c5c — a job's stop never ends a hub started by hand inside it
- THE HOSTED RUN'S RED (2.369.413 checkpoint 1, run 44652784592: test-jobs-memory-scopes, five legs, one cause — 主开发 01:57Z): small 2 measured the end through `procsOrNull`, whose bare catch answered null for ANY error — and a transient scope that EMPTIED is removed by systemd: its list is GONE, not unread, so a task that stopped cleanly ended «its scope's list could not be read: what it started may still run». THE LAW: the errno decides, by name — a list that no longer EXISTS is an EMPTY scope (the plain end): ENOENT (its path, the scope folder removed), ENODEV (a list opened while the scope lived, read after its removal), ENOTDIR (a component of the path no folder) — ENOENT and ENODEV seen on a real user scope on this box (kernel 7.0: bl-jobs/probes/errno/scope-gone.mjs); every other errno (EACCES, EPERM, EIO, EMFILE, ENFILE, …) is UNREAD and is now NAMED in the end («could not be read (EACCES)», exit.json `scopeUnread: <errno>`). The wrapper's `procsOrNull` and `scopeRows`, and the ENGINE's `_scopeProcs` (which read EVERY error as «empty» — the mirror fault: an unreadable list of an ended run read empty, its reap stopping unsaid), by the one set. THE ENGINE ON AN END WRITTEN «NOT EMPTY»: the sweep reaps that run (`_reapScope` → `_reapOnce`); a gone scope's list reads empty, the reap stops there — nothing killed, nothing said; its only kill is that scope's own cgroup.kill (the unit names the run's start: no other run's scope, no process outside it). ### lg-remote-hardening unit 6 — B-7f0b: the reverse tunnel's own door (q-042 D8b)
- THE HOLE: the hub end of a remote conversation's tunnel (a device's tcp-listen, an ssh -R) was the hub's WHOLE loopback http server. A hostile device was a local caller of the login page (one 127.0.0.1 rate-limit bucket), /otel (which trusts loopback), /hook and every page route.
- THE CURE: src/server/agent-listener.js, a second listener on 127.0.0.1:0 over the hub's own app.
  - It serves /api/agent/… and /api/editor/open; 404 for everything else, /api/home too (the `vibespace` CLI asks the hub on its own box, never through a tunnel). A dot segment, a doubled slash, a backslash (raw or encoded) or an encoded dot is refused, and so is an encoded slash that decodes into a dot segment or a doubled slash; any other encoded slash after the prefix is a name's own (a job name).
  - No upgrade listener is added (§89): an upgrade is answered as a plain request.
  - The FOUR tunnel ends take tunnelPort(PORT): a dialed device's tcp-listen, its back-tunnel re-owned at every dial-in (server.js), the ssh -R of a session and of a re-adopted one.
  - THE PORT IS KEPT across restarts (data/agent-door.json, 0600, as tailnet-door keeps its own): a remote ssh session survives a restart with its -R fixed in its argv. It is chosen in 20000–32767, outside the default ephemeral ranges of Linux, macOS and Windows (a range widened over it is not covered), so no outgoing connection holds it while the hub restarts, and never the hub's own port. A kept port that is taken gets a new one, said once. A re-adopted session waits for the door (ready()); once listening the door keeps an error listener.
  - Before it listens, it falls back to the hub's port, said once in the journal.
- THE ROAD CENSUS (test-agent-door ③): every hub path the shipped tools name (hosts.js AGENT_TOOLS, each read where it lives: data/bin, the files copied there at boot, the generated helpers), 128 of them, crosses the door; a path counts after a quote, a `}` or a `$VAR`. OTEL is local-only, so it needs none. THE END CENSUS (④) reads server.js and src/ LINE BY LINE: a `.reverseForward(` call or an ssh -R `reverse:` template names tunnelPort(PORT) on its line (a push mount in its one form), and the one -R push into an argv passes its caller's target. Each has a RED (a planted page route; a named connectLocal, a sink over two lines, an -R to localhost).
- LIMITS, said:
  - a push mount's reverse tunnel (src/machine-mounts.js) still ends at the hub's own port, for its /dav: a door of its own is not built;
  - /api/editor/open keeps its own check (a token only when sign-in is on, not tied to the session) — the door's one route outside /api/agent;
  - a session started before a restart whose kept port was taken reaches its tools again when it restarts;
  - a tool that builds a page-route path at runtime from parts would not be seen by the census (none is known).
### lg-remote-hardening unit 5 — B-7f0b: the hub proves ITS key (q-042 D3, half b; 主开发's ruling 2026-11-18 00:00Z)
- THE HOLE: a stolen host token (a data/ copy) could drive every paired device (T2). The device checked ONE bearer.
- THE CURE: the hub's identity lives in the vault (`hub-identity`) and its public key rides every hello. The device pins it at the first verified ok (bound to the token that admitted it; a new pairing voids it) and from then on refuses:
  - another hub key: hub-key-mismatch;
  - a hello without one: hub-key-missing (no downgrade);
  - an ok whose signature over THIS device's key and nonce fails: hub-signature-bad.
  The device is authed only after the ok.
- THE FOUR LAWS, as built:
  - (1) the signing door signs ONE shape it builds itself (label, machine key, device nonce);
  - (2) only a conversation of THAT machine (its session; the device key it brings must be the record's pinned one); a job token resolves no session;
  - (3) no downgrade, no hang (a device too old to ask is never asked; every hub-* refusal is terminal); a LOST hub key is hub_identity_lost by name, and a new one is the person's act;
  - (4) the refusal reaches the card (chip + Host key… door) and For you.
- LIVE WHEN: the hub half and the attach child at this release; the device half only after a device's agent updates to a signed release carrying it. A device that has not updated pins nothing and works as today.
- CURE after the lane's adversarial read (2 musts, 7 shoulds, notes):
  - MUST 1: the vault name `hub-identity` was not one the vault takes, so a set-up vault refused every read and put. It is now `host:hub-identity`, with a vault-road leg.
  - MUST 2: a re-pair did not void a device's pin, because the host token does not rotate. The pairing command run ON the device now removes state/hub.pub, and renew clears an ssh machine's pin over ssh.
  - SHOULDS:
    - a locked vault refuses before the hello;
    - the hub's own key trouble is said as itself;
    - a device without its own key never asks;
    - a refusal after the settle tears the link down;
    - hubPinned is recorded at the ok that pins;
    - this box's DeviceManager carries the identity;
    - the card clears on a link that opens, and «Forget» is hidden for hub-side refusals;
    - «Forget» rebuilds the cached link;
    - a first mint is exclusive;
    - attach-cli logs the refusal's code.
  - LEFT, said: link-sign writes no audit row of its own (its link-token sibling does). The PTY-mode resize-before-ok is unreachable today: only the dial bridge, which never asks.
  - HAZARDS, said: before the vault is set up, the hub's key sits in data/agentd beside the host tokens (a data/ copy holds both; the vault closes that). A hub rolled back below this release is refused hub-key-missing by every updated device that pinned it.
- CURE after 主开发's verdict of 2026-11-18 (NOT TAKEN: 4 musts that are TWO defects; the line file lg-remote-hardening-u5-cure.md):
  - MUST A: THIS BOX'S OWN AGENT NEVER WAITS FOR THE VAULT. The local DeviceManager asked the hub's identity. A set-up vault is locked after every start, so the read threw vault_locked, the refusal was terminal, and the box's own machine was gone for the run, even after the unlock. The cure: NO HUB KEY ON THE LOCAL ROAD. server.js builds the local DeviceManager with no hubIdentity: a same-user socket, where a pin proves nothing a reader of the same files could not forge. The agent pins nothing there.
  - A PAIRED machine while the vault is locked, said exactly: a running link is not cut (the hub's key is read at a connect, never during a link); a new connect waits, refused by name (vault_locked) in the words the chat's chip turns into «unlock the vault», before any hello; after the unlock the next connect opens.
  - MUST B: A PIN ALWAYS HAS A DOOR, AND A KEY IS NEVER MINTED SILENTLY OVER A PIN.
    - An ssh machine pinned to an older key of this hub gets a door on ITS road: «Let it pin this hub's key» (DELETE /api/hosts/:id/hub-pin, human only). Its state/hub.pub is removed over ssh, THEN the record and the link are cleared. A dialed device keeps its pairing command.
    - Before a key is minted, every pin is counted: the wirings hand the pinning machines' names. A lost key with pins standing is refused by name with its recovery («re-pair these machines: …»).
  - SHOULDS taken: the renew awaits its ssh clear before it rebuilds the link; the attach child treats a vault_locked link-sign as the vault wait (exit 7) and a key not learned yet as a wait.
  - LEFT, said:
    - the pre-vault key file is read at each use, not cached: a cache would hide a deleted key from the lost-key law. It is the same class as the host tokens' reads in data/agentd;
    - 'hub-pinned' is marked when the hub sends its ok, the conservative direction;
    - link-sign writes no audit row;
    - the renew's person check is its siblings'.
- PROOF (test-device-key-pin ⑦):
  - the PURE shape and verdicts;
  - signForMachine's laws, lost / renew;
  - the door's route (job token, another machine);
  - the REAL agent: pins, says it pins, another hub refused, no downgrade, a new pairing voids;
  - the attach child against a strict device: its ok goes before its op;
  - RED: an agent copy without the check, and an attach copy without the ok.
- UNIT 5's CURE 2 (one machine, two agents — over unit 3's cure): a machine upgraded to dial-out runs its dial agent under its own root (dialRoot), which pins the hub too. «Let it pin this hub's key» (and the renew) clears the pin under EVERY root of the machine (mounts-plugins-wiring `hubPinRm`; a dialRoot of another shape is never put into the shell line), and a link that opened on ONE road («linked», said with its road) never clears the other road's refusal or its urgent item.

  - a fake device over the real Mux: learn, keep, a swap refused with the dialed stream kept, no proof refused, the old agent not judged;
  - the record's acts and the re-pair forget;

  - the route refuses a bearer;

- ONE PIN, ONE ROAD (the cure of 主开发's verdict): a machine upgraded to dial-out runs a second agent under its own root, with its own key. Its device key is judged on the DIAL road only (where a copied pairing is the threat); its ssh road is guarded by ssh's own host key check and pins and refuses nothing (client.js `deviceJudged`, wired by hosts.js). The upgrade starts the dial road with no pin, and removing dial-out drops it.

The row draws its buttons by it, and the For-you item and the «pinned its new key» notice word their doors by it.
### lg-remote-hardening unit 4 — B-7f0b: the device's greeting judged (q-042 D8a, the part that is buildable)
- THE HOLE: client.js kept the hello-ack WHOLE as the link's `info` and drove decisions from it (platform → the shell road, capabilities → which ops are asked, posixShells → the Windows door, daemonVersion → the update). A hostile device could send any shape, up to the 64 MiB frame.
- THE CURE: `helloAckVerdict` runs first in the handler. A field that is PRESENT must have its shape; an older agent that never says a field is not judged on it. A bad greeting is refused by name (hello-ack-shape), with one journal line, and nothing of it is kept.
- The bounds: platform one Node.js names; capabilities ≤ 256 × ≤ 64; posixShells ≤ 16 names; the text fields ≤ 64; booleans; the whole greeting ≤ 64 KiB.
- THE BOUNDS DEPART FROM THE DESIGN'S NUMBERS, said: the design wrote capabilities ≤ 64 × ≤ 40 and posixShells ≤ 8. This tree's own agent already says 43 capabilities (21 characters at most), so 64 would refuse the fleet within a few releases. The unit takes 256 × 64 and 16 shells. The version grammar is device-upgrade-watch's verOf, copied, because client.js reaches no server module.
- CURE after the lane's adversarial read: a refused greeting is thrown at once by the connect loop on every road. It used to retry over the dead stream, wait out the 8 s handshake timer 14 times, and end as «cannot reach the local daemon» with the name lost. A dialed stream is kept, as on auth-fail.
- NOT BUILT, NAMED: the design's chan-0 control line ≤ 1 MiB and per-op answer caps. chan-0 carries answers far over 1 MiB today (session-events ≈ 19 MiB a line, per the separation programme's census), so that bound waits for the separation's piece 2, held on its own branch.
- PROOF (test-device-policy ⑤b, fast):
  - a PURE 13-row table, plus this tree's own agent's capability list measured from the source;
  - over the REAL Mux + DeviceManager: a good greeting connects; 300 capabilities or a foreign platform are refused by name with nothing kept;
  - RED: a copy without the verdict keeps all 300 as `info`.
- CURE after 主开发's verdict of 2026-11-18 (TAKEN, with one should kept as if a must; the line file lg-remote-hardening-u4-cure.md):
  - A REFUSED GREETING ON A DIALED STREAM IS REMEMBERED, as a refused sign-in is. dial-pairing.js `refusedStreams` (every terminal refusal of the handshake by name — client.js TERMINAL_REFUSALS, a locked vault excepted) refuses every op on that stream at once by name for the re-greet interval: no new DeviceManager and no new hello.
  - The refused handshake lets go of the stream: mux.js `detach()` ends its listeners and heartbeat, and the stream stays open. So N ops leave the stream's listeners where they were (RED: a copy that keeps the Mux piles N).
  - The row reads `greeting-refused`, with its door: update its agent, or rerun its install command.
  - Small: a platform WORD Node.js does not name yet passes (never a lock-out); daemonVersion is said to be the one required field; the version grammar is one copy (agentd-signature.js `verOf`, read by the upgrade watch too).
### lg-remote-hardening unit 2 — B-7f0b: a machine's ssh host-key pin (q-042 D6)
- THE HOLE: src/hosts.js dialled every ssh machine with StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new over the hub user's own known_hosts, so the first key ssh met was trusted. A pod has none: every fresh hub's first connection to each machine could be anyone. Over that road go the device host token (installAgentd), the session tokens and a remote session's account env.
- THE PIN (src/host-keys.js, SHARED):
  - A record may carry `hostKeys` [{type, key, fp}]. `sshArgs` / `sshCmd` put `HK.hostKeyOpts` FIRST (ssh keeps the first value), and `SSH_BASE_OPTS` lost its accept-new.
  - Unpinned ⇒ accept-new, as before. Pinned ⇒ StrictHostKeyChecking=yes + HostKeyAlias=<host> + UserKnownHostsFile="<data>/ssh/known_hosts.d/<id>" + GlobalKnownHostsFile=/dev/null. The alias keeps a config alias or a tailnet IP from moving the lookup.
- The person's three acts: `hostKeyScan`, `pinHostKeys`, `unpinHostKeys`, behind GET / POST / DELETE /api/hosts/:id/host-keys. Any bearer is refused as human_only.
  - The scan is ONE fresh ssh over the record's own road into a scratch known_hosts. ssh writes the key at key exchange, before any login.
  - A pin re-scans and keeps only keys shown NOW whose fingerprints were chosen; otherwise host-key-not-seen.
- THE REFUSAL BY NAME: `_ssh` and `sshRefusal` name ssh's host-key words `host-key-changed`, with the fingerprint shown. `sshRefusal` checks this before the 255 ⇒ unreachable verdict.
  - The row's chip says «host key changed», and its Host key… door gets the accent.
  - src/server/host-key-watch.js files ONE urgent For-you item per (machine, key shown). Its ledger survives a restart. A new pin or an unpin resolves it. It is wired on server.js's existing dial-health line (no new line).
- Files: the pin file is healed at boot from the record, removed with the machine and written on import. The /api/hosts row carries type + fingerprint only.
- LIMITS, said:
  - A ControlMaster opened BEFORE a key change rides its old connection until ControlPersist ends (600 s idle).
  - Only `_ssh` callers (probes, Test, discovery) raise the For-you item; a session's own ssh shows ssh's words in its pane.
  - Existing records stay unpinned until the person pins them. No live session breaks at the upgrade.
- CURE after the lane's adversarial read (4 musts, 6 shoulds; the read's table is in the line file):
  - A NEW machine's key is offered for a pin BEFORE its first test (the add flow).
  - The heavy RED copy dials with a fresh known_hosts (accept-new refuses a CHANGED key; it trusts only a first one).
  - The row keeps the refusal's code across a re-probe.
  - Test never re-diagnoses a key refusal over a live master.
  - sshCmd single-quotes the pin's path for rsync.
  - A pin or unpin drops the record's master and its cached device link.
  - Only ssh's exit 255 is judged.
  - The scan attempts no login.
  - UpdateHostKeys=no.
  - A record's keys are re-judged before the file.
  - A removed machine takes its item.
  - NOT built, said: a read-write folder mount (rclone sftp) checks no host key at all.
- CURE after 主开发's verdict of 2026-11-18 (NOT TAKEN: 1 must, 1 should raised to a must; the line file lg-remote-hardening-u2-cure.md):
  - THE MUST: mount-reader-census kept a row for host-key-watch.js, which reads nothing since the watch keeps no file (§86 dead row). The row is gone; the kb's two mentions of a ledger file are corrected.
  - THE ITEM OPENS ITS OWN DOOR: its `action` {type 'host-key', hostId, kind} names the machine by its record's id; the registry row DECLARES `opens: 'host-key-dialog'`; the jump's one declared-dialog door opens that machine's Host key… before the `machines` key's Manage Agents (which has no key control). The refusal and the item say ONE door phrase, «Remote → {machine} → Host key…».
  - The address is the pin line's NAME: whitespace or a control character in it is refused before anything is written, and the file's text is read back by unit 1's parser as exactly the keys under the one alias (`host-key-name`).
  - The machine's keys are judged by unit 1's one function (ssh-key-format hostKeyWhy / isHostKey).
  - A machine never pinned is told to pin the key it shows now, not «again». The scan also turns off GSSAPI and host-based authentication.
  - A removal passes the kind through to the watch; an import that drops a machine is a removal (pin file gone, items resolved).
  - The heavy test-conversation-needs gains the watch's producer row (it was missing at the first tip).
  - SAID in the kb: a pin applies to new dials; why the boot heal's synchronous calls are allowed (before the first loop turn, one per pinned record; production's data folder is a network mount, so «local» is not the reason); exit 255 can be a nested ssh's own.
- PROOF:
  - fast test-host-key-pin: the PURE table, options and files, routes (RED: a copy without the person check lets a bearer unpin), For you, the page. The cure's legs: one door phrase, «again» only when pinned, the scan's methods, the one judge, the alias refusals (read back by the parser), the import drop, the kind through a removal, and THE DOOR (RED: the release's item, its key alone, lands on Manage Agents).
  - heavy test-host-key-pin-real: real ssh against a loopback sshd -D child (no login). Scan, unpinned, pinned, THE SWAP refused by name, Test, a stale choice refused, re-pin, unpin. RED: a copy that ignores the pin trusts the swapped key.

### lg-remote-hardening — the row reads the order the hub recorded (list line 144's cure)
- Between a connect and a refusal of the same machine (a greeting refused, a sign-in failure, the dial road's device-key refusal) the row now reads the order the hub recorded them, never the luck of the clock: hosts.js stamps a refusal never at or before the connect it was recorded after, and a connect never before a refusal it was recorded after (a tie of the clock or a clock that stepped back read right in both directions; test-dial-link-kept's UTC-only red was an accept and its refusals in one millisecond).

### lg-rewind B-69a7 cut cure — a process is named by its PROGRAM, never by its main thread (主开发 10:15Z: the cut of .413 stopped on test-left-behind ④)
- THE RED: on the hub box (Node 24.22.1, production's Node) the planted node process was found and ended but named «MainThread» — the stat's name in its parentheses is the MAIN THREAD's, which Node 24 renames; the test machines and the hosted runner run Node 22 («node»), so every gate before the cut's was green. A person would read «MainThread» for whatever node program a tool left.
- THE LAW: the row's name is the base name of the program the kernel says the process runs (its exe link, « (deleted)» stripped), bounded as before (32); only when the link cannot be read, the stat's name. src/left-behind.js nameOf (PURE) + exeOf (one readlink per row FOUND, inside the read's raced bound — the link takes no memory-map lock); the press's re-check names the same way and still judges by pid, start time and mark. The device agent's op is the same code.
- LEGS (test-left-behind): ④ the planted processes named by the suite's own node's base name (path.basename(process.execPath)) on every Node; ① a stand-in row whose stat says «MainThread» with a program link reads «node», one with no readable link its stat's name; PURE nameOf; RED CONTROL the release candidate's stat-only read names it «MainThread».

### bl-vault — B-6721 cure (主开发's round wdtmcza5y on 276cd57c3): a pending fork is never the parent's window; For you marks an event, not a state a boot finds
- THE MUST: the wake chain found its conversation's session by the raw id (`widOf` by `cidOf`) — a PENDING FORK carries its parent's id, so a fork's payload armed a stopped parent's chain on the fork's window (5 s … then every 10 min for as long as the fork stayed pending). The chain now resolves through the ladder's own predicate (`ownCidOf` = `addressableId` → `ownWidOf`) in summaryFor, noteLive, quiet, tryWake, the turn-end road `runArmed` and `handOver` (the raw `widOf` is gone). A post INTO the fork: the ladder's local rungs never write into a pending fork (conversation-deliver findRpcPeer :1309, localSessionFor :1530 read `addressableId`); the peer-inbox rung posts to the socket the CLI's OWN registry record names for the id (peer-messaging lookupPeer, `rec.sessionId`) — and that record CAN be the fork's own CLI: a fork whose CLI resumed the parent instead of forking writes its lock/registry file under the parent's id (B-8b7b) until the hub's proof (two sightings) stops it, and on a device that proof never runs. So on 276cd57c3 a wake look landing in that window billed a turn into the fork's process (leg (g)'s RED of the raw road shows the post); with the cure the wake never resolves a pending fork — neither the timer nor the post exists. ALSO CURED (the cure's fresh read): a pending fork's strip showed the PARENT's stash and its «Hand over» billed the parent's notices from the fork's window — the fact and the hand-over are the session's own conversation's (`no_conversation` for a pending fork).
- THE RULING (the first boot's wave, measured on the owner's hub: 3 conversations with a not-running notice, two a month old): a For-you item marks an EVENT — JobManager marks a conversation when a `not-running` notice is stashed for it while the hub runs (`_stoppedThisRun` — by the notice just stashed, never the queue's tail after the cap; cleared once its queue is empty, a claimed entry included); `sayWakeWaiting` files only for such a conversation (the item then counts every notice waiting there); the boot's own announce ends AWAY with no item, its notices still handed over when the conversation runs again.
- THE SHOULDS FOLDED: the drain's judge (`_judgeHeldView`) that drops the owed notices settles For you (`wakeSettled`); a hand-over that may have landed ENDS the chain — never a second billed post 30 s later (the notices ride the next prompt): a local post whose frame was handed to the socket and then TIMED OUT (`phase: 'write'`, reason timeout — an EPIPE / reset cannot have landed and steps on), or a device's post whose request was SENT and never answered (the ladder's remote rung now says `unanswered` — the hub's 15 s request timeout can expire after the device posted).
- CENSUS: test-msg-cli-groups §2c — the «notices wait» item's display-name read in jobs-wiring.js is the 11th addressing-idiom site (the existing «display name only» row classifies it); my gate list had been hand-picked and missed it — now built from every fast reader of the unit's files.
- LEGS (test-notify-retry §B-6721): (g) a pending fork carrying an owed parent's id: its payload arms nothing and its strip is not the parent's, a newer owed notice while it is pending posts and bills nothing, its «Hand over» is `no_conversation` — with a registration answering under the parent's id (REDs: the raw-id lookup arms the parent's chain; the raw wake road posts and bills into it); (h) the boot's announce of a month-old notice files no item, a notice stashed while the hub runs files one counting all, and back the month-old notice is still handed over (RED: the engine without the event rule files at boot); (i) the judge's drop closes the item (RED: open with nothing waiting); (j) a write-phase timeout ends the chain after one attempt, an EPIPE steps on (RED: the timeout re-steps). The remote `unanswered` half has no leg in this rig (no device link).
- THE SHOULD OF ROUND w8g2bt5bs (the cure's take): the remote rung said `unanswered` also when NOTHING was sent — a device agent without the capability, a policy refusal, an error the device answered — and the chain then ended with a journal line saying the frame may have landed. Now only a request that LEFT and got no answer (the hub's request timeout `peer-post timeout`, a link lost `link_lost`) says so. Leg: test-agent-msg over the real ladder's remote rung and a stand-in device (timeout and lost link say it; a capability gate and a device-answered error do not; RED: the previous shape says it for all).
- THE MOVE CHECK (round w3pnpw53m): the «unanswered» leg's two «left, no reply» errors are now MADE BY THE CLIENT's OWN CODE — the real DeviceManager over the stream transport against a stand-in device on the real Mux that never answers the peer-post (the client's own bound — `peer-post timeout`) or drops the link with it pending (the client's own close path — `link_lost`); a device-answered error and a missing capability never say it; and the ways the client's request maker ends a request are a CENSUS (test-agent-msg: six roads pinned by name and count — four before the send, the answer, the bound — plus the lost link's answer site; RED: a new way to fail). Should 7: a CLAIM is not a settle — `wakeSettled` keeps «notices wait» while an owed notice is claimed (a resume's claim may come back; test-notify-retry (k) + RED). Should 1: the doc block above its own method (JobManager.sayWakeWaiting).

### bl-loop-b B-460d — what a conversation starts never outranks the hub (nice +5 on the spawn itself)
- THE HARM (measured 2026-11-12): conversations and everything they start ran at the hub's own priority; with lanes building, the hub's main thread waited 320 s for a core in 17 minutes. The owner said yes to the proposal on 2026-11-17.
- THE LAW: a LOCAL conversation and a Background Work job START at `nice -n 5` (+5 over the hub's own niceness) on the spawn itself — src/spawn/line.js `priorityArgv` before `node` in THE session line (the dtach road and the daemon pipe both run it), and before `process.execPath` in src/jobs.js's wrapper spawn. The first process is born with it and everything it starts inherits it; no set-priority call after a fork.
- THE SETTING `agents.lowerCpuPriority` (default on; the owner's yes covers it): read at each start, a running conversation keeps its priority; off = the release's spawn word for word. A machine with no nice program still starts every conversation, at the hub's priority, and the journal says so once.
- SAID ONCE where a person looks for «why is my build slower»: Session Properties' identity section, «CPU priority» beside Connection / PID — below the server (nice +5), or the server's own with the reason (off in Settings, no nice program, another machine). The fact rides the session's meta, so a restarted hub still says it.
- THE CENSUS: scripts/spawn-env-census.mjs `PRIORITY_ROADS` names each road's one place, `PRIORITY_EXCEPT` the remote readopt; test-architecture §94b. A new caller of the session line with no row is red.
- REMAINDER (named, not here): a paired machine's conversations (the device agent needs a signed release); opencode's serve-owned terminals (no fact, no row); CPU weights or a group per conversation (the separation programme's) — and with it the job's own scope: on a systemd host a job's command runs in a `systemd-run --user --scope` beside vibespace.service, where a niceness does not compete with the hub; only a weight would (said in the kb).
- DEGRADATION, a real look (this box, two busy node processes pinned to ONE core for 3 s, both under the lane's nice): the one 5 lower got 25.4 % of the core against 74.6 % (the control, the same niceness: 50 / 50).
- ADVERSARIAL READ (a fresh reader given the diff, the row and the dispatch): F1/F2 test-vault-job and test-jobs-engine cut the job wrapper's argv array by its text — kept as ONE array (spread) so both mutants still find it; F3 an OpenCode serve terminal was given the fact — none now; F4 the cgroup limit above (words corrected: «gives way» for a conversation, the job's scope named as remainder); F6 the census's exception now has a count (a second line there is red); F7 the real-process leg refuses a runner above niceness 14 (where +5 would prove nothing); F9 the job wrapper's spawn gets an 'error' listener (a late exec failure can never crash the hub); F5 the suite's row restated; F8 / F10 / F11 / F12 said in the kb.
- PINS: test-session-spawn-line ④.

### bl-browser-b — B-b56d: the person's own browsing takes over an HTTP sign-in (the owner's ruling B, 2026-11-18)
- THE FACT (Chromium source, content/browser/devtools): `Fetch.enable` refuses `handleAuthRequests` with no pattern, and a challenge reaches DevTools only on a request paused at the Request stage (`InterceptionJob::CanHandleAuth`). So the person's hook is the agent's own: DOCUMENT requests at the Request stage, each continued at once; a sub-resource is never paused.
- THE RULE (browser-dialogs `authHookOn`): the agent's watch on a standard Chrome as before; the PERSON'S watch while a live window of the person shows the browser (`personWindows`, told by the live view's `noteViewers` over every relay of theirs), or while a sign-in of that tab is held (kept until it is answered or its bound cancels it; the tab's hook is read again after Chrome has the answer); a kernel never. Agent → person with a window open keeps a held sign-in for the person's form.
- THE PERSON'S WINDOW (`personPromptStateOf` → the relay's `prompt-fact` record): `ended` (a sign-in cancelled at its bound — said, with Dismiss) and `hook` (armed, or not with why: a refused Fetch.enable, a kernel). PURE `personPromptLines` (en / zh / ja); a proxy's challenge is titled as a proxy's.
- LAW 2 (browser-stream `answerPromptFor`, the PERSON'S window only — 主开发 15:42Z: the agent's road unchanged in this unit): a window whose handshake carried a bearer never answers a sign-in (`agent_forbidden`), and the window must be this instance's own page (`pageVerdict` over its handshake, `not_your_page`). No new route, no store key, no vendor call.
- ITS ADVERSARIAL READ (2 MUST, 4 SHOULD, cured): (M1) the person's window always drives its own tab, so its keyboard handlers sent every key to the page and reclaimed the form's boxes — `ownBox` (the address row and the form's two boxes) in all four handlers (keys, paste, beforeinput, focusin), the person's window only; (M2) the heavy Cancel ran on the host Chrome had just signed in to (it sends that answer by itself) — Cancel moved to `cancel.example.test`; (S1) a held sign-in the page abandoned (its tab committed another page) is dropped without a note, and a CancelAuth Chrome refuses writes none (never «VibeSpace cancelled it»); (S2) only the person's road's own notes, within the hour (a Dismiss holds for its window: a storage key of its own would be a census row and the storage master's, not this unit's); (S3) no open watch while a window is open is said, beside the passkey line; the person's road files no For-you item; a kernel draws no standing line. Law 8's fast leg runs its fake Chrome in a worker thread (a stall of the hub's loop is the page's wait).
- THE FAST CAP, by arithmetic: test-browser-prompts restated 1.7 → 5.9 s by its measured run (the base measured 2.8 s on the test machine; nine scenes and four RED controls are this unit's); the stated sum 1249.320 → 1253.520 s over 633 fast rows ⇒ FAST_SUM_CAP_MS 1250 → 1254 s (test-ci-gate's pin with it). test-browser-passkey's measured 10.9 s is the base's own (its row says 9.2 s, from 11-12): unchanged by this unit.
- LEGS: test-browser-prompts ⑥ (the watch over the fake CDP: no hook without a window, Document-only with one, a paused request continued, the form, ProvideCredentials / CancelAuth / the bound said, the hook kept while held and dropped after the answer, a refused hook told, the X road's native sheet, the agent → person hand-over; RED ×4), test-browser-passkey (the bridge, loopback: the record's two fields, the window count, the two refusals, a second window gets nothing; RED ×1), heavy test-browser-human-ui (g) (a profile only the person browses, a stand-in site on `signin.example.test` mapped to the loopback: the form names who asks, Sign in commits, Cancel commits the 401 body, a no-challenge page loses no request, the password in no journal line or data file).
- THE CURE (主开发's TAKEN 16:59Z + 主开发's five as-if-musts 17:00Z): A SECRET IS NEVER TYPED INTO THE PAGE — `focusSink` itself keeps the caret in a box of the window's own unless the person's own press moves it (`press`: the picture, the Keyboard button, the take press), so no redraw, record or transition takes it out; the hook's state is a journal line per change («the person's sign-in hook armed / off on tab …», the heavy leg reads it, never a sleep); the mode redraw's focus guard reads `ownBox` too (a declaration now — the redraw runs before the handlers bind), so a mode record while the person types never takes the caret out of the form; the person's window names the prompt it answers (an answer with no id: `no_prompt`); only the person's own windows are counted (`viewer.person`); the bound's line is drawn beside the passkey «unknown» line too (`drawPrLines`); the note keeps the bound it was armed with; the person's window clears both boxes at send; the census names the user name too. Left: the agent's road's bearer answer (its own backlog row).

### bl-browser-b — package 2, batch 2-1: the boot's process walk (B-f64b)
- THE WITNESS: test-boot-loop-hold went red at the hotfix's gate on a packed machine — «the longest gap cpu procArgv (src/cli-identity.js) 33407 ms (held 29572)». procArgv, and its siblings procCmdline / procUid, fell through to a synchronous `ps` (2 s timeout) for every pid whose /proc read failed — every pid that exited mid-walk.
- THE CURE (1): where /proc exists (hasProcfs), a pid /proc cannot read is gone and no second program runs — Linux's ps reads the same /proc, so it could add nothing. The ps rung stays where there is no /proc (macOS / BSD). procArgv takes `execImpl` / `procRoot` seams like readPsIdentity.
- THE CURE (2): the codex liveness walk (listOpenCodexRolloutPaths) NEVER runs on the main thread. The transcript worker's codexOpenThreads op answers null on the main thread (SafeFs's inline run when no worker is alive — locate's rule); the store's call has a null fallback and keeps no null; ONE walk in flight for both roads; the sync listing reads the kept answer (a stale one starts the worker's walk); a worker that cannot answer leaves the kept answer standing ≤ 2 min, then the rows SAY it (`liveness: 'unknown'` beside status stopped, so their actions, the status filter and a workspace restore are unchanged; the card says «Stopped (still checking)», zh/ja). The sync walk (listOpenCodexThreadIds) is gone. The witness's road was the async listing's fallback: the worker missed its 15 s deadline and the walk ran inline here (the adversarial read's must).
- THE SAME LAW, proc-identity startToken: on Linux's procfs an unreadable stat is gone — no ps (that one had no timeout; opencode-serve's spawn tick and tokenVerdict on the hub); its SHIPPED TWIN in data/bin/vibespace-remote-keeper carries the same lines byte for byte (test-pid-identity).
- CENSUS: test-loop-child-census — procArgv's and startToken's rows move from DEBT to FALLBACK (the no-/proc rung), readPsIdentity's words follow (its hub callers named), DEBT_MAX 28 → 26. test-architecture's pid census and test-writer-sweep's allowlist name the new execImpl spelling; test-writer-sweep §15's no-/proc child now has no /proc at all (statSync('/proc/self') throws too), so the JS twin still takes its ps rung; the shell twin keeps its ps rung (remote only, verdicts equal — said beside it).
- LEGS (test-codex-zst ⑦), counts: 25 pids that exist nowhere — ZERO ps where /proc exists, the ps rung where it does not; ZERO /proc walks on the main thread for the sync listing (`unknown`, then `stopped`), with the worker POOL DOWN (both listings say liveness unknown) and for the op run on the main thread; ONE walk in flight (five asks, one ask of the worker). RED ×4: the base's fallthrough (one ps per gone pid), the base's inline walk, the op without its guard, no shared in-flight walk. Not pinned: the kept answer's 2 min bound (no clock seam) and startToken's guard (no spawn seam; test-pid-identity pins its twin).
- THE CURE (主开发's TAKEN, 11:47Z, two as if a must + one small): (1) NOTHING AUTOMATIC STARTS A ROW STILL BEING CHECKED — the group press (resume-pacer resumeGroup), the boot's «resume all» (layout _resumeAll) and a layout restore skip a row whose liveness is unknown and say how many; resumeSession is the backstop: unattended or bulk starts nothing, a person's own press asks «still checking» first (_askStillChecking, a method a suite answers) and only a yes starts it. PURE livenessUnknown / unknownRowOf in resume-pacer. (2) THE POOL THAT FAILED ONCE IS TRIED AGAIN: every 60 s, five tries in all, each failure said with its try. (small) startToken's ps on macOS / BSD has a 3 s timeout, in both twins. Legs in test-resume-all-paced ⑦: the pure rule; the group press and the boot's «resume all» (2 creates of 3, said); the backstop (unattended, bulk, a no, a yes). RED ×3 (the boot's: without its filter the backstop still holds the row, but the person is not told). layout-dup-world's lifecycle stub map gains unknownRowOf (the rig stubs every relative import).
- THE CURE 2 (主开发's TAKEN of the cure, 12:17Z): a PERSON who loads a layout preset is TOLD how many rows it left because they are still being checked — the boot's sentence, with «Try again» (the same preset). ### bl-keys-misc B-37f9 — the pool's ten-second gate holds every per-record kick
- THE FIND (lane bl-accounts in B-403e's first line): `_poolAutoLast` («poolId → ts of last DECISION (eval gate)», renamed so in 2.266.1 when the switch floor moved to the 180 s dwell) kept its one setter after the default SWITCH. So the 10 s gate at the top of maybePoolAutoSwitchForPool held a kick only within 10 s of a switch, and every usage record could re-decide every auto pool (kickPoolEval runs at most once per 5 s across the hub).
- THE CURE: a KICK passes `{ kick: true }` and waits 10 s after the pool's last EVALUATION: `_poolEvalAt`, stamped by every pass that gets past the pool's own guards (the ledger whole, a current member, no post-reset reading still on the way), forced or not. The kicks are kickPoolEval's callers: every usage record, and a few readings (a rate_limit_event, a reset credit's answer no person pressed, a re-read probe, the codex fresh window, a workflow tailer, the ledger's added rows). The open / closed answer is PURE: account-pool-auto `evalGateOpen({ now, last, force })`, `EVAL_GATE_MS`; open when forced, with no evaluation yet, and on a clock stepped back. A held kick is counted (`_poolGateHeld`) and arms ONE re-run per pool for the gate's opening (`_poolKickTrail`, an unref'd timer): a held kick's decision comes at the latest 10 s on, not lost — except a kick inside 10 s of a default switch, which the release's switch gate returns before the kicks' gate (as the release; the 30 s tick or the next record decides it); under steady kicks the re-run is held again and re-arms.
- Every caller that OWES its decision is as in the release: the 30 s tick, a walled turn's end, the codex cold wall, the pre-fire first decision, the ledger's catch-up (onWhole), a compaction's end (its ask goes through kickPoolEval with `{ kick: false }`: the free move window closes at the next request-out) and the six forced callers are never held by the kicks' gate. Every un-forced pass still waits 10 s after a default switch (`_poolAutoLast`, its comment now says so).
- No new synchronous read on the pass (the stamp is one Map write, the re-run one timer; each pool's re-run is its own run, its reads once per pass as before), nothing the spend guard counts, no turn added.
- What a person could notice: a switch that only a kick would trigger can land up to about 10 s after the pool's last evaluation (at the re-run). The hub-wide 5 s throttle in front of the kicks is unchanged: a kick it drops is dropped as before.
- Leg (test-pool-auto, a fresh pin world): five kicks in one moment ⇒ ONE evaluation, FOUR held (none moves the stamp), ONE re-run armed; that re-run, ten seconds on, evaluates; an un-forced pass that is not a kick, 3 s after an evaluation, evaluates; a forced pass is never held; a compaction's end 3 s after the tick asks the pool at once. PURE: closed at 9 s and 3 s, open at 10 s, when forced, with no evaluation yet, and on a clock stepped back. MUTANTS: no stamp ⇒ no kick is held (the leg winds the stamp back only when the first kick stamped); the gate on every un-forced pass (the first round's shape) ⇒ the owed pass is held; the compaction's ask as a kick ⇒ held. The compaction legs' worlds clear their re-run timers at each moved clock's end.
- THE ADVERSARIAL READS. The first round (one stamp at every evaluation gating EVERY un-forced caller) had four musts: a kick 3 s earlier held the codex cold wall's switch, so its after-switch rung spent a reset credit while another member could serve; the pre-fire first decision was held, so its probe read the member being left; a walled turn's only end pass was held; this note's claims. The second round (kicks only) had two: the PURE check «no evaluation yet» read a `now` of 5 ms as 5 ms after an evaluation at 0, and a compaction's end asked through a kick, so the tick's evaluation could hold it (about one auto-compaction in three) until the summary's request had gone out. The third round had one: the leg's own wind-back wrote the stamp the «no stamp» mutant removes, so that control could not go red. All cured above.
- THE FOLLOW-UP (主开发's reading of 2438a6df7 — TAKEN, three readers, no must). (1) An owed ask is never DROPPED by kickPoolEval's hub-wide 5 s throttle: the throttle holds kicks only, an owed ask passes it and never stamps it (a kick a moment after one meets the kicks' gate and its re-run), and a pass already scheduled but not run (a usage record in the same chunk as a compact_boundary) is made UN-KICKED by the owed ask that rides it (`_poolEvalPending`). (2) A person's reset-credit press (`userAttempt`) asks the pool as an owed ask, `kickPoolEval({ kick: false })`, after the credit landed and after its re-read probe: its re-decision is never held (the credit itself never was). (3) The armed timer runs the engine's seam `poolKickRerun`, which the leg runs too (no Node internal of the Timeout). (4) An anchor pins the kicks' stamp right after the pool's last guard, and as the only stamp (no stamp before the guards); a wiring pin holds the press's two asks. The seam `poolKickRerun` clears a live timer, so a call runs once. (5) The words name the one case a held kick's decision is not re-run: a kick inside 10 s of a default switch. Legs: a compaction's end 1 ms after a kick asks the pool; in the same chunk as a kick it makes that pass un-kicked (evaluated, not held); a kick a moment after an owed ask is held and re-run, never dropped; MUTANTS: the throttle for every ask (the release's) ⇒ dropped; a pending pass left kicked ⇒ held. test-codex-pool's reset-hold control re-spelled for the press's line. LEFT: `_poolGateHeld` is never reset outside the legs — one number per pool, read by the legs alone; no leg drives each of kickPoolEval's other callers through the gate — they share the one function and its default.
- NOT HERE (the row's step two): a stop re-decides the whole pool (S stops = S² decisions) — the stop path is forced by design (its decision is owed at that stop); it rides its own row.

### bl-keys-misc B-28b1 (the same row as B-1c04) — a Stop that reached the follow-up only after its request left is TOLD, never hidden
- THE FIND (read only, no vendor binary run): in every hosted red of test-claude-steer-chrome §A ② and ③ (int361 prep398 mirror), the request that reached the mock model after Stop carried ONLY MARK-B: the frame the CLI already held at Stop, run by the CLI as its own follow-up turn. C (a message sent after Stop) was held correctly every time. chat-wrapper already answers that follow-up's init with a second interrupt IN THE SAME TICK, the earliest fact the CLI gives; whether the CLI reads it before its request leaves (about 12 ms after the init, measured on 2.1.312) is the CLI's own race, lost on a loaded runner (settle +57..66 ms against the box's +34..41 ms). The vendor's cancel controls are inert outside -p. No wrapper wait could become a fact.
- THE RULING (主开发 2026-11-18 10:41Z): (A) TELL, DO NOT PRETEND. The wrapper marks the follow-up it interrupted on its init (`stopping.followRun`) and judges it at its result (`stopLateOf`): it still reached the model when an assistant record of that turn came before its result (a `<synthetic>` one sent nothing), or its result's OWN `usage` counts tokens — that turn's main-thread calls only, on every CLI version (recorded on 2.1.312: where a background agent ran, `usage` said 20/6 while `model_usage_since_last_result` said 30/7; the follow-up that sent nothing said 0/0). Then the fact rides the follow-up's OWN result record (`webui_stop_late: { follow, how: answered | billed, cut, tokens }`), one log line says it, and nothing is sent, held or dropped because of it (C still waits for the settle).
- THE PAGE: message-manager carries the fact onto that result's «Interrupted» row (`stopLate`), and chat-renderers adds ONE line in it, through t() (zh / ja): «The Stop arrived after the message handed in earlier had already gone to the model — it was cut off at once, and it may be billed». A follow-up that ran to its end before the interrupt was read has no «Interrupted» row: it gets the line as its own row («…it was answered before the Stop reached it, and it is billed»). Never a toast, never a For-you item; live, a second client and a reload draw the same row from the same record.
- THE LEGS (fast, test-claude-steer §8, ten runs at once): the REAL wrapper over the stand-in CLI, which gained a STALL PLACED in the window BY ORDER, never by a clock (`STAND_IN_FOLLOW_HOLD_UNTIL=request|answer|end`: no stdin line is read after a follow-up's init until its request left / its answer was said / it ended; `STAND_IN_FOLLOW_HOLD_INTERRUPTS`: until N interrupts wait), a follow-up request (`STAND_IN_FOLLOW_REQ_MS`, its result then counts tokens), an answer (`STAND_IN_FOLLOW_ANSWER_MS`) and an agent's tokens in the since-last count (`STAND_IN_FOLLOW_AGENT_TOKENS`). The request left, THEN the interrupt was read ⇒ the fact (billed, cut), told once, live = reload; the model spoke, THEN ⇒ answered; it ended, THEN ⇒ its own row; the other way (the follow-up sends no request at all; the interrupt is read first and ends it) ⇒ nothing told; an agent's tokens alone ⇒ nothing told; a second Stop during the follow-up (held by count) ⇒ still told; a 2.1.308 CLI ⇒ told from its `usage`; RED CONTROLS: a wrapper copy that never marks the follow-up ⇒ the same leaked request and a clean stop; a copy whose rebuilt window drops the mark ⇒ the second Stop loses the fact; a copy reading the since-last count ⇒ a false «billed»; plus two result shapes no recording shows, judged on the record alone (no subtype ⇒ its own row; success with is_error ⇒ once, on its error row).
- THE HEAVY LAW (test-claude-steer-chrome §A ② ③, for the integrator's runs): after a Stop EITHER no request reached the model before the stop settled, OR exactly the held frame's ONE follow-up did and the stop-late fact was recorded and drawn once; anything else is red (a second leaked request, C before the settle, a leak not told, a fact told where nothing leaked). Every run prints the count of leaked follow-ups per leg.
- NO FALSE TELL FROM AN AGENT: the tokens are the follow-up's own (`usage`, above), so a background agent's tokens never make a tell (recorded on 2.1.312; other side calls — a title, a compaction — are assumed to stay out of `usage` the same way); a leg puts an agent's tokens in the since-last count alone and nothing is told, and a RED copy that reads that count tells falsely; a `<synthetic>` assistant record is no answer. A SECOND Stop pressed while the follow-up runs rebuilds the window (dropHeldForStop) and carries the follow-up's mark, so it is still judged at its result.
- THE ADVERSARIAL READ (reads/b28b1-read.md, on f19f3fe7e) had two musts: the provisional 1.2 s pushed the fast tier's stated sum over its cap (restated at the measured 0.6 s, the sum back under 1247 s, no cap move), and a second Stop during the follow-up rebuilt the window without its mark (carried; a leg and a RED copy). Shoulds taken: the false-tell guards, wide §8 margins (a 5 s tool, a 3 s follow-up, a 2 s request on the far side: Stop ends each run early), the stand-in's token count marked ASSUMED, the stale kb / header words, a 2.1.308 leg. THE DELTA READ (reads/b28b1-read-r2.md, on 2302f733d) had one must: the second-Stop legs leaned on load (the second Stop had to reach the wrapper inside the 80 ms stall) — the stand-in now holds by COUNT (`STAND_IN_FOLLOW_HOLD_INTERRUPTS`: nothing read after the follow-up's init until both interrupts wait) and the leg checks the wrapper saw the second Stop before the result. Its shoulds: the model match and the agent guard gave way to the result's own `usage` (above); the docs no longer say «never a false tell» beyond what `usage` proves.
- THE FOLLOW-UP (主开发's reading of f330ff10d — NOT TAKEN on one must, the coordinator's own rule): the main legs proved the race with a CLOCK (the request at 12 ms, the interrupt read at 80 ms): on a loaded machine the two can swap, and a leg is red, or green for the wrong reason. The stall is now placed BY ORDER in both directions (above). Small, in the same cure: a result with no subtype (and no is_error) that carries the fact gets its own row (it drew none: a missed tell; with is_error it is the error row's); the own row stores NO words (`text` empty, `stopLate.own`: the renderer says them in the reader's language — search, an export or a preview never shows English to a zh or ja reader), and the turn-meta walk skips it by that mark on the record (no bare property); a success result with is_error says it once, on its error row. The time stall switch is gone from the stand-in. A stdin end releases every hold.
- LEFT: a request the CLI aborts before the model's first event leaves neither signal; the heavy law's mock counts it and goes red («a leak not told») if it happens — and whether the real CLI counts an aborted stream's tokens is what the integrator's §A told/shown counts will say. If both parts of a split follow-up leak, one Stop says two lines (each a request). B's own bubble keeps «Unread when stopped — goes with your next message» even when the model read it (a question to the coordinator). (B) ending the CLI process on such a Stop is the row's open option, with what must be measured first written into it.

### bl-keys-misc B-128b — test-architecture's names census walks bytes (way 2, first by 主开发's rule); one shared parse (way 1) closed by measurement, not built
- THE MEASURE (lane bl-ci's B-2c31 probe as the template: throwaway commits run alone on the test machine). WAY (1) — ONE SHARED PARSE (run 1c3bc1cf7-20261118121418-box, both acorn builds counted: the suite's own ESM import and the CommonJS one §94's spawn-env-census and §107's bundle strip require): a one-thread run makes 1 045 parses, 4.3 s — §94 1.6 s over 366 texts, §103 1.5 s over 341, §93 0.8 s over 235, §91 0.2 s, the rest under 0.1 s. Texts two sections both parse: §94 × §103 102 (at most 0.66 s if each were parsed once), §93 × §94 81 (0.38 s), §93 × §103 50 (0.19 s), the rest under 0.11 s each — under their sum, ~1.6 s of one thread, and EVERY pair parses with a different option set (one shared parse would need a superset of options, dearer per parse). At two cores the sections are claimed by whichever thread reaches them: sharing reliably means pinning §93, §94 and §103 to one thread ('main' — ~3.9 s of parse work on it, the balance lost) or parsing in the prologue (which both threads run). WAY (1): CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BUILT (the coordinator, 2026-11-18 12:28Z: under one second at two cores for half a lane-day and a pinned thread). The first round's «at most 0.26 s» counted only the ESM build — the read caught it.
- WAY (2) — THE NAMES CENSUS (public-repo hygiene, sha256 digests of forbidden names, never the names): 2 992 text files, 138.8 MB. It split the DECODED text into letter runs with a regex, a substring and a map lookup per occurrence (decode 0.33–0.40 s + census 2.57–2.82 s, one thread). It now walks each file's BYTES (an ASCII letter is one byte in UTF-8 and no byte of a multi-byte character is one, so the runs are the same): a run is keyed by a 30-bit integer mixed from a hash of its bytes and its length (no number made per run), the slot keeps the bytes of its word, and a run is that word only when every byte matches (another word under the same key takes the string road, exact as before). No decoded copy of the tree, no string per occurrence: 1.78–1.92 s, one thread — about 1.2 s less (run 3660559dd-20261118120007-box, this form). The same count in every file under stand-in digests that hit (common words: 2 966 files counted, byte-identical lists), no offender under the real list either way. test-architecture's 973 titles identical, in order, and its other 506 output lines identical (run 83e732a45, the first form of the same walk; the gate of this tip holds them). A text file between 512 MiB and 2 GiB, which the old decode could not hold as one string, is now walked. Heap not measured (a slot per distinct word, the decoded tree gone).
- A CONTROL PROVES THE BYTE CHECK: two invented words of one length under the same key (found offline; the suite proves the shared key with the same mix) — the listed one written after the other is counted, the other alone is not. Folded into the existing CONTROLS check, so the suite's titles stay byte-identical.

### bl-machines-a — B-6c46: the install launcher ends on its own proof, never on a follower's return
- THE FIX: the launcher copies the log's new bytes by offset (`tail -c +N | head -c N`, no follow mode) every 0.2 s and ends only on its own proof — the exit file exists, or the runner is proven gone (`gone`: pid + starttime) — its exit READ first in each round (a start after the runner can hand it another's only inside one round's gap, ≤ 0.2 s), then the last bytes, a wait (about 2 s at most) on the runner gone (the script never checks the lock: the kernel drops it with its last holder), and that exit. A round whose wc failed is taken again; a reader gone (SIGPIPE) ends the launcher. Chosen over «wait after the follower returns» because the stream itself also stopped early on such a box.
- THE CURE (主开发's 21:59Z «taken», five items): (1) a ZOMBIE runner is gone — `st` reads the state field with the starttime; `gone` answers yes for state Z (a container whose pid 1 never reaps kept a killed runner's entry and starttime for ever, so a re-attached follower never ended, 30–40 short processes a second), `live` answers no; then 199, the true word — and the install facts too (its read's HIGH; this machine at once, a remote machine with its agent's next release — its agent reads its slot): src/cli-identity.js parseProcSample carries the stat line's `state`, and src/desktop-display.js installState calls a zombie no running install (it had sent every press to FOLLOW, 199 each time, no new install ever started); leg ⑥b: while the zombie stands, installState says none and a START runs its own install (RED CONTROL: live() without its zombie case follows it, 199); (2) leg ⑤, the 199 road: the runner killed mid-install, nothing recorded ⇒ 199, its line once, no reply before the kill; leg ⑥ + control, a zombie stand-in (a subshell whose parent execs `sleep`); (3) a skip (no Linux /proc, setsid or flock) is «SKIPPED (1 skipped, 0 passed — a skip is never green)», exit 2, as the browser suites end — never ALL PASS (0); on the fast tier that is a red (every ci host has Linux and util-linux); (4) one check at the launcher's top: a `sleep` that refuses a fraction ⇒ 125 by name, nothing run (leg ⑧; test-desktop-serve's poll counter skips that one call, its argument read from the module); (5) leg ⑦ + control, the reader gone (SIGPIPE ⇒ 141, the install untouched); the words: the wait is on the runner, never the lock; the cost a round as a number (6 processes, 8 with new bytes, under dash); head's errors off the card.

### boot-helper, the helper's round two (主开发 2026-11-17 05:48Z: piece 1 TAKEN at 7b3ef0a29; before batch 1's line, in its own commit)
- **A suite ended by a signal still dies BY that signal.** The armed handler ran the end and exited 143 / 130 / 129 — but ci.mjs `killedFromOutside` tells «killed from outside» from a product red by the SIGNAL, so every heavy suite on the helper that the gate's budget or a stale lock ended would have read as a red. Now it runs the same end the exit runs (every 'exit' listener), removes that signal's listeners and raises the same signal on its own process. Legs: SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP, each driven into a child suite whose parent reads the signal; red control: the exit-code form (the parent reads code 143, no signal).
- **The end never hangs on a process stuck on the network mount.** The selection read the environ of every process of the user; a process in an uninterruptible wait holds the memory lock that read waits on. Now the cheap facts come first — the owner (another user's process is never read) and the state from the stat file — and a process in state D is not read: the next pass looks again, and one still in D is said and left. Legs on a fake /proc (no read of its environ, cwd or argv is made — recorded); red control: the copy that reads it.

### bl-machines-b — B-b1f7: the fleet chart's probes — a startup probe for the boot, liveness over ten minutes (the owner's decision 2026-11-18)
- THE GAP: deploy/helm/vibespace-user/templates/main.yaml had no startup probe. Its liveness (GET /login, a 60 s delay, then a kill at the 10th failure in a row, (10 − 1) × 30 s = 270 s after the first) killed a hub alive but held for minutes, and a kill restarts the container and ends every conversation in the pod (2026-11-16: six kills in 36 minutes).
- THE FIX (tree only — NOTHING APPLIED: no kubectl, no helm against a cluster; it rides the next fleet update with the owner's word): three probes, all GET /login on 3456, whole seconds in values.yaml `probes.*` with the same defaults in the template (a `--reuse-values` upgrade from an older release carries no probes block). A probe flips at its failureThreshold-th failure in a row, (failureThreshold − 1) × periodSeconds after its first: startup (91 − 1) × 10 s = 900 s from the container's start (a boot resuming ~80 conversations held /login ~4 min, B-cd4b); readiness (3 − 1) × 10 s = 20 s — a held hub LEAVES the load balancer and comes back at its first answer, never killed (unchanged but for its 10 s initial delay, which the startup probe replaces); liveness (31 − 1) × 30 s = 900 s of continuous failure before a kill, no initial delay, never shorter than the startup budget (a hub that restarts itself inside the container — an update, a crash — boots under liveness alone). The render REFUSES a startup or a liveness window of 600 s or less and a liveness under the startup budget. The arithmetic is stated beside the probes and in values.yaml; deploy/README.md's rollout section says what the dry-run diff now shows.
- LEGS (heavy test-helm-render, section R): the default render's three probes, their keys, timeouts and seconds; the chart's and values.yaml's comments state the render's arithmetic; `probes=null` renders the same; the refusals (270 s, exactly 600 s, a 50 s startup, a liveness under the startup budget) named with their arithmetic, and just over the edges renders; all nine numbers by values, each to its line; three probes, each once. CONTROLS (chart copies): no startup probe; the liveness block as it was; the refusals removed; the comment out of step. The older charts' byte legs read R's block as one more stated difference (noProbes, the block's exact shape, puts back what every older chart rendered).

### bl-browser-a — the idle paint stop never freezes a page under a running verb (an agent's feedback, 2026-11-18)
- THE SCENE: a NEW profile's first open of a large web app left the tab busy about two minutes, and the person saw a crashed page. Opening the same site's sign-in page again recovered it at once.
- THE CAUSE (read, then PLACED):
  - The keeper's idle-paint sweep freezes every tab of a browser on an unseen rung after 30 s with no viewer and no verb (src/browser-idle.js idlePaintVerdict).
  - «No verb» was counted from a verb's START: the watch stamped lastVerbAt only in verbStarted.
  - Its paintFacts' `busy` counted an open dialog, a navigation in flight and a thaw, never a verb STILL RUNNING. So an agent's `open` still waiting 30 s after it started, on a page whose main frame had loaded, had its page frozen under it: JS and timers stopped, the app never settled, and the verb waited out its own timeout.
  - The next verb's thaw (at its /resolve) recovered it at once: the reported recovery.
- THE CURE (src/server/browser-dialogs.js):
  - paintFacts' `busy` counts a verb of ANY holder still running on that browser (the watch's own running map: verbRunningOn, bounded by VERB_RUNNING_MAX_MS for a crashed CLI's /resolve with no audit).
  - verbEnded restarts the idle clock (lastVerbAt), so a long verb's end never reads as long idle.
- THE LEG (fast test-browser-tabs ③d), the race PLACED over the real watch on a stand-in browser, on the leg's own clock:
  - a verb still running 31 s after it started, on a loaded page: the real verdict reads «busy», never «freeze»;
  - 10 s after its end, «recent»; the idle bound after its end, it stops drawing;
  - a crashed CLI's verb holds the stop off no longer than the watch's 5-minute bound.
  - CONTROLS, each RED: the release's `busy` (the page frozen under the agent's own verb); a clock stamped only at a verb's start (frozen 10 s after a long verb ended).
- NOT BUILT: a word on the Browser panel for «stopped drawing» (today only the journal says it). The row carries no paint fact: a new row field, its words in three languages and the view. That is more than one line.

The wait is journaled (`waits for its previous kernel to be put back`), never counted as the card's «waiting for the new kernel to land».

Shoulds taken: an ask that spent its bound on a landing that only deletes (r5: it goes on) gets ONE fresh bound for a put-back (`freshAsk`, never more than two bounds — before: «being put back» said at once for a put-back finding nothing); the keeper's first-use road refuses a start by the step-aside's own name (never «kernel missing» + a For-you item); the route answers engine_kernel_landing 409 (was 500). The scene grows variants — the waiting kernel asked after the first stepped aside, the boot first, a fleet download first — with CONTROLS for the boot's / the download's own put-back unbounded (⇒ it hangs). The «landing beside a put-back ⇒ the start hangs» control was dropped at the gate: in the scene the start's landNext declines before landing even without placeBusy's put-back line, so that line is a BELT, unproven by a red (said so). ### dial-bridge-credit (主开发 2026-11-17 — a master defect the separation's skeptic confirmed on the release) — the dial bridge follows credit both ways
- src/dial-session-bridge.js stands between a dialled device's link and one session's attach client. The hub credited the device as it DELIVERED the session's output (client.js credits every channel not under manual credit) while the bridge threw away the attach link's answer, so a stalled attach client made the HUB hold the session's whole output and a reattach replay; the input road credited the attach client at once whatever the device link took. Now the device session runs under MANUAL credit (client.js openSession / openPipeSession `manualCredit`, opt-in, with `handle.credit(n)` and `handle.onWritable`; `handle.write` takes bytes as bytes): output is credited to the device only for what the attach side took, input to the attach side only for what the device link took. The hub holds at most about one window each way; what a stalled reader leaves unsent now sits on the DEVICE AGENT's side of its link — its senders queue, they do not pause (that row and the attach program's own hold are parked by 主开发).
- The acceptance's two musts (take-after-fixes): THE GAP — bytes the device sends right behind its open answer (a reattach replay rides the same read) are kept until the open has gone to the attach side, then pass through the same accounting (they were dropped on the release, and the reviewed tip left them uncredited — a window lost for good); THE ORPHAN — when the attach side dies, a pipe session's device channel (still open, the keeper model) goes back to the release's road: what is owed is credited at once and every later byte as it arrives. An attach that dies while the open is asked: a pipe handle is an orphan from the start, a live pty is ended. Input passes as bytes (a character split across two frames stays whole).
- scripts/test-dial-bridge-credit.mjs (FAST, 1.5 s): the REAL DeviceManager over an in-memory device link that delivers each turn's writes as one read, the REAL bridge on loopback, NUMBERED chunks (content, order, exact counts), a stall placed in the reader: output and input each hold exactly one window (262 144 B); the open and a whole window in one read all arrive and are all credited; an attach closed in mid-stall leaves nothing at the device and a new attach reads its own chunks; the terminal road the same; a client that did not opt in credits as the release does. RED CONTROLS: the release's two roads (1 048 576 B credited), the gap as reviewed (the window lost), no orphan road (524 288 B stuck at the device).

- **The decision:** channel content (heads, bodies, attachments) stays PLAIN at rest, as transcripts and the search index are; only each account's sign-in token and app secret are sealed under the vault's channels key. The documents now say so (docs/kb-design-lessons.md «What the vault seals — and what stays plain at rest», docs/kb-features.md's channels section, the three user changelogs).
- **The accident closed:** the store set NO mode on its index and message logs (the process default, 0644 under a 022 umask), while its attachments, people and memos were already 0700 / 0600. src/channel-store.js now makes every folder 0o700 (msgs, archive, a conversation's log folder, its side folder), writes the index and the acts journal through the store writer with `mode: 0o600`, and opens a new log 'a+' with 0o600. A log rewritten whole (a prepend, a trim, a rewrite) and the other side files (the outbox, groups, aliases, the pace and dispatch files, the poll stamps, the audit) keep the process default, as on the base: the root's 0700 is what closes them.
- **An existing store, without a walk:** at the open, ONE asynchronous `stat` + `chmod` of the ROOT to `mode & 0o700`, never awaited and never a walk (some 200 000 conversation files). The root's 0700 closes everything under it; an existing log keeps its bits. The chmod only TAKES bits away: a read-only root stays read-only (0555 → 0500), so the store's BLOCKED rung (test-channel-store §r3, which makes the root 0555) still holds. An already-closed root gets no chmod. A refusal (EPERM, a filesystem without modes) is one log line; the store opens normally. `store.rootClosed` is that promise.
- **Pins:** NEW fast suite scripts/test-channel-store-modes.mjs (12 legs, 115 ms): a fresh store 0700 / 0600; an existing 0755 root closed by the root alone, its fs calls counted against the base's own open; bits only taken away; a refusing filesystem; red control = the base's copy (0755 / 0644). test-channel-store holds the store's laws but is heavy-tiered (12.9 s), so the fast legs have their own suite. ### bl-machines-b — the device agent's watches never end it (主开发 2026-11-19, found by the readers of the hub's watch hotfix)
- THE GAP: src/agentd/agentd.js armed fs.watch on the projects / sessions folders (recursive, with a non-recursive fallback) inside a try, but the watcher it kept had NO 'error' listener. On Linux a recursive watch adds one watch per new subfolder, so at the machine's limit of file watches the failure arrives LATER as the watcher's own 'error' event — and an 'error' with no listener ends the process: the device agent could end the way the hub did.
- THE FIX: NEW src/agentd/watch-guard.js (DEVICE; fs, log and the timers injected, no import). armWatch puts the listener on the watcher at once. A LOST watch (an error after arming; refused at arming for any cause but a missing folder; a recursive watch refused for any cause but «not on this platform», whose plain fallback sees the top folder only) is closed and dropped, and its feature FALLS BACK TO A SWEEP: its own kick every 60 s (discovery pushes discovery-dirty — the hub re-snapshots when a page is open and harvests usage; the usage feed walks), said ONCE per feature in the agent's log. The hub has no sweep of its own for these pushes (its page list refreshes on the push or ⟳; its usage dirty-kick rides the discovery push), so without this a lost watch meant silence for the link's life. endWatches ends a feature at the link's end: no word, no sweep, a late error (a recursive walk still in flight) silent. Both feeds (discovery-watch, usage-events-watch) arm through it; agentd.js arms no fs.watch of its own. The hub's src/watch-door.js does not ride the bundle: a plain listener is enough.
- THE SWEEP'S COST, said: ONLY on a device that lost a watch, every 60 s while its link lives, changes or not — a device snapshot and a usage harvest on the hub (the discovery-dirty road), and the usage feed's own walk; walks never overlap (st.running / st.again serialise them). That is the price of not going silent, on the machines that hit the watch limit.

### bl-accounts B-f4a1 — a stop re-decides only its own conversation (the owner's word 2026-11-18 14:48 PT)
- **The harm (B-403e's first line, from the production hub's witness):** every stop of a pooled conversation (noteTurnEnd, noteTurnStopped → maybePoolAutoSwitch {stop}) ran the WHOLE pool pass, so S conversations' stops cost S² decisions, each a full one.
- **The law:** a stop passes `only` (its own conversation). The per-session pass decides that conversation alone; the pool's default decision runs only when it follows the default (no link of its own) — its decision IS the default's. The decision itself is unchanged: it reads through the same decision door as the pass (one ask per file per run, src/run-reads.js; 主开发 01:20Z (a) — readings held in memory are a unit of their own).
- **Every other road keeps the whole pool:** the forced pass (the new-member wake, a login, a released reset hold, a basis flip, the pre-fire re-decision, a member removed), the 30 s tick, a per-record kick, the routes (an unplaced pool, a priority change). The pool's basis is still read over every conversation (its compared ids are the pool's fact).
- **Counted:** `_poolDecisions` (poolId → { session, pool }), a seam beside the gates. scripts/test-pool-stop-own: S stops ⇒ S decisions (the release's form, a copy built through anchored(): S²); a follower's stop is the default's one decision, as the release; the forced pass, the tick and a kick decide all S + the default; a stop moves its own walled conversation while another waits for its own stop or the tick; one stand-in day of twelve hours through the release and this unit — the same refusals (conversation, reason), the same blocked notices, the same placements at every hour's end.
- **The cure (round wpch21jqz, one MUST + seven smalls):** a stop's one-conversation run reads the basis as any other reader (`pass: !only`), so a flip it finds goes to redecideOnBasis — a forced WHOLE pass in the next turn decides every conversation and the default on the new basis (the release decided them in that run; before the cure the flip was said and stored, and nobody decided it until the un-forced tick). A stop's run no longer stamps the kicks' gate (`_poolEvalAt`): only whole runs are bounded by the gate and the tick. New legs: ⑥ a planted flip + one stop ⇒ the next turn decides all S + the default (RED: the flag back to true ⇒ one decision); ⑦ a kick right after a stop decides the whole pool (RED: the stamp kept ⇒ the kick held); ⑧ maybePoolAutoSwitch without stop (the pre-fire gate's forced call) ⇒ S + 1 (RED: `only` without the stop condition ⇒ 1); ② a mixed pool (own links and followers) pinned; ⑤ the refusals compared hour by hour, the notices non-empty. The kb says the delay by design (kb-features, the engine's essay).

### bl-proposals B-b0e3 — a Doc window's comment reaches the conversation it was opened from (two writers)
- THE HARM: src/server/doc-engine.js ownerOf took the registry's NEWEST holder of {host, path} before the window's own `from`. When two conversations wrote the same markdown file, a comment or a save made in a window opened from the OLDER one's card went to the newer one; the conversation it was about never heard it.
- THE CURE: `ownerOf({host, path, prefer})` (src/server/artifact-registry.js, PURE src/artifacts.js ownerOfIn) answers `prefer`'s conversation when ITS registry holds the path, else the newest holder as before. The doc engine hands the window's `from` as `prefer`, so its comments are typed into that conversation and its save touches that conversation's row.
- UNCHANGED: no `from`, or a `from` holding nothing ⇒ the newest holder; a window with no registry row ⇒ the `from` chat, then a stopped owner's memo (B-b51a).
- LEFT (said): a window whose own conversation has STOPPED while another live one holds the file reaches the live holder. The stopped owner's memo cannot tell whether the stopped `from` wrote this document.
- Gate: test-doc-model §6, the two-writer check over the REAL registry, the pure pick, and two RED controls (the engine without `prefer`, the pick without it), each proving its plant first.

### bl-loop-b B-7f18 — a vault run's command runs below the hub too (B-460d's follow-up)
- THE ROAD: src/server/vault-run-door.js spawned every `vibespace-vault run` command an agent asks for at the hub's own CPU priority.

The spawn itself stays the release's, byte for byte. A `nice` in front, as the conversation line has, would be one more program holding the minted env with none of the door's ownership checks; it cannot keep the argv[0] the agent typed (a multi-call program dispatches on it); and a failed exec would come back as a run that ran, its grant spent.

A refused set (a security module) leaves the run as it is. No nice program ⇒ priorityFor says none ⇒ the run is not lowered; the one journal line now names vault runs too.
