### bl-tests-e B-287c — an anchor helper «fails by name» only through a throw or check ABOUT its anchor (base 500911fd9)
- THE ROW (lg-leak-census batch 2-1's reader): scripts/mutant-copy.mjs anchorHelpers counted a helper as failing by name when its body held ANY throw or ANY ok / check / assert / expect call — an unrelated one (a missing file, `ok(true, 'loaded')`) let a helper that answers null when its anchor moves pass the census.
- THE RULE: a throw counts only when it stands under an `if` / `?:` / `&&` / `||` whose test is the anchor's edit or test; a check counts the same way, or when what it JUDGES — its first argument that is not a message (a string, a template, a string concatenation: `ok(name, cond)` and `ok(cond, name)` alike) — is one. The evidence = the anchor's edit call, a chain off it (`.join(to)`, `.length`), a test of the anchor (`src.includes(from)`, `from.test(src)`), a comparison of one, or a variable whose value is one (`const m = src.replace(from, to)` ⇒ `ok(m !== src, …)` — the form the row feared to lose); never a value merely HANDED an edit (`MUT.write(…, src.replace(from, to))`). A message naming the anchor tests nothing. anchored() stays the door.
- MEASURED (three probes of test-suite-files-parse on the test machine, the old walk beside the new over every script, each rule draft): NO helper moves — 40 in 22 files before and after; scripts/fixtures/anchor-helpers.json keeps its counts (its `//` words now say the rule). ### lg-rewind B-bba6 — the Antigravity wrapper says agy's last stderr words and a replaced process's late error
- THE HARM (found by lane bl-tests-a's reader, confirmed by two more): data/bin/agy-wrapper.js drained agy's stderr only on a newline and its exit handler never flushed the rest — an error, sign-in or soft-deny line agy writes LAST with no newline was said nowhere; and a late AGY_ERROR line (stderr lags stdout) of a process being REPLACED after its turn (a model or mode switch made during the turn, applied at its end) was only logged: the turn failed, its error notice never reached the chat.
- THE LAST WORDS: the pipe's end flushes what is left through handleStderr; the exit waits for that end (Node may emit 'exit' first) at most ERR_TAIL_MS = 500 (a grandchild of agy can hold the pipe). From a process's own exit on, nothing starts another (`childEnding` — a switch pending at a crash used to spawn a second agy just before the wrapper's exit). A sign-in head said last decides the exit's words (the sign-in notice, exit 1, no «Antigravity exited»); a soft-deny line said last is a notice naming the skip, never a card whose «allow and retry» would need the ended process. A write to a process already gone (EPIPE) is logged by a stdin error listener, never a crash.

### bl-loop-b B-f494 — a lowered job's cgroup scope weighs less (B-460d's follow-up)
- THE HOLE: a Background Work job on the cgroup rung runs in its own `systemd-run --user --scope`, a cgroup BESIDE the hub's service. Between two cgroups only CPU weights compete, so the job's `nice -n 5` held only inside its own scope: against the hub it weighed the default 100, the same as the hub.
- THE WEIGHT: a job started LOWERED carries `spec.cpuWeight` 33 — nice +5 weighs 335 of nice 0's 1024 in the kernel's table, ⇒ 33 of systemd's default 100. src/jobs.js reads the start's priority ONCE, before the spec's file is opened. data/bin/job-wrapper.js's PURE `cpuWeightArgs` adds `-p CPUWeight=33` to the scope only for a whole weight 1–10000 the server sent AND cpu ENABLED among the scope's siblings — `siblingsSubtreeOf` reads the cgroup.subtree_control of its parent (app.slice under the user manager, or the manager's own group where there is none); available only, or unreadable ⇒ nothing (the scope as before). The setting off ⇒ no weight.
- THE LAW (主开发 04:23Z): the unit never switches per-unit CPU scheduling ON where it was off. Where cpu is only available, the siblings share one group and the job's nice already competes with the hub — no hole; the first weight asked would make systemd split every sibling (the hub's unit one group of 100 against each browser scope's 100), a topology nobody measured. Measured read-only on a production hub: the manager's cgroup.controllers and app.slice's cgroup.subtree_control both hold cpu, the hub's unit has a cpu.weight — there the weight is asked.
- PINS: test-session-spawn-line (the spec carries 33 lowered and none when off; a RED CONTROL through mutant-copy + anchored()), test-jobs-memory (cpuWeightArgs' rows — enabled, available only, unreadable, the range's edges — `siblingsSubtreeOf` over a fake tree, the spread and the read in the scope argv), test-jobs-memory-scopes ①b HEAVY (PROVE: ONE lowered job on the real cgroup rung, its scope's CPUWeight read back off the user manager and its cpu.weight off the kernel — 33; an unlowered job beside it asks none; skipped by name where cpu is not enabled among the siblings).
- SAID: the weight is per scope, so four lowered jobs at once weigh 132 against the hub's 100 (as nice +5 adds up per thread too) — a shared jobs slice would bound them together; a hub started outside the user service (./run.sh from a login shell) is not a sibling of the scopes, and the weight does nothing against it.

### bl-scratch — B-3767: the hub's temp folders are its own (with its owed list)

- THE FIND (the second test machine's proof run, 2026-11-18): test-plugin-trust and test-chat-attachments failed with EACCES on /tmp/vibespace-plugin-uploads and /tmp/claude-webui-uploads, which another user's hub already owned there; test-raw-filename ⑨ hung to its 600 s deadline on the same folder (its bare router answered nothing when multer failed). The product made FIVE fixed machine-wide names under the temp folder: the chat uploads' multer dest, the plugin .vsp multer dest, the client's «open in editor» folder /tmp/claude-webui, the window CLI's default shot folder <tmp>/vibespace-window, and run.sh's log /tmp/vs-server.log (a second user's supervisor could not open it and respawned for ever). Its neighbours in the shared root: the paste file and the browser CLI's default screenshot (both readable by every user), and the Ctrl+G helper's per-pid signal file (a reused pid met an old signal and Ctrl+G returned at once).
- THE CURE: src/server/hub-tmp.js — every folder the hub makes there is <tmp>/vibespace-<uid>-<8 hex of the data folder>/<purpose>, made 0700 and judged before use by sock-path's own socketDirVerdict (a directory, not a link, this uid's, no group/other bits); a refusal says the path and why, and it reaches the PERSON: the upload's own error in the page (the chat's and the file explorer's toast now carry the server's reason when nothing landed). Both multer dests and the paste file go through it, and the upload routes answer a refusal by name instead of hanging. A name another user planted on purpose is refused, not worked around (guard against mistakes, not a deliberate act; two users' hubs never meet a name, the uid is in it). «Open in editor» asks the hub (POST /api/file/temp answers the path it wrote); its failure reaches the person (it was silent). The window CLI's default folder is per user (vibespace-window-<uid>; its refusal of a folder that is not private stays); the browser CLI's default screenshot moved into vibespace-browser-<uid> (0700, refused by name when not private); run.sh's log is vs-server-<uid>.log; the Ctrl+G signal file (the generated helper and the shipped editor-helper.sh) takes a fresh mktemp name.
- WHAT A PERSON HAS STAYS REACHABLE: nothing moves. The multer folders held nothing a person keeps (each upload is copied or moved to its place and unlinked in the same request; the agent is handed the final path). An old editor file or window shot is read in place (its old path keeps resolving; the old folder is never touched — a folder another user owns is never moved or chmodded).
- WHO READS THOSE PATHS: the upload handler alone (placeFile / SafeFs copy / remote write, then unlink); plugin-install's install({ file }); the client's editor window (through /api/file/read; a temp editor is never saved in the layout); a window shot's path, printed to the agent (its transcript, its own Read); the paste file (the agent, and the 24 h sweep).
- THE CENSUS, a red test: test-architecture §110 — every product line naming the temp folder, the shell the product ships included, wherever the path starts (93 rows with unit 2's sweep: per-data 4, per-user 17, unique 16, system 2, read 26, words 22, by-hand 6 — the five wrappers' no-buffer log fallbacks); a new line is red until it is a row, a stale row is red; the release's two upload lines are its red control. Known narrow: a fixed name joined through a parameter is seen only where the parameter's default names the folder. (vs-cm-<uid> and vibespace-zst-<uid> were owed here; unit 2 judges them.) Legs: test-raw-filename ⑩ (the temp lands in the hub's own 0700 folder; a linked folder is the upload's answer by name; POST /api/file/temp writes into the editor folder and answers the path, refuses a name that is not plain and a folder it cannot use; the verdict refuses another user's folder, one open to others at 0777 or 0755, and a file; two data folders and two users never share; the client asks the hub and spells no /tmp folder), ⑨'s upload gets a 15 s bound that ends by name. test-browser-tmpdir ④ made the browser maker's RAM fallback root (<tmp>/vibespace-<uid>/browser-tmp) for real under the shared temp folder and left it; that one call now runs with the suite's own scratch as its temp folder (主开发 06:54Z, a name the second test machine found left behind).
- B-3767 follow-up (the readers, 主开发 11:37Z): a refusal of the hub's own temp folder names the way out (remove that folder if this hub did not make it, or start the hub with TMPDIR set to a private folder) — in the upload's and the editor's answers and the browser CLI's [shot_dir_unsafe]; §110 COUNTS each row's lines (one by default, a fifth field past one), so a second line carrying an existing row's words is red (its control plants one of files.js's lines twice); the paste is written off the loop (the sync-fs census row retires); the Ctrl+G signal name is never empty (a fallback when mktemp fails).
- B-3767 unit 2 (主开发 11:40Z, the owed list): the two per-user folders that had no ownership verdict are judged before use by sock-path's ensureSocketDir (0700; a folder, not a link, this uid's, no group/other bits) — the codex zst cache (src/adapters/codex.js) refuses a planted name with EZSTCACHE by name and the way out and writes no twin through it; the ssh control folder (src/hosts.js vs-cm-<uid>) turns connection sharing OFF (no ControlPath into it), said once with the path and the way out, and judged again at each ask while refused (its removal brings sharing back, no restart; the probe no longer names a false cause with sharing off). The way out leads with restarting under a private TMPDIR: in a shared, sticky temp folder only the owner or root can remove a planted folder. Legs in test-codex-zst ⑦ with the release's mkdir-in-a-catch as RED controls; the sync-fs census row of HostManager's constructor retires (its one sync call moved into ensureSocketDir).
- B-3767 unit 2, the sweep (B-4371): src/server/hub-tmp.js sweepHubTmp — the tree's age sweep over the hub's OWN temp root: the root and each purpose it makes (uploads, editor, paste, plugin-uploads) are judged first (a folder not ours is skipped and said, never entered); in them a plain file or a link (removed as a link, never followed) older than 24 h goes; never a name pattern over the shared temp folder. The upload, temp-file and paste routes ask it, at most once in 10 min, never awaited; the paste sweep keeps only its legacy leg (B-5527 retires it). Leg in test-raw-filename ⑩ with the sweep-without-judgment as its RED control (it deletes through a planted link); §110 + §86 rows.

### think-tools-phone — a control never covers the words it serves: a block's tools are its own row; a Thinking block has ONE Copy beside its title — its one cost, by design: a row reserved above every desktop code block (~28 px, shown on hover, blank otherwise) (the owner 2026-11-07 17:56 PT, from a phone: «这个换行和复制按钮挡住了字，并且隐藏不掉。»)
- **Measured on the base first (f5e087bb5; headless Chrome, a 360-px touch phone in zh, then a 1280-px desktop with the mouse over each block in turn; a fixture of the owner's thinking word for word, a long thinking, a js and an html fence, a Bash call, two Reads, an Edit).** Every kind's toolbar lay over its own first lines: 2–16 words under the buttons (the owner's thinking 5, a Read file 16), and under the desktop's hover 7 of 9 kinds too; the buttons 30 × 24 px with 9-px words beside 16-px prose. Words = `\S+` ranges clipped to the block's visible box (a pre-wrap line box carries its hanging space). One detail of the brief's mechanism differed: the always-shown rule is chat.css's `@media (hover: none)` block, not the shared phone block (the phone block carries the sizes now).
- **LAW 1 — decided by measure: the row, on every device.** `addWrapToggles` makes the toolbar the wrapper's FIRST child: a block-level flex row, right-aligned, above the block and outside its scroller; chat.css drops the `position: absolute` overlay. A desktop keeps its hover fade, the row reserved whether it shows or not. The overlay could not be kept on the desktop: on a scroller it covers whatever line scrolls under it (the base, a fence scrolled sideways to its end: code under the corner). Cost: a desktop code block is ~28 px taller.
- **LAW 2 — ONE per-kind table, `preToolsOf(block)` (chat-renderers.js, exported, PURE over the block's classes and ancestors).** file = picker (+ Preview on html / xml) + Copy + Wrap; diff and code (a fence, a tool's input / output / error) = Copy + Wrap; PROSE = Copy only — `PROSE_PRE`, the blocks chat.css draws pre-wrap: `.chat-system-notification pre` (a hook's output, VibeSpace's note to the assistant, the CLI's details, a wake-up's details), `pre.chat-pre-wrapped` at birth (a machine card's command / output), the call stopped while it ran, a permission's / a helper ask's command; a Thinking block = ONE Copy in its `<summary>` beside a `.chat-thinking-label` span, shown while open (chat-view's streaming frame rewrites the label alone — `textContent` on the summary would have taken the door). The base's Wrap on a born-wrapped block UNWRAPPED it while its label still read «Wrap».
- **LAW 3.** In the shared phone block (`(max-width: 768px), (pointer: coarse) and (max-width: 1023px)`): the toolbar's buttons, the language picker and the thinking door ≥ 44 × 44 px with 14-px words (13 in round 2; the recovery's reader asked the For-you floor, 14) — measured 52 × 44 at 360. The row and the door are user-select none (in the flow, a selection across a block would otherwise carry «Copy Wrap»).
- **LAW 4.** Copy (a diff keeps its +/- prefixes, a file drops its gutter), Wrap (`chat-pre-wrapped` + Wrap ⇄ No Wrap), Preview and the picker unchanged. The exit-runs dialog's own Wrap is a header button, never an overlay — untouched; a diagram card's toolbar is not a pre — untouched.
- **Pins.** NEW fast test-chat-pre-tools (0.46 s; the real renderer bundled over a fake DOM, each kind through its own render path + addWrapToggles: the census, the row before its block, the label / door, law-4 copies and the toggle, PROSE_PRE ⇔ chat.css pre-wrap, theme vars only, the 44 px rule in the shared phone block; RED controls on the same bundle text). RED on the base: 22 checks by name. test-mobile-select ⑩ (heavy): at 360 px and under a desktop mouse, no shown tool covers a word, at rest and scrolled sideways; the thinking's one door; 44 px / 12 px; its Copy tapped = the whole thinking. RED on the base: the 7 ⑩ checks by name, ①–⑨ unchanged. Wall alone on the box 26.5 → 34 s.
- **The fast cap** is not this lane's: master's 1066 s (int397, by arithmetic) stands, and the train sets it by measure at its cut (test-chat-pre-tools adds a 0.46-s row). Ported 2026-11-13 by alignment from f7d7fd76f (written on .386 for .387, delivered into the 11-08 thermal hold, never judged). Master's test-still-press ⑤ (since .390: a heavy suite's direct coordinate presses are a ratchet) counted ⑩'s two new sites: T2's desktop click now goes through THE still door (stillPresser), and the person leg's finger drag rides the suite's one touch-press site (touchPress gained a path) — test-mobile-select stays at its ledger's 4.
- **Round 2 (the r1 acceptance: the laws held by render; the tap leg was red 7 of 8 on that box).**
  - **T1 — what moved the list: the chat's RESUME re-tail, armed by the suite's own other pages; a finger is never moved (measured: a writer log on the drawn view — every scrollTop write with its caller, every scroll event, the pin's changes).** ⑧'s desktop and ⑨'s tablet pages open the same session on the same hub; the hub's window sync reaches the phone page during ⑩, where `_createRemoteWindow` focuses the remote window and then the phone's own — on the narrow layout a 4-ms `setHidden('mobile')` on → off of the chat, which arms its resume (re-tail rungs at 1.24 and 2 s; for 2.8 s an input-less scroll away from the tail is displacement — `unpinSkipResume` → the tail). r1's leg brought the door into view with `scrollIntoView` (input-less) ~2 s into it: the list went back to its tail within a frame (the door 267 → −300 px) and the synthetic tap's click hit the pre. Inside a resume armed the same way, a finger drag is positioning (`_cancelForcedScroll('touch')`, the settle ends, the rungs return early): a tap right after it copied 3 of 3 and the door stayed put past both rungs. No product change — it was the leg's synthetic sequence.
  - **The leg** waits for the door to SETTLE (its rect equal over 2 frames and 300 ms without a scroll; scrolled again, at most every 250 ms, if a re-tail took it off screen) and asserts its rect did not move between the touchstart and the click. A new leg pins the person: the resume armed through the view's own `setHidden` (the control: an input-less scroll there IS re-tailed), then a finger drag held still before lifting (no fling), then a tap as the list stops ⇒ the whole thinking copied, the door unmoved past both rungs. A tap on the summary's label folds the block, a tap on its door never does — Chrome's activation target is the button, so a door without preventDefault stays open too (measured); test-chat-pre-tools ③ pins the handler's preventDefault + stopPropagation.
  - **T2 — `.chat-code-toolbar:focus-within` → `.chat-code-toolbar:has(:focus-visible)`.** A mouse click focuses the button, so r1's rule kept a clicked block's row shown after the mouse left (the base's hover fade changed). Keyboard focus still shows the row; an open language list's search field is :focus-visible by its kind, so the row stays while the list is open. Pinned by test-chat-pre-tools ④ (the rules that show a row or the door use :focus-visible only) and test-mobile-select ⑩ (the desktop: a mouse click on Copy, the mouse away ⇒ opacity 0; a Tab ⇒ 1). Headless reports `(hover: none)` on the desktop page, so the leg turns that one chat.css block off for its clicks and back.
  - **RED on 2dc2df38c (r1):** test-mobile-select 1 FAILED (49 passed) — «desktop: a mouse click on «Copy» focuses it, and its row FADES once the mouse leaves (opacity 1)…»; test-chat-pre-tools 1 FAILED (47 passed) — «the row and the door show on KEYBOARD focus only (:focus-visible)…». The tap legs pass there, as they should: the product did not change.
  - **Walls, measured under the thermal cap:** test-mobile-select 50 checks, 42 s alone (r1's 34 s); test-chat-pre-tools 48 checks. The fast row stays 0.46 s, measured at full clock on 11-07 (the acceptance read 0.63–0.68 s under the cap) — not restated. Known limit, the suite's own: test-desktop-small-chrome's 270-s watchdog in ①.
- **A box trap, not the product:** every headless Chrome hung at its first navigation while `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` was set (the lane env passes it): the cookie store waits on the Secret Service before any request leaves (net-log: `COOKIE_PERSISTENT_STORE_KEY_LOAD_STARTED`, never done). The chrome legs ran with it unset.

- **The shape that escaped on the release (test-stop-tree §1's control proves it):** a child that BOTH leaves the job's group AND drops its environ — `setsid env -i …`, `systemd-run --scope … env -i …`. A child under the timeout program leaves the group but keeps the environ, so the member walk's mark finds it.
- **The mechanism (src/proc-identity.js):** `childTreeOf` / `treeOf` read the tree by the parent chain — each process's main-thread children list and stat (the file the release's member walk reads; no directory listed) — synchronously like that walk (procfs, the tree's own cost, ≤ 512 rows / 50 ms), BEFORE the first signal: the stop's signal stays synchronous (test-jobs-memory pins it) and no thread pool stands before it. `_termRun` writes the stop's intent WITH the tree and signals in the same tick — the fix for tb's round-2 red (the group's signal reaches the main and the wrapper at once; the main's children were re-parented before a wrapper-side read). Round 3's asynchronous read was withdrawn: it broke the synchronous stop the jobs-memory suite pins. The wrapper carries `childTreeOf` as a SHIPPED TWIN; `endTree` / `treeLine` serve the conversation door.
- **The doors:** a job's stop through its WRAPPER's one table (the stop step signals the tree's members outside its group, once; the drain ends what is left, on both rungs); the ENGINE's `_killTree` before a SIGKILL of the group (a force stop, the ladder's kill step — the wrapper cannot); a local conversation's kill (ws-handler: the dtach master(s) or a local chat pty; survivors 3 s after the teardown). ### bl-jobs B-70f9 — option A (the owner, 2026-11-18 ~00:53Z): no cross-machine jobs; a job says where it runs
- **① A JOB SAYS WHERE IT RUNS, A WRONG MACHINE IS REFUSED BY NAME.** PURE `jobWhereVerdict` (src/job-model.js): a conversation on the hub's machine — «runs on <hub> in <path>»; a conversation on ANOTHER machine (its session's `host`) — the folder is asked on the hub before anything is created (the blocked-path door `mount-door.pathBlocked` first, then `fs.promises.stat`): missing ⇒ `400 wrong-machine` «jobs run on <hub>, not on <there> where your conversation runs; this folder is not there: <path> — nothing was created»; a mount that does not answer ⇒ `folder-blocked`; there ⇒ it runs, and the answer says on which machine (the path used as it is there — two same-named folders are never told apart). THE OWN READ'S CURE (r1 F1 F2 F4 F5 F15): the check moved into src/server/job-where.js `jobWhere` (the route awaits it; a check that throws answers 500 by name — never a request left open): the door is `mountDoor.blocked` (the first cut called a `pathBlocked` the door does not export — every remote create hung); a schedule's task's folder (`action.task.cmd.cwd`, `--every` / `--cron` / `--at`) is asked too; ONE stat, bounded (3 s ⇒ `folder-blocked`, 503); only ENOENT / ENOTDIR (or a file) is «not there» — EACCES decides nothing; a relative folder or none from a remote conversation ⇒ `relative-cwd`; the CLI resolves `--cwd` where it runs. - channels-outbound `restOf(p)`: the attachment parts of a SENT proposal that did not land, aligned with its stored files by position (a `left-out` file — the account carries none — is not the rest). `resendRest(id, { ctx })` builds a NEW proposal from the kept bytes (sent proposals keep theirs KEEP_MS = 7 d; read with fs.promises, off the loop's sync census), answering the same message, no text; the OWNER's door (POST /api/channels/outbox/:id/resend, the card's «Send the rest», armed like every decision) is an own send — the press is the approval; the DRAFTING agent's (`vibespace-channels resend <id>`, POST /api/agent/channels/proposals/:id/resend, the withdraw route's caller rules) proposes it for review. ### bl-msg B-84b4 — a stop inside a held digest's send: the person decides, knowing (ruled B by 主开发 23:35Z)
- THE SCENE (read on b06f36e90): Deliver writes its press record (`held.inFlight`) before the block; the block reserves its ledger row, SENDS (deliverToConversation), then one durable update finalizes the row and clears the carried rows. The next press clears the mark and its answer carries `inDoubt` + `doubtNote` once.

### bl-msg B-be02 — a secret NAME=value inside a prose line (the triage's cause was not the real one)
- MEASURED on b06f36e90: «A prose line: API_KEY=… should be hidden.» and «set it so: DB_PASSWORD=…» gave 0 redactions; the same sentences WITHOUT the colon after «line» / «so» were redacted. So the dotenv rule is not line-shaped: KV_HEAD needs ONE opener character before a name, and a PUBLIC head before it («line», «so», «status», «path») took the blank after its colon as its own separator; redactKv walked on past it and the next name had no opener.
- THE CURE (redactKv, one line): a public head gives back its trailing BLANKS; every holder path already sets lastIndex itself. Never its `:` (the first cut did, and the test machine's run reddened the live-value legs of test-secret-shapes and test-vault-masker-once: the mark `[vault:apikey:k]` opened `apikey:` and was masked again) — so «line:API_KEY=…» with no blank stays as on the release, said. Both modes: the line mode hides to the line end as for any stored head, the message mode (B-3e61) one token. No R2b continuation is re-opened (the row's worry): R2b is a separate per-line pass.
- Legs: test-secret-shapes (four prose lines × both modes, the neighbours that must not move — a vault mark among them —, idempotent; red controls = the give-back removed (4/4 leak) and the colon given back too (the mark re-masked)).
- R2, THE LANE'S OWN ADVERSARIAL READ: the wrapped forms agents write were still 0 — «`DB_PASSWORD=…`», «"API_KEY=…"», «**API_KEY=…**», «<API_KEY=…>» — and a flag carrying an assignment («--set-env-vars=API_KEY=…,DB_PASSWORD=…» hid only the second): KV_HEAD's openers gain `=` and the wrappers (` " ' * <), a bare `=` separator is given back (never a `:`), and in a message the wrapper's closing twin stays outside the mask. The vacuous leg (a comma already opened `secret`) is replaced; one more red control (the base's openers ⇒ the wrapped forms leak).

### bl-msg B-3e61 — a message between agents arrives whole (seven sightings of the belt cutting a lane's brief)
- THE CAUSE (measured on b06f36e90): R2 of src/secret-shapes.js runs a bare value to the END OF ITS LINE — right for a stored head (exit output, a job log: hides more, never less), wrong for a message, where one line is often the whole brief. Five of the seven sightings reproduce as written (the session word glued to a token, a data-key selector, a suite name ending in schema + a colon, a lane name ending in shield + a colon, Chrome's password-store flag); the third no longer triggers. And the CLI's sent line read the shorter count as «the last N were CUT».
- THE MESSAGE MODE (`redactSecrets(t, { message: true })`, asked by the two message sinks — the group log, before the @-scan, and the kind-less msg stash): a bare or never-closed value is ONE token (past the blanks a head left, to the next blank or CJK stop); a closer the prose opened before the head and one sentence-final dot stay outside (R7's queryTail); a value whose first word is an HTTP auth scheme keeps the line-end extent (`Authorization: Bearer …` would otherwise leave the credential after the scheme word). Quoted values, JSON, YAML continuations, PEM blocks keep their own rules. Accepted trade, said: an unquoted multi-word passphrase in prose loses only its first word to the mask — the row's own bounded-token rule.
- A KNOWN FLAG (`KNOWN_FLAG_VALUES`, both modes): `--password-store=` with a value from Chrome's closed list (basic, gnome, gnome-keyring, gnome-libsecret, kwallet, kwallet5, kwallet6, detect) is no credential; the scan walks on past it (a later `--api-key=` is masked); any other value of it is masked.
- THE SENDER IS TOLD: `said: []` collects each trigger as written (`session:`, `data-key=`, `Bearer`, `ghp_…`, at most 8); the group engine's post answers `masked`, the msg route passes it, and sentLine says «the secret belt masked the value at «session:» (each now «redacted»); the rest arrived whole» instead of a cut. The owner's @-picker places are moved by the mask before each (the prefix masked); the usage of vibespace-msg says the belt exists.
- Legs: test-secret-shapes (the sightings, line mode unchanged, headers, multi-line shapes, the flag; 3 red controls), test-channel-groups (send keeps the rest, `masked`, @ places on the kept words; 2 red controls), test-cli-one-text (the sent line pure + through a fake route; 1 red control).
- R2, THE LANE'S OWN ADVERSARIAL READ (2 blockers, 6 majors on the message mode): a HEADER (`Authorization:` of any scheme, `Cookie:` / `Set-Cookie:` lists — LINE_HEADS) and a first token opening a key block (`-----BEGIN` flattened onto one line) keep the line end; a first token that is a scheme or a credential word (`auth: password …`, `token: Bearer …`) takes the next token with it — never the line end, so «auth: token rotation is broken, …» keeps its rest; a mention (`@beta`) is never a value (R2, and R5 in a message), so the @-scan still wakes; the flag's value ends at a stop only before a blank; the heads the sender is told go through the msg belt (msgName — a head could carry a frame opener) with «and more» past eight; sentLine no longer claims «the rest arrived whole». THE PROSE SINKS (task progress + detail, a For-you item, a status reason + detail) ask the message mode too — B-be02 made «blocked: session: waiting …» a head, and their line-end extent would have cut those lines. Jobs keep the line mode. Two more red controls (the header list removed, the two-token rule removed).
- THE CURE (the coordinator's verdict: NOT TAKEN — a value opening on a full-width bracket or a CJK stop walked on; an @ value under `=` was taken for a mention; then two rounds of my own reader refuted two cures by shape: secrets after a stop, a bracket, a mention, a head inside the region, a value opening on a mark such as `=>`, an O(N²) trailing-run regex, and a corpus whose controls could not fail). ONE LAW, by construction: in a MESSAGE the masked value's region is the line rule's own (to the line end, or a JSON closer), and inside it `messageValue` keeps ONLY PLAIN WORDS. The region splits at blanks and CJK stops (kept as they are). THE FIRST CHUNK: the mask itself, or a MEMBER's @ under a `:` head (the group engine passes its members' names and ids; a sink with none spares no @), is kept; a pair closed on its line has its inside masked and the pair kept; anything opening on a mark, a stop or an open pair is no value the mode recognises — the line rule, the region masked whole; otherwise the chunk is masked, and after a scheme or credential word the next one too. EVERY LATER CHUNK is masked unless plain (letters with prose edge marks, a word's own case in any script — lowercase, Capitalized, an acronym of at most 3 — at most 14 ASCII letters, at most 64 characters, a mark run at most 3); ASCII glued to the value through a stop or a pair stays the value's; after a grouped first chunk (4–8 of one class: an app password, a TOTP key) every chunk of its shape is masked. A HEAD INSIDE THE REGION (KV_HEAD's own shape at a place KV_HEAD opens — a quoted key, a blank before `=`, a header, a credential word, a quoted value) ENDS the region there and the main scan judges it with every rule (round 4: the reader's blocker was a second key judged by a weaker in-region check); one glued behind a CJK stop masks the chunk after it. Round 5 (the fourth read): the text between an inner head's own end (a closed quote, a JSON closer, a typed scalar, a flag) and the outer region's end is judged by the same plain-words rule before it is copied (redactKv's gap filter — nothing the line rule hid goes unjudged); a full-width colon or a lone `:` / `=` after a holder word masks the next chunk; a chunk that already holds the mask stays as it is, so a second pass changes nothing; an acronym is at most 3 letters; a value with nothing to hide, a head whose value is the mask already, and a known flag are copied as they are (rounds 6–7 — the fifth and sixth reads: the gap filter re-read a kept head, its member's @, a second pass's own head); a head's own opener or a wrapper twin before an inner head stays (a typed number inside another head's region is judged by the gap filter: no plain word); the last word seen is remembered whether it was kept or masked, so «…，password : x» masks x (round 8 — the corpus's first run on the test machine found it, with an oracle that did not know a head glued to its value's opener); and ANY error inside the message mode returns the LINE result whole (the fourth read found a definition my third round dropped: the throw skipped most rules for the whole message — now a red control throws on purpose). Headers (LINE_HEADS), quoted values and typed scalars keep the line rule. R5's @ exemption is gone. THE PROOF (test-secret-shapes): a differential over a generated corpus — every opener class (glued, and marks with a blank: `=> `, `:= `, `- `, `( `) × 10 heads (a JSON, a YAML and a wrapper-opened key among them) × 5 separators, crossed, closed and open pairs; 10 value shapes (letters-only mixed case, app-password and TOTP groups among them) × 15 tails (secrets after a stop, a bracket, a plain word; a SECOND HEAD in 8 spellings) on every head; a member's-mention pass: where the line rule hides a token the message mode hides it, and every chunk it keeps beyond the line rule is plain by a STRICTER, independent rule; red controls = the musts compiled back in (the stop half, the bracket half, the @), each finding a leak OF ITS OWN SCENE (the opener of the line); the main loop's guard is a COUNT of steps (marks in every loop) over nine hostile lines, each ≤ 6 × its length. Every line also passes a second message pass unchanged. test-exit-run's rule controls follow the rules' current lines (the `say` collector) — HEAVY, owed. SAID: a passphrase or a machine-made phrase with blanks (an app password in four groups, a seed phrase) keeps its later plain words in a message, and so does a plain-looking word right after a member's @; the strict (line) mode is not byte-for-byte the release's — B-be02's openers and give-back mask more, KNOWN_FLAG_VALUES keeps Chrome's password-store value in both modes; the separators that open no head (a blank, none, a full-width colon or equals) are outside the corpus because both modes match there; «told BEFORE it is sent» is not met (told on the send's own answer).
- CURE 2 (主开发's verdict on the cure: NOT TAKEN on two musts, and the unit closes after it; ONE new commit on batch 59's tip). MUST 1: a first chunk that opens on a letter or a digit of ANY script is a value the mode recognises (it ends at a blank or a CJK stop) — «session: 已修好 @beta 请验收» had taken the line rule, so the owner's picked @beta was refused and a typed one woke nobody; and a MEMBER's @ is never eaten by the glued rule, by the word-after-a-credential-word rule, or by R5 (`password @beta`; the @ to a CJK stop, what the stop glues behind it masked) — the member set is in hand, so sparing only a member invents no mention. MUST 2: the piece before a glued inner head is judged like any later chunk (`keeps`, the one judgement of a later chunk: the next-chunk, glued and group rules) — «auth: password hunter,token=x» kept «hunter». Also from the test machine's run of the cure (dcdd8d590): a group's last group before a comma stayed in clear (`groupAt` reads a later chunk without its trailing prose marks), and the corpus's own checker read a head the line rule glued to its mask as a kept piece (the mask is a separator now; the corpus's head pieces are its own names). A mask made by the gap filter is named in `said` (the region's head). The corpus gains five glued openers (a Han letter, an accented and a full-width Latin letter, a Cyrillic letter, an Arabic-Indic digit), a member's @ in four scenes, the piece-before-a-head and group-before-a-comma rows, and six red controls, each finding a leak of its own scene. The belt's doc comment and kb-file-structure.md (src/secret-shapes.js, THE MESSAGE MODE) say the mode as it is.

Three states and the fall-back: LEARNING (fewer than 5 pairs — nothing is drawn), PROVISIONAL (5 or more, better — drawn and marked with its count of readings, never read by the pool), ON (30 or more, better — drawn, and the pool may read it), OFF (worse at any measure — the plain line, nothing more). Each threshold is a named constant with its reason; the verdict is the instance's own and moves as pairs arrive.
- **The estimator.** linesMeta gathers each identity's calib pairs in the pass it already makes; `predictVerdict(source, lane)` aggregates one source's identities (60 s memo, dropped when a file moves); `predictStatesFor`; `poolEstimateFor` = the estimate held to ON lanes; every estimate carries `sinceRequests` (the ledger's own count since the reading).
- **The pool.** Its one decision door (poolReadCache) overlays `poolEstimateFor`: a learning, provisional or off lane is read as the raw reading. The auto-cli scheduler's drift read keeps the whole estimate (it decides when to refresh, not where to place).
- **/api/usage and the popup.** Every estimate passes a screen gate: a lane is drawn only where ON (a PROVISIONAL lane apart, for the popup — law B4 above), and each lane says its state and count. The popup writes «about Y%» (law B4: no bound is claimed), «· from N readings on this hub» on a provisional band, and «N requests here since» where nothing is drawn; its «est N%» chip is gone (the rings' tooltips keep their «est N%» for now). The ledger counts requests, not turns, so the plain line says requests.
- **Gates.** scripts/test-usage-predict.mjs (new, fast): the rule on made pairs, the gate, the estimator over a made anchors folder, the wiring, six mutant copies. Suites whose fixtures MEANT «the pool reads the estimate» (test-account-reset-door, test-fable-cap-pool-storm) state the verdict ON; test-usage-ledger-walk compares the released code's estimate without the new `sinceRequests`; test-quota-model classifies the new module and the popup's lane keys.

### bl-mail B-166e part 2 — a company preset's client swapped under its key is SAID; the owner's own client change stays refused (主开发 2026-11-18 20:07Z «A (BOTH)», confirmed 20:11Z)
- (1) THE FLEET'S PRESETS CANNOT BE REFUSED, SO THEY ARE SAID: `clientSwapCheck` (src/server/channels-engine.js) runs at a presets reload or the vault opening, at boot, and after an account's sign-in landing, removal or enable change (channels-auth; never awaited by the door). Per company preset (integration row + `cluster:` key): the client the preset names now against each enabled account's MINTED client (the token's `client.id`, B-166e); those on another client keep refreshing with their own until the vendor deletes it. ONE For-you item a preset, naming it («{kind}: the company preset «{preset}» signs in with another client now — {n} account(s) still signed in with the old one; re-authorize each»), its door (`channel-reauth`) the next such account by label, REDRAWN as N falls (src/user-todos.js `redrawItem` takes an `action` of the SAME kind — a door moves, never changes kind) and RESOLVED at zero.
- THE MEMO IS THE PRESET'S, on the adapters store — its shape and rule are the cure 2 bullet below (what was SAID: `{to, named, itemId, sig}`, the PURE `clientSwapStep`). Nothing is judged while the vault is locked (its opening checks again); a preset with a token the check cannot read, or a withdrawn preset, is left as it stands. A token minted before the B-166e rule names no client and is not counted (its refresh uses the preset's client; a refusal there is the dead sign-in's own item). The checks run one after another.
- THE CURE, ITS SHAPE RULED (主开发 2026-11-19 00:42Z — two rounds of «the client in force at the close» brought the same must back in a new coat: one field cannot hold two facts): THE MEMO IS WHAT WAS SAID — `clientSwaps[row|key] = {to, named, itemId, sig}`: the client in force at the last check, the accounts NAMED in an item for it, the item, its last words. The rule is the PURE `clientSwapStep(memo, to, need)` (need = the COUNTED accounts not on the client in force): (1) another client in force = a new swap, the memo starts again with nobody named (an open item of the old client superseded); (2) owed = need not yet named: if any, ONE item (the open one redrawn, else a new one) listing ALL who must act now, and they are named; (3) nobody left and the item open: it closes, the named stay named. So a swap is said once however many it touches; one named who comes back is not said twice; one never named (disabled / dead AT the swap) is said once when back; a revert is a new swap. No stray field, no special close. WITH IT (the 22:35Z rule): a DISCONNECT, the re-authorize door's re-enable, a RENAME and a dead sign-in set / cleared are triggers; NO REDRAW when nothing moved (`sig`); the item's DETAIL in zh / ja; a burst COALESCES (one running, at most one queued); a BLIND preset said ONCE in the journal while it lasts (the choice named: say it, never count only the readable part); the preset named by its LABEL (two presets of one label: label + key); a dead sign-in not counted; the new item filed BEFORE a superseded one closes, with the dead-sign-in item's open cap; no write after stop; a failed memo write said; a hand-edited memo read strictly.
- (2) THE OWNER'S OWN CLIENT: the law held in 2.369.410 (per account, key «custom»: `setCustomSecret` refuses another client id with 409 `client-change-needs-reauth`, nothing written) — PINNED, no product change.

### bl-loop-b B-f534 — no watchdog session across a stop (the loop watchdog's «Waiting for the debugger to disconnect…» line)
- THE LINE: Node prints it when the process exits with an inspector session attached. The loop watchdog keeps one up to SESSION_MS (20 ms) while it asks a main thread ON THE CPU, so a stop within 20 ms of such an ask printed one line (no wait, nothing lost — test-fs-canary §11 pins the harm).
- THE CURE (src/server/sync-fs-witness.js exitMark, the worker's post/closeSession): at the process's 'exit' — every exit that runs its listeners (a signal's shutdown, an uncaught exception's, any process.exit; never an abort) — the main thread stores EXITING in the live slot's [7] and reads the note slot's [7], the count of sessions the watchdog holds (counted up BEFORE a connect, down AFTER its disconnect; the watchdog counts up, then reads EXITING; the main thread stores EXITING, then reads the count — sequentially consistent Atomics, so one always sees the other). None ⇒ no wait. One or more ⇒ it posts `exiting` (the watchdog closes them) and waits for 0 with Atomics.wait, at most SESSION_MS + 5 ms on the monotonic clock. After the mark nothing connects. ONE process 'exit' listener over every live witness (EXIT_MARKS), so a suite's many witnesses never pass Node's ten-listener warning.
- SAID: a watchdog starved past the bound leaves the one line, as before. The 'exit' runs before loop-day-report's [loop-exit] line; it waits only while a session is held (sub-millisecond when the watchdog is awake). The count is written by the watchdog alone (a load and a store; `Atomics.add` would read as a For-you add() site to test-user-todos-layout's scanner).
- PINS: test-loop-hold ⑫a — the REAL thread in process: before the mark a hold is asked; after it, a hold the witness itself records past the bar (spins in steps, warmed, doubled until recorded — never a clock) is asked nothing; the two threads name the same slots; the ORDER the pair rests on, by source (count up → read EXITING → connect; disconnect → count down; the memory answer before `exiting`; store EXITING → read the count → wait on it alone). NOT in the fast tier: the 20 ms window of a NATIVE hold at an exit, where the residual lived — a first child leg that stopped four children right after a JavaScript hold's ask met no held session at all, and the release's copy printed 0 lines of 4, so it was cut. PROVE test-loop-hold-live: its legs 5 and (7) sweep exits after asks and count the residual their exitJudge excuses; with this cure that count should read 0.

### gmail-connect-wall — B-e40d: a Gmail / Google Drive storage mount keeps the OAuth client its token was minted under
- **The hole (the 2026-10-23 outage's class, left after B-166e cured the channel accounts):** a preset-backed Drive or Gmail mount stores only the preset KEY and resolved the client under it at every mount / refresh — another client swapped in under the same key (the outage) made every refresh refused.
- **The rule (B-166e's, src/channels/gmail.js refreshClientOf):** a record names the client its token was minted under — `mintedClient {id, key, sealed}`, the secret sealed with .mounts-key (`sealed`, not «…Enc»: in a mount record a «…Enc» name is a secret a person writes in a page field, the convention test-write-only-secrets holds; this one is the hub's own and never leaves it) — taken from the SIGN-IN that minted it (Drive's startDriveAuth and gmail-sync's startAuth keep the client they used, and keepSignIn keeps it a day after the flow ends — a Save after the flow's 10 minutes or after another sign-in — by a hash of the refresh token; a saved token is that sign-in's when their refresh tokens match), never guessed from the key at Save (a swap between sign-in and Save, a withdrawn key whose sign-in fell to another preset, an import). The same refresh token saved again keeps the client it names; another token clears it. A token no sign-in of this hub minted (or one from before a restart) names none — no key on the record — and its FIRST PROVEN-GOOD REFRESH adopts the client: a Drive backend probe that ANSWERED while the token its env carried was spent adopts the client THAT env carried (MountManager._adoptProbed — never one worked out after the run, and only while the record still holds that token; a probe that never ran rclone proves nothing); a gmail-sync refresh that worked (onClientProven, with the refresh token — a stopped worker or a token the record no longer holds proves nothing). A secret rotated under the same client follows into the sealed copy; a refresh under another id never re-names it. src/mounts.js MountManager.refreshClient: the preset's values while they name that client, the MINTED client when the preset under the key names another or is gone — said ONCE per mount and pair in the hub's log (and a sealed copy that cannot be opened is said too: it refreshes with the preset); a record with its own client names none. ### bl-machines-b — B-b968's edge: the sub-agent JSONL watcher takes whole lines only (主开发 04:23Z: «yours as a small unit on utf8-stream if it reaches a person»)
- THE HARM: src/server/stdout/claude-stream-json.js `readNewLines` read [offset, size), set the offset to the file's end and parsed every line. A line the CLI was still writing (a read landing mid-append) failed to parse and was dropped; its rest arrived at the next read as a fragment that never parsed either. So the sub-agent's message (its text / thinking, which stream-json does not carry) was missing from the sub-agent's view. A cut character never showed, because a cut line never parsed.
- THE CURE: only whole lines are taken. A line being written is HELD until its newline, read once (a long line written in many chunks is never read again; only the new bytes are searched — its read's should), and the offset moves past whole lines only. A newline byte never sits inside a UTF-8 character, so no character is cut and utf8-stream is not needed here. `readSync`'s byte count is honoured, and its fd is closed in a finally.
- LEGS: test-helper-ask ㉒ — the REAL consumer under a scratch HOME. A JSONL holds one whole line and half of the next, cut inside a character; the rest and a third line are then appended (real fs.watch). Lines 1, 2 and 3 arrive in order, and line 2's words are intact. RED CONTROL (anchored): the release's read drops line 2.

- THE REMAINDER (the close's remainders list): a kept stopped copy (`<sock>.json.stopped`, a session whose socket died while the server was down) was consumed only by a /api/sessions sweep that saw a live session address its conversation. Only a turn that ended WELL proves the resume (PURE `turnRan`): a resume the CLI cannot load answers an error `result` (`error_during_execution`, is_error, «No conversation found with session ID» — test-resume-breaker's stub) and exits 1, and an ACP prompt can end in 'error' or 'cancelled' (acp-events now stamps `session._promptStopReason`, its session-schema row beside `_turnOpenSaidAt`); all keep the copy, as does a claude Stop or API-error turn (the safe direction: the sweep's road). r1 of B-a5a4 consumed at registration and lost a failed resume's copy (reverted in cad68d2d6). A terminal session (no turn-end record) keeps the sweep's road.
- r2 (its adversarial read — 1 must, 2 shoulds, 5 nits, all taken): the must was exactly that a failed claude resume ends a «turn» (its error result) — the first cut consumed on it. Taken: the `turnRan` guard, the ACP error end, warnings instead of silent catches on the server.js line, the legs below. r3 (a delta read — 1 must, 3 nits, all taken): the new session field's session-schema row (test-session-schema scans every stdout consumer's writes; the build ends with it), an ACP 'cancelled' end refused too, the user line says «once it ran a turn».
- LEGS (test-dead-socket-keeps-chat-meta §10 (2)): CONTROL first — before any turn end a next boot lists the stale row with the old account; a FAILED resume's end (the stub's exact error result) and an ACP prompt ended in 'error' keep their copies (listed by the next boot, account and all); a claude success result, an ACP end_turn and codex's task_complete (no record) consume theirs; a live pending fork and another harness's session with the same id, asked first, consume nothing; `turnRan` PURE; the WIRING (server.js hands the record, claude-stream-json forwards its `result`, acp-events stamps its stop, codex calls only at task_complete, the stub's record as the suite spells it). - LEG (test-usage-trim §7, counts; its row restated 5.0 → 5.5 s, the fast cap stays 1203 s: the stated sum 1202.911 s (its 1162 → 1163 on 2.369.408 is not needed on the checkpoint)): 12 000 appended rows taken in ≥ 3 steps of ≤ one 1 MiB slice, the cache = a synchronous load's; a sync reader mid-way takes over within TAKEOVER_MAX_BYTES; CONTROL the release's road (the next reader) takes all 12 000 in one call.
- THE ADVERSARIAL READ'S MUST, cured: with more than the takeover bound left, `_waitBigWarm` waited on the boot's warm (ended long ago), so the whole-ledger gate and aggregateAsync asked again in microtasks forever and the absorb's next turn never came. Now an async reader waits for THE ABSORB (`c.absorbing`); the reading of what is left is reset at each absorb's start (a stale small one let a sync reader take it all); bytes that come mid-absorb are taken by the pass it chains. SAID: while a big absorb (more than 8 MiB) runs, the ledger says it is loading for those turns — the boot warm's rule: an estimate waits, the Usage window says loading — where the release held the loop to parse it all. The second read's must, cured: the absorb's promise is the cache's BEFORE its first step runs (a pass ending inside it — nothing new, a throw — clears it; before, a settled promise was left there and every later ask returned it: U5 off for good). A rebuild's or the boot's swap takes the bytes appended meanwhile through an absorb too. Legs add (§7): an async reader mid-absorb waits for it; a sync reader takes nothing past the bound; the chained pass; an absorb that found nothing leaves no promise behind and the next append is still taken stepped; CONTROL the release's `_waitBigWarm` settles before one loop turn while the absorb still runs (a reverted cure hangs the suite — the watchdog names it).
- NOT CURED HERE: a reader's takeover may still take up to TAKEOVER_MAX_BYTES (8 slices) in its tick — the boot warm's bound, kept; the cold columns' settle and `_sortHot`'s concat after a big absorb run in one turn (O(rows), as the release's).
### bl-loop-a — usage-cpu, the chain's cure (its read: TAKEN, three readers, no must; one as if a must + two smalls; on U5 = acad2351a)
- AS IF A MUST — THE TELEMETRY STASH IS ON DISK BEFORE ITS ANSWER: U4 answered the exporter at once, the post's stash lines owed to the store writer at its pace — a kill inside that pace lost rows the exporter never sends again after a 200, and those rows are what the ledger's backfill and a billing question are answered from. Now the route awaits the store writer's URGENT road for the stash (`durable`, bounded at STASH_DURABLE_MS = 4 s: two waits + the 1 s Retry-After stay inside the exporter's own 10 s) whenever lines are owed or being written — the loop never waits (a promise); past the bound or a failed write the answer is 503 «retry» with Retry-After 1, and the resend is answered once the owed lines land (a known org's rid is never stashed twice; an unknown org's row may be — its readers skip those rows). Its cost, said: each post marks the stash URGENT, so while sessions export a person's act can wait behind a few more urgent writes (U4 had avoided that; the ruling chose the disk).
- SMALL — THE MEMO IS ITS IDENTITY'S: an estimate memo entry is refused at its next ask when its account now resolves to another identity (as fresh as the pool engine's identity groups, cached 30 s) (a switch: the scan's invalidate names only the groups it walked, so the old identity's entry lived its 30 s); the hit asks the identity (the pool engine's cached groups, a lookup). An entry of an identity no scan names still lives ≤ 30 s — bounded by the TTL and the fresher-reading check (kb-file-structure, the usage-estimator.js section — the INDEX row stays ≤ 300 characters, §82).
- SMALL — THE EQUAL-INSTANT TIE PINNED: a coldable row that comes while a trim's stage is open at the same ms as a row the trim moves waits hot and moves at the next trim, after that row in the columns; test-usage-trim §3t pins the scene (a tie with a moved row, held hot, moved next), the row neither lost nor doubled, every priced row and count = the untrimmed twin's (the signature) and a read-order sum within 1e-12 relative — a one-row reorder's ulp is inside that, so the leg pins the scene, not the last bit (its line says whether equal to the bit).
- LEGS: test-otel-truth (the route driven): a 200 comes with its line on disk; a writer past the bound ⇒ 503 «retry», the resend 200 with ONE line; RED acad2351a's answer at once ⇒ the 200 with its line not on disk. test-usage-ledger-walk: an account switch rebuilds the entry for the identity it resolves to now; RED acad2351a's hit (a copy) ⇒ the old identity's served; U3's own leg now counts estimates by `ratesFor` (a memo hit asks the identity, never the rates). test-usage-trim §3t as above.
- its TAKEN verdict (主开发 13:44Z, riding the restack's line) — THE TWO BOUNDS SIDE BY SIDE: the store writer's back-off after a FAILED write is 1, 2, 4 … 60 s (store-pace retryMs, the ceiling from the 7th failure in a row); the exporter retries inside its own export timeout (~10 s, OpenTelemetry's default — stated, not measured here). From the fifth failure in a row the first outlasts the second, so «bound the wait to this post's own line» cannot help (its line is in the same failing file). The split instead: a FAILING storage (`whyNotDurable` = failed) answers 200 — every record of the post is already held (take() put it in the truth map and owed its line) and lands with the writer's retry; a kill inside that outage loses those lines, as the release's failed append did. A QUEUE (the writer healthy, busy) still answers 503 «retry». The writer is asked inside a try (a writer that cannot be built: a 503, never a hung post). A RETRIED post IS the same record: its rid (a known org's) is in the truth map, so no second stash line and no second labelDiffers count (arrivals.kept and .events count arrivals, as they always did). Leg: a failing storage ⇒ 200 with the record held; RED the cure before the split ⇒ 503. THE MEMO HIT'S COST, by count: the identity groups' rebuild is shared (one per 30 s, whoever asks first after the cache expires); a hit adds no rebuild — it may be the caller that pays the one there is; its time needs the hub's hourly line. The tie leg keeps its honest sentence (it pins the scene, not the last bit).
- ci: test-otel-truth restated 1.2 → 3.3 s by its measurement on the test machine at the cure's tip (3.1 / 3.3 s in the two zones; U4's +0.7 s was an estimate), the fast cap 1203 → 1206 by arithmetic (stated 1205.011 s). test-usage-ledger-walk is read at 15.5 / 16.7 s on that machine — as every lane's tip reads it there (15–41 s today); its row's 9.8 s is the box's measure, the cure's share two 1 500-row worlds: left to the integrator's whole tier.
- LEFT, said: U5's absorb polling a pass's pending with setImmediate (bounded, small — a promise from the pass's end is a refactor of its own); U2's device agent gets the work-based yield with its agent's update (the parity law, as built); U3 S1 (the oracle cannot fail on a key-only drop) and U5 S2 (the swap's absorb without a leg of its own) — the lane's open shoulds, unchanged here.

### lg-rewind — one life for a rewind request (B-437e, the four follow-ups named in lines/lg-rewind-U4-cure2.md)
- THE MARK FROM THE CONVERSATION'S OWN RECORDS: the claude wrapper says our `vsr-` request as it reaches the CLI (`rewind_out {request_id, at}`, stdout + its buffer; a dropped frame is never said); the normalizer keeps it (`rewindAskedOut`) until the CLI's answer. A hub restart reads it back from the buffer; a new wrapper's buffer starts empty.
- WHILE THE REQUEST LIVES: the hub's «one at a time» holds until the answer (a local 2.1.322 never expires a request, so two could reach it after a stalled pipe). `session._rewindOut` holds one life only for the moment before the record is read, or for a wrapper older than the record.
- THE PERSON'S SEND WAITS, BOUNDED (主开发 20:05Z): src/server/user-input.js refuses it by name (`rewind_out {left}`) while a rewind is out — the CLI would run the rewind first and the message after it (the watchdog scene) — but only until the stated expiry (`rewindFenceLeft`), and the words name the door (send after the answer, the seconds left; or stop the conversation). After the expiry the send goes through, so a CLI that never answers never locks the box. The ws answers `error rewind-out` (scope action) and ChatInput `refusedSend` puts the words back; the For-you reply gets 409. An agent's dispatch is not guarded.
- THE TAB KEEPS THE BINDING: sessionStorage `vs-rewind:<session>`, so a page reloaded before the answer binds it again.
- Gate: test-checkpoints — each part a leg and a red control that asserts its plant first; the send-in-the-window race proven by a stall placed between the press's write and the wrapper's record; the REAL wrapper against a stand-in CLI says the record.

## 2.369.411 — 2026-11-18

### bl-loop-b — THE WATCH HOTFIX (the production hub ended at 2026-11-19 01:14Z): a file watch the machine refuses never ends the hub
- THE CAUSE: the machine's inotify watches were used up (65 339 of 65 536, most of them by the lanes' own CLI processes); the hub armed one more — a helper's transcript watch in src/server/stdout/claude-stream-json.js, from its retry timer — fs.watch threw ENOSPC and nothing caught it; systemd restarted the hub 6 s later (the vault locked again).
- ONE DOOR, src/watch-door.js (new): every watch the hub arms goes through it; a refused watch becomes a bounded poll in its place, and the person is told once in For you. The notice never flaps: it lifts only after 3 watches armed in a row and 10 minutes since the last refusal (while limited, one probe watch every 5 minutes, closed at once); the pollers are bounded. The offered command doubles the machine's CURRENT limit, never under 524 288 — it never lowers a limit that is already higher.
- The watch chain changes no module of the device agent's bundle: src/desktop-serve.js and src/opencode-events.js are exempt by name (each watch there already sits in a try with its error listener); src/agentd/ is the device agent's own process.
- THE CENSUS: any bare fs.watch, fs.watchFile, or inline-required / destructured watch in the hub's code outside the door is red by name; new fast suite test-watch-door; the lane's gate 68 of 68 in both zones at its last two tips.

### bl-windows — B-f276: THE TASK GROUPS STORE HELD UNREAD (主开发 2026-11-18 23:05Z, found by a hunt in the release)
- THE CAUSE: src/task-groups.js read and parsed task-groups.json in one try whose catch said «no file»: any failure (a storage hiccup, a permission error, a full file table, damaged bytes) let the boot save tasks.json, or an empty store, OVER the store it could not read — every Task Group, backlog row and activity log of the instance gone, nothing said. The owner's hub keeps this store on a network mount.
- THE LAW (the release's own for jobs.json, src/store-read.js): only a truly ABSENT file falls to tasks.json (migrated forward, left in place) or to an empty store. A failed read, bytes that do not parse or are not the store's shape HOLD the store: nothing writes it; every act that would record something is refused by name (TASK_GROUPS_UNREAD); background roads consume nothing; the read is tried again off the loop (30 s doubling to 5 min) and at every start, and the hold lifts when it reads whole; the person is told once in For you (en / zh / ja).
- THE CURE (89cc87fd0): every grant reader answers UNKNOWN while held, never «in no group» (a row «…, except Task Group G» would admit G's members): TaskGroupManager.groupIdsForGrant throws by name, and the doors that judge a live agent from its groups (channel-acl, channel-filter, channels-grants, automation-keys) ask a hold predicate that src/grant-model.js holds — set by the hub at boot, inert in the device agent's bundle (its one changed module, re-signed at the cut); the page keeps a held mirror. Two reader rounds; the gate 856 suites green in both zones; PROVE test-task-detail-chrome, test-stash-strip.

### lg-text-legs-3 — carriesFrame tests its compiled twin: no expression built per call (the production hub's top hold, measured 2026-11-19)
- THE CAUSE: src/channel-record.js carriesFrame built `new RegExp(FRAME_TAG_RE.source, 'iu')` on EVERY call. The belt (src/peer-text.js toAgentText) calls it once a piece, and the agents' search and list doors (the reach walk in src/server/channels-access.js; agentTitle in src/server/channels-engine.js) belt every conversation title an agent can see, on the main loop — the hub's top hold: 225 s of the last 45 minutes, holds of 1.1–1.7 s about ten times a minute while one agent searched a large account.
- THE MEASURE (the coordinator's, on the release's own module over 20 000 stand-in titles): 291 ms through carriesFrame against 1.5 ms through one compiled expression; ON THE PRODUCTION HUB, read from its journal: that stack was 243 of the 320 main-loop holds of the 50 minutes after its restart (a hold of 1.1 to 1.7 s about ten times a minute).
- THE CURE: carriesFrame tests FRAME_LIVE_RE, the twin the file already holds — the same source, flags `iu`, no `g` and no `y`, so no state between calls; every verdict the same. FRAME_LIVE_RE is exported for its suite. A look for the same shape in src/channel-record.js, src/peer-text.js and src/hidden-chars.js found no other.
- THE LEGS: scripts/test-channel-record.mjs ⑩ — no expression built per call (a counting stand-in over 1 000 calls: 0; RED CONTROL, an anchored copy with the old line back: 1 000), no state (the twin holds neither g nor y; a framed text reads true three times in a row, a clean one false after it), parity with the old construction over a table of hostile shapes. The lane's gate: 1135 suites, 0 red, both zones.
- THE DEVICE AGENT'S BUNDLE reaches the module (src/browser-profiles.js → src/peer-text.js → src/channel-record.js): it is one of the bundle's two changed modules in this release, beside src/grant-model.js; the bundle is re-signed at the cut.

### bl-mail B-2f6c — a Gmail re-authorize after a Disconnect never read the mail added to known threads
- THE REPRODUCTION (step 0, on 2.369.407, the REAL engine over a mailbox-shaped fake vendor: history ids, an INBOX listing newest first, a refresh that dies): 5 named threads, then 16 INBOX adds over a 6 h dead sign-in (10 into known threads, 6 new threads), then four roads. A plain re-authorize, a client-switch rebind and a restart inside the dead window lose NOTHING (the cursor rides `rec.state`); DISCONNECT then re-authorize loses the 10 adds to known threads — the incident's count with this mix (chosen, not evidence; the pod's journal says whether its account went through Disconnect).
- THE CAUSE: `disconnect()` wrote `rec.state = {}` since 2.369.106, when the mailbox cursor lived in memory and the adapter survived a Disconnect; the cursor moved into the state (2026-09-26) and the Disconnect began rebuilding the adapter (verify r4), so the wipe dropped it. The next sync reseeded from /profile with no `walkFrom`, the listing walk put every listed thread in `walked`, and `history()` answered each known thread empty.
- THE FIX: the Disconnect keeps the adapter's state (the mailbox cursor) — except the install's setup report (`state.setup`: the next sign-in may be another app; its probes answer again) and on a record whose identity was never stamped (its next sign-in is not bound: it keeps nothing, as before). Defence in depth in gmail.js: a reseed walk with NO lost cursor reads every thread the engine already HOLDS once (a new `held` dep — the index has the row; `named` missed rows a catch-up past the naming budget left unnamed), a never-held thread is walked (its birth reads it); that walk is persisted (`gmailMustWalk`), so a restart mid-walk walks again. The account card words the feed's `lastCatchUp` for 24 h after a gap ≥ 30 min (channel-caps `feedResumeText`): «Caught up from 08:15 — 11 conversations had new messages»; a gap that ended in a reseed (the vendor's history expired) is recorded too (`walked`) and said as the walk.
- THE ADVERSARIAL READ (a fresh reader on the first commit) found: the backup keyed on `named` not held; a restart mid cursor-less walk dropped it; the card said nothing after a 404 reseed; keeping the state froze Slack's setup report; an unbound record's next sign-in may be another account; only one road pinned; the price misstated. All cured above, each with a leg and a red control.
- LEGS: test-channels-gmail-shape ㉔ (fast) — six named threads, 16 adds (10 into five of them, 6 new threads) over a 6 h dead sign-in, then all FOUR roads over the real engine: Disconnect (cursor on the record after it, the setup report gone, 16/16 read), plain re-authorize, client-switch rebind, restart inside the window (16/16 each, their catch-up said); an unbound record (no cursor kept, the defence reads all); a history that expired (404: nothing lost, `walked` said). The price: a kept cursor 11 thread reads (5 changed known + 6 new), a lost one 12 (every held thread once, the unchanged one too), the release 6. RED CONTROLS: the wipe restored in an auth copy the engine copy requires (the defence still reads all), the wipe + the old walk line = the release (the 10 known-thread adds unread), `named` for `held` (an unnamed held row walked unread), the old restore line (a restart mid-walk drops the walk). test-channel-caps: the words table (9 shapes) + the card's wiring pin.
- NOT DONE BY THIS: mail an account already lost is not re-read — a thread that got later mail healed itself (its read takes everything after its anchor), the others keep their hole. The incident's own road is not proven: the pod's journal (a «disconnected» line before the re-authorize) says whether its account went through Disconnect; a lane cannot read it, and the sibling's clean catch-up is unexplained by this.
- LIMITS: a lost cursor over more than CHANGED_CAP (5 000) held INBOX threads overflows into the CHANGED_CAP walk, which judges against the reseed's own cursor — no worse than before; `touched` counts the first sync's changed set (a catch-up longer than 20 history pages undercounts, and «caught up» is said at its first page).

### bl-loop-b B-9169 — the sync fs instrument's own cost per wrapped call cut to about a third
- MEASURED (this lane, Node 24.22.1 and 22.23.4 alike, raw and wrapped statSync interleaved in 10 000-call chunks, the median of 30 rounds): a call outside the instance's tree 1.06–1.17 µs → 0.30–0.36 µs over the raw call; inside it 0.83–0.90 → 0.30–0.32 µs. The hook alone over a fake fs (no syscall): 0.51–0.94 µs → 0.18–0.21 µs, a transcript-shaped home path 0.93 → 0.18. At the owner's shape (13 112 wrapped calls in the busiest second of 38 sessions restoring, hub-loop-stalls' rig) about 1.4 % of that second → about 0.4 %.
- THE CUT (src/server/loop-blame.js, src/server/sync-fs-witness.js — the two INSTRUMENT_FILES, so the sample's trim is unchanged):
  - An outer wrapped call reads performance.now twice (start, end) and hands its start to the hook; the live slot's start is that value plus ONE offset read at load (PERF_TO_MONO, as loop-holds' perfToMono), so the slot reads no clock of its own. `mono` stays process.hrtime (test-loop-hold (10) pins its spelling); a suite's own `now` still stamps the slot itself.
  - The wall clock only for a call of 1 ms or longer (LB.AT_MS; its start = its end less its length, rounded); a shorter call hands `at` = NaN and a ring held below that dates its own. A call made inside a wrapped call (readFileSync's openSync) reads no clock at all.
  - A path's verdict (MPC.rootOf outside the own tree; the data dir's own mount inside it) is kept per path string until the roots refresh (a new CTX), at most ROOT_MEMO_MAX 4 096 paths, oldest out first. A one-path call is judged with no list; the call in flight is four hook fields, never an object; the slot's path is encoded only when it changes.
- PINS (test-fs-canary §10, fast, in-process, every clock patched to count — never a clock bound): 2 performance.now / 0 hrtime / 0 hrtime.bigint / 0 Date.now per sub-millisecond call; 1 classification, 1 own-tree test and 1 encode for 50 calls on one path; inner calls read nothing; a refresh judges once more; the bound; a 60 ms call dated once at end − length in both rings; the slot's start on the monotonic clock with inflight() from the fields. RED CONTROLS (six mutant copies): each cut put back alone reads its count once per call again (an inner call taken through the outer road: 6 clock reads a readFileSync, not 2).

### B-3b0f (lane bl-accounts) — an unreadable spend ledger refuses; it is never an empty one, and never written over
- **The finding** (the account-reset-door r4 panel, 2026-11-11): `src/server/spend-guard.js` create() read `data/spend-budget.json` inside `try { } catch { }` and went on with `A.emptyBudget()` when the file was torn, a directory or unreadable — three unattended continues were authorized as if no turn had been spent. Found while building: the next persist (any `note()`, an attended press, `noteNudge`, the exit flush) renamed that empty ledger OVER the file, so one restart made the forgiveness permanent.
- **The change:** the load tells ENOENT (nothing spent yet: an empty ledger, as before) from UNREADABLE (any other read error, not JSON, JSON that is no object). Unreadable ⇒ `authorizeUnattendedSpend({ ledger })` refuses every unattended reason by name — `ledger-unreadable`, after the attended answer (a person's press is never counted, so the count cannot decide it) and before the caps; the guard never writes the file while it cannot be read (no rename, no `.tmp`); it reads it again at most once a `LEDGER_RECHECK_MS` (60 s, at `authorize` and at a would-be write). Reads again ⇒ its stamps count, merged with the ones made meanwhile (PURE `mergeBudget`: both kept, never deduplicated); removed ⇒ the count starts over. ONE notice for the instance (`inbox|*|ledger-unreadable`, urgent, the refusal's 6 h cadence), its own door words (repair or remove the file; the limits cannot help), no count line (there is none to say); the hand-over toast says it in words. The journal says it at load; `snapshot().ledgerUnreadable` carries it.
- **Pins:** test-spend-paths §3f, 29 legs: torn / a directory / EACCES / null / an array / a number ⇒ refused by name; ENOENT ⇒ allowed; one notice; the bytes unchanged after a press, a nudge and the flush; a restart still refuses; the bounded re-read; repaired ⇒ the file's stamps count and the press made meanwhile is kept; removed ⇒ allowed and written again; the notice rendered in en / zh / ja and the toast. Three patched-copy controls, each RED: the release's load (authorizes on the empty count and writes it over the file), the write guard removed (the next boot authorizes), the pure rule removed (allows).
- **The adversarial read** (a fresh reader given only the diff and the row): the shape check reached only the top level — `{"budget":"x"}` loaded as an empty ledger and was written over; a ledger is now an object holding a `budget` object (what writeNow writes) or an older build's budget itself (`{}`, a string or array budget ⇒ unreadable). The notice was filed again after every restart and stood 6 h after the file read again: it carries its own itemKey (`spend-ledger-unreadable`, ONE item across restarts) and is resolved (done) the moment the file reads again. A frame carried while the file was unreadable may count twice for a day after the merge — the safe side, now said so in the comment. Legs: three more shapes, the one item across a restart and its resolution.

### bl-browser-a — B-70af: a shared profile's conversation opens a tab again after its last tab closed
- THE CAUSE (read, then MEASURED): on the scope road (an agent lease on a local shared profile) the keeper's `tab new` with no live tab of the lease (after `tab close` / tab_gone, or a fresh lease's first window) makes the window on its OWN CDP socket (openOwnTab → openWindow: no opener in the lease's scope). Chrome announces it (`Target.targetCreated`) to every connection; the mediator's filterEvent drops it there (out of scope at that instant, remembered in the scope's `recent` only for the lease's own createTarget reply), and the keeper's `mediator.admitTarget` only widened the scope. The driver (agent-browser 0.38.2) learns a tab only from that announcement, so every `--pin-tab tab <id>` bind answered «No tab with target id» — refused window_busy bind_failed on every retry (fb-9fedbb37b0, fb-c55ad95d9d). The opener rung (window.open from a live anchor: its openerId is in scope) was never affected.
- MEASURED with the real driver 0.38.2 over the real cdp-mediator on the scope road, Chrome 154 headless (a lane harness, not a suite): base — after the lease's tab closed 0 of 3 keeper windows bound, a fresh lease whose driver was connected 0 of 1, the opener control 1 of 1; with the cure 3 of 3, 1 of 1, 1 of 1 (binds in 21–25 ms).
- THE CURE: each mediated connection keeps the target announcements it was NOT shown (`withheld`, bounded at RECENT_MAX like the scope's `recent` — browser-mediation `withhold`); an entry ends when the connection is shown that target by any road or the target is destroyed (shown or not). An admission OUTSIDE a connection's own reply (the keeper's admitTarget, a grant's targetIds) that brings a target INTO the scope replays the entry there ONCE (`replayOnAdmit`, cdp-mediator `admitInto`); a target already in scope only ends its entry. An announcement that arrives after the admission passes filterEvent as before (in scope then), so a connection hears of a tab once, never twice, never a gone one.
- ROUND 2 (the lane's adversarial read, must-fix): r1 replayed on EVERY out-of-band admission and ended an entry only by the replay or an out-of-scope destroy — the lease's own createTarget (dropped before its reply, replayed by the reply) and every grantFor at a CLI call (holderTabs, a stale targetId) would have told a tab twice, or one already closed in scope. r2's rule is the in-scope test + the shown/destroyed end; ⑨ (a)–(c) pin the three roads, a CONTROL (a replay that ignores the scope ⇒ the lease's own tab told twice) and copiesCensus. The real-driver measure above ran on r1; r2 replays the same out-of-scope→in-scope admissions the measure exercised (A, B), and the box was closed to runs after 23:29Z.
- NOTES (not this row): the relaunch rebind road (keeper attach, «tab <pick>» on the browser's one unrooted page) binds a page the lease was never admitted to on the scope road — it falls back to `tab new` (bound, one blank tab more); fb-61e4794124 («No tab with label», a retry worked) is the r5 ③ class, not this one. The refusal words stay: with the cure «run the same `tab new` once more» is true again (the r5 ③ class — a window closed between the create and the bind).
- LEG: test-browser-fact ⑨ (fast) — the PURE pair (once, latest info, destroyed never, bounded) + the REAL mediator on the scope road over a fake Chrome: the keeper's tab is heard once after its admission, never before, never twice; a late announcement passes once; a destroyed tab and another holder's tab never. CONTROL: a mediator copy whose admission only widens the scope ⇒ never heard.
- NOT in this row: B-679d (merged here) — the ~30 s CLI bind stall under another holder's tab churn is the page-enable freeze class (browser-shared-profile-freeze), not this permanent refusal; not measured again here.
