### B-f169 — the exit run verb hands its argv word for word (lane bl-machines-b, HIGH, its own line)
- CURE (the lane's adversarial read): F1 the cmd.exe refusal thrown inside the run's try was turned into «run_failed — the link failed» by its catch (the leg's own check) — it passes the catch as itself and sits after canRunLine (an old Windows agent stays agent_outdated); F5 cmd.exe gets its OWN line (`winArgvLine`: a word with spaces in double quotes, backslashes / any letter as typed — the manual's `powershell -Command "…"` form works again; a double quote, `& | < > ^ ( ) % !`, an empty word or a trailing backslash is refused by name); a record that says win32 composes that line BEFORE the ask, and an agent that says cmd.exe only after an ask on the sh line runs it only when the two lines are equal; F2 the chat's history card names the hub's line (src/exit-call.js), never the joined words; F3 an empty word is a word; F4 the refusal's words carry no malformed example; F6 the early refusal is audited; F7 a first word sh would read as an assignment or a reserved word is quoted.
- THE HARM (lane bl-keys-misc, 2026-11-18 00:01Z): `vibespace-exit run <m> -- bash -c 'ls /x'` ran `bash -c ls /x` — data/bin/vibespace-exit JOINED the words after `--` with spaces and the machine's `sh -lc` re-split the line, so the quoting was lost and another command ran on another machine than the one written.
- THE LAW: one quoting step. ONE word after `--` is a line as written (the machine's shell reads it — pipes, redirects: unchanged); TWO OR MORE are an argv, posted as `{ argv }` and quoted ONCE by the hub for the far POSIX shell (src/exit-shell.js `argvLine`: a word of plain characters as it is, every other in single quotes). Everything after — the belt (hidden order, encoded command), the ask, the card, the audit, the device's `sh -lc` — reads that ONE line, so what the person approves is what runs. cmd.exe reads no POSIX quoting: words that need it are REFUSED by name (bad_command, `argv: 'cmd-exe'`) — before anything is asked when the machine's record says win32, else once its agent says so; plain words run there as typed.
- THE ROADS: the dial road and the ssh road both hand the device's run op the line; legs in test-exit-reach run the hub's line under the device's own plan (`shellPlan('linux', line)` = a REAL `sh -lc`) for a dial host and an ssh host — a script holding spaces, both quote kinds, a semicolon, `$`, a backtick, a glob and `~` prints each word as written and «echo pwned» never runs; one word stays a line; cmd.exe refused by name (and before the ask on a known-Windows record), plain words run. test-exit-call ⓪: the REAL CLI posts the words as words, one word as `cmd`. docs/agent/exit-manual.md and the CLI's usage say it.

### bl-keys-misc — B-6ed4: a set's mark whose unlink fails is kept and removed again (ledger-dedup-law r18)
- usage-hold-road `_unmark` cleared the memory mark BEFORE the unlink of `<set>.unread` and dropped its failure: the next start read the leftover disk mark as an earlier start's, the set's first EIO became «the disk's answer», the set went aside unread and its count was lost (r17's probe: gone 0 vs 3).
- Now the disk decides: the earlier start's fact goes (the set read), but a failed unlink keeps the mark as THIS process's (`_marksMade` — never «twice»), says it once and retries with the list retry's backoff (unref'd timer, `_track`ed); a new failure of the set stops the retry (`_setUnread` → `_unmarkStop`: the mark is that failure's own).
- r1 (the lane's read): a start that ENDS before a retry lands (the unlink refused its whole life — accept-r17 legA A1/A2) left the mark to the next start as an earlier start's. A failed unlink now also writes the set's READ NOTE `<set>.unread.read`; the next start's listing reads it by NAME (no content read): a mark with its note is swept, never «twice»; a note whose mark went is swept. A retry in flight when the set fails again (`_markGen` moved) writes back a mark its unlink took. Residual, said: a disk that refuses the note's write too leaves the old behaviour.
- Leg: test-ledger-dedup-law ⑨ (a real UsageHistory over a scratch dir): the unlink denied once ⇒ kept + known + no «twice» + said once, removed after the disk settles; denied for the start's WHOLE life ⇒ mark + note left, the next start sweeps both with no «twice»; CONTROLS RED: the release's `_unmark` planted on one instance, and the same leftover without its note ⇒ the next start's «earlier» mark; a retry in flight while the set fails again keeps that failure's mark. (test-ledger-whole-law has no unlink-fault leg — the r17 probe's scene lives here.)

### bl-chat-a — B-b291: a cleared group message is not found by Search everything
- THE GAP: the search index (src/search-index-worker.js, search.db) took every user / assistant card as written and never heard a clear, so a cleared group message stayed findable through every copy it held: a report card the ring placed live (`<sid>:gm:<group>:<instant>`), a wake's card (the ladder's, its own id, the words as written), a transcript's wake frame converted into a peer card (claude, codex — its text drops the report head: only `peerGroup` names the group), a report pasted into a typed message (the head stays), a harness card that carries no group at all (the Antigravity wrapper's peer marker drops it). The record-clear census had declared the index a transcript-class copy.
- THE PROOF is the release's own, not the held store-writer follow-up's (proveDrawn / GC.proveMessage ride no train): the ladder judge's witness — the first 40 code points of the folded words, read from the log by `originalsOf`, cached per group by the size of its cleared index. The rule moved into PURE record-clear.js (`clearWitness`, `redactWitnessLines` with a substring floor and a whole-line set) so the ladder and the index share it; the ladder keeps its floor of 4.
- WHAT THE ENGINE HANDS (`clearedCopies(gid?, {cachedOnly})`, `clearedCopiesAsync()`): per group the card keys (`<group>:<record instant>`), the witnesses and the whole-message digests (sha256, 22 chars) of every FORM the words take in a copy — the record's bytes, a report line's (`G.reportWords`: folded, cut, belted — a control character is a space, a format character gone) and a card's (`GC.normalizeCard`: control characters out, TEXT_MAX). Never a record. The clear's own records grow the cache (`noteClearedNeedles`) — no re-read of the log; a set missing a record is read again after 10 min. At a boot the set is read OFF THE LOOP (`originalsOfAsync`: readTailAsync in 64 KB windows).
- THE DOORS: the channels wiring sets the source and its clear hook calls `SEARCH.noteCleared(gid)`. Every worker's FIRST op is `setCleared` (one FIFO ⇒ before any row): the hub hands its cache (`whole: false`), the whole set follows as `addCleared({whole: true})` and a search waits for it (≤ 5 s); a row written in between is swept then. `judgeRow` runs before every insert: a card id `gm:<key>` of a cleared key → the sentence; a row whose folded text IS a cleared form (digest + length) → the sentence — of its group, or of NO group when the message is ≥ 12 units; a line carrying a witness ≥ 12 units, or being a shorter one whole (its «Name: » tail, a report line's await note set aside), in a card of that group (`grp`) or a text naming `(<gid>)` → the sentence line. `sweepCleared` rewrites the rows already written: the group's cards (partial index `msg_grp`), the reports naming it (the FTS phrase of the group id), the rows holding a long message whole (the FTS words of its witness, a cut last word dropped). Meta `clearedSig` (keys + counts, no words) skips a sweep of a set already swept. `secure_delete` on.
- SCHEMA 2: `msg.grp` + `msg_grp`. A schema change drops and rebuilds the index — the only way the rows the release already wrote are judged; one idle-paced backfill per hub after the update.
- THE ADVERSARIAL READ (one fresh reader on the diff, before the line): F1 a card holding a message as written whose first line carries the whole witness kept its later lines → the whole digests; F2 an Antigravity card names no group → digests on rows of no group (≥ 12 units); F3 a format / control character in the first 40 → the belted forms; F4 a boot and every clear past 8 read whole logs on the loop → grown from the clear's records, the boot set async; F5 a cut token in the sweep's query → the group id's phrase + the witness words without the cut word; F6 a 4-unit witness cleared every line holding it → floor 12 in the index; F7 the await note → set aside; F8 a set missing a record cached for ever → retried; F9 old bytes → secure_delete + the FTS leftover declared; F10 (a snippet cut inside the sentence shows its English piece) named, not cured.
- NAMED, NOT CURED: an agent quoting the words in its OWN reply (no group, not the whole message) — the transcript class; a cleared record past REPLACEMENT_READ_MAX (5000) in one group.

### lg-remote-hardening unit 1 — B-7f0b: the plugin-git ssh host-key pin (q-042 D6, merged B-4ff5)
- THE HOLE: src/server/plugin-install.js handed git `StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new` with the hub user's default known_hosts. A pod has no known_hosts, so every fresh hub's first credential-bearing ssh clone trusted whatever key answered (a man-in-the-middle window that carries the deploy key).
- THE PIN: the plugin-git row gains an optional, NOT secret, multiline `knownHosts` (validator `knownHosts` = ssh-key-format `parseKnownHosts`, PURE).
  - `pinnedHostsText` keeps the keys for THIS host's ssh name: a plain name, `[host]:port` off port 22, a hashed `|1|` name checked by HMAC-SHA1, or a bare `type key` line. Each is written under that name as a 0600 `known_hosts` in the same shredded `.cred-*` folder.
  - ssh then runs `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` over that file alone (`GlobalKnownHostsFile=/dev/null`; the path is double-quoted inside the -o value, because ssh splits option values on spaces).
  - A pin that cannot be read, or that names no key for the host, is refused as `plugin_git_hostkey` before git runs, in 'auto' too.
  - ssh's own refusals (Host key verification failed / REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED / No … host key is known) now read as `plugin_git_hostkey`, with the fingerprint the host showed. They used to read as plugin_git_auth.
  - No pin ⇒ the road is unchanged.
- NOT IN THE TREE: the cluster preset's GitHub / GitLab key values live in the presets Secret (a cluster write). deploy/README now says how to fill `knownHosts`.
- PROOF:
  - fast test-plugin-trust ③d: the PURE parse table + the row's validator; a recorded pinned clone (only this host's keys, under the alias, 0600, in the key's folder, shredded — hard-link witness); a port host's pin; the refusals before git runs; ssh's words, the changed banner vs a bare «Host key verification failed» on each road.
  - heavy test-plugin-git-clone ⑨ (THE TIER RULE: no real ssh in the fast tier): a private sshd on loopback run as a -D child (scratch host keys, AuthorizedKeysFile /dev/null, no login), real git + real ssh through a routing shim. A wrong pin ⇒ plugin_git_hostkey with the stand-in's real fingerprint; the right pin ⇒ past the host-key check to plugin_git_auth, read from a root with a space in its path. RED: an accept-new copy trusts the stand-in's key on the same wrong pin.
- ADVERSARIAL READ (cured in this commit): real ssh legs moved out of the fast tier; HostKeyAlias added (a hub ssh config rewriting HostName / Port moved the lookup off the pinned lines); a bare «Host key verification failed» on an unpinned anonymous clone stays plugin_git_auth; the stand-in sshd is a child that dies with the suite; the card shows a long public multiline value as its first line + the count.
- TRAP (measured): real ssh expands `~` from the passwd entry, never $HOME. The first run of that RED copy appended a fixture line to the box user's real ~/.ssh/known_hosts; it was removed by hand (91 bytes). The shim now hands any command naming no UserKnownHostsFile a scratch file.

### bl-browser-a — B-346d: the live view's watch follows its browser across a daemon restart
- THE CAUSE (read; the row's real-Chrome reproduction is owed to a real-driver leg the integrator runs — this box runs the real driver only through the tree's legs): a conversation's own browser's CDP url was cached per CONVERSATION (keeper withCdpUrl, key `child:<conversation>`), and cdpEndpointFor's answer never fails, so nothing evicted it — and the dialog watch's `down()` deletes the watch, so every later arm asked with `fresh: false`. After the daemon restarted (a new Chrome on a new port) every arm — the verb's, the view's, a re-arm, Retry — got the OLD port: the owner's ECONNREFUSED, then «not watching».
- THE FIX: the url is cached per RUN of the browser (`childUrlKey` — PURE in browser-profiles: the record's start, else its pid; the previous runs' urls dropped), so a relaunched daemon's key misses and the url is asked of the live daemon (never ephemerals() on the way — one profile looked up). And the watch comes back by itself while a live view is open: the keeper gives it its viewer count (`viewersFor`); a failed socket re-arms while a person holds the browser OR a view watches it (bounded as before), and a browser STARTED AGAIN under an open view is armed at once. The accepted rule stands: nobody browsing it and no view open ⇒ no re-arm, its next verb arms it. A disarm now also ends a stopped browser's pending re-arm and its tries.
- LEGS: test-browser-keeper (the run key: one run one key, a relaunch a new key, the pid, no record + the wiring + a CONTROL: one key per conversation ⇒ the old port); test-browser-passkey (an agent's browser with its view open re-armed by itself; a browser started again under an open view watched at once; the accepted CONTROL: nobody looking ⇒ neither).
- NOT IN THIS BATCH (the lane's adversarial read): law 2 («ended», not «idled out»). The words alone contradict the record's own stoppedBy (the Housekeeping chip, the kept note), one road stamps the last command just before it judges (takeover C3: a real idle-out would read «ended 0 s after»), and test-browser-ephemeral (heavy) pins the old words — a unit of its own, with the cause measured by the real driver. Law 3 (the banners) likewise, for want of a picture: a live view of a running agent browser needs the real driver.

### bl-loop-a B-f35e — the usage fold's soft cap judged the heap's READING, not what the fold holds
- THE CAUSE: src/usage-cold-worker.js refused a fold when `used_heap_size` passed the cap at a 2 000-row check. That reading counts what the collector has not taken yet (the young generation too). Where the soft cap is the only bound — a parent `--max-old-space-size` replaces the Worker's resourceLimits (V8 flags are process-wide; `execArgv: []` since 2.369.246 does not stop it), or a cap under `_spawnJob`'s 64 MB floor — the collector lets the reading run far past the held set: 800 MB held read 1551 MiB of a 1536 cap and was refused «retrying will not help» (measured 11-12 by B-a77d's lane).
- THE FIX: the judge follows WHERE THE WORKER'S LIMIT IS (src/cache-bounds.js `foldCapRule`, PURE). Where the cap is the old-space limit V8 kept (the production hub: no parent flag) the release's reading check stands — judged on the held set, a fold too big would die of the limit with «retry» (adversarial read, finding 1). Where the limit is elsewhere (a parent flag; a cap under the 64 MB floor) a reading over the cap is judged after ONE full collection of the worker's own heap (`overCap`), refused only if what it still holds is over («N MB still held after a collection, at R rows»); after a collection that fits, the next waits until the reading has grown a quarter of the cap past the held set (no collection per check near the cap). The collector: the process's own `gc` under --expose-gc, else reached once through `vm.runInNewContext('gc')` with the flag set and cleared at once. The main loop never waits on it.
- MEASURED (this tree, §30's month: 120 000 rows, 5 000-row chunks, the 64 MB floor): the chunks HOLD 7.8–9.6 MB after a collection and READ 10.5–30.3 MB (29 of 60 checks over 20 MB, three runs alike); the whole group holds 58 MB after a collection.
- LEGS: test-cache-bounds §30b — the chunks under a 20 MB cap fold all 120 000 rows; RED CONTROL: the reading judged everywhere (a worker copy with the rule forced to 'reading') refuses them FOLD_TOO_BIG; §30's whole-group control still refuses (58 > 46) and names what is held; §30c (PURE) the rule at the measured shapes (the hub as shipped reads; a parent 4 096 flag and the 64 MB floor hold); §14 (a 4 MB cap under a parent 4096 flag) still refuses (the worker's own heap after a collection is over 4 MB), its no-soft-cap control's needle follows the new check.

### bl-loop-a B-b17f — the groups engine's boot warm-up held the loop 80–100 ms a turn for 8 s
- THE CAUSE (measured 11-13 with the shape C reader's cost driver; reproduced here: 40 groups × 2 000 records, a 5 ms gap clock, the longest gaps 47–63 ms, 10 over 20 ms): `warm()` in src/server/groups-engine.js walked four groups per setImmediate, and for each the owner's `unreadFor` and every member's ran `readLog` — the store's SYNC readTail of up to LOG_READ (2 000) records, parsed in full — once per reader: (1 + members) whole reads per group, four groups a turn.

### digit-zero — what an agent types arrives; a fill that cannot set a field says so (主开发 2026-11-17 20:26Z, from the owner's own agent)
- **The report:** on a web form's native date field, `keyboard type 01072027` left the year 0227, month 01, day 07; four presses for 2027 gave 227; `fill` of an ISO date answered Done and left the field empty.
- **The measurement** (a loopback form logging every key and input event; Chrome 154 headless, headed on Xvfb, and through the tree's real cdp-mediator — identical; the driver this tree pins, 0.38.2, the box's only one): `press <digit>` is a real keyDown / keyUp (code Digit0, windowsVirtualKeyCode 48, text "0") and every digit arrives in every field, the zero included; `keyboard type` and `type <sel>` send one Input.insertText per character, `fill` one of the whole text — a native date / time field takes none of it, nothing lands, and the driver answers «✓ Done»; `press Digit0` sends the code as the key with no text. The wrapper's own argv keeps every zero; the mediator never rewrites an Input call. The owner's zero-less date (non-zero digits ARRIVED) stays unplaced: 主开发 asks the reporting conversation for its exact lines.
- **The cure, in the wrapper (no fork of the driver):** every fill / type / keyboard type is read back before it answers. A date / time / datetime-local / month / week field (and a colour / range control) gets the value through its own setter in the form its kind accepts, read back; another form is refused `field_form` with the form; nothing landed is refused `nothing_landed`; a different value is said `field_differs` — never «Done». A press of a key's code is refused `key_code_name` with the key's name. The manual teaches the date / time recipe and a file into a frame's file input (`frame <its selector>` → `upload <the input>` → `frame main`).
- **For the vendor (one paragraph, to file):** agent-browser 0.38.2 — `keyboard type <text>` (documented as «Type text with real keystrokes») and `type <sel> <text>` send one `Input.insertText` per character, and `fill <sel> <text>` focuses, clears and sends one `Input.insertText` of the whole text. A native `<input type=date|time|datetime-local|month|week>` (and `color` / `range`) accepts no inserted text, so all three land nothing in such a field — no input event fires — while the CLI answers «✓ Done». Expected: `keyboard type` dispatches key events as `press` already does correctly (keyDown with code / key / text, then keyUp), and `fill` either sets a typed field through its value setter or fails when the value read back is not the one asked. Also `press Digit0` (a `KeyboardEvent.code`) sends key "Digit0" with no text and types nothing — map the code or refuse it. Repro: a page with `<input type=date>`; `focus` it; `keyboard type 01072027`; `get value` ⇒ empty after «✓ Done» (Chrome 154, Linux, headless and headed).

### B-403e (lane bl-accounts; 主开发 2026-11-18 02:38Z, GO 02:58Z) — ONE ASK PER FILE PER SYNCHRONOUS RUN: the pool pass, a record, a broadcast
- **The witness** (the production hub's last five hours, every hold over 1 s ranked by the site its sample names): about forty percent of the held time was ONE synchronous function, the pool pass `maybePoolAutoSwitchForPool`, asking the SAME files on the data mount again and again — each member's reading about S·(M+2)·(1–2) times, each conversation's link 6–8 times, each member's credential file about 9 + 2·S/M times; ≈ 1,250–1,970 synchronous mount asks per pass at the witness's size over ≈ 90 distinct files (the first line's count, by reading).
- **The change — src/run-reads.js:** within one synchronous run each file under the watched folders (the readings `data/usage-cache`, the logins `data/subs` + `codex-subs`, the links `data/pool-links`, the estimator's anchors) is asked AT MOST ONCE and every reader in that run shares the answer — an error included (a missing file and the mount's own error alike: each caller does with it exactly what it did with its own failed read). The memo lives exactly as long as the run (dropped at its microtask checkpoint). A credential file's stat and text ride ONE open (`facts`; a failure other than «no such file» still carries the file's mtime, so `loginState` answers «unreadable, written at T» as before); a link's existence is its readlink's answer (`entryExists`: EINVAL = an entry that is no link = exists, as the lstat answered).
- **A read after a write of this process in the same run sees the write — BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a list:** the `fs` write functions are wrapped once in run-reads; any synchronous write under a watched folder, whoever makes it, drops the run's memo whole. (No module of the tree destructures `fs`; an ESM named import sees the wrapper through `syncBuiltinESMExports`.) A write by another process or thread (the statusline, the device agent, the store writer's worker) is concurrent with the run exactly as it is today; an fd-based write is seen at its write-flagged open.
- **Routed:** the engine (the reading, the raw cache, the identity-group walk, the sealed orders' readlink, the credential stat, the four link lstats, the panels' cache reads), accounts (poolCurrent, poolCurrentFor, the placement lstat, the link folder readdir; it watches its folders), harnesses/claude.js (parseClaudeAuth, claudeLoginState), src/login-state.js (loginState), src/usage-estimator.js (the anchor files' signature stats). No decision changes, no reading is attributed differently, no rejection is counted differently: the money suites run untouched.
- **Words only (the coordinator's ruling 1):** the eval gate's comment named one force; it now names the six, each by its reason. THE GATE ITSELF IS UNCHANGED — its stamp is set only after a default switch (born a switch floor in 2.252.0, renamed «last DECISION» in 2.266.1 with its setter left where it was); filed as its own row.
- **For step two (ruling 2, not here):** every stop of a pooled conversation forces a WHOLE-pool pass, so S stops cost S² decisions — «a stop re-decides only that conversation» is a decision change, for the hardening work (decide from memory, design-account-hardening.md §4.1).
- **Censuses restated:** mount-reader (accounts 22→20, the engine 23→11, login-state's row gone, usage-estimator 12→7, run-reads +7) and sync-fs (accounts 37→33, the engine 25→12, login-state's row gone, usage-estimator 13→8, run-reads +8); the loop census owns run-reads under «money».
- **The cure on top (the coordinator's own read, 03:15Z — none changes the design):** (1) THE WRITES TABLE IS A RATCHET over the running runtime — the suite classes every Sync function of `fs` as a read, a path write (run-reads `WRITES`, now with mkdtempSync, mkdtempDisposableSync, chownSync, lchownSync) or a descriptor call, an unclassed one red; one table-driven leg makes every path write between two asks in one run seen by the second. (2) ONE WRAPPER PER PROCESS, found by a process-wide key (`Symbol.for('vibespace.run-reads.writes')`), never a mark on a function (the loop witness copies a wrapped function's own properties): it drops the memo of EVERY copy of the module; the witness installed after it keeps it inside. (3) A CENSUS DERIVED BY SEARCH: no module of src or server.js destructures or aliases an fs write function (by design: run-reads, loop-blame). (4) NO WRITE THROUGH SOMETHING THAT IS NOT fs under the watched folders: the synchronous children in the tree (the oat probe's scratch, cli-env's --help/xset/xauth, usage-routes' keychain read) write none there, and no writer of those folders keeps a descriptor open across runs. (5) THE HEADER SAYS what the microtask checkpoint means: for a run begun in a macrotask, a nextTick callback it queued and a promise continuation already queued share the answers; a leg pins it. AND the readings folder is now registered by the engine (`RR.watch(USAGE_CACHE_DIR)`, missing at a5bab1744 — found curing).
- **The cure for the readers' round (the coordinator's seven musts + four of its shoulds + three from the lane's own reader, 03:25Z; the design stands):** (M1) the readings folder is watched (d06924379) and a leg DERIVES it — every path the routed readers ask in a pass, a record and a broadcast is under a watched folder, RED an engine that does not watch its readings; (M2) memberLoginState's cross-run signature is the file's stat whenever a stat answers, exactly as at the release (a read failing while the stat answers keeps the remembered state; «present but unreadable» never shares «missing»'s signature), a leg per scene with the a5bab1744 line as its red; (M3) leg four's red control watches the same folders as the owners (a copy with an empty watch list memoized nothing); (M4) the fast cap restated by arithmetic, the row's time measured; (M5) NOTHING AT LOAD — the first watch() wraps fs's writes, never a require (the claude harness descriptor reaches the helper, and the device agent's bundle and workers load it: they watch nothing), the helper classed SHARED in test-architecture, a child-process leg with the load-time wrap as its red; (M6) A LOOK-AGAIN READ asks the mount itself — `forget(dir)` before every check whose purpose is «look again before I write»: ensureSessionPoolLink and setPoolTarget (a billing link written to a member), pendingSignin and discardPendingSignin (a row handed to a sign-in or removed), reloginResolve (a login moved), and the ledger's «from» before each re-point; a leg per site where ANOTHER process changes the folder mid-run (the run's memo still answers the old state — the control in kind); the read-modify-write readers of the usage cache stay direct (fresh by design); (M7) the counting leg's FLOOR (every member's reading and sign-in file and every conversation's link asked at least once — the pass ran), its counter keyed by path AND kind, the law judged between two writes of this process (a pass that moves a conversation writes; a STEADY second pass must write nothing). Also: a write through a DESCRIPTOR is seen (a write-flagged open under a watched folder marks its descriptor until closeSync; FD_WRITES wrapped, a table-driven leg); a failed fstat carries the path's stat; `dropRun()` exported for a write no wrapper sees (the store writer's worker hand-off); the loop witness names the real caller, never run-reads; the token signature and the api-window sidecar read route through the helper; the helper's own mutants (the write-flagged open's row, the folder test's separator, the stat on an error, «not a link», the listing's copy) each caught in a child process. Two money suites counted the MEMO, not the code, and now count the code: test-pool-auto r2 ③ (its per-roster probe shared the run of the roster call before it — 0 reads) and test-auto-cli-tick-reads §4 (the reverted tick rode the memo too) — each counts with every routed ask going to the mount, its pins exact, its red control the release's faulty form.
- **The cure's gate, every red read (66600b92e: 11 red, both zones):** ONE PRODUCT ANSWER HAD CHANGED, and it is put back: setPoolTarget's «is the target signed in» check went through the look-again door, which read with `readSubCreds` where the release reads with `_readAuthFor(be, subId)` — the same file and parser, but test-oat-identity states an oat-held member signed in by replacing `_readAuthFor` on the instance, and the new call went around it («subscription not logged in»). THE SLOT LAW (test-oat-materialize: ensureSessionPoolLink / setPoolTarget byte-identical) was red for the same lines. Both slot writers are their release text again; their look-again (forget the member's folder, the conversation's link and the pool's default link) runs in front of them, from a table outside their text. The other reds were pins: test-oat-mint ⑧ (accounts.js's require edges: + ./run-reads.js), test-pool-serve-lapsed (it compiles a slice of the engine with no `RR` — the reading came back null), test-architecture §78 (`_lookAgain` branched on the harness: now claude-only), and this suite's first pass (the estimator's two once-per-process reads of rates.json, named and pinned once per process). THE DOUBLE ASK of each sign-in file was a memo drop by the pass's own write: on a fresh data dir the estimator's first write creates its anchors folder (once per process); the steady pass writes nothing and asks every file exactly once. The instruments that name a site now pass the helper's frames, as the loop witness does: the boot trace and loop-hold's instrument files (else a channel store's write would be booked to the helper). Suites that wrap fs themselves: test-key-file-law's belt passes the helper's frames, test-ledger-whole-law arms the helper before its fault shim takes the originals, store-slow-preload skips the helper's frames, test-login-expiry's pin reads the write time from the same open. test-auto-cli-tick-reads counts BOTH ticks with the memo off (the fixed tick too: the old tick put back would otherwise read green). The lane's own second reader found the one remaining hole in «by construction»: with VIBESPACE_BOOT_TRACE=1 the boot trace wraps fs's writes BEFORE the first watch and, ~90 s later, put the originals back over the helper's wrappers for the life of the hub — its undo now restores only while it is the outermost and otherwise turns into a pass-through (a child-process leg, the release's undo its red). Also: a read before the api-window sidecar is rewritten, and both pool self-heals before they re-point the default, look again; a falsy thrown value is still the run's answer. THE CLASS IS PINNED: test-pool-pass-reads ⑯ finds by parse every site in the tree that assigns into fs (a binding of fs, a member chain of one, a parameter defaulted to or handed one) — today three, each rowed with its undo: this helper and the loop witness (never undone), the boot trace (restores only while outermost); a fourth is red, a planted control counts five — and runs each row's install and undo in a fresh process, after which a path write, a descriptor write and a rename under a watched folder still drop the memo. The 2ae16d9e9 gate's reds: test-account-reset-door's cache-read census counted the sidecar's look-again line (+1, a forget, no new reader); test-auto-cli-tick-reads in UTC counted 635 against 600 with the memo off, because a sign-in read is now one open plus a read through its descriptor where memberLoginState's release form was a stat (the counter now counts path-named asks — a descriptor's read is its open's); test-loop-hold ⑫ and test-loop-census (d) are red in packed runs with the unit and without it (the train checkpoint's whole tier on 191e02d46) and green alone; they run on the test machine's serial lane since 05:09Z (row B-518e). NEVER MORE THAN THE RELEASE, ON ANY ROAD: memberLoginState's signature was the one road that asked more — the release stat its file, the cure opened and read it — so `signature(p)` answers it from this run's read of the file when one was made (no ask), else with ONE stat, as the release did; the counting law is per file AND question (a sign-in file is asked twice only when its signature came before its content). test-auto-cli-tick-reads §4 gets what §3 has — a fixed clock and a fixed rand handed to the tick — and its count ends when the tick's own promise settles (the 5 ms after it is the loop-gap probe's, never the count's): the counts are EXACT now — 395 / 520 / 625, reverted 11073 / 41500, the same in both zones (the test machine's «box» zone is UTC too: the earlier 635 was the clock and the window, not a date). ## 2.369.408 — 2026-11-17

### hub-loop-stalls — HOTFIX: the live view's picture shows the tab it says it shows (the owner's inc-mwl4yeom)
- THE OWNER, 2026-11-17: the agent's browser view stopped changing; later, «two tabs in the row, I switch to the form one and it still shows the gmail page».
- THE CAUSE: every tab VibeSpace opens for a holder opens in a window of its own (src/browser-windows.js), but a viewer's X ticket named ONE window. The keeper read the lease's own window first, and nothing re-issued the ticket when the tab on show moved. The agent's new tab, a person's chip and a tab opened while the page was hidden all left the first window on screen until a new viewer attached.
- THE CURE: PURE `xShownTarget` / `xWindowLookups` / `xTicketMoved` in src/browser-picture.js:
  - the keeper reads the window of the tab on show first;
  - the relay's `xFollow` re-issues a viewer's ticket when that window moved — on an active-tab change, a watch, a return to following, or a failed watch;
  - the page re-mounts its X view on the new ticket.
- PROOF:
  - test-browser-picture §8b (fast, 3.6 s). On the release's relay, placed on the scene, the viewer stayed on the first window for the agent's new tab, a chip, following again and a tab opened while hidden. On the hotfix it follows each. The release's order and ticket rule are the red controls;
  - test-browser-x-picture ⑦ (heavy, the integrator's run).
- ITS CURE ROUND (主开发 21:14Z, three readers, one refuter), each law with a leg and a red control (test-browser-picture §8c):
  - (1) a stale first look (the keeper's 750 ms row cache) is looked at again with FRESH rows, up to three times inside about two seconds; still untold ⇒ SAID, and the page shows its own picture of the tab;
  - (2) another holder's tab, watched through a chip, is drawn with the WATCH seat and never sized;
  - (3) the page's own ask is always answered, even when a follow supersedes it;
  - a burst of tab flips is one keeper ask per viewer, and a viewer that left is skipped.
- CURE ROUND 2 (主开发 22:13Z): test-browser-x-picture ⑦, run alone by the integrator on real xpra, was RED. The picture kept the old window for the agent's new tab, «connected», with no «untold».
  - «Moved» is now judged by the tab's own CDP window (PURE xFollowVerdict). The bounds match only FINDS an X row: a new window at the old one's place and size is missing from the rows until xpra maps it, while the old row still matches.
  - A tab whose window is not told yet is waited for, SAID: the page shows its own picture of the tab with «waiting for this tab's window» (en / zh / ja). Fresh looks, bounded at 10 s, then «could not be shown as a window». An unmounted view never reads «connected».
  - Proof: a stall leg holds the new window's row 2.05 s, past the old 1.95 s, with the tip's rule as red control. Step ⑦ asserts the page is never «connected» on the old window after a 1.5 s grace.
  - THE DIAGNOSTIC (one sanctioned run alone, with debug lines): on this suite's road the lease's own `tab new` lands IN its window. Both tabs had CDP window 862276532, every look answered X window 4194311 by bounds, and the stream's active flag moved correctly. Only a MEDIATED lease's tabs get windows of their own. So step ⑦'s first red was its fixture (it wanted a new window). ⑦ now walks both roads: the same window (the picture draws the new page there), and another window (a real second Chrome window, the agent switched to it).
- CURE ROUND 3 (主开发 22:36Z): a relay can outlive its browser's run, and a new Chrome hands out the same X ids under new CDP windows. So the minted windows and the tickets are kept PER RUN (the keeper's instance). A new run's answer mints; it is never a wait for an id the old run owned. Leg: the same X id under a new CDP window after a new run ⇒ a ticket. Red control: the run ignored ⇒ the viewer waits, locked out.
- NOT HERE (unit two): the view's own watch when a picture stops while its source moves (a held hub loop, a return from hidden), and a watch of a background tab that shares ONE window.
- Fast sum: test-browser-picture restated 1.5 → 6.5 s (its scenes side by side), so 1154.839 s over 599 rows and cap 1155 by arithmetic.

- THE FIELD MEASURE (the owner's hub, 24 h of the witness's own lines): 725 holds and 2 455 s in the kernel — 562 holds / 2 221 s at channel-store's writeJsonAtomic (adapters.json 549, groups.json 12), 19 / 75 s at peopleWrite's mkdirSync, 15 / 51 s at the poll-stamps snapshot's temp file. The data directory is on a fuse.bindfs mount (a create there ≈ 4 s).
- THE MOVE: adaptersUpdate, groupsUpdate, the outbox door, the aliases door, peopleWrite and the poll-stamps SNAPSHOT hand their bytes to the store writer (dirty with produce); the writer's thread makes a missing parent directory (0700) ONLY for a write that asks (`makeDir` — the people door, a new account's directory); any other store whose directory is gone fails ENOENT, said, as before (cure r1).
- TWO COLUMNS: a bookkeeping stamp (`adapters.update(fn, { paced: true })` — 15 sites: pass stamps, cursors and counters, host facts, push-lane stamps, the boot heal) resolves after the in-memory change and several coalesce; everything else is durable by default (a sign-in, a credential, an owner's act, the outbox's write-ahead — the attempt on disk before the send). Only a FAILED write rejects; «queued» is still owed.
- The poll-stamps journal's append and fold stay on the main thread — a named, pinned exception (an incident needs the kept descriptor to survive a kill); after a snapshot lands the journal is folded DOWN to the stamps set since its bytes were produced — one line each, written back in the same synchronous step as the truncate (cure r1, C2: the fold used to be skipped whenever a stamp came during the write's flight, ~4 s on the field's mount — a steady account never folded, the journal grew for the life of the process and the next boot replayed all of it on the main thread). The key-mint check reads the live records; close() flushes the moved files through the writer.
- STILL HOLDS, said in the kb: a synchronous flush behind a write in flight (the index's flush() on a person's clear-history, close()) waits up to the writer's bound — a third of the stop grace; and every LISTED row of the file (wake pace, dispatch ledger, lru, attachment / avatar metas, search memo, feed-miss memo, message / side-log appends and rewrites, audit, the outbox files' removal) — rows that only fall.
- THE CENSUS learns mkdirSync, openSync for write / append, rmSync and unlinkSync: the base's true debt is 904 (it said 516); of the 11 rows the unit touched, 10 sites MOVED to the writer and fell to zero, and 1 was RECLASSIFIED — the journal's truncate, now a named exception beside its append; DEBT_MAX 893. Cure r1 (C3): a door's body may not WAIT either — a writeNow, any flush or an Atomics.wait in it is red by name (a negative control proves it), and owe()'s one writeNow stands only after close().
- PROOF: a stall PLACED in every main-thread fs call under a scratch dir (scripts/fixtures/fs-stall.cjs) over one real pass of the fake adapter — 35 calls stalled and a timer 14 006 ms late on the base, 0 and 0 ms here (test-channel-store-loop-free); a slow writer (paced at once, durable on disk, queued never rejects); a kill right after the outbox's resolve finds the attempt; a flush behind a flying write bounded; test-store-slow-storage leg (o).
- THE NUMBER: the held seconds per day by cause, derived from the srv-loop-hold-ms rows the hub already keeps (UTC days: today, yesterday, seven days) — the summary's loopHeld and a table under Diagnostics' «Main loop held»; the srv-sync-fs-held-ms detail names its call site (site=src/channel-store.js:275 writeJsonAtomic).
- CURE ROUND 1 (the acceptance's three must-fixes, each a law; test-channel-store-writer-laws, fast 5.6 s — red on the first cut 44c05c1e8, green here):
  - C1, a warning that a sign-in did not reach the disk is withdrawn only by a write that LANDED: the pass's update is paced (memory), so «its refreshed sign-in could not be saved to disk» now waits for `store.adapters.landed()`; a write that fails again keeps it. (g): a sign-in rotated while the storage refuses (the fake adapter's named seam `VIBESPACE_CHANNELS_FAKE_ROTATE`, in its sign-in check) — on the first cut the same timer pass withdrew the item with nothing on disk; here it stays, and goes once adapters.json holds the token.

  - C3, the gate sees a door that waits: (i) the writer holds every write 600 ms — a paced update, a durable act and a group verb leave the main loop on time (worst lateness 0 ms); a door given a synchronous writeNow: 1 193 ms late, and census ② red by name.
  - Named, accepted as paced (a kill inside the writer's pace window loses them; each costs one more vendor call, none bills a turn or writes to a person): the feed's park after a vendor refusal, the learned rate ceiling, the push lane's demotion.
  - Noted, by design: a durable act on a storage that never answers waits with no word to the person (a channel pauses, it raises no alarm); close() outside an exit waits once per moved file, each up to the writer's bound; the outbox prune's removal stays on the main thread as its named row — if the day's number names it, it is the next door.

### session-events-ends (主开发 2026-11-16, after soak-can-fail) — nothing a device link armed outlives the link; the parity soak removed; parity as a deterministic leg
- U1, the device agent: the session-events watch ENDS WITH ITS LINK. `onDead` cleared the discovery watch and the usage-events watch but never this one — its one-second tick and its tails (a normalizer per pipe session) ran on for every dead link, in a daemon that outlives the hub, reading the sessions folder and normalizing every session's output once more per reconnect. Now the tick is cleared and the tails dropped at the link's death; the discovery watch's pending kick and the usage watch's pending kick / re-walk die with their link too (a dead link's usage watch walks no more). test-session-brain-dark counts it in the real daemon's reads (/proc/<pid>/io rchar with no link connected), red on 70efb5e10.
- U2, THE PARITY SOAK REMOVED: session-brain's dark comparator (`sbNoteServerOp`, `sbCompare`, its two rings, `sb-parity-hit` / `sb-parity-miss`, the `sb-parity-diverged` event and its log line), server.js's device-side ring loop and both server taps (ws-create, boot-restore) are gone — it could not fail from the day it was written (both taps read `op.msg`; every create carries `message`) and gated three activation switches for three months. The step-2/3 device feed is untouched (the raw records still fill a paired machine's conversation). CLAUDE.md's activation paragraph, the three-tier design's status and activation lines and the kb say it plainly; the switches stay off, no setting or default changed.
- U3, PARITY AS A DETERMINISTIC LEG: test-session-brain-dark feeds ONE recording (made once) to the daemon's REAL normalizer (its session-events stream) and to the server's, and compares the creates by id AND content in stream order — its control: a create's text changed, an id changed, a create missing, one extra, each red. CURED: the old parity leg read `e.msg?.id`, a field no create carries, and compared the text «undefined» with itself. A FAST leg in test-unknown-records («THE CREATE'S FIELD») pins the field a create carries — `message`, as the shared normalizer emits it (also after the JSON round trip the device stream makes) and as the hub reads it (the chat view, the message window): a rename is red in the fast tier.

### agent-lock-own-pid (主开发 2026-11-17, found by the pod design's skeptic) — a lock that names this process is stale
- The agent's one-instance lock lives in its state folder (in a fleet pod: the home volume, which outlives the container). A killed container's agent dies without its exit handler, so the lock keeps its pid; the next container's fresh process table can hand the new agent THE SAME pid — alive (it is the agent itself) and named like an agent, so `acquireSingleton` answered «a genuine second instance» and the agent refused to start, for good (the same after a reboot that repeats the number). A lock whose pid is this process's own is stale by definition (the agent has not written it yet): it is removed and taken. A dead pid is taken as before; a live sibling agent still refuses. test-agent-lock (fast, three real agents in scratch roots; red control = the release's agent refusing its own pid). The remaining hole — ANOTHER agent-named process reborn on the old pid — is not shown real and not built. The agent bundle changes: re-signed at the train's cut.

### keeper-sweep-yields — retiring orphan ephemeral browser records never holds the main loop (`src/server/browser-keeper.js`)
- **The incident (a fleet instance on 2.369.387, measured read-only by 主开发):** one conversation held 437 ephemeral CHILD browser records; when it went away the keeper's reconcile retired them all in ONE loop turn (the «takeover C3 (§5.2)» block's `Promise.all` over `retireEphemeral`), about one second per record on the main thread — the hub's witness said «pipe_read in read» (a fork wait). The liveness probe killed the hub after six minutes, six times; each boot removed some and the count persisted, so the sixth finished the list. Every conversation running there died at the first restart.
- **L2, the cause BY MEASUREMENT (`chrome-157/ksy/measure-retire.mjs`, a scratch registry, a stand-in browser CLI on PATH, every child start counted with its frame):** a record whose browser record still read `ready` but whose daemon was GONE went through `stop()`, whose `rt.closeAll` ran the browser CLI's `close --all` under that record's own session — ONE child start per record (`src/browser-facts.js` `run` ⇒ `execFile`): 300 records ⇒ 302 starts (the 2 others: the keeper's once-per-boot `--version`). A child start forks the whole hub and holds its main thread until the child execs: on a hub of several GB that is the field's second. A stopped record started none. THE CURE: `retireEphemeral` judges the daemon first — a live-looking LOCAL record whose daemon is gone (dead, recycled, never recorded; not starting, not stopping) is recorded stopped by the tick's own act (`markEphemeralGone`: its left browser reaped by identity, the reap awaited) and removed, with NO CLI start; a daemon that runs is still closed by the CLI (one start per LIVE browser). 300 ⇒ 2 starts.
- **L1, THE SWEEP IN BOUNDED STEPS:** `retireInSteps` — one record per step, the loop given back before each (`setImmediate`), at boot and on the tick alike (both read `reconcile`'s `retired`); a record whose conversation is carried again by the time its step comes is kept. Measured over 300 records in the scratch process: the worst loop hold 443 ms ⇒ 23 ms (records left `ready`), 155 ms ⇒ 18 ms (stopped records: on 2.369.404 each removal committed the whole registry, so one turn of 300 removals grew with the count).
- **L3, the lifecycle as the code has it:** a sub-agent's child handle (`newChild`, «reaped with the parent») and the ephemeral record its first verb makes live EXACTLY as long as the parent conversation is carried (reconcile §3.7: the same rule and grace as a lease); the browser idles out and the record stays, stopped; only a JOB's handle is dropped earlier (`releaseJobHandle` ⇒ `dropChild` ⇒ its record retired). No record outlives both its browser and its handle while the parent lives — the 437 were the parent's, by design (the cap: 999 handles per conversation). A bound on live children is not built: after the cure a dead child record costs one step with no child start; a live one, one CLI close.
- **L4:** the walk's removals reach the registry file once per piece of the walk and at its end (F5), and at an orderly stop (K1: the keeper's shutdown writes what the walk deferred); a restart redoes at most one piece — pinned (③, and a stop mid-walk in ⑧).
- **The legs (`scripts/test-keeper-sweep-yields.mjs`, fast, in-process, the REAL keeper):** ① 50 and 300 orphan records — the records retired per loop turn COUNTED (a setImmediate ticker numbers the turns; a 1 ms stall placed in each removal by `Atomics.wait`; a timer's lateness printed as evidence only — test-ci-gate §2e: no wall-clock bound in a fast suite): one per turn on the tip at reconcile, boot and tick; on 2.369.404 50 and 300 in one turn (lateness 70 ms and 510 ms); MUTANT the yield removed ⇒ 300 in one turn. ② 300 records left `ready` with gone daemons: 0 browser-CLI starts (counted through the runtime's `execFileImpl` seam) on the tip, 300 on 2.369.404; CONTROL a running daemon (a process of the test, its start time recorded) is still closed (1 start) and ended; MUTANT the judgment removed ⇒ 300. ③ the file loses one record per step; a keeper booted over a copy taken after 40 of 120 retires exactly the 80 left. ④ the child handle lives with its parent and goes with it. FAST_SUM_CAP_MS by arithmetic for the new row — on 2.369.406 the release's 1110.989 s over 591 + the row restated 6.1 s with legs ⑨ ⑩ (alone ×3: 6.09 / 6.03 / 6.05 s) = 1117.089 s over 592 ⇒ 1118 s.
- **The follow-up (主开发's three fixups after the take):** F1 A CLAIMED LAW HAS A LEG — among 20 orphans, the one whose lease comes back before its step is kept, its browser record untouched (still `ready`), no CLI start, the other 19 go (⑤; on 2.369.404 it is stopped first). F2 NOTHING OF A CARRIED CONVERSATION IS ENDED BY THE SWEEP — `retireEphemeral` reads the lease again after the reap's await and before the stop: a stall PLACED in the reap's window (its scan by launch mark held open; the conversation resumes there — its lease back, its browser started again) ⇒ the record kept and that browser left running (⑥); on b93d46418, and in a mutant without the re-read, the browser the conversation had just started was closed (1 CLI start, the process ended). F3 THE FIELD'S SHAPE — 30 records left `ready` with a scratch directory and a launch mark each pay the reap's own road (the directory's lock read, a /proc walk by mark each — counted: 30; ~27 ms a walk here, asynchronous) and still start no child, one per loop turn. Then two more from the design run: F4 THE WHOLE TURN THE CONVERSATION ENDS IN — a conversation with 300 leases, 300 child handles and 300 records ends at run time (the tick, past the grace): the one turn that drops its leases and reaps its handles is counted — in-memory acts only (0 registry writes, 0 broadcasts, 0 child starts in it; the loop spans ~3 ms for the 600 items), so nothing of those loops changes — then its records retire one per turn (⑦). F5 ONE REGISTRY WRITE AND ONE BROADCAST PER PIECE OF THE WALK, NOT PER RECORD — a removal the walk makes (its id in `sweepIds`) marks `sweepDirty` instead of committing; `retireInSteps` commits once per piece of `SWEEP_PIECE_MS` = 250 ms of the REAL clock and at its end (the keeper's `batched()` is synchronous, so around an async walk it would defer every other conversation's commit too): 300 removals ⇒ 2 writes and 2 broadcasts (300 and 300 before); the file loses a piece per write and a boot over a copy taken at a write mid-walk retires exactly what is left (③); MUTANT the batching dropped ⇒ 300, red (⑧). THE RETIRE'S «GONE» IS SEEN (the unit's last commit): `retireEphemeral` takes its no-start road only for a daemon the keeper has SEEN gone (`daemonSeenGone` — a recorded pid that is not there, or is another process now by its start time); a record with no pid or no recorded start time cannot be told, and its daemon is closed by the CLI as before — the tick's wider `daemonGone` would read the absent fact as «gone» and leave a live daemon and its browser running. After a restart the recorded pids are not there (seen gone), so the fast road is unchanged. ⑨: a live daemon with no pid, and one with no start time, is closed (1 start, ended) — red on 9f06f4872 (0 starts, left running); MUTANT the tick's judgment ⇒ red. THE UNION'S RED (2.369.406, test-browser-mediation-chrome ⑧b) was something else: the leg retired a record its conversation still HELD, which F2 keeps with its browser (the base stopped it first); every product caller lets go of the lease first — the leg now detaches first (test-only, 9f06f4872; ⑩ pins the retire's contract). The last round (K1–K4): the keeper's `shutdown()` writes what the walk deferred (`dirty || sweepDirty`) — a stop mid-walk leaves on disk what memory holds (red on 100600670: 60 on disk, 50 in memory); the writes and broadcasts are asserted as COUNTS bounded by the pieces the walk spanned in the same run (`floor(span / SWEEP_PIECE_MS) + 1`, the constant exported; a slower machine spans more pieces, never fewer) and below the removals — never a ceiling a clock decides; the incident's entry in kb-bugfix-invariants and the keeper's line in kb-file-structure.

### ps-zone (主开发 2026-11-17) — ps prints a process's start in the zone the parser reads it in
- `starts()` in src/agentd/stream-mac.js ran `ps -o pid= -o lstart=` with the helper's env plus the C locale, and src/machine-window.js `psStarts` parses the printed start with `Date.parse` in THIS process's zone. When the helper's env carried no zone while the process had one (an agent started with TZ set; every lane's UTC run of test-stream-mac on a box in another zone), each start was off by the two zones' offset against the launch time the window look compares it with. The ps call now carries `TZ: process.env.TZ` — none when the process has none (an undefined entry leaves a child's env, so ps reads the machine's own zone, as the parse does).
- test-stream-mac §4b: the suite's zone set away from the machine's, the real read lands within its bound; RED CONTROL, the release's call — 825 min off (Asia/Kathmandu against a −0800 box). The twin road (src/proc-identity.js:71) inherits the process's env and compares the `lstart` TEXT, never parsed: it agrees within one process.

### hub-loop-stalls — loop-day-report (a measurement release: the main loop's hour in the journal, readable without the page)
- THE LINE: once an hour (the UTC hour) and once at exit, ONE `[loop-hour]` / `[loop-exit]` line of a fixed shape (PURE src/loop-day-report.js `line`, its own check `LINE_RE`): held seconds and holds, the longest, the busy share, the three top causes, the engines' shares of the busy time, memory (the hub's heap and RSS; its processes by kind), the sizes and the hour's counts. Every field always present — a value never read prints `?`, never 0. Counts and code paths only: a cause is a code location of the hub's own or one of the hold verdict's fixed words, else «(other)».
- M1: the held seconds per day by cause (Telemetry.heldDays → the summary's loopHeld, ⚙ Diagnostics «Held per day, by cause»; the sync-fs held metric names its call site) — the channel store unit's «number» commit, cut alone on 2.369.405: it needs nothing of that unit's move.
- M2: every hold the watchdog books is handed to the hour as it is booked (src/server/loop-holds.js `onEach`) — one entry per cause, never a walk over rows; the busy share = performance.eventLoopUtilization between two cuts.
- M3: the engines' shares of the busy time — the watchdog thread's CENSUS (src/loop-census.js, its own commit): a tick about once a second over the hour, an ask only when the main thread is on the CPU and nothing else asks (a hold, a profile or a capture takes the census's ask over); the answer booked on the family of the innermost frame of the hub's own code (channels, pool, parse, browser, jobs, page, hook, rest — each of the 1 077 files under src/ in exactly one); taken once at the cut. COST, measured: 0.11–0.16 ms of main thread per ask (0.35 ms max), the same on a 1 GB heap; a loop busy half the hour ≈ 1 800 asks ≈ 0.27 s (0.008 %; 0.02 % with the inspector's own dispatch).
- M4: memory once an hour — the hub's heap and RSS; the hub's processes by kind (agent CLIs, browsers, the device agent, the rest), counted and their RSS summed, read with fs.promises only: the hub's cgroup members in a service / scope unit (dtach keeps a conversation's CLI there), else its process tree; a node process's command line read only to tell the device agent and a node-based CLI apart, never kept.
- M5: live conversations, open page sockets, device links at the cut; the hour's page-socket messages in / out, characters of conversation output handed to a parser, creates / resumes, store writes handed to the writer thread and the longest (src/server/loop-counts.js — a property add at each site).
- THE CUT HOLDS NOTHING: it swaps the hour first, takes the counts, awaits the census and the process table, writes one line; zero synchronous fs calls on a real cut (counted). The last 24 hours are kept in memory and read by ⚙ Diagnostics «The main loop, by hour» (GET /api/loop-holds `hourly`). No file, no setting, no request to anyone; server.js gets one line.
- CURE r1 (the acceptance's eight laws + one addition): R1 the census's own cost is PRINTED at the price paid (`census-asks`, `census-paid` = the asks' own run + the inspector's dispatch, measured 0.3 ms a piece); R2 the page socket's counter bound once (a bump is an add); R3 an hour no watchdog watched prints «?», never a clean hour; R4 each field counts what its name says — the nine engine fields (eight families + native) add to 100 % of the busy ticks, `census-ticks` / `busy-ticks` / `not-sampled`; R5 the day (Telemetry.heldDays) and its hours share ONE cause key (the hub's code location, else the verdict) and keep a boot's hold apart in both (the row's « · (the boot)»); R6 the census books on the NEAREST named family walking outward (a shared helper is its caller's engine) and the verifier's misfiles moved (session-brain → parse; task-fanout and ws-create out of page; exit-hook and hook-root-watch → hook); R7 a login shell's scope counts only the hub's own (its tree + the dtach masters of its sockets folder); R8 a container counts the whole container; M6 the conversations by turn and idle age (running, waiting, under 1 h, 1–2 h, 2–4 h, over 4 h, unknown) and the keeper's ready browsers / those idle over an hour.

### grants-read-is-a-lookup (主开发 2026-11-16 18:33Z — part of the root fix of the hub's held main loop): a channel grant read is a lookup
- **The field (主开发's count of the owner's hub, 24 h of «loop-hold» lines):** 452 JavaScript holds, 787 s held, ~420 s of them in ONE chain — normalizeString (node:path) 104 s · grantsOf 88 · cleanName 59 · grantsForConversation 41 · rowOf 33 · viewOf 26 · factsOf 23 · normRow 20 · grantsOfConversation 14 · principalApplies 13; the hold lines name the walker: reachCountFor.
- **L1, measured first (a scratch process at the owner's size — 197 110 channel conversations on 8 accounts, 10 reach rows, 10 rules, 41 sessions; a counting copy of the model):** WHO = the agent PROMPT HOOK (agent-routes channelsTaughtFor → channels-access reachCountFor; a 60 s memo per session, fresh at SessionStart) walking store.index.live() to the first conversation the agent may read — an agent that reads nothing walks all 197 110; READS PER WALK = 197 110; NORMALISATIONS PER READ = 12.7 (channel-acl principalApplies built a one-entry row per grant per check and GM.admits re-normalised it) + 5.1 store lookups (grants-store forDir → path.resolve — the engine is built with its dataDir, never handed the store). One walk 2.4 s in scratch.
- **L2, a read is a lookup:** GM.admits takes rows and facts the model already normalised (`prepareRow` / `prepareFacts`, marked by a registered symbol — a patched copy of the model knows them too); channel-acl principalApplies and channel-filter rowNames keep the one-entry row per principal object and the facts per asker, each re-made when a field it was made from changes; the door resolves its store once per install (`GS.installGeneration`) and forDir keeps an absolute dir's resolved form; a resource with no row hands out one frozen empty list (no view kept per conversation key on the shared EMPTY row). THE WALK WAS THE WASTE: a conversation no reach row of its own names and no rule's row derives a grant on reaches exactly what its account's rows reach — judged once per (asker, account, rows' generation: CG.generation moves at every channel row's change), and a walk (reachWalkOf) asks the door once for what is the same for all of it. reachCountFor: 197 110 reads → 2, 2.49 M normalisations → 0 on the warm walk, 1.01 M store lookups → 1; 2.6 s → 0.09 s in scratch.
- **L3:** the async walks (the agent's search, `--full`) give the loop back every 50 000 conversations scanned (a count); an agent's list keeps the newest 200 of each kind in a heap as the walk offers them (never a sort of every candidate: 173 306 for an agent granted the largest account) — same rows, same order, same `more` counts. The list 2.2 s → 0.2 s.
- **Proof (fast, in-process):** new scripts/test-grants-read-lookup.mjs (21) — ① counts at the owner's size and ② L3 (RED on 70efb5e10: 9 of 21); ③ parity, ④ the writer and ⑤ the walk across a change answer through 70efb5e10's OWN code — its six changed files frozen under scripts/fixtures/grants-read-lookup/base, loaded as an old engine in a module graph of their own. The first round's mutants were run by hand from the lane, not in the suite. The fast cap 1101 → 1107 s by arithmetic (the new row 6.7 s).

### readings-attribution-2 (主开发 2026-11-15) — a reading is never filed on an account the conversation was not using
- P0, the measurement: when does a RUNNING claude spend a re-pointed credential? scripts/measure-claude-cred-read.mjs gains `midturn` (one turn of three requests: the shared probe's mock answers a Read tool call, the link moves as request 1 lands), `midturn-late` (request 1's answer held 70 s) and `symlink-quick`; its hot-switch variants now say their fences like the oat ones (guarded reads, foreign tokens, the trace gap). Measured on the real 2.1.322 and 2.1.321 (rung loopback-real: fake credentials, the loopback mock, the strace belt — it never fired; no open under the person's home): THE NEXT REQUEST, inside a turn too. Record: scripts/fixtures/claude-cred-read-midturn-2.1.322.json; `hotSwitchEvidence.midTurn`; kb-design-lessons §18.
- P1, law 1 — ONE answer to «which account»: a reading's account is the account its REQUEST went out on. usage-pool-engine `requestSlotFor` reads the link at the conversation's latest request-out (turn-state's request-out writer now keeps `_lastRequestOutAt`; session-schema row) off the conversation's own re-point ledger: the `from` of its first move after that instant, else the link now. `readingSlotFor` asks it first; the turn pin is the fallback of a producer with no request. A request-stamped reading whose window contradicts its request's account is ARCHIVED by name («the reading and its request disagree»), never re-filed. Every stop of a conversation no longer in a turn (the CLI's idle, the attach reconcile, an exit) and a move of one not in a turn clear the old pin — on d64075ba4 a reading that trailed the turn's result re-made it and only noteTurnEnd cleared it (the road of the owner's misfile). The rejection pin's sentence «a re-point does not reach a RUNNING CLI» is marked measured-false; the rejection pin itself awaits its own ruling. Proof: test-reading-truth (fast, new): an invented episode of the owner's shape (scripts/fixtures/reading-truth-episode.json — no real id, instant or figure) replayed through the real engine and account manager, the no-turn-end road, P0's mid-turn shape, the disagreement archived, a hard-move row; mutants: the request stamp gone (the in-flight reading lands on the new member), d64075ba4's pin road whole (the second member's numbers on the first). 10 of its legs red on d64075ba4.
- P2, law 2 — A MODEL'S CAP IS STATED BY THAT MODEL'S REQUESTS (measured on the owner's instance: a cap reading came, all but never otherwise, in hours that served a request of that model). `noteModelRequest` records each answered request's model family under the account its request went out on (`_turnAsks`, session-schema row; cleared with the reading pin). After the cap lane is named on the key the reading LANDS on, a NAMED model cap this turn never asked that account for is archived by name («a <family> model cap on a turn that asked <account> for no <family> request») and the rest of the reading is written; a cap-only record is dropped whole; the placeholder names no model and is not judged. The request in flight counts for the conversation's own model (a quota record can precede its assistant record). The reading archive's append is ONE helper now (`appendReadingArchive`), the guard's and law 2's. `requestSlotFor` takes `{ requestOutAt }` (a replayed statement's request instant) and is exported. The cap episodes the research found were each an answer IN FLIGHT across a pool move (the slot ledger shows a move minutes before each); invented rows of that shape are law 1's in test-reading-truth; law 2's legs (an Opus turn's Fable cap archived, a Fable turn's written) and its mutant are red on P1.
- P3, law 3 — A FALL IS NOT A RESET UNTIL SOMETHING CONFIRMS IT (measured on the owner's instance over two weeks: such falls were mostly misfiles or flips, a few real early resets). usage-pool-engine `heldFallOf`, right before the cache write: a lane of the record that fell `FALL_HOLD_MIN_DROP` (3) points or more under an unchanged, still-ahead reset against the account's stored reading, from a conversation the pool re-pointed inside the shadow time (lastRepointRow, 10 min), is HELD — not written (the account keeps its number; the pool and the estimator read that), a held representative holds the record whole. A fall a producer that was NOT moved reads is its own confirmation (the real resets in the research were read live). The hold is the reset-claim store's new outcome `fall-unconfirmed` {lane, before, usedPct, readAt, until} (usage-reset-claim `noteFallHeld`; its words: «{name}: {what} fell from {before}% to {after}% in one reading — not confirmed yet; it counts as {before}% until a reading confirms it», en / zh / ja, account-wall-words — the UI unit draws it). It ends at the lane's next measurement (`noteLanesRead`: a panel read, a person's ⟳, an unmoved producer, the window rolling — one that confirms the fall then shows 'reset-seen' against the kept number, one back near it refutes) or, for an idle member, at the window's own reset (`until`, prune). ### resume-all-paced — L1: a bulk resume never floods the hub (主开发 2026-11-16 18:13Z; a field incident, twice in one day on one fleet instance)
- **What happened.** After a restart the boot offer's «Resume all» (layout.js _resumeAll) fired one resume every 400 ms on a fixed clock, whatever the hub had answered: 68 conversations created in five minutes, about forty of them with transcripts of 100–184 MB. The hub's loop was held 10–139 s, its memory went from 2.3 to 18 GiB, the sign-in page went unanswered for five minutes, and the liveness probe restarted it — every conversation just resumed died again. The sidebar group's ▶ fired every resume in ONE synchronous loop.
- **The law.** NEW src/lib/resume-pacer.js: ONE create in flight; the next when the previous one's create has ENDED. createSession gains `onCreateEnd(how, msg)`, said once from `settled(how)`: 'created' / 'refused' (the matched answer), 'error' (an error naming no request), 'lost' (a reconnect that will not re-send it), 'closed' (its window). NEVER at the 15 s reply watchdog: a hub too slow to answer is a hub not to feed. resumeSession passes it through.
- **Why one in flight, not a few.** The hub does each resume's pre-resume read and continuity check on its main thread (L2 measures them), so two in flight hold the loop twice as long and save the person nothing.
- **What the person sees.**
  - ONE progress toast «Resuming i of n…», updated in place, with Stop: the in-flight create finishes and nothing follows; «Stopped: d of n resumed — the other k were not started.»
  - A refusal or failure of one is collected and said at the end, with names and the hub's why; the rest go on.
  - The sidebar's button goes through `resumeGroup`: live members attached and tmux ones opened at once, the stopped ones paced.
- **The legs** (NEW test-resume-all-paced, fast, 3.2 s — the REAL page and resume door over a stand-in hub that answers each create after a placed 420 ms, longer than the old clock):
  - ① 3 creates, never two in flight; ONE progress line, updated, gone at the end, with Stop;
  - ② a refusal said by name and why, the next create still sent;
  - ③ Stop with create 1 in flight: nothing after its answer, said;
  - ④ the watchdog fired: create 2 NOT sent until the answer;
  - ⑤ the group button: the live member attached at once, three creates one in flight at a time; the button calls resumeGroup;
  - ⑥ RED CONTROLS — the master's _resumeAll verbatim (the 400 ms clock): in flight at each send [1, 2, 2]; a pacer that never waits: a flood on the group button.
- **On master d7f42cc21** (the new suite copied onto its product): ① red — creates in flight [1, 2, 2], no progress line.
- **test-layout-dup-storm.** Its §PR rig (prResumeAll) is now a stand-in hub that answers each create. §PR (a) sets the progress line apart from «no other toast» and pins it (ONE line, «Resuming 3 of 3…» last, gone at the end). Seven mutant patterns follow createSession's `settled(<how>)` lines. 290/290.
- **FAST_SUM_CAP_MS** 1101 → 1104 s by arithmetic: 1100.089 s + the new row 3.2 s = 1103.289 s over 589.
- **主开发's look at b10ddda89 (19:11Z, «not taken yet»), the cure:**
  - M1 — every end of a create is seen: the watchdog settle no longer unregisters the lost-socket watch. For a harness whose resume is not re-sent on reconnect, that watch is the only thing that can say «lost».
  - M2 — only the press acts as a press: a group's first stopped member as the press, every later one `stay` (quiet, no desktop switch).
  - M3 — test-layout-dup-storm's (owe) leg drives its order over the real request contract: the bulk in flight when the person switches desktop, each create answered ONCE after it. Its «ONE save» became «each owed recipe carried once»: paced answers come one at a time, so one save per answer that owed one.
  - M4 — `whyNotResumed`: a sentence of ours (zh + ja) for every end without the hub's text.
  - S1 — Stop answered at once («Stopping after the conversation now starting…»).
  - S2 — the stopped line's numbers add up.
  - S3 — the failure line bounded (≤ 3 names, 40 + 60 characters); `pressResumeGroup` says a throw.
  - New legs ⑦–⑪ in test-resume-all-paced, each RED on b10ddda89, green on the cure. The suite takes 3.6 s alone (the sum 1103.689 s stays under the 1104 s cap).
- **The fast list's one red (cured, test-only):** test-contributions' census pins the one declared error release line of session-lifecycle verbatim; it is now `settled('error', msg)` (the create's end is named for the bulk resume), and the census follows it.
- kb-features, kb-patterns («Resume-all boot popup»), kb-file-structure (INDEX + essay).

## 2.369.405 — 2026-11-16

### vault-login hotfix — a vault fill and a verb of our own are the hub's own act: no local check of the browser program refuses them (`data/bin/vibespace-browser`)
- **The defect (found in the field an hour after 2.369.404):** on a conversation of an Antigravity named account, `vibespace-browser fill <target> --vault <entry>/<field>` was refused «config unavailable — $HOME is not this account's home», while `open`, `snapshot` and a plain `fill` on the same local mediated named profile worked. VibeSpace spawns an Antigravity account with HOME = the account's own root (`src/harnesses/antigravity.js` `spawnEnvOf`), a server-side vault fill's resolve leaves the environment basis out on purpose (`src/routes/browser.js`, the session road and `resolveForJob`), and the CLI built the child's environment and ran `composeConfig` — whose first line is the HOME fence — BEFORE the branch that hands the fill to the hub without starting the browser program.
- **The law:** a vault fill is the hub's own act; the CLI starts no browser program for it, so nothing about that program's environment or config file is built, checked or refused for it — and the same for every verb of our own (`stop`, `site-reset`, `passkey`, `permission`, `answer`, `surfaces`: `runOursPage`). `runPage` decides it once, at the top (`startsNothing` = a parsed vault fill, or `cls.ours`): for it `daemonCwd`, `realBinary`, `installedVersion` and the flag table's drift re-reading, the launch-version pick (`wantCli`), `V.childEnv` with its `[env_twin_dropped]` note, and `composeConfig` with its HOME fence are not run. A verb that starts the program keeps every one of them, the HOME fence included. The closure (every local check that can fire before the hub is asked, for a verb that starts nothing): NEEDED — the verb table's classification, the fill's own argument parse, the session check, the page facts the resolve brings back; CANNOT FIRE — the upload and write path judgments (the table gives these verbs no file words); SKIPPED — the six above. Only the Antigravity named accounts move HOME at the session level (Codex moves `CODEX_HOME`, Claude `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR`); the sealed vault-run child points HOME nowhere and carries no session token.
- **The legs (`scripts/test-browser-verbs.mjs`, a stand-in hub, the CLI as a child process):** HOME = an account root the product set, the resolve names no config: the vault fill is answered by the hub (prepare, then the fill), no program run, nothing composed; the same fill on the JOB road (a job's token, the job resolve's answer); `site-reset` answered by the hub; CONTROL — `open` from the same HOME is still refused `config_unavailable`. RED on 2.369.404 (`d7f42cc21`): the three hub legs refused with the field's sentence, the control green (3 failed, 581 passed). Two older negative controls patch a COPY of the CLI by the exact text of a line this fix rewrote; their patterns now match both forms.
- **Why no leg met it:** the HOME-fence legs drove only `open`, a verb that starts the program, and every vault-fill suite (test-vault-login-chrome, test-browser-login, test-browser-mediation-chrome) runs the CLI with a preload that makes the account's home EQUAL to HOME — none drove a vault fill from a HOME the product moved.

A post-lift guard is no longer retired by an address move (`retirePostLiftGuardOnTab` and the verdict's `retiredGuardCount` are gone): it lives until the document ends, so a value an SPA writes back after an in-app move re-arms there. Cost: every read on such a tab rechecks until its next document — one isolated-world scan, measured on the fake kernel at p50 1.69 ms against 1.11 ms after a new document (40 reads; the Chrome figure rides the real-browser claim). The fake kernel mints a loaderId per new document (`Page.navigate`, `setDom({newDocument})`), keeps it across a move, and re-binds an isolated world to a re-render inside the document (Chrome's own behaviour — its stale world had hidden the twelve cells' value from the check).

### ui-language pick 1 — every sentence a person reads goes through t(), with zh AND ja rows (the UI walk's L1 list; 主开发's GO 07:02Z)
- **The owner (2026-11-13):** «走查一下所有界面找到可优化的布局，提示文本等». The walk found 57 language findings (9 major) in about a dozen patterns. The law: fix by rule, not by surface; pin every rule with a census derived from the tree.
- **THE CENSUS — scripts/test-ui-language.mjs (fast, PURE).**
  - The universe: the src files the three browser entries reach (src/client.js, src/design-viewer-entry.js, src/doc-editor-entry.js), found by a relative-import walk. Worker threads parse it with acorn (15 MB; one thread took 1.4 s). The workers' PARSED imports check the walk (491 files, equal to the bundle's metafile set).
  - ① Visible English outside t(): a literal that reads as English in a sink a person reads (textContent / title / placeholder / innerHTML / setAttribute / toast / dialog / label-like keys / HTML template text). Held by a shrink-only baseline, scripts/fixtures/ui-language-baseline.json: a NEW hit is red, a gone row is red until `--lower`. Seeded at **667** on 935960b7e; **508** after this pick.
  - ② Every extracted key has a zh AND a ja row (i18n-check only warned). 7 were missing.
  - ③ Every {param} in a literal key is filled by its call. A settings `[t(key), {params}]` pair is filled where drawn; an embedded-control marker says `// ui-words:`.
  - ④ A key carrying markup never reaches a TEXT sink, and a dict value adds no markup its key lacks: 5 backticked settings descriptions, the resume dialog's <b>/<br>, 7 translator `**`.
  - ⑤ No zh / ja row is English for a word key: baseline 50, plus a GLOSSARY_PENDING list (agent / harness / reset credit / token) held for the owner's glossary (lane L3).
  - ⑥ The For-you heads: every literal `sessionName` a producer files is a row of src/foryou-actions.js FORYOU_HEADS, worded at display (65 producer lines, 20 heads).
  - Every leg's negative control runs first on a planted source or row.
- **Measured:** ~0.75 s in-process (three runs 636–750 ms). The fast row states 0.8 s; the .398 cap (1068 s) is raised by arithmetic at the train, as 主开发 ruled.
- **Found on the way:** scripts/i18n-extract.mjs `dictEntries` skips every row with a trailing `// lane …` comment (~500 of 11 400), so i18n-check's duplicate and parity checks never see them. The census reads the dictionary MODULES instead. Not changed here.

### ui-language pick 2 — ONE door from a stored value to a word (src/lib/value-words.js)
- **The rule:** a protocol or stored value stays EXACTLY what it is on the wire and in storage; the page words it at DISPLAY through `valueWord(set, value, t)`. A value the table does not know is shown as itself, never hidden.
