### artifacts-by-intent cost pick — the shown cost is each segment's LAST total, never a sum of running totals (the owner's red «本次对话约 $63854.44»; 主开发's GO 00:54Z)
- **Measured, records only (no turn billed):** a claude `result` record's `total_cost_usd` is the CLI PROCESS's running total. Read on the real CLI's stdout through the real chat-wrapper against a loopback mock API (the prices are the mock's, the arithmetic the CLI's): 2.1.308 and 2.1.312 (scripts/fixtures/claude-cli/2.1.312-frames, 2.1.312-stamped, 2.1.308-stamped; claude-steer-inject's r5 / r6 buffers). Each total = the one before + that result's own share, which 2.1.312+ also writes as `model_usage_since_last_result`. The 2.1.322 binary builds the field from `costLedger.totalCostUSD()`, the figure its own status line calls the session's cost. A new process restarts at zero.
- **The arithmetic:** the restore (session-store chatStatus) summed every result, and the bar added each turn_complete's total on top (`_statusCost +=`). One process of n equal turns of cost c read c·n(n+1)/2 instead of n·c: 150 turns ⇒ 75.5×. Recorded: 945 µ$ for a real 540 (2.1.312-frames, three processes); 840 for 465 (both stamped); 4 335 for 2 190 (steer-inject r6).
- **THE LAW (PURE src/cost-segments.js, ONE fold):** the shown cost = Σ over the conversation's segments of each segment's LAST total. A segment begins where the total restarts: a total that IS its own since-last share (a process's first result), or one lower than the one before (a CLI older than 2.1.312). The restore (`costShown(costOfResults(msgs))`) and message-manager's live road (`costStep` per result, replayed or live) fold the same records. The turn_complete op carries the folded figure, and the bar's `turnCost` (was `addCost`) REPLACES its number. A buffer whose head was trimmed still counts: the first total kept already holds it. A resume that carries the total forward stays one segment. Why the last total and not Σ since-last: Σ since-last loses what a trim took.
- **Unchanged:** what the figure means (the CLI's own estimate at API prices); red only when the billing basis is unknown and the figure is over $5. The ACP road (opencode, antigravity) still ASSIGNS the agent's own `usage_update.cost.amount`, already a conversation total. Codex and the ACP turn_complete carry 0 (no figure). The chip's amount goes through the page's own number formatter (ui-language's page-time `num`, handed into the PURE `costChipWords`): «$63,854.44».
- **Pins (RED on 66c6d99c0):** scripts/test-cost-segments.mjs (new, fast, in-process, about 0.3 s):
  - ① the law over the records — 540 not 945, 465 not 840, the 2.1.308 drop rule;
  - ② the restore;
  - ③ the live road carrying the restore's figure after every result;
  - ④ interrupted results change nothing;
  - ⑤ a head trimmed mid-line ⇒ 390;
  - ⑥ a resume, restarted or carried ⇒ 465 (a sum reads 840 / 1 380);
  - ⑦ the thousands mark in en / zh / ja;
  - ⑧ the census: no src file adds a total_cost_usd; the restore and the live road call the one fold; the bar never `+=`.
  test-status-bar-chips ① now drives `turnCost` with the folded figures and pins «$0.30» three times reading $0.30, and «$63,854.44». The two suites that named `addCost` follow the rename: test-desktop-switch's stub and test-unknown-records' slice end.
- **The kept fact (主开发's follow-up, 01:54Z):** 主开发's own conversation's buffer (494 KB, its head trimmed) held 2 results of ONE process: the restore summed 42 595.76, the law reads 21 299.99 — and every earlier process of that conversation was gone from the buffer, so after a hub restart the figure SHRANK to the present segment. Now the fold's state {done, last, key} is kept on the conversation's own meta (`costKept`, written paced by the claude stdout consumer after each result it feeds) and resumed BEFORE the buffer: the boot seeds each claude normalizer with `costResume(meta.costKept, resultsIn(buffer))` (the results after the kept one's key, or all of them when its own was trimmed away); a rebuild carries the old normalizer's fold and its replay passes over what that fold counted; the restore reads the normalizer's fold before the buffer. The same result twice folds once. On a CLI before 2.1.312 (no share) a result's `result_index` 0 marks a process's first result; with the share present the share decides (a resume that carries its total forward stays one segment). Pins ⑨ (RED on the pick without it: the restore 195 not 465, the live op 240 not 510, the rebuild); five mutants red by name; the store-write census gains the row `create > attach > keepCost` (paced).
- **The first attach after a boot, end to end (主开发's question, 09:46Z):** the boot seeds the session's bare normalizer with the kept fact resumed over the saved buffer (no seek); the first attach does NOT replay into it — ws-handler calls `rebuildHistory`, which makes a NEW normalizer seeded with the old one's fold WITH seek, so its replay passes over every result that fold counted (a replay into the seeded one would count the present segment twice). Pinned on the real road by scripts/test-cost-kept-chrome.mjs (heavy): a stub CLI writing the 2.1.312 cost records behind the real chat-wrapper — process A $2.50, process B $1.95, a 650 KB answer that makes the wrapper's 500 KB ring drop process A from the buffer file, the hub SIGKILLed and restarted — the chip reads $4.45 at the first attach after the boot, at a second attach and after a reconnect (the buffer alone would read $1.95, the double count $6.40), and $4.75 after a live turn; RED over the pick without the kept fact (`--tree`).
- **Open:** whether a `--resume` of the same session carries the old total forward is shown by no record; the law holds either way.

### artifacts-by-intent — the Artifacts list is ordered by what the person most needs to see, and every row can be found (the owner 2026-11-06, a phone shot: 「这个界面你得好好优化下了 根本找不到想找的东西」 + 「分一下哪些可能是用户最需要看的，比如 publish 这种行为显然就是 agent 想要让用户看的，自动检测修改过的文件这种优先级就更低」)
- **LAW 1 — intent is the first axis.** PURE `intentOf(row)` in src/artifacts.js → `foryou` (a published / presented page, a hand-over, a running service with its link, any row a publish · present · handover · open op named — the new sticky `shown` fact) · `made` (born by a write, the person's uploads, a page taken down, a stopped service, a design no window opened) · `touched` (code, rows born by an edit). `view()` orders by INTENTS then newest; every card block carries `intent` (+ `shown`); `listFor` adds the conversation's `cwd` / `host`. The list model's default group is `intent` (kind · helper · day stay in the ▾); a view stored before VIEW_VERSION 2 with group kind reads as intent. The window's rail opens with the three bands; its table reads band by band until a column is clicked.
- **LAW 2 — every row can be told apart and found.** The meta line starts with the row's folder (`folderOf`: from the cwd, `~/…`, `…/a/b/c`, `host:`; never the whole absolute path); colliding names wear the shortest distinguishing path suffix (`shownNames`, over ALL rows, linear) and are cut from their start on screen; a section over 8 rows in two folders or more sub-groups by folder (collapsible heads, remembered); the filter matches name · folder · the path from the cwd · helper · the kind's word; 最近 holds only what no open section draws (by intent: just above «touched»). Phone (≤ 480 px, or a coarse pointer under 1024 px): a full-height sheet under the phone's top bar, the search row pinned with ⤢ ⋯ ✕ (44 px), the auto-open switch inside the ⋯, heads ≥ 44 px, rows 56 px, names + field 16 px, meta 14 px (the house touch scale).
- **Choices.** The sticky `shown` field (the brief's `lastOp ∈ …` alone would drop an ask's `--artifact` from «for you» at the agent's next edit). The 最近 band by intent sits above «touched», not first: its rows are the folded ones and the first screen stays the attention list. A band that is ONE folder gets no sub-head; folderless rows (a service, a page link) sit bare at the band's level. The README example: with exactly three README.md the shortest suffix of `traces/v3-or1/README.md` is `v3-or1/README.md`; the owner's shape fixture adds the README the agent edited in `mirror/v3-or1/` (code, «touched»), which grows it to the brief's `traces/v3-or1/README.md` — names are told apart over every row, not per band. The bands' words are a PURE table (INTENT_WORDS, the KIND_WORDS precedent) because t('For you') is already the tray's 待你处理.

### B-0a33 — the ceiling was passed by queueing: a reservation is counted where its turn runs (law 1's money; 主开发 07:20Z, round 1 08:03Z)
- **The finding** (the .399 readers, int359/acc-399/l23b/drivers/d2-money.cjs F2, real guard + queued-wakes on one clock): cap 5/h, 5 frames queued behind a hung turn filled hour 0; at +3 h 5 unattended turns were spent; then the turn ended and its 5 ran — 10 billed unattended turns in one hour.
- **The law:** no window of the ceiling holds more billed unattended turns than its cap, whenever the turn a reservation pays for runs; the day axis and «given back once» unchanged.
- **The change** (src/spend-authorizer.js): a WAITING reservation is in the hour of every authorize; a carried one is in the hour it ran (`ran`); one queued-wakes gives up unknown (process gone or replaced, conversation archived) is in the hour it stopped waiting (`end`, via `note({ended})`). A waiting stamp is kept past the day horizon while its entry lives (7 days). The day count reads `at`; a carry a day after its send is counted in the day it runs, as the aged-out stamp's re-stamp was.
- **Cost:** a frame waiting behind a running turn takes a slot of every hour it waits through, so unattended turns are refused sooner while a queue waits. A full hour of waiting frames promises no «next allowed» instant.
- **Round 1** (its reader, verdict wf_ffa65a83: the hour cure held — F2 5 against 10, 0 hour overruns in 2000 seeded timelines against the release's 560, never looser in 240 000 states):
  - THE DAY SAYS WHAT THE HOUR SAYS: every window (hour, day, the instance's day) counts a stamp at its count instant — waiting = now, carried = where it ran (`ran`, a stash drain too), given up = where the hub stopped (`end`). The send re-base goes. The reader's day scene (day cap 5, five frames queued at 0 h and run at 20 h) is refused at 24 h 01 (the release and 39ab2d834: free, ten in (20 h, 44 h]).
  - A WAITING STAMP NOBODY HOLDS IS LET GO, SAID TRULY: queued-wakes reconciles the guard's waiting reservations (`waitingReservations`, wired beside reservationState) against its live entries, at load and at each sweep. One no entry holds ends as «given up» at that instant, once: counted there, never returned, no longer said to wait. The 7-day bound is read inside the count (true with no prune running).
  - THE REFUSAL SAYS WHAT WAITS AND WHERE: a reservation's stamp names the conversation it waits behind (`wb`: its For-you key and name, from the ladder). A refusal those frames hold names them — at most three, then «and N more» — in the journal line and the notice. The notice is filed under the first one's key (its own link opens it), its door says so, and it comes once per wait (the release re-filed every 6 h). The «promised» line now says truly: «counted while they wait, given back only if they are known not to have run». CHOSEN: the refusal notice itself, not shape B's item — the two picks ship apart.
  - Evidence on the new tip: the reader's d7 property, 2000 seeds × 4 days (≈ 139 600 billed turns, with and without restarts): 0 violations of any kind (39ab2d834: day 268, instance-day 134). d8 ①b: the worst rolling 24 h 5 (was 10). ⑤b and ⑥ — with the server's wiring (the driver builds queued-wakes without the new dependency) — let the orphans go at load: refused that hour, free the next, «0 waiting».
- **Pins:** test-spend-paths §5f, 26 legs (457 → 483 with the rest):
  - the reader's scene through the real guard + queued-wakes;
  - THE LAW over 40 seeded 4-day timelines: no hour window and no rolling 24 h over its cap;
  - the reader's day scene; the unit legs (carried, waiting 30 h, the 7-day bound in the count, given up, a stash drain — the reader's M10 — and the prune past the last instant — the reader's M11, looser, cap 1);
  - the load and sweep reconcile through the real guard; the refusal's names, door, key and once-per-wait;
  - ten patched-copy controls, each red: every window at the send, the day at the send, a carry keeping its send's instant, a drain keeping it, the prune by the send, «ended» ignored, no age bound in the count, no reconcile at load, the refusal without its names, plus the build check.
- **Follow-up** (主开发 08:35Z, on b0b11962a):
  - THE NOTICE DOES NOT GO SILENT WHILE THE WAIT STILL REFUSES: exactly one notice of a wait is open. It is filed again at the first refusal after the previous one expired — its expiry IS the 6-hour re-file mark — never two at once, and a person's dismissal stands until that mark (leg: a 13-hour wait refused every 61 minutes ⇒ notices at 0 h, 6 h 06, 12 h 12).
  - AN UNREADABLE msg-queued.json IS NOT AN EMPTY ONE: the load tells ENOENT (nothing on disk) from any other read or parse failure. After a failed read the reconcile holds off for that process's life, so the waiting stamps stand — counted, under the 7-day bound — never freed by a read that failed (legs: EIO, a torn file).
  - Both legs are red on b0b11962a, and nothing else is.
- **Follow-up 2** (主开发 08:53Z, on 980991658): THE KEY IS THE PLACE, not the frame. The notice is keyed by (the account, the cap, the conversation the frames wait behind) with the 6-hour cadence — the oldest frame changes at every carry of a draining queue (leg: eight frames, one carried each hour, a refusal every ten minutes ⇒ notices at 0 h and 6 h 10 only; a second conversation's wait gets its own at once).
- **Known** (named by its reader, not asked; each the release's too):
  - a frame the hub stopped waiting for — aged out at 7 days, or a process wrongly judged gone — can still run uncounted in its hour (the reader's d8 ③b: worst hour 3 at cap 2; ④: worst hour 6 at cap 3, plus 3 repeat copies stashed);
  - carries the release made in the hour before the update are counted at their send: one window of at most an hour (d10: 10 in (3 h, 4 h] at cap 5);
  - frames already waiting run past a cap lowered below them (d8 ⑦: 5 run at cap 2 and at cap 0); a null setting reads as 0 (budgetLimits gives 30 / 0 / 30 / 30 for false / null / 'off' / -1).

### queued-is-not-woke laws 2 + 3 — SHAPE C: a wait is read from the hub's own record at that moment; nothing is kept (row B-580f; closes K6 of 2.369.398)
- **The ruling** (主开发 2026-11-13 13:35Z / 13:42Z). The cut (a ledger of instants kept in per-group files) was right in steady state: 15 000 walk steps, 66 SIGKILLs, 0 divergence. Its readers broke it on every SWITCH, each in machinery that existed only to keep the ledger. A fleet day measured the noise: about 100 owner items a day at one hour, and 254 lines to a coordinator. Shape C keeps nothing.
- **Law 1 — only a conversation in a RUNNING turn** (turn-facts `turnOf`: running / waiting). An idle conversation's quiet mail waits by design.
  - THE SENDER, at one hour of its own oldest message not handed: ONE entry per sender in the ladder's new keyed stash slot (conversation-deliver `stashSlot(cid, 'waiting', …)`), naming every such member with a count, the oldest instant, and «in a turn since T» where a record states the opening (else «in a turn»).
    - It is replaced in place, never counted against the stash's 30 (so it never evicts), and rendered whole.
    - It is filed again ONLY when its set of members changes. The set it last handed rides the stash file (`__slots`, which a release drops), so the same set is never handed twice.
  - THE OWNER, at four hours of the conversation's oldest: ONE For-you item per conversation and turn, key `messages-waiting:<cid>:<the turn's opening, or the instant this process first saw it run>`.
    - At a first sight after a restart, the newest item a restart left (open, or a person's ✕) is this turn's: two turns across a restart read as one.
    - Its only door opens the conversation. A ✕ stands for that turn, and an Undo is drawn again.
    - Its two ends: «the turn ended» and «they were handed to it».
  - The sweep runs every five minutes (ages are in hours).
- **Law 2 — «not yet handed» is asked of the record at that moment** (groups-engine `readWaiting`):
  - each group's log through `readFoldedAsync`, the fold over the store's async tail (`readTailAsync`, a FileHandle), off the loop;
  - the marks through `reachFor` — the reach the next report uses: mute reaches nothing, `mention` only what @-names it or an awaited reply; messages only, never its own;
  - plus each held frame's records.
  THE GATE: a group is read only when its mark — or a held frame's start — is older than an hour with records after it. Those are persisted facts, so a restart changes nothing. At the bound (2 000 records) no count is said: «since at least» the oldest it saw.
- **Law 3 — what is remembered is only what was SHOWN:** the item and its ✕, by key, in the For-you store; the sender's slot and the set it handed. No wait record, no told mark, no ledger.
- claude says «in a turn», never «since» (no record states its opening). The turn's opening is said only for the turn running now (law D).
- **Measured on reader B's fleet day** (its driver, copied: seeds 42 / 7 / 99, with and without the 8 h hang):
  - owner items 4–10 a day (about 100 at one hour);
  - entries handed to the coordinator 11–14 a day (254 lines before), never the same set twice;
  - reads a sweep median 28–31, max 39; a sweep 4.5–5.7 ms at the median, 26 ms at most;
  - the hang seen after 284 and 389 minutes. In seed 7 the hung worker's first message came four hours into its turn, so by the law it is never seen.
- **Its reader's list (主开发 15:30Z «yes after a list»), one commit:**
  - test-wait-walk's red control runs at the walk's own 3 000 steps (in 800 it never bit; the first divergence comes at step 1 590). The walk's compare is now the reader's own, with a GATE leg: no wait older than its bound is hidden.
  - {X} → {} → {X} is a leave and a join: when a sender's set is empty at a sweep, its entry leaves AND the set it handed is forgotten.
  - A sweep in which any reading failed touches no slot (a reading not taken says nothing and ends nothing).
  - A restart adopts only an OPEN item: a ✕ of an earlier turn never silences a later wait. A ✕ of the same turn still stands, because the key is the record's opening.
  - THE LOOP (no single hold over 20 ms): the reading has its OWN bound — the newest 200 records or 256 KB, read in 64 KB windows. The sweep yields to the loop between reads, and the store's async tail takes a byte budget and says whether it reached the start. Beyond the bound: no count, «since at least». The sender pass yields after each sender (owner-facts.when costs 0.18 ms a call, 15 ms at its first).
    Measured with the reader's cost driver (300 groups × 2 000 records × 1 KB, 40 conversations in running turns, 600 reads a sweep), the release's boot unread warm-up done first:

### fable-52-cli-321 round 10 — a pick shows on every harness; a page with no server facts never says «fallback»; the matrix
- **Out of the .393 candidate.** Five readers with master e74fabc6b as the oracle drove the merged candidate (acd96510b), and a skeptic attacked each finding. Two stood, and nine rounds had missed both: nobody drove a pick on a harness WITHOUT server model facts, or the view-only page.
- **LAW A — A PICK SHOWS ON EVERY HARNESS.** The defect fix had dropped master's optimistic `_statusModel = model` from the pick. On every row whose capability says `modelFacts: false` (codex, shell, opencode, antigravity), the server answers a press with `facts: null`. So the chip flashed «old → new ⏳», went BACK to the old model titled «as last reported by the CLI», and stayed there until a re-attach. On Antigravity the next reply then turned it amber with a false «Auto-fallback». Now, on a bar holding no server facts, the ANSWERED pick is the fact the chip shows: `answerModel` writes master's `_statusModel` and re-targets a standing lock as the server did. A refusal or a lost answer changes nothing. Such a bar's chip is master's: the label and the mismatch are master's rules (the served model against the model last reported, the lock target where one stands, the alias-tolerant `sameModel`). The r2–r9 law owns only a bar that holds the server's facts.
- **LAW B — A PAGE WITH NO SERVER FACTS NEVER SAYS «FALLBACK».** `SessionMessages.chatStatus()` carries `servedModel` (the newest assistant record's) beside `model` (the FIRST key of a cumulative `result.modelUsage`). The view-only attach, the transcript route and the resume / fork withStatus fetch send it without facts, and the bar judged one against the other. A stopped conversation moved Opus → Fable on purpose opened «⚠ Auto-fallback … (capacity/overload)». Now a status that declares no facts never sets the served model: it names the model its record shows LAST and judges nothing. «Fallback» is said only from the numbered facts of a LIVE conversation.
- **THE MATRIX (the pin that was missing).** `scripts/chip-matrix.mjs` drives every harness row of backend-caps × every door a chip is painted from, on one root's REAL code:
  - the doors: the re-attach, a pick, a pick and its reply, a locked pick, the live init, the view-only attach, the transcript route, the withStatus fetch, the cost op;
  - the code: the bar with its own pick / Lock closures, chat-view's own meta lines and live-init road, ws-handler's own set-model case and attach lines, model-ask, `SessionMessages.chatStatus()`.
  - test-status-bar-chips ⑪ derives each cell from its row. A facts row follows the r2–r10 law. A row without facts follows master's chip, read from the same driver run on e74fabc6b (`scripts/fixtures/chip-matrix-master.json`, written by `--write`).
  - A row that declares nothing, a row the oracle lacks, and a call site of the bar's model setters the DOOR CENSUS cannot place (14 today) are each red.
  - On 4f4743c61 (= acd96510b) ⑪ is red by name: every no-facts pick snaps back, Antigravity's reply is amber, Claude's three history doors are amber.
- **SMALLER.**

### B-6ded — a usage walk that does not reach its commit point leaves the cursor map as it found it (lane usage-walk-one-folder; 主开发 03:50Z GO)
- **The loss, on the release too.** The hub walks transcripts IN-PROCESS over its own cursor store (`UsageHistory._cursors`), and the mount gate stops a timed walk at a budget point (`onBudget` throws `paused`).
  - The walker advanced the store's entries IN PLACE (`cursors[fp] || …`, then `cur.offset += nb`), while the stopped walk's buffered rows were dropped.
  - So the requests of the bytes it had consumed never reached the ledger and were never read again. The acceptance's drivers lost 7 of 22 (int359 acc-399 uw1 `pause.js`) and 2–5 per scene (the refuter's `pause.mjs`).
  - It escaped test-mount-health's «a walk in flight stops at its next yield, cursors untouched»: that leg runs on an EMPTY map, where an entry is only added at a file's end.
- **The law, per spelling:**
  - **src/usage-walker.js:** the walk's cursors are its own. A map handed in is copied, and each entry is copied before it advances; the walk returns them. Every field is a scalar, so a shallow copy per entry is whole.
  - **src/usage-history.js:** `this._cursors = walk.cursors` moved from before the shard appends to after them, just before the cursor write (the block stays synchronous).
    - A paused walk, a thrown one, or an append that fails on one shard (EISDIR, ENOSPC) leaves `_cursors` as it was.
    - The next walk re-reads those bytes, and rows already in a shard are refused by the ledger's id filter (`knows`).
  - **data/bin/vibespace-usage-scan:** its commit point is a flushed stdout.
    - Measured on this box's Node: a dead pipe calls the write's callback FIRST, with EPIPE, and emits 'error' after. The release wrote the cursor file in that callback, past every event the hub never received.
    - Now an error skips the write (exit 1).
    - What it covers: a write the scanner SEES fail (the hub's end gone before or while it writes: EPIPE, ENOSPC). Bytes that already left are not covered — see «Known» under the readers' list below.
- **Pins:** test-usage-walk-parity «B-6ded», 15 legs.
  - Module, 2 legs: a walk stopped at a budget point, and a whole walk. The handed map stays as found, its entries the same objects.
  - Hub through UsageHistory, 10 legs:
    - the readers' nine scenes: `pause.js` one name / two names; `pause.mjs` prior / alias-prior / alias-finished / two files; `pause2.mjs` link-after / link-before / other-link-after;
    - plus the commit's own failure: December's shard path made a directory after November's rows landed ⇒ 3 appended, 3 re-read refused, none missing.
  - Scanner, 1 leg: a dead stdout pipe leaves the cursor file byte for byte, and the next live run emits all 400 events.
  - A planted control: the walker advancing the caller's own entry fails the module leg.
  - RED on the release (an export of 935960b7e with this suite): 13 of 13.
    - The two-name scenes keep their rows on the release through the alias's second read. They are red by the law: the map advanced.
    - `pause2.mjs` at its own 1 MiB default has no budget point in a 7-request walk, so the release cannot be cut there; its scenes run at 300 bytes.
- **Cost:** row 717 → 790 ms (×1.10 vs the .398 copy: 1 072 → 1 180 ms, three runs each, one box). A walk copies the cursor map once (O(keys); the walk already stats every file it lists) and each entry it visits.
- **Not changed:** the device road (`--usage-scan-child`). The hub keeps that cursor and commits it after a durable ingest (lane ledger-dedup-law F2); the child's map is its own.

### B-6ded, the readers' list — two readers, ACCEPTED AFTER ONE LIST (主开发 09:13Z; int359 acc-399 verdict-batch3, keys b6ded-walk and b6ded-scanner)
- **What held, driven by the readers:** every exit a walk has (a pause at every yield, a throw in the walker or a line handler, an append failing on the first / middle / last shard, a cursor write that throws, a second scan, a reload, SIGKILL at ten points) leaves the map as found, and the next walk writes every request. The release loses 1–15 of 18. The scanner keeps its cursor on EPIPE before the start, EPIPE mid-write and ENOSPC. 480 seeded rounds with 162 cuts lost 0 (the release lost 367 and 2 162).
- **1. A harvest that cannot finish makes progress every run.** This was new with B-6ded: on the ssh road a backlog over the hub's limits failed every harvest the same way (the cursor rightly kept), and was retried at the next kick — a full remote walk and up to 128 MiB buffered each time, while spend made after it never landed.
  - src/hosts.js: the hub's limits are ONE constant, `USAGE_HARVEST_LIMITS` (maxBuffer 128 MiB, timeoutMs 180 s). `usageScanBound` takes half the bytes and a third of the seconds. The ssh command carries it (`VIBESPACE_USAGE_SCAN_MAX_BYTES=… VIBESPACE_USAGE_SCAN_MAX_MS=… node …`), and execFile takes its limits from the same constant.
  - data/bin/vibespace-usage-scan: a run that has read something stops after a WHOLE line once its output bytes or its walk time reach the bound. The file it stopped in keeps that line's cursor and the files after it keep theirs, so the cursor written is exactly what was printed. Without the env: 32 MiB and 60 s (the device road's script-ship rung has a 120 s deadline).
  - A compressed rollout stopped part-way keeps `zpart: 1` beside its `zsize`. Both spellings read such a rollout on from its offset instead of skipping it: src/usage-walker.js reads the mark, and only the scanner writes it.
  - A failed harvest backs off: 1 min, doubling, at most 30 min (`_harvestFailed` / `_harvestLanded`). A forced harvest, the owner's own ask, goes. The dial road's failure takes the same backoff.
  - Legs:
    - the hub's own `harvestUsage` over an ssh stand-in that relays through a pipe, its limits scaled to a 30 000-byte buffer: 240 requests land over 4 harvests of at most 73, with the 40 made meanwhile, none missing;
    - the bound sits below the limits;
    - a failed harvest backs off 1 → 2 min, and the link back clears it;
    - the scanner run in-process, held to 1 500 bytes and to 12 ms (a clock that moves 1 ms per look), emits over 13 and 9 runs exactly the 90 events of one walk, in its order, and ends at the walk's cursors (a .zst rollout read part-way, then on).
    - RED on 817b0f4fb: 4 (the hub states no limits, one harvest takes the whole backlog, a failed harvest is retried at once, the scanner ignores the bound).
- **2. The codex half pinned.** A module leg (a handed map with a rollout entry, the walk stopped at its 2nd budget point) and the hub's paused walk over a grown rollout at yields 1 / 3 / 6 (the reader's `codex-pause.mjs`). RED on the release: the map moved, 2 / 5 / 10 of 22 missing. The planted control now also reverts the codex copy (the reader's mutant W3) and must fail the codex module leg.
- **3. Known — where the fix ends, on the ssh road.** The scanner's commit point is its flushed stdout, BEFORE the hub's durable ingest. The release and this fix both lose the batch when:
  - the hub DEFERS the ingest (`ledger-index-loading`: the first remote ingest after a hub start, into a month shard over 8 MiB). Nothing is appended, and the remote cursor is past it;
  - the ingest fails (an append EISDIR or ENOSPC, a hold that could not be written);
  - the hub cuts a harvest whose bytes already sit in the pipe and ssh buffers. A typical incremental harvest of a few MiB is written whole before any drop, so the scanner sees success.
  - Also known, read only: the old-daemon script-ship rung (`runStream`) ingests partial text (no `truncated` check) while the device-side scanner, its pipe drained, writes its cursor; its 120 s deadline does not stop the device child.
  - Also known, older than B-6ded: a torn shard append on the hub (half a text, then ENOSPC) glues the re-walk's first row onto the fragment, so one request is missing on the cold road (the release misses more).
  - The lasting cure for the ssh road is the device road's shape: the hub keeps the cursor and commits it after its durable ingest (lane ledger-dedup-law F2).
- **4. The id filter's sentence made true.** On a WARM ledger the cache had not loaded what a half-done commit appended (our own append only marks it for a re-check), so the re-walk appended those rows again. Readers never counted them (the first row per id wins).
  - Now the ids a commit DID append before an append failed are kept (`_partialRids`), and the next walk's filter refuses them until a commit completes.
  - Leg: the warm failed append. RED on 817b0f4fb: 11 rows for 8 requests.
- **Cost:** row 790 → 968 ms (×1.35 vs the .398 copy: 1 109 → 1 497 ms, three runs each; the harvest legs run the ssh stand-in 8 times).

### chat-attachments-persist — the cut: a picture Claude Code or Codex showed is read FROM ITS RECORD; a file a person dropped into a temporary folder lives with the conversation (the owner 2026-11-11: old conversations lose their pictures)
- **The map (no build before it).** Pasted pictures were never lost: the CLI transcript keeps their bytes inline (409 / 409 in one 2 GB transcript) and the view draws them. What vanished:
  - (d) an AGENT's pictures, drawn from their path through /api/file/raw;
  - (a) files dropped into a conversation whose cwd is temporary (9 of the owner's 100 live sessions);
  - (b) Antigravity's pasted pictures under such a cwd;
  - (c) the agent's copy of a channel attachment (os.tmpdir()).
- **Two rounds of a COPY store were not accepted** (round 0 e5e2879f7, round 1 d41dc0496): a prototype-open extension table, one picture under two conversation ids, a bound that re-trimmed on every read, decoded bytes queued per replay; then round 1's own ledger did not converge after a kill, and its bounded queue backfilled about 5 pictures per read after a restart. 主开发's ruling (2026-11-13 08:47Z / 08:54Z), from the lane's page: «the record is the store» — NO copy, NO bound, NO ledger, NO queue, NO setting chat.keptPicturesMB.
- **(d) THE PLACE.** A lifted picture carries `place {b, tx, agent?, key, n}`:
  - Claude: the record's transcript id, the uuid, the sub-agent's agentId, and the ordinal in document order.
  - Codex view_image: the rollout id and the output's call_id.
  - MEASURED on the real 2.1.322, against a loopback mock: the live stream's user record carries the same uuid as its transcript line, a sub-agent's in <session>/subagents/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl. So a live card has its place at once (fixture scripts/fixtures/claude-cli/2.1.322-picture-records.json).
- **THE READER — src/transcript-picture.js, SHARED: the hub's transcript worker and the device agent run it.**
  - An index per file of the lines holding a picture (or a rescue stub), built in one native-indexOf pass and EXTENDED, never rebuilt, when the file only grew; indexed again when it was replaced or shrank. 16 held, LRU.
  - The line is read once; a structural scan skips strings by indexOf; the answer is the picture's base64 byte range (the hub) or its text (the device).
  - GET /api/chat-picture/:tx/:key/:n: found only through the harness's own locate in ONE dedicated transcript worker. A sub-agent's file must be among the conversation's own.
  - A paired machine's agent is asked only when its hello-ack names `transcript-picture`, else 409 old-agent. **The agent bundle changes: the cut signs it.**
  - The owner's cookie only (a bearer is refused by name); the type from an own entry of a null-prototype table; nosniff, private immutable + ETag.
  - At most 3 readings at once; a closed page's requests leave the queue; past 10 s ⇒ 503 finding and the view asks again. The decode is streamed block by block from the file's byte range.
  - Every OLD conversation's pictures come back at once, with no migration. A record the owner's rescue stubbed answers «rescued»; a compressed Codex rollout answers «compressed», in words.
- **(a) THE UPLOAD.** chat.uploadDir unset + a cwd under os.tmpdir() / /tmp / /var/tmp ⇒ data/chat-attachments/<hub conversation id>/files/ (a remote host: ~/.vibespace/chat-attachments/<conv>/), said in the answer and a toast.
  - Each file is a temp file in the folder LINKED to a free name, so an existing file is never overwritten («a (1).png», also between two writes at once). The numbering is ONLY on this kept road: the explorer and a chat in an ordinary folder replace a same-named file, as the release did (the reader's moderate).
  - Only the writer's own temp shape (`.<name>.<pid>-<8 hex>.vs-tmp`) older than a minute is removed at start; a person's own «….vs-tmp» file stays.
  - THE LINK `<conv>/conversation.json` (which conversation the folder is: backend + transcript id; through the store writer) is written at the upload and refreshed while the hub lists the conversation.
  - Settings › Chat («Upload files to») says what is kept, and «files of conversations that no longer exist» with a Remove door that acts only on the count and size it named. «No longer exists» is PROVEN (the reader's MUST): no live session, no session record in any form (.json / .json.orphan / .json.stopped), and the link's transcript proven absent by the harness's own locate. A terminated conversation, one a restart kept as stopped and an archived one keep their files. THE CLOSURE (主开发 15:15Z): absence is proven only by reads that SUCCEEDED — the transcript trees are walked whole (the channels' pair-sweep indexes; the projects directory itself read), a link that cannot be read or parsed is kept, an unreadable records folder offers nothing; the folders a failed read kept are said in Settings («could not check whether N conversations still exist — their files are kept»). VibeSpace has no conversation delete; removeConversation is the door a future one calls.
- **(b) Antigravity:** its wrapper resolves the same folder from CLAUDE_WEBUI_SESSION_ID. It writes temp + link, and the extension comes only from an own entry of its table.
- **(c) the agent's channel-attachment copies** (a change against the release, not only against round 1): they lived in os.tmpdir(), which the system empties at a reboot; now ~/.vibespace/channel-attachments/<instance>/<adapter>/, bounded at 512 MB with the oldest removed and the count said in the CLI's output — so a path an agent saved earlier can be removed by the bound.
- **(1) the paste road:** nothing moves; the CLI's «[Image source: /tmp/…]» note reads «The picture is kept in this conversation's history».
- **Not covered:** ACP agents draw no picture today (their tool images are text), so the user lines name Claude Code and Codex.
- **Gates:**
  - scripts/test-chat-attachments.mjs (rewritten, fast);
  - test-transcript-parity (+ the picture over a real agent: the same bytes);
  - test-desktop-remote's capability pin; test-image-cards, test-channels-agent-cli (the cache legs), test-kept-copies, test-card-grammar;
  - test-sync-fs-census (the upload route); test-architecture §86 (the rows).

  - **4, each row's reason.** The plan keeps each row's reason («the download failed (…)» or «not the pinned file (its SHA-256 differs)») and its last line names them all. runStreamInstall's error is that last line, never «the log above says why».
  - **5, the pins.** ⑦ holds a digest of FFMPEG_BUILDS. test-approval-census pins that a streamed plan's digest covers its argv, and §3c holds the fingerprint of the ffmpeg plan's bytes. The surviving mutants each have a leg: M1–M4 (⑦), M8 / M9 (⑧, on the new lines), M10 / M12 / M16 (⑨, through the real router).
  - **6, the plan's edges.** One placement keeps the old copy at .old until the new one is in, so a kill never leaves no ffmpeg.exe. A stray .old with no ffmpeg.exe is put back first. A killed run's `.dl-<guid>` folder is swept by the next run. A stamp that fails after the move is said truly, and the run counts as done. The run writes its pid to `ffmpeg.fetching`: after install_timeout / install_link_lost the hub holds its slot while the machine's facts say `fetching` (the agent's run-stream child outlives a lost link). A hash that could not be read refuses that once and is never cached.
  - **7, a settings door says why.** settingsRefusalText goes by the answer's code: not connected, an older agent, the hub refused, the machine's own failure, no answer. A refusal at the hub's send point (`stage: 'gate'`) comes back as that refusal, never as host_unavailable.
  - **8, the census says what it is.** Its header and kb-features say it is a net over sentences that carry a machine word and a need word. It cannot see a need worded past those words, a device's own refusal strings, or a log line.
  - **Two heavy reds of 7774887da's own claim (jb-f61e721e):** test-stream-op's mutant copy of stream-screen.js re-points its requires, and now re-points ffmpeg-install.js too. test-desktop-webrtc-chrome's strip-order anchor names ffEl.
  - **How the fingerprints were obtained** (the lane's ffmpeg-builds measurement, 2026-11-12): each archive was downloaded with `curl -fL` into its own new folder (logs dl-gyan / dl-btbn-gpl / dl-btbn-lgpl: time, URL, HTTP code, bytes, SHA-256) and hashed with sha256sum. Each archive's hash matched the publisher's own checksum file and GitHub's digest. Only `bin/ffmpeg.exe` was unpacked (unzip) and hashed. Only the gyan.dev zip is kept on the box (re-hashed 2026-11-13: the pin; 主开发 hashed it again at 12:43Z — 114,768,076 B, the row's SHA-256). The BtbN archives were deleted after measuring: the second row's pin stands on that measurement — the publisher's checksum file + GitHub's digest (log dl-btbn-gpl) — and nobody downloads it again without the owner's word.
  - **THE POWERSHELL WAS NEVER EXECUTED.** There is no Windows and no pwsh on this box: every line of the plan is pinned by READING it (⑧), never run. The owner's acceptance on a real Windows PC is its first run.

### machine-needs-at-pairing pick 3a — xpra.org's apt key is PINNED (主开发: «a fix of the shipped plan whether or not xpra rides pairing»)
- **The gap.** src/desktop-apps.js xpraRepoSteps (and deploy/docker/Dockerfile, the same lines) fetched https://xpra.org/xpra.asc straight into /usr/share/keyrings and named it as the repository's signer — whatever that address served was trusted as root.
- **The pin, measured 2026-11-13.** The primary key «Xpra <xpra@xpra.org>» B4993B57323148E37977E5D873254CAD17978FAF (created 2023-06-10). The same fingerprint is on keys.openpgp.org (its e-mail verified there) and keyserver.ubuntu.com. The file's SHA-256 4df3209e…ed7d is pinned too, for a machine without gpg.
- **The steps now:** fetch to xpra.asc.new → XPRA_KEY_CHECK → move into the keyring → the deb822 source → the apt pin.
  - XPRA_KEY_CHECK is ONE subshell line (as of pick 3d): sha256sum checks the FILE against the pinned SHA-256, gpg or not — an earlier cut asked gpg only whether the fingerprint was in the file. A mismatch removes the download, says so and stops with exit 3, nothing changed.
  - A person's copy of the line is `sudo sh -c '…'`, as for every `(`-line.
  - THE FETCH LINE TOO (int402, 2026-11-14 — found by the release claim's test-desktop-serve §6, on a cut that was never pushed): pick 3d made the fetch a brace group, and src/install-slot.js `planLines` chose `sudo sh -c` by a step's FIRST CHARACTER (`(` or `printf`), so a person's copy of the fetch was `sudo { … } || { … }` — sudo runs a program, never a shell word: «sudo: {: command not found», and the group after `||` ran unelevated. The root script was right all along; only the copied line was wrong. Now the builder decides by what a step IS: one simple command is handed to sudo as it is, a step that holds a shell operator or begins with a word only a shell knows goes through `sudo sh -c '…'`. Of every plan the product shows, one line changed (the fetch). test-desktop-apps §copied-lines pastes every copied line of four plans into a real /bin/sh over stand-ins (sudo that runs what it is handed, a sh that only parses) with the old line as its red control; test-desktop-serve §6 pins nine commands and no `sudo {` / `sudo (`.
  - The image runs the same lines (test-desktop-apps §xpra-repo pins both).
- **Pins.** test-desktop-apps §xpra-repo: the order; the check run in a real sh — the fixture key (scripts/fixtures/xpra/xpra.asc.hex — the public key file's bytes in hex, decoded by the suite: one armored line has a secret scanner's shape) passes, another key is refused and removed, and with no gpg on PATH the SHA-256 passes it and a changed file fails it.

### stream-udp-leg-fallback (accepted 2026-10-26 as 6787e9096, never released; ported by alignment onto 2.369.397, 2026-11-13) — a screen stream never waits 45 s on a leg that carries nothing (the owner's Mac, 2026-10-26: «leg up» at the offer, `connect_timeout` 45 s later, then a 7–10 s flap)
- **Cause (code + the hub log):** the hub's election left only a SILENT leg (35 s idle) and every PING flagged UP was life, so a leg whose 34-byte PINGs round-tripped but which carried nothing stayed elected through the page's whole connect budget; the daemon put its answers on the leg on its own whenever its PONGs came back. No stream file changed .356 → .358; the Mac's dead leg is for 主开发 to measure (the report lists what).
- **R2:** PING `ANSWERS` / PONG `WORDS` flags; the hub takes a daemon that answers only when its PROBE (r2: the largest leg DATA, 1247 bytes — legProbeBytes, derived) came back as the ECHO, then WORD TAKE; every fall WORD LEAVE; a lost LEAVE ⇒ the daemon unanswered a while (its misses). legVerdictOf names a dead leg (no_socket · bind_failed · flapping · carried_nothing · probe_lost · firewall? · unreachable · silent) on `relay.leg.verdict` + ONE log line.
- **R1:** legElect `ask` — nothing back 7 s (`legFirstMs`) after the first browser datagram on a taken leg ⇒ the device link, «(the leg carried nothing for 7 s)»; an older daemon is then left unanswered for the session. Judged on a hub timer; a page still connecting asks an ICE restart at the fall (legFallStep). Every take is a TRIAL (WORD TAKE + TRIAL): both sides keep the device link until the leg's first DATA — make before break.
- **Found end to end, not in-process:** test-stream-op §11 (a real daemon + werift, real ICE) showed the fall waiting for a browser datagram that never came (werift gave the dead pair up and sat in «checking») and the 5 s re-take cutting the device link's half-formed connection — the timer, the page's restart and the trial are its answers. **R3:** 3 falls in 2 min pin the device link (one line); re-probes back off 5 s × 2^(falls − 1). **R4:** the chip «串流 · 直连 UDP» / «串流 · 设备链路», the WHY in one line, «正在重新连接…» only when no road delivered anything.
- **Round 2 (acceptance):** a word is a state — the daemon's PING flags TRIAL, the hub says its TAKE again until the PING says up (`retakes`, `dup` on the record) and the daemon ends a trial that never heard its word at legTrialMaxMs (legFirstMs + legEchoMs) after its first DATA (`trialEndedBy`, ONE hub line); the probe = the largest leg DATA (src/stream-h264.js `RTP_OVERHEAD` + `maxDatagram`, stream-model `legProbeBytes()`), a lost one says its size. RED on f34c96b2: one lost TAKE ⇒ 120/120 answers doubled for the run; a 1210-byte path ⇒ taken, 1 of 80 answered.
- **Round 3 (acceptance):** the trial's ONE hub line is per take and never early — every WORD carries the take's number (flag bits 3–7, echoed by the daemon's PING and facts as `takeSeq`), so a re-take never reads the take before's «bound»; the line counts its take's own (the session's beside); «still on trial» waits past the daemon's bound + `legTickMs` + the round trip + `statsMs` and a later bound corrects it once («…after all»). RED on 5d9d2be7: 120 ms each way ⇒ «still on trial» in 1 of the stats timer's 4 phases; a re-take ended by the word ⇒ a second «bound» line with the first take's totals.
- **Gates:** new heavy test-stream-leg-fallback (r3: 36 — §9 the trial's line per take, a delaying middlebox; r2: 31 — §7 the lost TAKE, §8 the probe's size; 22 in round 1, each rule against the .358 pair: 45 s on the leg with 0 answers · never leaves · a 19-line flap); test-stream-op §11 (3: first picture ≈ 0.2 s in both dead shapes, the .358 hub: none in 20 s); test-desktop-webrtc §14e PURE (+ §14 flag pins `UP | ANSWERS`); test-desktop-webrtc-chrome SLOW_SAID + ⑲ control moved. The new suite is heavy because the fast tier's stated sum had 0.8 s left under its 910 s cap.

### mac-locked-capture (accepted 2026-10-26 as e35bde49a, never released; ported by alignment onto 2.369.397 after stream-udp-leg-fallback, 2026-11-13) — a locked Mac is SAID, never a black window: bounded ScreenCaptureKit waits, the lock a state of the session, the capture again in place at the unlock (FIX lane on 91bf7e18 = 2.369.358; 方案 A — measured 2026-10-26 with the owner at the Mac, macOS 27.0.1)
- **The measurement:** a capture started on a LOCKED screen waited in ScreenCaptureKit's enumeration (`getExcludingDesktopWindows`, the helper's first wait) for good — 0 % CPU, still there 4 min after the unlock; CoreGraphics answered through the lock in 43–90 ms. A display-on lock interrupted the running capture 34 s later; the agent's capture-again waited the same way. The window said «串流中断：没能及时连上 — 正在重新连接…» over a black pane until it was closed.
- **The helper (vs-5d0cce28e54e → vs-11f32156ba0a):** every ScreenCaptureKit wait bounded (`wait(bound, f) -> T?`: the enumeration + the Settings row 5 s, startCapture 10 s); a bound that fires = `end locked` on a locked screen, else `enumeration_timeout` / `start_timeout`; `locked()` read before the first ScreenCaptureKit call. Not compiled on the lane's box (no Swift toolchain) — the change is mechanical; the Mac builds it.
- **The agent:** src/agentd/stream-mac.js THE LOCK (PURE SP.LOCK_RULE {3 s, 30 min, start 20 s} + lockStep): no helper while the facts say locked, the facts every 3 s, the capture again IN PLACE at the unlock (same session, key frame first, the rate reached, the sound), `screen_locked` past 30 min, the agent's own 20 s start bound (`start_timeout` — a helper without the bounds no longer parks). stream-host pushes `paused` on every stream-stats; agentd.js unchanged.
- **The hub + the window:** desktop-webrtc records `paused` / `resumes` and logs `[stream] <host>: session <sid> stopped (locked) …` / `resumed (locked N s)`; stream-view holds its connect budget while paused and calls `onPaused`; machine-desktop + machine-app say «Mac 已锁屏（HH:MM 起）— 解锁后自动继续», chip «串流 · 锁屏中»; `screen_locked` ⇒ the two-button ask at once.
- **Shipping:** the agent bundle carries the Swift text — an upgraded Mac agent sees the helper version move and installs it (built on the Mac, or the hub's prebuilt from scripts/build-mac-helper.sh pushed at the first stream); the new helper is a new Screen Recording client ⇒ the owner switches it on once more (helper_changed_regrant).
- **Acceptance round 2 (the second commit):** the page's stall watch neither held while paused nor started again at the unlock — after a lock ≥ 12 s the machine's count moving before the page's first resumed frame ended the stream `stalled` (⇒ a reconnect, not the in-place resume). stallStep takes `paused` (no watch), stream-view drops its watch at each paused change; test-stream-locked §5 drives the REAL stream-view over the REAL hub module on a fake clock with the race forced to its bad order (RED on 244f8e2a, green here), test-desktop-webrtc §14d gains the PURE row.
- **Gates:** test-stream-locked (heavy, new — 36 legs incl. RED controls on the base's rule), test-desktop-webrtc-chrome ㉑ (+ /prelock RED), test-exit-forensics (stream-mac.js kill sites 3 → 4), test-stream-mac / test-desktop-webrtc / test-stream-plan unchanged and green.
- **The all-displays window (recovery .400 — the picture S2's claim took, display-modes-chrome ⑦):** a view stays `playing` while its capture waits, and `drawMany` counted a paused display as playing (`sum.playing ? the numbers : paused ? 锁屏中 …` — inherited from e35bde49a), so the window of every display read «串流 · 设备链路 · 2 个显示器 · 60 fps» over a locked Mac while its panes said the lock. Now a paused display is not playing, and any paused display ⇒ «串流 · 锁屏中» with the lock's words and every display's row locked, no road words — the one-display path's rule. Pin: ⑦ «every display in one window» (red on 8cc585971; its wait now lets every display's own long poll answer, ≤ pollMaxMs).
- **The moved view's pane (recovery .401 — S3's picture, cbd0aa1b5):** in the all-displays window only display 2's pane said «Mac 已锁屏…». One view MOVES between the one-display window and the all-displays set (spreadAll: the one view becomes its display's pane; collapseTo: a display's view becomes the one) and kept the onPaused it was born with, which asked only its birth role (`v === stream` / `many.get(did) === v`) — so the moved view's pane never heard the lock (verbatim in e35bde49a). Now `sayLock(v, p)` says it in the pane the view shows NOW. Pins: ⑦ every display's pane says 已锁屏 (red on cbd0aa1b5: display 1 silent), and ⑦ collapsed to one display while locked — the view that stays still says it.

The rows stay the menu's own children (every `:scope >` reader keeps reading them).

### ui-controls-and-bugs pick 4b — A PANEL KEEPS ITS NATURAL WIDTH AND SLIDES (the width list's final rule 4, 主开发 11:25Z: the chat status bar's health panel at a 320 px window was squeezed to a 130 px strip, its rows six deep, half the window empty)
- **The cause, read.** chat-status-bar.js `showDropdown` — THE ONE place a status-bar panel gets its width and place — clamps BEFORE the caller fills the panel: with no width intent it knew only the CSS 130 px minimum, kept the anchor's x near the right edge and capped the width to what was left.
- **The fix.** NEW PURE menu-place.js `panelPlace({wantLeft, containerW, natW, minW, maxW, pad})`: the width is the content's natural width within [minW, maxW] and the room, and the panel slides left until that width fits. `showDropdown` runs it once the caller has filled the panel (a microtask) and again whenever its content changes (a MutationObserver, one frame); every width write stays inside `showDropdown` (test-init-frame's single-clamp census).
- **The pin.** test-control-says-why ⑦b: `panelPlace` evaluated from its own source (a 300 px panel opened at x 250 of a 320 px window slides to x 12; one that fits stays at its chip; one wider than the window takes the window) + the wiring in `showDropdown`.

### ui-controls-and-bugs pick 0 — THE WRITE-ONLY LAW: a storage record's secret bytes never reach the page (the UI walk of 2026-11-13: the storage Edit dialog showed a Drive record's OAuth token in an edit box; 主开发's ruling the same day: every secret field)
- **The defect was the ROUTE, not the box.** `GET /api/mounts/:id/config` answered `MountManager.config()` — the record DECRYPTED for the Edit dialog's prefill (the 2.107 directive «prefill real values»; the dialog's own comment called it the design). A set-up vault masked it outside the page's reveal window; with no vault, or inside the window, every secret travelled to the owner's page. `list()` and `drive-defaults` were already clean (checked). 主开发 withdrew that design for every secret field.
- **The one mechanism.** src/mounts.js `writeOnly(out, m)` — config()'s ONE return: a secret is what the record SEALS — every `<cell>Enc` (token, clientSecret, secretKey, sessionToken, pass, bearerToken, cephSecret: read off the record, so a new provider's sealed cell is covered with no row of its own) — and, in a raw rclone record (which seals every parameter), a parameter by its NAME (`MountManager.SECRET_PARAM`: token / secret / password / key / credentials / pem; an `_id`, `_file`, `_path` is not). They leave the answer; `held` names the ones the record holds. The vault mask still covers the other sealed parameters outside the window. Server-only readers (`oauthTokenOf` / `oauthClientOf` for the channel API) are untouched.
- **The page half.** src/lib/sidebar-mounts.js `heldFields()` + `wireHeld()` (beside `maskVaultFields`): a held secret is «已保存» + «替换…», which opens an EMPTY box sent only when typed (the Integrations page's shape); an unset one is an empty password box; the OAuth token is ONE line «已授权 · Google Drive» / «未授权 · …»; the existing Re-authorize door stays in the footer, as the channel Edit's (test-oauth-field-parity §7) — Gmail, which has no such door here, gets «替换…» to paste a new token. The submit skips a field with no box; `_mountClientSwitch` counts a HELD secret. The design comments that said «secrets included» say the law now.
- **The pin.** NEW scripts/test-mount-write-only.mjs (fast, 24; pick 0b renames it test-write-only-secrets and widens it): every sealed cell named in the tree, planted into every registry row + a child, answers none of its bytes inside the window or out, and is named in `held`; the parameter rule (5 secret names held, 3 plain ones kept); `mounts.config(` has ONE caller and the server-only readers are named; the dialog's hooks, SECRET_FIELD covers every sealed cell, no `cfg.<secret>` read; a copy without `writeOnly` leaks 45 (control). AT THE ROUTE: test-vault-contents — the owner's cookie, in the window and out: `secretKey` held, never the bytes.
- MOVED: test-mount-providers ② (the fake acme row's sealed key is held — a new row is covered) and ③ (the named write-only delta, 14 scenarios); test-vault-inventory ③b (the s3 secret key and an rclone client_secret held, not masked); test-voice-boxes (Gmail's token replace box: a row with its reason).
- **Not taken here (said on the lane page):** the channel accounts' `GET /api/channels/adapters/:id/config` still answers the custom app secret to its Edit dialog.

### ui-controls-and-bugs pick 0b — THE WRITE-ONLY LAW is a census over the tables that mark a field secret (主开发's ruling 2026-11-13: «make the LAW a census, not two fixes»)
- **The second instance.** `GET /api/channels/adapters/:id/config` (channels-auth.js `adapterConfig`) answered an account's custom app secret decrypted to its Edit / Re-authorize / Duplicate dialogs (the D3 «storage rule»). Now `client` is `{appId, secretSet, undecryptable}`. `reauthorize` reads the SAME client id with an EMPTY secret as the account's own sealed client (`ownCustomChoice`); a new id still needs its secret. The Edit save sends a credential only when a new secret is typed.
- **The page half, shared.** mounts-dialog.js `renderFields` gains `held`: «已保存» + «替换…» over an empty, hidden box (heldSecretRow). The channel dialogs draw their custom secret through it; the hint says «密钥保存后不再显示，只能替换。». The old «Prefilled with the real current value, the secret included…» key is gone from zh / ja.
- **The census.** scripts/test-mount-write-only.mjs → scripts/test-write-only-secrets.mjs (fast, 42). It derives its tables from the tree and each leg plants and reads the real answers:
  - ① storage sealed cells × every provider row, ② the rclone parameter rule;
  - ③ every Integrations card's secret field (`secret: true`, the company-preset env) — list() / publicView() carry at most the declared 4-char tail, `set` says it is set;
  - ③b every per-machine row (remoteapp, desktop-signin) through setMachineValues — machineView carries not even a tail;
  - ④ every account-bound vendor with a client secret (lark, gmail, slack) — an account sealed by the engine's own key: adapterConfig / adapterView / the accounts digest carry no byte, `client.secretSet` says held;
  - ⑤ no GET handler decrypts in its own body; `mounts.config(` and `adapterConfig(` have ONE route each; the server-only OAuth readers are named;
  - ⑥ the storage dialog's hooks, the shared renderer's `held`, the channel dialogs never read `client.appSecret`;
  - ⑦ five copy controls (storage, integrations mask, channels answer, a channel view with only a tail) RED.
- **The rule as ruled (主开发 2026-11-13):** a secret's bytes never reach the page, except the declared tail on an Integrations card (R.maskValue: the last four, only for a value of 12 or more); per-machine rows, storage cells and channel clients get none — so the channel account view's `customClient.secretMasked` tail is gone (customClientView = {appId, secretSet, undecryptable}).
- **Duplicate** needs no secret from the page: the server copies the source's sealed secret (re-sealed, a fresh nonce); an undecryptable one is refused by name (409 custom-undecryptable, «enter it again before duplicating») — never a silent copy without one.
- MOVED: test-channels-engine (the owner's prefill, the card), test-channels-accounts (the prefill, the row, the PUT answer) — held, no tail; test-integration-registry's env-name allowlist gains the census (it plants through the store's env HANDLE, never process.env).

### ui-controls-and-bugs — the closure on the storage secrets (主开发 15:15Z: THE LAW is deny by default; rides with picks 0 / 0b)
- **THE ONE TABLE** (src/mounts.js NEW `RCLONE_PARAMS`, frozen; `MountManager.RCLONE_PARAMS`): a raw rclone parameter is a SECRET unless its name is a row marked `plain`; the tree's own credential options are rows marked `secret`. A name with no row — what the owner typed — is a secret whatever its value or its ending: the boolean-value rule and the _id / _file / _path / _url / _uri / _type / _mode suffix rule are GONE (a password literally «true» was shown). test-write-only-secrets ② reads every option the providers write (`P('X')`, `RCLONE_CONFIG_VS_X`, a `*_KEYS` set — 27 today) and is red for one with no row (planted `BRAND_NEW_OPT`: red by name).
- **A CREDENTIAL URL is a secret whatever its row** (NEW `CREDENTIAL_URL`): a value that parses as a URL with userinfo, or with a query naming sig / signature / x-amz-* / x-goog-* / token / access_token / auth / key / api_key / password / secret — rclone's http backend authenticates by `url = https://user:pass@host`, a webdav url, an S3 endpoint and sia's api_url the same (the closure's verifier: url / endpoint / api_url / a signed storage_url came back in clear).

### lane chrome-157 — THE WHOLE-PROFILE LAW (the owner's, 2026-11-13): an agent's lease never acts on the person's whole profile or the whole browser; a download BORROWS the profile's folder only while it is in flight (on the cure below, 743ed06fb; the .401 read's list, 主开发 18:08Z)
- **Measured with the real driver (agent-browser 0.38.2, Chrome 154.0.8037.57 + Chrome for Testing 157.0.8103.50; the lane's work/measure/probe-*.mjs):** the driver sends no whole-profile call when it connects; `cookies clear` sends Network.clearBrowserCookies; `download` sends Browser.setDownloadBehavior **on its page session** `{behavior:'allowAndName', downloadPath, eventsEnabled:true}` and listens to Browser.download* AND Page.download* (withholding the Browser ones, its download still worked). Both forms move the WHOLE profile's folder (the person's file landed in the agent's folder); Page.setDownloadBehavior too (not scoped to its page). With the browser form + eventsEnabled the PERSON's download reached the agent's connection (its url, its file name) and the agent's Browser.cancelDownload(guid) canceled it; with the session form only that page's own downloads reach the session; a download's frameId is the tab it began in. `{behavior:'default'}` from ANY connection puts the profile's place back; with `eventsEnabled:true` that connection keeps seeing downloads.
- **The law, ONE verdict on both roads, every wire shape:** `wholeProfileVerdict` over the rows marked `law` — 22 `whole-profile` (the profile's acts; the read's L1: every refused row that acts on the whole BROWSER — Browser.close / crash / crashGpuProcess / executeBrowserCommand / addMockCamera / setGlobalPrivacyControl, Cast.startDesktopMirroring, Extensions.loadUnpacked / uninstall, Target.setRemoteLocations, Tethering.bind / unbind — and Target.sendMessageToTarget / exposeDevToolsProtocol, which carried a call past the verdict; on the scope road they were forwarded), 4 own-context, Browser.cancelDownload own-download, Browser.setDownloadBehavior the window (`deny` and another's context refused). Every refusal carries its own recipe — 22 of 22 pinned FAST (test-cdp-census ⑫, both roads), with the own-context «ask the person».
- **THE WINDOW, rebuilt (the read's W1–W6 — the pick's first window opened at the set, had no bound, was closed by anyone's download, never opened for the real driver's session form, and leaked the person's downloads):** ONE state per profile, the PURE `windowStep` (src/browser-mediation.js), executed by the mediator's `stepWindow`: counts only the lease's own downloads (by frame), a bound when none begins (15 s and a later download canceled at 831913e2c — the closure list below made it 30 s, measured, and never canceled), one window per profile (another lease's set refused by name), every wire shape of the set, closed at the download's end / the bound / a takeover (told: the card and the handback) / the lease's end / its LAST connection closing; a repoint drops it, a hub stop puts it back best-effort, a hub start's adoption (`mediator.adopt`) puts it back before the profile's first grant (3 tries, said). A lease is told only its own downloads, only if it asked, nothing after its window closed; Browser.cancelDownload only for its own. The put-back rides the lease's own connection when it stands (ordered before its next set — the read's race).
- **THE TABLE (generated, scripts/download-window-cells.mjs):** 7 states × 19 acts — 122 cells, 11 culls named — the expected cell written from the laws, never from the code; the PURE windowStep agrees with all 122 (fast); the real mediator over a fake that models the measured Chrome agrees with all 244 (both roads), the set on the page session and with no session. **On 639e093b8 (the pick as read): 175 of 244 cells RED with the real driver's session form (no window ever opened for it), 149 with the browser form.**
- **The words made true (L2):** the scope road FAILS CLOSED (a scoped url that cannot be made refuses `scope_unavailable` by name — the raw endpoint was handed out before) and its grant learns when the person drives; a Separate-tabs profile on a hub with no proxy is worded UNAVAILABLE (every lease there is refused); the window's one sentence carries its bound (CHANGELOG, manual, kb); the manual separates the cache wipe from the site-state wipe; VibeSpace's own `permission` verb is said as what it does (ONE origin's permission in every watched context, the person's included; a geolocation position on every watched tab) — whether it becomes a proposal on a shared profile is 主开发's to rule. Rowed, not solved: the any-origin writes (B-771e).
- **Gates:** test-cdp-census 112 (⑫ the law in the FAST tier), test-browser-mediation 307 (⑥c / ⑥e: every window cell over the real proxy, two leases, two downloads, the person's download, the adoption door; behavioural mutant controls — the first completion, any lease's end, events unfiltered, the scope road without the verdict; ④: a hub start's adoption through a second real keeper, the no-proxy words, the scope road failing closed), test-everyone-principal 106; test-browser-mediation-chrome: the pick's real-driver leg (own grants and sessions, both roads: `cookies clear` refused by name, `download` works and the window closes, a person's download lands in the person's place once it closed, and is never told to the lease while one stands — the session and the browser form) — a heavy, its claim after «before done».

### lane chrome-157 — the closure list (主开发 19:58Z, S1–S8): every state of THE WINDOW has an end the hub can see, the window speaks, a lease hears its own downloads once
- **Measured again (Chrome 154 + Chrome for Testing 157; the lane's work/measure/probe-driver-slow.mjs, probe-fixed-at-begin.mjs, probe-session-default.mjs):** the real driver clicks 1–3 ms after its set; its download begins when the page's first byte comes (1.03 s / 10.03 s after the set for a 1 s / 10 s page); it gives up at 30.05 s (its own timeout — a 30 s page and a page that never answers alike) ⇒ **the bound is 30 s** (S2 d). ## 2.369.400 — 2026-11-13

### ui-phone-and-fit pick 0 — THE OWNER'S CASE: a For-you row's options are whole at every width, and the strip's row opens in place (the owner 2026-11-13; 主开发's law, both halves)
- **What the owner saw:** a ~500 px chat window, zh. The strip «等你操作 · 9 个问题» drew the question cut, «52 分钟前», four icon buttons, then «回复：保留 ag», cut by the window's edge. «这样我都看不到推荐回复选项…考虑不同窗口尺寸了吗？». A minute later: «这个下面没法展开看详情，每次都要点击跳回对话位置才能看».
- **Causes (on 935960b7e):**
  - The base `.ut-opt` and `.iw-opt` were `nowrap` + ellipsis.
  - The strip's options were ONE line that scrolled sideways (`flex-wrap: nowrap; overflow-x: auto`), with pills capped at 24 em with an ellipsis.
  - The phone's pills were clamped to two lines.
  - On the desktop, the strip's question press only landed in the conversation; its detail fold was hidden in the strip.
- **THE OPTIONS LAW** (style.css + chat.css): every rule that styles an option or an options row draws the option WHOLE.
  - The pill wraps inside itself: `white-space: normal`, `overflow-wrap: break-word`, no ellipsis, no clamp.
  - The strip's options take a line of their own (`flex 1 1 100%`) and wrap. The question then gets two lines.
  - «Reply:» is said ONCE: `.ut-opts-label` / `.iw-opts-label`. Each pill is its own words, and its accessible name and tip keep «Reply: …» (lane controls-that-lie). The agent's first option, its recommendation, stays first.
- **THE ROW OPENS IN PLACE** (chat-needs-card.js):
  - The question's press toggles `cad-open` on every class.
  - The open strip floats over the transcript (`_dockOver`). A `.cad-spacer` of its closed height keeps its place, so the transcript's size and scrollTop never move. It stands on the same bottom edge, at most half the view, scrolling inside. It is taken out of the flow FIRST and then measured — measured while it still stood under the spacer, it came out a strip too high and the observer moved it down a frame later, after the open had armed its Allow (the first claim's test-phone-dock-chrome ㉓ r2: an Allow pressed at 821 ms answered nothing). Its place is read again whenever the view, or what sits below the spacer, resizes (a ResizeObserver: a window resized, a message box grown, a keyboard up). On the phone its 45 % bound is also bounded by half the view (`min(45dvh, --cad-max)`), so a keyboard that shrinks the view never pushes it past the view's top.
  - The whole question, the detail fold open (THE tray's renderer, links live), every option on a line of its own.
  - The landing is a worded door, `.cad-jump` «Show it in the conversation»; the meta's press still lands.
  - Law 7: while open, the item stays the strip's item (`_dockPass` keeps it). A newer ask or a count change redraws around it.

### connection-notice-once (the slow-link pick, on the notice pick) — a slow client is not a dead one: the heartbeat waives a miss only on proof the peer drains, capped in bytes per episode with a bound proved by search (the same evening as the notice: the loop cut a slow link about once a minute with the owed frame never read)
- **Law 5 — THE LOOP IS REAL, AND ITS CUTTER IS THE HEARTBEAT.** `lagged` closes no socket (it stops one session's frames until the re-attach). But the ping rides the same queue, so a frame that takes the link > 30 s makes its ping late however healthy the client is; the cut loses the half-read frame (a WebSocket message is applied whole), the reconnect is owed the same bytes, the next round cuts them again. Measured on 8b3fdb6ab, a real hub + Chrome at 200 kbit/s (a proxy: CDP throttling does not reach websocket reads), 5.2 MB backlog: 180 s = 3 heartbeat cuts, a socket drop about once a minute (57 / 117 / 177 s), 0 `attached`, stuck at 829 / 838. FIX (the heartbeat over src/ws-keepalive.js `drainVerdict` + `drainMark`): a miss is waived only on proof the peer is reading — bytes left a NON-EMPTY queue, i.e. the kernel's buffer was full and the peer ACKed — plus one round of grace for what the kernel still held. Bytes merely handed to a kernel with room are no proof: a half-dead path swallows a trickle, and that first cut (never shipped) would have kept ghosts ~15 min. Same path: 420 s = 0 cuts, 0 drops, `attached` at 209 s, 838 / 838. The bounded slab the brief proposed for this loop was not built: the queue's bound was never the cutter.
- **Rounds 3–5 (the bound's history).** Round 3 F4, one rule and one measurement: the heartbeat reads src/ws-keepalive.js `livenessVerdict` over `drainMark`, which moved there, and the stream bridges' keepalive reads the same mark. It carried no ghost but was blind inside a frame (real sockets, one 12 MiB frame at 400 KB/s, 2 s rounds: cut at round 2, never landed; now landed, never cut). **New limits:** the proof needs WAN-sized socket buffers (a deep ~4 MB loopback buffer moves `taken` in 1.5 MB bursts, so behind a local relay the link must reach the limit stated in the heartbeat's comment and the kb, measured on the model in round 6: kept from 650 kbit/s; 200–560 kbit/s kept through its drain, then often cut once the queue is empty; ≤ 160 kbit/s cut on its second round — the round-3 estimate of ≈400–500 kbit/s is superseded); a queue that empties is carried for queued ÷ R, then the grace round, then the judging round, 60–90 s after it empties. (Round 4 bounds a queue that does not empty.) Round 4 G1, major: draining is not keeping up. `output` frames carry no seq, so `lagged` never stops them; a reader moving bytes every round was waived every round while a faster producer filled the hub's queue (a reader at ~1 MB/s under 3.2 MB/s, 2 s rounds: never cut, 73 MiB in 30 s; 8b3fdb6ab cut at 4 s, 6 MiB). `drainVerdict` (src/ws-keepalive.js: `livenessVerdict`, byte-unchanged, + keeping up) reads `losing` when a pong-less round's backlog is past `backlogAllowance` and grew; that waives nothing and ends the grace. The heartbeat's allowance is `lagged`'s 4 MiB; the bridges stay on `livenessVerdict` alone, their high-water / frameGate stop their producers. **Bound: cut on the first pong-less round past the allowance; the ceiling is the larger of the allowance and one round of reading, + one round of the producer's surplus.** Measured at the real 30 s round: 25 KB/s under 100 KB/s through WAN-sized buffers, cut at 60 s, 4.4 MiB, the same as 8b3fdb6ab (f046350ae: never cut, 11 MiB and rising at 150 s); 1 MB/s under 1.6 MB/s, cut at 90 s, 51 MiB of backlog, the same as 8b3fdb6ab (f046350ae: never cut). A reader that keeps up is still kept at any size. Round 5 H1, major: round 4 judged growth only on rounds that drained, against the round before; on a deep send buffer the kernel takes bytes in ~1.45 MiB bursts every 3–4 s, so a reader at 400 KB/s under 520 KB/s grew the backlog between bursts and shrank it at each one, never `losing` (the acceptance: 7.7 MiB and rising at 59 s; its model at 30 s rounds: 31.5 MiB in 30 min). Now `drainVerdict(memo, round)` judges EVERY pong-less round against the stretch's last round of the same kind (drained against drained, not against not; a stretch's first drain against the round before); a pong ends the stretch. Model, on the tree's own heartbeat: 400/520 at 2 s cut at 24 s, 4.4 MiB; 30 KB/s under 45 KB/s at 30 s cut at 180 s, 4.5 MiB; a reader that shrinks the backlog across bursts (400 KB/s under 250 KB/s, 8 MB owed) kept through its drain. Bound: the larger of the allowance and a round of reading, + one burst, + two rounds of the surplus. Price: a reader keeping up by less than its own burst noise (5 %) is cut, as on 8b3fdb6ab. Not reproduced on real sockets on this box (the kernel's autotuned buffers absorbed a 60 s run; the acceptance of 3b4f37610 reproduced it on real loopback sockets with SO_RCVBUF 4096); pinned on the model.
- **Round 6 (acceptance on 4a34eed82: H2, the gates and the .387 rehearsal hold; the stated bound did not).** B1 + B2, majors: a random search found the stated bound false (179.9 MiB on one socket; a reader that stalls one round after each ping never cut): the same-kind heuristic left rounds unjudged. Now the waiver is capped in BYTES: an episode runs from the first round past the 4 MiB allowance (pong or not) to the first round back under it, a pong does not end it, its ceiling is its first backlog + 4 MiB, and a pong-less round above the ceiling is cut; the same-kind heuristic is gone. **Bound, proved and searched:** ≤ max(4 MiB, owed) + 4 MiB + 2 rounds of production at a round the socket survives (3 at the cut); the new heavy suite test-connection-notice-bound searches it on the acceptance's model (3 seeds × 10 000 + a 21 600 grid + the ratchet + a stall-and-catch-up reader): 0 over; 4a34eed82: 61 / 66 / 74 over. B3: the price is gone (every keep-up margin 0–30 % kept, a backlog that holds exactly too, where round 5 cut up to 25 %); the cost is that a reader falling behind is kept until it is 4 MiB behind its episode's start (25 KB/s under 100 KB/s: cut at 120 s, ~9 MiB; the base 60 s, 4.4 MiB). The deep-buffer line restated to the model's measure. B4: the episode is pinned at the heartbeat (`_hbEpisode` survives a pong).
- **Not built, by choice: the bounded slab the brief proposed.** It answered a `lagged` → cut → reconnect path that does not exist (`lagged` closes no socket), and the loop's cycles are 0 and the transcript whole without it. (No slab, but the queue does have a bound since round 4: see above.) The cost of the choice: a link that dies by itself more often than a frame takes still restarts that frame from zero.
- **Acceptance of 3b4f37610 (two readers, 主开发 09:13Z): the bound holds.** 50 000 searched profiles, a 15 120-point directed grid and the counter and episode edges all stay within max(A, ceiling) + Pr (worst 0.997); 0 of 20 000 keep-up readers cut, and never a reader the release keeps; on real plain / TLS sockets at 30 s rounds the release cuts a slow reader at 60 s with its frame unread, the tip delivers it. THE LIST, words and pins, applied in one commit: (1) against the release the law adds at most max(4 MiB, owed) + 4 MiB + **one round of production** (the sentence without it was short: 172 of 10 000 profiles passed its number); (2) a peer that dies with a backlog standing is cut up to 3 rounds (≤ 90 s) after it died, the release ≤ 2; an idle dead peer as before; (3) the stall exclusion also covers the clean rounds after a stall while a ping sent in it is still outstanding (the release has the same hole); (4) the bound suite's PRICE legs now assert «kept through its drain» (never cut while the backlog stands; a backlog that holds exactly, 30 min), red on the release (7 of 7: cut at 4 s or 60 s), where they asserted only «not cut as outrun» and were green on it; (5) fast ⑩ pins drainMark's `bytesWritten − taken` term (a backlog behind the write in flight opens the episode; mutant M9 `backlog: queued` red); (6) real loopback sockets DO show the kernel's bursts once the reader's receive buffer is small (SO_RCVBUF 4096), and the limit then cuts on the tip as on the release — the docs said they did not.
- **The user line says the limit (the merged-tip read of .400, 主开发 16:41Z).** «A slow connection no longer keeps cutting a chat that is catching up» was unconditional; behind a relay or reverse proxy on the hub's own machine (a deep send buffer) a very slow link is still cut: ≤ 160 kbit/s on its second round, 200–560 kbit/s often after its drain, kept from 650 kbit/s. The line now says «unless it is very slow and passes through a relay on VibeSpace's own computer» (zh / ja the same). By design and unchanged: a reader that trickles while its backlog stays under the 4 MiB allowance is never cut (no cap in rounds), its memory bounded per socket at about 8 MiB.
- **Gates.** test-connection-notice (fast: + ⑩ the heartbeat over fake sockets, ⑭ one rule over one mark); NEW test-connection-notice-slowlink-chrome (heavy: ② the drain mark on real plain / TLS / demux sockets, ③ the slow-link frame — split out because round 6's legs and the page's ⑤ need more than one 10-minute claim: the whole ran out at 590 s with 83 passed, 0 failed); test-connection-notice-bound (heavy, ~12 s in-process: the search, 0 over; RED on 4a34eed82 by count). RED on the notice pick's tree with its clock (a5644f599): ⑩, ⑭, slow-link ② ③.
