## 2.369.399 — 2026-11-13

### connection-notice-once (the notice pick) — a connection state is ONE live notice, never a log line per event (the owner 2026-11-06, on a phone: «以后别拿这个刷屏了吧»)
- **The mechanism.** `_stateHandler` appended a system row on every real transition to disconnected and every reconnect; ws.js's guard stops only the RETRY loop, so a real flap (open → close → open) paid two rows. Each was a `.chat-msg` with no record, which every reader of the window's cards counted: `_trimEdge`'s ceiling and its bounds arithmetic (a trim of rows moved `_windowEnd` by rows it dropped), the index landings, the timestamp walks.
- **What the pager's number was.** `_total` is the server's `totalCount` + one per live create; appendSystem never touched it. «677–726 / 726» was the transcript's 726 RECORDS and the 50 of them in the window — never rows, so never «363 cycles». Telemetry 2026-11-06 to 20:30 PT: 66 `ws-outage-ms` across every client, 22 hub cuts. The shot shows 30 rows on one screen; nothing records how many there were above it.
- **Laws 1–3.** src/lib/connection-notice.js: PURE `noticeStep` + one element per view. A drop = one row; the reconnect rewrites it («已重新连接 · 断开 12 秒»); a later cycle rewrites and counts («连接不稳定：断开 N 次，最近 21:01 已重连»); `_total` moved ⇒ a new row. The row has `.chat-msg-system` (every rebuild's sweep takes it) and NOT `.chat-msg` (no card to any reader); the search highlight walks past it; `data-first-at` + the tooltip keep the first drop's time; a trim drops a row left outside the cards; a row paged over goes back to the tail at the next cycle. No toast existed per cycle and none does (the one connection toast answers the person pressing Send).
- **Law 4.** `_reconnectAttach()`, the 2 s + jitter retry, the 401 bounce and the lagged re-attach are untouched and pinned.
- **The client's road (addendum 1).** Measured with desktop Chrome on a scratch hub: a page frozen 10 / 40 / 70 s gets `onclose` 1006 at its resume and is back in 2.3–3.4 s, the hub logging nothing; a tab backgrounded 70 s and a browser suspended 20 s keep the socket; a browser suspended 70 s is cut by the heartbeat and cycles once at SIGCONT (the lane's first table said 0: it predated the ghost fix). `ws-outage-ms` starts at the page's `onclose`, so a frozen page reads ~3 s however long it slept (≤ 4 s = 112 of 339 outages in 7 days). The road itself is the browser's and stays. Not reproduced on a real Android.
- **Round 2: a cycle nobody could have noticed is not a notice (law 1 amended by 主开发 on that measure).** A cycle that BEGINS while the page is hidden or frozen says nothing and counts nothing, so «断开 N 次» counts awake outages only. Two things break the silence, once each: the re-attach asked to resume by seq and the hub could not (`slab:'held'` did not come back; `answered(true)`, after the rebuild's sweep when the road is a rebuild), and the socket still down 10 s after the page woke (the person is looking at a chat with no server). A drop heard within 5 s of a wake still began asleep: the browser delivers it at the resume. An awake drop is always the notice, whoever cut it. **A hub's cut of a sleeping page is not a miss by itself (the amended law first said it was; 主开发 agreed to this on the measure).** A radio that sleeps answers no ping, so the heartbeat cuts it within 60 s on any long lock (reasoned from the two-miss rule, not measured on a phone) and the seq resume still loses nothing; a row there would count unlocks again, and it would need new wire. A frozen cut that really lost frames is a row through the gap rule; the frozen + cut + held case is pinned silent. NOT covered: a page that sleeps with no event (a laptop lid with the tab still «visible») reads as awake.
- **Addendum 1.** The Resume dialog printed literal `<b>` / `<br>`: `showConfirmDialog` sets its message as TEXT. Plain words, the key renamed in zh + ja + test-dead-socket-keeps-chat-meta §7.
- **Rounds 3–5, the notice's fixes (three acceptance panels held the notice).** Round 3: F1: a quiet cycle nobody answered (a read-only view's `_reattach` returns at once) no longer hands its start to the next one: 75 s read «down 5 h». F2: only a freeze dates a row from the sleep: a hidden tab whose code ran, shown, then a 15 s drop read «down 2 h». Round 4 (G2): a freeze dates only the FIRST close at its end; a reconnect spends it, and past the grace after the resume it is gone («down 5 h» for a 15 s drop right after a reconnect, «down 2 h» after 2 h hidden and running). Round 5 (H2): every freeze dates its row from its OWN start (a second freeze after a reconnect read «down 1 h» for 10 min; a first one after an hour hidden and running did too).
- **Two picks (主开发 2026-11-13).** Law 5 (the heartbeat cut a slow link about once a minute, the owed frame never read; fixed by a miss waived only on proof the peer drains, capped in bytes, with its bound proved by search) is its own pick on top of this one. Every panel's «not accepted» was about that bound, and the owner's complaint is the notice. This pick changes no line of src/server/ws-heartbeat.js or src/ws-keepalive.js, and carries neither test-connection-notice-bound, fast ⑩ / ⑭ nor chrome ② / ③.
- **The row's time is the owner's clock (主开发's merged-tip read, 09:05Z: a follow-up commit on the accepted pick).** The notice printed the browser's locale (`toLocaleTimeString([])`), so an English browser with the interface in Chinese read «最近 02:05 PM 已重连» beside a For-you «14:05». chat-view hands the notice `timeOn` (src/lib/owner-facts.js over src/when-words.js: 24-hour `HH:MM` + the zone's short name, in the page's zone). Pinned in fast ⑪ (the source line + the formatter's own words for a fixed instant) and chrome ⑤ (no AM / PM on the page). connection-notice.js keeps its browser-locale default for callers that pass no clock (the suites' stubs).
- **Gates.** test-connection-notice (fast, PURE: the tree's own handler over a stub list, the page's lifecycle over a stub document and clock, the re-attach's answer from the tree's own lines); test-connection-notice-chrome (heavy: CDP freezes of 10 / 40 / 70 s, a frozen page the hub cut, a hidden tab, a frozen page that lost frames, a hub's cut while awake, 10 real flaps at a phone's shape, the trim, the Resume dialog, and ⑤ the owner's pictures at 390 px in Chinese: 10 flaps, a hide / show cycle). Pin moved: test-hidden-view-suspend §6. RED by name and behaviour on a copy of the release (fd4acdc61): 726 rows for 363 cycles, 20 rows for 10 flaps; CONTROL on a round-1 copy: every cycle counted, ⑬ and ④ red. RED on a round-2 copy: «down 5 h», «down 2 h»; on a round-3 copy: «down 5 h» after a reconnect; on a round-4 copy: a second freeze «down 1 h».

The worker's heap after its requires rose 6.36 → 6.47 MiB from .363 to the cut; a reading that sits on its cap moves with a tenth of a MB (test-ledger-dedup-law ⑧ records the same: +0.32 MB took §30 to red 13 of 34).

### account-reset-door K2 — the claims store is a store: through the store writer (主开发's read of the .397 tip, K2)
- **The finding (minor).** src/usage-reset-claim.js saved outside the store writer: fs.promises (the threadpool) on each save, and a synchronous fsync on the main thread at the process's exit (`stopAll` → `flushSync`). Its test-store-write-census row was classed «exit», which let three main-thread syncs past the debt ratchet. As «debt» the same row goes red, 521 > 518. It also made the census's own sentence («the «exit» class is empty») untrue.
- **The fix.** The store writes through src/store-writer.js like every store since .396: `W().dirty(file, {name: 'reset-claims.write', mode: 0o600, produce})`.
  - Memory is authoritative, and the writer's own thread does the temp, every byte and the rename. At a stop, the writer's exit flush writes what is owed.
  - A person's claim and dismissal are ACTS (rank 0). `persisted()` is the writer's `durable(file)`, and both routes answer after it; one that did not land answers `durable: false`.
  - What a reading settles (a confirmation, a contradiction, a reset seen) is paced.
  - `flushSync`, `stopAll` and the module's own exit hook are gone.
- **The censuses.**
  - test-store-write-census: the «exit» row and the WAITS row are gone. The «exit» class is empty again, so its sentence is true, and DEBT is unchanged.
  - test-sync-fs-census: the «create > flushSync» row is gone.

  - The routes answered 200 with a `durable: false` the page never read. They now take the status route's shape (src/agent-routes/status.js): 503 `not-durable` with the store writer's own sentence, the claim's fields beside it. The claim is APPLIED (in memory, and the pool reads it).

  - Each `then()` has a second arm, so an answer is always sent.
  - Pinned in the route leg: the writer made to answer false for the claims file ⇒ 503 `not-durable`, the claim applied (/api/usage shows it claimed), the page's words carry both, and the dismissal answers 503 too. ### mount-class-by-source — A VIEW OF A MOUNT IS CLASSED BY WHAT IT SHOWS (the data-move read: the owner's checkout leaves the NAS for the local disk)
- **The finding.** src/mount-path-class.js `rootsOf` classed a fuse.bindfs mount by WHERE THE INSTANCE LIVED: 'home' while it held rootDir / dataDir, otherwise 'storage' (STORAGE_FSTYPE matches every fuse.*).
  - The owner's workspace is a bindfs VIEW of the kernel NFS mount /mnt/nfs_workspace, and the instance lived on it: 'home', witnessed, never refused.
  - Read by two drivers on the released tree: the day the instance moves to the local disk, the SAME view turns 'storage'. The guard then refuses every main-thread sync call on a project path (EVSMOUNTSYNC), and every storageRootOf caller takes its storage road, with nothing said.
  - Where the hub lives changed what it may touch.
- **The law.** A passthrough view (VIEW_FSTYPE = fuse.bindfs, one constant) is classed by the mount its source lives on:
  - over NFS: 'network';
  - over a storage mount, or under a product storage row: 'storage';
  - over anything that is neither network nor FUSE (a local disk, tmpfs, an NTFS stick …): the new kind 'disk' — witnessed (a stopped FUSE daemon holds every reader, whatever it shows), never refused. This is 主开发's ruling on the first post; «no root» would have worded such a hold «not under a mount». Only the REFUSAL follows the source; the WATCH follows the daemon.
  - **below the source (round 2, law 3 made exact: a path is refused when what it REACHES is storage, by whichever spelling).** bindfs crosses into every mount below its source, so each mount listed below a view's source, and each product storage row there, is a DERIVED root at the view's spelling, with the class it has when reached; its row carries `shows` and `through`. A storage view already refuses all of it; a view the instance lives on derives nothing (home wins, as on the release); a real row at the same spelling wins.
  - A source that cannot be told stays 'storage', and so do a product storage row (whatever it is made of), rclone and sshfs.
  - 'home' still wins when the instance lives on the view.
  - The module stays PURE (rows in, classes out).
- **The source and the match** (no disk touched):
  - bindfs (1.18.4) passes its source through realpath(3) at start and shows it as the row's fsname: absolute, symlink-free, as of mount time, octal-escaped. A source that is not absolute (an fsname given by hand) cannot be told.
  - The match is the longest mount point holding the source among the rows handed in. Never matched: the view itself, or a row listed after it at or under its own mount point (`bindfs /d /d` shows what lies beneath).
  - Equal mount points (round 2): the last row listed BEFORE the view — what it entered when it started; a mount put over its source afterwards does not change what it serves. None before ⇒ the last listed. LINE order is mount order; mount ids are reused (the box: view 714, its NFS 732).
  - '/' holds a source. A view of a view is followed; a loop ⇒ storage (round 2: no depth rule — the seen set ends every loop). A view's row carries `shows` {root, fstype}.
  - NOT FOLLOWED, said in the module: a source lazily unmounted while the view still serves it; a view that started BEFORE its source's mount (it reads that mount though it serves the folder beneath — the rows cannot tell it from a remount, and both are watched, never refused); mergerfs / fuse-overlayfs / gocryptfs (they stay 'storage' until named).
- **The words.**
  - PURE `viewWords(row)` adds «— a fuse.bindfs view of the nfs4 mount «…»» (or «of the storage folder «…»», or «whose source the mount table does not show (refused until it can be told)») to the witness's line and to the guard's refusal and log-only lines, for a view's own row only.
  - Every other row's words are byte for byte as they were (test-fs-canary and test-sync-fs-guard-server pin «the mount «…»$»).
  - A derived root adds «— the fuse.rclone mount «…» reached through the fuse.bindfs view «…»» (or «the storage folder «…»»).
  - callWords for 'disk' names the type shown: «under the mount «…» — a fuse.bindfs view of the ext4 mount «…» (witnessed, never refused)» (round 2: never «this machine's own disk», untrue of tmpfs or a stick).
  - mount-health HELD_TAIL.disk: «This folder shows another folder of this machine through a FUSE program: its calls are watched, never refused.» (zh + ja).
- **The standing sweep.**
  - Agree by construction (they read the classifier's rows): storage-path's storageRootOf, the canary, and the For-you hold item.
  - local-index netMountOf / landedPathOf, mounts.js _onNetworkFs and vfs-cache-place's statfs answer «is it a network or FUSE file system» (where the index or a cache may live). They say yes on every view row, and so does the classifier now (the 'disk' row is a root): no row parts.
  - The mounts panel shows the product's own records (all 'storage' still).
- **The storageRootOf callers, as rows**, on the owner's box after the move. Each answers what it answered before the move: realCwdOf, task-groups `_realOf` and the Context reads, the transcript-folder decode, a project's agent-browser.json, execHere, the pending editor. A census in test-fs-canary §9 makes a new caller without a row red.
- **Round 2 (the verifier: the release as the oracle over 155 mount tables, 39 730 probe paths; the guard end to end).**
  - MUST, fixed: an rclone / a product row BELOW the NFS source was reached through the view as «network» (five sync calls ran). It is now a derived storage root, refused and named.
  - Small 1, fixed: a local mount over an rclone source after the view started read «disk» — the last row before the view now decides.
  - Small 2, fixed: the disk words name the type shown; the tail is softened.
  - Small 3, fixed: two surviving mutants (rows after the view not skipped; equal mount points first-wins) now pinned; the depth rule removed.
  - Small 4, named: a view started before its NFS was mounted reads «network» where it serves the disk beneath (24 paths, watched either way).
  - The verifier's sweep re-run on the amend: 0 differences outside a view, 0 regressions; new ≠ truth only the 24 of small 4. Its guard driver: all eight scenes hold.
- **Gates.**
  - test-mount-path-class ⑥ (29 pins) and test-fs-canary §9 (25 pins).
  - On the release's classifier and witness swapped back in: 5 ✗ and then a crash (`viewWords` absent) in the first; 13 ✗ in the second. The controls are green there by nature.
  - Each control is red under its own mutant (lane battery).
  - test-fs-canary restated 6.7 → 6.95 s (§9's three 120 ms holds), proportionally: against the 2.369.397 copy on one box, three alternating runs, 14.90 s → 15.45 s (×1.037). The .397 stated fast sum is 1065.85 of 1066 s.

### hub-sync-holds (for .398) — the Plugins modal's close ends its broadcast listener at once (the .397 dialog seam's product answer)
- **What lingered.** Rank 13's Plugins panel listener («the rows follow the broadcast») checked `body.isConnected` at the next socket frame. A closed panel's handler sat in `app.ws.globalHandlers` until one came. test-dialog-yield-chrome ㉞ read that as one handler fewer when a frame landed inside its window (the .397 seam f639acb12 settles every count).
- **The change (src/lib/plugins-ui.js).** `offWs` and the redraw timer are declared BEFORE the shell — the set-up dialog's pattern, since a close can run before the handler registers. The modal's `onClose` clears the timer and ends the listener.
- **The rail stays lazy, said in the comment with why.** Its shell's close is a no-op, and the next render replaces the body, so there the listener ends at the first frame after its body left.
- **What never happened, checked.** No lingering listener redraws a gone panel: it returns before anything once its body is off the page, and the 150 ms redraw re-checks. The form is single-subject, so a second open raises it and it is never queued (the «queued body opens deaf» class cannot reach it).
- **The pin.** test-dialog-yield-chrome ㊴ (the phone tier, where openPluginsDialog is the modal) opens and closes it by its ✕ in ONE synchronous task, so no socket frame is dispatched between the readings. The RAW count is back at once; on 2.369.397 it read +1 until the next frame.

### job-logs-sweep — A RUN THE HUB FORGOT STILL OWNED A DIRECTORY FOR EVER (found by the data-move rehearsal: int359/data-move/rev3/runbook.md §12, follow-up F11)
- **The finding.** A job's record keeps its last 20 runs (src/jobs.js `_spawn`: `job.runs.splice(0, len − 20)`). The directory of a run it drops, `data/job-logs/<id>/<runTs>/` (pid.json, current.log, exit.json, bound.json, stopping.json, answers.jsonl), stayed for ever.
  - The 14-day gc ages a TASK by its LAST run, and a scheduled job fires ONE child task for ever (2.343.3), so a cron child never ages out.
  - `rm` of a live record removes no directory at all.
  - **The owner's hub** (its local copy, 2026-11-12, counts only — lane work/census.mjs): 123 523 entries under job-logs, the largest store by entry count. That is 2 152 job dirs and 26 104 run dirs:
    - 1 242 listed by a record;
    - 23 367 dropped by a live record, 15 309 of them older than 14 days (15 105 cron children, 189 services);
    - 1 422 job dirs that no record names (removed jobs, 1 495 runs).
  - **10 run dirs started more than 14 days ago but wrote within 14 days**: a run's age is its NEWEST file, not its start.
- **The law** (src/job-logs-sweep.js):
  1. A run dir that no record lists (the store's or the archive's) is removed once its newest entry is 14 days old, whether its task lives on or not. A job dir that no record names goes once emptied.
  2. **Never removed:**
     - a run whose wrapper lives (pid.json judged against /proc by proc-identity: pid + starttime + boot id, not a zombie). A stamp that cannot be read KEEPS its run;
     - a listed run;
     - a run held for an unfinished scope reap (`_reapLater`);
     - a skeleton record's dir (corrupt-store recovery's `runs: []` is not «lists nothing»).
  3. **Paced:** B = 500 run dirs a pass, and G = 30 s between passes while a catch-up is open. **Said twice:** at the start with the count, and when done with the total. The catch-up's record, data/jobs-logs-sweep.json, goes through the store writer (paced; a TS.STORES row `jobs-logs-sweep.write`; a ② pin in test-store-write-census).
  4. **NOTHING under job-logs is removed on the main thread.** There is ONE remover (`createRemover`):
     - a queue, and one worker_threads thread at a time, which lingers idle 1 s and then goes;
     - a batch timeout of 120 s (480 s for the counting pass); a batch that times out is queued again once;
     - **HELD:** a terminated thread that has not ENDED 2 s later is wedged in a syscall the storage never answers. No second thread is started beside it, every batch answers `held`, and this is said once until the thread ends.
- **ONE REMOVER (the coordinator's ruling 1).** The five whole-dir removals keep their verdicts; their syscalls move to the worker:
  - `_gc` leg (a), a done task past 14 days;
  - `_gc` leg (b), an archived record past 14 days;
  - the archive cap;
  - the ✕ (`rmArchived`);
  - the boot collapse of pre-2.343.3 children.

  How each case ends:
  - **A run whose wrapper lives:** a whole-dir removal never takes it. The law's pass removes that dir once the run has ended and aged (no record names it any more).
  - **The ✕'s routes** (jobs-wiring, agent-routes) answer after `logsGone(id)`, bounded at 10 s; the loop never waits. Past the bound the answer carries `logsPending: true`. The panel then toasts «Removed. Its log files are still being deleted in the background.» (zh + ja), and the CLI prints «removed — its log files are still being deleted in the background».
  - **A whole-dir batch the storage did not take** (held or failed) is OWED: it is kept in memory (≤ 5 000 ids) and re-sent before the next pass. A restart forgets it, and the law's pass takes those dirs 14 days after their newest file.
- **The pass.**
  - **When it runs:**
    - hourly from `_gc`, unless a catch-up's own timer is armed (the catch-up keeps its own pace; a stalled one is picked up here);
    - ONE pass 2 min after each boot, because a hub that restarts more often than hourly never reached its hourly gc;
    - every G while a catch-up is open; a failed or held pass inside it re-arms a retry after 5 min, so a catch-up never stalls.
  - **The keep set** is built on the main thread from memory: the store, and the archive when it is loaded. Otherwise the WORKER reads jobs-archive.json — never `_loadArchive`'s synchronous read, which held the owner's loop in hub-loop-stalls' capture. An unreadable archive removes nothing.
  - **The worker walks** each job dir's runs oldest first:
    - listed / held / skeleton is decided by name;
    - a run that STARTED after the cutoff is young by name (no stat);
    - otherwise its age is the newest lstat mtime (an empty dir is aged by its start);
    - then its pid.json goes to proc-identity.
  - **After a boot,** the first pass reads the catch-up record in the worker. A restart therefore resumes with no second start line, and the done line counts across it.
- **NUMBERS (ruling 3).**
  - **The owner's copy at 14:26Z, with the REAL verdict as a dry run** (removal syscalls stubbed to throw, max 0, count): 16 707 run dirs and 66 726 entries to catch up. It kept 1 242 listed and 8 155 young runs; the walk took 371 ms on local disk.
  - **The kit's rule** (every run dir STARTED more than 14 days ago that jobs.json does not list) gave 16 702 at 14:06Z: 15 297 dropped by a live record, 1 389 with no record, and 16 archived records' runs. The coordinator's 16 696 is the same rule a few minutes earlier; about one run a minute crosses the line.
  - **What B and G give:** B = 500 ⇒ 34 passes, and G = 30 s ⇒ about 17 min. That is about 2 000 entries a pass, roughly 1 s of NAS unlinks at the runbook's 2 800 entries/s. The first, counting pass walks every candidate (about 30 s on the NAS; its timeout is 480 s).
  - **On a synthetic tree of the owner's shape** (26 748 run dirs, local NVMe, G shortened; lane work/shape-probe.mjs): 34 passes; the counting pass took 524 ms and the others 40 ms median. **THE MAIN LOOP's worst delay over the whole catch-up was 19.1 ms (p99 3.1 ms):** the main thread only builds the keep set and posts one message per pass.
- **Pins:** scripts/test-job-logs-sweep.mjs (fast). It drives the real JobManager, the real cron fire road and the real job wrapper in a scratch dir, plus seeded trees of 5 000 dropped runs through a slow-storage stand-in around the real worker (0.2 ms a removal). Red by name on b19f0ecdb (23 legs). The pins:
  - **P1** a cron fired 30 times: 10 dropped ⇒ gone past the retention, 20 listed stay, the job's page still serves its last log.
  - **P2** a dropped run alive past the retention stays; an unreadable stamp stays; the run goes once its process ended.
  - **P3** a job `rm --orphan`'d with a run alive: kept while alive; once it ended, its run dir AND the job dir go.
  - **P4** the catch-up: paced at 500 a pass with each pass after the gap; the main loop's worst delay < 60 ms while a pass is ≥ 100 ms of removals (control: one pass of the same removals on the main thread ≥ 60 ms); said twice with the exact count.
  - **P5** a restart mid catch-up: no second start line, and the done line counts the whole. A failed pass inside an open catch-up re-arms its retry, and with no timer armed the hourly gc picks it up.
  - **The rules:** newest-file age, an empty dir by its start, reap-held, another name never touched, the hourly road on a service's dropped run, an unloaded archive read in the worker, an unreadable archive removes nothing.
  - **The removers:** the ✕ returns with its dir still there and `logsGone` resolves after the worker; the gc's leg (a) keeps a live run, which the law's pass removes later; a HELD ✕ is owed and re-sent; the wedged thread (a FIFO's open) ⇒ HELD with no second thread, said once, going on after it ends.
  - **Static:** no rmSync in jobs.js; four whole-dir verdict sites; both routes; the words; `_logsPass` never calls `_loadArchive`; the worker uses lstat only.
  - **The PURE verdict** + 4 mutant copies (alive ignored, age by the start, listed ignored, unproven removed).
- **ROUND 2 (6908eef73 not accepted; two adversarial readers, int359/acc-398/jls).** The verdict itself held in every scene they drove, but one road round it did not. Each group is its own commit on top:
  - **GROUP 2 — the guards pinned.** 13 mutants were each driven and are KILLED by name. The stamp judge never throws, and whole() unlinks a link under a job's name, as the release did.

After a restart, a torn store's skeletons were gone and the boot pass removed a live service's listed run. Now:

  - Pins §H, one per road: the gc; a list then a pass; a pass then the gc; a torn store, a restart and its boot pass; a non-list through the load and through the worker; an EIO with a refused rename; a store read that failed at boot.
  - **GROUP 3 — THE PACE FOLLOWS THE STORAGE, AND A PERSON CAN STOP IT.**
    - **The rest:** max(30 s, 10 × the pass's own time). A cut sweep batch is never re-queued; a cut pass rests max(5 min, 10 × its timeout) and keeps its partial count.
    - **The count:** the counting pass counts by name (readdirs only) inside the normal timeout, and its done line reconciles: start N = removed + kept + what crossed the line meanwhile.

### queued-is-not-woke — A QUEUED MESSAGE IS NOT A WAKE (law 1 of 4; row B-580f, 主开发's brief and the 2026-11-11 incident)
- **The census first (law 4, measured on master b6d980014, probe/census.mjs over the REAL groups-engine + delivery ladder).**
  - 60 cells: 5 harness rows × {wake, next turn, notification} × {idle, in a turn, in a turn with no life, ended}.
  - Lying: every rpc-queue cell in a turn, every live lane behind a dead turn, and claude's in-turn charge.
  - Honest: every idle cell, stash-only, next turn, ended.
- **Law 1.** A frame an rpc-queue wrapper QUEUES behind a running turn is said waiting («waiting (not billed yet): <name>'s current turn (running since HH:MMZ)»). Its group row is `queued`, never «read», and its charge is OWED.
  - Authorized at the send. The hold goes back at the 'queued' answer, because guard holds live 3 min.
  - Charged ONCE when a turn carries it: its queue item left and a turn started. Released when handed back.
  - Persisted across a hub restart (msg-queued.json through the store writer).
  - The marker moves at the queue, so no report re-sends it; exactly one road carries it.
- **Ruled by 主开发 2026-11-12.**
  - claude cli-inbox into a running turn keeps master's charge; only its words change («handed into <name>'s running turn», `intoTurn`).
  - codex's free notification steer is left as it is and rowed for the owner.
- **Restated pins.**
  - test-spend-paths §5b: «a human peer message mid-turn is charged» ⇒ owed, then charged once at its turn.
  - test-peer-delivery agy-peer-wake ②③: the busy notification is queued and owed; Stop's hand-back is never charged.
  - test-channel-groups: the closed set gains `queued`.
- **New.**
  - test-queued-wake (fast, 46). ⑦ replays the incident on the REAL agy wrapper over the fake agy's new `stuck` mode, through the REAL acp-events consumer.
  - test-harness-contract «a frame queued behind a turn», per harness from its declared lane.
- **Round 2 (主开发's panel: «an owed charge slips past the owner's money gate»).**
  - THE RESERVATION:
    - the unit is taken at the send as a guard stamp named by the frame's id, counted like a spent turn — the ceiling holds (cap 3: sends 4 and on refused at the send);
    - the carrying turn is that unit (idempotent by id: a kill between a carry and its persist charges once);
    - a hand-back returns it.
  - The moderates:
    - the hub ASKS a holding wrapper for its queue at every attach and at boot;
    - a gone or replaced wrapper's frames are handed back BY THE HUB (stash with a ref; read at its drain; «waiting — <name> is stopped» before the queue);
    - the bounds refuse at the send (`queued-full`) and never drop;
    - an answer that beats markQueued is kept.
  - The readers: the owner's toast, vibespace-msg's hand-in echo, the worker dispatch, channel receipts.
  - Pins: test-queued-wake 63; test-spend-paths §5c (the reservation arithmetic + the ceiling with the real guard); test-channel-groups (the queued row, stopped before the queue); test-dispatch-model (a queued brief).
- **Round 3 (主开发's panel: «two ways money is still forgiven»).**
  - A give-back returns only its own unconverted stamp (one Stop no longer forgives 637 spent turns). Its prune used the live limits here; round 4 replaced that with LOAD_RETENTION.
  - A carried reservation is CONVERTED in the guard, on disk before the carry's record.
  - The hub hands back only on knowledge: the wrapper's answer, or a seen end with the frame in that process's last queue (the ws kill road at the act).
  - «Gone» is the holder pid's death, never «not attached yet»; unknown keeps the unit and hands the words once, marked as a possible repeat.
  - Live-only bound; eviction, archive and age exits; orphan rows settle at the next turn start; «spent or promised» refusals.
  - Pins: test-spend-paths §5d (the 100-after-a-Stop row, the census, the converted mark across a reload, boot tags, both bounds, the words); test-queued-wake 70 (⑬b the boot roads (a) / (b) / (c) with the real guard, ⑬c kill and archive).
- **Round 4 (主开发's panel: «the roads hold; two ways a spent turn is still forgiven»).**
  - ONE predicate (`knownNotRun`) for every unit-returning exit: a fresh listing, from the holder, newer than every turn start. Codex's cached re-publish at the turn start and an old wrapper's listing are no evidence (unknown: kept, marked).
  - Every prune keeps LOAD_RETENTION (d3b: the caps lowered and raised the same day forgive nothing; the census reads every tracked file and catches null and an alias).
  - No write inside the send or the carry: the guard's own debounce, with the kill-window bound named and the four boot states pinned.
  - A drain never stamps; a live carry of a never-stamped frame stamps once; the converted mark is on both lists.
  - An evicted or aged-out entry's row says «not delivered — … send it again» (a handed-back entry whose words still wait in the stash stays).
  - Smalls: the guard asked before a marked copy; a 38-character repeat mark; live entries age; an identity-less carry finds its stamp; «Spent or promised by»; the 80 % notice on the carried path.
  - Pins: test-queued-wake 105 (⑯ the predicate through the three exits, the record census knowing `fresh`, U3 / U3c / U3k, the person's turn; ⑰ U10; ⑱ U12 / M7f / a reservation never recorded; ⑲ evict 30 + 10, U14, the age; ⑳ the four states); test-spend-paths 457 (§5d the census; §5e d3b ×2, the burst, M7f / M7g, the smalls).
- **Laws 2 and 3 are not in this commit:** the wait bound, the owner's item, the life witness and agy's store-proven close.

### reply-door-follows-enter — a person's words reach a running turn the same way whatever door they came through (the owner's screen, 2026-11-13 00:2xZ)
- **The scene.** A For-you reply to a running conversation's own question sat «queued — runs after this turn», while a message typed in the composer AFTER it carried «Steered» and was already inside the turn. The owner: «这条消息状态异常了，这个似乎是已经处理过的消息却还浮动在下面».
- **The cause.** The composer's send carries the person's door: the page asks the harness row's `enterDoor` intersected with the running wrapper's verbs, and passes `steer: true`. The For-you reply route (both sends: the live one and the reopen), the design comments and the doc comments called the same typing path with no door, so the wrapper held them until the turn ended.
- **The fix.** ONE door decision, PURE, in src/backend-caps.js: `sendDoors` + `doorCapsOf` + the moved `SEND_DOOR_TABLE`.
  - The page's composer reads it (agent-meta `composerSendModes`, chat-view `_queueCaps`), and so does the server's typing path. src/server/user-input.js `door: 'enter'` is a person's words through a door with no keys of its own: it follows the conversation's own Enter door (its harness row ∩ the running wrapper's sidecar verbs; a wrapper with no queue ⇒ a plain send).
  - The reply route, design-engine and doc-engine name that door. The composer keeps passing its own `steer`, the hold door included, and the dispatch's compact stays the machine's.
  - A harness row with no steer door on Enter (codex), or an older wrapper, keeps today's behaviour, and the reply's bubble says «queued». The bubble's state is the wrapper's own `queueState` for that message, so «Steered» / «queued» is true for the reply as for a typed message.
- **Money.** None moves: the reply is the person's own typed send (the route's existing row in test-spend-paths).
- **Pins (scripts/test-reply-door.mjs, fast, through the REAL typing path and the REAL reply route over a fake session and its wrapper sidecar):**
  - the owner's scene: a reply mid-turn, then a composer Enter ⇒ both handed to the running turn, the reply first;
  - the hold door: a held message stays held, and a later Enter passes it;
  - an older wrapper and a wrapper with no queue: the reply is not steered;
  - the door decision PURE and the composer's equal to it;
  - the typing path's caller census: every caller names `door: 'enter'`, its own `steer`, or `origin: 'dispatch'` — a planted caller without one is RED.
  - RED: the release fd4acdc61 (a COUNTED skip without it) and this tree with the reply's door removed — the reply HELD.
- **test-queue-steer's pin** on chat-view's intersection now reads the one derivation in src/backend-caps.js `doorCapsOf`.

### Known in 2.369.398 — named by the merged-tip reads of .397 (2026-11-12 12:18Z) and of .398 (2026-11-13 03:35Z) and still open; each a pick of a later train (K1 was cured in .397; K2 and K3 in this release)
- **K4 (minor).** A stopped update says the checkout is clean, but not that the code on disk is already the new version. On an install with no supervisor, ⚙ → Update stops the server and nothing starts it, as in 2.369.396. A plugin status child in flight at a stop outlives the hub.
- **K5 (law 1, driven on the real agy wrapper).** A wake queued behind a turn can be bound to the queue item of a message written just after it. Its record can then say «read» while it still waits, and after a kill it can be sent twice, or lost while marked read. 2.369.397 said «woke / read» for every such message, so this release is better in each case.
- **K6.** Laws 2 and 3 of queued-is-not-woke are not in this release: a message behind a turn that never ends waits with no bound and no For-you item.
- **K7 (job-logs-sweep meeting the release's torn-store recovery, driven).** After a restart, moving the set-aside jobs store away as the For-you item says lets the next pass remove the logs older than 14 days of the jobs that were in the torn file. Nothing lists them any more, and the item's words do not say so.
- **K8 (K3).** The age mark's hours are still «h» in Chinese and Japanese; only its minutes and days follow the interface's units (the user line says so).
- **K9 (law 1).** For a group with several members, vibespace-msg calls a dropped copy «not delivered (ended)» though the conversation is alive.
- **K10 (job-logs-sweep).** The For-you notices about an unreadable job store can carry English fragments in Chinese and Japanese.
- **K11 (the hosted runners' Claude Code 2.1.323).** With Claude Code 2.1.323 on the hosted runners, the suite of the hold door and of Stop (test-claude-steer-chrome) is red on about half its tries on 2.369.397 as well: a held message's bubble across a hub restart, and a request that reaches the model just before or after a Stop settles. On this box, with 2.1.322, it is 8 of 8 green on every tree. Whether 2.1.323 moved the CLI's Stop window is being measured (a lane has it); nothing in this release touches it.

## 2.369.397 — 2026-11-12

### passkey-lend-walk — every other way a lent sign-in ends takes the passkey back, or says it could not (B-97ae's second commit; the acceptance's walk a–d)
- **(d) MEASURED first, on real Chrome** (test-browser-passkey-chrome S12, the suite's own headed Chrome on its Xvfb). The question: what does a tab keep when the DevTools session that lent a key goes? The hub's `shutdown()` closes the watch's socket with no clean-up (a restart, a crash), and a tab can lose its session alone.
  - The control, with the lending session alive: the page signs at once — «ok in 2 ms» (A and B). It also signs after a reload — the look's own control, asserted in S12.
  - A, a second CDP connection lends and then closes: «held 2500 ms».
  - B, the session detached while its connection lives: «held 2500 ms».
  - C, the person's watch lends the vault key (UI on), then the hub goes mid-ceremony (socket terminated, `shutdown()`): «held 2500 ms». The page's own request is still held 3 s later.
  - In each case the look is the same: a fresh session enables WebAuthn with UI off and the tab is reloaded with no hook. The empty environment holds the request; nothing signs it.
  - So Chrome takes a virtual authenticator — and the keys and UV in it — with the session that added it. A restart needs NO sweep at re-arm; S12 pins it (a Chrome that changes this goes red there).
- **(a) A document gone mid-ceremony ends its ceremonies through THE ONE END on both roads.** `pkPageGone` sends each ended record to `pkEnd`.
  - Before, it removed only the person's once-authenticator. On the agent's tab, which keeps its authenticator, the loaded key and UV stayed until that tab's next ceremony ended (and that ceremony's load of the same id failed: «its id is already registered»).
- **(b) A clean-up step the browser REFUSED is said, never believed.** `pkUnload` / `pkOnceGone` judge every answer.
  - A step counts as a miss when it is answered with an error or no answer while the tab's session is LIVE: the watch open, the session still mapped, and the error not naming a gone session.
  - Misses that leave a key or UV with the authenticator not removed (and the environment not disabled) are said ONCE by name in the server log, which names the steps.
  - The tab is named to the person in the For-you tray (`PK.leftForYouItem`, en / zh / ja). The item resolves when the tab closes, since a closed tab takes its authenticator.
  - One refused step the later steps make up for is not said. A gone session's failures are not said: (d) measured that the key went with the session.
- **(c) The Cancel ends what was pending when it was sent.** `cancelPasskey` marks only the records that were pending before its await.
  - A start that lands in the same socket read as the cancel's answer is a new sign-in. ws runs both frames before the await continues, as the acceptance measured. It is gated and released as any other.
  - Before, it was marked «cancelled» by the person and never released; the page waited out its hold.
- **Pinned** (test-browser-passkey, fast, judged at rest with not one line said unless named):
  - «B-97ae walk (a)» ×5: the agent's / the person's document destroyed / cleared, and never the next document's key;
  - «B-97ae walk (b)» ×4: three refusals on a live session ⇒ said + For you + resolved at close; one refusal made up for ⇒ silent; the agent's road ⇒ said; a gone session ⇒ silent;
  - «B-97ae walk (c)».
  - RED on d5bc4c67d (.391 by itself): 6 legs — (a) the agent's destroyed / cleared / the next document, (b) the two «said» legs, (c). Green there by design: the person's road in (a) (`pkOnceGone` covered it) and the two silent legs in (b).
  - test-browser-passkey-chrome S12 on real Chrome.
- **Pin scans** of every suite naming a changed src file: string literals (412 suite × file pairs) and regex literals (28 421 tried) — clean.
- **Round 2 (the acceptance of 0723db7e0, 主开发 2026-11-11 12:12Z: «WHAT IS SAID ABOUT A LEFTOVER IS TRUE FOR AS LONG AS IT IS SAID»).** Two verifiers drove master and the tree through the tree's own fixture (world2's modPath seam). They confirmed (a)–(c) and (d) and found that the one new thing the commit shows a person could be wrong.
  - **MUST 1 — the item lives exactly as long as the leftover.**
    - A leftover is now kept per tab (`e.pk.left`: its authenticator and the keys SEEN in it).
    - Its For-you item carries the producer's identity (`itemKey: pk-left:<profile>:<tab>`): a re-file is the same item, reopened.
    - It is resolved by whatever ends the leftover:
      - a later clean-up on the tab that LOOKS and finds none of its keys (`pkLeftCheck`, said once: «… is gone now»);
      - the session detaching;
      - the socket or the browser going (`down()`, the hub's shutdown included);
      - the tab closing;
      - a hub START, which sweeps a past life's items (`forYou.sweep('pk-left:')`, the wiring's new door): an item whose tab this hub does not hold is not kept, because the hub that held it took its sessions — and, per S12, their authenticators.
    - The log's once-key goes with the leftover, so a NEW leftover on that tab is said again.
  - **MUST 2 — «refused» is said only of a refusal.**
    - Every answer is one of four: ok · refused (an error on a live session) · silent (no answer in callTimeoutMs) · gone (the session or socket went, or the error names a gone session).
    - After a missed step THE LOOK reads what the authenticator holds now (`getCredentials`, and UV off once more if that step missed); what is said is what was seen.
    - A removal done but answered late ⇒ nothing.
    - A look with no answer ⇒ «… could not be checked — the browser did not answer», and the item «VibeSpace could not check whether …».
  - **MUST 3(ii) — the agent → person handover** (`toPerson`) judges its removeVirtualAuthenticator / disable as (b) does: both missed on a live session ⇒ the look ⇒ said and filed.
  - **Smaller.**
    1. ONE tab name for the line and the item (`pkTabName`): the title through ST.pageText (no bidi or invisible characters, no line breaks), else the ORIGIN — never the address's path or query.
    2. A cap: past `leftMax` (3) tabs of one browser, ONE item counts the rest (`PK.leftMoreItem`).
    3. A cancel the page did not take (its call missed, or the hook answered 0) says «VibeSpace could not cancel the page's passkey request (…) — … it is still waiting», never «No passkey request is waiting».
    4. «its id is already registered» is a key that IS there (a leftover's, an heir's): no «not loaded» line.
    5. (d)'s premise is named where an engine is judged: kb-features, the custom-kernel passkey section, «The limit — what a lent key rests on». This is the kb option, not a feature row: nothing would act on such a row except a sweep, which was ruled out.
  - **MUST 3(i) — a crashed page, MEASURED first on real Chrome (S13).**
    - A renderer crash during a lend says `Target.targetCrashed` on the browser's discovery (this watch's) and `Inspector.targetCrashed` on a session with Inspector on. There is NO context event until a reload, and `Page.crash` never answers.
    - The lent authenticator keeps its key (1).
    - The reload says `Inspector.targetReloadedAfterCrash`, `Runtime.executionContextsCleared`, the new contexts and `Page.frameNavigated`. The key is still there (1), and the reloaded page signs with it «ok in 2 ms».
    - So the CRASH ends the ceremony: `Target.targetCrashed` / `Inspector.targetCrashed` clear the tab's dead context maps (a call into them would wait out callTimeoutMs) and end its pending records through `pkPageGone` → `pkEnd`.
    - S13b, the person's watch on real Chrome: lent, crashed ⇒ the ceremony ended and the lent authenticator removed (the watch's own session: «Could not find a Virtual Authenticator»).
  - **Pins:** test-browser-passkey round-2 legs (MUST 1 ×4, MUST 2 ×2, MUST 3(i) ×2, MUST 3(ii) ×2, smaller 1 ×2, smaller 2, smaller 3) — 269 / 269. On 0723db7e0 by itself: 13 of the 14 red (the fourteenth is the done-handover control); the two round-1 (b) legs read the new words. test-browser-passkey-chrome S13 (the measured crash) and S13b (the watch on a crash).
- **Round 3 (the acceptance of 09d06e499, 主开发 15:57Z: «three places where what is said is still not what is so»).** One verifier drove the tree with its own fixture and the REAL UserTodoManager (33 scenes on master, 0723db7e0 and the tree), and 主开发 ran seven mutants of their own.
  - **MUST 1 — user verification left on is a leftover too.** `pkLook` tries UV off once more and judges it whatever the keys: the key removed but UV kept ⇒ «… could not be taken back (0 keys, user verification on)», and the item with the UV words. A later clean-up that turns it off ends it. A UV-off with no answer (no key left) ⇒ «whether user verification on the tab … was turned off could not be checked».
  - **MUST 2 — the person's own Cancel.** browser-stream.js `cancelPasskeyFor` answers `failed` (never `ended`) when the page did not take the cancel. The live window says «VibeSpace could not cancel the page's passkey request — … it is still waiting. Closing the tab ends it.» and keeps the banner, where before it said «The passkey wait had already ended».
  - **MUST 3 — a title that is an address is an address.** Measured on real Chrome (S14): an untitled page's TargetInfo.title is its address, query and all. `tabName` (module-level, PURE, exported) names such a tab by its ORIGIN, and so too a title that parses as an address or equals the tab's own; a real title stays.
  - **Smaller.**
    1. A look the browser REFUSED is said «refused to show what the tab holds» (line and item detail), never «did not answer».
    2. Only what was LENT is counted: a key the page made, left behind, is said as what it is («a passkey the page made on the tab … could not be removed from it»), never filed as lent.
    3. A record whose page went (destroyed, cleared, crashed) is marked `pageGone`; its drain sends no call that would look for the dead context and wait out callTimeoutMs.
    4. The handover's look sees UV like the others.
    5. kb-file-structure's browser-engines essay points to the premise.
  - **Pins:** test-browser-passkey «round 3» ×9 — red on 09d06e499 by itself, all nine; 278 / 278 on the tree. test-browser-passkey-chrome S14 (the untitled page measured).

### hub-sync-holds, rank 13 — a plugin's status is a kept fact: a snapshot or a broadcast runs no synchronous child
- **The hold (the owner's hub, 2026-11-11 profile rank 13):** 4.7–4.9 s asleep in a pipe read — `spawnSync` ← `systemTailscaled` (src/plugins/tailscale.js). The manager's `_snapshot()` called every plugin's `status()` on every snapshot and broadcast; tailscale's ran `pgrep -x tailscaled`, `sudo -n true` and `tailscale status --json` synchronously, and frp's ran `which frpc`.
- **The law:** a plugin's `status()` is sync and runs NO synchronous child — the KEPT answer (a stale `which` answer starts ONE async `which` in the background). A status that needs a child declares the optional verb `statusAsync()`: every child async with its timeout (which 5 s, pgrep 5 s, sudo -n 3 s, status --json 5 s), the answer kept. The manager's `refreshStatus(id)` runs ONE refresh at a time, bounded at 20 s, and broadcasts only when the kept answer changed. It is asked at boot (`bootReplay` → `refreshAll`), on a person's press (`GET /api/plugins` kicks every refresh; `GET /api/plugins/:id/status` awaits one) and on the plugin's own event (`h.notify`). Before the first answer a row says `checking: true` with what the files say.
- **Where a command lives, kept:** `src/plugins/which-kept.js` — `whichKept` (sync callers: the kept path, a stale one refreshed in the background) and `whichNow` (async callers). tailscale's `start` / `stop` / `setup` / `bootReplay` / `install` and frp's `install` are async now (the routes await them); none runs a sync child.
- **A decision that ACTS reads a FRESH answer:** frp's boot install-or-start asks `frpBinNow()` (its own bin, else `whichNow`) — the kept answer is empty before its first read, so the boot would have DOWNLOADED a frpc the PATH already has (the old sync `which` found it). Pinned in §13: frpc on PATH only, the relay default-on, `fetch` stubbed — the boot starts the PATH's frpc and fetches nothing; red under the kept read (it fetched frp's release tarball and never started).
- **Round 2 (the acceptance panel's three moderates):** (1) OUR daemon running and no tailscale command resolvable: `run(null, …)` threw inside its promise, every refresh rejected, the row said «Checking…» for ever with its switch disabled — `run()` never throws now (no program ⇒ `{code: null}`) and the probe answers what it knows (`running`, `cli: false`; the row says so in its own words, no «Log in…»). (2) The 20 s bound did not stop the ask it abandoned (tailscale's worst case: which 5 + pgrep 5 + sudo -n 3 + sudo -n 3 + which 5 + status --json 5 = 26 s): a second set of children started beside the first, which later wrote its answer unbroadcast. The bound now ABORTS the ask — `statusAsync({ signal })` checks it before each step and before it writes, `run()` passes it to execFile (the held child is killed): an abandoned ask starts nothing more and writes nothing. (3) frp had no «Checking…»: before its first `which` its row said «not installed» and offered Install over the PATH's frpc — `whichKnown` (has a lookup finished?) and frp's row says `checking` until it has. Minor, fixed: a FIRST answer that failed now says «Status unknown» and frees the switch (a running daemon can always be stopped — the switch no longer waits on `installed` while the daemon runs); the stale mark is a visible line on the row, not only a hover title; «never refreshed by a timer» is pinned as a census of the manager's refresh callers.
- **Gates:** test-hub-sync-holds §13 (new, fast) — a 3 s stand-in pgrep on PATH: the snapshot answers at once (loop turn < 250 ms, «checking»), the fresh status is ONE async refresh that takes the children's time with no loop turn over 250 ms, the next snapshot answers the kept fact, two asks share one refresh; each red on b6d980014 (the snapshot took 3012 ms). test-tailscale-dns follows the async verbs (and no longer counts the boot's kept-status sudo probe as a DNS act); test-plugins-grammar knows the helper file; the census rows: the pgrep allowlist (test-architecture) and three spawn-env probe rows. Round 2: our daemon running with no tailscale command answers (running, cli false); an ask abandoned at a 1 s bound starts nothing after its 3 s pgrep and writes nothing; frp says checking before its first which; the refresh-caller census; the panel's words. MUTANTS, each red: the bound not aborting, frp never checking, a timer refresh, round 1's tailscale.js (both no-command guards gone).

### hub-sync-holds, rank 16 — the mail folder is read off the loop: one async walk per pass; a walk that did not finish is never an answer
- **The hold (rank 16):** 1.5–1.7 s per pass, every pollSeconds (300 s) per mailbox, growing with the mailbox — `GmailSync._seenIds`, a recursive `readdirSync` (depth 2) plus a regex per file name, called from `_syncOnce` on every pass, and once more synchronously in `start()`. The tree IS the dedup index.
- **The fix:** every pass reads the tree ONCE, ASYNC (`_seenIds` → `_walkSeen`: `fs.promises.readdir`, the same depth and names; a second ask while a walk runs shares it); `start()` walks nothing of its own; within a pass the set grows by what `_writeMessage` writes.
- **Round 2 (the acceptance panel's MUST 1 — «the folder is the index; a kept set never contradicts it»):** round 1 KEPT the set across passes, and it drifted: a folder emptied to sync again (rm -rf + mkdir, the state file gone) re-seeded with 0 of its mail downloaded and recorded the seed as finished; a walk cut short by EACCES / EIO (the catch swallowed it) was kept as «0 seen» for the worker's life; a file deleted or added on disk was read wrong. Now nothing is kept across passes, and a walk that did not finish THROWS (`mail_walk_failed`, naming the folder; a folder that does not exist is a finished walk — empty): the pass fails before any download, the mount's state is `error` with those words, the loop tries again after 120 s (never later than a normal pass would come: `min(120, pollSeconds)`) and walks again, and `count` stays the last finished walk's (null before the first). The sidebar SAYS a failed pass («Sync stopped: … — it tries again in 2 minutes», en / zh / ja) — before, an error showed as «Synced — N emails».
- **Gates:** test-hub-sync-holds §16 — 20 000 stored messages: each pass walks once, async (0 readdirSync), counts every one, no loop turn over 250 ms (red on b6d980014 by the walk count: 3 readdirSync per pass). THROUGH `start()` (the real worker and loop, its waits compressed, a stubbed API): an emptied folder re-downloads all 30 on the next pass; an unreadable root, an unreadable subfolder and a first walk that fails — the pass fails before any download, the state names the folder, the count never 0 over files, the next pass reads 40 and downloads nothing; a deleted file re-downloaded when listed, a file added by another process counted and never fetched; the folder missing at the first walk; an id listed twice on one page fetched once; one walk at a time; a failed pass retried no later than a normal pass (pollSeconds 0.3 ⇒ healed within a second). MUTANTS, each red: round 1's kept set (7 pins), the set not grown by a write (B), a failed walk read as empty (C), two walks in flight (D), a fixed 120 s backoff. The verifiers' drivers on this tree: m1b and r1 equal master's output; r gives state error (count null) during the fault, then 40 and 0 re-downloads; m1's deleted / replaced / shared-parent / missing-dir scenes equal master's, its walks are async. test-sync-fs-census: the walk's row removed (its site is gone).

### hub-sync-holds, the loop-child census — every synchronous child and tree walk on the hub is a row
- **The census (scripts/loop-child-census.mjs + scripts/test-loop-child-census.mjs, fast, pure):** acorn over every tracked src/ + server.js file that names a sync child or readdirSync. A SITE is a synchronous child — `execSync` / `execFileSync` / `spawnSync`, called bare, through child_process or through a destructured alias — a sync child function HANDED ON as a value (`child-ref`: its calls run under another name), or a synchronous directory-tree walk (a function that reads a directory with readdirSync and calls itself; `readdirSync(…, { recursive: true })`). Each is named by its enclosing scope (scripts/sync-fs-census.mjs's `scopeOf`, now exported with `walk`). A binding the scanner cannot follow (a computed member, a rest binding of child_process) is UNCLASSIFIED: red, never skipped.
- **The rows (43 sites, 39 rows):** OFF-LOOP with its why (the device agent and its attach CLI are their own processes; the measurement runs in a forked child; safe-fs's walks run in a worker); FALLBACK with its why (NO-/proc or macOS-only paths); DEBT on the hub's loop with HOW OFTEN it runs (timer / boot / per prompt / per attach / per walk / per act) — 22 rows under `DEBT_MAX`, a ratchet that only shrinks: each conversion deletes its row and lowers the number. Controls: one more sync child in a rowed scope (a moved count), a new recursive walk, an aliased sync child, an unfollowable computed call, a recursive readdirSync — each red.
- **Found by the census and removed here:** server.js handed `execFileSync` to the sessions routes and to the ws handler, and neither called it — the dead dependency is gone (server.js now imports no sync child at all).
- **Round 2 (the acceptance panel):** (1) Two censuses contradicted each other: safe-fs-worker's walks were OFF-LOOP rows, but after a worker timeout SafeFs.call runs them INLINE on the main thread (the panel drove 6 main-thread readdirSync) — both are DEBT rows now, naming that road; startToken's ps (it runs on Linux for an exited pid, with NO timeout) is a DEBT row saying so — not bounded here: the remote keeper ships it byte for byte (test-pid-identity's twin), so a bound is a change to both; readPsIdentity's row says it runs ps for an exited pid too (no hub caller). (2) It was green for 16 planted shapes it claimed to follow: it FOLLOWS now fs under another name, a destructured readdirSync, a bound call (`.call` / `.apply`) and an ITERATIVE stack walk — which found three real hub walks it had missed (codex's `_walkJsonlFiles` per find, the builds picker's `treeOf`, usage's `listRecentCodexJsonlFiles` per GET /api/usage) plus agentd's `du` (its own process); its header NAMES what it still does not follow (recursive cpSync / rmSync — 68 such calls, the next census; a helper in another file; mutual recursion; a computed require; ESM forms; a variable `recursive:`). (3) The class was free text: an OFF-LOOP row now must live in a file that runs outside the hub's process (src/agentd/, the forked measurement) and a FALLBACK row must name its guard — a hub file's DEBT row moved to OFF is red (a control). Two frequencies corrected (GET /api/version: once per process, memoised; rcloneAvailable: every GET /api/mounts and the pinned-rclone check). DEBT_MAX 22 → 28 — not six new holds: the census now SEES three walks and its rows tell the truth on every road. A ratchet in a file can be raised in the same commit; the raise and its row land in the diff a reviewer reads, as with every ratchet here.

### hub-sync-holds follow-up (round 3) — the accepted round's moderates, one commit on the four picks
- **The door has ONE caller (the panel's item 1):** a boot that ran scripts/update.sh ITSELF — a spawn from a timer after listen — passed every pin, because the update-door census looked only for the words pull / fetch / merge / install / build. Now any call naming `update.sh` by any spelling (a literal, a template piece, a path.join / path.resolve piece) is a site, counted at the outermost such call. Today the door has two sites, both in POST /api/self-update's handler (its existence check and its spawn). The panel's plant «update.sh 20 s after the boot» is red as a plant, with a path.join spelling, `execFile('scripts/update.sh')` and a path held in a variable. test-boot-keeps-version's boot legs run under a 50× clock (a preload records every timer the boot arms in its first 15 s): the watch runs at most 30 s on that clock — and on every real boot it takes that CAPPED branch (server.js arms two 6 h intervals at load: 432 s at 50×), so the leg SEES an update armed up to about 25 minutes after the boot; a later one is the static update-door census's to catch (the docs-and-tests commit after the follow-up: the follow-up's own note said «covers the LONGEST», which no real boot does); a third boot carrying the plant is SEEN (stand-in git calls). The boot legs' PATH has a systemctl stand-in too: update.sh's restart step can never reach the box's own units.
- **Rank 13:** a status that keeps failing the same way keeps its stamp (one broadcast, no redraw → GET → refresh loop). An ACT (install / start / stop / login) supersedes the refresh in flight: it is aborted, its answer dropped, and a fresh read follows the act (a Stop mid-refresh no longer leaves «connected»). The act keeps its VERB's contract — a sync verb's refusal is thrown in place, an async one's promise returned (the first draft made every act async; test-frp-plugin's revoked-identity leg, which catches start()'s refusal in place, went red on it). An aborted ask kills its `which` child; any child still alive a grace (1 s) after its abort or past its timeout is SIGKILLed (our own handle). A `which` that cannot be spawned answers null with no rejection and no poisoned name (the memo was set after a synchronous end). «Status unknown» frees the switch. «Never by a timer» is now a SYNTAX-TREE census of the manager's refresh callers (six, by scope; a planted setInterval → refreshAll on its own line is red).
- **Rank 16:** a pass that ends in error, and the one that heals it, are pushed (`onProgress`) — an open panel says «Sync stopped» at once. An id history lists twice is fetched once on the incremental road too. The flat mailbox's one readdir callback (47–76 ms at 100 000 mails) is named in the kb, not paged.
- **The census:** the builds picker's treeOf runs every second during a download; startToken also on a recorded pid's verdict (tokenVerdict); the alias table's per-file scope is named (a false site, never a missed one); the update-door census header names what it does not follow (a helper handed an argv array, the program or `sh -c`'s command in a variable, npm-cli.js through node).
