### groups-sweep-on-change commit 1 — A SWEEP ACTS ONLY ON A CHANGE (the owner's performance profile 2026-11-11, rank 2: «the frontend keeps getting worse»)
- **Measured on the owner's hub** (a 20 s capture 40 s after the .393 boot): the ended-groups sweep chain was 5 729 ms (28.6 %) — groupsForSession ≈ 5.2 s, the groups.json write 289 ms — and a named hold of 1.1–1.3 s (folderOf ← insideFolder) is that chain in one turn. Starring, renaming, archiving or a session setting froze the hub a second or more, and every page redrew its groups list.
- **Read:** channels-wiring `noteUserState` (← persistence.js `writeUserState` → server.js `onUserStateWrite`) swept on EVERY user-state write; groups-engine `onConversationEnded` for an end already said in a live multi-member group changed nothing, yet ran `store.groups.update` (groups.json rewritten) and `announce([], …)` (the FULL list rebuilt and broadcast); a ledger row alone and a revive with nothing to lift did the same.
- **The law.** (1) A user-state write starts a sweep only when what the sweep JUDGES moved since the last one saw it — `judgedSig`: the archived set (the user state's one input to liveness), the members of the unarchived groups and the ended ledger (sha1, ≈ 0.4 ms at 6 291 archived); the first ask (boot) and a re-run always sweep; a write during a sweep re-runs it only when its judged state differs from the sweep's start. (2) An end that changes nothing writes nothing and announces nothing (`onConversationEnded` returns early: the ledger already says it and no unarchived group would close or be told). (3) An announce names what changed: a ledger row alone announces nothing; a lifted archive announces the member's own groups, nothing to lift writes nothing. (4) A «GONE» IS STILL SAID WITHIN MINUTES: a transcript that leaves the disk moves nothing the signature reads, so a quiet write still sweeps when the last sweep ENDED more than ten minutes ago (`SWEEP_STALE_MS`) — at most one sweep per ten minutes of activity; the invariant «A MESSAGE TO A CONVERSATION THAT ENDED WAITED FOR EVER» (a dead addressee is said, its pair closes) keeps its own bound.
- **Stated:** a «gone» (a transcript deleted) is judged at boot, at the next change of what the sweep judges (an archive, an un-archive, a group's members, a ledger row) and at the first user-state write ten minutes after the last sweep — no longer at every unrelated write. A hub with no write at all judges it at the next write or boot, as on master.
- **The drill** `test-groups-sweep-on-change` (fast, 1.6 s), through the REAL channels wiring, its own transcript trees: 50 quiet writes ⇒ 0 sweeps / 0 groups.json writes / 0 broadcasts; an archive ⇒ 1 sweep and 1 announce naming that pair, the waiting member told it closed; a member added to an unarchived group (nothing else moving) ⇒ the next write sweeps and says the joiner's end; an ended-ledger row written ⇒ the next write sweeps; a transcript removed ⇒ 50 quiet writes inside ten minutes start no sweep, and at eleven minutes of virtual time one quiet write sweeps once and the waiting sender is told; an end already said ⇒ 0 / 0; a ledger row alone ⇒ 1 write, 0 broadcasts; a revive announces its groups only, nothing to lift ⇒ 0 / 0. RED on master 3c7ae82a2 (2.369.394: 50 sweeps; 1 write + 1 broadcast; 1 broadcast; 1 write — a COUNTED skip on a clone without it), and on three patches the suite carries on this tree's channels-wiring.js: the members out of the signature (the joiner not swept), the ledger out of it (the row not swept), the ten-minute bound out (the «gone» not said).
- **The bench** (the drill's, at the owner's shape: 358 groups, 724 member rows, 561 ended ids, 36 live, 7 Task Groups of ~200, 6 291 archived, the roster built as server.js hands it): master 3.2 s a user-state write at the owner's shape, the roster 5.5 ms, the gate 2 ms — the measured answer to rank 2 of the owner's profile (master: BENCH_MASTER=1, the roster rebuilt per member; the roster: this tree with the gate taken out, a patch the suite carries).
- **Follow-up (主开发's green mutant on 4f63129ce):** the members out of the hash with their count kept in the prefix passed every leg — a join moves the count, a SWAP does not. Leg `member-swap-sweeps`: one member out, another in at an equal count ⇒ the next quiet write sweeps once and says the joiner's end; RED on that patch (the suite carries it). No product change.
- **Pins moved:** test-roster-per-pass's two gap legs — each write now ARCHIVES something (a write that changes nothing the sweep judges starts none), so they still measure the gap rule.
- **Seam:** on 2.369.395 b6d980014 the fast sum is 971.295 s over 553 under 972; the roster row's seam makes it 978.095 s over 554; this row adds 1.65 s (979.745 s over 555) — the cap is the train's.

### roster-per-pass — ONE ROSTER PER PASS (channel groups): the owner's hub held its main thread 85–93 %
- **The defect** (perf investigation wf_1bf1c0bc-e1e; the owner's shape: 358 groups — 356 pairs, 305 archived, 178 closed — 724 member rows, 339 members, 561 ended ids, 36 live, 7 Task Groups): groups-engine `sessionOf(cid) = live().find(…)` rebuilt server.js's whole live roster (each conversation's `groupsForSession`) per member read — 1 448 builds per `list()`, 340 per fan-out `groupsOfSession` loop; `sweepEnded` (every user-state write) rebuilt it per id and walked the codex sessions tree SYNCHRONOUSLY per id; every write queued a sweep.
- **The law, as built.** (1) A pass builds the roster once — `src/server/roster-pass.js` (`sessionRoster` = the builder moved verbatim from server.js; `createRosterPass` = the door): list / listFor / noteRoster→announce / a sweep's synchronous segment in one pass, `sessionOf` its index, channels-access / outbound / engine through the same door. (2) A sweep reads each transcript tree once — `claudeTranscriptIndex` (session-store.js) + `codexTranscriptIndex` (adapters/codex.js) through fs.promises, ONE readdir per directory (the wiring's shared listing: data/remote-jsonl is read by both), bounded 10 s, a stuck walk not doubled. ### window-close-stall C — the page never asks for a frame it does not paint (the owner's own recording; its own commit behind the hotfix)
- **Measured (the owner's DevTools recording, 2.369.392).** In its quiet stretches one function asked for a frame at every vsync: 1 120 of 1 182 RequestAnimationFrame calls came from the minified «o», whose callback only re-asks. That is telemetry-client.js installCompositorStallWatch's `loop`, the frame-gap ring's and the compositor-stall arm's source. In the 33 frames where nobody acted (98 Hz) each forced frame cost about 1.9 ms: two IntersectionObserver passes 0.41 ms, the commit 0.39, the rAF service 0.26, a 4-element style pass. That is about 190 ms of main thread a second, all day.
- **The fix (src/lib/telemetry-client.js).** No loop.
  - (1) A long frame is the browser's own word: the Long Animation Frames observer (`long-animation-frame`). A frame of 300 ms or more is pushed as `{t: its end, gap: its length}`.
  - (2) ONE rAF a second, asked by the existing 1-s tick. A probe answered late, with no long frame covering it (the compositor did not deliver while the main thread was idle), is a gap too. It is judged a tick later, once the observer has named any long frame, and never counted twice.
  - THE STALL ARM, ROUND 2 (主开发's read of the first form). The first form asked «how long since the last answer» of a once-a-second heartbeat. A plain main-thread task of 1.1–1.9 s that delayed the next tick was then filed as «compositor stall … GPU side»: 4 / 9 / 24 / 44 of 50 phases in 主开发's virtual page, against 0 on master. Now the arm counts how long a frame THE PAGE ASKED FOR went undelivered while its timers ran and its own main thread was free. A HELD tick is on time (< 1.5 s) with no long frame or long task of the page's own since the tick before. A stall opens after two held ticks, dates from the request, and closes when the frame comes. A late tick, or one the page's own long frames explain, restarts the count from that tick. A main-thread task, or a storm of them, is never a compositor stall. That also closes master's pre-existing false name at ≥ 2 s (50 of 50 at 2.5 s → 0).

A click as a window froze then fell outside it: an incident in 0 / 12 / 33 of 50 phases at 0 / 300 / 700 ms into a 3-s stall, against master's 50. Now it is 50 of 50 in every cell (3-s and 6-s stalls, the act at 0 / 300 / 700 / 1 200 / 2 000 ms), 0 with nobody there. The stall's stated length still dates from the request.

### cli-self-measure INCIDENT (the owner's hub, 2.369.393, 20:12Z): «cannot-run (guarded-read)» half a second after every check started
- **What happened:** the owner's hub was updated to .393 for this feature; every check of Claude Code 2.1.322 ended `cannot-run (guarded-read)` in 473 ms, before any variant, and nothing kept which path was read. The pool kept 11 long-lived-token accounts held.
- **The cause (reproduced in the lane, the binary never run — a stand-in checkout under ~/.cache with package.json, CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .git; the fake CLI; the hub road):** the hub's data dir is under the home (its checkout lives there), so the run's scratch was too (data/cli-self-measure/run-…). The first traced process is the trampoline, COPIED INTO the scratch (round 4), and node, starting it, walks UP from the script's folder for a package.json — it opened the checkout's, inside the fence's deny root (the real home) and outside its allow roots: the `--version` run voided. Next in line: the CLI's own walk up from its cwd (CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/, .mcp.json, .git at every ancestor — the clean 2.1.321 trace) would have read the checkout's files and, at the top, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Every gate before had its data dir under /tmp or /var/tmp — outside any home.
- **The fix — the hub's own choice of where a run lives can never void it:** each run gets a fresh private folder (0700, made by mkdir that refuses anything already there, named for this hub so two hubs never sweep each other) under the first base whose REAL path lies outside the person's home and the data dir — $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, then the system temp, /tmp, /var/tmp; none ⇒ cannot-run `scratch`, said by name. The data dir keeps only the record (.393's run dirs there are swept). A credential store the CLI reads still voids (the fence is unchanged). On this box both bases' ancestors (/run/user/1000, /run/user, /run, /tmp, /) hold none of the walk's names.
- **The record keeps what was read:** a void's guarded paths (the version run's and every variant's, ≤ 8, the home as ~) are the reason's observation; the journal line names the first; the For-you item says «What it read: …».
- **A probe that changed measures again at once:** PROBE_VERSION 1 → 2; a FAIL or a cannot-run measured by an older probe is due at once (and a cannot-run from an earlier hub life was already due at start) — no 6-hour wait, no second restart. «Check again» runs it at once too.
- **`home`** (the probe's and the ORCH's): ADDS a deny root — a suite's stand-in for a person's home; it never replaces the real one, and a hub never sets it.
- **Gates:** test-cli-self-measure §12 — THE CELL as a fast pin (the real ORCH's placement + the real judge over the exact walks a run makes: node's package.json walk and 2.1.321's walk up from its cwd) with the data dir under a stand-in home that is a git checkout, red on 5c77612ef; the incident's walks from 5c77612ef's placement as a RED CONTROL; a runtime dir under the home skipped (the fallback) and none left ⇒ `scratch` by name; the record / journal / For-you paths; the probe-bump re-run. test-oat-measure-fake: the same cell on the real tracer with a fake that walks up like 2.1.321 — the old placement VOID on the checkout's package.json, the new one PASS, both again through a symlinked parent.

### B-1409 — a hold that also waited for a CPU is still named by its function (lane hub-loop-stalls; the .393 mirror's test-loop-hold-live red, read 18:05Z)
- **The reading.** test-loop-hold-live went red on the .393 release mirror (two shared cores, ci 43067119641 heavy 2/6), on both tries, in different legs. Three of the legs were THE RUNNER: the watchdog thread itself was late, so its asks landed in the tail and (A)'s count floors went unmet — 5 of 8 asks, sN 0 for the «never gc» mutant. In one more, an ask caught the main thread asleep at the stat read and running at the syscall read. The fourth leg was THE PRODUCT'S RULE ORDER: «waiting for a CPU» at 20 % of the window took the WHOLE hold before law B's parts. So on a congested hub, a hold that ran JavaScript 0.9 s of 1.2 s and waited 0.3 s printed «waiting for a CPU» alone, with its function unnamed.
- **The product (src/loop-hold.js).**
  - «waiting for a CPU» is the verdict only when the window's wait is at least 20 % of it AND its larger part (wait ≥ run). Otherwise the hold is said by its parts, with «it also waited N s for a CPU» beside them (`waitedMuch`).
  - An ask whose stat read said asleep, and whose syscall read a moment later said running, says «asleep at the ask, on the CPU a moment later» — never the self-contradicting «asleep: on the CPU (…)» (`RUNNING_KERNEL_WORDS`, `WOKE_WORDS`).
- **The suite (scripts/test-loop-hold-live.mjs).**
  - (A)'s sweep runs again, at most twice, adding its holds, until its floors are met (8 asks inside the native call, 6 of them 5–55 ms). Otherwise the count is a NAMED and COUNTED skip: «the watchdog was late on this box: N of 8 asks inside the native call». The laws on what was asked still run.
  - The strict set takes only asks posted in state R (the product's own road to «native»).
  - The «never gc» mutant sweeps once more, then is skipped by name when the box fed it no ask.
  - The summary prints the skips: «ALL PASS (N, K skipped)» and the list. A skip is not a green: the release's self-hosted claim runs the same legs on the box.
  - The starved judge takes «it also waited» as the wait said.
  - ⑭'s starved scene has TWO spinners on the child's cpu (68 % wait measured; one spinner makes the new rule a 50 / 50 coin). Its «always waiting» mutant becomes «any wait the verdict».
- **Pins (test-loop-hold, fast, 144 → 147).**
  - A hold of 1.2 s that ran JavaScript 0.9 s and waited 0.3 s is named by its function, «it also waited 0.3 s for a CPU» beside it (RED on 8fad60fd1: «waiting for a CPU»).
  - A hold that waited 0.9 s of 1.2 s is «waiting for a CPU» (the control, green on both).
  - The woke ask's words (red on 8fad60fd1).
- **The follow-up — (B)'s fourth case (the .393 cut's self-hosted gate, Node 24, load 9.5; green on its retry and on Node 22).**
  - The red: with the watchdog started 921 ms into the mixed hold, no window covered half of it, so the samples decided by count. One ask found execFileSync's own wait («asleep: ep_poll in epoll_pwait»); two were answered at JavaScript speed with only undici frames ⇒ «JavaScript» 2 : 1.

The leg's own collector got its first message right after the sync child ended, so that load ran in the hold's tail. The late watchdog's asks, posted after the child ended, met it.

### vault-masker-once — the forms of a secret are built when the vault changes, never when a text is masked (hotfix; the owner's hub spent half its main thread building the output masker)
- **Measured (主开发's named CPU samples of the owner's hub).** 2.369.391 degraded, 120 s: formsOf 30.9 %, percentForms 16.2 %, createRunMasker 13.4 %, jsonForms 7.5 %, base64Forms 2.7 %, vault.js open 4.0 % — about three quarters of the thread under «http request handlers». 2.369.392, an ordinary minute: over half.
- **The cause.** src/agent-output-belt.js maskForSink, called for every piece of an agent's output (a job's log chunk, a message, a status, a progress note), decrypted every maskable entry (`maskableSecrets`) and compiled every form of each (`createRunMasker`) for EACH text. The owner's vault holds 44 entries.
- **Reproduced (lane bench, a real vault engine, 44 invented entries = 724 forms).** At e74fabc6b, ms per call: 200 B 3.57 (2.86 of it the build) · 4 KB 3.61 · 64 KB 8.90 · 1 MiB 76.6.
- **The fix.** src/vault-run.js `compileForms(secrets)`: the table, the ONE alternation and the window, built once and frozen. `createRunMasker` takes either a secrets list or a compiled set, and every masker keeps its own stream state.
- **The fix, continued.** src/server/vault-engine.js `maskForms(build)`: ONE compiled set per vault state, shared by every sink. It is dropped at every record write (an entry added, edited or removed — even a write that then fails), at every load and at EVERY lock (a quiet shutdown lock too, which runs no lock hooks). It lives in memory only and is answered by no route; `masksHeld()` is a gate's question. src/agent-output-belt.js `compiledFor` asks for it; a provider without the memo (a test double) compiles per call, as before.
- **Numbers on the tree, ms per call.** 200 B 0.041 · 4 KB 0.33 · 64 KB 5.2 · 1 MiB 79. The 1 MiB case is the scan itself, which the cache does not touch; the next step is said to 主开发 before it is built.
- **Equality.** scripts/test-vault-masker-once.mjs ④ compares against the per-call build. The lane corpus against master's OWN files (e74fabc6b src, both belts in one process over one real vault): 494 texts, 0 differences, before and after an add, an edit and a removal.
- **Pins (red on e74fabc6b: 12 of 16).** N texts ⇒ one decrypt pass and one compileForms. A change ⇒ one rebuild, and the very next text sees it. A lock (door or quiet) holds nothing compiled. The test-vault-run-model mutant «no window» still hits: compileForms keeps the `const W = maxLen - 1;` line. test-vault-law classifies maskForms and masksHeld as hub-only.

Before the push, the four self-hosted suites that load the changed code run on the release, with test-loop-hold-live. The seven suites that only read the changed files' text run after the push.
- **The fast tier's sum cap 971 → 972 s, by arithmetic (the train's seam, step 0).** The .394 tree states 971.125 s over 553 fast rows: the .393 tree's 970.325 s over 552, plus test-vault-masker-once at 0.80 s. The cap is the next whole second above the stated sum.
- **test-loop-hold-live runs in every release's self-hosted claim from this train on (B-1409).** On the hosted runner the watchdog thread itself can be late, so its count legs may end as a named, counted skip: «ALL PASS (N, K skipped)» and «SKIPPED BY THE BOX …». A skip is not a green. The suite's run on the box is the one that judges those legs.

## 2.369.393 — 2026-11-11

### totp-request-card — an agent asks the person for a TWO-STEP CODE on one card; what they type lands as ONE two-step entry (fb-251bb41646; the owner said yes 2026-11-11 04:55Z)
- **The gap.** An agent that meets a two-step prompt OUTSIDE a browser login (a CLI, an SSH jump, an API console) had no road. The totp row's `request` was NONE, and `--kind totp` was refused; a free secret could hold a seed, but nothing turns it into codes.
- **The fourth target on the SAME road.** `vibespace-vault request "<what>" --purpose "<why>" --kind totp [--name <name>]` files the same `secret-request` item (its record, limits, quiet period and receipt road).
  - The proposed name is judged by THE two-step name rule (src/totp.js `entryOf` — the 两步验证… dialog's own). A bad one, a `--host`, a `--note` or an `--into` is refused by name before any card.
  - The refusal of an unknown kind names every kind the road takes.
  - The card's FIRST line is «<who> asks you for a two-step code (TOTP) for: <purpose>».
- **The card is the dialog.** src/lib/vault-totp-row.js `totpFields` — the 两步验证… dialog's field set (its two ways, the name, the hub's preview with Save drawn only after it, the words) — is extracted ONCE. It is drawn by the dialog (`showTotpAddDialog` = a shell + the field set + its footer) and by the card (src/lib/vault-paste-box.js `totpBoxEl`). The agent's proposed name is pre-filled, and the person's edit wins.
- **ONE writer, ONE door.**
  - The answer (the link and the seed taken off the body as `totpLink` / `totpSeed`) goes to src/server/vault-totp.js `addEntry` — THE person's two-step writer (`totp:<name>`, by: human, «exists» never overwrites). Never `agentAdd` (the agent-owned road), never a free `secret:` entry.
  - The tick («Let <who> read its current code — never the seed — while it runs», default `vault.requestGrantsRequester`) writes ONE grant through the same engine's `grant` — the entry's «Use for…» — for THIS conversation, held for its CURRENT RUN.
  - A conversation not running at the press: stored, not given (`not_running`), said in the toast and the receipt.
  - No new grant grain. No use line: storing a seed is the person's act; the asker's first use is its first `vibespace-vault totp`.
- **The receipt.** STORED, the name, the grant in words (three outcomes: given · ticked but not given · not ticked) and ONE constant TOTP_USE. Never the seed, never a code.
- **The table.** src/vault-kinds.js: the totp row's `request` is `REQUEST({ lands: 'totp', kinds: ['totp'] })`. test-vault-kinds-census CHECK.request takes the `totp` landing.
- **A new cross-check:** every kind the paste road takes is ONE family's request. RED controls: the totp row back to NONE; `--kind totp` gone from the usage. `src/totp.js` joins test-architecture's PURE set (it imports nothing; vault-paste reads its name rule).
- **Gates.**
  - test-vault-paste ⑩d (the ask, the card, the writer, the run grant, the receipt, `exists`, the link way, not running) and ⑫ mutants (agentAdd, the grant without the tick, the branch gone — each RED). The ⑪ sweep finds none of the typed seeds.
  - test-vault-kinds-census, test-vault-law, test-vault-words, test-approval-census (the action and route pins widened, the writer pinned, the agentAdd mutant a gate).
  - Heavy: test-vault-paste-chrome ⑩ (the real card on the desk and the phone) and test-vault-totp-add-chrome (the dialog on the extracted field set).

### hub-loop-stalls commit 3 — THE SATURATED LOOP NAMES ITS TOP FUNCTIONS (the owner's hub and a fleet user's, 2026-11-10)
- **The report.** The owner's hub (2.369.390, up 6.5 h) ran its main thread at 85–93 % of a core in user space with a median loop lag of 0.5–1.9 s, requests waiting 5–8 s behind it — and the holds of a second or more commit 1 names were 178 in 12 h (1.4 % of the time). The saturation was MANY MEDIUM CALLBACKS under the hold bar; the box forbids outside sampling and nobody attaches to a production hub. A fleet user's pod showed the same signature with no network mount.
- **The ruling (05:44Z): commit 1's witness-thread sampler at a dense rate, not V8's Profiler** — Profiler.start held the main thread 2.1 s at a 2.3 GB heap and that grows with the heap. Four conditions, each built and pinned: (1) idle is never work — the kernel state first, an ask never posted while the thread sleeps in its own poll; (2) native time is counted on its JavaScript caller, said in the block; (3) the collector's share from the process's own record (the gc entries of the window), or «GC not split»; (4) the asks' own cost printed, one past its bound halves the rate, the sum past its bound stops it.
- **The build.** PURE src/cpu-capture.js: the trigger verdict (the sysinfo lag watch's level ≥ 1 — src/sysinfo.js `loopLagNow` — or the hold watchdog's holds ≥ 5 in 10 min; one capture per 30 min, the door's counted too; 6 automatic a day; never with the switch off, a debugger port open, the heap near its limit), `tickOf` (the tick's class by the main thread's kernel state), `rawFramesOf`, `profileOf` (the .cpuprofile from the ticks — the V8 format, ≤ 5 000 nodes), `aggregate` (the table read off any .cpuprofile: self time by function summed over call paths, a built-in's time on its caller, node_modules / Node's internals grouped by package with the install's function they ran through, relative paths, idle / GC / program classed, every share of the whole window, under 3 % not listed), `gcSplit`, `blockLines` (≤ 15 lines). The watchdog thread (src/server/sync-fs-witness-worker.js): a tick every 50 ms ON AVERAGE — each interval drawn between 25 and 75 ms — through commit 1's one-ask road; the ticks an ask waits for booked on the stack that answers it; a hold open ⇒ «held» (its own [loop-hold] line names it); the frames interned raw (≤ 1 MiB) and named at the end (fs.promises, one read at a time, 2 s); the file under data/cpu-profiles (temp + rename, the newest 10). The note slot carries the sample's own run (µs). The main thread's book (src/server/loop-holds.js): the trigger every 15 s, the window's gc entries (an observer for the window only — the capture is refused near the heap limit, where an observer costs memory), ONE block in the journal, ONE telemetry row `srv-cpu-profile`, `report().capture` (Diagnostics, the incident bundle), a due capture that did not run said ONCE a cause; POST /api/loop-holds/capture answers the table when it ends, GET /api/loop-holds/cpu-profiles/<name> by its own name only — the owner's cookie. ⚙ System → «Capture a CPU profile (20 s)»; the Diagnostics «Main loop held» section shows the newest capture and the kept files.
- **Measured (live, production timings: a 20 s capture at 50 ms, the beat 250 ms, a hold 1 s).** A known function at ~80 % in 50–200 ms callbacks: commit 1 said nothing; the capture named it first — **77.7 % against the child's own 78.7 %** (Node 22: 77.6 % against 78.7 %), 400 samples, the asks' own run 34–39 ms of the 20 s (0.2 %). One big JSON.parse a call: **jsonCaller 54.2 % against 55.1 %** (Node 22: 61.6 % against 61.3 %). An allocating function: «GC: 2.6 % of the window» = the child's own gc record 2.6 %. A 10 %-busy callback: the tick's class is exact (a probe that dated every tick: every tick inside the busy spans booked on its function, every one outside idle); the share's spread is the binomial one (8.2 / 8.8 / 10.0 / 12.0 % at 200 ticks; Node 22 10.1 % at 400).
- **Found while measuring — a fixed tick aliases.** At an exact 50 ms period the 10 %-busy callback (a 200 ms period) read **5 %**: the ticks phase-lock with any timer whose period is a multiple of 50 ms — and the hub's own beat (250 ms), lag watch (500 ms) and many intervals are. Each interval is now drawn between half and one and a half of the rate; a tick stands for the time to the next, so the shares stay the window's own.
- **The capture's own cost (a busy child, ABBA, work units per second of the main thread's own CPU — its schedstat):** without a capture 172.3 / 172.1, with one 181.7 / 182.8 — no slowdown measurable; the runs with a capture did 5.8 % MORE work a CPU second, unexplained and stated as measured (the two runs without one differ by 0.1 %). The asks' own run is printed in every block.
- **Gates.** test-cpu-capture (fast, 61): the table off a RECORDED V8 profile (scripts/fixtures/cpu-capture/recorded-v8.cpuprofile — its share = its own time, each sample lasting until the next, not its count), the block, idle never work, the .cpuprofile, the trigger, the collector, the files, a real sample answer, the book's doors with fakes, the routes; MUTANTS «idle counted as work», «the kernel state not read first», «the interval removed» red by name. test-cpu-capture-live (heavy): the legs above + the switch off (nothing automatic, the door works), the rate halved / an early stop, a debugger port (the door refused, the trigger silent; opened mid-capture: it stops), a MUTANT of the worker's tick (its idle rule removed: idle 0 %) red by name; Node 22. Each red on commit 1 by itself (no src/cpu-capture.js).
- **Seams (named for the train).** The heading assumes the .391 cut's package.json bump (test-changelog-style takes the newest heading as package.json's version or the next patch). Commit 2's store-write census row for src/server/sync-fs-witness-worker.js (1 site) grows by this commit's writes there (mkdir, the temp's write, the rename, the prune's unlink — the watchdog thread, «not-main»). The zh / ja blocks sit after commit 1's at the end of both tables.

- **Measured — how a second thread sees the main thread's stack** (Node 24.22.1 and 22.23.4, the same; a worker with `inspector.Session().connectToMainThread()`; hogs of seconds inside the probe's own process; lane dir probe/). `Profiler.start` on demand: 120–180 ms of the main thread at a 55 MB heap, 2.1–2.2 s at 2.3 GB (it re-logs every code object) — REJECTED. `Debugger.enable` + `Debugger.pause`: the frame 0.6 ms after the ask, but the enable costs ~0.19 s per 1 300 scripts + ~0.25 s per GB of heap (0.67 s at 2.3 GB), the first pause on an idle loop ~0.5 s at 2.3 GB, and while enabled `await` runs 8× slower (20 M/s → 2.4 M/s) — REJECTED. `Runtime.evaluate` of one expression capturing `new Error()`'s call sites, NOTHING enabled: delivered by a V8 interrupt, it runs AT the held point — a busy loop, a catastrophic regex (irregexp services interrupts), Atomics.wait, sync zlib (between its chunks) — 0.3–2 ms a sample at any heap size; a free loop gapped 1–2 ms; a connected, idle session costs nothing — CHOSEN. - **Gates.** test-loop-hold (fast, PURE, 110 — Node 24 and 22; nine mutants, one per round-3 law, red by name); test-loop-hold-live (heavy, 81 with the Node 22 legs — round 3's ⑪ red on d174ac207 in 12 of its 13 asserts: the planted hogs, the boot, the cap, the off switch by real evaluates, a debugger port, law C against sampling-off runs, the stack-limit soak, heap-flat samples, exits, the profile, and the acceptance's seven must-fix + four smaller); test-auth ⑨; test-memory-census §3b; test-fs-canary unchanged and green; mount-reader-census (the worker: ONE reader); test-sync-fs-census (the worker's readProc and its real-file stat); the stop rows measured once at production timings (probe/stoprows.mjs): 0 of 10 in each of seven, both Nodes.

### cli-self-measure — a Claude Code update never idles the pool until a release ships: the hub measures a new CLI itself
- **The incident (2026-11-09).** The owner installed Claude Code 2.1.321 at 12:54 PT. Production (.386) had records only through 2.1.319, so the 13:05 tick held 11 long-lived-token pool members (`held / cli-unmeasured`). The one full-login member was at its weekly cap, so conversations were walled until 2026-11-13. The same had happened three days earlier (2.1.319 ⇒ .385): eight versions, eight measurement lanes, eight releases. The owner: «每次更新都要重新测量也太弱智了？这个用户体验是你觉得最好的方案吗？» His founding requirement (2026-03-22, item 7): «使用原生claude code，确保claude code更新不需要重新更新本项目代码（除非claude code有breaking change…）»
- **The mechanism.** The measurement's core moved VERBATIM from `scripts/measure-claude-cred-read.mjs` into `src/claude-oat-probe.js` (SHARED; the script keeps its argv, the sudo netns re-exec and the fixture writer). `src/server/cli-self-measure.js` (ORCH, created by the pool engine — no server.js edit) forks the module's child entry at the first sight of a (version, sha256) with no PASS (the fixture's, or this hub's ledger `data/cli-self-measure.json`). The gate (oat-file, oat-file-401, oat-file-switch) runs FIRST; its PASS places the members and fires the pool's one edge (`onMemberReadingFresh`) per member; the record's other three complete behind it.
- **Measured on this box.** The gate takes 271 s on 2.1.321 (68 + 70 + 133 s), the six 445 s, one variant 68.6 s / 1.55 s CPU. The 65 s gap dominates and stays (the same measurement on both roads). Worst case, the gate takes 17 min with every turn timing out; the child is killed at 20 min (`cannot-run timeout`). A streamed sha256 of the 342 MB binary costs 340 ms wall with a worst loop gap of 1 ms; it is memoized by stat identity.
- **Law 3.** These are refused by name before the binary starts:
  - managed settings: 2.1.321 OPENS `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json`, `managed-settings.d` and `managed-mcp.json` whatever HOME is;
  - remote tokens: it opens the hard-coded `/home/claude/.claude/remote/{.oauth_token,.api_key,.session_ingress_token}`;
  - `no-strace` / `strace-denied`, a scratch that meets a forbidden dir, the mock's nonce, the proxy's CONNECT canary, and the env allowlist (`ENV_ALLOW`).
  - After a run, a token the run never made (P1) or a successful open of a guarded path (P4) voids it.
  - 2.1.321 makes no name lookup under the mock proxy (no resolv.conf read, 0 connects to :53).
  - strace was missing from BOTH Docker images; it is added here.
- **Rulings.**
  - R1: place at the gate.
  - R2: no For-you item while the check runs inside its bound; the pool card's one calm line and the roster's clause say it. The blocked-pool item is not filed during a check.
  - R4: the 60 s binary-identity check asks the version clock at once.
  - R5: `cli-oat-measured` / `cli-oat-measure-fail` (version, sha256, verdict codes).
  - R6: a FAIL is never re-run for the same version + sha + PROBE_VERSION; cannot-run is retried at the next start or after 6 h; aborted never; the owner's «Check again» runs it regardless.
  - R7: this heading.
  - R8: the second runtime gate's words. A newer build is a quiet fact, never «not registered … until the next release». A record kind is counted once per build (`cli-record-kind`, or `cli-record-surprise` for a REGISTERED build). There is no red card in the chat for either; none had been drawn since .344.
- **Law 5, the census of version gates** (scripts/test-cli-self-measure.mjs §8, grep-derived, printed). Two gates decide at runtime: the oat gate and SCHEMA_CLI_VERSIONS. The rest are test pins or text matches. Each row answers «does an ordinary Claude Code update need a VibeSpace release?» — NO for every row. A planted gate is red.
- **Deviations from the law page.** The words use durations («about 5 min, started 2 min ago»), never clock times: the pool's other sentences print UTC, and a stored line goes stale. The two «Check again» verbs (the browser version's, the held CLI's) are one family read off the foryou-actions registry (`CHECK_AGAIN_TYPES`, `checkRoute`, `checkSaid`), which lowered inbox-window's id-branch baseline 18 → 16.
- **Not moved (follow-ups).** Spawn-time checking of the binary (the window is ≤ 60 s now; 主开发 files it). A new pool conversation is still refused during the check (its words name the check). An oat-only DIRECT spawn uses the env road on a held CLI (oat-env measured: Sonnet by default). `hotSwitchEvidence` has no version key. The «newer than the record table» line could draft its own dump.
- **The tip fix (b0ae071c5).** test-billing-badge-live went red on the tip only (the .388 base 48/48): `child_process.fork` hands the PARENT's execArgv to the child by default, so a hub run as `node -r <hook>` (the suite's preload) ran that preload inside the measurement child, which stole the suite's command files. The fork now passes `execArgv: []`, and a hub holding no long-lived token forks nothing at all (`accounts.hasLongLivedTokens()` — nothing to place, nothing to measure).
- **Acceptance r1 (not accepted, one round) — what changed in r2.**
  - A: an unreadable ledger (EISDIR / EACCES / EIO) is said ONCE and read again no faster than the 60 s tick; until it reads nothing is placed on this hub's own PASS and nothing is forked (r1 looped: 19 112 lines in a second).
  - B: the PASS is of BYTES. A changed binary identity drops the hub's own PASS on that tick even when `--version` is silent (`accounts.noteCliBinary`); an unchanged identity whose hash read failed changes nothing (no flap). oat-file-sync keeps `bin` as the command string; the facts object is `binFacts` (the seam with cli-update-needs-nothing).
  - C: the run ends itself. The child entry kills every group it started and every pid the tracer named (recorded with its /proc start time at first sight, signalled only while it holds), removes its own run dir, and exits on the hub's disconnect, a SIGTERM or its own deadline; the hub's exit handler sends SIGTERM (r1's SIGKILL skipped that cleanup).
  - D: ONE launcher (`launch`) runs the binary for every variant AND the `--version` read — env checked, under strace, in its own group, belted; the record names the version run's traced exec. test-vendor-whitelist §13 reds a second way to run it, a real API host as base, and a deleted assertEnv.
  - E: the file fence denies by default. A successful open (strace -y: the resolved path behind the fd, so a relative open counts where it landed) under the person's REAL home (passwd, never $HOME — test-architecture §68's one reasoned src site) or the hub's data dir voids the run unless it lies in the run's scratch, the binary's install dir (only when that dir holds no deny root — a binary dropped straight into the home or the data dir allows only its own FILE; test-oat-measure-fake's own wrapper found that hole), or the ONE interpreter file a #! CLI runs under (node opens its own binary — measured). Preflight refuses a scratch inside, containing or linking into a credential store (`credentialRoots`: ~/.claude, ~/.claude.json, ~/.codex, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, gcloud, keyrings, ~/.gnupg, data/subs, codex-subs, agy-subs, vault.json, pool-links).
  - F: the run reaches the mock's port and nothing else. Measured first on the recorded clean 2.1.321 run (8 connects, all 127.0.0.1:<mock port>; no unix / inet6; no resolv.conf / hosts / nsswitch read — no lookup at all). The trace is now %file,%network,%process; any connect / sendto / sendmsg / sendmmsg to another destination of any family (inet6, unix path or abstract name, a UDP send with no connect, 127.0.0.53) aborts the run; NETLINK is counted in the record (`netlink`), never off the box.
  - G: a check never hides a wall. The blocked notice always says everything; the checking line is an ADDITION under its own hourly key; «the conversations waiting continue by themselves» only when a PASS alone unblocks (else «If it passes, N accounts it holds rejoin the pool»), and only then is the blocked For-you item skipped (R2). The PASS edge is PLACEABLE: `onMemberReadingFresh(id, 'cli-measured', { placeable: true })` skips the 10-min freshness gate (the member's eligibility changed, not its reading) and still fires only onto a member whose last reading is usable. The conversation's own card, watch notice and chip carry the arm's `checking` facet (cause.checking, dropped the moment that run is no longer checking — `liveCause`).
  - H: the spawn-env census sees the hub's fork as a `literal` site in its own file (no alias); with its env removed it is `raw` with no row — red.
  - I: a PASS is the JUDGE's (cli-caps oatInFile over the row's three verdicts) under the CURRENT probe version — on the child's message, on a row read from the file, and after a probe bump (measured again, once).
  - Smaller: a press during a check answers «already checking — about N min left»; stop() never leaves the view at checking; pool-link-notify exempts the four label strings, not the file; oat-mint ③ says three calls; the version census sees compare helpers, bare string compares and build-keyed JSON tables (its limit, named: untracked files); assertEnv requires CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 on every run.
  - The census file adopts the shared shape ({"//", schema: 1, rows with match / sites}); test-cli-self-measure §8 reads the keyedOn 'version' rows.
- **Acceptance r2 (not accepted, one narrow round) — what changed in r3.**
  - 1, the file fence reads EVERY open: strace prints an open another thread interrupted as two lines («openat(… <unfinished …>» … «<… openat resumed>) = 23</path>»); r2's reader kept only call-name lines and dropped the half with the resolved path. `parseTrace` is now THE grammar (a call, an unfinished half, its resumed half — joined by pid before anything judges them —, process and signal events); any other line, or a trace ending in a broken line, VOIDS the run `trace-unparsed` (unknown is not clean). The recorded clean 2.1.321 trace (sanitized fixture: 1749 lines, 98 split pairs, 620 opens) replays whole and is still a PASS.
  - 2, the --version run is fenced like a variant (the same roots, the same grammar); a version run that voids runs no variant.
  - 3, /proc/<pid>/… of a process that is not one of the run's (environ, mem, cmdline, fd — an agent session keeps its tokens in its environment) voids.
  - 4 + 5, the kernel ends the run — no pid is ever read from text: every run is `setpriv --pdeathsig KILL -- strace --kill-on-exit -f …` in its own session. Measured on this box: the measurement child SIGKILLed ⇒ the tracer, the CLI and a setsid grandchild gone within 1.5 s; WITHOUT --kill-on-exit the CLI and the grandchild live on (the kernel's default only detaches tracees); strace ignores SIGTERM in `-o FILE PROG` mode (its -I 3), so a stop is SIGKILL on the tracer's group, and its log still ends on a whole line. The pid + start-time list (r2) is gone. The tracer's logs live OUTSIDE the scratch, in a deny root (a tracee touching them voids). Preflight refuses by name a strace without --kill-on-exit (`strace-old`, < 6.6 — Debian bookworm ships 6.1, so the Docker images' own check is cannot-run until their base moves) and a missing setpriv (`no-setpriv`).
  - 6, the promise looks at the member that would come back: «the conversations waiting continue by themselves» (and the conversation's own card / chip / watch notice saying the check) only when a member the check holds could serve on its last reading (`memberServable`, the verdict the PASS edge reads); otherwise the blocked words, the wall's date and the For-you item stand.
  - 主开发's ruling on strace < 6.6 (14:10Z): refused by name, the members held exactly as without this lane, the release road unchanged; the version from the tracer's own `strace -V` (`straceVersionOf`: a version it cannot read is old — pinned 6.1 / 6.5 / 6.6 / 6.19 / garbage); said only on a hub that HOLDS a member for the build (a hub holding none never even starts the check); the words name the door per machine kind (a VibeSpace image: `/usr/share/vibespace/image.json` or `/.dockerenv`). The images (bookworm, strace 6.1) move with a fleet change, not here.
- **Acceptance r3 (KILL accepted; WORDS confirmed; the FENCE proven here) — what changed in r4.**
  - 1, THE RECORD'S STREAM (round 5 states its limit — what it buys is that the build's own writes and an accident cannot damage the record, not a fence against a build that sets out to deceive): strace writes its record to ITS OWN stderr — a socketpair end this process holds (a socket cannot be reopened through /proc; no file of it exists) — with `--always-show-pid`; the first traced process is a TRAMPOLINE (`src/claude-oat-trampoline.js`, copied into the scratch) that hands the binary its own stderr file, so no traced process ever holds the record; the judge reads only the stream, kept whole as it arrived. Proven on the real tracer: a fake that reads a canary and then truncates / appends forged lines / renames a clean file over / deletes / overwrites every record it can reach ⇒ five VOIDs naming the canary; the same five against the r3 module (the record a file beside the scratch, read back by path): the rename turned the void into a PASS (each line in the suite's log).
  - 2, EVERY CALL ACCOUNTED FOR (`recordGap`): an unparsed line, a broken tail, a stream that never ended, a tracer that had to be killed (something outlived the CLI's stdin), no death line of the first process, a half that never resumed, or an OPENING call cut by its process's death ⇒ VOID; the one exemption, by name and position: a call that opens nothing cut AFTER the tracer saw its process die. Measured on a clean run (the good fake): 0 dangling, 0 cut, split calls joined.
  - 3, THE DOORS: io_uring_setup ⇒ ENOSYS injected by the tracer (the runtime falls back — measured: node 24 tries it 3× per process), handle opens / another process's memory or fds / ptrace ⇒ EPERM injected; all traced, and one that SUCCEEDED anyway voids `door` by name.
  - 4, /proc of a process not of the run is judged on the path ARGUMENT too (pipe / socket / anon inode / /dev/null / a dirfd + a relative name / task/<tid>), against the pids the run had AT THAT LINE (a pid that joins later was someone else when opened).
  - 5, the store keeps the refusal's version and machine kind (oatFileCaps); 6, an image is its stamp (/usr/share/vibespace/image.json, now written by the root Dockerfile too — /.dockerenv no longer counts); 7, every destination of a sendmmsg; 8, the launcher census closes a later assignment, the o.claude member, /usr/bin/env + a shell, dash / ash / busybox, a second module alias — and counts 6 child-process calls (r3's report said 7: wrong); 9, the belt kills only while the tracer's handle lives; 10, a SIGKILLed measurement child reads `child-killed`.
  - `scripts/oat-trace-judge.mjs`: the fence run on a trace of a reader's own (no binary) — the grammar, the gap, the file fence, the doors, the network fence.
  - Smaller: (a) the one-launcher census is DERIVED from every child-process call in the module (any spelling, aliases, a binary by another name, a shell) — exactly one runs the binary; (b) the network classifier reads the destination from the ADDRESS argument (`sockaddrOf`: the first `sa_family=` outside every quoted string), never from a payload; (c) netlink is counted once; (d) the binary's identity carries its change time (an in-place rewrite that restores the mtime still moves the ctime).
- **Acceptance r4 (confirmed: the grammar, the hub fails closed and signals only its own children, the proof log, the store's words, the image stamp, the launcher census, child-killed, the gates) — round 5, the tidy, under 主开发's ruling.**
  - THE LIMIT, in words (the probe's header, the kb essay): the measurement is a WITNESS of an honest build's conduct — does this unknown build handle the long-lived token the way the recorded builds do — and fails closed on what it cannot account for; it is NOT a sandbox against a binary that sets out to deceive its tracer (same user, no namespace). The person is protected by what the run is given — a made-up credential, a scratch HOME, a loopback mock — not by the trace. «The record is not the tracee's to write» is no longer said as a guarantee.
  - 1, a clean build can pass: the resolved path of a result (`= N</path>`) is read OUTSIDE every quoted payload (`unquoted`, the address scan's reading; strace -y prints a `"` in a path as `\"` — measured).
  - 2, the launcher is the shipped one at every launch: the scratch copy is compared byte for byte with the shipped trampoline before the version run and before each variant — a difference VOIDS `launcher-changed` and nothing more starts.
  - 3, a link's or a rename's SOURCE (link / linkat / rename / renameat / renameat2 / symlink / symlinkat; a relative one against its dirfd, a symlink's against its link's directory) is judged like an open's resolved path — deny roots included; a relative source with no directory in the record cannot be placed and voids (a clean 2.1.321 run renames absolute paths only — 12 of 12).
  - 4, the record has a size: 64 MiB a launch (a clean variant: 263 KB); past it VOID `trace-oversize`, nothing more kept, the belt still reads every line.
  - 5, a record with no call at all (a death line alone) voids `trace-unfinished`.
  - 6, the kill guard is liveness: `isLive` = exitCode AND signalCode null at all four sites and in killAll (a child that died by a signal keeps exitCode null for ever — measured).
  - 7, words: a tracer that did not say its version is said so («the strace on this machine did not say its version»), never «(this one is ?)»; the user changelog says what a person in a VibeSpace image gets today (the check does not run there yet; those accounts wait for a release, as before), with no tool name.
  - 8, the census row says the image rule (the stamp's EXISTENCE — its content is never read); the launcher census catches a template-literal path to the binary and any dynamic import of child_process; a pid leaves the run's set at its death line (a reused number is someone else's until a clone of the run names it).

## 2.369.392 — 2026-11-11

### usage-ledger-walk — the ledger is walked by what is NEW (hotfix; the owner's hub and a fleet hub froze 5–6 s every half minute)
- **Measured.** A perf sample of the owner's production hub (30 s, then two NAMED samples after a restart with a perf map): the one main thread 64–93 % busy, one handler in 5–6 s bursts every ~30 s; by name about a third of the thread is `costBetweenMulti` (usage-anchors.js) + the cold rows it builds (cache-bounds `rows`) + `_events`, through THREE doors — the pool engine's evaluation (maybePoolAutoSwitchForPool → readCache/viewFor/burnOf → estimateFor/burnFor, 37 % inclusive), GET /api/usage's estimates (14 %), and ratesFor → learnRates → extractPairs (21 %).
- **Reproduced (lane bench, the released code).** The brief's suspect — the estimate windows of accounts read 28–94 days ago — does NOT show: a stale reading's 7d / scoped bucket ROLLS to its last weekly boundary (usage-estimator.js estimateBuckets), so one window is ≤ 7 days; one pass of 25 identities at 3 M rows = 0.2 s. What shows is the relearn: every 60 s the anchor sweep calls `estimator.invalidate(identityKey)` for each identity a statusline keeps fresh, and the next ask relearns it over EVERY anchor pair — one costBetweenMulti per pair; the owner's 27 identities hold ~82 k pairs against the interval memo's 20 000-key cap (random victim) ⇒ three asks in four walk, the old pairs through the cold columns (a light row built per visit). At the owner's shape (2 M rows, 82 k pairs): one relearn of every identity = 4.85 s, and again 4.95 s. Two more costs grow with uptime: `noteLive` clears the 30 s estimate memo on every streamed record, and `_liveDelta` scanned the whole live ring (up to 3 000 entries) on every costFn call; `_sortHot` re-sorted every hot row whenever one arrived (two of a fresh hub's saturated seconds).
- **The fix (src/usage-anchors.js, src/usage-estimator.js, src/usage-history.js).** ① THE INTERVAL'S OWN VERSION: the memo is keyed ids|from (up to two intervals per start) and versioned by the rows IN [from, to] (two binary searches), not by countUpTo(to) — a backfill elsewhere no longer invalidates a pair, a late row INTO it does; a pricing edit or a new ledger generation empties it; entries are compact Float64Arrays of RAW sums, 200 000 keys. ② THE PREVIOUS SUM + THE NEW ROWS: an interval asked again with a later end whose own part saw no new row adds only the rows after its old end, in the walk's order — the bits of a full walk; a `to = now` window on a burning account costs what arrived since. ③ THE FIRST LEARN IS ONE SWEEP (a boot, a pricing edit, a rewritten ledger): every identity's pairs in ONE walk (primeCosts — the same rows in the same order per interval), stepped in 6-hour slices off the request path (primeCostsStepped); meanwhile the estimator answers as while the ledger loads (no estimate, the reading stands; rates from the frozen costSince, never persisted); a span ≤ 50 k rows primes at once. ④ THE LIVE RING BY RANGE: in ts order the entries in [from, now] are one block — binary search, the same entries in the same order; an interval outside the ring's span answers at once; an out-of-order ring keeps the scan. ⑤ `_sortHot` sorts the arrived rows alone and appends / merges them (the full stable sort's order).
- **Numbers (owner shape, lane bench).** One relearn of every identity: 4.85 s → 0.40–0.44 s with ZERO ledger rows visited; the one sweep: 1.54–1.58 s at 82 k pairs / 1.81 M rows (was 4.85 s pair by pair), stepped: the plan (every interval's version) 0.21 s at once, then 1 085 two-hour slices summing 1.23 s, the longest 108 ms (the store).
- **Equality (law 2).** The lane corpus against a git archive of 05082bbd0 (cold + hot rows, both CLIs, a remote host resolved and unresolved, absent counts, late rows into old intervals, new anchors + invalidation, a pricing edit, a rewritten ledger, a loading ledger ⇒ null): 3 seeds × 19 447 values, 0 differ.
- **Round 2 (主开发 08:09Z — the verifier: equality 48 seeds × 150 steps, 388 848 comparisons, 0 differ; every identity relearned 12.47 M rows / 21.9 s → 58 059 rows / 0.65 s). Commit A, amended:** A1 an ask whose START is after its END (estBucket's costFn with a reading newer than the caller's now) never reads or leaves a slot — it left one with a negative row count and every later ask from that start extended from before it ($0.628 served for master's $0). A2 PRIMING IS LOADING FOR EVERYONE: the ledger's own ledgerLoading() says it while the first learn runs (usage-hold-road `_holdForPrime`, whenWarm resolves at its landing) and the pool engine's wholeLedgerGate starts the prime before it reads the signal — the sweep (anchor, calib) and the automatic decisions wait, costs are partial, no rate is persisted; before, only the estimator waited (the pool decided on raw readings; a calib from frozen rates was persisted). A3 the COUNT pins at shapes where 05082bbd0 walks (21 000 pairs: 1 walk vs 1 773; a stale identity's rolled windows: 200 rows vs 4 216) and two mutants red by name (the version ignoring the ledger's generation; a prime landing after the price table moved). A5 THE HOLD ALWAYS ENDS, AND A PRIME THAT FAILS IS MASTER'S ROAD: every step of the stepped prime is guarded whole (the memo's version read, a slice, the store — built first, stored all or nothing, a failed store empties the memo); a throw anywhere or steps that stop coming back (PRIME_HOLD_MAX_MS 30 s, an unref'd timer) end it — the hold released, nothing landed, nothing thrown out of the timer, said once — and that epoch's costs are walked interval by interval as on master. A4 (1) THE NORMAL ARRIVAL: a ledger row's ts is its transcript record's time and the scan appends it ~15 s later, while GET asks every 8 s — a burning conversation's rows land BEFORE the last ask's end, and the version counts every account's rows, so one such row sends every identity's windows back to a full walk, exactly as master (a GET pass with 25 scan-lagged rows: 750 638 rows on both trees). (2) The prime's plan (every interval's version) holds the first ask 436–452 ms on the verifier's box (0.21 s on mine) and its longest step is 140–203 ms. (3) A relearn of every identity is 622–674 ms and recurs every 10 min (ratesFor's TTL, all identities at once). (4) The memo is ~509 bytes a key — 97 MB at its 200 000-key cap (not the 250 B first stated). (5) A prime landing clears the estimate memo: estimates are fresher than master's 30 s memo at that instant. (6) eventForRid / eventForMid (the popup's billing lookup) scan every hot row on the main thread. The census greps the whole tree. These are the next commit's (B) pins.
- **Pins.** test-usage-ledger-walk (new, fast): §1 equality to 05082bbd0's walk (a frozen copy, to the bit; the released code from a git archive when the clone holds it — SKIP by name otherwise); §2 a COUNT per door — one relearn after an invalidation visits 0 rows at 300 and 2 400 pairs, one GET-shaped pass visits what arrived, one pool evaluation (36 conversations × 4 members, the ring full, a conversation streaming) visits what arrived and reads the ring by range; §3 a ratchet (2 400 pairs ≤ 6× a free cost); §4 mutants red by name (countUpTo(to) as the version, the cap at 20 000, no forward extension, a version blind to the interval's rows ⇒ equality red, the whole ring scanned); §5 THE CENSUS of every main-thread reader of the ledger's iterators with its cadence and bound — one NAMED DEBT: usage-pool-engine darkTaintedAccounts walks 7 days per pool decision while a host is dark (≈ 18 ms a call at 3 M rows — 405 k rows in 7 days — the same on 05082bbd0). test-usage-ledger-perf, mount-reader-census, test-sync-fs-census: rows restated (the prime's two reads of data/usage-anchors, once per memo epoch).

## 2.369.391 — 2026-11-10

### passkey-lend-cleanup — the kept passkey leaves with its ceremony however it ends (B-97ae, HIGH; the HOTFIX commit)
- **The defect (measured).** test-browser-passkey-chrome S11b was red 6 of 10 on .390 (2 of 8 on .389, seen since .370). The person's Cancel was answered ok (AbortError), yet nothing went out after it — not in 10 s, on the SAME socket (int361's probe, wsSame=true). The page's own record still named the virtual authenticator at +10 s: a key with user-verified set stayed on the tab after the person said «no».
- **The cause (traced).** `cancelPasskey` awaited the hook's `cancel`, then marked every pending record of that context ended itself (`rec.outcome = 'cancelled'`) and never called `pkEnd`. The page's own end report (`Runtime.bindingCalled`, ev `end`) was the only road to `pkEnd`, and `PK.applyEvent` matches only a PENDING record. So the order decided:
  - the page's report first ⇒ pkEnd → the drain → pkUnload (the green, +4–5 ms);
  - the cancel's answer first ⇒ the report matched nothing ⇒ the cleanup NEVER started.
  - The trace, the real module over the fast suite's fake CDP: answer-first — `cancel-answered k=1 [[1,7,pending]]` → `binding end matched=false [[1,7,cancelled]]` → no pkEnd.
- **The fix.** A ceremony `cancelPasskey` ends goes through the ONE end, `pkEnd` (the tab's drain → `pkUnload`: its keys, its UV, the once-authenticator). The page's later report finds no pending record, so there is never a second end.
- **Pinned.** test-browser-passkey (fast) «B-97ae the person's Cancel takes the lent passkey back in EVERY order» — the answer first, the report never coming, the report first.
  - The fake loads the key for real (Chromium's model with `keys`), and the leg checks it went in.
  - Each order is judged AT REST: every call answered and the link quiet for 20 ms (≥ 5 loop turns). At rest the key is removed once (`removeCredential`), UV is off and the authenticator is removed exactly once.
  - Not one line may be said from the lend on (the lines the watch says while opening on the fake are named).
  - RED on 05082bbd0 in the answer-first and never-reported orders and in «never their NEXT sign-in's»: there the key left only with the authenticator, when the next sign-in's belt removed it.
  - test-browser-passkey-chrome S11b on real Chrome: int361's six runs on 869d6ac7b.
- **The census (every place in browser-dialogs.js that ends a person's-browsing ceremony):**
  - the page's own end report (`Runtime.bindingCalled` ev `end` → `PK.applyEvent` → `pkEnd`) — THE ONE END;
  - `cancelPasskey` — the banner's Cancel (browser-stream.js `passkey-cancel`, by 'user'), the CLI's verb (routes/browser.js, by 'agent') — marked the record ended itself: NOW each ended record goes to `pkEnd` (the fix);
  - the tab closed (`Target.targetDestroyed` → `PK.endPending`) — cannot hold a lent key: the target and its session, which own the virtual authenticator, are gone (nothing to send on);
  - a frame's context destroyed / the page's contexts cleared (`PK.endPending` → `pkPageGone`) — the person's once-authenticator (the person's key and its UV live in it) is removed through a drain — goes;
  - a refusal after the lend (`outranked`) — the person's road removes the once-authenticator before the release; the agent's road refuses and the page's report reaches `pkEnd` — goes;
  - a gate step that threw (`pkFailed` → release) and the page's hold running out (`pkHold`, bounded) — the page's own end report → `pkEnd` — goes;
  - the session detached / the socket down (`Target.detachedFromTarget`, `down`) — the record is not ended there; what Chrome keeps on a detached session is the walk's measurement;
  - the kernel road (`pkKernelCancel`) — VibeSpace signs, no authenticator — cannot hold a lent key.
  So, in the person's browsing, `cancelPasskey` was the one place that ended a ceremony past the cleanup and could leave the person's key lent. (On the agent road, a document gone mid-ceremony leaves the loaded key in the tab's authenticator — «Not closed», (a) below.)
- **Exactly once.** The report first then the cancel's answer: the cancel finds no pending record (nothing more). The answer first then a late report: the report matches nothing (`PK.applyEvent`). Over a fake that behaves as Chromium does (a second remove is an error, said): one `removeCredential`, one UV off and one authenticator removal, with nothing said, in every order.
- **Never the next ceremony's key.** A sign-in started at once after the Cancel waits for the clean-up (the tab's drain), pairs its OWN authenticator, loads its key, sets its UV and keeps all three; only the cancelled one's go. (The base's r5 belt already removed a stale once-authenticator at the person's next hooked sign-in — so before this the lent key stayed until then, and any request Chrome met without the hook met it.)
- **The controls and the mutants.**
  - «B-97ae RED CONTROL»: `cancelPasskey` without the `pkEnd` it hands each ended ceremony (05082bbd0's) — red by name.
  - «B-97ae TIMER CONTROL» (the acceptance's): the one end reached 50 ms late — the key, its UV and the authenticator still lent at rest, in both the answer-first and never-reported orders.
  - On a copy of the tree, the whole suite against browser-dialogs.js mutants:
    - no end at all, or the end 50 ms or 1000 ms late ⇒ answer-first, never-reported and «next» red by behaviour;
    - 25 ms late ⇒ never-reported and «next»;
    - 10 ms late ⇒ «next» (the next sign-in's belt removes the authenticator first: the cancelled key is never removed by its own end).
    - Below the at-rest window the order legs alone cannot see a delay.
- **The acceptance (2026-11-11 03:18Z) and its tidy.** The product change was accepted. The verifier's own walk ran 2 000 seeds over the order of the cancel's answer, the page's report, each of pkEnd's replies, a 2 s late answer, a double press, and both Cancels at once. The fix was at rest every time; master left the key in 1 144 of 2 000. The tidy touched only the suite and the docs (src byte-identical):
  - the first legs' fake refused the load (no `keys`; the product said «a stored passkey was not loaded», and the legs' word filter missed it), so only the authenticator's removal was pinned;
  - a pkEnd 50 ms late passed every leg that waited until clean.
- **Not closed (the second commit, after .391 — each pre-existing on master, none in ordinary use):**
  - (a) the agent road: a document gone mid-ceremony (context destroyed or cleared between the lend and the assertion, under 0.2 s) leaves the loaded key and UV in the agent tab's authenticator until that tab's next ceremony ends — `pkPageGone` unloads only the person's once-authenticator; one line by the same law (each ended record through the one end);
  - (b) a cleanup step that fails is never said: if `removeCredential`, `removeVirtualAuthenticator` and `disable` all fail on a live session, the key stays while VibeSpace believes it gone — say it by name, and name the tab to the person;
  - (c) `cancelPasskey` marks every pending record of the context, also one that arrived in the same socket read as the cancel's answer and that the hook did not cancel (never released; the page waits out its hold) — mark what was pending before the await;
  - (d) UNMEASURED, needs real Chrome: what a tab keeps when the watch's socket closes or the hub restarts during a lent ceremony — measure it first; it decides whether a re-arm needs a sweep.

### dialog-press — a suite presses only what holds still, and checks where its press landed (B-8b8c; the .390 mirror's red)
- **Measured, not assumed.** test-refresh-note-chrome's desk 确定 landed on 取消 (the .390 mirror, both tries) or the footer (.373). A per-frame recorder on the suite's own road showed the cause: the suite unfolds the session list and opens the form 21–30 ms later, inside `#main-wrapper`'s 0.2 s margin-left slide, which carries the WHOLE workspace. 确定 stays the same node and its window never re-places; the ground moved +40.6 px in one frame between the helper's read and its press. Reproduced on the box: the base suite's desk leg was red 3 runs of 4. CPU throttling made it rarer, because it slowed the suite past the slide.
- **Not the product.** The form's buttons never move inside it. On the desktop, only the person's own act changes the list's width.
- **THE still door** (scripts/scratch.mjs `stillPresser`; PURE `stillVerdict` / `landingVerdict` / `stillLookSource`):
  - It presses only a still target: the element at its point, enabled, the same rect on two looks, and no running box-moving animation on it or an ancestor.
  - It then checks where the pointerdown and the click landed; a miss is named.
  - `realClicker` shares both halves.
  - test-refresh-note-chrome presses through the door everywhere.
- **Gates.**
  - test-still-press (fast) carries the verdict table, both mirror rows as named misses, two mutants red by name, and THE CENSUS (a ratchet ledger: 126 heavy suites, 299 direct coordinate presses on 2.369.390).
  - test-refresh-note-chrome's new leg runs the page's own slide slowed by CDP `Animation.setPlaybackRate` 0.1, with two RED controls.
  - The Chrome mutant (the gate removed) is red by name on both tries.

  - **Round 4 (the acceptance of e4cc4acee: 13 of 15 confirmed; ONE law, two instances, both from this lane's Cancel).** THE LAW: after any await a handler draws and keeps nothing unless it is still the latest act — and closing the dialog is an act; what a superseded or closed act started on the hub, if it cannot finish without the dialog, is ended.
    - Both live dialogs (mounts-dialog `wireOAuthConnect({live})` for Connect + Duplicate, `reauthDialog({live})` for Re-authorize): every act — the button, the other road, Cancel, the close — takes the next generation; after each await a handler checks it (and the close) before it draws. Cancel never says «cancelled» over a newer act (instance 1).
    - A close is an act: `wireOAuthConnect` returns `{close()}` (the Connect dialog closes every type's block before `endNeedingDialog`, Duplicate before its delete). A press whose answer lands after the close draws nothing, opens no page, registers nothing, and its sign-in is ENDED whatever its road — no page was opened for it, so nobody can finish it (instance 2). R5 is about a SHOWN sign-in: one whose page is open and comes back by itself still keeps running at the close.
    - An answer of a press that is no longer the latest act ends the sign-in it started, by its id (`strayEnd`); the shown one is never touched.
    - The smaller point, my choice: while a press or a Cancel runs, BOTH press controls (the button and the other road) are busy — one act at a time. Cancel stays usable during a press and ends what that press starts.
    - Every cancel a dialog sends names its sign-in: `POST /api/channels/adapters/:id/auth/cancel` takes an optional `{flowId}` (channels-auth `cancelAuth(id, {flowId})`: another sign-in of the account is left running, `cancelled: false`); Re-authorize and Duplicate send it. A late cancel never ends a newer press's sign-in (a close then a quick reopen and press).
    - Found by the new driver, not by the verdict: the Connect dialog's poll read status through `capi`, which THROWS on the hub's error answer — and the poll swallowed it, so a sign-in the hub had ended (replaced by another dialog's press, cancelled elsewhere, past its time) stayed on screen with its Cancel for ever. The status read now hands the poll the hub's answer (`{running: false, error}`, worded by its code); a network failure still throws.
    - THE PIN — the class, not the two cases: test-consent-road ⑭, the REAL Connect dialog (esbuild; only utils / i18n stubbed at their import line) over a fake page, in front of the REAL engine, routes, store and loopback. A seeded scheduler holds every request and every answer and releases them in a random order (the newest half the time) between weighted acts — press, the other road, Cancel, close, reopen — only on controls a person could press. At rest (all delivered, the poll ticked twice) the invariant: a block with its Cancel ⇔ the one sign-in the hub runs, the one it follows; nothing running ⇔ no such block; no listener without a shown sign-in; no sign-in that needs the dialog behind a closed one; no consent page after its dialog closed. Two worlds: a silent company preset from another computer (a loopback that needs the dialog) and a listed one (the route). 100 seeds per world by default (`CR_SEEDS`, `CR_SEED0` = another reader's seeds); a failing seed prints its shape and whole sequence.

(2) A busy control always comes back: Re-authorize's failed press now ends its busy for the other road too; a failed Cancel gives the presses and the watch back. (3) «Cancelled» is said only when the hub runs nothing: a Cancel, and the poll that hears its sign-in ended, read what the hub runs for the kind (`adoptOrEnd`) and SHOW it — a sign-in another tab started — and a reopened dialog shows any running sign-in of the kind (not only one that comes back by itself); a lost start answer whose dialog closed while it read ends what it started. (5) The ended line is worded on the client by the answer's code (`endedLine`: superseded / cancelled / timeout / gone, a neutral line for an unknown code) in en / zh / ja. ### agy-models-report — Antigravity reports its own models per account (the owner, 2026-11-10: «Antigravity 支持的模型为什么是写死的呀？不应该从 Antigravity 自己汇报吗？»)
- **The door** (ORCH `src/server/cli-models-door.js`, generic: a descriptor declaring `modelsReport {argv, parse, cwdOf, by}` — antigravity's `agy models`, parsed as DATA by PURE `src/harnesses/antigravity-models.js`): ONE account per call (a named account's HOME root, cwd its empty login dir; the machine's own login = the key «machine»), the CLI the read-time check answers, the agents' env with the descriptor's keyEnvVars dropped, stdin closed, STDERR NEVER READ, 20 s, stdout capped at 64 KiB (past it — or at the timeout — the CLI is killed AND the pipe let go: a child of the CLI holding stdout cannot hold the listing open).
- **The act (rulings R1 + E1):** a listing starts ONLY from `POST /api/cli-models/open` (the New Session model field's pointer press / opening key; a chat's model menu opening) under the floors — 6 h after an answer, 15 min after a failure (persisted, so a restart keeps it), a CLI file that changed (realpath + size + mtime) reads again — or `POST /api/cli-models/refresh` (the explicit row «Refresh from Antigravity»: the floors set aside, once a minute). Both are `personVerdict` doors (an agent's bearer / another site ⇒ 403). A GET NEVER lists: the opening is a POST, not a GET parameter, because a same-origin GET from a page on plain http carries neither Origin nor Sec-Fetch-Site, so no GET can show a person's page. The listing's end broadcasts `available-models-dirty {backend, account}`; the re-read it causes is a GET.
- **The menu:** a harness with no provider record that reports ⇒ `models` = exactly the reported rows (agy's order and labels) under the Default row, `report {source, listedAt, lastError, listing, account, host, by}`; before any report the shipped AGY_MODELS; another machine ⇒ the shipped rows and «that machine's Antigravity is not read yet» (the device op is deferred). One line under the New Session field / atop a chat's menu (PURE `src/lib/cli-models-words.js`, the moment by the client's agoText): «As reported by Antigravity 5min ago» · «VibeSpace's list — Antigravity has not reported yet» · a failure in amber, its door «Sign in to Antigravity» when signed out (a named account's own sign-in; the machine's: Manage agents). An answer that changes no row never rebuilds the open field.
- **The cache (ruling E2):** `data/cli-models.json` (tmp + rename, 0600) — only the door names it (no export section, no import, no sync); an account removed takes its entry at the delete route, and any write drops an entry whose account is gone; stdout only, so no value of the sign-in can reach it. A failure keeps the last good rows.
- **E3 (closed by the owner):** no derived row and no hook for one — the menu offers what agy reports or the shipped rows.
- **The drill** `test-agy-models-door` (fast, 64 legs, 2.3 s): the parse, the door on a fake clock with a /bin/sh stand-in (a HANG never holds a person's menu — it answers at once with the last rows — nor the floor: killed at the timeout, the slot freed, paced like any failure), E1 on a loopback express app (a GET, a stale `list=open` GET, the dirty re-read loop: 0 calls; 10 openings signed out: 1), the words in en/zh/ja, the callers' census over EVERY src file (a call planted on a timer / at boot / per spawn / from an agent / from a GET / in a brand-new file — each RED by name), four patched copies (no floor, no failure floor, stderr read, no timeout kill) each RED by its leg. test-vendor-whitelist 5d rows the door's one caller; test-exit-forensics and spawn-env-census row its child.
- **Round 2 (acceptance of 017693b83: seven laws, each pinned red on 017693b83 by name):** A the press — `press(req, kind)` mints (personVerdict inside the door), a WeakSet, used once; `ask` refuses a caller's `{person: true}` «no-press»; the census pins ONE mint (provider-models cliDoor) and `modelsReport` read by the door alone. ### phone-take-photo (commit 1 of 2) — a phone's + sheet takes a photo (the owner, 2026-11-09 14:14 PT, Android Chrome, photographing device labels: «为啥我在手机上添加图片的时候不能拍照»)
- **The facts (f5e087bb5).** The composer's image door was ONE hidden `<input type=file accept="image/*" multiple>` with no `capture`; the phone's + sheet (lane phone-chat-composer) offered 图片 / 文件 / 文件夹 = that input, the upload input, the folder input. Android Chrome hands an image-only input to the system photo picker (a gallery sheet, no camera in it — the owner's screenshot); iOS Safari's own sheet for the same input offers Take Photo. No `capture` attribute existed anywhere in the client.
- **The camera door.** `cameraDoor(onShot)` (src/lib/chat-input.js, exported — THE helper for a phone door that offers a picture): its OWN hidden input — `accept="image/*"`, `capture="environment"` (the back camera opens at once), one shot — appended to the phone face only (the desk row's children and the pinned desk DOM signature are unchanged); `row()` = the 拍照 sheet row or null. The shot goes to `_addImageAttachment` — the picked image's reader, chip, zoom and send (an image block in the `chat-input` frame). A cancelled camera fires `cancel` / no file: nothing added, nothing said. The gallery input is untouched (image/*, multiple, no capture).
- **The touch test.** `isTouchDevice()` (src/lib/utils.js: `(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)` — the media query app.isTouch reads), asked each time the sheet opens. A phone-wide desk window (fine pointer) shows 照片 / 文件 / 文件夹, no 拍照 — never a greyed row. An iPad at desk width keeps the desk row (its image button's input already gets Safari's Take Photo).
- **The rows.** 拍照 · 照片 · 文件 · 文件夹 (en Take photo / Photos / File / Folder, ja 写真を撮る / 写真 / ファイル / フォルダ — two new keys), each with its glyph: `UI_ICONS.camera` (new in icons.js, the set's 16-grid stroke style), `FILE_ICONS.image` / `.unknown` / `.folder`; the sheet (`.chat-plus-sheet`, phone-gated in chat.css's PHONE COMPOSER block) takes the phone sheets' row size (style.css `.mobile-sheet`: 44 px, 14 px words, 20 px glyphs) — in the product's CSS order viewers.css's 11 px desk row had won over the 40-px touch rule.
- **Every file input a phone can reach (law 3).** The composer: built (the + sheet). The channel window's reply attach (src/lib/channel-window.js `createComposeFiles`: one input, `multiple`, no `accept`, behind the paperclip) shares none of the composer's attach code — a 拍照 row there = a small sheet behind the paperclip + `cameraDoor`'s input, its shot pushed into `picks` through the same reader the input's change uses, judged by `composeFilesVerdict` like any pick; an accept-less input is not handed to the photo picker on Android Chrome (not measured on a phone). The file explorer's Upload (src/lib/file-explorer.js `uploadInput` multiple + the folder input) saves into a folder — a camera row belongs there only if shots should land as files; the same helper with `_uploadFiles([shot])` as its road. The For-you answer boxes take no file. Not photo doors: the plugin install (.vsp / .zip), the config import (.json), the SSH key file in Mounts.
- **Gates.** test-phone-composer (fast census: the four rows in order, the door's attributes, the touch gate, the road; RED controls: the row on every device, many shots, the upload road, capture on the gallery, 拍照 opening the gallery) — 5 RED by name on f5e087bb5. test-phone-composer-chrome ③ (390, Android UA, touch: the inputs' attributes, a cancel, a JPEG set on the camera input by CDP `DOM.setFileInputFiles` = ONE chip, sent as one image/jpeg block with the words) and ④ (390 on a fine pointer: no 拍照); the page now loads viewers.css in the product's order — 12 legs RED by name on f5e087bb5, the desk legs green on both. A headless Chrome has no camera: the owner accepts on the phone (+ → 拍照 → shoot → ✓ → the chip; send).
