### login-request-card — an agent asks the owner for a WEBSITE LOGIN on one card; what the owner types lands as ONE web-login the browser can fill (B-a681; the owner 2026-11-09 «agent 自助登录浏览器网站什么时候上线？»)
- **The gap (measured on f5e087bb5).** `vibespace-vault request … --kind api-key|password|secret` landed a FREE entry `secret:<10 hex>`, which is run-only. An owner who pasted a site password and a two-step seed on an agent's ask got two free entries that no browser road can use. So every agent fell back to a takeover.
- **The third target on the SAME road (law 1).** `vibespace-vault request "<what>" --purpose "<why>" --kind login --host <site>` is the same `secret-request` item, record, limits, quiet period and receipt road. `targetOf` gains `{kind:'login', origin}` and the action's existing `hosts` scalar carries the site: no new record shape, no new store key.
  - The answer goes to the same `POST /api/vault/secret-requests/:id/answer`. The route takes `loginPassword` off the body, as the add door's own route does.
  - The door calls THE web-login door's ONE writer and validator, `logins.addOwn`. The site always comes from the REQUEST, never from the body. No free entry is made beside it.
- **The site the owner reads is the site the fill compares (law 2).** The brief's `siteOriginOf` does not exist; the add door's rule is `BL.originOf` + `BL.secureOrigin` (WHATWG URL ⇒ a punycode host; https, or http on this machine's localhost only), and both are CALLED, not changed.
  - An origin the add door refuses is refused at the CLI by name (`login_site_required`, `login_one_site`, `login_bad_origin` in the add door's own words, `login_words` for `--name` / `--note`).
  - The card's FIRST line (the item's text and dedupe key) is `{who} asks you for a website login on {site} — it is typed only on that site`. For an `xn--` host, PURE `siteWords` puts the Unicode form beside the punycode one; the ORCH door hands in node's `url.domainToUnicode`, so no builtin enters PURE.
- **The card's form is the add door's (R1 = A).** `src/lib/vault-login-row.js` `loginFields({site, fixed})` and `loginRefusalWords` are extracted from `showLoginAddDialog`, and the dialog and the card both draw them (Site read-only on the card).
  - **The two-step field is a NAME**, as the add door has always taken it, never a seed. «Two-step code…» opens THE 两步验证… dialog. `showTotpAddDialog` now hands `refresh({name})`, and the card fills its field with that name.
  - The door refuses a name that names no entry (`login_totp_unknown`) BEFORE `addOwn`, because the add door checks only the name's shape. That add-door gap is forwarded to the pivot chain, not fixed here.
  - A password's line break is refused by name (`login_password_lines`), never stripped. A page's input strips it, so only a non-DOM client ever sends one.
  - The user name the vault keeps (lower case, what the fill compares) is said under the field when it differs from what was typed.
- **The grant (R2 = B).** master's browser-login gate (`fillVerdict`: own OR `GM.admits` over `<origin>#<user>` / `<origin>#*` / `*`) has a per-conversation grain but no time grain (no `browser-login` ENTRY_FIELDS, so `admits` / `fillVerdict` read no `until`) and no lock end. The free entry's 8 hours is the run door's in-memory Map.
  - So «Let <who> sign in to <site> with it» writes ONE STANDING row through `logins.grant` (`session:<cid>` on `<origin>#<user>`, nothing wider). It is ticked by default when `vault.requestGrantsRequester` is on.
  - Before the press, the card says what «allowed» IS — «<who> can sign in as you on <site> with it until you remove it in Vault ▸ Web logins ▸ Use for… — there is no time limit» — for every site alike, and the button names the moment: Save and allow / Save only.
  - The Vault window's button is «Use for…» (用于…). master's agent words in `grantWords` say «Used by…»; that is reported, not moved (the pivot's file).
  - Revisit the default when the pivot lands a time grain: it is ONE constant.
  - **The owner's law (2026-11-09, the identity-provider addendum withdrawn).** The person's grant is the boundary; the product does not build a fence it cannot hold. A login for an identity provider (accounts.google.com) is allowed exactly like any site, and nothing on the card or in the receipt implies a narrower limit than the gate enforces.
- **The receipt (law 3).** PURE `loginReceiptText` says STORED / UPDATED for the site and names the user ONLY when the grant was written. An agent that may fill a login reads its user in the login answer; one that may not never learns it.
  - HOW TO USE IT is ONE constant, `LOGIN_USE`: `vibespace-browser login <site> --user <u>` on a custom-kernel profile. On standard Chrome the vault sign-in is paused since 2.369.364, and the next road is `ask-human`.
- **Every surface is a row (law 5, R3).** PURE `src/vault-kinds.js` gains its 11th surface `request` (`REQUEST({lands, kinds | into, site})`): free-secret, integration and web-login declare it, and the other twelve families say NONE(why).
  - scripts/test-vault-kinds-census.mjs CHECK.request: both doors mounted, each `--kind` / `--into` in the usage, and THE PURE verdict landing the family's own target. Four RED controls fire.
  - test-approval-census `secret-request`: the a-pin is widened, and two c-pins are added (`loginPassword` taken off the body; `addOwn` with the request's site), plus the login mutant as a gate.
  - test-conversation-needs gets a fixture (kind `secret`), and test-peer-text-census gets the declared receipt words.
- **The fill engine is untouched (law 7).** No edit to src/browser-login.js, src/server/browser-logins.js, browser-dialogs.js, browser-login-fill.js or the browser CLI. The lane only CALLS `originOf` / `secureOrigin` / `parseName` / `hostOf` and `addOwn` / `grant`.
- **Found, not moved.**
  - `addOwn` accepts a `totpName` that names no entry; the fill then has `otpMissing`.
  - `fillVerdict` lists an origin's users in `login_ambiguous` BEFORE its grant check.
  - `grantWords` says «Used by…» where the button says «Use for…».
- **r2, the rebase onto 2.369.388 (2056c98de) — the paste plan follows THE item's words renderer.** A login card's first line carries no agent words (law 2), so its agent words ride only in the paste plan. `secretAskHtml` drew that plan as `escHtml` text, the one For-you words block outside `wordsHtml`. So a masked link there (the door's belt puts «redacted» inside a link) had no note. A free-entry card's first line did have it: measured in the tray, login 0 notes / free 1.
  - The plan now draws with `wordsHtml`, like every other row's words: a masked link is its words plus THE note inline, and a link is a For-you link.
  - test-vault-paste-chrome ⑧ checks a login card and a free-entry card with the same masked-link words: every masked run has its note, the plan included; never the link whole, never a live link to it, no note inside a `<pre>`.
- **r3, the acceptance of r2 (accept-r2-verdict.json) — four laws.**
  - **A. The user name reaches the asker ONLY with the grant, on every road it can read.** The door recorded the STORE as the asker's USE of the entry (`noteUse`, door paste). `vibespace-vault uses` then read `web-login:<origin>#<user>` back to an UNGRANTED asker.
    - Storing a login is the OWNER's act, so no use line is written. The asker learns the user from the receipt alone, and only with the grant; its first use is its first fill.
    - test-vault-paste ⑩c is a census: every agent route the hub mounts has a row (a route without one is RED). It is answered with both askers' bearers after an unticked and a ticked answer, and every answer and stash entry is searched raw / hex / base64 / base64url for the runtime-built user names ⇒ 0. The ticked one appears in its own receipt only.
    - The owner-side audit (`vault-web-login-saved` from addOwn, the hub log's `[vault]` line, this door's `vault-secret-stored` with `place: entry`) names the entry exactly as the add door does. It is unchanged: the owner's record, no agent road.
  - **B. What the owner typed is never lost by opening the helper, on EVERY surface that draws the card.** The r2 fix was tray-only: in the title-bar mini inbox, a press inside the 两步验证… dialog closed the popover with both fields typed.
    - Now ONE road in the box itself: «Two-step code…» first moves THIS box into its own form window (`showSecretPasteDialog` with the box, on a self-model whose verb is `postSecretAnswer`), unless it stands in one already, and only then opens the dialog.
    - A surface that redraws the row draws «This login card is open in its own window · Show it» instead of a second, empty box.
    - The panel's tray-only branch and its outside-press exception are gone: user-todos-panel.js equals the base.
    - test-vault-paste ⑬ is a census of the surfaces derived from src/lib (every file that draws the row or the box: the tray, the mini inbox, the phone's page, the chat's needs card, the For-you window, the Vault window). Each surface has its `surfaceLeg` in test-vault-paste-chrome ⑨: type both fields → «Two-step code…» → a press INSIDE the dialog → both fields hold → save a code → its name lands in THAT box. Two RED controls.
  - **C. The unsaved question covers everything typed.** The card's form asked only for the password. `boxTyped` now watches a login's user name / password / two-step name, a pasted value, and a new entry's name or description changed from the agent's (`data-was`). Chrome ⑨ checks that a typed user name alone asks on Escape.
  - **D. The receipt says what happened.** Three outcomes, three sentences: granted · not ticked · ticked but the permission could not be written. A grants store that refuses its write pins the third (⑩c).
  - Small: the CLI's line for a login ask says what the card is, and the form window's plan draws through THE words renderer (`linkedHtml` + the note).
- **Traps.**
  - test-bundle-globals reads a NONE sentence `a card's own field (…` as a bare call to `field(` (a symbol of the client). Reword words that put an identifier before a parenthesis.
  - test-record-clear-census reads `const entry = String(r.name)` in a journal line as an `r.name` receiver (five rows RED). A log line names the request id, never the entry.
  - test-wake-approve-card pins `box.append(row, note, state);` verbatim.
  - The m3 mutant of test-vault-paste now finds the answer line by its head, not by a spelled-out copy.

### cli-update-needs-nothing — an ordinary Claude Code update (a new version, a new model) needs nothing from VibeSpace: the installed CLI is the source of truth for its models (the owner, 2026-11-09: «每次更新都要重新测量也太弱智了» · «你准备以后怎么彻底解决这个问题？»; his founding requirement, 2026-03-22 item 7)
- **The road (measured on 2.1.312 / .314 / .319 / .321, nothing run, no vendor contact).** Every build carries ONE baked catalog literal (`var X={"//":"Hand-maintained baked-in model catalog …",schema_version:1,pricing_tiers:{…},models:[…],aliases:{…},…,latest_per_family:{…}}`, 19.9–22.1 KB) beside `VERSION:"…",…,BUILD_TIME:"…"`: every model id, family, display name, window + 1M flags, max output, a pricing tier with every rate (Haiku 5.5's `long_prompt` included), the aliases, `latest_per_family`, `best`. Read in 53–70 ms (warm; ~200–300 ms through the hub's async 8 MiB chunks). The other roads, measured on a loopback mock with a fake key and a strace belt (0 off-loopback connects): `control_request initialize` / `list_models` = 5 alias rows with `resolvedModel` and prices as TEXT, no sizes, no cache rates, a spawn; `<config>/cache/model-catalog/published-*.json` exists only after the CLI fetched and RSA-verified downloads.claude.ai's remote catalog (0 files under the mock); `init.model` + `result.modelUsage` equal the literal's values (evidence after the fact).
- **The reader** (PURE `src/claude-model-catalog.js`): a STRICT literal grammar (objects, arrays, strings, numbers, `!0`/`!1`, `null`, `void 0`; a call, an identifier, a template, a spread, `__proto__` refused by name — nothing is ever evaluated), then every field validated by the provider record's own validators (`ID_PATTERNS`, `LABEL_MAX`, `CONTEXT_MAX`, `MODELS_MAX`); a rate outside 0…1000 $/MTok, a window past 10 M, an 80-char label are REFUSED BY NAME, never clamped (the id keeps the shipped answer). A real 1M form = `native_1m` or the 1M beta (`supports_1m_suffix` alone is only a spelling: Haiku 4.5 has none).
- **The ledger + the trigger** (ORCH `src/server/cli-model-catalog.js`): ONE call on the tick that already reads `claude --version` (oat-file-sync: 20 s after boot, every 15 min — no timer of its own), keyed by version + the file's stat identity; a binary read ONCE into `data/cli-model-catalog.json` (atomic, ≤ 20, the evidence: anchor, offset, bytes, ms, the version string agreeing). Unreadable ⇒ the shipped rows + ONE quiet line, never a broken menu.
- **The readers, catalog first, the shipped tables the seed.** Picker (cli-env `menuRows`): the aliases labelled by what they mean on THIS CLI («fable · Fable 5.2 · 1M»), per family the catalog's latest + every id we ship, each with its 1M form, sized by the CLI; any other catalog id resolves when typed, its `[1m]` form too (`resolveModel`'s open branch now accepts `<id>[1m]`). Prices (`src/catalog-pricing.js`, ruling R3): the person first (a row on disk equal to no shipped row, or a per-account override of the row an id falls on); an own shipped row vs the catalog by the newer of the CLI's BUILD_TIME and `SHIPPED_PRICES_CHECKED` (2026-11-09; a tie to the shipped row); a family / `_default` fallback yields to the catalog; an agreeing catalog adds no key; a catalog row is never written to pricing.json (setPricing keeps an unchanged one the catalog's); the editor's new Source column says «VibeSpace's table» / «From Claude Code {v}» / «Entered by you». Families (model-family `setCatalogFamilies`, acceptance r1 law C): the catalog's family is read PER MODEL (an exact id map, never a word) and has its quota lane only on an account whose OWN reading carries a scoped bucket of that WHOLE name — every other reading judges it by all its caps (fail closed: a vendor may meter a new family under an existing cap, as Mythos under Fable); a catalog word never names a bucket («Model cap», «Overage Included» stay family-less). On this release's table 2.1.321's catalog moves exactly two prices — Haiku 5.5 (on Haiku 4.5's row, ×10, no long tier) and Sonnet 5.5's cache hit ($0.20 → $0.10) — the rows the fable-52 follow-up types by hand.
- **The maintainers hear first** (`global.__vsEvent`, local; each ONCE per hub, kept in the ledger): `cli-model-catalog-read`, `cli-unknown-model` per id 2.1.321's catalog did not name, `cli-unknown-model-price` per disagreement, `cli-unknown-model-catalog` per unreadable catalog or refused value, `cli-unknown-model-alias` when an alias leaves its word (the lock's `modelsMatch` and the chip's `sameModel` hold an alias by its word — true for every alias of .312–.321). The `cli-unknown-` ones are Diagnostics' Harness drift rows.
- **The drill** (`test-claude-update-needs-nothing`, fast; the stand-in = `scripts/claude-catalog-stand-in.mjs`, a /bin/sh stub whose bytes carry 2.1.321's catalog + Fable 6 + the new family Quill): pickable in the 1M form, priced from the catalog with the source said, in its family's lane, no «wait for a release» in any model-side word, said once (a restart says nothing), an unreadable binary = the seed + one line, bounds refused by name, the person first — every scene with its RED control (the shipped tables alone). §M = the census: `scripts/fixtures/cli-update-census.json` (25 model rows `{id, file, keyedOn, needsReleaseOnOrdinaryUpdate: false, road, suite}`; cli-self-measure's version rows join it at the train). The hub leg (`…-hub`, heavy): a scratch hub with the stand-in as CLAUDE_CMD lists, prices and says it through its own routes.
- **Seams (named for the train).** The key becomes cli-self-measure's sha256 and its 60 s identity check when that lane lands; scenes A (the token-file accounts placed again — its probe core), G (its quiet record line) and E's chip (fable-52's follow-up) join the drill in a second commit; `SHIPPED_PRICES_CHECKED` reads `scripts/fixtures/anthropic-pricing.json`'s date once that fixture is on master. The fast row states 0.7 s, measured under the cap (the census reads only `git grep -l` candidates; the 340 MB real-binary read is the hub leg's): with .389's `FAST_SUM_CAP_MS` of 956 s the sum is 955 975 ms, 25 ms under — no cap move.
- **Acceptance r1 (7c695e80a, not accepted — six laws, fixed in this amend).** A: the ledger is loaded at the server's boot (cli-env create) — in force from the first answer, before any tick, with no claude at all. B: the person first PER MODEL — the catalog adds no key under a row the person entered (a family row, a custom key); an account's override shields THAT account only (`_rateFor` applies it to the model's catalog row through `fileTierOf`). C: above. D: one read's synchronous work is bounded (≤ 8 starts, ≤ 512 KB parsed in all: a crafted file's worst loop gap 77–81 ms, was 339–364); a read is opened O_NONBLOCK, must be the file the stat saw, and races 60 s — past it a later tick tries again. E: the load drops what the save could not write; a failed save is said once; a kill's tmp file is removed; an I/O failure is retried, a content verdict stays. F: kb-api / kb-features / the scripts INDEX lines; the census gained the `family-key` kind (short keys, Maps, switches, DEFAULT_PRICING) and a per-row `sites` count. Smaller: passive rows survive a read; one `available-models-dirty` push; plain aliases on a conversation on another machine; the price table scrolls on a phone; built-in property names and markup labels refused by name.
- **Acceptance r2 (22f4305e6, not accepted — two money defects the r1 fixes opened, law C tightened, seven small; fixed in this amend).** B1: an account's override is judged on the table WITHOUT the catalog (`fileKeys`), so a newer catalog that replaces a model's own shipped row never hands it to the account's family override (an `opus`-only override at $50 no longer prices Opus 5.5 at $50). B2: a disagreement is said when it comes to exist — usage-history hands every recomputation's list to the hub module (at the read, at boot, at the person's save), said once. B3: `pricingTable()` is the disk table again (the config export and its summary carry what a person entered); the editor reads `pricingView()`; an import drops a row the exporter's `sources` called the catalog's. C final: a quota lane is a fact about ONE account's reading — a catalog family has its lane only on a reading that carries a bucket of its whole name; no process-wide memory. Small: an over-bound catalog is `literal-long`; realpath / stat inside the read's bound; the load drops entries the reader could not have produced; the census catches `{ opus: …, sonnet: … }` on one line; test-pricing-tiers' control runs a patched copy with the .388 open branch; every door for another machine goes through one `host` parameter (`remoteRows`); the downgrade consequence of «the newest build wins» is said where the rule is.
- **Acceptance r3 (48bbc29e0: THE PRODUCT ACCEPTED; one tidy amend).** The «said» set forgets nothing still true: no slice by age; at every save it keeps what is still true (a kept build, a model it names, a disagreement some live price table still reports — each table reports every recomputation, an empty one too) — 10 000 padding lines, two restarts: 0 repeats, then 10 lines on disk. An import names, by key, each row the export marked as the catalog's (persistence's summary) instead of dropping it in silence. The census prefilters take the escaped `\[1m\]` regex. Stale words gone (familiesOf's comment, the unused plainAliases). Named debt: the large-file half of the loop law is pinned only by the heavy hub leg.
- **Not moved (reported):** cli-registration's «until the next release» sentences (cli-self-measure's, ruled there); usage-anchors / usage-estimator's private four-lane splits (Mythos → other, model-family says fable); session-store's `> 190k ⇒ 1M` guess; fast mode stays unpriced (its rates are not in the literal).

### report-mark-on-ack — a hook-route mark moves when the turn CARRIED the answer (confirm, then mark)
- **The incident (2026-11-09, the owner: «我看它不是回你了吗？» … «没送进你上下文，那不是你的问题吗？自己看一看。»).** The coordinator asked the device-operations conversation with a wake at 23:14Z; the reply landed in their direct group at 23:17:31Z and the log said «read by VibeSpace 主开发 23:18Z». The coordinator's 23:18:20Z turn (a background-task notification) carried no hook context at all — like four other turns that day (5 of 19). The next injection (23:24:32Z) did not carry the reply either: the hub had counted it handed over. For six minutes the coordinator told the owner «no answer yet».
- **Measured (claude 2.1.321 against a loopback /v1/messages mock, unbilled — lane measure/probe-cli.mjs).** A background-task notification turn RUNS UserPromptSubmit and attaches the answer (not a cause). The product hook aborts its fetch at 3 s, far inside the CLI's registered 10 s: a hub answering at 3.5 s gives `hook_response {outcome:'success', exit_code 0, stdout ''}` and a record with no `hook_additional_context` — the five turns' exact shape; 2.5 s still carries. A Stop during the hook makes the CLI SIGTERM it ~45 ms later (`cancelled`, exit 1). 10.5 / 12 KB answers are persisted as a 2 KB preview. A hook's stderr (exit 0) never reaches the model request or the transcript; the stream hands it over in `hook_response.stderr`.
- **Reproduced (measure/probe-hub.mjs: the REAL groups engine + prompt-context route behind node http, the REAL hook spawned like the CLI does).** An `Atomics.wait` stall of 4 s / 9 s when the hook connects: the hook printed nothing, the route ran after the stall, moved `reportedUpTo` and drew the card; the next turn lacked the reply — LOST. At route time the socket looked alive (the request is parsed before the FIN): the hub cannot see the drop from its side. Hub down / a 401 right after a restart: an empty turn with nothing marked.
- **The law (src/turn-carry.js, ONE helper).** Both hook routes (task-context = SessionStart, prompt-context = UserPromptSubmit) STAGE every mark they would move (`carry.stage(kind, apply)`, the values captured as told). A caller that sends `X-VibeSpace-Confirm: 1` gets `delivery: dl_…` (18 random bytes) and returns it to `POST /api/agent/prompt-context/carried` after its OWN write: the hook once its stdout write callback said ok (the request flushed before exit, ≤ 1 s, never awaited by the turn); codex-chat after `thread/inject_items` answered; acp once `session/prompt` is written (send()'s writable test); agy after its stdin write — each wrapper confirms the turn's own id (a prompt Stopped before dispatch confirms nothing). Unconfirmed by the next call ⇒ dropped: nothing moved, the same content composed again under `<vibespace-sent-again>` («sent again — the previous turn did not confirm it …»), the drop counted in the hub journal: `[inject] not carried: <key> — the <person|machine|session start> turn's <route> answer (<n> B: <riders>) was not confirmed before the next call; its request had waited <s> s …` (no content; the hook's `X-VibeSpace-Hook-Sent` gives the wait).

A state write in either route or the drain / preamble helpers outside a staged closure reds, unless on the not-told list with its reason (6 rows: empty-map makers, the restore normalisation, the no-inject baseline, the empty jobs marker, the unchanged flag with nothing told, integration-off's consume-and-drop, a helper called with no stage); a kind without a row cannot be staged (turn-carry throws by name).

It runs the staged applies of that delivery and nothing else, then persists the seen marks (the persist moved into the close: at the confirm, at once for a legacy caller). - **Round 3 (主开发's acceptance r2: eight of nine confirmed; the restart line had two holes and one route could poison the other).**
  - **The restart is a fact about the CONVERSATION:** a delivery handed out and not yet confirmed is written to data/turn-carry-outstanding.json under the conversation's key (`TC.createOutstanding`, setupAgentRoutes' new `carryDir`, which server.js gives as data/). A NEW process reads what a dead one left. The first answer that CARRIES anything to such a conversation says «the hub restarted …» and retires the row, however its record was made (restored or RESUMED). An empty SessionStart (a compaction, a /clear) or an empty prompt spends nothing. A conversation made here, one whose delivery was confirmed before the restart, and a LEGACY caller get no line. A previous process's id answers 404 unknown.

An unconfirmed SessionStart no longer starts every later prompt with the line. The preamble's seen hash moves only forward (a per-process compose sequence: two answers in one ms are still ordered), and so does the jobs marker. A delivery's owner is the SESSION OBJECT, never its status key: a key that changes when the conversation id arrives no longer gets 403.

What an answer stages is CLAIMED meanwhile (`claimStash` / `claimRetry` / `jm.claimNotifs`, released when the answer is dropped or another answer may compose it again): a hand-over, a retry wake or the cap of 30 passes it by. Cards are drawn only for what a confirm actually TOOK, so a second confirm of the same entries draws none.   - **A claim belongs to the conversation and always ends.** The unconfirmed deliveries are registered by CONVERSATION, whichever session object holds them: the next answer from ANY session object of it (a RESUMED record — every create mints one — or a second session) releases what they claimed and owes the repeat line. A claim nobody touches again ends at its own bound (`LIMITS.claimBoundMs`, 5 min, said in the journal). Boot releases what a dead process left, and the boot journals now call a `carry` claim «an unconfirmed answer's claim», never «a hand-over».
  - **The carry may fail; the answer may not.** No throw inside the machinery (open, stage, wrap, close, the file's write) empties or fails a hook answer: open is guarded in the routes (`openCarry`), and the others catch themselves. The answer falls back to the legacy answer (composed and marked at send) with ONE journal line naming the cause. A failed write of the outstanding file is said ONCE and keeps the confirm law (the file only serves the restart line).
  - **The file.** The load takes an OBJECT of rows and nothing else (an array, a primitive, broken JSON, an unreadable path ⇒ an empty table, said once). It is BOUNDED: rows older than 48 h leave, then the newest 1000 stay (at the bound an answer costs ≈ 4 ms against 0.7 ms with an empty file — the verifier's measurement; the report had said ≈ 1 ms). A row is retired 2 s after its confirm (`LIMITS.clearAfterMs`, above the notice store's 500 ms write), and only if no newer delivery marked it. A row follows its conversation when the key changes (the conversation id arriving), at its next answer.

Removing either claim reds the fast tier (measured). `_newProcess()` stands for a process boundary in-process.

  - **Every claim has its bound from the instant it is stamped, and a failing claim call is said.** The drains no longer call `claimStash` / `claimRetry` / `jm.claimNotifs` bare: they claim through `carry.claim(kind, call, records)`, the answer's claim book. Its bound is armed BEFORE the stamp, so a claim ends whatever happens to its answer next (closed, confirmed, dropped, a throw before the close, a route that never closes). A claim call that throws breaks the carry like any other door: ONE journal line, the legacy answer (the section rides, marked at send). What it stamped before throwing is unstamped by the records' own `carry` tag. The jobs digest is now rendered (spill + render) BEFORE its records are claimed and its take staged, so a throw there stages nothing. Measured RED on c721ffcf5: the section silently missing with no line, and a claim-then-throw left claimed until a reboot.
  - **The boot line is true end to end.** A `carry` claim posts no frame, so its release line names no hand-over and no frame to look for. A hand-over's line keeps its words, and both kinds on one conversation are named apart (the stash's, the retry park's and the jobs engine's boot lines).

### fable-52-cli-321 F1 — a locked model chip holds the served model against the LOCK TARGET, and every client is told when the lock moves (the owner's 🔒 fable[1m] served by 5.2)
- **The fix (a slice ahead of the full round: the bar, its two server writers' frame, chat-view's door).** The owner's phone read an amber «🔒⚠ claude-fable-5-2» on a conversation locked to fable[1m] and served by Fable 5.2: `_modelMismatch` held the served model against `_statusModel`, which a DRAWN record sets (the init of a turn from before the CLI update, met on a scroll up — the virtual scroll draws older history after the newest), and the locked label was `_statusModel` itself («🔒 claude-fable-5-1» after a reload). Now, locked with a known target (`_lockTarget()`), a served model the LOCK TARGET holds is never amber (an alias lock family-wide through the bar's sameModel, a full-id lock exactly) and one it does not hold is amber; the locked label names the served model, else the target; the fallback tooltips name the target; nothing reported yet ⇒ the target as the label, the title crediting no CLI report. Round 1 (e8060fcbe, not accepted) held a target the bar learned only at attach: on a second client, after the lock was re-targeted, unlocked or relocked elsewhere, it was amber where master was plain and right (2 808 scenes in 主开发's table) and hid real fallbacks (10 920). So THE LOCK IS TOLD (the multi-client law: a persistent change reaches every client live): stream-wall `lockFrame` — the attach status's two fields as a `model-lock` meta op — is broadcast at every server writer of the lock (set-model's press and its pick under a lock in ws-handler; the parse's target-less latch and its alias → full-id upgrade); chat-view applies it through the bar's attach door (applyStatus, with `lockMoved`: a served fact standing when the lock moved is judged as before, against the model last reported, until the next served model). A bundle that does not know the subtype ignores it and draws master's chip. Unlocked conversations and a lock without a target read exactly as before.
- **Measured (lane tables, master as the oracle of «plain and right»).** Unlocked and target-less locks, 800 scenes: markup, class and title byte-identical with c4762d5af's bar (its control, a fable[1m] lock, differs in 132 of 160). TWO clients, every sequence of up to five events (a turn, a turn seen mid-way, a fallback, a pick of opus / fable / sonnet on A, /model opus typed on A, Unlock and Lock on A, scrolls on either, a reload of B — 402 233 sequences, 804 456 judged steps; the slice's world tells both clients, master's tells none): 0 steps where master is plain and right and the slice amber; 0 where master is amber and right and the slice plain; the residue is 71 858 false ambers of master's dropped, 10 123 real fallbacks master hid, and 9 143 steps of a /model typed under the lock (below); the slice's bars hold the server's lock and target at every step (master's second client keeps a stale lock badge at 97 041). The table can fail: without the broadcast 3 093 + 609, without the lock-move mark 221.

Red: c4762d5af's bar 11 legs; the bar comparing with `_statusModel` again 8; no broadcast in ws-handler 6; none in the parse 1 (the census); chat-view ignoring the op 7; no lock-move mark 1; a label naming the drawn model 7. test-mobile-gaps' 5-1 scene on the phone (40 pre-update turns, locked, attached, 40 turns of 2.1.321 live, the older history loaded: c4762d5af reads amber «🔒⚠ claude-fable-5-2» there).

### mask-value-shape — the secret belt judges a NAME (its head), never a value; a masked link never looks whole (the owner)
- **r8 (a second commit on the accepted 5c56b367e; the r7 verifier's two minors).** (a) A LETTER never leaves a URL. path-linkify's CJK_PUNCT ranges also hold letters, numbers and marks (々 〆 〇, 〱–〵, 〻, 〼, the Hangzhou numerals, the combining 〪–〯), and a URL's trailing shed took them: `https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/人々` linked `…/wiki/人` on the base's For-you and text roads, and on r7's markdown too. foryou-links `URL_LETTER_RE` (`\p{L}\p{N}\p{M}`) guards every URL tail walk: `tailEnd`, the chat's `_urlEnd` / `_maskedToken` / `_cjkAutolink`. A change on the two base roads, for the better. (b) For-you segmentText was QUADRATIC, on the base too: `relHits` (and the path / mail hits) ran cleanPath's `[…]+$` over a whole blank-free token, so `see ` + 16 384 dashes + `，然后` took 18 M steps, ×15.7 at ×4 input, about 1 s. Pins: test-secret-shapes / test-path-linkify / test-user-todos-layout `r8 (a)`; test-masked-note-chrome three `r8 (b)` count legs on exactly that shape (+ a path's dots before a letter). **r9 (this commit, amended — the r8 verifier refuted «every road»):** the chat's path pass and file-URL pass ran the same `[…]+$` (`see /a/b` + dots + `c`, `file:///a` + dashes + `x`: ×15.3–15.9 at ×4 input on the base and on r8). path-linkify `cleanPath` is now the backward walk itself, over the trailing set defined ONCE (`isTrailing`, exported). For-you's r8 copy (`cleanTail`) and both client files' `TRAIL_CH_RE` copies are gone. Parity with the old regex: all 65 536 UTF-16 units and 35 490 strings (the lane suites' literals + a seeded corpus), equal on every one. ### ci-heavy-verdict — a marker vouches for exactly the suites that ran; the CI mirror's verified run is the hosted half (B-e381)
- **The block, and the road around it.** heavyBlocker cleared a red heavy marker only with a newer FULL green descending from it, and the box wrote no marker after 2026-11-01. That day's red (109 suites under a broken PATH) blocked every production push. Measured: both repositories set `core.hooksPath` to the repo guard, whose pre-push chains to the git-dir's own hook. The production checkout has this gate there; a cut worktree has none. So .385–.388 were pushed from cut worktrees AROUND the gate (only the secret guard ran), and `VIBESPACE_SKIP_CI=1` skips the check and the post-push launch alike. What stood in was the CI mirror on the exact sha: the fast tier and the HOSTED heavy half (338 of 399). Of the 61 self-hosted heavies, 53 never ran on a .387 or .388 sha.
- **The union (heavyBlocker).** A red clears when every suite that failed in it has since run green on a descendant: a FULL green alone, or the union of list-scoped greens (affected `selected`, a slice's `partial`, the mirror's hosted list). A red with no failed list clears only by a FULL green. On the 30 markers production held on 2026-11-10 every HEAD's verdict is unchanged (fixture + parity leg).
- **The mirror verdict.** `node scripts/ci.mjs --heavy-verdict <sha> --gh-run <id> --markers=<dir>` reads the run and its jobs through gh (two bounded GETs, `filter=latest`; no retry, never on a timer). It writes `<sha>.mirror.green` listing exactly the hosted heavy names of the commit's own plan (`scope: 'hosted'`, `partial` set, never «full»), only when the run is this repository's, the ci workflow by path, a push, headSha byte for byte, completed + success, and fast + every `heavy i/n` the workflow at that sha defines + the gate are each success (every job of a needed name; a paged list refuses). Every refusal writes nothing and exits 3. The list is read from the COMMIT (its ci.mjs must be the running one; the suite sources by `git cat-file`), so a skip-worktree edit cannot move it. The reader trusts any well-formed marker; «verified» is the writer's promise.
- **LAW A — a marker that cannot be read never opens the gate.** Round 2's reader failed open: a `null` mirror file or a string `failed` made the guard print «not blocking». Older: an empty / unparsable / `[]` / string box green, a directory or a dangling symlink, read as a FULL green. Now a green that is not a record of its kind (a JSON object; `sha` = the file's commit, `result` = its kind, `failed` a list, `endedAt` a number) covers nothing; such a red still blocks, named UNREADABLE, until a FULL green on a descendant; a marker directory that cannot be read is BLOCKED (exit 1); none or empty stays CLEAR. **LAW B:** a list-scoped green's `absent` covers nothing (a non-list one fails closed); a FULL green clears every red, as before. **The other readers see what the gate sees:** a partial run never overwrites an unreadable `<sha>.red` / `.green`; `--status` lists it UNREADABLE; «already green» is never answered beside one; pruning keeps the 30 newest commits with all their files. A refused verdict leaves no directory. KNOWN GAPS (B-479e): a hosted suite that skips itself on the runner is still listed; a FULL green from an older table never ran the suites added since.

### ci-heavy-queue — the machine's heavy lock serves its waiters oldest first, and only ci.mjs takes it
- **The race.** The heavy lock was one O_EXCL file and its waiters slept 3 s between tries, in no order. A lane's private claimer polling at 50 ms took the lock at every release; the train's 53 self-hosted suites ran 0 in 45 minutes. The wait line cut the holder's label to eight characters («lane cli»).
- **The queue.** Each waiter writes one ticket into `<lock>.q/` and may try only while its ticket is the oldest live one. A ticket holds its place only while its waiter is alive AND polling. Every poll touches it, and a ticket that is dead, recycled, untouched for 15 s or stamped more than that into the future is reaped, so a frozen head loses its turn and rejoins at the back; a waiter behind it says the lock is FREE while it waits for the one ahead. The head polls at 200 ms, the rest at 3 s. The winner's ticket goes and the lock record names it; a timeout removes the ticket. Without a usable ticket directory a waiter tries as before. Each new holder gets a wait line with pid, cmd, sha / label uncut, suites, «WITHOUT a ticket» when it went around the queue, and our place. A census pins that no script under scripts/ or data/bin except ci.mjs names the lock.
- **Not done:** a waiter on an older ci.mjs ignores tickets and can still win a release; the one-door census is a text match that a split spelling escapes.
- **Pins.** NEW fast suite test-ci-heavy-queue (35 legs, real processes; its row says 8.4 s measured under the box's thermal cap): ticket order with a 10-ms poller last, reaping (SIGKILL, recycled pid, a live older ticket waited for, a FROZEN head and its wake), the winner and a timeout, the edges, the wait line and its wiring, the one-door census, three mutant controls, nothing left behind.

#### Round 3 — the r2 acceptance of fb33c6988 (N1–N7 and the gates held on every stated leg; one major, a security finding and four minors beside them)
- **N1 — every current device is routed; a cap belongs to a display only.** r2 kept the first 200 peers of `tailscale status --json` (node-key order — nothing to do with names) and reachOf capped at 200 again: on a 250-device tailnet dev237 went DIRECT and was told «not a device on your tailnet» while ssh (the plugin's full `names.list`) still resolved it. The plugin keeps (and persists) the WHOLE table, reachOf and pacFor read all of it; the owner's «known: …» list shows 8 and says «… and N more» (en / zh / ja). Measured: the PAC is 15 KB (kernel) / 25 KB (userspace) at 250 devices and about 1 MB in userspace at 10 000 — Chromium's PAC fetch limit (1 MB, read from its source, not measured here) is that far edge.
- **N2 — the door is never a way back into the hub, and listens only while the road is on.** r2's allow() admitted every non-numeric, non-localhost name and dialled it by DNS on any port — `GET http://localhost.localdomain:<port>/x` through the door answered a hub-bound 127.0.0.1 server; boot() re-listened on the kept port whatever the plugin's state. Now a name the table does not list is resolved FIRST (egress-proxy.js takes a PROMISE verdict naming `to`, the address it vetted — dialled with no second lookup — or `error`) and refused by PURE `vetAddress` when any answer is loopback / unspecified / link-local / a metadata address (169.254.169.254, fd00:ec2::254, 100.100.100.200) / Tailscale's own 100.100.100.100 / one of this hub's own interface addresses; a device only at its tailnet address (Self's included). The door follows the road: `sync()` opens it (kept port + token) while the plugin is up with the row on and closes it — its tunnels cut, egress-proxy `close({cut})` — when either goes off; mounts-plugins-wiring's plugin broadcast calls `roadChanged()`; boot() never opens it with the plugin down; a request that finds the road off (a daemon that died without a word) is refused and closes it. The PAC sits on `/tailnet-<token>.pac` — a random 128-bit token kept with the port in data/tailnet-door.json (0600; rotated only with a new port, so a browser that outlived a restart keeps its names — 主开发's ruling), compared in constant time, never logged; any other path 404. The stated bound (kb-features, kb-api): a local process that reads Chrome's argv learns the token, and a local process can reach tailnet devices / public names through the door — reach it already has (the tun; tailscaled's own unauthenticated SOCKS5 / HTTP proxy).
- **N3 — a launch while signed out or starting carries no PAC.** launchFor ignored sign-in: Chrome kept an empty PAC (`var names = {}`) for its life and later heard «joined after this browser started». Not signed in ⇒ off:signed-out / off:starting, said once in the console; the stamp's own reason names the words — «started while Tailscale was signed out», «started while «Reach tailnet hosts from browsers» was off», «VibeSpace could not open its tailnet door when this browser started (the hub log says why)», «started before Tailscale was up» (starting / the plugin off).

- **N5 — one wait per launch + its PAC.** reachSettled shares ONE pending read among its callers and marks a read that did not answer in its bound as hung (the persisted table at once for 30 s); the plugin's reachFresh waits on a pending read only for what is left of its bound. Measured: a hung read ⇒ launch + PAC inside one bound, fresh() called once (r2: 2058 + 2055 ms, twice).
- **N6 — the certificate words are a person's, and true for each browser.** The in-page page's detail line is the code + the message's plain clauses (Node's «try running Node.js with --use-system-ca» dropped), no literal backticks anywhere in WORDS; the in-page browser «… a certificate the in-page browser does not trust (self-signed?) — it cannot open it from here: give the device a trusted certificate (tailscale cert)», Chrome (`cert-warning`) «… a certificate Chrome does not trust (self-signed?) — Chrome shows a certificate warning: accept it in the live view, or give the device a trusted certificate (tailscale cert)».

Now PluginManager.watch(fn) is ONE subscription to what a plugin is — its every broadcast (`{type: 'plugins-updated'}`: a start, a stop, a sign-in) and its rows written through the settings store (`{type: 'rows', id, keys}` from onSettingsWrite, any apply kind); tailnet-door.follow(plugins) is the wiring's one line (configure + that subscription), r3's broadcast hook is gone. The built-in Tailscale plugin has no uninstall — r3's «an uninstall» was wrong; its removal from the road is a stop. The road-off 403 names its input; the row-off words: «… the tailnet road is off: turn on «Reach tailnet hosts from browsers» in ⚙ → Plugins → Tailscale». #### Round 5 — the r4 light acceptance of eb17bf7d5 (N1–N5 held, every RED control by name, the https-hub suite green at the tip; four minors, the words, the rows)
- **m1 — a client that leaves is not a device failure.** r4 destroyed a GET's upstream when its client left; Node then emits ECONNRESET «socket hang up» on the pending ClientRequest ⇒ upFailed counted `stats.errors` and called the door's `failed()`, which remembered ECONNRESET for that host:port for 60 s — the agent's next tunnel-error words for the device said «failed (ECONNRESET)» for a request the browser had cancelled, and the engine egress's error count (egressFor) rose. Now the close handler marks the request `left` before it ends the upstream, and upFailed ignores it. The device dropping the request itself still counts (the control).
- **m2 — the refusal reaches the client.** r4's offRoad() called sync() before returning the refusal; inside the lookup's `.then` the sync job runs one microtask before decide() hands the verdict to the proxy, and close({cut}) destroys every socket synchronously — a request whose road went off while its name was looked up got an empty reply (Chrome: ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE), never the words. Now the refusal carries `answered: () => sync()`, and egress-proxy runs a refusal's `answered` once its 403 is out (the response's close; the CONNECT socket's finish or close) or at once when its client is already gone — the door closes AFTER the words, as the PAC's 404 already did. Bound: an input switched OFF (the row written, the plugin's stop — heard by the subscription) still cuts every connection at once, one whose name is mid-lookup included (no words for it; nothing dialled).
- **m3 — the row says when it takes effect, truthfully.** Its description said «A browser picks up a change at its next start» — false in kernel mode since r4 (OFF closes the door at once). Now: «Kernel mode: a change takes effect at once for running browsers. Userspace: a running browser follows at its next start. A browser started while this was off reaches tailnet hosts from its next start; the in-page browser always follows at once.» (zh / ja the same).
- **m4 — no jargon.** «the tailnet road is off» was the lane's word, not the person's. The row-off sentence is now «<host> is a Tailscale name — reaching Tailscale devices from browsers is off: turn on «Reach tailnet hosts from browsers» in ⚙ → Plugins → Tailscale» (zh «从浏览器访问 Tailscale 设备已关闭…打开「从浏览器访问 tailnet 里的机器」», ja «ブラウザーから Tailscale のデバイスへの接続がオフです…「ブラウザーから tailnet のマシンに接続」をオン…» — the switch's exact label). The door's road-off 403 («… this door carries nothing until it is on», English only) is now LAW 2's own sentence for the input that is off, in the owner's language; the PAC's 404 says «reaching Tailscale devices from browsers is off — this PAC is served again once it is back on».

### phone-resume-keeps-layout (userW 2026-11-05 11:30Z, after his pod's rebuild: eleven desktops lost every window position, three never-visited desktops previewed empty; one commit on a5dedfed1)
- **The measured shape** (the brief's reading of his layout-history + layouts.json): the hub restarted, his PHONE page reconnected first and accepted «Resume all»; at 11:30:40Z it wrote eleven desktops' records stamped `viewport: phone` whose session rows had window ids minted that minute and no `gridBounds`, the evidence naming the old rows `closed` and the new ones `moved`. Reproduced on a5dedfed1 three ways: the fast door (V → `[v-f, win-n1 (no box)]`), the loop's §14, and real Chrome (new window ids, `gridBounds` null on every resumed row — the user's shape).
- **The writer**: `_offerResumeAll` → `resumeSession` closed the read-only window of a conversation on the desktop on show (evidence 'closed') and, for a desktop not visited (scanStoppedInDesktopStates), moved a new window there with `replaces` ('replaced'); both new ids were windows the record did not hold, and PURE captureForViewport gives a phone-born window no box. The belts saw a close / a move; layerGate judges only held ids.
- **LAW 1 — A RESUME RE-OPENS ITS ROW** (session-lifecycle `resumeSession`, desktop-manager `heldRowOf` / `reopenRow` / `reopenedRow`): the first window `resumeSession` closes for the conversation is its row (the restore re-keyed it to the row's id) — `reopenRow(id)` makes purgeClosedWindow keep the row in every held record (no evidence, nothing dirty) and createSession builds the new window under that id (`syncId`); with none built, `heldRowOf({backend, backendSessionId, hostId, winId})` finds the row (the named one first, then the desktop on show's; a live session's window excluded; a placeholder tile of the row closed as a re-open). The row's box / z / maximize ride `winBounds` (createSession applies `zIndex`; `replaces` only for another id); `reopenedRow` queues the row's tab group (queueRecordChains). A resume with no place named (a card, a sidebar row) of a row on another desktop reveals it there (`revealHeld`); the resume-all passes `stay` and switches nothing. `resumeSession` returns `{row, desk, created}` when it re-opened a row. PURE: mergeDesktopRecord's `replaced` carries the replaced row's arrangement (`carryPlace`) and its seat in its group (`renameMember` over every chain of the record — `_updateCachedDesktop` queues that group for the newcomer); `duplicatesOf` hands a boxless survivor the copy's arrangement (`carry` → desktop-manager `_placeSurvivor`); `captureForViewport` writes a held row in its own key order (a phone's capture of a desktop it did not change is byte-identical).
- **LAW 2 — THE PREVIEW DRAWS EVERY ROW** (desktop-manager `_renderSwitcher`): a not-built row with no `gridBounds` (and not minimized) is a `.desktop-preview-win-unplaced` dashed box in a cascade (PURE `placeholderBoxes`, ≤ 6) + `.desktop-preview-unplaced` (the count; title «N windows · not placed — opening this desktop lays them out»). The digest already covered the held rows' boxes.
- **LAW 3 — NOTHING SILENT**: PURE `shrinkVerdict` → `unplaced` (refused at any count, also in `unexplained`): a kept row whose box is gone; a row dropped 'replaced' / 'dup' whose `by` is a boxless row of the write; a boxed row dropped 'closed' beside a NEW boxless row of its own conversation (the 11:30:40 shape). ws-handler adds `unplaced` to the refusal frame (spread — the §6 pin moved) and names the rows in the journal; onSyncRefused says it once in its own words (`_sayRefusal(…, 'unplaced', …)`); the reconciled record carries the kept boxes. `_offerResumeAll` asks, `_resumeAll` resumes and says «Resumed K conversations where they were» once. A person's close, a move, a window born on the phone stay accepted (controls).

### channel-upload-retry — a failed bytes upload is retried before any refusal is said (userW inc-mw35tppf-jrvo, 2026-11-05: «使用 channel 发文件会 Slack 报 504»)
- **What happened.** Three PDFs in one agent reply to Slack (review mode, approved by the owner): file 1 landed with the text; files.slack.com answered file 2's bytes POST HTTP 504 (~37 s, 109 KB — inside the 60 s timeout); `sendFiles`' shipped «the first refusal STOPS the chain (never retried)» ⇒ file 2 not landed, file 3 `not-sent`, the proposal `sent` «partly sent — …», and no resend door (a new draft, a new review). Lark's pieces chain had the same ladder.
- **The law.** The bytes step has no vendor-visible effect until the completing call ⇒ its TRANSPORT failure (a 5xx from the upload host, a network error, the 60 s timeout) is retried INSIDE the adapter: 3 attempts in all, 1 s then 3 s ±20 %, each attempt a whole request through the gate — Slack `uploadFile`: a FRESH `files.getUploadURLExternal`, then `uploadBytes` (bucket `take` + pace + meter, its own 60 s window); Lark `upload`: `callForm` again (the multipart form rebuilt), pace + meter, `heldRefusal()` after each wait (no request inside the account's send hold). Never retried: a 429 (ONE request, the hold armed — ③ untouched), any other 4xx (`forbidden` / `too-large` / `vendor-error`), the URL ask and every Web API call, the COMPLETING call (`lost: true`, `retryable: false`). The first FINAL refusal still stops the chain; `parts` say per file.
- **Slack's docs on the upload URL** (docs.slack.dev, read 2026-11-05). files.getUploadURLExternal: «This method gets a URL that can be used for uploading a file to share within channels.» · «Slack will return HTTP 200 if the upload is successful; a non-200 response indicates a failure.» · «If files.completeUploadExternal is not called, the upload will be aborted and clients will receive an error.» The working-with-files guide says the same («The response will contain a URL to which you can then post the contents of your file»). Neither page says whether one URL takes a second POST — single-use is not documented, nor is re-use ⇒ the FRESH URL per attempt is pinned as the safe choice (R⑧ + the old-URL control); the abandoned file id is never completed, so Slack aborts it.
- **What callSlack does today on a transport failure** (unchanged): a typed `transport` ChannelError, `retryable: true`, `detail.lost` only for `chat.postMessage`, the Bearer scrubbed by value; `api()` arms a 429's hold / stamps a revocation and re-throws — no retry anywhere in the adapter; the engine's ladder decides.
- **Said.** A part landed after a retry carries `retried: n` (channel-policy `sendParts` keeps it, an integer ≤ 9) and the hub console says «[slack] <account>: slack files.upload: HTTP 504 — retried, landed on attempt 2» (Lark: «[channels] lark <account>: lark upload file: HTTP 504 (504) — retried, landed on attempt 2»); `partsWords` says «"a.pdf" (retried, landed on attempt 2)», so the agent's `reason`, the receipt's `parts:` line and the card's outcome line (a partly-sent card prints the reason — outcomeOf is null for `sent`) carry it. A part failed every attempt: «slack files.upload: HTTP 504 (after 3 attempts)» in its `why`; the error keeps `retryable: true` + `detail.attempts`. No new human-visible i18n string (the words ride `why` / the reason, English like the rest of partsWords).

### desktop-blink-colour — the strip's waiting blink in the window's OWN colour (userW inc-mw2oamb4-vain on 2.369.378; the owner's ruling «闪烁和颜色互不干扰»)
- **The complaint** (userW): the desktop strip's preview blink is always yellow, so a window that turned red blinks yellow and the person cannot see it is red. The owner confirmed the meaning with userW: «闪烁和颜色互不干扰» — the BLINK (cadence, pattern, which elements blink) stays exactly as it is; the COLOUR is the window's own state colour.
- **The cause — one selector.** The warmth block's square rule stepped aside for both short signals: `.desktop-preview-win[data-warmth-tier]:not(.desktop-preview-win-waiting):not(.desktop-preview-find-flash)` (cache-warmth-band's «the blink is untouched»), so a waiting square fell back to `.desktop-preview-win-waiting`'s `var(--yellow)`. The blink is an opacity pulse of the whole square (blink-fade 0.7 s ease-in-out infinite reverse) — the square's fill IS the blink's colour.
- **The fix (public/style.css only, no JS).** The tier rule steps aside for the find flash alone: `.desktop-preview-win[data-warmth-tier]:not(.desktop-preview-find-flash) { background: var(--warmth-c); }` (0,3,0 over the waiting rule's 0,1,0). The colour source is the one the square already had — the `data-warmth-tier` attribute warmth-chrome.js paintPreviews writes, through `--warmth-c` — never a second table. The waiting rule keeps the cadence and its yellow, which now means «no state colour» (warmth off, an unknown conversation, a held window); the find flash (cyan, 0.3 s) keeps its own. NOT the var road (`background: var(--warmth-c, var(--yellow))` on the waiting rule): `--warmth-c` inherits from the desktop's ring (`.desktop-preview[data-warmth-tier]`), so a no-state square on a critical desktop would blink red — the fast leg's planted control shows it.

### layout-dup-refusal-storm — FIX (userW inc-mw1ogdno-5jny, 2.369.374 on his pod): a 2 Hz layout-sync refusal ping-pong with a warn toast per round — a duplicate explained wherever it is shown, the refused record never re-sent, the server never answering a storm, one toast per cause, and the writer of the triple found
- **The measured shape** (read-only forensics on his pod, nothing of his in the tree): the ws ring held 222 `layout-sync` sends and 222 `layout-sync-refused` answers in 130 s (median gap 515 ms); the journal repeated «REFUSED a record of desktop "V…": it drops 1 window(s) … — 5 → 4; 1 LIVE (the sender could not build them)». layouts.json listed ONE live conversation (server session S) under THREE desktops' records, three window ids; the page showed it on X.
- **The loop**: replaying V, desktop-manager `_replayMissing` found S live under X's window and settled V's copy as a duplicate (attempt at 0) ⇒ `_unbuilt` dropped it with evidence 'unbuilt' ⇒ the server's `shrinkVerdict` explained a duplicate only inside ONE record (`nextSessions`) ⇒ «1 LIVE» refused ⇒ `onSyncRefused` reconciled, replayed (opened 0), `rearmSave()` ⇒ 500 ms later the same capture, the same drop — a refusal + a toast + a journal line + a telemetry count per round.
- **The writer of the triple** (a door census over the anonymized shape, test-layout-dup-storm-loop §5, peak = the most distinct window ids of S any write left on disk): session-lifecycle `attachSession`'s shortcut `_focusExistingSession` searches only the windows this page BUILT (`this.sessions`); a desktop's windows are built at its first visit, so a person's open of a conversation whose window waits on a desktop not visited since the page loaded created a NEW window on the desktop on show. 86add763e: 2 entries, then 3 on a second page booted on a third desktop — the triple; the switch's replay, a move and an open of a built window keep 1.
- **A** (PURE desktop-record.js `shownBy` in `shrinkVerdict({…, elsewhere})`): `{id, why:'dup', by}` is explained when `by` shows the same session in the record written or in ANY other desktop's stored record (ws-handler hands `otherRecords(layoutData, desktopId)`); a `by` that shows nothing ⇒ refused at any count, named in `dup` (before: ANY why but 'unbuilt' explained a drop — a 'dup' word alone would have). The page (`_unbuilt`) says 'dup' with `by = _showerOf(S)` — a built window of S the wire lists for its desktop (the server holds it); none yet ⇒ the copy waits.
- **B**: `onSyncRefused` keeps a shrink refusal's `unexplained` (`_kept`): carried as the server's rows, never dropped again until the person's close or a reload; THE BREAKER — `_sentJson` per desk ({state, base}); the rearm only when `recordFor(d)` differs from the refused text; `holdsBack` before the autosave's dirty sends, the desktop on show's send and a switch's broadcast; ≥ 2 refusals of one `refusalKey` ⇒ «This page and the server disagree about desktop “…” — reload to take the server's record» ONCE (a Reload now action); an ack of the desk clears it.
- **C** (ws-handler, PURE `refusalKey` / `refusalStorm` / `stormEnd` / `stormSweep`): before each of the three refusal branches, `layoutStormed(ws, desktopId, key)` — the same key from the same client within 10 s of its last ⇒ `break` (no frame, no journal line, no telemetry, no ring note); the storm ends on a changed key, an accepted write or 10 s of quiet (an unref'd sweep) ⇒ ONE «[layout-sync] STORM: client #N … refused for the same reason <n> more time(s) in <s> s — not answered» + telemetry `layout-sync-storm` <n>; a client that never stops gets one answer a minute (`STORM_MAX_MS`). An older bundle's storm therefore stops after its first unanswered repeat (no refusal ⇒ no rearm).
- **D** (`_sayRefusal`): per desk + reason per 30 s, the windows named (namesOf: the title without its cwd tail), «(refused N times)» on the next; a refused 'dup' cleanup is the page's own initiative — silent.

No server-side normalization: only a page knows which window the person sees; the server's by-check makes two pages racing to dedup converge (the second's `by` is gone ⇒ refused ⇒ kept).

  - **(F, major) WHO IS LOOKING IS A FACT ABOUT THE PAGE, NOT A STATE OF ITS SOCKET.** r2 counted «another page shows S» as another OPEN socket in `session.clients`. A page whose socket was down at that moment (a backgrounded phone, a laptop lid, every page during a hub restart) was not counted, another page's dedup was ACCEPTED, and the first page's reconnect re-read closed the window it was showing (probe 1: B closed [win-v-s], 0 toasts; base: both kept). The hub's half is the trace: no time limit, the newest 50 dedups per desktop, an entry gone when a write lists its window again; on disk, so a hub restart (a new process: no memory of any page) reads it back. Why no number: a timer would guess how long a laptop sleeps or a phone stays in the background; the trace only has to name the copies the hub let go. A page's reload is the same shape (its previous socket showed S), and a refused copy is kept for the page's life — so any grace stopped the cleanup after every reload. Dropped; the trace alone keeps both windows on both roads (F1–F4).

Now the page's group WAITS for the verdict: a dedup is ASKED (`_ask` → `_dupAsked`: desk → id → the `sentAt` of the write that left it out — `noteSent(d, st, sentAt)` at its three call sites); `recordFor` reads every row's chain without the asked ids in the record it SENDS (`chainsWithout` — mergeDesktopRecord's `add`, the one writer) while the members' captures keep the waiting chain; the ack of that write (or a later one) re-forms the group (`_settleAsked` → `dropUnbuiltMembers`); a refusal forgets the ask, so the record rebuilt from the server's rows and the untouched captures IS the server's. ### cli-shell-truth — B-fb02: the person's LOGIN SHELL is the truth for where an agent CLI is (the owner's two rulings: NO registry, NO pins, NO managed prefix); a found-nothing create is REFUSED by name with a dialog before anything spawns; Manage agents shows the observed census; the shell's PATH rides the spawn
- **The incident** (the owner, 2026-11-03 10:31 PT): codex under nvm's node v24.12.0, the hub's systemd PATH with v24.22.1/bin only. The boot `which` found nothing, and every spawn logged «… found nothing — spawning it as before» and died ~30 s later in silence. `command -v codex` in the owner's zsh found it.
- **The rung** (src/server/cli-cmd.js `askShell`): `<shell> -l -i -c '<line>'`, stdin /dev/null, TERM=dumb, `serviceEnv` + USER / LOGNAME + SHELL + VIBESPACE_SHELL_PROBE=1 (never a VIBESPACE_* name, a token or npm_*). It runs in its own session (`detached`: an rc's `kill 0` cannot reach the hub's group), bounded 10 s (the pid, then the probe's own session). The answer sits between `__VS_CV_BEGIN__` / `__VS_CV_END__` / `__VS_PATH_END__`, the LAST pair wins, and the PATH comes from `printenv PATH`. Answers: path / alias / none / unanswered (timeout · exit:<n> · spawn:<err> · no-shell). The ONE `setTimeout` in cli-cmd.js is the ask's bound: it ends an ask, never starts one (test-cli-env's «nothing on a timer» pin restated so).
- **The ladder, spelled once** (PURE src/login-shell.js): SHELL › the account record (os.userInfo(); a device's dscl / getent passwd) › zsh / bash on PATH › /bin/sh. dial.js's device shell terminal reads the same `S0_SH` (moved byte for byte), and test-cli-env runs that sh against `pickLoginShell` on the same inputs.
- **Provenance**: `hub-path` (boot's which + walk: provisional, never a shell at boot — §19) · `shell` (asked lazily ONCE per CLI at the first spawn / first status read; REPLACES a working provisional path; cached = one access; gone / Re-check ⇒ re-asked; missing ⇒ asked again at each create) · `boot` (a configured absolute path). `unanswered` keeps the provisional path and is NAMED (census + one journal line); refused only when the hub's walk has nothing either.
- **Fail closed** (src/ws-create.js): the ONE `forSpawn` moved ahead of the local ladder, so a refused resume never runs the pre-resume writer sweep. The ACP `adapter.installed === false` branch FOLDED in. It could never fire: cli-env leaves an unresolved command as its bare name, so `installed` was always true.     |---|---|---|

Measured: stdout carries only the CLI's line, stderr only its own, on pipes and on a pty; the alias road keeps the shim's pid. ### hotfix-attach-engine-args — HOTFIX on 2.369.374: the attach road DROPS an engine's driver-only switch and SAYS it; every launch the road does not start is journaled by name
- **The incident** (主开发, 2026-11-03 13:12 PT, the owner's hub on 2.369.373, `browser.defaultEngine` = the custom kernel's plugin): `vibespace-browser new` made the profile; `use` answered «the attach argv failed its census (missing -; forbidden --disable-sync) [bad_argv]»; the journal said only «its display session … stopped — its launch was refused». The plugin's launcher passes `--disable-sync` (a driver-road switch); attachStart hands the engine's launch arguments as `extra` into `AT.attachArgv`, whose census (ATTACH_FORBIDDEN) refused the WHOLE launch — no new profile on the kernel could attach.
- **The law**: an engine's launch arguments are additive switches the hub judges (L1b's switch-only rule, LAUNCHER_SWITCHES); one the attach road forbids is the hub's to DROP and SAY, never a reason to refuse the engine — the plugin's author cannot know this road's rules, and the hub owns the attach argv (q-026 §2.1).
- **PURE** (src/browser-attach.js): `stripForbidden(extra)` → `{kept, dropped}` (the census's own rule, `isForbiddenSwitch`, the bare switch or its `=value` form); `attachArgv` builds with `kept` and answers `dropped`; a forbidden switch the HUB puts in the argv (the table, its quiet switches, its mark) is still the census's red, and a refusal answers `offending` (the forbidden items; every `--user-data-dir` when there is not exactly one — its words now say «--user-data-dir ×2»). `droppedWords({engine, dropped})` = the journal sentence; `argvItemsText(items)` = a journal-safe item list (anything but plain printable ASCII JSON-quoted, ≤ 8).
- **The keeper** (attachStart): `av.dropped` ⇒ ONE `log.warn` «[browser] <profile>: engine <id>'s launch switch --disable-sync dropped on the attach road (driver-only; the attach road needs Chrome's sign-in entry)» + `rec.engineDropped = {engine, switches}` (each launch writes a new record ⇒ a launch that dropped nothing carries none). Every launch the road does not start is journaled BY NAME — `sayNotStarted(code, msg, items)`: «[browser] <profile> "<label>": NOT started on the attach road [<code>] (<items>) — <words>» — BEFORE its display session is stopped: `refused` for the four refusals that stop it (launcher switch, padded, switch-only, bad_argv), the spawn failure and the unidentifiable pid say first too, the lock / socket-dir refusals through `failed` itself (`said` keeps it one line).
- **The panel** (the profile's note): the housekeeping row carries `engineDropped` (src/server/browser-trace.js, from `keeper.browserOf`); src/lib/browser-panel-model.js `stateLines` adds `engine-dropped` (info tone, LAST — the state's own sentence keeps the row's second line; the fold's State and the cell's title read it): «Left out --disable-sync, which its engine asked for: it would stop this browser signing in to Google» (+ zh / ja rows).

The pool suites' fixtures carry `_lastRequestAt` as the real record does (test-fable-cap-pool-storm: 21 fixtures; test-pool-auto: the world's `mk` + 3 lines). ③ `desktop.cacheWarmth` is HELD: a new settings-view row field `held: '<why>'` — the row exists (key, default, settings.md line, `settings.get`) but `settingsViewModel` never draws it (no search, no modified row); test-architecture §44 names every held row with its why; test-settings-view's V1 law («every row reachable by searching its key») carves out exactly the held rows and pins that none is reachable. test-stdout-registry's engine stub carries `noteModelRequest` (its dep census caught it). ④ test-cache-bounds §30 (the usage fold's memory cap) went red once in three whole-tier runs and green alone ×2 + in the two other runs — a flake outside this lane.

No new stamp: every move (per-session, pin, cross-provider, removal, gather, a manual default and its sweep) already writes that ledger.
- **The hold reads it**: the three `warmCache(` sites spread `cacheFactsOf(…)`; `warmCache({lastRequestAt, cacheTtlSec, cacheLostAt, nowMs})` is warm iff the TTL is known, no move at/after the last request, and ago < ttl (`lost: true` when a move decided it).
- **The session list** (routes/sessions `warmthDiff`): `/api/sessions` (the 5 s poll — the cached answer and a fresh sweep alike) carries `{warmth: {<webuiId>: {lastRequestAt, cacheTtlSec, cacheLostAt}}, serverNow}` ONLY while `desktop.cacheWarmth` is on (off = not computed); an unknown TTL is left out. The poll's cadence and document.hidden rule unchanged; no new endpoint, no timer.
- **The client's tiers** (PURE CJS `src/cache-warmth.js` — src/, not src/lib: test-architecture §78 counts a src/lib file no client module imports as dead until r1b's band imports it): `tierOf({agoMs, ttlMs})` in sixtieths (fresh < 20 · mid < 40 · late < 50 · critical < 60 · expired; unknown), `warmthOf(fact, {serverNow, receivedAt, now})` by the hub's clock (the For-you deadline cards' rule), `warmthTitle` (en / zh / ja — «about N min»: the stamp is the request's response, at most one response late).
- **The switch** `desktop.cacheWarmth` (Window group, default OFF — the owner's opt-in; docs/settings.md regenerated). **The tokens**: `--warmth-fresh / -mid / -late / -critical / -expired` derived in style.css's `:root, [data-theme]` block from `--ok-text / --accent / --warn-text / --bad-text / --border`; the theme editor's «Cache warmth» rows start as those derivations, so a theme saved from a built-in base keeps deriving. No high-contrast theme exists in the tree (the built-ins: dark, light, dracula, nord, solarized, monokai).
