### cache-warmth-band — r1b: the prompt-cache warmth DRAWN on every surface the owner approved (q-059 rounds 1–4 + the ruling «按照这个实现吧»; on cache-warmth-tiles r5)
- **The data road.** `Sidebar._poll` (the page's only 5 s session poll) takes `{map: data.warmth, serverNow, receivedAt: Date.now()}` from the SAME parsed answer inside its fetch try and, after the render try, calls `noteWarmthAnswer(app, sessions ? warmthAnswer : undefined)` once in its own try — `undefined` (the fetch failed) re-derives from the last good ON answer at the current time; `null` (a good answer without warmth: the switch off, an older hub) clears every mark once and forgets the stored answer, so a later failed poll never re-derives from it. Warmth stays OUT of `LIVE_SESSION_FACTS`, the sidebar digest, `syncSessionIdentity` and `setTitleMeta`.
- **ONE computation** (NEW src/lib/warmth-chrome.js): the only `warmthOf` call on the page, over the answer's map into `app._warmth.byId`; every surface is painted from that map and every builder that rebuilds one re-applies from it (tab-group makeTab; taskbar _rebuildTaskbarItems / _buildGroupItem / showTabGroupList / fitTaskbarStrip / showWindowList; desktop-manager _renderSwitcher's full path AND _renderCompactSwitcher — the compact early return is pinned byte for byte; sidebar-render _buildSessionCard; mobile-nav _buildWindowItem). Each mark = a `data-warmth-tier` attribute + an inline `--warmth-frac` (3 decimals), key-guarded on the element; style.css maps tier → `--warmth-c` ONCE; no colour from JS. No timer, rAF, transition, observer or settings listener — a band STEPS once per tick; off = one early return.
- **Window ↔ conversation.** A built window: user-todos-panel keysForWin's ladder (`webuiIdOfWin`). A HELD window (another desktop's record, not built): the layout restore's ladder — (1) its conversation id through the page's LIVE active-sessions list (`sidebar._webuiSessions`: `id` = the webui id), (2) the record's `serverSessionId`, (3) its attach openSpec's `serverId` (desktop-record `sessionOf`); the rung kept in `app._warmth.held`. Deviation from the brief: rung (1) was to resolve through the poll answer's own `sessions` — but `/api/sessions` rows are the DISCOVERED sessions and carry no webui id (routes/sessions `_runSessionsSweep`; the webui id is the active-sessions broadcast's `id`, server.js activeSessionsPayload), so it resolves through the live list instead.
- **The surfaces** (the choices the drawing left open): the title bar's band = `::before` on `.window-titlebar` (`::after` is the waiting blink, which paints over it), `bottom: -1px` over the bar's border, `:not(.seamless)`, `:not(:has(> .tab-bar-tabs))` ⇒ a tab-group frame draws none with no JS; hover words on the BAR (the band is a pointer-events-none pseudo-element), native `title`, every known tier (expired said, never drawn). A TAB = a child node `span.tab-warmth` prepended (both pseudo-elements are taken: the active cover / blink / pane cover, the split pane underline), length × the TAB's width; its words on `.tab-label` — `_markStrip` owns `tab.title`, so a tab's band row is silent on hover. Tiles, chooser rows, the folded button: `svg.warmth-ring` (constant markup; `stroke-dasharray: calc(var(--warmth-frac) * 100) 100` over `pathLength=100` — Chrome honours it, the shots show partial arcs); a group tile = `worstOf` its tabs; expired = the full ring in `--warmth-expired`. Preview squares take the tier colour (`:not(.desktop-preview-win-waiting):not(.desktop-preview-find-flash)` keeps the blink and the find flash); a preview's ring = an OUTLINE at offset −3.5 px (inside its border: outside, neighbours 3 px apart would merge), none while its worst is fresh; nothing enters the switcher digest or the taskbar structKey. «+N»: `fitTaskbarStrip` keeps its line, stores the hidden ids, clears the chip's key and calls `paintOverflowChip` (the dot + words naming the dot's tier). The summary chip beside For-you: customize-mode `slotBeside` (the vault lock chip's pattern; re-seated by `placeWarmthChip` after every arrangement), a stable 214 px min width; its press = `showWindowList(app, chip, { all: true })` — the window list's second mode, its rows the list's own jump (`goOtherDesk`; taskbar.js still has 5 `revealWindow(` calls). The window list: a band + «N min left» per row and ONE «By time left» flag (pressed by default, the POC's one `sortBy`, shared with the summary list); off ⇒ byte for byte as before (no head, band or `data-win-id`). Phone: `.sess-warmth` + `.sess-warmth-left` on session cards (phone classes only) and on switcher rows (one per tab). Every SUMMARISING expired mark (squares, preview / folded rings, dots) is `--text-dim`, as drawn — `--warmth-expired` (= `--border`) would vanish at the squares' 0.5 opacity.
- **PURE additions** (src/cache-warmth.js): `worstOf` (the worst LIVE tier, a tie → the smaller frac, expired only when nothing is live — the POC ranked expired worst; the approved rule does not), `warmthCounts`, `byTimeLeft`. Not built (the brief's overrides): the POC's «减淡» tweak, the desktop list's per-row dots, the «+N» list rows, a phone summary, desktop sidebar cards.
- **Rebased on cache-warmth-tiles r3** (cb94e2701: `lost` / `inFlight` / `turnStartedAt` replace `cacheLostAt` / `inTurn`): the client reads only warmthOf's result, so nothing in warmth-chrome.js changed; the suites' rewrite and fixtures moved to `lost`, the moved hover to r3's sentence. A request in flight draws a FULL fresh band; a turn paused on the owner ages like idle. Round 2 rebased onto r5 (78d174e1f — r4 / r5 moved only the facts' producers, the list's fields are r3's): no conflict in a file of this lane's code; one in docs/kb-file-structure.md (r4 / r5 append to cache-warmth.js's essay, where this lane's warmth-chrome.js essay had moved — theirs kept, the warmth-chrome.js section after them).
- **Measured** (the chrome suite's heaviest state — 14 conversations, 8 desktops, a 4-tab group, the compact form): one pass 0.5–0.7 ms per tick; ×150 conversations ≈ 7–8 ms per 5 s tick (an EXTRAPOLATION, linear in the conversations).
- **Round 2 (the acceptance of ca2670be0: one MAJOR, one minor, three to measure, one docs):** H1 THE WORDS STAY WHOLE — the ⧉ list's label had no shrink rule, so a «name — /path» title pushed «N min left» / «Expired» past the row's 400-px edge on every row (the summary list had the rule); paintListRow now marks the label `wl-name` and `.overlap-switcher-item > .wl-name` shrinks it with an ellipsis on every list row (the ⧉ list, its «Other desktops» rows, the summary list), `.wl-left` never wraps or shrinks, and an OFF tick takes the mark back off the ⧉ list. H2 an «Other desktops» row of a tab group painted its host alone: `tileIds(app, id)` = a built chain, else a HELD record's (heldOf keeps each member of a host entry's `tabChain.tabs` — read as layout.js `_recordChainOf` reads it, a guest's entry names none — in `app._warmth.heldChains`), else the window alone; the row, the tile and the square take the worst over it (a held group's squares had the same gap). H3 MEASURED REAL: at the 90-px floor the inline ring (12 px + the 6-px gap) cut «ops bot 3» to «ops b»; the ring now rides the tile's icon (`.taskbar-icon` / `.taskbar-icon-stack`, absolute at the bottom-right on `--bg-taskbar`), so a floor tile shows the same characters on and off (951 / 1024 / 1100: 3 / 4 / 5 floor tiles, every one equal); a chooser row keeps it inline. H4 MEASURED REAL on the r1 budget: at the switcher's boundary with warmth on (1066 px, 4 desktops) the strip kept 3 whole tiles behind «+2 · 2 critical» (104 px against the 48 budgeted); taskbar-fit.js now holds `OVERFLOW_CHIP_PX` (48) and `OVERFLOW_CHIP_WARM_PX` = 137 — the longest warm form measured in Chrome (ja «+88 · 88 期限切れ» 127 px; en «… expired» 121, «… critical» 117; zh 115 / 103) + the plain room's own margin over «+88» (10) — and `_switcherFormFor` budgets the warm one while warmth is drawn: a constant, never the chip's width. Its price: with warmth on the previews fold at a wider viewport than r1 judged (r1 kept them full by under-counting the chip) — the chrome suite's ⑧b prints the boundary, ⑤ the form at 1100 px. H5 the warmth-chrome.js essay moved out of cache-warmth.js's.
- **Round 3 (the acceptance of 6550a3a51: one MAJOR, measured on the real bundle):** J1 THE CHIP AND THE STRIP REFIT EACH OTHER — the warm «+N» chip's words get SHORTER when one more tile is hidden (an expired-only tail «+N · k expired»; a live tile hidden too ⇒ worstOf ranks it above expired ⇒ «+N»), and the strip is `flex: 1` beside the chip, so the chip's width changed the strip's, its ResizeObserver refit, the words flipped back: a 60 Hz rewrite loop at 16 of 46 widths with warmth on (0 off). The law: the fit reads a constant, never the chip's content — while warmth is drawn the chip sits in a CONSTANT box (`.taskbar-overflow.warmth-box { width: 128px }` = taskbar-fit.js `OVERFLOW_CHIP_WARM_BOX_PX`, the longest warm form, the words ellipsised inside if ever longer; paintOverflowChip toggles it with the drawing); the switcher's room `OVERFLOW_CHIP_WARM_PX` stays 137 = the box + the bar's gap + the floor's three tile gaps (a 137-px box would leave the ON boundary 3 whole tiles). The words still name the hidden set; the price: with warmth on, a shown chip is 128 px whatever it says.
- Gates: test-cache-warmth (fast; ⑤ flipped — the row DRAWN, `held` still hides as the control; ⑧ worstOf / warmthCounts / byTimeLeft over the real warmthOf; ⑨ the poll's one call from the same answer, one `warmthOf` site, no timer / rAF / listener / `_notify` / `setTitleMeta` / colour write / innerHTML, every builder's re-apply, the CSS block's guards and no literal colour with a PLANTED control; ③ the 8 new keys in zh + ja; RED on da86012d5: 19 by name) + NEW test-cache-warmth-chrome (heavy: the real road, a CDP rewrite of the session list's EXISTING entries for the tier matrix, the blink, the tab group + a strip rebuild with no tick, the desktops + a reload, «+N» at four viewports, the summary chip + its list, the window list, the phone, off/on live with ZERO warmth mutations and a failed poll, the pass time + a stack census of timers with a planted control, the settings row + the theme editor, RED controls; shots dark + light; round 2: ⑥ the floor's characters on / off + the r1 DOM re-planted, ⑧ the path-title rows' words + the shrink rule undone, the group rows built and held + their squares, ⑧b the switcher's boundary on / off + the forms' widths + a chip planted wider; test-cache-warmth ⑨ pins each with a planted r1 line; round 3: ⑥b the strip's room swept 1040 → 1220 px on and off — no change of the chip's words or box in 1 s at any width — + the RED with the constant box taken away, ⑧b the boundary's chip = the box; ⑨ pins the box rule with its control). settings-schema: `desktop.cacheWarmth`'s `held` removed (§44 prints none; settings-view V1 passes).

### phone-dock-restore — A: the phone's «waiting for you» strip took a third of the screen (the owner 2026-11-02 ~23:20 PT on the iPhone, 2.369.373: «你那个等你操作的那个橙色的菜单，在画面最下方的 iPhone UI 上占据的显示面积过大»; lane on 74b98357e)
- **Reproduced first** on 74b98357e at 390×844 touch (a scratch hub + stub CLI, three item shapes delivered through the page's own ws handlers, 3 waiting, dark + light — /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/phone-dock-restore/logs/shots/before-*.png): a hub permission ask (Allow once / Always on this machine / Deny) **254 px = 30 %** of the 844, a 3-option question **192 px = 23 %**, a vault run card (command, «Sends to», Allow once / Allow for 1 hour / Deny, the hour's line) **338 px = 40 %** — half of what stood between the top bar and the composer.
- **Fix:** on the phone classes (html[data-vc] compact / regular — src/viewport-class.js) the strip is ONE row until tapped: the amber head «waiting for you · N» (the count alone — `.cad-num`; the kinds stay in its title), the newest item's question (the row's own `.ut-text`, one line, an ellipsis), «View» (`.cad-look`) and the door to all of them («All» — `.cad-all`'s `data-short` drawn by CSS; its name and title keep «N more · View all»). A tap on the head, the question or «View» opens THAT item in place (chat-needs-card.js `_dockFold` → `cad-open`: the card exactly as .373 drew it, at most 45 % of the screen and scrolling inside, its head held at the top with a ▾); the head folds it; a newer item drawn folds it (`_dockStrip`, each pass); nothing waiting folds it. The open arms the strip (foryouRows.arm — what the open moved under the finger answers nothing for ARM_MS). **After: 53 px = 6 %** folded in all three shapes; open = 210–338 px (≤ 380); the composer on screen throughout; a newer item keeps the composer's focus. The desktop (≥ 1024) is untouched — every new rule is under html[data-vc]; the head is a door (role=button, aria-expanded) on the phone only.
- **Choice — the folded row offers «View», never an answer:** the brief allowed «the item's first answer button»; every first answer a strip holds is an Allow / Approve whose command, facts or clock the earlier laws put ABOVE it (verify-r4 F4 — the whole command above Allow; r15 / r16 — a press point shows what it decides on, every warning row; the deadline law), and a question's options are a choice of several. So no decision is ever pressed on the one-line row; the open card is one tap away. Flagged to 主开发 in the interim line; **ruled (2026-11-03): KEEP «View» only** — what you approve is what runs.
- Gates: test-chat-needs-card-chrome ㉓ (three shapes folded ≤ 56 px → «View» opens the item ≤ 45 % → the head folds it; a newer item while open; the desktop never folds; RED CONTROL: the block's 17 rules cut out of the page's sheet ⇒ «FOLDED on the phone» red), its phone legs ⑰ / ⑲ open the strip first (`openStrip`); test-user-todos-layout's two `_dockPass` belts stub `_dockStrip`.
- **Round 2 (the acceptance of 6aed457b7 — three confirmed on the real build):** (P1, major) «View» opened the card in place and the card's last row landed where «View» was — 150 ms after the tap the first option chip of a 3-option question, ✕ on a plain one — and a second tap sent the reply / the dismiss: only the Allow-type buttons were armed (armExitButtons). **Fix:** the open stamps the dock (`_openedAt`, the accordion's own rule in `_create`) and the strip's capture listener refuses EVERY button of the opened item for ARM_MS (the chips, ✓, ✕, Deny, Reply, ⤢ and the Allows) with the accordion's words. (P2, major) the folded rule hid `.ut-deadline` — the base strip said «按服务器时间还剩 40 秒». **Fix:** `.cad-clock` after the words (`_dockStrip`, after the row is drawn: the item's line's own stamps + `data-deadline-short`), THE page ticker writes deadlineOf's new `short` words («41 sec left» / «剩 41 秒»; past the end «time is up», «timed out» for a late card) with the line's accent; none for an item with no line. (P3, minor) the folded head's `.cad-num` had no attention fill — chat.css's fill rule takes `:is(.cad-count, .cad-num)`. Gates: ㉓ r2 (three shapes: «View», a tap on the same point at ~150 / ~450 ms ⇒ no POST, the item open; at ~820 ms it answers — RED CONTROL: the open's stamp taken back ⇒ the 150 ms tap POSTs; the folded clock counting, past its end, absent without a line — RED: its 4 rules cut; the fill under window-announce — RED: the rule cut); ㉑ r14 checks the clock on the FOLDED run strip again (the base leg's intent) before it opens the strip; test-user-todos-layout's fill pin reads the new selector list.
- **Round 3 (the acceptance of 6ad39f934 — two minors):** (Q2) the folded row's clock was a dead tap zone beside «View»: `.cad-clock` is a child of the dock, not of `.cad-rows`, so the strip's capture listener skipped it and nothing else matched. **Fix:** folded, the capture listener opens the item from ANY tap on the row (`if (open && !head) return;` — the clock and the gaps included). Gates: ㉓ r3 — a CDP tap on the clock's rect ⇒ `cad-open`; nothing waits ⇒ no `[data-deadline-at]` in the page and a line put in after it is never ticked — RED CONTROL: a bundle with the two r2 lines put back ⇒ both red.

### phone-dock-restore — B: «Restore a previous layout…» was slow and said nothing (the owner, the same report: «你那个恢复之前布局的那个按钮加载速度有点慢，然后也没有任何提示让人那边 confused»)
- **Measured on 74b98357e** (a scratch hub with 200 — then 40, the ring's HISTORY_MAX — rollback points of a 10-desktop × 12-window layout; phone 390×844 touch and desktop 1440; logs/shots/before*-history-*): the menu tap → the dialog's shell in the DOM 61 ms / painted 90 ms on the phone (24 / 52 ms desktop), the list painted 107 ms (40 points) / 126 ms (200 points). ### agy-wall-signal — an Antigravity usage wall the stream names becomes a READING, and fires ONE /usage re-check (the owner 2026-11-02: «antigravity会话撞墙了但是用量一直没刷新出来，一直显示0%，我刚才手动刷新才刷出来»; the one-shot = the owner's ruling «A»; target .372 — re-headed at integration)
- **Cause:** AGY_QUOTA was NULL_QUOTA's nothing + `onDemand` (a person's Re-check): no stream signal, and src/server/stdout/acp-events.js had no wall road. The wrapper's two wall records (the `agy-error` notice «RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (code 429) … Resets in 90h39m34s.» and the error `prompt_end`) were shown in the chat and thrown away; the account row kept its last Re-check's reading. RED on 63f59d572 by name: the incident's records through the base's real consumer left the account's limit set byte-identical; `caps.autoResume.signal` false.
- **The signal (PURE src/harnesses/antigravity-wall.js, AGY_QUOTA.signalFromStream):** notice / prompt_end → ONE `{source:'stream', kind:'exhausted', limitId, window, usedPct 100, resetsAt = ts + duration, measuredAt ts}`; limitId = the session model's GROUP (gemini-* ⇒ «Gemini Models», claude-*/gpt-* ⇒ «Claude and GPT models» — the on-demand reading's own names); window = '7d' when the reset is more than 5 h away (a 5h window cannot reset further out), else '5h'; the duration grammar «90h39m34s» «4h12m» «59s» «1d2h» — anything else (or an unknown model) is `kind:'unread'`, said once, never a guess. The incident's own re-check read the Gemini weekly reset at exactly ts + 90h39m34s (1793952070).
- **The road (src/server/stream-wall.js, configured where the door is made — account-usage-routes; called by acp-events for notice / prompt_end / usage records):** the session's ACCOUNT (`_accountId`; the machine's own login has no account row — not written, said once) through usage-cache-write `writeReading` (per limit, per window, the newest measurement wins: a measured reading after the wall replaces the 100 %, a late wall never overwrites a newer reading, a wall whose reset passed writes nothing); the notice + its prompt_end are ONE wall (`sameWall`: same limit + window, same prompt or ≤ 2 s); the file's non-reading fields (agy's `windowNames`) ride along.
- **The one-shot (the owner's ruling «A»):** `quota.onDemand.onWallSignal: true` (a declared capability, gated in the door itself: `read(id, {wall:true})` → 400 `no-wall-read` without it) — the wall fires ONE `agy -p /usage` of that account through the existing door (its pace, its setting, its judge): once per (account, limit, reset ± 60 s), only for a LIVE record (≤ 5 min old), never retried; `turn-started` ⇒ nothing written and the one-shot DISARMED for that account until the hub restarts; no timer anywhere.
- **The surfaces:** the roster donut draws the wall through the existing `homeAccounts` road (8 s poll); the wall notice carries `wallRoom` {name, usedPct} (normalizer `_processNotice`, sanitized) when another group's weekly window is READ (windowDisplay) under 90 % — the client adds «{name}: weekly limit {pct} % used — switch this conversation’s model to continue» (en/zh/ja); known only after the one-shot ⇒ one `usage-wall-room` notice line; `readingSource('stream')` = «own session (limit hit)».
- **Auto-resume stays derived OFF:** the descriptor's 'prompt' resume verb is withdrawn (`resume: null`) — signal AND verb would have armed unattended continues; the client caps mirror follows (`{signal:true, resume:null, supported:false}`).
- **The «0 %»:** the ring draws only a cli-usage reading (an account never read has an empty cell) — the owner read his last Re-check's reading (a 0 % 'empty' window never rolls, B-8b12; a landed reset is drawn reset). Latent beside it, fixed: `onDemandUsageView` drew a `usedPct: null` window as a 0 % donut (`Number(null)` is 0).
- **Census rows:** test-quota-model ㉑ (antigravity-wall names the 5h kind it produces) + ㉒g (the room line's percent is windowDisplay's); test-vendor-whitelist 5c (the door's two callers with their gates, a planted timer RED); test-harness-contract (the antigravity row + onWallSignal through the real door for every harness); test-antigravity-usage / test-agy-harness (the old NULL-signal pins); the fake agy answers `AGY_STUB_USAGE=file:<path>`.
- **Gates:** NEW scripts/test-agy-wall-signal.mjs (fast, 60, ~290 ms; fast sum 918.50 s < 919 s).
- **r2 (主开发's acceptance of cf5c0b5e1 — one MAJOR, four minors):** ① THE MAJOR: acp-events read `engine.sessionModelFor?.(…)`, absent from server.js's 25-key session-stdout literal (every r1 gate stubbed it) — the first wall of a session was dropped «unread (model)», a wall after a model switch fell to the old group. ### run-open-jump — the owner's «expanding the folded run at the bottom jumps back to its bar» (inc-mvzai8oc-j70t): NOT reproduced on 63f59d572; the capture could not name the input, so the recorder now does (B-a7a9)
- **What the capture says (aligned with the action ring):** four times, one scroll event moved the list 826 → 59 (−767 px) 0.3–2.7 s after the open / the ↓, with a `_lastUserScrollAt` stamp 0–1 ms old and no stamped writer (`by fsb`, writeAgo 333–2716). The ring has no ptr / key at those instants, so the stamp was a wheel (the ring kept none). 59 is NOT the run header's offsetTop: the owner's next press on the OPEN header was at y 811 / 798, 51–68 px above the folded bar's press (862 / 866), so the header sat near the viewport's BOTTOM — the view went from the run's end to just above its start. sh 1663 → 1964 was four new records (total 28 → 32), not late heights.
- **What was measured (lane probe, Chrome 154 headless + windowed under a private Xvfb; 2195×1100 dpr 1.75, compact, the owner's collapseKinds, a live turn, 10–55 members, `contain-intrinsic-size` 20/40/80, history and creator roads, wheel −57…−343, a 39 px row under the list shown / hidden at the wheel × `overflow-anchor` auto / none):** the press lands pinned at the bottom and stays ≥ 3.5 s; a wheel-up moves by its delta only; ↓ lands and stays. A `scrollTop` setter wrapper saw only fsb's writes — runsRestore, `_landOnHeader` / the run bar and the ax band never wrote; native anchoring on late heights: no height change after frame 3.
- **The arithmetic:** a PageUp on the list moves 0.875 × ch = 732 px here; 767 = 0.875 × 876 = 0.875 × (837 + 39), the same 39 px as the unexplained ch 798 ↔ 837. The owner's answer: his wheel is normal (a few lines a notch, no page mode, no free-spin), the bottom landing is right (⑪ stands), and the bug stopped the view at the run's START. So the page-sized move followed a normal notch — browser-side, not reproduced here.
- **The recorder (B-a7a9), so the next capture names it:** src/lib/scroll-forensics.js (PURE). A wheel ring of its own (r2) gets ONE record per 100 ms burst {t, k:'wheel', el, deltaY summed, deltaMode, ctrl, n, stBefore, stAfter} — `stBefore` from a capture-phase scroll listener's last position per scroller (measured: a compositor-threaded wheel scroll is already applied when the main thread dispatches the wheel event; read in the listener it said 1775 for a move from 1950) — and every ptr record carries `pointerType`. Each chat view keeps a FINE scroll trace: every scroll event for 2 s after a run toggle outside a pass or the ↓ ({t, st, sh, ch, by = the `_traceExpect` writer since the previous event or 'none', writeAgo, wheelAgo}; an arm marker with the geometry; its own ring of 300, so the coarse ring keeps its history), shipped as `chatTraces[win].fine`.
- **Gates:** test-incident-recorder ⑦ (shapes + a stBefore CONTROL + the wiring pins + a MUTANT, a full ring's bytes); test-chat-scroll ⑪ reads the page's REAL capture back from the hub's bundle (the −700 wheel record with before > after, the ↓'s pointerType, the fine trace's arms and events).
- **r2 (the acceptance of 76ffbc349):**
  - **THE WHEEL RING IS ITS OWN.** In the shared 500-entry action ring, 60 s of 60 Hz wheeling after 20 presses left 0 presses and no count of the loss. Now `rings.wheel` (WHEEL_RING_CAP 200 bursts, `pushCapped`): its first record carries `droppedBefore`, cumulative, and the action ring keeps ptr / key / ime only. Measured in ⑦: 20 of 20 presses kept, «dropped 378 of 578».
  - **A FINE WINDOW KEEPS ITS HEAD.** At 240 Hz a 2 s window is 480 events, and r1's 300 cap lost the arm marker and the first 180 events. Now the arm plus the first FINE_HEAD 200 events, ONE `{dropped}` marker, then the last FINE_TAIL 200; the ring holds 600, so the window in progress (≤ 402) is always whole.
  - **THE ARM READS NO LAYOUT.** It runs as the first line of `_setRunOpen`, before the toggles, and records the geometry the scroll handler last saw (`_geomSeen`, from its own rAF read) as «at: press».

- **r3 (the acceptance of 73dda2eef, ACCEPT-WITH-NOTES):** the fine ring's 600-entry front trim was SILENT. That file is the per-call DERIVED config of a conversation's browser on an engine (src/server/browser-display-config.js `engineFileFor`): `{args: [43 strings], headed, noAutoDialog, profile, executablePath}` beside the Chrome road's `{args: STRING, …}` — the engine's list appended to the base's split list, written as a list; and never deduped (--no-sandbox, --ozone-platform=x11, --use-angle=swiftshader, --enable-unsafe-swiftshader twice each).
- **Why no gate saw it:** the named-profile road (AGENT_BROWSER_ARGS, a string) is the one the real-driver heavy drives (test-browser-mediation-chrome ⑧); the conversation road ran only against the shared fake agent-browser, which parses any JSON; test-browser-builds ⑦ asserted `(cfg.args || []).includes('--vibespace-engine=fixture')` — true for a list AND for a string.
- **Measured on agent-browser 0.38.2** (engine-args-string/probe/args-split.sh + env-split.sh: a dump-argv «chrome» launched with each config): the driver cuts `args` — the config's and AGENT_BROWSER_ARGS alike — at EVERY comma AND newline, trims each piece, drops empty ones; no quoting (`--a="p,q"` → `--a="p` + `q"`); a space stays inside its switch (`--a=1 --b=2` is ONE argument); a list ⇒ the whole file refused (the owner's line, byte for byte). So `engineLaunchEnv`'s «newline-joined when one holds a comma» was wrong too: `--a=1,2` reached the browser as `--a=1` + `2` (a URL to open).
- **The serializer rule (THE ONE WRITER, PURE src/browser-verbs.js `driverArgsText`):** a string is the driver's shape already — kept byte for byte (another spelling would relaunch a running browser); a list → its switches joined with `,`, each first proven to read back as ITSELF by the driver's rule (`driverArgsList`) — a switch holding a comma or a line break, a NUL, nothing but blanks, or a blank at either end is REFUSED by name (`browser_args_uncarried`), never dropped, never split. Wired at both file writers: browser-display-config `derived()` (the display plan's and the engine view's files) and the keeper's `machineConfigFile` (the Chrome road — a list from a user file leaves as its one line); `engineLaunchEnv` (AGENT_BROWSER_ARGS) goes through it too. The engine launch verdict (src/browser-engines.js `engineAnswerVerdict` launchOptions) asks it FIRST, so an engine argument the line cannot carry is refused at the door by name (`browser_engine_protocol`, «… named "--enable-features=A,B" — … tell the plugin's author») — before any file, never Chrome in its place.
- **The dedupe rule (PURE `mergeLaunchArgs(keeper, engine)`):** ONE switch per NAME (`--foo=bar` and `--foo` are `--foo`; a word that is no switch is its own name), kept where its name first appeared. Both sides naming one switch: the KEEPER's value stays for its own control switches (`RAW_ARG_RE`: the launch mark `--vibespace-keeper`, `--remote-debugging-*`, `--remote-allow-origins`, `--user-data-dir`, `--profile-directory` — the engine's copy dropped; the engine verdict already refuses the endpoint and the directory by name), the ENGINE's value wins for every other switch (its rendering switches — Chromium reads a switch's LAST value, so that is what the keeper-then-engine list always meant). Within one side the last spelling wins. Used by `engineFileFor` (the conversation road) and `engineLaunchEnv` (the named-profile road). The attach road builds a real argv (src/browser-attach.js `attachArgv`, no driver) and is unchanged.
- **The driver's refusal, in VibeSpace's words (≤ 10 lines):** PURE src/browser-profiles.js `configRefusalOf` (asked first by `launchFatalOf`) — «the browser driver refused the launch settings VibeSpace wrote for it — the setting "args" of bk-…-engine-….json: it holds a list where the driver expects a string (a VibeSpace fault, not the page's)»; the setting is read off the line the driver names through the keeper's `ownConfigLine` (files under data/browser-env/ only); the file by name, never a path.

### plugin-update-button — a plugin that can update has a labelled «Update…» on its row (the owner, 2026-11-02, asked to press Update on the Custom Browser Kernel plugin — installed from Git at ref main, its author shipped v0.1.5 — answered «有问题，看聊天» with a screenshot of the row: name · switch · ⚙ · 「运行中」 · 「卸载…」, no Update; lane on 63f59d572)
- **Cause:** the action lived ONLY in the context menu the status chip opens (plugins-ui.js `onChip` ⇒ Open {window}… / Show capabilities… / Update). A status chip reads as a badge; nothing on the row said an action sat behind it, and for a zip or hand-placed plugin the item was a greyed «Update» with no words.
- **Fix (src/lib/plugins-ui.js):** a manifest plugin whose recorded install source can update (`p.install`, source git / path / github-release) has «Update…» (`.mounts-btn.plugin-install.plugin-update`) beside «Uninstall…», both in ONE cluster `.plugin-row-actions` in the row's [install] grid slot (public/style.css — `pluginRow` unchanged). Measured in the rail (~200 px at 1000 × 600): two buttons in that slot widened the switch / ⚙ columns and broke the plugin's name per letter, so a row holding «Update…» lays the cluster on its own third line across the name column (`.plugin-row:has(> .plugin-row-actions > .plugin-update)`); a row with Uninstall… alone keeps its two lines. It posts the same road (`POST /api/plugins/manifests/:id/update`), is disabled while the request runs (pressable again after a refusal), keeps the same toasts and refreshes the list. No greyed button (the owner's rule): a zip install shows none and its fact line says «Installed from an uploaded file — upload the new .vsp through Install plugin…»; a hand-placed folder (no install record) says «Placed by hand — reinstall it through Install plugin… to make it updatable» (the loader's own refusal words; one key each, zh + ja). A fleet install is git: it gets the button and keeps its «Installed and trusted by the cluster» line.
- **One door:** «Update» left the chip's menu; the chip stays the status + the windows / capabilities menu. No reason was found to keep both: the item repeated the button, and its disabled state for zip / hand-placed rows was the greyed control with no words.
- **Honest words after the press:** `update()` (src/server/plugin-loader.js) answers `unchanged` — git: the fetched sha = the recorded one (nothing new on the ref); path / github-release: the package fingerprint (`contentHash`) = the recorded one. The toast then says «{id} is already up to date ({version})» instead of «Updated {id} to {version}». The consent drift check is untouched (a changed capability surface still trips it). docs/kb-api.md names the field.
- **Docs:** the 「已安装插件」 hint under the panel's heading names the folder shape + docs/plugins.md and lists no row actions — unchanged. docs/kb-features.md (HOST-CAPABILITY PLUGINS + the Plugins list), docs/plugins.md (Update), docs/kb-file-structure.md, docs/kb-bugfix-invariants.md.
- **Gates:** test-plugins-grammar ⑦ (fast — the REAL plugins-ui.js esbuild-bundled with its imports stubbed, over a fake DOM: five install kinds, the press with `unchanged`, a new package, a refusal, the chip's menu; RED CONTROL = the base 63f59d572's file through the same walk; the suite's row restated 630 → 730 ms) · test-plugin-trust (the real loader's `unchanged`: path, same bytes ⇒ true, a changed package ⇒ false; git ⑦, the ref still at the recorded commit ⇒ true) · test-plugin-consent-chrome ⑨ (heavy — the planted plugin carries a git install record: «更新…» beside «卸载…» inside the row and the 1000 × 600 viewport in zh, the switch / ⚙ columns not widened, no 更新 in the chip's menu, a real press on a path-installed plugin says «… 已是最新（0.1.0）»; PNG <prefix>-row.png; RED on a `git archive 63f59d572` copy).

### B-4291 (lane int361) — A LEG THAT RAN ONLY WHERE A LANE OBJECT EXISTED WAS CALLED A FLAKE (the push gate's test-stash-strip red at 472483e7d, c0faf8120, f008b7527, 6aa57dfbc; each pushed on a by-hand verdict)
- **The cause, measured.** test-stash-strip's r5 leg read r5's module with `git -C REPO show 280ccd2e:src/agent-routes.js` and SKIPPED where that failed. 280ccd2e is a LANE-BRANCH commit (channel-jump verify r5, 2026-09-27), never on master: the production repo had it, the lanes repo did not, the runner clones at depth 1 — so the push gate's isolated worktree (made from the production repo) was the only place the leg ran, and every lane gate, mirror and by-hand rerun «passed» by skipping it (/tmp/vs-stash-strip-f008.log:252 and -6aa5.log:252: «(r5 byte-identity SKIPPED …)»). Reproduced in a lane worktree with that one object made reachable (GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES=<the production repo's objects>, read-only): «1 FAILED (292 passed)», every run. Both byte strings dumped: full / diff / quiet / reminder differed by exactly two product changes made after r5 — the reminder's tools line (now src/agent-cli-registry.js) and a stash entry's stamp (r5 «[01-01T00:00Z]»; now the hub's own zone, which follows TZ: «[1969-12-31 16:00 PT]», «[1970-01-01 00:00 UTC]», «… GMT+9»); identical once those two were folded. The lanes that made them never saw this leg.
- **Refuted.** A race (red on every run with the object reachable, green on every run without it); load (2.2–7.1 and quiet alike); the hook's env (git adds GIT_EXEC_PATH, GIT_PREFIX, git-core on PATH, repo-guard's REPO_GUARD_* — nothing the suite reads); the isolated copy (`ci.mjs --isolate --sha=6aa57dfbc` in a lane worktree: the whole fast tier green, the leg skipped); a lane-1 neighbour (lane 1 is only where the gate's plan put the suite).
- **The fix.** scripts/test-stash-strip.mjs reads no history: r5's section ORDER per shape, computed ONCE from 280ccd2e (int361, 2026-11-01), equals THE ORDER pin already in the suite on full / diff / quiet / reminder and on manager but for its jobs-missed section (r6's fit) — so THE ORDER pin is that comparison, ONE pin, named; the r5 read and its SKIP are gone; the byte-identity is retired by name (its subject moved twice, legitimately; each change has its own legs). The class: test-ci-gate §2j — every literal sha a script hands git to READ must be an ancestor of HEAD. Its reads (r2, after the acceptance found it blind): a quoted sha on a show / cat-file / rev-parse / ls-tree line (single, double or back quotes; `<sha>:path`, `<sha>^{commit}`, a concatenation), a git command string (`git show <sha>:`), a binding (`const X = '<sha>'`, `= process.env.Y || '<sha>'`) fed to such a line, and a FUNCTION ARGUMENT (a function whose body hands its parameter to git, called with a literal — `fixBaseShaped('f36369057')`); each form a planted control, red by name (03901a1b8's scanner was blind to six: double quotes, `cat-file -p <sha>:path`, ls-tree, a concatenation, an env-defaulted binding, a function argument); the env-defaulted sites on master (test-discovery-spawn 9516bd8d, test-fixture-isolation e87d9893, test-mount-providers b48b26ae4) are read and judged on master. The verdict resolves `<sha>^{commit}` first — an ambiguous short sha is its own red («lengthen it»), never «off-master» (none today: the 34 read shas are unique prefixes in the production repo's objects too) — then `merge-base --is-ancestor` with the full sha (GIT_ENV, no alternates): a full clone holds every ancestor, so absent and off-master are one verdict in every full checkout; a shallow clone says NOT JUDGED and counts nothing. Six latent reads are a named ratchet, one backlog row each — 296a748f test-windows-device-fs [B-8390], 6f1aad6d test-channels-gmail-shape [B-3642], 7b6fa3c7b test-plugin-settings + test-plugins-grammar [B-43a0], 817550d4 test-queue-steer [B-4075], a7321ff0e test-ci-gate §2e [B-874f], f36369057 test-phone-desktop-sync [B-44c5] (its ⑩–⑬ + ⑭ RED controls boot a server from a WHOLE worktree at that lane commit; no master ancestor holds captureForViewport without captureBuilt — the 2.369.264 squash brought both); a new one is red, a stale row is red. REDs: the base's test-stash-strip ⇒ «NEW off-master reads: test-stash-strip.mjs:1469 280ccd2e»; the f36369057 row removed ⇒ «test-phone-desktop-sync.mjs:185 f36369057 (argument of fixBaseShaped)».

## 2.369.367 — 2026-10-31

### int361 dst-job-model (.367 pin #0) — A CRON CREATED IN THE REPEATED HOUR FIRED AT EVERY TICK; THE GATE READ THE REAL CLOCK (test-job-model red on master c0faf8120 from 2026-10-31, the eve of the fall-back)
- **The gate's red.** test-job-model «daily cron next-fire lands within 24h» read `Date.now()`; from Oct 31 03:00 PDT to Nov 1 03:00 PST the next 03:00 local is up to 25 real hours away, so the leg failed while the product was right (lane needs-card-tail's fast tier 525/526; master the same; logs/dst-red-c0faf8120.log in the int361 lane). The leg takes a fixed instant (Aug 17 05:00 PDT); the suite pins TZ = America/Los_Angeles at its top (the runner is UTC).
- **The product bug the DST legs found.** nextFire stepped the LOCAL clock; inside the repeated hour (Nov 1 01:00–01:59 PST) `setSeconds(0, 0)` re-resolved now() to the first pass, an hour back, and answered a fire before now — a cron created, started or resumed in that hour fired at every 30 s `_cronTick` until its wall time passed (measured: `30 1 * * *` 61×, `*/15` 100× before 04:00 PST). Fixed: the scan walks real minutes; a repeated wall time fires ONCE — at its first pass, or at its second when the schedule did not fire it at the first (nextFire's new `lastFireAt`: jobs.js passes the slot it fired for after a fire, null at create / start / resume; a cron created 01:10 PST fires 01:30 PST that day); a wall time the spring-forward gap skips fires once at the jump.
- **DST behavior, measured (TZ America/Los_Angeles).** `0 3 * * *`: 03:00 PST 18 h after Oct 31 10:00 PDT (25 h fire to fire); 03:00 PDT 16 h after Mar 7 10:00 PST (23 h fire to fire) — unchanged. `30 1 * * *` on Nov 1: one fire, 01:30 PDT. `30 2 * * *` on Mar 8 (02:30 does not exist): it SKIPPED the day on c0faf8120; now ONE fire at the jump (03:00 PDT, the first instant after the gap — the integrator's ruling, as cronie and systemd timers do), next Mar 9 02:30 PDT; the hourly 02:00 meets 03:00 there (one fire). Hourly / `*/15` skip the repeated pass (01:45 PDT ⇒ 02:00 PST). A full-year no-match scan: 25 ms (58 ms before).
- **The second-pass rule, measured against the literal one.** The ruling «skip the second pass when lastFireAt is that time's first pass» read literally fires a running `*/15` twice (last fire 01:45 PDT ≠ 01:00's first pass ⇒ 01:00 PST fires again); the rule shipped compares on the WALL clock — the second pass fires iff the last fire is before it there (null = none) — and keeps every ruled leg. Known edge (ruled): a job paused after its 01:30 PDT fire and resumed in the second pass before 01:30 PST fires 01:30 again (jobs.js keeps no last-fire field; resume passes null).
- **Gates.** test-job-model 451 (+16 legs); RED controls: c0faf8120's job-model.js (8 legs red by name), d69617894's — first pass only (the 4 created / resumed legs), a literal-rule mutant (the running `*/15` leg), a mutant without the first-pass check (5 legs), jobs.js's after-fire call passing nothing (the wiring leg); the full fast tier bare; test-ci-gate; test-architecture; secret-scan.

### vault-standing-request — round 4 (THE ROOT MODEL — the r3 acceptance of 45c537a29: three MAJORS all in the replace rule + three unverified; held out of .365, target .366)
- **Why a root model, not a fifth patch.** Four rounds moved ONE end per member between «merge» (r1/r2: hosts ∪ — an end dropped onto hosts never asked for) and «replace» (r3/r3b — the hosts the owner gave lost: P1 two cards both «Always» ⇒ only the second host; P2 a standing Allow dropped a 30-day grant that landed after it was filed; P3 a two-entry run ended X's no-end grant unnamed; P4 the restore judged against the partly written row left a REFUSED press's no-end grant). - **A member's scopes carry their own ends.** src/grant-model.js vault-use `scopes` (scopeListOf: host scopes `{host, until?, tool?, source?, at?}` ≤ 16, command scopes `{command, until?, source?, at?}` ≤ 16, each named once; a member is ONE shape — `scopes` beside a one-end field ⇒ refused / dropped). src/vault-use-grant.js `scopesOf` is THE ONE reader (a one-end member read as each scope with its end); `withMember` adds the scopes a write names, REPLACES only the same scope held with another end or ended (`changes.replaced` {scope, was, until, expired}), never touches another, keeps a wildcard held for another tool as it is, prunes the oldest ENDED host scope past the cap; the carry takes the EARLIER end. `canonOf` (moved PURE) is over what a member MEANS: a one-end member and its scoped shape are the same bytes — so the migration keeps every mark.

- **All-or-nothing for real.** standOpen snapshots each entry's VERIFIED row (`snapshotRow`) and restores it RAW on a partial failure (`restoreRow`: no row rules — what WAS, re-marked at a new generation, no resume); every restore and the switch save are read; a failure ⇒ `restore_failed` {cause, failed} by name + one `vault-restore-failed` audit line.

The suite runs every door leg on BOTH kinds (`for (const K of ['local', 'cluster'])`, each leg's name tagged) — Ⓜa–Ⓜd RED on e19220cc7 on the local door by name; Ⓜe the control (a local «Allow once» still runs by `seen` after the hour).
- **除了.** A card whose conversation an entry's grant EXCEPTS (useVerdict `excepted` — itself or its Task Group) offers no window; `facts.window = {offered: false, excepted: [names]}` and every client says why (««Allow for 1 hour» is not offered: you excluded this conversation from “X” in the Vault window.»); U.withMember refuses a window for an excepted principal (`window_excepted`, 409). Option (a) of the brief: the owner's row rule wins; no restore machinery. Ⓝa–Ⓝd, Ⓝe a control.
- **MINOR 3 — the card budget.** The window's lines leave the card's `detail` (DETAIL_MAX is the For-you store's own 8000 — it cannot grow): `facts.window` is their only home (+ `switchOn`, the line the detail used to carry), bounded by WINDOW_FACTS_MAX 4000 (over ⇒ no window). The clients draw the answer only beside its words (user-todos-row `winWords`, inbox-window-layout `windowWordsFiled`); answerWindow's belt refuses a press whose item carries no `facts.window` (`window_not_offered`). The bisect (a 4000-byte template + a pad): the longest drawn pad 3477 here, 3230 on e19220cc7 (the 247 the acceptance measured), detail 8000 at the edge with the window offered.
- **MINOR 4 — the window's own ✕.** U.withoutWindow (PURE) + the writer's `revokeWindow` + the door's `takeBack` (the route `/use-grants/revoke` `{scope: 'window'}` goes through it; the member's ✕ too): only the window goes; the record of the press — its fact now names `principal` and `entries` — is told `{endedAt, endedBy: 'revoked'}` once no entry it named holds that window. saveScopesOf sends no window (`kept` names the live one for the preview); setRow carries the stored LIVE window into the page's member (a window-only member saved with no scope keeps it) and still refuses a page-minted one (`window_card_only`).
- **MINOR 5 — prune + caps.** U.withoutEndedWindows prunes every member's ended windows in withMember / withoutMember / withoutWindow (and setRow drops an ended one); the writer's `pruneWindows(id)` is the door's hour-end write (an unref'd timer at the press — nothing to prune ⇒ nothing written). The writer refuses `window_too_long` (past now + WINDOW_MS); the reader's liveScope admits no window more than WINDOW_READ_MAX (24 h) ahead. The rollback hazard is in kb-design-lessons (the .366 reader drops a member holding any `kind` scope).
- **MINOR 6.** The notice's `entry` is the window-admitted entries only (`wins`).
- **MINOR 7 (the surfaces claim).** publicGrants `sourceKind` ⇒ the chip's source «“Allow for 1 hour” on a card» (never «“Always” on a card»); an ENDED window is drawn as the other ended scopes (its «ended HH:MM» title, no warning accent, no ✕); vsr-17 re-shot with no toast over the pane and the window maximized; the r7 report's vsr-4 row corrected; the CSS comment put back on its rule.

The cache is never rewritten for it (the stored window keeps the vendor's instant — the shape agreed with no-5h-window r3 in g-f453e781). `memberProofState(cache|set, nowMs)` → proven | reset-unconfirmed | unread over the windows that may name a deadline (an empty window is no evidence of now; a tombstone never leaves a member unread).

### cli-2-1-314-records — CLAUDE 2.1.314: ONE UI RECORD AND ONE CORRECTION SENTENCE, CLASSIFIED; THE ORACLE RE-PINNED (the box's claude self-updated 2026-10-30 17:33 PT; test-record-shape §4 strict-red on two lines; .365 was cut with the 2.1.312 knob)
- **The drift list, all of it.** The static `--auto` draft of 2.1.314 against 2.1.312 = exactly two changes, the two red lines: `system/ui_placed` (UNLISTED) and the sentence `m9t` (UNCLASSIFIED). No field grew or went on any shape, no nested key, no key gone, no sentence gone, no zod non-record ⇒ no FIELDS_314. The binary was only READ (0644 copies; the tracked dump by `dumpBinary` with the version off the versions-dir name).

- **m9t — a call STOPPED WHILE IT RAN, never «denied».** createSyntheticErrorMessage("user_interrupted") writes `${Nh} Correction to the text above: this call was stopped while running, not refused before it ran. …` when the abort reason is `remote-cancel` (the stream-json interrupt VibeSpace's Stop sends) AND the call was running (`ql(call)` = `callRunning === true`); 2.1.312 wrote Nh (= ww, «…The tool use was rejected…») alone there. The binary's own words: «No permission prompt was involved» — the brief's «a stop raced a permission answer» is not this sentence. ww is its PREFIX, so the first-match lookup read every such stop «denied».
- **What read it «denied» on .366 (RED by name on c0faf8120):** a main card whose result came before our allow record (a rebuild with no record ⇒ «✗ Denied»), a helper's ask on a rebuild (denied, then sticky: `denied + record-allow → denied`), and the bypass line, which turned into «Auto-allowed (bypass), but the CLI did not run it» for a call that ran. Live, a card our allow drew kept «✓ Allowed» and the tool card printed a red «✗ Error» opening with «The user doesn't want to proceed with this tool use. The tool use was rejected». No other reader exists: `permissionOutcome` has one caller (`_resolutionFromResult`, three sites) plus `_autoAllowRefused`; nothing in the ask / spend ledgers reads an outcome word.
- **The fix.** src/permission-outcome.js: a fifth outcome `stopped` (allowed, then cut off; may have run in part or in full), the row `m9t` (since 2.1.314, binary IS), and the LONGEST matching row wins. message-manager: the merge site patches `allowed` → `stopped` on the SAME card (an edit op), an allow record never turns `stopped` back, the tool block carries `stoppedWhileRunning: true`. helper-ask: `mainAskSettledWords('stopped')` («Stopped while it ran — it was allowed, and may have run in part or in full», grey), `RESULT_EVENT_OF.stopped = 'result-allow'`. chat-renderers: an error block with the mark draws «✗ Stopped while it ran — it may have run in part or in full» with the CLI's words folded under it. ### desktop-x-seat-browser — Round 5 (主开发's acceptance r4 on eaaa68afc: MAJOR 1 / 2 hold through the real client and the real bridge; 1 major, 2 minor + one docs point; ONE commit on eaaa68afc)
- **MAJOR A — r4 drew an agent's popup UNDER his window, and his press there landed on that popup in X.** r4 ranked his reach above every window, popups included: an agent's <select> menu, context menu or tooltip over his window was drawn and hit-tested under it, his click there was addressed to HIS, the bridge passed it (identity + his rect), and the XTest press landed on the popup on top in X (the acceptance's probe: at 91487da3c the same click went to the popup, refused and said). And r4's raise was none: xpra 6.5.4's `_focus` returns when it holds the focus (x11/server/seamless.py), `_move_pointer` raises only on a pointer MOVE while another window was raised last (a press where the pointer rests moves nothing), and an override-redirect window's birth never resets `last_raised`. Now:
  - ONE stack rank (PURE xpra-proto `stackRank`): a main, a dialog, his reach (his main, then his dialog), then EVERY popup by z. The view's z-index (`Z_FLOOR` + the rank), windowAt and frontOf all read it (r6's correction: frontOf no longer — the drawn order is not the front, Round 6). An agent's popup over his window is drawn above it; his press there is addressed to the popup, refused and said, as at 91487da3c.
  - A REAL raise: `focus 0` (xpra's reset_focus: no window, nothing in X) then `focus HIS` — xpra raises and focuses HIS whatever it held. The client sends it for the seat word (his seat begins, or focus left his reach) and before his press or wheel on a window of his that a top-level the client saw mapped or raised after it covers at that point (`coveredInX`: z is the client's model of X's order; r6's corrections: on a FRESH socket the seat word came before xpra's windows and raised nothing — the raise is now owed to his first window — and a wheel raises only the window that holds his focus, Round 6); a press on his focused window that nothing covers sends no focus packet. The bridge passes `focus 0` from his seat. MEASURED on the display (test-browser-x-picture ⑥, lane log heavy/test-browser-x-picture.heavy.r5dev1.log): an agent's window mapped over his resting pointer is on top in X (xwininfo, topmost first: the agent's 0x400019 over his 0x400014); his press there with no move raises his window (after it, his 0x400014 over 0x400019) and lands in his page (his mousedowns 1, the agent page's 0). ### touch-chip-cause, acceptance round 13 — unread text is never inert: a STOP keeps a line from ending its jobs, it never hides a command (the thirteenth commit, on r12 d5fa8a382; the r12 verdict: safety holds on the ended / lingers side, two defects on the command-reading side)

A fast leg drives it over the real holderRows and the real watch (his browsing alone ⇒ the person's watch; a conversation beside him ⇒ the agent's) and pins that both callers use it. ④ The nits: the person's once-authenticator leaves only with the ceremony that paired it (`onceFor`; a passed request's end touches no authenticator and sends no drain); his own browsing window's arm is his (`by: 'person'` on a `?browse=` relay — after a hub restart it arms first and his Close still ends the watch he opened); a recorded refusal goes with its browser (disarm, browser-ready); a browser with no open watch and no refusal says «VibeSpace is not watching this browser right now» (NOT_WATCHED_TEXT — before the first arm the cause is not known, so none is claimed; UNKNOWN_TEXT's «started before» stays the open watch's tab whose hook never armed). Gated: test-browser-passkey ⑨r4 (6 legs + the r3 queue leg over a fake Chrome that takes one request per page, all RED on cd3185a84 by name; 9 hand mutants each red on its own leg); heavy test-browser-passkey-chrome S11c / S11b green on real Chrome, live ⑪ a2 / g green over the composer.

**Round 5 (the r4 acceptance of 772222399 — all five r4 claims held; one MAJOR, one minor).** ① THE ONCE-AUTHENTICATOR LEAVES WITH ITS CEREMONY HOWEVER IT ENDS: r4's `onceFor` (only the end of the record that paired it removes it) turned a leak into a permanent one. Two roads end a record without its end reaching pkEnd — a navigation (`Runtime.executionContextDestroyed` / `executionContextsCleared` end the document's pending records through PK.endPending, and the page's later end is dropped: applyEvent matches only a pending record) and the gate race (the end lands while pkGate is still inside pairAuthenticator: pkEnd finds no authenticator, then the gate sets it and loads his key). On cd3185a84 the next ceremony's end removed it; on 772222399 nothing did — his vault key stayed loaded in Chrome's virtual authenticator, and every later sign-in on that tab (his phone, his platform passkeys) went to it with no Chrome window, until the mode flipped or the watch was disarmed. Now ONE remover, `pkOnceGone(w, e, rec)` (the person's mode, `once`, the authenticator, `onceFor === rec`), wherever a record can end: pkUnload (its own end, as before); `pkPageGone` (a document that went — the once-authenticator of a record it ended); pkGate right after pairAuthenticator (the record already over ⇒ removed at once, no key loaded, nothing released); and a belt at the next ceremony's start (a once-authenticator whose record is not pending is removed before the gate runs — no leg reaches it while the others hold: with the navigation remover dropped it heals the tab at the next start, with both dropped nothing does). 7.1 stands: a passed request's end touches no authenticator. ② THE ONE-REQUEST RULE AT THE RELEASE TOO: an autofill request that starts while his modal one is HELD (the watch's verdict pending — a card, his policy) did not queue (`busy` is set only by a released ceremony) and was passed to Chrome; the modal's release then met OperationError (the same on cd3185a84). The hook now supersedes again at a non-autofill request's release, inside the same ≤ 1 s settle wait: the autofill rejects AbortError, the modal reaches Chrome; a modal the watch refuses ends nothing (it never goes to Chrome). ③ The given-up socket's line goes with its browser, as a refusal does (`gaveUp` cleared by disarm and browser-ready — the one-liner the acceptance offered beside its refuted finding). Gated: test-browser-passkey ⑨r5 (6 legs, all RED on 772222399 by name; 7 hand mutants — each remover red on its own leg, the belt reached by none alone and proven with the navigation remover dropped, an unbounded re-arm red on the trimmed ⑨r2 leg); the heavies (test-browser-passkey-chrome S11c / S11b, live ⑪ pk) re-run on this commit, their counts in the lane report §11.

**Round 6 (the r5 acceptance of 76fabe39f — both r5 claims held; one MAJOR, one finding refuted).** EVERY REMOVE OF THE ONCE-AUTHENTICATOR IS A DRAIN THE NEXT CEREMONY WAITS ON: r5's three new removers (pkPageGone, the gate-race return, the belt) did not register as the tab's drain, and `e.pk.draining` is the only thing the next gate waits on before it pairs — so pkOnceGone's `WebAuthn.disable` could reach Chrome after the next ceremony's `enable` (a navigation with the new document's sign-in at load in the same batch: remove → enable → disable → add) or after its `addVirtualAuthenticator` (the gate race with his retry at once). Chromium's disable drops the tab's whole virtual environment (an enable over a live one is a no-op), so the new addVirtualAuthenticator was refused («not been enabled») or the new authenticator and his «always» key vanished under his sign-in. Now ONE rule — `pkDrain(w, e, fn)`: every unload (pkEnd), every pairing of the person's once-authenticator together with the gate race's remove after it, and every remove (pkPageGone, the belt) is chained onto the tab's drain in flight (begun at once when there is none), and the gate's wait `pkDrained` stays the single serialization point — before his autofill's pass too (a disable after the pass drops the environment Chrome holds that request in). The wait is BOUNDED: `drainMs` (PK_DRAIN_MS 1 s, under the hook's 1.5 s hold) — a drain not over by then is said once (`pk-drain:<profile>`) and gone past; a pkOnceGone gone past sends no disable once a newer pairing began (`e.pk.pairs`). A pairing whose record ended before its turn is skipped. The refuted finding (the agent road's release-time supersede beside a keyed autofill) needs an autofill real Chrome never keeps open (S5 / S6). Gated: test-browser-passkey ⑨r6 (6 legs over a fake Chrome with Chromium's environment rule — CDP order sent / answered — all RED on 76fabe39f by name; 6 hand mutants: the registration dropped in pkPageGone / the gate race / the belt, the autofill's wait, the bound, the late-disable guard — each red on its own legs); the heavies (test-browser-passkey-chrome S11c / S11b / S5 / S6, live ⑪ pk) re-run on this commit, their counts in the lane report §12.

**Round 7 (the r6 acceptance of d63b4cf6e — both r6 claims held; two MAJORs on one mechanism, a MINOR, an honesty item).** A CLEAN-UP ACTS ONLY ON WHAT ITS CEREMONY OWNS: r6's 1-s cap on the drain wait let a gate go past a slow clean-up, and pkUnload read `e.pk.auth` live at every call — his retry's new authenticator lost his key and UV to the old unload (the NEW HOLE: removeCredential + setUserVerified false onto it while it was pending), and on the agent's ONE shared authenticator the late unload removed the key the retry had just loaded (probe B). Now (1) the gate records what each ceremony loads BEFORE it loads (`e.pk.holds`: its authenticator, its credential ids, its UV) and pkUnload acts on that alone — its authenticator gone or replaced ⇒ nothing more; on it everything goes but a key or the UV another ceremony still PENDING holds there, and pkOnceGone passes the once-authenticator to such a ceremony instead of removing it; (2) the gate's touch of the authenticator — his pairing, the load, the release — is ONE drain, so an end that lands mid-load unloads after the load (the leak r5's report left as is); (3) the wait has NO cap: the gate waits while the CDP session answers (a closed socket answers every call at once, a silent one each call at its own timeout); `drainMs` is now the slow mark, said once per EPISODE (`pk-drain:<profile>:<tab>`, cleared when the tab's drain is over — the MINOR); (4) BREAK 6: a sign-in that waits keeps its page's hold — the hook's `wait` at once and every `holdBeatMs` (1 s, under HOOK_HOLD_MS 1.5 s) for `holdMaxMs` (5 s) at most — and a ceremony over while it waited gets nothing (no pass, verdict, load or release). Gated: test-browser-passkey ⑨r7 (11 legs over a fake Chrome that also keeps each authenticator's credentials and UV — 10 RED on d63b4cf6e by name, BREAK 4's kept green on both; 9 hand mutants: the cap back, the live read, no holder filter, no hand-over, the load outside the drain, no beat, no ceiling, no over-check, the slow line never cleared — each red on its own legs); the heavies (test-browser-passkey-chrome S5 / S6 / S11b / S11c, live ⑪ pk) re-run on this commit, their counts in the lane report §13.

**Round 8 (the r7 acceptance of 779318821 — the law held on both roads; ONE MAJOR, a regression of r7's one-drain gate, + the kb gap).** ONE «ALLOW ONCE» RELEASES ONE REGISTRATION: r7 moved the gate's load and release into one drain job and the registration grant's delete with them, while the gate still read the grant and took its verdict outside the job — so a job queued behind the tab's drain (a get loading ahead of it) left the grant in place, and a second registration of the same conversation and site (its other tab, or another frame of the same tab) found it and was released too (measured: 779318821 released both; d63b4cf6e refused the second `no-grant`). Now the grant is READ, JUDGED and CONSUMED as one step, at the verdict, and handed into the job; a job that lets its ceremony go WITHOUT the vault (over before its turn, over while the authenticator paired, no authenticator there) GIVES IT BACK as it was — its own 10-min clock, never extended; a newer answer at that key wins (the kernel road already consumed at its verdict). The slow line names whatever job is the slow one: «a passkey sign-in's set-up or clean-up on this tab is still running after N ms — the next step on this tab waits for it». The bounds the r7 report left as is are written in kb-bugfix-invariants' lane essay. Gated: test-browser-passkey ⑨r8 (4 legs in a fake world with a second tab — RED on 779318821 by name; 3 hand mutants: the grant consumed inside the job again, no give-back, the old wording — each red on its own legs); the suite's fact poll every 2 ms (was 5) keeps it inside its 4.8-s row with the new world, and the r7 slow-link leg's page hold is 50 ms (six 10-ms answers measured 59 ms once — libuv counts a timer from the loop's cached clock); the heavies re-run on this commit, their counts in the lane report §14.

## 2.369.366 — 2026-10-31

### dead-socket-keeps-chat-meta — A STOPPED CONVERSATION VANISHED AT THE NEXT BOOT (the owner, 2026-10-30: a local antigravity chat whose CLI died at 01:58 had a dead dtach socket at the 05:00 boot; retireDeadSocket deleted its meta — window, sidebar row, name, folder, account link gone, the 68 MB conversation intact in the account's store)
- **The invariant.** A conversation the product can resume is never forgotten by a boot: a dead socket STOPS it, it does not erase it. `retireDeadSocket` (and its re-probe twin, B-92a4 — the same function) keeps a LOCAL meta whose harness names a resumable id as `<sock>.json.stopped` (2.369.365's file, out of every live `*.json` scan) with `status: 'stopped'`, `stoppedAt`, `stopReason: 'dead-socket-at-boot'`; only a meta with nothing to resume (a shell, a session that never learned its id) keeps the old deletion; a write that fails leaves the meta as it is (never deleted on a failed keep).
- **THE HOOK, never a generic rule.** `store.resumeIdOf(meta)` on every chat descriptor — claude: `claudeSessionId` (spawn.conversationIdField) then `backendSessionId`; codex: the thread; antigravity: the conversation uuid `--conversation` takes; ACP (opencode): the session the wrapper loads. A store-less harness (shell) is PROVEN to have none (test-harness-contract's census: every harness row answers it or has no store; a fake harness's own field reaches boot-restore through register() alone). A backend no registered harness answers for keeps its generic id — it cannot be asked, so it is never deleted on a guess.
- **2.369.365's settle deleted the owner's exact kind.** layout-stopped-window's `settleStopped` asks the transcript worker's `locate` op, which answered `!!store.locate(id)`: antigravity's and every ACP harness's locate is `() => null` (no per-conversation file), so a kept agy / opencode meta was deleted seconds after the boot kept it. `store.locateIsProof: true` (claude: the `.jsonl`; codex: the rollout walk + the remote cache) is now the only place a null means «no transcript»; anywhere else it is «unknown» and the copy stays.

### dead-socket-keeps-chat-meta — Round 2 (主开发's r1 acceptance: every claim held; 2 major + 3 minor + hygiene)
- **A BORROWED ID IS NO CLAIM ON A KEPT COPY (major 1).** keepStopped keyed a copy by `resumeIdOf(meta)` and stoppedSessions' live set by raw ids, so a PENDING fork (it still carries its parent's id: `forkRequested`, `forkSourceId` = its own id) superseded its dead parent's copy at boot (one copy left, the fork's name and account on the parent's row), and a LIVE pending fork consumed the parent's copy. Now the ONE predicate: a copy is keyed by its conversation only when its meta holds the id as its own (`restoredForkPending` false — claude-lock-capture's rule); a pending fork's copy is keyed by its own socket (never supersedes, never superseded, never consumed through the borrowed id), and the live set is `addressableId(session)`. stoppedSessions lists both (the fork's says `forkPending`); `mergeKeptStopped` never puts a pending fork's copy on its parent's row. Two copies of one conversation from ONE pass share the pass's stop instant, so the later-CREATED session's copy stays, not the one the readdir met last.
- **A RESUME THAT STATES NO ACCOUNT GOES TO THE ONE ITS CONVERSATION IS HELD ON — SERVER-SIDE (major 2).** r1 routed the row's account into the page's resumeSession only; the For-you reply reopen (src/inbox-reopen.js reopenCreate: the saved config's account or none) now FOUND kept / indexed agy rows and started agy on the default account, whose store does not hold the conversation (the wrapper then adopts the new one agy answers with). The fix is in the create itself (src/ws-create.js, before the session counter — every door crosses it: the page's Resume, the For-you reopen, an automation's open): a local resume with no account takes `heldAccountOf(backend, id)` (src/routes/sessions.js, over the last sweep's rows: a STOPPED row's account); a harness that keeps a conversation in its account's own store (`store.accountBound` — antigravity, a descriptor fact) whose row names none is refused by name with the old words («no transcript of this conversation was found on this machine — it cannot be reopened here»), nothing spawned. An account the door states is never overridden. agy's own-login root now names its account the create's way (`subscription` = the CLI's own login), so its rows resume there, never on the default (r1's open item, closed).
- **ONE ACCOUNT FOR THE VERDICT, THE CREATE AND THE RE-CHECK (minor 1).** `resumeAccountOf(saved.account, rows, backend, id)` (src/lib/stopped-why.js) feeds resumeSession's create and `_resumeAccountVerdict` — which the create-failure re-check asks too — so a signed-out kept account is refused IN THE RESUME BAR with its doors (sign in again / switch), never a create failing into a bare toast; a healthy kept account is no longer refused for a signed-out default.

### jobs-memory-bound — round 12 (the light review of r11 c48fba1f5: the one-set law, the B classifications, the event-driven fast legs, the calibrated pin and its floor held — ONE major, one minor)
- **Base:** r11 c48fba1f5 on origin/master 43d0f8d2d, ONE commit on it.
- **The major — r11 took ANY drain SIGTERM for «heard the stop» (data/bin/job-wrapper.js drainGroup).** A helper forked after the stop step of a deaf main was first SIGTERMed by the drain once the grace was already up (the wait skipped) and killed in the same millisecond — r11 said no `short` (the reviewer's harness: a pod task, grace 2 s, SIGTERM at 2051 ms, SIGKILL the same ms; the base said «1 process got less than the full grace»). Now each entry of the termed table names its PASS — `stop` (the stop step), `drain` (the drain with grace left; a wait always follows it, one nap at least), `kill` (the drain once the grace is up: our own stop timer fired, `graceUp`, or the stop's deadline passed) — and `short` = what was killed that was never termed or was termed in the `kill` pass. A state the table holds, no clock in the count; short ⊆ killed ⊆ n still. The harness, r12 vs c48fba1f5's wrapper: deaf short 1 vs none; slow (SIGTERMed 1.74 s into the 2 s grace, killed at it) none on both — it had what was left; quick none on both. scripts/pid-identity-census.mjs rows for termOnce / termMain follow the new text (each delivery records `{ at, pass }`).
- **The minor — ㊱ asserted a count a fork race decides.** Whether the escapee's sh forks its next sleep between the drain's SIGTERM and its SIGKILL is the scheduler's (the reviewer forced red 3/3 with sh under SCHED_IDLE). ㊱ now asserts the state: everything stopped and attributed, 0 ≤ short ≤ n, the words naming that count, plus its order facts (never cut by the engine's kill step).
- **Gates:** heavy test-jobs-memory-scopes ㊾ gains `late-killed` (a task whose deaf node main starts a helper once the stop step is over; the helper never ends on SIGTERM, so it is alive at the kill — no race): «the job left 1 process running — it was stopped by force (1 process got less than the full grace); …» — RED on c48fba1f5 (12/1 for the ㊱ + ㊾ legs alone, that one row), GREEN on the fix (13/0); the full suite at the calibrated pin (three cores, 300 %) 123/0 alone under the machine lock (5 ratio rows skipped by name: the floor probe 145 ms against 110); fast test-jobs-memory 139/0 ×3 at one core 25 %, test-job-model 409, test-pid-identity 58, test-record-clear-census 243, test-ci-gate 91 + wall-clock-census rc 0, test-architecture 919, i18n-check ok, test-changelog-style (a private .365 copy) 40, secret-scan --company clean (planted: rc 1). ### layout-stopped-window — a window is never written without its name; a session window a page cannot build is a placeholder, never dropped (the owner 2026-10-30 09:19 PDT «我的个人桌面丢了很多窗口»)
- **Cause (proven on the owner's ring, replayed in the lane):** after the 02:55 outage the resume-all offer (`_offerResumeAll` → `resumeSession` → `createSession`) opened each stopped conversation in a NEW window titled with the bare name and no identity until 'created'; resume placement (`moveWindowToDesktop(…, { replaces })`) captured it into 个人's record IN PLACE of the named entry, and both identity carries pair by winId — 09:18:22 wrote seven of eleven nameless; 09:19:35 a new page dropped the seven as 'unbuilt' (11 → 4). The 04:59 boot had also deleted every dead LOCAL session's meta.
- **Fix:** PURE `keepNames` (src/lib/desktop-record.js) at the server's layout-sync write — a nameless NEW entry takes the name of the entry it replaced (evidence `by`, else the one dropped entry of its name), else it is left out and journaled; the client's `recordFor` leaves a nameless newcomer out ('nameless' evidence), `_updateCachedDesktop` carries the replaced name (`replaced`), `createSession` names a resume's window from birth (`_conversation`). `shrinkVerdict` refuses a stopped / unknown session window dropped as 'unbuilt'; the page shows such windows as placeholder tiles («会话已停止 — 点击恢复» / «会话不可用», their capture = the record's entry; the live record rebuilds or closes them in place; a spec-less entry of a running conversation attaches). `retireDeadSocket` keeps a local meta as `<sock>.json.stopped` while the harness store finds its transcript. `POST /api/layout-history/:id/restore` `{desktop}` restores one desktop; the 恢复之前的布局… dialog gives each desktop of a point its own button. The ring names the windows of a write's evidence by title.
