### vault-login-fill — R1 + R4 of lane vault-login-chrome: `vibespace-browser login` on standard Chrome (`w.kernel === false`) over CDP with zero secret leakage
- **PURE `src/browser-login.js`:** `STEPS` (`email` | `password` | `totp`), `stepOfForm`, `classifyLoginField`, and `classifyChromeForm` classify candidate inputs from a read-only DOM descriptor into a single step (`totp` when a visible one-time-code input is on screen, `password` when a visible password input is on screen, `email` when only a visible identifier/email/username input inside a sign-in form or heading is on screen; a plain search box is rejected as `null`). `loginText` includes `Step: <step>.` when present.
- **ORCH `src/server/browser-login-fill.js` (THE ONE WRITER on standard Chrome):** `inspectTabLoginForm(call, {formId, step})` evaluates a read-only DOM inspector on the active tab over the watch's CDP session (never reading `.value`), stamps `data-vs-login-field="vs-f-<i>"` on visible candidate inputs, and returns `{id, kind, step, pageOrigin, frameOrigin, fields}`. `fillVaultLogin({tab, call, origin, loginId, step, values, form, submit})` re-verifies the live tab's origin (`stale_origin` ⇒ `login_phishing`), focuses each target field, clears via the native `HTMLInputElement.prototype.value` setter, types the secret via CDP `Input.insertText` (triggering real input events and React/Closure `VALUE_TRACKER`), masks `.value` on secret inputs (`type="password"` / `otp`) with a configurable getter returning `MASK` (`'••••••••'`) while preserving native `<form>` submission (`HTMLInputElement::Value()` in Blink C++) and React state, drops its local copy immediately, and submits only when `submit: true`.
- **Wiring:** `src/server/browser-dialogs.js` (`fillLogin` when `!w.kernel`), `src/routes/browser.js` (`step: r.step`), `data/bin/vibespace-browser` (`step: a.step`).
- **Gates:** `test-browser-login` (142, +13 PURE `classifyChromeForm` / `stepOfForm` legs) · `test-vault-law` §⑫ (89) · NEW heavy `test-vault-login-chrome` (24, real headless Chrome + `agent-browser 0.38.2` over `/one`, `/two` → `/two/challenge/pwd` → `/totp`, `/react`, `/plain`, R4 zero-leakage sweep across CLI stdout/stderr, `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `get value`, `eval`, hub logs, dialog trace, browser audit, and `vault-audit.jsonl`, plus 6428c67e RED baseline control and leaking-fill RED mutant control).

### touch-chip-cause — a conversation entry hangs on the act that caused it; a strip never squeezes a chip unreadable (BUILD on 90c995a3 = 2.369.360; the owner 2026-10-28: 「这个展开方式对吗？」)
- **The cause, measured:** no hub delivery records a touch — the witness's only writer is agent-routes `touchChannel` (every `/api/agent/channels/*` verb). The 17 rows on the owner's `vibespace-status` card were the agent's own CLI acts bound to a call that could not have made them (`bindToCall`'s «latest running call» fallback). The coordinator ruled: no new delivery writer; `delivery` declared and DEFERRED.
- **Built:** `cause` on every record (the witness refuses a writer naming none; the census in test-channel-touch ⑧); `callCauses` (a shell call without the CLI is never the cause; a helper may be); the turn's VibeSpace note row takes what no call in view caused (and every `delivery`); a chained command's compact head opens at its `vibespace-channels` segment; the strip's measured readable minimum + «+N more» fitted to the width (one ResizeObserver per view) + the expansion into rows.
- **Gates:** test-channel-touch ⑧ (tables, the owner's shape, H1/H2/H3, the writer census, seven patched copies) · heavy test-fold-ux (1280 + 390, real presses, shots, a patched-view RED control; on 90c995a3 the new legs read 12 red) · test-architecture §63 pins `recordMany(id, touches, { cause: 'agent' })`.
- **Acceptance round 2 (主开发, two reviewers + three claim runners + skeptics; the second commit on 4b769a66).** (1) MAJOR, a regression: r1's cause rule found the CLI by a regex over the command text, so a LONE script / interpreter / `bash -c` wrapper / codex Sub-agent card that ran it lost its rows (the base bound them). Built the ladder: the CLI as a COMMAND WORD (PURE `channelsRuns` over a small shell scanner), else a lone running call that could have run anything (`callCanRun`: not made only of `INERT_COMMANDS`; a helper by its TOOL NAME — a WebFetch is not one), else the note row. (2) MAJOR: the readable minimum mixed on-screen and CSS px (129 px for 156 at UI scale 80 %); every width is CSS px now (`zoomOf`, the ruler in the box). (3) MAJOR: a steer typed mid-turn was a turn boundary and a wake was not; `opensTurn` reads the transcript's turn (`midTurn` marked by the normalizer — codex's mark — the wake's record read through the view's message list). (4) MAJOR: a long account label at 390 clipped «另有 N 个»; the control now has priority (chip 0's tight floor, 6 characters + «…»). Minors: the head opens only at a command word; the skew window never crosses a turn; a note row's proposal card on its own line; the suite fails by name on an older tree; the census names the 16 call sites and scans every src file (an injected-handle writer is red); `appendTouch` never merges two causes. test-channel-touch restated 523 → 915 ms (the fast sum 913.162 s of 914 s, margin 0.838 s).
- **Acceptance round 3 (主开发, two reviewers + three claim runners + skeptics; the third commit, on 8211ed8e).** (1) MAJOR: a codex shell call was never inert — the scanner counted the outer `bash` / `zsh` as a command, so a lone codex `vibespace-status` took the rows (skeptic-a A2 / A3 / E2: S 5 → the note), and a re-joined argv lost the CLI's verb (the codex batch: LOOP 3 → SEARCH 3). ### csp-mermaid-sites — a sanitized diagram filed a security notice on Chrome 156 (FIX on 5055b9ad6 = 2.369.361; found by lane ci-mirror-hygiene: the runner's image ubuntu24/20261025.353 = Chrome 156.0.8078.47)
- **The symptom.** test-chat-mermaid-chrome ⑦'s probe label `<img src=x onerror=window.__pwned=1>` was reported on the runner as «script-src-attr inline — «window.__pwned=1», set by code in /mermaid.js at 2:10038». Measured on a scratch hub (Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.47, the suite's own payload in a chat's history): the diagram drew, nothing ran, and the hub filed the For-you notice «The page security policy would block script-src-attr: inline» (Page security), its line `noticed: true`, the Diagnostics count «1 on the app page». Chrome 154: no report on either tree.
- **The cause.** mermaid bundles its OWN DOMPurify (public/mermaid.js: `node_modules/dompurify/src/purify.ts:1078`, its symbol map), which parses a label in an inert DOMParser document; since Chrome 156 a handler is reported when its attribute is SET (lane chrome-156-followups). `app-csp siteOf` admitted a parse site only in `/bundle.js`, so the report from `/mermaid.js` was the app page's.
- **The fix.** app-csp `PARSE_SCRIPTS` — ONE frozen table of the served scripts that embed a DOMPurify (`['/bundle.js', '/mermaid.js']`, paths only); `siteOf` → `{ script, v, line, column }` for a report from any of them. The sink (src/server/csp-reports.js; option `publicDir`, was `bundle`) reads THAT script on disk, the build its OWN `?v=` names, once per script and build, and keeps its `purifyParseSites` — each script's own sites, never a union; no line:column is written anywhere.
- **The pin (test-csp-report ③e, 139 → 161 checks).** THE CENSUS: every esbuild step of package.json's build built in memory (metafile + symbol map), plus scripts/build-novnc.mjs into the scratch dir — a build carrying the dompurify package has exactly ONE parse site (bundle.js 721:19136, mermaid.js 2:10038 on this tree), one without has none (design-viewer, doc-editor — 4 non-DOMPurify parseFromString calls —, novnc), and `PARSE_SCRIPTS` = exactly the scripts with one. mermaid.js's site pinned on its own symbol map. Through the real sink: the probe at mermaid's site ⇒ ONE `sanitizer-parse` line, no notice; CONTROL — the same directive and handler from mermaid.js at ANOTHER line (one of its innerHTML writes) ⇒ the app's line and its notice; another build, the bundle's `?v=` on mermaid.js, the bundle's site named in mermaid.js and the reverse, no mermaid.js on disk ⇒ the notice. MUTANT (the table's `/mermaid.js` cut) ⇒ the census says «/mermaid.js embeds a DOMPurify and is NOT in the table» and, behind the real sink's code, the probe files the notice again. The new test on 5055b9ad6's src: RED by name (the table undefined; the probe noticed).
- **Cost.** ③e's builds run at once, noVNC's while esbuild works: base / head back to back at load ~10, 4.89 / 5.34 s (×1.093) ⇒ the row 3.7 → 4.1 s; the fast tier's sum 913.17 of 914 s (margin 0.83 s).
- **Live, Chrome 156.0.8078.47 (a scratch hub, the probe in a chat's history):** 5055b9ad6 ⇒ the line at mermaid.js 2:10038 `noticed: true`, ONE Page security notice in For you; this tree ⇒ the same line `kind: sanitizer-parse`, For you empty, Diagnostics «Sanitizer dropped an inline handler: 1», «0 on the app page». Chrome 154.0.8037.57 ⇒ no report, no line, no notice on both. Shots and the harness: the lane dir.

### apple-signing — DESIGN (docs/design-apple-signing.zh.md) + P0 of the Mac screen helper's stable identity: a Developer ID signed helper keeps its Screen Recording grant across versions; the agent judges a pushed prebuilt before it runs; the signed manifest row (DESIGN + BUILD lane on 2.369.358 91bf7e18; the owner 2026-10-26 「我受不了了，我们来做开发者签名吧，把 mac helper 和 duo 的 app 版都做了」)
- **The design (zh, the design-doc law):** §1 the Apple Developer Program (Individual now, Organization later — D1), §2 the helper's identity (the designated requirement = identifier + Team ID; hardened runtime; notarization belt-and-braces, never blocking), §3 who signs where (the owner's Mac through the exit road at the cut; the signed row in release/agentd/manifest.json; the ladder: a signed prebuilt wins), §4 the iOS WKWebView shell for the iPhone Duo (P0 scope; the posture handed to the page natively — Apple: the Safari flags «cannot be enabled in WKWebView»; distribution: FOUR roads compared against Apple's current pages — TestFlight first per the owner's follow-up, Ad Hoc as the fallback, App Store at the earliest phase 3 (4.2 Minimum Functionality), Enterprise n/a — D3), §5 the build + upload road (xcodebuild archive / export with the App Store Connect API key; nothing in GitHub Actions — D4, D5), §6 the owner's exact clicks (nothing secret leaves the Mac), §7 gates, §8 as built, §9 D1–D5.
- **PURE src/mac-helper-identity.js** (imports nothing; the PURE set): the DR text, `verifyPlan` (--verify --strict first, then -dv), `signArgs`, `parseCodesignInfo` (keys, not positions), `identityVerdict` (developer-id only by a PINNED team with THE identifier and the Developer ID → Apple Root CA chain), `swapVerdict` (the §2.3 table: no pin — today — ad-hoc as before, anything signed refused; pinned — a Developer ID build taken even over the same-version ad-hoc install, ad-hoc / other / unsigned ⇒ `helper_unsigned`), `regrantVerdict` (signed → signed of the same team never re-grants), `wantSigned`, the manifest row ≡ agentd-signature's line. `HELPER_TEAM_IDS` is EMPTY until the owner reports a Team ID (one commit).

## 2.369.362 — 2026-10-29

### reaction-approve-shown — a reaction or recall proposal could never be approved from its card: the card's Approve posted no `shown` digest, the route refused every one, and the refusal blamed a stale tab (FIX on 90c995a3 = 2.369.360; the owner's hub, 2026-10-28 19:37 PT)
- **What was measured and read.** An agent proposed a 👍 on a Lark message. The card («提案 · 一个表情回应 · 待批准», «批准并立即唤醒 agent») refused every Approve with «请求被拒绝: shown is required — the digest of the card being approved (reload the page if this tab is from before the update)». Reloading changed nothing. The card (`renderProposalCard`, src/lib/channel-outbox.js) had TWO approve roads. The text road's `doApprove` posted `{…, shown: P.shownDigest(p)}`. The reaction / recall road (`if (reaction || recall)`) posted `{expectWakes: 0, deliver: 'next-turn'}` with no digest. `POST /api/channels/outbox/:id/approve` refuses a body without `shown` (400 `shown-required`). The requirement and the reaction road landed together in b0bead420 (2.369.197), and the recall kind joined that road in int326 (52810a929), so no reaction and no recall was ever approvable from its card (acceptance r2 corrected «again»: nothing broke later, it never worked). Nobody saw it because every engine leg approves with `eng.approve`, which accepts a missing digest. The real-card recall leg checked `expectWakes` and `deliver` but never `shown`, and no chrome suite approved a reaction.
- **A second untrue label on the same card.** The reaction's primary carried `data-deliver` like a text's. `relabelPrimaries` and a kept card's patch therefore moved it to this device's remembered «wake now». The button read «批准并立即唤醒 agent（会开始一轮）» while the press posted next-turn, and the engine never wakes for a reaction (`receiptChoiceFor`). The chrome leg shows this RED on 90c995a3: that label with `data-deliver="wake-now"`.
- **The fix.** `approveProposal(p, body)` is now THE ONE approve POST. Both roads call it, and it adds `shown: P.shownDigest(p)`. The reaction / recall Approve is armed like every Approve (`cardArmed` + `armCard`, r6 F6). It also carries `data-deliver-fixed`, which `relabelPrimaries` and the kept-card patch skip, so its words stay «Approve — tell the agent with your next message». The route's refusal now reads «this card did not send the digest of what it shows (shown) — nothing was approved», with no «reload». The route cannot know a tab is stale: no request and no WS hello carries the bundle's version, so «reload» could only be a guess at a cause it cannot see. The client shows the refusal in the interface's words (`routeErrorText`, why `shown-required`, zh + ja).
- **The census, in test-channel-outbox (fast; the suite that owns the card's harness and its F6 pins).** THE APPROVE CENSUS reads every non-comment line in src/client.js + src/lib/** that names an `/approve` URL. Each line must be either another family's, by prefix (channels/api, browser, apps, reach-requests), or an outbox approve. An outbox approve must carry `shown: P.shownDigest(` on that line and must be THE ONE: the door, called by both roads. Three controls go RED BY NAME: a planted site (`src/lib/zz-planted.js:1`), the base's road as a mutant of this source (`src/lib/channel-outbox.js:603`), and an approve URL of no known family (`src/lib/zz-other.js:1`). On the 90c995a3 tree the census names `src/lib/channel-outbox.js:590`. The real-card legs check that a person's click on a fresh reaction card is held and the next one posts the digest, and that the recall card posts it too. They also check that «wake now» relabels a text card's Approve (CONTROL) but never a reaction's, and that the refusal toast names what is missing. The route legs send a reaction AND a recall through the real route, engine and fake vendor. Without a digest the answer is 400 with the new words, and the proposal still awaits. With the digest of the card as the Outbox lists it the proposal is sent: the vendor's fold holds the account's reaction, and the revisions file says recalled. The suite has 541 checks. Median 4.34 s against 4.24 s for the base suite, measured interleaved at load 5–6: the row stays under its stated 4.5 s.
- **The chrome leg: test-chat-proposal-card ⑦ (heavy).** This is the suite that drives the chat card and the Outbox window on a scratch hub with the fake adapter; no suite had «Reaction added». The leg gives access back, makes the device remember «wake now», and runs one turn that proposes three reactions, each after a read. In the chat, the card says next turn, and a REAL Approve gives «已添加表情回应»: the proposal is sent and the fold holds the account's own 👍. A card kept through the re-render still says next turn, and a REAL Reject gives rejected (that road is unchanged). In the Outbox window, 「批准…」 opens the card, and a REAL Approve sends it; the chat's copy then says sent. RED on 90c995a3: the toast «请求被拒绝: shown is required — … (reload the page …)» and the label «批准并立即唤醒 agent（会开始一轮）»; the reject road is green there. PNGs: chat-reaction-card-zh, chat-reaction-sent-zh, outbox-reaction-sent-zh.
- **What the chrome leg does not cover: a recall.** No fake-vendor record is ever the user's own: `toRecord` stamps `isSelf: false`, and a plain sent message is not echoed. `recallVerdict` reads the stored record's `isSelf`, so a recall cannot be proposed on a fake scratch hub (`not-yours`). Its road is proven in the fast suite instead: the real card, then the real route, engine and fake vendor. A fake seam for an own message would let the chrome leg take one back.

- **Found, not fixed (another lane's code).** (1) `appendTouch` (src/channel-touch.js) merges two touches of one op on one conversation within `MERGE_MS` (2 s) and keeps the FIRST `proposalId`. An agent that proposes reactions (or replies) back to back therefore files ONE chat card, and the later proposals never appear in the chat. The PURE repro: three reacts 900 ms apart give one touch, and `filedProposals` = [p-1]. The leg puts a read between reacts. The leg therefore addresses the card by its proposal id.

A pan across the boundary is none (the exit goes on). Not carried, read from the code and said in the kb: leaveBy's own nothing() road — no watch follows it (the ONE named load is unwatched, as since round 1). Fake world only (no Chrome leg). Gates: test-back-guard 225 (was 220; straddle legs — a press down at 600 ms, nothing() at 700 ms, up at 750 ms: the tap lands, the next hop's go() aborted, hop stay why input; every hop starting nothing: the page stays at the release; a pan across it: no tap, the exit goes on; RED CONTROL from bd7dd961: nothing() hands no pointer on), test-incident-recorder 41, test-boot-phase 47, record-clear-census 243, architecture 850, design-docs 38, ci-gate-watchdog 14, ci-gate-shards 55, test-changelog-style 39 + ④ red (all 40 on a scratch copy with package.json at 2.369.358), every fast suite run on its own — 510 — green but ④; bare test-exit-slow-chrome 27/27 in 707 s, test-exit-late-chrome 23/23 in 631 s, test-mobile-back-chrome 44/44 in 503 s, test-exit-hop-chrome 15/15 in 351 s; on a bd7dd961 tree test-back-guard goes red where round 8 says (4 FAILED / 221: the two straddle legs — no step, the exit goes on, on to the cap — and the control and pin bound to the new lines; the pan across the boundary holds).

### desktop-doors-table — ONE table of desktop doors for the taskbar's preview tile, its compact list and the phone sheet; the phone can reorder (BUILD on bbca26b4 = int358, the 2.369.358 tree; the audit 2026-10-26 — the owner's registry law: a family is one PURE row per member + a census)
- **The drift (the audit's skeptic, verified on bbca26b4):** the desktop doors were enumerated by hand in five places — `_deskItems` (the preview tile's right-click; a compact-list row's right-click / ⋯, + Move up / Move down), the phone sheet's long press (desktop-switch-sheet.js: Rename · Delete), the phone window switcher's tab long press (mobile-nav.js: Rename · Delete), and three «+» labels (the preview strip's untranslated `'Add desktop'` title, the compact list's «+ Add desktop», the sheet's «New desktop», the tab strip's «Add desktop»). The phone offered no order door and has no drag: a phone could not reorder desktops at all. Its label read «Rename» where the desk said «Rename…»; its Delete ran outside the manager's done/after cancel guard. The pins were single-surface (test-desktop-switch ⑥ the sheet's two verbs, test-mobile-gaps #7 the tab's, test-duo-layout ⑧ the sheet's) — they pinned the gap as correct.
- **The table (PURE src/desktop-switch.js):** `DOORS` (switch · rename · delete · move-up · move-down · new, ONE t() key each — 『Rename…』 everywhere: the desk's ellipsis rule holds on the phone) + `DOOR_WHY` (gone «“{name}” is no longer there», only «Your only desktop — it cannot be deleted», first «Already the first desktop», last «Already the last desktop»); `desktopDoors({desk, desktops, order, tier})` → EVERY door, always, in one order, `enabled` by its rule (delete needs ≥ 2 desktops, move up not the first, move down not the last, a gone desktop shuts all but new), `why`, and `draw` — the ONLY thing the tier changes: 'row' (the tile / row tap; the list's «+»), 'item' (the doors menu), 'drag' (the preview's order — `order` false; a phone has no drag, its order doors are always items), 'off' (a shut door in a DESK menu is left out — the compact row's menu unchanged; the phone draws it greyed WITH its why). `doorItems(doors, {t})` = the menu's shape (ONE separator before the order doors); `sheetItems(rows, {t})` = the sheet's rows (each desktop's switch door + rowWords, then the 'new' door) — the sheet's DOM is drawn from it.
- **Every surface renders the table:** `DesktopManager._deskItems(desk, {order, after, tier})` is the ONE builder (doorItems over desktopDoors on the manager's own `_startRename` / `deleteDesktop` / `reorderDesktop`, each through `done` — a cancelled Rename… brings nothing back on either tier); the sheet's and the tab's long press call it with `tier: 'phone'` (`extraClass: 'mdesk-doors'`: 44 px rows, a shut door's why on a second line); after an act the sheet comes back on its new state (a delete re-shows the desktop on show, as before), the tabs re-draw. `_doorLabel(id, deskId)` gives every «+» (preview strip, compact list, tab strip; the sheet via sheetItems) the 'new' door's words and every switching row (preview tile, compact row, tab, sheet row) the switch door's as its title. No surface keeps a door literal.
- **Not folded in (judged):** taskbar.js `Move to Desktop` (a WINDOW's destinations — getDesktopMenuItems, with the Stage's refusal row) and the ⧉ list's «Other desktops (N)» (other desktops' WINDOWS — PURE otherDesktopWindows) list desktops as targets of a window, not a desktop's doors; each already reads one source. mobile-nav's «+» tab (the brief's mobile-nav.js:336) reads the table.

### chat-needs-you-card — what a conversation asks of you is a card in its chat, answerable where it appears (the owner 2026-10-26: «这个界面里是不是应该有个地方能让我看到需要approve？» — a channel watch's approval sat only in the tray)

- **The cause:** a For-you item reached its conversation's window only as the title-bar mini inbox badge (2.369.169 — cut in a maximized / tabbed title bar) and the top-bar tray; the chat drew S1's helper asks and the permission card, nothing else. A channel watch / access request is filed under the group key 'channels' — nothing on the item named the asking conversation, so not even the mini inbox counted it.
- **THE FOR-YOU ACTION REGISTRY — PURE src/foryou-actions.js (amendment 1, 主开发 07:5xZ — the owner's registry law «这种不是应该有个统一的注册表之类的吗»; imports nothing; test-architecture's PURE set):** ONE row per action type (24) — `{type, identity, producer (+ builtIn), waits, answer: card | buttons | reply, card: row | inbox-window | none, handled, chat (+ owner), kind, cli: {bin, verb, line: filed | wait | own}, scope}`; DERIVED from it: `ACTION_IDENTITY` (src/user-todos.js — its literal table is gone), `WAIT_ACTIONS` (src/attention-model.js), `CARD_ACTION_TYPES` + `ANSWER_ACTION_TYPES` (src/inbox-reply.js) — byte-identical sets but the audit's fix: `vault-rotate` merges by its `entry` (two keys' same-worded suggestions were ONE item, the second replacing the first's action); `vault-use-failed` is a row (in no table before; it merges by its text on purpose — head + cause). The rest of the module is the brief's row 1 (folded in from src/conversation-needs.js): `needsOf(items, keys)` / `recordsOf` — sessionKey OR the new `about` ∈ keys, a row's `chat` decides (S1's `helper-ask`, the permission card's `main-ask`, the proposal / API / wall cards keep their own chat card — never drawn twice); `placementOf(item, transcript)` — named (the tool card whose RESULT names the item or its request id) › tool (the row's CLI ≤ 15 min before the filing, 2 s skew) › turn (the record at the filing) › end (an open card is never hidden in history not loaded; a resolved one there is not drawn); `chipWords` · `settledWords` · `filedLine`.
- **scripts/id-branch-census.mjs gains the `foryou` family** (its ids ARE the registry's types, the registry its owner) as a RATCHET: 96 branch lines in 18 files measured today (`--seed-family foryou`, a new option that seeds a family the baseline lacks and refuses one it has); test-architecture §78 lets them only fall. test-approval-census's door regex reads a CONSTANT type too (src/main-ask.js, src/browser-takeover-request.js) and its MERGE-CELL pins read the registry rows.

### kernel-asset-credential — the custom kernel ships in its plugin's own repository: a GitHub Release asset downloaded with the Plugin Git credential, first hop only (BUILD lane on 2.369.358 91bf7e18; the owner 2026-10-26: 「内核是支持文件，应该放到仓库里」; docs/design-custom-browser-plugin.zh.md §5.3)
- **The fact:** the kernel side's v0.1.4 (e21f1064…) names its linux-x64 kernel as `https://api.github.com/repos/<o>/<r>/releases/assets/<n>` of its PRIVATE plugin repository. GitHub serves a private asset to `Accept: application/octet-stream` + `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with a 302 to a signed file-host address (404 without the token); the file host answers 400 when an Authorization arrives beside the signature. Before this lane the download sent no credential: 404 ⇒ build_fetch_failed.
- **R1 (PURE `kernelCredentialVerdict`, src/engine-kernel.js):** `use` only when the install record is a git source on the `plugin-git` row's host and the URL is that repository's release asset (GitHub's API form or `releases/download/<tag>/<file>`; another git host: the same host under `/<o>/<r>/`); every no by name (other-host · not-the-repository · not-a-git-install · no-credential · credential-other-host · not-https).
- **R2 (ORCH engine-distribution `credentialOf` + `kernelFetch`):** the row read through `resolveIntegration('plugin-git')` only for the repository's own asset, before any byte; vault_locked / kernel_credential_unusable (a deploy key) by name with zero requests — the fleet's boot download ('auto') goes anonymous on a deploy key; the token on the first hop's host only, dropped for good at the first other-host hop, `Accept: application/octet-stream` on every hop; the record / fact carry `credential: 'plugin-git'`, never the token.
- **R3:** the engine card says «· from the plugin repository's Release (with the Plugin Git credential)» (zh / ja / en); the `plugin-git` row gains engine-distribution as a consumer and says where a github.com credential goes; STATUS kernel_credential_unusable 409.
- **R4:** values.yaml and the design record name v0.1.4 = e21f1064…; test-helm-render's PIN fixture moved.
- **Gates:** test-browser-builds ⑧c (loopback API / file host / stranger in GitHub's shape; RED copies: no credential ⇒ 404, any host ⇒ the stranger sees Authorization, kept across hosts ⇒ 400) · test-plugin-trust ③c (the token census over a recording fetch; RED copies: URL, journal line, every hop). On 91bf7e18 the asset leg answers «api.github.com answered 404» (build_fetch_failed).
- **Round 2 (acceptance r2, five minors):** the credential is OPTIONAL — a locked vault / an unreadable store / a deploy key goes anonymous and is named (vault_locked · «the Integrations store could not be read (…)» · kernel_credential_unusable) only when that try answers 401 / 403 / 404, so a public repository's kernel downloads again with the vault locked; GitHub's browser form never gets the token and its refusal is kernel_asset_browser_form (kernel.json must name the API form — tell the plugin's author; zh / ja / en); ONE git-source grammar (PURE gitRepoOf, read by plugin-install's gitSpecOf); a token is one printable line (the row's validator; the download never builds a header from one) and a transport error is said by its code, never its message.
- **Round 3 (acceptance r3, one major + two minors):** git is handed EXACTLY the string the grammar parsed — PURE `gitSourceVerdict` answers ONE record `{host, web, path, https, url, ref}` that gitSpecOf and gitHostOf both read (9d02b48f validated a trimmed copy and cloned the untrimmed slice: a space / tab / CR / LF before `#ref` reached `git fetch --`); whitespace or a control character anywhere is refused `plugin_git_spec` (a new GIT_CODES row), every refusal with its reason (the closed set GIT_SOURCE_REFUSALS, tabled in kb-file-structure); a first use's launch waits for the download's first answer (≤ 10 s) and says the named refusal instead of «downloading». Grammar table b43799e5 vs round 3: 57 rows, 44 identical, 13 narrowed and named, 0 widened. RED on 9d02b48f: test-browser-builds FAIL (6), test-plugin-trust 2 FAILED; the suite restated 8.8 → 9.1 s (+0.3 s beside 9d02b48f's own run).

### desktop-small — the desktop tier at a small mouse viewport: a release never buries a window, the taskbar overflows visibly and its desktops fold, menus stay inside the screen (BUILD on cc7d4e5f = 2.369.356; the owner: «桌面档应该测试屏幕尺寸比较小的时候什么地方不可用来修复一下», «userW有一大堆桌面，屏幕尺寸小了之后桌面就堆积在一起了»)
- **The evidence:** /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/desktop-small-usability/report.md — a naive-user walk + an independent verifier at 951×585 / 1024×600 / 1100×700 / 1280×640 (mouse, sidebar open): P2-1…P2-6, P3-1…P3-3, four unverified claims, twelve suggested fences. Every finding was re-measured first on the base with a lane probe (a scratch hub + stub chat claude + headless Chrome at the four viewports): all six P2 and three P3 reproduced at all four sizes; of the unverified claims the cascade reproduced (three Files windows on an empty desk opened on ONE spot at ≤ 1100 px, 30 px apart on one top at 1280 — 0–4 % of the earlier title bars visible), the toast-over-menu claim reproduced in a milder form (the desktop toast — anchored beside the tray's For-you button, z 100000 over every menu — stood over the desktop menu's lower rows and on the bottom-right composer; its body passes presses through, so «Delete» still took the click here, but its ✕ / action buttons would not), the model dropdown in a lower Quad cell did NOT (bounded by --dd-room and scrolling since phone-refusal-wrap P2-17 — 15 rows in a 157–215 px panel, the first row hittable), and Files at 320×195 keeps its 24 px head buttons (a squeezed path box, not a defect).
- **P2-1 a window buried under the taskbar.** `_snapToGrid` snapped only to the cell UNDER the pointer; over the taskbar there is none, so the free drag's place stood (1024×600 Quad: y 553 of a 556 px workspace, 2 px of the bar left); the tile minimized it, a second click restored it to the same place, the window list only raised it. PURE (src/lib/drag-end.js — the ONE door): `releasePoint` (a grid release outside every cell is judged just inside the workspace ⇒ the nearest cell), `releaseBox` (EVERY release keeps RELEASE_KEEP 80×32 of the title bar inside — window.js `_keepReachable` at the end of the title-bar drag's last drop branch and the tab tear-off's, plus every `_reflowWindows` as this client's fit, never captured; `_barKeep` adds the window's own border so it is 80×32 of the BAR), `reachable` / `insideBox` (THE RECOVERY: `revealWindow` — every door that names a window: its tile, its window-list row, the palette, a card — brings an unreachable window WHOLLY inside, witnessed as the user's act, its grid bounds captured; the focused window's tile minimizes only while `wm.isReachable(id)`). No new drag door (test-window-drag §5 census unchanged: 17 feed doors).
- **P2-2 the taskbar past ~8 / 12 windows + the owner's many desktops.** Tiles were 60 px (1–2 characters), the strip `overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: none` with nothing to say what it cut, the wheel's deltaY inert; eight desktops' previews took 432 px of a 691 px taskbar. PURE src/lib/taskbar-fit.js: `TILE_MIN_PX` 90 (= style.css `.taskbar-item` min-width), `stripHidden` (the cut tiles ⇒ ONE `#taskbar-overflow` «+N» chip after the strip, its list = exactly them, a row raises its window and scrolls its tile in — taskbar.js `fitTaskbarStrip` at every update / scroll / strip resize), `wheelScroll` (a vertical wheel scrolls the strip sideways, a non-passive listener), `switcherForm` (the previews fold to ONE «Desktop k/N ▾» button when they need more than a third of the bar or would leave the strip under 4 × 90 px — desktop-manager.js `_switcherFormFor` over the bar's measured room, part of the switcher's digest, re-asked by a ResizeObserver on #taskbar; `_renderCompactSwitcher` + `_openDesktopList`: every desktop with its window count (built + held), the Stage first when on, «Add desktop»). The sibling lane desktop-switch-phone's PURE `desktopRows` was not on this base — the compact list is minimal and self-contained (no shared file).
- **P2-3 a lower-row title menu above the viewport.** `showWindowContextMenu` (and the desktop previews' menu) re-anchored the menu's BOTTOM on the pointer after showContextMenu had placed it — no top clamp: 243×430 at y −124..306, Switch window / Move / Minimize unreachable. NEW PURE src/lib/menu-place.js `menuPlace` = THE ONE placement (below, or above with `up`, flipped when its side lacks room, else clamped, capped + scrolling when taller than the viewport); showContextMenu takes `{ up }` and places every `.context-menu` / `.taskbar-context-menu` through it; both callers pass `up` and write nothing after.
- **P2-4 the chat window's fixed chrome.** The desk bar wraps (three rows, 69 px at 340–376 px) and the composer is 79 px. chat-status-bar.js `_oneRow()`: a phone, OR a desk window narrower than `NARROW_BAR_PX` 480 or shorter than `SHORT_WINDOW_PX` 300 ⇒ the phone's own one-row fold (PURE phoneBarFold, ⋯ opens it in place; `.chat-status-narrow`); the bar AND its window are watched (`_onSize`: a flip re-renders, the ⋯ chip comes or goes); a short window marks its view `.chat-short` (composer one line, the shortcut hint hidden). Measured: 340×244 Quad cell 86 → 115 px of messages (47 %), 520×250 105 → 136 px.
- **P2-5 the hover buttons on the first line.** Open in editor / Fork stand absolute at the message's top-right; the text ran under them. A message that carries them keeps their column free: chat.css gives its `.chat-text` a right padding of the buttons' width (28 / 56 px; none on touch, where the … button serves). A first cut reserved the corner with a 26 px float as the text's first child — it made every one-line compact row 26 px tall and test-ax-budget's band (④b–⑦) went red: bisected to the float, so it was dropped.
- **P2-6 the 24 px mouse target.** Window buttons 24×24 and 4 px apart (were 20, 3) — a title bar under 440 px sets its ⧉ overlap indicator aside (window.js `_observeTitleWidth`, ONE ResizeObserver; its act is the title menu's «Switch window»), so the 19 px the row grew never comes out of a narrow window's title or a split group's tab doors (test-window-binding ⑦c measured it); every clickable status chip ≥ 24×24 and `flex-shrink: 0` (an explicit min-width replaces a flex item's content minimum — without it the billing pill's full form shrank under its words, test-phone-chip-ui) (the model pill's paint clipped to its padding box; the bar's vertical padding 1 px, so one row is 27 px); a dialog's ✕ keeps the header's line with `margin: -2.5px 0` (a 5 px taller header put the S3 storage dialog's «Connect» under its scroll fold — test-mounts-dialog-extract's control); the wide toast keeps its ✕ beside the words (body basis 100 % − 48 px); the hover buttons, the code toolbar's Copy / Wrap, the composer's ⤢, a toast's ✕, a dialog's ✕, Sort, the «+» desktop, «Show details», the New Session chips / links, the Apps dialog's Check again / Show them. Named exception (the census's table): the session row's Star / Archive 14 px column — the owner's own density call (2.224.0), both in the row's right-click menu at full size.
- **CI .358 — P2-5's right padding exposed THE COLLAPSE (ci358-reds; the mirror red on test-chat-scroll ③ ④, both tries, here green):** the chat list is a flex COLUMN and a `.chat-msg` under content-visibility:auto is size-contained (automatic minimum height 0), so an overflowing list SHRANK the cards it laid out off screen to 0 px — contain-intrinsic-size never applied, the cards above the view stacked on each other with their words clipped, scrollHeight short by their height. NOT a pull to the bottom: the forced-scroll chain was idle (`fsb:0` every frame). Fix: `.chat-msg { flex-shrink: 0 }` (chat.css). Reproduced exactly (the runner's numbers) under the runner's fontconfig + 2 cores; test-chat-scroll now runs in two FONT LEGS (DejaVu through a scratch fontconfig — scratch.mjs `runFontLegs` / `runnerFontEnv` / `drawnFace` — and the box's own), with a collapsed-card census in ③ (RED on d29dd915 in BOTH faces) and its CONTROL (`flex-shrink: 1` put back ⇒ collapsed cards); `VS_CPU_THROTTLE`. **The 0 px of B-1192's release frame WAS this shrink:** with cards that cannot shrink, test-chat-paging §4e's pre-fix two-frame release laid no fresh card out off its height (0 of 11 landings — its NEGATIVE CONTROL went red on the commit), so §4e's control now restores the pre-fix WORLD (the release + `flex-shrink: 1`, last in the cascade: 4 of 11), prints the release alone as information and gains a census (every `.chat-msg` computes flex-shrink 0, 269 cards); test-desktop-resume-paging §5's source-level control likewise strips the new layer from its tree's chat.css (with layers (1)–(6) stripped it had gone green on the fixed build).

Fix: the phone block (chat.css) sets `min-width: auto` back on its chips — the touch bar keeps its own scale (its 36 px search and ⋯ rules untouched). test-artifacts-handover-ui runs both font legs; ⑤ judges the chip IN the row (never folded; the row's widths reported — it was written for the old swipe bar) + a CONTROL in the DejaVu leg (the desk floor put back folds it); CDP calls bounded; `VS_CPU_THROTTLE`. ### passkey-sink — P2 of the custom browser kernel: on a kernel with `webauthn` the passkey ceremony sinks to VibeSpace — the kernel transports (`VibeSpace.webauthnRequest` / `webauthnAnswer`), VibeSpace signs with the sealed key; UV = the owner decided THIS ceremony; no OS / GPM authenticator ever (BUILD lane on 1cdf214b = browser-surfaces, int356 pick 3; docs/design-custom-browser-plugin.zh.md §3 rewritten as built)
- **The switch (src/server/browser-dialogs.js):** `features` lists `webauthn` ⇒ `armPasskey` returns at once (no hook, no virtual authenticator — both stay for standard Chrome and a surfaces-only kernel); the tab is armed when `VibeSpace.enable` is taken (`none`, never `unknown`); `onDesktop` false. ONE record: `VibeSpace.webauthnRequest` → PURE `PK.kernelEvent` → the same `applyEvent` start (+ `kernel`: ids, `op` over `kind`, the hash, challenge, clientDataJSON, key types, UV asked, exclude, user.id); the webauthn SURFACE is the held card only (P1's row gains its answerer `sink: 'webauthn'`, PURE `SF.sinkOf`): in `w.surf`, never `w.open`, never a browser-surface card; its close ends a pending record; an orphan surface (no request — a reconnect) is cancelled after `passkeyOrphanMs`.
- **The gate:** PURE `WA.requestVerdict` first (rpMatches injected; the clientDataJSON, when handed, must hash to the hash we sign and name this type / origin / challenge ⇒ `webauthn_rp_mismatch`; no ES256 ⇒ `webauthn_alg_unsupported`), then `PS.gateVerdict` unchanged, then `PS.kernelFlags` (UV only for the card's once / always, the one-use grant, a takeover; policy yes ⇒ UV 0; UV required on an automatic release ⇒ the card; BE / BS never).
- **The signer (NEW PURE src/webauthn-sign.js, node crypto handed in):** authenticatorData, ES256 assertion (DER, P-256 only), makeCredential (32 random id bytes, COSE key, attestation `none`), a canonical CBOR encoder (uint / negative / bytes / text / array / map), the re-check. Get: `PS.signOrder` → unseal ONE key → bump + reconcile WRITTEN before the answer (`pkWrite` answers whether it reached the disk; no write ⇒ no signature). Create: the pair made on the server, SEALED before the answer (a lock ⇒ `webauthn_key_locked`, never a key we cannot keep); a page gone by then ⇒ the row dropped again.
- **The use law:** every signature / new key = `vaultUse('passkeys', {by, door: 'passkey', conv}, {purpose})` — the wiring hands `vault.noteUse` (the ONE writer); the receipt stays on the record. Cancel = `VibeSpace.cancelSurface` ⇒ the page sees NotAllowedError (Q4, the peer's answer); `PK.cancelText({kernel})` says so. REASONS + `webauthn_alg_unsupported` · `webauthn_rp_mismatch` · `webauthn_key_locked` (its sentence in the vault rule's words — the user was told, a person unlocks it on this instance's page, never ask them).
- **The fake kernel (scripts/fixtures/fake-kernel.mjs, extended):** `triggerWebAuthn` (the peer stub's field names) → `{request, answerPromise}`, `webauthnAnswer` (`no_such_request`), cancel / any surface answer ⇒ NotAllowedError, `abortWebAuthn`, `mode.features`.
- **Gates:** NEW test-webauthn-sign 37 (fast, 28 ms) · test-browser-passkey 151 (⑧ +43: the kernel road over the fake kernel; 1.4 s) · test-browser-passkey-store 38 (⑦) · test-browser-surfaces 133 (the answerer row) · test-vault-law 73 (⑪: a REAL vault + the engine's noteUse; the locked vault ⇒ webauthn_key_locked) · test-key-file-law 121 (RANDOM32 row: the credential id) · test-vault-words 11 (the locked sentence's row) · test-architecture 853 · i18n-check 9746 / 9746 · the whole fast tier · heavy test-browser-passkey-chrome 46 (K1–K5 + three mutant controls RED: UV always true · the count not advanced · the request not re-checked; 1 SKIP = the installed agent-browser is 0.38.2, as on the base) · test-browser-mediation-chrome 125 (unchanged).

### browser-login — P3 of the custom browser kernel: on a kernel with `credentials` the password manager is VibeSpace's vault — the kernel reports a page's login forms and fills what the vault holds (the agent never sees a value); an account the agent registers goes THROUGH the vault and is saved automatically with its provenance; a password the agent typed itself is saved too, marked `agent-typed` (BUILD lane on 6dcf2b5e = passkey-sink, int358 pick 6; the owner's D3 yes / D5 reversed; docs/design-custom-browser-plugin.zh.md §4 rewritten as built)
- **The entry (NEW PURE src/browser-login.js):** a vault ENTRY `web-login:<origin>#<user>` (never a STORE_KEYS row; the engine's SECRET_RE gains the same shape as a second anchored alternative), the sealed record `{v:1, origin, username, password, totpName?, createdAt, by, source: owner|vault-minted|agent-typed, strength: generated|unknown, createdIn?, submittedAt, pending?, previous?, lastUsedAt}`; THE ONE WRITER = NEW ORCH src/server/browser-logins.js (`writeEntry` → secretPut, the provenance word as the box's `kind`); every fill a use through the engine's `noteUse` (door `browser-login`, purpose «sign in at <origin>», a receipt; a refused grant a line too).
- **The grant:** src/grant-model.js DOORS + `browser-login`, resource `<origin>#<user>` · `<origin>#*` · `*` (NEW `RESOURCE_SHAPES` — another shape is `bad_resource` at the write, `unknown_shape` at the read); the three scopes' rows ADD through `GM.admits`; the owner's 「用于…」 in the Vault window → `grants.set / remove` (§97 (a) reader + (c) writer rows).
- **Detect / fill (src/server/browser-dialogs.js, the login road):** `VibeSpace.credentialFormDetected` → PURE `formOf` (fieldId kernel-private — Q5; each password field's `constraints` — Q5b; labels / names / rects never kept) → the tab's `e.forms` (≤ 8, a new document clears them). `vibespace-browser login [<origin>] [--user <u>] [--submit]` (OURS_PAGE; passes a held dialog) → `POST /api/agent/browser/login` → `fillLogin` → `planFill` → PURE `fillVerdict` (form · THE PHISHING RULE: the page's own origin, its frame's equal, https / localhost http, entries of that exact origin only · one entry, else `login_ambiguous` · the grant · the vault) → `VibeSpace.fillCredential {surfaceId, values, expectedOrigin, submit}` (the kernel's stale_origin ⇒ `login_phishing`) → the values dropped → `{ok, mode, origin, user, filled, submitted, receipt, text}` through the belt (`loginText(` — the peer-text census's new door). D3: a paired `totp:` entry's code is filled (`vault-totp.codeForLogin`, no second grant). A held http-auth surface is answered the same way (its credential answer). P1's credential row: `sink: 'credentials'` (its line names the verb); webauthn's sink is matched by name.
- **Register / save (D5 reversed):** `login --new-user <u> --generate` ⇒ PURE `generatePassword(constraints, rng)` (20, every class, the site's min / max and pattern — the charset ladder; a cap under 12 or a pattern none satisfies ⇒ `password_rules_unsupported`) → the entry SEALED (`vault-minted`, `pending: register`) BEFORE the kernel gets a byte → filled; `--generate` on a change-password form = a change (the old value in `previous`). `VibeSpace.credentialSubmitted` → PURE `saveVerdict` (new · same · update · agent-typed · owner-card · none) → the ONE writer → ONE For-you notice (`kind: notice`, i18n en / zh / ja); a person's own sign-in in a takeover ⇒ the save-login card (`POST /api/browser/logins/cards/:id/approve|reject`, its password held only until answered); a locked vault holds a submission until the next unlock; the flood guard saves ≤ 6 new agent-typed logins a site in 10 minutes (a page inventing submissions never floods the vault).
- **The Vault window:** PURPOSES + `web-logins`「网站登录」; the row `<user> · <site>` with its provenance (by you · agent 铸造 · agent 见过明文 + rotate); 显示 = the password; 删除; 添加 → 网站登录…; 用于… (src/lib/vault-login-row.js; `GET|POST /api/vault/web-logins`, `DELETE …/:name`, `POST …/grants|ungrant`). The output belt masks a web login's PASSWORD (not its JSON).

### phone-back-reload — a back on the phone never costs a load: the boot rebuilds the sentinel a discarded / history-loaded tab stands on, the 「再返回一次退出」 exit leaves past VibeSpace's older entries in ONE go(-n), the tab's navigation diary (+ an automatic incident when a back still costs a load), the stale-tab notice (FIX on 2.369.357 fbaf6988; the owner on an Android phone, Chrome, the hub over the tailnet, 96 open For-you items: the back button reloads VibeSpace — the loading screen, then home)
- **Why the first probe saw nothing:** it pressed `history.back()`. Chrome's back-button logic (NavigationController::GoBack with the history-manipulation intervention's skip) runs only for the BROWSER's back; the lane measured with CDP Alt+Left — the path Android's back takes (lane mobile-back-guard's finding). Chrome 154, headless and headed on Xvfb, phone emulation 382×580, a throwaway server from a scratch copy, each document numbered by an init script.
- **H1 cross-document traversal — REPRODUCED, three roads.** (a) A tab DISCARDED (chrome://discards' Urgent Discard, a debug page — Local State `internal_only_uis_enabled`; DevTools must be off the tab, and the tab comes back as a NEW target) and shown again: the restored document reports `document.wasDiscarded` true, navigation type `back_forward`, `history.state` {vs:1}, `navigation.entries()` both entries `sameDocument: true` — and the FIRST back (closing a window) was a cross-document load: bootStep had KEPT the sentinel over the dead document's page entry. (b) A renderer KILLED (Page.crash — Android's low-memory kill) and reloaded: navigation type `reload`, `history.state` null, `history.length` +1 (the boot pushed a second sentinel), the old page entry correctly `sameDocument: false`; the window back stayed same-document, the 「再返回一次退出」 exit LOADED the older entry (bfcache on or off). (c) A second load of the app in the tab (`location.href = '/?session=…'` over an earlier document): the exit landed on the older document — a full load with bfcache off, its cache restore with it on. A tab-start variant (the app the tab's first entry) needs the named load (below).
- **NOT the cause (measured):** `location.reload()` (the stale-tab path), the browser's reload, two reloads — entries `S*S`, the next back a same-document popstate; a cross-site previous entry — the exit lands on the other site. H2 dropped go(1): go(1) lands in 2–3 ms (8 of 8 window backs); with a patched history.go that drops it, the 500 ms belt pushes (511 ms) and the next back with no tap since stays same-document — on this Chrome; the diary now records every go1 (ms, or landed 0 + the push) so an Android export answers it there. H3 stale-tab reload: a scratch server at a version the bundle never matches ⇒ ONE reload (the per-tab sessionStorage stamp), then two reconnects SILENT; the back after it same-document ⇒ bounded already, only the silence was wrong.
- **H4 Chrome's documented behaviour (read, not guessed):** the Chromium history-manipulation-intervention doc — only the browser's back/forward buttons skip entries, never `history.back()`; an entry becomes skippable when its document creates another entry without a user activation, an activation un-skips it, all same-document entries share one state; all entries skippable ⇒ CanGoBack false (Android: back closes the tab). The Page Lifecycle doc — the browser freezes and discards hidden tabs at its discretion, a discarded page must be reloaded to be used, NO event fires at a discard, `document.wasDiscarded` says it at load. Close watchers (blink-dev intent to ship: Android's back closes a `<dialog>` / popover / CloseWatcher first, user-activation gated) — VibeSpace has none (no showModal / popover / CloseWatcher in src/lib), so nothing there applies. Predictive back: no Chrome documentation on same-document entries found; not measured.
- **The fix (PURE src/lib/back-guard.js + src/lib/mobile-back.js):** `bootStep` 'rebuild' — standing on a sentinel when wasDiscarded, the type is back_forward, or the Navigation API says the entry below is another document: `history.replaceState(null, '')` (the entry becomes this document's page entry) then the sentinel `push()`; a reload with the entry below same-document keeps. `exitPlan({ current, block, length })` over `navigation.entries()` — the contiguous same-origin block (主开发's rule: the browser exposes no other entry, so the page's index IS how many older entries stand below): null ⇒ the arm stays on the page's entry as before; else the arm re-arms AT ONCE and the next back inside 2 s (a popstate now) leaves with ONE `history.go(-(current + 1))`; the whole tab VibeSpace's (`history.length === block`) ⇒ `go(-current)` to the first entry — ONE load the diary names (`leave load 1`), no incident (主开发's rule); a go(-n) that did nothing (an entry outside the block was a FORWARD one) ⇒ 700 ms later the same named load. `backCostLoad` at boot — back_forward right after the previous document's rows (< 5 s), none a 'leave' ⇒ `app.autoCaptureIncident('a back press cost a page load', …, { toastKey })`, once per tab per 30 min. The rebuild's push without a tap was kept (never skipped) on every road measured.
- **The diary (NEW src/lib/nav-log.js):** 60 rows in sessionStorage `vibespace.navLog` — per tab, surviving every load in it; rows boot / pop / go1 / leave / hide / show / stale / cost / capture with a per-document id; never a URL (test-incident-recorder ⑥'s navNote census); every incident snapshot carries it (`navLog`). The stale-tab step (PURE `staleTabStep` in boot-ladder.js): ONE reload per server version per tab, then ONE notice («This tab still runs VibeSpace {old} after its one reload for {new} …», a warn toast), never a loop.
- **Census fallout:** test-record-clear-census H1 — the client's history writes are now exactly `history.pushState({ vs: 1 }, '')` + `history.replaceState(null, '')` (its control extended), storage rows `nav-log.js NAV_LOG_KEY` (telemetry) and `app.js noticeKey` (marker); test-boot-phase's stale-tab wait pin follows the line's new shape; test-back-guard §4 pins the ONE replaceState.
- **Chrome suite notes (test-mobile-back-chrome G/H):** ONE Chrome with `--disable-features=BackForwardCache`, `--window-size=382,580` (a discarded tab's restored page boots before any emulation reaches the new target — the window makes it a phone) and Local State for chrome://discards; attaching DevTools to a discarded, unloaded tab never finishes its handshake — show it first, attach after; the RED bundle = esbuild of the scratch tree with mobile-back.js's two anchors replaced (the base rule), served by swapping public/bundle.js (the index stamps `?v=<mtime>` per request); a capture's toast can be gone from the screen — judged from the toast history; a target created at about:blank keeps that entry (the tab-start leg creates it at the app's URL). Run by hand the suite needs VIBESPACE_SUITE_BUDGET_MS (the default 300 s budget fires before G ends); under the gate its row's 900 s holds the 480 s cap.
- **Not touched:** the phone home's boot rule (foryou-honest's lane).
- **Acceptance round 2 (主开发, two reviewers + two skeptics per finding; the second commit on 8449a450).** (1) MAJOR, reproduced: `history.go()` moves by JOINT-history steps and one iframe link followed inside an older VibeSpace document adds a step `navigation.entries()` never shows — tab [prev, V-old page, V-old sentinel, +1 iframe step, V-page, V-sentinel]: entries current 2 ⇒ go(-3) landed on V-old's page (a load; the probe's own CDP history list). (3) MINOR: the stale-tab stamp is written as the reload fires; `staleTabStep` gains `pending` (`this._staleReloadAt`) — test-boot-phase replays the app's own method over fake timers: two reconnects 300 ms apart ⇒ `reload@1 RELOAD@1 notice@2` (round 1: the notice on the OLD page before its reload). ### engine-distribution — P4 of the custom browser kernel: a plugin installed from a PRIVATE git repository with the `plugin-git` credential (files only, shredded); the kernel downloaded by VibeSpace into `kernelPath(id)` with a receipt; its version MEASURED once; the fleet's plugin installed at boot at its pinned sha and pre-trusted (D2) (BUILD lane on 77800e7d = browser-login, int358 pick 8; docs/design-custom-browser-plugin.zh.md §5 rewritten as built)
- **The credential row:** `plugin-git` in src/integration-registry.js — host · username (optional, empty = x-access-token) · token (secret) · deployKey (secret, `multiline` ⇒ the card's textarea). Validators gitHost / sshPrivateKey (a passphrase-protected key refused by name). clusterEnv + the presets' integrations.json. Test reachability = git ls-remote (the loader registers the runner over a repository it knows on that host). Consumer src/server/plugin-install.js (no `wiredIn`: it lands with its consumer). `groupOf`: the installer's rows are Plugins rows (`PLUGIN_INSTALL_CONSUMER`).
- **The git road (src/server/plugin-install.js):**
  - `gitSpecOf` (a tag / branch / full sha ref; `#ref` still read) and `credentialFor(spec, null | 'plugin-git' | 'auto')` through the store's `resolveIntegration` — refused `plugin_git_credential` when unset, the vault locked, for another host, or the wrong kind.
  - `credentialFiles`: a 0700 `.cred-*` folder; https = 0600 token + user + a 0700 askpass that cats them; ssh = a 0600 key named by `GIT_SSH_COMMAND -i … IdentitiesOnly BatchMode StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`.
  - `gitRun` is one child per step (init · `fetch --depth 1 -c credential.helper= -- <url> <ref|HEAD>` · checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD · rev-parse): serviceEnv(egress) + named switches, its timeout. §94 FIXED row.
  - `shredFile` (src/secret-file.js) on every way out. `GIT_CODES` by name; `plugin_tree_rejected` for every manifest / tree refusal; `testCredential` (ls-remote).
- **The loader (src/server/plugin-loader.js):**
  - `install({ref, credential, by})` records `{ref, sha, credential, by}`; a ref change is a source change.
  - D2: a fleet install of the id fleet.json names, at a FULL sha the clone arrived at, gets `trust {by:'fleet', sha, contentHash}` + enabled. `fleetTrustHolds` lets it hold only while all three still hold — a tag is never the anchor (主开发's pin, 2026-10-25: v0.1.2 = 7085e75f…).
  - `trustedBy` / `install.{ref, sha, by}` in `list()`, `installRecord(id)`, `fleet` on GET manifests; the route takes `ref` and `credential` (`plugin-git` only).
- **The kernel (PURE src/engine-kernel.js + ORCH src/server/engine-distribution.js):**
  - Inputs: kernel.json's verdict (the platform layout merged over the top one; the fleet's url + sha256 win), design 004's two hard rows factored into `downloadHardRows` (buildCompatVerdict asks it too, words unchanged).
  - Steps: https fetch with every hop https → sha256 → a LIST pass over node's zlib zstd + a streaming tar reader (ustar / GNU long names / pax) with every entry and the shape judged before a byte is written → the unpacked total vs the disk → extract → requiredFiles → `install-receipt.json {sha256 (the archive's), bytes (chrome's size), verifiedAt, version, archiveBytes, binarySha256}` → ONE rename.
  - `measure` = `--version` once (5 s, serviceEnv, §94 FIXED row) keyed by the receipt, on `data/browser-engines.json`.
  - Downloads start on a person's POST /api/browser/engines/:id/kernel, on a boot with `preinstall`, or on the FIRST USE (keeper: refused `browser_engine_kernel_missing` «VibeSpace is downloading it now»). An unwatched failure files ONE For-you notice per code (origin plugin).
- **Measured / declared:**
  - PURE `engineAnswerVerdict` takes the kernel side's optional `declaredVersion` / `integrity`; `engineChoiceVerdict` reads measured › reported › declared.
  - The keeper measures before the first launch, so the record's `browserChoice.version` is the measured one.
  - The card / Settings line: «· measured x · verified» / «· declared x (not measured)» / «downloading its kernel… N%» / the failure by code (`kernelFailWords`).
- **The cluster:** `bootFleet()` (server.js, 4 s after the listen, async). It installs when the record has no such id or a different source / ref, never a re-pull. `preinstall` ⇒ the kernel right away. Helm `customBrowser.preinstall` → fleet.json `browserEngine.preinstall` (parseBrowserEngineFact), the values documenting the ref as a FULL sha and the plugin-git integrations entry.
- **The no-echo gate (主开发 with the kernel side, 2026-10-25):** the real kernel sends no password in credentialSubmitted while the box still holds the vault's value. scripts/fixtures/fake-kernel.mjs `mode.omitFilledPassword` (+ `typeCredential`, `submissions()`) and test-browser-login ⑧b: a pending register promoted (new + ONE notice) · an existing login none (no write, no notice, the fill's use still written) · a typed-over value rides (agent-typed). RED control: a saveVerdict copy reading a missing password as «same». On their own stub too once it names the flag (today: SKIP with that evidence).
- **Census moves:**

- **Traps:**
  - A new file is invisible to §94 until `git add -N`.
  - The stage cleanup removes the credential folder, so "gone" proves nothing about a shred; a hard-link witness proves it (the token's inode holds other bytes).

- **Gates:**
  - test-plugin-trust 90 (③b +18: the git road over a real bare repository through a recording git + four RED copies);
  - test-plugin-loader 95 (②c +17 + RED);
  - test-browser-builds 198 (⑧ +29; 200 with the kernel side's package named — their kernel.json + their CLI stub measured);
  - test-browser-keeper 86 · test-integration-registry 324 · test-cluster-presets 269 · test-helm-render 87 · test-vault-law 88 (⑬) · test-browser-login 137 (⑧b);
  - NEW heavy test-plugin-git-clone 8 (a real clone over https on loopback; /proc swept);
  - the whole fast tier — see the lane report.
- **Round 2 (主开发's acceptance, 2026-10-25 — a second commit; each with a RED copy):**
  - The extract's writes: ONE `fileWriter` per file (one 'error' + one 'drain' listener from its creation) for `.part` and every entry. An injected ENOSPC is `disk` by name with no uncaughtException (the old code: an unheard 'error' — the hub's exit — and 24 'error' listeners piled on one 3 MB file). Its own first cut ignored `end()`'s error argument and landed a truncated file — the leg caught it.
  - `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` on every git child: a HOME url.insteadOf is never followed (fast: real git under the wrapper, rewriting to a second bare repository; heavy: a second https host on loopback sees no request, and the copy without it hands that host the token).
  - A Node without zstd (`zlib.createZstdDecompress`, 22.15+) ⇒ `engine_node_unsupported` in `kernelPlan` before any fetch, on the record for THAT Node, ONE notice, the card's words; the keeper's first use reads it. The copy without the gate fetches the archive and blames it.
  - The landing: a failing final rename puts the previous kernel BACK; an aside copy is restored before a landing could delete it.
  - credentialFiles shreds what it wrote when a later file throws (the hard-link witness).
  - The fleet's kernel is merged over the package's field by field; an http fleet URL ⇒ `engine_url_not_https` with zero requests, never the package's address.
  - A `./` root entry is the archive's root, never a second top folder.
  - Census: §86 engine-distribution 8 → 10. Suites: test-browser-builds 198 → 218, test-plugin-trust 90 → 96, test-plugin-git-clone 8 → 10 (the CA through a gitBin shim, since the HOME config is no longer read).
- **Round 3 (主开发's delta review, 2026-10-25 — a third commit; each with a RED copy):**
  - The writer settles on 'close', not 'finish'. Measured on Node 24.12: `end(cb)` answers at 'finish' with no error, and a close-time failure comes after it as 'error' then 'close' — so round 2's writer landed a file whose close failed (the owner's data/ is an NFS bind; close-to-open reports ENOSPC / EIO at close). After the close it compares the size on disk with the bytes written. Injected through the stream's `fs` option: a close-time ENOSPC on an entry or on `.part` ⇒ `disk`, nothing landed; a close that cuts the file to 699 of 700 bytes ⇒ refused by name. The copy that settles at 'finish' lands both.
  - The aside kernel is put back FIRST — in installKernel, in measure and once at boot (`bootRestore`, before the fleet's job) — with no download; a first use then launches it. A put-back that fails leaves the record with NO kernel (`engine_kernel_aside`; the old record kept as `aside` and restored with it), ONE For-you notice, the card's own line. So does a landing whose final rename and put-back both fail. An empty place (ENOENT) seen by measure drops the record's kernel. RED: a boot without the put-back, and the round-2 landing record — both say «installed» over an empty place.
  - git's trust root: `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` / `GIT_SSL_CAPATH` join `EGRESS_ENV` (src/agent-env.js; names that carry a path). Since round 2 a HOME `http.sslCAInfo` is not read, and this box's git 2.53 on libcurl-GnuTLS ignores SSL_CERT_FILE / DIR. Fast: real git under the child's env reads no HOME sslCAInfo, and the hub's GIT_SSL_CAINFO reaches every child. Heavy, real TLS: a CA named only in HOME is refused on the certificate; through the door the clone works, and the copy whose door lacks the names fails. The gitBin shim is gone; the suite uses the door. Recorded in design §5.1.
  - A malformed fleet sha256 ⇒ `engine_sha_malformed`, zero requests — the same shape as round 2's url. The silent fallback had two halves: src/preset-layers.js BLANKED a malformed sha (and clipped at 64, so a 65-hex value became a valid-looking pin), then the verdict took the package's. The fleet.json reader now keeps both kernel fields as named; a field of another type is named too (a number url ⇒ «not https»).
  - The user changelog gains ONE bullet under 2.369.356 (the Node floor line and the «not https» refusal).
  - Suites: test-browser-builds 218 → 232 (ci row restated 8.5 → 8.8 s; the fast sum stays 908 s under 910), test-plugin-trust 96 → 99, test-plugin-git-clone 10 → 12, test-agent-env (EGRESS_ENV pinned), test-cluster-presets §6 (kept as named).
- **Round 4 (主开发's delta review of round 3, 2026-10-25 — a fourth micro commit):** putBack's target predicate was ANY error. A `.removing-<tag>` leftover beside a GOOD kernel (reachable: the post-landing rm is `.catch(warn)`; an NFS silly-rename) plus ONE transient stat (EIO / ESTALE) renamed onto the non-empty place ⇒ engine_kernel_aside, the record's kernel dropped, a FALSE For-you notice — and nothing healed it (a later putBack returned before its restore branch; measure wrote only `measured`).
  - The put-back happens only onto a place whose stat answers ENOENT; any other answer is a transient (nothing moved, nothing said but the journal, asked again next time). A leftover beside a kernel in its place (its binary a file) is deleted, never put back over it. The put-back's stats ride the `io` seam (`io.stat`) so the transient is injectable.
  - `placeHeld`: a measure that finds the kernel in its place while the record holds none sets the record from the place's receipt (the `aside` record when it is that kernel; the aside failure cleared). The keeper also measures when the probe says installed but the record does not — so the next first use heals it.
  - Gates: test-browser-builds ⑫c (a) / (b) / (c) + RED (12) round 3's predicate, (13) no heal, (14) the keeper's round-3 condition — 232 → 239, 8.3–8.8 s alone (the ci row's 8.8 s holds). Census: §86 engine-distribution 11 → 10 (two direct stats now ride the seam, whose default is one site).
- **Open:**
  - ssh host keys are TOFU (accept-new) — a `knownHosts` field is not built.
  - The kernel's redirects are https-only but not host-limited (the sha256 is the authenticity).
  - The peer still owes: the stub's `omitFilledPassword` default flip (v0.1.3); `/probe`'s `declaredVersion` + `integrity` (the settled contract — our fixture answers both; their plugin process was not run here, only their kernel.json and CLI stub); the real kernel.json url / sha256 for a fleet artifact host.
  - A «Download kernel» button on the card (the route exists; the card says the state and the first use downloads).

A row = `switchDesktop`: `stage.leave(id)` when staged, else `dm.switchTo(id)`, then `_showOnDesk` (§6b guard 10: the window this tab showed there, else `_focusMostRecent` — re-looked every 250 ms for 4 s while a lazy replay lands, unless the person pressed something).

Its desktop tabs now take `switchDesktop` too (the base switched and left the old desktop's hidden window active — the phone showed nothing until a row was tapped).
- **§6b guard 10 hole closed:** `_noteShown` ran in a switch's in-between (the new desktop active, the old desktop's window still `activeWindowId`) and noted the OLD desktop's window as the new desktop's window on show — it now skips a window of another desktop.

### draft-focus-guard — a draft another client saved never replaces what you are typing (FIX, B-b0fa — the naive-user walk 2026-10-25, report §P1-2, re-run by an independent verifier)
- **The case:** two clients on one conversation; B's 300 ms autosave landed in A's FOCUSED box mid-sentence («oko好，退款那条也改成同样的策略\nk» was sent); a×8 / b×8 interleaved left one «a» in both boxes; B's own pending autosave then saved the overwritten value back (the typing lost on both sides). `_draftSyncHandler` ended with `this._textarea.value = value || ''`, the autosave saved the box when it fired.
- **One verdict, the same family:** PURE `landDraft` joins src/queue-putback.js next to `landDraftPrepend` (which stays the put-back's arithmetic and is landDraft's first row): putback · superseded · same · focused ⇒ hold · typing ⇒ hold · typed-here ⇒ hold · free ⇒ replace (`DRAFT_LANDING_TABLE`). chat-input.js only applies it (`_landDraft`); the held value waits in `_heldDraft` — the store already has it, so holding sends nothing and no frame type is new.
- **Re-judge points:** the box's own autosave (supersedes — its timer now nulls itself, so `dirty = _draftTimer !== null` is honest; `_send` nulls it too), `_send` after the box empties (the pin supersedes; a send without text lets it land), and the textarea's blur via `afterPress`: a press on Send blurs the box BEFORE its click sends, so the judge waits until no pointer is down, then one task (one pair of window capture listeners per page; 10 s cap for a release the page never saw). Measured: judged AT the blur, a real press on Send sent the held «hello world» instead of the typed «hello» (test-draft-focus-chrome ③ RED).
- **Focus = `document.hasFocus()` and the box active:** a background window's box got its blur and is not «focused» — a phone's draft still lands on an idle desktop window, as before. `_draftTaken` (what the box last took from the store) adds `typed-here`: a held value never deletes words typed since unless it keeps every character of them (another device continued the text), so leaving the box after two devices typed at once does not throw away your words.
- **Belts:** a replace clears any pending autosave (no autosave writes back what it replaced); `storeBefore` is `null` while a draft is held (the pinless deferred clear must not take another client's draft).
- **Gates:** test-queue-putback 156 (§0 the landing block + the autosave callback cut verbatim; §8 the rows, a 1536-combination grid, two composers on the real StateSync world — RED = the 2.369.354 composer: «x» lost on both sides, 8 and 15 of 16 lost); NEW heavy test-draft-focus-chrome 16 (two pages in two windows on one Antigravity conversation; RED = the overwrite sends «okok策略», loses 8 / 15 of 16; a judge at the blur sends «hello world»); test-queue-steer 897 (its storeBefore pin re-pinned); test-phone-composer-chrome 39.
- **Residual:** one register per conversation — two devices typing at once each keep their own words and the store keeps the last save; words superseded that way live only in their box until it closes.

## 2.369.354 — 2026-10-25

### close-toast-wording — the «asked to close» toast names why the second ✕ stops the app (主开发, owner 2026-10-25)
- src/lib/desktop-app-window.js:843 + zh/ja keys: «Asked {app} to close — no agent is using it, so pressing ✕ again within {n} s stops the app». The A2 verdict (src/desktop-fit.js outerCloseVerdict) is unchanged: a leased (agent-held) app closes the view only; a user-held app gets the app's own close, then Stop on a second press. kb-file-structure A2 paragraph carries the rule.

### claude-wrapper-queue — Claude's mid-turn queue is the WRAPPER's: a message sent during a turn is held by data/bin/chat-wrapper.js, Stop drops it and puts it back, nothing runs after Stop (BUILD, the owner 2026-10-25 «可以 按照你推荐来» — open question ① of stop-refills-composer)
- **Why:** stop-refills-composer (.353) MEASURED on Claude Code 2.1.308 with a local mock of `POST /v1/messages` that the CLI RUNS a frame it queued itself mid-turn right after `control_request {subtype:'interrupt'}` (dequeued AT the interrupt, a new turn +27 ms) — VibeSpace never held that message, so Stop could neither stop it nor put it back, and the 2026-09-07 law («Stop means stop») did not hold on claude. Re-measured here: +22 / +25 ms.
- **The wrapper (data/bin/chat-wrapper.js):** `promptQueue` items `{id, ts, line (the WHOLE stdin frame — images included), msgId, origin, text, preview, attachments, buffered}`; `publishQueue()` → top-level `queue_changed {items:[{id, msgId, preview, text?, ts, kind, from}], turn_id:null, verbs}` + sidecar `meta.queue`; `queued_input {msg_id}` per hold; the advert `caps {frameFile, inputQueue:true, queueVerbs:['remove','reorder','edit'], queueResync:true}` + a BASELINE empty publication at boot; `queue-op` (remove / reorder with afterId null = the front + anchor-gone / edit BY EXCLUSION — the first text block takes the words, an image stays; steer ⇒ not-steerable, run-* ⇒ not-startable, an unknown id ⇒ gone) and `queue-resync`, neither ever forwarded; the drain = ONE held frame per turn end, in the strip's order; Stop (`control_request interrupt` on stdin) = per-item `queue_op_result {reason:'stopped'}` → ONE `queue_dropped` (the person's rows — a frame with `webui_origin` is dropped, never put back; the BYTE-IDENTICAL droppedRecordFor twin, the fourth) → the emptied `queue_changed` → THEN the interrupt line goes on to the CLI as before (the server's 2 s SIGINT fallback unchanged). A frame-file body joins the history buffer when it reaches the CLI, never at the hold.
- **THE TURN GATE — the brief's predicate was MEASURED wrong, and so was this lane's first one:** the brief named `meta.streaming` («flips on the child's user record») — but in stream-json the CLI never echoes a prompt on stdout (2.1.308: the only user records are tool results and «[Request interrupted…]»), so a text-only turn never set it. The lane's first gate ended a turn at `session_state_changed idle` — MEASURED wrong too: a BACKGROUND AGENT keeps the session 'running' past the turn's `result` (no idle until the agent ends, ~12 s in the probe) while the CLI takes a new prompt at once (+114 ms) — waiting for idle would keep the person behind background work (test-claude-wrapper-queue ⑥'s control: held 7.9 s). The FINAL gate (`turnBusy`): OPENED by the wrapper itself the moment it writes a user frame (no echo to race: a frame written in the same tick is held) and by the CLI's own turn start — a top-level `system/init` said WHILE the CLI's last state word is running / requires_action (every turn has an init; the turn the CLI starts itself for a background task's notification has ONLY an init — no state change). A STATE word alone opens nothing: after the turn's result a background helper's permission ask says `requires_action` (and its work `running`) while no turn runs and the CLI takes a new prompt — test-helper-ask-ui's bridge probe caught a version that opened on it. An init said while idle or before any state opens nothing either: the real CLI says nothing before its first input (fresh or `--resume`, measured), but older suite stubs say an init at startup and wedged a version that opened on any init (test-chat-send-landing / -hygiene-ui / -scroll / channel-jump / inbox-window-ui / inbox-reply-ui / chat-proposal-card red until fixed; test-queue-putback §6 pins it with an any-init CONTROL); CLOSED by the turn's top-level `result` or `idle`; an `idle` that arrives after we wrote a frame and before that frame's turn started (`awaitingStart`) belongs to the turn before it and is ignored (the drain writes on a result, that turn's idle follows 1–2 ms later). A background Bash does not hold the session (idle follows the result). Measured: EVERY user frame starts with init and ends in `result`, local slash commands included (/context, /cost, an unknown /command, an empty or blank text, an empty array); a frame whose `message.content` is neither a string nor an array is IGNORED by the CLI without a word (no running, no result) — such a frame never opens the gate. `{type:'user'}` with no message makes the CLI exit 1 (unchanged; never sent by VibeSpace).
- **The frame names its message (src/adapters/claude-code.js):** `formatChatInput(text, msgId, {origin})` puts `webui_msg_id` (+ `webui_origin` for auto-resume / dispatch — server.js auto-resume and src/server/user-input.js pass it) at the frame's TOP LEVEL; a client-built frame (an image paste) is SPLICED (`{"webui_msg_id":…,` in front of its first key — never re-encoded). MEASURED: the CLI accepts unknown top-level keys and strips them (the transcript never holds them), so a pre-.354 wrapper that forwards the frame verbatim loses nothing — no caps gate needed on the send path. `formatQueueOp` real (the acp frame vocabulary), `formatQueueResync`.
- **The caps row + the rest:** src/backend-caps.js claude `inputModes.queueVerbs: ['remove','reorder','edit']` (+ the client mirror in src/lib/agent-meta.js; `deriveInputModes` does the rest — queueOps true, steer false); the ws `queue-op` case unchanged (its `no-queue-ops` refusal was already by the CAP; an old claude wrapper now gets the `wrapper-no-queue` sentence «predates the input-queue update … Terminate + Resume»); the ws attach asks `queue-resync` of a claude wrapper that adverts it. server.js `CLAUDE_STREAM_TYPES` learns `queued_input` / `queue_changed` / `queue_op_result` / `queue_dropped` (same line — the 1907-line budget). src/server/stdout/claude-stream-json.js passes them to the normalizer untouched (it spells none of them — test-queue-putback §5 pins that the put-back door sits at the gate). src/message-manager.js: `userMessageIds` + `webuiMsgId` stamped on a bubble from a `_fromWebui` record's msgId, `_stampQueueChip` / `_processQueuedInput` / `_processQueueChanged` / `_processQueueOpResult` (+ `queueOpFailureText`), `queue_dropped` → the base `_processQueueDropped`. Client: nothing new — the strip, the chips, the hint («Enter queues», no Alt+Enter), Session Properties' «Sending during a turn» row and the .353 put-back/toast all follow the caps row.
- **Spend:** a drained frame is the PERSON's turn (or VibeSpace's own already-authorized machine turn) deferred to the turn end — the same frame through the same typed door; no new SITE (test-spend-paths 366 green; this lane adds no producer to its census).
- **Measurements (real CLI 2.1.308, the wrapper over a local mock, no vendor traffic; base b214278b's wrapper = the RED control):** ① Stop — lane: B never reaches the mock, no queue-operation for it in the transcript, `queue_dropped {B}`, no turn after Stop; base: B requested +22–25 ms after the interrupt (enqueued at send, dequeued AT the interrupt). ② drain — lane: B's request +16 ms after A's `idle`, its enqueue only at the drain, a plain user record; base: the CLI enqueued B at send and ran it inside A's own running…idle span. ③ same-tick burst — lane: held at +2 ms, before the CLI's first record at +4 ms; base: the CLI enqueued B 5 ms after A. ④ a background Agent (`run_in_background`) — raw CLI: the turn's result at +127 ms, NO idle until the agent ended (+12.2 s), a prompt sent at +2.2 s requested +114 ms later; a background Bash: idle right after the result. Through the lane wrapper: B reached the CLI 116 ms after send while the agent worked; the idle-only gate (control) held it 7.9 s. Probes and run summaries: the lane dir's measure/ (probe-raw.mjs, probe-wrapper.mjs, runs/).
