### lane path-field — ONE path field at every door: the candidates come from the person's own groups, folders and history, computed for the machine in question; a typed value takes effect on blur or says why not (L1 of the New Session train; base c8aa8820 2.369.344)
- **Why:** the owner accepted POC v2.2 (area-first-new-conversation, 2026-10-23 05:3x 「没啥问题」); its `rankCandidates` and the field's behaviour in poc/designs/area-first-poc/Main.html are the spec, now product code. Before: `setupDirAutocomplete` at seven doors — a parent listing + prefix filter, a task's folders floated on top, Enter-only, no relative paths, no remote recommendations beyond a host's recent cwds, the day-one chips PRESELECTED ~/vibespace on a fresh pod (study round 4: the product's own checkout holds the most files).
- **THE RULE (NEW PURE src/path-candidates.js, imports nothing):** `resolveRelative(input, bases, listing, {files})` (the bases in order — the selected groups' folders in selection order → the field's own context → home; every base that has it is a resolution, the first used; a link to a folder resolves to its target; an exact hit beats a completion), `rankCandidates(query, {bases, groups, recent, listing, name, machine, files, self})` (the POC's function byte-for-byte in its scoring: ① the groups' folders, one absent on the machine greyed with the create road · ② 由名字 one `<group folder>/<name>` per SELECTED group in selection order + `~/<name>`, a bare word plays the name when it is empty, −3000 so it never beats a real hit · ③ recent with counts · ④ the listing under the typed prefix / the whole-path fuzzy: segment prefix > subsequence > token, CJK plain · ⑤ mounts), `missingVerdict` (parent there ⇒ create; missing ⇒ said), `groupOn` (a group as seen from one machine: probed / declared `host::/abs` / absent), `isExcludedPath` (the ADDENDUM: the instance checkout, its data dir, dot-folders — never offered unasked, typed explicitly they resolve; a group folder or a recent one the person made stays theirs), `sliceListing` / `mergeListing` / `sliceAsk` (the hub's raw facts ⇄ the field's per-machine memory), `fuzzyFilter`, `recentCounts`, `legacySuggestions`. Words never live there: chips / whys / lines are `{ key, params }`, the field says them through t().
- **THE SERVER:** `GET /api/dir-complete` takes `bases` / `q` / `probe` / `kind` and answers the listing slice + `self` + `took` (+ `partial`) BESIDE the old `suggestions` (a caller sending none of the new params gets the old shape). NEW src/server/dir-slice.js: two NEW SafeFs ops (`dirSlice` — each asked folder listed once with its facts, `known` mtime ⇒ `same`; `dirIndex` — the folder index, 4 levels, ≤ 6000, dot / dependency folders, the checkout + data dir and every mount skipped, a budget inside the worker), a listing cache per folder with mtime invalidation (reused < 2 s, else re-stated), the index kept 30 s and refreshed BEHIND an answer, the whole answer raced against the 450 ms budget (a SafeFs deadline is never shortened — a timeout terminates the worker). `GET /api/home-folders` drops the excluded folders (day one starts in work/, not ~/vibespace).
- **THE HOST RUNG (the owner's note ④ «为啥在 mac 选项下就没有默认路径推荐了？»):** `hosts.dirSlice` runs ONE sh script there (NEW PURE src/dir-slice-script.js: list / probe / index / mounts / the Mac's display names via mdls) over the device link's runCmd first, the ssh rung otherwise, and the SAME sliceListing builds the answer; the index kept 60 s per machine (refreshed behind), the display names 10 min. `/api/hosts/:id/dir-complete` takes the same params; `/api/hosts/:id/recent-cwds` answers `recent: [{path, count, last}]` beside `cwds`. The brief said the rung «already knows» the Mac's display names — it did not (no code read them); the script asks mdls kMDItemDisplayName.
- **THE COMPONENT (NEW src/lib/path-field.js; its contract is frozen for the train's other lanes, new-session-form and task-group-context):** `pathField(input, {bases, groupsOf, host, kind, onCommit, name, onState, create, createWhen, picker, chips, id})` → `{el, input, value, verdict, commit, set, refresh, open, close, ensure, destroy}`; `appGroups(selectedIds)` (every door's default groupsOf: the person's groups) and `pathSuggest(text)` (the palette). The list floats in a body-level layer (inline on the phone), never pops by itself (a press, typing, ↓ or a Tab INTO the field), closes through utils.js onOutsidePress (§59); BLUR COMMITS deferred past pointer-up; 「未生效：…」 with 「用第一名」; the «不存在 — 创建？» tick (a 新建 row picked IS the consent), `ensure()` makes it; THE PICKER (createModalShell over the dialog: pinned groups with badges, the tree without the excluded folders, a preview with files / sizes / dates, «新建文件夹» inline, «选这个文件夹», the last node per `id` in localStorage, opening on a search).
- **THE DOORS:** New Session (app.js — the Create button awaits `commit()` + `ensure()`, the dialog's Enter skips while the field prevented it; the day-one chips row `_fillCwdRecent` kept as it was, its chips fill through the field — L2 owns the form), the storage / machine-mount dialogs (mounts-dialog.js — what takes effect is written back absolute, a mount point may be made once ticked, Submit commits each path field first; sftp's key path declares `pathKind: 'file'`), the app launcher's working directory, the Task Group panel's three (Link folder — Enter OR leaving links it; Context folder; Export / Import file — L3 re-wires these to the Context table on this field), the Files path bar (no folder button: the window IS the browser; the line under it only shows what did not take), the tour's first chat, the session palette's /path (pathSuggest). src/lib/autocomplete.js DELETED; its CSS replaced by the path field's.
- **CENSUS:** test-architecture §98 (NEW) — setupDirAutocomplete gone, every door row names its live call, every path-shaped input (markup id / class / placeholder, a `.placeholder = t('…folder…')`, a file-path-input) covered or exempt with a reason; planted controls. PURE set + 2; §86 reader counts moved (safe-fs-worker 24 → 39: the two new ops; files.js 42 → 43: the slice's SafeFs door); §59 the list's closer is onOutsidePress; §78 the package name is a constant (`SELF_PACKAGE`).
- **TESTS:** NEW test-path-candidates (fast, PURE, 57: the POC rank-test ported with its fixture and its 13 cases — scores identical to the POC's log — + the exclusion with a RED CONTROL), NEW test-dir-complete (fast, 39, ~2.3 s: the real files router over a temp HOME, the budget, the mtime cache, the host rung with a FAKE Mac — the real HostManager, its ssh rung run here), NEW test-path-field-chrome (heavy, 42: the component in real Chrome in zh against the real routes). test-mounts-dialog-extract draws both variants' path inputs as one canonical box before its pixel compare (the field is the ONE deliberate change; both count the same rows); test-slack-landing-nologin stubs path-field.js where it stubbed autocomplete.js.

### lane task-group-context — a Task Group's Context table: the standing instructions first, every path a row told at a chosen depth (four levels), a live preview of what a new conversation receives (base c8aa8820 = 2.369.344)
- **Why:** naive-user study 3 (findings C1–C4): files reached agents as names only, one rule lived in three drifting copies (objective + POLICY.md + desk CLAUDE.md, the last only for conversations started in that folder), and «what it reads» was invisible. The owner accepted the POC v2.2 Group board (2026-10-23 05:3x) with ONE change: 告诉 agent gains a level between 文件名 and 内容.
- **The record (ONE commit, NO version bump):** `ctx` = ONE ordered list on the Task Group (PURE src/task-context.js): `{ path (as typed), note, tell: note|names|index|contents|null, tags: discover|notes|readonly, share: null|ro|rw, keys? }` or `{ ref, note }`. A relative path resolves against the row above's folder, then the group's first folder, then home (the first that exists; `resolveRows` over the store's stat behind the mount door). DERIVED, never stored twice: the 自动发现会话 rows = the old `folders[]` (`foldersOf`, recursive — `groupsForSession`, the sidebar's `_folderPaths`), the 记笔记 row = the old `contextDir` (`contextDirOf` — the `.vibespace/TASK.md` mirror, ctx-sync, the CLI's brief). The live record holds NO old field: `_holdLegacy` moves them into `_legacy` at load, `_save` writes them back beside the record (one release), `migrateContextRows` is their only reader. The wire (`list()` / `view()`) carries `ctx` + `ctxRes` + the DERIVED `folders` / `contextDir`, so the New Session dialog (lane new-session-form's) and every other reader keep working untouched. The old write doors (create / PATCH `folders` / `contextDir` — the CLI's --folder / --context-dir on other hosts, a manager agent, an old bundle) become the rows they mean (`applyLegacyPatch`).
- **ONE migration** `2026-10-task-group-context-rows` (src/server/migrations.js via the runner, at most once): THROUGH the live TaskGroupManager (server.js hands `tasks` in on the existing create line — no new line), the file atomically without one; folders[] → rows 文件名 + 自动发现会话, contextDir → a row 文件名 + 记笔记 (one row when it IS a folder); a group with `ctx` skipped; an unreadable store fails by name. Owner-shaped (masked) fixtures from the instance's 6 groups: folder + a notes folder inside it, two folders, a non-recursive folder (now recursive — counted), contextDir only ×2, a folder typed with a literal `/**` (it matched nothing before and matches nothing now — the row says «not there»; flagged for the owner), contextDir = a folder (merged).

Every ci.yml setup step carries timeout-minutes (a few times its measured worst; the suite steps keep their job's), and ci-apt.sh gives up a stalled connection at 30 s and an apt call at 80 s by name. test-ci-gate §2h holds all of it (20 mutant copies of ci.yml / ci-fonts.sh, each red for its own reason, + the road over a file:// fixture serving the wrong bytes); §2f runs the apt bound over a stub that never answers. ### lane hub-dies-dead-ssh-host — a paired ssh machine that cannot be reached never stops the hub (the .346 verify round's CONFIRMED HIGH; base 3180045d 2.369.346)
- **Why:** lane new-session-verify (report claim 3): a hosts.json record for an unreachable ssh machine, picked in the New Session host row ⇒ the hub's last journal line `Error: write EPIPE at WriteWrap.onWriteComplete`, every later request refused — 2 of 4 runs on the int tree. Mechanism: src/hosts.js fed ssh children on stdin with NO `'error'` listener (`child.stdin.end(tar)` ×2, `.end(script)`, `.end(JSON op)`, `.write(bootstrapScript())`); ssh to a machine it cannot reach exits at once (BatchMode), the bytes meet a closed pipe, the stream error is uncaught and server.js's uncaughtException handler exits the hub. Same shape in src/remote-fs.js `write` and src/machine-mounts.js `_run`.
- **Measured before (base 3180045d, this lane's probes/walk w3x-roads.mjs: a scratch hub, the dead record, a stub `ssh` exiting 255 first on PATH — never a real machine):** «install tools» on the dead machine ⇒ the hub DIES 2/2 (`write EPIPE`, every later request «fetch failed»). The verify round's exact New Session walk (w3c-sshdead.mjs, fake-Mac rung + real harvest) survived 4/4 on this box today — it reaches no stdin road at this box's timing (only `_run`'s `printf $HOME` and the git probe, no stdin); the crash is timing-bound there (a pipe smaller than the payload), deterministic on any payload bigger than a pipe holds (the tools tar is MBs). In-process, the base's HostManager over the five roads: 2 uncaught EPIPEs, 9 ssh spawns, errors without a name.
- **THE ONE FEED (src/hosts.js `feedStdin(child, bytes)`):** attaches the stdin `'error'` listener BEFORE the first write, keeps the error as `fed.error` (never a throw); `sshRefusal(h, err, stderr, fed)` names the failure — `host-unreachable` (ssh's own exit 255 / no answer in the bound) or `ssh-exited-early` (EPIPE / ECONNRESET / ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED with another exit) — with the machine's id + name + ssh's last stderr line; a remote command's own failure keeps the caller's words. All five hosts.js feeds + remote-fs `write` + machine-mounts `_run` go through it (machine-mounts' result carries `refusal`); `bootstrap` also listens on the child's `'error'` (no ssh binary) and its `done` event carries `refusal`. Exported: `feedStdin`, `sshRefusal`, `unreachableError`, `refusalBody`.
- **THE HOST RUNG REFUSES BY NAME BEFORE ANY SPAWN:** `hosts.reachable(id)` — a live device link ⇒ yes, a fresh `_hostDownUntil` memo ⇒ no (no spawn either way), else ONE `ssh -o ConnectTimeout=3 … true` over `_ssh` (BatchMode, the shared ControlMaster — a yes warms it; a test's patched `_ssh` answers it too), single-flight per machine, verdict kept 60 s; `refuseUnreachable(id)` throws `unreachableError` (code `host-unreachable`). Called first by `dirComplete` / `dirSlice` (ssh machines; a dial device answers through its link as before), `GET /api/hosts/:id/recent-cwds`, RemoteFs `home` (`/api/home?host=` ⇒ 400 `code: host-unreachable`, FS_REFUSALS). The dir-complete routes (exit-routes + files.js `?host=`) answer `{ suggestions: [], error, unreachable: { host, hostId, line } }`.
- **THE FIELD (src/lib/path-field.js):** the answer's `unreachable` is the machine's fact in WORLD (cleared by the next answer without it); the verdict is `{ status: 'unreachable', text: «my-mac 连不上 — 用本机路径或稍后再试» }`, the line under the field and the list say it, the list offers nothing for that machine (no «not on my-mac» guesses), and New Session's footer refuses Create with the same words (`createRefusal` takes `unreachable`); switching the machine back to this one is a usable form at once. i18n en / zh / ja.
- **CENSUS (test-architecture §101):** (a) the ssh roads (hosts.js, remote-fs.js, machine-mounts.js, server/dial-pairing.js, remote-shell.js) write no child's stdin themselves — `feedStdin(child, ` counted 5 / 1 / 1 / 0 / 0, its body listens before its write; (b) everywhere else in src/ + server.js (git ls-files) an unlistened `X.stdin.write|end(` (no `X.stdin.on('error'` in the 25 lines above) is a counted DEBT101 ratchet — 22 sites in 11 files (src/agentd/ = the signed device bundle, untouched here; codex-reset-helper, codex-thread-read, desktop-mic, desktop-sound, input-inject, server/cli-usage-door = local children) — a new site is red, a fixed one must lower its pin; (c) CONTROLS: a bare `child.stdin.end(tar)` in hosts.js, the helper's listener after its write, an unlistened write in a new file — each red; a listened one green.
- **TESTS:** test-dir-complete ⑦ (fast, in-process; the real HostManager + a stub ssh on PATH): five keystrokes + a dirComplete refused BY NAME with ONE probe spawn, the route says `unreachable`, a machine that answers keeps its rung; the five stdin roads with payloads bigger than a pipe ⇒ every one `host-unreachable`, 0 uncaught; RED CONTROL a mutant hosts.js whose feedStdin does not listen ⇒ uncaught EPIPEs. test-restore-liveness §7 (heavy): a REAL worktree hub with the dead record ⇒ the tools install 400 «my-mac cannot be reached — ssh: …», the harvest names it, dir-complete / recent-cwds `unreachable`, home 400 host-unreachable, the next request 200, no `write EPIPE` in the journal; RED CONTROL the same hub with the no-listener copy DIES (exit, EPIPE, next request refused).

### lane signin-card-real-screen — the .344 Claude sign-in card never showed a link on a real CLI; the chat's «not logged in» was no card; the guided terminal went deaf (hotfix; base c8aa8820 2.369.344)
- **Measured (study naive-cluster-4, two fresh fleet pods on Claude Code 2.1.309, reproduced here on 2.1.308).** `claude auth login --claudeai` prints «Opening browser to sign in…», «If the browser didn't open, visit: <OSC-8 link>», and the prompt «Paste code here if prompted >» on the VERY NEXT line. `oat-mint-model findUrl` returned a URL only before a BLANK line, the 2.1.296 setup-token shape. So every run sat at «starting» with url null for the 10-minute TTL, and the card kept showing a pressable «Sign in» (`signinCardView` mapped starting → no-login). Each press hit 409 `signin_running`, and the card answered with a NEW `sub-*` row (3 rows on naive40, 2 on naive41).
- **The reader (one, both roads).** `findUrl(text, raw)` reads the OSC-8 hyperlink's TARGET first (whole however the text wraps, complete once its terminator arrived), else the visible text: to the end of its line, wrapped pieces joined, ended by a blank line, a line of words or the prompt. A `KNOWN_LINES` table + `screenUnknown` say when the screen ends on a line no row places. Fixtures are the captures, byte-exact: `scripts/fixtures/claude-signin/cli-2.1.308-auth-login.pty` and `cli-2.1.309-auth-login.txt` (query redacted; the same screen line for line). RED on c8aa8820: the base reader reads `[code-prompt]` only.
- **The owner's fallback (04:2x, 「如果解析不出来还能切换成旧模式查看」).** Each run keeps its raw PTY bytes in memory (`rawAppend`/`rawSince`, a 64 KB ring), answered only to the asking page by `GET /api/accounts/:id/signin/screen` and `…/oat/mint/:mid/screen` (`?from=`, no-store, human-only). Never broadcast, logged or written; only the cue rides the snapshot: `rawHint` 'stalled' (no link N = 4 s after the first output) or 'unknown' (an unplaced line standing last). The CLIENT `RawScreen` (src/lib/raw-screen.js) draws it read-only in a small xterm with the code box below; `sendCode` takes a code while `starting` + the cue. 「切换原始画面」 is always there while a run lives, and a later recognised state flips the parsed view back. The mint road freezes its screen BEFORE the token's success screen (`RAW_STOP_RE`). On both roads the tty's echo of the pasted code reads as • (`rawSince` mask), so test-oat-mint §4's one-road law holds; two new RED mutants prove it. test-oat-mint-ui caught two false flips mid-mint: the token's wrapped success screen, and the tty's echo of the code on its own line. The token screen never flips now, the echoed code is a known line (`typed`), and RawScreen opens its xterm only once its box is in the page (opened on a detached box, xterm's viewport sync threw).
- **One run per account.** `start` on a live run answers `{ok, joined}` with that run; `accounts.pendingSignin` hands a row with a live run to the next press (`joined`) before an idle one. The card disables its button while live («Starting the sign-in…»); a joined card's close leaves the run to its starter. The boot / start sweep of never-signed-in rows past the TTL (door-signin-fixes) covers the pods' debris rows: they are all marked.
- **The chat road (measured on real 2.1.308, scratch config, no credentials, fixture `cli-2.1.308-not-logged-in.jsonl`).** The CLI no longer DIES not-logged-in. It answers each turn with a synthetic assistant record (`model <synthetic>`, `error authentication_failed`, `is_api_error_message`, «Not logged in · Please run /login») and waits, so `classifyCliDeath` (untouched) never ran. `/login` gets `local_command_outcome {kind: unavailable_headless}`. Fix: a PURE table row (`signin-model LIVE_WALLS`/`liveWallOf`) read by the claude stream consumer → WS `signin-wall`; the chat makes it the same wall as a death (read-only, the card; Codex/remote keep the terminal bar). «Send my message again» on a live wall kills the CLI, waits for `exited` (or 15 s), then resumes. A signed-in live wall with nothing waiting restarts in place. chat-input intercepts `/login` (before `/goal`) → the card.
- **The default account (主开发 04:27, approved with conditions).** A fresh pod has no Claude default and no machine login, so a chat after the card's sign-in still ran on the signed-out global login. The finalize route reads `signinPending` before finalize clears it. PURE `firstSigninDefault` makes the card's row the default through `accounts.setDefault` (the one default road) only when there is no Claude default, the machine login file is signed out, the platform is not darwin (the Keychain is unknowable) and there is no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The answer carries `madeDefault`; the card says «Set as your default account · change it in Manage agents». An existing default is never swapped.
- **The terminal link.** The «dangerous link» confirm was xterm's OWN `linkHandler` default for an OSC-8 hyperlink, not the WebLinksAddon (door-signin-card fixed only the addon). Fix: `src/lib/terminal-links.js` (`openTerminalLink` + `TERMINAL_LINK_HANDLER`) on every `new Terminal(` and every `new WebLinksAddon(`. test-terminal-zoom-select adds the census plus a real CDP click on an OSC-8 link: the no-handler control pops the confirm, the product handler opens a tab.
- **The dead guided modal (naive41 R2, naive42 R3).** The page was suspended (68 s on the claude.ai tab), its socket came back, typed keys never echoed, and the HTTP done-poll still flipped it to ✓. app.js re-attaches only the terminals in `app.sessions`; `runGuidedCli`'s modal terminal is not one, so it re-attaches itself on `onStateChange(true)` now. 主开发's TTL hypothesis is refuted by test-claude-signin ⑰: real node-pty, a run's TTL kills its own helper tree only, and a second PTY on the same account dir lives on. The Advanced road's Claude «Log in» now opens the card's own run on its raw screen (`rawFirst`, sticky; a live run is joined). Codex keeps the guided terminal.
- **Gates.** New / extended suites: test-signin-model (56), test-oat-mint (151), test-claude-signin (76), test-signin-card-ui (66), test-setup-flows (16), test-terminal-zoom-select (census + OSC-8 click), test-day-one-chrome (a 60 s CDP freeze + socket drop, then typed keys echo in the guided modal). The ci.mjs fast rows were re-measured. Owner-run re-measure on the next CLI: `script -qfc 'claude auth login --claudeai' /tmp/cap.pty` under `env -i HOME=<scratch> CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<empty scratch> BROWSER=true PATH=…`, kill it at the prompt, replace the fixture, run test-signin-model ⑦ + test-claude-signin ⑮.

### gate red — the 2.369.344 branch run (ci/hotfix-344 = d3595662, Actions run 39925587509) red on THREE heavy suites: test-worktree-userchan-ui (shard 3), test-claude-hot-switch (shard 5), test-channels-i18n (shard 3) (lane ci-344-reds; base d3595662 = the .344 cut; one user-visible fix: the first-week rail's floor)

The fact is a filter, not a fact to carry, so carrying it would be a dead row. Fix (test-only): `purpose` joins the census's HANDLED set, pinned by a new leg (the `isSignInRow(ws)` continue at the top of the webui loop + day-one.js `row.purpose === SIGN_IN`); a mutant without the filter, or reading another key, fails the pin. No user-visible change (the row was already dropped). 86/86 ×3 (base: 83 passed, 2 failed).
- **Red 2 — test-claude-hot-switch «✗ the measurement ran — exit 3 … 168.63.129.16:53 = -1 ENETUNREACH», «✗ baseline … ABORTED», «✗ THE VERDICT on 2.1.309».** Not an unreachable runner network, and not 2.1.309. claude (2.1.308 too, measured from strace's sendmmsg payloads) resolves `api.anthropic.com` at start even with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL on the mock. This box's resolver is 127.0.0.53 (a loopback connect); the runner's is 168.63.129.16, so inside the loopback-only namespace the lookup is refused (ENETUNREACH), the belt kills the CLI at that first off-loopback connect, every turn comes back ABORTED with `accts: []`, and the gate judged that empty record as "the CLI kept its member". Fix (test-only): ① `measuredOf(r, rec)` — exit 3 / `aborted` / every step ABORTED / nothing answered + ENETUNREACH|EAI_AGAIN ⇒ ONE `SKIP: unmeasured — <reason>` line; REFUSED ⇒ the cannot-run SKIP as before; an OPEN namespace ⇒ RED; a record that RAN ⇒ `verdictRows` (the shipped judgement, unchanged, NOTE included). ② scripts/measure-claude-cred-read.mjs, namespace rung: each non-loopback nameserver goes ON lo inside the measurement's existing `sudo unshare -n` shell (no new namespace), and the belt counts an address on lo as loopback; the record carries `resolver` + `loAddrs` and the gate asserts «the namespace stayed closed». Proof: the base under a runner-shaped resolver reproduces the three ✗ exactly; the fix measures 2.1.309 for real (ALL PASS (15), hotSwitch verified) ×2 under it and ×1 on this box's resolver; an unpinnable resolver (`fe80::1%eth0`) takes the skip road for real; fake-record controls for both roads. The runner's failed-jobs log (shards 3 + 5) carries no record-shape drift line for 2.1.309; the hot-switch suite itself never got far enough to read a record.
- **Red 3 — test-channels-i18n THE LOOK «cut 5 · outside 4 · hscroll 6», all at list-focus-200, every language.** Not a hang: the suite ran to the end both times (564 s, 173 passed, 1 failed; locally on the base 551 s, the same failure). door-day-one-landing's first-week rail words widen the rail 44 → 68 px, and the look driver (scripts/dbg-comm-surfaces.mjs `prime`) wrote only `vs-onboarded` — not the `vs-rail-labels: done` the scratch.mjs PRESET_KEYS passport gives the chrome suites — so every IM shot had the words. ### lane door-day-one-landing — day one asks one thing and lands in a chat on the person's files (base d3ab5db5 2.369.342)
- **Why:** two naive-user studies on real fleet pods (2.369.342, seven testers: study 1 D5–D8, D10, D11; study 2 C4–C9, C14, M3; lane 3's folder table). The welcome pitched «Your workspace for coding agents», «Sessions that never die», «raw terminal TUI» and showed 6 themes × 4 languages on screen one. Two non-technical testers asked "is this even for me?". Tour step 3 said «SSO is already configured, so no password is needed» right after a password sign-in. «Set a second password … there is no recovery» came at Start Chat Session and again at every sign-in, because «Later» was a sessionStorage snooze. The first-session box showed a grey `/home/<user>`, and every LATER New Session dialog kept the PREVIOUS area's folder in the field: testers typed the path 5/5 and 3/3 times, and lane 3's T3 had the typed folder appended to the pre-filled one. The sign-in terminal and the claude it ran showed as two ACTIVE sessions nobody made, and the first chat was «Session 3». The rail was unlabelled, so the way to Agents and Remote was found by hovering every icon. Git had no identity on a fresh pod.
- **MEASURED (code, base):**
  - the welcome's step 0 = `src/lib/setup-flows.js:228`; the SSO branch = `:324`; the guided login's ws create sends `name` and `ephemeral`, and **the server reads neither** (`src/ws-create.js` reads `sessionName`), so it became an ordinary live «Session N».
  - Manage Agents' Log in types bare `claude` into a login shell in `$HOME`. The claude REPL writes `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`, discovery lists it with no name, and the ladder falls to the cwd folder, so it reads as the account name (the home folder's name).
  - the window title's ladder put `webuiName` («Session {server seq}», a counter that includes the sign-in shells) before discovery's first-message `name`. The sidebar card already had the first message.
  - the dialog's cwd field was never cleared, so `if (cwd) …value = cwd` left the previous open's value in place.
- **THE FIX — PURE `src/day-one.js` (imports nothing; test-architecture PURE set):**
  - `tourSteps`: `protect` only where nothing protects the workspace. SSO or a sign-in password already set means the step and its SSO sentence leave.
  - `folderChips`: a Task Group's folders, then the home's folders WITH files (most first, ≤ 4), then «the last one you used», then the home's other folders, then the other recents (≤ 8). `firstFilesFolder` picks the folder the tour's chat starts in.
  - `vaultSetupAsk`: asks only `not_set_up && facts.secretWaiting && !snoozed`. `vaultLaterUntil` = 3 days.
  - `railLabels` / `railUsed`: the first week, or until every door was used once.
  - `gitIdentityPlan`: never over git's own identity, never mixing two people.
  - `SIGN_IN` / `isSignInRow`.
- **The wiring:**
  - **The tour (setup-flows.js):** step 0 is one sentence + three asks; the theme and language chips are gone (⚙ keeps both). The empty desktop's welcome (public/index.html) says the same sentence instead of «Multi-session terminal manager with tiling window support». Step 2 is skipped when the plan has no protect, and its SSO branch is deleted. Step 3 = the home's folders as chips with the files folder CHOSEN and the field filled, ONE primary «Start the chat», and the terminal as a link. The guided login sends `purpose: 'sign-in'`.
  - **The New Session dialog (app.js):** the field is `cwd || ''` on every open, with words for a placeholder. `_fillCwdRecent` paints `folderChips` through the new `src/lib/folder-chips.js` (loadHomeFolders / recentLocalCwds / chipWords / paintFolderChips; words chips read LTR).
  - **`GET /api/home-folders`** (src/routes/files.js, local only, cached 10 s): runs the new SafeFs op `folderCensus` (src/safe-fs-worker.js; deadline 15 s). It lists the home's non-hidden folders, each with a BOUNDED recursive count of files (cap 2000 entries, depth 4; `.`-names, node_modules, `__pycache__` and `snap` skipped). A mount point (in /proc/self/mountinfo, or on another st_dev) is named and never walked.
  - **The vault (src/server/vault-engine.js):** facts gain `secretWaiting` (not set up only). It is TRUE when:
    - a store's key file is minted in the legacy branch (a store's FIRST secret; stores mint only on encrypt);
    - a key file or a `data/agentd/host-*.token` exists beside the data (read lazily by `facts()`, at most every 5 s);
    - or secretPut / agentMint / agentPut refused for want of a vault.

    The moment it turns true is announced. NO new engine key: test-vault-law (a) classifies every exported key, and the file is untouched (64).
  - **The vault ask (vault-unlock.js):** `maybeNagVault` asks `vaultSetupAsk`. `onVaultState` asks at the BROADCAST whose `secretWaiting` turns true. «Later» = localStorage `vs-vault-later` = now + 3 days (it was a per-tab sessionStorage flag), and the setup dialog says why now.
  - **The sign-in terminal:**
    - ws-create keeps `_purpose: 'sign-in'` (persisted in meta, restored by boot-restore), and the live list carries `purpose`.
    - the sidebar skips such a live row.
    - routes/sessions.js drops a discovered row whose pid is under a sign-in terminal (its shell, two levels of children).
    - `openSignInTerminal` is used by the guided login, Manage Agents' Log in and the 8 add-account login terminals.
  - **The title (app.js syncSessionIdentity):** `given || match.name || match.webuiName`, so the first message names the window and the taskbar.
  - **Git (`src/server/git-identity.js`, ORCH):** at a local spawn, at most once a minute until settled. It reads `~/.claude.json` `oauthAccount` (emailAddress, displayName) and asks `git config --get user.name/user.email` from `/`. Where unset, it writes `git config --global user.*` (execFile, serviceEnv, 3 s bound). The log names fields, never values.
  - **The rail (sidebar-rail.js):** every door gets a `.rail-label`. The rail is `rail-labelled` (68 px, the collapsed strip too) while `railLabels` says so. A press records the door. The record is localStorage `vs-rail-labels`. `scripts/scratch.mjs` PRESET_KEYS sets it `done`, so every chrome suite keeps its 44 px pins.
- **Owner's ruling kept:** the Claude sign-in stays per person and is never skipped. The connect step (step 1) is untouched; lane door-signin-card reshapes it.
- **Gates:**
  - test-day-one is NEW (fast, 90, 120 ms). It covers every PURE row, with two RED CONTROLS (the base's recents-only chip rule; the base's not-set-up vault rule); the real vault engine (mint → true + broadcast, boot over a key file / a device token, a refused store, set up → false, no new key); folderCensus over a temp home (/proc as another device); git identity with real git over a temp HOME; wiring pins; and i18n.
  - test-day-one-chrome is NEW (heavy, 43, ~38 s, `--password-store=basic`). It runs a pod-shaped hub with a sign-in password and HOME/work holding 23 files. RED CONTROL: a bundle rebuilt from THIS source with the base's vault rule and prefill brings back the day-one ask and the carried folder.
  - test-new-session-dialog 103: A1 now asserts the field reopens EMPTY, and A1b covers the chips.
  - test-record-clear-census 242: the vault-later row moved to localStorage, plus a vs-rail-labels row.
  - mount-reader-census §86: counts moved, plus a git-identity row.
  - test-architecture: PURE set and §78; 13 orphaned i18n keys deleted (the old pitch, the old start step, the SSO sentence, the empty desktop's terminal-manager line).
  - test-vault-law 64 untouched; vault-engine 175; vault-secrets 159.

### lane door-signin-card — the humane Claude sign-in: a card, not a terminal TUI (base d3ab5db5 = 2.369.342)
- **Why:** two naive-user fleet studies (naive-cluster-1 D1–D4/D9, naive-cluster-2 B1/C2/C3/M1) — 7 testers on fresh 2.369.342 pods — ALL stopped at the Claude sign-in within the first minute. It is Claude Code's terminal TUI behind an unlabelled rail icon: a colour-theme picker with a code sample, "Select login method 1/2/3" (subscription / Console API / Bedrock-Vertex), a sign-in link cut at the window edge, "Paste code here if prompted >", then "Security notes" and "Do you trust this folder?" defaulting to "No, exit". The chat's own remedy was a DEAD END — a first task answered "Not logged in · Please run /login", and typing /login answered "/login isn't available in this environment" (Claude Code's print-mode text passed straight through). A silent user with no colleague to drive it never gets past it (the silent cohort: 9 of 17 fleet users signed in once by a colleague, or never started). The owner's ruling: the sign-in STAYS per person, made humane.
- **The fix (ONE commit, NO version bump; targets .344 because .343 is being integrated now):** the product drives `claude auth login --claudeai` ITSELF, in a hub-owned PTY, over the account's own pre-seeded config dir — so the person meets ONE card wherever the wall is (the chat's «Not logged in» card, the tour's connect step, Manage agents), never a terminal, a theme picker or a trust prompt.
  - **PURE src/signin-model.js** — `signinStep` reads the login screen off the PTY (steps: url / code-prompt / connected / error), reusing the OAT mint's proven reader (src/oat-mint-model.js: `cleanPty` strips OSC/CSI, `findUrl` rejoins a URL wrapped across a narrow PTY — we spawn 400 cols so it never wraps — `codeVerdict`) so a harness's login screen is read in ONE place. `signinCardView` maps the flow to the card's five states (no-login / url-shown / waiting-code / connected / failed+why). `publicSignin` is a whitelist — the OAuth login prints no token, and the credential bytes are the helper's, read in-process at finalize. Added to the test-architecture PURE set (with oat-mint-model, which it reuses, PURE → PURE).
  - **ORCH src/server/claude-signin.js** — runs VibeSpace's existing subscription-login helper (data/bin/vibespace-claude-subscription-login.mjs → `claude auth login --claudeai`) in a node-pty IT owns, in a 0700 scratch HOME with a no-op $BROWSER opener (a headless pod launches no browser; the person opens the URL in their own tab), CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = the account's OWN seeded dir (where the helper lands the credential). The env is the oat mint's allowlist (`mintEnvOf` over `agentEnv` — no hub secret rides along; §94 clean). It feeds the pasted code to the PTY and NOWHERE else. It does NOT re-implement finalize: on `connected` (the helper's "subscription credentials saved." line, or exit 0 + its success status file) the CLIENT calls the EXISTING /api/accounts/subscription/:id/finalize route — so the duplicate-identity merge, the login-expiry sweep and the pool wake are unchanged (signing in again folds into the existing account by e-mail). Routes POST/GET/DELETE /api/accounts/:id/signin (+ /signin/code) are human-only (an agent session/job bearer is refused by name); live phases ride a WS `claude-signin` broadcast. Wired in src/server/account-usage-routes.js beside the oat mint (no server.js change — the deps were already handed in). A hub killed mid-run leaves a scratch dir swept by age at boot.
  - **CLIENT src/lib/signin-card.js** — the shared card (escHtml / theme vars / SVG icons / i18n zh+ja / NO native dialog): «Sign in with Claude — your company uses a Claude subscription» + an «Open the sign-in page» link (a real anchor, target=_blank rel=noopener) + a paste-the-code box; `signinShowVerdict` drops a stale/older-run snapshot (the oat-mint HTTP-vs-WS flake class). Mounted at all three walls. The account dir is pre-seeded (`hasCompletedOnboarding`/`hasTrustDialogAccepted`, src/harnesses/claude.js seedDir shape), and `--claudeai` preselects the subscription, so no method menu / theme / trust prompt ever appears.
  - **The chat (src/lib/chat-view.js):** the `not_logged_in` exit branch mounts the sign-in card instead of the «run /login» bar; the waiting user message (the last user turn) is remembered so «Send my message again» re-sends it in ONE press — `resumeSession` now forwards `createSession`'s `initialMessage` (src/lib/session-lifecycle.js). The old dead-end system line and login bar are gone.
  - **The tour (src/lib/setup-flows.js):** the «Connect your agents» step shows the card inline and CANNOT be skipped silently — Continue, when nothing is signed in (`_obReady` from /api/backend-status, `_obSignedIn` from the card), warns once («You are not signed in yet — you won't be able to start a chat. Continue anyway?») and relabels to «Continue anyway» before it advances; the terminal/Codex login road folds under «Advanced».
  - **The terminal (src/lib/terminal.js):** the WebLinksAddon gets a handler — an http(s) link opens in a NEW TAB via `window.open(uri,'_blank','noopener,noreferrer')`, never xterm's default native «WARNING: This link could potentially be dangerous» confirm that scared 3 of 7 testers off the sign-in link (D3 / C2); non-http(s) is ignored.
- **Scoped out (said here):** remote-host subscription sign-in keeps the terminal road (the card drives the LOCAL hub's account dir); Codex sign-in is unchanged (the card is Claude-subscription-specific — the brief's humane card). The REAL 2.1.30x `claude auth login --claudeai` screen is OWNER-RUN: the shapes are modeled on the measured 2.1.296 capture (oat-mint-model header) + the helper's success line, and every test uses a FAKE claude.
- **Tests:** test-signin-model (fast, PURE: the recorded 2.1.30x login-screen fixture fed in chunks split mid-URL — url/code-prompt/connected — the no-half-URL rule, an error screen, the five card states, codeVerdict, the publicSignin whitelist, signinShowVerdict), test-claude-signin (fast, a FAKE claude in a stub PTY: url→code-prompt→connected, the pasted code reaches ONLY the PTY spied over every broadcast, the allowlist child env, scratch wiped on connected, the error + exit-code backstop, one-per-account, cancel, routes refuse an agent bearer), test-signin-card-ui (fast, the REAL card esbuild-bundled over a lean DOM: the five states, begin → create+signin, the code POST rides only /signin/code, connected → finalize, «Send my message again» → onResend, an older-rev snapshot ignored), test-setup-flows (fast, the tour step's non-silent Continue + the card mount + the Advanced fold), the terminal link-handler leg in test-terminal-zoom-select (heavy chrome: terminal.js's REAL handler with the REAL @xterm/addon-web-links — http opens via window.open with no confirm, non-http ignored), test-architecture (PURE set += signin-model + oat-mint-model; §86 reader-census +1 own-tree row). test-harness-contract untouched.
- **Gates:** build GREEN (test-architecture 797, i18n balanced 9146/9146, agentd unsigned). Fast GREEN on a scratch .343 bump (the `## 2.369.344` user heading is one ahead of the .343 cut 主开发 is integrating — test-changelog-style's ④ wants package.json's version or the next patch; no bump is committed). The full `--affected` heavy tier is for 主开发 on a quiet box.
- **Owner-run (never run here):** confirm the real `claude auth login --claudeai` 2.1.30x screen matches signin-model's reader (the printed URL + "Paste code here" + the helper's success line), and that the seed suppresses the method menu / theme / trust on a fresh pod.

### verify round — lane door-signin-fixes: the five findings of door-signin-verify on the humane Claude sign-in (base 959d583e = door-signin-card on 2.369.342)
- **Why:** the verify lane (door-signin-verify) cleared claims 1/3/6/7 with controls and found no HIGH, but five things on the card: (claim 5, MED-LOW) what «Send my message again» re-sends, (claim 8, PLAUSIBLE) the Claude card on a Codex / remote-host death, (claim 4, LOW) closing the card never cancels the run, (claim 2, LOW) the pasted code rides a failed run's error, and the debris of a never-logged-in «Subscription» row per failed attempt. ONE commit on 959d583e, no bump; int344 takes the pair. Each verify repro (scratch t2/t3/t4/t5) is PROMOTED into the lane's own suites as a leg that is RED on 959d583e.
- **1 · claim 5 — the re-send.** RED on base: chat-view's `_lastUserText` (read off the source, run over `_messages`) answered 'deploy to prod' for `[user, assistant 'Deployed.']` (an answered history), skipped an image-only waiting turn for an OLDER turn's text, re-armed the card's button on a later push. FIX: PURE `waitingTurnOf(messages)` (src/signin-model.js), taken AT THE WALL (`_showSignInCard` → `_waitingTurnText()`): walking back, an answer (assistant / tool, not the CLI's own login refusal — `<synthetic>` with no spent usage, or the classifier's "Not logged in" line) ⇒ nothing waiting; a record the person did not type (originKind / synthetic / imageAttachment / typed:false) is passed over; the first typed turn is it, its words (an image-attached turn's included; images alone ⇒ ''). Nothing waiting ⇒ «Connected», no button. The chat consumes `_waitingText` on its press and the card's `_resent` keeps a later re-render from re-arming it. NOTE: the verify's t5 ③ modelled "a turn with an image" with the `imageAttachment` flag — that flag marks the CLI's page images (message-manager.js), and a composer image turn (image block + text block) kept its text on base; the real base red for images is the image-ONLY waiting turn (an older text re-sent), which the leg pins.
- **2 · claim 8 — the wall.** RED on base: the exited branch (read off chat-view.js, run over a stub view) mounted the card for a Codex and a remote-host death. FIX: PURE `signinWallOf({oauthSubscription, host})` — the card only for a LOCAL conversation of the harness whose subscriptions it signs in, read off the declared caps row `capsOf(backend).oauthUsage` (a first cut on `backend === 'claude'` went RED on test-architecture §78 — no file branches on a member id; the subscription account the card creates and finalizes IS an `oauthUsageAccount`); any other death keeps the base's `_showLoginBar` and words verbatim (3 i18n keys restored, zh + ja). test-harness-contract untouched (no descriptor row, no verb — the one §7 EXEMPT line stays as door-signin-card left it).
- **3 · claim 4 — a run dies with the card that started it.** RED on base: `destroy()` sent no DELETE; the ORCH had no owner. FIX: `SignInCard.destroy()` and `pagehide` send `DELETE …/signin` (keepalive) for a live run — also when the close lands while the start is in flight; the card HOLDS its run over its socket (WS `claude-signin-hold {accountId, id}` → src/ws-handler.js → `socketHold`; again after every reconnect, then a GET to learn what it missed) and the socket's `close` calls `socketClosed` → the ORCH cancels a run whose last holder left and nobody re-held within `SIGNIN_ORPHAN_MS`. CHOICE: 3 min, not 0 — a reconnect or a phone that switched to the mail app for the sign-in link drops the socket while the person is mid-sign-in; an explicit close (card / modal / tour step / page) is immediate. Real node-pty legs (the REAL helper + a `sh` fake claude, /proc): close (the DELETE route) → helper + grandchild gone in ~26 ms, scratch removed; the holder's socket closing (orphanMs 0) → ~25 ms, scratch removed.
- **4 · claim 2 — the code never rides a failure.** RED on base: an echoing stub PTY + a silent exit 1 after the code → `error: "Paste code here if prompted > zq7Lk9#stateXYZ"` in the broadcast and the GET answer; the same on a REAL tty (the line discipline echoes what `read` takes); and in the heavy walk's new §6 over a real server: `"error":"Paste code here if prompted > SNTL-si1c#walkstate"` (base: 2 RED of 164). FIX: `sendCode` marks `codeSent`; the exit backstop then says ENDED_AFTER_CODE («the sign-in ended before Claude confirmed it — try again»), never the screen; `signinStep`'s lastLine is cut at PROMPT_RE (a bare prompt line is never a «why» either); oat-mint-model `redact` masks what stands after a code prompt (defense in depth — the OAT mint's sibling backstop publishes its lastLine the same way). test-record-clear-walk §6: a stub `claude auth login` reads the code on its tty and dies silently ⇒ no route answer, broadcast, file or journal line holds the typed word.
- **5 · debris — a row per failed attempt.** RED on base: three attempts in one card → three `POST /api/accounts/subscription`. FIX: the card reuses its own never-signed-in account across «Try again» (a reused id answering `unknown_account` / `signin_running` ⇒ one fresh create); `POST /api/accounts/subscription {signin:true}` → `accounts.pendingSignin({busy})` reuses an idle row MARKED `signinPending` (never one with a run live), else creates a marked one; `finalizeSubscription` clears the mark on login; the ORCH sweeps a marked never-signed-in row past the TTL (since its mark or its last run) at boot and at each start — never a signed-in row, a pool's named member, a harness default, a row with a live run or a terminal-Add row (unmarked). The route now passes only `name` to createSubscription (a body cannot mark a row). REAL AccountManager leg: three failed attempts → ONE row; a success converts it; the sweep at start and at boot.
- **Unchanged, said:** test-spend-paths — the re-send is the owner's own per-occurrence press on the chat's existing `resumeSession({initialMessage})` → `_sendChatMessage` road (the composer's WS message); no server-side producer primitive was added, so the census has no new site. test-harness-contract — see 2. The CHANGELOG's existing «The chat's “not logged in” message is now that sign-in card» line now says «A Claude chat's …» (a Codex chat keeps the terminal road), ×3.
- **Also red on 959d583e, fixed here:** test-reach-model §6 (the boot sentinel's GET census) — door-signin-card's `GET /api/accounts/:id/signin` was in neither list of scripts/fixtures/boot-sentinel-gets.json; it is a smoke row now (a scratch boot answers `{signin: null}`); test-takeover-census ① — the card's paste-the-code `<input>` (src/lib/signin-card.js) was an unclassified key surface; it is a `text` row now. (The fast tier is fail-fast, so each hid the next.)
- **Tests:** test-claude-signin ⑪–⑭ (52), test-signin-card-ui ⑦–⑫ (41), test-signin-model ⑥ (34), test-record-clear-walk §6 (heavy, 164). RED on 959d583e (a scratch worktree with only the new suites copied in): test-claude-signin 9 failed, test-signin-card-ui 17 failed, test-signin-model 6 failed, test-record-clear-walk 2 failed.

### lane door-healthy-chat — the first turns look healthy: no record-kind card in a person's chat, a waiting permission said in words above the message box, the page keys move the chat and every dialog, a document waits for its file, the cost says what it is (base d3ab5db5 2.369.342)
- **Why:** two naive-user studies on fleet pods (2.369.342, 7 testers; study 1 W1 W2 W3 W4 W5 W9, study 2 B3 C1 C10 C11). Every tester's first impression of a working assistant was a stack of red «⚠ Unknown event · api-request-blob» / «⚠ New fields on a known record · Claude Code 2.1.309» cards (the pods had self-updated to a build the release had not registered), a first turn stopped on a «Permission: Bash» card below the fold, 6–10 cards of raw shell per task, a chat they could not scroll, a page-sized summary that opened as «Could not read this document: ENOENT» and stayed so, and a bare «$0.47» everyone read as a bill.
- **MEASURED first (lane probe: a scratch hub + a stub claude 2.1.309 behind the real chat-wrapper + raw CDP).**
  - **The «dead wheel» was the study's harness.** The testers drove `vibespace-browser batch "mouse move 700 300" "mouse wheel -600"`; agent-browser 0.38.2 dispatches `mouse wheel` at clientX/Y 0,0 whatever the move said (an in-page listener saw x 0, y 0 on both a separate and a batched call) — the left rail, which scrolls nothing. The study's control («the harness wheel scrolls an ordinary page») holds for a document scroller from any point. A real `Input.dispatchMouseEvent mouseWheel` over the list scrolled it on the base (1443 → 1013), over the minimap strip too (the compositor scrolls the scroller under the point), and over a dialog's list.
  - **PageUp / PageDown were dead (real).** `.chat-message-list` had no tabIndex; a press in the transcript focused `.chat-view` (tabindex −1, the list's PARENT), where the page keys find no scroller — and the list's own NAV_KEYS listener never heard them. The message box kept the keys (a textarea). A dialog: a press inside focused the overlay (tabindex −1 with escapeToClose) — the same ancestor trap.
  - **Every live unknown record threw in the page (real).** `_noteUnknownRecord` (claude) and `_noteUnknown` (codex) emitted `{op:'create', msg}`; the view's create path reads `op.message` ⇒ `_onCreateMessage(undefined)` threw on `msg.id`, poisoning the seq watermark — 28 op failures for 28 records in one turn. test-unknown-records pinned `o.msg`, test-record-shape accepted either key.
  - **The document:** the artifact auto-open fires at the Write's tool_use (before the permission); `doc-window-ui.js` load() on a first failure left `S.base` 0 and `check()` returns early on `!S.base` — no retry, ever; a later open of the same path reveals the same broken window.
- **Fix — the record kinds leave the chat, the signal stays the admin's** (the 2026-10-15 ruling's lesson: never hide the update signal from the owner). `renderSystemMsg` returns null for an `unknown-record` / `unknown-fields` notice; the normalizers keep each kind once (`_noteAddedKind`, src/message-window.js — record / fields, the newest CLI build) and say a change as ONE `record-kinds` meta op; the attach payload carries `recordKinds`. The chat's status bar draws ONE quiet chip LAST (never moving another chip): «3 record kinds this version added — Diagnostics», each kind in its title, a press opens ⚙ Diagnostics; the rail's Diagnostics counter adds the day's drift kinds. The create key is `message`. The card CSS and six dictionary keys left with the cards (§78 dead text).
- **Fix — the permission card in words.** NEW PURE src/command-words.js: `commandPhrases` (agent-tool-rules' quote-aware `splitShell`; installs, reads (one phrase), lists, searches, deletes, git, downloads, a loop, a snippet; ≤ 3 + «and N more steps»; a heredoc / substitution line is «run a Python snippet» / «run a shell script»; a shell's `-c` line by its own phrases — `bash -c "rm -rf ./ds-out && ./sign.sh"` is «delete ds-out · run sign.sh», never «a snippet») and `requestPhrases` (Write / Edit by the file, WebFetch by the host). The card shows the line above the command, the command folded under «Show the command» — OPEN when the request holds a hidden character (F7); VibeSpace's own tools keep their words. F4 stands (a summary ABOVE the raw line, never instead of it).
- **Fix — a waiting permission said above the fold.** The typing line reads «Waiting for you to allow: install python-docx · read 3 files» (`_waitingQuestion`: the oldest main ask, its loaded card's input or the ask's command line) and is a door: a press runs `jumpToPendingAsk`.
- **Fix — the third prompt's folder offer** (the owner's day-one rule, on the road Always Allow takes). `folderOfferFor` (agent-tool-rules.js): ONE `addRules` allow update — Bash, Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit → localSettings (the CLI writes the folder's .claude/settings.local.json) — withheld on a hidden character, never for a codex approval / a question / an ACP option / another answering lane. The card offers «Let it work in <folder>/ without asking» from the conversation's third permission prompt, its updates in its title and a sentence under it; the press says `folder: true` only — `answerFromRecord` sends the RECORD's offer (F6). The shipped ask rules (`vibespace-page publish`) still ask: an ask rule wins over any allow rule. The rule's behaviour is the named constant `RULE_ALLOWS` (test-helper-ask ⑲ keeps answer frames to the adapter).

- **Red 2 — the CSP teardown: «script-src-attr inline, line 1 column 101, source ""» on the app page** (test-record-clear-ui and test-channel-jump, every attempt). THE ELEMENT is no product element: it is the suites' own NEGATIVE CONTROL. Each parses its hostile `<img src=x onerror=…>` in `document.implementation.createHTMLDocument('')` from code evaluated over CDP. Column 101 is the `=` of `d.innerHTML =` in that one-line expression, and no source means a script with no URL (Runtime.evaluate). Measured on 156 against 154 (a loopback page served with the app's policy, report-uri + the CDP Audits issue):
  - **Chrome 156 reports an inline handler when its attribute is SET**, an inert document's too — createHTMLDocument, DOMParser, a `<template>`'s content, `Document.parseHTMLUnsafe`, a plain `setAttribute('onclick', …)`. It reports as the page that ran the code, at the statement's position. No handler runs (`window.__xss` stays unset); the violating node is not in the page's document (`DOM.resolveNode`: «does not belong to the document»).
  - **Chrome 154 reports none of those.** It reports a handler only when it compiles (a live detached `<img>` whose load fails).
  - **The same rule reaches suites that did not run on a 156 runner yet.** Found by running every chrome suite that carries `on*=` markup under 156, with the collector naming each line's code:
    - test-channel-window-render ④'s control: the same inert-document parse.
    - test-inbox-reply-ui ⑦ and test-docx-viewer: each planted live handler now reports TWICE against their `=== 1` — once when its attribute is set (source "", at the statement) and once when it compiles (the page, at 1:1), with the same sample.
    - test-channel-window-render ⑭: the hostile .md attachment `<img src=x onerror="window.__pwned=14">` reaches the viewer's sanitizer. DOMPurify's inert parse SETS the handler before it drops it: `bundle.js 127564:35` is `new DOMParser().parseFromString(…)`, sample «window.__pwned=14». Nothing ran.
- **The fix:**

  - **Takes match the suite's own code.** inbox-reply-ui ⑦ and docx-viewer take their planted handler by its SAMPLE and accept 1–2 reports (≤ 155 one, 156 two). channel-window-render ⑭ takes the report of its own attachment's sanitizer parse by sample AND by the bundle as its source (0 on ≤ 155, ≤ 1 on 156). A product report with other code, or this handler compiled on the page, is never taken: the sample in a suite's line key closes the position-only take's hazard (lane mirror-331-reds-chrome).
  - **The collector names the code:** the app policy's `script-src` gains `'report-sample'`, which allows nothing; a report then carries the first 40 characters of the handler it names. A chrome suite's sink (handed the suite's file) keeps that sample; a hub's own data/csp-reports.jsonl never does (`reportsOf(text, { sample })`, the never-a-value law kept). The teardown prints beside every line WHAT was reported (`cspWhat`): the sample, the code's source or «code with NO URL — a script this SUITE evaluated over CDP», and for an inline handler the Chrome 156 set-time rule. The runner's line now reads «script-src-attr inline — «window.__xss=1», set by code with NO URL at 1:101 …».

DOMPurify parses it into a DOMParser document, and that parse SETS an `on*` attribute before DOMPurify drops it. Chrome 156 files `script-src-attr inline` as the app page. The result was the pair's one For-you notice «The page security policy would block script-src-attr: inline», plus a line in the count that says whether the policy is complete. Nothing ran.
  - **The mail frame is not one of them** (a correction of chrome-156-drift's note). A mail's HTML reaches the frame's DOMPurify only through mail-frame step 1, the allowlist re-serializer, which drops every handler: `<img onerror>`, `onclick`, `ONMOUSEOVER` and `<svg onload>` — none survive. No report comes from a mail; test-csp-report ③d pins it.
  - **The recognizer** (PURE src/app-csp.js + the sink, src/server/csp-reports.js):
    - A candidate is a script-src-attr `inline` report that carries a handler's sample (`'report-sample'`) and was set by this page's own `/bundle.js` (same origin, the build in its `?v=`). `reportOf(…, { site: true })` keeps its line and column (numbers only).
    - The sink reads the bundle on disk once per build: stat for the mtime (the `?v=`), read the text, keep `purifyParseSites` (a handful of numbers), drop the text.
    - It names the report `sanitizer-parse` when the code at that position IS DOMPurify's parse: `.parseFromString(<var>, <var>)`, then DOMPurify's own `.createDocument(<ns>, "template", null)` fallback.
    - Another build, no bundle, no sample, another origin or script, or any other position ⇒ the report is what it always was.
  - **Pinned on the bundle's symbol map, never on a column alone** (test-csp-report ③d):
    - Both builds the tree makes are rebuilt in memory with an external map: package.json's release step (minified) and the chrome suites' (the same minus `--minify`, read off test-channel-window-render).
    - The map names EVERY `parseFromString` call in each — three: DOMPurify's, docx-preview's XML parse and zrender's SVG parse. The new `scripts/symbolicate.mjs lookupMany` does it in one pass that keeps only the asked lines (`decodeMappings` holds ~2 M arrays); it equals `lookup` on 4000 random positions.
    - `purifyParseSites` returns exactly DOMPurify's call (purify.ts:1078) on both builds. MUTANT: the signature cut to the bare call ⇒ 3 sites, RED.
  - **What the owner sees:**
    - The line is of kind `sanitizer-parse`: no For-you notice, and never in the app page's count. `GET /api/csp-reports` gains `sanitizer: {reports, lines}`; Diagnostics shows «Sanitizer dropped an inline handler: N» as its own chip when N > 0.
    - It is never a chrome suite's teardown failure: scripts/scratch.mjs prints it, and `cspWhat` words it.
    - Every other report keeps its line, its count and its notice — including the CONTROL: the same attribute and sample at our own code's position (file-viewer's `innerHTML`).
    - The approval-census-gated sanitizer is unchanged. The sample is read to judge and never written to a hub's data/.
  - **Not changed:** a hub that already filed the false notice keeps it (resolve it in For you), and its old lines carry no kind.
- **Item 2 — ⑩h's CONTROL FIXTURE on 156 (test-only).** Measured with the control's own layout printed on both Chromes:

It now sets ⑩d's own page (1400 × 1600), where the maximized list is far taller than the room on any Chrome — it fits by construction. The FIXTURE assert names the page, the list's height and the margin. ⑩a–⑩g are untouched.

### lane agy-card-details — an Antigravity conversation's cards carry their details: the file a Read names, the command a run names, every subagent of one step, and a killed subagent said as killed (base d3ab5db5 2.369.342)
- **Why:** the owner, in an Antigravity conversation with two screenshots (2026-10-22): «你 review 一下 agy 支持，我发现很多卡片都缺少细节». The screenshots and the owner's store (read-only, shapes only) showed five gaps: a Read card with no path and «✓ 1 行»; the store road handing QUOTED paths to the sub view and the artifacts reader; a Bash card that is agy's own truncation notice with no command; two invoke_subagent calls of one planner step drawing one card; and a KILLED subagent whose window showed its reads «运行中» for ever while its card said «已停止 · 它没有发回答复».
- **MEASURED (the owner's parent conversation + its two subs, a store COPY + the parent's live ACP journal of 1292 records, production read-only; the owner's ids / text out of the tests):** agy's tool args reach a card by TWO roads — the LIVE stream (tool_info.parameters, CLEAN: `{Path, StartLine, EndLine}`, `{CommandLine}`) and the STORE (the db step args / transcript `tool_calls[].args`, every value a JSON-ENCODED STRING: `"Path":"\"/home/…\""`, `"StartLine":"1"`, `"CommandLine":"\"…\""`, `"Content":"\"…\""` — all 32 read_file calls carried a \"-wrapped Path). A read_file's stream output is a ONE-LINE summary («113 lines, 24215 bytes»), never the file's text; the text is in the store (transcript_full / the DB). The two subagents spawned in ONE planner step each got their OWN stream step index (:24 / :25) and a distinct «Created the following subagent: {id}» at that transcript step; the sub rows' `spawnStepIndex` was 27 for BOTH (not the link). The killed sub's last planner step issued 12 view_file calls and was killed (manage_subagents kill_all) before any result.
- **The normalizer (new PURE src/agy-tool-args.js, in the test-architecture PURE set):** ONE pass both roads take — `decodeScalar` (a value that is a JSON-encoded SCALAR becomes that scalar; a clean path / command / number stays itself — an object/array arg keeps its string), then agy's keys get the card's canonical aliases (Path/AbsolutePath/TargetFile→file_path, CommandLine→command, Cwd→cwd, StartLine→offset, EndLine→limit, toolAction→title, toolSummary→summary) while the raw keys (decoded) stay for the card's 技术细节 fold. The invariant: a harness's tool arguments are normalized ONCE. The wrapper's live tool_call and the store's stepRecords both emit `normalizeAgyToolArgs(args)`; pathArg + artifactRecordsOf decode (the artifacts reader's `agyFilePath` shares it) so a write's path and content are never \"-wrapped.
- **Link by ID, not by a counter (gap 4):** `subIdForStep(read, parent, step)` reads the parent transcript's own «Created the following subagent: {conversationId}» at the step — unique per call, and the stream-vs-transcript index drift cannot break it (spawnStepIndex 27 was shared; the step number was not the link). snapshotOf and the wrapper's linkSpawns try it FIRST, the message-step scan stays the fallback. Two invoke_subagent rows of one planner step keep distinct stream steps, so each becomes a spawn and each gets a card (never folded into one).
- **A process that ended is never «running» (gap 5):** a TERMINATED sub (killed / stopped-with-parent / failed — not an answered sub, which agy leaves ALIVE) closes its still-open tool cards: `closePendingRecords` turns each into a `tool_call_update` status 'failed' carrying the SUB_TERMINATED sentinel, which the renderer (src/helper-ask.js isSubTerminated) draws as the localized «terminated with the subagent» — never the token, never a spinner. The parent card (src/lib/subagent-card.js) says «被父代理终止» with the sub's «最后进展» (its last planner prose, else its last tool's own words), not «它没有发回答复».
- **The cards (src/lib/chat-renderers.js):** the Read card shows the normalized path and, for agy's «N lines, M bytes» summary, «N 行 · size» as its status (not «1 行»); the run card carries agy's toolSummary in its head (toolSummaryChipHtml — only agy sets input.summary, so claude / codex are unchanged); the truncation notice's `file:` path is already clickable (lane agy-links-file-url, in this base).
- **Scoped out, said here:** the Read card does NOT yet inline the file's text from the store (transcript_full / the DB). The «1 行» confusion is resolved by the summary-as-status + the clickable path (the file is one click away); inlining the text per read is a bounded helper-door read with marginal value over the path, and this lane is ONE commit — left for a follow-up.
- **Tests:** test-agy-store ⑫ (+9: decodeScalar / normalizeAgyToolArgs / artifactRecordsOf decode, subIdForStep by-id, a KILLED sub's cards closed + lastText, two-in-one-step → two cards, a made-up store — owner ids out), test-search-card-title (+5 render under the DOM shim: the Read «N 行 · size», the run card's toolSummary chip, the terminated sentinel → localized, the KILLED parent card's «被父代理终止» + «最后进展», a non-agy tool unchanged), test-agy-harness / test-antigravity-session / test-artifacts / test-path-linkify / test-page-link-ui / test-harness-contract / test-architecture (green; the gap-5 close is gated so an answered sub's dangling card keeps the base). +5 i18n keys (zh + ja).
- **Owner-run (real agy, never run here):** whether a NEW run's live stream carries the invoke_subagent output (the owner's journal, from a pre-cards wrapper, had none — the by-id link reads the store either way); whether the store text is worth inlining in the Read card.

## 2.369.342 — 2026-10-22

### lane agy-status-bar-facts — an Antigravity conversation's status bar shows what agy reports; what a bar shows is a descriptor row (base 72056f53 2.369.340)
- **Why:** the owner, on an Antigravity conversation (2026-10-21): «agy 的 chatview 缺少很多信息啊 什么 context 啊，cache rate，产物啊啥的下面都没有了». agy's stream carries `usage` on its result, but data/bin/agy-wrapper.js kept it in the sidecar only (`usage keys seen: {}` over the owner's 429 journal frames), so the bar — which reads the stream's usage — had nothing; the Artifacts reader was the ACP one, which reads `diff` contents agy never sends.
- **MEASURED (the owner's two agy conversations, production read-only, shapes only; the login file never opened):** `result.usage` = the CONVERSATION's RUNNING TOTAL. It equals, to the token, the sum over every model call of every turn in agy's own transcript (`<HOME>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<conversation>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl`, one JSON row per step, a MODEL row carrying input_tokens / cache_read_tokens / output_tokens): 1 turn of 90 calls = 545 062 / 172 175 / 6 556 922; 5 turns = 577 850 / 58 173 / 4 065 912 (the binary names the computation `steps.CalculateTokenSums`). total_tokens = input + output; input EXCLUDES cache reads. So the live context is the turn's LAST call (90 228 tokens = 9 % of 1 048 576); the brief's «the last turn's input + cache_read» on the per-turn sum would read 677 %. step_update `usage` is NOT used: no capture of it exists (what it counts is unmeasured); the sidecar keeps its copy.
- **The record:** at each result the wrapper reads the tail (≤ 4 MiB) of THIS conversation's transcript through ONE gate (a uuid id, the realpath inside the store root, O_NOFOLLOW, a regular file; nothing else in agy's store is opened) and journals ONE `{type:'acp', kind:'usage', total, turn, last, model, modelFrom, durationSeconds}` (PURE src/agy-turn-usage.js). The ACP normalizer's `_processUsage` turns it into the ONE usage meta every bar reads: `last` = context + cache (claude's last-message reading; no transcript ⇒ nothing overwritten — a sum is never a context), `total` = the odometer in codex's totals shape, the turn's spend + time beside; a slug agy NAMED (init.model) is the served model, the one it was only started with is not. chatStatus replays it on attach — and for a conversation whose wrapper predates the record (dtach keeps the old wrapper across an update) the sidecar's own running total (meta.usage) is the odometer until it restarts. No new stdout consumer (acp-events.js unchanged; the side-effects road untouched).
- **THE ROW (PURE src/status-bar-facts.js):** `ui.statusBar` {context 'reported'|'table'|null, cache, odometer, model, duration, windows} on every chat descriptor + the client META (test-harness-contract deep-compares): claude reported/cache/model; codex + odometer; opencode reported/model only (ACP usage_update has no cache field — its bar used to draw ⚡0%); antigravity everything with a WINDOW TABLE; shell / a register()ed harness without a row = nothing reported. The bar gates context / ⚡ / Σ / the turn time on the row and draws ONE «not reported» chip naming what a harness lacks (claude: token total, turn time).
- **The window table (antigravity descriptor, DOCUMENTED not measured):** Google's Gemini API model pages read 2026-10-21 — gemini-4-argon «Context window (unified input and output token limit) 1,048,576» (page of 2026-10-14); input token limit 1,048,576 for gemini-3.8-flash (2026-09-02), gemini-3.7-flash (2026-10-12, deprecated), gemini-3.6-flash (2026-07-30), gemini-3.1-pro-preview (2026-10-09). agy slugs are `<code>-<level>` ⇒ prefix rows; an unknown slug ⇒ «window unknown» with the token count.
- **Artifacts:** `artifactsOf` = agy's own reader (src/harnesses/artifacts-of.js `antigravity`): the stream names its writes write_file / edit_file with an absolute `Path` (measured), init.tools the model-facing write_to_file / replace_file_content / multi_replace_file_content — both read; a file: URI percent-decoded, a relative path the cwd's. src/artifacts.js: agy's brain/<conversation>/ is its own artifacts dir (a report there + .metadata.json), so it is no longer «agent config» (the owner's report there was code, no card).
- **Todos:** left out — agy's CHECKPOINT steps are context checkpoints and manage_task names background command tasks; neither is a list of named steps with states.
- **Tests:** test-status-bar-facts (new, fast, 34: PURE + the normalizer (+ the sidecar odometer of a wrapper that predates the record) + the REAL bar per harness under a fake DOM; mutants: the cache gate cut ⇒ opencode ⚡0%, the context from the sum ⇒ 677 %), test-harness-contract (+24: every chat harness's row, RED rows, a register()ed harness), test-artifacts (+10: the owner's shapes, names replaced; a diff-carrying call still reads as ACP's; the base ACP reader produces nothing), test-agy-harness ⑬ (+9: one record per turn from the fake agy, the gate refuses a brain dir linked out of the store + its RED copy), test-antigravity-session ⑤ (+5, heavy: two turns through the real create path on a named account), test-agy-status-bar-chrome (new, heavy, 15: the agy bar's five facts + the Artifacts chip, a reload, a claude chat's «not reported»). The fake agy (scripts/fixtures/antigravity-agy) now speaks the measured semantics (running sums, agy's transcript under $HOME with AGY_STUB_TRANSCRIPT=1, write/edit steps).
- **Owner-run (real agy, never run here):** the step_update `usage` semantics; whether a real agy flushes the transcript row before its result (else `last` is the call before); whether init names the served model.

### lane device-node-version — the installer provisions Node 22.23.4 and replaces its OWN older node; the Machines card says which Node each agent runs, 「运行时过旧」 below the floor (the Node.js security releases of 2026-10-21; base 72056f53 2.369.340)
- **Why:** the Node.js 2026-10-21 security releases — 4 HIGH: CVE-2026-111497 (the Brotli decoder's out-of-bounds write), CVE-2026-105482 (dns.resolve NUL truncation), CVE-2026-105483 + CVE-2026-106069 (TLS hostname-check bypasses); fixed in 22.23.4 / 24.22.1 / 26.12.1. A paired machine's agent runs the node its installer provisioned (`<root>/node`, the pin v22.22.0) or found (a system node ≥ 18); the hub kept none of it, so no card could say «this agent runs an old Node».
- **The base, measured:** the hello-ack has carried `nodeVersion` since M0 — the hub's client read it and dropped it (no field on the record, none on the row). The installer's `find_node` takes `$ROOT/node/bin/node` second (after `--node`) whenever it runs ≥ 18, so a moved pin never reached an install that already had its own node — test-node-bootstrap ⑨'s RED CONTROL runs the 2.369.340 installer over the same fake mirror: the pin moved to v22.23.4 and its own node stayed v22.22.0, nothing fetched. The ps1 (by reading — no pwsh here) does the same, and `$nodeExe = $null` wiped `-NodeExe` (PowerShell names are case-blind: the parameter and the variable are one), so a `-NodeExe` was never tried.
- **The installer (sh + ps1):** the pin is v22.23.4 (the comment names the advisory and the hub's table). THE PIN MOVED: an install whose OWN node is older than the pin gets the pinned one in its place through the same road as a first provisioning (the mirror or the hub's `/vibespace-node/` fallback, SHASUMS256.txt verified, a smoke run, a rename inside the root); a second run downloads nothing, an older pin never downgrades, a failed download keeps the one it had (said, exit 0). A node the machine HAD (PATH / nvm / /usr/… / `--node`) is never touched. The sh replaces before the take-over (a POSIX rename leaves the running agent its inode); the ps1 after it (Windows will not move a folder whose node.exe runs) and moves the old folder aside first so a refused move changes nothing. The ps1 keeps `-NodeExe` in `$nodeArg` before the variable is reused.
- **The hello + the record:** the daemon's hello-ack adds `openssl` (process.versions.openssl) and `nodeOwn` (its execPath under realpath(`<root>/node`)). ### lane runtime-floor — VibeSpace OWNS its Node runtime: ONE floor table + ONE provisioner; a Node security release = one commit that moves the table + the product's own update, never an image rebuild or a pod rollout (the owner 2026-10-22: «每次有漏洞都要更新 pod 也太麻烦了吧 有没有更好的解决方案？»; base 724baa52 = lane device-node-version on 72056f53)

Lane device-node-version wrote the table first (src/device-runtime.js); it is MOVED here and re-exported there (the same objects, `===`) — the Machines card's chip, the hub's boot line, the updater and the provisioner read ONE file.
- **THE PROVISIONER:** src/node-runtime.js (SHARED) `provision(wanted, {root, mirror})` — SHASUMS256.txt first (an archive it does not list is never downloaded), the archive's sha256 must match BEFORE `tar` unpacks it, the unpacked binary must answer `wanted`, then `<root>/runtime/current` flips (a relative symlink renamed into place; win32: current.txt); writes ONLY under `<root>/runtime` (a link there ⇒ `not-own`, nothing written through it), so a system node is never touched; KEEP 2 versions; bounded (≤ 160 MiB archive, ≤ 256 KiB sums, ≤ 10 min) and never holding the loop (streams + child processes). `fetchFile` = THE ONE downloader of a node release file — the hub's device mirror route /vibespace-node now fetches through it (the same name list). **Pinned key: none** — the trust anchor is the mirror's HTTPS + its SHASUMS256.txt, the device installer's own rule; the release team's `.sig` is not checked (said, not hidden). nodejs.org is the default mirror (`VIBESPACE_NODE_MIRROR` overrides, the installer's name).
- **THE SAFETY ADDENDA (主开发's acceptance condition, 2026-10-22):** (1) THE HASH LIVES IN THIS REPO — src/runtime-floor.js `ARCHIVES` carries, per floor version, the six archives' SHASUMS256.txt lines (linux / darwin × x64 / arm64 tar.gz, win x64 / arm64 zip): 22.23.4 + 24.22.1 = the lines 主开发 fetched from nodejs.org and cross-checked against the hub's verified download (byte-for-byte equal), 26.12.1 fetched once over HTTPS by the lane (06:39Z). The provisioner checks the archive against the TABLE first (`archiveSha`), the mirror's SHASUMS256.txt second (`sums-disagree` before the download, `sha-mismatch` after it); a version / platform with no line is NEVER provisioned (`no-table-row`, not one request) — VIBESPACE_NODE_MIRROR can serve only the bytes this repo names; a musl archive has no line ⇒ Alpine is never provisioned. A security release now adds the six lines with the moved floor (test-update-road's release commit does). (2) THE SWITCH RE-VERIFIES WHAT IT EXECS — provision writes `<runtime>/node-v<ver>/.vibespace-runtime.json` {version, platform, sha256 of bin/node, archive + its sha256, provisionedAt}; `reexecOnOwnRuntime` hashes bin/node (1 MiB chunks, ~0.2 s) against it before the execve: `tampered` / `unverified` ⇒ no switch, one log line, the base node runs (a planted or corrupted binary never runs; the device agent's switch is the same function). Pinned key: still none — the release team's GPG `.sig` is the known gap.
- **THE ROADS — no unit, no image change:** server.js's FIRST line (src/server/runtime-boot.js `boot`) runs `reexecOnOwnRuntime`: when `data/runtime/current` is a NEWER node of the SAME major line (a native addon such as node-pty is built for one major's ABI — the provisioner only ever installs the running major's fixed release) that answers its version, the process REPLACES itself with it (process.execve — the same pid: the unit's baked node, run.sh and a pod's image entrypoint start the base node and keep supervising; once per start, `VIBESPACE_RUNTIME_REEXEC` dropped before any child; `VIBESPACE_RUNTIME_SWITCH=0` off; a node without execve / win32 stays). Then the `[runtime]` verdict line, and the boot pull's check 20 s in (`node scripts/runtime-check.mjs --provision` as a child; never in a throwaway root or with NO_AUTO_UPDATE). scripts/update.sh (hub + pods; ⚙ Update runs it) runs the same check after the pull + build, before the restart — it never fails the update. GET /api/runtime + ⚙ Diagnostics report «Node runtime» (zh + ja). server.js stays at its 1907-line ratchet (ONE line).
