### lane auto-cli-oat-unprobeable — an account the quota probe cannot prove is never sent; a failed probe names its reason where the owner looks (the owner 2026-10-22 02:1xZ: «为什么现在开始出现很多长时间没刷新过用量信息的账户 因为一直没用到过吗？»; base 72056f53 = 2.369.340)
- **Measured on the owner's hub (read-only: data/auto-cli-state.json, data/accounts.json key names, data/usage-probe-log.ndjson outcomes, the journal; no token read):** six accounts with 11–36 consecutive `fails` were exactly the six with `oatEnc` whose login had ended (loginState `oat-only`, the row's 「仅长期 token」); the two others with `fails: 1` were transient. Their last probe-log rows are `written` on 10-19/10-20 (the logins were alive then) and NONE after: since the login died, refreshViaCliPanel's oat-only door (2026-10-13) refuses them with no spawn, no log row, `false` — and the loop booked every refusal as a failed probe (`attempts` + `fails` + the 5 min × 2^min(f,6) backoff), journaling `failed (stale-idle; …)` with no reason. So the brief's «the probe is `claude -p /usage` under that account's CLI dir» was the base's design, not what ran: the cost was phantom failures and a re-ask every ≤ 5.3 h for ever, not vendor calls. The owner's guess was right: those rows refresh only when a session bills on them.
- **The ADDENDUM (主开发 2026-10-22 02:49Z, measured on the hub — the brief's premise was wrong):** the six tokens are NOT profile-less: every oat-only row's `oatShape.scopes` is `user:file_upload, user:inference, user:mcp_servers, user:plugins, user:profile, user:sessions:claude_code` (re-read here, key names + scopes only); `claude -p /usage` works on the token MATERIALIZED in the row's folder (a mint-time probe succeeded 10-20; OAT-in-file is measured PASS per version — the fixture's `oat-file-scopes` FAIL is a file WITHOUT the row's real scopes). So an oat-only row is PROBEABLE through the same door and the same spawn (CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR = its folder) when its facts allow, and named when they do not. On the hub today the CLI is 2.1.308 (journal: «not measured (fixture: 2.1.296, 2.1.306)»), so the six read `unprobeable:cli-unmeasured` until a measurement adds 2.1.308 — said on the row and once a day in the journal.
- **The verdict (PURE src/auto-cli-model.js, imports only secret-shapes):** `probeEligibility(row)` reads the row's OWN facts, in this order: an oat-only row (checked FIRST — an expired login and our token file still parse loggedIn) is `unprobeable:oat-no-profile` when `oatScopes` lacks `user:profile`, `unprobeable:cli-unmeasured` when `oatCli.measured` is not true (oatFileCaps: the hub's CLI is not one oatInFile measured — the folder never gets the token), `unprobeable:oat-not-in-folder` when the folder does not hold the token (`loginState.oatFile` + `oatFile.state === 'written'`; a refusal the token chip names), else `probeable`; a row with no login is `unprobeable:no-login`; any login is `probeable` (an `expired` login without a token too — its own probe says why it fails). null = not a subject (not a subscription, a pool, a harness whose rung is not `cli-usage`). `accounts.list()` puts the facts on an oat row (`oatScopes` from the recorded shape — no secret; `oatCli: {cli, measured}` from oatFileCaps) and the verdict beside them; the loop, the probe door (before its spawn) and the row read the same verdict. The `oat-not-in-folder` kind is beyond the addendum's two: «measured» alone does not put the token there (a write that failed, a vault-locked key, a sweep not yet run), and probing then would spend a spawn on the expired login — so it is named, not sent.
- **The loop (src/server/auto-cli-loop.js):** an unprobeable account costs NO attempt, NO failure, NO backoff; `[auto-cli] quota refresh <id>: not probed — <the fact that failed>; refreshes when a session uses it` (e.g. `long-lived token only, and claude 2.1.308 is not measured with it in the account's folder`) ONCE a day per kind (`said`, `<id>|<kind>`, a new key in data/auto-cli-state.json beside the attempt clock, clamped like it — a restart says nothing again; a changed reason is said). The FIRST tick that sees one clears what the base booked against it (its `fails` and its `attempts` stamp) and says so on that line: `(36 failed attempts booked before this cleared)`. The cadence and the wandering threshold are untouched; no new vendor call (test-vendor-whitelist 316 = base).
- **A failed probe names its reason:** the door (src/usage-routes.js) now gives its two silent failures a verdict — `exit` (the CLI exited ≠ 0: `exit N: <its first line>`) and `parse` (exit 0, no quota line: `no quota lines in its answer: <its first line>` — the measured 152-row shape on the owner's hub). The first line skips a `Warning:` line (the CLI's stdin warning rides every probe, the successful ones too), stderr before stdout. Every verdict of the door goes through ONE function `panelSays`, which keeps the last failed one on the account RECORD (`probe: {at, ok: false, why}`, accounts.noteProbe through the one atomic writer, broadcast by `_notify`) and drops it on the next WRITTEN answer; an oat-only refusal (code `login`) is not a failed probe. The loop's failed line ends `— <why> [<class>]`. The ⟳ route's ladder is unchanged: it stops on `login` / `identity` / `write` only, so `exit` / `parse` fall through to the token rungs as before.
- **THE ONE scrub:** `probeWhyText` — control characters out (ANSI too), secret-shapes `redactSecrets` with `runs: true` (R1–R8 incl. unnamed key-material runs), THEN the 200-character bound (a cut after the redaction can only shorten). Applied at the door, again at the record (`probeRecordOf`) and again in the loop line (idempotent). The raw probe ring (data/usage-probe-log.ndjson, 2.369.109 — the owner's verbatim debugger log) is unchanged and keeps the CLI's bytes; it is never a row, a journal line or a broadcast.
- **The row (src/lib/manage-agents.js `acctProbeNote`):** an unprobeable oat-only row's AGE CHIP tooltip names the fact — «Long-lived token only, without the profile scope / and claude {cli} isn’t measured with it / not in its folder: can’t be probed — refreshes when a session uses it» (zh 「仅长期 token（无 profile 权限）/ 且 claude {cli} 未测量 / 未写入账号目录：无法主动探测，用到时才刷新」, ja too) — and so does its 「仅长期 token」 chip's, at the END, after the facts the owner ruled lead the hover (2026-10-15; test-oat-materialize pins the token-in-folder chip's lead and caught the first draft). ### lane browser-uppercase-keys — capitals and symbols in an xpra window arrive as the viewer's machine typed them (a fleet user on a Mac, 2.369.340: inc-mvj6nj3e-av0w «在 Chrome 浏览器里无法输入大写，导致输入密码的时候无法输入大写» + inc-mvj6ysm7-kmhw; base a4b07508 = the 2.369.341 cut)
- THE REPORT, AS THE RINGS TELL IT: the Agent browser was an XPRA app window (div.xpra-win in picture-shell, the keys in textarea.xpra-ime); his Mac's Caps Lock switches the input method (a CJK IME); the captured attempt: Shift down → the letter's keydown OWNED by the input method + a composition on the same tick → Shift up 80 ms later → the commit 1.4 s later → Enter. His pod: xpra 6.5.4-r0, the version measured here.
- THE TWO ROADS, MEASURED (probes in the lane dir: the DOM keystrokes as a Linux and a Mac Chrome fire them, a text box and a password box):
  - CDP (the live view: browser-live-window onDocKey → keyRoute / macChord → keyRecord → the bridge → the driver's stream → Input.dispatchKeyEvent): CLEAN on base — 32 of 32 through the real driver 0.38.2, launched, headed and ATTACHED to a Chrome already running with the attach argv (the fleet's one-browser shape). The record's `text` IS the DOM key, so Shift, Caps Lock and the layout arrive as the viewer's machine applied them.
  - XPRA (xpra-view keyInputOf → xpra-client keyDown / typeText → xpra-proto keyActionFor / ImeKeymap.plan → key-action): xpra 6.5.4's OWN server keyboard code (KeyboardConfig parse + set_keymap + get_keycode + make_keymask_match + the XTest press, in do_process_keyboard_event's order) programmed with our keymap, a real Chrome on the display, the browser started before the keymap (the fleet's order). The brief's two candidates do not hold: the published keymap HAS the shift level for letters ([a, A]; every SHIFTED_TABLE symbol on its base key) and `shift` rides every packet — Shift+a, Shift+1, Caps Lock + a, Shift held over letters and typeText('Ab1!') (with Shift held, and released before the commit) all type right. RED on base: 14 of 36 — every keystroke whose FLAGS disagree with its CHARACTER. keyActionFor names the lower-case keysym and leaves the level to the `shift` / `lock` flags, and X applies the US map's Linux rule (Shift undoes Lock on a letter; Lock alone capitalises): the Caps Lock FLAG over small letters (a Mac whose Caps Lock switches the input source) typed a ⇒ "A" and Shift+b ⇒ "b"; a Mac's Caps Lock + Shift + a ("A" on the Mac) ⇒ "a"; a French layout's Shift+& ("1") ⇒ "!" and & ⇒ "7". (Shift+1 under a Caps Lock flag stays "!" — a two-level key ignores Lock.)
  - HIS CAPTURED SHAPE (the composition road) was right on base too, on the real rung with Chrome's own IME machinery (Shift down → imeSetComposition → Shift up → insertText commits): the committed capital typed "A", a committed "Ab1!" typed "Ab1!" — ImeKeymap.plan presses by the character. So his exact trigger is not proven: what this lane closes is the class his keys can hit on the keydown road; a CJK method's own full-width symbols (Shift+1 ⇒ ！ in Chinese mode) are what his Mac typed.
- THE FIX (src/lib/xpra-proto.js, PURE `typedModifiers`): for a character on a two-level key of the published map `shift` = "the character sits on the shifted level" (an upper-case letter, a SHIFTED_TABLE name — ImeKeymap.plan's own rule for a composed character); `lock` is never sent and the Caps Lock key is not forwarded (keyActionFor ⇒ null), so X never applies a Caps Lock of its own on top of the machine's (a Mac fires Caps Lock's keyup only when it turns off); a chord (control / mod1 / mod4 / mod5) and a one-level key (Space, Enter, the keypad, F-keys) keep the flags as held (Shift+Space, Shift+←). Fixed tree: 36 of 36 (48 of 48 with the IME rows).
- GATES: test-xpra-client 415 → 436 (§3e +21 through the VIEW for Mac and Linux viewers, X's level rule modelled from the measurement, the keymap's shift-level census, RED CONTROL = the pre-fix trio types "a" / "A","b" / "!","7"; the Ctrl+C row loses its `lock`; the new suite on the BASE code: 11 FAILED); test-live-input 201 → 222 (§3b +21: the CDP record carries the character, Linux + Mac viewers — green on base too, the CDP road never had it; RED CONTROL = a text rebuilt from `code` types "a"); test-desktop-xpra-window-open §8 +7 on the REAL rung (fix: all green; the base tree with the new suite: a Mac's Caps Lock + Shift + w ⇒ "w", the Caps Lock flag over small letters ⇒ "Wx", a French & ⇒ "7"; HIS composition shape and "Ab1!" green on both; the in-session pre-fix packet types "w"); test-browser-live-input ③ +1 (ALL PASS 175 — the Mac viewer's real keys through the real driver type "A!1&"); test-browser-live ALL PASS 247 (its first run's ⑤ headless pre-fix pointer CONTROL red at 29 / 18 px — the known intermittent screencast-metadata control; green on the re-run and on base); test-modifier-map 59; test-changelog-style 40; test-architecture 788; the fast gate ALL GREEN 474 suites.

## 2.369.341 — 2026-10-21

### lane speaker-passthrough-v1 — the machine's SOUND reaches the viewer beside its picture: the strip's 「声音」 (backlog B-aec9; the measured road: lane stream-audio-probe; base 319f0bdf = the 2.369.339 cut)
- THE ROAD (the probe's V1, built): ONE werift audio TRACK on the stream's audio m-line — the microphone's (lane stream-mic-road): `stream-offer {audio: true}` (asked by src/agentd/client.js only of an agent whose hello-ack says `stream-audio`) on a machine that can send its sound ⇒ `addTransceiver(track, sendonly | sendrecv with mic)` and the VIDEO sender's `streamId` = the sound's (`vibespace-desktop`): ONE msid, so the page's <video> carries both (measured in Chrome: 1 video + 1 audio track in its srcObject). Opus payload type = werift's audio-first assignment (96; the video's moves to 97 — werift rewrites both).
- NOTHING IS CAPTURED until the strip says so: `stream-audio {sid, on}` (THREE-TOUCH: the handler in agentd.js, `stream-audio` in the hello-ack, the client's gated `streamAudio` + `stream-audio-result` in the routing set; a READ in src/device-acts.js — the person's own session, stream-offer's class). The hub: `POST …/stream/sound {key, on}` → desktop-webrtc `sound(key, on)`; `…/stream/start` takes `audio`.
- WINDOWS (src/desktop-sound.js, SHARED; the microphone helper gets a second verb — tools/vibespace-mic/vibespace-mic.cs `loopback`, the same csc build road): WASAPI loopback of the default render endpoint (event-driven, AUTOCONVERTPCM → 48 kHz float stereo; polled every 5 ms where the engine signals no loopback event) + a SILENT render stream on the same endpoint (AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_SILENT — the probe's leg 1b keep-alive) → s16le on stdout → behind a streaming WAV header (src/sound-model.js soundWavHeader) into the stream's ffmpeg (soundEncoderArgs: `-fflags nobuffer -probesize 32 -analyzeduration 0 -f wav -max_size 1920 -ignore_length 1`, libopus 64k lowdelay 20 ms, flushed, `-f rtp rtp://127.0.0.1:P?rtcpport=P` — its RTCP to the same socket, never port + 1) → a UDP socket of the agent's whose FIRST sender (port + SSRC) is pinned (a stray datagram is dropped and counted) → the track. The helper's end `device_lost` (the default speaker went away / changed) ⇒ a fresh run, twice a minute at most; else the capture ends by name and the stats say `failed`.
- A MAC (src/agentd/stream-mac.js `source.audio`; tools/vibespace-screen/vibespace-screen.swift): `audio on|off` on the screen helper's stdin = `capturesAudio` on its OWN SCStream (`updateConfiguration`; excludesCurrentProcessAudio) — no second capture, no new TCC class; SCK's float planar stereo → AudioToolbox's in-box Opus (AVAudioConverter, 960-frame packets, 64 kbps — the probe's leg 2a encoder) → FLV AUDIO tags (Enhanced FLV: 0x91 + 'Opus' + the packet) beside the pictures → SP.flvReader `type: 'audio'` → the track. A live switch the helper refuses ⇒ the same capture started again IN PLACE with `--audio` (the picture freezes a moment); a GONE restart asks `audio on` again. The helper's VERSION moved vs-054d5cc35456 → vs-5d0cce28e54e: the owner switches Screen & System Audio Recording on once more (helper_changed_regrant); the Machines card says so.
- THE CLOCK (PURE soundRtpStep): one sequence and one 48 kHz timestamp per session across every on / off — a new run continues the sequence, moves the timestamp by the wall-clock gap, and is marked (measured on the daemon: 2520 ms of samples for a 2504 ms gap; seq n → n + 1). LIP-SYNC: werift sends an RTCP SR on each sender (measured: the stand-in got SRs for both; Chrome holds remote-outbound-rtp for audio AND video) — the browser syncs one MediaStream's tracks by them.
- THE RATE (PURE src/stream-model.js videoKbpsOf, the stream host's `retarget` at every estimate and every switch): while the sound is on the picture is told the estimate less 80 kbps — never under STREAM_LIMITS.maxKbpsMin because of the sound and never MORE than the estimate (the first rule floored at 300 and RAISED a 222 kbps loopback estimate — caught by ⑳, fixed: `min(base, max(floor, base − 80))`). The estimate counts the picture's packets only (the sound's carry no transport-cc number).
- THE STRIP (src/lib/stream-mic-strip.js createSoundToggle, wired in src/lib/machine-desktop.js — the phone's the same; PURE src/sound-model.js soundStep / soundStartOf): shows once the stream carries the track; OFF for a machine until pressed, ON remembered per machine (`vibespace.streamSound`, the HDR switch's shape); the press unmutes the <video> IN the click and sends the op; the second press mutes it and ends the capture; a RESTORED window (`syncId` — a reload, a layout replay) says 「点一下开声音」 and captures nothing until a press — even on a page that had the person's gesture; the title says nothing is recorded or stored (+ a Mac's permission). ### lane agy-links-file-url — an Antigravity conversation's file links could not be clicked: its `[SKILL.md](file:///…)` reached the chat as a bare `<a>` (the sanitizer drops every file: href), and a relative path whose first letter is Chinese was never a link (the owner 2026-10-21: «文件链接怎么都点不了»; base fd843910 = the 2.369.339 cut)
- THE MEASUREMENT (the owner's conversation buffer, read-only): agy in chat mode wrote 10 file references as markdown links with `file:///…` URLs in raw UTF-8 (the cwd a CJK folder: `…/标书研究/.agents/skills/…/SKILL.md`, a script beside it, a report under its brain dir) and 6 `[`<id>`](conversation://<uuid>)` subagent links; its tool output says «the full output in a file at file:///…» as bare text.
- WHAT THE BASE DID WITH A file: HREF: marked's href percent-encodes it (`file:///home/u/%E6%A0%87…/SKILL.md`); DOMPurify's URI rule (IS_ALLOWED_URI: a few schemes, or a first character that is not a letter) has no `file:` — the attribute is REMOVED and the anchor stays `<a>SKILL.md</a>` (no target either: safe-html's afterAttributes adds one only to an href); linkify preserved every `<a>` untouched; the delegated click handler reads `closest('.chat-link') || closest('a[href]')` — neither matched, so a click and a Cmd+click did nothing: «点不了». Measured twice: the node harness (a sanitizer stub keeping hrefs exactly where DOMPurify's own rule does) and the real sanitizer in chrome.
- TWO MORE ON THE SAME ROAD: `[doc](/home/u/标书研究/a.md)` kept its href, but marked had encoded it and `_linkTargets` handed the click `/home/u/%E6%A0%87…/a.md` — never found; a bare `file:///…` in text linked only its `///…` tail (the path rule's match). And the code-span relative rule's first character was `[\w@%+=.\-]` — JS `\w` is ASCII, so `标书研究/方案.md` stayed plain.
- PURE (src/path-linkify.js): `fileUrlPath` — `file:///p`, `file://<host>/p` (localhost or a name: the host dropped), `file:/p`; percent-decoded per UTF-8 run (a run that is not UTF-8 stays as written); `?query` dropped; `#L12` / `#L12-L20` ⇒ `:12` / `:12-20`; a `:line` kept; null for `file://host` alone, a `//server/share`, a control character. `hrefPath` — file: or the click rule (`/…`, `~/…`, never `//host`), decoded. `looksRelPath`'s first character is `[\p{L}\p{N}_@%+=.\-]` with the `u` flag (the same delimiters excluded); `{ prose: true }` keeps it ASCII for the For-you tray's PROSE (foryou-links relHits): Chinese is written without spaces, and with the Unicode gate alone `请看docs/plan.md` / `报告：docs/x.md` linked the glued word (measured on the base vs the lane); a code span delimits its path, so both code-span rules (chat, For-you) take the Unicode gate.
- THE RENDERER (src/lib/chat-renderers.js): `_fileHrefs` turns an anchor's file: href into its path BEFORE the sanitizer (only real tags: inside code marked writes `&lt;a` / `&quot;`; a `%` carried as `%25` so `_pathAnchor` decodes once) — the sanitizer still sees the whole output and its rule stays (a path `_pathAnchor` would not take — the bare root `file:///` — is not carried: it would reach the DOM as `href="/"` and open the app's root in a tab; it is dropped, as before); `_pathAnchor` (linkify's anchor branch) makes every anchor whose href names a local path the bare path's own span (`clickablePath`: data-path decoded, the label the link's TEXT, «Click to copy, Ctrl+Click to open»); a `/p/<id>` page anchor, a web anchor and the `conversation://` anchor are left as written; `linkifyFileUrls` (after URLs, before pages and paths, through `_linkifyBareText`) makes a bare file: URL ONE path span, the URL as written its label. No file: href reaches the DOM. Every decoded path is escHtml'd.
- THE PINS MOVED WITH IT: test-approval-census pins the four markdown sites' exact lines; chat-renderers' is now `let html = sanitizeHtml(this._fileHrefs(marked.parse(text || '')));` (the parse still on a sanitizeHtml( line), and the (h6) control's replace follows it — 60 = base. test-codex-subagents and test-codex-p2-wrapper pin «renderMarkdown is the sanitizeHtml path» as `sanitizeHtml\(marked\.parse` within 600 characters of `renderMarkdown(text) {` — widened to accept the `this._fileHrefs(` step (the first fast run stopped there: fail-fast). test-foryou-links' SIG (the rule's own pattern lives in ONE file) follows the new gate.
- TESTS: test-path-linkify 63 → 97 (⑧: 19 fileUrlPath + 7 hrefPath + 14 looksRelPath rows, the prose rule, the renderer rows — Antigravity's message, localhost + :12, #L12-L20, a raw-HTML anchor, `<a href="/home/…">` decoded, the label as text, a bare file: URL in a message and in tool output, CJK / kana relative paths in code spans — the page / web anchors as written, the conversation:// PIN, 5 XSS rows, the bare root never carried as `href="/"`; RED CONTROL the base = the three renderer lines + the gate reverted on patched copies: the dead `<a>`, the encoded anchor path, the `///` tail, the plain CJK path; the census CORPUS gains an Antigravity row); test-page-link-ui 26 → 38 (⑦: the REAL sanitizer + REAL clicks — one path span per file: link with no file: href in the DOM, a click copies the decoded path, a Cmd+click asks the file probe and opens it, `:12` at its line, `标书研究/方案.md` opens against the session's cwd, a markup-carrying path held as text with nothing run, a javascript: link keeps no href, the conversation:// DOM pinned as today; CONTROL the base on the live renderer: a click and a Cmd+click on the bare `<a>` copy, ask and open nothing); test-foryou-links 57 → 59 (a CJK-first code span links; prose unchanged).
- NOT IN THIS LANE: `conversation://` (lane agy-subagent-cards — pinned in both suites so it sees a change); a markdown `/p/<id>` page anchor still classifies as a file path on click (`_linkTargets`, unchanged — a page written as `[x](/p/pg…)` copies its bare path; noted for a follow-up); Windows drive paths (`file:///C:/…` becomes `/C:/…`; the chat links no Windows path anywhere yet).

### lane agy-subagent-cards — an Antigravity subagent is a CARD that opens its own timeline; what a harness shows of its subagents is a declared row (the owner 2026-10-21, in an Antigravity conversation: «使用子代理的时候怎么没有子代理卡片查看细节» / «子代理细节不在你设计的harness框架里吗？»; base fd843910 = the 2.369.339 cut)
- THE FINDING (the owner's conversation, its journal and its agy store — shapes only, the login file never opened): agy's `invoke_subagent` became ONE ACP tool row (title invoke_subagent, kind other, rawInput {Role, TypeName}) and ONE notice «Antigravity started 1 subagent: self (…)». Neither of the owner's two rows ever got a tool_call_update — agy's DONE for that step rides the subagent_info update, never a tool step — so both spun for good.
- WHAT AGY KEEPS (measured, agy 1.4.x): `conversations/<id>.db` (SQLite; `steps` blobs are protobuf), `brain/<id>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl` (ONE legible JSON line per step; `transcript_full.jsonl` untruncated), `subagents/<sub>.json` in the parent's brain {conversationId, subagentDescriptor{typeName, role}, state, spawnStepIndex, workspaceUris}, and messages in the RECIPIENT's brain: the parent's task in the sub's dir (`sourceMetadata.tool.stepIndex` = the parent's spawning step), the sub's answer (send_message) in the parent's. invoke_subagent is ASYNC: its output is only «Created the following subagent: {conversationId, logAbsoluteUri, workspaceUris} The subagent will send you a message…»; the answer arrived 2.5 min later as a SYSTEM_MESSAGE; the state stays SUBAGENT_STATE_ALIVE after it. spawnStepIndex is NOT unique (both of the owner's subs said 187; their tasks said 186 and 187) — the task's step is the link. The brief's «the answer comes back as the tool's output» and «the task is in the parent's messages» were both measured otherwise; the report.md the brief named was written by the PARENT (its write_file with ArtifactMetadata), not by a sub.
- WHAT WAS LEGIBLE IN THE BLOBS (a 60-line wire reader, field names unknown): the step type (14 / 15 / 23 / 101 / 132 = USER_INPUT / PLANNER_RESPONSE / CHECKPOINT / SYSTEM_MESSAGE / GENERIC), the status (3 DONE, 5 DONE before a checkpoint, 7 ERROR — the row is updated in place), the created time (metadata 1 = {s, ns}), the tool call (payload 20.7 {id, name, argsJson}), the text / thinking (20.1 / 20.3), a delivered message (114.1), the tool output (140.2.1), and the render words only the db has (render_info 5 verb «Ran» / «Analyzed» / «Messaged», 9.1 summary, 10.3 terminal {command, exit code}). A nested message whose first byte is a newline (`\n` = field 1's tag) and whose length byte is printable reads as a string to a naive reader — render_info.9 did — so a legible string may never start with a control byte. db ⇄ transcript on copies: the sub 23 / 23 steps agree; the parent 203 / 231 (the 28 planner rows before a CHECKPOINT carry no tool calls in the db). The transcript is the timeline's source; the db the fallback.
- THE ROAD: PURE src/agy-store.js parses (the PURE set); data/bin/agy-wrapper.js — on the machine that holds the store — does the I/O through ONE gate (`storePath`: agy-store's verdict, then the path must resolve to itself under the real store root; files opened O_NOFOLLOW): the row looks for its sub (the stream's own output / subagent_info when they name it, else the task's step), journals THE CARD as a `subagent` record (on a change only — a step never re-sends the task and the answer) and the sub's steps as `sub` records {subId, toolCallId, rec: <ACP record>} (clipped: text 4000, a tool output / a thought 1500, an argument 400 — 23 steps ≈ 27 KB); THE TAIL ticks every 2 s only while a spawn looks for its sub (≤ 60 s) or a sub works, and stops when the sub's last step is a final planner response or its state left ALIVE; a parent send_message to the sub wakes it; agy's exit says a working sub stopped. The row's own end (tool_call_update completed) rides the subagent_info update; the «started 1 subagent» line stays only where no row carries the card.
- THE HUB: src/acp-message-manager.js `_processSubagent` turns the row into the Agent card (taskInfo {subId, agentRole, typeName, status, startedAt, endedAt, elapsedMs, steps, files}, input.prompt = the task, output = the answer; a later tool update never overrides it); src/server/stdout/acp-events.js routes `sub` records to src/server/acp-subagents.js (subagentBuffers + `subagent-message` {…, subId} + the viewer's AcpMessageManager); ws `attach sub-<subConvId>` re-reads the parent's journal when memory has none (a restart) and builds an ACP normalizer for an ACP session. THE HELPER DOOR now asks every record (claude's hook still answers only a user record): a finished `subagent` record names the sub's transcript_full.jsonl in the record's store; its write_file / edit_file calls are this conversation's rows «By subagent <role>».
- THE CLIENT: src/lib/subagent-card.js (PURE) — the card keyed on taskInfo.subId (role, type, a running elapsed time on the view's one-second ticker, the task folded, the answer through the one sanitizer, the files, «Open timeline» → `sub-<subConvId>`; every store string escaped); `[x](conversation://<id>)` is MARKED in the markdown before the renderer's one pinned sanitize line and becomes `.chat-sub-link[data-sub]` after it (a sub with no card here: «unknown subagent»); the generic link handler leaves it to ChatView. Lane agy-links-file-url's row pinning today's conversation:// rendering (inert text) changes with this lane — its `file:` links untouched.
- THE ROW: `ui.subagents` on every descriptor = `caps.subagents` (`subagentView`, both tiers): claude virtual · codex threads · antigravity cards · opencode / shell none — a subagent tool row of a 'none' harness says «This harness shows no subagent details» (opencode's task row recognised by its ACP title `task` / input `subagent_type`, read from opencode's source — not measured here). register() derives it ('none' when undeclared).
- TESTS: test-agy-store (NEW, fast, 52); test-agy-harness ⑫ (100; its four wrapper legs run together — 8.2 s); test-harness-contract «the subagent row» (594; + RED rows, a register()ed proof); test-vault-law ⑩ (62) — the real wrapper over a store whose every tailed file is a LINK to the login file (a canary in all three shapes the reader parses) journals no byte of it, RED copy that follows links journals it; test-antigravity-session ④ (heavy, 21: the hub's real consumer on the dtach pty — the card frames, `subagent-message`, the tail on/off, sub-<id> rebuilt from the journal alone, the sub's file in the Artifacts rows, an older agy's row); test-agy-subagent-chrome (NEW, heavy, 21, three runs: the card, Open timeline, the conversation:// link + an unknown sub's chip, the Artifacts chip, CONTROL = the pre-lane normalizer). Suites a changed line touched: test-approval-census / test-codex-subagents (the sanitize line kept verbatim), test-helper-ask (the viewer's virtualId line kept), test-artifacts-handover (its two control needles follow the helper door's new gate), test-task-lifecycle (the chip's two call sites: the card uses renderTaskChip), test-takeover-census (+1 row: the card's <details> folds), test-live-bar-layout (no new dead token), test-claude-md-retire (e) (the .340 hunk that picks a VERBATIM row, byte-identical).
- THE GATES: the fast gate on the REAL next base — the .340 cut 72056f53 + this lane (git apply --3way; the changelogs' block on top; kb-file-structure a union) bumped to .341, every file tracked: ALL GREEN, 474 suites, 257 s (a keep-going sweep of every fast suite there: 474 / 474). On this base fd843910 bumped to .341, test-job-model is red BY SCHEDULE only (the protocol-1 compat this base still has expires at .340; the .340 cut removed it) — green at the committed .339 (381). ### lane agy-slash-guard-paths — an Antigravity message that starts with a path is sent; only agy's own closed list of slash commands is refused (the owner 2026-10-21 23:0xZ; base 72056f53 2.369.340)
- **Why:** in an Antigravity chat the owner attached a zip and typed a line; the chat answered «Error: /home was not sent: Antigravity answers its slash commands itself …». data/bin/agy-wrapper.js `slashRefused` refused every line matching `/^\/[A-Za-z]/` and named `t.match(/^\/[\w:-]+/)`; the composer's upload (`_insertUploadedPaths`) writes the file's absolute path first, so EVERY message with an attachment was refused, and so was any line that starts with a path or a "/"-word that is not agy's.
- **The base, measured** (the base wrapper over pipes, the fake agy; lane probe.mjs): `/model`, `/usage opus`, `/help` refused (right); `/home/u/x.zip 这里是…` refused as «/home» and `/tmp/a.txt` as «/tmp» (the owner's error); `/notacommand hello` refused as «/notacommand»; `~/x`, `./run.sh`, `/ 2`, `/2026` passed the guard — and the base FAKE ended its stream on `/ 2` (exit 2), because it modelled agy as "any line starting with /".
- **The closed list:** scripts/fixtures/antigravity-cli-1.4.3.json `slashInPrint.answeredWithoutATurn` — /usage /quota /credits /model /effort /skills /permissions /hooks /help /changelog /config (provenance 'changelog', the binary's own `agy changelog`); `stream.inputErrors` says such a command in the stream ends the session (exit 2).
- **The fix:** src/harnesses/antigravity-slash.js (NEW, PURE — no require, no import): `AGY_SLASH_COMMANDS` (frozen, the fixture's spelling) + `agySlashCommand(text)` = the first word up to whitespace, lower-cased, when it is on the list, else null. ONE definition: the wrapper requires it beside src/ (`require(path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'src', 'harnesses', 'antigravity-slash.js'))`, the claude-transport.js precedent — no wrapper is on HostManager.AGENT_TOOLS), src/harnesses/antigravity.js re-exports the same array. `slashRefused` asks it; its sentence is unchanged and names the command in the list's spelling. Not in src/adapters/agy.js and not the descriptor file itself: the wrapper would pull the ACP adapter / normalizer / accounts helpers into its process.
- **The fake agy** (scripts/fixtures/antigravity-agy) ends its stream on the fixture's list only (any case); any other line is a turn. It reads the FIXTURE, not the product module, so the suites cannot agree with the guard by construction.
- **Tests:** test-agy-harness 87 → 92 (7.1 s, fast; ①b the list = the fixture, PURE, one definition, the 32-row table, RED = the base rule as a module mutant: the attachment message «/home»; its five wrapper RED copies moved to `<root>/data/bin` beside a `<root>/src` link — a copy elsewhere cannot resolve `../../src`). test-antigravity-session 12 → 17 (heavy, 4.7 s; ④ over the real create path's pty, one batch — the journal reaches its file on the wrapper's ~1 s flush: three commands refused by name in the exact sentence and never read, eight path-first / "/"-headed lines read exactly and in order, the conversation alive; RED = a wrapper copy with the base guard: the attachment message refused as «/home», never read). test-agy-attach-chrome NEW 9 (heavy, 32 s: a worktree server + the fake agy as ANTIGRAVITY_CMD behind the real wrapper; the composer's REAL upload ⇒ the box `<cwd>/brief.zip `, the typed words, Enter ⇒ agy reads the line path-first, its reply drawn, no error card; /model still refused, the next line answered; RED = the scratch tree's wrapper given the base guard: the error card «/tmp was not sent …», agy never reads it). test-architecture 783.
- **Not measured:** what the real agy does with a path-first line in its stream (an unsigned agy refuses before reading stdin; a signed-in capture settles it), and whether agy has TUI-only commands outside the print-mode list. `--disable-slash-commands` ("Disable slash command and skill expansion in print mode") might let the stream carry `/model` as text — a signed-in measurement, not this lane.

### lane agy-subagent-backfill — the cards' addendum: a subagent that ALREADY RAN before the update gets its card and timeline too (主开发's follow-up 2026-10-22, the owner asking once the trace showed it; base 099c41b6 = int341 on 72056f53, cherry-picked at the .341 cut)
- MEASURED on the fixture (probe: the .339 wrapper fd843910 byte for byte + the stub agy's `subagent` turn over the fixture store, then the new code): the old wrapper's journal = the invoke_subagent row + «Antigravity started 1 subagent: self (…)», no `subagent` record, no `sub` step ⇒ re-attach / the restored history (both rebuild from the session buffer) drew the plain row — 0 cards, `sub-<id>` seed null; the same subagent under the new wrapper = 1 card (completed) + 13 sub records. ### lane layout-stale-record-sync — 工作's windows vanished from the owner's desktop after the phone woke, and 恢复布局 did not hold: a NAMELESS record the phone saved before its attaches answered, a desktop restore that built none of it, an 'unbuilt' drop the belt took (the owner 2026-10-22 00:18Z «我的工作桌面里的窗口怎么突然都没了», «我刚才点了恢复布局也没正确恢复»; URGENT, data-loss class; base 72056f53 2.369.340)
- **The evidence (read-only: data/layout-history shapes, telemetry events, the server journal — no window title quoted).** A point holds the state BEFORE the write that made it. 23:32:38Z 工作 = 5 windows, desktop-stamped, every chat with serverSessionId + backendSessionId. 23:37:09 the phone wrote 工作 with the SAME five ids but NAMELESS (no serverSessionId / backend / backendSessionId / claudeSessionId / cwd, `openSpec.backendSessionId` null; 研究 / 个人 written at 23:37:14 / :32 kept theirs) — the phone's page-load at 23:37:08 (after an 11 453 s ws outage), then `ws-lagged 5 MB` and sixteen `ws-reply-timeout:attach`, the first five exactly 工作's sessions. 00:16:52 the journal: the Mac dialed in (woke); the Mac page reloaded at 00:16:47 (page-session-end 38 475 s), open-windows 0 at 00:17:17, 研究's eight built at 00:17:29; 00:17:31.509 the write 工作 5 → 0. 00:18:04 the restore of the 00:17:31 point (the nameless five); the Windows page booted at 00:18:05; 00:19:05 6 → 1 (its first save after opening a chat). 00:23:04 the phone's write, identities back — why reopening on the phone fixed it. No `[layout-sync] REFUSED` line all evening.
- **Not a stale record.** The 23:37:09 record was the newest when written; nothing older replaced anything newer. The brief's staleness gate ships as the belt it asked for (below); the three roads are:
- **Road 1 — the write (the phone, 23:37:09):** a chat window has no `app.sessions` entry until its attach answers ('attached'), and `restoreState`'s alive branch called `attachSession(alive.id, …)` WITHOUT the conversation id (`openSpec.backendSessionId: null`), so `captureWin` (src/lib/layout.js) wrote neither id; `mergeDesktopRecord` takes a page's capture WHOLE in the record's place — the save the phone made 1 s after its reload replaced five named entries with nameless ones.
- **Road 2 — the read (the woken desktop, 00:16:52):** `restoreState` matched a chat by backendSessionId (window or openSpec) or serverSessionId only; a nameless entry matched nothing and NO branch built it (its `openSpec.serverId` — a live session — was never read). desktop-manager.js `loadFromServer` then noted the five as build attempts.
- **Road 3 — the belt (00:17:31, 00:19:05):** 20 s later (`BUILD_GRACE_MS`) `recordFor` dropped them as 'unbuilt' evidence; the owner's switch to 研究 sent 工作 = [] and `shrinkVerdict` counted 'unbuilt' as an explanation although every session was alive. 恢复布局 restored the newest pre-loss point — the nameless one — and the Windows page that booted on it repeated roads 2 and 3 (6 → 1: only the window that was named stayed).
- **The fix (ONE commit):** (1) IDENTITY IS NEVER FORGOTTEN — PURE `keepIdentity` / `keepIdentities` / `sessionOf` (src/lib/desktop-record.js) in `mergeDesktopRecord` and in ws-handler's write (in place: the relay carries it); `restoreState` passes the conversation id to the attach (chat + terminal). (2) A NAMELESS ENTRY IS FOUND by the session its openSpec attaches to (`restoreState`). ### lane oat-in-file-2-1-306 — the long-lived token in a pool member's file is granted on 2.1.306 too: the fixture holds ONE record per measured version, and a new measurement ADDS its record and never drops one
- **Why.** `cliCaps.oatInFile(version, fixture)` grants the token in a member's credential file only on the EXACT CLI version the fixture measured, and scripts/fixtures/oat-in-file.json held one record (2.1.296, 2026-10-14). So on a 2.1.306 CLI every oat-only pool member was escaped as unmeasured: no token written to its folder, no new placement on it, the spawn on the env road. That is a follow-up named by lane cli-2-1-306-records.
- **The measurement (主开发's rung, 2026-10-21 17:55–18:02Z).** `scripts/measure-claude-cred-read.mjs --variant oat --write-fixture` ran inside the loopback-only namespace with the strace watchdog, against the 2.1.306 linux-x64 ELF that lane downloaded (sha256 520bc6c1f40af466…). The verdicts are IDENTICAL to 2.1.296's: oat-file PASS, oat-env FAIL, oat-file-401 PASS, oat-file-near PASS, oat-file-switch PASS, oat-file-scopes FAIL. The notes say the same too. This lane ran no measurement, no real claude, no namespace and no sudo.
- **The shape: `{versions: {'<exact version>': <record>}}`.** Each record is exactly the one-version file's object (cliVersion, measuredAt, script, netns, variants), keyed by its own cliVersion.
  - **Why one file rather than one per version:** the store keeps reading ONE file (accounts.js `_oatFixture`, its read census unchanged), and the writer keeps one path.
  - The 2.1.296 record is the old file's object, unchanged. test-cli-caps ⑥ pins the sha256 of its JSON.
  - The committed file was produced with the writer's own rule, `withMeasured(the old file, the 2.1.306 record)`.
- **src/cli-caps.js (PURE).**
  - `oatInFile` reads the record keyed by the exact version. A key whose record names another version, a key in `--version` words, an inherited entry, or a versions value that is not a map grants nothing.
  - A bare record still reads as the fixture of its one version: an older `--fixture` scratch file, and the suites' own fixtures.
  - `measuredVersions(fixture)` lists the versions, oldest first. The store's `oatFileCaps().measured` is now `'2.1.296, 2.1.306'`, the words oat-file-sync's log says beside an unmeasured CLI.
  - `withMeasured(fixture, record)` is THE WRITER'S ONE RULE. It adds the record under its exact version and keeps every other entry as it was (even one that is not a full record, and other top-level keys). Re-measuring a version replaces only that version's record. The map is written oldest first and the input is never touched.
  - `withMeasured` throws on a record naming no exact version, and on a fixture that is neither shape: rewriting it could drop what it holds.
- **The writer changed.** In scripts/measure-claude-cred-read.mjs, `--write-fixture` wrote this run's record ALONE, which would have dropped 2.1.296. It now:
  - checks `withMeasured` over the file BEFORE the run and refuses (exit 2, no variant run) when it could not add;
  - re-reads the file at write time;
  - writes `withMeasured(the file now, this run's record)`;
  - logs `it holds 2.1.296, 2.1.306, …`.
- **The readers.** Every one goes through `accounts.oatFileCaps()`, so 2.1.306 now behaves as 2.1.296 everywhere:
  - `_placeable` (no escape);
  - the pool's `oat-cli-unmeasured` refusal;
  - `_syncOatFileNow`, which writes or takes back the file;
  - `resolveForSpawn`, which reads the file, not CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN;
  - the row's door (`written · CLI 2.1.306`);
  - oat-file-sync.
  - The client's words take `{cli}`. data/bin has no reader. Nothing else changes.

- **What the owner gains.** Updating the hub's claude to 2.1.306 no longer takes the token files back from oat-only pool members. The pool keeps placing on them as on 2.1.296. The hub's CLI stays 2.1.296; this lane is only the measurement's record.

### lane incident-paint-gap — a paint gap on an idle desktop is not a freeze: a gap is jank only with a busy main thread or a person there; an unpainted gap is a `paint-gap-s` metric, never an auto incident
- **The report (2026-10-21).** The auto incident recorder filed two «jank storm» incidents on the owner's Windows desktop that were no jank: inc-mvi50qdh-ygmh (13:18Z «9.1 s») and inc-mvi5ggqh-1tz8 (13:30Z «620.8 s — worst frame 620 780 ms»), 2.369.336 client, Windows Chrome.
- **The bundles (measured).** longTasks: two, 690 ms / 306 ms, both minutes before the storms. frameGaps: 9 144 ms, 71 266 ms, 620 780 ms and smaller. compStalls: 9.9 / 3.1 / 6.7 / 6.7 / 71.7 / 6.4 s — the SAME gaps, seen by the compositor-stall arm. screenEvents empty; visibility 'visible'; ws connected; the action ring's last input 13:16:55Z (a pointer on the chat input), nothing during the gaps.
- **The cause.** The main thread was never blocked (no long task near 9 s, let alone 620 s; the 1 s timer kept ticking — that is how the "storm" was measured). rAF stopped because the window was not PAINTING — an idle Windows desktop (monitor off / lock screen / an occluded window; Chrome keeps `visibilityState` 'visible' on a lock screen, so neither the hidden gate nor the tab-return filter caught it). `jankStormVerdict` summed the one 620 s paint gap as «slow frames», `onRendererFreeze` (≥ 5 s) filed the incident, and the compositor-stall arm pushed a stall for the same gap.
- **The fix (src/lib/telemetry-client.js).** New PURE `paintGapKind({t, gap}, {longTasks, inputs})` → `jank` (a long task overlaps ≥ half the gap, or a pointer/key during it or within 1 s after) | `unpainted`. `jankStormVerdict` counts only `jank` gaps. The compositor-stall arm files its «compositor stall» incident only for a `jank` gap (person present — the GPU/RTX-5090 case it was built for, RED control kept) and otherwise writes a `paint-gap-s` metric + a `paint-gap` event — never an incident. `installInputStamp` (pointerdown/keydown) is the "a person was there" stamp ring (`recentInputs`); `installScreenWatch` now also records window `focus`/`blur`, Page-Lifecycle `freeze`/`resume` and the Idle Detection verdict when the permission is already held (never a new prompt), stamped into `screenEvents`. incident-recorder.js is unchanged — its snapshot already carries `screenEvents`.
- **The two incidents re-judged.** Both `unpainted` (620 s / 9 s gaps, the long tasks 690/306 ms minutes away, no input) ⇒ no storm, no auto incident — a `paint-gap-s` metric and a ring line instead. A 9 s gap with a 9 s long task ⇒ `jank`; a 6 s gap with a key 300 ms after ⇒ `jank`; a 71 s compositor stall with no input ⇒ `unpainted`.
- **Gate.** test-freeze-probe (PURE + wiring, 48 legs — the base verdict that counts every slow frame files both incidents as the RED control). No new i18n (telemetry-client has no UI strings). CHANGELOG ×3 + docs/kb-bugfix-invariants.md (index + essay) + docs/kb-features.md + docs/kb-file-structure.md, same commit. No version bump — integrated, signed and cut by 主开发.

### lane vault-chip-zone-errors — two uncaught client errors at every start, found and fixed at their causes; the console ring keeps the stack and an offline tool names the line (incidents inc-mvi50qdh-ygmh / inc-mvi5ggqh-1tz8, 2.369.336 client, Windows Chrome, 2026-10-21 13:12–13:13Z)
- **What the bundles said.** The page loaded at 13:12:54Z. Its console ring then held `unhandled: Failed to execute 'insertBefore' on 'Node': The node before which the new node is to be inserted is not a child of this node.` twice (at load and at +5 s), then `uncaught: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` twice, 4 ms apart, from `bundle.js?v=…:1`. The minified bundle is one line, so `:1` named nothing.
- **Error 1 — the lock chip, `src/lib/vault-unlock.js:76` on the base.** `drawChip` did `host.insertBefore(chip, document.getElementById(beforeId) || null)` with host `#taskbar-tray` and the For-you button found document-wide.
  - The owner's synced `chrome.arrangement` (read-only, chrome keys only) has For-you in `toolbar-row2` between springs, and `taskbar-tray: []`. The bundle agrees: the For-you press was at y = 67 of a 1100 px viewport, the second toolbar row.
  - So the reference was not a child of the host, and the insert threw at every apply of the vault's facts. The two `unhandled` entries are `maybeNagVault` (the onboarding check) and `initVault`'s boot read, each reaching `applyVaultFacts`. A scratch hub with the owner's shape reproduced both, with these frames.
  - The throw stopped `drawLockStrip`, `drawGearMark`, the facts listeners and `onVaultState`'s `showUnlock`. So on the owner's desktop a locked vault showed NOTHING at start: no dialog, no strip, no ⚙ mark, no chip. The owner reached the dialog through the For-you item 12 s later.
- **Error 2 — the incident recorder, `src/lib/chat-enter-keys.js:76` on the base** (called from `src/lib/incident-recorder.js:55`). `actionKeyWords(e)` read `e.key.length`.
  - Chrome's autofill and saved passwords dispatch a bare `Event('keydown')` with no `key` on each field they fill, then input, change and a bare keyup. Measured through CDP `Autofill.trigger` on a card form: one keyless keydown per filled field.
  - The action ring fits this. It shows `C-Control`/`S-Shift`-shaped words, a modifier up and a fourth key, and no «typing» marker at all, so no character was typed into the dialog. Two fields were filled at once: two throws, 4 ms apart.
  - Right after the unlock, the owner triple-clicked the sidebar's session filter and pressed one key. That reads as clearing a user name the password manager put there (formless inputs are one synthetic form for it). This is inferred, not shipped: see the report.
  - The brief's suspect, «a renderer reading a missing list after the unlock broadcast», was not it: the throws came 0.7 s BEFORE the Unlock press.
- **The fix.**
  - `customize-mode.js` `slotBeside(id, fallback)`: the slot beside a movable chrome element is its OWN parent (the zone applyArrangement put it in) before it, else the fallback's end. The reference is always a child. `drawChip` uses it for both pairs (the taskbar and the phone nav), and app.js re-seats the chip after every arrangement (`placeVaultChip`), so it follows For-you when Customize moves it.
  - `applyVaultFacts` draws each lock sign under its own try (a `[vault]` console.error), so one sign's throw never takes the others or the dialog.
  - `actionKeyWords` answers a keydown with no string `key` as `{ key: '(fill)' }` (FILL_KEY) — the ring says a fill happened, never what (`keyMatches` already had this guard).
- **The ring keeps the stack.**
  - `src/lib/incident-stack.js` (PURE) `stackHead(err, origin)`: the first 3 `at` frames, the origin cut, the bundle's `line:column` kept, whole frames only, ≤ 400 chars. A frame too long for the room keeps its location and loses its name.
  - The recorder spreads it onto `uncaught` (`e.error`) and `unhandled` (`e.reason`) entries.
  - A full console ring of worst-case entries is 224 KB in bundle.json (+79 KB for the stacks), against the hub's 50 MB body cap (`express.json`). Measured by test-incident-recorder ③.
- **The map, served to nobody.**
  - `src/server/static-public.js`: express.static for every path but `*.map`, judged decoded (`%2E` is a dot). Such a path falls through to the later routes and ends in a 404. WebDAV and proxy `.map` paths are untouched. server.js keeps one line, at the bootstrap-size cap.
  - `scripts/symbolicate.mjs <bundle.json>` maps the ring's frames OFFLINE. The map is NEVER a file (主开发's ruling: the product keeps no map on disk; the build line is unchanged). It is rebuilt in memory (0.3–0.8 s) with the client esbuild step's flags PARSED off package.json's build script at run time — never a copied list; test-incident-recorder's census pins parsed == the script's — and refused unless the JS equals public/bundle.js byte for byte. A frame whose `?v=` is another build is refused (`--any-build` maps it anyway).
  - The `source-map` package is not in node_modules, so a 40-line base64-VLQ decoder is in the script.
- **Tests.**
  - test-vault-chrome Z: the chip before For-you on a default chrome and on the owner's shape, at a load and live as Customize moves it (row 2 → the right zone → the default). The dialog, strip and ⚙ mark show at that load, and the phone pair is placed the same way. A two-field bare-Event fill and the REAL `Autofill.trigger` path throw nothing; the captured ring says `(fill)`; the unlock + 6 s throws nothing. Every page exception is captured with CDP `Runtime.exceptionThrown`.
  - test-vault-chrome Z-RED: a patched bundle with the pre-fix chip and key words throws both errors. The ring keeps both stacks, and symbolicate names `src/lib/vault-unlock.js` (the insert) and `src/lib/chat-enter-keys.js` (the `.length`) from the real capture.
  - test-chat-enter-ime §2c (+ control).
  - test-incident-recorder (new, fast).
  - test-csp-report ⑨: the map in public/ answers 404 on every spelling; MUTANT: the guard cut serves it.

### lane job-wrapper-proto1-retire — the job wrapper's protocol-1 compat is removed as scheduled: a ≤ .330 server's spec on the command line is never read again (the expiry test-job-model set at .333 — lane job-wrapper-update-window, agent feedback fb-7f7be1e24e; base 609993e2 = int340 on the 2.369.339 cut)
- **What was due.** .333 kept a second door in data/bin/job-wrapper.js. A ≤ .330 server put the job's spec — argv, cwd and env, the job's secrets — on the wrapper's command line as base64 JSON (protocol 1), and the wrapper READ it, loudly, for an update's window (`COMPAT_PROTO_1` + `argvSpec()` + a warning line). Its expiry was 2.369.340: test-job-model went RED there while the flag was live, which int340's scratch .340 bump showed.
- **Why retire rather than move the date.** Every hub of the fleet is ≥ .331 (主开发's reading for this lane; the owner's 18 instances were measured ≥ .318 on 2026-10-15 and update through the product). A ≤ .330 server spawning a .340 wrapper is a hub that skipped nine releases in the middle of an update.
- **The wrapper.** COMPAT_PROTO_1, argvSpec and the warning line are gone.
  - An argument that is no file of the ctl dir, with no `--proto=`, is judged by its SHAPE only: base64 of a JSON object (`eyJ…`, a length that is a multiple of 4) = a ≤ .330 caller.
  - That run ends «[job-wrapper] not started: the server spoke protocol 1 (a server older than 2.369.331) — this wrapper speaks 2; an update in flight, or a server not restarted after one»: exit 75, exit.json reason update_window with proto {server 1, wrapper 2}. That is the road a protocol-3 spec takes.
  - The argument is never decoded, never echoed and never written; the ctl dir holds only the run's pid.json, exit.json and current.log.
  - Any other shape keeps «the spec path names no file of the ctl dir» (exit 2).
- **Who judges that end — measured with the REAL 2.369.330 engine (a scratch worktree at the .330 release) over this wrapper.**
  - Its 5 s sweep usually runs before its restart in a 45 s window. That engine predates update_window: it reads exit 75 as an error and files the run failed — «failed exit=75 error» to the agent, «Task …: failed (error)» to For you. That is fb-7f7be1e24e's false failure, now worded «not started … an update in flight» in the job's log. A cron child's next fire runs it.
  - When the restart comes first, this tree's engine judges the exit.json at boot: update_window (the run started before its boot), interrupted, no failure notice, and the one-shot task runs again (update-rerun → done, exit 0).
  - The .333 essay listed this residual («its old server says failed (once)»). An old server cannot be taught; the false failure stays possible only on a hub that skipped nine releases, and the fleet has none.
- **Tests.**
  - test-job-model: the expiry row is now the PIN of the removal — the wrapper's code holds no COMPAT_PROTO_1, no argvSpec, no base64 decode and no atob (its header records the removal in words). CONTROL: the ≤ .339 compat patched back whole, the flag alone, and one decode in the branch are each RED.
  - test-jobs-engine §12: the .330 call on the REAL wrapper, with a canary in the spec's env, gets exit 75, update_window (1 → 2). Its stderr and log are exactly the named line. No byte of the spec (the canary, its name, any 16 chars of the argument) is on stderr or in the ctl dir. NEGATIVE CONTROL: the read patched back in runs the job with the canary.
  - test-jobs-engine §12 M1 (the spec on argv again) now ends «not started» too. Its cmdline rows read the wrapper's own /proc/self through the front script, because the wrapper is gone by then.
  - test-agent-output-sinks §3: the .330 call is not run, and no word of the job reaches the log.
  - The new tests over the base wrapper are RED at each of those rows.
- Gates: the fast gate on a scratch copy bumped to .340 (never committed: package.json, package-lock.json, src/agentd/version.js and release/agentd/manifest.json stay .339) + test-job-model ×3, test-jobs-engine, test-agent-output-sinks, test-jobs-browser, test-record-clear-census and test-architecture (the lane report has the counts). No version bump — integrated, signed and cut by 主开发.

## 2.369.339 — 2026-10-21

### lane werift-lite-multihomed — a desktop stream stayed black once the viewer's browser was allowed the microphone on a multi-homed computer: werift wrote a=ice-lite where no browser reads it, and kept its FIRST nomination for good (backlog B-c7d7, found by lane stream-mic-road 2026-10-21; base c1aba74c = 2.369.337)
- THE MEASUREMENT (the base, this box — 6 adapters: two LAN addresses, two docker bridges, the tailnet v4/v6; headless Chrome, the real bundle): granted `audioCapture` (CDP `Browser.grantPermissions` — a person who pressed 「麦克风」 once), Chrome offered 6 host addresses (+ 6 TCP) instead of ONE mDNS name. ICE reached `connected`, DTLS stayed `connecting`, the selected pair changed 10× in 30 s, no picture (the view's ICE restarts at 15 s and 30 s changed nothing). A probe hooked into a bundle copy logged werift's checks: the FIRST check it received already carried USE-CANDIDATE — Chrome's docker-bridge candidate → werift's LAN-candidate socket — and werift took it as THE pair (`checkComplete` sets `nominated` only while none is). werift's sockets are wildcard-bound: its answer to that peer leaves with the source address the route picks (the bridge's, not the LAN address Chrome checked), so Chrome never matched it — the pair never validated on Chrome's side — and werift's DTLS went there for ever. Chrome's selected pair (bridge ↔ bridge) sent ClientHello retransmits (1463 B) and received 0 B.
- THE ROOT CAUSE: werift 0.25.0 writes `a=ice-lite` only inside each MEDIA section (its session never writes it). RFC 8839 §5.3 makes it a SESSION-level attribute and Chrome reads it only there — its own copy of the offer (`pc.remoteDescription.sdp`) has no a=ice-lite at all. Taking the agent for a FULL agent, Chrome nominates semi-aggressively (USE-CANDIDATE on its first checks, before any pair is valid). With one mDNS socket the first nominated pair happened to be the working one; with six adapters it was a cross-interface pair. A page-side experiment that ONLY moved the line to the session level played in 526 ms (3 of 3). The mic lane's hub-side filter of the browser's host candidates could not help: werift learns the same addresses as peer-reflexive from the checks.
- THE LATENT SECOND HALF (measured with the attribute fixed): Chrome then nominates only its selected, VALIDATED pair — and ~0.4 s later RENOMINATES another as more pairs pass; werift ignored it. It played only because Chrome still accepts packets on the old connection (504 KB arrived on the abandoned pair, 0 B on the selected one).
- THE FIX (the device; kind (a) for the pairs — werift's own option — plus the attribute where RFC 8839 puts it): `liteSessionSdp` (src/stream-model.js, PURE) = the offer's SDP with ONE `a=ice-lite` before the first m= (the media copies dropped), on the first offer and every ICE-restart offer. `followChoice` (src/agentd/stream-host.js) on werift's `iceFilterStunResponse` hook (asked before werift answers a check — always true, every check is answered): a USE-CANDIDATE check under THIS generation's ufrag moves the sending pair (`connection.nominated`) to the pair werift just took, a microtask later; the agent's log says «the browser moved its pair: …». No werift patch file: the tree has no patch mechanism and package.json is not this lane's to change; the hook is werift's public option. No hub-side candidate filter, no pinned address.
- THE STRIP — NEVER SILENT before a picture (src/lib/machine-desktop.js): when the view's connect budget (STREAM_LIMITS.connectMs, 15 s) runs out and it asks an ICE restart (streamStep code `timeout`), the strip says leg ⑥'s words 「串流中断：没能及时连上——正在重新连接…」 until a picture plays (one stream; a ② pane through its own `said`). Before: 「串流 · 连接中…」 for the whole restart budget, 45 s, then the VNC picture. No new words: with the fix there is no multi-homed failure left to name, so no 「多网卡：…」 line.
- THE NUMBERS (this box, 10 runs each, open → playing): the default origin (one mDNS name) 527 ms median (523–530) on the base, 426 ms (424–535) fixed; the microphone allowed: never on the base (0 of 3 within 10 s, 0 of 2 within 30 s), 527 ms (524–528, 10 of 10) fixed.
- THE GATES: test-desktop-webrtc-chrome ⑲ (the lane's ⑰ — renumbered at int339, lane stream-mic-road's ⑰ / ⑱ came first) — the real grant: 6 host addresses, it plays, the browser's copy of the offer says a=ice-lite at the session level, the picture arrives on the browser's selected pair; RED CONTROL = the bundle copy as werift alone runs it ⇒ black for 8 s, DTLS connecting (judged where the browser offers ≥ 2 addresses — a one-address runner says so); the mDNS road plays both ways; an agent that answers no check ⇒ the strip's words at 15 s, RED CONTROL = the pre-lane window silent. test-desktop-webrtc §15 (fast, deterministic on any box): two raw sockets nominate in turn against the REAL host + werift — its DTLS retransmits follow to the second, RED CONTROL the werift-alone copy keeps the first; a nomination of an older ICE generation moves nothing, RED CONTROL without the guard.

### lane stream-mic-road — the viewer's microphone reaches a paired machine's apps through a virtual microphone (backlog B-7af0; the product step after lane stream-mic-wheel-probe; base c1aba74c = 2.369.337)
- THE PREMISE, MEASURED FIRST: the brief named «the existing audio m-line» and «beside 「声音」». On c1aba74c the desktop stream had neither — src/agentd/stream-host.js offered ONE video transceiver (sendonly) + the `input` data channel, src/lib/stream-view.js answered video only, B-aec9 (speaker passthrough) is still parked, and the intercom (the voice on the machine's speakers) existed only in the probe's rig (mic-road.mjs offered its own sendrecv m-line). 主开发 confirmed the reading (16:12Z): the m-line is built HERE, offered only on the page's ask; 「麦克风」 is the strip's first audio control; the speakers road is built here as the same renderer; separate helpers per OS.
- THE M-LINE: `stream-offer {…, mic: true}` (asked by src/agentd/client.js only of an agent whose hello-ack says `stream-mic` — an older agent streams without it, never asked) ⇒ the agent adds `addTransceiver('audio', {direction:'recvonly'})` (Opus) inside the one BUNDLE; the answer's `mic: true` tells the page. The page (stream-view) takes it SENDONLY with no track; the strip's press = `setMic(track)` = `sender.replaceTrack` — no renegotiation; off = `replaceTrack(null)` + `track.stop()`. B-aec9's seam: the machine's sound turns this same m-line sendrecv. The page's `ontrack` never takes an audio track as the picture.
- THE DEVICE (src/desktop-mic.js, SHARED): its OWN helper per OS (tools/vibespace-mic/ as text in src/mic-helper-source.js, scripts/mic-helper-embed.mjs; built on the machine: Windows csc into %LOCALAPPDATA%\vibespace\helpers — the window helper's way; a Mac swiftc both slices + lipo + ad-hoc — the screen helper's pipeline, a separate binary so the screen helper's version, identity and TCC grant never change; the compiler found by FILE). Facts: the helper's endpoints/devices + defaults, `installedAt` (~/.vibespace/mic-installed.json, written by OUR install's starter) vs the last boot, the default it replaced (~/.vibespace/mic-default.json); `prepare` on a Mac builds + STAGES the plug-in (clang -bundle, ad-hoc) and says its SHA-256. THE RECEIVER (one per stream session, made at the audio track): started by the first RTP packet, stopped after MIC_LIMITS.idleMs 1500 without one and with the session; Windows = each packet a live Ogg page → the stream's ffmpeg (the probe's -fflags nobuffer -flags low_delay) → s16le 48 kHz stereo → the helper's `render` → «CABLE Input» (VS_MIC_DEVICE) or the default speaker (VS_MIC_SPEAKERS=1); Mac = each packet length-framed → the helper (AudioToolbox decodes the Opus) → the plug-in's device by UID. Every name rides the env, never argv. Its numbers ride `stream-stats` as `mic` (where the voice IS going).
- THE OP `stream-mic` (THREE-TOUCH: the handler, `stream-mic` in the hello-ack, the client's gated `streamMic` + `stream-mic-result` in the routing set): `action:'facts'` (`force`, `prepare`) = a read; `action:'default'` (`to: virtual | restore` — 「设为默认麦克风」 / 「改回」) = an ACT (src/device-acts.js `stream-mic:default`, `streamMic` in CLIENT_ACT_METHODS, its `by` at every call — §91).
- PURE src/mic-model.js: the tables (VB-CABLE Pack45 URL + zip SHA-256 + setup SHA-256 + its EV signer «BUREL VINCENT»; BlackHole 2ch 0.7.1 URL + SHA-256 + team Q5C99V536K, GPL-3; «VibeSpace Microphone» UID VibeSpaceMic_UID), micStateOf (absent / installed / reboot_owed / inactive / unsupported / unknown + where the voice goes), micStep (the toggle's table: only a press asks, only a grant attaches, close / lock / stream_end / track_ended stop, `restore` never re-opens), micRoadWords, the build plans + spawns.
- THE SETUP ROW 「安装虚拟麦克风」 (PURE src/mic-install.js virtualMicInstallPlan / virtualMicRemovePlan — beside src/machine-desktop-model.js, NOT in it: the agent bundles that one through src/installed-apps.js and a Mac plan names `osascript`, a word the agent bundle never carries (test-stream-mac §7, lane mac-window-list-helper) — registered in src/installs.js as `virtual-mic` / `virtual-mic-remove`, `from: 'mic'` — planned from the `stream-mic` facts with `prepare`): Windows = the probe's mic-install.ps1 as the plan's commands (an admin-only directory, the zip SHA-256 before Expand-Archive, the setup SHA-256 + Authenticode signer before `-i -h`) behind ONE UAC (the TightVNC starter; no elevation = exit 5 = no_admin), and THE STEP TightVNC lacks — the default speaker AND microphone of every role snapshotted before UAC and put back after (IPolicyConfig, three passes 2 s apart), said «Kept your default speaker and microphone»; the restart note; never a reboot. Mac = the administrator password dialog with OUR text (the page's language) running a FIXED root script whose names ride the env (`quoted form of`): ours = copy the staged bundle, chown root, check the INSTALLED binary's SHA-256 against the staged one, restart coreaudiod; BlackHole (no compiler to stage ours) = downloaded at the press, SHA-256 + Developer ID team checked before the dialog, copied root-only and checked again before installer; a dialog nobody answers is withdrawn after 300 s (exit 6 = no_password; nothing copied before a password). The uninstall door: Windows = VB-CABLE's own setup in C:\Program Files\VB\CABLE (signer checked) — the person presses «Remove Driver» (the unmeasured silent `-u -h` is not used); Mac = the bundle out of the HAL folder + coreaudiod restarted. src/server/desktop-access.js runs both through the UAC runner (`adminDialog` beside `uac`, `env` on runStream); the route re-reads the facts (`still-absent` / `still-present`).
- THE STRIP (src/lib/stream-mic-strip.js in src/lib/machine-desktop.js — the ONE strip, the phone's too): shows once a stream offered the m-line; a press asks the browser (MIC_CONSTRAINTS: echo cancellation + NS + AGC, mono); live = aria-pressed + the red dot (`--red`) + «你的声音 → 本机应用的麦克风『…』» (the agent's own word from the stream's numbers first) or «对方电脑会从扬声器播放你的声音» + 「安装虚拟麦克风…」 every time the speakers road is in force; stops with the window, the page hidden (a lock), a press, its stream's end, the track's end; nothing remembered ⇒ a restored window starts it off. THE MACHINES CARD (showMachineDesktopDialog): the virtual microphone in one line + 「安装虚拟麦克风…」 / 「设为默认麦克风」 / 「改回」 / 「移除虚拟麦克风…」; the install dialog shows the plan's facts (what, from where, the license — VB-CABLE donationware with vb-cable.com, BlackHole GPL-3 — what the person will see) above its commands.
- A RISK FOUND (NOT this lane's code — base c1aba74c reproduces it; 主开发 opened lane werift-lite-multihomed, and the microphone does not ship to master before its fix): once a page's origin holds the MICROPHONE permission, Chrome gathers on EVERY adapter (6 on this box: 2 LAN, 2 docker bridges, tailscale v4/v6) instead of the default one behind mDNS, and a NEW stream to werift's ICE-lite agent never connects on a multi-homed box (test-desktop-webrtc-chrome on base: plays before `Browser.grantPermissions(audioCapture)`, never after — with the track live and after it stopped; skipping the browser's host candidates at the hub does not help). `--use-fake-ui-for-media-stream` alone reds the base suite's ①. ### lane reply-infer-owner-between — the judged plain-reply road is TOLD what the chat's owner wrote between the send and the reply (agent feedback fb-377439b167 from a fleet instance on .334; base c1aba74c = 2.369.337)
- THE INCIDENT (the agent's own words, 2026-10-21): a peer's plain two-word message at 09:04Z was judged (0.90) an answer to the agent's send of 01:43Z. But the person who owns the chat had sent a voice note ([audio], untranscribed) at 09:01Z, between the two, and the peer was answering THAT. The agent was woken for nothing.
- WHY: `PLANS['reply-infer']` gave the judge only `sent`, `reply` and `gap` («never another message of the conversation — cost»). The fact that decided it, the owner's voice note 3 min before, sat in the engine's own thread index for free and was never passed.
- PURE (src/channel-filter.js):
  - `inferBetween(record, sent, ctx)` reads `ctx.turnsBetween(sentAt, at)` and returns `between {own, ownLast {kind, minBefore}, others, capped}`, now carried on `inferCandidate`'s answer. It keeps only turns strictly between the two instants, at most the newest `INFER.between` = 5. No reader, or a reader that cannot read, gives `null`, and the judge works as before.
  - `turnKindOf`: a voice note (an audio attachment or the vendor's `[audio]` token), else words, else a picture, else a file.
  - `inferBetweenLine` words the fact in FIXED words: counts, a kind and minutes, never anybody's words. «Nobody else wrote between sent and reply.» when the list is empty; «In the last 5 messages before the reply, …» when capped.
- THE JUDGE (src/decision-model.js):
  - `PART('between', 300, { kind: 'line' })`, last in the record.
  - `recordCeiling` 700 → **804** (+104 = estTokens of «between: » + 300 characters + the newline = 310 ASCII / 3). Every part at its cap now fits whole; at 700 the same record would be cut.
  - `REPLY_INFER_VERSION` 2: the question reads `between`, and a reply that follows the owner's own message more closely «is more likely an answer to THAT message: score it low unless its words clearly answer the agent's message».
  - The version is in the memo key, so a v1 answer judged blind (the incident's 0.90) is never reused.
- THE ENGINE (src/server/channels-engine.js):
  - `placeCtx` gains `turnsBetween`, over the thread index the place rules already read: the newest THREAD_IX_RECORDS of the stored log plus the batch, sorted once per batch and only when asked. No vendor call.
  - Each turn is `{at, self, kind}`. `self` = `FO.selfRead` AND not any agent's send from here: an agent writes from the owner's account, so its echo is not the owner's turn.
  - The asking principal's own sends (the send, its parts, its echo 0.8 s later) are not «between» at all. Vendor notices are nobody's.
  - `preInfer` passes `between: F.inferBetweenLine(c.between)`. The judge stays the ONE caller.
- THE AGENT:
  - A judged hit after the owner's own message has why `INFER_WHY_BETWEEN` «judged an answer to your message of <time>; the user also wrote in between». «The user» is the agent manual's word for the owner; the brief said «the person».
  - `sent.between {own, ownLast}` rides the hit, and the hand-over line prints it beside the score: «judged 0.90; the user also wrote in between — a voice note, 3 min before this».
  - The CLI's `watch` / `--show` print rules, not hits, so the words live where the score is printed, in the wake / next-turn block.
  - channel-words reads the new why before the plain one, in zh + ja.
- NOT IN THIS LANE: transcribing voice notes (a billed ASR call per note; the owner decides). No vendor call was added.
- THE GATES:
  - test-channel-filter ⑳: 21 new checks (363). They cover the incident, the brief's line word for word, nothing between, no reader, others only, the K bound, strictly-between, the line ≤ 300, the kinds table, the thread / no-send / before-the-send exclusions (reader never asked), the why + the hand-over, zh + ja + the reader order, and 2 patched-copy controls (no fact = the base; no K bound).
  - test-decision-model ㉑ (260): the part, the ceiling 804 = 700 + 104, the cap fits whole, v2 ≠ the v1 memo key, the line rides last.
  - test-channel-agent-watch ⑪ (94): the real decision engine's input ends «between: Nobody else wrote between sent and reply.».
  - test-channels-engine ㉗ (heavy, 817 = 810 + 7): THE INCIDENT over the real ingest loop, with a judge STUB recording its parts. Inputs: the agent's send at T, its echo from the owner's account, the owner's `[audio]` at T+7h18m, the peer's «Sounds good» 3 min later. The between line names the voice note; the echo is not counted.

### lane mac-repair-retires-stale — a re-pair retires the older installs of the SAME hub; the «second agent with an old token» notice names the live install and its stop words stop the agent itself (backlog B-06e9 — the owner's Macbook 2026-10-18: four installs, three re-dialing with old tokens)
- THE GAP: each pairing installs a root keyed by the dial ADDRESS (`~/.vibespace/device@<host>`; its launchd job / user unit / scheduled task keyed by that root). A re-pair through another address (the LAN name, the Tailscale name, the relay) left the older roots running, each re-dialing with its retired token every 30 s for ever; the take-over block stops only THIS root's daemon. dial.json held `{url, token}` — no hub identity — so nothing on the machine could tell an older pairing of THIS hub from another hub's install (installs of different hubs coexist by design). The hub's stop words were generic (`launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/<label>`), and bootout alone does not stop the agent: the launchd job is a supervisor that exits 3 («already running») while the agent runs detached (ppid 1) holding `<root>/state/agentd.lock`.
- THE HUB'S ID: `src/server/dial-pairing.js` `hubId()` mints `vh-` + 16 hex ONCE into data/agentd/hub-id (O_EXCL, 0600; the PURE rule `hubIdOf` in src/dial-facts.js). A device hears it only after it proved its pairing: the --dial-check probe's 200 (`hub`) and, on a dialed link, the hub's `hello` (`hub`, a DeviceManager option — a field an older daemon ignores). `--dial-check` prints `hub id: vh-…` under its ok line; both installers keep it in dial.json; the daemon writes it at an ACCEPTED dial (after the host token matched, never over a dial.json rewritten for another address), so an older install learns it when it next dials in.
- THE RETIRE (install.sh `retire_siblings`, the ps1 twin): only when the dial check ran and passed AND the new daemon dialed in (its own state/dial-status.json `connectedAt` ≥ this run's start; ≤ 20 s, else «→ older installs on this machine were NOT retired: this install has not dialed in yet …»). Every other `~/.vibespace/device@*` root: the same `hub` ⇒ retire; another ⇒ kept («→ kept: … (another VibeSpace's install on this machine)»); a hub on one side only ⇒ unknown; no hub on either side ⇒ the same device id (the dial URL's `device=`) retires, another is unknown. Retire = the supervisor first (launchctl bootout / systemctl --user disable --now / Export-ScheduledTask + Unregister-ScheduledTask), its plist / unit / task XML MOVED to ~/.vibespace/disabled-launchagents/ (a name already there gets a `.<epoch>` suffix — never overwritten), then the agent holding the sibling's lock, ONLY when its command line names vibespace-device (TERM, ≤ 5 s, KILL if still alive). The root and its state stay. Said once: «→ retired N older installs of this hub: … (kept under ~/.vibespace; their launch items moved to ~/.vibespace/disabled-launchagents/)»; an unknown one is LISTED with its exact stop command and never touched.
- THE HUB'S WORDS (PURE src/dial-health.js): `liveInstallOf(dial.mintedBase)` = the installer's own root rule (the suite runs the installer's sed + tr in bash on each base); `dialHealthRow` adds `live`; `stopRecipeOf(platform, {liveKey})` = list the installs (with liveKey the live one is left out), stop the supervisor, AND kill the agent by its lock pid — per platform. The row (sidebar-mounts.js) and the For-you item (dial-health-watch.js itemOf) add «The live install on that machine is {live}; stop the others — …» (when the record names a base) and the door «Re-pairing this machine from its Machines card retires the older installs of this hub for you (an install too old to know this hub is listed with its stop command)», zh + ja. Copy copies the recipe.
- WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: the owner's three stale installs predate the hub id and are never accepted (retired tokens), so they never learn it — a re-pair LISTS them with their commands and does not retire them (the brief's rule: an unknown install is never touched). One way to attribute them, not taken: probe each sibling's own address with its own token and let the refusal name the hub — an unauthenticated answer (spoofable) and a network call per sibling.
- Pins moved: test-agentd-upgrade-signature (the dial link's `serveConnection` gains `onAuthed`), test-writer-sweep (+ the new `ps -p "$SP"` argv read, with its reason), mount-reader-census (dial-pairing.js 1 → 2: data/agentd/hub-id). test-device-install-check's control (n) follows the dial.json writer's new `"$HUB_ID"` argument.
- Tests: test-device-install-check +16 (R-1…R-16, controls (p) (q)): a scratch HOME with five siblings (two plists + a unit of this hub, one lock naming an innocent `sleep`, another hub's, a pre-change one), stub launchctl / systemctl recording ms-stamped calls; the REAL installer against the REAL dial gate retires the three, stops the two fake agents (not the innocent pid), keeps the other hub's, lists the unknown one; the first retire call comes after the new daemon's `connectedAt`; a daemon learns the hub at its next accepted dial through the hub's real device client (CONTROL (p): without `onAuthed` it never does); CONTROL (q) the installer without the retire step leaves all five; a link the hub drops ⇒ «NOT retired»; the classifier's table; the ps1 road pinned (no PowerShell here). test-dial-health ROW-1…7 (ROW-7 runs the copied recipe in bash: the listing names only the others, the kill line stops that agent, never the live one), W-0, H-2b, CONTROLS (e) no kill line (f) no live install. test-host-stale-dialer-ui: the REAL daemon learns the worktree server's hub id; the row names device@127.0.0.1 and the door (zh + en); Copy copies the recipe.
