## 2.369.325 — 2026-10-20

### lane vault-relock-door — the vault's restart was silent on an open tab (the owner 2026-10-20: 「为啥我有的时候更新后需要重新输入二次密码有时候不用」; B-9674-class)
- THE SYMPTOM: the vault locks at EVERY restart by law (the DEK is zeroed on SIGTERM; no auto-unlock — unchanged). What differed was the ASK. The unlock dialog opened only at a page LOAD (`initVault`, src/lib/app.js) or after the stale-bundle reload an UPDATE triggers (`_checkBundleFreshness`). A restart that KEEPS the bundle (a crash, a same-build `systemctl restart`, the `Restart=always` respawn) reconnects the open tab WITHOUT a reload — and nothing re-read the vault state, so the tab sat on its stale `unlocked` UI while everything vault-gated (device links re-dialing, the relay, account switches) waited in silence until the owner noticed.
- THE FACTS NAME THE PROCESS: `facts()` (src/server/vault-engine.js) gained `startedAt` = the engine's construction time (the server's boot, ms), captured once at `create()` and unchanged by lock/unlock — a NEW process is the only new value. It is how a page tells a RESTART (a new startedAt) from a lock ACT (the same one). test-vault-engine §L pins it.
- THE OPEN TAB ASKS ON A RESTART: src/lib/vault-unlock.js `onVaultState(f)` applies the facts, then opens `showUnlock()` ONCE when `state === 'locked'` AND `startedAt` differs from the one this page last saw. The `vault-state` broadcast and a reconnect re-read both route through it; a lock ACT (`立即锁定` from another device, an agent's lock, the idle lock) carries the SAME startedAt — the chip and the strip only, no dialog (the RED CONTROL). On every ws reconnect AFTER the boot read (`vaultBooted`), the tab re-reads `/api/vault/state` so a bundle-preserving restart re-asks; the first connect is the page load itself, which the boot read handles. THE LOAD-TIME ask stays UNCONDITIONAL on locked — `maybeNagVault` (app.js) may pre-read the facts, so gating the boot on startedAt would wrongly suppress it (the gate caught this: ③/⑤ reds until the boot path was reverted to the original unconditional ask).
- THE PERSISTENT STRIP (owner decision 2026-10-20 「那需要一个常驻的警告提醒还没解锁」): `drawLockStrip()` draws `#vault-lock-strip` — the maintenance banner's shape, a flex child of #main-wrapper below `#maintenance-banner` when both show (public/style.css, a `--red` tone, SVG lock icon, zh+ja). It is drawn by `applyVaultFacts` (shown WHENEVER locked, incl. after a person's lock act; removed on unlock/not-set-up) and is NOT dismissable (no ×, no 稍后 — only the dialog's 稍后 closes the dialog). Its `解锁…` button fires `vs-vault-door`. The modal overlay (z 99998) sits above it, so the strip is reachable once the dialog is dismissed and never covers the dialog's button.
- THE FOR-YOU ITEM: src/server/vault-hooks.js `wireVaultHooks` now takes `userTodos` (wired in mounts-plugins-wiring.js) and, at boot when the vault is SET UP and LOCKED, files ONE tray notice (`userTodos.add('vault', {origin:'vault', kind:'notice', action:{type:'vault-unlock'}, i18n})`); its body-click door (src/lib/user-todos-actions.js) opens the unlock dialog via `vs-vault-door`. `onUnlock` resolves it (a person's unlock on any device clears it everywhere through the store's broadcast); a second boot while still locked re-files the SAME row (the store dedupes by sessionKey+text+action); a vault that is not set up files nothing. The item key: sessionKey `vault`, origin `vault`, action type `vault-unlock`. New English key extracted via `i18nKey(...)` in vault-hooks.js; zh+ja added.
- GATES: the unlock LAW is untouched — test-vault-law green. test-vault-engine (+§L startedAt, 83). test-vault-secrets (+⑨ the For-you filing: not-set-up files none, set-up+unlocked none, set-up+locked ONE, a second boot keeps one, unlock resolves — 130). test-user-todos-layout ② origin census: PRODUCERS gained `src/server/vault-hooks.js: vault`, the site count 54→55 (314). The heavy test-vault-chrome (56): the strip on ③/⑤/after 稍后/gone after ④; the new ③c (the OPEN tab re-asks on a bundle-preserving restart with NO navigate; a same-startedAt idle re-broadcast is the chip only — the RED CONTROL); and ③c-RED a patched worktree bundle (the reconnect re-read and the broadcast re-ask reverted) stays silent on a reconnect — the fix is load-bearing.

### lane channels-attachment-outside-archive — backlog B-5f20: a file on a message OUTSIDE the saved copy is fetched (the owner's agent, 2026-10-20: `vibespace-channels attachment` answered `not-found` for a Lark DM file it had found by `search --full` + `read --around`, while the raw `api` verb fetched it — 200, 206 KB; FIX, base 558de12a = 2.369.323; dispatched in 主开发's conversation with lane stream-mic-wheel-probe)
- **Before.** src/server/channels-engine.js `attachment()` found the carrier in the ARCHIVE only — the agent gate (`store.findRecord(msg)`) and `ownerRecordOf` (findRecord, then the newest 5000). An `around` read answers older messages from the vendor and stores nothing (F8), so the line `read --around` printed (`fetch: vibespace-channels attachment <conv> <msg> <id>`) always answered `no message in this conversation carries that attachment`, ZERO vendor calls (measured on the base engine loaded as a scratch copy over this lane's fixture).
- **After.** `aroundFor` (THE around read — the owner's sheet and the agent's `--around`) remembers each answered message that carries a file (non-body parts: id, name, mime) by (account, conversation, message): `noteShownOutside`, memory only, ≤ 2000 messages, newest kept. `attachment()` asks the archive FIRST, then that memory (`shownCarrier`); a hit rides the SAME leg — `Att.fetchVerdict` (capability, enabled, one flight, back-off, budget), the agents' share, `spendAs('agent'|'owner')` + `vendor()` → `e.adapter.fetchAttachment(convId, {messageId, attachmentId, mime, name})`, the message-scoped LRU cache — and the answer carries `source: 'vendor'` | `'archive'` (the agent route's `X-VibeSpace-Attachment` JSON gained `source`). Nothing is stored (the log's bytes identical); the archive window is unchanged.
- **Why the memory, not the ids the caller typed.** Lark's resource address (`im/v1/messages/:message_id/resources/:file_key`) names no chat: a fetch by whatever pair a caller typed would serve a file of ANOTHER conversation through the reach of this one. The vendor's own `around` answer for THIS conversation is what places a message in it. So a pair never shown here is refused before any call (`not-found`: "that message is not in the saved copy, and no read --around showed it in this conversation — find it first: …"), and a shown message the vendor no longer has answers "…not in the saved copy, and the vendor has no such message (or no such file on it) any more — nothing fetched" (remembered like any vendor refusal). The memory dies with the process: after a restart the agent reads `--around` again (its line is printed again).
- **Capability.** An account whose channel lists files but cannot fetch them (`caps.attachments !== 'fetch'`) answers `not-supported`, naming the account — the capability row, never an adapter id.
- **The fixture.** src/channels/fake.js: the fake vendor's `fetchAttachment` knows its search ARCHIVE (a vendor knows its whole history); the archive gained a Lark-`file`-shaped message — `<kind>-ops-old-file`, file key `file_v3_00fake_<kind>_q3plan`, `Q3-plan.pdf`, no type said — the owner's case with its ids rewritten.
- **The CLI and the manual.** data/bin/vibespace-channels: the `attachment` help names the road (`read <conv> --around <msg id>` prints its line; the file is fetched from the vendor by its ids); a vendor-sourced save prints one line under `saved …`: "(the message is not in the saved copy — read --around showed it; the file was fetched from the vendor by its ids, the message is still not saved)". The command is unchanged — `attachment <conv> <msg id> <attachment id>` (the brief's `--msg` is that positional `<msg id>`). docs/agent/channels-manual.md: `not-found`'s new meanings + the road bullet.
- **Left as it is.** The owner's Around sheet still draws its 「not saved — open the conversation」 chip and asks nothing (test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑪b pins zero asks); the owner's `?msg=` door now serves such a file — a thumbnail there is the window's design choice, not this fix.
- **Gates.** test-channel-search §D (+14, 106): `--full` finds the file message, typed ids before any read ⇒ not-found naming both + ZERO calls, `--around` shows the line, the fetch = ONE adapter call `{convId, messageId, attachmentId, mime:null}` charged to `spentBy.agent` (owner's share untouched), the second fetch = the cache (zero calls, nothing charged), a wrong message ⇒ not-found naming both, another agent ⇒ the uniform not-found, the owner's door on a shown picture ⇒ `type=image`, charged to `spentBy.owner`, nothing stored (log hash), a metadata-only channel ⇒ `not-supported` by name; a message the vendor lost ⇒ one call, "…the vendor has no such message", then remembered. §K: the pre-fix engine (archive the only carrier) ⇒ not-found on the line `--around` printed; an engine asking by the GIVEN ids ⇒ a vendor call before any read. test-channels-agent-cli (+3, 112). test-channel-acl's verbatim body-gate anchor (`if (!part || part.role === 'body') return`) kept: the gate was rebuilt around it after its control went red. The heading is .325 on a .323 package (the .324 is lane automation-open-limits): the fast gate judged on a snapshot bumped to .324.

### lane design-window-placement — a Design an agent opens is PLACED beside its conversation, never popped to the front (backlog B-9674; owner 2026-10-20 「design 那个窗口会自动弹出到前台，而不是在开始 design 的对话的右侧分屏」; base 01672d8d = 2.369.322)
- THE RULE (lane agent-window-no-steal, already law for the agent browser): an agent's action may PLACE a window; only a person's action may FOCUS one. The Design window's `design-open` push (the agent's `vibespace-design new|open|add|sync`) now reads the SAME PURE verdict as the agent browser — `agentWindowPlacement` (src/lib/desktop-app-placement.js), extended for the `design-open` kind. `agentPlacedSession` tells the two agent pushes apart; a person's door (a chat card, the Designs home, the gear menu, a layout replay) calls `openDesign` directly and never rides the push.
- THE DOOR: `installDesignWindow` → `app.placeAgentWindow(msg, open)` (src/lib/app.js). A FRESH window is born quiet (createWindow's asked `quiet` — the active window and the DOM caret stay) and placed: beside a shown chat it is SNAPPED to the right half while the conversation snaps to the left (`wm.snapToHalf`), on another desktop it is created there (no switch), behind the active window when the chat is minimized; its taskbar entry pulses (`wm.markArrived`). An EXISTING design the agent re-opens or syncs is never raised — `markArrived` + `revealWindow(id, {raise:false})`. The front setting (`desktop.agentWindowsFront`, default OFF) restores the old front + focus for designs too; its description now names a Design (zh + ja).
- WHY SNAP, NOT `linkPlacement`'s tab-chain split (the agent browser's door): the Design canvas fits itself to its pane through a ResizeObserver; born hidden as a tab-chain split guest it never gets a non-zero size and never loads its artboards. A snapped free half window renders exactly as a full one, so the owner's picture (conversation left, Design right, same desktop) is delivered as two half windows and the agent browser's bindSplit door is untouched.
- TESTS: test-agent-window-placement — the PURE design-open rows (beside / desk / behind / minimize / badge / phone / front-on control + the malformed-push negatives) and the door pins (56 pass). test-design-window (heavy) — the composer keeps the caret and the active window, the fresh Design is the right split (conversation left, Design right, same desktop), its taskbar pulses, a second `open` does not raise it, the front setting brings it forward (control), a direct `openDesign` raises it (RED control) (173 pass). test-design-canvas (287) + i18n unaffected.

### lane vault-e2e-password-fix-r2 — the secrets the first round left in the clear: device link tokens (and their per-spawn copies), login tokens, the frp relay token, the voice OAuth pair; the owner's decision ④ (30-day sliding logins, a lock signs every login out); the verifier's 「登录已过期」 card finding; base 0510a073 (the vault + verify r1)

A host-<id>.token left beside the data is sealed by the vault's OPEN SWEEP (after the setup and every unlock — the engine's new `onOpen`) or at its first read (`secretAdopt`: wrapped, the record READ BACK, the file overwritten then unlinked; a file that differs is kept and audited). The engine's new SECRET entries (`host:` / `frp:` / `file:` names, AAD-bound like the store keys; `secretGet/Put/Drop/Adopt`, facts `secrets`) live beside the store keys in data/vault.json.
- THE ONE ROAD to a session (the brief: "pick ONE road for dial and ssh"): neither the fd/stdin road (the attach child is respawned by a wrapper inside dtach that outlives the hub — no fd survives) nor the process env (a token in every wrapper's env, and an attach respawned after an upgrade would have none) — a MEMORY-ONLY handle: the attach child (src/agentd/attach-cli.js) asks GET /api/agent/vault/link-token at every (re)start, its own session token (VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN, already in its env) naming the session, and holds the answer in memory. session-<id>.json carries `hub: {port}` and NO token (dial chat / dial terminal / ssh chat); `stripCopies()` takes the token out of every config an older build wrote, at every start (the old inode's bytes overwritten: src/secret-file.js `replaceShredding`). LOCKED ⇒ 423 `vault_locked` ⇒ the attach exits 7 with the vault's words (the chat-wrapper's reconnect line shows them, retrying every 30 s ⇒ the session reattaches after the unlock); a spawn under lock is refused `vault_locked` by name before anything is set up (no silent fall back to the keeper road); a pairing mint asks the vault FIRST (a rotation it could not finish would lock the holder out — 423 before anything is minted); the DeviceManager asks its token at every connect (`hostToken` may be a function) and the dial bridge answers a locked hello by name instead of throwing in a listener. A rollback below this build breaks a running remote session's NEXT reattach (its config no longer holds the token) — restart it.
- LOGIN TOKENS (src/auth.js): auth.json keys a login by sha256(token) (the token never meets a comparison — the lookup is over digests; no stored key opens anything); a plaintext map is hashed at the first start (every login inside the cap valid ONCE — the migration counts as a use; the old bytes overwritten). 30 days from the LAST use (the slide reaches the disk + re-sets the cookie's Max-Age at most hourly), never past 180 days from the sign-in (the cap); a sign-in's cookie is the 30-day one. A vault LOCK act (door / agent / idle — NOT the shutdown's quiet lock: a restart keeps the logins, the unlock modal is the gate) revokes every login and closes every page socket with 4401 (src/server/vault-hooks.js) — the page probes /api/home, reads 401, shows the sign-in, then the unlock.

- THE ROW: `desktop-signin/<hostId>` — a `bindsPerMachine` integration row (src/integration-registry.js, the RemoteApp row's shape) {auth: ard | vnc (non-secret), username (secret, ARD only), password (secret)} + the store's `updatedAt`; sealed by the integrations store whose key is the vault's. Written ONLY by the sign-in dialog's 「记住这台机器的登录」 tick, AFTER the machine took that sign-in (vnc-view's new `onAccepted` beside the credentials, called at 'connect', never for a refused one) → `POST /api/desktop/machine-desktop/signin {host, username?, password}`; the row's kind is the hub's own probe of the machine (rowAuthOf(type)), never the page's word.
- THE HAND-OFF CHANNEL: the password never goes back to a browser — except the Vault window's audited reveal (int317: the second password again, a 5-minute window for ONE page, one value per answer; the verify r1 note). The machine-desktop target now carries `signIn {take, said}`; the ONE bridge hands it to the RFB relay, which runs src/server/rfb-signin.js's GATE on the socket's FIRST upstream before a byte reaches the page: it answers the machine's handshake itself — ARD 30 (BigInt DH over the machine's prime, MD5 → AES-128-ECB, byte-for-byte noVNC's), VNC 2 (DES with the bit-reversed key = DES-EDE3 K‖K‖K: OpenSSL 3 has no single DES), TightVNC 16 (no tunnel + STDVVNCAUTH_) — and on success shows the page `RFB 003.008`, ONE type (None), SecurityResult 0, then steps out (the input sieve now follows a Mac's session too: None, not the opaque ARD stream). Refused / unusable / silent 20 s / closed ⇒ that upstream is dropped unseen and a fresh one is relayed plain (the person signs in) — once per socket, never a loop.
- THE BEHAVIOUR: remembered ⇒ no dialog. Refused (the password changed there) ⇒ nothing cleared, the hub remembers the refusal against THAT row (updatedAt) and never tries it again — a machine's lockout counts failures — and the dialog says 「上次记住的密码不对，请重输」 with the tick ON (the page reads GET …/signins fresh before the dialog). UNPAIR: src/hosts.js `onRemoved(fn)` (new) ⇒ desktop-access forgets the machine's desktop sign-in AND its RemoteApp sign-in (audited, why unpaired). The Machines card (Manage agents → Machines) wears 「登录已记住」 (src/lib/machine-signin-chip.js). The ticked sentence replaces 「VibeSpace 不会保存」 only when ticked.

- THE STORAGE PATH'S CRYPTO: nothing in the page — the seal is the hub's (the store's box under the vault DEK); the remember POST crosses the page's own transport once, like the vault's unlock POST on the same page (a Clerk-less http page: plain http, as every secret form there; the RFB sign-in itself keeps the AES fallback).

The "≤ 2.5× from 64 to 128 KiB" clause never ran: it waited for a take over 10 ms. `process.threadCpuUsage` is no way out: it is tick-stale here (a 0.5 ms spin reads 0, a 1 ms spin 0.67–0.89 ms).

Those sizes are below every cut: a cut text at 64 KiB ends in `…` and costs up to ~30 % more, once. Linear ≤ ×8.8 (the house bound; msg:read reads ×8.00, cut sites ×1.00–7.97, quadratic ×64), and a hostile shape's work ≤ 6 × plain words' at the same site (max 1.96 ×, lone < at stash:msg; 3 × that). 108 counts are identical on node 22 and 24, and on every run quiet or loaded. The child starts at the suite's top and counts beside §1 / §2: wall time A/B (5 rounds, back to back) base 11.04 s vs lane 11.14 s median; the row keeps its 7.1 s.

- NOT CHANGED, SAID: the suite's two other clock legs (the line belt ≤ 40 × plain lines, measured 6.4; the engine ≤ 8 × two plain records, 1.1–1.6) keep it on FAST_SERIAL / CLOCK_JUDGES (rows reworded). ### lane device-allow-flags — a paired device carries its OWN allow list, set only by the install command run on it; the hub cannot widen it; a cluster-paired device starts without socks / lan / input (design q-042 §3 D5, owner decision ③ 2026-10-19); base 42f694ab (device-act-audit, .313)
- THE FLAGS (PURE src/device-policy.js, imports only device-acts): `run` (commands, desktop apps, a browser, a Settings pane), `files` (write / move / remove / place / serve a file, the reverse tunnel — READS are never gated), `input`, `socks`, `lan` (a socket to ANOTHER host of its network; the device's own loopback stays a read), `sessions` (conversations, terminals, text posted into them, their pool orders — IMPLIES run + files: a conversation runs commands and writes its tools), `upgrade`. FLAG_OF maps every one of device-acts' 51 session / act / code rows to ONE flag, or ALWAYS (the handshake + the 9 stops — ending what is open never widens anything); an unknown action takes its family's flag, an unknown op needs every flag (fail closed). The census + a mutant row: scripts/test-device-policy.mjs ①.
- THE FILE: the installer's `--allow all|none|run,files,…` (`-Allow` on Windows) is judged by THE parser through the agent bundle's own `--write-policy` → <root>/state/policy.json (atomic, 0600) AFTER the dial check and BEFORE the host token / dial.json / the unit (an unknown flag ⇒ exit 2, nothing installed); without --allow a re-run keeps the file. agentd reads it ONCE at boot (no file = paired before the list: every flag, `legacy`; an unreadable file = reads only).
- THE DEVICE (src/agentd/agentd.js, after `authed`, before dispatch): `policyVerdict` — the file itself first (a place-secret / fs-op write / stream / mkdir onto policy.json, a removal / rename of it or a folder above it, a move / copy onto it ⇒ `policy_is_the_devices`, `files` on or not; lexical on the device's path module, `~` = its home, Windows case-insensitive), then the flag ⇒ `op-not-allowed {flag, remedy}`; the answer in the shape its caller waits for (`op-refused {id}`, `session-error {chan}`, `upgrade-failed`); acts.log gets the refused line whatever its layer. The hello-ack states the list (`policy`, read-only for the hub).
- THE HUB (src/agentd/client.js): `_request`, `_streamOp`, `tcpForward`, `openSession`, `openPipeSession` ask the same verdict over the stated list BEFORE anything is sent or a channel held — refused = an Error whose message names the op, the flag, what it allows and THE re-run (`re-run the pairing command on "<machine>" with --allow <the whole new list>`), ONE audit line `op-not-allowed` (head = the re-run); a version drift on a list without `upgrade` pushes nothing (said once per link + one line). `refusalOf(payload)` lets a chain ask before its first act: a dial session's setup (src/spawn/dial.js) asks `sessions` before it ships a tool, the session token or an account key / OAuth env. `onPolicy` keeps the stated list on the host record (`devicePolicy`, hosts.notePolicy, broadcast when it moved); `machine` names it in the sentence.
- THE DEFAULTS: POST /api/device/dial-pair answers `allowDefault` + `clusterInstance` (VIBESPACE_INSTANCE_NAME on the hub ⇒ run,files,sessions,upgrade; else all); an ssh graduation installs with it. The pairing dialog's boxes (src/lib/sidebar-mounts.js `_fillPairCommandBody`) compose `--allow` / `-Allow`; a re-pair defaults to the device's OWN stated list. The Machines card's line (src/lib/device-allow-words.js): 「允许：命令 · 文件 · 会话 · 更新 ｜ 未开：SOCKS · 局域网 · 键鼠」, its title the remedy; Activity… words the refusal.
- EXIT ROADS: an agent's `vibespace-exit run` / `use` / push refused by the list answers 403 `op_not_allowed` with the device's sentence (pre-lane wording would have been "the link failed while the command ran").

### lane hub-act-ask — on a cluster instance a hub act nobody clicked asks the owner first: ONE card per machine per kind, 60 s; a local instance does not ask; a person's click never asks (design q-042 §3 D4 the asking half, owner decision ② 2026-10-19); base 42f694ab (lane device-act-audit, .313)

- THE KIND = the act's op family (KIND_OF over device-acts keys): run (run-cmd, run-stream, pool-orders) · files (fs-op write / rm / rename / mkdir / copy / move / write-stream, place-secret, design-fs write-user) · input (input-events, desktop-grab / -input, window-pin, settings-open, peer-post) · forward (tcp-connect to another host, serve-socks) · serve (serve-folder, browser-serve start / remove) · install (desktop-serve app-install / -remove / -fetch) · upgrade; an act without a row = run (the strongest words). test-hub-act-ask ① reds an act / code row of the layer table with no kind.
- THE ASK (src/server/hub-act-ask.js, exit-proxy's `_ask` rules): the act is HELD at THE ONE SEND POINT (src/agentd/client.js `_gate`: `_request` before connect, `_streamOp` before its channel, `fsWriteStream` before its open — a refusal sends nothing, not even an abort; a stream's own request is never judged twice) while ONE URGENT For-you card (origin machines, action `hub-act-ask`, expiresAt +60 s) per machine + kind is up; a second act of the key JOINS it; the answer settles every waiting act. ### lane stream-hdr-passthrough — 「HDR 直通」: a Windows HDR display streams as TRUE HDR (AV1 10-bit PQ) to a viewer that can show it (q-041 r3 P4 road B, owner 2026-10-19 「可以 按你推荐来」); base 2d7e2c64 (.313)

The SDR roads' argvs are pinned byte for byte (test-stream-hdr §5).
- THE NEGOTIATION (src/stream-model.js streamCodecsOf; src/agentd/stream-host.js): `stream-offer {hdr: true}` to a source that `offersAv1` lists AV1 (fmtp level-idx=5;profile=0;tier=0) FIRST, then H.264; the page puts AV1 first in its answer (setCodecPreferences); werift sends the answer's first codec, and at `connected` — before the source starts — `source.useCodec(mime)` picks the hdr plan for AV1, else the SDR plan. ### lane tailscale-plugin-pod-dns — the Tailscale plugin never takes over a container's DNS (the owner's fleet pod 2026-10-19 12:3xZ: the plugin's tailscaled rewrote /etc/resolv.conf to 100.100.100.100 + the ts.net search domain; `getent hosts github.com` failed, scripts/update.sh could not fetch, the canary stalled on that pod alone while the canary instance — no plugin — updated); base 882c5e3e (.314)
- THE CAUSE: the pod has /dev/net/tun (chart `tun.enabled`) and the pod user is NOPASSWD: ALL, so mode `auto` picked KERNEL and ran `sudo -n tailscaled` — root. Nothing ever passed --accept-dns, so Tailscale's default (true) let its direct DNS manager overwrite resolv.conf (no systemd-resolved / resolvconf in a pod; header "# resolv.conf(5) file generated by tailscale", the original kept in /etc/resolv.pre-tailscale-backup.conf — both read off the 1.102.3 binary here). Userspace networking never configures the OS resolver.
- THE VERDICT (PURE src/tailscale-dns.js `dnsPolicy`, first match): a cluster pod (VIBESPACE_INSTANCE_NAME) ⇒ false `cluster`; resolv.conf OR Tailscale's backup beside it cluster-managed (a cluster.local / svc.* search domain, a 10.96.0.0/12 nameserver) ⇒ false `cluster-resolver`; no tun (userspace) ⇒ false `userspace`; a bare machine in kernel mode ⇒ false `not-asked` unless the new row `plugin.tailscale.magicDns` (boolean, default off) is on ⇒ true `asked`. `heal` = Tailscale's header present while the verdict is false.
- THE PLUGIN: `up` carries `--accept-dns=<v>` (a typed --accept-dns joins the OWNED upFlags, dropped); ONE `tailscale --socket=<ours> set --accept-dns=<v>` (sudo -n for a kernel-mode daemon, as setup's `up`; retried 20 × 500 ms while the socket comes up; one in flight) at every start (also when already running), after an install over a running daemon, and at boot for a daemon of ours that outlived the server — the plugin now owns its bootReplay (else the manager's default rule: enabled + desiredUp ⇒ start; the default skipped a running daemon, so an old install would never heal). tailscaled's direct manager restores its backup when the OS config empties. A heal logs ONE line `[tailscale] <why>: /etc/resolv.conf carried Tailscale's header — set --accept-dns=false (<why>); …`.
- THE NAMES: MagicDNS names never ride the system resolver. status() / lookup() keep a host table from OUR daemon's `status --json` (Self + Peer: DNSName → TailscaleIPs, IPv4 first, the bare label too); PluginManager.tunnelLookup(name) asks whichever plugin provides 'tunnel' (optional verb `lookup`); src/hosts.js `_tailnetOpts` adds `-o HostName=<ip> -o HostKeyAlias=<name>` to sshArgs and sshCmd (known_hosts stays keyed by the name); wired in mounts-plugins-wiring (`hosts.nameLookup`). Userspace mode's SOCKS5 already resolves tailnet names itself.
- THE ROW: a running tunnel row's fact line — 「DNS：集群解析器（Tailscale 名字经插件解析）」 / 「DNS：本机解析器（…）」 / 「DNS：Tailscale MagicDNS」 / a still-held rewrite (off and on restores it); status() carries `dns: {acceptDns, why, rewritten}`.
- NOT DONE HERE: the real pod leg (主开发's `tailscale set --accept-dns=false` on the owner's pod is the same call); other dialers of a tailnet name (rclone sftp / a dial device's http base) still use the system resolver — ssh hosts are the hub's host records.
- TESTS: test-tailscale-dns NEW (fast, 56, 5.6 s): ① 13 verdict rows + the reader + the lookup; ② a fake tailscale/tailscaled/pgrep/sudo through the REAL manager + plugin on a cluster-shaped box (start ⇒ ONE set --accept-dns=false, `up` carries it, a typed true dropped, the row's dns, tunnelLookup); ③ the boot self-heal (ONE set, ONE line, no restart; a clean file ⇒ the set, no line; bare kernel through the fake sudo: row on ⇒ true, off ⇒ false); ④ ssh argv + the rsync string + the wiring line; ⑤ zh/ja words; ⑥ MUTANTS: start without the apply, `up` without the flag, no own bootReplay ⇒ RED.

### lane win-device-boot-hidden — a Windows device's agent never shows a console window: not at logon, not after a reboot, not on an old install (owner 2026-10-19 after a reboot: a black Windows Terminal window titled 「vibespace-device」 on the desktop — 「这是啥 能关掉吗」); base 882c5e3e (.314)
- THE GAP: scripts/vibespace-agentd-install.ps1's AT-LOGON task ran `cmd.exe /c set VIBESPACE_DEVICE_ROOT=<root>&& set VIBESPACE_AGENTD_ROOT=<root>&& "<node>" "<root>\current\vibespace-device.js"`. A console program a task starts gets a console of its own; Windows 11 hands it to Windows Terminal; the daemon's `process.title` named the window. Closing it ended the agent until the next logon. The other launch sites were hidden already (the first launch `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden`, the re-exec `detached + windowsHide`, the --stdio bridge) — .310's census covered the daemon's CHILDREN only.
- THE TASK: Execute `powershell.exe`, Argument `-NoProfile -NonInteractive -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "$env:VIBESPACE_DEVICE_ROOT='<root>'; $env:VIBESPACE_AGENTD_ROOT='<root>'; Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden -FilePath '<node>' -ArgumentList ([char]34+'<root>\current\vibespace-device.js'+[char]34) -RedirectStandardOutput '<root>\state\agentd.out' -RedirectStandardError '<root>\state\agentd.err'"` = the installer's first launch (the shape the owner's box never showed) at every logon; the settings gain `-Hidden`; the name and `-Force` stay. Paths are PowerShell literals (`'`, ‘ ’ ‚ ‛ doubled), the script is quoted for node by `[char]34`, so the text holds no `"`. The env reaches node by inheritance (`-Environment` needs PS 7.3+). ONE text: the ps1 builds it (`Quote-Ps`, `$launch`, `$taskArgs`) and the daemon builds it (src/agentd/hidden-start.js `logonTaskArgs`) — a twin pin.
- WHY NOT `conhost.exe --headless`: undocumented, listed as an execution proxy (EDR rules alert on it), and not measurable here. The trade of the PowerShell form: the launcher PowerShell itself may show for about a second at logon (unmeasured); the daemon is never in it, and the launcher exits at once, so the task instance ends (the task's 72 h ExecutionTimeLimit never reaches the daemon either).
- SELF-HEAL, two halves. ① The console step (`consoleStep`, sync, inside the daemon body BEFORE the singleton): a win32 daemon not yet marked with a console handle on fd 0/1/2 (`tty.isatty`) runs ONE hidden PowerShell one-shot (Add-Type, FreeConsole + AttachConsole(pid) + GetConsoleWindow + IsWindowVisible of the window or its owner — Windows Terminal owns the pseudo-console window; the answer is the EXIT CODE 20 visible · 21 hidden · 22 no window · 23 none, 30 s bound). Visible ⇒ `startSuccessor(reExecArgv(argv[1]), {VIBESPACE_AGENTD_HIDDEN: '1'})` + exit 0 (cmd.exe ends, its window closes); the marked successor never looks again. Hidden / none / could not tell ⇒ stay (the last one logged once). ② The task step (`ensureLogonTask`, async 3 s after the start line, win32 only): read the task (`vs-task <b64 execute> <b64 args>`, UTF-8 base64 — a Chinese profile path survives the pipe's code page); absent ⇒ never created; foreign (our name, no vibespace-device.js / agentd.js) ⇒ left alone, logged; the hidden text already ⇒ nothing written; else (the old cmd.exe, a moved node) ⇒ the installer's own Register-ScheduledTask, ONE log line naming what it was.
- THE RE-EXEC IS ONE SITE: the self-upgrade's spawn moved into `startSuccessor(argv, env)` (detached, stdio ignore, windowsHide, `{...daemonEnv(process.env), ...env}`); each caller hands `reExecArgv(<script>)` at its own site — the upgrade with its version, the self-heal with the mark. The mark is ONE hop: read by the daemon, NOT in DAEMON_ENV_KEEP (daemonEnv drops it; test-agentd-session's derivation names it).
- ALSO FIXED (same launch site): the first launch's `-ArgumentList @("$current\vibespace-device.js")` — PS 5.1 joins -ArgumentList unquoted, so a profile path with a space split the script path and the installer said "the daemon exited immediately". Now `@("`"$current\vibespace-device.js`"")`.
- MEASURED in a real PowerShell engine (portable pwsh 7.4.6 on Linux; no Windows box may be touched): the ps1 persistence block run with stub ScheduledTasks cmdlets == `logonTaskArgs` for four profile paths (plain, `Jo O'Brien`, `张三 李`, a curly quote); the Argument through the Windows command-line rules ⇒ ONE -Command text ⇒ a stub Start-Process bound -FilePath, -ArgumentList `"…"` (quoted), -WindowStyle Hidden, both redirects, both env roots; the first launch's argument quoted; the three one-shots parse (0 errors), are ASCII, and run through -EncodedCommand with stub cmdlets (read old ⇒ rewrite, none ⇒ absent, hidden ⇒ same; write: powershell.exe + the exact Argument, -Hidden, -AtLogOn, -Force); `exit 20` is the process exit code; the probe off Windows exits 1 ⇒ unknown ⇒ stay (fails closed). NOT measured: a real Windows logon. The owner's box heals at the next release's self-upgrade (the task re-register); the console step is the backstop for a cold start under an old task.
- TESTS: test-agentd-hidden-start NEW (fast, 44): the rules + consoleStep over fakes (one re-exec, the loop guard, the silent hidden case, the said unknown), the ps1 task unit, THE TWIN ×4, the launch-site census (agentd AST: 2 daemon starts, both detached + ignore + windowsHide; ps1: 2 starts; 3 hub / POSIX rows) + 5 CONTROLS, MUTANTS (cmd.exe back in the ps1 ⇒ RED; logonTaskArgs back to cmd.exe ⇒ twin RED; no `same` row ⇒ 2 writes ⇒ RED), the wiring. test-agentd-spawn-hide (31): the re-exec row renamed, + the two one-shots, control (b) re-indented. test-agentd-session: the mark dropped. test-agentd-reexec-argv: the hand-over pin follows startSuccessor (the upgrade calls it inside handOver; ONE re-exec spawn; the self-heal's start precedes any listener). test-dial-facts: the first-launch pin quoted. test-architecture: hidden-start.js is DEVICE. ci.mjs: the new fast row.

### lane device-act-audit — a hub act on a device is never anonymous: `by` at the ONE send point, audited on both ends, three urgent For-you items (design q-042 §3 D4 audit + D10 — P0-c of the 2026-10-19 incident); base 07036579 (.312)
- THE LAYERS (PURE src/device-acts.js): every op the client sends and the daemon answers is in ONE layer — read (facts, discovery, usage, stream-*, window-track, proc-list, dial-status, quota readings, fs stat / list / read, a tcp-connect to the device's own loopback) | session (open / attach / kill a session, opencode-serve, a launched app's fit / pin / stop, the reverse tunnel, unserve-*) | act (run-cmd, run-stream, fs write / rm / rename / mkdir / copy / move / write-stream, place-secret, input-events, a tcp-connect to another host, serve-socks, serve-folder, desktop-serve app-install / app-remove / app-fetch, browser-serve start / remove, design-fs write-user, peer-post, pool-orders, settings-open, window-pin, desktop-grab / desktop-input) | code (upgrade). An op or action without a row is `act` (fail closed: it needs a `by`, it is audited).
- THE ONE SEND POINT (src/agentd/client.js `_request`, `_streamOp`, `_upgrade`): an act / code op without a valid `by` — `human:<12 hex of the sign-in cookie's sha256, never the cookie>` | `agent:<sessionKey>` | `job:<id>` | `system:<module>` — is refused in-process `act_without_by` (a journal line + an audit line, NEVER sent). Every act sent = ONE line {at, hostId, machine, op, layer, by, summary, ok, code, outHead ≤ 200 B redacted, ms} through the construction's `onAct` (all three DeviceManagers: ssh in hosts.js, dial in dial-pairing.js, this machine's in server.js → hosts.noteAct → src/device-audit.js). A write-stream is one line (its open), a run-stream one line at its END (the exit code, its first bytes), the upgrade the `code` line by `system:device-upgrade` (from → to, the size). The summary is bounded and secret-free: argv heads, paths, SIZES (a placed secret, a written file, typed keys, a posted text: their size only), through secret-shapes' redactSecrets.
- 76 CALL SITES IN 20 FILES pass `by` AT THE CALL (the census: scripts/device-acts-census.mjs, acorn; test-architecture §91 + test-device-acts ⑧; MUTANT hosts.js `_hostShell` run-cmd without `by` ⇒ RED): the owner's routes their sign-in (`byOfReq(req)` — Files via `RemoteFs.as(by)`, System panel's signal, kill a remote pid, Test, dir-complete, the pairing route's in-place push, desktop install / run / Settings / pin), an agent's exit verbs its conversation (`byAgent(keyOf(session))`: use's SOCKS, run, push), vibespace-msg's delivery its sender (else `system:<spendReason>`), a session's setup on a dial device the socket that created it (ws-handler stamps `ws._actBy`, else `system:spawn`), the upkeep its module (`system:usage-harvest`, `system:machine-mounts`, `system:port-forward`, `system:ctx-sync`, `system:writer-sweep`, `system:usage-pool`, `system:device-mount`, `system:desktop-webrtc`, `system:hosts`). A relay that cannot reach the person names its module (`system:remote-fs`, `system:desktop-access`, `system:browser-access`, `system:design-engine`) — never nobody.

- BEFORE: a hub whose bundle version differed from a device's streamed its own data/bin/vibespace-agentd.js (client.js `_upgrade`) and the device landed it, repointed `current` and re-exec'd (agentd.js `beginUpgrade`) — no signature, no second source, and `version` (a hub-supplied string) was joined into a directory path unchecked. A compromised hub replaced every paired machine's code at its next hello.
- THE VERDICT (PURE src/agentd-signature.js, node crypto handed in): ed25519 over 'vibespace-agentd-bundle/v1' ‖ version ‖ sha256(bundle) ‖ keyId; `verify(trusted, bytes, version, record)` → ok | malformed / version-mismatch / unknown-key / bad-signature / unsigned. The digest is computed over the bytes handed in (the record's own sha256 is never trusted). A rotation ships as a KEY CHAIN inside every manifest (each successor signed by its predecessor, domain-separated); a link that claims a reachable signer but does not check is a forgery (refused, never skipped); a successor reached through the chain REPLACES the device's pin.
- THE DEVICE (src/agentd/agentd.js): the version must be version-shaped BEFORE a directory is made; after the last byte the bytes ON DISK are judged before the rename, the repoint and the re-exec (the only writer of `current` — test-architecture §92 + the suite's census); a refusal deletes the temp file (and the empty dir), logs one line and answers `upgrade-failed {code, keyId}`. TOFU: the first start of an install pins the release keys IN its bundle (<root>/state/trusted-keys.json, 0600, atomic); both installers delete the pin on a (re-)pair (a new trust-on-first-use = the lost-key recovery).
- THE HUB'S OWN MACHINE: every upgrade of the hub's OWN daemon (signed or not) carries a local proof — the hub writes 32 random bytes into the daemon's state dir (<root>/state/upgrade-proof, 0600) and sends them as `localProof`; on its own socket (never a dial link: `serveConnection(ws, { dialed: true })`) a matching proof is enough (sha256s compared in constant time, the file deleted on any read). Whoever writes that dir is already that machine's user; dev boxes and lane worktrees keep their local daemon current, and a hub's daemon that once ran an unsigned build (no baked key ⇒ no pin) never sticks on `unknown-key` at the next signed release — found in review, pinned by a real-daemon leg.
- THE HUB (src/agentd/client.js): `_releaseState()` = the manifest beside the bundle (data/bin/vibespace-agentd.manifest.json) names THESE bytes and this version (cached by mtime+size); otherwise `unsigned-local-build` — no upgrade to another machine (`_mayPush` at the hello, and `_upgrade` itself throws), said once per version (log + the door). A device refusal (SIG.REFUSALS) is never pushed again (the ledger gives up at once) and reaches hosts.onAgentUpgrade('refused') from all three construction sites (server.js local, dial-pairing, hosts.js ssh).
- THE DOOR (src/server/device-upgrade-watch.js `refused`): ONE URGENT For-you item per (device, version, code) — machine, from → to, the code, the key, who pushed (`hub` until P0-c brings the act's `by`); a refusal's item is never retracted (a later `matched` drops only the row). `unsigned-local-build` = the machine row's line only (`agentUpgrade.unsigned`), no item. - RED-1, a validly signed OLDER release landed and re-exec'd (the replay of any past release). Fix: THE VERSION FLOOR. <state>/release-floor.json holds the newest version this install ever ran; it is raised at every start (0600, atomic), and `floorNow()` is never below the running VERSION. After the signature checks, `SIG.verify(…, {floor, honoured})` answers `downgrade` (+ `floor`) for a version below it. The device deletes the bytes and answers `upgrade-failed {code: 'downgrade', floor}`; the hub gives up at once (it is in SIG.REFUSALS); the watch files the same URGENT kind in its own words (「有人向 <machine> 推送了旧版本 X」, who pushed) plus the row's line. A deliberate rollback is a SIGNED statement: the record's `allowDowngradeTo` (= its own version; `sign-agentd --allow-downgrade-to <v>`, typed as a confirmation) is an optional line INSIDE the signed message, honoured ONCE per bundle (its sha256 lands in the floor file's `honoured`; the floor does not move). Never an env, never a hub-side flag. The hub's OWN daemon (the local proof) is exempt: whoever writes that state dir is that machine's user.
- RED-2, a device installed from a hub whose RELEASE_KEYS was empty pinned nothing, so every later signed release was `unknown-key` until a re-pair. Fix: TRUST ON FIRST USE at the first validly signed release. Every record now SIGNS the release's key set (`keys` = RELEASE_KEYS in sign-agentd; SIG.sign's default is the signer alone). A device with NO pin file and NO baked key (`trustsNoKey()`) passes `tofu: true`; the PURE verdict takes the record's own key set only when it is self-consistent (every row its key's id, the signer among them) and the signature over the bytes AND that set checks ⇒ pin `from: 'tofu'`, `upgrade-done {tofu: [ids]}` ⇒ client `_trusted` ⇒ hosts.onAgentUpgrade('trusted') ⇒ ONE URGENT item 「<machine> 首次信任发布钥 <fingerprint>」 (the undo: re-pair). A pin file that EXISTS (even unparsable) never re-TOFUs, and the PURE branch also needs an empty trusted set. The installers carry no key themselves — the bundle they fetch bakes RELEASE_KEYS; today's set is EMPTY, so a device paired before the first signed release now TOFUs that release instead of needing a re-pair.
- low ③, ssh hosts took the hub's unsigned bundle (installAgentd). Fix: THE SSH ROAD LANDS THROUGH THE SAME landBundle. The device's landing is ONE function, `landBundle` (verdict → rename → repointCurrent → the pin / the rollback record; test-architecture §92 counts exactly its two callers). Callers: `beginUpgrade` (the stream) and a new CLI mode `agentd.js --land-upgrade <staged> --version <v> --manifest <record>` (no lock, no socket, one stdout line, exit 0 / 3 / 4). installAgentd ships the bundle, plus its manifest when `DeviceManager.releaseOf` says these bytes ARE the signed release. The remote step (`installAgentdScript`) moves `current` only on these rungs: same bytes ⇒ nothing; nothing installed ⇒ lands as is (the owner's add-host act = the installer's TOFU); an install + an unsigned build ⇒ `unsigned-local-build` (row only); the installed agent knows --land-upgrade ⇒ IT judges (signature, floor, pin); a pre-signing agent there ⇒ the SIGNED release lands unverified once. Chosen over "a verify script shipped beside the bundle" (the hub's code judging the hub's bundle proves nothing) and "the daemon verifies itself at first boot" (the newcomer's bytes judging themselves): the agent ALREADY trusted on the host judges the newcomer, exactly as over a dial link. Refusals and first trusts reach the same door. Not a fence against a hub holding the host's ssh key (that is a shell — D6). The MANUAL real-host suites (test-agentd-switchover, test-host-mounts-tunnel) now need a signed build or a fresh host.
- low ④, `trustAfter` replaced the pin with the single successor. Fix: a successor ADDS. The pin after = pinned ∪ every key the chain reached − signed retirements (the signer first under the 16-key cap). A retirement is a KEY_CHAIN entry `{retire, sig}` signed by the RETIRING key ('vibespace-agentd-key-retire/v1'). It counts only for a reachable key; a bad one is `bad-signature`; a release signed by a key its own chain retires is `unknown-key`. `gen-release-key --retire <pem>` prints one; `--rotate-from` now says ADD the row (RELEASE_KEYS = every valid key).
- low ⑤, the `--encrypt` doc. gen-release-key's header now says when to use it (any machine that also runs a VibeSpace or agent sessions — they run as your uid and can read a plain PEM), how (≥ 12 characters; typed twice on a terminal, otherwise the FIRST stdin line with no confirmation), and that it is never stored. The release recipe in kb-design-lessons follows the verifier's corrected first-release order.

- THE AGENT'S VERBS (`vibespace-window`, mode pixels, no tree — the window-targets routes send `md-` handles to the engine): list (`machines` rows: only the desktops handed to THIS conversation), screenshot (`desktop-grab`: ONE still, image/png + X-Window-Shot {w, h, originX, originY, machine}), click --at x,y [--button 1|2|3], key <chord>, type "text" (default THE OWNER'S PASTE: `clip` + the machine's primary modifier + V — any text, any layout, any IME; `--keys` = US-layout physical keys, ASCII), scroll; attach answers held (nothing to take), snapshot ⇒ mode_pixels, watch = the owner's window; every verb re-asks the lease AFTER its await (a pause landing while a still was taken ⇒ window_paused, no picture handed).
- THE TWO OPS (THREE-TOUCH): `desktop-grab {sid}` → the stream session's source `still()` (Windows: ONE more ddagrab frame of the same display — SDR: ffmpeg's PNG; HDR: the FP16 bits through THE stream's own table, src/stream-plan.js rgbFromHalf → pngOf, written by the agent; the fake source: a 1280×720 ramp; a Mac: `mac_still_pending` — the helper has no still verb and a new verb = a new helper VERSION = the owner's Screen Recording switch again: rides the helper's next version, coordinator's choice B); `desktop-input {sid, events}` → stream-host `input()` → THE SAME `onInput` the page's `input` channel feeds (the window's live place, the Mac's target; fix r2: in the agent's own lane, the owner's first), refused records by index + name. Capabilities appended to the hello-ack; client.js routes both replies; desktopGrab / desktopInput refuse an agent without them BEFORE asking (host_needs_daemon → the engine's `host_needs_update`, also checked at the give).
- THE FENCES (named refusals): desktop_not_handed (nobody handed it to you — the sentence names the owner's door), window_paused, desktop_switching, outside_display (--at outside the still; before a still the stream's own picture size), screenshot_first, chord_refused by name per platform (win32: Win+L lock_screen, Ctrl+Alt+Del / Ctrl+Alt+End secure_attention; darwin: ⌃⌘Q lock_screen, ⇧⌘Q / ⌥⇧⌘Q log_off; both tables when unknown; power/sleep keys) — plain ⌘Q (quit the front app) and Alt+F4 pass; type_too_long (> 1500), not_ascii (--keys). The local desktop's P10 refusal is untouched: a `dw-` act still reaches the window engine (desktop_injection_refused) — the mutant that routes `dw-` to the hand-over is RED.
- THE AUDIT: data/window-audit.jsonl (the windows' file), origin `machine`: lease-give / pause / resume / rebind / end (+ cause), screenshot (w, h, display, bytes), click (x, y, button), key (chord; a refused one with refusedAs), type (LENGTH + road, never the text), scroll; who = the holder's conversation key.
- THE AGENT'S POINTER: the agent's last point (a click / wheel) rides the facts as `dot` (4 s) and the window draws it over the picture with browser-live-window's labelled cursor (its classes + CSS, the holder's name as the label).

### lane stream-mac-ax-respawn — a Mac's resident input child is REPLACED when its Accessibility grant changes (owner 2026-10-19 ~09:1xZ: vibespace-screen re-added under Accessibility, the stream's keys and clicks still did nothing, no error); base 07036579 (.312)
- THE CAUSE (measured on the owner's Mac): the injector keeps ONE resident `vibespace-screen --disclaim input` child per daemon — born 09:01Z, the Accessibility row deleted + re-added ~09:03Z. macOS judges event posting PER RUNNING PROCESS: the child kept the verdict it was born with and posted into the void, while a fresh child answered `ok` and `--disclaim facts` said granted. Killing the child fixed it on the spot.
- THE RULE (PURE `macRespawn(state, ev)` in src/input-inject.js): the child is replaced when ① its own answer flips ax_denied → ok, or a facts read says granted after it answered ax_denied (never for a child born BY a replacement — no loop); ② the facts' tcc.accessibility changes value, either way (unless the child was born under the new value); ③ the first facts read after the Accessibility door. Never on an ax_denied alone (however many), an `ok` with no denial before it, a value read again, an unknown value. Only M/D/U/W/K answers feed it (`P` / `C` answer ok without the helper's AX check).
- THE WIRING: src/agentd/stream-mac.js keeps the last tcc a facts read saw and tells ONE hook, `helper.onTcc(fn)` (the kept value at once; every read; the door); openSettings('accessibility') tells the door and, once `open` answers, re-reads the facts (forced). The injector subscribes when it takes the helper — agentd.js unchanged. A replacement logs `[input] replaced the Mac input child: accessibility <from> → <to>` once, answers the old child's lines in flight `err replaced` (refused by name: injector_replaced) and kills it through the one kill site; the next inject spawns the new child outside the 3-a-minute crash budget. A replaced or timed-out child's late stdout never answers the next child's lines. The Windows injector is untouched (the rule runs for `cgevent` only).
- GATES: test-stream-mac §5b (fast) — the rule table (PURE) + five legs over the fake helper and the REAL createMacScreen facts: the facts flip under an ax_denied child ⇒ a NEW pid lands ok; granted → denied ⇒ replaced; 50 injects (a `P` line before each, five more denied reads) ⇒ one child; the child's own flip ⇒ replaced once, the facts after it replace nothing; a line in flight ⇒ `err replaced` at once; the Accessibility door's re-read ⇒ replaced (value unchanged), the Screen Recording door nothing. MUTANTS M1–M7 all RED (respawn on every ax_denied · in-flight lines unanswered · no hook · no born guard · no origin guard · no door re-read · `P` answers counted). The stream-mac-stall door pin now expects ONE disclaimed facts re-read after the Accessibility pane. The fake helper (scripts/fixtures/stream/mac-fakes.mjs): cfg.inputLive (the child's own check flipping), cfg.inputDelayMs (lines in flight), the child's pid on each input line.

- WHY THE CLICK WAS DEAD: the voice teach engine filed its 「Dropline 建议加入词库」 items under the key `voice-input` (no session) with origin `server`; a body click ran `jump()` ⇒ `sessionFor('voice-input')` ⇒ 「Session not found in the list yet」. Its option chips (加入词库 / 忽略) were never drawn in the tray either (replyVerdict `no_session` ⇒ hidden), so the For-you chip path in the engine could not fire from the tray.
- THE RECORD: a new origin `plugin` (src/inbox-origin.js, label Plugins; display order after apps) + the item's `plugin` (the plugin id — it files under that id, so ONE tray group per plugin) + `open`, THE DOOR (src/user-todos.js `normalizeOpen`): `{kind: 'plugin-settings', plugin, panel?, prefill?, done?}` — OPEN_KINDS is closed; an unknown kind, a foreign field, another plugin's door and a door on a non-plugin item are refused BY NAME at filing; `prefill` ≤ 8 flat fields (strings ≤ 200 / lists ≤ 32 of strings ≤ 100); `done` = an English t() key saying what ✓ does. A re-file points the door at the newest proposal. THE GATE: `setPluginGate(fn)` — mounts-plugins-wiring hands PluginManager's `provides.includes('reminders')`; src/plugins/voice-input.js now declares `reminders` (a plugin without it is refused by name). record-clear SHAPES todo drops `open` (its prefill = the suggested words).
- THE PIN (PURE src/lib/user-todos-layout.js): `pluginOf` (declared origin + id only — never a key, a name or the words), `trayBand` (0 urgent whoever filed it · 1 a plugin's reminders · 2 the rest) as sortGroups' first key after Background Work (plugins ordered by their newest item, any urgency; with no plugin item the order is the old rule exactly), and `trayRank` / `traySectionOf` in inboxSections (the LLM plugin's sections: every non-urgent reminder lifted into 现在要你 right under the urgent rows, newest first; an arrival while the popup is open appends — the slot law). The popup and the For-you window both order through sortGroups.
- THE DOOR, CLIENT: `jump()` (src/lib/user-todos-actions.js) opens `item.open` before the session lookup ⇒ `app.openPluginDoor(open)` (src/lib/plugins-ui.js): the plugin's sheet chosen by its DECLARED capability (`dictation` ⇒ the voice sheet's teach panel) with `focus` — the proposal's card marked (`.voice-proposal-focus`) and scrolled to, its chips = the reminder's words, 加入所选 (n) focused, so one press adds them; a proposal already handled says so; another panel ⇒ the plugin's settings rows (`_openPluginSettings`), a plugin with none ⇒ the Plugins list (never a click that does nothing). The row's ✓ title = t(open.done) (「把这些词加入 Dropline 词库」).
- THE VOICE PRODUCER (src/server/voice-teach-engine.js): files origin plugin + its door (prefill = the proposal id + its preselected words). ✓ = ONE ✓ by the owner adds those words (POST /v1/terms through confirm); the store's status event now carries `batch: true` from setStatusMany, so 「全部标为已看」 on the section sends nothing; × = dismissed, nothing sent, the batch still waits on the sheet (忽略这批 lives there); a ✓ that could not add (teach off, the hour's cap) REOPENS the row. At boot the engine gives its OPEN older items (origin server, no door) the plugin origin + door via `reshapeItems` — the owner's current rows pin and jump too. TEACH_WORDS.detail now says ✓ adds and a click opens the item.
- Gates: test-user-todos-layout ⑬ (the PURE verdict over mixed fixtures with the switch off and on; no plugin item ⇒ the old sortGroups / inboxRank exactly; a MUTANT sorting plugin items by time into the general list is RED in both modes; the door's refusals; the gate; the batch flag; the record-clear row; the ✓ title and the jump pins), test-voice-teach ③ (the REAL store: the filing, ONE ✓ adds once, batch / × / a failed ✓ send nothing, boot adoption; CONTROLS: the pre-fix listener RED, a batch-blind listener RED), test-voice-teach-chrome ⑨ (heavy — the REAL tray over the REAL store and the REAL voice sheet: pinned right under an urgent ask above a high one, the ✓ title, a body click opens the focused card with the words chosen, a mutant bundle m3 without the door line stays shut, ✓ ⇒ ONE /v1/terms with exactly the words, × ⇒ nothing sent). test-builtin-plugins pins `dictation,reminders`; test-peer-text-census gains the `plugin` origin row; test-record-clear-census judges boot-restore's `tally` (its `.open` is a list of sock files — the new SHAPES `open` row made it a candidate).

### lane desktop-picker-instant — the machine rows answer at once from the hub's last known state; the probes refresh them in the background, timed in the log (owner 2026-10-19: 「这个界面的加载时间怎么越来越长了」 — the picker sat on 「正在查看机器…」 longer every time); base 07036579 (.312)
- THE CAUSE: GET /api/desktop/machines awaited, per paired machine in parallel, `handleIfConnected` (a bounded 3 s dial when the handle is not cached) and — a connected Windows / macOS machine — `probeDesktop` (the agent's tcp-forward to 5900 + up to 3 s for the RFB greeting). Nothing cached, nothing timed; the Desktop picker and the Apps dialog's 「运行于」 painted only after the slowest machine. Measured over the REAL access layer + route (scratch/measure.mjs, a Mac whose greeting takes 5 s, a Windows box with nothing on 5900, a Linux agent): base 07036579 5029 ms, again 5005 ms (every open waits); this lane 28 ms cold / 2 ms warm, the Mac's row landing 4996 ms later by the page's follow-up and the broadcast.
- THE ROWS (src/server/desktop-access.js `machinesNow`, PURE rules in the new src/desktop-machines-cache.js): the hub keeps each machine's LAST probed row `{row, at, ms}` in memory and in data/desktop-machines.json (channel-store `writeJsonAtomic`; read once at boot — a restart paints too). The route answers at once: each row from its entry + `probedAt`, `ageMs` (the hub's clock — never the browser's), `probeMs`, `stale` past 60 s; a machine never probed = `code: 'checking'` (that row only, never pressable; a handle that already said win32 / darwin makes it a desktop row). `refreshing: [hostId]` names the probes in flight; `?wait=1` answers after them; `?fresh=1[&host=]` = Check again (that machine, now, waited for). `machines()` keeps its meaning for callers (every machine probed now).
- THE REFRESH: every answer kicks `refreshHost` when MC.refreshDue says so — never while one is in flight (a second asker JOINS it: one probe per machine), no history / Check again / the daemon's hello always, a link the hub sees NOW that differs from the one the row was probed on at once (a dropped link is said without the floor), else 10 s after the last probe. The landed row is kept, written and BROADCAST — `desktop-machines-updated {hostId, machines}` (the cache-invalidation-must-NOTIFY law). The daemon's hello (the existing dial-in hook) re-probes that machine `helloListMs` later: after a restart each machine's row turns from the file's to the live one as it dials in.
- THE PAGES: `watchMachines(app, onRows)` (src/lib/desktop-picker.js) = the answer at once, then every broadcast, and ONE `?wait=1` follow-up when probes are in flight (a broadcast missed while the socket reconnects still lands); a row never goes back to an older probe (by `probedAt`; the socket and the follow-up may arrive in either order). The Desktop picker's nodes are KEYED (`r|group|hostId`, the group heads, the notes, the running apps) and re-used, put in order by `syncChildren` (only an out-of-place node moves) — a late probe patches its row and the focused row is never rebuilt or detached; the Apps dialog's machine buttons are keyed by hostId the same way. A row's title = 「上次检查 N 秒前 · 探测 M ms」 (machineProbeText); 「检查中…」 = the new row state `checking` (src/desktop-screens.js ROW_STATES, not pressable). Check again (the machine dialog's recheck) = `recheckMachines` (`?fresh=1&host=`).
- TIMED AND SAID: every probe logs ONE line `[desktop] <host> probed in <ms> ms → <code> (<why>)` — why: picker · recheck · hello · open (the window's gate) · install (TightVNC's after-probe); a probe over 2 s logs a second (warn) line naming its slowest step with every step timed (`dial` = reaching the agent, `forward` = its tcp-connect, `greeting` = the server's first bytes): `[desktop] mac probe slow: 5002 ms — the greeting took 4999 ms (dial 1 ms · forward 2 ms · greeting 4999 ms)`.
- THE INSTALLED APPS (brief item 3 — verified AWAITED): the machine dialog paints at once, but its installed list waited for `installedApps(why 'open')`, which re-lists a list older than 10 min ON the machine (391–446 apps in 5–20 s on the owner's Windows box) before answering — the old list never showed. Now the route's open asks `wait: false`: the list the machine gave last at once + `listing: true`, the listing runs behind it (joined by the page's `&wait=1` follow-up; a refused listing is caught for the open that did not wait) and its landing is announced (`desktop-installed-updated {hostId, listedAt, total, code}` — no rows: hundreds of them); an open dialog whose list is older re-reads it from the store. `fresh=1` (Check again) still waits. The Desktop picker never asked for the list.
- GATES: scripts/test-desktop-picker.mjs (fast, 45 legs, ~4 s): §I PURE (fresh / stale / none, the floor + coalescing, the checking row, answerRows, both payloads, the log lines, the file, probeAge, the row state, the zh / ja words), §II the real access layer + route over fake machines — the route in 7 ms with a 2.2 s greeting in flight (CONTROL: the pre-fix route, which awaited machines(), 424 ms over a 400 ms greeting), the probe JOINED (1 forward for 2 opens), `?wait=1`, the 3 broadcasts, the log lines + the slow line, the floor, Check again for one machine, the file, the hello, a restart painting from a 2-min-old file (stale) and its refreshes broadcast, the installed list at once (2 ms, CONTROL: the waited shape 301 ms). scripts/test-desktop-v2-chrome.mjs ⑯ (heavy, Chrome): a never-probed second machine with every greeting at 1.5 s — every row drawn in 13 ms (RED CONTROL: the pre-fix route showed no remote machine for 1510 ms), WIN-DESK2 检查中…, the ?wait=1 follow-up HELD so only the broadcast can patch: the SAME row node turns 就绪 with title 「上次检查 0 秒前 · 探测 1502 ms」 and the focus stays on the person's row. ### lane stream-audio-probe — the machine stream's SOUND: speaker passthrough and the microphone road, measured (owner 2026-10-19 「开始研究下透传麦克风和扬声器」; independence rule: no third-party host/driver); base 07036579 (.312)
- PROBE ONLY, nothing built: scripts/probes/stream-audio/ (win/ WASAPI helper + on-box Node legs, mac/ SCK-audio scratch helper + the AudioServerPlugIn and its no-install load test, hub/ werift ⇄ headless Chrome). Tones = 1 kHz, −20 dBFS, 200 ms. On Windows most legs ran on an idle virtual endpoint, so they were inaudible. Captured audio was never written to disk.
- WINDOWS SPEAKER (WASAPI loopback, in-box COM, csc):
  - 10 ms packets; event-driven capture works. AUTOCONVERTPCM gives 48 kHz float stereo from a 5.1 mix.
  - An app's sample reaches our capture 20 ms (virtual endpoint) / 31 ms (the owner's USB device) after the app writes it. Loopback stamps it with its PLAY time, so capture runs 20–35 ms AHEAD of the speaker. 0.5–2 % CPU.
  - A render endpoint that nothing plays to delivers NOTHING: 0 packets and no events in 3 s. The fix is a silent render stream of our own (zeros, 100 packets/s, the first after 10.6 ms).
- WINDOWS ENCODE (the agent's ffmpeg; libopus is present):
  - Raw `-f s16le` over a pipe (or UDP) comes out in ~90 ms clumps: the PCM demuxer reads ~4096 frames per packet, and no option changes that. A sample takes 62–100 ms to reach its RTP packet.
  - A streaming WAV header + `-f wav -max_size 1920 -ignore_length 1` gives a packet every 20 ms, 1–10 ms after the sample passes. App write → Opus RTP packet in the agent's hands: 21–30 ms.
  - ffmpeg ≈ 5 % of a core and ~0.9 s to its first packet. 10 ms frames add +29 kbps of headers.
- MAC SPEAKER (SCStreamConfiguration.capturesAudio, a scratch helper under the probe's granted launcher):
  - It rides the Screen Recording grant. tccd shows ScreenCapture (allowed) and only a coreaudiod Microphone PREFLIGHT (preflight_unknown: no prompt, no row). No System-Audio service was asked.
  - 48 kHz float32 stereo planar, 960-frame buffers, delivery p50 35 / p95 47 ms. Our tone is stamped +22 ms after its scheduled host time and is in hand at +58–73 ms. The level is exact.
  - Starting an output engine at capture start held SCK audio for ~1 s once.
- MAC OPUS IS IN-BOX: AudioToolbox (AVAudioConverter) encodes Opus in 0.28 ms per 20 ms packet; the packet exists ~1 ms after the buffer. It also decodes it (0.03 ms per packet, level intact). A Mac needs no ffmpeg for audio.
- THE WEBRTC ROAD (werift 0.25.0 → Chrome 154, hub):
  - Opus needs no packetizer: one Opus packet = one RTP payload, written with writeRtp on an audio track (werift rewrites SSRC / PT / seq).
  - One msid puts audio + video in ONE MediaStream, so the product's `<video>` can carry the sound.
  - Clean loopback: send → Chrome's audio graph 36–67 ms, → its output clock 73–103 ms (outputLatency 30–37 ms). NetEq 31–41 ms, 0 lost.
  - With 0–30 ms of jitter: NetEq 46–63 ms, output 88–122 ms, no gaps.
- THE DATA-CHANNEL FALLBACK (Opus on an unordered DC → WebCodecs AudioDecoder → an AudioWorklet): 22–39 ms to the graph, but 4–6 underruns per run with a 20 ms cushion. With a 60 ms cushion it costs the same as NetEq and still has no concealment. Not needed: V1 = the RTP track.
- THE MIC BACK (getUserMedia → the same audio m-line, sendrecv → werift receives Opus RTP): it arrives within ±13 ms of Chrome's own WebAudio stamp of the captured sample. ~7 kbps on the tone fixture (Chrome's encoder, DTX off).
- INTERCOM (no virtual mic; the viewer's voice plays on the machine's speakers): on Windows, PCM → our render stream reaches the mix in 31–36 ms; Ogg Opus → ffmpeg decode (< 1 ms) → render takes 57–60 ms. Both were measured on the virtual endpoint; the owner's device plays ~23 ms later than the virtual one.
- WINDOWS VIRTUAL MIC: there is no user-mode way to publish a capture endpoint.
  - Every virtual audio device on the owner's box (Steam Streaming Mic/Speakers, Voicemeeter VAIO, NVIDIA Broadcast, Dubbing) is a kernel .sys signed by "Microsoft Windows Hardware Compatibility Publisher" (attestation/WHQL).
  - Our own would be a SYSVAD/ACX-class driver + an EV certificate + a Partner Center account + an admin pnputil install. That is the same class as the parked virtual display (B-f6b3). Not built.
- MAC VIRTUAL MIC: our own AudioServerPlugIn (user space, no kernel) was BUILT on the owner's Mac (clang; 69 KB arm64 / 84 KB universal; ad-hoc signed).
  - It was load-tested WITHOUT installing: vsmic-host loads the CFPlugIn factory from the Info.plist, gets the driver interface, walks the HAL's 24 properties, then runs StartIO / zero time stamps at 48 kHz / WriteMix → ReadInput. 25/25 passed.
  - The tone written on the output side is read on the input side with 0 frames of added delay. A stopped feed reads as silence.
  - NOT measured: loading inside coreaudiod. That needs /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/HAL + admin + a coreaudiod restart; distribution needs Developer ID + notarization.
- SIDE FINDING (not audio): werift 0.25's ICE-lite keeps sending DTLS to the FIRST pair the browser nominated.
  - On the multi-homed hub, Chrome 154 nominated a tailnet pair and then moved to a LAN pair. werift answered the ClientHello on the tailnet pair, and the handshake never completed: both sides stayed "connecting" while Chrome retransmitted.
  - The probe pins werift to one address (iceInterfaceAddresses). A viewer that reaches a machine over BOTH a LAN and a tailnet may hit the same problem.
- NOT MEASURED:
  - a real viewer's output device (only headless Chrome's output clock);
  - the AudioServerPlugIn inside coreaudiod;
  - Windows' Steam Streaming Microphone as a loop (it would open a microphone endpoint on the owner's box — ask first);
  - bitrate on real program audio (the target is 64 kbps).

RTCRtpSender notes a sent packet after `await dtlsTransport.sendRtp(…)` under `dtlsTransport.transportSequenceNumber` — by then the number of the burst's LAST packet — so a picture's packets leave ONE record (loopback, a real Chrome: 14 093 packets sent, 979 distinct records; of the 14 579 the browser reported, 974 matched); its `packetResults` drops status-vector chunks, adds a phantom packet per run (`i <= runLength`) and numbers every chunk from the base again. That is the owner's 300 on the Windows window road too (.306); its replay tool fed a correct estimator, so it looked like an echo. ## 2.369.310 — 2026-10-18

### hotfix (主开发) — a Windows device's own children flashed a terminal window on the owner's desktop (owner 2026-10-19 00:4xZ 「现在还是一直在弹 而且路径里有.vibespace」; the console-flood census 00:2xZ)

The owner's desktop held 143 of them (most from his Codex app's own spawns; ours flashed on every hub sweep: the discovery-snapshot child and the usage-scan child, plus every `vibespace-exit run`).
- THE FIX: `windowsHide: true` on the SEVEN device spawn sites in src/agentd/agentd.js — the console code-page probe, the stdio-bridge daemon spawn, the two discovery-snapshot children, the usage-scan child, the pipe-session spawn, run-cmd (the re-exec already had it; node-pty's ConPTY needs none; stream-screen / stream-window-source already had it). No behaviour change elsewhere: the flag only drops the console window on win32.
- WHAT FOLLOWS: lane win-run-hide-console delivers the grep-derived census over every child_process call in src/agentd (a dropped flag ⇒ RED), the code-page probe that is asked until known (the 5 s single attempt had cached `null` under the first run's 28 s stall ⇒ every cmd.exe message decoded as UTF-8 mojibake) and the card line that names a fallback decoding.
- A device must be UPDATED to stop flashing: the hub ships the bundle, the Windows daemon self-upgrades a minute after the hub restarts on .310.

## 2.369.303 — 2026-10-18

### lane mobile-back-guard — the phone's back gesture closes the open panel first, and at home asks for a second back (the owner 2026-10-18: 「在手机版上能不能 block 一下那个返回手势啊？我有时候不小心返回返回着，就多返回了几下」); base 5342d803 (.300)
- WHY: the client had no history handling at all (no pushState / popstate under src/lib, no overscroll rule), so on a phone every edge swipe was the browser's history back and left the page.
- WHAT: PURE `src/lib/back-guard.js` (imports nothing): `backVerdict({ phone, enabled, target, lastBackAt, now, deepLinkFirst })` → `{ action: none | close | arm | leave, toast }`, `backTarget` (Esc's order: every `[data-popover]` → a dialog → the window switcher → a sheet → the window area (yields to the sidebar, the phone's home) → the sidebar's drill-down → null = home), `bootStep` (push / keep / none). The wiring is `src/lib/mobile-back.js` (phone code in its own module, kb-design-lessons §7a); app.js holds one import and one install line under `this.isMobile`. Each layer closes through its own closer: the floats are removed (Esc's rule), a modal shell through its ✕, the static overlay through `hideDialogs`, the For-you tray through its own `hidePopup` (new `vs-back-dismiss` event — drafts stashed), the drill-down through its ‹ row, the window area via `sidebar.toggle(true)` (the window stays open). At home: the toast `再返回一次退出` (showToast, 2 s; `noteOwnGesture()` — new in utils.js — so it is recorded seen, never an unread notification). Setting `mobile.backGuard` (new category Mobile, under Appearance & layout, default on, read live; off = the next back leaves). `@media (pointer: coarse) { html, body { overscroll-behavior: none } }`.
- MEASURED (Chrome 154, the browser's own back = the Alt+Left accelerator → NavigationController::GoBack, the same skip logic Android's back gesture runs; loopback two-page probe): re-arming with a fresh `pushState` in popstate is fragile — with backs 6 s apart (the tap's transient activation expired) the THIRD back skipped VibeSpace's entry and left; after one tap at boot, the SECOND back left; a push 1.5 s after load with no tap was skipped 4 of 4. Re-arming with `history.go(1)` onto the existing sentinel (a traversal adds no entry, marks nothing) held in every sequence (spaced backs, touch taps, no taps between backs). A tap un-skips an entry pushed before it. A reload or tab restore standing on the sentinel keeps the entry below same-document (back = popstate, no reload), so boot keeps the sentinel it stands on instead of pushing a second. A no-tap push at boot was skipped on some cold pages and kept on others (the app's own boot push: kept 4 of 4); either way an untouched page is never stranded. Hence: ONE pushState ever (plus a fallback if the forward entry vanished), re-arm by `go(1)`, and "arm" stands on the page's own entry for 2 s so the second back is the browser's and leaves even when VibeSpace is the tab's first page (a script `history.back()` there does nothing); a timer steps back onto the sentinel when the window lapses.
- SAME-DOCUMENT NAVIGATION: Chrome fires popstate on a `#fragment` navigation too. Every `href='#'` link and the chat's link handler preventDefault today, but rendered markdown elsewhere could navigate to a fragment; the wiring remembers the URL the sentinel stands above (`baseHref`) and reads a popstate onto ANOTHER URL as a navigation — nothing closes, a sentinel is pushed above the new entry (the click's own activation covers that push).
- DEEP LINK: the client reads no `?` link today; `location.search` non-empty marks the first back after boot `deepLinkFirst`: it closes no WINDOW (arms instead), a menu or dialog opened since still closes, then the same rule.
- OVERSCROLL: the rule stops Chrome for Android's own swipe-past-the-edge navigation and pull-to-refresh. Android's system back gesture and iOS Safari's edge swipe ignore it; they arrive as a history back, which the sentinel catches. Neither is reproducible in desktop Linux Chrome (synthetic touch/touchpad overscroll and pull-down: no navigation, no reload, with or without the rule), so the suite pins the computed style (none on a coarse pointer, auto on a fine one) and no phone browser was measured.
- NOT DONE: the optional web-app manifest — iOS standalone back-swipe behaviour could not be measured here (no iOS device or simulator) and the brief forbids guessing.
- TESTS: scripts/test-back-guard.mjs (fast, in-process · 125 ms, 65 ✓): the verdict table at the 2 s edges, backTarget order, bootStep, the REAL wiring esbuild-bundled over a fake history + clock (16 legs), RED controls (the edge `<=`, deepLinkFirst ignored, a pushState re-arm, no URL check). scripts/test-mobile-back-chrome.mjs (heavy, ~92 s, 20 ✓): 390×844 DPR 3 Android UA + 1280×800, the browser's own back and history.back(): switcher, "+" sheet, New Session dialog, For-you tray, window → sidebar, Task Groups drill-down, the seen toast, 2 s re-arm, the second back leaves to the previous page, untouched page, reload, a `#fragment` navigation, `?` link in zh, setting off, desktop untouched.

- WHY: the stream showed only a Windows machine (ffmpeg ddagrab → NVENC). A Mac agent advertised `stream-screen` but its source refused `not_windows`, and its injector refused `input_unsupported`.
- THE HELPER (tools/vibespace-screen/vibespace-screen.swift, one file):
  - `facts`: displays (points + pixels + scale + EDR), windows (CGWindowList; minimized via AX + `_AXUIElementGetWindow`), TCC (`CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess` / `AXIsProcessTrusted`), lock, its version.
  - `capture --display|--window`: SCK 420v, `colorSpaceName = sRGB`, `NSApplication.shared` first. VideoToolbox H.264 CB with low-latency RC and a BT.709 / sRGB VUI. Encoded off the SCK queue (newest wins, ≤ 2 in flight). FLV on stdout. `key` → ForceKeyFrame; `bps` → AverageBitRate, set in the encode loop and NEVER in the output callback. JSON lines on stderr: started / frame / stats / end.
  - `input`: one answer per stdin line. `P <pid> [<window>]`, M / D / U / W / K (virtual key codes) / C. A frontmost target goes to the HID tap, any other pid to CGEventPostToPid.
  - `--disclaim` first: the helper re-spawns ITSELF with `responsibility_spawnattrs_setdisclaim`, so it is its own TCC client.
- FRAMING: FLV (the agent's existing `SP.flvReader` — no new parser; VideoToolbox already writes AVCC). The SPS/PPS sequence header is rewritten when the parameter sets change.
- TCC FLOW, measured on the owner's Macbook (tccd log): the agent code spawned `vibespace-screen --disclaim facts`. Attribution `requesting/accessing = vibespace-screen-<cdhash>` by path, with NO `responsible=node`. Every ScreenCapture check was `preflight=yes`; there was no "Notifying" and no alert. Accessibility published a Modify event for the helper's path (an off row). The grant survives agent updates that keep the helper's VERSION; a new VERSION is a new client ⇒ `helper_changed_regrant` until the facts see the grant.
- THE FIXED PATH (src/agentd/stream-mac.js, createScreen's darwin branch): `~/.vibespace/helpers/vibespace-screen` + `.version` + `.state.json`. VERSION = `vs-` + sha256(source)[:12] (src/agentd/mac-helper-source.js, generated by scripts/mac-helper-embed.mjs).
  - ensure() order: the version matches ⇒ ready (nothing runs) · the hub's pushed `vibespace-screen-<version>` ⇒ put in place · a compiler found BY FILE under `xcode-select -p` ⇒ built (both slices in parallel, lipo, `codesign -s -`) · else `no_helper`. The /usr/bin trampoline is never run without the tools: it would open the install dialog on the owner's screen.

- HUB: desktop-webrtc `start({source})` (stream-model `streamSourceOf`). An offer refused `no_helper` gets `pushMacHelper` (data/bin/helpers/vibespace-screen + .version — same version only — over fs-write-stream), then the offer is asked once more.

STREAM_SOURCES += 'window'. The page sends picture pixels and the daemon adds the live origin. DIFFERENCE: the Mac ENDS `window_minimized` (SCK sends `suspended`, no picture), while p2w HOLDS it (WINDOW_HELD). The integrator picks one.

| picture | rung | size | fps |

| ≤ 2560×1600 px | native60 | native | 60 |
