### lane browser-probe-transient — one failed probe of the browser CLI's version never decides for ever (B-0b8c; base rel271 f57d1cbe9)
- **The incident:** the .268 boot (00:48:24 PDT) — the boot `--version` probe of the pinned binary (data/browser-tools, NFS) timed out ONCE under boot I/O ⇒ browser-env's toast 「Could not read the installed agent-browser version, so shared profiles stay off」; the 10-min memo had `floor.sharedProfiles` true again by 00:5x. Reproduced as a RED control on the base tree (test-browser-probe-ladder ④: one killed probe ⇒ the notice at once).
- **A miss is a state (src/browser-facts.js):** `lastProbe()` `{at, ok, why, attempts, since, nextAt, exhausted}`, `probeWhy` (timed out after N s / ended by SIG / exited N without a version / could not run / answered without a version), `onProbe`, `stop()`, `probeVersion({fresh})`, `timeoutMs` (8 s, `PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`). THE LADDER (opt-in `retryMs`, the keeper's facts only): after each miss 5 s → 15 s → 45 s → 2 min → 10 min (`PROBE_RETRY_MS`), stopped by the first answer; a miss after the last rung = `exhausted`. Table (fake clock, 8 s per hung try): attempt 1 boot · miss → 5 s; 2 · miss → 15 s; 3 · miss → 45 s; 4 · miss → 2 min; 5 · miss → 10 min; 6 · miss → exhausted ⇒ 6 tries over 833 s ("14 minutes"). The brief's example said "5 tries over 13 minutes": its five delays are five RETRIES after the boot's miss, so the honest count is 6 and the span includes the 6 × 8 s timeouts.
- **Found + fixed on the way:** a synchronous execFile answer (every fake in the suites) left `inFlight` set to the settled promise for ever (`finish` cleared it inside the Promise executor, then the assignment re-set it) — every later probe past the memo answered the stale value. The flight is now cleared by ITS answer only and never set when the answer came synchronously.
- **The verdict + words (src/browser-profiles.js):** `floorVerdict(v, floor, probe)`: `undefined` (never asked) ⇒ `unknown`, `settled: false` (was `absent`); `''` ⇒ `unknown` + `{settled = exhausted, attempts, why, spanMs}`; `floorNotice` ⇒ null for an unsettled unknown; settled: «Could not read the agent-browser version after 6 tries over 14 minutes (timed out after 8 s): shared profiles stay off until it answers. Per-session isolation is on and working; `npm ls -g agent-browser` shows what is installed.» `floorNoticeDetail` (no CLI name — §52b) names the ladder, the wait per try, Check again, the withdrawal.
- **The keeper owns the notice:** its facts carry the ladder; `boot()` asks once (not awaited); `judgeFloor` (on every probe) files ONE For-you item (origin browser, kind notice, action `browser-floor-check`) only when exhausted, adopts an open one after a restart, and resolves it (`done` by agent) on the first non-unknown verdict; `checkFloorNow` = the door; `GET /api/browser/floor` → `{version, floor, lastProbe}`, `POST /api/browser/floor/check`; the digest carries `floor` + `lastProbe`; `shutdown()` stops the rung. browser-env's `checkFloor` no longer toasts (nor latches on) an unknown — its one-shot facts never settle; too-old unchanged. The panel shows no floor line today, so no panel words changed.
- **Client:** For-you window: «Check again» first on the item (inbox-window-layout `floorAsk`, inbox-window button + verb, user-todos-actions `runAction` → the door; toasts «The browser version reads again: {version}» / «Still no answer: {why}»), zh + ja.
- **Census moves:** test-user-todos-layout 47 → 48 declared add sites; test-approval-census + row `browser-floor-check` (a probe, not an approval; the add spells the action type literally so the grep sees it); boot-sentinel-gets + `/api/browser/floor`; test-architecture §52b r2 renders a SETTLED unknown; test-browser-profiles' unknown-notice leg (now: unsettled ⇒ silent, settled ⇒ the words). The record-clear census delimits a route by the next registration — the new routes sit after `/api/browser/display` (placed after `cli/install` they inherited its trailing text and made its row "dead").
- **Gates:** NEW scripts/test-browser-probe-ladder.mjs (fast, ~7.4 s, 46): PURE, the ladder on a fake clock, the REAL keeper over the fake binary (new fixture modes `version-hang` / `version-fail` / `version-hold`, hung pids reaped): hangs twice then answers ⇒ ok after 3 tries, NOTHING filed; never ⇒ ONE notice after 6, the door through the real router (still failing ⇒ no second item; answering ⇒ withdrawn); single flight (3 readers, 1 counted fork); restart adoption; shutdown; RED: the base tree's one-shot + an empty ladder. test-inbox-window-ui ⑭ (chrome): the seeded notice, Check again first, pressed for real once the fake answers ⇒ toast + item done. fastpar, test-browser-cli-pin 100/0, test-browser-profiles 480/0, test-browser-continuity 69/0, test-browser-unresponsive 37/0.

### lane owner-write-origin, commit 1 — the hotfix: an anonymous POST /api/auth/set-password took a Clerk-only instance (found mid-lane, HIGH, credential; base 39c57b070 rel272, rides .273 alone — 主开发 ruling "split it")
- **Measured (in-process, the real src/auth.js mounted in server.js's order):** server.js:159 `auth.registerRoutes(app)` precedes :160 `app.use(auth.middleware())`, so the auth routes never met the cookie gate (the route's comment claimed "the request already passed the auth middleware"). The handler judged only `passwordEnabled`; on an SSO-only instance (Clerk on, no local password) that branch is skipped, so a cookie-less `POST /api/auth/set-password {newPassword}` answered 200, set the password (`userSet`), revoked EVERY session token and handed the caller a fresh `vs_token` cookie — a pre-auth takeover that also signs every real user out. Password instances were safe (the current password is required); auth-off instances are open by design.
- **Fix — the route judges its own caller, by the instance's state (src/auth.js, one line + the comment made true):** SSO and no password ⇒ a signed-in request only (`requestAuthed`, the session cookie), anonymous ⇒ 401 `unauthorized` before anything is read; a password configured ⇒ the current password (unchanged); neither configured ⇒ open (first-run onboarding: setup-flows.js `#ob-setpw` posts `{newPassword}` alone). No mount order moved; logout and login are untouched.
- **Gates:** new scripts/test-auth.mjs (fast, ~330 ms): ① the mount order READ from server.js; SSO-only — anonymous `{newPassword}` / `{remove:true}` / an unknown-token cookie ⇒ 401 with no password, no cookie, the signed-in session kept; the signed-in owner sets one (200 + a fresh cookie); a password instance — wrong current 401, right current 200 (as before); auth off — the onboarding POST sets the first password (200 + cookie) and the gate stands after it; RED CONTROL (a patched copy without the check) ⇒ the anonymous POST answers 200, sets a password, revokes the owner's session and hands out a cookie. There is no test-onboarding suite in the tree; the onboarding leg is ① here.

### lane reconnect-storm-band — test-reconnect-storm (d) judges the storm's work on the server's loop, never a wall band; the wall-clock census reads the band
- **The red:** (d) asserted the server's loop-delay max (a 5 ms histogram) ≤ the control's + max(25 %, 25 ms). ubuntu-latest read 61 vs 31 and 60 vs 25 (int270's heavy shard 6/6, load < 1: the page and the server share 2 vCPUs, and the fix's window is ~2 × the control's); the hub beside an integrator's heavy read 1207 vs 16, 1141 vs 307, 349 vs 126, 46 vs 14 (int269, int270). A relative bound with a literal band is still a wall-clock assertion, and K = 2 on the same histogram would still be red on 5 of those 6.
- **(d) now (scripts/test-reconnect-storm.mjs):** a harness-only meter in the server's preload stamps every `attach` frame the server handles with its loop TURN and the CPU its handler spent (`process.threadCpuUsage`; node < 23.9: `cpuUsage`). A loaded session's re-attach is synchronous from the verdict to the send, so that is its whole work on the loop. Three checks replace the band:
  - the server's own receipts: every re-attach is handled, and ≤ 5 of them arrive before the first slot (`RECONNECT_BASE_MS`);
  - against the in-run control: the costliest turn is ≤ ½ the control's whole storm;
  - the product's heartbeat counters: 0 rounds tainted, 0 clients terminated.
- **Printed, never judged:** the histogram, `srv-loop-gap-ms` and Σ CPU. The stagger spreads the work, it does not shrink it: each spread attach pays its own cold start, so Σ fix / control read 0.45 idle and 0.88 beside a sibling fast tier.
- **Measured on the hub:** the control's 19 land in ONE turn of 110–145 ms CPU (loop delay 118–147); the fix's land in 15 turns [5, then 14 × 1], the costliest (the 5 displayed) 19–26 ms, ratio 0.14–0.24.
- **(b) and (c) lose their literals too:** (b) = the 5 displayed windows are the first five sends, and their p95 is ≤ the control's (no `+ 50`); (c)'s `+ 6000` is `RECONNECT_CAP_MS`.
- **The census reads THE BAND (scripts/wall-clock-census.mjs):** a bound carrying a measured span plus a literal ms term is LITERAL at the band — `ctl + 25`, `ctl + Math.max(ctl * 0.25, 25)`, a floor `Math.max(ctl * 1.25, 50)`, `ctl - 10`, on either side of the comparison. So is a literal in ms scaled by a factor that carries no unit (`250 * slack` off `process.env`, `50 * rows.length`). `k × ctl`, `ctl + ctl * 0.25`, `mechanism + literal` (`2 * DP.DUP_PROBE_MS + 500`) and a timestamp + a number (`T0 + 1000`, a deadline — the flow's `mark - const` over-approximation read test-channel-store:638 (heavy) as a band until this rule) stay control. The fast tier's findings are byte-identical (0 LITERAL, 18 control); the baseline stays {}.
- **test-ci-gate §2e:** 7 band spellings read LITERAL and 5 look-alikes stay out. THE THIRD INCIDENT: rel270's test-reconnect-storm, planted with its `loopMax` / `gapMax` / `visP95` read as durations, is RED on its 3 bands; today's holds none. Against the d934d7264 census both new legs are RED (420/2).

### stage-hero-key-race — the shared-hero publish law (rel271's Actions mirror: test-stage-overlap B2 + D red twice on a 2-vCPU runner; green on the hub and on the code-identical candidate runs 38606144701 / 38574037916)
- **The red, measured:** a Stage-born hero is materialized by its creation-tail focus BEFORE its session id lands (a new shell learns its id only in app.syncSessionIdentity — on the hub 18–30 ms after the materialize, the merges are event-driven); `_publishHero` returned on the null key ("publish next time") and the landing's publish (B-8194 `onIdentitySync`) was gated on `_active` and on a null `_heroKey`. The test's leave() ran inside that gap (the hub won it by 1 ms in the measured run); enter() saw a shared record and followed it: `{rec: born0, heroKey: null, hero: born1}` ⇒ born[0] borrowed onto the slot, born[1] parked — the runner's B2 + D. Reproduced on f57d1cbe9 every time with the landing HELD (the lane's probe, HOLD=1: B2 + D red; the released landing published nothing).
- **The publish law (stage-manager.js):** every hero publish is STAMPED `{key, openSpec, by: <this page's id>, seq}`; the page keeps `_heroWitness` = the raw record it last stood on (its own publish; the record a local pick superseded, taken at every `_materializeInner`; the record it followed or cleared). enter() follows the shared hero only when ANOTHER client wrote it since (`shared !== _heroWitness`, or no local hero); `_followRemoteHero` returns on the witnessed record (a reconnect snapshot's notify too). A pick with no key is OWED (`_heroOwed`); `onIdentitySync` — still app.syncSessionIdentity's per-merge hook — pays it on the Stage or off it (no `_active` gate), only while the record is still the witnessed one (a newer pick by another client is never overwritten), and records `ws:<landed key>` (`_scheduleRecord` staged, `_recordActiveWorkspace` off the Stage). A same key + openSpec publish writes nothing. No timers, no polls.

### lane exit-close-cadence — an app's window closes at its exit, not ~3 s later (B-8778; base d419156bd rel269, rides .271)
- **Measured (hub, private env — scratch HOME / XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, no session bus; the real keeper in-process + xpra + GNOME Calculator 50 closed by `wmctrl -c`):** the app exited at +12 ms, the keeper's exit census answered at +32 ms, then the app-session teardown SIGTERMed its one member, `dbus-launch --autolaunch=<machine-id>`, which lived until the keeper's SIGKILL at STOP_GRACE_MS (+3 044 ms); the server/X session went in 10 ms; the commit that broadcasts `exited` landed at +3 171 ms. With a private session bus in the keeper's env: no such member, commit at +159 ms.
- **Cause:** with no DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS (and no `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus`) GLib autolaunches a bus over X11. dbus-launch's babysitter stays in the app's session and catches SIGTERM/SIGHUP (SigCgt 0x4003) by ending its bus and sleeping 3 s: a bare one dies 3 007 ms after a SIGTERM and 3 002 ms after its X server dies. onPartExit committed only after `teardown()`, so every client closed its window ≥ 3 s late. AIDev was green because ci-remote gives each run a private session bus; the hub's env.sh hands the suite the owner's bus, env-priv.sh none.
- **Fix (src/desktop-serve.js onPartExit):** the exit + its census are the verdict: `commit()` right after `windowsLeftAtExit`, then the teardown and its own commit. The in-memory record already read `exited` during the teardown; only the save + broadcast moved. A crash between the two commits leaves an exited record with live leftovers, which boot adoption's reapTerminalLeftovers already reaps (marker census + same-starttime parts). The file-changed signal still waits for the teardown (`fileChanged` is set by noteFileEnd). Not touched: Stop (its answer is its teardown's verdict, so an autolaunched bus still costs a Stop ~3 s), the display-gone branches, STOP_GRACE_MS.
- **Gates:** test-app-launch-once ⑦ (fast, 42 → 48 legs, 2.8 s): a sh app whose session keeps a TERM-proof member ⇒ the exited commit within EXIT_CENSUS_MS of the exit while the member runs, then the teardown reaps it (the keeper's clock moved past the grace), clean; RED CONTROL = an in-memory copy of desktop-serve in the pre-lane order (no commit 400 ms after the exit; the commit only past STOP_GRACE_MS). test-desktop-xpra-window §10 (1)(2) assert the EVENT chain (the app pid gone → the exited broadcast on each page ≤ EXIT_CENSUS_MS → the window gone one task later), never 2 s. On the -close part (.270, hub, env-priv): base 3 152 / 3 144 ms ✗✗; fixed 7–96 ms, 3/3 green at load 11–20. The .270 split deletes the giant: exit-close-cadence/post-merge.patch carries the same §10 hunk to test-desktop-xpra-window-close.mjs.

### Lane passkey-binding-isolated — the passkey hook's report binding moves to an isolated world (B-7c9a, security hygiene; closes the §2.8 residual lane passkey-prewrap-fix left open, on rel270 25cd69aef)
- The residual (docs/design-passkey-store.zh.md §2.8): on a live-document re-arm `Runtime.addBinding` left the new per-arm binding on the page's MAIN-world global for a few round trips until REARM took it; a page polling global names could grab it and call it to forge a passkey trace row / For-you card — no key, no cross-origin (the §2.8 ceiling). MEASURED on a real private Chrome 154 (scratch Xvfb, the real watch driving the real re-arm, passkey-binding-isolated/measure.mjs): a MessageChannel-speed poller saw the `vs`+24-hex binding and landed a forged `start` record in 16/16 live-document re-arms, window ~1.8–2.7 ms (out/measure-base.json).
- The fix: the binding is armed with `Runtime.addBinding({ name, executionContextName: <per-profile world> })`, so it lands only in the hook's ISOLATED WORLD and never on the page's main-world global (CDP-verified: with executionContextName the name is absent from the main world, present in the named world). The main-world hook (`installHook`) no longer holds any binding; it reports by dispatching a per-profile SECRET-named CustomEvent on `document` (dispatch + CustomEvent captured at document start, before any page script). The isolated-world reporter (`installReporter` — a second `addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` with `worldName` for new documents, `createIsolatedWorld` + `evaluate` for a live document on a re-arm) holds the binding and forwards the event's detail to it. `Runtime.bindingCalled` now arrives from the isolated-world context; the watch maps it back to the document's MAIN-world context by `frameId` (where `ctl` lives, so cancel / hold still reach it by identity). REARM hands the main-world `ctl` only the fresh key — the report path is the stable channel, so no binding is handed over (`REARM_FN` simplified; `dropExpression` removed — there is no main-world binding to drop).
- After: the same poller saw nothing and forged nothing in 16/16 re-arms (out/measure-fixed.json). The page can neither enter the isolated world nor guess the 128-bit channel, so it can no longer see the binding name nor forge trace / card events.
- Tests — the lane's heavy `test-browser-passkey-chrome`: S10 (across 8 live-document re-arms the page never saw the binding on its main-world global and never forged a record) GREEN; the control `"the arm bares the binding (no executionContextName)"` reopens the window and the forge lands, RED; a census that every `Runtime.addBinding` in the watch carries `executionContextName`. S0–S9 and the six prior controls unchanged — 36 pass, 1 skip (no real agent-browser 0.38.1 on this box). The PURE `test-browser-passkey` rewires its realm to the isolated-world reporter (one shared `document`, the secret channel) and the re-arm hands only the key — 122/0.
- Ceiling unchanged: no key theft, no cross-origin — Chrome's rpId↔origin check and the authenticator boundary still bound a forged event to trace/card noise.

### lane affected-static-reach — the affected heavy set narrows a BOOT dependency by static reach, and ONE boot sentinel is always in (q-036 P0; the owner: 「都按推荐来吧」; rides 2.369.270 — heads this section only because test-changelog-style caps the newest heading at the next patch)

- **The rule (scripts/reach-model.mjs, PURE; ci.mjs `reachContext` does the reads).** A heavy suite selected ONLY because it boots the product — the boot prefixes, or the graph behind a composition root it names — is selected by a changed product file iff its REACH meets the file's ATTRIBUTION. Every other dependency keeps the old rule: a suite that loads, names or declares the file keeps it, whatever its reach. The old rule stays the upper bound (`reach: false` is it).
  - REACH: the tokens of the suite's own code (its closure's scripts/ files minus the harness ≥ 60 heavy suites load, minus ci.mjs / affected-model / reach-model): `win:` (a registered window type's open action, `createWindow({ type })`, a hyphenated type literal; a bare `type: 'system'` is a transcript record), `api:<seg1>[/<seg2>]`, `mod:` (a src/ or data/bin/ path), `bin:` (a data/bin program by name), `cls:` (a selector's class). A route ≥ 60 booting suites spell is the boot's own probe (`api:home`) and nobody's reach.
  - ATTRIBUTION: a file's own tokens (its path, the windows it registers, every '/api/…' it spells, the classes a client module draws) + ONE HOP (each importer's path, windows, mounted routes). The composition roots add nothing: server.js, the bundle's entry (package.json's `--outfile=public/bundle.js`), and any module importing ≥ 60 src modules (src/lib/app.js 70; the next is 44). A class ≥ 4 client modules draw (`active`, `hidden`, `btn-create`) is nobody's key.
  - WHOLE CLASSES: a HUB (≥ 20 src/lib importers, derived: i18n utils icons window-types channel-chrome agent-meta contributions telemetry-client) and everything a hub imports (i18n-zh/ja), a page asset (public/…) and a shared TABLE affected-model models ⇒ every suite that drives a browser. A client module (src/lib/) never reaches a suite that drives no browser. server.js and a data/bin program a server module's CODE spawns (14: the wrappers, keepers, hooks — a comment naming one spawns nothing; rel269's src/agent-cli-text.js names vibespace-msg in one) keep every boot; an agent CLI no server module spawns (vibespace-msg, -channels, -task …) reaches the suites that run it and the routes it calls.
  - Composition roots are also LEAVES of a suite's own closure: a suite spelling 'server.js' walked the whole server graph as "loads" (152 suites "loaded" src/accounts.js), one pinning app.js's text walked the whole client.
- **The rows.** `reach: [...]` / `'all'` on a row is the author's assertion; undeclared = derived; derived empty = 'all'. The census (`ci.mjs --census`) pins declaration ⊇ the derived non-class tokens, `reach: []` only beside a `reads:` list, and no `reach:` on an always / non-booting row. The derivation left 9 booting suites empty (the design counted 16 with a quote-anchored `/api/` regex): test-helm-render (`[]`, its reads:), test-attach-ack, test-sidebar-scroll, test-desktop-drop, test-run-collapse-fold, test-stage-overlap, test-resume-breaker, test-update-dialog, test-toolbar-resize — each declares the modules / window it drives.
- **`--why`.** One ◇ line per changed product file (its attribution, how many booting suites it reaches alone), then ✓ per selected suite (`boots the product (…) — reach win:foo ∩ src/lib/foo-window.js`, `drives a browser ∩ public/style.css (a page asset …)`, `always (the boot sentinel …)`) and ✗ per suite the reach dropped (`reach {win:doc} ∌ src/lib/foo-window.js {…}`). Without `--why`: the old `·` lines + one line counting the drop.
- **The three train ranges (pre-bump, through the real wiring, ~2 s per call; `node scripts/test-reach-model.mjs --table`).** .265 79743b74b..a6e60f7a7 (78 files): 272 → 238 (−12.5 %). .266 a6e60f7a7..2dd2f322a (81): 270 → 229 (−15 %). .267 2dd2f322a..d5f352538 (68): 270 → 270 (server.js is in it; 219 without it, −19 %). The design estimated 197 / 206–220 / 242: its estimator read only quoted `'/api/` literals and treated the harness-loaded and literal-named product modules as boot-only; this rule keeps every own-closure load (the rail), and a hub in the range (.266 utils.js) reaches every one of the 154 browser suites (the owner's ②).
- **The sentinel (scripts/test-boot-sentinel.mjs, heavy, always: true; 30 s measured here — the boot 0.5 s, 244 GETs 0.8 s, 28 window types 23 s).** ① the census before any boot: every GET /api route the server files register is in scripts/fixtures/boot-sentinel-gets.json `smoke` or `skip`-with-reason (a new one is RED here and in test-reach-model), every registered window type is opened or skipped with a reason (4: hex-viewer, machine-app, machine-desktop, stage-placeholder). ② a scratch worktree + its own HOME. ③ every smoked GET: non-5xx (a 5xx a row names as deliberate passes: mount-clients' 501), JSON parses, ≤ 2 s — after the jobs engine settles (its routes answer 503 'starting' for ~2 s after the listen). ④ headless chrome, each type opened through `app.replayOpenSpec({ action, …spec })` (a window of that type CREATED, no console error, no uncaught), then closed; a live control plants a console.error and an uncaught throw (both RED).
- **Found on the way (not fixed here).** GET /api/file/content, /file/info, /file/raw, /file/binary and /api/download never answer without `?path=`: `safePath(undefined)` throws before the handler's try in an async express 4 handler — an unhandled rejection, the request hangs. The sentinel smokes them with a fixture path (`query` rows).
- **Gates.** test-reach-model (new, fast, 59, 2.1 s): the derivation over three real suites, the attribution over real files, the meet rule, the hubs (CONTROL: without the hub rule utils.js reaches fewer suites), the rails over a stub repository (CONTROL: a suite with its reach emptied is dropped; without `always` no sentinel), the declaration census (CONTROL: a missed derived token), the sentinel's census over the tree (CONTROL: a new GET, a dead row) + its two judges. test-affected-model 66 (the page stubs carry the §47 passport; §4: the table fallback = the old reach with `reach: false`, the browser suites + own loaders with it). test-ci-gate 395 (+ the sentinel is one heavy always row; reach-model.mjs in stubGateRepo — and test-ci-heavy-launch's). `reachContext` costs ~1 s per real-table call; test-ci-gate shares one memo over its four (16 s here at load 6).

### lane jobenv-strip-census — a Background Work job's env strips EVERY harness credential variable, derived from the descriptors (B-6be2; found by job-vendor-ban verify r3, LOW: latent — the production server env held none of the names)
- **The gap:** `src/jobs.js` `jobEnv` typed its credential strip by hand (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR`); codex's `creds.spawnEnvVar` `CODEX_HOME` — and every other login name the vendor CLIs read — rode into every job from the server's env.
- **ONE derived list — `src/harness-env.js` (PURE, imports nothing; every answer is over the descriptors it is handed):** `credentialEnvNames(descriptors)` = every descriptor's `creds.*EnvVar` / `creds.*EnvVars` ∪ `VENDOR_CREDENTIAL_ENV` (the names the CLIs read as a login, measured in the binaries: claude 2.1.296 `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_FILE_DESCRIPTOR`, `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_FILE_DESCRIPTOR`; codex-rs `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CODEX_API_KEY`, `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` — its own sentence lists them). Today 11 names. The descriptors gain two fields: `homeEnvVar` (claude `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, codex `CODEX_HOME`) and `keyEnvVars` (the names `accounts.resolveForSpawn` writes: claude `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; codex none). A new `creds.fooEnvVar` joins with no other edit.
- **TWO DOORS.** The JOB door (`jobEnv(extra, base = process.env)`, exported) strips the whole list over the registry at call time (a plugin-registered harness joins); a job's own env / secrets are laid on after and win. The AGENT door (`agent-env.js` `agentEnv(base, { keep, drop })` / `daemonEnv(base, { drop })`, PURE, so the server-side callers hand in `agentCredentialEnvNames(list())`) strips every DECLARED name except a `homeEnvVar` = `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR`. **Choice:** the agent door keeps `CODEX_HOME` / `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (a no-account spawn deliberately runs on the machine login — ws-create's "CODEX_HOME inherited from the server" — and the server reads the same variable as its own home: codex `creds.sharedHome()`, agentd's transcript discovery) and the vendor names no descriptor writes (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, … — an OpenCode / ACP agent may hold its own login that way; the agent filter stays a narrow denylist). Callers handed the drop: `ws-handler.agentEnv` (every session / attach / plugin / discovery spawn), the usage-pool reset-credit helper, and the daemon's birth (`agentd/client.js`) — a daemon child's env is the server's laid OVER the daemon's own, so a name ws-create deleted came back from a daemon born holding it (latent before: only local sessions lost `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR`). oat-mint is an allowlist over it (checked: no credential name in `MINT_ENV_ALLOW`).

### lane enter-recorder-keyup — the incident recorder's key ring tells a Shift chord from a Shift tap from a shifted character (inc-mv7mdv6b-emxq, the owner 2026-10-14 「又出现回车提前发送了」; no user line: nothing the user sees changes)
- **What the bundle showed, and what it could not:** the ring's tail was `ime end commit` → 196 ms → `S-Shift` → 554 ms → `Enter` (plain: no S-, no c:1) → the send 1 ms later. Five earlier sends that night had the same shape and their messages end in 「？」 (Shift+/); this one ends in 「）」 (Shift+0). The Enter came 750 ms after the commit with no Shift on it, so EnterGuard did what its rules say. Whether the Shift typed the 「）」 before a separate Enter, or was a Shift+Enter let go early, the ring could not say: a shifted printable key folded into the one-per-3-s "typing" marker, and a modifier's key-up was never recorded, so both read `S-Shift, Enter`.
- **The change (PURE in src/lib/chat-enter-keys.js, wired in src/lib/incident-recorder.js):** `actionKeyWords` writes `SHIFTED_CHAR` `'S-·'` for a character typed with Shift held and no Ctrl/Meta/Alt (c:1 when the IME owned it; never the character; C-/M-/A- chords still name the key, e.g. `C-S-A`). The new `actionKeyUpWords` returns `{ key, up: 1 }` for a Shift / Control / Alt / Meta key-up (null for every other key), and the recorder pushes it from a capture + passive `keyup` listener as `{ t, k: 'key', key, up: 1, el }`. Now the three shapes differ: a character then a send = `S-Shift S-· Shift↑ Enter`, a chord = `S-Shift S-Enter`, a tap then a send = `S-Shift Shift↑ Enter`; the up's time gives how long the Shift was held and how long before the Enter it was let go.
- **Not touched:** EnterGuard and its 50 ms window, the typing marker, the ime markers, the ws ring, CAP.action 500. The cost: a capital is three ring rows (down, S-·, up) where it was at most one burst marker. inc-mv7mdv6b-emxq's 500 rows covered 47.5 min with 31 modifier key-downs, so the window shrinks by roughly a tenth on that kind of typing.
- **Gates:** test-chat-enter-ime 58 → 74 (fast, PURE). §2 is the table for both functions (a shifted A / ")" / "？" ⇒ S-·, the IME's ⇒ c:1, a bare letter ⇒ null, Cmd+c / Ctrl+Shift+A / Alt+Shift+x unchanged, the four modifier ups, other ups null). §2b replays the bundle's shape through the recorder's own keydown/keyup order with its 3 s marker: the three sequences are distinct, the character is never in the ring, and a Shift+Enter let go 9 ms early still reads "tap" with its times (held 546 ms, up 9 ms before the Enter; the tap: 91 / 464). §4 is the keyup wiring census. §5 controls: without S-· the character and the tap read the same; without the ups the tap's hold and gap are gone; without both (the .267 recorder) character, tap and early chord are all `S-Shift Enter`, the bundle's shape.

### pool-oat-materialize verify r1 → fix — the sweep merges into the CLI's credential store instead of replacing it, ownership is the mark's, every act is guarded and off the loop (lane pool-oat-fix; pool-oat-verify REFUTED 4c1be7e0e: 1 blocker, 5 medium, 7 low)
- **F1 (blocker) — the file is the CLI's bag of top-level keys:** CLI 2.1.296 keeps `mcpOAuth` in the same file store as `claudeAiOauth` (read off the binary by the verifier), and r1 rewrote the whole file whenever it was not byte-equal to our body — an MCP sign-in made through a pooled session was deleted at the next sweep. Now the store writes `oatFileMerge(file, body)`: ONLY `claudeAiOauth` + the `vibespaceOat` mark replaced, every other key kept; `current` is `oatFileCurrent` (claudeAiOauth + the mark only); over a DEAD login the archive keeps the whole old file and the new file keeps its other keys; taking ours back strips our two keys and unlinks only an empty bag (the remover's `rest`).
- **F2 — a failed READ is not an unreadable login:** account-material `readCredentialFile` (lstat dir + open + fstat + read) answers `read-failed` with the errno for anything but ENOENT; the verdict refuses by name (`read-failed`: nothing archived, nothing written, the row says `could not read the account folder (EMFILE)`); `unreadable` is only bytes that are not a JSON object. The write never runs after a failed archive (one try, the archive first).
- **F3 — ours is the MARK's:** the mark names the row (`vibespaceOat: {v, mintedAt, account}`; `oatFileOurs(file, id)` = the mark naming this row + no refresh token), never the token value, so a re-mint's older token is OURS and is swapped in place — in the unknown-CLI boot window too (the window stops a NEW file, never the swap); a re-mint whose write failed says `write-failed` until the next sweep swaps it. `mergeSubscription` copies no materialized file (only the CLI's other keys in it) and re-derives ours on the survivor, its shape riding along.
- **F4 — a token that does not decrypt moves nothing:** `{readable: false}` ⇒ verdict `none`, reason `oat-unreadable` (no archive, no write, no removal across sweeps; the row: 长期 token 无法解密——重新铸造, ahead of `written`); `writeCredentialFile` refuses a non-object body by name (`not-an-object`).
- **F5 — 主开发's ruling: an unmeasured CLI never pulls a linked member's file:** a KNOWN unmeasured CLI keeps our file while a conversation's pool link names the member (`_oatMemberLinked`: the per-session links under data/pool-links — a claude conversation always has its own, ws-create passes the session key), the verdict says `cli-unmeasured` + `held`, the row 此 CLI 版本未测量：现有会话继续，不再新派; the pool stops PLACING on it (`_placeable` behind poolMembers / isPoolMember / the spawn's live-target test: our file on a known unmeasured CLI is no candidate — an unknown version stays one, its file was written under a measured CLI); a new conversation in an all-token pool is refused by name (`oat-cli-unmeasured`); the next sweep after the last link ends takes the file back. A stale ours under a held link is still swapped in place.
- **F6 — the census judges behaviour, and structure by function:** test-oat-mint §8 runs every oat flow (mint ×5 on a shut gate, the CLI measured, a re-mint, a sweep, an oat-file-sync tick, a link + an unmeasured CLI + the link's end, clearOat ×5) under a stack-aware spy on fs + fs.promises (59 mutations inside member dirs, each by write / archive / remove reached from `_syncOatFileNow`; a removal only through the remover, which REFUSES without its `isOurs` question and asks it on the bytes it removes); the structure census is by enclosing function, never argument text (④ the three acts' callers across src, ⑤ the private writers' callers, ⑥ the oat clock holds no write door). The verifier's guarded plants g1–g6 are each RED by structure; plants that run (a path-variable write, a rename, a plaintext copy, a yes-man remover) are each RED by behaviour.
- **F7 — guarded acts:** the archive checks a fresh stat (inode + mtime + size = what the verdict read) and, after its rename, that what moved IS what was judged (else it is linked straight back — link(2) never lands on a file); the writer replaces only the file it read (`expect`) or, for an absent one, links its tmp into place (EEXIST = a login landed: refused, `changed`, retried next sweep).

### lane app-launch-singleton — one program, one instance: a running app is OPENED, a launch that ends as it starts is SAID, an installed browser gets its own profile (fleet inc-mv7hxc2n-2cvr on .266; 「我一点开它数一秒就闪退」 + addendum 「我本来也找不到它启动的 Chrome 到底在哪儿」)
- **Defect #0 (why the Chrome had no --user-data-dir):** the install plan's Chrome is a Layer 0 row `app.<entry>` from its .desktop file (`Exec=/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable %U`, `category: 'browser'`). desktop-serve `launch()` gives browserArgv's own profile dir only to a row with `row.browser` — set on the catalog's two browser rows alone — so every installed / witnessed / registered browser ran AS TYPED on the user's default ~/.config/google-chrome. The second start on :5 was handed by Chrome's process singleton to the agent's :2 instance and exited code 0 within a second.
- **Fix — the launch:** desktop-serve `registry()` passes every served row through `launchFacts` — PURE `appBrowserVerdict` (src/desktop-apps.js; `browserFamilyOf` by precise basename in src/desktop-browser-app.js: chrome/chromium/edge/brave/vivaldi ⇒ chromium, firefox/librewolf/waterfox/floorp/icecat ⇒ firefox) gives an installed browser its family (`browserBy: 'exec'`, re-judged for a variant), so it takes the B-bfe6 profile + a11y + portal path; a launcher (`flatpak run`), a sandboxed app id or an unknown browser stays as typed. Every row carries `runsTwice` (PURE `runsTwiceVerdict`: own profile / LibreOffice / one-process terminal ⇒ yes; a default-profile browser, anything GApplication-like ⇒ no).
- **Fix — attach, never relaunch:** PURE `launchVerdict({row, apps, host})` (src/desktop-fit.js, shared with the client): a live record of the row (its appId, or a typed command of its exec, on that machine; a record being replaced never) ⇒ `attach` (target = the newest ready one; `again` only when `runsTwice`); the LOCK FACT (`display.profileLockFact`: Chrome's SingletonLock `<host>-<pid>` in the family's default dir, its holder's /proc session id ⇒ `row.lock.recordId`) makes a typed command / an older default-profile launch an instance of every row of that browser; a live foreign holder + no own profile ⇒ `held`. The card's press OPENS the target (the existing attach path) and says 「正在 :2 运行 · 由 agent 会话 X 启动」, every live instance listed under it with 打开 / 关闭, 「再开一个」 only when it runs twice; the card's POST carries `ifRunning: 'attach'` (also For you's Open) and the keeper answers the running record `attached: true` (journalled; never for a document; the launch row's share is not applied to it). Records carry `launchedBy` (agent session by name — `vibespace-window open`, the agent browser, a session token on the launch route; the person; a relaunch keeps it).
- **Fix — the quick exit:** `rec.appAt` is stamped before the app's spawn; an app that ends within `QUICK_EXIT_MS` (3 s) gets `quickExit {afterMs, sinceReadyMs, code, signal, running, runningDisplay}` (the same app's live instance); every app-exit journal line gains its timing (`[desktop] da-… exited: application exited (code 0) — under 0.1 s after ready`); the hub files ONE `desktop-app-quick-exit:<id>` notice (PURE `quickExitNoticeText`: where it runs, who started it); `exitCloseVerdict` keeps the window (`quick-exit`) — the window says it over its empty pane with 「打开在 :2 运行的那个」; the card says it on the next open (10 min, only when no instance of ours took it over).
- **The addendum (an agent-started app listed nowhere):** the Desktop button's popover has a 「正在运行的应用」 group (`GET /api/desktop/apps?records=1`, then the broadcast): every live app window, where / who, Open, Close. The Apps dialog's Running rows say where / who too; the cards follow an instance starting / ending (only when that set moved, never under a held press).
- **xpra-ui import during teardown:** xpra-client's worker `onerror` from a worker finish() already tore down is ignored and `preventDefault`ed — the window keeps its exit sentence, no uncaught worker error over it.
- **Tests:** test-app-launch-once (NEW fast, ~1 s: the real keeper over a fake display recipe + sh fake apps, one a Chrome-like singleton — the handover ⇒ quickExit + timed journal + ONE notice + the window kept; ifRunning attach (no second record); launchedBy; an installed google-chrome-stable launches with `--user-data-dir=<data>/desktop-apps/<id>/profile`; the SingletonLock reader on a private HOME — live / dead / other host / none, list() maps the holder to its record) 32/0; test-desktop-apps +28 PURE legs (the verdict table, families, runs-twice, quick exit, notice words, lock parse, wiring pins) 458/0; test-desktop-app-window §S (heavy chrome, real Xvfb + x11vnc, two witnessed fixtures: an agent-started Single listed on its card + in the Desktop list, the press opens it with no second record, the old door's handover kept with its door, Close, Blink's window + card sentence, zh at 390; §E presses "Open another" for its second xterm) 160/0; fast tier 376/1 (the one red: test-changelog-style's newest-heading rule — a .268 block on a .266 base). ### lane display-secret-fd — the app-secrets key never rides a display's bus environment: it is handed over once, in a file the service unlinks (B-6c6d, oat-verify F5 LOW, credential class)

- **The finding.** `secretServicePlan` laid `VS_APP_SECRETS_KEY` (the per-display key that unlocks the app's keyring) over `portalPlan`'s `env` in desktop-serve's bring-up (~931). That env is the environment dbus-daemon is STARTED with, and every service the bus activates inherits it. **MEASURED on the base tree (d5f352538, a real private bus + the libsecret probe + one Introspect of the portal and one org.a11y.Bus.GetAddress — /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/display-secret-fd/environ-census.mjs): the key sat in `/proc/<pid>/environ` of SEVEN live processes** — dbus-daemon, the secret service, xdg-desktop-portal, xdg-permission-store, xdg-document-portal, at-spi-bus-launcher and the a11y bus's own dbus-daemon — for the display's lifetime, readable by anything of the same uid (an agent's `cat /proc/*/environ`). **After: zero**, same seven-process session.
- **Why not a pipe.** The brief's first choice was an inherited fd. MEASURED (dbus 1.16.2, a `<type>session</type>` bus with the product's own bus.conf): a bus-activated service inherits the daemon's ENVIRONMENT (`VS_APP_SECRETS_KEY=…` arrived) but NOT its file descriptors — dbus's spawn closes every fd above stderr before exec, so the daemon's fd 3 (a pipe we held open) was gone in the child (`/proc/self/fd` = 0,1,2 only; a read of fd 3 is EBADF). A pipe cannot reach a service the BUS starts; it can and does reach the service's own child.
- **The handoff.** PURE `secretServicePlan` now answers `{ secrets, store, keyFile, files: [service file, key file] }` and NOTHING for an env (the `env` field is gone). The key file is `<app dir>/portal/run/secrets.key` — under the plan's private `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, written 0600 in a 0700 dir with the rest of `plan.files`, before dbus-daemon starts — and its path is the service's 5th Exec argument. `src/secret-service.py` reads it with `O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW` and UNLINKS it before it owns `org.freedesktop.secrets`; no key file ⇒ `[secrets] no per-display key: the key file is gone (secrets.key ENOENT) — it is handed over once, when the display starts` and exit 1 (libsecret is answered with Spawn.ChildExited in ms, never left hanging), as does an Exec line from an older tree (fewer than 5 argv). The sealer (`src/app-secrets-seal.js`) now takes the key off an inherited PIPE — `VS_APP_SECRETS_FD` is the fd NUMBER, `pass_fds` on the service's side — so even that short-lived child's environ carries no key. desktop-serve pushes `secrets.files` and assigns nothing into `plan.env`; its teardown unlinks the key file (an app that never asked for its keyring leaves it behind, and it must never sit at rest beside the sealed store).
- **The census (test-app-display-secrets ①c, printed).** `VS_APP_SECRETS_KEY` appears NOWHERE in src/ any more (RED control: the .267 line put back in a copy of desktop-apps.js ⇒ the census names it); every name of `plan.env` / `plan.appEnv` / the secrets plan is judged by shape — a secret-named key (KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASS|CRED) is allowed only when its value is an fd number (RED control: the key planted back over plan.env ⇒ `VS_APP_SECRETS_KEY`); and desktop-serve's bring-up is pinned to `plan.files.push(...secrets.files)` with no `Object.assign(plan.env, secrets…)`.
- **Gates.** test-app-display-secrets (fast) **49/0, 4.4 s** (was 40/0, 2.5 s): ①c the census above; ③ on the real bus — the ENVIRON CENSUS over `ps -s <bus pid>` (no process of the session carries the key or a secret-named env), the key file gone once the service ran, the RED control that re-lays the key over plan.env (the census then names dbus-daemon AND the service), and the no-key-file bus refusing by name in ≤ 3 s; the .267 legs (store / lookup / search / delete / Unlock / restart / Forget all / no secret in a log / the logging mutant) unchanged. test-app-display-secrets-chrome (heavy, the lane's one) **10/0, 9 s**: ①b scans EVERY readable `/proc/<pid>/environ` on the box (691 read) while a real Chrome 154 runs on the private bus with nine processes in the bus's session — only a planted control (`sleep` with the key in its env, the scan's positive control) holds it. test-app-display-session-census 25/0, test-architecture 690/0 (§86 row `src/app-secrets-seal.js` 2 → 3: the key read off the pipe fd), the whole fast tier 378/378.

### lane mediation-chrome-hub-red — test-browser-mediation-chrome r4 judges each refusal's code, not stderr's first line; ④ r3 M1 CONTROL reads Chrome's environ by the shape (B-a23c; no user line: a gate fix)
- **The standing hub red (int261 → int266, each "BASE by A/B"):** r4's `state load <crafted>` row. The hub's PATH agent-browser is the global 0.38.1 (nvm, 2026-09-25); since 2.369.250 the flag table is 0.38.2, so vibespace-browser says `note: the browser CLI here is 0.38.1; … [flag_table_drift]` BEFORE every refusal it makes after the binary lookup — `state load` reads its file there — and the leg took stderr's FIRST line as the refusal. A/B on the same tree: a copy of 0.38.2 first on PATH ⇒ r4 green. The runner was never green on this leg: ci.yml installs no agent-browser, so ③ r4 (and ② / ③ r3 / ④) SKIP there.
- **Refuted, measured:** the hub's Chrome 154 (the row never reaches a browser; every Chrome CONTROL green); locale (LANG=C.UTF-8 both, the CLI's sentences are not translated); a case-/path-sensitive spelling (`FILE:` refused alike); a leftover profile / lock (ROOT and SOCK3 are per-pid; red 3/3 on fresh dirs); timing (a local refusal before /resolve; deterministic).
- **Fix (r4):** each row's code = its refusal line (the first un-indented line that is not a `note:`), equal to the PURE verdict of the same spelling (`classify(args, {ours: true[, stdin]})` / `stateFileVerdict(json)`); a measured row says the CLI's own drift (the version its note names vs `TABLE_VERSION`) and holds the note to exactly the spellings refused after the lookup (none without drift); a CONTROL keeps the pre-.268 first-line read and shows it misreads exactly those rows under drift. A mutant CLI that lets `state load` through is red on r4.
- **The second private-shape red (④ r3 M1 CONTROL, every bus-less gate shape, master too):** the CONTROL read "the relaunched Chrome's /proc environ carries no AGENT_BROWSER_*" as the daemon's scrub. Measured on Chrome 154 (a bare headless Chrome + a marker variable): with DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS set (any value, `disabled:` too) Chrome's process-title rewrite overwrites the environ region; unset, the region stays — the daemon's whole environment, the same 10 AGENT_BROWSER_* keys at the first launch and at the relaunch (the daemon scrubs nothing). The CONTROL judges the reading by the shape: bus set ⇒ `title`, unset ⇒ `environment` holding exactly the daemon's AGENT_BROWSER_* set.
- **The load flake (④ r3 M1 `{"orphanB":[],"state":"stopped","left":[]}`, int222 / int239 "known", red here once at load 23):** the ④ keepers were built without `tickMs`, so the keeper's OWN 5 s timer (attach / start ⇒ ensureTimer) ran beside the hand ticks and, when it fired between the daemon's SIGKILL and the orphan read (a window load stretches), ended the relaunched Chrome first. One `kk.tick()` injected in that window = the same red byte for byte, every run; a 100 ms timer reds ④ in a cascade. Both ④ keepers now take `tickMs: 3600e3` (test-browser-ephemeral's hand-ticked legs' rule).
- **Labels:** "the REAL 0.38.1" (lane L r5 F1, ④ r5 MAJOR 1) print the measured version.
- **Not a cause here, measured on the way:** an XDG_RUNTIME_DIR long enough that the daemon's socket path passes 103 bytes makes the binary refuse the session ("Socket path would be 125 bytes (max 103)") — ② skips and ③ r3 CONTROL reads `null`; a short private dir is green.

### lane layout-deferred-writer — a phone record no longer replaces the desktop record deferred before it (B-4767, phone-arrangement-verify r2 F5)
- **Cause:** §6b guard 3's slot (`LayoutManager._pendingRemote`) kept ONE record per desktop regardless of writer. While this page's pointer was down a desktop-class record (another desktop's window move) was deferred; a phone-class record for the same desktop then REPLACED it, and at the release the phone record was applied — membership only under the .264 law (guard 10) — so the move never landed here. Not a regression (the slot predates the writer stamp).
- **Fix (PURE src/lib/layout-model.js):** `writerClass` (THE phone/desktop predicate — the apply's membershipOnly asks it too; unstamped = a pre-.264 sender, an unknown stamp and a re-read are desktop), `deferKey` = one slot per desktop AND class (`'phone:' + id` beside the old key), `releaseNext` = lowest seq first + drop a record not newer than the newest APPLIED for its desktop (`_appliedSeq`, noted by every `_handleRemoteSync`, cleared on reconnect), `deferKeysOf` for a deleted desktop. layout.js: a record that lands while others still wait (the drain's 300 ms after a pointerup) joins them — applied live there it made the waiting desktop record older than the newest applied, and the drop rule would have lost the move again; an armed drain is never shortened; the re-read drops a phone record deferred before it was asked. Guards 1 / 2 / 4 untouched.
- **Gates:** NEW test-layout-model (fast, 42, 0.1 s): the class / key / release tables, F5 / mirror / pre-.264 / burst / drop scenarios, a 3 000-sequence fuzz (deferred-then-released = applied live in arrival order), the wiring, 4 patched-copy controls (single slot, map-order drain, no drop, resync as phone). test-phone-desktop-sync ⑮ (heavy chrome: D holds a press on its desktop, a second desktop DW and the phone write): a F5, b mirror, c pre-.264, d a phone record in the drain's 300 ms — RED copies of this source: the pre-fix slot line (a, c, d red; b holds), no join (d red). Pins moved: test-desktop-record §6 + controls one-slot / drain-no-sort, test-window-binding-model guard 3.

### lane browser-windows-rung-race — B-81c6: test-browser-windows ⑦ c31 raced in its HARNESS (two 40 ms sleeps), never in the keeper's plan read; the row is ordered by events now and the keeper journals its rung-2 lock queue (no user line: a test harness + one journal line)
- **The red (mirror-267 heavy 1/4, twice in a row; also twice on 2026-10-13):** row c31 got `aRung2Ran: true` beside A's correct `window_busy / user_driving`. c31 slept 40 ms for "B is inside its rung 2, holding the browser's lock", snapshotted the GLOBAL rung-2 count, started A, slept 40 ms for "A waits for the lock", then began the takeover.
- **Reproduced (the runner's shape: everything on cpus 0-3 with 8 CPU spinners, 2 node spawn loops and an fsync/tar IO loop):** base d5f352538 (a pristine `git archive` tree) red 10/10 (9 × the CI row, 1 × a third wrong ordering: B so slow that its own plan read came after the takeover began, so B refused itself); 4 spinners alone 0/2; quiet 0/1. A traced copy (each probe, rung-2 entry, lock queueing, plan read, takeover and release, timestamped) names the orderings. PASS: B enters rung 2 at ~15 ms, before the 40 ms snapshot; A probes, queues at the lock, the takeover begins, B is released, A's plan read refuses. FAIL ① (the CI row; reproduced with B's first probe held +30 ms): B's way to rung 2 outlasts the snapshot, so B's OWN rung 2 is counted as A's. FAIL ② (+60 ms): A overtakes B to the lock and reads its plan before the takeover began (A runs, B is refused). The keeper's verdict was right in all three: its plan read is synchronous with the lock grant (`await prev` → `fn()` → `planNow()` → the act, no await between), and a takeover or a live view registers synchronously (`inputs` / `watchers`).
- **Fix (the harness):** c31 waits on EVENTS: B's entry into rung 2 (the model's `rung2Entered`, called as B's rung 2 takes the hold) and A's place in the lock queue (the keeper's journal line, written before its wait). A rung 2 is A's only by A's own anchor (`rung2Log[].anchor`). New row c31v: a live view that opens during the lock wait ⇒ A's rung 2 runs without the cycle (⑦ rows 5 → 6).
- **Keeper (src/server/browser-keeper.js):** `rung2Serialized(profileId, fn, onWait)`: the map holds the queue's TAIL while any rung 2 of the browser is queued or in flight (r3 stored `prev.then(…)` but compared `cur`, so an entry never left the map); `onWait` runs synchronously when the lock is HELD, and the ladder journals `[browser] <holder> on <profile>: rung 2 waits for the browser's lock — another holder's rung 2 is in flight; the plan is read when the lock is granted`.
- **Controls:** (q) r5's slept harness with B's way to rung 2 +60 ms calls the PRODUCT keeper red, deterministically (B's rung 2 counted as A's, or A overtaking B); the event-ordered harness under the same delay is green. (r) A keeper copy that reads the plan after rung 1 but BEFORE the lock wait ⇒ c31 (A's rung 2 runs under the user's hands) and c31v (the cycle under the live view) red. (s) A keeper copy with r3's compare (`cur`) keeps the map entry, so a holder ALONE at the lock is journaled as waiting behind nobody (the rows' `bQueued: false` goes red).
- **Gates:** test-browser-windows 132/0 (127 before: + controls q, r, s and the setups of r and s); after the fix green 10/10 (each run the whole suite 132/0, on cpus 4-7 with the same noise beside the base's runs) under the same shape; fast tier 378/378 (every fast row of ci.mjs; the docs-reading suites again on the final text).
- Not .267's boot ordering: the suite never boots the server (the keeper runs in-process over the fake target model), and the row flaked on .262 too. The sharpener is CPU contention on the 4-vCPU runner.

### lane oat-row-one-word — a row on its long-lived token says 「仅长期 token」 once (owner 2026-10-14, two screenshots: "这些提示有些多余，直接说仅长期 token 就行了" / "这里为啥没有仅长期 token 的提示了")

### lane cli-one-text-arg — an agent CLI never silently drops words: a free-text command takes ONE text, refuses a stray word by name, takes long text from a file or stdin, and echoes the route's count

- **The incident (the owner, 2026-10-14).** An agent ran `vibespace-channels reply lark/<conv> "…若对照"有源码权限的人 vs 人员名单"会对不上。…" --to <id>`. The inner `"` closed the shell string, so the CLI got three words. `reply` sent `args[2]` and DROPPED the rest: the person read a message cut mid-sentence and nothing told the agent. The same shape was in `vibespace-msg send` (`args[2]`, the rest ignored) and in `vibespace-channels compose`, which took the LAST free word, so it sent only the tail. `vibespace-ask` (the default form) and `vibespace-task progress` / `backlog-add` JOINED every word, which lost the quotes and hid the mistake.
- **THE rule, once: PURE `src/agent-cli-text.js`** (imports nothing; the CLIs hand it `fs` as `io`). `takeDoors` (`--text "…"`, `--text -`, `--text-file <path>`, `--detail-file <path>`; `-` = stdin; one stdin per command), `textOf` (the argument OR its door, never both), `positionals` (the channels CLI finds flags by name: per-verb `valued` / `optional` / `bare` lists in `CH_TEXT_SPEC`), `strayRefusal` (the brief's sentence: count, first stray word quoted, cause, both doors; a stray FLAG or a word after an unknown flag is named as such), `oneText` (door error → stray → text), `sentLine` (`sent: N characters` from the route's `chars`; fewer than given ⇒ `the last K were CUT`; no `chars` ⇒ the CLI's own count), `chars` (code points). A file's text is its UTF-8 with ONE trailing newline trimmed. Stdin that is a char device (a terminal, `/dev/null`) is refused, never waited on.
- **How the CLIs reach it.** A checkout: `require('../../src/agent-cli-text.js')` (when `../../server.js` exists). A host: `require('./agent-cli-text.js')`, the boot-time copy (`createCliTextCopy` in agent-tool-generators, gitignored, `HostManager.AGENT_TOOLS` — §52a pins it). Both names are LITERAL, because test-peer-text-census refuses a computed require and walks a required module: the rule joined `PRINT_CLIS` (it prints nothing; every CLI print of its sentences is a row). A free-text verb REFUSES when the rule is missing (exit 2, it could not tell a stray word); other verbs work. `tty` is a stream builtin the census bans, so the stdin check is `fs.fstatSync(0).isCharacterDevice()`.
- **Per command (the census in test-cli-one-text, grep-derived from the four usage tables: 50 commands, each a verdict).** one-text (a stray word ⇒ exit 2, nothing sent; doors; echo): msg send, msg dispatch (`--file` kept), channels reply / compose / request, ask (the question; `--detail-file`), task progress / backlog-add (`--detail-file`). guard (a stray word ⇒ exit 2; no text of its own): channels react / unreact / withdraw (a `--why` that split), channels search (never a narrower search), task group-create / group-update (`--title` / `--objective`). text-flag: task backlog-edit (`--text` / `--text -` / `--text-file`; the ref stays a lookup). lookup (joined on purpose; a miss is named): ask resolve / show / clear, task progress-redact / backlog / backlog-claim / -unclaim / -done / -drop. members: msg group create / invite (a stray word is a member the server refuses). name: msg group rename (joined; the answer echoes it whole). no-text: the rest (`channels watch` rules are parsed by the server, which refuses an unexpected word).
- **The echo is the route's count.** `chars` (and `detailChars`) is the count of what the route KEPT: `msgSendAnswer` counts the stored message (so `dispatchAnswer` does too), `task-progress` the kept note (`addProgress` slices a note at 2000 and a detail at 6000 WITHOUT saying so — now the echo shows it), `task-backlog` the stored item, `user-todo` the stored question (cut at 500). Channels reply / compose (+ `--caller`) / request count the text they got.
- **Traps met.** (1) test-record-clear-census's alias pass scans at most 6000 characters of a block (`iSpan`). In the msg send handler, `deliverToConversation` sits right at that limit on the base, so ANY characters added above it pushed the call out of scan and the `req.body.text` row went dead. The count moved into `msgSendAnswer` (the handler is byte-identical above the call). (2) A call of the `chanAnswer` wrapper is a sentence sink, so `b.text` cannot sit in its arguments: the routes set `r.chars` before the call. (3) test-backlog-nudge finds the backlog-edit branch by the first `cmd === 'backlog-edit'` text, so the edit door is read inside that branch.
- **Gates.** test-cli-one-text (NEW, fast) 111/0: PURE rule; the census (+ a planted usage line caught); every one-text command — the incident's three pieces ⇒ exit 2, the sentence, ZERO calls on a counting fake route; the same words as ONE argument ⇒ sent whole + `sent: N characters`; `--text-file` / `--text -` byte for byte (quotes, newline, CJK, `$( )`, backticks, tab, emoji); `--detail-file`; given twice / missing file / nothing piped ⇒ refused; the cut echo; CONTROLS: msg send and channels reply without the scan send the FIRST piece and drop the rest, exit 0 (the incident), and ask's pre-fix join glues the pieces — each RED under the same judge; a host layout reads the copy beside it and REFUSES without it. Suites moved: test-peer-text-census (rows + the module walked + 2 print helpers), test-msg-cli-groups (dependency-free but for the rule), test-foryou-links (the loose question is refused), test-backlog-no-truncation (controls carry the rule beside them), mount-reader-census (agent-tool-generators 21 → 23), test-architecture (PURE row, §52a).
- **Docs.** The usage block of each CLI and `vibespace-docs msg|channels|ask|task` say: long or quoted text: `--text-file <path>` or `--text -` (stdin); the CLI refuses stray words. kb-api, kb-file-structure.

### lane peer-registry-identity — a conversation's CLI is found by its registration's PROCESS IDENTITY, never by a pid number (owner 2026-10-14 04:58Z: 「现在交给它」 → 「没有交出去 —— 联系不上这个 agent」 on 企业助手)
- **Cause (measured on the hub, read-only):** the host hard-froze at 10:26 and rebooted; the CLIs never cleaned ~/.claude/sessions, so 11 of 19 conversations held TWO registrations (30 records). Pids restart low after a reboot: 4 pre-freeze pids (15585 / 15598 / 15609 / 15622) now named kernel threads or another user's processes. `findPeer` took the FIRST record in readdir order (libuv sorts: "15622.json" < "17654.json") whose `kill(pid, 0)` held — EPERM counted alive — so the stale record won, its socket /run/user/1000/cc-socks/15622.sock did not exist, the post failed ENOENT and the ladder logged "the socket is not served: the conversation is not running"; 34 posts stashed (企业助手, 米哈游监控, Proxmox和Docker管理, Kaixu 学习). The other 7 twins' stale pids stayed free (dead ⇒ skipped).
- **Fix (src/peer-messaging.js, SHARED — the agentd bundle carries it):** PURE `registryIdentityOk(rec, probe)` — live iff the pid's /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 equals the record's `procStart` (the CLI writes it as a string; EPERM alone is never liveness there; no procStart / no /proc ⇒ pid-only, said in `identity`) AND `messagingSocketPath` is an existing socket (statSync isSocket; a Windows named pipe `\\.\pipe\…` — the CLI's own form there, matched by its own regex — has no inode to stat and is left to the post, else agentd on a Windows machine would find no peer). `lookupPeer` judges EVERY record of the session id, the newest passing `startedAt` wins, failing records are skipped (never cleaned); it answers `{peer, candidates, stale, why}` with `why` = "candidates: n, stale: m (pid-gone: g, pid-reused: k, socket-absent: j)". `findPeer` = its `peer` (all callers + agentd unchanged). The starttime comes from src/proc-identity.js `starttimeOf` (the pid+starttime law of Background Work).
- **The ladder's words (src/server/conversation-deliver.js rung 1):** stale registrations only ⇒ `[deliver] <cid>: no live inbox on this machine — stale registration(s) only — pid reused / socket absent (<why>)`; a final post refusal re-judges the registry — "the socket is not served: the conversation is not running" only when no record passes now, the stale words when only stale ones are left, and "the socket refused the post, though a registration still passes its identity check (pid, identity; why)" otherwise. A stub `peerMsg` with findPeer alone keeps working (no lookupPeer ⇒ the plain lookup).
- **Gates:** test-peer-messaging §4 (32: PURE verdicts over an injected probe — pid+start, pid-reused under EPERM, pid-gone, pid-only without procStart / without /proc, no socket path, a Windows named pipe never statted; the hub's shape with the stale record sorting first ⇒ the live record + its key + why `candidates: 2, stale: 1 (pid-reused: 1, socket-absent: 1)` + a real post; the mirror; two live records ⇒ newest `startedAt` either order; single stale ⇒ null + why; RED control = the pid-only first-record rule in a patched copy picks the stale record and its post fails ENOENT), test-peer-delivery (87: the ladder over the REAL lookup — the hub's shape delivers to the live socket, stale-only logs the new line and never "not running", no records ⇒ rung 1 silent, the three re-judged refusal verdicts, RED control through the ladder). test-notify-retry (307) and test-park-step (36) rigs now SERVE their stand-in sockets (a registration counts only while its socket exists). mount-reader-census: peer-messaging 3 → 4 (the socket stat). Fast suites reading the two files 20/20; the whole fast tier 379/0; test-architecture 690/0. Read-only proof over the hub's real registry (the .json records only, never a .key): the base rule picked the stale record for 4/11 twins, the new rule picks the live one for 11/11.

### lane decision-vendor-hygiene — a 402 / 400 stops the Decision API row like a 401; the owner's words in the questions pass the ONE scrub (B-2979 + B-d375)
- **Cause (B-2979, money):** `judge()` stopped the row only on 401 / 403 (`reconnect`: no call until a new key) and backed off on 429 / 5xx / 0. A 402 (the plan does not allow the model) and a 400 (the model refused the request shape — measured 2026-10-12: two models answered 400 to every call) fell to the `vendor-error` branch — unbilled, but one call and one journal line per record, every pass.
- **Fix (PURE, src/decision-model.js):** `rowStopOf(status)` → `reconnect` (401 / 403) | `plan` (402) | `shape` (400) | null, `ROW_STOPS`; WHY + `budgetVerdict({plan, shape})` after a refused key, before the walls and the money. **Engine (src/server/decision-engine.js):** ONE stop record `{sig, why, status, at}` — sig = sha256 of provider + model + key, so a new key, provider or model lifts it (the owner's Test still calls; its 200 lifts it too); `status().stop` {why, status, at} (`reconnect` kept for the card), the plugin row's `why`; `plan` / `shape` say ONE server notice per stop (`decision-stop:<why>:<sig12>`, i18n key = the chip title's sentence; said again at the next refusal only when no client received it); journal outcome `plan` / `shape`. The attention scan's STOP list takes the three row stops (its queue empties instead of re-asking a stopped row). **Client:** plugins-ui `DECISION_STOP_WORDS` (reconnect | plan | shape → the chip word, warn, + the title's sentence), zh + ja.
- **Measured (test-decision-engine I, the fake vendor, a pass of 5 records):** 402 — 5 calls before (the old classification, stubbed) → 1 after; 400 — 5 → 1; the same key + model with the vendor answering again: 0 calls, no second notice; a new model / a new key / the owner's Test: calls resume (5 of 5); a 422 stays one call a record. The attention scan runs ≤ 3 calls in flight, so up to 3 may land before the first answer stops the row.
- **Cause (B-d375, privacy, LOW):** a rule's condition, a routing rule's option descriptions and a webhook rule's condition ride `questions[]` (channel-filter `decisionQuestion` — the channels engine's ONE question site for rule / routing / webhook rules), which `buildInput` never sees ⇒ `buildRequest` sent them raw. `src/server/permission-rules.js` has no judge() site at this base.
- **Fix:** PURE `scrubQuestions(questions)` beside `cleanPart` — every string field of a question, its choices and its levels through `scrub` (the ONE table: secret-shapes `redactSecrets`, runs on), except the identifiers the answers are keyed by (type, name, choices[].value, levels[].label); a copy, nothing cut. The engine calls it once in `judge()`, right before its ONE `buildRequest`. The `[userBlock]` part already went through `cleanPart` (pinned now).
- **Gates:** test-decision-model 212/0 (the row-stop table + 5 budgetVerdict rows; the question scrub over the REAL channel-filter builders — 4 marks, identifiers kept, 30 product questions byte for byte, both dialects, the userBlock pin; census: ONE buildRequest caller in src (the engine) on the questions scrubQuestions returned, 5 judge() sites with their uses, the chip words ⊇ ROW_STOPS with zh + ja, the notice = the title's sentence; RED control: scrubQuestions = identity leaks 3 of 3 shapes), test-decision-engine 46/46 (I: the before / after counts with the old classification as the RED reference, notice once, status / plugin why, journal, the three lifting triggers, 401, 422; J: the fake vendor receives the condition + the option description redacted, RED control: scrubQuestions stubbed to identity sends the token; the card leg: desk «stopped — plan refused» warn, phone 390 zh 「已停 — 套餐不支持」).

### lane prepush-partner-patterns — the local push gate catches what GitHub push protection catches (B-89da; no user line: a gate change)
- **The incident:** 2.369.263's first cut (79cb1d60b) was refused by GitHub push protection (GH013 "Slack API Token") for the literal Slack-token fixture in decision-input-scrub's SIX (scripts/test-decision-engine.mjs:171, scripts/test-decision-model.mjs:246); it was re-cut as fb904524a with runtime-built fixtures.
- **Measured cause — the allowlist, applied per LINE (neither a path allowlist nor the regex):** both local scanners (repo-guard's scan.mjs in the global hook and scripts/secret-scan.mjs) MATCHED the token (slack-token, 43 chars) and then dropped it: the allow check was `allowed(line) || allowed(hit)`, and the SIX line also carried a PEM header that `.repo-guard-allow`'s `BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY` row matches, so one row silenced the Slack, Anthropic and GitHub shapes on that line. Reproduced over the refused range 69f2a59c1..79cb1d60b: with the repo allowlist both scanners rc 0; without it 8 findings, both Slack lines among them; the SIX line alone with ONLY that row rc 0, the same line with its PEM header cut rc 1. Hypothesis (a) holds but is not the cause (the pre-push gate never ran scripts/secret-scan.mjs, yet repo-guard's copy carries the same Slack rule); (c) refuted (38 characters after the prefix, the rule wants 10+); (d) refuted (the Actions workflow scans the tree after a push, and under the same allowlist it passed the two files too).
- **THE ONE TABLE:** scripts/secret-scan.mjs `RULES` — 21 partner rows (slack-token, slack-config-token, slack-app-token, slack-webhook, github-token 36, github-pat 82, gitlab-token, anthropic-key, openai-key, google-api-key 35, google-oauth-secret 28, google-oauth-token, aws-akid, aws-secret, stripe-key, twilio-api-key, sendgrid-key, npm-token 36, pypi-token, huggingface-token 34, private-key-block) + 9 generic rows. A partner row never consults the allowlist (GitHub never reads it); a generic row is silenced only by an allow row that overlaps its hit; every match on a line is judged. New modes: `--range=<a>..<b>|<b>` (every commit's added lines + the combined diff + the touched files' full text; a never-fetched base falls back to what no remote-tracking ref has; an unknown tip exits 2) and `--tree` (every tracked text file in one process, ~1.8 s).
- **Three callers, one file:** scripts/git-hooks/pre-push runs `--range` per pushed ref BEFORE `VIBESPACE_SKIP_CI` (that line moved below the scan), the heavy verdict and the fast tier; scripts/ci.mjs's fast tier runs `--tree` right after the build (absent at an old sha ⇒ not judged); .github/workflows/secret-scan.yml runs `--tree` (its per-file loop retired).
- **The tree under the table:** 22 findings on 2dd2f322a, all fixed. Partner literals are now built at runtime: test-exit-run (four GitHub tokens, an OPENSSH block, the AWS example key id, an OpenAI project key, the JWT-glued Slack / GitLab / Google shapes), test-cluster-presets (8 Google OAuth secrets), test-integrations-store (2), test-mounts-oauth (4). Three partner rows left .repo-guard-allow (each one allowed itself); two value rows were added for the second token of a fixture line that the line-wide allow used to cover (dbg-comm-surfaces' expired refresh token, lark-shape's echoed bearer).
- **Gates:** NEW test-secret-scan (fast, 113, ~0.7 s): every row RED at runtime plus two near-misses each; the rel263 shape through the REAL hook (refused before any tier with file:line and the fixture rule, also under VIBESPACE_SKIP_CI and as a new branch; a fix in a later commit is still refused; the squash goes through); controls: the hook without its block, the line-wide scanner and the base scanner each pass it; the allowlist cannot allow itself (rows for the literal, the path and `.*` stay RED, and the literal row is a finding of its own); the --range legs; the three-callers census. Also test-ci-gate 358 (its §4 stub repo carries the scanner), test-exit-run 547 (heavy, run alone), test-cluster-presets 231, test-integrations-store 29, test-mounts-oauth 17, test-channels-slack-send 73, test-channels-lark-shape 428.

### lane doc-table-native — a standard table holding a bare `<absent>` is a TABLE, never a raw block; the raw chip says what it is (owner 2026-10-14 「这下面不是标准的表格吗 为啥显示说是源码？」)
- **Cause (bisected on the shape, scripts/fixtures/doc-wheel/32-table-placeholder-cells.md):** an agent's adjudication report — a paragraph whose code span held `…/golden_imports/<case>/paper.txt`, then a 10-column GFM table — drew the table as a raw block (chip 「Markdown · 原样保留，点此改源码」). Hypotheses on base 2dd2f322a: (a) the `<case>` in the code span before — REFUTED (marked consumes a code span whole; paragraph + table with or without a blank line); (b) underscores in a cell's code span, (c) `"` `§` `(` `…` `$`, (d) 10 columns / no trailing pipe, (e) alignment rows `:--` `:-:` `--:`, (f) a short row — all tables on base (controls); (g) a BARE `<absent>` in a cell — RAW (the trigger: CommonMark inline raw HTML ⇒ `hasHtml` ⇒ the block raw, by design since .241, while the reading already showed the tag as text). Minimal failing `| 1 | <absent> |`, minimal passing ``| 1 | `<absent>` |``.
- **Fix (the rule):** ONE predicate doc-window-model `literalTag(src)` — a placeholder (no HTML element: `<absent>` `</sha>` `<id/>`) or an unpaired open tag (unpairedOpenTag; a `</name>` inside a code span closes nothing, `CODE_SPANS`) — asked by the reading's LITERAL_TAG AND the editor's inline tokenizer (doc-markdown `htmlInlineToken` ⇒ an `htmlLiteral` token ⇒ a text node, `HtmlLiteral`; `INLINE_START` = any `<letter`). Choice: the editor carries every tag the reading shows as text, so the r2 ruling's raw block (fixture 31's bare `STEP-<code>-nn` table) retires too, and a `/p/<id>` paragraph is a paragraph. Still raw: a paired / attributed real tag outside the marks, an HTML block, excess cells (GFM drops them).
- **The chip:** `t(RAW_KIND_WORD[kind])` + "· shown as its content · edit source" / "· cannot be shown, source below · edit" (zh 「Markdown 块 · 已按内容显示 · 点此编辑源码」 / 「… · 无法显示，给出源码 · 点此编辑」, ja likewise); the retired keys ("kept as written", "cannot be rendered", lower-case "front matter") are gone from both dictionaries.
- **The tall rows (confirmed, not a fault):** at 1400 px the R003 row is 181 px = its 168 px quote cell + padding; the code-span cell holds one 25 px line — the "tall blank" is the row's long text columns.
- **Tests:** test-doc-wheel 53/0 (the literal table 6 shapes × paragraph / item / cell / heading; the bisection (a)–(g) printed + excess-cells / attributed-tag raw controls; the minimal pair; fixture 32: native, an edit after `<absent>` saves one line; RED controls: the literal rule stubbed ⇒ (g) + fixture 32 raw, a close inside a code span counted ⇒ red); test-doc-window-width 65/0 (literalTag PURE table, reading legs, the chip pins, RED control: CODE_SPANS dropped); test-doc-window §17 (chrome, 1400 zh: native 5×10 table, no chip, both `<absent>` editable text, the tall row measured, Ⓧ after `<absent>` + Ctrl+S ⇒ that row only, the new chip words; before/after PNGs) + §12 / §13 pins moved to the new behaviour and words.

### lane pool-oat-measure — design q-035's six measurements (a long-lived token as a pool member's credential file) as variants of the creds-read measurement; a PURE reader of their fixture (no user line: a measurement + a reader nothing calls yet)
- **The question (design-pool-oat §2 A):** may a pool member whose only credential is its long-lived token hold it as a CLI-shaped `.credentials.json` (`claudeAiOauth.accessToken = <oat>`, `expiresAt` = mint + OAT_TTL, the standard scopes, NO refreshToken) and be spent like a login? scripts/measure-claude-cred-read.mjs gains six variants on member O (that file) beside member A (a login): `oat-file` (every request's bearer is the oat; no refresh; no write), `oat-env` (the same token as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, the hub's oat-only spawn today; its request heads diffed field by field against oat-file's, anthropic-beta flag by flag, plus the calls each made), `oat-file-401` (the mock 401s msg2: does the CLI rewrite, blank or delete the file? msg3 after it clears), `oat-file-near` (expiresAt +30 s: msg1 inside the refresh window, msg2 past it), `oat-file-switch` (link A → O → A, each + utimes), `oat-file-scopes` (no scopes / subscriptionType / rateLimitTier). Each prints PASS / FAIL + a note. The record holds every request head (the credential as a label), both files' sha / inode / mtime / shape before and after, and every strace write on them, one by one.
- **Fixture + reader:** `--write-fixture` (all six in one run) writes scripts/fixtures/oat-in-file.json `{cliVersion, measuredAt, script, netns, variants: {name: {verdict, note}}}`. PURE src/cli-caps.js `oatInFile(version, fixture)` is true only for the exact version the fixture names with oat-file, oat-file-401 and oat-file-switch PASS (design §5 gate 5); `OAT_VARIANTS` is the one spelling of the six (the script imports it). No fixture is committed: 主开发's namespace rung writes it, and until then oatInFile is false for every CLI. Nothing reads oatInFile yet (A's materialization is a later lane).
- **Isolation (主开发's ruling in this lane):** a lane creates no namespace or sandbox of any kind and never runs the real CLI. `--no-netns` refuses any `--claude` that is not a `#!` script or that lives under …/claude/versions/, before it runs. The lane's self-test is a FAKE claude (scripts/fixtures/oat-measure/fake-claude.mjs: good / rewrite401 / stale; it statx()es the creds file every turn and re-reads it on an mtime change, the 2.1.281-measured mechanism). The oat variants set HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY = the mock in both rungs (each CONNECT recorded and answered 403). A strace watchdog rides both rungs: the first non-loopback connect() SIGKILLs the CLI's process group and the run exits 3 (a belt; the namespace is the isolation). Tokens are built at runtime (no token-shaped literal in the tree); outputs carry labels, never bytes.
- **Gates:** test-cli-caps (fast, in-process, 41 legs, 130 ms): the two lists; the reader's truth table (RED control: 2.1.297 / 2.1.295 / 2.1.29 / 2.1.2960 / 2.1.296.1 ⇒ false); 4 patched readers, each turning its leg RED; a census (the script imports the list, writes the fixture path and holds no token literal; the reader imports nothing); `--no-netns` refusing an ELF and a script under …/claude/versions/ before either runs; the committed fixture's shape once it exists. test-oat-measure-fake (heavy — the measurement runs strace, which THE TIER RULE keeps out of fast; 9 legs, 7 s): the measurement over the fake — good ⇒ six PASS and a fixture oatInFile reads true for 9.9.9 only, the oat as a Bearer label, the file's bytes + inode kept, no token bytes in the outputs, nothing off loopback; rewrite401 ⇒ oat-file-401 FAIL with the tmp + rename named; stale ⇒ oat-file-switch FAIL. The hot-switch variants ran over the fake through the refactored spawn (baseline / symlink / hardlink-same / refresh read as 2.1.281 measured). test-claude-hot-switch (heavy, sudo) is 主开发's to run.
- **Fix (lane pool-oat-measure-fix, HOT):** 主开发's first namespace rung (claude 2.1.296, 2026-10-14 01:03Z) died at oat-file on `read ECONNRESET`, an unhandled 'error' on a Socket. Cause, by elimination and then reproduced: Node hands a CONNECT socket to the 'connect' handler without its own 'error' listener (the only server socket left bare; an Upgrade is destroyed when nobody listens), the oat variants send every proxied call there, and the CLI reset one the mock still read (after the 403 + FIN, before its own FIN). Every error path of the inner process now lands in `events` (the variant's evidence, and `· N events survived (where code ×n)` on its verdict line), never a crash: server clientError (a TLS ClientHello named `tls-hello-on-plain-port`, no request bytes kept) + error, each socket via 'connection' (CONNECT ones labelled), request / response / SSE, a throwing route (answered 500), the CLI's spawn + stdin/stdout/stderr, process uncaughtException / unhandledRejection. Two side fixes the handlers made necessary: a rejected main() exits 1 (the process handler would have swallowed it to exit 0), and a CLI that exits mid-turn ends that turn as EXITED, not a 90 s TIMEOUT. The fake gains five misbehaviours (reset, tls-hello, keepalive-drop, connect-reset = the crash's own shape, connect-rst-early). test-oat-measure-fake 9 → 17 legs, 12 s: each misbehaviour ⇒ exit 0, oat-file PASS, its event recorded; a census of the 12 handlers; RED control = a copy with them stubbed ⇒ connect-reset dies with the crash's stack (`read ECONNRESET`, no record); belt = only the process handlers kept ⇒ survives as `process uncaughtException ECONNRESET`. On the base, reset / tls-hello / keepalive-drop never crashed (Node's default clientError) but left no trace; connect-reset and connect-rst-early killed it.
