### lane doc-print-fidelity (Opus) — the Doc window's Print / Save as PDF and Export HTML render the markdown source (owner 2026-10-08 "你这个存为PDF效果很差 需要优化")
- **The shot**: Chrome's print preview of a lane brief opened in the Doc window (rel239): the H1, the numbered list and the `TESTS:` paragraph as monospace boxes cut at the right edge, scrollbar thumbs painted, "1 page". **Cause**: rel239's `exportBody` printed the EDITOR's DOM (`S.ed.getHTML()`) — every block the wheel carries as a raw block (`pre.doc-rawblock`) printed as a code box under the editor's `pre{overflow:auto;white-space:pre}`, and PRINT_CSS made nothing wrap.
- **Item 4 — why those blocks are raw**: each holds a bare `/p/<id>`. CommonMark reads `<id>` as inline raw HTML (an unknown tag); doc-markdown.js `hasHtml` carries any block holding raw HTML as written (the editor would drop the tag). NOT a gap for ordinary markdown — the em dash, quotes, parentheses, `**"…"**` and inline code all round-trip; the screen is left as is (a brief that writes `` `<id>` `` opens rich).
- **Fix** (the leaving path only): doc-window-model.js `readingHtml(src, {Marked, sanitize})` = the source as it stands (`sourceNow`, unsaved edits included) through marked (the main bundle's class — doc-window.js hands `Marked` in beside `sanitizeHtml`; the lazy entry gains no second copy) + THE one sanitizer; `placeholderHtml` (marked's html hook) keeps a bare `<word>` naming no HTML element as text (as a tag, DOMPurify stripped it with the word: the brief printed `/p/`); front matter reads as a plain block; the read article (`.doc-read`) has `white-space:normal`. `PRINT_CSS` rewritten: pre / code `pre-wrap` + `overflow-wrap:anywhere`, every box `overflow:visible` + no max-height under print, html / body / page `height:auto`, tables `width:100%` with wrapping cells and a type step by column count (`colsBand`: 5–6 → 90 %, 7–9 → 80 %, 10+ → 70 %, carried as the export wrapper's `data-cols`), img bounded, body 11 pt, code 9.5 pt, a pre never `avoid` (one longer than a page breaks), no scrollbars. printDoc prints once the frame's fonts + images decode (≤ 5 s).
- **Gates**: test-doc-window-width §5 (fast): the brief fixture (scripts/fixtures/doc-print/lane-brief.md, paths neutralised) ⇒ `<h1>` first, an `<ol>` of 4 items each with inline `<code>` + `<strong>`, no raw block, every `/p/<id>` kept; RED CONTROL = the editor's DOM exported again (ProseMirror `toDOM` specs) ⇒ raw blocks, no `<h1>`; the print sheet as text + a patched-sheet red. test-doc-window §11 (heavy, `VS_DOC_WINDOW_ONLY=print`): the brief printed through `Page.printToPDF` = 2 pages, every source line's end in the `pdftotext` text, nothing wider than the 673 px A4 page box under print media, no scroll container; 40 paragraphs + a 90-line code block + an 11-column table = 9 pages, the table at `xl`.

### lane server-memory-census (Opus — B-9428 step (c), the owner 2026-10-08 "可以" on finding what holds 2 GB): the server's resident memory is accounted for without an inspector
- THE ARITHMETIC (PURE src/memory-census.js): base = /proc/self/smaps_rollup Anonymous (RSS when there is no smaps); native = base − main heap − Σ answered workers' heap − external (main + workers), clamped ≥ 0 with the clamp said as `over`; the sum identity is pinned. Heap parts are the RESIDENT heap (v8 `total_physical_size`), not heapTotal: on a fresh scratch server heapTotal's committed-but-untouched pages pushed the parts 44 MB past the anonymous memory (native clamped to 0); heapTotal is kept beside it in every row.
- THE WORKERS (SHARED src/worker-memory.js): every worker script answers ONE `{op: 'vs-memory'}` first thing in its message loop (`answerMemory`, never queued behind a FIFO); every creator `trackWorker`s what it starts (SafeFs slot k = `<pool>#k`: safe-fs#0–3, transcript#0–1, fs-canary#0; search-index; usage-index = the production's 9). `askMemory` waits ≤ 2 s; a silent worker is UNKNOWN (counted, never 0). The creators' own handlers skip `ev: 'memory'` (usage-index: not a heartbeat).
- THE SAMPLER (src/server/memory-sampler.js, wired in server.js as `memSampler` with no net line): every 60 s, async (the smaps read is fs.promises, 0.6 ms on a small process); srv-worker-heap-mb / srv-external-mb / srv-native-mb on every 5th sample, ONE srv-mem-census event (`name used/resident/total` per worker, ≤ 900 chars) on every 10th: 912 B per 10 min with 9 workers. The first sample (at listen) logs ONE `[memory] boot census:` line. GET /api/sysinfo carries `serverMemory`; the System window draws it (this instance only) with the per-worker rows under a fold kept open across the 5 s refresh. A census, not a guard.
- MEASURED (scratch server, 50 shell sessions restored after a SIGKILL): see the lane report; the boot sample took ~12 s of wall time because the restore held the loop (the sample is async and only waited).
- Gates: new fast test-memory-census (47: the arithmetic + identity + clamp, the event bound with 300 workers, askMemory + the sampler on fake timers, 4 real SafeFs threads, a handler-less safe-fs-worker copy ⇒ unknown, the `new Worker(` census + 3 controls, the rows in en/zh/ja); test-restore-smoke gains the boot-line + every-worker-answers leg; test-architecture PURE / SHARED rows; test-channel-quote-topic names zh 工作线程 (`Workers ({n})`) as a CPU-thread meaning in NOT_CHANNELS.

### Lane daemon-orphan-end — a browser daemon (and its Xvfb) with no browser, no lease and no conversation is ended by the keeper, by identity

- **The fact (a fleet pod, 2026-10-07):** 13 `agent-browser` daemons + 7 `Xvfb -auth …/agent-browser-xauth-*` with no Chrome child, up to 2.6 d old, each from a conversation that had ended or a temporary browser recorded "stopped (idle)". The keeper ended a daemon only on Stop / Forget / a leased browser's idle ceiling.
- **The rule (PURE src/browser-orphans.js):** `daemonVerdict` ends a daemon the keeper started (its record's pid + starttime, or its env's `AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIG` = one of the keeper's `machine[-ephemeral]-<mark>.json`) after 10 min with no Chrome child, no lease, no verb / viewer, and its conversation gone or its record stopped-idle; a running conversation's stopped daemon is kept for the next verb up to 6 h idle. Its Xvfb (child, or the one whose `-auth` its env's XAUTHORITY names) goes with it. A daemon without the mark — incl. a lease session's `machine.json` daemon attached over CDP — is reported (once), never ended.
- **The keeper:** `orphanCensus` — one /proc walk (`browser-facts.daemonRows`, ≈50 ms for 944 processes) every 60 s from the tick and once at boot after adoption; SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 5 s, by pid + starttime; ONE journal line per ending; the row's note "stopped — the daemon was ended after N idle (restarts on the next command)". The tick's timer stays on while an unheld daemon waits out its grace.
- **Paired machines:** `browser-serve status` answers `daemon {pid, starttime, startedAt, chrome}`; new op `end-daemon {profileId, pid, starttime}` (only that profile's daemon, only with no Chrome), capability `browser-end-daemon` (an older agent is never asked; the row says it was reported). `lastVerbAt` is the hub's own profile stamp (the machine has none).
- **Gate:** test-browser-orphans (fast, 24: the verdict table 68 rows + 2 mutant controls, the process-table shape, the real keeper over a fixture table, the serve op + the gate); test-desktop-remote capability pin.

### fork-flag-server-side — a fork is a fork whoever asks (B-8b7b)

- **The fact (2026-10-02 20:12 PDT).** A ws `create {fork: true}` sent through the API (no client extraArgs) spawned `claude --resume <parent>` without `--fork-session`: the "fork" resumed the parent and wrote one stray turn into its JSONL (the B-4058 two-writer class). The flag came only from the client (`_doForkSession`'s extraArgs).
- **One producer.** `claudeForkArgs` (src/adapters/claude-code.js) derives `--fork-session` (+ `--resume-session-at <uuid>` from `forkAt` = `data.forkAtUuid`, id-shaped only) from the fork fact; every transport (local dtach, daemon pipe, ssh, dial) composes that argv. A copy of either flag in extraArgs is dropped with a note (a stale client: spelled once; without the fork fact: a guarded plain resume). The client sends `fork` + `forkAtUuid` only.
- **The proof.** `forkResumedParent` / `captureForkProof` (src/claude-lock-capture.js, an `onSeed` sighting inside `pickClaudeLock` — the seed is still never a pick): a pending local fork whose own CLI holds its parent's id on two consecutive sightings (~1 s apart) is a resume in disguise; ws-create's chain SIGKILLs that CLI, ends the session (`_exitAsked.by = 'fork-resumed-parent'`) and answers the creator `{type:'error', code:'fork-resumed-parent'}`.
- **Gates.** New fast test-fork-flag (25: the argv table, buildRemoteExec + spawn wiring, the one-producer literal census, the client-extraArgs adapter control RED, the proof table and the armed chain); test-fork-restore's forks are now created API-shaped (no extraArgs) and still adopt their own ids; §78 id-branch baseline lowered (session-lifecycle.js 2 → 1).
- **Not done.** No server-level leg where a stub claude resumes the parent and the parent's JSONL is compared byte for byte; a remote fork has no local lock, so the proof is local-only; the first sighting comes ~2 s after the spawn.

### pid-identity-census — a pid is never an identity (B-1cc6)

- **The fact.** This box's pid_max is 4 194 304 and its pids wrapped ≥ 3 times since the 09-17 boot; the lane's own scratch `sleep` drew pid 4 096 971. A pid recorded hours ago can name a stranger: `process.kill(pid)` kills it, `kill -0` reads a dead one (or a zombie) as alive.
- **One helper.** SHARED `src/proc-identity.js`: `identityOf` {pid, starttime, bootId} (`ps -o lstart=` with no /proc), `judge` (same / zombie / pid-recycled / gone / unknown-identity / unknown), `sameProcess`, `aliveIdentity` (null = unprovable, never alive), `signalIdentity` — the choke point, refusals said once ("a process this build cannot prove is ours — restart it to re-record"). Re-pointed: jobs.js (identical rule, moved; gained the zombie rung), browser-facts.js procStart/sameProcess (identical), agentd pidStartTime (verbatim) + `kill(sid)` behind `_childProven` (was weaker: an unverifiable child was assumed alive and signalled; a legacy meta passed on a cmdline substring).

### discovery-cursor-persist — a server restart never re-walks an account's whole listing; the discovery cursor is persisted beside the feed's (B-6638)

- **The fact (found by gmail-feed-gap):** discovery's walk state lived in memory ⇒ every restart re-listed every account (100 listing pages for a 10 000-conversation account, 0 reads) and a walk the restart cut started over from page 1.
- **PURE (src/channel-drain.js):** `listingVerdict({persisted, complete, refused, intent})` → `resume | rewalk | none`; `discoveryOf` (heal), `discoveryRecord` (write shape), `cursorRefused(err)` (the adapter's typed `detail.cursorRefused`, or `not-found` on a call that carried a cursor).
- **Engine:** `e.disc` is born from `rec.discovery` (`discFromRecord`); `discover()` writes it at every walk's end via `keepDisc` — `store.index.flush()` FIRST, then `saveAdapters()`; a refused kept cursor is caught inside the `vendor()` call ⇒ ONE walk from page 1, one journal line; `dropLive` clears it (every lifecycle verb re-lists as before).
- **Adapters:** Gmail (400 "Invalid pageToken"), Slack (`invalid_cursor`), Lark (a page_token refusal) type `cursorRefused` only on a call that carried a cursor; fake / agents list one page (nothing to resume). No vendor lacks stable page tokens.
- **Measured (test-channels-aggregate ㉓, one 10 000-row account):** restart +30 min ⇒ **0** listing pages (BEFORE: 100); a walk cut at page 40 ⇒ 60 pages after the restart, 0 unlisted; a refused cursor ⇒ 1 + 100 calls, said once. ㉒'s restart leg now asserts 0 listing pages.
- **Tests:** test-channels-aggregate ㉓ (CONTROL: the in-memory base ⇒ 100 / 100), test-channel-drain (verdict table, round-trip, heal, refusal typing), test-channel-adapter-contract (the listing cursor contract), test-channels-engine (its OWED BEFORE CURSOR crash leg went red until the index flush preceded the record write).
- **Note:** built on gmail-feed-gap (5b89a9fce, cherry-picked as this branch's first commit — drop it at replay).

### gmail-feed-gap — a gap in the change feed is ONE history walk from the saved cursor, never a whole-index pass (B-5134)

- **The fact (int226 on the .227 tree):** channel-feed-authority made Gmail's history.list the AUTHORITATIVE feed (`feed-only`: no per-row timer), but `feedState` judged it "behind" (not carrying) once its last good page was older than the fresh bound — a laptop asleep, a restart, an outage, a rate-limit park — and every row fell back to its tier: ONE whole-index pass. Reproduced here (test-channels-aggregate ㉒, the base rule as a patched copy): a 20-min clock jump over 10 000 rows ⇒ **10 000 rows due, 10 101 vendor calls in one pass** (1 feed + 10 000 reads + 100 listing pages) — the owner's number to the call.
- **PURE (src/channel-feed.js):** `gapVerdict({cursor, lastPageAt, now, coldTierSec, expired, freshBoundMs})` → `catch-up` (a cursor and a gap of any length, a boot included) | `rewalk` (expired / no cursor — the listing re-walk, as built) | `fresh`, with `overCold`; `addGap` (merged, ≤ GAPS_MAX 20) and `coverageOf` = `sample` with the declared gaps excluded (a record inside a gap is counted `excluded`, never judged a miss).
- **The carrying fact (src/channel-caps.js `feedState`):** an authoritative feed holding its cursor (`feed.carrying = {since}`, persisted on the adapter row, stamped by a good page, cleared only by a refusal) stays `carrying` through a silence (state `catching-up`, `gapSince`) and through a back-off (state `backoff`, parked by name) — `feed-only` holds, the tiers stay parked, the due index is not rebuilt. A measured (Lark) feed still reads `behind` (it has no cursor to resume). Words: "Catching up since {time} — the change feed resumes from where it stopped" / "… {vendor} asked the change feed to wait; it resumes from where it stopped at {until}" (zh / ja).
- **Engine (`historyFeed`):** the gap is judged before the call; a catch-up page returns `{due, pages, catchUp:true}` and writes ONE journal line per gap: "<account>: the change feed resumed after <n> min — <p> history pages, <m> conversations touched, 0 per-row reads"; a rate refusal logs the park once by name and keeps carrying; a refusal clears the fact. The measured feed's long-stop span (`window().gap`) is declared to the net (`f.gaps`); `feedSample` reads `coverageOf`.
- **Drain rule 21a:** a catch-up is ONE `feed` action with its pages (`pass.feed.walked`), done for the pass, its rows ahead like a page's.
- **Gmail adapter:** a history walk refused mid-way or longer than HISTORY_PAGES_PER_SYNC (20) keeps its page token (`mailbox.walk`) and the next sync RESUMES there; the cursor moves only after the walk's last page (it used to jump to the mailbox's newest id after page 20 — every change past page 20 was lost — and a refused page re-asked pages 1…n). `changes()` answers `pages`; the registry passes it (bounded).
- **Measured (test-channels-aggregate ㉒, 10 000 rows, scripted history fake, 10 changes a page):** 20-min jump ⇒ 0 due, **31 calls** (ONE walk of 3 pages + 30 named reads, 0 listing), still carrying, the since unchanged; restart +30 min on the same store ⇒ boots carrying (persisted since), the same ONE walk + 30 reads (+ discovery's boot listing, 100 pages, as before); 404 ⇒ the listing re-walk (100 pages), 0 reads, no catch-up line; rate-limit mid-walk ⇒ parked (backoff · rate-limited, carrying), 0 due / 0 reads, resumed ⇒ 30 reads.
- **Tests:** test-channel-feed ⑩ (the gap table, addGap, the net excludes a declared gap; CONTROL: a copy counting the silence as misses demotes a complete feed), test-channels-aggregate ㉒ (above; CONTROL: the base rule ⇒ 10 000 due / 10 000 reads), test-channel-caps (catching-up / park / measured / refused + words), test-channel-drain (rule 21a in the paced walk, exercised, never violated), test-channels-gmail-shape (a 429 on page 2 resumes from its token; 25 pages ⇒ none lost past page 20).

The kept facts' minute re-sum (`ROW_RESUM_MS`) is removed.

### lane search-card-open — opening an agent's search row shows what the agent found, from the memo, with 0 vendor calls (owner 2026-10-07)

REVISION (owner 22:27Z): 「缓存其实不用失效吧」 — a search over history only gains newer messages, which the saved copy receives.
- **What:** PURE `searchMemo` (src/channel-search.js): NO TTL (size / LRU only: 64 entries, 2 MiB an account); a put FANS its page's hits per conversation (`conv:<id>`, ≤ 16 a put) and under `all` when the agent's scope `covers` every conversation of the account — a derived entry carries no page token, never replaces an own answer, leaves with its origin; `memoToDisk` / `memoFromDisk`. The engine persists it per account (`<account>/search-memo.json`, 0600, atomic, read at first use; dropped by dropLive's disconnect / removal, or when the file names another identity). The card's search touch carries the search's `memo` scope; the owner's `/search/full` takes `memo` + `conv` and reads [that scope, all, conv:<id>] (an answer from anything but his own `all` has no page token; "Search again" forgets all three). The dialog shows the remembered hits in section two (Around + open conversation as before), the agent count moves into section two's head, the age line is information ("asked by the agent", minutes then the day), nothing remembered ⇒ "The agent searched {vendor} {when} — its results are not remembered here · Search again".

### lane reply-to-sent (Opus) — a Notify trigger "a reply to a message this agent sent" (owner 2026-10-07: "通知功能好像缺少'回复了这个 agent 之前发送的消息'的 trigger"; revision 21:50Z: a group = each member for its own sends, no automatic watcher) — on master fc91b7cd5 (2.369.230); its user line was headed .231 in the lane (test-changelog-style allows ≤ the next patch) and int232 folded it into .232

- **Before:** `reply-to-mine` fired only for a message IN A TOPIC under one of "mine" (the owner's or this principal's sends, one `ctx.mine` set). A quote, a Gmail thread reply, a DM's next message — the ways people actually answer — woke no agent that had sent the message.
- **The rule (src/channel-filter.js, PURE):** RULE_KINDS + `reply-to-sent` (a PLACE rule). `sentHit(record, ctx)` judges five shapes against `ctx.sentByMe` only (Map vendorId → {at, words, subject}): (a) a quote / reply naming a sent id; (b) a topic reply / (d) a Slack thread reply under a sent parent / root / threadKey; (c) a record in a MAIL thread (`convKind 'thread'`) newer than a sent mail; (e) a DIRECT chat (`dm`): the peer's message within REPLY_WINDOW_MS (24 h) after the newest send. A fixed why per shape (SENT_WHYS, `{when}` = the answered message's UTC clock, `{subject}` = the mail's) — channel-words `wakeWhyText` words each in zh / ja. `matchRecord` returns `sent: {at, words}`; `renderWakeBlock` starts that hit's line "Reply to your message (<when>, "<first words>"): from …".
- **The ctx split (channels-engine onFresh `placeCtx`):** `ownerMine` (the log's isSelf ids), `sentIds` (the index ledger `sentBy`), `sentByMe` (the outbox's SENT proposals of this drafter on this conversation, the last 30 days, ≤ 500 per drafter — SENT_WINDOW_MS / SENT_MAX), `convKind` (the index row's kind). `reply-to-mine` / `in-thread-with-me` read all three (unchanged meaning); `reply-to-sent` reads `sentByMe` only — the owner's messages are never an agent's sends.
- **A group = each member (the owner's revision):** `fanOutWatchers(eff, live, {filterOf})` fans a GROUP row whose filter carries `reply-to-sent` out to its live members — one item each, keyed `group:<gid>><cid>` (principalKey / fanOfKey / fanTargetOf / fanWatcher grew the group shape; the ledger is the stored row's `stats.fan[cid]`, as All agents'), `split:'sent'` = only the sent half (`splitFilter`; a match-every filter whole), the row's other rules (match any) stay ONE round-robin group item (`split:'rest'`). `resolveTarget` names a member item's member; `storedWatcherFor` drops a member that left the group; `rowNames` names a member item for that member alone. All agents was already per conversation (its fan-out reads each target's own sends).
- **The dialog:** the kind "is a reply to a message this agent sent" for every principal, with the note "Set this on a group to cover each of its agents for their own sends — a reply notifies only the agent whose message it answers." (zh / ja).
- **Not built (the owner's revision 21:50Z):** the automatic per-send watcher and its `channels.autoReplyWatchDays` setting — a trigger the owner sets in Notify….
- **Gates:** test-channel-filter ⑮ 23 (every shape + why, ctx split, zh/ja words, the per-member fan-out; 3 patched-copy controls RED: DM next message ignored, the owner's messages counted as sent, the group as one round-robin item) — 254/0; test-channel-agent-watch ⑨ (a real engine: group of A + B and All agents — two replies to A's ⇒ A twice, B's ⇒ B, the owner's ⇒ nobody, nothing billed; the stash line begins "Reply to your message"; CONTROL: the engine without the per-member fan-out hands a reply to the wrong member) — 58/0; test-channels-engine 789/0.

### channel-feed-authority — a mailbox is not 89 000 chat rooms (Opus; base 189aadbb0)

- **Root cause (fleet pod, 4 Gmail accounts, 88 915 threads):** every conversation carried its own poll timer by activity tier (channel-caps `cadenceFor`), and `dueList` walked every row of the account each pass to find the due ones. Gmail's adapter already asked `history.list` once per pass, but declared no change feed, so the engine never let the feed REPLACE the per-row timers: cold threads came due by the thousand, each a 40-unit `threads.get` (the 2026-10-05 quota storms).
- **OWNER'S LAW (2026-10-06, "不能'获取更新'而不是'查询每条是否有更新'吗！"):** an adapter that can say what changed has no per-row question: no per-row timer, no per-row staleness check, no per-row vendor call beyond the rows the feed named, the window the user is looking at, and the owner's press.
- **Feed authority (PURE channel-caps + channels/index.js + channel-feed.js):** `changeFeed.authority` is `authoritative` (only `via: 'history'`, Gmail) or `measured` (Lark's search, unchanged). An authoritative feed is `carrying` from its first fresh good answer (not measured; positive evidence only — never run, behind, backing off or refused carries nothing), and `laneState` answers `pollCadence: 'feed-only'`: `cadenceFor` = 0 s for every row (never due by the clock), the hot cadence for a WATCHED row. Named rows, kicks, presses and owed marks are due through the engine, as before.
- **Gmail (`changes()`):** the pass's ONE history.list (forced; the per-thread `history()` reads after it reuse the 20 s memo) → `changed`. A changed thread the engine has not named is listed from the head page of the listing's own query (so the feed never births a thread outside it); one that page does not hold is dropped (the daily re-walk is its net). Expired cursor / CHANGED_CAP overflow / first connect = the RESEED WALK: `threads.list` answers each thread's `historyId`, judged against the LOST cursor (`walkFrom`, persisted as `gmailWalkFrom`): newer ⇒ named changed, else walked. No per-thread read rides the walk; it ends only on a walk from page 1 to the last page.
- **Engine:** `feedPage` → `historyFeed` for an authoritative row (ONE `changes()`, births through `admitListed` — discovery's per-row code moved out verbatim, a reseed ⇒ `discoverSoon`, refusals through `feedRefusal`); the named rows go ahead of the plain ones (drain rule 21, the drain module untouched). Under `feed-only` the listing re-walk is daily (`FEED_ONLY_REWALK_MS`), never every cold cycle (890 pages each 15 min at 88 915 threads).
- **The due index:** `dueList` reads per account a sorted (dueAt, key) array + a Map + the owed-mark set. Each row's key is a LOWER bound (a tier only relaxes as time passes); a head the clock did not make due is re-keyed to its true instant. Re-keyed at `store.index.onTouch` (every row write), `store.stamps.set` (wrapped) and a watch start. Rebuilt in ONE O(rows) pass at boot, on a whole-map touch, when the tier settings or the lane change, or when more than an eighth of the rows are dirty. The forced pass (`all`) still walks. `dueRow` is the one rule for both paths.
- **Measured (test-channels-aggregate ㉑):** a pass = 1 feed call + 20 named reads = 21 vendor calls at 1 000, 10 000 and 90 000 rows; dueList at 90 000 rows with 20 due is under 2 ms, linear in due rows rather than total rows. Four patched-copy controls: per-row timer restored, scan restored, measured feed treated as authoritative, watched refresh removed.
- **Follow-up (not built):** Gmail PUSH (`users.watch` → Pub/Sub) is the next rung; it needs a topic in the cluster's GCP project.

### artifacts-handover — a helper's deliverable reaches the conversation the user talks to (Opus; base 1bff5f7a0)
- **Sidechains are the parent's (lane artifacts-handover, owner 2026-10-06):** MEASURED first on an invented fixture (a parent JSONL + `subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` with a Write): before this lane the parent got 0 rows live and 0 rows / 0 cards at a rebuild (the stdout consumer never read the sidechain file; a streamed sidechain record would have birthed a row WITHOUT `via`). Now a parent record that ENDS a helper — the Task's tool_result, a `<task-notification>` (background agent / workflow run; a "Run ID: wf_…" launch result is remembered) — names the helper's transcript through the new descriptor hook `helperTranscriptsOf` (src/harnesses/helper-transcripts.js; claude only, linked by `agent-<id>.meta.json`'s `toolUseId`), and the registry reads its write records through the SAME `artifactsOf`: the parent's rows with `via: {kind:'subagent', name[, wf]}`, the card at the Task result, the rebuild's deriver asks the same door (normalizers `setArtifactHelperSource`) — replay parity. A stream record stamped `parent_tool_use_id` / `isSidechain` is left to that door; op ids already folded (`session._helperArtifacts.seen`) count once. A remote conversation reads none (its sidechains are on its machine).
- **Hand-over across conversations:** `vibespace-msg send <agent|group> "…" --artifact <path|/p/id>…` (≤ 20; the CLI appends the list to the text) — the route prechecks BEFORE posting (the bound, the helper's OWN rows via `AF.rowFor`, a group needs an @/--at receiver), posts, then `artifact-registry.handover` gives each receiver (reach = the groups engine's `resolveTarget` over msg-acl, required) a row with `via: {kind:'handover', from}` (a REG op: never a write), its card ("Handed over by …" / 移交自), and marks the helper's row `handedTo`. Files are never copied: another machine ⇒ refused by name. A design re-registers in designs.json under the RECEIVER (`via` on the registry row; the Design home says "via <helper>") and its window opens there; the helper's own `open` later keeps it with the receiver. `vibespace-design open <dir> --for <conversation>` = the same door.
- Tests: new fast suite test-artifacts-handover (36: sidechain live + rebuild parity, background + workflow agents, the hand-over over the REAL registry + msg-acl, 4 patched-copy controls); peer-text census rows for the hand-over print lines.

### mirror-green-222 — the 2.369.222 Actions mirror's fast red (test-browser-passkey ④, run 37419676410): the dialog watch said ready before the passkey hook was armed

- **The red:** ④ "the dialog watch over a fake CDP socket", right after the arm leg: `no ceremony ⇒ none`, `start ⇒ pending`, `after 3 s ⇒ passkey_open` (`{"state":"unknown"}`), the routes' fact, the verb in flight (`null`) — 59 passed, 5 failed; 64 / 0 here on c34711faa.
- **Cause (measured):** `arm()` resolved on the watch's ready (Page.enable answered on every tab) while the hook's three calls were in flight — `armPasskey` was fire-and-forget, `pk.armed` set on Runtime.enable's ANSWER; the suite waited until Runtime.enable was SENT (5 ms ticks). An event loop ≥ 5 ms late fires that tick in the same timers pass as the reply that sent it ⇒ asked before the answer ⇒ `unknown`. Not the clock (no Date.now on the path), not the keeper fake (`unknown` ⇔ answer not delivered, 233 / 233). The UNMODIFIED suite: a 2 ms / 1 ms event-loop stall preload 8 / 20 red, `taskset -c 0-3` + 8 burners 3 / 30, each the runner's 59 / 5 shape; idle 0 / 20, 3 burners 0 / 30. The MODULE_TYPELESS warning prints here too (② imports i18n-zh.js) — unrelated.
- **Fix (browser-dialogs):** the open step awaits each enabled tab's arming (`armPasskey` hands back its promise as `pk.arming`; the body is `armHook`) before `ready()` — `arm()` resolves after the hook is armed, still within its budget; readySeen / prune untouched.
- **Tests:** test-browser-passkey ④ reads at once after `arm` (the Runtime.enable-sent loop gone) + ⑤ CONTROL: a copy ready before the hook's last answer ⇒ `unknown` right after arm (every run). Fixed: stall 0 / 20, 8 burners 0 / 30, idle 0 / 10; the new suite on the base product: the arm leg + the runner's 5 legs red every run.

Engine: `budgetDecl().limit` = the learned ceiling (the setting = its cap), `paceDecl` scales `perSec` by the same ratio, `failPass` steps 'refused' (burstStart = rateStrikes === 1) inside the record write it already made, a good pass steps 'quiet-minute'; state persisted as `rec.budgetLearned` in adapters.json (never the index). ### lane brand-marks — the Lark and Gmail monochrome marks redrawn by COLOUR ANALYSIS, verified by measurement (owner: "多色转单色 logo 要注意不同颜色的对比度")

- **The rule:** a multi-colour mark goes monochrome by keeping every boundary between strongly contrasting colours (ΔL* ≥ 20 or a hue jump ≥ 60° on ≥ 25 % of its length) as a NEGATIVE GAP; similar colours merge. `scripts/measure-brand-marks.mjs` (official marks by path, never committed) prints the boundary table and the proof; `scripts/test-brand-marks.mjs` (fast) pins the SVG contract and the gaps on the path data.
- **Lark** (official app icon, 3 colours): wing #00d6b9 ↔ head #133c9a HIGH (ΔL* 48, hue 116°), body #3370ff ↔ head HIGH (ΔL* 23) ⇒ three facets with two 1.3-unit gaps. **Gmail** (Google's current 192px.svg): flap ↔ left leg red-on-red low (merged), flap ↔ right leg red/yellow on green HIGH (hue 66°) ⇒ one uniform-stroke M (4.75 stroke, round caps) with a 1.4-unit gap under the flap on the right only.
- **Measured** (48 px dilated-edge IoU new / old, ≥ 0.6): Lark 0.78 / 0.60 and 0.76 / 0.31, Gmail 0.68 / 0.38; every gap is background at 14 px and the badge's 10 px in ≥ 1 of DPR 1 / 2. Slack unchanged (already the official mono shape).

### lane chat-enter-ime-r2 (Opus) — the Enter that commits an English word in a Chinese IME sent the message (inc-muukd9oq-qyc3, the owner's correction)

- **The correction** (the owner): "其实是中文输入法用回车上英文词的时候触发的 bug，而不是切换中英文". The ring re-read: Enter :09.651 and :10.802 composing (no `chat-input` frame), Shift :11.860, Enter :12.243 → `chat-input` at :12.244. The commit is the :12.243 Enter itself — Chrome 152/macOS delivered the commit's Enter as a PLAIN keydown (keyCode 13, isComposing false); the Shift was a capital letter inside the composition (the 2.369.207 recorder's one-per-3-s typing marker hides the letters after it), not its end. r1's 383 ms was Shift→Enter, not commit→send: the committing Enter follows compositionend within a millisecond or two, in either order.
- **The fix:** `EnterGuard` drops r1's exemption (`keydown` / `_lastKeyEnter`, the Safari 229 disarm, `isEnterKey`): EVERY compositionend arms `_imeEndedAt`; a plain Enter within `IME_COMMIT_BURST_MS` 50 ms ⇒ `'ime-swallow'` — ChatInput preventDefaults it (no newline, no send) and shows "Input method just ended — press Enter again to send" once; the next Enter sends. Cmd/Ctrl+Enter, Shift+Enter, `chat.enterSends` off and touch unchanged. The window is 50 ms, not r1's 600 (主开发's acceptance call): the commit's Enter lands 0–1 ms after the end, in the same event burst, while a human's two presses — Space commits, Enter sends, every Chinese sentence, often < 600 ms — are ≥ 80–100 ms apart; 600 ms would have swallowed a real send once per message, 50 ms never does.
- **Forensics:** the `k:'ime'` end marker carries `how: 'commit' | 'cancel'` (compositionend `data` non-empty / empty — the length only, never the text).
- **Gates:** test-chat-enter-ime (fast 58/58 — the owner's table: Enter(229) → compositionend → Enter(13) +1 ms ⇒ swallow; commit → +1/+30 ms ⇒ swallow, +120/+300/+700 ms ⇒ send; Space → Enter at 120/250 ms ⇒ send; Cmd+Enter ⇒ send; Safari order ⇒ no send, one hint; patched copies: r1's exemption restored ⇒ the owner's sequence SENDS, 600 ms back ⇒ Space → Enter swallowed) · test-chat-enter-ime-chrome (heavy 14/14 — the measured compositionend → keydown gap asserted < 50 ms; CDP imeSetComposition → a 229 Enter → insertText → a plain Enter 20 ms later ⇒ no send, no newline, the line; 150 ms ⇒ sent; mutant bundles r1-restored / window-removed ⇒ SENDS).

### lane split-restore-hidden — a side-by-side group on a desktop not shown since the reload comes back side by side (userW inc-muundq37-cjay)

- **Cause (reproduced in chrome first, the owner's steps):** split on B, A→B (still split), reload on A, B ⇒ two plain windows, and ~2.5 s later the autosave wrote B's record without the chain. desktop-manager `_replayMissing` (a desktop's first visit) replayed the openSpecs but never the record's chains; it failed for a files+files pair exactly like for browser-live. The boot / remote doors' 5–8 s deadline on a 200 ms timer grouped what was there (a split without its pair ⇒ tabs).
- **Fix:** one queue for all three doors (`_queueChain` / `queueRecordChains`); WindowManager.createWindow → `layoutManager.onWindowCreated` settles it (no timer, no deadline); chain-layout `restoreVerdict` (PURE) rebuilds the chain whole; `pendingChainOf` keeps the record's chain in every capture until then; `dropUnbuiltMembers` (from `recordFor`) shrinks it only when the record drops a member.
- **Pins moved:** test-window-binding-model's two pins on the old deadline / `restoreTabChain(present, …)` now pin the new verdict and the three doors. New: test-chain-layout ⑯ (7 rows).
- **Heavy leg (lane split-restore-leg):** the owner's steps are now a CI suite, test-split-restore-hidden (headless chrome over a worktree server). It covers files+files, a file viewer guest, a browser-live guest, a second client on B throughout the reload, and a guest that lands 3 s late. Each must come back side by side at the record's ratio, and the record must still hold the split 9 s later and after A→B again. Control: a patched desktop-manager.js copy without the `queueRecordChains` call ⇒ red, record flat.

### lane slack-landing-nologin — the Slack consent landing needs no VibeSpace login (userW)

- **Incident:** a fleet user on a Clerk-SSO pod pressed Allow on the cluster-preset Slack app in ANOTHER browser profile (their Slack identity lives apart from their SSO login); `src/auth.js middleware()` answered the cookie-less GET `/api/channels/oauth/cb/slack?code&state` with `302 /login` and the code was lost — design 018 assumed one browser profile.
- **Fix:** the ONE gate exempts exactly `GET /api/channels/oauth/cb/<kind>` (regex over the path, GET only); the route gets a per-address door limit (`landingAllowed`: fixed one-minute window, ≤ 30, bounded at 1000 addresses, 429 with `landingHtml({why:'too-many'})` before the state is judged); `LANDING.ok` (en/zh/ja) says "Done here — go back to the VibeSpace window where you pressed Connect", no sign-in words; the consent block's finish line names `st.user` (`connectedLine` in src/lib/mounts-dialog.js; the Duplicate dialog's `finishText` is a function of the identity, its watcher answers `row.auth.user`); a `public` flow's paste-back hint no longer promises a 127.0.0.1 address (`publicPasteHint`, per flow from `start`).
- **Gate:** scripts/test-slack-landing-nologin.mjs (fast, ~270 ms): a real `Auth` + the real channels router over express, password AND a stubbed Clerk — the no-cookie landing lands; `POST /oauth/callback`, `GET /oauth/status`, a POST to the landing path, `/oauth/cb`, `/oauth/cbx/slack`, `/oauth/cb/slack/extra` stay 401 / `302 /login`; forged / expired / used refused by name without a cookie; the 31st landing 429 with the engine stub asked 30 times; a DOM-free `connectedLine` render (en + the zh/ja tables); controls via scripts/mutant-copy.mjs — exemption removed ⇒ `302 /login`, limit removed ⇒ the 31st judged.
- **Verify r1 (adversarial, credential class):** the exemption's edge holds (trailing slash, `..`, `%2e%2e`, case, `//`, `sl%2fack`, HEAD / OPTIONS, a fragment: the landing or 302 / 401, never another handler — `p` is `req.path`, the gate is mounted once at the root); replay / 10 concurrent landings = ONE `oauth.v2.access`; a stolen state on a NEW account's flow ends it as the lander (the owner's dialog names them before Create & connect — no record without the owner's tab); both re-authorize doors (the record's own flow and the switched-client rebind) refuse another identity, token untouched. **MED fixed:** the now cookie-free page printed a refused re-authorize's sentence — the account's label and its HELD Slack identity — to whoever held the state; `oauthLanding` answers fixed words for an existing account's flow (the owner's window keeps the sentence). **LOW fixed:** a clock stepped back kept an address at 429 until it caught up (`t < h.at` opens a new window); the 429 page said "start again" — its own en / zh / ja words now say wait + reload. Behind an ingress every landing shares one `remoteAddress` (no `trust proxy` anywhere; X-Forwarded-For deliberately unread): 30 / min is the pod's one user, and a stranger flooding it only delays that user's landing (the paste-back stays open).

### lane mount-cache-scan (on 7fceb8a7)

- **mount-cache-scan: a mount still rebuilding its cache is STARTING — not failed, not writable** (lane mount-cache-scan, the owner's OneDrive, 2026-10-04): rclone `--vfs-cache-mode full` rebuilt its VFS cache index (164 788 cached files) for 4.5 min before mounting (spawned 16:52:33, first mount attempt 16:57:09); `_waitMounted(m, 5000)` called it failed, `unblockPath` freed the bare mount point, an outside writer dropped `WestcliffCourses/AIWorkspace/.restore` into it at 16:52:59 and rclone died `is not empty`. The three 16:52 "stale daemon … at mount time — killing it" lines were Connect clicks killing the scan before them. The 15:09:43 / 16:41:43 "daemon survived lazy unmount" lines came from `_healthSweep`'s hung branch (both on the 60 s watchdog's :43 phase; that branch logs nothing before the kill): a mounted OneDrive whose `ls` took over 6 s while its daemon was busy was lazily unmounted, then killed.
  **Build (src/mounts.js):** a live daemon with no fuse mount is `starting` (`_starting`; the `list()` row's `starting: {since, files, capped, maxMin}`). `_waitMounted(m, pid)` waits while the pid lives: `hung` = no utime+stime progress (≥ 30 ticks) for 60 s, `ceiling` = 15 min (≈ 3× the measured scan), both SIGKILL; the path stays blocked (`blockPath(mp, ceiling + 60 s)`) and shadowed until the mount exists. A connect while starting JOINS (`mount()` hands back the in-flight promise; `_mountInner` answers `'starting'`; a daemon found on the mount point with no mount — a restart mid-scan — is ADOPTED, never killed). A mount within 5 s answers the caller as before; past that the route answers `{success: true, starting: true}`. rclone dying "is not empty" → the connect-time stranded move (`<mp>.stranded-<ts>/`) + ONE retry; every connect-time stranded move is said on the row (`stranded`) beside the existing level-2 server-notice. NOT DONE: a For you item — the wiring file is the census's `browser` producer (test-user-todos-layout ⑪, exact site count) and test-record-clear-census must classify the new receiver; it needs its own producer row (proposed follow-up). The sweep skips a starting record, and its hung branch keeps a daemon that made CPU progress during the 6 s probe connected (path blocked 65 s, "storage busy" on the row); an idle daemon whose listing hangs is still torn down. The cache count is a child `find -printf .` stopped at 200 000 (never a walk on the event loop). UI (sidebar-mounts.js): the row says "Starting — rebuilding its cache index (N files), <elapsed> so far …" (keyed `mount-start:<id>`, elapsed patched in place every second); no Connect button or row click while starting.
  **Tests:** new suite test-mount-starting (24 checks, 14.9 s — a heavy "slow —" row at int213: over the fast tier's 10 s rule): a fake rclone (bash re-exec'd with argv[0] = …/rclone, as the /proc scan needs) drives the real MountManager through ① the starting row + count + blocked/shadowed path, ② a joined connect, ③ adoption by a restarted manager, ④ sweeps that never touch a starting or CPU-busy daemon (an idle one still goes), ⑤ a hung daemon killed, ⑥ "not empty" → stranded + one retry, said on the row; ⑦ patched-copy controls via mutantCopies: the 5 s verdict restored ⇒ the scanning daemon is killed (red); unblock before mount ⇒ the path is writable (red).
  **Gates:** npm run build green (i18n); every suite naming src/mounts.js / machine-mounts.js / mounts-plugins-wiring.js / sidebar-mounts.js (57) + test-mount-starting 24 + test-user-todos-layout 242 green, except test-auto-graduate (its `agentdDeps.publicUrl` pin is red identically at base 7fceb8a7 — pre-existing) and test-host-mounts / -tunnel (manual: need a hostId); test-architecture 514, test-changelog-style 40, test-record-clear-census 238, test-exit-forensics 343 (its kill census: mounts.js 5 → 7 declared calls).
  **User line (for the integrator, Fixed):** en "A storage connection that is still rebuilding its cache (minutes for a large OneDrive) now shows Starting with its file count and mounts when ready, instead of failing and getting stuck as “not empty”." · zh "仍在重建缓存的存储连接（大的 OneDrive 要几分钟）现在显示“启动中”和文件数，就绪后自动挂载，不再报失败、也不再卡在“目录非空”。" · ja "キャッシュを再構築中のストレージ接続（大きな OneDrive では数分）は「起動中」とファイル数を表示し、準備ができると自動でマウントされます。失敗扱いや「空でない」で止まることはなくなりました。"

### lane chat-enter-ime (Opus) — an Enter meant for the input method sent the message (inc-muukd9oq-qyc3)

- **The incident** (the owner, Chrome 152 / macOS / a Chinese IME): two composing Enters swallowed, a Shift tap, Enter 383 ms later ⇒ sent mid-turn. Reading: the Shift tap ended the composition (a Chinese IME commits on Shift), so the Enter was plain; the recorder had no `shiftKey` / `isComposing` to prove it.
- **Forensics first:** the action ring's key record carries `S-` (Shift) and `c:1` (the IME owned the key), and `k:'ime'` `ph:start|end` markers for a textarea's compositions (no text) — `actionKeyWords` / `imeMarker` in the new PURE `src/lib/chat-enter-keys.js`.
- **The narrow guard:** `EnterGuard` — a compositionend whose last keydown was not the physical Enter (key, or code Enter/NumpadEnter: Chrome/Windows reports 'Process') arms `_imeEndedAt`; a plain Enter within 600 ms inserts the newline and shows "Input method just ended — press Enter again to send" for 2 s (zh/ja); once — the next Enter sends. Safari's compositionend-before-keydown order disarms on the 229 Enter. **Why 600 ms:** the incident's gap was 383 ms; a fast typist's Space-select → Enter lands at ~150–300 ms and loses nothing (the newline stays, the line explains, Enter again sends); a deliberate commit-then-send reads the committed text first, well past 600 ms (the 700 ms row sends).
- **The setting:** `chat.enterSends` (desktop, default on = today) — off ⇒ Enter newline, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends; `composerSendModes(caps, {enterSends})` adds a send segment (or names the key in the queue segment) so the mid-turn line says which key sends. Touch keeps `chat.touchEnterSends`. docs/settings.md regenerated.
- **Gates:** test-chat-enter-ime (fast, PURE — the sequence table incl. Chrome/Windows/Safari commit orders, the recorder words, 6 patched-copy controls: the window removed ⇒ the incident SENDS); test-chat-enter-ime-chrome (heavy — CDP `Input.imeSetComposition` → Shift keydown → `Input.insertText` → Enter on a real ChatInput: no send, newline, the line; 2 s later hidden; Enter ⇒ sent; 700 ms ⇒ sent; enterSends off; the mutant bundle ⇒ sends).

### lane update-reload-ready (Opus) — B-0ece: after ⚙ → Update the page sat on the loading screen

- **The hang, traced:** the splash waits on `app.ready` = 1.5 s, then `layoutManager.loadAutoSave()` → `GET /api/layouts`, then `restoreState` → `GET /api/active` → `GET /api/sessions` (+ the stopped-session scan's two), all awaited with NO timeout. The update dialog reloaded the moment the new server answered `/api/version` (listening ≠ ready): a cold `/api/sessions` sweep (ps/pgrep per session — 44 here, under 5.5 s loop stalls) sharing Chrome's six sockets with a 77.5 MB `/api/channels` left one of them unanswered and `app.ready` pending for good.
- **Server — the boot phase** (`src/server/boot-phase.js`, wired in server.js): `booting` until the listen callback ran, `restore` (restoreSessions) and `sessions-index` (the FIRST sessions sweep, now run at boot via `routes/sessions.js warmSessions()` and shared with any request in flight) are done → `ready`. `GET /api/boot` (no-store, no network) = `{phase, waitingOn, stuck, sessions, readyAt}`; `/api/version` carries `phase`. A step not done after 90 s turns the phase `ready` anyway with `stuck` + ONE `boot-stuck` telemetry event naming the steps. `VIBESPACE_TEST_BOOT_HOLD_MS` (TEST ONLY) adds a `test-hold` step. Channels are NOT a step: nothing on the first-paint path asks for them.
- **Client — the boot ladder** (`src/lib/boot-ladder.js` PURE, `src/lib/boot-splash.js` DOM): `app.ready` first waits for `ready` (the splash line "VibeSpace is starting… (N sessions reconnected)"), then the first-paint requests ride `layout._bootJson` — 10 s stall bound per try, retries 1 → 2 → 5 → 10 s with a countdown line, then the reason in words + Reload now, one `boot-stuck` client event naming the request; a request that gave up never resolves (restoring from nothing would let the first autosave overwrite the saved layout). The update dialog's reload and the stale-tab reload (`_checkBundleFreshness`, its once-per-version key set only after the wait) both go through `waitServerReady` (404 = an older server = ready).
- **Gates:** test-boot-phase (fast, PURE + wiring + 4 patched-copy controls) · test-boot-reload-ready (heavy, chrome: a page opened mid-boot loads by itself after ready; the update reload across a REAL restart onto a slow-booting server lands after ready; a never-answering `/api/layouts` climbs the ladder into the button + a server-side boot-stuck event; a pre-fix bundle rebuilt in the scratch worktree turns ① and ② red).

### app-system-l1 — App persistence Layer 1: the app system on the PVC (B-5b73, Opus; base 6fb5b43d)

### app-system-harden — Layer 1 root paths made defensively robust, with tests (Opus; base 18000665)

- **Owner's choice (2026-10-04):** the Layer 1 code does what the design says even when files inside the app system or under HOME are not what the code expects; one structural guard per item, a test that shows the guarded case, a patched-copy control per test.
- **Helper:** `#!/bin/bash -p` + an `env -i` re-exec (same pid) before any external command — root code runs on a fixed PATH with LC_ALL=C, the allowlist reaches the app only as VS_KEEP_<name>, `--root` gets a fixed env; `inside` walks every bind target / root write level by level (a link refused by name, parents root's, mkdir one level at a time); passwd/group must be regular files; the lock is the userland's etc directory (no lock file).
- **SYS_SCRIPT:** `rdir` / `put` (dir canonical + root's via `cd` + `pwd -P`, then a relative install + `mv -T`), `stage` (user-side sources + keys copied O_NOFOLLOW into root's $T from a held cwd), `cpin` for Rebase copies, `rmchild` the only recursive removal (expected child of the canonical sysroot, root's real dir, `--one-file-system`). INSTALL_SCRIPT checks root's private copies against `HELPER_SHA256` / `SUDOERS_SHA256` before visudo / install (the pod's checkout is on the PVC).
- **Machine half:** `inRoot` + O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK fd reads for identity / entries / .desktop / sys icons; `existsIn` resolves Exec targets inside the rootfs the way the chroot will; `verifyRow` re-checks a sys row's shim at every catalog read (exact `shimText(target)` bytes, this user's, not group/other-writable) → `shim-not-ours` + one log line, and desktop-serve refuses to launch a blocked sys row; the gate is shut under systemd (`INVOCATION_ID`). `planDigest` binds `sysDigestPart` (layer + SYS_SCRIPT argv minus the nonce); a plan whose layer and argv disagree has no digest and installPackage refuses it.
- **r2 (the residual closed, coordinator's ask):** the drop-in carries `#<uid> ALL=(root) NOPASSWD:NOSETENV: <helper>` (INSTALL_SCRIPT writes the server user's uid for `#VS_UID`, visudo-checks, then requires that line); the file is now `/etc/sudoers.d/~vibespace-sysroot` so it is read after boot-root.sh's user-named drop-in (the last match wins; the user's ALL rule implies SETENV). sudo now refuses LD_PRELOAD / BASH_ENV / PATH… on the command line for the helper; ENV_KEEP (= what a command line may set) is pinned free of loader / shell / PATH knobs. Container proof with the user's drop-in named `zz-node` (sorts after `vibespace-sysroot`) + a control drop-in without the line. After r2: test-app-system 115/115, test-app-system-enter 45/45 in 81 s, build + the brief's gates green.
- **Gates:** test-app-system 112/112 (§5 census rules envClean / inside + staged / put / removal / digest, §6 controls, §8 in-process items 4 · 6 · 7 · 8 with controls); test-app-system-enter 44/44 in 81 s (the 7 hardening legs, each with its patched-copy control, in the disposable container; the first run hung silently — a walk that refused Debian's /etc/localtime link cascaded; found with a streamed container run); the census pins it touches stay green.

### lane exit-runs-dialog-fit (Opus) — the machine's Commands list fits its own width (the owner: 「这个界面展示不全」)

- **Cause:** `.exit-runs-body { min-width: min(640px, 92vw) }` inside the base `.dialog` (a fixed 440 px, `overflow: hidden`): on any viewport over 768 px the body was 640 wide in a 440 dialog — the intro line, every row's head, the decoded script and every stdout line ran 200 px past the dialog's right edge and were clipped (the pres wrapped, at 640). The summary is a grid — time · who (`fit-content(14em)`) · ONE `minmax(0, 1fr)` column holding the head (two-line clamp; the whole command is the open row's body) over an outcome line (verdict · duration). Below 560 px (a container query on `.exit-runs-list`) time + who share a line, the command goes under. Script / stdout / stderr pres carry the chat's `chat-pre-wrapped` (the class the chat's machine cards draw their command with) and the chat's Wrap toggle (`chat-wrap-toggle`, 换行 / 不换行): off = `white-space: pre`, the pre scrolls sideways inside itself. ### job-publish-stable — a published service keeps its public URL across restarts, and the CLI prints it (Opus)

- **The incident (2026-10-04 04:43Z, before a demo):** a `--keep-up --port 8766 --publish` service's public URL answered 404 after a reboot + stop/start while 127.0.0.1:8766 answered 200 — the frpc proxy had become `type = "tcp"`, `publicSub` null. Two causes: `_ensurePublish` called `pf.publish` the instant the job spawned, `frpPublish` PROBED the not-yet-listening port, and `probeProto` read a refused connection as `tcp`; then the adopt line `rec.publicSub = r.subdomain || null` threw the name away (and the job stop path's `unforward` deleted the record outright).
- **Sticky name (src/port-forward.js):** `_adoptPublish` keeps `publicSub`/`publicPort` across mode changes; only an explicit `unpublish(id)` clears them; job stop/park = `unpublish`/`unforward(id, {keepName:true})` → `port-forwards.json` `names[id]`, restored by `forward()`.
- **No probe race:** `plugins.probeProto` throws `EUNREACHABLE` when no pass connected; `_decideProto` = override › fresh probe › LAST protocol (else http) + `protoPending`; `reprobe(id)` (heal sweep + the job's `_publishRecheck`) republishes under the same name when the answer differs. Jobs wait ≤ 60 s for the port before publishing. One log line per decision.
- **Said, never silent:** `lastPublicUrl` on the job; a different URL (or a failed publish of a job that had one) = one owner notice through `_notifyOwner`. CLI `show`/`poll` print `public URL:` (publishing… / the failure / the URL the next start brings back), `list` appends `↗ <url>`; manual §6 "How to find the URL".
- **Tests:** test-port-forward +20 (restart keeps the subdomain, late listener → http same name, undecided keeps the last protocol, TCP→http repair, explicit unpublish clears, keepName stop/start; controls: pre-fix adopt line loses the name, pre-fix probe publishes `tcp://`); test-jobs-engine §11 +14 (late-listening real service via the real PortForwardManager + fake frp, CLI show/list/poll against a stand-in API, stop/start same URL, change notice once; control: no wait ⇒ the publish runs on a silent port). test-peer-text-census: 8 judge rows for the new `public URL:` prints (all VibeSpace-minted: the relay URL, flags, an enum, ports, the publish error sentence) — red without them (38 ✗, the walk names each).
- **User line (for the integrator):** en "A published Background Work service keeps its public URL across restarts, and `vibespace-job show` prints it" · zh "已发布的后台服务重启后公网链接保持不变，`vibespace-job show` 会显示该链接" · ja "公開中のバックグラウンドサービスは再起動しても公開URLが変わらず、`vibespace-job show` で表示されます"

### lane win-run-codepage (Opus): a Windows device's `run` output arrives as readable text, not GBK mojibake

- **The case (2026-10-04):** on the owner's Chinese Windows box `vibespace-exit run WIN-DESK1 -- 'dir … 2>nul'` and PowerShell errors came back as mojibake — cmd.exe and console programs write in the console's OEM code page (936 = GBK) and agentd `run-cmd` returned `String(stdout)` (UTF-8). The stored heads, the card and the Commands list kept it.
- **The fix (device side):** PURE `XS.decodeRunOutput` in src/exit-shell.js — each stream judged alone: valid UTF-8 stays UTF-8, else the code page `chcp` names (registry OEMCP next; asked once per daemon, cached) → gbk / shift_jis / euc-kr / big5 / windows-1252 / utf-8, else latin1; decoded BEFORE the 1 MiB / 64 KiB cut (a stream cut by maxBuffer or a kill drops its torn last character); `cmd-result.encoding` names it, `utf-8-fallback` when this node lacks the label. POSIX unchanged (no `encoding` key, `String()` byte for byte).
- **Full ICU:** the Windows installer provisions node from nodejs.org/dist (official builds are full-icu since Node 13; an existing `Program Files\nodejs` is the same build); a small-ICU node falls back by name.
- **Found on the way:** GBK 系统 (cf b5 cd b3) and 路 (c2 b7) are VALID UTF-8 on their own — the judge must read the whole stream, and a fixture for it must not be one of them; a UTF-8 stream torn by maxBuffer must not be mis-judged as GBK (stream-mode decode).
- **Tests:** test-exit-run §9 — byte fixtures (GBK, Shift-JIS, UTF-8, chcp in zh / ja / en, reg's OEMCP line), the whole-stream judge, an invalid sequence, the cut, a no-ICU stand-in; a REAL daemon from this tree's bundle made a fake Windows box (`dir-missing` → 系统找不到指定的路径。 encoding gbk; UTF-8 stays; 2.2 MB of GBK past maxBuffer cut clean at 1 MiB; chcp asked once for three runs); POSIX byte-identical; controls (w1) a String() decoder (7 rows red), (w2) a daemon keeping String(stdout) (the production mojibake).

### lane win-upgrade-pipe (Opus, base b5eb3d29) — a Windows device's self-upgrade must not kill its agent

- **Incident (owner's Windows box, 2026-10-04 01:38Z):** `upgrade to 2.369.205 landed — re-exec` → `vibespace-device 2.369.205 starting` → `server error: listen EADDRINUSE … \\.\pipe\vibespace-agentd-ecce10a7eeb5`, then nothing until the owner reran the install command at 01:57Z. The re-exec unlinked SOCK, spawned the successor and exited; on Windows SOCK is a NAMED PIPE — no unlink frees it, it stays bound while any pipe handle of the old process is open. The successor reached `listen` first and its error handler exited; then the old one exited; no agent. The hub logged "upgrading (attempt 1/3)" and nothing spoke (`stuck` needs a device that answers).
- **Fix ① (src/agentd/reexec.js `handOver`, wired in agentd.js beginUpgrade):** the old daemon closes its listener, THEN unlinks the lock + spawns the successor + exits — bounded at 1.5 s (a lingering local connection keeps a Windows pipe bound until the process exits; the line says so and spawns anyway). Every platform.
- **Fix ② (`listenWithRetry`, agentd.js serve):** EADDRINUSE is retried every 250 ms for ≤ 15 s while the lock file names this pid (one line when it starts, one when it listens or gives up); any other error / a lock not ours ⇒ the old `server error` exit. This is what saves the .205 → .206 hop: the OLD (.205) code runs that re-exec and still spawns before it lets go.
- **Fix ③ (src/server/device-upgrade-watch.js `begun` / `answered` / `sweep`):** client.js reports every upgrade start (`onUpgradeBegin`) and every hello (`onAnswer`) through the same door (dial-pairing.js, hosts.js ssh); a device silent `GONE_AFTER_MS` = 5 min after its upgrade began gets ONE high For-you item per (machine, version) — "<machine> stopped answering after its upgrade to <v> began — rerun its install command (Remote → <machine> → Pairing command)" — retracted (`system`) when it dials in. The deadline is persisted (`gone` in data/device-upgrades.json): a hub restart inside the window still fires. 30 s unref'd tick.
- **Tests:** test-agentd-reexec-argv (e) — a win32 named-pipe model on a fake clock over THE functions: CAUSE (pre-fix shape dies EADDRINUSE), ① free at the spawn, ② the .205-code hop listens after retries, ①+② a lingering connection, the lock-not-ours refusal (no retry), the 15 s bound, a REAL net.Server re-listen after EADDRINUSE, wiring + bundle census, 3 patched-copy controls (no close / no retry / no lock gate). test-agentd-dial: a REAL POSIX re-exec through the real dial gate (old closes, then the successor starts and listens; door events answered → begun → answered → matched; a third daemon exits 3 "already running"). test-device-upgrade-watch GONE-1..10 + 3 controls (no retract / no (machine, version) rule / the pre-fix door without `begun`).
- **Not done (listed):** item 4 — `run` output on a Chinese Windows arrives as mojibake (console code page 936); decoding stdout/stderr with the console's code page on win32 (TextDecoder gbk / shift_jis, UTF-8 first when valid) is a follow-up.

### lane channels-badges (Opus, base 9d448a44) — what an avatar's corner badge means, VibeSpace's own badge, folding VibeSpace's own talk (the owner, 2026-10-03)

The owner: 「虽然需关注部分的头像有了角标，但这个角标的含义不明确，至少应该在账号下面把图标对应上吧。其次对于vibespace自己的内部沟通也应该提供角标，就用vibespace图标就行。再其次提供一个选项可以把vibespace内部沟通收缩起来」.

- **One badge per account, used everywhere.** The 账号 card's icon is now the SAME element its conversations wear at the avatar's corner — channel-chrome.js `accountBadge` over the build's ONE `accountBadges(adapters)` map (same glyph, same hue); the old kind tile (`kindGlyph`: a chat / mail glyph on a per-KIND hue, which is why three Gmail cards looked alike and unlike their rows' badges) is retired. A badge's hover title names the account (`accountTitle`, "Office · ada@example.com" — `accountName`'s first rung now asks it, one spelling).
- **VibeSpace's own talk wears VibeSpace's mark.** Agent groups, agent private chats (pairs) and the built-in agents source get `INTERNAL_BADGE` (icons.js `vibespace` = the favicon's three stacked windows in currentColor, on a teal mixed from `--cyan` / `--green`; `data-vs`). A Lark / Gmail conversation handed to an agent ("→ VibeSpace 主开发") keeps its account's badge: it is a person's conversation.
- **The fold.** PURE `internalBlock` (src/channel-focus.js): a list's internal rows stand as ONE block under a head "VibeSpace internal (N)" at the place of its newest row; folded, the head alone, with the block's unread and @-you counts. A row that @-mentions the owner (`atYou`) or awaits the owner (the awaiting / unknown tags) keeps its own row, on top. The fold is `channelsPanelFolds.internal` (a new PANEL_PARTS entry: user state, the existing PATCH + `user-state-updated` broadcast ⇒ every client). **Default UNFOLDED — the owner's call** (he chose FOLDED: lane channels-fold below). Under a query nothing folds. Unfolded, the internal rows now sit together under their head (they were interleaved by activity).
- **Gap, said plainly:** the group model refuses an @ of the owner today (`unknown-mention`) and statusTag gives an agent group no tag, so no internal row can need the owner yet; the never-fold rule is in place (PURE rows + a no-@ mutant copy) for when one can.

### slack-connect-easy — connecting Slack in two pastes, nothing to choose in Slack (Opus build, design 017; base 9d448a44)

- **The ask:** the owner tried 2.369.204's Slack connect and ended on Slack's "Create new app" chooser and an empty User Token Scopes page (「不知道选啥」). Design 017's minimal set 1–5 is built: the Connect dialog's Slack type is three numbered steps — ① a one-time app configuration token (`xoxe.xoxp-…`) → VibeSpace makes the person's own app with ONE `apps.manifest.create`, ② the app's install page by id, ③ the `xoxp-` as before — and the 2.369.204 link stays folded as "Another way" with "Copy app setup".
- **The credential:** the setup token reaches slack.js `createApp` as the exchange's `code`, is the Bearer of one JSON POST and is dropped in the create branch's `finally`; the create's `credentials` / `oauth_authorize_url` are never read (http path). It is in no flow status, record, call record, log line, frame, answer, error or file of the data dir — slack-shape ⑧ and slack-send ⑧ census it with planted-leak controls (a copy that puts it in the step facts over an unfiltered loopback, a copy that words a refusal with it). `xoxe.` / `xoxe-` joined secret-shapes (PREFIX_RE, the whole token now redacted incl. its `xoxe.` head) and secret-scan (`slack-config-token`). Fact found: the base scanner already flagged `xoxe.xoxp-…` through its `xoxp-` rule; only the refresh token `xoxe-…` was unseen (slack-send ⑧ shows both on the base's scanner).
- **The flow machine:** oauth-loopback's `paste` mode accepts `{continue:true, step, facts}` — a step that landed keeps the flow running (`step`, `stepFacts` ≤ 8 short strings, carried by `status()` and the engine's `safeFlow`); a step that lands on a flow ended meanwhile is still recorded. Each paste names its box; slack-manifest.js `pasteAction` (the closed table) refuses a wrong-box token by its shape before any call; refusals carry a closed `why` to the card (`detail.code`).
- **Rules the gates enforced:** test-oauth-field-parity §6 (the account dialogs build no form control) moved the stepper's DOM into mounts-dialog.js `wireStepPaste`; test-record-clear-census H1 classified the remembered-app key (`owner`: id, app name, workspace name — never a token).
- **Not built / to check:** the https variant (design step 6 — no https instance at hand). The workspace is named before step 2 only when the create's answer names one — the documented answer does not, and no second call is made for it. The JSON body shape, the answer's fields and the install link by app_id are built against the docs and a fake Slack; q-017-probe.md (the coordinator's live probe) had not landed when this lane closed.
- **Gates:** test-channels-slack-shape (158), test-channels-slack-send (58), test-vendor-whitelist (227, §12 + 3 controls), test-oauth-loopback, test-channels-accounts, test-channels-gmail-shape, test-channels-lark-shape, test-integration-registry, test-record-clear-census, test-oauth-field-parity, test-exit-run, test-architecture, test-approval-census, test-channel-acl and the other suites that read the touched files (fast); test-integrations-ui (heavy, 178: the stepper at 375 / 860 px, the wrong box, the resume, Copy app setup = the link's JSON, Connect); `npm run build` (i18n zh / ja).

- **test-desktop-app-snap**: the proposed cause (a repaint between the screenshot and the backing read) measured and REFUTED — with before/after backing reads 0 of 105 states moved and 9 ✗ kept the base's numbers; the cause is the server's port sweep: a "New port on This machine" toast for any process's new port ≤ 32767 (on this shared box other runs' chrome / python3) over windows at the bottom right. The judge now measures only a clean shot (no toast of ours over the picture — waited out ≤ 10 s; strips, rects and toasts equal before and after the shot), ≤ 6 takes, a clean verdict final (the old best-of-3 is gone); THE TOAST LEG + CONTROL (the suite's own port ⇒ the toast ⇒ a single read 23.6 %, the judge 99.2 % after a 6.1 s wait); an instrument line counts the waits and re-takes of each run.
- **test-agentd-transfer**: the gc'd `arrayBuffers` sampler replaced by THE MEMORY JUDGE — bytes in (the socket's `bytesRead`; a push: the source's own pushes) minus the target + its part on disk, at every arrival; two controls (the whole-range read, a hoarding sink) 100.0 MiB; no `--expose-gc` re-exec.
- **Measured**: pull hold 0.26–0.27 MiB, push 1.6–2.5 MiB — no real hold (the old probe on the same base: pull 0.1–16.4, push 0.1–27.1 MiB).
- **Reported, not changed**: the port toast announces other processes' ports on a shared host and covers windows at the bottom right — a product question.
- Gates: test-desktop-app-snap 3/3 green (load 19→6, 6→60, 60→50; 1–7 states a run waited a toast out), test-agentd-transfer 10/10 (load 24–27) + 5/5 beside a CPU burner, test-ci-gate 299, test-architecture 428, test-fixture-isolation 109, test-changelog-style 40, test-harness-honesty 182 (all green).

### around-sheet-fix — the Channels search's "Around this message" sheet drew its rows cut and overlapping (Opus)

The owner (2026-10-03, zh, 2.369.203, a Lark full-history hit → 这条消息前后): 「这啥玩意啊！」 — every row's left edge cut ("李天雨" showed "雨", "没事" showed "殳事"), the round avatar on the name and the first line, a horizontal scrollbar, and a picture row saying "图片 未找到 重试" for a message VibeSpace never stored.

- **Cause (measured on 3452dce3 by the new leg, not guessed):** the sheet put the window's `.chanmsg` rows in a bare `.chan-around-list`. The row's `padding-left: calc(6px + var(--chan-gutter))` is invalid where no list defines `--chan-gutter`, so it fell to 0 under the row's `margin: 0 -6px`: the name and first line started 6 px left of the box (179 < 185 at 1400 px), the absolute avatar covered both, `scrollWidth` 481 > `clientWidth` 475 (347 > 341 at 390 px), and `scrollIntoView` left the found row 21 px off centre. The picture asked our attachment route, which serves only an attachment of a record we STORED (`fetchVerdict` rule 3, the route is not a proxy) ⇒ `not-found` with a Retry that could never work.
- **Fix:** the list is `chanwin-list chan-around-list`, the outbox's way: one rule for the gutter, padding and scroll, and the sheet only caps its height. `renderAroundRows` draws `unsaved` rows. A file there is a named chip, "not saved — open the conversation to see it" (zh/ja), with no link and no Retry, and it asks nothing because the vendor read is not allowed for a record we never stored. The rows also get the window's day separators. The found row is centred by the list's own `scrollTop`, vertically only. `dayLabel` names another year's day with its year, because the sheet reaches years back.
- **Fixture:** the fake vendor's archive gains `<kind>-ops-old-pic` (author 李天雨, a Lark-shaped `[image]`). It never matches a search, so ⑪'s 20 hits and test-channel-search are unchanged.
- **Gates:** test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑪b (new, 30 rows: zh / en / ja × desktop + 390 px, each on a fresh page). It checks every row's avatar, name, first line and chip inside the list's box, the avatar on none of them, `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`, the found row centred with the page unscrolled, the chip's words with zero `/attachment/` asks, and the picture's separator carrying its year. It counts only asks that name the picture, because a fresh page restores the channel windows earlier legs opened, and their thumbnails are not the sheet's. It is red on 3452dce3 (all 24 judged rows; the six page and panel loads pass) and green after (the whole suite 171/171, run alone). The channel-window and chrome suites that pin row layout are green: window-render, threads-ui, lark-threads-ui, channels-e2e, groups-e2e, channels-i18n, press-select and record-clear-ui. test-channels-images' pin on `placed.add(id); return attachmentNode(rec, a, base);` is kept verbatim; the unsaved branch comes one line before it.

### lane desktop-workarea — the work area follows the pane (the blank strip under WeChat)

- **Measured (the owner's display, read-only, 2.369.203):** the root (1660×1296) followed the pane, `_NET_WORKAREA` (0,0,1573,973) did not, and WeChat's main window states max 1574×974 = the work area ⇒ the strip under it. **Cause (xpra 6.5.4 source):** the work area comes ONLY from the client's `screen_sizes` rows, which `display-configure` never updates — every resize after the hello kept the hello's work area. Reproduced red on 4a1dd019 on the real rung (DPR 2: root 2776×1566 under 0,0,1796,1110 = the hello's pane; 228 CSS px blank under a GTK main capped at the work area).
- **Fix (src/lib/xpra-proto.js):** `displayPacket` sends the FULL legacy `desktop_size` (rows whose work area is the whole desktop, then the same size + dpi xpra re-dispatches as a display-configure) whenever the server names it; `display-configure` only when that is all it takes (XPRA_BACKWARDS_COMPATIBLE=0 — the root follows, the work area cannot; a keeper-side `_NET_WORKAREA` write would be the fallback, not built). One packet ⇒ the keeper's held-display replay is unchanged. `screenSizes` is shared with the hello.
- **Gates:** test-xpra-client (121 sizes, a modelled 6.5.4 server on the owner's sizes, a patched-copy control) · heavy test-desktop-app-fixed WORK AREA at DPR 2 and 1 (xprop / xwininfo on the root; fixture mode `workarea`; red on 4a1dd019, and the control tree's lever) · test-desktop-apps · test-architecture · test-changelog-style · `npm run build`.

### lane exit-transfer — agents copy ONE file between machines: `vibespace-exit pull` / `push` (design 013 B)

- **The ask** (owner, 2026-10-03 03:5x PDT, in a project conversation): 「agent有能力在远程机器上生成一个大文件并pull回本地吗？还是只能通过命令行一点一点读？」 — the nomad agent had built its own transfer from `run` calls and the `use` proxy aimed at the machine's loopback.
- **Built** (base dc4f6bd2): PURE `transferVerdict` / `transferPathVerdict` / `transferMaxOf` / the words / the row (src/exit-reach.js; 7 new refusal codes); ORCH `pull` / `push` (src/exit-proxy.js `_transfer`: the run verdict, the ask with the transfer line, remote_session, the browser CLI's physical write fence for the local side, the stat, 8 MiB windows, per-window sha256, re-judge between windows, one audit line + one card + the Commands row); routes `POST /api/agent/exit/pull` and `/push` (the body IS the file; a refusal before it answers at once and drains the rest); the device: `read-range` + `sha256`, the new `write-stream` op + capability `fs-write-stream`; the hub client: `fsReadRange(…, {sink, sha256})`, `fsWriteStream`; the CLI verbs + help; the setting `exit.transferMaxBytes` (MB, default 1024); the Commands list draws transfer rows (both ends, size, hash; zh/ja).
- **Measured** (this box, real agent): 100 MiB pull 1.0 s, hub memory +14.6 MiB over the run (gc'd probe; the whole-range read of the same file +185.8 MiB); push +7.7 MiB; 0 child_process calls on the agent across every transfer (its hello's shell probe aside).
- **Choices**: not resumable (design D); the local side of a push is the CLI's own read (the hub never opens a local path for an agent); `~` only for an agent with `fs-portable`; the transfer is not a run (no `lastRun`, no 30 s cap); the hello-ack's posixShells probe is not a transfer's spawn (the census filters it by its command).

### desktop-vnc-native — a Windows / macOS machine's whole desktop (Opus build, design 014 D1; base ed1e0b83)

- **What shipped:** the `vnc-native` rung (src/desktop-display.js `VNC_NATIVE` + PURE `rfbGreeting`), the picker rows for darwin / win32 (`desktop_ready` / `no_vnc` / `offline`, Linux rows byte-identical — frozen from ed1e0b83's own machinePickRow), the access layer's probe / open / target / gone / runOnDesktop / UAC install, the bridge's `human_only` + `upstreamWhy`, the routes (`/api/desktop/machine-desktop/{open,run,last-close}`, `what: 'tightvnc'`), the page's dialog + window (src/lib/machine-desktop.js) and vnc-view's `credentials` / `resizeSession`. No new device op; no keeper row.
- **Design vs code (said in 车道群 before building; the coordinator chose option A):** the Windows agent runs UNELEVATED (scripts/vibespace-agentd-install.ps1: a logon task without `-RunLevel Highest`, "no admin"), and the xpra install door's runner is POSIX sh + setsid / flock / `tail --pid`, so "TightVNC through the same door, silently, the password typed in the hub's dialog" could not run. Option A: the same slot / plan / digest, but the agent's argv asks Windows for elevation on that machine's screen (UAC); the person there clicks Yes and types the VNC password into the elevated window — it never passes through VibeSpace. `run-cmd` is not detached (execFile, 30 s cap): the run plan detaches itself (nohup on macOS, Start-Process on Windows).
- **MSI facts (measured 2026-10-03):** tightvnc-2.8.85-gpl-setup-64bit.msi, 2,531,328 bytes, SHA-256 d8fbed7b…5f3e; every property in the flag table was read out of the MSI's own string pool (SET_/VALUE_OF_ LOOPBACKONLY, ALLOWLOOPBACK, ACCEPTHTTPCONNECTIONS, RFBPORT, USEVNCAUTHENTICATION, PASSWORD; SERVER_REGISTER_AS_SERVICE, SERVER_ADD_FIREWALL_EXCEPTION, SERVER_ALLOW_SAS; ADDLOCAL). TightVNC refuses loopback connections by default — ALLOWLOOPBACK=1 is what lets the agent's forward in. UNCONFIRMED until the owner's first use: which sign-in the owner's Mac's Screen Sharing offers noVNC (the probe names it; ARD-only and VNC-password both handled), whether `start "" blender` finds Blender on WIN-DESK1, and that LOOPBACKONLY binds 127.0.0.1 (the install script checks the listen addresses and fails by name otherwise).
