### lane usage-index-shadow — a shadow SQLite index of the usage ledger, and the cursor store's hygiene (design 011 lane 3: L0 + L1)

- **L1, the index as a SHADOW.** `~/.vibespace/db/<sha256 of data/'s real path, 16 hex>/usage.db` on LOCAL disk, survey §2.2's schema (`usage_event` keyed by rid, INSERT OR IGNORE in _loadEvents's order — the first row of a rid wins; `shard_mark`; the `attribution` table waits for lane 4's reader — a schema change is a version bump, a version bump is a rebuild). It feeds NOTHING: every `/api/usage-stats` aggregate is asked a second time of the index and compared (costs to 1e-9 relative, everything else exact); a difference is a telemetry event `usage-index-diff` carrying the query, never shown. Owner Q1 (SQLite for this index, assumed yes): a "no" drops L1 whole — the three new files, the push, the comparer line, §73 — and L0 stands alone. Owner Q2 (local disk, assumed yes): a "no" is `indexDirFor` in src/server/usage-index.js.
- **One thread owns the database.** PURE `src/usage-index-model.js`; `src/usage-index-worker.js` is the ONLY file naming `node:sqlite` and refuses the main thread (test-architecture §73, seven planted readers / openers as controls); ORCH `src/server/usage-index.js` starts it 30 s after boot (from account-usage-routes.js), keeps one FIFO, names every unavailability. EXCLUSIVE + WAL + NORMAL: no -shm; a second server on the same data/ gets SQLITE_BUSY, says so, never retries. user_version ≠ 1 / NOTADB / CORRUPT ⇒ delete and rebuild; SQLITE_FULL / IOERR / READONLY / ENOSPC ⇒ off by name. Owner Q3 (the 22.16 floor lands with lane 4): node:sqlite loads only inside the worker, so an older Node has the shadow off BY NAME and the server never notices.
- **Read-your-writes (design 011 §2).** Both commit points push the bytes they just appended (`_pushIndex`: shard, start offset, inode, text) in the same synchronous step, and the comparer posts its query in the same step as the memory answer — the FIFO answers over exactly the appends that answer saw. A push is taken only when it starts at the shard's mark with the marked inode; anything else (a dropped push, a torn tail before it, a rewrite in between, the first build having read past it) re-reads that shard from its mark. The commit point's order is unchanged: append (+ push), cursors, ack.
- **Recovery by shard marks** — (size, inode, sha1 of the first ≤ 4 KiB, bytes consumed) → append | rebuild (every repair's tmp + rename is a new inode; a shrink; a changed head) | gone | same; 16 MiB chunks, each committed with its mark (kill -9 loses at most the chunk in flight); `reloadEvents` and the re-bake ask for a re-check.
- **Measured: process.exit() joins worker threads.** With the worker blocked in a syscall (open() of a FIFO) the process never exits (`timeout 10` killed the probe). The owner's `exit` hook asks the worker to close and waits ≤ 2 s on a SharedArrayBuffer flag, then re-raises SIGTERM with the default action (systemd: a clean stop). A deadline answers 503 `unresponsive` and never terminates the worker.
- **The aggregate is ONE grouped pass**: session × the raw columns every dimension derives from × UTC day × local hour / weekday (JS `getHours` / `getDay` registered as SQL functions — the calls memory makes), folded in the worker, priced per (model, account) cell by the ledger's own `_cost`. 500 000 synthetic rows: ~1 s, against ~6 s for a GROUP BY per dimension and ~5.3 s through a temp table. Build: 160 000 rows in 1.2 s, 57 MB.
- **L0 — the cursor store.** `_cursors.json` is written only when its bytes change (`_cursorsJson` = the text on disk; JSON.stringify of production's parsed file gives the file back). The walker's unchanged-file path stamps `sid` into an entry once (parity-pinned with the shipped scanner), so the first idle walk after a scan still writes; an active machine still writes most walks — the size is what shrinks. Keys whose transcript is gone are dropped by the walk's writer at most hourly and only on proof (under a readable walk root, stat ENOENT); an unmounted projects dir drops nothing. Production, read once 2026-10-03: 37 024 keys, 25 817 dead (4.1 of 6.7 MB), every key under the two roots, 45 ms to stat them all.
- **Scratch sweep.** `scripts/ci.mjs` `sweepUsageIndexDirs` (after every suite, both runners) removes `~/.vibespace/db/<x>/` only when its owner.json names an absolute data/ that is gone.
- **Gates.** NEW test-usage-index-parity (fast, 2.3 s, 40 ✓ — L0; 14 query shapes over duplicate rids differing in account, rid-less rows, an empty shard, a torn line, a remote harvest into an old month, a push onto a torn line, a missed push, a repair rewrite; read-your-writes through both commit points with a tail-only CONTROL worker; a TZ=America/St_Johns child across a DST change). NEW test-usage-index-owner (fast, 7.4 s, 32 ✓ — kill -9 mid-build and mid-push-stream, deleted / newer / older / not-a-database rebuilt, a second opener, a deadline 503 keeping the worker, SIGTERM bounded with a wedged worker + CONTROL, SQLITE_FULL / no node:sqlite / a dead worker named, the sweep). test-architecture §73 + the PURE set.
- **Verify r1 (on a copy of the real 296 MB ledger: 613 710 rows, built in 4.3 s, a 343 MB index, parity on every Usage-window dimension and the 8 heaviest pivots).** Four fixes, each a test-usage-index-owner §8 leg with its pre-fix CONTROL: L0 drops a dead key only when the key's own directory answers and its root still holds a live key — an unmounted FUSE transcript root (an EMPTY mount point) dropped every live cursor, and one 1.1 GB transcript walked again appended 21 MB of duplicate rows; a full disk (SQLITE_FULL / ENOSPC / EDQUOT) deletes the disabled index's files (a stopped build left 146 MB on the full disk); the worker's V8 heap is capped (`heapMb` 128) and the aggregate streams its grouped rows (`iterate`) — uncapped, a first build left the server +262 MB RSS for good, now +109 MB, same build time; liveness runs on `performance.now()` (a wall-clock step back after a deadline kept the index "unresponsive" for the size of the step). Measured, no change: the wedged worker on a stopped bindfs mount ends SIGTERM, SIGINT and an uncaught exception in 2.0 s (a `systemctl --user stop` with KillMode=process: 2.0 s, the detached child lives); the comparer adds ~76 ms of main-thread work per all-time window read (1.90 → 2.05 s).

### lane channels-quiet-index — a poll that brings nothing writes nothing to the channels index (design 011 lane 2)

**on a server with tens of thousands of conversations the channels index is no longer rewritten every two seconds while nothing arrives**

#### Every poll rewrote the whole index (design 011 F4, the db survey)

Measured on userW's pod: `data/channels/index.json` 87 MB, rewritten whole about every 2.3 s (≈ 35–40 MB/s) with no message arriving — every pass stamped `lane.lastPollAt` / `lastScanAt` / `walkStartedAt` into the conversation's row (src/server/channels-engine.js: the ingest's index update, the refusal), so a row was dirty after every poll and each flush wrote every chunk (`writeBuffersAtomic`).

- The three stamps leave the persisted row for `data/channels/poll-stamps.json` (`{v, fields, stamps: {key: [lastPollAt, lastScanAt, walkStartedAt]}}`, one line per conversation): memory first, written at most every 120 s (`STAMPS_FLUSH_MS`) and at close (tmp + rename); a key whose row left the index leaves at the next write; a row born under a departed key starts unstamped; an unreadable file is set aside like every store family there.
- They still persist (a row is due at `lastPollAt + cadence`): a clean restart or a kill -9 keeps every due time (the journal, below); a kill while the journal cannot be written (said) re-polls at most the rows whose due time fell in the lost 120 s; a deleted side file is SAID at the start (with the count of rows now due) and that re-poll goes through the vendor's budget and pace.
- `store.stamps` = `set` (the ONE writer) / `lane(row)` (the ONE read: the row's lane with the stamps over it — the engine's `laneOf`: the due list, the scheduler census, the watch, the refresh answer, the change feed's by-id gate, the agent's `polledAt`; channel-caps' `freshnessClaim` is handed that merged view, no signature change) / `get` / `flush`.
- The row serializer omits the three keys (`INDEX_KEYS`); `serializeChunk` heals a row that still carries them (an index written before this lane, or a write past the door): the newer instant wins into the side map, and the side file is written BEFORE the index write that drops them. Read-compatible, no migration.
- `flush` skips equal bytes: a touched chunk is compared with its cached bytes, a whole rebuild with the previous layout (as one byte stream), the top-level tables as text; `updatedAt` moves only with a real write; `flushStats()` gains `writes` / `skipped`.
- MEASURED (test-channels-index-scale ⑩): a quiet minute at 50 276 rows (51.9 MB on disk) — the timer's 12 passes polled the account in 2 of them and brought nothing: 0 index writes (2 flushes skipped, the same file); CONTROL the stamp back in the row: the 51.9 MB index written 2 times, once per polling pass. Printed, not judged: discovery's own cycle (every coldSec = 900 s) stamps `listedAt` on every listed row — 1 index write(s) per cycle, a fourth stamp outside this lane's three.
- Gates: test-channel-store ⑭ (a pass that brings nothing writes 0 index bytes; restart; legacy read + heal + kill after the heal; a departed / re-born key; the deleted file said; the engine census; the journal — 12 controls), test-channels-index-scale ⑩ (heavy), test-channels-engine (after a restart none due early + control; the side file deleted: said, spent through the budget), test-channel-drain ②c (a restart's re-poll in the model: clean 0, kill -9 ≤ the lost interval's share, file gone = 873 paced inside the minute), test-channels-census-pace unchanged.
- verify r1: a FOREIGN-shaped `poll-stamps.json` (another `v`, its columns renamed or gone) was read as "no stamps" in silence — every conversation due at once, unsaid; it is now set aside and said like every family (`v === 1` and a `lastPollAt` column required), and a v1 entry that is not a list is counted in a start line (test-channel-store ⑭ + a patched-copy control)
- fix (the 2.369.203 heavy run's test-channels-e2e ⑰ — the integration reverted this lane; bisected red on 103238d2, green on cc20f5c6): a kill -9 lost every stamp set since the side file's last write (≤ 120 s; that run's server never lived 120 s, so it had none), the restored window's row read "never polled", and its open fetched it at once as the owner's — ahead of discovery (drain rule 12); the vendor refusing that first fetch (Retry-After 20 s) held the 40 new conversations back for the whole wait. Each `stamps.set` now appends ONE line to `data/channels/poll-stamps.log` (the key's whole triple — O(the change), never the index); the side file's write folds it (truncated after the rename), a start replays it in order (the last line per key wins), a line a kill cut short is counted and said and the next line starts on its own. Gates: test-channel-store ⑭ (a SIGKILLed child: 40 of 40 instants read back with no side file; a torn tail; controls: no journal → 0 of 40, no replay → 0 of 40, no fold, close() leaves it unfolded), test-channels-engine (a kill → 0 due early; control no journal → every row due), test-channel-drain ②c words, test-channels-index-scale ⑩ prints the journal's bytes in the quiet minute, heavy test-channels-e2e ALL PASS 205 (⑰ red on 103238d2 in the same run shape).

### slack-core — Slack as the fourth Channels adapter (design 012 lane S1, B-ff09; Opus, base ed1e0b83)

- **The adapter** (`src/channels/slack.js` + PURE `slack-text.js` / `slack-limits.js` / `slack-manifest.js` / `slack-words.js`): each person's OWN internal Slack app, made from Slack's share-a-manifest link (user scopes only, rotation off); the User OAuth Token (`xoxp-`) is PASTED — `oauth-loopback` gains a third mode, `paste` (no listener; the paste is the exchange's `code`; a refused paste keeps the flow open). ONE `auth.test` per paste: identity `userId = T…/U…` (D11), scopes from `x-oauth-scopes`. Poll only: `users.conversations` (all four kinds; an app's DM flagged `app`), `conversations.history` to the anchor (`oldest`), `conversations.replies`, `reactions.get` (answered from the last page while fresh — no request), `files.info` + the private URL on files.slack.com ONLY.
- **Per-method buckets inside the adapter** (D3, the contract unchanged): Tier 1–4 floors per method in a sliding minute, one message a second per conversation (a sub-second gap is waited once), a 429 holds that method for its `Retry-After` (≤ 15 min); a spent method is the typed `rate-limited` with `retryAfterSec`; a clock that steps back frees nothing.
- **Render** (D10, no schema change): mrkdwn / rich_text / Block Kit / legacy attachments / files onto the existing block kinds; strikethrough as text; lists as "• " paragraphs; an UNKNOWN block is a card titled with its type; `thread_broadcast` is ONE record; `ekm_access_denied` said in our words; a clip's transcript is words. Mentions carry a closed `kind` (person / broadcast / group — a broadcast or a group never equals a person).
- **Three new contract rows** (`src/channels/index.js`): `caps.policyModes` (Slack: review only — `channel-policy.policyMode(policy, caps)` clamps a stored `direct`, the engine refuses `setPolicy direct` by name, the picker hides it), `caps.prepareSend` (each `@Name` resolved to an id ONCE at propose — handle › display › full › first name tiers; two people ⇒ the proposal refused `mention-ambiguous`; stored on the proposal, shown on the card, sent verbatim), `caps.retention: 'purge-on-remove'` (removing the account deletes msgs/<id>/, attachments/<id>/ and its ended proposals — store `purgeAccount`). `convCaps.audience` (dm / private / public / external + the organizations) is the card's "Seen by" line.

### lane accept-fixes-jobs (Opus fix, base ed1e0b83) — the agent browser inside a Background Work job: F5, F6, F10, F11 of the owner's acceptance of 2.369.202

- **F5 — `status` inside a job lied** ("no profile attached / pin: none (ephemeral)" while the next `open` landed on office-devices): the route answered `statusFor(<the job's child handle>)` — an empty set, no pin. Now `/api/agent/browser/status` for a `jbt_` adds `job` (src/routes/browser.js `jobBindingOf`): the profile the next page verb lands on by the ONE verdict `resolveForJob` runs (`jobResolveVerdict` over the owner's set — read only, nothing attached or told), the owner's pin, the job's own lease (its window) once it has one; the CLI prints those three lines (or `job_no_profile` with its words).
- **F6 — a job could not save into its own directory**, and the refusal told it to restart a "session started before this version": the jobs engine never exported a directory. `_spawn` now exports `VIBESPACE_JOB_CWD` = the job's `cmd.cwd` when absolute (never the server's `process.cwd()` fallback); vibespace-browser's fence takes it as the root inside a job (job token, no session token — the shell's `cd` never counts); `writePathVerdict({job})` says "the job's working directory" and, with none, names the job's case ("a run started before this VibeSpace version, or a job created without a directory").
- **F10 — the browsers row read "帮手 1" for the job's window:** `browser-profiles.attachmentsFor` rebuilt the child list as `{handle, since}` and DROPPED the `job` tag the keeper's `childrenOf` carries, so `/api/browser/session/:id`'s `jobNames` loop never ran and the row fell to "Helper {n}". The tag is kept (one line); the strip's UI files are untouched (browser-live-window's `Job: {name}` already existed).
- **F11 — a stopped job's window stayed open** in the shared profile: `releaseJob` → `detach(by:'user')` keeps a conversation's page for its return (`noteLeftTab`) — a job never returns. `releaseJobHandle` now closes the job's own tabs over CDP (`jobWindowCloser`: the holders snapshotted before the detach, `TBS.tabOwners` over one target read — the ownership its `tab list` uses; the user's, another holder's and orphan tabs untouched) and keeps no left-tab record for it. Decision: CLOSE, not keep — a kept window would be nobody's (the handle is dropped; no holder could close it). Every end reaches it: exit / crash / stop / boot through `_finalizeRun` → `onRunEnded` → `releaseJob`, archive / missed finalize through the reconcile sweep.
- **Gates:** test-jobs-browser 98 → 111 (④ + F5 before/after the first verb + the REAL CLI's status words, F10 through the route → `browserListFor`, F11 window closed at finalize and at the sweep with the owner's window untouched; ⑥ NEW: a real JobManager runs the real CLI — screenshot into the job's cwd passes the fence with TMPDIR elsewhere, outside it / no cwd refused in the job's words; exit / crash / stop each call `onRunEnded` once). Base ed1e0b83 + the new suite: 10 red (all 9 new rows + the copy's git-status row). Patched-copy controls (fixed tree, one file back to base): routes ⇒ the 2 F5 rows, jobs.js ⇒ 2 F6 rows, browser-verbs.js ⇒ 2 F6 word rows, browser-profiles.js ⇒ F10, keeper ⇒ 3 F11 rows.

### lane app-fit-fixed (Opus, 2026-10-03) — a window whose app fixes its size: frame = picture, not resizable, never scaled

- **The owner (2.369.202, "2× · 自动"):** WeChat's login filled the top-left ~45 % of a blank window; Inkscape 1.4.3's welcome was cut at the bottom between two bands. Correction mid-lane (binding): the app's title area under our bar is expected (the bars auto-hide); a fixed-size window is FOLLOWED and resizing is disabled — no "scaled-down 75 %" rule.
- **Root cause, measured (real xpra 6.5.4, headless Chrome 1920×963 DPR 2, sidebar 470, xprop beside xpra's metadata):** both apps state min = max (WeChat 560×760, Inkscape 1420×1356 device px). WeChat: the fit honoured the maximum but the window learnt only a minimum ⇒ a 280×380 CSS picture in an 898×618 pane, 81 % blank. Inkscape: the welcome is a lone DIALOG (modal, no transient-for, the only window) ⇒ no main: never fitted or named, mapped at X's centre 188,0 (94 CSS px bands), 678 CSS px tall in a 555 px pane. A 1000×900 GTK fixture at 2× was scaled to fit (stage 0.903, badge).
- **Fix:** xpra-proto `fixedSizeOf`; xpra-client `fixedWindow` / `loneFixed` / `on.fixed` (a lone fixed dialog at 0,0, held by the belt, contained by the display); xpra-view `onFixedSize` + no scale while `fixedFollows()`; desktop-app-window → `WindowManager.setFixedSize` (min = max inline, uncapped, no handles / maximize button (style.css), no resize drag, no maximize, no snap/grid zone, `_placeWindow` moves only, `resizeWindowTo` refuses; null restores the pre-lock size). After: pane = picture to 0.0 CSS px for WeChat (282×382 window), Inkscape (712×743), both fixtures; stage 1.
- **Larger than the workspace (asked by the owner to report):** the window keeps the app's size, its top on the workspace, the rest past the bottom / right edge and clipped by #workspace (the 1000×900 fixture at 2× on an 878 px workspace: 86 CSS px); it cannot be dragged above the workspace top, so Scale ▸ 1× is how to see that strip. Phone layout: today's scale-to-fit kept.
- **Gates:** test-xpra-client §8 + test-window-minsize §5 (each with patched-copy controls), new heavy test-desktop-app-fixed (DPR 2 zh / DPR 1 en + a CONTROL tree), test-desktop-app-snap unchanged; the fast suites that read any touched file run singly.

### lane windows-device-fs — the Files view and every other hub→device shell call on a Windows machine

- **The report** (coordinator, 2026-10-03 02:50 PDT): GET /api/files?host=host-dial-WIN-DESK1 → 400 "command failed (127)" — src/remote-fs.js ran `sh -c` for every device file operation; a Windows machine has no `sh`.
- **Files**: a Windows agent's files go through its own fs ops (`fs-portable`: + `home` / `copy` / `move` / `du`, `~` expanded on the device, downloads over read-range); folder .zip and the archive verbs are refused by name; an agent without `fs-portable` gets "this machine's agent is X, too old to browse files on Windows — rerun the device's install command (Remote → <machine> → Pairing command)". POSIX machines unchanged.
- **The door**: src/agentd/client.js refuses a `sh` / `bash` argv or session spawn asked of a win32 agent by name (`windows_no_shell`) before sending; the census (36 sites) judges every hub→device shell site.
- **verify-r1 F1 (HIGH, fixed)**: keyed on the PLATFORM, the door refused a Windows machine WITH `sh` (Git for Windows / MSYS2 / Cygwin put sh.exe on PATH; node resolves `sh` to it) the 28 sites it ran before, and an old agent's Files view. Now the agent measures at its first hello which POSIX shells start there (`posixShells`); the door refuses only a shell that list leaves out; an agent too old to say is asked (once per link on the Files route) and a failed spawn is named (`windows_no_shell` / the outdated sentence), never a bare 127.
- **verify-r2**: the agent's shell probe is async, parallel and bounded (3 s, the child killed): a shell counts only if it RAN `echo vs-$((40+2))` and answered `vs-42` — a hung `sh` (WSL booting / a prompt), a broken one (exit ≠ 0), a non-POSIX one are absent (r1 counted all three present and blocked the agent 5 s per shell: first link 5.5 s → 3.0 s); every hello re-measures (a shell installed later is seen at the next link). An old agent's one-per-link `sh -c 'exit 0'` counts only an exit 0 (a broken `sh` ⇒ the outdated sentence). The Files routes send the refusal as a CODE + params (`fsErrorBody`), worded client-side in zh / ja (`fsErrorText`); du stopped at 10^6 entries reads "at least …"; a cross-drive move that fails says what is left where (no partial copy, no errno).
- **Gates**: test-windows-device-fs (new, fast, 134), test-exit-run, test-sysinfo-op, test-raw-filename, test-agentd-switchover, test-architecture, test-changelog-style, `npm run build`, every fast suite that reads a touched file.

## 2.369.203 — 2026-10-03

### prod-stall-202 — the 6–15 s production stalls (Opus): 2.369.202 stopped its event loop every one to two minutes

- **Diagnosed on the live process (read-only):** SIGUSR1 → V8 inspector on 127.0.0.1:9229, Profiler at 1 ms for 240 s (11:51:19–11:55:20Z), inspector closed (`process._debugEnd`, 9229 no longer listening). The profile's 16.9 s busy run (11:54:59→11:55:16Z = the journal's 04:55:20 "longest loop gap 11s") is 13.4 s `readFileUtf8`: the auto-cli `tick` (auto-cli-loop.js:121) → `projectionRereadFor` × 13 accounts → `sessionBillingMember` × 25 pooled conversations → `validateBillingSlot` → `accounts.poolMembers` → `parseClaudeAuth` × 13 members × 2 files ≈ 9 K synchronous reads a tick (10.1 s), plus `maybePoolAutoSwitchForPool` (2.9 s), the usage walker's per-line `resolveAccount` → `accounts.list()` (2.0 s), `loginStateOf` (1.2 s). The data dir is bindfs over NFS (100–180 µs per 2 KB read, worse under load 29). Not new code: the hot functions are identical in 2.369.201 (whose telemetry already shows 0.5–3.6 s max lag, one 9.2 s); the stall length follows the NFS latency. Profile + analysis scripts: /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/prod-stall-202/.
- **Fix:** `accounts.isPoolMember` (one login read, the same predicate as `poolMembers().some`), `projectionBillingIndex` (who-bills-where once per tick, dropped with the tick; `projectionRereadFor(member, now, index)`), `accounts.poolsWithMember` (memberPoolsOf's hot-pool answer read live, one login per pool), server.js `resolveAccount` from the record. 11 514 → 498 fs calls a tick at production's shape; 1.8 s → 82 ms synchronous at 150 µs per call.
- **Gate:** test-auto-cli-tick-reads (24) — decisions equal to a fix-reverted patched copy across login-file states, hot/held pools and mid-tick login changes; WORK linear in conversations and members; LOOP < 250 ms with the reverted copy > 1 s. test-auto-cli-refresh's four wiring pins follow the new signature. Hotfix-sized (5 files, no state format, no route): fit to ship on top of 2.369.203 alone.

### lane channels-followups — an agent's `list` bounded to the newest 200; Gmail's own search behind channel search (designs 008 S6, 010 S6)

**an agent's channel list names the newest 200 conversations it can see and says how many more (found with search); searching a Gmail account also asks Gmail's own search over the whole mailbox — each hit marked "not saved here", its thread a click away**

- design 008 S6: `engine.listFor` sorts the conversations the caller may see (reach asked of every row — the count needs it) by `lastAt` and builds only the newest `LIST_FOR_MAX` (200). The answer adds `more` (the rest of what it may see), `moreRequestable` (the same bound over `--all`'s directory titles) and `max`; a hidden conversation is in neither count. The CLI prints one line after the rows — `… N more conversations you can see — only the newest 200 are listed; use search: …` — and `… N more you may request` under the directory; the manual says the bound.
- design 010 S6: Gmail declares `caps.search {via:'query', scope:null, pageSize:10, pagesPerPress:2, perMin:6, cost:205, snippet:true, context:'thread', match:'tokens'}`. `search` = `messages.list?q=<words>&maxResults=10` with no label filter (all mail but spam and trash — also the threads outside the synced scope), the page judged (not an object, `messages` not a list, more than 10 ⇒ vendor-error); per id: not shown to the caller ⇒ dropped with no read at all (neither the vendor nor the local log); held locally ⇒ the hit at its stored instant, no read; else ONE `messages.get format=metadata&metadataHeaders=From` (internalDate, the From address, Gmail's `snippet` through `SR.snippetOf`); a message gone between the list and its read ⇒ malformed; a 429 re-throws (the engine backs the account's search off). `around` = ONE `threads.get format=full` (no memo, no title cache, no body held), ≤ 50 messages centred on the hit.
- Engine: `vendorSearch` hands the adapter two HINTS — `storedAt(convId, vendorId)` (an index row, then `store.findRecord`'s instant) and, for an agent's `--full`, `shows(convId)` (its visible set) — so a per-hit read is spent only on a hit the person is shown; Lark's one-request page ignores both. Floor, share, minute, budget, reach after the await, no page token for agents, nothing stored: Lark's leg unchanged.
- Units: the quota table (`unitsFor`, read 2026-09-26) charges `messages.get` 20 — the design's "5 units per hit" is `messages.list`'s price. A page costs ≤ 5 + 10 × 20 = 205 units (`cost`), paced at the account's 40 units/s (≈ 5 s for a page of ten new hits).
- Words: `match: 'tokens'` (Gmail matches words) ⇒ the dialog says "may be related". Gmail has no change feed, so the VS1–VS4 counters (`rec.feed.counters.fullSearch`) are Lark's alone.
- Words (verify r1 F2): a search row declares what its hits ADD — `caps.search.adds: 'older' | 'unsaved'`, required and refused by name in the registry (Lark and the fakes `older`, Gmail `unsaved`: mail outside the synced scope or a reply newer than its stored thread is not "older"). `SR.statusText` / `SR.sectionHead` and the agent's `--full` line read the row, never the adapter id: Gmail's dialog says "Not saved here — from Gmail's search" / "Asked Gmail's whole mailbox: N not saved here — may be related" (4 keys × zh / ja); Lark's words unchanged.
- Gates: test-channels-agent-cli ⑳ (the REAL engine behind the stub: 205 visible + 230 newer hidden ⇒ 200 rows + "5 more"; `--all` 200 + 200; CONTROLS: no bound ⇒ 205 rows, a whole-index count ⇒ "237 more"); test-channels-gmail-shape ⑳ (a fresh engine connected through the consent loopback: the press reads 4 metadata — never the held msg_ops_b; an agent that sees one thread reads 1; around = one threads.get, 50 of 60; nothing born or appended; a 429 ⇒ `backoff` and no call inside it; the adapter alone; the hints' order — `shows` before `storedAt`; CONTROLS: an engine copy without the hints reads the held and the hidden hits, an adapter copy asking `storedAt` first reads the hidden thread's ids, an adapter copy without the reader returns the 1 MB snippet); test-vendor-whitelist §FS-G (Gmail's words request and per-hit read live in `search` only, the thread read in `around` only; two planted controls); census rows in test-peer-text-census (the list's counts) and test-record-clear-census (`vendorSearch`'s `store.index.has(` gate).

### lane store-timing — measure the stores' sync writes and the mount, off the main thread (design 011 lane 1, step M)

The owner asked which parts are dragged down by file reads and writes and need a real database (2026-10-03). Design 011 answers "SQLite only as the usage ledger's index" and orders everything else by measurement — this lane is that measurement. It fixes nothing.
- **The clock.** NEW PURE `src/timed-sync.js`: `timedSync(name, fn)` with a CLOSED name table `STORES` (20 rows: session-meta, session-status, user-todos, task-groups, jobs, job-notifications, channels index, usage shards, usage cursors, otel-truth (read / boot rewrite / append), the telemetry summary read), a fixed-bucket histogram per name (≤1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500 ms, 1, 2, 5 s, slower), per-minute maxima for the last hour. OFF until server.js turns it on before any store is built (`VIBESPACE_STORE_TIMING=0` keeps it off); off = `if (!on) return fn();`, no clock read. The span is the write call as the store makes it today (a helper that stringifies inside the call counts its stringify). An unknown name runs untimed — a typo can never break a write.
- **The sites** (24 calls): writeSessionMeta + readSessionMeta (session-stdout.js), session-status / user-todos `_flush` + their boot reads, task-groups `_save` / `_load`, jobs `_save` (jobs.json and job-notifications.json apart) / `_saveNotifs` / `_load`, the channels index write (`writeIndex`, both the incremental and the fallback write) and its boot read, the usage commit point (shard appends in `_walkAndAppend` and `ingestRemoteEvents`, the cursor write) and the cursor read, otel-ingest's boot read + rewrite and its per-request append, telemetry `summary()`'s shard reads. The commit point's order (appends, then cursors) is unchanged — timedSync is synchronous.
- **Reported**: every 5 min one `srv-store-ms:<name>` metric per name with samples (value = the window's max, detail = n + the bucket counts) — the Diagnostics summary gives their percentiles; `/api/sysinfo` (this machine only) carries `storeWrites` = the three slowest writes of the last hour; the System window draws it as one line, "Slowest store writes (last hour): jobs 812 ms · channels/index 240 ms" (en/zh/ja).
- **The canary off the main thread.** The 2.108.6 canary moved from server.js into NEW `src/server/fs-canary.js` + `fs-canary-worker.js`: the stat runs and is timed in its own one-worker SafeFs (an ASYNC stat on purpose — it watches the shared libuv pool), and the main side measures only how long the answer waited. `srv-fs-canary-ms` (worker clock, the only fact that strikes; three timeouts → `srv-threadpool-wedged` + the mount health sweep, as before) and NEW `srv-loop-canary-ms` (a blocked loop) are logged and counted apart; a probe with no answer is `srv-fs-canary-lost`, never a strike. Before, a main-thread stall longer than 5 s struck as a wedged pool.
- **Gates.** NEW scripts/test-timed-sync.mjs (fast, 21): buckets, the closed names, zero clock reads when off, the hour window, the real stores' names in a scratch dir. NEW scripts/test-fs-canary.mjs (fast, 20): a 1.5 s and a past-the-deadline blocked loop read as the loop's fact only; a pool saturated from the main thread reads as the fs fact; three timeouts strike and kick the sweep; a lost probe; CONTROL — a copy that times the stat on the main thread again reads the same blocked loop as a 1500 ms stat. test-architecture §72: every sync write inside a write row's sites sits inside a timedSync of that file's rows (unwrapped ones printed), every call is a literal row in its own file, every row used; planted controls + the real jobs.js `_save` unwrapped. Both suites registered fast in scripts/ci.mjs.

### lane design-changes — the Design window's changes strip (design 003 §2.2, B-6351 lane B)

The owner (2026-10-02 20:32 PDT) asked the design desk to replicate the online Claude Design; design 003 ranks "one round for many changes" second, and the owner decided Q1 NO (22:06 PDT): edits are previews handed to the agent in one message, never written to the files.

- **The frame (design-pick.js).** While picking, a text's pick waits 280 ms for a second click; a double-click on a text (its words, inline markup at most) makes it `contenteditable=plaintext-only` — Enter or a click away reports `design-edit {edit:'text', ref, path, tag, from, to}`, Esc restores this edit's words, typing never reaches the page's key handlers. The parent's `design-style {ref, prop, value}` previews one nudge inline (`!important`) and is reported with the computed value it replaced; `design-undo` drops a preview. A pick carries the element's `ref` (`<frame seed>-<n>`) and a `css` snapshot.
- **The fence (design-canvas-model.js, design-canvas.js).** PICK_KINDS gains `design-edit` (editFence: closed props color / background-color / font-size / padding, the hub's value grammar, bounded words); FRAME_KINDS gains `design-style` / `design-undo` through `frameSay`, the canvas's ONE postMessage site (`say`). `canvas.listen` hands a seam module change + edit events — a TEXT edit only while picking (+ EDIT_GRACE_MS), from the frame that has or just had the keyboard, through its own rate gate; `canvas.tell(file, msg)`.
- **The hub.** design-model.js `changesVerdict` / `changeLine` / `changesText` (≤ 30 chips, refusals by name with the chip's index, one folded line per chip, heads of ours softened) + `CHANGE_PROPS` / `styleValueOk`; design-engine.js `changes()` → the WHOLE block through THE belt (`changesText(` is a peer-text census door) → `userLine`, the comment's sender split out (the spend census pins unchanged); `POST /api/design/changes`.
- **The window (design-changes.js).** One mount line + one composer seam in design-window.js; the strip at the stage's top (chips, × undoes, "N changes · Send all"), device-kept per design; "Add" + the Style row in the composer; 24 words ×2.
- **Gates** (final tree): build ✓ · test-architecture 455 · test-design-model 149 — §5b (the exact message, the 30 bound, a forged frame tag / "2. [Design comment]" line neutered by the belt, refusals, 3 new controls) · test-design-canvas 228 (editFence + frameSay tables, the picker's edit run on fake timers, the widened censuses, 4 new controls) · test-design-routes 128 — §5b (one message for 3 chips on the stub sender, the stash, refusals, agent 403) · heavy test-design-window 98 ✓ / 1 SKIP (the headless print dialog, as before) — A⑧ (real double-click edit, chip × ⇒ preview undone, a click AWAY keeps the words (Chrome fires no blur on the iframe ELEMENT when focus leaves a frame — measured; the canvas tracks the keyboard's frame on its own window's blur / focus), Style font size, Add, a forged design-edit adds nothing, Send all = ONE message on the stub's stdin) · census rows: test-record-clear-census (the storage key), test-takeover-keyboard (3 surfaces), test-peer-text-census (the door).

### lane design-tweaks — the Design window v2 lane C: Tweaks, the free knobs (B-6351, design 003 §2 S4)

The owner asked for the online Claude Design replicated (2026-10-02 20:32 PDT); design 003 ranks Tweaks fourth ("genuinely new", free to move). The agent declares knobs in design.json, the owner moves them in OUR panel, the artboards restyle at once with no agent turn, and the values live in `user.json` — the contract's user layer, written ONLY by the hub on the owner's act (design 003 §2 "Two contract additions"; it ends F4's agent-and-human race on one file).

- **The contract.** design.json gains the closed key `tweaks`: ≤ 12 `{id, label?, kind: color|range|select|toggle, var: "--x" | attr: "data-x", default}` (+ range `min, max, step?, unit?` from a closed unit set; select 2–12 `options`); closed keys per kind, one knob per target, never `data-vibespace-…`, refusals by name (`tweaks[i].<key>`). `user.json` = `{v:1, tweaks:{id: value}}`, judged like any input; a value that no longer fits its knob, or a knob that is gone, is dropped and SAID (a warning), never applied.
- **Split by the viewer's budget.** design-model.js is bundled whole into public/design-viewer.js (test-design-canvas trips at 60 KB; lanes A + B took it from 44.6 to 55.2 KB; everything here would have made 67.5). It keeps only the list's shape, the fence word `tweakSay` / `tweakWordOk` (a value cannot close a rule, the style block or the root tag) and its walker pieces (`WALK`); each knob's rules, the user layer and the baking live in the new PURE **src/design-user-layer.js**, reaching the manifest through `validateManifest(json, {tweaks})` (`UL.validateDesign` = the hub's reader). Without the hook (the viewer, bundleCanvas / readBundle) the manifest carries no knobs — their values are baked. Viewer: 57.8 KB.
- **Baked where it is served.** `applyUser` writes EVERY declared knob (the user's value, else the default) into each artboard the read serves — the window, `preview`, publish: ONE `<style id="vibespace-tweaks">:root{… !important}</style>` at the head's start + ONE marked attribute run right after `<html` (the parser keeps the first of a repeated attribute). Found only at those two places by a linear tag walk, only when exactly ours ⇒ idempotent; every word re-judged at bake time.
- **Restyle in place.** A move posts `design-tweak {var|attr, value}` through the canvas's outgoing fence (FRAME_KINDS + 1) to every frame; the picker sets the root property (inline `!important`) or attribute from its parent only. The write says ONE `file-changed` for user.json; a re-read whose html differs from a LIVE frame's ONLY in the layer (`tweakSwap`) restyles it by message instead of reloading (design-canvas.js `setSwap` + a `live` flag) — on every device, scroll and state kept.
- **Hub.** design-engine.js reads user.json with the folder (O_NOFOLLOW; a link or non-file is said, `user_not_file`; ssh: the one read emits it, `@@ULINK` for a link), bakes in compose, watches it; `readMeta` (design.json + user.json; ssh = one command); `setTweaks` (one write chain per folder, merge, null = default, Reset; lstat + O_EXCL temp + rename, a link / directory refused by name; ssh = ONE `remoteUserWriteScript`: mktemp, base64, mv); `requestTweaks` ("+ Tweaks" = ONE `[Design tweaks]` line through THE belt down the comment's sender). Owner routes `GET` / `POST /api/design/tweaks`, `POST /api/design/tweaks/request` (an agent bearer 403). `check` / `show` print the knobs and what the user set (belted).
- **Window.** src/lib/design-tweaks.js: the bar's "Tweaks" button (`sliders`, priority 1, ⋯ row) → a side panel on the stage's left under the top dock / a bottom sheet on the phone; colour, range (+ readout), choice (pills or a select), switch; writes 300 ms after the last move (at once on release); a knob in flight keeps its value through re-reads; Reset; no knobs ⇒ "+ Tweaks" with optional words. 18 words ×2 (zh/ja).
- **Shared-file hunks (for the integrator).** design-model.js: KEYS.top + `tweaks`; validateManifest's signature + the shape block + the return spread; the section before "the published page"; exports. design-engine.js: header, STATUS line, `UL` require, isWatchable, the remote read (`@@ULINK` + user.json in its loop + the parse line), readLocal (user.json in the read loop + `userOdd`), compose (`ul` line, `applyUser` on html, 1 return line), two `UL.validateDesign` reads, the tweaks block before "publish", agentView (2 lines), the returned API, module.exports. routes/design.js: header + 3 routes. design-canvas-model.js: import + FRAME_KINDS + 1 frameSay line. design-pick.js: header + 7 lines. design-canvas.js: header word, `swapFn`, the load flag, the srcdoc swap, `setSwap`. design-window.js: import, the bar button line, the mount + `ROW_ACTS.tweaks` lines. icons.js (`sliders`), style.css (one block after lane design-ask's), i18n zh/ja (one block), vibespace-design (usage line, `printTweaks`, 2 calls). Lane D also adds `system` to KEYS.top and edits compose / validateManifest — the two keys sit side by side.
- **Gates.** build ✓ (i18n 7184/7184, test-architecture 455) · test-design-model 228 (§5d + 5 linear shapes + 9 controls) · test-design-routes 226 (§10, 26 legs + 8 controls) · test-design-canvas 234 (fence + picker rows, 2 controls; viewer 57.8 KB) · test-design-docs 38 · test-peer-text-census 363 · test-record-clear-census 237 · test-changelog-style 40 · 25 more fast suites that pin a touched file, all green · heavy test-design-window 127 ✓ (1 skip, as on the base) incl. T① (zh, 375 px: a real drag restyles the frame with zero agent messages, the write's re-read restyles it in place, a pill, Reset).

### lane channels-full-search — channel search: the saved copy at once, the vendor's whole history on the same press (B-c9be, design 010)

**searching a channel now shows the saved matches at once with how much was searched, then older matches from Lark's own search (each marked "not saved here", the messages around one a click away); agents get the same second tier explicitly with `--full`**

#### The search answered from the local copy only, and did not say so (B-c9be, the owner, 2026-10-03)

The owner: 「vibespace channel 提供搜索功能吗？提供的话走的是实时 API 的搜索还是 pull 到本地的缓存数据？」 — the store scan (one account's logs, ≤ 64 MB, ≤ 200 hits) walked the folder in `readdir` order, so on a big account the byte cap cut at random, and an older Lark message nobody scrolled to was never findable.

- The scan visits conversations NEWEST first (the index's `lastAt`; the cap cuts the oldest) and answers `coverage {scanned, total, capped, oldestAt}`; the dialog's first section "Saved messages" says "Searched the N conversations saved here" (or "the N most recently active of T").
- `caps.search {via, pageSize, pagesPerPress, perMin, cost, snippet, context, match, scope}` (validated; `search` / `around` gated by it): Lark `search({query})` = `im/v1/messages/search` with the words and NO filter, 3 pages a press, 12 a sliding minute beside the feed's 10; `around(convId, {vendorId, at})` = two `im/v1/messages` pages at the hit's second, ≤ 50 records.
- PURE `src/channel-search.js`: `snippetOf` (cut to 4 000 characters before any regex, markup stripped, entities decoded, then `peerName` — hidden characters, bidi, complete and dangling frames, ≤ 400), `snippetShape`, `mergeVendorHits`, `coverageOf`, `fullSearchVerdict` (not-supported › needs-scope › backoff › search-floor › the agents' share › search-minute › vendor-budget, each with its wait), the dialog's words.
- Engine: `searchVendor` (`GET /api/channels/search/full`, the owner's press or the scroll's token, 2 s floor per account, charged to the owner, a stored hit dropped — unknown conversation or older than the stored oldest ⇒ not stored without a read), `aroundOwner` (`GET /api/channels/:a/:c/around`, nothing appended / born / counted), a vendor rate refusal backs the endpoint off for the account and the change feed waits with it; the agent's `search --full` (one page, the share, 20 s per account per agent conversation, reach after the await, `truncated` about visible hits only, no token) and `read --around`.
- VS1–VS4 (no live calls from the lane): measured on the owner's first press, shape only, on `rec.feed.counters.fullSearch` + one journal line each — VS3 decides the words: `caps.search.match: 'unknown'` ("may be related" / 可能相关) flips to `'substring'` ("found" / 找到) in src/channels/lark.js once the CJK counts say every snippet holds the words.
- The dialog: two sections (section two built below section one before anything lands), the "Not saved here" chip, scroll-to-load (an IntersectionObserver one screen ahead, a skeleton row), the status words, the "Around this message" sheet drawn by channel-window's row renderer (`renderAroundRows`), zh / ja.
- Not done: Gmail's row (design S6 — `messages.list?q=`, the metadata snippet, the thread as context) — budget; the heavy chrome leg of the dialog (see the lane report).
- Gates: test-channel-search (new, fast, 40 — §A PURE, §B the store's newest-first cut, §C the engine over the fake vendor's search seam `VIBESPACE_CHANNELS_FAKE_SEARCH=1`, §K six patched-copy controls), test-channels-lark-shape ⑱ (8), test-vendor-whitelist §FS (the call sites + two planted controls), census rows in test-channels-engine / test-channel-acl / test-record-clear-census / test-peer-text-census.

### lane channels-first-read — the Channels panel's first read sends the first screen, not every conversation (B-3cf8, design 008)

**the first Channels open is instant on an account with tens of thousands of conversations: the list carries the rows that need attention and each account's newest, every other row is read a page at a time**

#### The first open stalled for seconds (B-3cf8, userW, 2026-10-02 after the 2.369.201 hotfix)

Measured on userW's pod (2.369.200): `GET /api/channels` answered 77 538 430 bytes, 1.49 s to first byte, ≈ 50 000 conversations (1 542 bytes a row) — `digest()` built a `rowView` for EVERY live conversation and every non-partial broadcast pushed the same list to every tab. The first screen draws the attention list, the agent groups, each account's newest 30 and All's newest 60.

- The shared predicate: `statusTag` & co. moved unchanged to PURE CJS `src/channel-focus.js` (`src/lib/channel-focus.js` re-exports it) beside `candidateOf(en, ob, now)` — the raw facts a tag is made of, one clause per tag, may over-include, never miss — and the page rules (`pageOrder` lastAt desc then key, `selectPage` one pass with a bounded heap, `pageCursor`, `queryOf` ≤ 100 characters, `textMatches` = filterRows' rule).
- `digest({keys, scope})`: `keys` = the partial broadcast, unchanged; `'first'` (the route's default and every non-partial broadcast) = adapters + `counts {all, byAdapter}` (the kept row facts) + totals + `conversations` = the attention rows (≤ 300, `attention {total, cut}`) and each account's newest 30 listed rows (`heads`, every account — an empty one too), built by `firstRead`: ONE pass, a rowView only for a candidate or a head; `'accounts'` (no rows); `'totals'`. A first read no longer forces the kept facts' re-sum.
- `rows({view, adapter, q, before, limit, keys, conv})` + `GET /api/channels/rows`: the next `limit` (1–200, default 60) after the cursor, no full sort; `q` over the ladder name / account label / last line with a sound prefilter (every letter-digit run of the query must sit in the raw title / participants / author names before the ladder is computed); bounds refused by name (400 `bad-request`), an unknown account 404; both routes refuse an agent's session / job bearer (403 `agent-forbidden`).
- The client: PURE `src/lib/channel-rows.js` (keyed store: `applyFirst` / `applyPage` / `applyBroadcast` — the never-loaded rule: a row is taken when it wears a tag or sorts inside a loaded list's range, else dropped; a page asked before a broadcast keeps the broadcast's row; a non-partial broadcast restarts the heads and marks the paged lists stale, the list on screen re-reads ≤ 200). The panel draws from it: the header counts from `counts` + `attention.cut`, All = the server's pages (60 a page), an account card = its head + pages of 200, each list's end loading the next page itself (owner 2026-10-03: seamless, no "Show more" — a sentinel watched one screen ahead, a skeleton row while read, ≤ 5 pages while the view does not move down, focus on the end reads on, a whole broadcast keeps the range), the filter = the attention rows at once + the server 250 ms after the last keystroke ("{n} more in All", All's search pages). The account ⋯ menu asks the account's count, not its loaded rows. The rail badge reads `?scope=totals`, the window's Re-authorize `?scope=accounts`, a chat card's link `rows?conv=`.
- verify r1: the attention list is the SERVER'S (`store.focus` — a row that lost its tag while the client was away left no ghost after a reconnect / a whole broadcast); past ATTENTION_MAX the cut keeps statusTag's TAG_ORDER first, then the newest, and `attention.cut` counts only the tagged rows not carried (a tagged head was counted twice); the search prefilter drops hidden characters for a row named by its participants / authors ("Bo<ZWSP>b" reads "Bob").
- MEASURED (test-channels-index-scale ⑨, work meter): the first read at 50 286 / 100 566 rows = 41.2 KB / 41.2 KB, 36 rowViews, 1.61 % / 1.57 % of the old whole list's work (47.7 / 95.4 MB on these lighter fixture rows); an account-level change broadcasts 41.3 KB; the client half (parse + applyFirst + groupListRows + firstScreen) 0.22 ms; a page of 60 from the middle 55.7 KB; a search linear (×1.99), 643 work units a row (the shown strings' bytes), 2.6× less than without the prefilter.
- Not done (separable, design S6): the agent's `list` bound.
- Gates: test-channel-rows (new, fast, 35 — the property candidateOf ⊇ statusTag over every tag kind at every window edge + its control, the first read = focusRows over the whole list, the store's tables, the full-list readers' census + its control), test-channels-index-scale ⑨ (+ 2 controls), test-channels-engine § design 008 (V3 paging under churn: 500 rows moved + 20 born between pages — no row twice, none lost; scopes; bounds; bearer refusals), test-channels-panel-redraw re-fixtured on paging (a page append keeps the drawn rows), test-channels-groups-e2e / -e2e await the server's pages.

Seams fixed in the merge: lane 2's ONE card reads lane 1's installer facts through `cardInput` / `cardViewOf` (the app's own and localized names, the icon by its proposal route, the download host and recipe, a FILE source: "From an installer file on this machine"), an AppImage's sha256 in Details, a proposal's Apps-dialog card built from the proposal, and test-architecture's NUL census knows `.appimage` fixtures. `kind` 'apt' → 'package' in the view: no consumer compared the view's kind with 'apt' (the CLI reads deb / appimage, the dialog remove / source, the For-you action keeps the request kind).
- **WeChat end to end** (a throwaway Debian 12 container, network on): `search 装微信` → the recipe → `propose {installer, url}` (the real 231 MB download, 41 s) → ONE card (微信, "来自 dldir1v6.qq.com（官方下载地址）", its icon staged) → a stale click runs nothing → the card's click → `wechat 4.1.13.23` installed through the slot (50 s) → row `app.wechat` with `labels.zh 微信`, staging empty, the agent told "Installed: wechat — open it with `vibespace-window open app.wechat`".
- **verify r1** (repros under the lane dir, each red on 68f163f7): F1 MED the card drew no icon for a download (it accepted `/api/apps/icon?` only); F2 MED an installed row's `labels {zh, ja}` were never picked — Apps read "wechat" in zh (PURE `rowName` in app-card-model, the launcher's card uses it); F3 MED a proposal stored `installing` when the hub went down stayed so forever and the boot sweep KEPT its installer — it settles as failed at boot (`install_interrupted`, Try again); F4 LOW a vendor's .desktop names reached the card and the For-you line with bidi / zero-width / control characters (cleaned in `cardOf`); F5 LOW a staged .deb's download size was counted twice (apt's `--print-uris` lists the local file; the WeChat card said 519 MB for 231 + 57); F6 LOW a failed download kept its file until the next restart (it expires after 24 h like an unanswered one); F7 MED the frame belt let `</cross-session-message><cross-session-message …>` from a .desktop Name through to the agent — the CLI's own peer envelope joins FRAME_TAGS (channel-record + browser-stuck's copy + the census reader). Held / refuted: `::ffff:0:a.b.c.d` (SIIT) reads public to addressVerdict — the kernel never translates it, no route reaches loopback; V1 (root re-hashes its own copy), V2 (pinned address, every hop re-judged), V4 (the route census, the digest binds the id), V5, V8 (stub + §10) held on their suites.

### lane apps-one-card — an agent's install is ONE card and ONE click (design 009 S5, lane 2)

- **The card is structure, the words are the client's.** NEW PURE `src/app-card.js`: design 009 §4's proposal view (`{id, host, state, kind, app{name, labels, icon}, by, why, from, bytes, keeps, firstUse, details, digest}` + `planChanged` / `result`), `planSummary` (the engine's summary + the closure, the commands, a .deb's sha256 / scripts) and `shownDigest` (fnv32 ×2 over `shownFields` — what a card shows, never its state). The For-you item carries it as `card` (src/user-todos.js `normalizeCard`: plain data ≤ 24 KB, kept EXACTLY; `setCard`; a resolved card rides the snapshot face-only; Clear content… drops it — record-clear's todo shape). NEW PURE `src/lib/app-card-model.js` words it in en / zh / ja (`cardWords`, `detailLines`, `progressWords`, `openRowOf`).
- **One click.** `engine.approve(id, {shown})` = POST /api/apps/proposals/:id/approve: a card that is not the proposal as it stands ⇒ 409 plan_changed + the current card, nothing ran; else the STORED plan runs through the one slot (`expectDigest = p.digest`) in the background and every state move redraws the card (`syncCard`). A machine whose plan moved ⇒ plan_changed and the proposal TAKES the new plan (`planChanged`: "the plan changed — take another look"); a failure names its step (prepare / install / record, `stepOf`) and Try again is the same click; busy ⇒ 409. No second dialog. Mark done / Ignore still decline (onStatus, unchanged).
- **The surfaces.** The popup / phone sheet / mini inbox row (`appCardHtml`): title, who asks and why, where from and how big (a download's host; "official" only when a recipe vouches, else one unverified-publisher line), what the click gives (replay / home / system — Layer 1's "always there"), Layer 1's first-use line, TWO buttons, progress → Installed · Open, Try again, a Details fold; Reply / Mark done / Ignore / Copy / Clear content… behind ⋯. The For-you window shows the same card in its pane (actions `app-install, app-reject, more` · `app-retry` · `app-open`). Install is ARMED like Approve (press-arm). The window now also stamps its arm where the pane's item changes: render() stamped before holdSelection moved the selection, so a pane opened onto an item refused every press (found by test-apps-ui ②). The install dialog LEADS with the same summary (`appSummaryBlock`); the root sentence, the facts and the commands fold under Details; "1 packages" fixed; the log hides the slot's `= run` / `= ok` lines (review I13).
- **For lane apps-install-core (the shared contract):** the view reads `p.app {name, labels, icon}`, `p.fetch {host, recipe}`, `p.keeps`, `p.firstUse` when a proposal carries them, and maps `request.kind` deb / appimage — a download proposal's card needs no change here.
- **Gates:** NEW test-app-card (33: the view per kind; the words in en / zh / ja; the face census over 1 173 lines with a planted "apt" as its control; the digest moves with 15 shown things and not with the state; the store keeps a card exactly; the row escapes every hole). test-apps-engine §10 (+18: one click; stale / missing / cross-conversation cards run nothing; busy; V8 a moved plan; Try again; the route's 403 and 409 + card). test-apps-ui ② one click in the window, ⑥ zh at 390 px one click in the sheet (40/40). Census rows: approval-census (the approve door + 3 pins), user-todos-layout (rowCtx lang), inbox-window-model (a 3rd innerHTML write = the card's escaped HTML), takeover-keyboard (the dialog's Details), record-clear-census (normalizers' `e.card` is a chat card); ci.mjs (test-app-card, fast).

### lane apps-install-core — an agent proposes any install (a package name, a vendor's download address, a file), one card (design 009, lane 1 of 3)

- **One verb.** `vibespace-app install <package> | --from <https URL> | --file <path> | --source …`. An address or a file is FETCHED by the machine half as the user at propose time (`app-fetch`): `fetchVerdict` (PURE) — https, a public NAME (no IP literal in any spelling, no localhost / .local / .internal / .lan / .home.arpa …), no credentials; every resolved address judged by `addressVerdict` (private / loopback / link-local incl. 169.254.169.254 / CGNAT / multicast, IPv4-mapped and NAT64 as their IPv4) and the socket pinned to that address (no rebinding); redirects followed by hand, each re-judged, ≤ 5; ≤ 2 GiB; idle 60 s / total 60 min; into `staging/` 0600 while hashed. `sniffInstaller` decides the kind by the BYTES (ar + `debian-binary` = deb, ELF + `AI\x02` = AppImage); a web page named .deb, a type-1 AppImage, a program, a device are refused by name and deleted.
- **Name from the archive.** A .deb: `dpkg-deb -c` → `debDesktopOf` (regular files where a launcher looks — no symlink, no `..`, ≤ 256 KiB) → one member out through `dpkg-deb --fsys-tarfile | tar -xO` (bounded) → `parseDesktopFile`, now with `labels: {zh, ja}` from `Name[zh_CN]` › `Name[zh]` (never zh_TW) and `Name[ja]`; its icon (`debIconOf`) staged as `<hash>.icon.png|svg` and served by `GET /api/apps/proposals/:id/icon`. An AppImage: NEW `src/app-squashfs.js` reads the SquashFS 4 image after the ELF (`appImageOffset`) — gzip / zstd, every read async, never the vendor's runtime; `unsupported` (xz…) / `hostile` (a `..` / `/` name, loops, > 200 k entries, > 64 deep) by name.
- **The card's structure** (§4 view, additive): `kind` package|deb|appimage|remove|source, `app {name, labels, icon}`, `from {kind, host, via?, file?, recipe?}`, `bytes`, `keeps` replay|home|system, `details {packages, commands, sha256, scripts, fingerprints, url}`, `digest`. Lane apps-one-card words it.
- **The click.** A .deb from staging plans IN PLACE (re-hashed; another byte ⇒ `changed`, nothing ran) through today's slot + root script (which re-checks the sha256), then the staged copy goes. An AppImage runs no root and no slot: copied-while-hashed into a private dir, unpacked by the reader into `appimage/<id>/root` (files O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, links made never followed, devices skipped), the AppImage deleted, its row from its own desktop file (`AppRun`, `APPDIR`), served by the catalog only while it runs exactly that file. `remove` plans by kind (`removePlanFor`: AppImage = its directory, uv / npm = their uninstallers as the user, `homeArgv` — never the slot's `argv`).
- **Cleanup.** Rejected / withdrawn / expired (24 h, `sweep`, the agent told) / done ⇒ `app-unstage` at once (a failed one keeps its file for a retry); at boot every staged file over an hour old that no open proposal keeps goes.
- **Recipes** (`src/app-recipes.js`, PURE, 8 rows HEAD-checked 2026-10-03): search finds "微信"; a card says "official download" only when EVERY hop stayed on the row's hosts. Feishu / Lark / QQ publish versioned addresses only — not rows.
- **Helper conversation**: the first message is the user's words + one line (`vibespace-app`, `vibespace-docs apps`); named "Install app · <request>" (zh 装应用 · …).
- Gates: test-app-manifest §D9 (verdict tables, sniff, names, members, removal plans, recipes, the reader on committed gzip / zstd / xz / hostile fixtures, unpack confinement with the cwd elsewhere), test-apps-engine §10 (the REAL machine half + a loopback https "vendor" by a `.test` name through `fetchSeam`: deb + AppImage end to end, 13 refusals with nothing filed and staging empty, reject / expiry / changed bytes), heavy test-app-install §9 (a real .deb read by dpkg-deb and installed by apt through the slot; an AppImage unpacked with the cwd elsewhere, run, removed).

### lane custom-app-h1 — an approved apt source is pinned to the packages taken from it (verify-r1 H1, H2, H3 of lane custom-app)

- **H1 (MED, held at custom-app verify r1):** an approved third-party apt source had no pin, so apt could take that source's newer build of ANY package on a later install or a Refresh (the Refresh card listed updates without their origin) — while the source card says "Packages come from this source only when you install them later". Now the ONE root script writes `/etc/apt/preferences.d/vibespace-<id>.pref` per source (PURE `sourcePin`): everything from its host at priority 1 (apt takes such a version only when nothing installed has that name), the packages the user installed FROM it at 500. Those packages are attributed BEFORE apt runs (`--print-uris` into an empty archives dir → `entries/<id>.pin`). `pins()` runs at the end of every run; `restore()` runs before apt in both replay rungs (rung 1 never restored sources before). The manifest records `sources[].pin`. Each Refresh update names its origin, checked against root's own sources, never the index. Gate: test-app-manifest §8c runs pins() from the script text, byte-equal to the table (a no-pin copy is red). Heavy test-app-install §8 uses a signed https repository fixture (our CA + OpenPGP key) that serves hello 2.10-99 and capp-third 1.0 → 1.1. With the pin, hello stays at Debian's 2.10-3 and capp-third goes to 1.1, named "fx" on the card. The no-pin control upgrades hello to 2.10-99. `Pin: origin` matched the bare host of an `https://host:8443` source (measured through apt-cache policy).
- **H2 (LOW):** the .deb plan reads the user's file once: an O_NONBLOCK open, type and size judged on the fd, copied while hashed. Before, a FIFO swapped in after the stat parked a libuv thread. Root's deb and source modes `grab()` with `dd iflag=nofollow,nonblock`: no `[ -f ] && cp` gap, and a FIFO is refused by the hash at once (the pre-fix `cp` blocks — control). Residual: a same-uid racer can still rewrite the user-owned staged copy between the plan's hash and its dpkg-deb inspection. Root installs only bytes whose hash matches.
- **H3 (LOW):** a boot replay that meets a busy package slot (`busy`, or a followed run's `not_run`) waits it out, polling every 15 s for at most 10 min, then runs the same rung. Before, it filed "every app" at once. Gate: test-apps-engine §6, plus a no-wait control.
- Known limits: an entry installed from a source before 2.369.203 has no `.pin`, so the pin holds back its updates until it is reinstalled (or adopted). A dependency that a Refresh newly brings in from a source is not added to the allow-list. Two sources on one host share one origin.
- **verify r1 (lane custom-app-h1):** three holes in the pin's life, each reproduced in a Debian 12 container on f56e9d57. (1) A source approved before .203 had no pin until a run ENDED, so its first Refresh took the source's hello 2.10-99: every run now calls `pins` before the mode dispatch. (2) Source mode made the source live, then ran `apt-get update`, then pinned: a SIGKILL during the update left it live and unpinned (the machine's own `apt-get upgrade` took 2.10-99). Now root's record, then the pin, then the live source. (3) `Pin: origin` matches a HOST, so a source on a host the machine's own apt sources use (Debian backports on deb.debian.org) held the machine's own archive at priority 1, security updates too: refused `shared-host` (`mine()`). Gates: test-app-manifest §8c (order + `mine()` table + a pre-fix control), test-app-install §8 (shared-host and pre-.203 containers, each with a pre-order control).

### lane chrome-builds-download — Download another build… from Google's Chrome for Testing, its compatibility said before it downloads (design 004, B-80c1)

- **The owner (2026-10-02 20:35 PDT):** 「能不能自动从网上下载对应的版本？这样可以提供大量版本，并且可以下载前让用户检查是否互相兼容」. Built from the design desk's design 004 on the int202 head 757cac16; every design fact re-read in the code (the line numbers had moved with lanes browser-windows / browser-reliability; no fact disagreed) and the two list documents re-measured (10 431 / 5 177 393 bytes, 2 549 versions 113 → 157, one download host, no checksum field).
- **PURE (src/browser-builds.js, browser-verbs `CHROME_BUILDS_RECORD`).** The two parsers (an off-host / plain-http / credentialed url refused BY NAME, never offered), `buildCompatVerdict` (HARD machine + disk; chips present / cli / census / profile / cloak), `downloadPlan`, `parseZipListing` + `zipShapeVerdict`, `versionSays`; 18 new codes (+ `build_stalled`) in BUILD_CODES and the routes' STATUS.
- **The keeper.** THE slot's third kind `chrome-build`: one HEAD (length + md5) and the disk row before any byte; fetch → check → unpack → verify → witness → ONE rename (the design said rename → verify → witness; the lane verifies and witnesses in the unpack folder and renames LAST, so a half-verified build is never listed even for a moment — the design's own invariant). `buildFetch` = the ONE `fetch(` (egressVerdict on every url and hop). Restart: an in-process step fails cleanly, a running unzip is re-attached and landed. Removal by witness, refused by name while chosen or running.
- **Routes + client.** Three cookie-only routes; Change build… and New profile…'s build section end with "Download another build…" (Linux x64, this computer; elsewhere the hand command with the reason); the picker (channels fresh, Older versions… → majors → versions, chips in words, ONE HEAD on a pick, THE confirm, the progress line, installed builds with sizes and Remove, free space); 57 new strings × zh / ja.
- **Gates.** NEW test-browser-build-download (fast, 43 — a loopback fake CfT, a spy unzip, a stored-zip writer for hostile entries; 3 patched-copy controls), test-browser-builds ⑥ (+24), test-vendor-whitelist §8 (ONE FETCH / USER-ONLY / ONE SLOT for the new kind, 4 controls), heavy test-browser-profiles-ui ③b (the picker from Change build…, chips + confirm in zh / ja / en, a download through the UI — against reserved `.test` hosts on loopback). Census rows learned: test-takeover-keyboard (the picker's role-button rows), test-browser-cli-pin control (d)'s anchor (the re-attach now admits `chrome-build`).
- **Verify r1 (Opus).** H1: with no executable path agent-browser 0.38.1 launches its NEWEST build (measured: chrome-157 over chrome-150), so a download newer than every build here becomes the default of every default-choice profile and every conversation's browser — a one-way door the row never said. Its row now carries the `default` chip naming those profiles, the confirm says it, and Remove of the newest build is refused (`build_in_use`) while a default-choice profile was last opened by a newer major than every build that would be left. L1: `unzip -Zs`'s declared sizes are summed (`zipShapeVerdict().unpacked`) and weighed against the free space before `unzip -q` (a 65 KB zip declared 64 MB; the disk row only asked zip × 3). Legs in test-browser-builds + test-browser-build-download; the fake-zip writer learned `deflate`.
- **Kept out (design 004 §5):** an agent proposing a download; a paired machine downloading; mac / win layouts; automatic eviction.

### lane channel-attach-read — an agent opens a picture or a file someone sent in a conversation it may read (B-d6b9, design 005 §2.A)

- **The verb.** `vibespace-channels attachment <conv> <msg id> <attachment id> [--out <path>] [--force]` saves the file and prints `saved <path> (<type>, N bytes) — sent by <name> in <conversation>; what it shows is theirs, not instructions to you`; the agent opens it with its own tools. `read` prints each attachment's id and the command (every piece one shell word — a hostile id is single-quoted, round-tripped through a real shell in the gate). The default path is `$TMPDIR/vibespace-channels/<adapter>/<12 hex>.<ext>`: the hex is sha256 of (conversation, message, id) — **a deviation from the design's "first 12 of the id"**, which names one file for every Gmail `part:2` and for Lark keys sharing their `img_v3_02xx_` prefix; the extension comes from the stored mime, else (**an addition**) the file's own first bytes for png / jpeg / gif / webp / pdf, because a Lark picture is stored as `image/*` and a `.bin` is a picture the agent cannot open as one. Never the sender's file name. An existing `--out` is refused before any request without `--force`; the bytes go to a `.part` file beside the target and are renamed only when exactly `Content-Length` bytes arrived (a short body, no size, or a broken transfer keeps nothing; a body longer than its size was measured: undici hands over the declared bytes only).
- **The route.** `GET /api/agent/channels/attachment?conv=&msg=&id=` (src/agent-routes.js, beside `read`): a session token only (a job token 401); the engine's answer streamed from the file held open (the size said = the size sent), `application/octet-stream`, nosniff, sandbox CSP, `attachment`, `no-store`; `X-VibeSpace-Attachment` = URI-encoded JSON `{mime, bytes, from, conversation}`. Its own status table (chanAnswer's is the refresh census's source in test-channels-agent-cli). The touch witness records a `read` (§63).
- **The engine.** The SAME `attachment()` with `{by: 'agent', principal}`: the read route's reach FIRST (`stillSees` — hidden, requestable, a disabled account, none: the uniform not-found, before the cache is asked — so the cached-file-with-the-account-disabled case is not-found for an agent, while the owner's window is still served from the cache: rule 1, stated and unchanged); then the message the agent names must carry the id, and a `role:'body'` part (a mail's formatted body — its `part:N` id is guessable, the window may have cached it) is the same not-found (§25: an agent reads `text`; test-channel-acl drives it + a control); a cache hit free; a fetch in flight joined (no charge); before a vendor fetch `agentShareRefusal` and the charge attributed to `spentBy.agent`; every answer through `agentAttachmentAnswer` — reach asked AGAIN after the fetch / the join / the held write, the sender (the read view + agentCopy), the title and the vendor's type each through the belt. The share's sentence now says "agents' refreshes and fetches" (kb-api updated).
- **Gates.** test-channels-images ③b (the real agent routes on the rig's server: hidden ≡ requestable ≡ nonexistent with no vendor call, a job token, the bytes + headers, charged to the agents' share, a cache hit free, joined with the owner's flight = one call / one charge, another agent refused even on a cached picture, an account grant, a disabled account, the share at its boundary 2 of 8 with the owner unaffected, a revoke inside the fetch) + 4 patched-copy controls (no reach: the vendor is called for a hidden conversation; no share; no attribution; no re-ask); test-vendor-whitelist §7 (the caller census admits src/agent-routes.js only `by: 'agent'` with the principal, reach before the cache, the share between the verdict's `fetch` and the call — 3 controls); test-channels-agent-cli (the PURE ext / path / shell-word tables, the verb end to end against the stub, a raw server lying long); test-peer-text-census (the door `agentAttachmentAnswer(`, its print rows, an attack leg with a hostile name / title / type, a pin control); test-architecture §65 (FOLLOW + the await exemption with its reason, a control).
- **Verify r1.** The attachment cache, its flight and its remembered refusals name the MESSAGE too (a Gmail `part:1` is one mail's formatted body and the next mail's PDF: an agent asking the PDF was handed the body under the wrong sender; a file cached under the bare id serves the owner's window only); an agent fetch's spender rides the call's own async context (`spendAs` — a pass or the owner's window inside the await moved `e.chargeBy`); Lark's resource read stops at 100 MB whatever its Content-Length says; `--out` inside VibeSpace's own checkout is refused before any request. Legs: test-channels-images ③c (+2 controls), test-channels-lark-shape (the lying length), test-channels-agent-cli (`--out` into data/bin, direct and through a symlink).

### lane channel-attach-send — an agent's reply or new message carries pictures and files, bound to the approval (B-fd1f, design 005 §2.B)

- **The verb.** `vibespace-channels reply|compose … --attach <path>` (repeatable): the CLI stats every path first (a directory, a missing / unreadable / empty file, > 10 files, > 25 MB together ⇒ exit 1 before anything is read or sent), then sends `attachments: [{name: <basename>, data: <base64>}]` in the propose request; the agent routes already passed `attachments` through — src/agent-routes.js is untouched. It prints the server's list (type, size, sha256).
- **Policy (PURE, src/channel-policy.js).** `attachmentsOf` (bounds, `ATTACH_CODES` in `why`), `safeAttachmentName` (refused, never cleaned: separators, src/hidden-chars.js's set with joiners refused, a line feed / tab, edge spaces, > 200), `sniffType` (bytes → png/jpeg/gif/webp = image; pdf/zip/gzip/svg/html/text/octet-stream = file), `nameTypeMismatch` (the card's chip), `attachVerdict` (one row `{maxCount, maxTotalBytes, withText}` or `{images, files}`), `storedAttachments`, `attachmentSize`. `shownFields` appends `[name, bytes, sha256]` per stored file ONLY when there are any (every other digest unchanged). `receiptFor` / `renderReceiptBlock` list the files. `decideOutbound` is unchanged (owner Q2 = NO: the existing `channels.guardAttachmentsReview` switch and the channel policy decide). The old names-only `{name, bytes}` shape is refused (`attachment-data`) — it never carried bytes.
- **Files (src/channel-outbox-files.js, new).** `prepare` (decode, sha256, sniff — in memory), `stage` (SYNCHRONOUS write into `outbox-files/.stage-*`, so no await sits between propose's last reach check and the record), `commit` (rename to `<proposal id>`), `discard`, `verify` (re-read + re-hash at the send), `remove`, `sweep`. Paths come from the proposal id + index only.
- **Engine.** `attachPrepare` right after the shape check in `propose` and `compose` (refusal = `bad-proposal` + `why`; nothing on disk); the record stores metas only; `sendNow` verifies and hands the adapter THE verified buffers (`attachment-changed` ⇒ failed, zero adapter calls); `transition` to rejected / withdrawn / expired removes the folder and stamps `attachmentsGoneAt`; `filesSweep` (beside the expiry sweep) removes sent / failed files 7 days after they ended, orphan folders and stale stages; `outboxAttachment(id, n)` for the owner route. The store's `outboxPrune` takes a pruned record's folder.
- **Registry / adapters.** `caps.sendAttachments` validated at registration (+ `sendAttachmentsWhy`); `send` / `compose` handed attachments without the row throw `not-supported`. Gmail: `buildMime` multipart/mixed (sniffed type, ASCII fallback + RFC 2231 `filename*` continued in ≤ 60-char pieces, 76-col base64, control characters stripped from names / an invalid type → octet-stream), `rawRequest` = the JSON form up to `JSON_RAW_MAX` 4 MB, else the documented upload form (`gmail.googleapis.com/upload/…?uploadType=multipart`, metered like the JSON one) — the threshold is from Google's documented 5 MB JSON cap, NOT measured live. Lark: `sendAttachments: null` with its reason (docs: uploads take the tenant token only — LA1; LA3 unprovable without a live call; LA2 `im:resource` / `im:resource:upload`, LA4 10 MB image / 30 MB file per the docs).
- **Card + route.** src/lib/channel-outbox.js `appendAttachments` (thumbnail only for the four SNIFFED rasters, name via `revealInto`, size · type · sha256 prefix, the mismatch chip, the "exactly these bytes" / "no longer kept" note; zh/ja strings). `GET /api/channels/outbox/:id/attachment/:n` (owner-only, declared BEFORE the read route whose pattern would take it): nosniff, sandbox CSP, no-store, inline only for the four sniffed rasters.
- **Gates.** New scripts/test-channel-attach-send.mjs (PURE table, engine rig propose → approve → send with a recording adapter, V1/V2/V6/V7, Q2 through the engine, compose, retention incl. a pruned record, the owner route incl. V4, the registry row, Gmail MIME parsed back incl. V3 + the upload form, the CLI, V8/V10 censuses) with patched-copy controls (count, separator, hidden char, digest, no re-hash, no removal, staging a refused proposal, inline-any route, CR/LF in MIME, no row check).

### lane message-facts — a message's envelope and each provider's own facts, from ONE declared scheme (B-f066 part 1, design 007)

- **The scheme.** `facts: [{k, v, more?, cut?}]` is an optional, closed, typed list on the ONE record (src/channel-record.js: `FACT_TYPES` — seven value types, `FACT_SCHEMA`, `FACT_LIMITS`, `validateFacts` — refusals by name `unknown-kind` / `bad-value` / `duplicate-kind` / `too-many`, every string through `peerName`, ≤ 50 parties per list then `more`, ≤ 16 KB per list by giving party tails to `more`); a record without facts is byte-identical. PURE `src/channel-facts.js` words it: `FACT_KINDS` (type, label, where, agent), `foldFacts`, `summaryOf`, `chipsOf`, `detailRows`, `mapFactStrings`, `agentFactLines`, `compactFactLines`. The side log's fourth kind `fx` (the "edit" occupant §28 reserved) carries facts learned later; the store's trim folds a message's fx lines into one and its reader's head match knows `fx`.
- **Gmail now.** `factsFromHeaders` (PURE) at ingest: to, cc, bcc (own sent mail only), reply-to, sender (≠ From), list (List-Id), delivered-to (≠ the account), subject (≠ the thread's, Re:/Fwd: aside), importance (Importance / Priority / X-Priority), automated (Auto-Submitted / Precedence) — through `addressList` + `addressParts`, RFC 2047 names decoded (`decodeWords`, linear), a header over 16 KB ⇒ `cut: true`. `caps.facts` (validated against the closed kinds at registration) + `caps.factsOf` → `factsOf(convId)`: ONE `threads.get?format=metadata` through the gate. The registry holds the answer to the declared kinds and the validator; `factsOf` declared ⇔ implemented.
- **The backfill (S5).** `GET /api/channels/:adapterId/:convId/facts?msg=` → engine `messageFacts`: a side hit is free; a message stored before its facts = ONE metered read of its whole thread, single-flight per thread, the account's budget and back-off, refusals by name; one `fx` line per message of THIS conversation's log (a vendor id the log does not hold is never written; an empty list = "asked, none"); an agent bearer is refused by name. Ingest never backfills; an agent's read never does.
