### lane message-facts-lark — Lark's own per-message facts as chips (B-f066 part 2, design 007 "Lark now")

- **Four rows, no new type.** `via` (party), `forwarded-from` (party), `edited` (time), `recalled` (flag) in channel-record `FACT_SCHEMA` + channel-facts `FACT_KINDS`, all `where: 'chip'` (a chat message with chips only shows them beside the time, no line of its own); `edited` / `recalled` are `mutable` (an `fx` may bring them late). Lark's `caps.facts` declares the four; no `factsOf`.
- **Lark emits them at ingest** (`factsOfItem`, module-private, called by `toRecord` — the poll, history, push and by-id paths all pass it): `sender_type: 'app'` ⇒ `via {id: app_id, name: the head's name}`; `msg_type: 'merge_forward'` ⇒ `forwarded-from {}`; `updated: true` ⇒ `edited` at `update_time` (no readable instant ⇒ no fact); `deleted: true` ⇒ `recalled`. An unedited person's message emits none (keys byte-identical). `author.isBot`, the "[deleted]" / "[forwarded messages]" texts and `raw` unchanged. `recordView` renames the `via` party with the head when an app's name is learned later, through `validateFacts`.
- **Two scheme changes, by row property / value type — no kind named, no engine / CLI change:** (1) the list item of a merged forward never names the original sender, so a `party` row may declare `nameless: true` — `v: {}` is "a party the vendor did not name" (validateFacts accepts it only there; chipsOf prints the row's `chipBare` — "forwarded"; agentFactLines prints the bare key); (2) the chip printer had no `time` branch (Gmail emits no time): `chipsOf` hands a time chip's instant over and channel-facts-view.js words it in the chip's title in the device's locale.
- **Gates.** test-channel-facts §10 (+21): the rows, the nameless rule, emitted ⊆ declared over EVERY recorded Lark item through the real toRecord (CONTROL: a copy emitting an undeclared `importance` is flagged; without the facts fixtures `edited` / `forwarded-from` are flagged unexercised), the name door end to end (CONTROL: a copy whose record skips peerName stores the raw 800-char bidi name), the engine page, the agent's line, edited / recalled arriving late as `fx`. test-channels-lark-shape ⑤c (+12) over the recorded shapes + a new `messagesFacts` fixture page (an edit, a merged forward, an app that updated its card, a recall); the via rename's two doors (CONTROL: both removed ⇒ red). test-channel-record: one SITES row (the via name). Heavy test-channel-window-render ⑬b: a zh Lark room — "经 Facts Bot 发送" / "已编辑" (title = the instant) / "已转发" / "已撤回" in the head, a plain message without any.
- **Not in this lane:** noticing an edit or a recall AFTER a message was stored (a re-delivered copy is a dedup no-op by vendorId); the `fx` path exists. Lark records stored before this lane carry no facts (`raw` lacks `update_time` / `deleted`; nothing is backfilled).

- **terra / luna corrected** ($2/$12, $0.20/$1.20), **gpt-5-codex / 5.1-codex(-max) / 5.2-codex rows**, long rule on 5.5 / 5.4, and 6.1-sol / 6-luna (on the official table, 0 rows yet). Cache-write rates are on the 5.6/6 rows (1.25× input); the walker still stores cw 0 for codex.
- **Stale stored rows:** setPricing saves every row, so an untouched old shipped gpt row on disk now takes the new default at load (`SUPERSEDED_DEFAULTS`); an edited row stays.
- **Retired Claude ids** (Opus 4 / 4.1 / 3, Haiku 3.5 / 3, Mythos Preview) got exact keys; 0 ledger rows — correctness for imports. The binary oracle now names claude-opus-4-0 / 4-1 / claude-3-5-haiku.
- **Fork double count.** Both walkers skip a forked rollout's replay (a token_count within 2 s of the fork's session_meta; local corpus 1,714/1,714, 0 false); migration `2026-10-archive-codex-fork-replays` archives the 1,661 rows already stored, with a reason each (src/codex-fork-ledger-purge.js).

A rerun after a crash between a shard's archive append and its rename no longer archives the rows twice. On a copy of the production ledger the migration archived 1,661 rows (278.5M tokens), kept + archived = the original, and a second run did nothing. ### lane presets-migration — a dropped override key leaves the release; the presets summary follows a change of layer (B-8145)

Found testing the fleet switch to the cluster presets Secret on a test release (2026-10-02 21:05 PDT), two defects. (1) The chart wrote the release's override through the release Secret's `stringData:`. helm's upgrade is a 3-way patch that nulls a dropped key in the field the old manifest named it in; `stringData` is write-only (the API server folds it into `data` and never stores it), so dropping `gdrive.clients` left `data.gdriveClients` in place, still projected as `override/gdrive-clients.json` — identical keys override the cluster per key, so a later rotation in the cluster Secret would never have reached that user. Now the override lives in its OWN Secret, `<release>-preset-override`, rendered with `data:` (b64enc) and owned whole by the chart (`data: {}` with no block); the projected volume's release source reads it; the release Secret carries no preset key under the volume form (the env form, `presets.volume=false`, stays byte-identical to 2.369.199). A release on the 2.369.200 chart keeps its stringData leftovers in the release Secret, no longer projected; deploy/README's migration section now says to drop the legacy blocks equal to the cluster's and how to list and remove the leftover keys. That upgrade rolls the pod once (the source is a new Secret); later override changes stay Secret-only. (2) `src/server/cluster-presets.js` replaced its snapshot only when the merged VALUES differed, so an equal override removed (the same values, now from the cluster) left `status()` — and `/api/integrations` `presets.groups` — on "release". The reader now compares the attribution too (`attributionOf` = the sorted `layerOf` pairs): the snapshot follows and the listeners run with `{kinds: [], sources}`, so the wiring re-pushes the summary; the journal line and the cards' re-derive stay for value changes only.

Gates: test-helm-render (heavy, 28; H new) — helm's 3-way merge modelled on the rendered Secrets (kind/k3d-free): a dropped key leaves the override Secret and `override/` on this chart, and on a 2.369.200 → this upgrade (leftovers stay in the release Secret, unread); the same model on the 2.369.200 chart reproduces the finding; CONTROL a chart copy rendering the override Secret through `stringData:` keeps the dropped key projected. test-cluster-presets (fast, 228; §4 new) — a release migrated with blocks equal to the cluster's, then upgraded without them, through the REAL integrations wiring: the summary and the `cluster-presets-updated` push move from "release" to "cluster", no journal line, no card re-derive, back again when an equal override returns, a cluster rotation shadowed while the override is projected and in effect once it is gone; CONTROL a values-only copy leaves the summary on "release" and pushes nothing.

### lane pool-scarce-lanes — pool placement keeps scarce model lanes for the conversations that need them (B-8a65)

Design desk 001 (`pool-scarce-lanes`, Fable), owner Q1 = yes (the spare lane leads the EDF deadline) and Q2 = yes (S5, added mid-lane 2026-10-03 03:37Z: 「Opus 便宜」). Owner, 2026-10-02: 「如果一个claude session在用opus，自动选择账号的时候优先选择fable用尽了的，避免占据fable额度（因为fable也要用全局额度）。然后想一想这个东西怎么做成针对不同provider普适的方案。」 The design's F5: 15 claude members each report ONE scoped lane, "Fable"; three are Fable-rich (72 / 71 / 52 %) and also hold the most 7d — exactly the members EDF and most-remaining handed an Opus session.

- **S1 — the projection hands back what it set aside** (src/model-family.js): `projectCacheForFamily` → `{ ...cache, scopedWeekly, spareScoped }`, view-only; a null family or no scoped lanes ⇒ the cache object itself (the storm's identity control holds).
- **S2 — the order** (src/account-pool-auto.js): `spareLaneRemaining` (MIN over the lanes that state a spend; null sorts as rich), every candidate row carries `spare`, `edfCompare` leads with it — after the manual priority, before the deadline. The sealed orders and the pool default decide on unprojected views ⇒ a tie ⇒ byte-identical.
- **S3 — the spawn**: `placing: true`, the chooser's one word (src/server/usage-pool-engine.js); a usable default is left for a settleable member with strictly less spare (`spare-lane`).
- **S5 — running conversations**: a hot pool's proactive pass moves an idle conversation off a MEASURED spare lane when the gain exceeds `SPARE_MOVE_MARGIN_PCT` (15); a warm cache holds it (`warm-cache`), a turn in flight holds it (`spare-hold`); one notice, SPARE_LANE_KEY (en/zh/ja dictionaries).
- **Where the build bent the design.** (1) The `healthy` early return is skipped under `placing` — else a healthy default never reaches the tier. (2) The design's literal `bestSettle.spare < (cur.spare ?? 100)` places a spawn onto an UNKNOWN member (`null < 70` is true in JS): both sides carry `?? 100`, pinned by a patched-copy control. (3) S5 needed two anti-flap rules the design did not spell out: the margin, and a guard on the EDF tier (never onto MORE spare lane). Without the guard the two tiers bounce a cold conversation every tick (replay control: ≥ 10 moves in 12 ticks); the guard also closes an S1–S4 gap — EDF dragged an Opus conversation off a spent member onto a Fable-rich one with a sooner week. (4) A running conversation moves only off a MEASURED spare lane; a spawn keeps "unknown = rich". (5) Four storm negative controls (§1, §5, §7, §11d) now read either sentence: the pre-fix mis-projected move leaves the rich member through the spare tier first, whose words name the same wrong family. (6) The user line rides in the lane report (the style gate refuses a newest user entry two patches past package.json's 2.369.200).
- **Gates.** test-pool-auto: new section "THE SPARE LANE (B-8a65)" — asserts 1–11 of the design, S5 (cold → moves, warm → held, mid-turn → held, no member better by more than the margin → stays, unknown current → stays, Fable → never, cold pool → never), V5 jitter replays, a seeded sweep byte-identical to 0e7dc5b4 for every view without a differing spare lane (+ 600 spawns with `placing` landing where they did), seven patched-copy controls (no key, unknown = spent, the unguarded candidate side, no spawn tier, across ranks, no EDF guard, no margin). test-account-pool: the projection's shape. test-fable-cap-pool-storm §19: the REAL chooser on the incident caches (Opus → a Fable-spent member, Fable → the default, the pre-change chooser as control) and the REAL per-session pass (cold Opus moves with its sentence, warm stays, Fable stays, no better member ⇒ stays). The §5b projection census stays at 7 sites. test-pool-placement-ui, test-quota-model, test-codex-pool unchanged and green.
- **Verify r1 (Opus).** S5 never moves a PINNED conversation waiting off its pin (`decidePinnedPlacement` passes `pinned`; the move used to speak the pin's sentence for a spare-lane move) nor one whose view keeps a model-scoped lane of its OWN family (`curOwnLane` — a vendor's second lane, Sonnet or Opus, would have started cold-starting Fable conversations); the chooser places on a spare lane only for a COMMANDED model (`hinted`: a claude resume commands none and the instance default stands in — an Opus default put resumed Fable conversations on Fable-spent members); an UNKNOWN default is left at a spawn only for a member whose spare lane is measured under its hot bar (`spareClaim`). Legs + patched-copy controls in test-pool-auto (r1 pin / own lane / unknown default / chooser) and the storm's §19 r1.
- **Tail (Opus, the design desk's ruling 2026-10-02 on verify r1's two open LOWs; no verify round).** L2, no behaviour change: the comment above `spareLaneOf` states MIN's real reason (an UNUSED known-family cap — every member's Sonnet at 100 % — would read every member spare-rich under MAX and mute the rule) and its known defect (two known lanes both in real use ⇒ a member with one spent lane reads spent), unreachable today (15/15 members carry only the Fable known lane); test-pool-auto spare (10) pins the two-lane answer as the status quo, and the planned switch ("only lanes some pool member has spent on, then MAX") waits for a second known lane in real readings. L3: the per-session pass's dwell band gives a `spare-lane` move `SPARE_DWELL_MS` = 1 h after the conversation's last move (src/server/usage-pool-engine.js; the 180 s belt line and its test-pool-auto pin unchanged, MIN_GAIN / the settle line / the EDF jitter untouched): the r1 F3 replay drops from 15 moves (8 spare-lane) to 4 (2) per 2 h; test-fable-cap-pool-storm §20 replays it on the REAL pass (≤ 2 spare-lane moves, ≥ 1, the move off the spent member never held by the hour) with a 3-min-belt patched-copy control (> 2).

### lane jobs-browser — a Background Work job browses as its owner conversation (B-dbc1)

- **Why.** A user's daily reconciliation job could not leave the old desktop Chromium: `/api/agent/browser/*` admitted only `vsst_`, a job carries `VIBESPACE_JOB_TOKEN` (`jbt_`), and `data/bin/vibespace-browser` read only `VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN`.
- **The principal (PURE src/browser-job-principal.js).** The job's lease key is a child handle of the owner conversation's browser key, tagged `job: <id>` — every admission rule judges a child as its parent, so the owner's who-may-use decides (a refused owner ⇒ a refused job, `not_owner`). Its profile = the owner's pin / default attachment (never the owner's temporary browser: `job_no_profile`). Read / act routes allowed (profiles status providers resolve audit tab dialog direct); everything that changes the conversation's browsers refused `job_token`, fail closed, a census of every route. Not running ⇒ `job_not_running`; no owner ⇒ `job_no_owner`; owner without a key ⇒ `no_browser_key`.
- **The wiring.** routes: ONE door (`agentFacts` → `jobAgentFacts`: route judged before anything is minted; the owner's live session or recorded binding; the belt resolves a job without minting); `resolveForJob` reads the owner's set (never changes it) and attaches the job's own lease ⇒ its own window. keeper: `jobRunning` dep; a running job's handle is in the live set (a job whose conversation stopped keeps browsing until it ends); `releaseJob` at the run's finalize (jobs.js `onRunEnded` → server.js); `reconcile` releases any handle whose job is not running (boot + every tick). The strip names the job's window "Job: <name>" (zh/ja), the name read live; the trace stores the job's id only (lane-redact r9: a job's name never rides its browsing). The CLI reads `VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN || VIBESPACE_JOB_TOKEN`.
- **Gates.** test-jobs-browser (new, fast, 98: tables + route census + admission through the real mayAttach + the real routes + keeper over test-browser-windows ④'s fake agent-browser 0.38.1 / window model: own lease + window in the owner's pinned profile, refusals by name, owner gone ⇒ still browsing, released at finalize + by the sweep; 3 mutant-copy controls); test-browser-identity-census 132 (+ the job's attach caller row); test-browser-share-model 241; test-browser-windows 94; test-job-model 156; test-jobs-panel; test-browser-mediation 247 / -profiles 477 / -stuck 287 (manual readers); build + i18n-check.

### lane browser-recipes — the agent is taught the steps for a browser with the user's login

userR's pod (2026-10-02): asked to operate an admin site "in the Chrome logged in as <her>", the agent ran `vibespace-browser status` ("no profile attached — ephemeral …"), concluded it had no usable browser, launched the system chromium itself and died on "Missing X server or $DISPLAY". Nothing it was shown named the recipe (a named profile, the user logging in once through the live view, the login kept); the manual's first screen was page verbs. Base b924041f; four steps, one commit each.

- **Step 1 — the manual's §0.** docs/agent/browser-manual.md opens with "What the user asked for → what you do" (≤ 40 lines, before the old intro paragraph and every verb): (a) the user's login = `new "<site> — <user>'s login"` → `use` → `open <url>` → the sentence "Open the Agent browser window and take over to log in; I will continue once you hand it back" (never a password; the login stays in the profile); (b) browse = bare verbs; (c) the same login for other agents (usable by all conversations unless narrowed; `--sharing instance` = own tabs; `not_owner` ⇒ the user widens "Who can use it"); (d) no display = only `vibespace-browser`, never chromium / google-chrome / playwright by hand. Each ends with one sentence for the user.
- **Step 2 — `status` and the first refusal.** PURE src/browser-recipes.js holds the words (pointer, first-verb pointer, intro clauses) and `noDisplayRung` / `noDisplayLine` (a live browser's recorded launch fact wins, else a probe of this machine; never for a conversation on another machine). The status route answers `recipe` + `noDisplay`; the CLI prints the pointer when no profile is attached and the sentence when the machine has no display. A page verb refused while the conversation has no browser yet carries `recipe` (`res.locals.recipe` through `fail` / `failVerdict`), printed `next: …`. The exit-machine sentence quoted from her transcript is not in this tree's `status` (it is `vibespace-exit list`'s); the gate pins its absence.
- **Step 3 — the tools intro.** The Browsing line's ONE clause names the recipe (on the isolated line it replaces the older "for a login other conversations can use too …" clause); the machine's display fact rides both delivery sites as `browserDisplay` (the keeper's last probe, sync, refreshed on demand when older than 60 s; one probe at boot) and adds the no-display clause. Whole intro with a two-profile set + the clause: 8 065 B (rung D), 7 427 B (shared) < 9 600 B.
- **Step 4 — the gate.** scripts/test-browser-recipes.mjs (fast, 0.5 s, 32): §0 first + the four recipes + the exact sentence; the naive reader (first 60 lines: `new "` before every page verb); the PURE no-display table; the status census over the REAL CLI against a stub server; the first verb's refusal over the real CLI (a fake browser CLI that must never run); the intro under the cap; wiring pins. Controls (scratch copies): a manual without §0 fails the first-screen leg; a CLI without the pointer fails the census. test-browser-profiles' call-shape pin follows the new `browserDisplay` fact.
- **Verify r1 (2026-10-02, one round).** F1 (MED): a conversation on another machine (rung H / `f.remote`) read the same `new` + `use` + live-view pointer in `status`, the first verb's `next:` and the intro — there `new` answers `remote_session` and that machine has no live view (§5), so the recipe was unfollowable where it appeared; fixed with `REMOTE_POINTER` / `FIRST_VERB_NEXT_REMOTE` / `INTRO_REMOTE_CLAUSE` (the login needs a conversation on the VibeSpace machine), picked on `f.remote` / `VARIANTS.H`, plus the manual §0 (a) row. F2 (LOW): §0 said "in these words" without saying the sentences are SAID in the user's language. The gate counts §0 proper (to its closing `---`), pins the three remote surfaces and gains a control copy of agent-routes without the clause. Held: the display fact is the connect-testing probe (a dead DISPLAY=:97 ⇒ none); `vibespace-docs browser §0` resolves (the CLI reads one argument); the intro's largest shape (every tool, 12 attachments, the no-display clause) is 8 793 B; `status` before any browser exists carries the pointer (real route).

### lane lark-threads — a thread born after its root was stored; who is this

**User line (Fixed):** A Lark message that got a thread after VibeSpace had already read it now shows the thread (checked about once an hour per chat, at once when you press Refresh); people who left a chat and bots are named; you can give any Lark author your own name from the message's author menu.

- **The forensics (read-only, production 2026-10-01).** The owner's post (Fish Audio B2B GTM+ Eng) is stored with `threadKey: null`; its group holds 73 records, none keyed; 432 Lark records elsewhere carry a key — every one a topic whose root was listed AFTER the topic existed. Four holes: the feed dropped a stored hit before its thread mark (H1), the log's dedup kept the key-less first copy with no patch path (H2), the chat walk never re-lists a stored root (H3), nothing could learn the `omt_` key (H4).
- **A1 the place door** (src/channel-store.js `widenPlaces`, PURE rules src/channel-thread.js P1–P4): widen-only (null → the vendor's key / root), a validated `pl` side line, folded on every read, kept by the side compaction, folded into the log at its trim; every append path offers its duplicates; the engine's write hook re-derives the thread index, owes the topic a walk, and broadcasts `threads` with `walked`/`separate` (the root grows "open to load" in place).
- **A2 drain rule 22** (PURE): the newest page of each live, separately-listed, active (14 d), walked chat once per `channels.threadRecheckSec` (default 3600), the lowest priority, ≤ 3 a pass, paced, never in a back-off; the OWNER's Refresh re-lists at once (floored 60 s on his own previous press — never the timer's), a window's open and an agent's refresh never. Lark `recentRoots` = ONE `im/v1/messages` page, no anchor.
- **A3** a stored hit naming a thread marks the thread (never an owed chat read). **A4** a feed hit the chat read did not find is read by id (`GET im/v1/messages/:message_id`, ≤ 5 per feed tick, every non-reply answer and refusal remembered 6 h): a thread reply becomes a record of its chat, its root is patched, its thread owed. Both new calls allowlisted in test-vendor-whitelist §8 with their gates + 4 controls.
- **A5 the measurement — UNMEASURED against real Lark.** Whether the search carries `thread_id` and whether it indexes topic replies at all is not known (the first production page had none; the doc marks it optional). The card's new line says it within a day: "Threads: N search hits named a thread · F of M messages the chats did not list were thread replies, read one by one · K chat checks for new threads found W"; the journal's first-page line now prints `thread_id on N of M hits` and `display_info`'s sub-field names.
- **B (MEASURED, binding): naming another person needs `contact:contact.base:readonly`** (an owner-approved probe: 99991679 under `contact:user.base:readonly`). The consent asks it + `contact:user.employee:readonly` + `contact:user.department:readonly` as optional groups after the reactions (one dropped per refused consent); without it no lookup is sent and the card says "One Re-authorize adds: reading people's profiles". With it: profiles once per 6 h per person, ≤ 3 a page (the unnamed first), ≤ 20 a minute; the organization's nickname + department / job title carried as `author.alt` and rendered Lark's way (`channels.larkNameField`, default department — "Ada (Marketing)" if that is what the API carries; UNMEASURED: the probe never read userN's profile); external authors by tenant (userN's `tn_other_0002` vs the account's own, learned without a call); a dissolved chat said once a day; a bot never "app" at the view door. Lark's chat-member API lists no bots and no app ids — a bot is named only by the application API (another tenant's app cannot be named; the owner's own name is the remedy). No API reads the owner's Lark remark (备注) — the VibeSpace name (aliases.json, owner-only `PATCH /api/channels/:adapterId/authors/:id`, "Set a name…" on the author's head, zh/ja) is the remedy and wins everywhere, the agent's read included.
- **Gates.** test-channel-feed 77, test-channel-store ⑬, test-channel-record 95, test-channel-thread 90, test-channel-reactions 113, test-channel-drain 396 (rule 22 in the seeded walk + ④d + 4 mutants), test-channels-lark-shape ⑮⑯, test-peer-parsers (readByIdAnswer row), test-vendor-whitelist §8, test-channels-engine ㉓㉔, test-architecture §65b, test-channel-authors 12 (new, fast), test-channel-lark-threads-ui 13 (new, heavy).

- Fixed: A reset credit that could not be sent no longer starts the ten-minute wait, and the dialog says why it was refused. · 无法发出的 reset credit 不再触发十分钟等待，对话框会说明被拒绝的原因。 · 送信できなかったリセットクレジットで 10 分間の待ちが始まらなくなり、ダイアログが拒否の理由を表示します。
- Added: You can use a codex reset credit from the Agents list even when no chat session is open on that account. · 即使该账号上没有打开的聊天会话，也能在 Agents 列表中使用 codex 的 reset credit。 · そのアカウントでチャットセッションを開いていなくても、Agents 一覧から codex のリセットクレジットを使えます。
- Fixed: After you use a reset credit, the chat card that offered it shows that it was used instead of its button. · 使用 reset credit 后，提供它的聊天卡片会显示已使用，不再显示按钮。 · リセットクレジットを使うと、それを提示していたチャットのカードはボタンの代わりに使用済みと表示します。
- Fixed: The usage menu's Codex refresh now says what it read (or why it could not) and updates the numbers at once. · 用量菜单的 Codex 刷新现在会说明读到了什么（或为什么读不到），并立即更新数字。 · 使用量メニューの Codex 更新が、読み取った内容（または読めなかった理由）を表示し、数字をすぐ更新します。
- Fixed: A reset credit is no longer spent a second time on the same limit when a new credit was granted in between — the dialog says the earlier request cannot be judged and nothing is spent. · 中间新授予了 credit 时，同一限额不会再第二次消费 reset credit——对话框会说明先前的请求无法判定，并且不消费任何东西。 · その間に新しいクレジットが付与されていても、同じ制限に対してリセットクレジットが二度消費されることはなくなりました — ダイアログは以前の要求が判定できないことを示し、何も消費しません。
- Fixed: A reset-credit answer VibeSpace cannot read is settled only by the account's own reading taken after it, never by numbers carried over from before; the notice about it is in your language, with a For-you item naming the word. · VibeSpace 无法读懂的 reset credit 回答只会由其后账号自己的读数判定，不再由之前带过来的数字判定；相关通知使用你的语言，并有一条 For you 条目指明该词。 · VibeSpace が読めないリセットクレジットの応答は、その後に取ったアカウント自身の読み取りだけで判定され、以前から引き継いだ数値では判定されません。その通知はあなたの言語で表示され、For you にその語を示す項目が加わります。
- Fixed: Codex records that arrive hours late (after a stalled connection) are no longer taken as current — a stale reading settles nothing and a stale limit starts no wait. · 延迟数小时才到达的 Codex 记录（连接卡住之后）不再被当作当前状态——过期的读数不会判定任何东西，过期的限额也不会触发等待。 · 数時間遅れて届いた Codex の記録（接続が止まった後）は現在の状態として扱われなくなりました — 古い読み取りは何も判定せず、古い制限は待ちを始めません。
- Fixed: a session on a machine whose clock runs behind no longer loses that recognition to a single odd record (a clock step, a replayed burst, one slow read) — and a wall or reading from its first minute is acted on as soon as the offset is recognised, instead of waiting for the next one. · 时钟偏慢的机器上的会话不再因为一条异常记录 (时钟阶跃、回放的突发、一次慢读) 而失去对时钟偏差的识别——而且它第一分钟里的上限或读数会在识别出偏差时立即生效, 不再等下一条。 · 時計が遅れているマシン上のセッションが、たった 1 件の異常な記録 (時計のステップ、再生されたバースト、1 回の遅い読み取り) で時計のずれの認識を失うことはなくなりました — また最初の 1 分間の上限や読み取りは、ずれが認識された時点ですぐに反映され、次の 1 件を待たなくなりました。
- Fixed: Use a reset credit now reads the account first, so a credit granted a moment ago is never counted as unused. · 使用 reset credit 时现在会先读取账号，刚刚授予的 credit 不会再被算作未使用。 · リセットクレジットを使うとき、まずアカウントを読み取るようになり、直前に付与されたクレジットが未使用として数えられることはなくなりました。
- Fixed: A conversation whose records arrive late no longer re-applies an old limit over a newer reading of its account, keeps the first limit it hit when many readings follow, recognises a clock offset that sits right at the two-minute edge, and tells you in For you when a late limit may have stopped it. · 记录延迟到达的对话不再把旧的上限覆盖在账号更新的读数之上，很多读数跟在后面时也不会丢掉它撞到的第一个上限，刚好卡在两分钟边缘的时钟偏差也能被识别，而延迟到达的上限可能让它停下时会在 For you 里告诉你。 · 記録が遅れて届く会話は、アカウントのより新しい読み取りの上に古い上限を上書きしなくなり、多くの読み取りが続いても最初に達した上限を失わず、ちょうど 2 分の境界にある時計のずれも認識され、遅れて届いた上限で止まったかもしれない場合は For you で知らせます。
- Fixed: Codex readings from a machine whose clock runs behind are no longer refused for good as a stalled backlog — after a minute of them the clock offset is recognised and the numbers are current again. · 来自时钟偏慢的机器的 Codex 读数不再被永久当作卡住的积压而拒收——持续一分钟后会识别出时钟偏差，数字重新变为当前状态。 · 時計が遅れているマシンからの Codex の読み取りが、止まった積み残しとしていつまでも拒否されることはなくなりました — 1 分ほど続くと時計のずれとして認識され、数字が再び最新になります。

Engineering:

- **The floor arms only on a consume that WENT OUT.** The try record was stamped at the WRITE of the verb, so a wrapper older than the idempotency key (codex refused `consume {}` locally), a wrapper that never answered and a vendor `nothingToReset` all armed "already tried in the last 10 minutes" (the owner's screenshot). The wrapper now emits `reset_credit_sent {idempotencyKey, attempt}` right after each consume write and advertises `caps.resetCreditKey`; the engine's attempt record (`openResetCreditTry`, one opener for both writers) carries the spend HOLD, converted into the charge at the send (`noteResetCreditSent`) or given back (`onResetCreditNotSent`, the 90 s ack window — `in_flight` 409 meanwhile). PURE `creditAnswerOf` / `attemptBlock` / `rungBlockUntil` (src/reset-credit.js): only `reset` and a sent-unanswered consume keep the floor; the AUTO rung tries once per limit EVENT and skips a conversation marked `_resetCreditStale`. The answer handler is ONE module-level `handleResetCreditResult` (the wrapper's record and the helper's), matching its attempt by the echoed key.
- **The helper path.** A person's press rides only a `keyed` wrapper (its own sidecar advert); otherwise ONE bounded `codex app-server` child on the account's own login (src/codex-reset-helper.js — initialize, initialized, consume {idempotencyKey}, rateLimits/read; 30 s wall; killed at the end; never rejects; the result a snapshot). Its reading goes through `writeCodexReading` (the one codex snapshot writer, factored out of `recordCodexQuotaSignal`'s `writeSnap`) as `codex-reset-helper`; usage-source names it. Allowlisted deliberately: test-vendor-whitelist §8 (an argv census of every `['app-server', …]` in the server tree with four rows, the helper's one caller after the spend ceiling and the attempt record, human-only route, never the auto rung or a timer, `MEASURED_CONNECTS`, a live strace leg over the stub with a loopback control, five patched-text controls). Measured with scripts/measure-reset-helper.mjs (codex-cli 0.159.3 under `sudo -n unshare -n` + setpriv, empty CODEX_HOME and HOME): our process 0 internet-family calls; the app-server's startup 4 DNS attempts (ENETUNREACH) from `git ls-remote https://github.com/openai/plugins.git` (its plugin marketplace sync), plus `lsb_release -a` and a `bwrap --unshare-net` probe; the logged-out consume answered in 167 ms. The stub app-server moved to scripts/codex-app-server-stub.mjs (one stub for the drift test, the UI suite and the whitelist leg). The dialog prints the harness on the account line ("Codex · CLI login") and the helper's sentence.
- **R3 — the card the credit outlived.** `resolveResetCreditCards(key, ev)` → both normalizers' `resolveResetCreditOffers` (open offers kept in `_rcOffers`, ≤ 64): at a `reset` answer (`used`, with the new window's end when the post-reset reading said it) and at every codex reading (`reset` past the card's stated `resetsAtSec`, `open` when usable) — never while a credit on it is in flight (the current wrapper re-reads BEFORE it answers: that reading is the credit's own). The resolution goes on the message; ONE `edit {resetCredit}` op per card; chat-view patches it in place (`patchResetCredit`) — no re-created card. Cards are in-memory only (never transcript records), so a server restart already drops them.
- **R4 — the answered ⟳.** `POST /api/usage/codex-refresh {key, sessionId}` → `refreshCodexForPerson` (a live local codex chat session on the identity the popup shows; the existing `readCodexLimitsViaSession` waiter, which now settles with the key it wrote) → the reading / `refused` / `archived` / `timeout` / `no_live_session`; PURE `codexRefreshToast` (zh/ja); the popup + roster repaint at the round trip, 2.5 s only as the fallback. The client no longer reads ANY live codex session when the popup shows another account.
- **verify r2 (the additions of r1 attacked; 888a75ab → ad3f3401).** ① MONEY: an attempt on an account whose stored count was unknown was recorded as `creditsAt: 0` (`Number(null)`), so the first reading ("count still 1 ≥ 0") settled an unanswered consume not-landed and the next press minted a second key — null now, a stored 0 read as unknown; then the witness-less attempt got rules (PURE `settleByReading`): `untold` when only the reading carries a count (the block ends, the count named, the next press spends on it), a window restated EARLIER is never a credit's (`R1 > R0`), one rolled to its next natural reset inside the 60 s grace is the clock, an attempt with no window expires once every window began after its send, and an unsettled attempt LAPSES at its wall's reset + grace (else 7 d) — free, said on the dialog (`lapsedLine`), still settled for the ledger. ② MONEY: the helper's app-server exited after taking the consume and the engine read its words as an answered error (free at once, a second key) — the helper's `answered` rides the payload; sent + unanswered = `unanswered` whatever the words. ③ D6: an attempt open at a stop came back `unknown` and was never charged (its hold died with the process) — charged at the boot restore, the file re-written. ④ A torn `data/reset-credit-tries.json` was silently ignored — set aside `.corrupt-<ts>`, warned, ONE For-you item (origin pool, filed lazily). ⑤ GATE: §8's never-a-timer census was engine-only — a tree-wide `consumeResetCreditFor` CALL census (route 2, engine 1; a setInterval in server.js and a new caller in ws-handler are red controls), the strace leg pinned to the FAST (push) tier and RED on a CI runner without strace. Held: the pool moved between the press and the read ⇒ the reading lands under the HELD member (measured); two ⟳ presses on one account ⇒ ONE read (both ride the first live session; two reads only when two clients name their OWN sessions — each conversation's own app-server, acceptable); a setsid'd grandchild survives the group kill (20/20 on a stub) — codex 0.159.3's binary carries bwrap `--die-with-parent`/`--unshare-net`, no `--new-session`, no `setsid` (strings, launch-free), so the real tree is reached; what the app-server WRITES into CODEX_HOME stays unmeasured (the rule: the real app-server is never launched here) — its strings name `sessions/`, `history.jsonl`, `state_5.sqlite`, `version.json`, `logs/`, `plugins/` + a 413-string marketplace block, so a throwaway home copy remains the open design item (with the refresh-token-rotation hazard a copy would introduce).
- **verify r3 (the additions of r2 attacked; the attempt lifecycle pinned as ONE closed table; a82b6f94 → ).** ① MONEY: an unsettled attempt behind a FREE newest record (a helper that never started — codex gone — ended `error` with the unsettled one as its prior) was hidden from the block; the next press carried no prior and consumed with no read first — the block walks the chain (`attemptBlock`), a new attempt's prior is the newest unsettled attempt wherever it sits (`priorForPress`, ≤ 8 live tail entries). ② MONEY: a consume answered in a word no measured table lists (or with no word) read as "answered, nothing spent" and freed the next press — `VENDOR_OUTCOMES` is a closed set (the drift gate pins it equal to every measured table); a word outside it is `unknown-outcome` (charged, the floor, unsettled until a reading), the person told the word. ③ The floor / ack window were judged by the timer's stamp — in the gap between the floor elapsing and the callback (a busy loop) a sent attempt was free and a press minted a second key; an open attempt on a non-reporting carrier past the ack window the same (the helper ran, the open attempt replaced with its timers cleared) — `armedByClock` + clock-judged `isUnsettled` / `settleByReading` / `isLapsed` (`clockOpts`), the timers only durable. ④ A lapsed prior was judged by the reading after its SUCCESSOR's consume (a false "did land") and a chain of lapsed priors grew per press — a send SUPERSEDES its priors (`supersede`: `supersededAt` refuses later readings; a lapsed prior dropped). ⑤ GATE: §8's call census missed `const f = engine.consumeResetCreditFor; setInterval(f)` and `.bind()` — a reference census + bind/call/apply red. T1: `attemptStep(record, event, clock)` (10 phases × 12 events) walked by test-reset-credit-verdict §9 (112 canonical states × 28 events = 3 088 cells + 17 920 seeded steps, an independent oracle, 7 patched-table controls) and the real engine in test-reset-credit-ui (20 seeded sequences × 5 steps, record / block / preview / ledger compared after every step); the walk found two more cells (a lapsed head hiding a live prior; a clock-armed attempt no send ever superseded). Held: the `untold` rule (a count is compared only when the send knew one); a late reading settles a lapsed prior only before the next send (after it never — the chat continues at the reset anyway); the helper's stdout cut mid-JSON ⇒ unanswered; a member removed between the stop and the boot is charged by the identity the record carries; the torn-file For-you item is once per boot (the inbox dedups the same text).

### lane channel-agent-watch — the agent's own watch, the requestable directory, access above a chat, next turn or wake now

The owner's three asks (2026-10-01) + the addendum. Base 7366587e (lane everyone-principal).
- **W3 — access is MAX over the grain and its ancestors.** Reproduced first on the real engine: account access for an agent, then Notify… on one chat ⇒ `watcher-needs-access` (and `grainOf` dropped such a row at read). ONE PURE rule (`eligibleKeys` / `eligibleFor` in src/channel-filter.js): a watcher is valid where its principal holds access at the grain, at an ancestor (the account, a matching rule) or a visible grant reaches it (an approved request); All agents covers everyone. `validateWatchers(list, access, {inherited})`, `grainOf(rec, legacy, {inherited})`, `effectiveGrants(…, {grantKeys, accountKeys})` all read it; the engine passes `convInheritedOf` / `siteInheritedOf`; the dialog reads `conv.eligibleAbove` (same rule) and lists those principals.
- **W5 — `deliveryModeOf(row)`**: `next-turn` (free: the hit block goes to `deliver.stashFor`, no ladder, no ledger) | `wake` (unchanged: cap + spend authorizer + pacer). A row with no `delivery` = every pre-lane row = wake, as before. Notify… gains "When is it told?" (a new row starts at next turn); `watcherView` carries `delivery` + `origin` so a whole-list save never loses them.
- **W1 — `vibespace-channels watch|unwatch`** (POST /api/agent/channels/watch|unwatch): reach first (hidden ⇒ the uniform not-found; requestable / directory ⇒ `no-access` naming `request`); next-turn written at once (ONE row, `origin:'agent'`, keywords as an inline filter), never over the user's row; `wake` = ONE request in the index's `watchRequests` + a For-you item (action `channel-watch-request`, Approve/Deny on the row) decided by the EXISTING `/api/channels/reach-requests/:id/:verdict` route, Approve = exactly the frozen row through `setGrain`. `--regex` refused by name (a pattern over peer text is a stall risk) — keywords only.
- **W2 — the directory**: per account `agentDirectory {groups (default on), singles (default off)}` (PURE `directoryOf` / `validateDirectory` / `directoryListable` in src/channel-acl.js; the Edit dialog's two switches; `PUT /api/channels/adapters/:id {agentDirectory}`); `list --all` = title (belt), kind, member COUNT, last activity, `requestable`; `request` accepts a directory row.
- Gate: scripts/test-channel-agent-watch.mjs (fast, 36; controls: a filter judging by its own grain only, an engine dispatch without the next-turn branch). The engine exports `onFresh` (the suite's seam).

### lane everyone-principal — "All agents" in every place that asks which agents may use something

The owner (2026-10-02, after userW asked for browser profiles every agent shares): every place that configures who may use something offers "All" — "every conversation, now and later" — as the first choice.

- **The census (E1).** scripts/test-everyone-principal.mjs is grep-derived and prints its table: every `principalPicker({…})` call in src/lib is a row — six SURFACES that offer the All row (`everyone:` in the call) and two EXEMPT with a reason — and every reach / ACL model (a tracked src file declaring PRINCIPAL_KINDS / WHO_KINDS / OWNER_KINDS or named *-acl.js / *-reach.js: 7) is a row whose check loads the module and proves its spelling. Before this lane three models had an "everyone" (exit reach's `everyone` mode, a browser profile's `instance` = "All my conversations", msg-acl's open-to-every-outsider levels); four did not (the picker, channel-acl, channel-filter, window-reach).

  | surface | model | everyone before | spelled now |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Channels · Grant access… | channel-filter ACCESS + channel-acl | no | `{kind:'everyone', id:'*'}` access row |
  | Channels · Notify… | channel-filter WATCHERS | no | the same principal; offered while All holds access; a fan-out, a cap per conversation |
  | Channels · Reach & policy → Grant reach to… | channel-acl | no | `{kind:'everyone', id:'*'}` grant |
  | Desktop app · Share with agents (launcher + window) | window-reach | no | `{kind:'everyone', id:'*'}` reach row |
  | Machine · Who can use <machine>? | exit-reach | yes (a radio) | mode `everyone` — the radio gone, the rows beside it kept |
  | Agent browser · Who can use <profile>? | browser-profiles | yes (a radio, the default) | `use.mode:'all'` = owner `instance` — the radios gone, rows kept |
  | Agent group · New group / Invite… | — | EXEMPT | membership, not a permission (§22 D1) |
  | Desktop app · Ask an agent to take control… | — | EXEMPT | a request to ONE agent that may bill |
  | agent ↔ agent messaging | msg-acl | yes | externalVisibility / reachability open to every outsider (no principal list) |
  | raw-API tiers (next lane) | the access row | — | inherits; the census requires `everyone` in src/channel-api*.js when it lands |

- **The picker.** `everyone: {key, name?, hint?}` (or `'roster'` when the caller's rows carry it) draws "All agents · every conversation, now and later" FIRST — above Recent, never hidden by a search, never a recent pick, its chip first, never greyed. It is never Enter's first-row fallback (`armableFirst`: typing "pag" + Enter picks a match) and the first ↓ lands on the first named row (All is one ↑ above) — "every conversation" is never granted by a stray Enter. A new glyph `everyone` (three heads); `users` stays a group's.
- **The models.** channel-acl / channel-filter / window-reach: a principal `{kind:'everyone', id:'*'}` (one spelling, no name) that names every agent; MAX with the specific rows (A's own `draft` row never narrows All's `send`; a session's own window row is named before All's), and removing All leaves every specific row as it was. exit-reach and browser-profiles already had the value: the All row IS their `everyone` / `all` (an `everyone` ROW is refused there — one spelling), and both now KEEP the rows picked beside All (`who` under `everyone`; owner `{kind:'instance', who}`), so taking All away restores them exactly — the brief's "never a silent loss of the per-principal rows". What a grant allows is unchanged.
- **The money rule.** An All WATCHER wakes every RUNNING conversation (a billed turn each — the row's hint and the Notify sentence say so). F.fanOutWatchers turns the one stored row into one item per running conversation, keyed `everyone:*><cid>`, each with its OWN pace ledger (`stats.fan[cid]`), pending hits, timers and scope chain; the engine's ten wake-path sites read `wakeEffOf`, the views keep `effectiveFor` (one All row on every card). Measured on the real engine: 3 running conversations × cap 2 × 4 batches ⇒ exactly 2 wakes each; a conversation that starts later gets its own cap; a named agent beside All is woken once per batch. Controls: one shared ledger ⇒ 2 wakes in all; no cap on a fan target ⇒ every hit bills every conversation. Known scale cost: a held burst keeps up to PENDING_CAP record copies per running conversation on the index row (bounded by the cap × the roster).
- **The request.** An agent's `vibespace-channels request` on a conversation All may see answers `already: true, via: 'everyone'` — no For-you card; the CLI says "already allowed".
- **The words.** All agents / 所有 agent / すべてのエージェント; "Shared with: All agents (N more rows)" on a window's chip, "All agents (N more rows)" on a profile's row, the card line names All first; the agent-facing `not_owner` sentence and vibespace-browser's way-out line name the button "All agents".
- **What the heavy legs caught.** The exit dialog's leg typed "运维" + Enter and picked nothing: `enterTarget` took the armed row only while it was `keys[0]`, and with All above every list it never was again. Now the armed row is "still first" when it is the first ARMABLE row (`enterTarget({…, skip})`), pinned by a table in test-principal-picker; the who-dialog's kept-rows sentence moved to its own line (a space between two zh sentences).
- **Gates.** test-everyone-principal (new, fast, 86); test-principal-picker 42; test-window-reach 110; test-browser-share-model 226; test-browser-pin 197; test-peer-text-census 355 (`r.via` rowed); test-channels-engine 712 (the release-sweep control re-anchored on the per-ledger loop); the fast tier (212 suites green; one earlier run red on test-browser-tabs's linear-work timing pin under a loaded machine — clock class, green alone). Heavy, run singly: test-browser-who-ui 59 (⑩ All picked, zh), test-channels-aggregate-ui 136 (Grant access… with All, zh), test-exit-access-ui 73, test-channel-window-render 162, test-channels-aggregate 390.
- **Verify r1 (authority + money class).** T1: THE REACH TABLE is a gate section (test-everyone-principal ⑦, 193 cells): five models × {All only / All + named / named only / none} × {a conversation that existed at the grant / one born after / a Task Group member / a fork (its source's id) / no Task Group / no identity} × read / request / act / be woken, three mutant-copy controls (an All row that names nobody, or only the conversations that existed, is red). A Background Work job (jbt_) is NOT a conversation on any All surface — channels, window targets, exit and the agent browser all take vsst_ only (exit refuses jbt_ by name) — it acts, where it acts at all, AS its owner conversation (vibespace-msg / jobs); on the fleet "every conversation" = every conversation on THIS instance, whichever allowed sign-in started it. T2 refuted on the real engine (r1-repro/money.mjs): ① every fan-out wake is its own `authorize()` under ITS conversation's credential slot through the real ladder + real spend-guard — the instance/day and identity/hour ceilings bound the fan (5 running, instance cap 3 ⇒ 3 delivered, 2 refused `instance-cap` and STASHED, no cap slot burnt); ② `stats.fan[cid]` is on disk in channels/index.json — a new boot over the same store wakes nobody at the cap and keeps the held hits; ③ a named agent beside All is billed once per BATCH, N batches = N per conversation, never N + N; ⑦ All at `requestable` = one card per requesting agent and each approval grants that ONE agent (per-agent by design; a fold would change what approval grants — held). FIXED (LOW, words): the Notify total under All now NAMES the multiplier ("N conversation(s) running now, All agents is at most {cap} a day for EACH of them (a conversation started later gets its own)"); Grant access… says a draft-only row beside an All row that may send is moot (re-said on every authority radio), Reach & policy says a requestable row beside a visible All row is moot; the exit dialog under All says per grant "Every conversation — the ones you start later included — can borrow the network of / run commands on {machine} as you, each after your Allow | without asking" (following the ask box). Held: a stopped conversation's over-cap fan hits are dropped at the next grain change (a named agent's are held) — the stated design, not a loss of a delivered turn; the picker census proves a surface OFFERS the row, the per-dialog wiring pins prove it MAPS it (a new dialog that offers but ignores it passes ① — the pins are per surface); zh "所有 agent" matches the dictionary's own "agent"; ja "すべてのエージェント" matches its majority spelling.
- **Verify r1 (2026-10-02, round 1 of ≤ 3).** F1 (MED, authority): the owner's removal of an agent's own watch in Notify… did not stick — the agent's next `watch` wrote the row back (reproduced on the real engine); fixed with a removed-by-user mark (`agentWatchBlocks`) `agentWatch` refuses by name (a wake ask still reaches the user; their Approve lifts the mark). F2 (MED, money/attention): no bound on an agent's own rows or open wake asks; past the tray's 20 open items the ask was stored OPEN with no item (undecidable, and the agent told otherwise); the 100-row table dropped open rows. Fixed: `MAX_AGENT_WATCHES` 20 / `MAX_OPEN_WATCH_REQUESTS` 2 (said with the count), `tray-full` refuses and files nothing, the item tells the owner the agent's totals, decided rows leave first. F3 (LOW): the manual now says when an agent may ask for `--mode wake` (only when the user asked to be told at once) and the gate pins the CLI's next-turn default. Held: a pending fork / a job token never writes a row (`ownConversationIdOf` + vsst_ only); the directory's titles ride the belt (`agentTitle`, the 10th site in the peer-text census); the member count and title are what the owner's directory switch publishes (groups ON by default — the only numbers an agent learns of a chat it cannot read); the dialog's whole-list save carries delivery + origin; a next-turn watcher's hits re-ask `stillInEffect`.

### lane hook-root-guard — a server's root is judged before any owner-file write (B-c77a, two strikes)
- verify r2 (2026-10-02): an `unknown` root at boot is re-judged with backoff (30 s → 30 min) instead of waiting for the hook-health probe's 60 s + 6 h — the probe never returns silently on it; the unknown notice is posted once per cause (a memo on disk, never one per boot); the registration that follows is said once ("registered at HH:MM after an earlier read error") and the Settings chip shows it; root facts age out after 60 s (a `.git` converted in place is seen); FORCE and the device daemon censused; zh + ja for the notices. Gate: test-server-root ⑦.

- **Why.** Twice a server booted from a lane worktree wrote the owner's real CLI config: 2026-07-21 (a /tmp rail-smoke worktree pointed every hook at its own path) and 2026-10-01 (notify-retry verify r1, a worktree under `/var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/` registered into `~/.claude/settings.json` and `~/.codex/hooks.json`). The old `hookRegistrationSafe()` judged only "my code is under os.tmpdir() or /tmp/" — a worktree under /var/tmp or beside the checkout passed.
- **The verdict.** PURE `src/server-root.js` `rootVerdict`: a git WORKTREE (gitdir under `<common>/worktrees/`, read with fs — the `.git` file + `commondir`, never a git child), a TMP root (os.tmpdir(), /tmp, /var/tmp, segment boundary), `VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS=1` (one rule of four) are refused by name; no absolute root fails closed; `VIBESPACE_FORCE_AGENT_HOOKS=1` lifts a refusal only under a scratch HOME (with the real HOME it is ignored and the why says so). `refusalLine` = the ONE journal line per boot ("hooks not registered: this server runs from a git worktree of /home/…/vibespace — the owner's CLI config belongs to that checkout's instance").
- **Every writer asks it** (src/server/agent-tool-generators.js reads the facts; `refuseOwnerWrite` latches the line): hook register + strip, the cli-config sync (boot and `onSettingsWrite`), the remote register helper runs (hosts install + uninstall, the ssh per-spawn prelude, the dial device setup — the tools still ship, the helper does not run). `/api/agent-hooks/install` answers 409 with the sentence. The status surfaces carry `refused`: Manage Agents shows "Not registered — this VibeSpace runs from a git worktree of …" instead of ✓ / Install / Remove; the Settings cli-config chip and "Check machines…" lead with it (5 new words, zh + ja).

Not ci.mjs's server boot env: ci.mjs boots no server, its suites spawn the children. VibeSpace itself writes no codex trust (the wrapper only `config/read`s). ### lane desktop-keepalive — the Desktop stream's liveness, and a Paste press that always speaks (userW inc-muoshmqn-dect)

- **K1 measured.** The bridge's keepalive was already a WebSocket protocol ping — the incident's "hidden tab freezes an app-level pong" guess was wrong. The ping frame queues BEHIND the send buffer (WS_HIGH_WATER 8 MiB): a live browser reading at 512 KiB/s behind a full queue never saw a ping and was cut "no pong" (test-desktop-stream-keepalive §6; the 2.369.118 pong-only rule as a patched-copy control reproduces the cut). Fix: ONE `keepAlive` for both bridges + PURE `livenessVerdict` — a pong, or bytes FROM the browser (a reading RFB client asks for each next update), or kernel-accepted bytes through a backlog (`bytesWritten − writableLength`; Node's `bytesWritten` alone counts the socket's own buffer — measured on a dead path) keep the stream; 2 silent rounds ⇒ cut, named `no pong for N ms and nothing acknowledged`.
- **K2.** Proved on the .199 shell (git): the paste box opened without a toast, and a never-settling `readText()` did nothing — the two ways a press left no ring entry. Now PURE `pasteVerdict` (send | queue | refuse), every press said, a 3 s read deadline, a press while down reconnects + queues + pastes on reconnect (30 s bound, then "not pasted"), a watching pane refuses by name, a dead RFB is never re-`disconnect()`ed (noVNC's console error ×3).
- **K3.** The status chip counts the ladder ("Reconnecting n/5…") and words the bridge's own last close (GET /api/vnc/last-close, closed code set `CLOSE_CODES` → zh/ja words).
- **K4 real leg.** test-desktop-keepalive-chrome (new, heavy, ~110 s, 10/10): a real Xvnc singleton + headless Chrome with its own background throttling — the Desktop tab hidden 90 s stays Connected and the bridge closes nothing; the VNC server killed ⇒ the press is said, the text (through the box — headless Chrome holds no system clipboard, measured) goes in while the stream is down and is read back from the X CLIPBOARD with xclip once the ladder respawns the server.
- **The fast tier caught one regression** (test-xpra-client): the shell's "Reconnecting n/5…" overwrote the xpra view's "Connection lost: <reason>" — the ladder words are opt-in (`ladderWords`), set by vnc-view only.

### lane chat-scroll — a send always lands on the sent message (B-172e); the paging gate's mirror flake (B-8c25)

- **B-172e (inc-mt1zrvj3-wsr4, owner on 2.361.6: after scrolling up, a sent message was not shown).** The incident bundle had aged out of data/incidents, so the cause was reproduced on b924041f with a new heavy suite (test-chat-send-landing: a live session behind the real chat-wrapper + a stub CLI over a 40 MB §1c transcript, real wheel + a typed Enter). Three mechanisms: ① `jumpToBottom` sized its slab by the total read before its fetch, and the user's own echo (fed live by the server in the same breath) arrived during that fetch on a view still in history — deferred, then replaced by a slab that ended before it; ② a teleported seek slab's stale accounting read "at the tail", so onSend pinned the slab; ③ an extend in flight across the send wrote its old slab into the new window (`window 776..377` on the base run). Fixes: `_tailHold` (live ops held across the tail fetch, replayed in order once the slab is the pinned view; window end = the slab's end), the slab branch in onSend, `_windowGen` + `_windowMoved` (a page answered after a full-window rebuild is dropped). Each fix has its own scratch-copy control that fails its own row.
- **B-8c25 (test-chat-paging ① red once on the 2.369.195 mirror).** Re-read from the job log: the red was `up-fast-3: landed at scrollTop 31 (inside the 100 px pageUp band) with 2472 messages and the gap still above`; the `runsRestore` ring the item cited is the §4d control's `up-mid-1` evidence, and its `by` is only the last writer (2.7 s earlier). Cause: a notch inside the 300 ms post-landing load lock scrolled into the pageUp band and nothing re-took the skipped decision (the lift re-checked `scrollTop < 10` only). Fix: `_lockSkippedPageUp` at the lift, on the scroll handler's own evidence (a real wheel-up ≤ 1200 ms, unpinned, history above). Gate: test-chat-paging §4g, constructed, with an instance-neutered control that parks.
- **Verify r1 (lane chat-scroll): a hung tail fetch held the whole view.** B-172e's hold was released by the last overlapping `jumpToBottom` to finish, so one tail fetch that never answered kept every live op held: the reader's ↓ landed a pinned tail slab without the sent message or its answer, and the next send did not show either, until the hung fetch answered and its older slab replaced the view. Fix: only the newest tail call (`_tailCall`) lands or fails for the view; an older call answered later drops its slab. Gate: test-chat-send-landing row `hang-return` + control `ctl-newest`.
- **Gates.** test-chat-trim-guard, test-hidden-view-suspend, test-text-window, test-fold-ux + test-run-collapse-fold (the brief's "test-chat-run-summary" does not exist; these two pin chat-run-summary.js and the fold pass), test-architecture, test-changelog-style, `npm run build`; heavy: test-chat-paging (with §4g), test-desktop-resume-paging, test-chat-send-landing (new, ci.mjs heavy). test-desktop-resume-paging's source-level control gained patch (6), the `_windowGen` layer stripped (old control, new layer): without it the control's ungated sentinel page was dropped as stale by the resume re-tail's rebuild and its `extendTop:done` check went red on the fix.

### lane page-link — a /p/<id> page link in chat opens the page (B-2dbc)

**a page link in an agent's message opens the page again (Cmd/Ctrl+click) and a click copies its full address; a web address in a code span or a tool's output is copied and opened whole**

- **The incident** (userW inc-murolahg-3rtv, 2.369.199; report /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/userW-forensics-4/report.md): an agent wrote "私有页 /p/pg5vex1gylcn（文件 …）"; two clicks copied the bare "/p/pg5vex1gylcn", a Cmd+click flashed "Not found" and opened nothing. Unchanged in .200 / .201.
- **Cause.** `linkifySegment` runs URLs → `/p/<id>` pages → paths. The path pass split the HTML at tags and linkified EVERY text run — also the text inside the spans the earlier passes made: `/p/pg…` matches PATH_SRC, and so does the `//host/…` of a URL (the lookbehind stops at `:`). The click handler's `closest('.chat-link')` found the INNER path span: a click copied its data-path, Cmd+click asked /api/file/info → "Not found". The page pass ran over the raw HTML, so `https://x/a-/p/pg…` put a span inside the URL's `data-href`. Assistant prose hides the URL half (marked autolinks a prose URL to `<a>`, which linkify skips); code spans and tool output (`linkifyText`) do not. test-path-linkify's ORDER pin claimed the path pass "never sees them" — it read the call order, never ran the renderer.
- **Fix** (src/lib/chat-renderers.js): `_linkifyBareText(html, fn)` — one alternation that skips a whole `<span class="chat-link…">text</span>` and every tag; the page pass and the path pass both run through it. Our link spans hold escaped text only, so the skip is exact. `/p/<id>/raw` still links the page shell (unchanged).
- **Byte identity.** Every cell the pre-fix rule rendered without a nested link is unchanged (15 of 27: paths with :line:col, CJK punctuation, relative code spans, markdown links, prose URLs); only the nested inner span is gone from page links and from URLs in code / tool output.
- **Gates.** test-path-linkify 14 → 26 (now in-process, ~0.5 s: ④ the REAL renderer bundled by esbuild — the userW message as an assistant message and as tool output, a URL in code / tool output, the page-in-URL attribute, the CENSUS over 9 texts × 3 entries (no link inside a link, no markup inside an attribute, reach 19 cells); ⑤ a patched copy without the link-span skip reproduces `span.chat-link > span.chat-link-path data-path="/p/…"`, the census goes red on 12 cells, byte identity over the rest). test-page-link-ui (new, heavy, chrome, ~9 s, 16): a stub claude behind the real wrapper answers with the incident's message; a REAL click copies `<origin>/p/<id>`, a REAL Cmd+click opens a tab on it (no "Not found", no file probe), a URL in a code span copies whole; ⑤ the pre-fix rule re-installed on the live renderer copies the bare path and flashes "Not found". On the base tree the node legs are 8 red, the chrome leg (head tree with only chat-renderers.js reverted) 8 red.

### lane window-targets-residuals — window-target residuals (B-a38d, B-f18a)

#### B-a38d — after a restart, `type` with no ref under an `auto` share acts as the resolved mode instead of answering the machine

- **Reproduced on b924041f** (the runner's shape, four ways the tree is unreachable, through the real engine): attach resolved `auto` to pixels, `type "hi"` with no ref answered `no_injection_backend` (the pixel road; no xdotool there); a second engine over the same data dir (a restart: the share and the lease persist, `resolutions` live in memory) answered the SAME call `python3_missing` / `a11y_unavailable` / `helper_error` / `helper_missing` — `act()` saw no resolution, so `pixelShare` was false and it asked the tree for the focused node and passed the helper's code through. The residual was named (not changed) in the 2.369.181 mirror-red entry of kb-bugfix-invariants.
- **Fix** (src/server/window-targets-engine.js `act` → `type`): an `auto` share with no resolution in this process is resolved (`ensureResolved`, the attach probe) BEFORE a no-ref `type` picks its road, followed by a re-check (`held()`), the share re-read; the road then follows the resolved mode (pixels ⇒ keys, tree ⇒ the focused node). The focused-node read gets its own re-check too (a revoke during it answered `no_focused_node` / the helper's code to a revoked session). The old `held()` before `actOnNode` is now redundant by construction and annotated `// no-await-before`.
- **Why not "refuse `mode_pixels`"** (the backlog's one-line hint): pixel mode ALLOWS `type` without a ref (keys); a `mode_pixels` refusal would have told the agent to "act with … type" — the call it just made — and the same call before the restart typed keys. The manual's table says `auto` acts "as the resolved mode"; the 2.369.181 entry's residual named exactly this road ("resolving first would add a re-check site the §5 census must pin").
- **Gates:** test-window-targets §4r (each shape: before and after a restart ⇒ `no_injection_backend`, the re-resolution names the reason; THE LAW: one code across four shapes; NEGATIVE CONTROL = a patched copy without the pre-road probe answers `python3_missing` / `a11y_unavailable` / `helper_error` / `helper_missing`); §5 two race legs (a revoke during the pre-road probe on a display with no injection backend ⇒ `not_exposed`, never the backend verdict; a revoke during the focused-node read with nothing focused ⇒ `not_exposed`, never `no_focused_node`) — the per-site census neuters each new `held()` and a leg goes red.

### lane pool-readings-truth — B-a4f1: the estimator's weekly roll waits the same landing minute as the pool's own reader

- **The premise was wrong; the switch was real.** B-a4f1 read the 2026-09-18 incident as "an empty-window reading (0 % with a sliding reset) on an exhausted member drew the pool onto it". The production record says otherwise. Journal 08:59:15 PDT (15:59:15Z): nine conversations moved onto Personal Max ("its fable quota was at 0%") and every continue was rejected; the vendor's wall named 16:00:00Z. The member's last reading before that was the isolated panel at 15:31:17Z (usage-probe-log): "Current week (Fable): 100% used · resets Sep 18, 8:59am", parsed as 15:59:00Z. That is a STATED reset, minute-precise and 15 s in the past, not an empty window. The 16:27Z write the item blamed came from the `control` rung (anchor stream, `source:'control'`), and it was TRUE: the week rolled at 16:00Z, the 16:04Z panel already read 0 %/0 %, and the 16:45Z panel read 5h 90 % after 410 requests. Its 5h reset 21:20Z was pinned (the window opened at 16:20Z), and `windowState` filed it as `empty` (425 s < 600 s jitter). That costs a deadline, never headroom.
- **Why 2.369.117 did not stop it.** That release named this very switch ("09:59:15Z … 45 s before", the PDT wall clock labelled Z) and put `RESET_GRACE_SEC` into `bucketRemaining`. But the engine reads members through `poolReadCache`, the estimator overlay. `estimateBuckets` re-based a weekly bucket on the bare stated instant (`resetSec * 1000 <= nowMs` → u 0, reset +7 d), and `overlayCache` replaced the raw dead bucket with that one, so the grace never saw it. The member's learned rates exist (rates.json `org:29c41b2c…`), so this was the live path. Reproduced on the base b924041f (`pool-readings-truth/repro/a4f1-replay.cjs`, the real writer, estimator and decidePoolSwitch): the raw path decides `null`, the overlay path decides `to:'pm' reason:'exhausted'`.
- **FIX.** `RESET_GRACE_SEC` moved into PURE src/quota-model.js (account-pool-auto imports and re-exports it). Inside the grace, `estimateBuckets` abstains on a weekly bucket, so the overlay keeps the raw reading and `bucketRemaining` rules it. One second past the grace it rolls exactly as before. The 5h roll is unchanged (it always abstained).
- **Not built:** "refuse placement whose only evidence is an empty window". No incident supports it, and quota-model's r4 measurement shows that refusing a stated 0 % regresses a fresh member to "no usage data".
- **Gates:** test-pool-auto (+4: the 15:59:15Z replay through the overlay, the grace edge, the roll one second past it, one constant), test-usage-estimator (+2). Pre-fix control: the same suites over `git archive b924041f`, where the 15 s, edge and constant legs are red.

### lane pool-readings-truth — B-9b40: the auto-cli /usage probe loads no MCP server

- **Measured, not assumed.** Production: under every member's probe cwd (`~/.cache/claude-cli-nodejs/…-probe-config-cwd/`) sit five `mcp-logs-claude-ai-*` dirs (Claude Docs, Gmail, Google Calendar, a writing assistant, Idiolect). There are ~515 files each for Personal Max, one per probe, the newest 2026-10-03T01:01:35Z, each starting "Initializing claude.ai proxy transport … Using claude.ai proxy at https://mcp-proxy…". In the claude 2.1.288 binary, `headlessSyncsClaudeAiConnectors` is `!vk() && !HYe() && !Hr()`, and `vk()` is `mcpProcessWiring.strictConfig()`, which `--strict-mcp-config` sets. So print mode lists the account's connectors (`/v1/mcp_servers`) and connects each through the mcp-proxy unless the MCP config is strict.
- **FIX.** One frozen `PANEL_PROBE_ARGS = ['-p', '/usage', '--strict-mcp-config']` in src/usage-routes.js, used by both the spawn and the probe log. With no `--mcp-config`, no MCP server is loaded, and the probe's one vendor call is the panel. §ban-safety: the change removes calls and adds none. I did not run the real CLI here (that would be a vendor call); the fake-CLI leg records the argv the binary received.
- **Gates:** test-vendor-whitelist §5b (+3: the flag present and no `--mcp-config`, /usage only, one spelling at the spawn), test-usage-probe-log §2 (+1: the fake `claude` records its argv, and the log names the same argv). Pre-fix control over `git archive b924041f`: all four are red.

### lane pool-readings-truth — B-ce1c: the machine login and the pool's copy of the same account are labelled as two sign-ins (the "reuse the machine login" half is a design question, not built)

- **The owner's misreading (2026-09-07).** `~/.claude/.credentials.json` held the owner's own address, alive to 09-10. The pool's copy `data/subs/sub-cac86a3ff4d1` (the same account) had expired on 09-02. Manage Agents' CLI-login row read `= “Personal Max”`, and the usage popup folded the CLI-login chip into Personal Max's ("also the CLI login on this machine"), so the live machine login was taken for Personal Max.
- **FIX (words only).** PURE `machineLoginLinkHint(name, vendor)` in src/lib/manage-agents.js. The row now reads `same account as “Personal Max” · a separate sign-in`, and its tooltip says: one Anthropic account, one quota, usage merged, but two sign-ins that each expire and renew on their own, and signing in one does not sign in the other. The codex twin (the machine ~/.codex login vs a ChatGPT account) uses the same helper. The usage popup's merged chip says "one quota, two separate sign-ins". Three new strings in zh/ja; the three superseded keys are removed.
- **Verified from the binary (claude 2.1.288):** the claude.ai OAuth refresh (`grant_type:"refresh_token"`) destructures `refresh_token: K = e` from the response and stores `K`, so the CLI keeps whatever rotated token the server returns. The repo already records server-side rotation ("token self-refresh ROTATES the refresh token out from under the CLI", kb-design-lessons; accounts.js: one credential copy per account so a rotating refresh token is never rotated out from under a sibling). So "reuse the machine login" cannot COPY ~/.claude/.credentials.json into the pool. Two files holding one refresh token lose one of them at the first refresh.
- **Not built, the one question for the owner:** when a pool copy has expired and this machine's CLI login is the same account and alive, should "reuse" MOVE the machine login into the pool (the machine's CLI is then signed out, one credential, rotation-safe), or should the pool keep its own device sign-in? A copy is not an option.
- **Gates:** test-roster-live-usage (+6: the pure words, the codex twin, both row wirings escaped, the popup chip wiring, zh/ja with {name}/{vendor}). Pre-fix control over `git archive b924041f`: all six are red.

### lane gmail-reply-all — Gmail reply-all, in the thread (B-a085)

The owner (2026-10-02 18:15 PDT): "a new thread is unfriendly to humans — speed this up". `vibespace-channels reply <gmail conv> --all` = To: the sender (Reply-To, else From) + the anchor's To, Cc: its Cc, the account's own address and duplicates removed — resolved when proposed, stored on the proposal envelope, sent verbatim in the thread (threadId + In-Reply-To / References). The adapter echoes `all`; the engine refuses an answer without it. `--cc <addr>` adds people (the compose address rule; listed apart as `added`) — chosen over `compose --in-reply-to` because it reuses the whole reply path (stored anchor, reach, the two-phase draft in the thread, reconcile). The window composer of a mail conversation has a "Reply all" box; the approval card lists every recipient (To labelled reply-all, the whole Cc, the drafter's added Cc apart). The agent's view of the envelope passes the belt (`agentEnvelope`). A recipient header over 16 KB is refused, never clipped; on the wire a non-ASCII display name is encoded on its own (`encodeAddressHeader` — one encoded-word over the whole To hid every address). Refused by name on chat channels (`replyAll` / `cc`). Gates: test-channels-gmail-shape, test-channel-outbox (+ the echo control), test-channels-agent-cli, test-peer-text-census (door + rows), test-channel-window-render ⑩i. Essay: kb-bugfix-invariants.md (B-a085).

Verify r1 (Opus): F1 HIGH — an agent's `reply --cc` now needs compose's reach (the whole account; a conversation grant ⇒ `bad-proposal` / `cc`, nothing created) and gets compose's verdict (direct only when a composed message would be); before, a conversation-only agent with `send` on a direct conversation mailed any address with no card. F2 MEDIUM — Gmail's address grammar (`addressList` + `addressParts`): a comment never splits a list or names the address (`j@x (张 <evil@x>)` went to evil on the wire), a group's members are plain recipients (we were not filtered out of one), an address never sits inside an encoded-word. Gates: test-channel-outbox (F1 legs + CONTROL), test-channels-gmail-shape (F2 + reply-all anchor-gone legs + CONTROLs).

Verify r2 (Opus): F3 MEDIUM — Gmail lists the owner's unsent DRAFT among a thread's messages and the sync stores it (ours), so a reply answering it (named with `--to`, or simply the newest stored message) went to the draft's unsent To — and with `--all` its Cc — direct on a direct conversation: people the thread never wrote to. `replyEnvelope` now refuses a DRAFT anchor by name (`reply-anchor-draft`; the engine answers `bad-proposal` / `reply-anchor`, nothing created). Held: every `--cc` / `--all` / Reply-To path and 54 address-grammar rows (card ≡ MIME).

### lane runaway-daemon — the 16:23 OOM: a leaked scratch daemon's fs worker storm, the reaper's age, the daemon a suite leaves (B-442c)

The 45.7 GB process was test-restore-liveness's §4 self-upgraded daemon (lane stdin-liveness's run, 16:20–16:23): a kill by the pid file missed the re-exec child, `rm -rf` deleted its bundle, and its fs worker pool turned one death into a doubling respawn storm (a failed Worker's `'error'` + `'exit'` both ran `die()`). src/agentd/worker-pool.js is the pool, bounded: one death per worker, `live` ≤ size, crash backoff 500 ms → 60 s, said in agentd.log. Reproduced on the real bundle (94 MB → 4.2 GB, 978 threads in 10 s); the fixed bundle stays flat. The reaper aged processes by the /proc dir's mtime (re-instantiated at 16:23:10 by the OOM's dentry eviction: "young: 42 s" for hour-old orphans); it reads btime + starttime now (scratch-run.mjs `procBornMs`). scratch.mjs `endDaemonsOf` / `endRootedProcesses` find a daemon by its own root env; test-architecture §57b names the 80 server-booting suites that never call the end helper (shrink-only debt). install-service.sh writes `OOMPolicy=continue`. Gates: test-agentd-worker-pool 16 (new, fast), test-scratch-reaper 141, test-restore-liveness 80, test-fd-limit 53, test-architecture 409, test-changelog-style, `npm run build`.

Verify r1: a worker blocked IN A SYSCALL (a hung mount; a FIFO with no writer) outlives its terminate — two such reads held both slots and every later fs op on the device hung with no deadline and no log line (measured on a real self-upgraded daemon: each `stat /` timed out at the client's 30 s). The pool now abandons a terminated worker still alive 2 s later (its slot refilled, at most 8 times, each said), a queued op fails by name at its own deadline, and with every slot wedged an op fails by name instead of running inline. `process.exit` joins every worker thread, so the same wedge held SIGTERM and the self-upgrade's re-exec (the daemon logged "exiting" and stayed, serving nothing); both exit through `pool.exit`, which runs the exit handlers and ends by SIGKILL while a worker is stuck. A worker that exits on its own (a bundle that parses and serves nothing) is a crash with backoff, not a silent 500 ms respawn loop. test-agentd-worker-pool §5–§7 + controls.

### lane mac-pull-refresh — a pull mount shows a file rewritten in place (B-35e3; B-0de9 not built)

#### B-35e3 — a held reader of a pull mount sees a same-size rewrite within the poll interval

- Reproduced on b924041f with the real chain (local agentd serve-folder → bridge → the pinned rclone 1.69.3): after a same-size rewrite on the device, fresh opens read the new bytes, but a held fd and a kept-open sqlite connection read the old ones until another process opened the file, and the mount's mtime stayed the mount time. Variants measured: without `--no-modtime` the mtime moves and the held reader stays stale; `rclone mount2` the same; `--direct-io` makes held readers fresh but `mmap(MAP_SHARED)` fails with ENODEV (rejected).
- src/device-mount.js: `pullMountArgs` (no `--no-modtime`) + `heldRefresher` (a GET through the bridge ⇒ a /proc fd scan, ≥ 10 s apart; a 5 s tick asks the device for each held file's stat by a Depth-0 PROPFIND through the bridge; a moved stat ⇒ one open in a child, plus one more pass; a newly found file gets one pass; at most 64 held files). Cost: an idle mount 0; the /proc scan measured 20k fds ≈ 300 ms async / 90 ms sync on the lane box, hence GET-triggered, never a plain timer.
- Gates: test-device-mount-rclone B-35e3 leg (heavy, real agentd + rclone, 10 checks; the held fd fresh in 3.5–4 s) — CONTROL on b924041f: 3 red (held fd still the old bytes after 15 s, the sqlite row old, the mtime pinned). test-pull-refresh (new fast suite, 18 legs, 1.8 s) — 4 mutants red: `--no-modtime` back, no once-more pass, no rescan, the prefix without its '/'.

#### verify r1 (Opus) — five fixes in src/device-mount.js, test-pull-refresh §10–§13 (29 legs)

- Cost, measured on the owner-shaped box (load ~35, 20.5k fds, UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=32, 5 mounts × 10 held files, a 300 ms device stat): event-loop delay unchanged (p99 2.1 ms vs 2.2), idle mounts 0 work, but every mount ran its OWN /proc scan (5 mounts read nonstop = 18 % of a core, ELU 9 %). Fix: one /proc pass serves every refresher (reused only by a mount whose GET came before it started — a sequence number; a clock tie reused a scan begun in the same ms).
- Device offline: it asked every 5 s forever, silently (8 tcpForwards/min per held file). Fix: 3 unanswered passes are said once in the journal and slow the pass to a minute; the first answer is said and restores 5 s. statRemote tells `false` (answered, not a file) from `null` (no answer). rclone dead (ENOTCONN): it kept asking silently. Fix: rclone's exit stops the refresher and says so.
- SQLite WAL (real chain): a WAL rewritten within its size now reaches a kept-open connection (4 s; base stale), but a reader that connected on an EMPTY -wal got `disk I/O error` (base: stale rows): rclone caps a held fd at the size its file had at open (an appended file: fstat grows, reads past the old end are EOF). Fix: a -wal grown past its first-seen size leaves its family alone, said once. `realpathSync(mountpoint)` → `await fs.promises.realpath`.
- Controls: base 10 legs red; minus the shared scan 2, the WAL rule 3, the journal 6, the exit stop 1, async realpath 1. `--no-modtime` was only ever in the pull argv: `ls -l` of 60 files = 1 PROPFIND with and without it (modtime rides the listing).
- OPEN: a change made before the refresher's first look at a held file can stay unseen by that fd (rclone relists, the fd keeps the old inode, `(deleted)` like a rename-over) — reproduced on b2f4a01c too.

#### B-0de9 — not built: a different code path

- The heal's log text is produced by our own bridge when the device-side tcp-connect to the serve-folder port fails: `catch { sock.destroy() }` in deviceFolderMount drops the device's reason (reproduced with a failing tcpForward: the exact "couldn't list files: Propfind … connection reset by peer"). That is the heal / tunnel bring-up, not the freshness path. Next step for whoever takes it: carry the tcp-connect error into the mount failure, then read userW's log.
