### lane desktop-wayland — a desktop app never reaches the machine's own Wayland desktop

The owner, 2026-10-02 21:36 PDT: Blender, started by the keeper on xpra :4, opened on the machine's physical screen while its VibeSpace window waited for ever. Read-only on the live process: no WAYLAND_DISPLAY in its env, fd 3 connected to /run/user/1000/wayland-0 — libwayland's default when the variable is unset.

- **Fix** (src/desktop-display.js): `x11Env` names `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=vibespace-x11-only` (`NO_WAYLAND_DISPLAY`) instead of deleting it, and sets `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11`. `startXServer` / `startX11vnc` / `startXpra` drop the variable (`withoutWayland`): x11vnc 0.9.17 exits on any value — re-measured with the new name — xpra reads any value as a Wayland session, and test-desktop-app-keeper §7's stand-in Xvnc (Xvfb + x11vnc inheriting its env) went red until the X server was in the set.
- **Callers**: desktop apps here and a paired machine's desktop-serve op share src/desktop-serve.js (app spawn, relaunch, `x11EnvFor` → window targets / tier 3). The agent browser's hidden-window rung (src/browser-display.js) does not use x11Env, runs only with no live Wayland socket, and keeps its measured `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=''`.
- **Gate**: test-desktop-display §9 — the env table, shim X parts, and the real libwayland pair (the pre-fix env connects to a scratch wayland-0, x11Env's env is refused, a wayland-0 control connects). test-desktop-display 201 ✓ 0 skip, test-desktop-apps 388, test-desktop-serve 210 (1 environmental skip: a directory owned by another uid), test-browser-display 117, test-architecture 425, test-changelog-style 40, test-browser-tier3 111, test-desktop-app-keeper 347 (heavy, 1 skip), `npm run build` green.

### lane channel-index-copy — a conversation read never copies the channels index (B-f32b)

**opening Channel windows on an account with tens of thousands of conversations no longer queues the server: a window costs its own conversation, and index.json is rewritten only where it changed**

#### One window copied the whole index up to five times (B-f32b, userW inc-muro2wt1-e8lu, 2026-10-03)

userW's pod (49,977 Gmail threads + 207 Lark chats + 90 agent groups, index.json 45 MB): 19 windows opened in ~20 s, the 9th still titled "Channel" 55 s later. `known()` — on watch, refresh, messages, mark-read and the broadcast's re-read — read one key through `store.index.snapshot()` (a deep copy of the whole index, 0.51–0.55 s each); the index write stringified everything every 2 s while anything changed; every partial broadcast summed unread over all rows; mark-read broadcast a bare id (a scan of every key). Every broadcast also walked every row of every account for the card's census (`schedulerView`, ~90 ms at 50,274 rows). Reproduced first on a generated 50,274-row index: nine windows clicked over 4.4 s finished at 3.0 … 24.4 s (event-loop stall 14.1 s); after the fix each finishes ≤ 8 ms after its click (longest stall 30 ms), the write after one row changed takes 30 ms (was 579 ms).

- One-row reads: `store.index.has(key)` (no copy) / `peek(key)` (that row) / `table(name)`; whole scans read `live()`; the engine calls `snapshot()` nowhere.
- The incremental index write: cached chunks of 256 rows, byte-identical to the whole-file serialization; `entry()` marks its row, an update reaching `ix.conversations` or `live()` marks every row (the conservative default), `rows()` + `touch(key)` for a scan that marks only what it changes (discovery's unlisting — every steady pass now writes incrementally); close() writes the whole file; every tick sweeps two chunks and writes + says a row changed outside `update()`.
- The kept row facts (`index.onTouch`): per account, listed / unread / unlisted / paused / overridden / the first read, re-summed on a full digest, a whole-map touch or once a minute; the digest's unread total reads them. Mark-read broadcasts its key; discovery pages and change-feed births ask `has()`.
- r2, the paced census (the coordinator's ruling on the lane's question): the clock counts (hot / warm / cold / due) walked at most once per 5 s per account, ONE trailing walk + broadcast after the last change (the card settles exact); the user-moved numbers exact on every broadcast. Engine deps `censusEveryMs` / `censusTimer`; `schedulerExact` / `censusStats` for the gates.
- verify r1 (the incremental write attacked: SIGKILL at each of 28 write steps, ENOSPC at each step + a real /dev/full, two racing writer processes, the loader on 14 truncations — the old file or the new one every time, never torn; a proxy census over 33 channel suites saw no write through a read surface): three LATENT tracker gaps closed in the store — an update's rows are marked again at its END (a write inside an async fn's await cleared their marks; no async update fn exists today), the sweep's cycle end counts the map against the cached chunks (a row BORN outside `entry()` sat in no chunk until close()), and a re-born row or a touch of a row not in the map is a whole-map change (the file kept the old place: content equal, bytes not). test-channel-store ⑬ (+7, a control per rule).
- `scripts/work-meter.mjs` `measureAsync` (an awaited call measured).
- Gates: test-channels-census-pace (new, fast, 10 — a 21 s burst over 50,274 rows: 5 walks ≤ 6, user-moved numbers exact on all 47 broadcasts, the trailing census = the full walk; controls pace 0 and a timer that never fires). test-channels-index-scale (new, heavy, 39 — the whole open bounded at 50,286 vs 100,560 rows, 120,905 vs 120,807 work, 0 census walks inside it, the base 358 M → 716 M; the write bounded, 588 K vs the whole-file 117 M; byte identity; the sweep; the verify census's own control; the kept total; ⑧ every engine writer incremental; controls for each). VIBESPACE_CHANNELS_INDEX_VERIFY over 32 channel suites: 0 drift. test-channels-engine's markRead control and ⑲d control re-modelled for the new code.

### lane fleet-image-2 — fleet image 3.6.0: a pid 1 that reaps, agent-browser baked, the fleet e2e's two product gaps, the suites' dev-box assumptions

The fleet e2e ran the browser and desktop suites on a pod of image 3.6.0-rc1 and found the image's pid 1 never reaped (thousands of zombies per pod; one suite hung on one), no agent-browser in the image, four suites calibrated on the dev box, and two product gaps. Image matters only — no user-visible change.

- **pid 1 = tini, both Dockerfiles.** The fleet image ran `runuser` as pid 1, the single-container image `node`; neither reaps, so every detached process whose parent died stayed a zombie until the pod restarted, and a zombie reads alive to `kill -0` and `tail --pid`. `ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/tini", "--", …]`. Measured on the built image: 100 orphans ⇒ 0 zombies (the previous image: 100, ppid 1). Shutdown unchanged (`docker stop` ≈ 2.1 s on both: runuser's own 2 s grace).
- **agent-browser 0.38.1 baked** (pinned = TABLE_VERSION; the build checks `--version`). A copy a user installed into /usr/local was wiped by every roll. With no `~/.agent-browser/browsers` it runs the Debian chromium 154 — headless, or headed on its own Xvfb (`Chrome/154`) — measured in the image with no network. **Tools:** x11vnc, xclip, ffmpeg, and python3-setproctitle (an xpra Recommends: with it xpra rewrites its environ — the shape the rung was measured on).
- **Product gap 1 — a screenshot without a picture never said the loop.** `vibespace-browser`'s direct `screenshot` of a looping tab that drew no frame in 4 s answered `[no_picture]` without the `[navigation_loop]` note its picture answer prints (met on a pod's chromium 154). Now both say it. Gate: test-browser-site-reset (the shotHang row: RED 106/1 on the pre-fix CLI, 107/107 after); test-browser-site-reset-chrome ③ already asserts it on a real page.
- **Product gap 2 — test-browser-propose-chrome ④b pressed a stale coordinate** (red 3 runs of 7 on a pod: the card moved ~22 px between the read and the press). The leg now presses the element it checked (a click recorder, a fresh rect per press, a miss pressed again); ④b' constructs that race on every machine (a 60 px move between read and press: the first press misses, the retry lands, a moved Approve does not count). 7/7 here (40/40 each).
- **The suites' dev-box assumptions:** test-desktop-serve's bounded launcher now dies with its `tail --pid` follower (its own process group) and a zombie runner is a named skip — under `runuser` as pid 1 (`unshare -pf --mount-proc`) the suite passes with that skip in 28 s, master's hangs; test-desktop-vnc-fit reads each top-level through xfwm4's frame; test-desktop-display pins xpra's environ by python3-setproctitle (both shapes measured on xpra 6.5.4 — the version was never the cause); test-desktop-xpra sends its clipboard token on every machine (the X-level legs skip by name without xclip); test-browser-display-chrome and test-browser-live ⑤ run on the system browser agent-browser launches (the Debian chromium on the fleet image) instead of skipping.

### lane trace-fits — the live view's page-size changes fold out of the agent's action list

The owner (2026-10-01): "浏览器每次resize窗口或者移动窗口你都会算作一次操作，导致我的操作列表里全是view fit操作，毫无信息量 … 但也不要完全不要这个信息". Production census (read-only, the busiest profile scope): 37 of 194 trace entries were `viewer-fit` rows ("live view: set viewport 1072 907 (fit)", kind `viewport`), each with a 3 KB before and a 33 KB after frame — every drag, resize, snap, split or desktop switch of the live-view window re-fits the page (lane S4 verify r1 F6 taps OUR resize as ONE `viewer-fit` pair, so the reflow between two agent actions is on the record) and wrote a row of its own; the Actions pane and the tool card counted page sizes as actions.

- **F1 — coalesced at the source** (src/server/browser-trace.js `finalize`, PURE src/browser-trace.js `fitCoalesceVerdict` / `coalesceFits`, `FIT_COALESCE_MS` = 10 s beside AFTER_SETTLE_MS). A fit landing within 10 s of the tap's last fit (measured from the run's `lastAt`, so a long drag is one row), with no other traced action between (`tp.lastCmd` / a pending record's `prevCmd`), REPLACES the run: the run keeps its id, its first `at`, its first before frame and its session; takes the last geometry / text / result and the last after frame as a NEW file `<id>-after-<n>.jpg` (a client may hold the old one cached under the same URL — the clients add `?v=<n>`); `n` counts, `lastAt` moves; the superseded after frame is unlinked at once, never left for the sweep. The index stays APPEND-ONLY as it was: the replacement is appended under the SAME id and `loadIndex` lets the later line supersede the earlier — no tombstone, the id is the key, the sweep's rewrite compacts the file. The stream `trace` record and `browser-trace-appended` carry `replaced: true` (+ `n`, `lastAt`) so the clients patch the row in place. A fit after a click, or 11 s after the last, starts a new run — the reflow between two agent actions stays its own row.
- **F2 — folded on every list** (PURE `foldFits` / `visibleEntries`). Consecutive fit entries are ONE dim row "Live view fitted ×N · 1072×907 (last)" (zh 实时视图已适配 ×N · {size}（最后一次）, ja ライブビューに合わせました ×N · {size}（最後）); the counts exclude fits everywhere — the tool card's "N action(s)" (`traceSummary.n`, the fits beside as "K page-size change(s)" through `countText`), the Actions pane's head and the window's "Actions (N)", the Agent browser panel's traced-actions column (`scopeDigest.n`), a session's `count` (`pairSessions`, the recorder's `bs.count`, the end marker — the end card's "N actions") with `fits` beside. ONE per-device toggle "Show page-size changes" (`vibespace.browserTrace.showFits`, localStorage, default OFF; a <label> wrapping its checkbox) in the Actions pane's head and under the replay's Actions head expands them wherever a list is drawn (an expanded coalesced fit says `×n`). The replay keeps a run as a thin tick (`.brp-tick`) between steps — never a step, never a frame of its own, unless the toggle is on. `GET /api/browser/actions` answers `summary` (`n` / `failed` / `fits`). The tool card's thumbnail strip draws one dim "×N" thumb per run.
- **F3 — retention.** `traceSizePlan` drops page-size frames FIRST (the plan's entries carry `fit`; oldest fit first across every session, `why` "page-size frames go first; its action list is kept"), then the old oldest-session rule; `kept[].fitFrameBytes`. `usageOf` → `{used, fitBytes, total, …}`: the panel's "{used} of {size}" is the agent actions' bytes with "page-size frames: 12 MB" (`.bprof-trace-fits`) under it, as the brief asked; `total` rides beside for the limit's own measure.
- **F4 — pinned, not rebuilt.** The bridge (src/server/browser-stream.js, lane S4) already bounds its own fit storm: `scheduleFit` re-arms ONE timer per relay (`FIT_DEBOUNCE_MS` 250), `runFit` parks a fit asked while one is in flight (`fitAgain`) and runs it once after, and the verdict reads the live `fits` map — the latest geometry wins. test-browser-trace ⑥ pins the three.
- **Measured** (test-browser-trace ③ — a synthetic trace in the census's shape through the REAL recorder: 157 agent actions + 37 fits in 10 storms 2.5 s apart): before, 194 entries, 37 fit rows, 388 frame files, 188 KB of fit frames; after, 167 entries, 10 fit rows (n = 4,3,5,3,4,3,5,4,3,3), 334 frame files, 29 KB of fit frames; the index 194 lines / 167 ids, folded at reload.
- **Gates.** test-browser-trace (fast, 67): the verdict table, the merge, the fold, the counts, the flood, the fit-first plan + usage / housekeeping, four patched-copy controls one per rule (a verdict blind to the action between, a fold that never folds, a plan without the fit-first pass, a recorder that leaves the superseded frame), the wiring pins (the three surfaces, the route's `summary`, the toggle's <label>, F4, zh + ja, ci.mjs). test-browser-replay-ui (heavy): ③ the replay's two ticks where the runs happened (after the 3rd and the 5th step), the toggle on (8 steps, "viewer-fit 1072×907 ×3") and off by a real mouse; ⑥ the Actions pane's two dim fold rows among nine agent rows, the count line "9 个操作 · 5 次页面尺寸变化 · 最新在最后", the toggle on / off. test-ax-paint 25, test-architecture 404, test-browser-housekeeping 190, test-browser-sessions 117, test-changelog-style 40; test-record-clear-census (237) gained the row classifying the toggle's localStorage key as a `pref` (the §H1 storage census went red on it in the fast tier, green with the row).

### lane group-pending — a group message says where it stands with each recipient

**The owner (2026-10-01, the pair window "生活方式助手 · VibeSpace 主开发"): "你这个最新回复应该还没有实际发出去，其实应该展示成pending的状态之类的防止confusion".** A message VibeSpace 主开发 sent to a next-turn pair was drawn exactly like a delivered one while it waited for the other member's next turn; nothing in the window said so. Every fact needed was already on the server — the record's instant, each member's report marker (`reportedUpTo`), its notify mode, the log's leave / kick records — but the marker was a private fact (not in the group view) and a hand-over moved it without any broadcast.

- **P1 — ONE rule, PURE.** `deliveryOf(group, rec, {log})` in src/channel-groups.js: one row `{member, name, state, at}` per recipient = every member but the author that was a member AT the record's instant (`joinedAt <= rec.at` — reportFor's floor is `joinedAt - 1`, pinned); the owner (observer) is never a row. `DELIVERY_STATES` = waiting | handed | muted | left. **THE PIN:** reportFor reads `r.at > marker`, so a marker EQUAL to the record's instant means the record was in that report ⇒ handed — the §1f table pins it against the real engine (the commit stamps the marker to exactly `rec.at`) and a `>` patched copy goes red. `left` reads the log: the member's earliest leave / kick after the record, with no invite of it in between (joined-after-then-left is no recipient; left-then-re-invited is `left`); a departed member the page does not witness is no row.
- **What reality forced (two things the brief assumed).** ① The marker is a RECORD instant, not a clock: `markReported` stores `rep.upTo` = the newest record the report covered, so "read at {time}" would have printed the message's own time. **The follow-up (the coordinator, same day): the hand-over CLOCK is its own field** — `markReported` stamps `members[].reportedAt = now()` beside a marker it moves (persisted with the group record through the same door, validated, in the view; a legacy row has none), `deliveryOf` carries it as the handed row's `at`, the window says "Read by beta · 12:41" (zh "beta 已在 12:41 读到", ja "beta が 12:41 に読みました"; the time drawn as the message head draws its own — local 24 h HH:MM) and the CLI " — read by beta 12:41Z" (UTC + Z like every other instant that CLI prints — the one deliberate deviation from the asked " — read by beta 12:41": an agent reads these lines on any machine). A row stamped before the clock existed still prints "Read by beta". Gates: test-channel-groups §1f (the clock rows, the on-disk persistence, the no-move control keeps the clock, an ENGINE patched copy that moves the marker without the clock ⇒ `at` null — red above), test-channels-groups-ui §2b (the clocked words en / zh / ja, the default formatter), test-msg-cli-groups (the clause with / without the clock, the real engine's stamp), test-channels-groups-e2e ④b (the title says WHEN in en / zh / ja). ② The engine keeps no wake receipt (a successful wake only stamps the marker; the `group-wake` audit line is not on the record or the member), and a mention is no proof (a refused wake rides the report), so `woken` folds into `handed` with no `via` — "已唤醒 {name}" is not printed anywhere.
- **The digest + the broadcast.** `view()` now carries `members[].reportedUpTo` (null before any report); `markReported` announces `channel-groups-updated` for the group when the marker MOVED (an unmoved marker sends nothing — the markRead lesson) — so the sender's window flips without a reload. No new broadcast kind, no new persistence.
- **P2 — the window.** Every message row (the owner's own too) carries `.chanmsg-dlv`: a CSS dot (hollow while anyone waits, filled once it reached everyone it could, dimmed when only muted / departed are left) + the words from `deliveryLineText` (src/lib/channel-words.js, `t`/`tc` injected): ONE recipient ⇒ "Waiting for beta's next turn" / "Read by beta" / "beta is muted and will not read it" / "beta left"; several ⇒ "1 waiting · 1 read · 1 muted · 1 left" with every sentence in the title. The counts are `tc('delivery', …)` keys — "{n} waiting" is also the stash strip's "{n} 条在等" (same spelling, another meaning). The line is keyed by its row and patched only when its signature (every recipient's state + name) moved; a broadcast carrying the group or landing a record re-judges every drawn line (`redrawDelivery`) — never a list rebuild. zh / ja entries for all eight strings; `chanmsg-dlv` is an i18n-census data path (it names a recipient).
- **P3 — the agent.** `GET /api/agent/msg/read` records carry `delivery` (the same rows, names through the belt; a system record `null`); `vibespace-msg read` ends each message line with one clause: " — waiting for beta's next turn" / " — read by beta" / " — beta is muted (never reads it)" / " — beta left", a group " — waiting: a, b · read: c". An older server's record (no rows) prints no clause. The manual's Groups section says it. `send`'s answer unchanged.
- **P4.** The recipient's card ring, the report injection, the wake path, the pacer, the spend guard: untouched.
- **Gates.** test-channel-groups 338 (§1f: the table, the engine pin, the announce + its no-move control, five patched-copy controls — `>`, no owner exclusion, no presence rule, no mute rule, no departure witness); test-channels-groups-ui 88 (§2b the words en / zh / ja from the dictionaries with width budgets in the words, the tone, the re-export; §4 pins on the window, the engine's view + announce, the CSS dot); test-msg-cli-groups 142 (the clause over the stub and over the REAL engine: waiting ⇒ handed after `commitReports`); test-channels-groups-e2e ④b (heavy: the owner's message reads "1 waiting · 1 read" with a hollow dot; one typed character into beta's session + its hook call hands the report over ⇒ the SAME node reads "2 read" with a filled dot, beta's stub recorded no frame; beta muted ⇒ "1 read · 1 muted", back to next-turn ⇒ "1 waiting · 1 read" in place; zh / ja pages: the line whole, the title in the language). ### lane reaction-hover — one hover action bar per message (Channels)

The owner (2026-10-01): "这个加表情的加号太丑了。做成 lark 官方那种鼠标指上去才会在消息的右侧出现，不改变上下布局关系。" + "把 reply in thread，quote 也都放在鼠标悬浮按钮里". Before: every message in a channel window wore a strip line with a boxed `+` (with or without reactions), the thread pane's replies an absolutely placed ↩, an agent group's rows a TEXT "⋯"; the main list had no human door to a quoted reply or to a new thread.

- **The bar (Lark's shape).** ONE small toolbar per message at its right edge, its middle on the message's first line: Add reaction · Reply in thread · Quote (an agent group's row: its ⋯ — Clear content…). An overlay (absolute; transparent and click-through when hidden): shown on hover, while the keyboard is inside it (`:has(:focus-visible)` — a mouse click leaves no stuck bar) and while its picker is open. A touch device (`(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)`) never draws it: a long press on the message opens the same actions as a menu (a link / picture / selection keeps the browser's own; a chip's long press is still its who-list). New glyphs `emojiAdd` and `quote` (SVG). PURE src/lib/msg-bar-model.js decides which actions a row offers (Quote only where the channel declares it, a composer can send and the message is not inside a topic — the engine's PL5; never in the pane); src/lib/channel-msg-bar.js draws it (a WAI-ARIA toolbar: one tab stop, ← → Home End) and re-syncs drawn bars in place when the offers change. The conversation view gains `threads.placements` (PURE `placementsOf`).
- **The same handlers.** Add reaction opens THE picker (`openReactionPicker`, anchored under the button; a reaction still never opens a turn — test-architecture §64 green); Reply in thread opens the thread pane — a message inside a topic is answered there as itself, any other message starts a NEW thread rooted at it ("No replies yet.", the first reply mints it and the message grows its chip and loses Quote); Quote puts `Quoted reply — to <author>: "…"` (the approval card's own words) above the composer with ✕, and the send carries `{replyTo, placement: 'quote'}`. The pane's per-reply ↩ became the row's bar (`pane.pick`). The reaction strip exists only under a message WITH reactions — the `+` and its reserved line are gone. A channel that lists thread replies INLINE (the fake) sends no `threads` broadcast, so the message a new thread was started on learns it from the re-read page (`applyPagePlaces` → `becomeTopicRoot`, shared with the broadcast path); the fake now echoes a quoted reply into its world as a vendor lists it, and a sent quoted reply gets the same one pass kick a thread reply gets.
- **One finding on the way.** The first chrome run read every bar button at a 0×0 rect: headless Chrome reports `hover: none` with a FINE pointer, so a bare `@media (hover: none)` hid the only door there (and would on a pen); the rule is "hover none AND a coarse pointer" — what the group window's ⋯ already used.

### lane exit-run-output — the shell is the device's fact; a spawn failure names itself; the output where the user looks

The owner (2026-10-01, a screenshot of a Windows box WINDOWS-PC): "这里执行了指令怎么看不到回复。侧边栏也看不到指令和结果历史". data/exit-audit.jsonl held four `run` lines from one conversation — `nvidia-smi …`, `cmd /d /c ver`, `hostname`, `echo NOMAD_READONLY_PING` — every one `code 1`, `ms 7–8`, `ok true`, no output; the chat showed four cards "ran `…` on WINDOWS-PC — exit 1 · 0.0 s"; the agent spent a turn guessing "远端缺少或无法启动 sh". Three layers: (R1) src/exit-proxy.js ran EVERY command as `dm.runCmd('sh', ['-lc', cmd])` — the HUB chose the shell, and a Windows daemon has no `sh` (execFile ENOENT in ~8 ms); (R2) the daemon's `run-cmd` folded a spawn failure into `code: Number.isInteger(err.code) ? err.code : 1` with empty streams and dropped `err.message`; (R3) the card printed head + exit + seconds, the audit line kept no output, nothing listed a machine's runs.

- **E1 THE SHELL IS THE DEVICE'S FACT.** PURE `src/exit-shell.js` (imports nothing; the daemon bundles it): `shellPlan(platform, line)` — win32 ⇒ `cmd.exe /d /s /c "<line>"` with `windowsVerbatimArguments: true` (THE QUOTING RULE, from cmd's own /? text: /S strips the first and last quote of the text after /C and runs the rest verbatim, so ONE pair of quotes around the line and node must not re-quote; a CR / LF line is refused `ESHELLLINE` before any spawn — cmd runs one line and would drop the rest in silence), every other platform ⇒ `sh -lc` as before. The `run-cmd` op accepts `{shell: <line>}` beside the argv form; `run-shell` joins the hello-ack capabilities; client.js `runShell` is capability-gated (`host_needs_daemon`); exit-proxy sends `{shell}` to a daemon that advertises it and `sh -lc` to an older one, and the reply + the audit line name the interpreter and the platform. The device's stated platform (the dial headers' F7 statement) is now on the machine row and the Machines card. No Windows box ran this lane: the cmd.exe branch is unit-level on the PURE builder (stated, pinned, never measured) — said in the manual and the gate.
- **E2 A SPAWN FAILURE NAMES ITSELF.** `spawnFailure(err)` (an errno string under a `spawn …` syscall — ENOENT / EACCES / …; never a non-zero exit, a kill at the cap or the maxBuffer overflow) ⇒ `cmd-result.spawnError {code, message}` beside `code` = the shell's own convention an older hub still reads (127 not found / 126 not executable / 1). The hub refuses `spawn_failed` (502) with ONE sentence (`could not start `hostname` on "WINDOWS-PC" — sh: not found on that machine (ENOENT); nothing ran. "WINDOWS-PC" runs Windows: commands there run under cmd.exe — its agent is older than this VibeSpace…`), the audit line / the row's last run / the card say why, the CLI exits by the shell's code. exit-reach's REFUSALS gains the row; the words census covers it.
- **E3 OUTPUT WHERE THE USER LOOKS.** `E.outputHeads` = the ONE bound + judge: each stream cut to 4096 BYTES (said), browser-trace's `withoutUrlSecrets`, then the peer-text belt per line (a frame in a command's output is never live) — stored on the audit line (`stdout`, `stderr`, `cut`), carried by the card as a structured block (`exitRun`, through `injectPeerCard` of the three normalizers) and drawn by chat-renderers: the first three lines of stderr (else stdout) in mono under the exit line + "Show output" holding both heads (an expander on the same card — never a second card, never re-created). test-peer-text-census gains the door `outputHeads(` with its rows and an attack-leg driver; the ONE audit writer now broadcasts `exit-audit`.
- **E4 COMMAND HISTORY.** `GET /api/hosts/:id/exit-runs` (cookie; any bearer 403 `human_only`) = the owner's last 50 runs on a machine with names, verdicts, durations and the heads; `GET /api/agent/exit/runs` (vsst_) = the caller's OWN runs (`vibespace-exit runs [<machine>] [--limit N]`). src/lib/exit-runs-dialog.js ("Recent commands…" in "Who can use it", "Commands…" on the Machines card): a fresh GET, keyed `<details>` rows patched in place off `exit-audit` (an opened row stays the same node, still open), 50 kept. test-architecture §65 (D) now also censuses data/bin/vibespace-exit's paths (agent routes only) with a control.
- **E5** docs/agent/exit-manual.md (`vibespace-docs exit`): the platform rule, the output bound, the history verb; the index row points at it.
- **Reality vs the brief:** the user line is three bullets (the changelog style gate caps a bullet at 160 characters); §65 is a channels-engine census, so the owner-route pin became a (D) row for the exit CLI + the 403 pin, not a roster row; the control daemon for the §6 leg is a rebased copy bundled by esbuild (mutant-copy's CJS re-binding cannot be bundled: esbuild renames a shadowed `require`).

### lane hooks-create — VibeSpace creates ~/.claude/settings.json when the CLI never wrote one, and tells the conversations that predate it

**The incident (2026-10-01 21:50 PDT, read-only forensics on a fleet pod, VibeSpace 2.369.199).** Every boot logged `Hook registration (claude) skipped: /home/<user>/.claude/settings.json not found (start the CLI once to create it)`. The CLI does not write settings.json on its first run — only when somebody changes a setting — so a user who only chats never has one: ~/.claude with projects/, plugins/, skills/ and no settings.json since the pod's first day. VibeSpace never registered SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit / Stop there, so her agents never got the tools intro, task context or bookkeeping (0 `vibespace-reminder` in 11 transcripts); asked to "just use the browser", an agent spent four minutes probing DISPLAY, installing gcloud and listing MCP servers before it found `vibespace-browser` through an env var. Four more pods were in the same state.

- **H1 — the create rule, a closed set.** `createIfMissing` ∈ `false | 'dir-exists'` (src/harness-config.js `CREATE_RULES` / `createRule`): the FILE is created when its directory exists (the directory proves the CLI has run here), never the directory. The legacy `true` was the same rule (the writer has never created a directory) and is read as 'dir-exists'; codex's hooks.json + config.toml now declare it by name — **codex's rule did not change**, only the created file's mode (umask before, 0600 now). claude's SETTINGS_FILE moved `false` → 'dir-exists'. A created file is written to a tmp and LINKED into place exclusively — a settings.json the CLI wrote in that gap is never replaced (EEXIST ⇒ re-read + re-apply over the CLI's content) — mode 0600, chowned to its directory's owner when the writer runs as root. Both writers answer `'created'` (truthy: every `&&`/`!!` caller unchanged); the refusal for a missing file carries `e.missing` = `no-dir` ("<dir> not found — the CLI has not run on this machine; nothing is created") or `not-ours`; `readConfigPlan` names the kind in the receipt's `reason` (`will-create` | `no-dir` | `not-ours`) — the only free field a remote helper's CFG line carries, so the chip reads it on every machine. The plan carries the rule by name (an older helper reads `'dir-exists'` truthy = the same rule). The boot CLI-config plan (cleanupPeriodDays) follows the same rule and logs `[cli-config] created ~/.claude/settings.json (the CLI had never written one) (boot)`. `ensureAgentHooks` logs `created ~/.claude/settings.json (the CLI had never written one) and registered VibeSpace hooks` and calls `onHookFileCreated`; `agentHooksStatus` adds `dirExists` / `creatable`. `hookRegistrationSafe` is unchanged (a worktree / temp server never writes). The shipped register helper (it embeds harness-config.js) is regenerated, so remote hosts follow the rule at the next install / spawn.
- **H2 — the words.** A missing file says what is true now (src/lib/cli-config-chips.js `receiptLine`): `will-create` locally = "… will be created at the next start — or press Apply" with `apply: true` — the Settings window draws a working **Apply** beside it, the Machines card's primary button becomes **Apply** while a file will be created (both `POST /api/cli-config/apply`, human-triggered: the hook registration with `auto: true` — the master switch and a Remove opt-out still hold — plus the CLI-config plan; a temp server root answers 409 `unsafe_root`); on a remote host "… will be created at the next tool install or session start on that machine" (no button); `no-dir` (dim) "~/.claude not found — the CLI has not run on this machine, so nothing is written"; no reason (an older helper) "not found". The Machines card's hook state reads "{label}: will be created at the next start — or press Apply" / "{label}: the CLI has not run on this machine". "start the CLI once to create it" and "{label}: run the CLI once first" are retired from code, zh and ja (test-harness-settings §8's census over 470 files).
- **H3 — the conversations already running.** A CLI process keeps the hook configuration it started with (the brief's premise; the 2.1.281 binary carries a per-session hooks snapshot — not measured live, no CLI was run). src/server/hooks-late.js (ORCH) gets `onHookFileCreated`, HOLDS it until `ready()` (server.js calls it right after `restoreSessions()` — the boot registration runs before the restore), then queues ONE note per running LOCAL session of that harness that reads the file (ssh / dial sessions and a wrapper-injected codex chat excluded; once per webui id) through the existing queue (session-status kind `hooks-late`, `replaceKind`): "VibeSpace's hooks were registered after this conversation started — Terminate and Resume it to get the tools context" — never a billed turn. **What the brief did not foresee:** for claude that queue is drained ONLY by the UserPromptSubmit hook — the very hook such a session may lack. So the note carries the webui id it was queued for and agent-routes drops it unread in any OTHER process of the conversation (`hooksLateStale`, before the queue is peeked): a Terminate + Resume starts with the hooks and must never read "Terminate and Resume it". If the running CLI does pick the new hooks up, the note rides its next prompt; if it does not, the For-you line is the carrier. The owner gets ONE For-you line (origin agent, kind action) only when at least one session predates it: "{n} running Claude Code conversations started before VibeSpace registered its hooks — Terminate and Resume them to give their agents the VibeSpace tools" (zh "有 {n} 个正在运行的 {label} 对话早于 VibeSpace 注册 hook 启动——终止并恢复它们，它们的 agent 才能获得 VibeSpace 工具", ja "実行中の {label} の会話 {n} 件は VibeSpace が hook を登録する前に開始されました — 終了して再開すると、それぞれの agent が VibeSpace のツールを使えるようになります"; the singular too), the conversations by name in the detail. The user's typed text is never rewritten (the typing path's directive stands).
- **Gates.** The brief's test-harness-config / test-agent-hooks / test-cli-config-chips do not exist; their asserts went to the nearest suites (the coordinator's rule): **test-claude-retention 88** (§6 the rule table: no-dir refused + said + no directory, created 0600 + registered, the CAS path + mode kept, a symlink written through, not-ours, a no-op creates nothing, the create-gap race, the TOML writer, the receipt kinds + CFG round trip, the boot plan alone creates; CONTROLS: a patched copy whose create path makes the directory fails the no-dir leg, the pre-lane `false` on the incident's shape registers nothing; §7 ensureAgentHooks on a /tmp/vs-hkc-<pid> HOME with ~/.claude absent / present, the journal line, the callback once, the belt; §8 the notes per session kind, the exact sentence, ONE For-you line + its zh/ja structure, once per session, the stale drop for a resumed process, no line when nothing runs, never a billed turn, the Apply route's three answers; §9 wiring pins; the owner's real CLI config hashed before / after — byte- and mtime-identical), **test-harness-settings 198** (§8 the four missing kinds + the retired-sentence census; the plan pins), **test-harness-contract 374** (the identity pin holds; the rule ∈ the closed set), **test-user-todos-layout 235** (the producer census learns src/server/hooks-late.js — 20 sites), test-architecture 404, i18n-check.
- **Scope kept.** No change to what the hooks inject, no new hook event, nothing written when ~/.claude is absent, never a directory created. Not covered: a session restored LATER than `restoreSessions()` (an R6 pipe session re-opened asynchronously — the switch is off by default) is not counted.

### lane hooks-create H5 — on a machine with no desktop session, an unset window preference means a hidden window (the owner's decision, 2026-10-01 22:05 PDT)

**Why.** `browser.headed` unset ('' = inherit the CLI's own config) meant headless on a fleet pod (no desktop, no user config), and Google sign-in refuses headless Chrome (the same pod tonight, another user before). The hidden-window rung (the CLI's own invisible Xvfb, UA Chrome/154 — measured in lane headless-fallback) existed but only answered a window someone ASKED for.

- **The rule, PURE** (src/browser-display.js `resolveHeaded({setting, display, mode})`): an explicit yes / no wins; UNSET on a machine with NO desktop session (no live Wayland / X socket — a stale DISPLAY counts as none) where Xvfb is installed and `browser.noDisplayMode` is auto ⇒ a window is asked for ⇒ the hidden-window rung; with a desktop, without Xvfb, Xvfb unknown, or "Always headless" ⇒ today's meaning (inherit). `noDesktop(d)` exported beside it.
- **Where it is resolved — at the LAUNCH, never at the spawn.** The keeper's launch fact (`displays.factFor({…, preference})` — both local launch sites, the conversation's browser and a named profile) resolves the stored preference against the probe it just took; the fact records `wanted.byDefault: true`, and `planForFact` re-derives the same plan from it, so every later call (the agent's verbs through /resolve, the keeper's own cdp-url, the live view) names the same planned file — `headed: true`, x11 pinned — and nothing restarts. Rung D's spawn config (browser-env) keeps the preference AS STORED: it is composed at the spawn, and a config that baked "no desktop now" would open a VISIBLE window on a dev box whose desktop logged in later. **The deviation from the brief's wording:** the keeper's `headedSetting()` stays the STORED value (it composes base configs and is what a paired machine receives); the ONE resolution is `resolveHeaded`, called where the display is probed — the keeper's launch fact for a local browser, and the paired machine's own `browser-serve start` (src/browser-serve.js `planLaunch`) for its browser: the hub's display must not decide a remote machine's (a remote desktop would otherwise get a visible window). An older daemon receives the stored null and keeps today's meaning.
- **The words.** The `browser.headed` row: the unset option reads "Unset: a hidden window without a desktop, else ~/.agent-browser/config.json"; the description "… Unset (default): on a machine without a desktop, a hidden window when Xvfb is installed; otherwise whatever your own ~/.agent-browser/config.json says. … Applies to the next browser that starts — a browser already running is not restarted." Settings' fact line (GET /api/browser/display now answers `preference`): on such a machine with the setting unset "This machine has no desktop session now — with the window setting unset, an agent's browser runs in a hidden window (the live view can still take over)"; with Headless chosen "… the window setting says Headless, so an agent's browser runs headless". zh / ja for all four (the retired option label and description removed from both dictionaries).
- **Gates.** test-browser-display 116 (① THE TABLE — 13 rows: desktop × Xvfb × preference × mode, the stale-DISPLAY pod row exact, the fact's `byDefault` re-derived from a base that says nothing or false; CONTROL: a patched copy without the no-desktop branch — the old inherit — reads exactly the 3 no-desktop rows as inherit; ③ a fleet-pod keeper: no user config, Xvfb on the launch PATH, setting unset ⇒ launched HEADED on the CLI's own Xvfb, the launch config it names carries headed:true, `wanted.byDefault`, UA Chrome/154, no restart; 'no' ⇒ headless + the fact line says so; a live Wayland socket ⇒ inherit; a paired machine's `browser-serve start` with the preference unset resolves against ITS display — hidden window with Xvfb, headless without; the keeper control's anchor follows the launch line); test-browser-env 36 (②b rung D's spawn config keeps unset unset, the keeper's launch config from it = headed:true on a no-desktop + Xvfb machine, inherit with a desktop / no / headless / an older caller). **A suite that depended on the box:** test-browser-env ③'s keeper ran with `/usr/bin` on its PATH, so on a box with Xvfb and no desktop session in the suite's env an unset preference now planned the hidden window and the x11 pin landed after the keeper mark ("mark last" — a composition convention; the mark is read anywhere on the command line); its keeper now runs on a private PATH holding only `sleep` (test-browser-display's rule: the rung is chosen by what the suite puts on the PATH, never by what the box has installed).

### lane notify-retry — one 5-second attempt decided for ever

The owner (phone screenshot of 设备运维大师, 14:55 PDT): "以前这个是自动唤醒的啊 怎么现在开始排队要我手动发了？". Forensics (read-only): the cron job dc-discussion-watch woke its owner conversation 7 times (09-29 → 10-01 07:36, `lane: message, ok: true`); at 14:17:13 one local peer post answered `timeout` (postToPeer's 5 s) ⇒ stashed ⇒ at 14:17:15 the stash "waits for the next prompt — the 900 B digest does not fit the 0 B left under the inline cap" ⇒ nothing until the owner typed at 14:53, and the hand-over card then said "These completed while this conversation was closed" (the CLI pid lived throughout).

- **The mechanism, measured.** `postToPeer` reported `timeout` only when the `connect` event never arrived in 5 s. On Linux a unix-socket connect completes AT THE SYSCALL or fails at once — measured here with a python listener that never accepts: `listen(1)` queues two, the third answers `EAGAIN@0 ms`, never a hang — and libuv hands the connect callback to the NEXT loop iteration's pending phase, which runs AFTER the timers phase. So any stall of OUR loop longer than the timer, right after `net.connect()`, fired "timeout" on a connection that had already succeeded (the box's load is 100+; the kb already records 11–17 s create/kill loop gaps on a fleet pod). Reproduced in test-notify-retry §1 (c) on the pre-fix copy (`scripts/fixtures/peer-messaging-prefix.js`): a 160 ms synchronous stall over a 40 ms timer = `{ok:false, reason:'timeout'}` while the frame reached the inbox.
- **R2 — the primitive judges by phases.** `postToPeer` now records `phase` (connect → write → written → closed), `elapsedMs`, `transient` (the timer, EAGAIN, ECONNRESET/EPIPE before the flush ⇒ true; ENOENT/ECONNREFUSED/ENOTSOCK ⇒ false: a socket nobody serves), `late` (how far past the timer the verdict came — the one number that tells a stalled loop from a refusing CLI in the journal) and `closeError` (a reset AFTER the flush is named, never a failure — the CLI dedups its inbox; whether it read the frame is the ambiguity). The timer defers its verdict one loop turn (`setImmediate`) so a queued connect / flush is heard first; a write still in flight gets one bounded grace (1 s); a flushed frame is never a timeout. The ladder's journal line carries `phase`, `ms`, `late` and `target mid-turn: yes|no|unknown` (the server's `_isStreaming`; a terminal session by recent output), the jobs engine's `notifyLog` entry carries `phase` / `busy` / `late` — the owner's instance tells us within a day which cause it was.
- **R1 — the retry park (src/server/conversation-deliver.js).** A transient miss while `findPeer` still names a live pid, for a caller that opted in (`opts.retry` — the jobs engine), is PARKED in `data/msg-retry.json` (never stashed): the same text is posted at the conversation's next turn end (server.js wraps the pool engine's `noteTurnEnd` — the ONE name the claude / codex / ACP consumers destructure — to wake the park) and on a bounded backoff while idle (30 s, 1, 2, 5, 10 min, then every 10 min; the SCHEDULE is bounded at 60 min from the first miss — a verifier-class find of my own: bounding at the attempt let the ninth retry schedule a tenth at 68 min), then falls to the producer's stash as `not-reachable` with the attempts' facts. A dead pid / a socket nobody serves stashes at once as before, typed `not-running` (the "no live inbox" answer too). The money: the first attempt's authorization is HELD on the parked entry and converted when the retry lands — ONE billed wake; a hold is given back on its own TTL (a timer at holdAt + RESERVE_TTL − 5 s, never on a reschedule: a turn end inside the TTL converts it without asking again) and the next attempt re-judges; a refusal / a throwing authorizer at a re-judge falls to the stash as `spend-cap` (fail closed, nothing posted). The park's own floor: no retry post within 30 s of the last SUCCESSFUL post to that conversation. On disk at every mutation, an `inflight` stamp during the post (a crash inside it is said by id at the next boot, a duplicate possible, the CLI dedups); the previous process's holds are forgotten and re-judged. A hand-over CLAIMS parked entries by id (`claimRetry`) and TAKES them (`retryTake`, the hold given back — the hand-over bills its own turn); a prompt's drain takes them too when the digest fits (free, `via: 'prompt'`).
- **R3 — the stash speaks through the post when the prompt cannot carry it.** `drainNotifsUnderCap` / `drainStashUnderCap` (agent-routes) ARM a hand-over (`deliver.armStashHandover`, only for a live local peer, in memory) when the section does not fit the inline cap, and log "N stashed notification(s) will arrive as a message when this turn ends" instead of "wait for the next prompt"; the stash-handover module's turn-end listener runs it as ONE frame under the new declared reason `stash-retry` (spelled literally beside `stash-handover`, the spend census reads the literal), after the ladder's floor if a post just landed (deferred, re-checked idle + live + still waiting; a turn running again re-arms for its own end); a refusal leaves the stash and is logged; the next starved prompt re-arms. The arm is consumed before the park's own attempts, so one turn end = one frame. The fact carries `armed: true` and the strip says "they will arrive as a message when this turn ends".
- **R4 — the words.** `renderNotifStash`'s tail is by the entries' `held` kinds ("These arrived while this conversation was not running." / "The agent did not accept these when they arrived (busy or unreachable) — delivered now." / "These were waiting for a retry — delivered now." / rate-floor / spend-cap / mixed); the hand-over card's head carries "— <why>" (`heldWhyOf`, a closed table read back by `handoverFacts` as a nested key the client translates — chat-renderers translates a `{key}` param); `HELD_KINDS` gains `not-running` + `retrying`; the Background Work panel words each kind and the Delivery log says "parked for retry (connect, agent busy) · next attempt 14:17:43" / "after 3 retries"; the strip: "1 notice is being retried for this agent · next attempt in 25 s or when this turn ends", the Details row "Background Work · dc-watch · being retried"; zh / ja for every string.
- **R5 — floors untouched.** The jobs engine's 30 s floor still stamps at the attempt; a delivery that LANDS re-stamps it with the raw text's digest (the floor counts the successful delivery); the park's retries re-ask the ladder's floor, never the budget.
- **Where reality forced a change.** (1) The 60-min bound is on the schedule, not the attempt. (2) A hold is released on its own TTL timer, not when the next step would outlive it — the first cut released it at the 90 s reschedule and the 100 s turn end had to re-authorize (two authorizations for one wake). (3) `not-reachable` for a REMOTE daemon miss keeps the old kind (the brief's scope excludes remote), so the sentence says "busy or unreachable". (4) The `busy` measurement on a terminal session is "recent output", stated as unknown otherwise. (5) The strip's "next attempt in N" is re-spelled only when the fact changes (every attempt re-publishes it) — no ticking clock.

### lane browser-admin — New profile…, a profile's Chrome build, the browser CLI VibeSpace drives

The owner's two browser gaps (2026-09-30): a profile could not be created by hand (the only create was a conversation's card menu, a label and nothing else), and nothing could pin a browser version. Five chunks, each its own commit.

Every provider is a row with its state for the chosen machine (never hidden; CloakBrowser not installed offers Install… behind the download confirm); machines are this computer + paired machines, greyed WITH the reason; "Who can use it" = the principal picker, default every conversation. ONE POST; `use` is judged by the PATCH's own verdict over an empty record BEFORE the mint (`ownerFromUse`) — the record is born with its list in one write.
- **2a · a profile's Chrome build.** `profile.browser` = default | a build under `~/.agent-browser/browsers/chrome-<v>/chrome` on the profile's machine | a chrome file the user names. F5 (LOW, credential — the lane's own "versions only" rule): a `{kind:'path'}` choice's PATH reached the agent on every profile-shaped answer (`agentProfileView` spreads the record: `browser.path`, `buildMissing.what`), on `status`'s lease rows (`browserView` carries `browserChoice` AND the launch view `launchEnv` with `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH`) and on the switcher view `forAgent`; only `providers` stripped its root. ### lane custom-app — apps that survive a rebuilt machine (Layer 0 of docs/design-app-persistence.zh.md, B-ce6d)

The owner: users install apps, their agents help, and the apps survive a pod recreation. Layer 0 = the manifest + the local `.deb` cache + the human gate, on every pod with no image or chart change (Layer 1, the app SYSTEM on the volume, is the next lane). D3 as revised: the door is the user's (the Desktop apps dialog); an agent only proposes; ZERO new lines in the per-turn teaching.

- **PURE src/app-manifest.js** — the index schema, apt's own words → the plan with named refusals (needs_snap · conflict · removes · not_found · bad_name · bad_source · no_sudo · no_apt · disk with the numbers · shared), .desktop → catalog rows through validateAppRow, the dpkg set byte-identical to the root script's `q` (the base sha), the repository's stanzas / file names (no `%3a` — the epoch dropped), cacheVerdict (closure − base ⊆ cache, P15), replayRungs, driftVerdict, and THE ONE root script (nine modes; every name an argv POSITION; every argument judged before root is asked; the authority root reads is root-owned `debs/` + `sys/`, never the user-writable manifest; `SUDO_UID`'s own apps dir only). Fixtures are REAL: this Ubuntu box's `apt-get -s` and a throwaway Debian 12 container's installs (scripts/capture-app-fixtures.sh); the one invented input is the snap simulation's empty dpkg status. Measured shape the parser had wrong at first: a Debian 12 security-mirror `--print-uris` line has NO hash.
- **SHARED src/app-serve.js** (bundled by the daemon through desktop-serve) — the six `app-*` ops of the desktop-serve table: plans as the user (the system's lists, else the user's own — a container image ships none), a .deb staged + bound by sha256, a source's key fetched over https with its OpenPGP fingerprints (checked against gpg's on two real public keyrings); the RECORD reads the slot's own log by the run's nonce and the ROOT-OWNED entries (a user-written list or a forged log line is never a row). Capability `app-install` in the hello-ack; the client asks the app ops only of a daemon that names it.
- **The slot, generalised** — desktop-access `installPackage(host, {what:'app:…', planOpts})`: the machine's own plan through a registered planner, its own argv through THE SAME launcher (one install per machine, a running one followed — test-desktop-serve §11), the digest binding the closure (an xpra digest unchanged).
- **ORCH** src/server/apps-engine.js + apps-wiring.js (server.js: one line + the replay after listen) + src/routes/apps.js — the proposal (planned first; ONE For-you item, new origin `apps`), the run (the user's press), Not now, `wait` (each move; a terminal answer takes the stashed copy back), the outcome through the stash (sender `VibeSpace apps`, a new NOTIFICATION_SENDERS row; package-written pieces through the peer-text belt — a new census row), the boot replay (marker hit = nothing; rung 1 offline then rung 2; ONE notice), `restoring…` rows, THE icon route (image types, nosniff, a sandboxed SVG). Every user route refuses an agent's token 403 (a census).
- **The client** — "Your installed apps" in the Desktop apps dialog, Install an app… / a .deb (+ the explorer's "Install this package…") / a package source / Let an agent help… (a temporary helper conversation through create + initialMessage; first message = the request + the whole apps manual + the machine's facts), the updates chip + Refresh, the drift row + Adopt; THE install dialog (`showInstallDialog` what:'app') shows the plan's facts above every command; the For-you row and window answer a proposal in place. zh + ja for every sentence.
- **The agent** — data/bin/vibespace-app (AGENT_TOOLS): search / list / plan / install + remove (= propose) / status / wait / docs, a source as its own proposal; `add --kind uv|npm|appimage` HELD (agent-tool-rules); docs/agent/apps-manual.md + one index row.
- **Gates** — test-app-manifest (fast, 174) · test-apps-engine (fast, 91: engine + routes + the CLI as an agent runs it; a package summary carrying a frame opener reaches the agent inert) · test-desktop-serve (210, §11) · test-desktop-remote (73, the slot's re-attach on the generalised runner) · test-app-install (heavy, 33, 62 s: a REAL apt in five Debian 12 containers over one home — install / .deb / a package built there that exists in NO archive / drift + Adopt / xterm's rows / remove / Refresh, the stanzas = the PURE builder, root refusing a foreign apps dir, then a fresh root filesystem with NO network replays all four offline in ~2.5 s, the next boot the marker hit (control: an empty repository); then a fresh root filesystem whose image changed replays ONLINE through rung 2 in ~7 s, the local-only package included — rung 2 reads the machine's sources AND the local repository, found by this leg (control: a patched copy without that line names the package failed)) · test-apps-ui (heavy, 30, chrome over the stub seam) · test-inbox-window-ui (heavy, the For-you window's Install… / Not now) · the censuses: inbox origin ⑪ (21 sites), the peer-text census (the stash row + vibespace-app a DECLARED CLI: package-written words belted at the agent routes), the record-clear reader census (three receivers named), the approval census (an `apps` row: the stored request shown, the digest pressed, plan_changed at the press), channel-record's frame census (the CLI's placeholders carry no hyphen), agent-tool-rules, test-architecture, user-todos-layout. The FAST tier green at the lane's head (213 suites, 427 s); its first two runs were red on this lane's own misses (a dead CSS token; the CLI unrostered) — fixed at the cause.
- **Verify r1 (authority · credential · kill · peer-text)** — F1 the entry id a run writes under is chosen against ROOT's records (an agent's edit of manifest.json made an approved install replace another app's root record, digest unchanged); a source root holds is "already added". F2 the same ask again is the open proposal; a For-you item per proposal id; nothing-to-install refused. F3 a plan / proposal view to an agent belted whole (a source's origin words, a .desktop Name). F4 the replay marker only after a replay with no failed entry (a partial one was never retried; an install before the boot replay suppressed it), `present`, the Put back door. F5 a held package is installed on both sides (`q` kept only `ii`). F6 an app with no saved .deb says it will not come back. F7 a plain `dpkg -i` is drift too (the dpkg status file's write time). F8 the why loses hidden characters at the door. Each with a heavy container leg or a fast gate and a patched-copy control.
- **Held for Layer 1 and later** — the app system on the volume (zero replay, `sys.` rows, Rebase / Repair), a base-id stamp + `base-packages.tsv` in the image (until then the base is the first-captured dpkg set, re-taken on a fresh root filesystem), the fleet-wide `refresh --all`, the sidebar hiding a helper conversation, a source proposal's packages chained, the replay of a PAIRED machine at its reconnect (its rootfs persists — Layer 0 replays this machine), services (`after: apps`), uv / npm / AppImage entries shown in the dialog.

### lane mobile-select — a long press on chat text selects it; the message menu opens from a … button

**User line (Fixed):** On a phone, pressing and holding text in a chat now selects it as it should — the message menu no longer pops up over the words you are selecting; it opens from the message's … button instead.
**zh:** 在手机上，长按聊天里的文字现在会正常选中它 — 消息菜单不再弹在你正在选择的文字上；改为从消息的 … 按钮打开。
**ja:** スマートフォンでチャットの文字を長押しすると、正しく選択されるようになりました — 選択中の文字の上にメッセージメニューが開くことはなくなり、メニューはメッセージの … ボタンから開きます。

- **The report and the measured order.** A tester's phone (via the owner): copying a passage of a chat opened the message menu and the selection landed on the menu. Measured in Chrome's own touch gesture path (`Emulation.setEmitTouchEventsForMouse('mobile')`, 390×844 DPR 3, Android UA — `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` never produces the native long press in headless): touchstart on the `<p>` → +501 ms OUR synthetic (untrusted) contextmenu, the chat cancels it and opens its menu with the corner at the finger → +680 ms the native long press: selectstart (the word is selected) → a TRUSTED contextmenu, pointerType touch → the chat cancels it and builds the menu a second time → selectionchange with the word under the menu. iOS fires no contextmenu on a long press: our 500 ms timer was the only menu, racing iOS's selection (the code assumes exactly that). The cause: design-mobile-gaps #5 (2026-09-20) made a long press ANYWHERE on a message open its menu, because the hover buttons are hidden ≤ 768 px.
- **M1 — one door, one rule.** PURE `src/lib/press-select.js` (press target class × device ⇒ menu | selection | native) and utils.js `installLongPressContextMenu`, THE door of a touch long press: on selectable text (a glyph within 6 px of the finger whose effective user-select is not none) the timer is never armed and a trusted touch contextmenu is stopped before any handler WITHOUT preventDefault (the platform's handles and Copy bar stay); controls (button, summary, role=button, menus), gutters, pictures and user-select:none labels keep the menu; once an app handler took such a menu press, `selectstart` is cancelled while the finger is down (the heavy leg's second measurement: a long press on a message's 3 px role strip opened our menu, then Chrome selected "Answer" and that selection closed the menu), and when the platform's long press comes first our contextmenu fires at its `selectstart`; a press nobody takes (the file viewer) keeps the platform's selection and its own long-press menu; the trusted contextmenu is one PURE table (pass / stop on text / swallow after ours was taken — it had built the menu twice). The chat's menu on touch: a … button per user / assistant message (`addMsgMoreBtn`, 36×28, floated as the content's first child — the words wrap around it; measured: over none of 8 messages' words), plus a long press on the role strip, a `<summary>` toggle or the role label (`.chat-role` is now user-select none). Mouse right-click unchanged. The rule reaches every `user-select` opt-in (the chat list, the For-you texts, the For-you window's item); their menus stay on the rows' non-text parts.
- **M2 — chrome text is never selectable.** style.css says `user-select: none` ITSELF on `[data-popover], .context-menu, #global-toasts, .global-toast, .overlap-switcher, .tab-item, .chat-msg-more` (unprefixed like the page rule — an inherited `-webkit-` none breaks typing in a field on older iOS), so chrome built inside a selectable region never inherits `text`; `onOutsidePress` gained `selection` (default = once): on a touch device a transient menu / popover closes when a text selection starts outside it (a long press is never an outside tap, so the closer never saw it), never on a caret, a form control's selection, its own opening selection or a mouse device.
- **M3 — Copy text names what it copied.** The touch menu's Copy text puts the WHOLE message on the clipboard and says so: "Copied the whole message (N lines)" (zh/ja added) — the terminal's Copy screen precedent; a code block keeps its own Copy button.

### lane-drag-release — a release over a pane the page cannot hear (userW's inc-muq7uk0f-e59s, 17:19 PDT; the addendum inc-muq7wwfq-rruz, 17:21 PDT)

The owner, twice within two minutes (Mac, DPR 2.2, UI scale 0.9, a PDF `viewer` window over a Desktop window): a PDF viewer dropped onto the cell of the Desktop window did not fit — the snap highlight stayed, the window stayed put, the drag stayed armed; a resize released over that window kept resizing when the pointer came back ("松开鼠标之后，仍然像是抓着这个缩放的角落"); and the viewer could grow but not shrink ("能放大，不能缩小").

THE CLASS (the lane M class, second strike). The title-bar drag and the resize ended on a document-level `mouseup`. A release hit-tested on another window's iframe never reaches this document (the embedded page gets it — the Web view, the PDF viewer's own page is an iframe); noVNC's canvas stops its mouse events (stopPropagation + preventDefault). So the release was never heard: the drag stayed armed with its highlight, and the moves of an inward resize over the viewer's OWN page were lost too (it grew, it would not shrink). REPRODUCED FIRST in chrome on a 2×3 grid with a Web view iframe, a real Xtigervnc Desktop, a fake agent-browser live view and the real xpra rung (scripts/test-window-drag-ui.mjs, DRJ_ONLY=D,R,P): the drop and the inward resize over the Web view and the Desktop reproduced red on b924041f; the live-view picture and the xpra pane do NOT stop a mouse release (measured, printed) — the Web view and the Desktop are the two provable swallowers, and the PDF viewer's own frame is the third.

D1 POINTER CAPTURE ENDS EVERY DRAG. The title bar and each resize handle take a POINTER press and `setPointerCapture` the pointer on that element; the drag is fed from it (capture delivers every pointer event there whatever the cursor crosses — an iframe, a canvas, another window, the page's edge). ONE end door per drag: PURE `src/lib/drag-end.js` `dragEndVerdict` names what ends one — pointerup / pointercancel / lostpointercapture of the drag's pointer, the window's blur, the page hidden, and a `pointermove` with `buttons === 0` (a release the page never saw); another pointer's events, a held move, the page becoming visible and a second end are no-ops (the drag ends ONCE — the snap highlight cleared there, the drop applied where the pointer last was). The existing holds (the pointerup's geometry witness `_boundsAt`, the `_bornAt` rule) key on the same door. A press the browser gives no pointerId (or refuses capture) falls to a document feed with every end rule still applied. The seamless hand-over (xpra `initiate-moveresize`) carries the press's pointerId and captures it too.

D2 THE DRAG SHIELD. `body.wm-dragging` (set at the drag's threshold and the resize's start, lifted at the end door) ⇒ every window's content — and iframe / canvas / img / embed / object by name — is `pointer-events: none !important` (public/style.css), so the snap hit test is the workspace's for the whole gesture and no pane takes the moves or the release. The title bar and the handles are `touch-action: none` (a touch drag is pointermove, never the page's pan).

D3 THE OCCUPIED CELL. Unchanged stacking: the drop fits the dragged window into the cell exactly as onto an empty one (`_snapToGrid` → `_positionToCell`), two windows share the cell (a cell is a position, never a slot — the occupant's box is untouched); the highlight is the keyed grid-cell element, cleared by the end door, never a timer.

D5 THE VIEWER THAT COULD GROW BUT NOT SHRINK. With capture + the shield, the inward resize over the viewer's own iframe is delivered and `clampToMin` holds the window at its minimum. A `viewer` / `editor` / `browser` window has NO minimum of its own — `windowMinForPane`/`setMinSize`'s only caller is the desktop-app window (pinned); the floor is the `.window` CSS 320×180. The clamp reads the pointer delta in layout px (viewport ÷ the UI scale), so at scale 0.9 × DPR 2.2 the shrink the pointer asks for is the shrink it gets. Measured in chrome: a 1000×700 PDF viewer at UI 90 % × DPR 2.2 shrinks to 320×180, left/top kept.

Gates: test-window-drag (fast, 33 — the PURE end-door table, the real WindowManager over a fake DOM modelling pointer capture + a swallowing iframe + a stopping pane: the incident, every end kind for the drag and the resize, D3, the D5 × zoom × dpr table, the setMinSize census; controls = one drag-end copy per rule + the pre-capture feed). test-window-drag-ui (heavy, the reproduction + the base commit b924041f as the control bundle via esbuild onLoad). test-window-minsize and test-desktop-seamless updated to the pointer door (their fake `fireDoc` now sets `event.type`, as the DOM does). test-desktop-move / test-stage-visibility / test-split-ux / test-outside-press / test-architecture unchanged.

VERIFY r1 (adversarial, 2026-10-01). Two findings, both reproduced in chrome on b2fc3f89 before the fix. (1) HIGH — the third and fourth drag doors were still the pre-fix feed: the TAB TEAR-OFF (`tab-group.js _setupTabDrag`) and the ICON-merge drag (`_setupIconDrag`) ended on the document's `mouseup`, so a torn-off tab released over the Web view / Desktop pane stayed `.dragging` with the highlight on and armed, and an icon drag released there left its source window `visibility:hidden` with the ghost on screen (the window vanished). FIX = ONE feed for the four doors: `src/lib/drag-feed.js` (`captureOn`, `attachDragFeed` — DRAG_FEED's four events on the capturing element else the document, the window's blur, the page's visibility, a per-drag controller joined to the owner's —, `setDragShield`); window.js's two doors moved onto it, tab-group.js's two doors take a pointerdown, capture the pointer (the tab drag on the strip's TITLE BAR — the element the tear-off's re-render keeps; the tab element is rebuilt and a capture on it would be lost under the finger), ask `dragEndVerdict` at one end door each, and raise the shield. (2) LOW — the xpra hand-over's hold (`xpra-view.js wmHold`) waited for a document pointerup alone: a drag the WM now ends on blur / hidden / a no-button move left the pane deaf (no motion to X) and the X button down until the next click anywhere; the hold now asks the same verdict (pointerup / pointercancel / pointermove buttons==0 / blur / hidden) and releases the button at once. Measured in chrome: a mouse OR pen release the page never saw arrives as `lostpointercapture` first, then a `pointermove` with `buttons === 0` — both rules end a drag; no title-bar re-render (rename, chips, a rebuilt tab bar) replaces the title-bar ELEMENT, so a capture on it survives every re-render (window.js:113 creates it once; `_renderTabBar` rebuilds children only). Gates: test-window-drag 36 (icon-drag end-kind rows over the real mixin on the fake DOM; the pre-capture control is now a closed world of three copies — drag-feed / tab-group / window — so one patched feed reverts every door; §4 pins ONE feed and no document mouse feed in either file), test-window-drag-ui (+ legs T / I: the torn-off tab and the icon drag onto each pane; the control overlays the base commit's tab-group.js too), test-xpra-client 279 (its fake events now carry `type`, as the DOM's do).

VERIFY r2 (adversarial, 2026-10-02; the door census + attacks on r1's parts). (1) HIGH — a window CLOSED mid-drag (closeWindow aborts `_listenerCtl` first ⇒ the feed died, no end door ran) left `body.wm-dragging` up for good: every window's content dead to the mouse until another drag completed (chrome: the Web view iframe `pointer-events:none`, grid overlay + highlight stuck, the icon's ghost stuck). FIX = the feed's `owner-gone` end (drag-feed.js, named by PURE drag-end.js) + every door CANCELS, nothing dropped. (2) LOW — the shield was a boolean: a mouse + a touch drag at once, the first end lowered it for the second ⇒ `setDragShield(on, key)`, a holder set. (3) THE CENSUS (T1): twelve handle-style doors still on the document's mouseup / a bare pointerup (Resizer, theme editor ×2, minimap, top-bar + taskbar handles, explorer column, viewer pan + pptx sidebar, customize move, split divider, queue reorder) ⇒ ONE call `startPointerDrag`; test-window-drag §5 = the grep-derived census (16 feed doors in 10 files, every document/window move-or-end listener named with its reason, 3 planted controls). Gate test-window-drag 36 → 53: owner-gone legs, the fake DOM's removal rule (T2⑤) + legs, two feeds as two holders, the `!win` branch pinned by its statements (T2⑥), two feed controls. Refuted: the 3-tab host / active-guest tear-off (chrome: ended + fit), the xpra hold's new ends, the widened pin's harm.

### lane profile-lock-roll — a renamed machine's profile lock, and the first command after a restart (userW's pod test, 2026-10-01 14:24–14:35 PDT)

Read-only forensics of userW's pod (2.369.198, image 3.6.0, agent-browser 0.38.1, Chromium 154) after a pod roll (hostname `vibespace-pod-a-5d6f7c8b9a-x1y2z` → `…-7e8f9a0b1c-p3q4r`, the same RWO home):

- **W1 — the lock of a dead pod.** His pinned profile "jarvis-work" refused every start: `profile_locked — … is held by another browser process (pid 452500 on vibespace-pod-a-5d6f7c8b9a-x1y2z) — the lock (…/SingletonLock) names another machine … remove …`. Chromium's `SingletonLock` is a symlink `<hostname>-<pid>` inside the profile directory on the PVC; the old pod died with it in place; Chromium judges the lock by hostname and refuses for ever. His agent removed `Singleton{Lock,Socket,Cookie}` by hand, as the sentence suggested.
- **W2 — the bound tab of the previous life.** Right after the hand-fix the first verbs answered `tab_gone: bound tab is gone (target DC0C…, last url about:blank). Run agent-browser tab new …` — the binary keeps a session's bound tab (by CDP target id) across a daemon restart (its own `tab --help`) and, pinned, refuses once it is gone; every tab of a replaced browser is gone. The keeper's `stop()` already marks every lease so its next attach binds a tab first — a browser life the keeper did NOT end (a daemon found dead, a boot that could not adopt it, an in-place relaunch) left the leases unmarked.
- **W3 — not this lane.** `navigator.webdriver` true under the hidden-window rung on 2.369.198: the automation flag shipped in 2.369.199 (lane browser-propose); the remedy is ⚙ → Update.

**L1 — the lock verdict knows a renamed machine (src/browser-profiles.js `profileLockVerdict`, src/server/browser-keeper.js, src/browser-facts.js).** The witness is the keeper's OWN registry, never an assumed RWO fact: every launch stamps the browser record with the machine's hostname (`rec.host`, the lineage `rec.hosts`, ≤ 8, carried onto every new record like the launch mark) and `save()` stamps the registry file with its writer (`reg.host`). `profileLockVerdict({…, launchHosts})`: a lock whose hostname ≠ ours AND ∈ the recorded launch hosts ⇒ `stale-previous-host` — `clearProfileLock` removes the three Singleton SYMLINKS (`F.removeSingletonFiles`, a regular file of that name is left), says in the journal "the lock named this machine's previous name <old> — taken over (… removed; this machine is <new>)", stamps the profile `renamedFrom {host, at}`, and launches; the chat and the panel never see `profile_locked`. A foreign hostname NOT in the launch hosts stays `foreign`, refused by name — the sentence now names BOTH hostnames and the ONE command (`rm -f '<dir>/SingletonLock'`), never "held by another browser process" for a lock nobody is known to hold. A legacy record (no stamp) inherits the hostname the registry FILE was last saved under (`fileHost`, read at load before this process's first save re-stamps it), else nothing — userW's pod, on its first update after the roll, still meets the old lock with no witness and is refused by name with the command; every roll after that is taken over by itself. `reapOrphan` passes a `stale-previous-host` lock over (nothing of that name can hold it; the next start takes it over); the heal removes it too.

**L2 — a bound tab of a previous life rebinds (src/server/browser-keeper.js, src/browser-tabs.js, data/bin/vibespace-browser).** `tabsLost(profileId)` marks every lease of a NAMED profile whose browser was replaced without a stop — `markDaemonGone` (the tick, a start, the boot's judgement), `adoptAll`'s not-adopted branch (the pod-roll shape: the daemon died while VibeSpace was down), `recaptureBrowser`'s `replaced` (an in-place relaunch, the heal) — with WHY (`reg.tabLostWhy`: `life` | `closed`; the four existing writers say `closed`). At the next attach the bind prefers the browser's ONE page that no holder roots (PURE `TBS.rebindPick` over the CDP target list + `tabHoldersOf`: a fresh launch's single `about:blank`; the url read off the raw target — `pageTargets` keeps none) ⇒ `tab <targetId>` (no second blank tab per relaunch); anything else (several pages, the only page another holder's or the user's, targets unreadable) ⇒ `tab new` of its own, never another holder's; a mediated lease keeps `tab new` through its grant. The attach's answer carries `rebound {how, targetId, url, why, text}` (PURE `TBS.reboundNoteText`), the CLI prints it once as `note: your tab from the previous run is gone (the browser was restarted) — bound to <url>; re-read the page before continuing [tab_rebound]`. `tab_gone` stays for the mid-run case (the agent's tab closed by the user, r2 F3).

**L3 — said where the user looks.** The journal (the takeover line, the loss line "its browser is gone with … — N lease(s) bind a tab again at their next command", the bind line); the Agent browser panel's profile row: a `renamed from <old>` chip (title: the two names) for a day (`B.renamedFromFact`, `RENAMED_SHOWN_MS`), a launch-host chip only when the record's host differs from this machine's (`list().machine.host`); zh / ja. The housekeeping row carries `launchHost` + `renamedFrom`.

### lane install-ellipsis — the Mac repair command died on one byte

- 2026-10-02 (the owner's Macbook, 2.369.199): `bash: line 253: DHOST?: unbound variable` — macOS /bin/bash 3.2 absorbs a byte ≥ 0x80 after `$NAME` into the name, so the dial-check echo's `$DHOST…` read an unset `DHOST\xe2` under `set -u` and the installer died before the check. Fix `${DHOST}…`; gate = test-dial-facts' macOS bash 3.2 census over every shipped shell script (installer, install.sh, scripts/*.sh) + the pre-fix line as the control (381). Workaround before the fix: pipe through `perl -pe 's/\xE2\x80\xA6/.../g'`.
