- **A digest's open window is no longer drawn as "held" (the R3 × R4 seam, backlog B-adb7 (a)).** 2.369.190's first screen called a conversation held (amber "→ X · held") whenever ANY message waited on it — but with R4 a digest notification keeps its matches waiting on the conversation until its window closes, by design. The server now says for whom each waiting message waits (`touch.pendingFor`), and the first screen counts a digest's messages as held only once its window has closed with them still waiting; a single conversation handed over on its own keeps its "→ X" (b). Gate: test-channels-focus ⑦ (a nine-row table, the real engine — a digest hit pending ⇒ no tag, 61 min later ⇒ amber — and two patched-copy controls: the pre-seam "any pending is held" rule, and a tag rule that does not pass the watchers).
- **R3's first-screen checks follow R4's model.** An account-grain and a rule-grain notification now both fire on a conversation both cover (another agent's rule never silences the account-wide one), so test-channels-focus ② expects three deliveries (Room 44 wakes the rule's agent AND the account's), and test-channels-aggregate-ui runs R3's checks (the account's conversations not listed for the hand-over alone; an agent's read lists exactly one, tagged) after R4's rewritten ⑤.
- **Merged by hand:** src/server/channels-engine.js (R4's rewritten wake / digest / receipt paths keep R3's facts — the wake names whom it reached, `touchView`, the one-shot `healSelfAt` — and 2.369.188's `kind: 'notification'` on every stash), the i18n dictionaries (union), the For-you producer census (15 sites: + the helper-ask item, + the composed-message pointer), the design's R4 section renumbered §24 (R3 holds §23).
- **Three heavy suites pinned what lane S1 changed (test-only).** test-fold-ux's swap census counted every `.replaceWith(` in chat-view — it now names both: the one message-element swap and S1's agent-chip patch (a chip inside a helper card's label, never a message element). test-tool-progress read the subagent branch's old spelling (it now also refuses control records). test-queue-steer's stamp pin follows the stagger into `_armViewReset`, and its ⑭b experiment gains a layer: S1's reset hold removes the same race on its own, so the PRE-FIX arm strips BOTH the recency guard and the hold (else it reproduces nothing), the recency guard is proven alone with the hold removed, and a third arm runs the whole product (the held payload first, the answer after, the row kept).
- **Gates on this tree:** npm run build (i18n-check 5259 zh / 5259 ja); fast tier 183 suites green in 1011 s (test-helper-ask 212, test-reattach-stagger 19, test-desktop-serve 198, test-channels-focus 160, test-channels-engine 257, test-channels-aggregate 296, test-user-todos-layout 190); the heavy tier's verdict is recorded in the release commit.

## 2.369.190 — the Channels panel opens on what needs you or an agent, each row with one small tag, and a Lark picture is shown as a picture; the Agent browser's live picture fits its window, and the phone gets a real live view

### Lane R3 — a Lark picture is shown as a picture; the Channels panel opens on what needs you or an agent, each row with one small tag, the full list one switch away

The owner, 2026-09-26, on 2.369.185 (docs/design-communication-panel §23): "lark图像不能预览吗？" (a Lark picture came out as the text "[image]" and a bare "image ⬇" chip) and "开头不要把所有消息都放进来，很多是没用的，建议只放重要消息/conversation（比如推送给agent了的，或者某个agent刚刚读取了的），并展示一个小tag表示状态。" (the panel opened on all 879 conversations).

**Pictures.**
- A picture in a Lark message (a picture on its own, or inside a rich-text post) is drawn as a thumbnail in the conversation window, fetched on demand through our own route and cached. Its "[image]" text line disappears once the picture is drawn (agents and search still see it). Clicking it opens the usual image viewer. A rich-text post wrapped in a language key (`zh_cn` …) now yields both its text and its pictures.
- **A picture that cannot be drawn says why.** Before, any failure silently turned the thumbnail into an "image ⬇" chip. Now:
  - If waiting fixes it (this minute's vendor budget is spent, the vendor asked us to back off, or it rate-limited us), the thumbnail shows "retrying in N s" and loads itself again, at most twice.
  - Otherwise the chip names the reason ("budget spent", "forbidden", "not found", "not cached", "vendor error" …), puts the full sentence in its tooltip and offers **Retry**.
  - A file that is not a displayable picture (HEIC …) becomes a download chip marked "no preview".
  - Every failure is reported to telemetry (`chan-attachment-failed`).
- **The picture's fetch stays cheap.**
  - Nothing is fetched while a conversation is ingested, only when a window shows the picture.
  - A cached picture is served even when the minute's budget is spent.
  - Five thumbnails asking for the same picture at once make one vendor request and one charge.
  - A picture the vendor refused is not asked for again for 10 minutes. Your Retry skips that wait; it never skips the budget.
  - A vendor rate limit pauses the whole account's picture fetches, not just that one picture.
  - A picture older than the newest 5000 messages is found through its own message.
  - A cache hit no longer rewrites the cache ledger (writes are grouped every 5 s and flushed on shutdown).
- The picture fetch is now explicitly allowlisted: scripts/test-vendor-whitelist.mjs §7 is a census that reads the source and names three gates (fetched on demand, cache checked first, charged to the budget). Four ungated patched copies each turn it red.

**The first screen.**
- The Channels panel now opens on the conversations that **need attention**. A conversation is listed when any of these holds:
  - an agent's draft awaits your approval, or a send's result is unknown;
  - it is handed to an agent or a Task Group on its own (a conversation handed over by a rule or with its whole account is listed only once a wake for it was delivered to the agent in the last 24 h, or its wake is held — see r2 below);
  - an agent read it in the last 24 h;
  - a wake for it is held;
  - you replied in it in the last 24 h.

  Your agent groups are always listed too.
- Each listed conversation shows **one small tag** in place of its source label, under the title at every width. The tags are "N to approve", "send unknown", "→ Agent" (amber when its wake was held), "Agent read 5m ago", "New since Agent", "last wake held" and "replied 3h ago". The agent's name is the part that shortens when space is tight; the words always stay whole.
- The header is a two-way switch across the whole bar — "N need attention" | "All 879". The row under it holds a **Filter** box, New group and Outbox (the two buttons moved down so the switch is never cut). In the attention view, matches outside it are offered as "N more in All", and any filter text can also start a message search across every connected account.
- Behind this, an agent's read (the `vibespace-channels read` route) is now recorded on the conversation (who, when, up to which message) and sent as a one-row update. A hidden read is never recorded, and re-reading the same messages within a minute records nothing new. Each wake records which agent it reached. Your own newest message comes from messages the vendor marks as yours or from your own send; conversations active in the last two days get it from their recent history once, at startup. Conversations nothing touched carry no extra data.
- Gates:
  - New fast suites **test-channels-images** (61) and **test-channels-focus** (116; 148 after r2).
  - Extended: test-channels-lark-shape (84 → 94, the resource request), test-vendor-whitelist (64 → 91, §7), test-channels-groups-ui (61 → 62).
- Verify r1 (the adversarial pass, same day): two ways of fetching every picture at ingest slipped both money gates green — an internal `attachment()` call queued for the next tick (the whitelist census only knew four receiver names, and the images suite's "no bytes at ingest" pin counted before the tick) and a wiring file's own `engine.attachment(`. The census now counts every `.attachment(` in the server tree and every bare `attachment(` in the engine, the pin settles first, and both mutants are its controls. A tag whose agent arrived without a display name showed the raw session id; it now says "an agent" / "a Task Group".
  - Heavy: test-channels-aggregate-ui ②b (a Lark-shaped picture, the overlay, a rate-limited picture that loads on its own retry, a refused picture's zh chip with Retry; after r2: the account-grain rows NOT on the attention list until an agent reads one), test-channels-groups-e2e ⑨ (5 handed over / 3 read by an agent through its real agent route / 1 awaiting among 51, the header counts, All, the filter in both views, one column at 375 px), test-channels-e2e ⑰ (every tag's words fit line 2 in en/zh/ja under both fonts, with a control), test-channels-i18n (the attention list shot).
- r2 (2026-09-27, the integrator's ruling D4): **handing a whole account, or the conversations matching a rule, to an agent no longer puts every one of them on the first screen** — the owner's 824-thread mailbox handed to an agent would have filled it again, the exact thing he asked to stop. Such a conversation is listed only once the hand-over acted on it: a wake for it was delivered to the agent in the last 24 h (tagged "→ Agent", the tooltip saying "with the whole account" / "by a rule"), or its wake is held (amber). Otherwise it is listed only for its own facts (an agent read, your reply, a draft awaiting approval). A conversation handed over on its own is listed as before. test-channels-focus 116 → 148 (the account + rule grains in every state, the spec fixture now 3 conversations + the account + a rule ⇒ 7 listed, one delivered wake per grain ⇒ 9, and two patched-copy controls: the grain check removed puts all 50 back, a delivered wake with no window never leaves); test-channels-aggregate-ui's account-grain leg now proves the opposite (none listed, then one after a stub agent reads it). The test-channels-gmail-shape suite now removes its scratch directory on every exit (it left one per run — 245 on the gate machine).

### Lane S4 — the agent's live view fits its window, and the phone gets a real one (naive-user study 2)

Study 2 (2026-09-26, all three testers): "实况画面只占窗格上面一截" — on the desktop the live picture used only the top 40–60 % of its pane, black below; "手机上的实况窗口" — on a 390 px phone "网页按桌面宽度缩成顶上约 260 像素的一小条，下面全空，Pricing 链接只有 20 像素宽", no pinch, the live view did not open when the assistant started browsing, and the only way in was a status-bar chip "整个在屏幕外" (x≈403 of 390); and a live view "一片白，网址栏写着 example.org、助手说已打开".

- **The page is laid out at the size of the window you watch it in.** While a live view is open, the agent's page takes the size of the view's pane, so the picture fills it exactly — a split pane 700×900 shows a 700×900 page, not a shrunk 1280-wide one with a black band. Resize the window and the page follows. With several views of one browser, the one whose person is driving decides, otherwise the largest one on screen (a hidden one never counts); the others show the same page scaled to fit, never stretched, and say "Sized for another window". When nobody has watched for 5 seconds the page goes back to its own size. A size the agent chose itself (`set viewport` / `set device`) is never overridden — the view scales it, says "Agent's size W×H", and "Fit the page to the window" takes it back. New setting *Lay the agent's page out at the live view's size* (`browser.fitPageToView`, on by default).
- **On a phone the live view is a real one.** The page renders at the phone's width (the Pricing link is its normal size, and tapping it works); it opens by itself, full screen, when the agent starts browsing in the conversation you are looking at, with "Back to the chat" in the notice; two fingers zoom the picture while you watch (one finger pans, a double tap zooms 2×) and your taps land where you see them when you drive; the status bar's "Agent browser" chip stays on screen however you swipe the bar. Notices with a button are no longer squeezed into half a phone screen.
- **No more blank picture under a loaded URL.** A page that painted twice in quick succession and then sat still could leave a viewer with its first (white) paint for good — the last frame is now always delivered. After a navigation the stream sent no picture for (a jump within the page), VibeSpace asks the page for one. If a view still has no picture it says "Waiting for a picture…" after 2 seconds (the old picture dimmed) and "No picture came in 10 s" with a Reconnect after 10.
- Measured on the real agent-browser 0.38.1 (scripts/fixtures/browser-stream/fit-0.38.1.json): a set viewport makes every frame that size; a device scale factor never enlarges the frame and changing it on a still page produced no frame at all (the fit keeps factor 1 — "DPR-aware" means the pane is measured in CSS px, so a DPR-3 phone gets a 390-wide page); a headed window cannot be narrower than 500 px (the view fits it there and says so); a jump within the page sends a new URL and no frame. PURE src/browser-fit.js; the bridge (src/server/browser-stream.js) sets the page through `keeper.setViewportFor` (the daemon's own `set viewport`, never starting a browser) and takes fresh pictures with `keeper.freshFrameFor` (src/server/browser-viewport.js `captureFrame`). Gates: test-browser-fit (fast, 116 — six patched-copy controls: device px, no holder rule, no trailing frame, no own-mirror recognition, no fresh frame, no re-check of a restarted browser) + test-browser-live-fit (heavy, 40 — the real 0.38.1 through a scratch instance, a desktop and a phone client: pane = frame ±2 px with a pixel census and its control, auto-open, the link, the pinch, the chip and its control, the waiting sentences, the viewer rule). The chrome suites' fake agent-browsers answer `set viewport`; lane J's letterbox legs run with the new setting off.

- **Verify r1 (the adversarial pass on this lane).** Two viewport sets in flight at once — the agent's own `set viewport` and the view's fit — are now told apart by the ORDER the browser processed them in, never by the size asked for: the agent's choice landing first is put back if the fit landed after it, and landing second it is announced as the agent's, never as "fitted". The 5 s restore waits for a running turn to end (no reflow under the agent's feet). The agent's choice and the size to restore to survive a server restart (a note on the browser's own record, gone when the browser relaunches). A live view on another virtual desktop stops voting (it kept the page at its size before). On a phone, a second browsing conversation's live view opened below the screen — an earlier split window was still displayed under the active one; only the active window is displayed now.

- **Verify r1, continued.** The same order rule also holds when the browser's record of the two commands arrives after the view's own command has already returned (both late: judged when ours lands; ours late: still recognised as ours, never taken for the agent's choice). A size the page did not take is said once in the view ("the page did not take the size") instead of being believed silently, and not asked again for 30 s. An agent-chosen width narrower than a headed browser's 500 px floor is no longer forgotten on a reconnect. The view's own resizes now appear in the agent browser's action trace as a "page size" row (`live view: set viewport W H (fit | restore | put-back)`), so the agent's clicks before and after a reflow are told apart; the agent's own `set viewport` stays an untraced observation.

## 2.369.189 — a browser profile with a name is usable by all your conversations — one browser, a second chat joins it in its own tab, and the Agent browser window says who can use it, with Rename… and Delete… (owner ruling A); an account on paid overage credits wears a money icon instead of a sentence (the owner: "这啥玩意啊 不如显示个钱的图标"); and the 2.369.187 / 2.369.188 mirror red was the release gate's own sample, not the browser release

### Lane S5 — a named browser profile is usable by all your conversations (owner ruling A, 2026-09-26, "A吧")

- **A named browser profile is usable by all your conversations (owner ruling A, 2026-09-26 — "A吧" = 有名字的档案默认给所有对话用).** Two naive-user studies failed the same task: a login made in one chat could not be used from another (`not_owner`, and the only way out offered was a command line that made a second, still-refused profile), and pinning the profile to the second chat in Session properties started a second Chrome on the profile's folder ("SingletonLock" in the live view) and then silently fell back to a temporary browser. Now:
  - **Every named profile is shared by default** — the ones you create in the Agent browser window, the ones an agent creates with `vibespace-browser new`, and "New persistent profile from this session's browser". A profile runs **one** browser: a second conversation joins it in its own tab; nothing ever starts a second Chrome on its folder.
  - **Pinning a profile to a conversation (New Session, Session properties) makes it that conversation's default browser** — its next browser command opens it (joining the running one), nothing is relaunched, and if it cannot open, the agent is told so by name (never a silent temporary browser). Your pick is the permission: it works even on a profile kept to another conversation, and your latest choice wins.
  - **One conversation drives a shared browser at a time.** While another chat's agent is working in it, a command is refused `browser_busy` naming that chat and how long to wait at most; while you drive it from another chat's live view, it says so. The live view's strip shows a shared profile's tab and names who is driving it.
  - **The Agent browser window's profile row** gains **Who can use it** (All my conversations / Only <a conversation> — narrowing takes it from every other chat, after a confirmation that says how many), **Rename…**, and **Delete…** (warns how many conversations use it, takes it from each, stops it, clears every pin, and keeps its logins under "Deleted profiles (kept aside)" until you press Delete permanently). The isolation chip reads "separate tabs".
  - **Refusals name a button, never a command line** (`not_owner`: "switch it to All my conversations in the Agent browser panel, or pick it for this conversation in Session properties"; a conversation's own browser from before this version holding the folder: "press Stop on that browser").
  - A shared browser counts toward the limit of each conversation that holds it, and once toward the machine's ceiling; joining a running browser never trips the machine ceiling.
  - Migration `2026-09-browser-profiles-all-conversations` makes every agent-made profile usable by all conversations (the conversation that made it is kept as its creator). Live sessions pinned before this version stop handing their own browser the profile's folder at boot.
  - Gates: test-browser-share-model (fast, 70 — the PURE tables + the real keeper and routes over a fake 0.38.1, with patched-copy controls: the pre-ruling route dying on SingletonLock, a silent-fallback route, a keeper without the one-driver check), test-browser-share (heavy, 21 — the real agent-browser 0.38.1 + a real Chrome: two conversations, one Chrome on the folder, `browser_busy` through the CLI, a takeover through the real live-view bridge, the switch's button refusal, Delete… with two pins, the migration on a pre-ruling registry), test-migrations (+ the migration leg); flipped asserts in test-browser-pin, -handles, -mediation and test-profile-blindness. Docs: design-agent-browser-v2 §3.2.6 (+ §3.2.5 / §3.3 / §6.2 / §11), the agent manual, kb-file-structure, kb-features, kb-bugfix-invariants.
  - **Verify S5 (adversarial, real 0.38.1 + Chrome; three fixed on the branch):** (1) MAJOR — a **fork** of a pinned conversation said "Pinned: work" in Session properties while its bare commands opened a temporary browser, silently (the ladder's 'conversation' rung was never recorded under the fork's NEW key, and no directory rides the spawn env any more): the keeper's `copyPin(parent, fork)` copies the parent's pin verbatim (its `by`/`at` — never a laundered authorization) and ws-create calls it on the fork branch. (2) MEDIUM — a live view a conversation had open on a profile the user then kept to ANOTHER conversation ("Only …") could still take it over and refuse the holder's agent `browser_busy` "the user drives it from <that chat>": `keeper.takeover` of a named profile now needs that conversation's lease (`no_lease`, naming the Session-properties button), and the bridge ends every view on a lease that goes (a typed "no longer holds that browser profile" — no stale picture). (3) MEDIUM — the migration treated an unreadable / torn `browser-profiles.json` as "no file" (ran, ledger stamped forever): only ENOENT is nothing-to-migrate; anything else fails by name and is retried at the next boot. Gates: test-browser-share-model 70 → 77, test-browser-share 21 → 26 (③b: the narrowing under a takeover from the other chat's real live view), test-migrations 210 → 213 (a torn registry, a `null` file, the file whole again). Held (pre-existing, measured on master): after a lane-H relaunch the agent's next verb is the binary's `tab_gone` until `vibespace-browser tab new <url>`; a killed driver frees the drive after DRIVE_HOLD_MS (90 s), its lease after the 2-min carrier grace.

### Lane credits-icon — an account on paid overage credits wears a money icon, not a sentence (the owner on the Agents roster: "这啥玩意啊 不如显示个钱的图标")

The owner, looking at a member row of the Agents roster that read 正在使用付费溢出额度 beside its next-usable countdown: "这啥玩意啊 不如显示个钱的图标" — "what is this thing? better show a money icon".

- **One money chip instead of the sentence.** An account billing paid overage right now wears a small chip beside its name — a coin with a dollar sign and one word (Credits / 按量 / 従量) in the warning tone. Hover it (or read it with a screen reader) for the whole sentence: the subscription quota is spent, requests are billed pay-per-use, the period's spend (e.g. $12.50 / $50.00), and that automatic turns on it are refused.
- **The same chip, dim, for an account whose org allows usage credits** (B-ad05: past 100 % it bills pay-per-use; the pool uses it last) — it replaces the grey "· credits" text tag. The usage popup draws the same chip.
- **Nothing moves the countdown column any more.** The sentence sat in the usage cell and pushed the next-usable column left; the chip lives on the name line, so the donut, age and countdown columns stay straight on every row.
- **The open roster keeps the chip current.** The 8-second usage refresh updates the chip in place (its tooltip follows the spend; it disappears when the state ends) instead of redrawing it.
- The green row highlight stays: it marks the two accounts whose quota comes back soonest, which is a different fact from billing (a member on credits whose reset is near is still one of them).
- A panel narrower than 340 px shows the icon only; the sentence stays in its tooltip. The Settings description of "Do not switch conversations onto an account billing paid overage" now says such an account wears a money icon.

- The release gate's check that an agent's browsers are released a few minutes after its turn ended now waits for every browser that check released, instead of reading the result the moment the first one stopped — a slow test machine stopped the second browser later and turned the 2.369.187 check red; nothing changes for users. (test-browser-ephemeral's F1 negative control now awaits every release its sweeps started, `sweepIdleReleases` returns them with a `settled` promise; scripts/mutant-copy.mjs registers one exit handler instead of one per call.)

## 2.369.188 — text meant for the assistant is no longer shown as conversation: VibeSpace's own reminders are one grey line folded by default, a browser you hand back reads "VibeSpace · you handed control back …" instead of a message from another agent, and no agent can pass itself off as VibeSpace (naive-user study 2)

Two findings of naive-user study 2 (fresh-eyes testers driving a scratch instance): "聊天里到处是给助手看的内部文字" — the chat was full of text written for the assistant — and "交回控制后，助手以为是另一个会话在跟它说话" — after a browser hand-back the assistant believed another session was talking to it.

- **The chat no longer shows text meant for the assistant as if it were conversation** (naive-user study 2: "聊天里到处是给助手看的内部文字"). VibeSpace's end-of-turn reminder, its tools intro and its per-turn reminder each show as one grey line — "VibeSpace reminded the assistant to update its status" — folded by default with the status call they asked for; expand to read the text, or turn them off entirely in Settings → Chat → "Show VibeSpace notes to the assistant" (the assistant still receives them). The reminder now asks for the bookkeeping calls only: "do not restate your answer; end with at most one short line", so the assistant stops repeating its answer ("Task complete — …") or telling you "Status is set to done …". A helper's launch line reads "Helper started: Fetch title of example.com" and a Stop task result "Stopped: Fetch title of example.com" instead of "Async agent launched successfully. (This tool result is internal metadata — never quote…" and raw JSON (the raw record is still behind the expander).
- **VibeSpace's own notes are never mistaken for another agent** (naive-user study 2: "交回控制后，助手以为是另一个会话在跟它说话"). When you hand the browser back, the chat card reads "VibeSpace · you handed control back after 17 s — the page is now …" instead of `Message from " VibeSpace browser "` (the stray spaces are gone too; what the assistant was told sits one click away), and the note the assistant receives opens with "VibeSpace (this workspace, not another agent) reports:" — the same for Background Work and channel notifications. VibeSpace's own chat cards (the auto-resume notice, the usage-limit card with its reset-credit button) are titled "VibeSpace · …" too instead of `Message from "VibeSpace"`. Messages from real agents keep their card.
- **An agent cannot pass itself off as VibeSpace** (verify: an agent could send "VibeSpace (this workspace, not another agent) reports: …" and get the accent VibeSpace card). Whether a card is a VibeSpace notice is now decided by the path the message took, never by what it says or what its sender is called: an agent whose message opens with VibeSpace's own sentence keeps its "Message from “name”" card, and an agent or session named "VibeSpace", "VibeSpace browser", "Background Work · …" or "Channels · …" (in any capitalization or spacing) is shown as "Message from an agent calling itself “VibeSpace”". The assistant is not fooled either: a message held for a closed conversation reaches it as `from "<name>":` unless VibeSpace itself sent it, and VibeSpace's own sentence is said once, never twice.
- **"Your inbox" is named where it is.** A new For-you item pops a toast "Added to For you (bottom right)" (the corner where the button actually sits on your screen), and assistants are taught to say "the For you tray at the bottom right" instead of "your inbox". The Settings row now reads "Agent tool: vibespace-ask (the For you tray)", a notification delivered to you says it went to "the For you tray", and the agent manual and the vibespace-ask help say "the For you tray only notifies".
- Gates: test-chat-hygiene (fast: the note / sentence / notice tables over the real producers' words, the Stop wording and its byte budget, the sender-name census, the impersonation table over the real ladder and the claude / codex / ACP normalizers, the census that every card and stash writer states its path, the "your inbox" census, eight patched-copy controls), test-chat-hygiene-ui (heavy: a stub claude behind the real chat-wrapper playing the study's records in chrome — and a peer named "VibeSpace" plus a peer whose words open with VibeSpace's sentence, live and from the held-message drain), test-migrations (a saved "Card kinds that collapse" selection gains the new kind once).

## 2.369.187 — handing a whole account (or the conversations a rule matches) to an agent with a filter saves again (the owner's toast "请求被拒绝: mode 'filtered' needs a filterId")

The owner, handing a Lark account to the group 工作 with 匹配过滤器的消息 (two time windows), one digest per window and 起草, pressed 保存 and got the toast `请求被拒绝: mode 'filtered' needs a filterId` — nothing was saved.

- **A filtered hand-off saves.** "Hand the whole account to an agent" and "Conversations matching a rule" save *messages matching a filter* again: the server stores the filter you built in the dialog and the assignment points at it (every such save was refused since 2.369.185; *every message* was unaffected). Re-opening the dialog shows your rules and saving again replaces them.
- **A refused save says what to fix, in your language.** A filter that is still incomplete, a missing agent, a negative wakes-per-day number and the like now read as a sentence about the dialog (e.g. 过滤器还没保存 — 请先添加规则，再保存), never as the server's internal English message.
- Cause: the server checked the assignment for a filter id before creating the filter the same request carried. Gates: test-channels-engine ⑩ (fast: the owner's exact request at both grains through the real routes, eight refusals worded by their code, a patched copy with the old order as the control), test-channel-filter, test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑦ (heavy: the owner's dialog in the browser).

## 2.369.186 — a window you pick by name is shown, even when it is the first tab of a tab group (inc-muiq348r-jwb5)

The owner, on an Android phone: "我在手机上怎么切换不到 vibespace 大开发这个 session？" — "VibeSpace 主开发" was the first (host) window of a tab group made on a desktop, with "Project B 大开发" on show; tapping its row in the phone's window switcher left Project B on screen while the title bar said 主开发.

- **Picking a window by name shows it.** The phone's window switcher (tap the title), a sidebar card, Ctrl+K, the taskbar window list and grouped chooser, Switch window, go-to / find, and re-opening Settings, Usage or any other one-of-a-kind window now switch its tab group to THAT window — the group's first window included — restore a minimized group and bring it forward. Before, only the group's other tabs could be picked this way; picking the first one raised the group on whatever tab it showed.
- **A click on the group keeps its tab.** Clicking or tapping a tab group's own title bar or the content on show keeps that tab and makes it the active window (the phone's title, highlight and close button used to name the hidden first window after any tap into the other tab's content).
- **Find window across desktops keeps your active window** (verify r1). Locating a tab of a group that lives on another desktop sets that group to show the tab there, without making the hidden window the active one — Ctrl+\ x, the taskbar highlight and the phone's title keep naming the window in front of you. (The same slip existed before for a group's other tabs; the one door now keeps it for every tab.)
- **The switch syncs like a tab click.** It is saved and sent exactly as a tab click is; another open client keeps showing its own tab. The phone switcher also lists a minimized group's other tabs under *Minimized*.
- One door: `WindowManager.revealWindow` (PURE `revealTab` / `pressTab` in src/lib/chain-layout.js). Gates: test-chain-layout ⑬ (fast, the verdict tables + two patched-copy controls), test-architecture §62 (fast, the census: every `.focusWindow(` / `wm.restore(` call in src/lib is a listed raise-only site, every naming door counted, four negative controls), test-split-ux 13 (heavy: the sidebar card, window list, palette and go-to on a desktop page; the switcher at 448×850, DPR 3, touch, Android UA; a desktop and a phone control with the door neutered reproduce the incident).
- **The Communication panel's freshness pill is always drawn whole.** 2.369.185's Actions mirror went red because, in the runner's font (DejaVu Sans, about 10 % wider than this machine's Noto Sans), "refresh paused" came out as "refresh pau…" in the 188 px panel; a CSS cap ellipsized every pill wider than 82 px. Now the pill never shrinks and the conversation title gives way instead (the full title stays in its tooltip). The pill uses short words: a paused conversation says "paused" (已暂停 / 一時停止中) and one that has never been scanned says "no scan yet" (尚未扫描 / 未スキャン). The full sentence ("refresh paused", "not scanned yet") stays in the pill's tooltip. This also fixes pills that were cut on every machine: English "not scanned yet", Japanese "まだスキャンしていません" (cut to "まだスキャンし…"), and "refresh paused" / "not scanning" / 还没有扫描过 in a linked account's ↳ rows, which are 17 px narrower. test-channels-e2e ⑯ now checks every word the pill can show (zh/ja/en, at most 82 px) in both a normal and a ↳ row, plus a pill with the longest sentence. Each check runs twice: in this machine's font and with DejaVu Sans forced. The control is the pre-fix product (the old CSS as a scratch copy plus the old words as a mutant module): it cuts "refresh paused" at 82 of 89 px in DejaVu Sans and draws it whole in Noto Sans, which reproduces the mirror-only failure on this machine.

## 2.369.185 — a linked channel account is an aggregated IM: every conversation of a linked Lark or Gmail account is listed and fetched (no Track step), read with its images and attachments, searched and marked read; refresh follows activity (30 s / 5 min / 15 min at most) with your own per-conversation override; an agent may refresh a conversation itself within named limits; and a whole account, one conversation or the conversations matching a rule can be handed to an agent

The owner, 2026-09-26 (docs/design-communication-panel §5 invariant 6, §6.2, §6.5, §7.3): once linked, the Channels panel is "an IM that aggregates all my IMs — I read the messages, download attachments, view images in it; on top of that I can hand the whole account, or one channel / chat / the chats matching a pattern, to a specific agent"; the old Track-first flow was "too restricted to be of practical use". And: "if the API allows callbacks, not polling is better; if polling is unavoidable … 15 minutes at most. Let me override any conversation's refresh period at any time. An agent should be able to fetch the latest messages itself. Make the cache cap 5 GB per account, and every time/capacity parameter configurable."

**Reading — every conversation, no Track step.**
- A linked account lists and fetches **every** conversation in its scope: every Lark group the account can see, and Gmail's Inbox by default (all mail, chosen labels or a search query per account under Edit → Mailbox). The "Track…" picker, the "Login only — no conversation tracked yet" note and the untracked grey rows are gone; every row carries its freshness pill.
- The conversation window shows images as thumbnails and every other attachment as a chip with its name, size and a download button. Both come through our own route: fetched once into a per-account cache (0600, least-recently-used first out, 5 GB per account by default), served with `nosniff` and a sandboxing CSP, downloaded — never run — unless it is a png / jpeg / gif / webp shown inline. Lark rich-text images and Gmail inline images count as attachments too.
- Scrolling up past the start loads older history from the vendor (Lark) — it is prepended, never wakes anybody, and the window says when there is nothing older.
- ⋯ → Search messages… searches one account's stored messages (at most 64 MB read, 100 results, "more exist" when cut) and opens the conversation you click.
- Unread counts only messages that arrived after the account was linked, so a freshly linked mailbox does not open on thousands of "unread". The row menu has Mark read.

**Freshness — push first, polling by activity, your override, and the vendor budget said out loud.**
- Each conversation has its own refresh time: **hot** every 30 s (open in a window right now, or a message in the last hour), **warm** every 5 min (a message in the last day), **cold** every 15 min — the most it ever waits. While push is live and carries messages, polling drops to every 15 min as a safety net.
- Row menu / window ⋯ → Refresh now, and Refresh every ▸ Automatic / 30 s / 1 min / 5 min / 15 min / Paused — persisted, shown on every client.
- Every vendor request is counted per account per minute in the vendor's own unit: Lark 60 requests/min (its cap is 1000/min per app), Gmail 3000 quota units/min (its cap is 6000 per user). When the minute's budget is spent the card says so with the numbers — "Vendor budget reached — 60 requests/min for this account; 12 conversations waiting, next refresh in 23 s" — and the waiting conversations go next minute, most overdue first. Typical Lark load for 55 groups ≈ 15.6 requests/min; Gmail polls the mailbox's change history (2 units) instead of each thread (40), and a thread the history names is fetched at once.
- Lark's push without the official SDK now says the remedy in full: "Real-time push is off: the official Lark SDK is not installed on this instance — run `npm install @larksuiteoapi/node-sdk` … Until then messages are polled (every 30 s – 15 min)."
- Lark sign-ins renew themselves while the instance runs: the card no longer counts down seven days; it says "renewals stopped — re-authorize in …" only when renewals have actually stopped (less than a day left).

**Agents.**
- `vibespace-channels refresh <conversation>` and `read --fresh` fetch the latest messages now. Refused BY NUMBER when it is too soon ("refreshed 8 s ago (floor 20 s) — read it now, or refresh again in 12 s") or when the account's vendor budget for the minute is spent; an agent that cannot see the conversation gets the same not-found as any other.
- Hand a whole account (⋯ → Hand to an agent…), the conversations matching a rule (⋯ → Conversations matching a rule… — a person in it, words in the title, an address or domain, DM / group / thread), or one conversation (Assign & filter…) to an agent — one editor for all three. The most specific one wins (conversation > rule > account); a new conversation that matches inherits in the pass that finds it. The agent's reach follows the assignment and is removed with it. The daily wake cap belongs to the assignment (an account-wide handoff is not 800 × 40 wakes a day), and a digest arrives once per window as ONE block for the whole scope. Before you save, the editor estimates "about N wakes a day" from the matching conversations' last seven days. Inherited rows say "(account)" / "(rule)".

**Settings** (Settings → Channels; every time and capacity number): `channels.pollHotSec` 30, `channels.pollWarmSec` 300, `channels.pollColdSec` 900 (also the maximum), `channels.hotRecentMinutes` 60, `channels.warmRecentHours` 24, `channels.agentRefreshFloorSec` 20, `channels.agentBudgetSharePct` 25, `channels.historyPageSize` 50, `channels.attachmentBudgetMB` 5120, `channels.budgetLarkPerMin` 60, `channels.budgetGmailPerMin` 3000.

**Upgrade.** Migration `2026-09-channels-aggregated-im` turns every previously tracked conversation into a 30 s refresh override ("tracked ⇒ hot"), marks existing backlog read, stamps `linkedAt`, and removes the `tracked` field. Assignments are kept. The first pass after the update discovers every conversation of each account to the end (the old 5-page discovery cap meant conversation 501 never appeared).

**Under the hood.** Discovery walks the cursor to the end, resuming across passes when the budget cuts it; the engine peeks one entry per conversation instead of deep-cloning the index; broadcasts carry only the changed conversations (`partial`, merged in place by every client); the full conversation view (identity warnings, reach) is fetched on open (`GET /api/channels/:a/:c`). A latent single-flight bug (the pass's `finally` could run before its promise was stored, wedging the account's loop) is fixed. An attachment's bytes are written and evicted asynchronously (up to 100 MB; data/ may sit on a slow mount), each write through its own temp file. The row pill is the short form ("19s ago", "refresh paused") so it fits a 188 px panel in every language; the full sentence is its tooltip. Gmail keeps its mailbox cursor across restarts (it used to re-walk every thread) and its health line / Edit dialog show the scope it really reads.

**Verify round (lane R2, 2026-09-26) — six findings, each reproduced on the build's bytes first.**
- **An account- or rule-wide daily wake cap now holds under a burst.** One pass that brought news to 100 conversations under a whole-account assignment with a cap of 5 started 100 billed turns whenever delivering a wake took more than a couple of milliseconds (it always does): each conversation's wake read the shared ledger before delivering and wrote it after. The wakes of one account- or rule-wide assignment now run one at a time, so exactly 5 go out and the other 95 wait with "daily wake cap reached (5 of 5 in 24 h)".
- **`vibespace-channels refresh` and `read --fresh` never say "0 new" without fetching.** Twenty refreshes at once used to answer eighteen of them with another refresh's result — "refreshed: 0 new" on stale data. Each refresh now waits for any fetch in flight and then runs its own.
- **An agent cannot use up an account's minute.** Agent refreshes together may spend at most 25 % of an account's per-minute vendor budget (new setting `channels.agentBudgetSharePct`); past it the refusal says so with the wait. A spent budget's sentence now says how much of it agent refreshes took.
- **A vendor rate limit is said from the first failure.** The account line said "last sync 12 s ago" from a failed fetch and the failure line waited for the third failure; now "last sync" is the last good fetch, and a failure shows at once as "rate limited — retrying in 30 s".
- **A setting out of range is said.** Typing 1800 into "at most 900" stored 1800 while the channels engine silently used 900. The Settings number field now keeps the value inside the row's own bounds and says so in a toast ("kept at the maximum, 900"); the engine reads the same bounds and logs a clamp once.
- **The upgrade's boot line reports what it changed.** The migration's log line always said zeros (it was filled a moment after it was printed) and a channels store that refused writes was recorded as migrated; the counts are now the rows changed, they ride the migration ledger, and a refusing store fails the run so the next boot retries it.

**Verify round r3 (lane R2, 2026-09-26) — one major, reproduced on the r2 bytes first, and one minor of a known class; the rest of the round returned lows (recorded in docs/design-communication-panel §6.5's "Lane R2 verify lows").**
- **An agent's refresh no longer pokes a vendor that just rate-limited the account.** A 429 puts an account into a back-off (30 s, then 2, 5, 15 min); the timer honoured it, but the agent's `refresh` and a window's open ran through the same door as the owner's own Refresh press, which bypasses it on purpose. Forty agent refreshes across forty conversations inside a 30 s back-off made fifteen vendor calls in a second (only the agent share bounded them), every one refused again, and the failure count climbed from 1 to 16 — the account's back-off jumped to its 15-minute maximum and the OWNER's whole account stopped polling because an agent pressed refresh. Now an agent refresh (and `read --fresh`) during a back-off is refused by name with the wait — "the vendor refused this account's last fetch (rate-limited) — it is retried in 27 s; read what is there now" (`backoff`, 429 + Retry-After, exit 4) — and makes no call; a window opened during the back-off is hot but pokes nothing; the owner's own Refresh press keeps its bypass (a person pressed it) and a failed press counts as one more failure.
- **The Channels panel and a conversation window re-read on every reconnect.** A digest broadcast sent while the socket was down never arrives, and a pass broadcasts only the rows it changed — so a row's unread count, freshness pill or held-hits note missed during a network blip stayed stale until the next whole-account change. Both now re-read once the socket is back (the same rule the desktop-app launcher and the For-you inbox follow).
- **Concurrent refreshes of one conversation share one fetch (verify r4, major).** Twenty agent refreshes of the same conversation fired together made twenty vendor calls — the per-conversation floor is asked before the wait for a running pass, and after the wait every caller ran a pass of its own — three refreshes queued behind a timer pass that had just fetched their conversation added three more, and five windows opened on one stale conversation made five. A pass that ran while a refresh waited and fetched THAT conversation now answers it (a real fetch of the conversation, completed after the call began; the r2 rule stands — a pass with no entry for the conversation never does). One fetch, every answer honest, the agent share charged once. Also: the owner's Refresh press that fails into a back-off now answers the retry instant (Retry-After on the route, "rate limited — retrying in N s" in the toast) instead of a bare "the refresh failed" that invited the next press — each press inside a 429 is a real vendor refusal and a step of the account's back-off (30 s → 2 → 5 → 15 min), so three presses parked an account 15 minutes while the toast said only "failed".
- **A refresh is a request the account's own fetch loop judges — the seam three rounds patched is closed (verify r5, structural).** r2, r3 and r4 each found one money defect at the same place: the caller's refresh deciding a vendor call against the account's running fetch pass, with N callers deciding at once (an answer taken from somebody else's pass; the back-off door; a pass per waiter). Now the owner's Refresh press, a window's open and `vibespace-channels refresh` only file a request into the account's set; the fetch loop alone drains it — every gate (a vendor back-off, the agents' share of the minute, the vendor budget, the per-conversation floor) judged once per conversation at drain time, each conversation fetched at most once per pass however many asked, a fetch the timer was making anyway carrying its waiters, and every caller answered by the drain that judged its conversation with that conversation's own outcome: fetched with its count, refused by name with the wait, or the pass's own failure. A decision for this new shape, in plain words: **inside a vendor back-off your own Refresh press is honoured once per back-off window** (one real attempt — if the vendor refuses it again the wait grows one step and that press is spent); every further press in the same window is refused with "rate limited — retrying in N s" and makes no call; an agent's refresh, a window's open and the open window's heartbeat never call the vendor during a back-off. Also: at most 200 refreshes may wait per account (past it: `refresh-queue-full`, 429, try again in a moment); a refresh still unanswered after 30 s answers "still running" and the window updates when it lands (the panel's toast says so — never "Up to date"); an account changed or removed while a refresh waited answers `account-changed`; the toast now words a spent budget, the floor, the full queue, the changed account and a restarting server in your language; pending refreshes live in memory — a restart drops them and never turns them into a burst of fetches at boot. The closing check on this shape found and fixed two more: a steady stream of refreshes could keep an account busy so its own timed polling never ran, and a refresh asked for during a long poll of a big account waited for the whole poll — now the loop takes up pending refreshes between every two fetches and a busy account still does its timed polling on its next pass.
- **The independent closing verify (r6): an agent's storm can no longer crowd out your own Refresh, and a refused refresh is told so at once.** Two hundred refreshes filed by one agent while a fetch was in flight filled the account's waiting set and refused the owner's own Refresh press (and a window's open) with "too many refreshes waiting" — now an agent may fill at most 180 of the 200 slots, the last 20 are yours. And a refresh the loop REFUSED (the floor, the agents' share, a spent budget, a vendor back-off) in the first second of a long poll was only told at the poll's end — behind an 18 s poll `vibespace-channels refresh` printed "refresh started — still running" for a request that was never made; a refusal is now answered the moment it is judged (an `ok` still lands when the poll ends, which keeps a stream of refreshes from starving the account's own polling). A timed or forced poll asked of a busy account now runs after the one in flight instead of vanishing into it (a connect's first ingest asked of a busy account used to be silently skipped).
- **Verify r7 (the round after the closing verify): a true refresh answer no longer waits for the whole poll, a stream of refreshes can no longer push your own polling behind it, and repeated Re-authorize presses no longer pile up full ingests.** r6 answered a REFUSED refresh at once but still held a TRUE answer for the poll's end — behind a long poll `vibespace-channels refresh` and the panel's Refresh said "still running" for a fetch that had landed seconds earlier (measured: heard at 2.8 s of a 2.8 s poll; now at 0.12 s). Delivering it at its fetch is safe now because the poll takes the timer's turn at every fetch boundary and alternates one requested conversation with one due one — a burst of refreshes serves the account's own due conversations DURING the burst (35 of 35 inside a 2.5 s storm; 0 of 35 without the alternation) instead of after it, and a trickle of refreshes heavier than the vendor carries still leaves the due list half the fetches. Three Re-authorize presses (or option saves) while the account was busy used to run three full forced ingests one after another — now ONE runs after the poll in flight. `vibespace-channels refresh` exits 4 (a refusal with its sentence — retry) on `account-changed` and `stopped` instead of 1 (an error). Held under attack: the waiting set's reserve is per account and counts a window's open as yours (many windows opened at once on a stale account can spend your own 20 slots — the rule, low), a job token never reaches the channels routes, a refusal leaves the waiting set the instant it is answered, an agent and you asking for the same conversation at once is ONE fetch charged to you, the timer's ledger, settlement under an adapter failure, the words in zh/ja through textContent.
- **Verify r8 (the independent closing verify of r7): under a steady stream of refreshes the earliest request for each conversation no longer waits for the stream to stop, and your own Refresh press is served before an agent's.** r7's poll never ends while requests keep coming (it takes the timer's turn at every fetch boundary), and its drain put every boundary's new requests IN FRONT of the ones already waiting and never let a repeat request for a conversation fetched earlier in that poll join the one still queued — so the first waiter for each conversation was pushed back by every later boundary until the stream stopped (measured on r7: with four windows re-filing, the owner's one Refresh press said "still running" at 30 s; 85 of 398 requests waited past 2 s, up to 11.8 s; 395 vendor calls for 398 requests on five conversations — no coalescing), and the owner's press on a due conversation behind 180 agent requests was fetched 181st (r6's LIFO riders had put it first; r7's filing order put it last). Now the requested items at the front of a poll are served in filing order across boundaries, a repeat request rides the one still queued (one vendor call), and the owner's press / a window's open go before agents' (each class in filing order). Held under attack on r7's bytes (measured): an `ok` is durable and readable the instant it is heard (the log, the index, `readFor`); a poll that fails after an `ok` still broadcasts its conversation; a taken timer turn runs discovery once per poll; one queued poll per account with `force` sticky (30 option saves during one held poll = one forced ingest; a forced ask during the queued poll runs one more; a forced ask racing the poll's end is not lost); the owner's reserve; settlement under a throw, a remove mid-fetch and stop; the back-off window (one honoured press per window, the exponent stepped once, a second window after an outside failure); a restart. Recorded, not fixed: the panel's "N new" toast can precede the window's repaint by the poll's remainder (the broadcast lands at the poll's end); a request filed inside a fetch waits for a taken turn's discovery walk; a stopped engine's in-flight poll keeps fetching to its queue's end; an ingest in flight when its account is removed re-creates that conversation's index row (invisible in the digest); the CLI's refused-set census derives from the route's table only.
- **Verify r9 (the second structural closure): the refresh scheduler is now one small, separately tested decision — and four rough edges it had are gone.** Seven verify rounds each found one money-class ordering defect in how the account's fetch loop scheduled refreshes, every fix written into the same asynchronous loop that the next round then found a new ordering bug in. The whole decision — which conversation is fetched next, who is answered with what, when a refusal is said, when your own polling gets its turn — is now a pure step function (`src/channel-drain.js`, 17 numbered rules) that the engine only drives, checked by a seeded random walk of 36 × 3000 steps asserting every rule at every step, with a mutant per rule that must turn it red. Visible changes: when your Refresh press brings news, the window repaints at the same moment as the "N new" toast (before, a whole poll later); an agent's refreshes judged together can no longer overspend its share of the account's minute; a steady stream of refreshes no longer keeps one poll running forever (it ends after 25 request fetches in a row and the next starts at once, so a Re-authorize or option save queued behind it runs); discovery never runs ahead of your own waiting press; a stopped engine or a removed account makes no further vendor call (43 before); and inside a rate-limit back-off, if you leave (your press times out) before its fetch, an agent riding it is not fetched on your press. Nothing else changed: the 70-cell table, every r2–r8 shape, the routes, the CLI and the words hold unchanged.

**Gates.** New fast `test-channel-drain` (256 — r9: the PURE drain's seeded walk, 36 seeds × 3000 steps over three profiles against an independent oracle, every one of its 17 rules asserted at every step and exercised, exactly-once / honest ok / no lost answer / liveness; the 70-cell table and the r2–r8 repros in the model's terms; fairness (the i-th of 35 due rows within i request fetches, a lone request behind 873 due rows waits one due fetch, the bound 25); 22 mutants each turning its repro AND the walk red; the census). New fast `test-channels-aggregate` (278 — r9: every control re-pointed at the model / driver seams through a closed world, r7's drain as three per-rule copies, ⑥g(11b)'s press moment made deterministic, ⑥g(8b) the broadcast at the fetch + its control; 276 — r8: ⑥g(11) the front run — a one-key 15 ms stream heard within a round (max 61 ms, 41 calls for 99 requests), the owner's one press under a 4-lane stream heard at 181 ms, the owner's rider ahead of 40 agent riders at position 1 (+ r7's drain as the control: 2706 ms and 74 calls, 1559 ms, position 41); 271 — r7: ⑥g(8) an `ok` heard at ITS fetch behind a 1.8 s pass (+ r6's ok-for-the-end control: heard at its end), ⑥g(9) a 2.5 s saturating storm's 35 due rows served DURING it + a 25 ms trickle with a mid-way re-due (64/70 due fetches, 0 pending) (+ the no-interleave control: 0/35 during, 25/70), ⑥g(10) ONE pass queued per account, `force` sticky (+ r6's per-ask control: 3 forced passes, 80 fetches), ⑥f's at-start control (the RIGHT fetch answered at its start — caught by the instant alone, 3/3), ⑥g(6)'s one-over-budget control, ⑥g(1) counted during the storm AND after `idle()`; r6: ⑥f's judge reads the answer's own instant (`answeredAt`), ⑥g(3b) the owner's reserve, ⑥g(6) the budget cut mid-pass — the two budget lines ⑥f's `budget` state never reached, ⑥g(7) a refusal heard at the first boundary of a 2.7 s pass, each with a patched-copy control; ⑥f (r5): THE CONCURRENCY TABLE, 70 cells — {1, 5, 20} callers × {one key, N keys} × {idle, a timer pass inside the fetch of our key, a timer pass not fetching it, a vendor back-off, the budget spent, the agent share spent, the floor fresh} × {agent, owner} against a scripted adapter that answers after 20 ms — asserting the vendor calls per key (0 or 1 per pass; the owner's ONE honoured press per back-off window, a second round of presses making none), every `ok` a fetch of ITS key that ended after the call began with `appended` = the news, the agent share charged exactly the agent-caused fetches, every refusal named with its wait, no waiter left in the set; controls re-pointed at the drain: answer-everyone-from-the-first-fetch lies 19 of 20, the gate line removed calls 40× and escalates to 41, one-item-per-waiter calls 20 / 5 / 4, every-press-honoured makes 2 calls and climbs to 3; run 3× for flake; ⑥e: 20 concurrent agent refreshes of one conversation, 5 windows opened on one stale conversation and 3 refreshes queued behind a timer pass each make ONE vendor call, the share charged once (control: the copy running its own pass after every wait makes 20 / 5 / 4); ⑥d: 40 agent refreshes + a window open inside a scripted 429 back-off make zero calls and leave `consecutiveFailures` at 1, the owner's press runs and its failure answers the wait it escalated into, the back-off lifts; control: the copy without the gate calls 40× and escalates to 41; the route maps, the CLI's refusal list and the two reconnect re-reads pinned; incl. patched-copy controls: the old 5-page discovery bound, a scheduler that polls everything, the per-conversation-only wake (100 wakes past a cap of 5) and the foreign-pass refresh (18 of 20 lie) must go red; the agent share at 100 % starves the hot rows); new heavy `test-channels-aggregate-ui` (25, zh). Updated: test-channel-filter (95), -caps (80), -acl (65), -store (135), test-channels-engine (142), -push (70), -lane-parity (33), -gmail-shape (95), -lark-shape (84), -accounts (125), -agent-cli (38 — r7: the refused set DERIVED from the agent route's status table, the two reply-only retry-ables excepted by name and proven absent from the request-set region, one fixture per code driven to exit 4 with its sentence, `pending` exit 0, a channel-words case per code), -groups-ui (61), test-oauth-field-parity (245), test-migrations (197). ## 2.369.184 — the 2.369.183 mirror red was the pen leg reading Chrome's post-layout mouse re-target, not the pen; and a grouped taskbar button no longer grows a hover chooser under a pointer that did not move (a rebuild under a resting pointer after a click or an Esc)

- **A grouped taskbar button no longer grows a hover chooser under a pointer that did not arrive.** Click a grouped button (or dismiss its hover list with Esc) and leave the pointer there: when any window title changed — a terminal's or an agent's, which happens all the time — the taskbar re-rendered the button under the pointer and the list popped up 300 ms later, unasked (5 of 5 when constructed). The hover is now armed only by the pointer MOVING over the button, once per visit; a press spends the visit until the pointer leaves, and the visit belongs to the group, so a re-render keeps it. A pointer that moved away while the button was being re-rendered still gets its next hover (PURE `hoverStep`, src/lib/taskbar-group.js).
- **The pen leg's mirror red (2.369.183) was the test, not the pen.** test-taskbar-group-ui (l) read the LAST pointerenter's type after the chooser opened; one or two frames after the open Chrome re-computes hover and moves the MOUSE pointer onto the button where the pen rests, so a slow runner read `mouse` (master's leg, CPU ×20: 17/20 red; ×1: 0/20). The leg now attributes the open to the pen's own typed enter (scripts/pen-hover-judge.mjs), waits for Chrome's re-target so the race is in every record, and runs once more at CPU ×20. `--only l|o [--trials N] [--throttle R] [--trace]` runs one leg N times.
- Gates: test-taskbar-group §10 (the judge over 360 fake-clock interleavings) + §11 (hoverStep over 378 timed scripts), each with patched-copy controls; test-taskbar-group-ui (l2) + (o) + CONTROL 2 (o). Chrome pins: (l) and (o) 40/40 at CPU ×20; the whole heavy suite green ×3 on one core shared with 8 busy loops (master: (a) and (l) red there).

## 2.369.183 — one session, many browsers (lane P): the Agent browser window lists EVERY browser of its session (its own, its helpers', its profiles), a per-conversation browser limit, pop out / fold back, and two grouped chats whose browsers follow them (docs/design-browser-multiview.zh.md)

The owner: "确实 得考虑一个会话里可能有多个并行浏览器，怎么展示的问题，你来设计实现一下吧。另外也得考虑如果两个tabbed窗口每个都打开了各自的浏览器，怎么展示的问题" — and on the design: "这个上限应该是一个属于对话属性的东西，可以调整" / "如果我已经开了并排展示俩 agent 对话呢？变成四列？" / "那得考虑重新合并的操作逻辑".

- **One window, every browser.** The Agent browser window's tab strip now lists all of a session's browsers — its attached profiles, its own browser, and each helper's (sub-agent's) browser — with who is driving (`agent` / `you`) and a state dot (running a command / running / released — hollow, "the next command starts it again"). It appears with two or more browsers; one browser looks as before. A browser that starts later becomes a tab at the END of the strip and never changes the picture you are watching — not even while you have taken over.
- **Helpers' browsers are watchable.** Click a helper's tab to see its picture (its own browser, never the parent's). A claude helper is named after its task ("Helper: check prices") when exactly one helper opened a browser at a time and its own call's result names it; two at once, or a codex helper, read "Helper 1 / Helper 2" — never guessed.
- **The strip folds** by priority into `▾+N` on narrow windows: the tab you are looking at never folds, a browser running a command outlasts a quiet one.
- **A limit per conversation.** The `2/3` chip at the strip's end is this conversation's running browsers against ITS limit (default 3 — Settings → Agent browser → *Browsers one conversation may run at once*; a Task Group can set its own default for its new conversations; each conversation can change its own from the chip's − / + or in Session Properties → Browsers at once, and a resume keeps it). Red at the limit; clicking it lists only this conversation's running browsers (helpers' too), each with Stop (a profile another conversation also uses says "detach it instead"). The agent's next browser past the limit is refused and told where the limit is changed. The machine's own ceiling (six, shared with desktop apps) stays, and its refusal now names only the asking conversation's own browsers — everything else is a count, never another session's name or id.
- **Released after the turn.** A conversation's own browser (and its helpers') is let go 3 minutes after its turn ends (Settings → Agent browser → *Release a conversation's browser after its turn ends*, 0 = never); the tab stays, hollow; the next command starts it again. Never while you drive it or watch it in a live view, and a live view never starts it. Chat sessions only: a terminal session publishes no turn, so its browser is kept until the browser tool's own idle timeout.
- **Pop out and fold back.** Right-click a strip tab → *Open in new window* opens a second Agent browser window of the same session showing that browser (same strip, its own selection). Fold it back from its title-bar menu (*Fold back into the Agent browser window* — the main window selects that tab) or by dropping its icon on the other window / its group (the one drag exception folds back instead of grouping two views of one session). Closing the main window leaves the next one as the main one.
- **Two grouped chats, each with its browser.** Still two panes, never four columns: a chat's browser is born beside it only while the chat is not yet side by side; otherwise it arrives as a pulsing tab (on the browser side, else its chat's side) and nothing on screen moves. With chats on the left and their browsers on the right, switching the chat switches the right to its browser (and clicking a browser switches the chat) — the views are already connected, nothing reconnects. When the other side shows a chat you placed there, nothing follows. The phone shows one pane and never follows.
- **Verify fixes (lane P verify r1, 2026-09-26).** A live view never STARTS a browser of any kind: a click on a hollow (stopped) profile tab now says it is released instead of launching it, and a live view opened before the conversation's first browser command waits, hollow, "Not started yet — the next command starts it" — it no longer asks the browser tool a question that starts a background daemon. Folding back the window you are DRIVING keeps your control: it moves to the other window before this one closes (no hand-back to the agent, no notice); driving in both windows is refused in plain words. A helper is named after its task only when its own call's result names the browser it opened and no other helper was opening one at the same time — never by order. A Task Group's browser limit applies to its NEW conversations (a running one keeps the limit it started with). A released own browser beside an attached profile says "Released — used again only when no profile is attached".
- **Verify fixes (lane P verify r2, 2026-09-26).** A terminal-mode agent's browser is no longer released 3 minutes after its last browser command while it is still working — the release after the turn now applies only where the session reports its turn (chat); a terminal session's browser ends by the browser tool's own idle timeout, as before. A live view that picks up a browser while it is still starting waits for the start to finish (a start that fails is what the view shows — it never starts one itself). And a conversation's browser is started with the idle timeout the conversation was spawned with, so the agent's first command (or a live view) no longer replaces the browser VibeSpace just started when the idle setting changed since the spawn; the new setting applies from the conversation's next start (a resume). Gates: `test-browser-ephemeral` (fast, 188 — the wiring's own facts over a terminal and a chat session, the slow-launch call order for own / helper / attachment, the failed start, the launch's idle; four patched-copy controls), `test-architecture` (fast, 298 — §61), heavy `test-browser-live` (128, 1 skip — the REAL 0.38.1: a view mid-start then the agent's command, one daemon, the recorded pid, never restarted; the pre-fix launch as the control).
- Gates: `test-browser-handles` (fast, 152 — the list's truth table + a negative control, the child rung, the three naming outcomes, the bridge's helper relay), `test-live-strip` (new, fast, 36 — the fold at 1400 / 900 / 600, the chip, the conversation cap beside the machine ceiling, two patched-copy controls), `test-browser-ephemeral` (fast, 139 — the refusal never carries another session's name / lease id with a patched-copy control, the release timing table, the real keeper's cap + release), `test-chain-layout` (fast, 83 — partnerFor / followFor / livePlacement / foldBackTarget + two controls), `test-session-schema` (7), `test-contributions` (219), `test-browser-pin` (181); heavy `test-browser-live` (116 — a helper relay draws its picture, a four-tab strip, a new browser mid-takeover lands at the tail on the same socket, the phone strip folds) and `test-browser-multiview` (new, 29 — real clicks: the follow with zero reconnects, the quiet tab, two chats side by side, pop out + both fold-backs, reload, phone).
- **Integration (2.369.183 — lanes F / H / I / J / M / N were already in 2.369.180–.182).** ONE refusal code for "a browser a view will not start": lane H's `browser_stopped` for every kind (P's `browser_released` is retired for views; the Stop route keeps it for "not started") — a view that WAS showing the browser greys by name and keeps its last frame (H), a view just switched to it reads the tab's own hollow words (P), and either picks the browser up by itself. ONE `EPHEMERAL_REF`, H's `~ephemeral` (persisted in 2.369.180 layouts; P's `@ephemeral` retired). ONE relay key over both helper shapes (P's view by handle, H's `~child:` recorder tap). The launch passes the pairs' idle once (H r4 LOW 5 and P r2 F2 were the same finding; H's `pairsIdleMs` reads P's PURE one) and keeps H's launch mark; P's in-flight wait runs before H's process judge. A fold-back's `pass` is not a stale-approval moment for J's sweep. A strip tab's *Open in new window* passes `popOut` — since lane H's naive-study fix a plain open FOCUSES the session's one view, so the pop-out is the one deliberate second window. The strip is its own row above I's bar (its `▾+N` is `stripMoreBtn`; `state().stripFolded`), the bind row keeps I's unbound-only rule inside P's `registerLiveViewMenus`, the auto-bind keeps H's `EPHEMERAL_REF` target inside P's placement; P's popovers and menus close through M's outside-press closer (createPopover / showContextMenu); test-browser-multiview hands its server `vncEnv()` (N's §57); P's turnKnown pin is test-architecture §61; test-browser-ephemeral's P sections are ⑦ / ⑧; P's F2 control strips H's attachment wait too (layered guards).

## 2.369.182 — RELEASE NOTE: sessions started before this version have no VIBESPACE_SESSION_CWD, so the browser tool writes only under /tmp and ~/Downloads until the session is restarted (Terminate + Resume). Five lanes: the window-targets refusal codes no longer depend on the machine and a window screenshot never lands in the agent's directory (E3); split tabs v2 (F); a grouped taskbar button opens its group (K); floating menus close on a click into an app's picture (M); VibeSpace's own tools stop asking for permission every step, and the browser tool's file reads and writes stay in the session's frame (L)

**Release note.** Sessions started before this version have no VIBESPACE_SESSION_CWD, so the browser tool writes only under /tmp and ~/Downloads until the session is restarted (Terminate + Resume): lane L's write fence is the directory the SESSION was started in, exported as `VIBESPACE_SESSION_CWD` on every spawn path — a session spawned by an earlier version does not carry it, and the tool then fences writes to `/tmp` and `~/Downloads` only.

### Lane E3 — mirror red on .181: window-targets refusal order was environment-dependent

The Actions mirror of 2.369.181 (fast tier, ubuntu-latest) was red on test-window-targets — 259 passed, 2 failed, 3 skipped — while this box and the integration's own fast tier were 320/0. A mirror-only red names the machine-dependent gate first: here the product answered a different refusal CODE depending on which capability the machine lacked.

- **Reproduced here by constructing the runner's shape** (a PATH without python3 / the gi binding / xdotool / Xvfb, DISPLAY and the session bus unset): exactly 259 / 2 / 3. Before the fix, `click @e1` before any snapshot answered `mode_pixels` (the `auto` probe ran first and resolved pixels because no tree was reachable) where this box answered `ref_unknown`; an `auto` window's snapshot answered the helper's own code — `python3_missing` (no python3), `a11y_unavailable` (python3 without gi, the runner's case), `helper_error` (gi but no accessibility bus: libatspi aborts) — where this box answered `mode_pixels`.
- **Preconditions before probes.** `act` checks a `@ref` (no snapshot yet, or a ref the last snapshot never minted ⇒ `ref_unknown`) right after the share-mode check and BEFORE the `auto` probe starts anything: the same answer on every machine, no helper process spawned.
- **An unreachable tree is one verdict.** Under an `auto` share, a snapshot that cannot reach a tree for ANY reason — the new closed set `TREE_UNREACHABLE` in src/window-targets.js: helper_missing, python3_missing, helper_timeout, helper_error, a11y_unavailable — resolves the window to pixel mode and is refused `mode_pixels`; the reason it saw is named in the sentence ("the accessibility tree is unreachable here (a11y_unavailable: …) — pixel mode") and rides as `reason: {code, why}` on the agent route. Attach's resolution names the reason too. An explicit tree share and the user's own desktop still pass the helper's code through (no other road there); a caller's error (`bad-request`) is never folded.
- **A remembered probe answer belongs to its environment.** The accessibility / portal / ScreenCast probe memos were keyed by name alone, so a process asking from a second environment heard the first one's YES. They are keyed now by PATH, the session and accessibility buses, DISPLAY / WAYLAND_DISPLAY, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (and the interpreter + helper for the accessibility probe).
- **The suite is honest about the machine.** §4r builds the runner's shape on EVERY machine (PATH = an empty directory, DISPLAY and the buses unset) and makes the tree unreachable four ways, each proven by an evidence line; the two mirror legs answer one code in all four (`ref_unknown` with no probe spawned, `mode_pixels` with the reason varying), and a patched copy restoring the old order is the negative control (it answers the machine — the mirror's red). §2 pins the environment-keyed memo (control: the key without the environment) and derives `TREE_UNREACHABLE`'s coverage from the helper runner's own refusals + the helper's import refusal. §5's no-tree window now sits on a pid no machine can hand out, so its mode legs run everywhere (the `if (!real)` gate is gone). Every SKIP says what is missing (§3's reason reaches §4's and §5's skips; the xdotool half of a control is skipped by name instead of passing silently).
- Gates: test-window-targets 346 / 0 / 0 here (×3), 286 / 0 / 3 in three constructed runner shapes (no python3; python3 without gi on a bare Xvfb; gi without a bus); test-window-reach 98 (+3 pure legs: four reasons one resolution, the one-line clip, a tree share ignores the probe).
- **A window screenshot never lands in your current directory** (the owner's pixel-mode test: `vibespace-window screenshot <handle>` without `--out` wrote `window-<handle>-<ts>.png` into the agent's cwd — the production checkout). Without `--out` the PNG goes to `<temp dir>/vibespace-window/<handle>-<ts>.png` (a private 0700 directory) and the path is printed as before; a relative `--out` is resolved against the SESSION's directory (`VIBESPACE_SESSION_CWD`, when the spawn exported it) or else that temp directory — never the shell's cwd. An `--out` under `~/.ssh`, `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.vibespace`, a `.git` directory, any other `~/.<name>` entry or VibeSpace's own data directory is refused `write_path_refused` by name (judged after symbolic links, the browser CLI's credential-store rule copied into this single-file tool), a final-component link or a missing directory is `out_unusable`, and every refusal is decided before the request, so nothing is captured. The agent manual says where screenshots land and shows `--out`. Gates: test-window-targets 363 / 0 / 0 (×2; §6 = 17 new legs, red 13 on the pre-fix CLI, the old default in a patched copy writing into the cwd as the control), test-window-target (heavy) 146 / 0 / 0, build (test-architecture 309, ws-contract 5, session-schema 5).

### Lane F — split tabs v2 (lane F): a strip half per side, drag a tab to reorder or move it across, both sides switchable, paths from a chat open side by side, two new settings (inc-muhfb5al-jzk6, docs/design-split-ux.zh.md §8)

The owner (2.369.177, Report a problem): "这个UX非常奇怪啊，首先并排之后tab列表都在左侧，比较难看出来哪边是哪个tab。其次我没法拖动tab重排序，最后我只能调整右侧展示的tab而无法调整左侧的。建议加入tab拖动+直接两侧分开展示的功能。" Then: "另外以后从窗口打开文件路径/本地链接的时候默认side by side展示吧。然后拖动窗口后是直接side by side还是普通tabbed，以及打开文件路径/链接默认用并排还是独立窗口也都加入设置选项。"

- **A strip half per side.** In side-by-side mode every tab belongs to a side (`split.left` / `split.right` in PURE `chain-layout.js`), and the tab bar is two halves laid on the panes' own columns — the title bar is a CSS subgrid of the window's grid, so the halves follow the divider while you drag it (±1 px every frame, measured) with no script. The tab shown in each pane is highlighted and underlined in its colour; the glyph sits over the divider. Measured before: at ratio 0.5 the right pane's tab sat 282 px left of the right pane; at 0.7 every tab sat over the left pane.
- **Both sides switchable.** A tab of the left half shows on the left, of the right half on the right (D19 (a), which only ever replaced the non-anchor pane, is retired). A press inside a pane now focuses that pane, so the keyboard and the menus act on the tab under your hand.
- **Drag a tab sideways to reorder it** (a marker shows the slot, Esc cancels); the first 8 px decide — sideways = reorder, down = the old pull-out. Across the middle the tab MOVES to the other side (a tab you were looking at stays visible there; its old side shows its neighbour); the last tab out of a side ends side by side. No drag ever creates a split. `Ctrl+Shift+PageUp / PageDown` and command mode `{` / `}` move the active tab within its list (a regular browser tab may keep the chord for itself — `{` / `}` always work). A window dropped on a group lands at the slot under the pointer.
- **Paths from a chat open side by side** (Settings → Window → *Opening a file path or link from a window*: side by side — the default — / as a tab / in its own window): a path or local link opened from a chat is born beside THAT chat (never the active window; if the window is already side by side, on the side the chat is not on); the same path again shows its tab (a `:line` link moves the editor). A text file goes straight to the editor.
- **Merge drop → side by side** (Settings → Window → *Dropping a window onto another*: tabs — the default — / side by side at once): the dragged window lands on the right; the toast offers **Undo** (it goes back where it stood) and **Unsplit** (stay grouped as tabs).
- **Other clients** apply a reorder / move / switch / swap IN PLACE (no content re-parented); a window still being opened asynchronously on another client (a CSV viewer) keeps its group waiting for it instead of landing free — which used to break the group on that client's next save. Layouts carry `order` + the side lists; a record written before this restores by one repair rule (no migration).
- **Fixed on the way:** a tab group dragged by its title bar onto another window's icon orphaned its other tabs inside the hidden host — the group now just moves; closing a tab left of the active one no longer switches the group to the active tab's right-hand neighbour (the index slid; it is re-found by window id now).
