## 2.369.68 — usage readings belong to the credentials that produced them (owner: "为啥不是从根源上解决假数据"); resume keeps the conversation's own effort/model (B-6b6d); re-login clears its own warnings

- **Root cause of the phantom usage.** Every VALUE reading (statusline, rate_limit_event, limit banners, the auto-cli panel, OTel corrections) was keyed by the OTel-observed org — the identity the CLI cached at SPAWN — while the pool's hot switch re-points the credentials a running CLI actually uses. After any switch a session filed its readings under the account it was spawned on; a logged-out member kept "receiving" other accounts' numbers, and the same misattribution happened silently between two live members. Now every reading is keyed by the credential slot in use at that moment (the 2.369.66 wall mechanism extended to values, captured once per turn), the OTel org is corroboration only (`orgVerifiedKey` is gone), link moves are recorded in a slot-transition ledger, and a one-shot migration re-attributes or archives the readings, anchors and ledger rows written under the wrong key (never deletes). Each member's panel names the source of its latest reading; a logged-out member's panel is frozen with "stale since".
- **Resume/fork/restart keep the conversation's own effort and model** (owner ruling): the client sends a value only when you explicitly chose one for this session; otherwise the server resumes with the rollout's own last turn (codex) or the transcript's last served model (claude); the instance default applies to NEW sessions only; Session Properties says which fact it is showing (chosen / conversation / instance / harness); the pool placement still gets the model family hint.
- **Re-login clears the warnings it caused.** The login-expiry watch now resolves the inbox items it filed the moment a member's login session changes (any rung), a successful Manage Agents login sweeps immediately (once per finalize, never per 3-second poll), and a measured short session (this org's logins last ~24 h) is mentioned in the 24 h warning.
- Merge review fixes: the pool-blocked notice again names dead logins (the readings chain's pre-filter had hidden them behind "spent: 5h"), the version-marker gate asks git instead of clearing an already-released number.
- Modules: the readings-by-slot attribution lives in `readingSlotFor` (src/server/usage-pool-engine.js) with src/slot-transitions.js and src/reading-repair.js; the resume rule is the resume-continuity module (src/resume-continuity.js: `resumeSpawnPick` + `spawnOriginHint`).
- test-readings-attribution 194, test-codex-effort-meta 245, test-login-expiry 257.

## 2.369.67 — login sessions expire: say it BEFORE the turn dies (owner: "OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed")

- **The incident.** Two members' Claude login sessions reached their absolute expiry (`claudeAiOauth.refreshTokenExpiresAt`); the CLI blanked their tokens on `invalid_grant`, and the pool only learned it AFTER a conversation's turn died with "Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed" — then moved the conversation to another member, so it "worked again" while nobody was told to re-login, and the pool kept moving other conversations onto the same dead login (four conversations, one dead turn each, on 09-02/09-03).
- **Login-expiry facts, passively.** New PURE `src/login-expiry.js` reads the credential file's own deadline: `ok / expiring (<24 h) / expired / logged-out (the wiped shape) / unknown`; the accounts API and Manage Agents carry it as a chip ("login expires in 17 h" / "login is signed out — re-login") next to the login button; the pooled account summarises its members' worst state. Zero vendor calls (file reads only; test-vendor-whitelist unchanged).
- **The pool avoids dead and dying logins.** A member whose login is expired or signed out can never be "usable"; one within 30 min of expiry is never a switch TARGET; an expiring member ranks below an equal healthy one. The auth-failure and pool-blocked notices now say what the wall IS ("Member F's login is signed out — re-login it in Manage Agents"), never "out of quota", and the quota remedy is not prescribed for a wall no window will heal.
- **Warnings before it happens.** Once per member per rung — 24 h, 1 h, and at expiry — an item lands in your "For you" inbox naming the account and the deadline; persisted so a restart does not repeat it, silenced by a re-login (a fresh deadline in the future clears the ledger); a fresh install never files a stale "expired" item for a member that died a week ago.
- test-login-expiry 185 (pure table incl. the wiped shape, fake-clock rungs, once-only + re-login reset + restart survival, the notice STRINGS, the engine wiring pins).

## 2.369.66 — auto-resume fired 130 times into a wall (owner: "你的切换功能发疯了") — four adversarial rounds

- **The incident.** Two sessions re-fired their "You can continue now" continue 130 and 32 times over 4.5 hours, up to twice a second, each cycle writing a "账号池已切换到 Member Y" card into the conversation. Root cause, confirmed on the frozen journal and reproduced against the real engine and a real pool: the CLI's rejection was attributed to the OTel-observed org (the identity the CLI cached at spawn), never to the member whose credentials it actually used, so that member kept a "usable" verdict; the engine re-armed with "switched to a usable account", the per-session hot switch re-pointed to the same member, and `fireNow` had no memory of the fire that had just failed and skipped the pre-fire gate.
- **Wall verdict by credential slot (owner decision ①④).** A rejection lands on the session's linked member — captured ONCE when the rejection arrives, because the first record of a rejection already re-points the link — and that member is dead-until-reset for verdicts and can never be the per-session switch's target; the OTel-observed org is telemetry only.
- **Loop breaker.** A fire answered by another rejection is a FAILED fire: same-identity quarantine (10 min), immediate-fire backoff (0 / 60 s / 5 min), a hard cap of three immediate fires per session per hour, all persisted so a restart cannot hand the loop a fresh budget; the immediate path runs the same pre-fire gate as the timed one. Only proof of WORK (a completed turn, the user's own prompt) clears the memory — a passive quota reading, twenty times more frequent than a rejection, only disarms the wait.
- **One honest line.** The refusal notice is a pure function of the refusal reason with a per-class budget: backoff and fire-pending are journal-only; "no member can serve — add a member or move the session" requires the pool's own verdict; the success card is once per distinct target per window.
- Mitigation is no longer needed: sessions that had auto-resume switched off can turn it back on.
- New suite scripts/test-auto-resume-loop.mjs (186 asserts: the frozen journal replayed at 2/s through the real engine, the negative-control matrix that re-fires ≥10 times, restart survival, the derived noteRecovered audit table).

## 2.369.65 — codex "Steer all" showed one bubble of 25 (owner 2026-09-07) — seven adversarial rounds + a merge review

- **Every inherited queue submission gets its bubble.** The app-server's queue belongs to the THREAD, so after Terminate+Resume the new wrapper inherits items it never recorded; the only live carrier for a steered submission entering the turn is `item/completed {userMessage, clientId}`, which nothing routed — 25 items steered, one bubble drawn. Now an unrecorded submission entering a turn grows its own bubble, keyed by the codex id (never by content).
- **A pre-existing data loss fixed on the way:** the rollout merge de-duplicated codex's own user records by CONTENT, deleting repeated messages on every reload — 27 of 95 user messages on the owner's rollout, 133 across the local corpus. Identity is the codex id; content matching only pairs OUR copy with codex's copy of the SAME submission, and a copy that codex never committed (a slash command, a failed send, an edited or removed queue item, a Stop sweep) WITHDRAWS its claim by name (`webui_user_retracted`) instead of eating a later genuine message.
- **Three producers, one spelling.** The server preview, the wrapper record and codex's own copy of a typed message now spell attachments identically (text first, `input_image` compared without codex's optional `detail`), so a message with an image collapses to one bubble on reload. Visible change: your own bubble renders the text ABOVE a pasted image, live and after a reload alike.
- **Raw NUL bytes never again in source**: the incident module had two, which made it invisible to grep/rg; test-architecture now runs a NUL census over every tracked file (git-driven, gitignored binaries out of scope, its own git calls in a sanitized environment so a hook's GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE cannot redirect them into a real repository — an earlier draft of that control flipped a checkout's core.bare).
- Merge review caught the one merge-only interaction: an `edit` queue verb (2.369.64) now retracts the pre-edit bubble's claim when the text really changed.
- test-queue-steer 697, test-codex-p2-wrapper 352, test-architecture 80 (+ the hostile git-env build battery).

## 2.369.64 — codex queue verbs + notification steering (owner rulings 2026-09-07; eight adversarial rounds + a merge review)

- **The codex queue is now operable, not just visible.** Drag a queued message to reorder it (relative `afterId`, never an index), edit it in place (every non-text variant — images, local images, skills, mentions, audio — is preserved by exclusion; `text_elements` is cleared), run one item now (refused while a turn is busy, with the reason), or run the whole queue as its own control. Peer messages are never editable. Every verb is gated on the running wrapper's advertised verb table (`queueVerbs`, in-band on every `queue_changed`), never on a backend id; a wrapper that advertises nothing gets the legacy verb set, and a session created before the wrapper answered reports `null` (unknown), never an empty list.
- **Eleven client laws for the queue strip** (docs/kb-file-structure.md, chat-input.js): typed words never live only in a textarea about to be replaced; every writer of the textarea is enumerated; the composer's `_send()` answers with one three-valued contract (the message id that went out, `true` when it took the box without a queueable message such as `/goal` or an edit, `false` when it bailed) so Alt+Enter steer (2.369.61) and the edit flow cannot misread each other; the 2.369.60 auto-collapse never fires under a live drag or an open edit (a collapse mid-drag used to turn the drag into a silent "move to the front"; the merge review reproduced it with trusted CDP input).
- **System notifications STEER into a running codex turn** (owner: "按照 TUI 实现"): a VibeSpace notification arriving while codex is busy goes in as `turn/steer` carrying only itself, the queue untouched; human peer messages keep queueing; our Enter default stays queue. Harnesses without a steer verb (ACP v1 / OpenCode) queue the notification and SAY the steer was unavailable; the notification lane for opencode is the durable stash (`peerDelivery: 'stash-only'`).
- Stop still clears the codex queue (2.369.55) and reports each drop as its own removal; on ACP the dropped-peer count no longer tells the user to re-send a message they never sent (B-7638 rule kept through the merge).
- test-queue-steer 600, test-codex-p2-wrapper 267, test-acp-harness 124, test-harness-contract 132; the merged chain is bisectable (test-queue-steer ⑫ asks git for conflict markers across the branch range).

## 2.369.63 — the two parked review follow-ups, closed (B-7638 seven rounds, B-3185 seven rounds)

- **B-7638 — the remote transcript cache's self-heal, from "seven review residuals" to a heal that pays once and never lies.** Seven adversarial rounds, every finding reproduced before it was fixed: the over-cap adoption scanned only the tail 4 KB (a buried splice passed as verified); the ssh rung could GROW an over-cap slot and never wrote its meta back; two polls appending to one slot at one offset had no single writer (single-flight per slot + positional append that refuses a stale offset); a degradable refusal was not a refusal (the moved-slot verdict is terminal on every rung); a rule written for one corruption condemned the innocent shape wearing its signature (`_prefixIsOurs`, typed SLOT_MOVED verdict); legacy over-stamped metas self-heal through a bounded remote gap probe (byte-for-byte against the host, one stamp of `sizeExact`); and round 7: the whole-file scan is memoized against the bytes it judged (ino:size:mtime, dropped by every writer) instead of running twice per poll and again on every poll, the degrade log throttles per fault CLASS (host + offsets blanked) so a different fault inside the minute still prints, and a slot that shrinks under the probe is the MOVED class — never a memoized "proven foreign" verdict. Plus the plugin-manifest `~/.*` expansion and the three acp-wrapper nudge/Stop residuals from the same review. test-codex-zst 222.
- **B-3185 — the writer sweep identifies a CLI by its executable, and its kill paths probe existence with `kill -0`.** Seven rounds: `*claude*` argv-substring matching used to SIGTERM any process whose argv merely named a transcript (`tail -f ~/.claude/projects/…jsonl`, tests under `.claude/worktrees`); per-process `ls /proc/N/fd` forks blew the 20 s budget at 2000+ processes (batched); identity rules collapsed into ONE module (src/cli-identity.js, JS + shell twins, `(deleted)` mirror); the retired rule survived on the uncounted /api/kill-pid path; busybox `ps` has no `-p` so the pre-kill existence probe was blind on busybox images (`kill -0` first, `/proc` second, `ps` last); and round 7: the STANDING SWEEP that enforces "no `ps -p` existence probe on any kill path" now DERIVES its file set by grep (every file that sends or probes a signal, extension-less agent CLIs by shebang, the built daemon bundle judged against the authored text) instead of a hand-written list that had missed 52 real kill-path files, with the marker alternation naming every spelling a kill takes (`kill -s`, numeric `kill -15`, bare `kill "$pid"`, node `handle.kill()`). test-writer-sweep 237, run from both a plain path and a `.claude`-shaped path.

## 2.369.62 — codex: the effort a turn actually ran at (owner: "调成了 ultra 但 metadata 显示 xhigh")

- **The message-meta popup showed xhigh for a conversation running at ultra.** Root cause, five faults stacked: the wrapper synthesizes the `turn_context` every reader takes a turn's effort from, at `turn/started` — and 0.153.4's TurnStartedNotification carries no effort, so the value came from the wrapper's mutable `effort`, which held the spawn env (the INSTANCE default `codex.defaultEffort` = xhigh, passed because a resume that names no effort falls back to the default); the turn had been started by the app-server itself (auto-continue on resume) so that value never reached codex, whose own record of the same turn says ultra; the `thread/resume` reply carrying `reasoningEffort: 'ultra'` landed AFTER the record and the adoption line is gated on an empty effort; that record was the only turn_context in the whole live buffer, so every message was stamped from it; and on rebuild the merge kept the FIRST twin of a turn id — ours — suppressing codex's authoritative copy forever.
- **Fix:** the synthesized turn_context reports the effort the turn was STARTED with, corrects itself when the resume reply lands late, and publishes `{effort, effortNext}` so a mid-turn attach is honest; set-effort refreshes the live status and the status-bar chip immediately (a live `meta/effort` op) and tells the app-server via `thread/settings/update` (a refused update fakes no codex record); the wrapper's effort reaches session-meta so a `/effort` typed into the chat survives the next resume; the merge never suppresses codex's own turn_context. **Honest label:** ultra renders as "ultra (multi-agent · reasoning xhigh)" using the served model's catalog `multi_agent_reasoning_effort` (codex's own models cache, never a constant) and a plain "ultra" when the catalog names none — gated on the harness META row, never a backend id.
- New suite scripts/test-codex-effort-meta.mjs (108 asserts: the incident replayed against a stub app-server with the REAL wrapper in the measured order, a negative control built from master's record shapes, the two-turn rollout fixture xhigh→ultra, set-effort live refresh, the merge fold, a git-backed version-marker assertion) registered in the gate.
- **Owner gate filed (B-6b6d):** on a resume that names no effort, the instance default still outranks the conversation's own saved effort — the remaining half of this incident; recommendation: the conversation's own value wins, the instance default applies to NEW sessions only.

## 2.369.61 — Alt+Enter steers (owner: "顺便加入一个queue的快捷键，不支持queue的就不显示")

- **A keyboard chord for the other send mode.** While a turn runs, Enter still queues (the web/desktop Codex default); **Alt+Enter sends the composer text as a steer** — it goes out on the ordinary send path and the queued item the harness reports back is converted with the same queue-op frame the strip button and bubble chip use (a steer names a queued item; there is no "steer this text" verb). Tab stays slash completion, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter stays send. The chord is the first core `registerKeybinding` contribution (`chat.steerNow`: the command registered once, the binding per view with the window's signal and a `when` scoped to that window), so plugins can see and rebind it.
- **Shown only where it works.** A one-line hint under the composer ("Enter 排队 · Alt+Enter 立即注入") is decided by the pure `composerSendModes(inputModes)` predicate from the harness caps ∧ the running wrapper's advert: codex shows both segments and takes the chord; OpenCode shows the queue segment only; Claude and shell show nothing (Claude holds a mid-turn message but publishes no queue to act on). Session Properties states the rule.
- **Phones (≤768px):** no chords — a bolt button appears beside Send while a turn runs and steer is supported, hidden otherwise. Measured at 375×667: 36×36 beside Send on the same row, the textarea keeps 3 rows, zero overflow.
- **Rounds 2–3 (adversarial):** the 8 s "could not be injected" notice is silenced only when the turn it was sent into really ended — the turn identity now advances on the normalizers' `turn_complete` meta op, not on the label arm, so an idle wrapper running the message as its own turn stays silent while a permission answer or a reconnect inside the same turn no longer counts as a new turn; Session Properties no longer renders two "Config overrides" headers. test-queue-steer 268, test-contributions 136.

## 2.369.60 — the queue strip is bounded (owner: "堆满了queue，不能翻页，然后看不到任何对话内容和发送框了")

- **A long queue no longer swallows the chat window.** The queued-message rows now live in their own scrollable body capped at 8 rows or 40% of the viewport, whichever is smaller (35% on phones ≤768px), so the message list and the input box stay on screen however many items are queued. Past 8 items the strip starts COLLAPSED to its header ("25 queued — runs after this turn", Steer all) with a chevron to expand; the choice is remembered per view. Measured with the real stylesheet and 30 rows in headless chrome: phone 375×667 → body 183 px, scrollable, textarea inside the viewport, 240 px left for messages; desktop 1280×800 → body capped at 216 px.
- Notification steering (system notifications inject into the running turn instead of queueing as billed turns) follows in a separate release once verified; the official Codex TUI's own semantics were researched today and shape it (Enter = steer, Tab = queue; a steer never carries the queue).

## 2.369.59 — the OpenCode background service is a plugin, default OFF (owner decision 2026-09-07; two adversarial rounds)

- **`opencode serve` is now the third built-in plugin** next to Tailscale and frp (⚙ → Plugins), DEFAULT OFF. The plugin is a control surface only: the keeper, the /proc runaway guard and every store fact stay in the shared serve module; the manager owns user intent (`enabled`/`desiredUp` move in lockstep, `promptedAt`). Disable STOPS the process, including one merely adopted from an earlier run, and nothing respawns it. `install()` names https://opencode.ai instead of offering a dead button (it runs YOUR CLI); config is refused (a free loopback port); boot replay = enabled + desiredUp. `decideAutostart({env, pluginWantsUp})` is THE decision: `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0/1` wins as an ops override (the panel says "forced by the environment" and disables the controls), else the plugin record, default OFF.
- **Setting `agents.opencodeServeAutostart` is removed** (schema, settings UI, docs, every reader; a stored value is ignored). The `VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS` serve belt that only existed because the old default was ON is gone with it.
- **First-use offer, once per instance:** creating an OpenCode session (non-blocking — a live session never needs the service), forking, or opening a stopped OpenCode conversation shows ONE dialog (createModalShell): what the service does, Enable & start / Not now. Either answer is remembered instance-wide (data/plugins.json, broadcast) so a second tab or device never re-asks; layout replay never pops it; Enable waits a bounded 25 s and then resumes the pending action (reopening a history window keeps its geometry AND home desktop), a service that never answers toasts its state instead of spinning forever. Persistent surfaces: the ⚙ → Plugins card (state line, Start/Stop, one switch) and a sidebar row "Stopped OpenCode conversations are hidden — its background service is off" with an Enable action, rendered by the workbench on desktop and mobile and gated on the harness descriptor's `store.servicePlugin`, never on a backend id.
- **Round 2 (verifier):** with default OFF, the old store-failure signal (`!ready && autostart === false`) became the normal shipped state and popped a RED error toast on every page load — the availability row now distinguishes "off by choice" from "failed"; `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0` did not actually keep the daemon off because `locate()` adopted a recorded live serve BEFORE the autostart gate — adoption is now behind the switch too.
- New suite scripts/test-opencode-plugin.mjs (81 asserts: fresh data → OFF and zero spawns from listing/discovery; enable → started + adopted + replay after SIGKILL reboot; disable → stopped, no respawn; env precedence incl. an EMPTY value not being an override; prompt-once flag; removed setting absent; chrome: the dialog appears once and Enable proceeds) registered in the gate.

## 2.369.58 — harness honesty batch: four production defects from the 2026-09-07 survey (owner-approved; two adversarial rounds)

- **codex personality no longer overrides the user's ~/.codex silently.** `personality:'pragmatic'` was hardcoded into thread/start AND turn/start; now the value comes from the same per-session slot claude's output style uses, and UNSET means the key is not sent at all (`none` is a real codex value, so it only arrives from an explicit pick). Accepted values = the schema's enum (none | friendly | pragmatic). A style change applies to the RUNNING codex thread via `thread/settings/update`; claude keeps its spawn-time path — the style chip, menu rows and the "Restart now to apply" row gate on a new caps row `responseStyle {live, closed, values}` (mirrored in the client BACKEND_META, deep-equal pinned), never on a backend id; `closed` is codex-only so claude's user-defined output styles are never rejected. Session Properties names the effective value and its origin; the effective style now survives a server restart (it was a dead field after boot-restore).
- **codex ServerRequest replies dispatched by method.** One method was matched by name and everything else got `{decision: …}` — four of the eleven ServerRequest methods have no such field, so those replies could not deserialize (a hung turn). Every method now has an explicit branch classified at arrival: auto (currentTime/read), unsupported (JSON-RPC -32601 + a visible system line + once-per-method telemetry), or a card. MCP elicitation renders through the AskUserQuestion card family with rows derived once from `requestedSchema`; two silent answer-eaters fell out (the shared UI sends one plain string per question; codex routes by question ID, not text). Round 2: the schema-invalid `acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment` branch (which the new gate had certified) was deleted rather than reshaped — upgrading a session-scoped "always allow" to an execpolicy amendment that outlives the session is a product decision, not a serialization detail.
- **ACP unknown sessionUpdate breadcrumb** (once-per-kind telemetry + one console line) — the installed OpenCode's 11-variant union had exactly one real gap, `session_info_update`, now known and card-less.
- **codex image generation + sleep converge on ONE card.** Three producers (live wrapper, thread-read fallback, rollout parser) now emit codex's own rollout spelling for `image_gen.generation` / `clock.sleep`; generated images render through the 2.369.48 media card (the multi-MB base64 never leaves the wrapper), sleep is a live countdown that freezes to "slept 30s".
- Round 2 also: the "Restart now to apply" row is gated on the running wrapper's advert as well as the harness caps; the origin row no longer mislabels an instance default as "your choice". New gate suite scripts/test-harness-honesty.mjs (190 asserts, fixture-vs-live schema diff where the codex binary exists).

## 2.369.57 — codex sub-agent chatter shows live progress (owner: "这种互聊如果连续发生…我好知道对话没卡住")

- **Live traffic readout** for codex multi-agent bursts, derived from the collab rows the normalizer already stamps (nothing stored server-side; every client renders the same numbers): the coalesced collab card's head reads "Sub-agent traffic · {n} messages · {m} agents · last {age} ago" and ticks once a second while the turn streams, then freezes to "over {span}"; the run header, footer and floating run bar carry the same count and age; the streaming status line switches to "Sub-agents working — {n} messages, last {age} ago" while the newest record is sub-agent traffic and yields the moment anything else arrives. Every row carries its record timestamp (or arrival time, named as such in the tooltip); the pure composers live in src/collab-row.js so the stored search text and the screen text cannot drift. ONE interval per ChatView, bound to the window's abort signal, a no-op while the window is hidden.
- **Round 2 (adversarial verify, 4 findings):** the per-second label repaint used to rebuild the Stop button once a second, silently eating ~40% of Stop clicks — the label now lives in its own `.chat-stream-label` span and a label change is a textContent write only (button node, focus and the two-step compaction arm survive; 10/10 trusted clicks delivered vs 7/10 before); a burst that ran entirely while the window was hidden never froze (fixed: freeze on turn end regardless of tick state); the "{n} sub-agents" chips keep their separator; card/run/turn scopes are named where they differ.
- **Encrypted payload tooltip** now says what the lock means: encrypted by OpenAI server-side (multi-agent v2, PR #26210), the key never reaches this machine, the official Codex TUI cannot show it either — openai/codex#28058 (today's research; nothing to decrypt).
- **Integration fix caught by the suite:** with 2.369.55's single-flight Stop, releasing the pending state (turn boundary or the 8 s fallback) went through the new label-only repaint and left the disabled "Stopping…" button in place — a dead Stop. `_endStopPending` now drops that button first so the full render hands back a live one. The suite also no longer copies the production data/ directory into its temp worktree (589 MB, >9 min — it runs in ~55 s now, budget-safe).
- New suite scripts/test-collab-live-counter.mjs (77 asserts: pure composers, normalizer leg on real 0.153.4 shapes, a live codex session through the real wrapper/normalizer/ws in headless chrome, read-only frozen totals, no encrypted blob in the DOM) registered in the gate.

## 2.369.56 — Update no longer dies on a stray `node_modules/node_modules`

- **Owner's ⚙ → Update failed (exit 236) at `npm install`:** `ENOTDIR: rename node_modules/node_modules`. A worktree agent's `ln -s <checkout>/node_modules node_modules` had run with its shell cwd reset to the production checkout (the harness resets cwd between calls), so the link landed INSIDE the real node_modules as a self-referential symlink and npm's reify choked on it. scripts/update.sh now removes a symlink (or an empty dir) at that path before `npm install`, saying so in the log; a populated directory is never touched.

## 2.369.55 — codex Stop also clears the app-server queue (owner decision 2026-09-07; three adversarial rounds)

- **Behaviour:** pressing Stop in a codex session now drops every QUEUED message, matching ACP (until now the app-server drained the queue the instant the interrupt landed, so a queued message RAN right after Stop). The wrapper's `interrupt` verb lists the queue and deletes every item BEFORE `turn/interrupt` (order, not a flag — clearing afterwards loses the race); each dropped bubble's chip reads **Removed (stopped)** through the same `queue_op_result` frame ACP emits; a queued peer/job message goes back to the delivery ladder (`peer_message_result ok:false`) for next-turn injection; failures speak (a failed list = "the queue was NOT cleared", a failed delete = that item is still queued and will run). No extra "Stop dropped N" notice for codex: every dropped item owns a bubble.
- **Stop only claims what Stop actually did (round 2):** the delete reply's `deleted:false` (the app-server drained the item between list and delete — it is RUNNING) is reported as `reason:'gone'` ("no longer queued — it already ran"), never as Removed, and such a peer item is NOT re-stashed (that would be a second delivery). The sweep latch moved to the single publish choke point so the `turn/started` republish cannot resurrect swept bubbles. The sweep is budgeted like a safety control: 2.5 s per RPC, 6 s overall, then `turn/interrupt` goes out anyway and the unreached items are reported `reason:'timeout'` (measured 15 s → 2.5 s on a wedged list, 25 s → 6 s on four wedged deletes).
- **A second Stop is normal (round 3):** stdin dispatches without await, so two `interrupt` frames (double-click, or two attached clients) ran two overlapping sweeps and the second reported the first's removals as "already ran". Both halves are now single-flight: a second Stop awaits the running sweep, and `turn/interrupt` is coalesced per turn (exactly one frame). Client: `_fireInterrupt` is the ONE Stop entry point — the button is disabled with a "Stopping…" label while in flight, re-applied across the status line's own repaint (the repaint used to hand back a fresh clickable Stop), released by the turn ending or by an 8 s fallback (deliberately above the wrapper's 6 s budget) so it can never stay dead. `steerOne` routes its post-steer delete through the same reader: a `deleted:false` there means the item may run twice and is reported `steered-not-dequeued`.
- Suites: test-codex-p2-wrapper 108 → 175 (slow/racing/wedged stubs, a natural turn end as the positive control for "a drained message clears its chip"), test-queue-steer 129 → 155 (trusted-CDP double-click legs). Negative controls reproduced every defect against the previous round.

## 2.369.54 — B-9702: a reader's page-up was undone by our own auto-scroll chain (desktop-resume residue, round five — measured before explained)

- **Symptom:** within ~1.4 s after a desktop resume, a REAL wheel-up page was re-pinned to the live tail about 1 in 4 runs (the realWheel leg, 20 runs → 5 failures). **Mechanism (captured, not inferred):** round two cancelled only the re-tail TIMER and left the `_forceScrollToBottom` ten-frame chain running — the "+1240 ms was merely covered by it" writer from that round's own comment; its last rung wrote `scrollTop = scrollHeight` **3 ms after** the reader's wheel, the pin re-engaged off our own write, and round one's "a pinned view never loses its tail" faithfully snapped back. The backlog's "collapsed-geometry re-pin" hypothesis was REFUTED by the same capture (`sh−ch` = 2.5 viewports; `collapsedGeomSkip` never fired).
- **Fix (src/lib/chat-view.js):** ① the chain carries an EPOCH; `_cancelForcedScroll(via)` bumps it from `_notePositioning`/`_noteUserNav` (a bare click via `_noteUserInput` does not — it moved nothing), so every queued frame is void; a new `_forceScrollToBottom` takes a fresh epoch, so a cancel can never kill auto-follow. ② The programmatic-scroll mute must outlive the write it mutes: the scroll event dispatches AFTER the callback that wrote it, so releasing `_programmaticScroll` in the same frame handed our own displacement to the boundary logic as reader geometry (`fsb:-1` in the capture); release is now one frame later, guarded by `_fsbActive`. ③ A `repin` trace (twin of `unpin`).
- **Measured:** the same 20-run realWheel leg 5/20 → 0/20. **Pinned:** test-desktop-resume-paging +3 (the +1400 ms leg now asserts the READER's outcome; a deterministic pre-armed-chain variant; per-mechanism negative controls) → 35; test-chat-trim-guard +8 (DOM-free chain semantics) → 112, 3 red against the pre-fix source.
- **Rule:** every automatic writer of `scrollTop` must lose to the reader's positioning act (the timer was only one of them), and a guard against one's own write must live at least as long as the last write it guards.
- Housekeeping: `.gitignore` gains a bare `node_modules` line so worktree agents' node_modules SYMLINK no longer dirties the tree (the `node_modules/` rule matched directories only, which kept the release gate from writing its green marker in worktrees).

## 2.369.53 — codex sub-agent view: no Resume bar (owner report)

- **Opening a codex sub-agent's conversation from a collab row showed the dead-session "Resume this session" bar.** The child thread went through the generic view-only path (`viewSession`), which offers Resume on every stopped transcript. A sub-agent's conversation is read-only by NATURE (it ran inside its parent's turn; resuming it would spawn a standalone session on that child thread), not by death. `viewSession` now passes `subagentView` (agentKind/sourceKind 'subagent') into ChatView; `_showResumeBar` renders a one-line explanation instead of the button. Same flag path serves the claude Task viewer.
- test-attach-rescue: legs D (sub-agent view: history renders, NO Resume button, note present) + E (negative control: the same transcript viewed as a primary session keeps its button); suite moved to freePort() + per-pid dirs (hard-coded 3989/9339 were the 2.369.51 collision class).

## 2.369.52
- **Codex send modes: QUEUED ⇄ STEERED (owner ask 2026-09-06; worktree agents, three adversarial rounds incl. runs against the real codex app-server 0.153.4).** A message sent while a turn runs is queued; its bubble carries a "Queued" chip and a queue strip above the input lists every queued item with **Steer now** (inject into the running turn via `turn/steer` with `expectedTurnId`), **Remove**, and **Steer all** when several are queued. Measured facts drove the design: 0.153.4's queue family is add/list/update/delete/reorder/start; `turn/steer` does NOT dequeue (the wrapper deletes on success or the message would run twice); several steers per turn are accepted (Steer all = sequential steers in queue order, stopping at the first refusal); an `add` on an idle thread starts a turn by itself. Semantics: steering item N injects only N, the others keep their order and still run after the turn; a steered/removed item never runs twice; a chip clears when the turn drains it. Refusals speak and say what happens next ("cannot steer a review turn — stays queued and runs when this turn ends", "the turn ended before the message could be steered — it will simply run next"). Framework, not a codex special case: `backend-caps.inputModes {queue, steer, queueOps}` (codex all / OpenCode-ACP queue+remove / claude queue only / shell none), `BackendAdapter.formatQueueOp`, ONE ws verb `queue-op` gated on the caps row AND the running wrapper's advertised `caps.inputQueue` (a session spawned before the update degrades to the old "Queued — runs after the current turn" card; refusals carry code `queue-op-unsupported`), `queue_changed` published by both wrappers on every change and on attach (`attached.queueSupported`), chips re-applied whenever the capability arrives after the bubbles (attach ordering). Coded per-session errors are scoped refusals only for an explicit set (input-rejected, not-codex-chat, queue-op-unsupported) or a server `scope:'action'` marker — `ended-during-attach` still takes the view-only rescue. ACP Stop marks dropped queued bubbles "Removed"; removing a queued peer/job message re-stashes it for redelivery. Codex Stop still leaves the app-server's queue to drain (owner decision pending). Gate: scripts/test-queue-steer.mjs (129), test-codex-p2-wrapper 41→104, test-acp-harness 91→100.

## 2.369.51
- Release gate: the ~9.5 min gate now outlives GitHub's SSH idle timeout (three green gates ended with "Connection to github.com closed by remote host" and no transfer), so `npm run ci` writes a green marker (.git/ci-green = HEAD sha, clean tree only) and the pre-push hook accepts a marker for the EXACT tree that is under 60 min old instead of re-running the gate inside the SSH session. Flow: run the gate, then push.
- Release gate: scripts/test-desktop-resume-paging.mjs takes free ports (it hard-coded 3989/9339; a parallel agent's gate running the same suite made the release gate's copy probe the other server, so its source-level negative control could not reproduce and 4 phantom reds blocked a green commit) and cleans up on SIGTERM.
- **Desktop switch no longer pages a pinned chat window into history (inc-mtq5bpjt-0o0n, inc-mtqip9wl-urz4: "切换桌面后窗口内容跳到历史消息"; five adversarial rounds, every one reproduced in headless chrome with TRUSTED input and a control that shows the pre-fix failure).** Root cause from the incident tracer: on resume the hidden subtree re-measures, scrollTop reads 0 for a frame while the view is still pinned, the top gap-sentinel IntersectionObserver fires (it had none of the scroll handler's intent/pin/settle/suspend gates), and the page-up's completion trimmed the live tail and landed at 0. Fix, structurally on the path that is alive in the failure state: (1) ONE predicate `_autoPagingBlocked()` (disposed / suspended / resume-settle / pinned / settling / no-input / input-resize) gates every automatic paging trigger incl. the observer and `_maybeSeekEarlier` (trace `gapSkip{why}`); an explicit retry click bypasses it. (2) A resume settle armed by `setSuspended(false)` (1240 ms incl. the re-tail slack): the scroll handler decides nothing (but still refreshes the floating run bar), the observer no-ops, the attach-fill rescue defers, and a window that was PINNED when hidden (snapshot taken in `setSuspended(true)`) is re-tailed by a bounded series (1240 / 2000 ms) with the unpin itself gated on positive evidence inside a 2.8 s horizon — an input-less displacement can no longer strand the view. (3) The repair LOSES to the reader: every positioning act — wheel, touch, navigation keys, minimap, search reveal, the run bar and footer, jumps, a real scrollbar drag keyed on WHERE the press landed (the gutter, cleared on pointerup; never a timer) — cancels it, while a plain click or non-navigation key does not (a click is not a positioning act). (4) `_extendTop` never trims the tail of a pinned view. Known residual: within ~1.4 s of a resume a real wheel-up is re-pinned ~1/3 of the time by the collapsed-geometry guard (B-9702). Also: the opencode serve follow-ups from its standalone verification (terminal naming refusals, real-repo check for the isolated cwd, honest availability reason, parked reason shown once per page load). Gate: scripts/test-desktop-resume-paging.mjs (32, real 36 MB transcript + real desktop switch + trusted CDP input, in the release gate), test-chat-trim-guard 15→104.

## 2.369.50
- **opencode serve runaway (2.369.42 regression, owner's machine: 1.6 cores, 4.8 GB RSS, 3.6 GB/s page-cache reads, 30 021 inotify watches — all on /tmp).** Measured root cause (the first hypothesis, "our /project × directory='/' discovery query keeps it hot", was REFUTED at 0.9 % CPU): OpenCode boots an INSTANCE per DIRECTORY and every v2 `GET /api/session/{id}/…` route boots one for that session's directory (+19 indexer threads, +180 MB, a full-tree inotify watch); 2.369.42's first-user-message naming used the v2 `?order=asc` route, the owner's store held one session whose directory was /tmp with no user message, and the 60 s name-retry poked it forever. Fix: naming reads the v1 message list (whole conversation, oldest-first) under a 1 MiB streaming cap, the listing is directory-less first, the serve runs from its own empty **git-init'd** data/opencode-serve/cwd (OpenCode walks UP for a git worktree — a plain dir inside the checkout resolves the whole checkout, a fake .git does not stop the walk), '/' and $HOME are never passed as directories, a /proc-based runaway guard parks a hot serve with a user-visible reason, `agents.opencodeServeAutostart` (default ON, `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0` still honoured) can turn autostart off from the UI, and a 2.369.42 serve record is replaced on boot. Also in this release: the codex collab `wait` row now says what it waits for ("waiting for sub-agent replies · cell N · ≤Ns"). Gate: test-opencode-serve 98→131.

## 2.369.49
- **Codex multi-agent v2 collaboration is ATTRIBUTED (B-7473; owner: sub-agent reports appeared as ordinary assistant messages, some twice, "根本没区分出这是subagent消息"; worktree agents, five adversarial rounds on the owner's real 0.153.4 root rollout).** Root causes: the wrapper ignored the `threadId` of every v2 item notification, so a child thread's `agentMessage` became a ROOT assistant message in the live buffer, and the rollout's plaintext FINAL_ANSWER `agent_message` records rendered as generic cards — live twin + rollout twin = the duplicate. Now: the wrapper gate is inverted (any notification carrying a foreign `threadId` is foreign unless allowlisted — covers `error`, thread/compacted, thread/queue/changed, turn/diff/updated), a child's agentMessage becomes an attributed `agent_message` record, a child's error a collab activity row (never the root's task_failed), an own-thread message carrying the inter-agent envelope is attributed to its Sender, `subAgentActivity` items fill the agentPath→threadId map, every record carries thread_id/turn_id (stripped from the merge fingerprint), `meta.agentPath` comes from the thread/start reply. Normalizer: ONE `item_completed` router (SubAgentActivity started/interacted/completed/errored → one-line collab activity rows, id-twinned records map-only, no double render), collab records get a first-class shape — inbound PLAINTEXT payloads become attributed **sub-agent report** cards (own collapse kind `report`, NOT folded by default; markdown body, "↩ usecases_v4 · FINAL_ANSWER" header, tinted strip), encrypted inbound + outbound + activity = compact one-line rows that COALESCE ("← 3 messages · water_research (FINAL_ANSWER), …"), twin dedup by id (encrypted messages by id + blob prefix — the content leg only when a body exists; 168/168 encrypted messages represented), bare `task_name` targets normalized to the absolute agent path (36 → 20 identities = exactly the real children; 408/409 rows carry a click-through thread id), each child error its own row. Client: `src/collab-row.js` (PURE) rows with SVG direction icons, the sub-agent NAME opens that child's rollout read-only in the existing sub-agent viewer (0.153.4 knows the thread id inline; fallback GET /api/subagents?backend=codex&threadId=<root> from each child's own thread_spawn, async, 10 s cache), fold headers gain "N sub-agents: …" chips and "N sub-agent messages"; `/api/session-messages` answers 404/502 instead of hanging on a loud reader refusal; dead `--bg-secondary` token replaced. Gate: scripts/test-codex-subagents.mjs (62), test-codex-0153 66→92, test-codex-p2-wrapper 41→62, test-codex-history 142.

## 2.369.48

## 2.369.47
- **Opus 4-lens adversarial review, three more areas fixed (worktree agents, two verify rounds each, every fix negative-controlled on real data).** *Codex discovery / zst / remote fetch*: a compressed rollout whose text compresses better than ~4× got an EMPTY head (7 of 40 real rollouts) and VANISHED from the sidebar, with the empty meta cached — the head is now read by bisecting compressed prefixes under a fixed output cap, and an unreadable head throws instead of caching '' (`_noteExtractFailure` logs it once per file per 10 min); the per-directory listing cache records settledness at FILL time (a same-mtime-tick sibling rollout is no longer invisible forever); .jsonl/.jsonl.zst twins de-duplicate to the PLAIN twin with merged facts (the newest-first producer order had let the .zst win and drop the name/cwd); the remote transcript cache records the resolved remote path + compressed flag, never delta-appends onto a compressed file, heals slots the pre-fix code corrupted (pre-provenance meta ⇒ one whole refetch; the file's own bytes testify: zstd magic under a plain remote, JSONL head byte, NUL/zstd frame in the tail) and `find … | sort | head -1` makes the pick deterministic. *ACP wrapper*: a Stop landing during the context fetch no longer dispatches the prompt afterwards (cancelled re-checked after every await); Stop always clears the queued prompts ("queue-cleared" notice) and a dropped bookkeeping nudge no longer disables bookkeeping for the session; a Deny with no reject-kind option answers `cancelled` — never allow_always (the tool used to execute); an agent that exits 0 before answering initialize is reported instead of a blank window. *Plugin security*: agent-tool descriptions/args are embedded via JSON, control characters and line terminators are stripped (a CR injected code into the generated shim that runs outside the sandbox with the session token), agentTools now require consent; fs capability paths are normalized (`//`, `/./`, `~//` no longer bypass the forbidden-root guard) and node's trailing `*` wildcard is modelled (`/*` and wildcards over a forbidden root are refused); reinstalling a DIFFERENT package under a trusted id resets enabled+trust and requires re-consent (keyed on content hash + recorded source, even when the folder was absent); proxied plugin responses carry nosniff + a sandbox CSP; write-implies-read is stated in the consent summary; the install staging walk is async with a bound; a per-child stopping flag; uploaded temp files always cleaned. Seven small residuals parked as B-7638. Gate: test-codex-zst 44→86, test-acp-harness 72→91, test-plugin-trust 71→72, test-plugin-loader 47→48.

- **Harness S9 — OpenCode serve-mode is the opencode harness's STORE (B-03f2 scoped; worktree agent, integrated; verified live against opencode 1.18.29).** The ACP harness has no transcript files (OpenCode keeps sessions in its own sqlite store), so stopped OpenCode conversations never reached the sidebar. Integrator fix: the resume-already-live guard is now gated on the harness caps row (any chat harness with a stream protocol) instead of a claude|codex id list — a stale card could otherwise spawn a second `opencode acp` on one live session. Not wired (recorded with exact API names in the design doc): revert, question, pty, SSE push invalidation; 'external' liveness (a TUI driving the same session) is undetectable; local machine only. ## 2.369.40
- **Wall → switch in the same tick (B-2c9b, plan A+B; worktree agent, integrated).** Three times on 2026-09-05 a walled turn's verdict read the POOL scope ("usable via <linked member>" off the linked member's healthy cache) while the limit banner had landed on the org the CLI was ACTUALLY on (a hot-switched CLI keeps its old token — 193 readings had been re-attributed away from the link); the pool only moved 1.5–3 min later when a reading arrived, and in-flight subagents died in the gap. (A) **A wall is ground truth for the account it lands on; readings only confirm.** Every wall signal (rate_limit_event, limit banner, the codex sites) now carries the org-verified cache key its mark landed on, and `demoteWalledAccount` runs FIRST in `onWalledTurn`: if that account is a member of the session's pool, the affected bucket is written exhausted NOW through the same write path readings use (`captureRateLimitEvent`, source `wall`: utilization 1, resetsAt = the signal's future reset, else the cached future reset, else the bounded 5h/24h guess), and the pool evaluation runs in the same `noteTurnEnd` AFTER the auto-resume arm, so a hot switch's fireNow continues the armed session immediately. Misattribution guard (the 2.368.34 class): demote only when the account saw ≥2 walled turns inside 120 s (any sessions, one entry per turn) OR it is the session's OTel-observed org (≤10 min); a single unverified wall holds — journal `[wall] … holding the demotion` + telemetry `wall-demote-held`; demotions log `[wall] demoted <name> <bucket> until <iso> (n walls / observed-org)` + `wall-demote`. (B) **Observed-org aware evaluation.** `sessionCurrentMember` (OTel truth ≤10 min → pool member, else the link) now drives `resolveUsageKey` for pooled sessions (live odometer, probe matching, every derived cache key), `quotaVerdictFor(scope, {model, session})` (the session's current member is judged first so `via` names what it is on; verdict carries on/linked/divergent), the per-session auto-switch pass (decides FROM the observed member; a same-target re-point is journal-only + creds-mtime bump) and both probe targets; divergence logs once per session per 10 min (`[pool] session <id> observed on <X> while linked to <Y>`, telemetry `pool-observed-divergence`). The hot-switch symlink still targets the chosen member. No product default changed. Known limit: a live CLI can hold its old token ≥25 min, so a re-pointed session may re-wall once — the second wall inside 120 s demotes (self-limiting). Gate: test-auto-resume §11 (real pool + real engine + real auto-resume, 125), test-rate-limit-capture ⑧ (42); design record docs/design-wall-machine.md addendum.

## 2.369.36
inc-mtox23xw ("content jumped after I sent a message"; the two DreamVanLife windows stuck at open/loading) — two faults, both fixed:
- **Server event loop blocked 10–59 s by the usage estimator.** Ground truth: `Debugger.pause` through the inspector caught the main thread three times inside `usageHistory._events` ← `costBetweenMulti` ← `extractPairs`/`learnRates` ← `ratesFor`, reached from `/api/usage` and from the pool engine's `sweepUsageAnchors` timer; strace showed ~90 `openat`/s (a readdir + stat per ledger shard per call) and no idle during the "loop gaps"; the CPU profiler's `(idle)` attribution had hidden it. `learnRates` costs EVERY historical anchor pair on every recompute (thousands of pairs, recomputed on every new anchor) and each cost was a full scan of the whole permanent ledger. Fix: the ledger keeps a lazily rebuilt time-sorted view and `_events(from,to)` binary-searches it (O(log n + k)); `_loadEvents` re-checks the shard directory at most once per second (its own appends reset the throttle); `costBetweenMulti` memoizes per interval, keyed by the count of events at or before `to` so a late backfill into an interval still recomputes it. Gate: scripts/test-usage-ledger-perf.mjs (brute-force parity over an unsorted 60k-event ledger, 2000 pair costs cold <1.5 s / warm <60 ms, memo invalidation, readdir throttle).
- **Chat view paged up on its own after the reconnect rebuild.** The heartbeat terminated the (frozen) client → reconnect → every window re-attached and rebuilt; 100 ms later the "auto-fill when content doesn't fill the viewport" check saw unresolved content-visibility heights (sh ≤ ch) on a tall PINNED window and fired an ungated `_extendTop`; the slab landed 7 s later (stalled server), `trimBottom` dropped the live tail and the view unpinned ~1500 px up. Now the check waits 700 ms for heights to settle and only fires for a genuinely short view (<30 rendered cards).

## 2.369.35
- **Image tool results froze the page** (owner: two DreamVanLife windows stuck at "opening"/"loading history" while this session opened in 2s): the agent had been `Read`-ing PNG screenshots — the CLI returns each as a base64 block, and the normalizer JSON-stringified it into the card's `output` TEXT (~600 KB per card; 78 cards; a 12 MB attach payload; the transcript grew 0.6→65 MB in 85 minutes). The renderer's escHtml/linkify over base64 froze the browser thread (telemetry: renderer-freeze-s, ws-reply-timeout:attach ×19, ws-heartbeat-terminate ×11 → reconnect storm), and the codex window in the same page could not get its attach ack. Fix: `splitToolResultContent` lifts image blocks out as `{mediaType, bytes}` metadata (the output keeps a one-line `[image image/png · 586 KB]` marker; text/array results keep their exact previous shape), and the tool card renders the FILE from disk via the file viewer's `/api/file/raw` URL (lazy) — or a size chip when there is no path. Binary never enters a normalized message or the DOM again.

An account that never showed a weekly reset (Member Y today) has nothing to project until its first reading.

## 2.369.17
- **Codex sessions could not reach the VibeSpace agent tools (P0 of docs/design-harness-plugins.md).** The codex chat wrapper started every thread and turn with `sandboxPolicy {type:'workspaceWrite'}` (or `readOnly`), whose network policy defaults to closed — and codex's seccomp filter closes loopback too (measured on this machine: `connect 127.0.0.1` → EPERM with `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED=1`; AF_UNIX is blocked as well). Every vibespace-status/-task/-ask/-job/-msg/-page/-docs call from a default / safe-yolo / read-only codex session therefore failed, while the wrapper kept injecting the tools intro each turn and the Stop nudge kept asking for bookkeeping the agent could not do; only yolo worked. Fix: the wrapper's readOnly/workspaceWrite policies carry `networkAccess:true` whenever the integration is on (`VIBESPACE_API` set by the spawner) — filesystem sandboxing unchanged; the TERMINAL path pushes the bare TOML override `-c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true` (the JSON-quoted form is a string, not a boolean); and the boot-time sandbox probe is now FUNCTIONAL (`codex sandbox -- true`, async) instead of a PATH lookup for `codex-linux-sandbox` that "failed" on every npm install and silently ran terminal 'default' sessions with danger-full-access while chat was sandboxed. Gate: scripts/test-codex-sandbox-net.mjs (real `codex sandbox` A/B when the binary is present, evidence-SKIP otherwise + static pins; the probe reports through a file because Node's socketpair stdio is swallowed by the network-disabled seccomp filter — a stdout-based control silently reads as "no output").
- **docs/design-harness-plugins.md** — the 2026-09-05 research (8 agents): Codex support-gap matrix (P0–P3), the HarnessDescriptor abstraction layer + conformance suite + ACP as the generic third-party harness protocol (Gemini CLI first; Claude never via ACP), and the VS-Code-shaped plugin system (manifest, derived activation, five isolation tiers, contribution points mapped onto existing registries). Tracked items filed in the backlog; four owner decisions listed in §4.

## 2.369.16
- **Post-restart attach storm no longer stalls the server, and a stall no longer kills the client (userW inc-mtndq0vb "一些 session 无法打开也没法 terminate，卡死了").** Forensics: the "stuck" session's process tree was alive and its socket connectable; the server had restarted 3 minutes earlier (self-update to 2.369.15). After a restart, every chat session's FIRST attach ran a synchronous `convertHistory` over its whole transcript on the main thread (this instance: 58 live sessions, 1.35GB of transcripts, 10–56MB each) — a desktop switch re-attached 19 windows and the event loop stalled for ~4 minutes (attach-acks arrived in 32s bursts, `attached` replies 4 minutes late). The 30s heartbeat then saw the pong it could not have read during its own stall, TERMINATED the live client, and the inbound frames still queued on that socket (the second attach, both kills) were dropped — the client reconnected into another re-attach round: blank window, Terminate a no-op. Three layers: ① **time-sliced first-attach rebuild** — `MessageManager.convertHistoryAsync` / `CodexMessageManager.convertHistoryAsync` yield to the loop every ~25ms; `normalizers.rebuildHistory(session, id, records)` is single-flight (concurrent attaches await one promise) and arms `session._rebuildQueue` so live records arriving mid-rebuild are held and replayed IN ORDER afterwards; `_historyLoaded` is still set only after success. Every live-feed site (stdout parse ×2, chat-input echo, permission payload) now goes through `normalizers.feedLive(session, msg)` — never `processLive` directly. ② **stall-aware heartbeat** (`src/server/ws-heartbeat.js`): a tick that fires >5s late is a no-terminate round (everyone re-pinged, judged next tick) — a missed pong measured across our own stall is not evidence; real half-open detection is unchanged. ③ **reliable kill**: the server now replies `killed {ok}` to the REQUESTER (ok:false = not found; `exited` only ever reached attached clients), and every client kill path (sidebar/taskbar/card Terminate, close-to-terminate, restart-with-permission, pool restart) routes through `app.killSession(webuiId, backendSessionId)` = `ws.request(..., {resend:true})`, re-sent on each reconnect until acknowledged. **Adversarial review (5 lenses) then hardened the design:** rebuilds run FIFO (fair round-robin slicing made every window land at the total time, past the client's 2-minute ladder — serialized, the first windows open in seconds) and the server re-acks every 10s with `{progress:{done,total}}` while a session waits/converts, the client ladder treating a fresh ack as proof of life (bounded 15min); the attach re-checks liveness after the rebuild (`error code:'ended-during-attach'` instead of a live-looking window on a session killed meanwhile); peer cards (Background Work notify, vibespace-msg, auto-resume notice) and auto-resume's continuation prompt go through the same gate (`feedPeerCard` / `feedLive`) — they wrote mid-history before; a failed rebuild still drains the held records; codex's async rebuild isolates per record; view-only, subagent and HTTP (`transcript-service.view`, which now joins an in-flight rebuild) converts are async too — no synchronous whole-transcript work is left on the main thread; the heartbeat got a second detector (a 1s loop-gap pulse taints the round — tick lateness alone had a blind band: a 30–35s block starting right after a ping ends with the tick only seconds late but the pong still unread) plus a bound (a client pong-less across 6 tainted rounds is still reaped) and logs/telemetry on every termination; the kill ack carries the id the client ASKED for (`sessionId` = requested, `resolvedId` = after the 2.179.0 stale-id remap — replying with the remapped id would have orphaned every stale-id kill), the client's 3-minute watchdog now DISARMS the request, and the backendSessionId frame is a one-shot sent before the resend-chased plain kill, so a resend can never kill the conversation's resumed successor. New gate suite scripts/test-attach-rebuild.mjs (45: sync/async parity on a 7500-record transcript with loop-turn proof, gate ordering + FIFO + peer cards + failure drain + malformed-record isolation, heartbeat matrix incl. the blind band and the bound, wiring pins across server.js + src/server for zero direct normalizer writes).

## 2.369.15
- **Stranded writes under a disconnected storage — quarantine + guard (owner's OneDrive `is not empty, use --allow-non-empty` failure).** Diagnosis: the mount point was not a stale fuse endpoint, it held REAL files — the task store's generated `.vibespace/TASK.md` recreated `<mountpoint>/…/AIContext/.vibespace/` on the bare local directory while OneDrive was disconnected (the boot regeneration runs before mounts exist, and every task change regenerates); rclone then refused every reconnect, and `--allow-non-empty` would only have hidden the files under the mount. Three layers: ① **connect quarantines leftovers** — `_ensureMountpointDir(mp, {quarantine:true})` (rclone AND cephfs connect paths; the mount-point EDIT path never quarantines) moves the whole directory aside to a sibling `<mountpoint>.stranded-<timestamp>/`, recreates the mount point empty, and broadcasts a level-2 server-notice naming the path and the items (never deletes, never merges; a dead fuse endpoint makes the `ls` fail ⇒ falls through to the stale-daemon kill); ② **`mounts.shadowedBy(path)`** = the registered storage whose mount point contains the path but is NOT mounted (gmail folders + credential-only records excluded; `isMounted(m, live)` takes a pre-read /proc/mounts) — `files.js` refuses every explorer/editor/upload op under it with 503 "“X” is not connected — this folder is its mount point" instead of writing into the bare dir; ③ **the TASK.md mirror skips shadowed context folders** (`isPathShadowed` dep, lazy TDZ-safe getter from server.js; warned once per group + telemetry `ctx-md-skipped-shadowed`) and `syncAllContextMd()` re-runs once mounts exist and on every `mounts-updated` broadcast, so the skipped file lands the moment the storage is back. New gate suite scripts/test-mount-stranded.mjs (26: real temp-dir quarantine incl. dotfiles + idempotence + edit-path negative control, predicate matrix incl. \040 escaping, writer guard + retry, wiring pins).

## 2.368.28

- **2.368.27 was the wrong scope — the owner's correction is the real story**: the pool (hot) had moved the session onto a member whose seven-day quota then died, while the five-hour-exhausted SIBLING (seven-day fine) was the account to come back to; the pool even switched back on its own at the sibling's 5h reset — **but a hot re-point does not move an idle limit-blocked session**, and the session's wait had been refused, so it sat dead on a healthy account. Three mechanisms, all functionally tested + wiring-pinned (test-auto-resume 71→79): ① `armBestReset` now merges **pool sibling members'** future bucket resets into the candidate set (the freeing reset lives in the SIBLING's cache, not the current member's — 2.368.27 only read the session's own identity); ② a HOT pool switch (per-session pass AND pool-level default-link pass) calls `autoResume.fireNow()` on ARMED sessions — the continue is delivered the moment the pool lands them on a healthy account, instead of waiting out a reset that no longer matters (armed-only: an unarmed session was never promised a continue; cold switches keep restarting via the client); ③ the timed fire runs a new `beforeFire` hook (engine: `maybePoolAutoSwitch`) BEFORE spending, so the continue rides whichever member is healthy at that moment.

## 2.368.27

- **Auto-resume arms for the NEAREST known reset, and a refusal is no longer silent** (owner: "c1206711…这个怎么没自动恢复？" — full forensics in the session buffer). What happened: the session armed for its five-hour reset, 90s later an `allowed_warning` event (a request genuinely went through) disarmed the wait — correct — then the NEXT rejection carried the **seven-day** bucket's resetsAt (~100h out, org overage disabled), `armIfEnabled` refused it (MAX_WAIT 26h) **journal-only**, and nothing was left waiting — while the five-hour reset 8h away, sitting in the usage cache the whole time, is exactly what freed the sibling session that had kept its arm. Fixes: ① `pickArmReset` (PURE, in auto-resume.js) — candidates = the event's own resetsAt + every known future bucket reset (fiveHour/sevenDay/opus/scoped) from the identity's usage cache; nearest-in-range wins (one possibly-wasted continue at a nearer reset beats hours of silence; a still-dead account just re-runs the ladder on the next rejection). Engine calls it via `armBestReset` at ALL THREE exhaustion sites (claude dead-branch + both codex sites — backend-neutral, wiring PINNED per the 2.355.0 lesson). ② A too-far refusal now **declares itself in the session** ("重置在N小时后，超过自动等待上限，不会自动续跑…", 1/h floor) instead of a journal line the user never sees. test-auto-resume 62→71, incident shape as fixture.

## 2.368.26

- **Agent messages now reach Codex sessions LIVE, with full claude-inbox parity** (owner: "继续对齐，还有第三方其它agent支持（注册表）"; reverses the "codex不能被唤醒" claim the 2026-08-25 research refuted). New delivery rung in conversation-deliver, **registry-gated**: `capsOf(backend).peerDelivery` ∈ 'cli-inbox' (claude — CLI cross-session inbox) / 'rpc-queue' (codex) / 'stash-only' (shell/unknown) — never a backend-id branch; a third backend claims the live lane by declaring the cap + serving the contract. The codex wrapper owns the app-server RPC connection, so the rung writes a `peer-message` stdin frame and the wrapper delivers natively: **idle ⇒ `turn/start`** (billed turn + reply — exactly claude's inbox behavior), **busy ⇒ `thread/queue/add`** (runs right after the current turn; upstream-test-pinned semantics). Capability-gated on the wrapper's own sidecar advert (`caps.peerMessage`, the 2.361.1/2.364.1 law — old wrappers get an honest miss→stash, never a swallowed frame); the wrapper records the peer user message itself (item notifications never carry userMessage — no double render, no invisible delivery) and reports `peer_message_result` both ways — ok:false re-stashes the text server-side so a promised message is never lost.
- **Dead-wiring fix (found while wiring the above, 2.355.0 class)**: `recordCodexQuotaSignal` was exported by the engine and destructured by session-stdout but server.js never passed it through — the `?.` call silently no-op'd, so the ENTIRE codex quota signal chain (rate_limits_updated cache writes, exhaustion escape ladder, reset_credit_result) had been dead in production since 2.368.21 while its unit pins glowed green. Wired through both server.js touch points; scripts/test-peer-delivery.mjs (19, in gate) now pins the wiring alongside the functional rung test (real deliver.create() + real sidecar + negative controls: old wrapper, claude-backend session).

- **P3 verdict: codex hot-switch is IMPOSSIBLE with the current CLI — experimentally refuted twice over.** The app-server canonicalizes CODEX_HOME to the real path at startup (a symlink repoint never reaches a running process — its own stderr prints the dereferenced `AbsolutePathBuf`), and a turn completed normally after auth.json's *content* was swapped to garbage tokens (tokens live in process memory). Cold-restart switching is codex's ceiling, not our implementation's.
- **Per-backend switching capabilities are now an interface** (P4 first slice, owner ask "接口化之后怎么区分冷切热切"): `src/backend-caps.js` declares per backend `{pool, hotSwitch: verified|impossible|unverified, planC, sealedOrders, resetCredit, quotaProbe}` — the pool engine gates on capabilities instead of backend ids (hot only where a live re-read is *verified*; an unknown backend gets no pool, cold, no credits). A future agent adds a caps row, never an if-chain. `test-codex-pool` 17→28.

New: Manage Agents grows "+ Add pooled account…" in the ChatGPT section; the codex spawn resolver takes a pool id with the same signed-out-target self-heal as claude's; the wrapper now RELAYS every account/rateLimits/updated push to the server (the sidecar was display-only) and forwards the typed codex_error_info on failures (it used to be dropped) — readings land in the current MEMBER's usage cache, a tripped rate_limit_reached_type or a usage_limit_reached/quota_exceeded/workspace_* error triggers the pool switch first and arms auto-resume as the fallback, and 'unauthorized' is surfaced as an event. **Hot switching is structurally OFF for codex pools** — claude's hot path rests on a forensically verified per-request credential re-read; codex's long-lived app-server has no such proof, so hot waits for the P3 symlink-swap verification. Sealed orders and plan-C per-session links stay claude-only. New gate suite test-codex-pool (17).

Codex collab/sub-agent turns stream **several message items concurrently, interleaved delta-by-delta** (real buffer: two item ids alternating per character); our delta handler finalized *every* open stream whenever a delta with a new key arrived, so each key switch chopped both messages into per-run fragments. ## 2.368.15

- **Background tasks no longer show "running" forever after they finished** (owner: "基本每个对话都有已经结束的后台任务依然显示为正在进行"). Root cause: every task-lifecycle closer resolved the task's card via `pendingToolCalls` — the permission/result matcher whose entry the tool_result DELETES. A background command's result arrives in seconds ("Command running in background with ID…"), its completion notification minutes later, so the lookup always came up empty and the 2.233.0 closer never fired (its test passed only because it skipped the tool_result).
